issues.body:
## Summary

The Microsoft Store update of the ChatGPT / Codex Windows app hangs forever in the `PackagesInUseClosed` state on my machine, even though the download and staging steps always succeed. The cause is a **leftover `codex-chrome-native-host.exe`** — the native messaging host of the ChatGPT browser extension — which keeps the *old* package's deployment metadata open, so AppX can never satisfy the "no one is using the old package" precondition and cancels the register after ~10 minutes with no visible error in the Store UI.

I believe this is **two independent problems** that are often conflated:

- **(A) `PrimaryRuntime` cleanup keeps failing** with `0x80073D02` / `Failure in the DynamicDependenciesInUse state handler`. This matches the behaviour reported in #62596 and #62868, is present on my machine too, but is **not user-fixable** — it only logs errors and does not by itself block the update.
- **(B) The main app package fails to re-register** because of the leftover native messaging host. This one *is* diagnosable and work-aroundable, and I believe it is the actual reason the update "hangs forever" for many users.

Note the difference between the two: **(A) produces error events; (B) produces the hang.**

## Environment

- Windows 11 Home (China) x64, `DisplayVersion=25H2`, build **26200.9457** (registry `CurrentBuild=26200.9457`)
- Note: I am **not** on the two KBs suspected by @mdruy — `KB5127936` and `KB5132061` are **not installed** on this machine (no matching `WinSxS` / CBS rollup package). The only cumulative rollup packages present are `26100.1742.1.10` and `26100.9457.1.0`.
- `OpenAI.Codex` package family `OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0`, Store-signed (`SignatureKind=Store`), Store ProductId `9PLM9XGG6VKS`
- Subscription: Plus
- Non-admin user, UAC elevation available

## (A) Persisting `0x80073D02` on `OpenAI.CodexPrimaryRuntime`

Present here as well, but with **no** `0x8007045B` / `0x800706D9` / `os error 1008` companions (I searched 14 days of `AppXDeploymentServer/Operational`, `AppModel-Runtime/Admin` and `System` — zero hits for all three). Also worth noting for triage: this machine does **not** have `KB5127936` or `KB5132061` installed, and the problem still reproduces.

### Current state — multiple `PrimaryRuntime` versions coexist

```
OpenAI.CodexPrimaryRuntime.v26-1111-570-0 | 26.1111.570.0 | NotAvailable
OpenAI.CodexPrimaryRuntime.v26-1118-904-0 | 26.1118.904.0 | Ok
OpenAI.CodexPrimaryRuntime.v26-1119-907-0 | 26.1119.907.0 | NotAvailable
OpenAI.CodexPrimaryRuntime.v26-1123-915-0 | 26.1123.915.0 | Ok
OpenAI.Codex                          | 26.1120.5083.0 | Ok
```

### Error volume — last 3 days, `AppXDeploymentServer/Operational`

```
total 0x80073D02 events = 40
  id=605 (Failure in the DynamicDependenciesInUse state handler) x19
  id=664 (The request cannot be processed because package ... is in use) x16
  id=404 (AppX Deployment operation failed)                     x5
  package OpenAI.CodexPrimaryRuntime.v26-1119-907-0  x16
  package OpenAI.CodexPrimaryRuntime.v26-1123-915-0  x2
```

### The failure loop is a remove/requeue cycle on every deploy

```
id=855 Finished resolving action lists. removePackageList: OpenAI.CodexPrimaryRuntime.v26-1119-907-0_...
id=603 Started deployment Remove operation ... Options DeferRemovalWhenPackagesAreInUse
id=664 Error 0x80073D02: The request cannot be processed because package ... is in use.
id=674 Removal of package ... is deferred because it is currently in use.
id=626 Deployment Remove operation ... has been requeued for user SID ...-1001
id=607 Deployment Remove operation ... has been de-queued and is running for user SID ...-1001
```

Notably `id=674` says *"Removal ... is deferred because it is currently in use"* and `id=626` says *"has been requeued"*, i.e. AppX itself decides to keep retrying forever.

### `Remove-AppxPackage` on an idle `PrimaryRuntime` never returns

This is the part I could not work around. With the app closed and the service stopped, removing a `NotAvailable` runtime hangs indefinitely:

```
Remove-AppxPackage -Package OpenAI.CodexPrimaryRuntime.v26-1111-570-0_...  -> TIMEOUT after 90 s, package still present
Remove-AppxPackage -Package OpenAI.CodexPrimaryRuntime.v26-1119-907-0_...  -> TIMEOUT after 90 s, package still present
```

The Restart Manager API (`RmStartSession` / `RmRegisterResources` / `RmGetList`) reports **no process holding any file** in those package directories — so it is not a file-handle lock, it is the package-removal path itself hanging.

### What does clear the marker

Deleting the stale markers under
`HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Appx\AppxAllUserStore\DeferredRemoval\<SID>\PackageFullNames\`
(**note: these are child *keys*, not values**) lets the deployment queue drain again and a subsequent register succeeds. This is a workaround, not a fix — the markers come back.

## (B) The update hang has a second, separate cause: leftover native messaging host

This is the part that makes the update *hang* rather than merely log errors, and I don't see it in the reports above.

### Symptom

The Store stages the new build fine, then the register step hangs in `PackagesInUseClosed` and is cancelled after ~10 minutes:

```
id=603 Started deployment RegisterByPackageFamilyName ... Options ForceTargetApplicationShutdownOption,RegisterHighestVersion,FailIfNeedsRemediation
id=678 Deployment Register operation with main parameter OpenAI.Codex_26.1116.6628.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0
      is hung and cancelled. Failure occurred in the PackagesInUseClosed state handler.
id=615 Deployment Register operation ... has been cancelled by the caller.
```

### The holder

`codex-chrome-native-host.exe` (the Chrome/Edge native messaging host for the ChatGPT browser extension) stays alive long after the browser tab is gone, holding deployment metadata of the **old** package under:

```
C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\AppRepository\Packages\OpenAI.Codex_<oldversion>_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0\
```

Restart Manager on that directory returns the holder(s):

```
pid=16312 extension-host.exe  (chrome-extension://hehggadaopoacecdllhhajmbjkdcmajg/)
pid=26412 extension-host.exe
pid=27780 extension-host.exe
pid=41212 extension-host.exe
```

with command lines like:

```
codex-chrome-native-host.exe chrome-extension://hehggadaopoacecdllhhajmbjkdcmajg/ --parent-window=0
```

`--parent-window=0` means a **background service worker** started it; it then waits for the native-messaging pipe peer to disappear, which never happens because the worker is gone. On my machine these processes survived **13–25 hours** (oldest `11-23 10:45:08`, newest `11-23 23:09:27`) even though I was not using the extension at all.

### Why killing them is not enough

Chrome/Edge re-launch the host immediately when the extension is still installed, so the "old package in use" condition re-arms within seconds. The only reliable way I found is to remove the native-messaging registration for the duration of the update:

```
HKCU\SOFTWARE\Google\Chrome\NativeMessagingHosts\com.openai.codexextension
  -> C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\OpenAI\extension\com.openai.codexextension.json
```

The manifest's `path` is an **alias resolved by package family name**:

```json
"path": "C:\\Users\\<user>\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\WindowsApps\\OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0\\codex-chrome-native-host.exe"
```

so it always launches from whatever version is currently registered — meaning the host is guaranteed to hold the old package during an update. I believe this alias is the underlying design issue (see also the Chrome-plugin packaging discussion in #32706): the Store's `ForceTargetApplicationShutdownOption` only closes the app's main window, and it cannot touch a browser-spawned native host or a system service, so the update waits out the full timeout and cancels.

### The successful sequence I used (for reference)

1. Delete `HKCU\...\NativeMessagingHosts\com.openai.codexextension` **and** rename the manifest `.json` → `.json.disabled` (the registry key is re-created spontaneously by the browser extension / app itself, so a single measure is not enough).
2. Stop `CodexSandboxService.OpenAI.Codex` (it is `Automatic` and gets reinstalled with `Start=2` on every package install, so it must be stopped for the duration).
3. Kill all `extension-host.exe` and `ChatGPT.exe`.
4. Optionally disable `WSAIFabricSvc` (`HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\WSAIFabricSvc\Start=4`) — it otherwise re-locks the *new* package payload directory and it auto-restarts.
5. Sanity-check that the AppX deployment queue is healthy by re-registering an unrelated healthy package in place (e.g. `Microsoft.Winget.Source` via `Add-AppxPackage -Register ...\AppxManifest.xml`). If that completes in a few seconds, the queue is not blocked.
6. Register the new build: `Add-AppxPackage -Register <new>\AppxManifest.xml -DisableDevelopmentMode -ForceApplicationShutdown`.

Result on my machine: `26.1111.9664.0 → 26.1117.4957.0 → 26.1120.5083.0`, all three transitions completing in seconds-to-minutes with `id=400 ... finished successfully`, **no reboot required**.

### Reproduction rate before the workaround

Every Store-driven update attempt in this cycle failed the same way (`id=678`, `PackagesInUseClosed`), across versions 26.1103.7773.0 → 26.1106.6628.0 → 26.1111.2228.0 → 26.1111.9664.0 → 26.1120.5083.0.

## Additional notes

- The app's own in-app updater (`CallerApplicationId: ChatGPT-SearchForUpdatesWithPausedAddAsync`) triggers the same path, so the failure also occurs without touching the Store UI.
- The Store UI itself failed to launch in my environment (`TWinUI/Operational` → `id=5961 Activation for Microsoft.WindowsStore_...!App failed. Error code: The app didn't start in the required time.. Activation phase: COM App activation`, plus `0x80040905`), so I had to drive the install through `Windows.ApplicationModel.Store.Preview.InstallControl.AppInstallManager` → `SearchForUpdatesAsync(productId, skuId)`. This may be unrelated, but it is reproducible here on Store build `22609.1401.13.0`.
- `Remove-AppxPackage` on the `NotAvailable` runtimes never completes (see above), so uninstall/reinstall of the runtime packages is not a usable workaround.
- Uninstalling and reinstalling the app does not help for (A): the `PrimaryRuntime` errors reappear immediately.

## What would help

1. Confirm whether the `PrimaryRuntime` `0x80073D02` loop is a known Windows/AppX regression (it reproduces on a build that has **neither** `KB5127936` nor `KB5132061` installed here, so it may predate those updates or have another trigger).
2. Consider making the ChatGPT browser extension's native messaging host **not** hold the registered package open — e.g. resolve the host binary from a fixed, version-independent location, or have the Store's update flow signal the host to exit (like `ForceTargetApplicationShutdownOption` does for the app).
3. Ideally the `PrimaryRuntime` packages would be superseded/removed by the same deployment operation that installs the new one, instead of leaving `NotAvailable` markers that are then retried forever.

Happy to provide additional logs (full `AppXDeploymentServer/Operational` excerpts, Restart Manager output, or a repro script) if useful.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1111.9664.0 -  26.1117.3838.0 

### What subscription do you have?

Plus 

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26300.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

Since more than a week (also after Windows 2026-10 Preview Update (KB5127936) and 2026-11 Security Update (KB5132061) on 11/11/2026), underlying AppX deployment, AppContainer, and package cleanup bugs introduced in this build are also impacting the Desktop ChatGPT / Codex app.

The ChatGPT for Windows and Codex App is throwing new errors and bugs. These `0x80073D02` (`ERROR_PACKAGES_IN_USE`) errors cannot be resolved on the user side—regardless of any troubleshooting. They only disappear when uninstalling ChatGPT and immediately reappear upon reinstallation:

### At every boot (`AppXDeployment-Server` - 3 errors) — `svchost.exe (wsappx -p)`
* `Error 0x80073D02: The request cannot be processed because package OpenAI.CodexPrimaryRuntime.<version>_x64__3k8sg7r9htsxt is in use.`
* `Deployment Remove operation with target volume C: on Package OpenAI.CodexPrimaryRuntime.<version>_x64__3k8sg7r9htsxt from: (OpenAI.CodexPrimaryRuntime.<version>_x64__3k8sg7r9htsxt) failed with error 0x80073D02.`
* `AppX Deployment operation failed for package OpenAI.CodexPrimaryRuntime.<version>_x64__3k8sg7r9htsxt with error 0x80073D02. The specific error text for this failure is: Error 0x80073D02: The request cannot be processed because package OpenAI.CodexPrimaryRuntime.<version>_x64__3k8sg7r9htsxt is in use.`

### Every time the ChatGPT / Codex app is opened (`AppXDeployment-Server` - 2 errors)
* `Error 0x80073D02: The request cannot be processed because package OpenAI.CodexPrimaryRuntime.<version>_x64__3k8sg7r9htsxt is in use.`
* `Deployment Remove operation with target volume C: on Package OpenAI.CodexPrimaryRuntime.<version>_x64__3k8sg7r9htsxt from: (OpenAI.CodexPrimaryRuntime.<version>_x64__3k8sg7r9htsxt) failed with error 0x80073D02.`

### Pre-existing errors on exits/reboots
These errors were already appearing occasionally before these updates (for months) on exits/reboots as Codex/OpenAI tries to start this system service early (along with the Codex OpenAI Sandbox service not being able to complete the function - `error OS 1800` on the subsequent boot):
* **`AppXDeployment` (2):** `Failed to start system service: appxsvc with error: 0x8007045B (2)`
* **`CodexSandboxService.OpenAI.Codex` (2, sometimes 4):** `unable to restore package uninstall listener: open the logged-in user’s token and os error 1008` *(the last error records disappear when `DelayedStart 1` is added to the service).*

### Also introduced with a recent Windows November Update (`AppModel-Runtime`) and only happening on Codex/Chat GPT Windows installations.
* `DeleteAppContainerProfile failed with error 0x800706D9 because it was unable to unregister with the firewall.`
* `CreateAppContainerProfile failed for AppContainer onecore\ds\security\gina\profile\profext\appcontainer.cpp Line:1962 defenderaiplatformhost DefenderAiPlatformHost with error 0x800706D9.`

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

- One time: Install the ChatGPT desktop app from Microsoft Store and sign in.

- Restart Windows.
- Do or do not not manually launch ChatGPT or use Codex.  
- Open the Windows Application event log.
- Observe the errors on boot : 3 AppXDeployment-Server (0x80073D02), 2 AppModel-Runtime (0x800706D9) 
- Occionally also 2 CodexSandboxService.OpenAI.Codex` (can't complete function / unable to restore package uninstall listener error 1008).
- Observe also other errors from shutdown/reboot such as 2 AppXDeployment: Failed to start system service: appxsvc with error: 0x8007045B.
- Repeat the restart: the same errors return. 

- Open the Chat GPT desktop app 
- Observe 3 `0x80073D02` (ERROR_PACKAGES_IN_USE) for OpenAI.CodexPrimaryRuntime

### What is the expected behavior?

1. No errors should appear in Event Viewer on boot or opening the Chat GPT Desktop app for the runtime package. 
2. The installed tasks and services should start or deploy successfully without producing bugs, duplicate errors after every single boot, including or besides when ChatGPT is not opened or used. 
3. The app package should be deployed or removed succesfully especially when resources are not in use.


### Additional information

Reinstalling or a clean Windows/PC reset and installation does not fix this. The version is marked with a placeholder because it updates frequently to a new version package, keeps trying to remove the current one, and keeps failing on boot—even when ChatGPT is not running or anything.

The only way to fix these errors is by uninstalling Codex / the Desktop ChatGPT app, but it comes back again after reinstalling — I have been through every troubleshooting step.

> **Note:** Please note that I monitor all logs (errors and alerts) across all log sources and files, not just the ones filtered under Administrative Events.

Version app : until 26.1117.3838.0 
Windows 11 Pro - 26H2 - 26300.9974 to 26300.10075

Errors started to appear after 30 October - 10 November 2026 - not before.

issues.title: Windows: Browser/Computer Use crashes on start: trusted-worker.js gets NODE_REPL_TRUSTED_SERVICES undefined (trusted Node process exited unexpectedly / cua is not defined)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
## Summary

After the sandbox ACL fix (#51822) landed in CLI 0.163.0, the os error 32 setup failure from #51590 is gone (`setup refresh: ... errors=[]`). Browser Use still fails every time, in both the desktop app and the CLI:

- `trusted Node process exited unexpectedly; kernel reset, rerun your request`
- on retry: `cua is not defined`

The cause is visible in the MCP server stderr: `trusted-worker.js` gets no `NODE_REPL_TRUSTED_SERVICES` in its environment and throws on `JSON.parse`.

## Versions

- Windows 11 Pro, build 26300
- Codex CLI 0.163.0 (npm)
- Codex desktop (Microsoft Store) 26.1007.9446.0
- Bundled plugins `unified-computer-use` / `computer-use` / `browser` 26.1007.71326
- cua_node runtime `a9ba6825a525118c`, Node v24.21.0
- `[windows] sandbox = "elevated"` (same result with `unelevated`, see below)

## Stderr from the cua_repl MCP server (every attempt)

```
<anonymous_script>:1
undefined
^

SyntaxError: "undefined" is not valid JSON
    at JSON.parse (<anonymous>)
    at Object.<anonymous> (%TEMP%\.tmpIveTVU\trusted-worker.js:23:33)
    at Module._compile (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1929:14)
    ...
    at [eval]:63:24

Node.js v24.21.0
```

`trusted-worker.js` line 23:

```js
const configuredServices = JSON.parse(process.env.NODE_REPL_TRUSTED_SERVICES);
```

## Where the variable disappears

1. The plugin's `.mcp.json` (`unified-computer-use/26.1007.71326`) starts `cua_repl` (`node.exe ...@oai/cua-repl/bin/cua-repl.mjs`) with `"NODE_REPL_TRUSTED_SERVICES": "{\"browser\":\"@oai/browser-desktop/service\"}"` in `env`.
2. `@oai/cua-repl/dist/.../launch.js` spawns `node_repl.exe` with `env: { ...process.env, NODE_REPL_TRUSTED_SERVICES: process.env.NODE_REPL_TRUSTED_SERVICES ?? JSON.stringify(default), ... }`, so the variable is set at this point.
3. `node_repl.exe` launches `trusted-worker.js`, and the variable is undefined there.

So the variable is dropped inside `node_repl.exe` when it builds the trusted worker's environment. It never reaches the worker.

## Ruled out

- **Stale config paths:** all `node_repl` / `cua_repl` paths point to the current runtime and plugin version, and every file exists.
- **`shell_environment_policy`:** same crash with `-c "shell_environment_policy.include_only=[]"`.
- **Elevated sandbox:** same crash with `-c "windows.sandbox='unelevated'"`. The sandbox log confirms `Windows sandbox selection: unelevated`.
- **Desktop app vs. CLI:** both fail identically. They share the same cua_node runtime.

## Repro

1. Windows, desktop 26.1007.9446.0, CLI 0.163.0.
2. Start a fresh session and ask it to "test browser use on example.com".
3. The first browser action fails with "trusted Node process exited unexpectedly", and the retry fails with "cua is not defined". The stderr above appears in `~/.codex/logs_2.sqlite` under `codex_rmcp_client::stdio_server_launcher`.

Related: #51590 (sandbox ACL failure, now fixed by #51822). This report is the failure that remains after that fix.

issues.title: Allow a configurable, input-method-independent shortcut for the skill launcher

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: skills
labels.description: Issues related to skills

issues.body:
### What feature would you like to see?

Please provide an input-method-independent way to open the Skill picker in the Codex desktop app, and ideally allow users to customize the trigger.

Today, explicit Skill invocation depends on typing the ASCII dollar sign (`$`). This is fragile for users who regularly switch keyboard layouts or input methods: the same physical key can produce a different character depending on the active input source, so the Skill picker does not open unless the user switches input methods or pastes an ASCII `$`.

Possible solutions:

- Add an “Open Skill picker” action under **Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts**.
- Allow the Skill launcher trigger to be customized.
- Provide a reliable composer command such as `/skills` in the desktop app.
- Optionally recognize suitable locale-specific/full-width variants and normalize them to the ASCII trigger.

### Why is this needed?

Skill selection is an application action, but its only reliable entry point is currently tied to producing one specific text character. This makes the workflow dependent on keyboard layout and IME state.

For multilingual users, switching input sources just to invoke a Skill is easy to forget and interrupts typing. It is also less discoverable than a normal configurable app shortcut.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a local Codex conversation in the ChatGPT/Codex desktop app.
2. Switch to an input method or keyboard layout where the key normally used for `$` does not emit the ASCII dollar sign.
3. Focus an empty composer and press that key combination.
4. Observe that a different character is inserted and the Skill picker does not open.
5. Switch to an input source that emits ASCII `$`, type it again, and observe that the Skill picker can open.

### Expected behavior

Users can open the Skill picker without changing the active input method, preferably through a configurable keyboard shortcut or a dedicated command.

### Current behavior

The Skill picker is coupled to the literal ASCII `$` character. The desktop app’s Keyboard Shortcuts settings allow command shortcuts to be customized, but do not expose a Skill-picker action or a configurable Skill mention prefix.

### Environment

- ChatGPT/Codex desktop app: `26.1120.41243`
- macOS: `26.5.1`
- Architecture: Apple Silicon (`arm64`)

### Related

- #30700 requests binding arbitrary prompts or individual Skills to keyboard shortcuts. This request is narrower: provide an accessible, layout/IME-independent entry point to the Skill picker itself.
- Documentation currently describes `$` as the explicit Skill invocation entry point: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills

issues.body:
I’m disappointed with my experience using GPT-6.2 SOL in Codex/Work. Compared with GPT-6.1 SOL, it feels like a regression in instruction following and in the ability to carry a task through to completion.

I use Codex to evaluate coding projects, including through computer use. In one Max/MSP project, it asked me to make selections so it could move the objects. It also presented very partial work and stopped, leaving me to keep directing it toward the original goal.

The problem extends beyond individual interactions. It showed little initiative in understanding the project’s objectives, identifying which functionality needed to be evaluated, or demonstrating whether the project fulfilled its purpose. Reaching the end goal required repeated follow-up instructions for steps I expected it to work out and pursue itself.

The experience feels passive and, frankly, lazy. I’m describing the behavior as a user: partial results, premature stopping, and routine work being handed back to me. I have experienced the same pattern across everything I have asked it to do today.

I expect Codex to investigate the project, connect its evaluation to the stated objectives, exercise the relevant functionality, and continue until the requested work is complete or it encounters a concrete limitation that it explains clearly.

With GPT-6.1 SOL, this workflow felt more capable and required less supervision. GPT-6.2 SOL has made it considerably more laborious. Please investigate this apparent regression in instruction following, initiative, and persistence.

issues.title: Automatically isolate and coordinate concurrent writes across chats and agents

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: subagent
labels.description: Issues involving subagents or multi-agent features

issues.body:
### What feature would you like to see?

Codex should automatically isolate and coordinate filesystem writes when multiple chats or agents work on the same local project.

Today, chat isolation is not filesystem isolation. A main chat, side/fork chat, or subagent can share the same Local checkout and modify the same file concurrently. This can overwrite newer changes, make an agent operate on stale file contents, or leave the user to resolve conflicts that the orchestration layer created.

The current workaround—manually deciding which chat uses Local, creating a separate worktree for every writing chat, assigning file ownership, and coordinating handoff/merge order—is too much concurrency management to push onto the user. Worktrees and Handoff already provide useful primitives, but Codex should apply them automatically.

### Example scenario

1. Open a local Git project in the Codex desktop app.
2. Start Chat A in Local and ask it to modify a file.
3. Start a side/fork chat, or have the task use a subagent, and ask it to work on an overlapping feature or the same file.
4. Both executions read and write the shared checkout without a clear ownership or coordination boundary.
5. One execution may overwrite or invalidate the other's changes, or the user must manually coordinate worktrees and integration.

The same underlying problem applies to multiple independent Codex chats that point at the same Local checkout.

### Expected behavior

Codex should make concurrent writing safe by default. For example:

* Automatically give each writing chat an isolated managed worktree, while allowing read-only chats to share the Local checkout.
* Detect overlapping write sets and serialize them, or assign explicit file/directory ownership between agents.
* Before applying a patch, verify that the file still matches the version the agent read; if it changed, re-read and recompute instead of overwriting it.
* Have the parent agent coordinate subagent writes and integrate their commits in a deterministic queue.
* Automatically rebase/merge isolated results and run relevant validation.
* Ask the user only when there is a genuine semantic conflict that Codex cannot resolve safely.
* Clearly show which checkout/worktree owns each active writing task.

Starting another chat or delegating to an agent should not require the user to understand and manually operate Git worktrees merely to prevent data loss.

### Related issues

* openai/codex#5807 covers overwriting files changed externally due to stale file state.
* openai/codex#24224 covers workspace context leaking across concurrent sessions in different projects.

This request is distinct: it is about safe, automatic coordination of concurrent writes by multiple Codex chats/agents intentionally working in the same project.

应用版本和 build 已从本机安装的应用信息核对。用户提供的新建页截图显示“工作”“使用 ChatGPT Work”，但没有原来的本地／云端运行位置选择器。截图与私人聊天记录不随本报告公开上传。

## 用户投诉

这是非常糟糕的使用体验。基础控制入口突然不见，没有清晰解释，助手还不断指引用户去点击根本不存在的按钮，让用户反复折腾。

请明确回答：这是故障还是有意移除？如果是故障，什么时候修复？如果是改版，替代入口到底在哪里？

请提供能实际操作的恢复方法，保留现有聊天与文件。不要再用“可以读取本地文件”回避“用户失去了运行位置选择权”这个问题。

## 复现路径与预期

1. 在 Mac 桌面应用中进入 Work（工作）。
2. 打开新建聊天页。
3. 查看消息输入区域及其下方的运行位置控件。

实际：没有可见的本地／云端运行选择器。

预期：用户能明确查看、选择运行位置；如果入口迁移或当前账号不支持，应显示明确说明和可操作的替代路径。

## 相关报告及证据边界

- #62943：Windows 新聊天缺少运行位置等控件，旧聊天仍有。
- #63042：Windows 用户报告运行位置选择器随联网状态变化。
- #62925：Windows 用户报告选择器消失后仍能访问本地文件，但本地服务连接受限。

本报告补充 macOS 的同类界面症状，不声称已证明与上述 Windows 报告具有相同根因。尚未确定是客户端回归、服务端配置变化还是有意调整；也没有在这台 Mac 上验证上述报告中的断网或降级方法。

请确认受影响范围、修复计划或受支持的恢复方式。

---

## English translation

### Problem and environment

In ChatGPT for macOS 26.1117.41037 (build 29803), the Local/Cloud selector is missing when starting a new Work chat. Users cannot explicitly choose where the task runs, disrupting their normal workflow.

The application version and build were verified from the installed application's metadata. The user's screenshot of the new-chat page shows Work and the “Use ChatGPT Work” placeholder, but not the previous Local/Cloud execution-location selector. The screenshot and private conversation records are not being publicly uploaded with this report.

### User complaint

This is a very poor user experience. A basic control has disappeared without a clear explanation, and the assistant keeps directing the user to click buttons that do not exist, wasting the user's time.

Please give a clear answer: Is this a bug or an intentional removal? If it is a bug, when will it be fixed? If it is a redesign, where exactly is the replacement control?

Please provide an actionable recovery method that preserves existing conversations and files. Saying that the task “can read local files” does not address the actual complaint: the user has lost the ability to choose the execution location.

### Reproduction steps and expected behavior

1. Open Work in the macOS desktop application.
2. Open the new-chat page.
3. Look for the execution-location control in or beneath the message composer.

Actual: No visible Local/Cloud execution-location selector.

Expected: Users can clearly inspect and select the execution location. If the control has moved or is unavailable for the current account, the application should explain this and provide an actionable alternative.

### Related reports and limits of the evidence

- #62943: New Windows conversations lack execution-location and other controls, while existing conversations retain them.
- #63042: Windows users report that the execution-location selector's visibility changes with internet connectivity.
- #62925: Windows users report that local files remain accessible after the selector disappears, but access to local services is restricted.

This report adds a similar UI symptom on macOS. It does not claim that the macOS and Windows reports have been proven to share the same root cause. We have not established whether this is a client regression, a server-side configuration change, or an intentional change. The offline-launch and downgrade workarounds reported elsewhere have not been tested on this Mac.

Please clarify the affected scope, the fix plan, or a supported recovery method.

issues.body: ### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)? OpenAI.Codex 26.1013.3656.0 ### What subscription do you have? ChatGPT Plus ### What platform is your computer? Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64 ### What issue are you seeing? I am unable to send messages in any newly created ChatGPT Work thread in the Windows desktop application. After opening a new Work thread and typing a message, the Send button remains disabled (dimmed) and does not respond to clicks. No message is submitted, and no error message is displayed. The issue occurs consistently, regardless of whether a local project is selected. It affects all newly created Work threads, not just one particular project. However, existing conversations in the desktop application continue to work normally, and I can successfully create and use Work threads in the web version of ChatGPT. The application itself opens normally and accepts text input. The problem appears to be specifically related to enabling message submission or initializing new Work threads in the Windows desktop application. The issue persists after updating, reinstalling, and repairing the application. ### What steps can reproduce the bug? 1. Launch the ChatGPT desktop application on Windows. 2. Start a new conversation. 3. Select the "Work" mode at the top of the interface. 4. Leave the project selector empty ("Select Project"). 5. Type a simple message, such as "Hello". 6. Observe that the Send button remains disabled and clicking it has no effect. 7. Select an existing local project and repeat the test. The same issue occurs. **Reproducibility:** Consistent across newly created Work threads. **Comparison tests:** - Existing desktop conversations: Sending messages works. - New Work threads in the web version: Works normally. - New Work threads without a project in the Windows desktop application: Fails. - New Work threads within a local project in the Windows desktop application: Fails. No code snippet or special prompt is required to reproduce the issue. ### What is the expected behavior? When I create a new Work thread and enter a non-empty message, the Send button should become enabled. Clicking the Send button or pressing Enter should submit the message, create the new Work conversation, and start processing the request. This behavior should work both with and without a local project selected, just as it does in the web version of ChatGPT. ### Additional information **Troubleshooting already performed:** - Updated the desktop application to the latest version available to me. - Uninstalled and reinstalled the desktop application. - Used the Windows application "Repair" function. - Tested newly created Work threads both inside and outside local projects. - Confirmed that existing desktop conversations still work. - Confirmed that Work threads can be created and used normally in the browser. - Attempted to open developer tools using F12 and Ctrl+Shift+I, but neither shortcut opened them. None of these actions resolved the issue. **Local data preservation:** I have important local Work conversations, research projects, and associated files. I have made a backup of the application's local package directory: `OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0` However, I have not verified whether this backup can fully restore local Work conversations. I have deliberately avoided using the Windows application "Reset" function because I do not want to risk losing existing local conversations or project data. **Questions for the developers:** 1. Is this a known issue affecting the Windows desktop application's new Work thread initialization? 2. Is there a fix or workaround that does not require resetting or deleting local application data? 3. How can I collect relevant diagnostic logs for this problem? 4. Can the application be reset without losing local Work conversations, and is there an officially supported backup and restore procedure? I can provide further diagnostics and screenshots if needed. **In-app diagnostic feedback** I have also submitted a bug report through the ChatGPT Windows desktop application's built-in feedback feature. The application confirmed that the feedback was submitted successfully and provided the following Feedback ID: `no-active-thread-01a14407-46d5-75a0-ab8b-f9d93e8abe9e` Please use this Feedback ID to correlate the in-app report with this GitHub issue, if supported. The issue remains unresolved: new Work threads cannot send messages because the Send button remains disabled.

issues.body:
### What happened?

In the Codex desktop app Hooks settings page, configured hooks are displayed only as generic rows such as `Hook 1`, `Hook 2`, `Hook 3` (localized as `钩子 1`, `钩子 2`, etc.).

When several hooks are registered under the same lifecycle event, it is hard to tell which toggle belongs to which hook without inspecting the underlying config manually.

Example from my current `~/.codex/hooks.json`:

```text
PreToolUse Hook 1: matcher=Bash  command=... run-hook-codex.sh vibeguard-pre-bash-guard.sh
PreToolUse Hook 2: matcher=Edit  command=... run-hook-codex.sh vibeguard-pre-edit-guard.sh
PreToolUse Hook 3: matcher=Write command=... run-hook-codex.sh vibeguard-pre-write-guard.sh

PostToolUse Hook 1: matcher=Edit       command=... run-hook-codex.sh vibeguard-post-edit-guard.sh
PostToolUse Hook 2: matcher=Write      command=... run-hook-codex.sh vibeguard-post-write-guard.sh
PostToolUse Hook 3: matcher=Bash       command=... run-hook-codex.sh vibeguard-post-build-check.sh
PostToolUse Hook 4: matcher=Edit|Write command=... run-hook-codex.sh vibeguard-post-build-check.sh

Stop Hook 1: command=... run-hook-codex.sh vibeguard-stop-guard.sh
Stop Hook 2: command=... run-hook-codex.sh vibeguard-learn-evaluator.sh
Stop Hook 3: command=... remem summarize
```

The UI only shows `Hook 1`, `Hook 2`, etc. for these rows, so the user cannot tell at a glance whether a row is `vibeguard-pre-bash-guard.sh`, `vibeguard-post-build-check.sh`, `remem summarize`, etc.

### Expected behavior

The Hooks settings page should show a human-readable label per hook row. Good fallbacks would be, in order:

1. An explicit hook `name` / `displayName` if the config schema supports it.
2. The command basename or script name, for example `vibeguard-pre-bash-guard.sh`.
3. The matcher plus command basename, for example `Bash · vibeguard-pre-bash-guard.sh`.
4. Only fall back to `Hook {index}` if no better label can be derived.

This would make the toggles understandable and reduce the chance of disabling or trusting the wrong hook.

### Actual behavior

All rows under an event use the fallback label `Hook {index}`. In zh-CN this appears as `钩子 {index}`.

I inspected the packaged webview bundle for the installed app and found the hook row title path using the `settings.hooks.event.fallbackHookTitle` string (`Hook {index}`). I did not see the settings page rendering a command/script-derived label for the row.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure multiple hooks in `~/.codex/hooks.json` under the same lifecycle event, for example several `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, or `Stop` hooks.
2. Open Codex desktop app.
3. Go to Settings → Hooks.
4. Expand a hook event section.
5. Observe that rows are labeled only `Hook 1`, `Hook 2`, etc.

### Environment

- Codex desktop app: `26.527.31326` (build `3390`)
- Bundled CLI: `codex-cli 0.135.0-alpha.1`
- OS: macOS `26.2` (`25C56`)
- Locale observed: zh-CN, but the issue appears to come from the generic fallback label rather than the locale itself.

### Notes

This does not appear to affect hook execution. It is a settings UI discoverability issue: the active hooks work, but the user cannot identify them from the settings page labels.

issues.title: Locked Use authorization plugin leaves the login keychain permanently locked for the rest of the session

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: auth
labels.description: Issues related to authentication and accounts

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.818.41509

### What subscription do you have?

pro 5x

### What platform is your computer?

## Environment  | | | |---|---| | macOS | 26.5.2 (25F84), Apple Silicon | | FileVault | On | | ChatGPT.app | 26.818.41509 (6962) | | Installed authorization plugin | **799** (`CFBundleShortVersionString` 0.1.0) | | Plugin bundled in ChatGPT.app installer | **1000816** (26.819.1000816) | | `~/.codex/computer-use/Codex Computer Use.app` | **1000816** | | Plugin installed on | 2026-05-29 |

### What issue are you seeing?

# Locked Use authorization plugin leaves the login keychain permanently locked for the rest of the session

## Summary

The Computer Use / Locked Use authorization plugin (`com.openai.sky.CUAService.AuthorizationPlugin`) installs itself as the first mechanism in the `system.login.screensaver` authorization rule. On my machine this ends with the legacy login keychain (`login.keychain-db`) locked and unrecoverable for the entire login session: `loginwindow` reports a successful password unlock, but the credential it forwards to `SecKeychainLogin` is rejected with `-25293` (`errSecAuthFailed`). From that point on, every subsequent screen unlock takes a different code path that never attempts a keychain unlock at all.

The practical result is that every app relying on the login keychain (Chrome/Edge "Safe Storage", Electron apps, Office, CLI tools storing tokens) silently loses credential access and asks the user to sign in again — repeatedly, forever, until reboot.

I also found a clear version skew: the plugin actually installed under `/Library/Security/SecurityAgentPlugins/` is build **799**, while the copy bundled inside the current ChatGPT app (and the installer that ships with it) is build **1000816**. The installer's own `status` subcommand reports `OK: installed` and does not detect this.


## Impact

- All apps using the legacy login keychain lose stored credentials access and re-prompt for login after every screen unlock.
- The condition persists for the whole session. Only a full reboot plus a real password login at the login window restores it.
- `security show-keychain-info ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db` returns error 51 for the rest of the session.
- Easy to misdiagnose as keychain corruption. The obvious "fix" found in most support threads — resetting the login keychain — destroys all stored credentials and does not address the cause.

## Evidence

### 1. The authorization rule is modified, plugin first

```
$ security authorizationdb read system.login.screensaver
rule    = ["com.openai.sky.CUAService.AuthorizationPlugin.remote", "use-login-window-ui"]
k-of-n  = 1
created  = 736611419.328243   (2024-05-05, stock)
modified = 801745631.421675   (2026-05-29, when the plugin was installed)
```

The installer correctly saved the pristine rule beforehand:

```
/Library/Application Support/CodexComputerUseAuthorizationPlugin/backups/
  system.login.screensaver.20260529-190711.plist
  → rule = ["use-login-window-ui"], created == modified
```

### 2. Version skew, not reported by `status`

```
installed:  /Library/Security/SecurityAgentPlugins/CodexComputerUseAuthorizationPlugin.bundle
            CFBundleVersion 799,     CodeDirectory size=377 hashes=4+3
bundled:    .../Codex Computer Use Installer.app/Contents/Resources/
              CodexComputerUseAuthorizationPlugin.bundle
            CFBundleVersion 1000816, CodeDirectory size=665 hashes=13+3
```

The two Mach-O binaries have different SHA-256 hashes; both are validly signed by `Developer ID Application: OpenAI OpCo, LLC (2DC432GLL2)`.

```
$ CodexComputerUseAuthorizationPluginInstallerTool status <RESOURCE_DIR>
OK: installed
```

No version comparison is performed, so a stale plugin from May keeps serving an August service build indefinitely.

### 3. `loginwindow` has two distinct outcomes for the same method

Healthy (2026-08-21 19:45:10), before the failure began:

```
-[LWScreenLockAuthentication _authSuccessUsingPassword:forUser:]
  | Unlock succeeded, with password, attempting to unlock the login keychain
-[LWKeychainSupport unlockLoginKeychainFromScreenLock:pwd:]
  | SecKeychainLogin returned success
  | returning; 1
```

Broken (2026-08-22 22:07:40 onward), 125 occurrences since 2026-08-15:

```
-[LWScreenLockAuthentication _authSuccessUsingPassword:forUser:]
  | Screen saver unlocked by admin, did NOT unlock the user's keychain
```

### 4. The transition event — this is the core defect

```
2026-08-22 22:02:44.384  -[LWKeybagSupport nullKeybagUnlockForScreenLock]
                         | MKBUnlockDevice returned: -3, so will return NO
2026-08-22 22:02:46.743  -[LWScreenLockAuthentication _authSuccessUsingPassword:forUser:]
                         | Unlock succeeded, with password, attempting to unlock the login keychain
2026-08-22 22:02:46.846  [LWError] -[LWKeychainSupport unlockLoginKeychainFromScreenLock:pwd:]
                         | ERROR | Unable to unlock the keychain from screen unlock,
                           SecKeychainLogin returned -25293
2026-08-22 22:02:46.846  | returning; 0
2026-08-22 22:02:46.846  | Unlock succeeded, with password, attempting to unlock the keybag
                           UnlockSuccess = NO;
2026-08-22 22:07:40.101  | Screen saver unlocked by admin, did NOT unlock the user's keychain
```

`loginwindow` believes a password authentication succeeded and takes the correct branch, but the credential handed to `SecKeychainLogin` is rejected with `errSecAuthFailed`. The data-protection keybag unlock fails in the same window (`MKBUnlockDevice -3`, `UnlockSuccess = NO`). Every unlock after this point falls through to the "admin" branch, which never attempts a keychain unlock at all.

### 5. Downstream failures follow within ~100 ms

On 2026-08-23, all 9 occurrences of `did NOT unlock the user's keychain` were followed by `securityd` `CSSMERR_CSP_INVALID_DATA` (`-2147415994`) within **0.08–0.16 s**:

```
12:18:02.987  did NOT unlock  →  12:18:03.189  CSSMERR_CSP_INVALID_DATA
12:46:47.622  did NOT unlock  →  12:46:47.729  CSSMERR_CSP_INVALID_DATA
14:31:37.273  did NOT unlock  →  14:31:37.383  CSSMERR_CSP_INVALID_DATA
...  (9/9)
```

Affected clients observed: `iCloudHelper` (101 hits in 6 h), `parsec-fbf`, `sharingd`, `akd`, plus every Chromium/Electron app using Safe Storage.

Note: the same log line on 2026-08-21 (12:08, 20:03) produced **zero** keychain errors, because the keychain was still unlocked from an earlier real-password login. The line alone is necessary but not sufficient — the failure requires the keychain to have been locked with no working path to re-unlock it.

## What I ruled out

- **Keychain file corruption.** `login.keychain-db` is structurally intact: valid `kych` magic, schema size consistent with file length (4-byte trailer), 103 key blobs, `DbBlob` present at the tail. Its SHA-256 has been stable for hours while errors kept accumulating.
- **Password mismatch.** The account password has never been changed (`passwordLastSetTime` = account creation date).
- **Keychain auto-lock settings.** Parsed from the `DbBlob`: `idleTimeout = 0x7fffffff`, `lockOnSleep = 0`. The keychain does not lock on sleep or timeout.
- **Environment issues.** A freshly created test keychain completes create → lock → unlock → write → read normally in the same session, so `securityd` and the crypto path are healthy.
- **Second user account.** Only `root` and the primary user are admins.

## What I could not determine

- I found no log entries showing the plugin explicitly returning `DENY`, and no `SecurityAgentHelper` Library Validation rejection of the plugin, though both have been reported elsewhere. I can neither confirm nor rule these out.
- I cannot tell from outside whether build 1000816 fixes this, since the installed plugin was never upgraded on this machine.
- The exact reason `SecKeychainLogin` received a credential it rejected at 22:02:46 is not visible from OS logs alone; it requires plugin-side instrumentation.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Make the installer detect and repair version skew.** `status` should compare the installed bundle's `CFBundleVersion` against the shipped one and report a mismatch instead of `OK: installed`; the service should refuse to engage the authorization branch when the versions disagree.
2. **Fail safe rather than fail silent.** When the plugin's unlock path cannot supply a credential that satisfies `SecKeychainLogin`, it should fall back to the stock `use-login-window-ui` mechanism so `loginwindow` performs a normal password unlock, rather than leaving the session in a state where the keychain can never be reopened.
3. **Do not let a failed unlock poison the rest of the session.** After the first `SecKeychainLogin` failure, every later unlock silently skips the keychain entirely. A retry or an explicit user-visible error would make this diagnosable.
4. **Document the authorization plugin.** It modifies a system authorization rule and installs into `/Library/Security/SecurityAgentPlugins/`. Neither the public docs nor the in-app UI mention this, which makes the failure extremely hard to trace.

## Workaround

Uninstall via the shipped tool (it restores the saved pristine rule, removes the bundle, and clears the manifest), then reboot and log in with a real password:

```
sudo "<ChatGPT.app>/.../Codex Computer Use Installer.app/Contents/Resources/CodexComputerUseAuthorizationPluginInstallerTool" \
  uninstall "<same RESOURCE_DIR>"
```

Do **not** reset the login keychain — the file is fine and resetting it destroys all stored credentials without fixing anything.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. macOS 26.5.x with FileVault on, and a login keychain in normal use.
2. Enable Locked Use / Computer Use so the authorization plugin is installed into `/Library/Security/SecurityAgentPlugins/`.
3. Let the Mac lock the screen, then unlock it via the plugin-mediated path.
4. Run `security show-keychain-info ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db` — error 51.
5. Any app using Safe Storage now re-prompts for sign-in and cannot persist credentials.

### What is the expected behavior?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

issues.title: [Windows Desktop] MXC sandbox: PowerShell InitializeDefaultDrives fails and py.exe cannot detect installed Python

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### Description
Codex Desktop for Windows exhibits two reproducible anomalies inside the MXC sandbox:
1. PowerShell reports an `InitializeDefaultDrives` failure involving the `FileSystem` provider on startup.
2. The Python launcher (`py.exe`) cannot detect an installed Python 3.13.5, although the same launcher works outside the sandbox.

PowerShell commands, direct Python execution, and filesystem operations through .NET APIs with absolute paths work. A shared root cause has not been established.

### Environment
- Codex Desktop Windows; latest confirmed version from prior tests: **26.1111.21308** (the version used for the most recent Python-launcher comparison was not independently recorded)
- Windows; MXC sandbox enabled
- Python 3.13.5, 64-bit, per-user installation under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Python\Python313\`
- PowerShell version not recorded

### Issue 1: PowerShell FileSystem initialization
In the latest sandbox test, all **nine** PowerShell invocations displayed:
```text
Tentativo di eseguire l'operazione InitializeDefaultDrives sul provider 'FileSystem' non riuscito.
```
(English equivalent: `Attempting to perform the InitializeDefaultDrives operation on the 'FileSystem' provider failed.`)

Nevertheless, `Write-Output "CODEX_OK"` returned `CODEX_OK` with PowerShell exit code **0**.

### Issue 2: Python launcher discovery differs inside/outside sandbox
**Inside Codex sandbox:**
- `py.exe -3.13 --version` → `No installed Python found!`, launcher exit code **112**.
- `py.exe --list-paths` → `No installed Pythons found!`.
- `python3.13.exe` was not found by `Get-Command`.
- Invoking `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Python\Python313\python.exe` directly works (Python 3.13.5); test script exits **0** with exactly:
```text
PYTHON_OK
MODIFICA_OK
```

**Outside Codex sandbox, in a normal Windows PowerShell session:**
```powershell
py.exe -3.13 --version
# Python 3.13.5
py.exe --list-paths
# -V:3.13 *    C:\Users\<USERNAME>\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python313\python.exe
```
The difference is reproducible; its mechanism is not yet known.

### Seven-step sandbox verification
| Step | Operation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Start PowerShell, output `CODEX_OK` | Passed with initialization diagnostic (exit 0) |
| 2 | Create empty temporary `codex_sandbox_test.py` | Passed; 0 bytes |
| 3 | Write `print('PYTHON_OK')` | Passed; exact contents verified |
| 4 | Reread and compare contents including CRLF | Passed |
| 5 | Append `print('MODIFICA_OK')` and compare | Passed |
| 6 | Execute script | `py.exe` failed (112); direct Python succeeded (0), exact expected stdout, empty stderr |
| 7 | Delete temporary file and verify absence | Passed |

Filesystem operations used .NET APIs with absolute paths. No commands were run outside the sandbox during the Codex test; no unrelated files were modified.

### Expected behavior
- PowerShell initializes the `FileSystem` provider without diagnostic errors.
- Unless intentionally restricted and documented, `py.exe` detects the same registered Python installation inside MXC as outside it.
- Standard commands do not require absolute executable paths or filesystem API workarounds.

### Actual behavior
- `InitializeDefaultDrives` diagnostic on each tested PowerShell invocation.
- `py.exe` fails Python discovery inside MXC (exit 112) but works outside.
- Direct Python and .NET absolute-path filesystem operations succeed.

### Related issue
Possibly related: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/58174 (MXC PowerShell `FileSystem` initialization). The launcher issue may have a separate cause.

### Request
Could the Codex Windows team investigate:
1. Why PowerShell `FileSystem` initialization fails inside MXC?
2. Whether sandbox restrictions on drive metadata, registry access, or user-profile visibility explain either behavior?
3. Why `py.exe` cannot discover a Python installation visible outside MXC?
4. Whether a fix is planned or already included in a specific **Codex Desktop Windows** release?

issues.title: Desktop: restore a supported Reload Window action in production builds

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

issues.body:
### Request

Please restore a supported **Reload Window** action for Codex Desktop production builds (menu + shortcut), or add an equivalent **Reload UI / Restart renderer** action under Settings → Troubleshooting.

### Why this matters

Codex Desktop still has multiple failure modes where the **renderer/UI gets stuck while the app-server/backend remains healthy**. In those cases, reloading the renderer is the fastest and least disruptive recovery path.

Production builds currently omit the reload action (`allowWindowReload == false` in prod), so users are forced to fully quit/restart the app or use unsupported debugging/CDP workarounds.

This is especially awkward now that Codex is moving toward a long-lived/shared app-server daemon: the backend task can remain alive while only the UI needs recovery. A renderer reload should therefore be a first-class recovery action rather than something hidden from production users.

### Expected behavior

Provide one of:

- **View → Reload Window** in production builds, with a documented shortcut; or
- **Settings → Troubleshooting → Reload UI**.

The action should:

- reload only the renderer/UI when possible;
- preserve active app-server/daemon tasks and thread state;
- preserve drafts if feasible;
- clearly warn only if a reload would interrupt active work.

### Existing evidence

This is not a hypothetical need. Existing reports already show cases where renderer reload recovers the app while the backend remains usable:

- #47216 — production builds have no reload path while the composer can deadlock on `loading-local-config`.
- #44342 — main-window reload clears a stuck local-config state while normal restart may recur.
- #48487 — reloading `app://-/index.html` restores a stuck startup UI.
- #43960 — repeated blank/loading UI is recovered by `Page.reload`.
- #51313 — renderer failures/restarts can happen while backend work remains alive.

### Regression / usability concern

Earlier Codex Desktop builds exposed a reload shortcut, and users could recover from UI-only hangs without killing the whole app. Removing that escape hatch from production makes existing renderer instability materially more disruptive.

Please either restore the production reload action or provide an officially supported equivalent.

issues.title: Windows: allow configuring the default session shell via config

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: tool-calls
labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

issues.body:
## Summary

Codex currently defaults to PowerShell for the Windows session shell path. That makes it hard for users who primarily work in Git Bash or another already-supported shell to make that shell the default for Codex sessions.

I prepared a change that adds an explicit Windows config entry:

```toml
[windows]
shell_path = "C:\\Program Files\\Git\\bin\\bash.exe"
```

When `windows.shell_path` is configured, Codex uses that executable as the default session shell. When it is not configured, the current behavior remains unchanged and Windows still falls back to PowerShell.

## Why this approach

I intentionally implemented this as an explicit config option rather than automatic shell detection:

- Windows does not have a single reliable equivalent to Unix `$SHELL`
- multiple `bash.exe` variants may exist on PATH (Git Bash, WSL, MSYS2, etc.)
- explicit configuration is easier to reason about and avoids changing behavior for existing users

## Implementation notes

The change currently does the following:

- adds `windows.shell_path` to config parsing
- supports `profile.windows.shell_path` overriding the top-level value
- validates the configured executable against Codex's existing built-in shell detection/execution logic
- uses the configured shell as the default session shell when no internal `user_shell_override` is provided
- updates the Windows shell tool descriptions so they refer to the configured default shell rather than hardcoding PowerShell wording
- updates docs and regenerates `config.schema.json`

This does **not** try to add arbitrary shell adapter support. The configured path must resolve to a shell executable already supported by Codex's built-in shell handling.

## Testing performed

I ran:

- `cargo +stable test -p codex-tools`
- `cargo +stable test -p codex-core config::tests::config_loads_windows_shell_path_from_toml -- --exact --nocapture`
- `cargo +stable test -p codex-core config::tests::profile_windows_shell_path_overrides_top_level_value -- --exact --nocapture`
- `cargo +stable test -p codex-core config::tests::invalid_windows_shell_path_fails_config_load -- --exact --nocapture`
- `cargo +stable test -p codex-core shell::tests::configured_windows_shell_path_uses_bash -- --exact --nocapture`
- `cargo +stable test -p codex-core shell::tests::invalid_windows_shell_path_is_rejected -- --exact --nocapture`
- `cargo +stable test -p codex-core shell::tests::finds_powershell -- --exact --nocapture`
- `cargo +stable test -p codex-core shell::tests::detects_powershell_as_default -- --exact --nocapture`

## Branch / commit

I could not open a PR directly because the repository currently limits PR creation to collaborators.

The proposed change is available here:

- branch: `LXL47/codex:feat/windows-shell-path-config`
- commit: `0d9010493`

If this direction is acceptable, I can keep the branch available for maintainers to review or cherry-pick from.

An actual attempted call to the previously available tool failed before any backend authorization response:

```text
TypeError: tools.mcp__codex_app__send_message_to_thread is not a function
```

Repeated enumeration of the currently exposed `ALL_TOOLS` confirmed that the management functions were absent. This is an absent callable-tool surface, not an observed permission-denied response. No tool-discovery/search capability that could expose these missing app tools was available in the affected turn.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The initiating transition is not yet isolated; the following is an observed diagnostic sequence, not a deterministic fresh-install reproducer:

1. In an existing local Desktop project task, ask the agent to inspect or create another task.
2. Enumerate the currently available app tools. The management tools above are absent, while basic navigation tools remain.
3. Attempt the previously callable task-message tool; observe the TypeError above.
4. As a separate fallback experiment, run `codex exec --json -C <new-git-worktree> <prompt>`.
5. The CLI emits `thread.started`, `turn.started`, and actual work output. However, the user cannot find this task automatically under the expected Desktop project and reports difficulty reading it through Desktop.
6. `navigate_to_codex_page` returns `{"navigated":true}` for that ID. This does not establish that the task content rendered or that project membership was assigned.
7. A read-only App Server diagnostic successfully reads the same persisted task:

```json
{"id":2,"method":"thread/read","params":{"threadId":"<redacted>","includeTurns":true}}
```

Sanitized result:

```json
{"readSuccess":true,"source":"exec","cwd":"<new-git-worktree>","turnCount":1}
```

The original Desktop task has source `vscode`; the fallback task has source `exec`. Both use paginated history and are not archived. A read-only local metadata check returned null `project_id` for both, including the existing Desktop project task, so null alone is NOT evidence of the cause. No state/history database was modified.

### What is the expected behavior?

- Supported Desktop task-management tools should remain available consistently, or the app should explicitly explain why they are unavailable and how to restore access.
- Instructions should not promise an app tool surface that the active turn cannot discover or call.
- Please clarify the supported path for creating a Desktop-visible, project-associated task. We do not assume `codex exec` must provide the same project association as the Desktop creation API.
- A navigation acknowledgement should not be interpreted as proof of readable content or successful project association; an actionable UI error would help distinguish these cases.

### Additional information

This installation has records of `0.153.4` tasks beginning September 7, and successful task-management calls earlier in this persistent conversation on September 8. Consequently, we have NOT established that a CLI update caused the failure. Desktop update timing, model/provider routing, feature flags, and task restoration remain hypotheses requiring controlled comparison.

The local config selects `gpt-6-astra` and provider identifier `openai-http`; this identifier alone does not establish a third-party endpoint or the actual route used for every Desktop turn. No provider endpoint or credentials are attached. No model/provider A/B test was performed.

The task itself is readable through App Server, so we do NOT claim transcript loss/corruption. We also do not claim a filesystem-permission problem, a confirmed regression in a specific release, or that changing repository rules can restore missing system tools.

Related reports: #31366 (older-task tool exposure), #33637 (model-dependent exposure), #37075 (provider-dependent exposure), #41404 (browser policy affecting tools), #40865 (missing replacement tools). Please consolidate if this is the same defect; this report adds the current macOS 26.901/0.153.4 observations and the successful backend-read versus Desktop/CLI fallback distinction. Unlike #43742, no duplicate-ordinal/history-projection failure has been established here.

No raw transcripts, task IDs, private project names/paths, repository source, credentials, databases, or unredacted logs are attached. No app restart, downgrade, permission expansion, or state-database repair was performed as part of this diagnostic.

If you're doing authorized security work, apply for Daybreak to get broader access. ``` My work involves debugging and maintaining my own SLAM/VINS research software. It does not involve offensive cybersecurity activities, unauthorized access, or exploit development. I believe these safety blocks may be false positives. **2. Repeated response stream disconnections** Codex frequently terminates responses with: ``` stream disconnected before completion: stream closed before response.completed ``` The issue has occurred across multiple conversations, including newly created sessions. Sometimes Codex successfully reads files, executes commands, and modifies code before the response is unexpectedly interrupted. Once affected, a conversation may become unusable. Even simple follow-up prompts such as "Continue" fail repeatedly, and restarting Codex or resuming the conversation does not reliably resolve the problem. The issue persists even after disabling Goal and subagents and reducing reasoning effort from Ultra to Medium. These repeated interruptions have significantly disrupted my development workflow and forced me to abandon several conversations. The same failure may recur. 8 - Restart Codex and resume the affected conversation. The problem may persist. 9 - Repeat the task in a newly created conversation, with Goal and subagents disabled. Similar interruptions can still occur. Reproducibility: Intermittent but recurring. I have not identified a deterministic minimal reproducer. The uploaded thread contains an actual affected session. Important: These tasks involve authorized debugging of my own software, not cybersecurity research or exploitation. ### What is the expected behavior? Codex should allow legitimate C++ development, compilation, debugging, and runtime diagnostics to proceed without incorrectly classifying these activities as restricted cybersecurity operations. Specifically: 1. Ordinary SIGSEGV debugging, GDB analysis, memory lifetime investigation, and thread synchronization debugging should not trigger cybersecurity safety blocks solely because they involve low-level system operations. 2. Responses should complete normally with the expected `response.completed` event. 3. Temporary connection failures should not permanently prevent an existing conversation from continuing or being resumed. 4. Context compaction and session recovery should remain functional whenever possible. 5. If a response is blocked by a safety check, Codex should provide a clear and actionable indication of the reason, without incorrectly implying that ordinary debugging requires Daybreak access. I would like to continue my legitimate academic software engineering work reliably without repeatedly abandoning and recreating conversations. ### Additional information **Environment** - OS: Ubuntu 24.04 Linux - Codex CLI: 0.171.0 (last confirmed) - Models: GPT-6.1 Sol (Medium and Ultra reasoning) - Subscription: ChatGPT Plus - Incident dates: November 23–24, 2026 (UTC+08:00) - Application: Academic SLAM/VINS research software, primarily written in C++ **Troubleshooting already attempted** - Restarting Codex CLI and resuming affected conversations - Creating entirely new conversations - Disabling Goal and subagents - Reducing reasoning effort from Ultra to Medium - Splitting larger tasks into smaller, independent tasks - Running `/compact` (failed in an affected session) - Running `/recap` (succeeded in an affected session) None of these measures has consistently resolved the issue. **Potentially related reports** - #57377 — Legitimate SIGSEGV debugging blocked by cybersecurity safety checks - #60363 — C++ development blocked, with conversation recovery problems - #48083 — Extensive cybersecurity false positives when debugging one's own code **Distinction from the potential duplicate #48083** While #48083 describes a similar potential false-positive safety block, this report additionally documents repeated stream disconnections (`stream closed before response.completed`), failures to resume affected conversations, and recurrence across newly created sessions, even with Goal and subagents disabled. These symptoms may indicate a broader or separate reliability issue. **Additional diagnostic information** - Some affected sessions had substantial context remaining, suggesting that the failures were not solely caused by context-window exhaustion. - Diagnostic feedback has already been uploaded through Codex CLI; the associated thread ID is provided in the reproduction steps. - The potential safety-check false positives and stream disconnections may be independent issues. I would appreciate an investigation into both.

issues.body:
### What is the type of issue?

Documentation / supported integration clarification; feature request only where no supported interface exists.

### What is the issue?

For Codex Desktop on native Windows, how can a downstream native process controller obtain a supported, version-bound capability describing its actual launch containment and descendant lifetime?

The observed command interface supplies command options, output and a session identifier. Those values alone do not establish the original OS containment objects, their generations, policy stability or a complete descendant-completion boundary. This is an interface limitation in the examined workflow, not evidence that isolation is absent, a security vulnerability, or a universal Windows limitation.

The Windows sandbox documentation describes MXC and legacy implementations, and says remaining MXC child processes stop when the foreground command exits. Please distinguish that documented behavior from the evidence available to a native consumer for a particular invocation. A fixed Windows Job topology should not be presumed across implementations.

### Requested supported contract

Please identify the owning component, applicable Desktop/runtime versions and API/schema, or state explicitly which guarantees are unsupported.

1. Read-only identification of the effective sandbox implementation and permissions for an invocation, rather than inferring them from an app version or a successful shell command.

issues.title: app-server file watcher wakes on every file open in /etc when /etc/codex is missing

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

issues.body:
### What happens

An idle `codex app-server` wakes once for every file opened in `/etc` by any process on the machine. On a busy Linux workstation each server woke about 650 times a second. With 9 servers that was about 15,600 wakeups/s and about 16% of a core, with no turns running. Under heavy exec load (builds, shells) it got much worse: each server used 50–84% CPU.

### Why

1. `/etc/codex` doesn't exist, so `codex-file-watcher` watches its nearest existing ancestor, `/etc` ("Missing targets are watched non-recursively through the nearest existing ancestor", `codex-rs/file-watcher/src/lib.rs`). The missing targets are `/etc/codex/{config,requirements,managed_config}.toml`.
2. `notify` 8.2.0 includes `IN_OPEN` in every inotify watch (`notify/src/inotify.rs`, `WatchMask::OPEN` in the watch mask). `/proc/PID/fdinfo` shows the `/etc` watch with mask `0xfee`, which includes `IN_OPEN` and `IN_CLOSE_NOWRITE`.
3. Every `exec` opens `/etc/ld.so.cache`, `nsswitch.conf`, `passwd` and so on. Each open wakes the `notify-rs inotify` thread, which forwards the event to a tokio task. That task then drops it, because `is_mutating_event` filters out `Access`. A watch with the same mask on `/etc` received 615 events/s on this machine.

Total cost: (number of app-servers) × (machine-wide rate of opens in `/etc`).

### Measurements

- codex-cli 0.171.0. The relevant code is unchanged in 0.172.0: no `file-watcher` changes between the tags, and `notify` is still 8.2.0.
- Linux 7.3.
- Per-thread context switches over 10 s, all 9 servers: `tokio-rt-worker` 9,771/s and `notify-rs inotify` 5,824/s.
- The other watched directories (skills roots, `CODEX_HOME`) saw about 1 event/s over the same window.

### Workaround

`sudo install -d -m 755 /etc/codex`. The fallback watch then lands on an empty, quiet directory.

### Suggested fixes

- Don't fall back to a busy system ancestor such as `/etc` (or `/`). Re-check a missing system config path on demand or with a slow timer instead.
- Avoid subscribing to `IN_OPEN`/`IN_ACCESS`/`IN_CLOSE_NOWRITE` at the kernel level when only mutations matter. Filtering in user space still pays for every wakeup.
