issues.title: bug(windows-os): desktop app "Long-lived" host WebSocket ignores system proxy and HTTP_PROXY, hardcoded URL

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

issues.body:
### Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| App | ChatGPT desktop app (Windows, MSIX `OpenAI.Codex_26.1013.4894.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0`) |
| Bundled app-server | `codex 0.163.0-alpha.10.2` (windows-x86_64) |
| OS | Windows 11 10.0.26200 x64 |
| Proxy | Clash Verge Rev (mihomo core); Windows **system proxy** enabled (`ProxyEnable=1`, `127.0.0.1:7897`); TUN **not** enabled |
| Network | DNS poisoning present: `chatgpt.com` resolves to random forged IPs |

### Problem

After `remoteControl/enable`, the desktop app also opens a WebSocket to the `hostId=durable` ("Long-lived") host:

```js
// app.asar — hardcoded, no config override
var uue = `wss://codex-cloud-backend.chatgpt.com/`;
function lb(e){ return { id: i.Ai, display_name: `Long-lived`, kind: `local`, websocket_url: uue } }
```

It is issued from the Electron **main process** using the Node `ws` package (not the Chromium network stack), and as a result:

1. it does **not** read the Windows system proxy (WinINET / `ProxyEnable` + `ProxyServer`), even though the HTTP client inside the app-server does;
2. it does **not** read `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY`, even though `codex.exe` in the same process tree does (see the A/B test below);
3. the URL is hardcoded and there is **no setting** to override it.

On any network that requires a proxy — in particular "system proxy on, TUN off", which is the default setup for a very large number of users in mainland China — this connection fails deterministically.

### Reproduction

1. Enable the Windows system proxy (pointing at a local HTTP proxy). Do **not** enable TUN.
2. Use a network where `chatgpt.com` is DNS-poisoned (or any network that requires a proxy).
3. Launch the ChatGPT desktop app, open Settings → Connections → Control this computer, enable "Allow connection".
4. Watch the desktop app log
   (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0\LocalCache\Local\Codex\Logs\`):

```
[AppServerConnection] app_server_connection.websocket_error connectionId=58 errorCode=unknown
  hostKind=durable message="WebSocket was closed before the connection was established" transport=websocket
[AppServerConnection] app_server_connection.closed code=1006 connectionId=58 failureReason=open_timeout
[AppServerConnection] app_server_connection.reconnect_scheduled baseDelayMs=20000 reconnectAttempt=57
```

5. In parallel, `Get-NetTCPConnection` on the main process shows a **direct** connection to a public IP stuck in `SynSent` (the DNS-poisoned address) instead of the local proxy:

```
RemoteAddress    RemotePort  State
127.0.0.1        7897        Established      <- Chromium traffic goes through the proxy
199.16.158.190   443         SynSent          <- long-lived WS connects directly, hits a forged IP
```

### A/B test: the app-server *does* honor proxy env vars

Same machine, same subscription, one variable changed at a time, using `codex remote-control --no-daemon` and looking for `connected to app-server remote control websocket` in the log:

| Group | `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` | Extra flag | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | set | — | ✅ `connected to app-server remote control websocket` |
| E | set | — | ✅ reproduces A |
| B | set | `-c features.respect_system_proxy=true` | ❌ `Error: Remote control is enabled on <name> but the connection is errored.` |
| C | cleared | — | ❌ `os error 10060` (WSAETIMEDOUT) |
| D | cleared | `-c features.network_proxy=true -c network.proxy_url=...` | ❌ `os error 10060` |

So the Rust app-server **does** honor `HTTP_PROXY`, while the main-process WebSocket does not — inconsistent proxy behavior inside the same app/process tree.

Two further observations:

- `features.respect_system_proxy=true` (which reads the Windows system proxy from the registry) makes the app-server WS fail outright with `connection is errored`; the system-proxy path appears to be broken for the WS transport.
- `network.proxy_url` / `network.socks_url` (`features.network_proxy`) only apply to network policy for **sandboxed commands**; they do not cover the app-server's own long-lived connections.

### The endpoint itself works (so this is not a server-side problem)

WS upgrade handshake through the local proxy:

```
$ curl -x http://127.0.0.1:7897 \
    -H 'Connection: Upgrade' -H 'Upgrade: websocket' \
    -H 'Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13' -H 'Sec-WebSocket-Key: <random>' \
    -H 'Origin: https://chatgpt.com' \
    https://codex-cloud-backend.chatgpt.com/

User-Agent: (none)                         -> HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
User-Agent: node                           -> HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
User-Agent: codex-desktop/26.1013.4894.0   -> HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols
User-Agent: ChatGPT/26.1013.4894.0         -> HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols
```

As soon as the request goes through the proxy with an acceptable User-Agent, the handshake succeeds — the server and the network egress are fine.

### Isolation: after fixing the proxy env vars, the toggle works but this channel still does not

This pins the problem precisely to the connection described here:

```
# after setting user-level HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY and restarting the app
Settings -> Connections -> Control this computer -> "Allow connection"  =>  ON, pairing QR dialog shown  OK
desktop log                                                                   =>  os error 10060 gone,
                                                                                 "connected to rendezvous"  OK

# but the long-lived channel is still connecting directly
codex.exe (app-server) sockets     =>  127.0.0.1:7897  Established        OK
Electron main process "durable"    =>  199.16.158.190:443  SynSent        still direct
```

In other words: the toggle itself is backed by the app-server tunnel (now working), but the channel the **cloud uses to call back into this machine** — issued by the Electron main process — is never taken over by the proxy. **"Allow connection" being on does not mean a remote session can actually be established.**

### Expected behavior (suggestions)

1. Honor `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY` for WebSockets opened by the desktop app main process, consistent with the app-server.
2. At minimum honor the Windows system proxy (WinINET), so the very common "system proxy only" setup works.
3. Provide a configurable endpoint override (e.g. `CODEX_CLOUD_BACKEND_URL` or a settings entry) for self-hosted gateways / enterprise environments.
4. Fix `features.respect_system_proxy`, which currently breaks the app-server WS when enabled.

### Impact

In mainland China and any other "proxy required, system proxy only, TUN off" environment, the desktop app's cloud long-lived connection is unavailable, so **remote control sessions initiated from a phone may fail to establish** even though the "Allow connection" toggle turns on and the device shows as online.

### Paths for further investigation

```
Desktop app logs:
%LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\OpenAI.Codex_2p2nqsd0c76g0\LocalCache\Local\Codex\Logs\<YYYY>\<MM>\<DD>\codex-desktop-*.log

Codex CLI binary shipped with the desktop app (copied into the user profile):
%LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenAI\Codex\bin\<hash>\codex.exe
```

---

*A full local investigation with all raw log excerpts, socket dumps and the A/B test matrix is also available at
https://github.com/Kirito14IT/chatgpt-codex-windows-remote-control-proxy-fix (contains one-click diagnostic scripts).*

### What issue are you seeing?

In the ChatGPT desktop app's Work mode, I started a new chat without selecting a project, attached several documents, wrote a prompt, and clicked Send. The message showed a red exclamation mark and the chat failed to start. When I opened another chat, I could find some of the uploaded files, but I could not recover the prompt or retry the original draft.

I then got a new Work chat to edit the files. I could not find the revised files on my computer from the conversation. When I asked it to save the results locally and tell me where they were, the interface displayed “You stopped, 0 seconds elapsed” before showing a reply or file operation.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Open the Windows desktop app, select ChatGPT → Work, and start a chat without selecting a project.
2. Attach several files, type a prompt, and click Send.
3. If the message shows a red exclamation mark, open a new chat and check whether the prior draft and its attachments can be recovered together.
4. In a subsequent chat, ask Work to edit the documents, then ask where the edited files are on the computer. In the reported case, the save follow-up immediately showed the zero-second stopped state.

### What is the expected behavior?

A failed send should preserve the prompt and its attachment selection together and offer an actionable error and retry. After completing a file task with a local output, Work should make the saved files easy to locate from the conversation. If a follow-up cannot start, the UI should explain the failure and let the user retry.

### Additional information

The initial startup symptom may overlap with #61847. This report also covers recovery of the failed draft and the later zero-second state when requesting local save.

issues.body:
After updating the ChatGPT desktop app on November 23, 2026, I observed two problems in an existing local Work conversation. I do not know whether they share a cause.

## 1. Earlier messages cannot be edited and rerun
1. Open an existing local Work conversation.
2. Hover over an earlier user message.
3. Try to edit the instruction and rerun the task from that point.

Expected: The edit action is available, as it was before the update.

Observed: Only Copy is visible. The controls resemble Chat, but I cannot verify whether the mode actually changed.

## 2. Attachments are intermittently inaccessible
1. Attach a screenshot to a message in the Work conversation and send it.
2. Ask the assistant to describe the image.

Expected: The assistant can inspect the attached image on the first attempt.

Observed: The screenshot appeared sent on my side, but the assistant reported receiving only text. After I resent the same image later, the assistant correctly described it. This resembles #63261.

## Environment and impact
- macOS, Apple Silicon
- Originally observed on 26.1117.41037 (build 29803)
- Version after reinstalling: 26.1120.41243 (build 30607)

Reinstalling did not resolve the problem for me. During document revisions, I have to restate earlier instructions and check whether the assistant can read the files I send.

issues.body:
## Environment

- macOS, arm64; desktop app 26.1027.30824, build 22943, production channel.
- Configured app updater reports up_to_date on 31 October 2026.
- Bundled in-app browser and supported CUA/browser APIs. No Chrome fallback.

## Problem A: a newly created background chat lacks its browser owner

1. Create a normal local chat through the supported create_thread tool and let it run without selecting it.
2. Ask it to open a neutral HTTPS page in its own hidden in-app browser.
3. It fails with "Browser is not available: iab" and inventory lacks an IAB endpoint for that chat.
4. Select that chat once. Desktop logs show browser owner-sync capturing its route before a page webview exists.
5. The unchanged tool runtime then discovers IAB and opens/reads the neutral page successfully.

Observed twice in existing normal chats. In the independent diagnostic chat, conversation-stream ownership preceded browser-route ownership by several minutes. No restart, runtime reset, or permission change was used for recovery.

## Problem B: completing a subagent removes the browser connection, and followup_task does not recreate it

Three separate diagnostic subagents each opened and read a neutral HTTPS page successfully, then ended a turn with one of these states:

- Only tab explicitly closed; empty tab inventory verified before completion.
- Temporary tab left open without a retention mark.
- Tab marked with markHandoff; presence verified after marking and before completion.

All three lost IAB on followup_task. The preserved browser binding failed, and inventory lacked IAB. In the first two cases, one fresh IAB tab-creation attempt also failed. The marked-tab case did not attempt fresh creation; logs establish that its whole route was disposed and its marked tab closed.

An additional completed file-only turn did not repair the first agent: another resumed turn failed both the preserved binding and one fresh IAB creation attempt.

## Controls

- The ordinary parent survived its own completed turn with zero tabs and the same browser binding, then created and read a fresh page.
- That parent remained usable while the resumed child tests failed.
- Closing the final tab during an active turn returns a valid empty list; a replacement can be created through the existing binding.
- A stale closed-tab handle produces a tab-specific error while another tab remains usable.
- Reading a page with panel visibility false succeeds.

## Read-only packaged-code trace

- The active host browser hook captures child routes on initial subAgentActivity kind="started". Saved followup_task activities are kind="interacted", which this hook ignores.
- Child routes use disposeAfterSessionActivity=true. endSessionActivity disposes the route/backend independently of tab handoff marks. Logs show no route recapture before failed resumes.
- A broader renderer registration hook exists, but its manager initializer has an unconditional false gate in this build.
- The active host thread/started registration path requires a child source with a parent. The ordinary chats' source is "vscode", so that branch performs no registration.
- Selecting a chat invokes browser-sidebar-owner-sync -> syncOwner -> bindSessionRouteOwner, supplying the missing ordinary-chat route.
- Eighteen isolated tests of extracted installed functions support these findings. Those tests use mocked dependencies; the live reproductions above are separate evidence.

## Requested correction and verification

1. Register and await an exact, trusted window/owner association before the first browser-capable turn of an ordinary background chat.
2. Ensure a resumed child's browser route exists at actual turn admission/start using its verified parent association. Preserve handoff-marked tabs when ending a child turn. Recreating an empty route alone cannot restore an already destroyed tab.
3. Preserve per-chat isolation. A generic "interacted" event can also be messaging, so it is not by itself a reliable new-turn boundary.
4. Verify never-selected background creation, all three child cases, an intervening file-only turn, retained original-tab survival, and unaffected parent/unrelated-chat tabs.

Discovery warning counts are not failure counts: probing wrong-session endpoints can produce "No ChatGPT browser route is available" alongside a successful matching endpoint in the same pass.

Related: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/58419 reports IAB discovery failure on the same macOS app version, but its cause and equivalence to these two reproductions are not established.

## Scope and privacy

No installed application files, permissions, security checks, profiles, or unrelated chats were changed. No app restart was performed. Test tabs were cleaned up. This report omits usernames, local paths, chat/session/tab identifiers, private websites, account details, raw logs, screenshots, transcripts, credentials, and proprietary source excerpts. No permanent repair has been applied or verified.

桌面端 Bug 反馈；经用户明确授权提交，使用 AI 协助整理。

关联但不直接等同：#51105 记录正常完成后的子会话延续不重建路由；本报告额外提供新建子会话首次调用前就释放路由的两组现场时序。与 #58419 共享外层错误，但平台、子会话条件和日志证据不同，尚未确认共同根因。

订阅类型：本次未采集。版本来自安装包标识，未读取 About 对话框。

# Bug 反馈：Windows Codex 子智能体的内置浏览器路由在首次调用前被释放

## 摘要

Windows Codex 客户端会为子智能体创建独立的内置浏览器（IAB）路由，但在部分子会话中，路由在首次浏览器调用前就被释放。子智能体随后执行 `cua.getBrowser({ id: "iab" })`，返回 `Browser is not available: iab`。同一子会话开始后续回合后仍然失败。主会话在同一调查期间可以连接 IAB。

已确认故障发生在客户端会话路由层。客户端实现还存在一条可复现的风险路径：通用 `idle` 通知结束浏览器活动，并删除被标记为临时的子路由，后续 `active` 不重建路由。**现场具体是否由该 `idle` 分支触发，尚未捕获原始通知或调用栈，因此仍属推断。**

## 环境与影响

| 项目 | 观测值 |
| --- | --- |
| 调查日期 | 2026-11-04 |
| 系统版本 API 返回值 | Windows `10.0.19045.0`，未独立核查完整系统版本标签 |
| 客户端安装包 | `OpenAI.Codex_26.1029.7803.0_x64`，Windows Store 包 |
| 浏览器后端 release | `26.1029.61003` |
| 浏览器工具 | `mcp__cua_repl.js`，选择器 `iab` |
| 使用方式 | 主会话通过 `collaboration.spawn_agent` 创建子智能体 |
| 用户影响 | 委派的浏览器验收无法开始；可能被误报为整个应用的内置浏览器不可用 |

客户端与浏览器后端属于不同组件，两种版本号不一致本身不是版本不兼容的证据。

## 复现步骤

前置条件：启用 Computer Use，主会话可使用 IAB，并可创建子智能体。无需访问公司内网或业务数据。

1. 在主会话中执行以下调用。首次使用时遵守工具的初始化要求，将它作为单独的一次工具调用：

   ```javascript
   let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ id: "iab" });
   ```

2. 确认主会话连接成功。后续独立调用可用返回的 `browser.browserId` 列出标签；空标签列表不表示浏览器不可用。
3. 创建一个诊断子智能体，要求它只进行以下操作，不使用外部浏览器、不读写业务数据：

   ```text
   先按 CUA 首次调用要求，单独执行：
   let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ id: "iab" });
   若失败，再执行：await cua.listBrowsers();
   报告结果；不要把子会话失败推断为主会话或整个应用失败。
   ```

4. 观察子智能体的返回值，同时按子会话 ID 筛选客户端日志中的 `IAB_LIFECYCLE` 事件。
5. 向同一个子智能体发起后续诊断回合，沿用 CUA 状态，再次执行 `getBrowser` 与 `listBrowsers`。

以上是已发生故障的最小操作路径，尚未在其他设备或其他版本上确认复现率。

## 预期与实际结果

**预期：** 子智能体开始浏览器工作时，它自己的 IAB 路由有效。初始化空闲或回合切换不应让之后的合法调用永久失去路由。若产品不支持此类子会话，应提前返回明确的能力限制，而不是先创建后释放路由并返回泛化的不可用错误。

**实际：** 子路由在首次调用前被释放。新建诊断子会话中，捕获路由约 29 毫秒后即释放，约 15 秒后的首次 `getInfo` 失败。`getBrowser` 返回 `Browser is not available: iab`，浏览器清单仅有已连接的 Edge 扩展，没有 IAB。开始后续回合后仍失败。

## 日志证据

以下时间为日志原始 UTC；北京时间为 UTC+08:00。会话标识已一致替换为别名，未更改事件顺序、时间戳或错误类型。

### 样本 A：原始故障

```text
2026-11-04T07:34:10.371Z info [browser-session-registry] IAB_LIFECYCLE captured session route conversationId=CHILD_A disposeAfterSessionActivity=true ownerWebContentsId=1 windowId=1
2026-11-04T07:34:10.375Z info [browser-session-registry] browser_use_iab_backend_startup_ready backend=iab platform=win32 release=26.1029.61003 sessionId=CHILD_A
2026-11-04T07:34:10.393Z info [browser-session-registry] IAB_LIFECYCLE created browser use host conversationId=CHILD_A routeKey=1:CHILD_A windowId=1
2026-11-04T07:34:10.394Z info [browser-session-registry] IAB_LIFECYCLE disposed browser use route conversationId=CHILD_A windowId=1
2026-11-04T07:34:10.394Z info [browser-session-registry] IAB_LIFECYCLE ended browser use session activity conversationId=CHILD_A disposeAfterSessionActivity=true windowId=1
2026-11-04T07:34:26.135Z warning [browser-use-iab-api] IAB_LIFECYCLE iab backend info request failed conversationId=CHILD_A errorMessage="No ChatGPT browser route is available for browser session CHILD_A" errorName=Error
```

这组日志证明：后端启动完成后，路由仍可能先被释放；`startup_ready` 不等于首次调用时仍有有效路由。

### 样本 B：新建诊断子智能体

```text
2026-11-04T07:46:13.943Z info [browser-session-registry] IAB_LIFECYCLE captured session route conversationId=CHILD_B disposeAfterSessionActivity=true ownerWebContentsId=1 windowId=1
2026-11-04T07:46:13.972Z info [browser-session-registry] IAB_LIFECYCLE disposed browser use route conversationId=CHILD_B windowId=1
2026-11-04T07:46:13.972Z info [browser-session-registry] IAB_LIFECYCLE ended browser use session activity conversationId=CHILD_B disposeAfterSessionActivity=true windowId=1
2026-11-04T07:46:28.659Z warning [browser-use-iab-api] IAB_LIFECYCLE iab backend info request failed conversationId=CHILD_B errorMessage="No ChatGPT browser route is available for browser session CHILD_B" errorName=Error
```

第二轮复测：沿用同一子会话和 CUA 状态，`getBrowser` 仍返回相同错误，`listBrowsers` 仍仅有 Edge。该样本未访问业务页面或修改设置。

### 样本范围与对照

- 在新建诊断样本之前，检索 2026-11-02 至 2026-11-04 的本地会话，找到 8 个由 CUA 调用实际返回此错误的会话，全部是子智能体。其中 7 个发生于 11 月 4 日；当天有 6 个执行过浏览器清单检查，均仅有 Edge。
- 新建诊断样本 B 额外复现一次，并在同一子会话的后续回合中再次失败。
- 主会话在同一调查期间成功连接 IAB、创建标签、导航、读取页面 AX 树并获取截图。该对照并非与每个失败请求严格同时执行。
- 此样本集合按错误检索得到，没有统计所有成功子会话的分母，不能据此声称“所有子智能体必定失败”。

## 已确认事实与推断

| 结论 | 证据等级与边界 |
| --- | --- |
| 子路由在首次浏览器调用前已经释放 | **已确认**：样本 A、B 的客户端日志与调用记录 |
| 连接失败的直接原因是会话无可用路由 | **已确认**：底层错误明确写出 `No ChatGPT browser route is available` |
| 客户端包含为子智能体建立独立路由的实现 | **已确认**：读取已安装包中的 `captureChildSessionRoute` |
| 通用 `idle` 分支可以删除子路由，后续 `active` 在该监听器中不重建 | **已确认的代码行为**：静态读取及提取函数回放；通知由测试注入 |
| 现场由初始化 `idle` 触发了提前清理 | **高可信推断**：代码路径和时序吻合；缺少原始通知与调用栈，尚不能排除其他 `endSessionActivity` 调用方 |
| 故障属于客户端生命周期缺陷，而非产品预期限制 | **高度疑似**：子路由创建实现、提前清理及恢复缺口支持此判断；尚无官方确认 |
| 网络代理、业务页面或登录态导致本次错误 | **无支持证据**：失败发生在会话路由查找层；未完成全面网络排除，不能扩展为所有网络问题均已排除 |
| 候选修改已经修复客户端 | **未确认**：仅在提取副本上验证，未安装、未完成真实子会话修复验收 |

## 实现定位与原因分析

来源：已安装 `app.asar` 中的 `.vite/build/early-bootstrap-632-62c641245a52ef0e.js`。本次仅做读取和本地副本验证。

1. `captureChildSessionRoute(childId, parentId)` 从父会话继承窗口信息，但使用子会话自己的 `browserConversationId`，并设置 `disposeAfterSessionActivity=true`。
2. 通用内部通知监听器在 `thread/status/changed` 且 `status.type=idle` 时调用 `endSessionActivity`。该分支没有验证此前是否开始过回合，也没有按回合 ID 或代次过滤过期状态。
3. `endSessionActivity` 既释放会话控制权，也在上述标记为 true 时调用 `disposeBrowserUseRoute`。
4. 同一个监听器没有处理 active 状态的路由恢复。浏览器连接入口 `prepareSessionRoute` 在 `canServeSession` 失败时直接抛错。
5. 另有子智能体生命周期监听器，在显式 completed、interrupted 和中断开始时调用清理。归档也有独立清理入口。

原 JavaScript 文件 SHA-256：`c16675e64dae86bdb09f7720f038a8c2f2beacf0e85bbadd369f407d38662aa4`。

## 建议修复点

优先在客户端会话生命周期层修复，保持子会话独立身份和窗口归属校验。

1. **将控制权释放与路由销毁拆分。** 通用 idle 可释放当前控制权；不要仅凭 idle 就销毁仍可能开始或继续运行的子会话路由。以明确的子会话/回合终态、关闭或归档等事件决定销毁，并检查事件代次。
2. **明确回合恢复策略。** 真正结束后若允许同一子智能体继续运行，应在后续回合开始时重新捕获其合法路由；不要让恢复只能依赖初次 `thread/started`。缺路由时的重建必须验证父窗口归属，不应借用任意主会话的路由。
3. **增加清理原因日志。** 记录触发通知、状态前后值、回合 ID/代次及清理调用方，让提前释放可以直接归因。
4. **返回更具体的错误。** 区分“后端不可用”“该会话无路由”“窗口已销毁”和“子会话能力不支持”，避免将单一会话故障泛化为整个 IAB 不可用。

本地候选修改仅验证第 1 点的一种实现：给 `endSessionActivity` 增加 `retainSessionRoute` 参数，通用 idle 调用传 true，显式生命周期清理沿用销毁行为。它是待评审方案，不是可直接部署的补丁。

## 已执行验证及限制

对从安装包提取的 `captureChildSessionRoute`、`endSessionActivity` 和通知监听器做函数级回放；Electron 窗口、通知源与部分依赖使用替身。

- 原版：注入“创建子路由 → idle → active”，确认路由被删除且不重建。
- 候选：同一序列保留原子路由，同时释放控制权。
- 直接调用显式清理仍删除路由；归档通知仍删除路由；父路由、其他子路由和未知会话处理符合断言。
- 共 8 项断言通过，候选 JavaScript 语法检查通过。

**限制：** “显式完成”和“显式中断”两项回放都直接调用同一个清理方法，没有独立覆盖真实完成/中断通知分发。测试不证明真实 Electron 通知顺序正确，也不证明长期路由回收无泄漏。

建议开发侧补充真实端到端用例：初始化 idle 后首次调用；同一子会话第二回合；完成/中断/归档；父窗口关闭；断线重连；并行子会话隔离；过期 idle 通知晚到；重复清理；长时间运行的路由回收。

## 当前状态与附件

故障仍存在。未修改已安装客户端，未修改安装目录权限或关闭完整性检查，未完成候选修复的真实端到端验收。

可随此报告提交的本地附件：

- `evidence.log`：两个现场样本的脱敏日志。
- `replay.cjs`、`extracted-functions.json`：提取函数及回放脚本，执行 `node replay.cjs`。
- `replay-results.json`：回放结果及验证边界。
- `candidate-replacements.json`：候选修改的 3 处精确替换。

附件不包含完整客户端代码、公司业务页面截图、业务日志、账户名称、凭据、浏览器配置或完整会话历史。本报告正文通过 GitHub 提交。上述 ZIP 和独立附件未上传；复现步骤、现场日志、原因分析和验证边界均已包含在正文中。

issues.body:
Over the past two weeks, I have observed a significant deterioration in the quality of ChatGPT's responses.

As a long-term paying customer who regularly uses OpenAI products for professional work, research, and complex analytical tasks, I find the current situation increasingly unacceptable.

The recurring problems include:

- An increasing number of factual and logical errors.
- Superficial analysis instead of the requested comprehensive investigation.
- Conclusions presented without sufficient verification of the underlying information.
- Incorrect interpretation of clearly formulated instructions.
- Failure to verify information against reliable and authoritative sources.
- Repeated mistakes even after the user explicitly identifies and corrects them.
- Confident answers based on assumptions rather than established facts.
- The need to repeatedly request deeper analysis and corrections to obtain a usable result.

This is not about occasional mistakes, which are understandable. It is about a noticeable and recurring decline in the reliability and usefulness of the service.

Instead of saving time, ChatGPT increasingly requires additional time to verify its answers, correct its mistakes, and repeat previously provided instructions. This directly undermines the purpose of using an AI assistant for professional work.

The current situation raises serious questions about the quality control of recent updates and the regression testing performed before their release.

Users pay for a reliable intellectual tool, not for the opportunity to continuously correct its mistakes or participate in uncontrolled product testing.

I would like OpenAI to address the following questions:

## Why

Normalized sandbox events become useful as an agent audit trail only when they retain thread, turn, and tool-call context and can leave the local process through a stable telemetry path. Local SQLite should support recent inspection, not grow into an unbounded compliance ledger.

This PR adds bounded local persistence and OTel emission on top of #17573. It also keeps two different facts separate: a sandbox violation means enforcement blocked an action, while an `auto_review_decision` means automated review judged a proposed action.

## What changed

- Added migration `0041_security_events.sql` and typed insert, query, and delete APIs in `codex-state`.
- Persisted filesystem and managed-network violations with thread, turn, tool-call, resource, backend, reason, and relevant path or network context.
- Emitted `codex.sandbox.violation` audit events with stable fields such as `sandbox.resource`, `sandbox.backend`, and `sandbox.reason`.
- Propagated audit context through shell, unified-exec, apply-patch, and managed-network paths.
- Defined `sandbox_violation` and `auto_review_decision` as distinct security-event kinds, with optional review provenance fields in the shared schema.
- Capped storage at 1,000 rows per thread and event-kind bucket.
- Deleted events older than 10 days during startup maintenance, then checkpointed and incrementally vacuumed SQLite.

1. #17573: normalize filesystem and network sandbox violations in `codex-sandboxing`
2. #22866 (this PR): persist the normalized events in bounded SQLite and emit OTel audit events

- `just test -p codex-core sandbox_detection --lib`

prs.title: Release unchanged prompt image buffers when callers drop them
prs.body:
Release unchanged prompt image buffers when callers drop them

## Why

The prompt image cache keeps original image bytes in memory after the
last caller releases them. A later request already supplies those bytes,
so the cache only needs to remember that they decoded successfully and
could be used as-is.

## What changed

Cache the format and dimensions of validated, unchanged images with a
weak reference to the source buffer. Matching requests share the buffer
while it is live. After it is released, a cache hit takes ownership of
the new input buffer without copying or decoding it again. Concurrent
misses reuse the first live result when inserting into the cache.

Key entries by a BLAKE3 hash of the input, image mode, and decoder
choice. Keep transformed outputs in the cache and apply the byte budget
using source length for unchanged images and allocation capacity for
transformed outputs.

## Testing

Cover buffer sharing and release, reuse after release, concurrent cache
misses, and byte-budget eviction. Verify that a warm cache still rejects
a PNG with corrupt pixel data.

Add gateway enrollment to local managed requirements

## Why

Administrators who use one gateway for managed configuration and model
requests need to configure the gateway URL and OAuth settings in two
places. A single enrollment keeps those settings together.

## What changed

Accept `[gateway]` with a base URL and `[gateway.auth]` in system
`requirements.toml` or MDM. Use the same OAuth settings for the config
server at the gateway root and the required Responses API provider at
`/v1`, with model discovery at `/v1/models`.

MDM enrollment replaces system enrollment as a unit. Requirements
composition rejects remote enrollment, conflicting config server or
provider settings, and empty or reserved provider names.

## Testing

Add composition tests for MDM precedence, remote enrollment and
rerouting attempts, and invalid or conflicting enrollment settings.

prs.title: Support encrypted context from MCP session-start hooks
prs.body:
Support encrypted context from MCP session-start hooks

## Why

MCP hook results were flattened to text, so `SessionStart` hooks could
not pass encrypted context to the model as encrypted tool output.

## What changed

Recognize text blocks marked with `codex/encryptedContent` in synchronous
MCP `SessionStart` hooks. Send them to the model as standalone
`function_call_output` items with the originating tool name and namespace.
Keep ciphertext out of hook previews and plaintext spill files. Reject
empty encrypted blocks and cap the serialized encrypted output at
40,000 bytes per hook run.

## Testing

Add a scenario that checks that ciphertext above the plaintext spill threshold reaches
the first model request unchanged, appears once after a cold resume, and
stays out of hook previews and spill files. Cover discarding encrypted
context when hook output fails JSON parsing under both failure policies.

prs.title: Reuse config server discovery when loading managed policy
prs.body:
Reuse config server discovery when loading managed policy

## Why

CLI login and interactive TUI startup could look up the same config server's
OAuth metadata again when loading managed policy, even after resolving it
for sign-in.

## What changed

  loading and through TUI startup and worktree setup. Reuse them only when
  the configured server, outbound proxy policy, and system proxy fallback
  setting match.
- Rediscover anonymous servers after onboarding so the TUI can pick up a
  newly enabled OAuth requirement.
- Use discovered OAuth settings to classify app-server startup errors as
  config server errors when applicable.

## Testing

Add a regression test that blocks discovery requests and checks reuse for
matching OAuth and anonymous resolutions, as well as cache misses when the
server or either proxy setting changes.

prs.title: Speed up remote control reconnects when a controller is active
prs.body:
Speed up remote control reconnects when a controller is active

## Why

A silent WebSocket can leave an active controller waiting up to 60 seconds for the host to detect the outage. Reconnect backoff from earlier failures can delay recovery further.

## What changed

- Reconnect after 30 seconds without incoming WebSocket frames when a live controller is present. Keep the 60-second pong timeout when only the relay client is connected.
- Start at the initial jittered delay for the first five retries when controller activity resumes after a period with no live controllers, then increase backoff if failures continue.
- Preserve live streams and their terminals when a sequenced `initialize` request is replayed. Ignore cleanup from an old writer if a replacement connection has reused the stream.

## Testing

Cover the attached and relay-only timeout paths, retry backoff across controller lifecycle changes, and writer cleanup after stream reuse.

prs.title: Honor explicit plugin disablement without a global default
prs.body:
Honor explicit plugin disablement without a global default

## Why

Without `plugins._default`, the activation policy ignored a plugin's explicit `enabled = false`. The CLI also reported remote plugin enablement directly from the marketplace, so its output could disagree with the effective state.

## What changed

Apply per-plugin enablement before falling back to `plugins._default.enabled`. The `codex plugin list` command now applies that policy to remote plugins, so an installed plugin can appear as disabled while retaining its installation and account settings. Plugins disabled at their source stay disabled.

## Testing

Cover explicit disablement without a global default in config and remote plugin loading tests, and check that the CLI reports the plugin as installed and disabled in both JSON and table output.

Support model and reasoning effort overrides in remote exec

`codex exec --remote` rejected model and reasoning effort overrides,

subsequent turns. Omitted settings retain the thread's current values
or use the server defaults for a new thread.

precedence, and inheritance across turns. Check that invalid or

prs.title: Defer paginated thread history updates on NFS
prs.body:
Defer paginated thread history updates on NFS

## Why

Live rollout writes also update SQLite, so lock contention in rollback
journal mode can delay recording thread activity.

## What changed

For local threads with paginated history on NFS, defer SQLite updates on
the live write path and materialize rollout history when serving history
pages. For pools configured to prefer rollback journaling, cap the pool
at two connections and allow 60 seconds for SQLite locks and 120 seconds
to acquire a connection.

Skip work already committed by another history reader. Remove rollout
files before clearing their history checkpoints and reject stale batches
that would recreate deleted history.

## Testing

Extend the thread deletion test to verify that applying a stale batch
after deletion returns `ThreadNotFound`. Check SQLite settings on every
connection using the configured pool size.

prs.title: Keep TUI event receivers with their threads
prs.body:
Keep TUI event receivers with their threads

## Why

Clearing the active thread could drop its receiver and discard unread
events. A queued close from an old stream could also trigger close
handling while the same thread was being reattached.

## What changed

Keep each receiver in its thread's event channel and look it up by the
active thread ID. When a live attachment replaces the active thread's
stream, drain pending events and skip the old stream's `ThreadClosed`
notification unless the TUI is waiting for it to finish shutting down.

## Testing

Cover switching focus away and back without losing or misrouting unread
events. Exercise same-thread reattachment with a queued close, both
with and without a pending shutdown.

Keep active turns running when `/compact` is rejected

## Why

Manual compaction could interrupt a running turn before discovering that
the session settings prevent compaction. This can happen when a policy
refresh requires auto review for the current model.

Validate the session settings before interrupting the active turn for
`/compact`. If validation fails during a turn, emit a warning and leave
the turn running. If the session is idle, report a bad request and set
the agent status to errored.

## Testing

Add a regression test that verifies the running turn completes after
a compaction warning and that retrying `/compact` while idle reports an
error.

releases.body:
## New Features

- Follow thread links from search results and transcripts to open saved conversations and nested agents in the terminal. (#62332)
- Press `Tab` to complete arguments for supported slash commands. For example, `/mcp lo` completes to `/mcp login`. (#62343)
- Jump between task groups in the agent command center with `Shift+Up` and `Shift+Down`. (#62200)
- Optional stdio MCP servers with cached tool lists now start on their first tool call by default. (#62366)
- Set an approval reviewer for individual connected app tools in `config.toml`. (#62360)
- App-server clients can select Amazon Bedrock Runtime during setup or sign-in. (#62222)

## Bug Fixes

- `codex exec resume` restores saved sandbox permissions, the working directory, and workspace roots unless explicitly overridden. (#62194)
- Remote sessions preserve working directories, workspace roots, and writable paths when the client and server run on different operating systems. (#62375, #62376, #62377)
- Codex reports provider errors as soon as they arrive in a response stream and identifies which API spend limit was reached. (#62329, #62356)
- Interrupting a parent turn preserves queued replies from child agents for the next turn. (#62348)
- Use `PageUp` and `PageDown` to read and submit answer choices that are taller than the terminal’s answer area. (#62209)
- Cloud replies that finish after history loads now update in place, keeping the terminal transcript in order. (#62403)

## Documentation

- The bundled `openai-docs` skill now covers migration to GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, including endpoint choices and tool-calling requirements. (#62447)

## Chores

- Code Mode now uses gRPC for all host connections. The `code_mode_host_grpc` setting is deprecated. (#62476)
- Python formatting and SDK type generation now verify dependency hashes against the repository lockfile. (#62346)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issues.body:
This EPIC tracks a series of investigations as to whether there is value in AST aware file read, search, or codebase mapping.

AST aware tools can be used to 1) more precisely read method bounds with a single tool call, reducing turns from misaligned reads, and reducing noise in tokens, 2) navigate to usages and definitions of syntax elements via syntax aware search (AST grep), and 3) compress high level context about the codebase, such as the location of specific classes and their members by collapsing code down to just top level classes and types and their children's signatures.

```
 1. tilth (Rust)
  tilth is built specifically to generate a structural outline of a codebase. It uses Tree-sitter under the hood but ships as a single binary. It gives you an
  immediate map of the repository's symbols.
   * Installation: cargo install tilth (or download the binary from their releases)
   * Usage:
       * tilth map . (Prints a tree-like overview of the whole codebase structure)
       * tilth read <file> (Prints the structural outline of a specific file)


  2. glyph (Go)
  glyph is another single-binary tool designed to generate clean, multi-file symbol maps. It's excellent if you want to quickly see the skeleton of a
  directory of source code.
   * Installation: go install github.com/benmyles/glyph@latest
   * Usage: glyph cli './**/*.go' (Prints a tree of functions, structs, and methods)


  3. ast-grep (sg) (Rust)
  While primarily known as a structural search-and-replace tool, ast-grep is the industry standard for distributing Tree-sitter as a fast, single binary. You
  can use it to extract landmarks via the command line.
   * Installation: brew install ast-grep or cargo install ast-grep
   * Usage: You can write quick one-liners to extract specific symbols (like all function declarations) and format the output.


  4. The Classic: Universal Ctags (C)
  If you truly want zero modern dependencies, u-ctags is the classic UNIX approach. It uses a hybrid regex/parser approach rather than full AST generation, so
  it's incredibly fast and supports over 100 languages out of the box.
   * Installation: brew install universal-ctags
   * Usage: ctags -R --output-format=json .
   * Note: It outputs a flat list of symbols (or JSON) rather than a visual tree, but it is the most robust and portable way to extract codebase landmarks.
```

issues.title: Subagent recovery after MAX_TURNS is reported as GOAL success, hiding interruption

labels.name: priority/p1
labels.description: Important and should be addressed in the near term.

labels.name: area/agent
labels.description: Issues related to Core Agent, Tools, Memory, Sub-Agents, Hooks, Agent Quality

labels.name: 🔒 maintainer only
labels.description: ⛔ Do not contribute. Internal roadmap item.

labels.name: workstream-rollup
labels.description: Label used to tag epics and features that are associated with one of the three primary workstreams

issues.body:
### What happened?

**Summary**: `codebase_investigator` subagent reports `status: "success"` and `Termination Reason: "GOAL"` even though its own result says it hit the maximum turn limit before doing any analysis.

While using Gemini CLI to investigate two local repositories (`t3code` and `superset`), the agent invoked the `codebase_investigator` subagent and it failed immediately without doing any analysis.

I ran the Gemini CLI on these two local repositories with an objective asking it to understand their architectures and AI agent integrations. The saved session log shows:

- The main agent called `codebase_investigator` with a valid, concrete objective.
- The tool result was reported with `status: "success"` and `Termination Reason: "GOAL"`.
- The embedded result text simultaneously says the investigation was interrupted because the "maximum number of turns was exceeded" before any specific task was identified or initiated.
- `RelevantLocations` was empty and no actual codebase analysis was performed.

This looks incorrect because:

1. The subagent appears to have exhausted its turn budget before performing any actual analysis.
2. The termination metadata is internally inconsistent: the parent tool call is surfaced as `status: "success"` with `Termination Reason: "GOAL"`, but the embedded payload describes a limit-induced early termination with no findings.

Relevant evidence from the session log:

```text
session file: session-2026-03-09T18-34-10479ef5.json

line 50: "name": "codebase_investigator"
line 53: objective: "Understand the architecture of t3code and superset..."
line 61: "Termination Reason: GOAL"
line 61: "The investigation was interrupted by a system-mandated termination (maximum turns exceeded)..."
line 61: "\"RelevantLocations\": []"
line 66: "status": "success"
line 79: "The `codebase_investigator` was unable to complete its analysis due to a turn limit..."
```

Full snippet from the saved session:

```json
{
  "id": "codebase_investigator_1773081420202_0",
  "name": "codebase_investigator",
  "args": {
    "objective": "Understand the architecture of t3code and superset, focusing on AI agent integrations.\nSpecifically:\n1. In t3code, how is 'Codex' integrated? Where is the core logic for agent interaction?\n2. In superset, what are the different agent/harness integrations (e.g., Mastra, MCP, Claude, etc.) and how are they implemented?\n3. What are the common patterns or interfaces used in superset that could be adapted for t3code to support multiple harnesses?\n\nIdentify key files, symbols, and architectural patterns in both repositories."
  },
  "result": [
    {
      "functionResponse": {
        "response": {
          "output": "Subagent 'codebase_investigator' finished.\nTermination Reason: GOAL\nResult:\n{\n  \"SummaryOfFindings\": \"The investigation was interrupted by a system-mandated termination (maximum turns exceeded) before any specific task could be identified or initiated. As a result, no codebase analysis was performed, and no relevant locations or insights could be gathered.\",\n  \"ExplorationTrace\": [\n    \"Received system notification that the maximum number of turns was exceeded.\",\n    \"Followed emergency termination protocol as instructed.\"\n  ],\n  \"RelevantLocations\": []\n}"
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "status": "success"
}
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I expected one of these outcomes:

- `codebase_investigator` should actually explore the repositories and return findings.
- If it truly hits a turn limit, it should do so after some visible work, and the tool invocation should be surfaced as a failure or explicit limit condition, not as `status: "success"` with `Termination Reason: "GOAL"`.

At minimum, the CLI should not report a contradictory success state for a subagent that says it exceeded its turn budget before beginning analysis. If the subagent hits a system-imposed turn limit before doing useful work, the tool result should be reported as a failure or explicit limit condition (e.g. `status: "error"` with a clear error code), not as a successful `GOAL` completion.


### Client information

<details>
<summary>Client Information</summary>

Run `gemini` to enter the interactive CLI, then run the `/about` command.

```console
> /about
Gemini CLI package version: 0.32.1
Platform: Windows
OS: Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0
Node.js: v20.20.0
PowerShell: 5.1.26100.7920
```

</details>

### Login information

Google Account, Pro tier from students promotion

### Anything else we need to know?

- After the failed `codebase_investigator` call, the main agent continued with manual file exploration and eventually produced an implementation plan. So the overall conversation did not fully crash, but the specialized investigator tool clearly failed.
- My current inference is that this may be either:
  - turn-budget state leaking into a fresh subagent invocation, or
  - an incorrect mapping of a subagent limit/error state into a successful `GOAL` termination in the parent session.
- If useful, I can provide the full saved session JSON or a redacted version of it.

labels.name: priority/p2

labels.name: area/agent

issues.body:
# [BUG] Browser Agent ignores `settings.json` overrides (e.g., `maxTurns`)

## What happened?
The Browser Agent completely ignores any configuration overrides provided in the global or project-level `settings.json`. While the `AgentRegistry` correctly reads and merges these settings during initialization, the `BrowserAgentInvocation` and its factory (`browserAgentFactory.ts`) skips the registry and recreate the agent definition from scratch with hardcoded defaults.

## What did you expect to happen?
The Browser Agent should respect settings overrides like `maxTurns`, `maxTimeMinutes`, etc., just like other sub-agents (e.g., `codebase_investigator`). For example, setting `maxTurns: 0` in `settings.json` should cause the agent to terminate immediately upon invocation.

## Client information
<details>
<summary>Client Information</summary>

Platform: Linux (Ubuntu 22.04)
Gemini CLI Version: 0.35.0-nightly.20260311.657f19c1f

</details>

## Login information
Google Account (OAuth)

## Anything else we need to know?
### Root Cause
The Browser Agent's unique invocation flow skips the `AgentRegistry` where settings overrides are maintained. Instead of using the pre-merged definition from the registry, it re-instantiates a fresh definition using hardcoded defaults.

**Relevant Files & Code Snippets:**

1.  **`packages/core/src/agents/subagent-tool-wrapper.ts`**
    The Browser Agent is explicitly branched out of the standard flow that uses `LocalSubagentInvocation`:
    ```typescript
    if (definition.name === BROWSER_AGENT_NAME) {
      return new BrowserAgentInvocation(this.config, ...);
    }
    ```

2.  **`packages/core/src/agents/browser/browserAgentInvocation.ts`**
    The `execute` method calls `createBrowserAgentDefinition`, passing the `config` object but omitting the merged definition from the registry.

3.  **`packages/core/src/agents/browser/browserAgentFactory.ts`**
    The factory re-runs the `BrowserAgentDefinition` constructor, which returns hardcoded defaults (e.g., `maxTurns: 50`):
    ```typescript
    const baseDefinition = BrowserAgentDefinition(config, !visionDisabledReason);
    ```

### Suggested Fix
Update `browserAgentFactory.ts` to attempt to retrieve the existing definition from the `AgentRegistry` before falling back to creating a fresh one.

### What would you like to be added?

The `browser_agent` (specifically `BrowserManager.ts`) currently employs a restrictive "fail-fast" strategy when encountering a locked browser profile (e.g., when `sessionMode: 'persistent'` is used and an existing instance or orphaned process is active):


```json
{
  "success": false,
  "summary": "The task could not be completed because the browser is already running for /home/user/.gemini/cli-browser-profile.",
  "fullErrorMessage": "The browser is already running for /home/user/.gemini/cli-browser-profile. Use --isolated to run multiple browser instances.\nCause: The browser is already running for /home/user/.gemini/cli-browser-profile. Use a different userDataDir or stop the running browser first."
}
```

I propose to make it more resilient with the following capabilities:

1.  **Automatic Session Takeover:** If `persistent` mode fails due to a profile lock, the agent should automatically attempt to connect to the existing instance (as if `sessionMode: 'existing'` were specified). This requires a graceful "fallback-and-probe" mechanism in `BrowserManager.connectMcp()`.
2.  **Orphaned Process Recovery:** If an `existing` connection is not feasible but the profile remains locked, the `BrowserManager` should proactively detect orphaned `chrome` or `chrome-devtools-mcp` processes associated with the Gemini CLI profile and offer (or automatically execute) a "Self-Healing" routine (process termination + lock file removal).
3.  **Intelligent Error Remediation:** Replace the current static error messages with an interactive recovery flow. Utilizing the `ask_user` tool, the agent should present the user with a "Choice" menu featuring numbered options to resolve the lock (e.g., **1. Attempt Session Takeover**, **2. Force Termination & Reset**, or **3. Launch Isolated Session**). 
### Why is this needed?

Forcing the user to manually `pkill` processes or close browser windows is a friction point that degrades the autonomous agent experience. The agent has sufficient context (profile path, PIDs) to resolve this internally without user intervention.


### Additional context

issues.body:
### What happened?

This is purely anecdotal, but IME Gemini does not use custom skills and sub-agents on its own, basically at all.  It will if I instruct it to explicitly, but won't when it's doing something very related.

For example, I have "gradle" and "git" skills with descriptions like:
> Executes and manages Gradle builds authoritatively with high-performance background orchestration 
  and surgical failure analysis. This skill is the STRONGLY PREFERRED way 
  to run any Gradle task, providing superior reliability through managed background processes, 
  task-specific output capturing, and deep diagnostic integration. Use it for executing core 
  lifecycle tasks like 'build' or 'assemble', starting persistent development servers, 
  or performing complex build troubleshooting. Do NOT use for specialized test diagnostics 
  (use running_gradle_tests).

and 
> Audits Git repository status, examines history, and implements non-interactive modifications. Processes surgical staging, descriptive commits, and multi-file diff analysis. Use for repository introspection and history-based truth verification. NEVER stages or commits without explicit user directives. Avoids interactive prompts via --no-pager.

that never ever get called when using the relevant tools.

I even have this in my `GEMINI.md` in the "priority rules" section:
> 4. **Agent & Tool Hierarchy:** Whenver considering how to approach a task or do anything, ALWAYS follow the hierarchy of preference: **Sub-Agents** > **Skills** > **Specialized MCP Tools** (NOT a Shell tool or similar) > **General/Builtin Tools** (e.g., `run_shell_command`, `grep_search`, `read_file`).
> 5. **Intentionality Protocol:** Before starting ANY task, you MUST stop and consider which agent, skill, or tool is most appropriate for the specific context. If your plan involves using the shell (even via a tool like `run_shell_command`), you MUST stop and reconsider if a more specialized tool or skill exists to handle the task more reliably.

I expected Gemini to use related skills when working on tasks that match the skill description.  Same for sub-agents.

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

## Objective
Ensure the Gemini CLI understands its own mechanics well enough to act as its own expert guide. The agent must be able to provide users with accurate facts about how it works, its hotkeys, and the exact CLI flags needed to run itself for specific workflows.

## The Problem
Users rely on the CLI to learn how to use the CLI. If the agent hallucinates flags (like suggesting the deprecated `--yolo` instead of `--approval-mode=yolo`) or forgets UI hotkeys (like `Double Esc` for `/rewind`), it blocks progress and creates friction. The agent needs strict grounding in its own documentation to accurately guide users.

### Why is this needed?

1. **Accurate Internal Facts:** The agent (specifically the `cli_help` subagent) must have flawless recall of its own UI keyboard shortcuts, slash commands, and settings hierarchy.
2. **Flag Construction:** It must be able to tell users exactly how to run it from the terminal for various use cases (e.g., suggesting `gemini -i "prompt" --sandbox --output-format json` for safe, headless scripting).
3. **Self-Execution & Guidance:** It should be able to write the exact commands needed to run itself, restart itself, or execute sub-tasks with the correct environment variables and flags.

type.description: Related Changes across multiple feature sets

issues.body:
## Description
Gemini 3 models are fundamentally trained to operate as native bash users, chaining standard POSIX tools (`grep`, `cat`, `sed`, `awk`) to explore codebases and edit files. To make full use of the model's native and preferred capabilities without compromising user security or UX, we need to allow the model to use these tools directly to interact and make changes.

## Prior Art
Historically, we have attempted to force models to use custom tools (such as `replace`, `grep_search`, `write_file`, etc.). However, these methods fight the model's core training. Malicious prompts or complex scripts are inherently hard to control and catch via parsing, and forcing custom tools creates significant downstream UX and security issues.

## The Challenge & Value Proposition
Because the model strongly favors raw bash calls even when nudged towards custom tools, it frequently outputs large, complex bash scripts to accomplish tasks. Under our current security model, these scripts require explicit user confirmation. 

This creates a critical point of failure: users are frequently presented with dense, hard-to-read bash messages to evaluate. This leads to severe prompt fatigue, causing users to either blindly confirm the execution or enter "yolo mode" (auto-approving all actions). This behavior is highly detrimental to security and degrades the overall user experience. 

**Value Proposition:** By safely embracing the model's native bash tendencies, we can eliminate confirmation fatigue, prevent unsafe "yolo mode" habits, and drastically improve both the UX and our underlying security posture. 

## Proposed Solution
A highly viable solution is to utilize a secure sandbox. ALL standard shell commands will execute within a zero-dependency, kernel-enforced sandbox. Instead of trying to predict intent before execution (which led to the parsing challenges described above), we can safely observe and handle the results *after* execution.

### Method
By running commands in a sandboxed replica of the workspace, we achieve three distinct UX lanes:
1. **Reads:** Commands that do not mutate the filesystem (e.g., `ls`, `grep`) are auto-approved. We must ensure this does not read from protected spaces or outside our trusted workspaces.
2. **Edits:** Commands that mutate the sandboxed filesystem (e.g., `sed -i`, `>`) trigger a post-execution Diff UI before the changes are synced back to the host, allowing for a seamless "Edit" tool experience using the model's preferred mechanisms. 
3. **Side-Effects:** A dynamic command router will handle commands requiring host credentials or network access (e.g., `git`, `gh`), completely bypassing the sandbox but requiring strict upfront user confirmation (i.e., stays the same as today, utilizing the policy engine to execute or ask for user confirmation).

## Architectural Mandates
In order to support this properly, we must explore, investigate, and implement the proper sandboxing for all major platforms: Linux, macOS, and Windows.

## Epic
This is an epic that tracks this investigation and implementation. It will contain subtasks used to track progress towards its overall completion. After initial investigation, if this is not a feasible route, the epic can be marked as closed.

issues.body:
## Motivation

Current context baseline is approximately 36.6k tokens per turn. Large file reads often 'firehose' the context, leading to bloat (previously observed at +15k tokens/turn). 

The goal of 'Tactful Extraction' is to establish a surgical code-discovery hierarchy:
1. **grep_search**: Primary scout for locating symbols.
2. **shell/sed**: scalpel for semantic block extraction (preferred for specific line ranges).
3. **read_file**: surgical range-reading (migrated to 1-based start/end lines).

Telemetry indicates that making ~2.1% more targeted tool calls results in a ~6.9% reduction in total input tokens.

## Changes

- **read_file migration**: Switched from 0-based 'offset'/'limit' to 1-based 'start_line'/'end_line' for better model alignment.
- **Surgical Guidance**: Updated tool descriptions and system prompts to mandate 'token-frugal' behavior.
- **Tool Hierarchy**: Emphasized the use of 'grep_search' and 'sed' via 'run_shell_command' for efficient context management.

## Status

This work is temporarily sidelined in favor of other priorities but remains a key architectural goal for efficiency.

issues.body:
The current WriteToDo tool relies on "in-context" task tracking, which maintains the todo list solely within the LLM's conversation history (prompt context). This creates issues with "context rot," high token costs, and total memory loss between sessions.

This issue proposes deprecating WriteToDo in favor of a persistent task tracking system (e.g., a local tasks.json) that allows the agent to maintain state across restarts and manage complex dependencies.

### Proposed Solution

Implement a new set of tools backed by a persistent local file (e.g., .gemini/tasks.json) to replace WriteToDo.

1. New Tool Definitions
The agent should have access to specific CRUD tools rather than just "writing" a list:
task_add(description: str, priority: str, dependency_id: int)
task_list(filter: str) (e.g., "show only 'ready' tasks")
task_update(id: int, status: str)
task_complete(id: int)

2. Storage Backend
Tasks should be serialized to a local file  in the working directory.

Benefits
1. Persistence: The agent can pick up exactly where it left off after a restart.
2. Efficiency: We stop burning tokens passing the entire completed history back and forth. The agent only queries task_list when it needs to know what to do next.
3. Complexity: Enables multi-step reasoning where the agent can plan out 20 steps and execute them over several days.

Address concerns and suggestions in https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/17035 
Doc [go/tracker-gemini-cli](http://goto.google.com/tracker-gemini-cli)

prs.title: fix(cli): cover all extension content in install and update consent
prs.body:
## Summary

Extension install and update consent now describes everything that an extension adds, not only its manifest fields, and updates compare that description between the installed folder and the new one. An update asks for confirmation again when its hooks, context files (and the files they import), skills, sub-agents, custom commands, policy files, MCP server entries, or the files that hook and MCP server commands reference through `${extensionPath}` change. It doesn't ask when they stay the same, including for extensions with skills. On updates, the prompt also lists what changed, and the interactive extension consent dialog now selects "No" first.

## Details

- **Content signatures (`packages/cli/src/config/extensions/contentSignature.ts`)**: Walks a file or folder inside the extension and hashes each regular file with SHA-256 (raw bytes, `/` paths, and UTF-16 code unit order, so the result doesn't depend on the platform, the locale, or where the folder is). Links that stay inside the extension folder are followed. Links that leave it, broken links, link loops, and special files get a marker and are never read. Display helpers escape control, zero-width, and bidirectional characters, and wrap each value in a Markdown code span.
- **Content summary (`packages/cli/src/config/extensions/extensionContentSummary.ts`)**: Builds the same summary for the installed folder and the new one from the raw files, without resolving variables and regardless of settings such as `hooksConfig.enabled`:
  - Hooks: each hook in `hooks/hooks.json` with its event, matcher, name, full command, and environment variables (sensitive values masked with the same rules as MCP servers), plus every file under `hooks/` and the paths referenced through `${extensionPath}`. A `hooks.json` that isn't valid is listed without failing.
  - Context files: the declared files or the default `GEMINI.md`, plus the files they import with `@`, resolved with `processImports` and limited to the extension folder. `processImports` is now exported from `@google/gemini-cli-core`.
  - Skills: `Source:` paths relative to the extension folder, and a signature over `skills/`.
  - Sub-agents, custom commands, and policy files, matching what their loaders read: `agents/*.md` (except names that start with `_`), `commands/**/*.toml` (hidden folders included), and `policies/*.toml`. Sub-agent MCP servers are listed with their values as written, including `Trust` when it's set.
  - MCP servers: read from the raw `gemini-extension.json`, resolving only `${/}` and `${pathSeparator}`, so the `Config signature` no longer depends on the folder path or the workspace. Each server that references files gets `Files used` and `Files signature` lines.
- **Consent text (`packages/cli/src/config/extensions/consent.ts`)**: Renders one section per kind of content, one entry per item, and one signature line per section. On updates, a "Changes since the installed version" block right above the question names the new, changed, and removed items; it isn't part of the compared text. Without a summary, the text is the same as before, so existing snapshots don't change, and `skillsConsentString` (used by `gemini skills install` and `gemini skills link`) doesn't change either.
- **Staged copy for local installs (`packages/cli/src/config/extension-manager.ts`)**: After the manifest is validated, a local source is copied to a temporary folder. The summary, the consent text, and the installed files all come from that copy, so the installed files are the ones that the prompt describes. The existing cleanup removes the copy. Linked extensions don't change.
- **Declined updates (`packages/cli/src/config/extensions/extensionConsentErrors.ts`, `packages/cli/src/config/extensions/update.ts`)**: Declining throws `ExtensionConsentDeclinedError` with the existing `Installation cancelled for "<name>".` message. `updateExtension` keeps the `ERROR` state, so auto-update doesn't ask again in the same session, but it no longer logs a rollback or copies files back, and it rethrows the error as is. `updateAllUpdatableExtensions` waits for every update with `Promise.allSettled` and logs each failure with the extension name. Non-interactive prompts run one at a time, so each one reads its own answer.
- **Dialog default (`packages/cli/src/ui/components/ConsentPrompt.tsx`, `packages/cli/src/ui/components/DialogManager.tsx`)**: `ConsentPrompt` accepts an optional `defaultToNo` prop. `DialogManager` passes it only for extension consent requests, so pressing Enter declines them. Other consent dialogs keep "Yes" first.
- **Inline code spans (`packages/cli/src/ui/utils/markdownParsingUtils.ts`)**: Inline code now matches on the length of its backtick fence and removes one space of padding from each side, as Markdown does. Values that contain backticks, `*`, `_`, or `$` render as written in the consent dialog.
- **Docs (`docs/extensions/reference.md`)**: Describes when updates ask for consent again, that declining keeps the installed version, and that `--consent` skips the prompt and its details.
- **Commits**: Each commit builds and passes its own tests, so the PR can be reviewed commit by commit.

Planned follow-ups, not part of this PR: a dedicated "declined" status in `/extensions list`, the `extensions update --all` summary when every update fails and exit codes for `extensions update`, restoring the previous files when an approved update fails partway, and `trust` handling for sub-agent MCP servers.

## Related Issues

N/A

## How to Validate

1. Run the new and updated tests:

   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/config/extensions/contentSignature.test.ts src/config/extensions/extensionContentSummary.test.ts src/config/extensions/extensionUpdateConsent.test.ts src/config/extensions/consent.test.ts src/config/extensions/update.test.ts src/ui/components/ConsentPrompt.test.tsx src/ui/components/DialogManager.test.tsx src/ui/hooks/useExtensionUpdates.test.tsx src/ui/utils/markdownParsingUtils.test.ts
   ```

2. Run the extension suites and the core import processor tests:

   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/config/extension src/commands/extensions
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/memoryImportProcessor
   ```

3. Optional manual check: create an extension with `gemini extensions new <path> hooks` and install it with `gemini extensions install <path>`. Expected results:
   - The prompt lists `SessionStart: node ${extensionPath}/scripts/on-start.js`, `Files used by hooks: scripts/on-start.js`, and a `Hooks signature` line.
   - An update that only changes the `version` doesn't ask for consent.
   - An update that changes the extension's content asks again and lists the changes under "Changes since the installed version". If you decline, the installed version stays as it is.
   - In the interactive CLI, the extension consent dialog starts on "No".

Edge cases covered by the tests: links that stay inside or leave the extension folder, broken links and link loops, binary and malformed files, a `hooks.json` that isn't valid, imports outside the extension folder, files skipped by the loaders (for example `agents/_notes.md`), a source folder that changes while the prompt is open, concurrent non-interactive prompts, and `update --all` with one declined and one successful update. Tests that need symbolic links are skipped on Windows, following the existing pattern.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [x] Noted breaking changes (if any): The interactive extension consent dialog now starts on "No", so pressing Enter declines. Extension consent text now lists hook commands, context and imported files, skills, sub-agents, custom commands, policy files, and signatures, and updates ask again when any of them change. `gemini extensions update --all` finishes every update and logs each failure instead of stopping at the first one.
- [x] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [ ] MacOS
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
    - [ ] Podman
    - [ ] Seatbelt
  - [ ] Windows
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
  - [x] Linux
    - [x] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker

prs.title: fix(core): cap total_max_matches and clarify context overflow message
prs.body:
## Summary

Broad `SearchText` (grep/ripgrep) queries can overflow the context window (#17448). On current `main` several guards already exist: a default 100-match cap (hard-enforced via a streaming break), per-line 2000-char truncation, a 64KB tool-output cap, and a hard block in `client.ts` that refuses to send a request estimated to exceed the remaining context. This PR closes two gaps that remain.

This PR bounds the match **count** and clarifies the overflow message. It does not bound the total output **size** (for example, large context lines per match). That is handled separately in #30109, so this PR is related to #17448 but does not close it on its own.

## What was still missing

1. **`total_max_matches` had no upper bound.** The schema only set `minimum: 1`, so the model could pass `total_max_matches: 100000` and defeat the default cap, flooding the context.

2. **The overflow UI message was misleading.** The request is already hard-blocked, but the wording ("Sending this message... might exceed") read like a soft warning, and the actionable `/compress` guidance was hidden behind a "more than 25% of context used" condition, so in the broad-search case the user saw a vague message with no next step.

## Changes

- Add `MAX_TOTAL_MAX_MATCHES = 5000` (`packages/core/src/tools/constants.ts`) and a `maximum: 5000` constraint on `total_max_matches` in both tool-family schemas (`default-legacy.ts`, `gemini-3.ts`). The framework now rejects oversized values before execution. Regenerated the tool-schema snapshot. The parameter description states "Must be at most 5000; larger values are rejected", since oversized values are rejected rather than clamped.

- Add an explicit upper-bound check in `validateToolParams` for both `GrepTool` and `RipGrepTool`, so programmatic callers that bypass schema validation are also covered. Tests cover both sides of the boundary.

- Rewrite `handleContextWindowWillOverflowEvent` (`useGeminiStream.ts`): the message now states the request was not sent, formats token counts with separators, and always offers next steps (narrow the request, `/compress`, or start a new session).

## Related Issues

Related to #17448 (the output-size cap is in #30109)

## How to Validate

- `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- --run src/tools/ripGrep.test.ts src/tools/grep.test.ts src/tools/definitions/coreToolsModelSnapshots.test.ts`

- `npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- --run src/ui/hooks/useGeminiStream.test.tsx`

- `npm run typecheck`

- Manual: ask the agent to run `grep_search` with `total_max_matches: 10000`. It is rejected with `params/total_max_matches must be <= 5000`, and the model retries with a valid value.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [ ] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)

- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)

- [x] Noted breaking changes (if any): none; opt-in behavior, default unchanged

- [x] Validated on required platforms/methods:

  - [x] Windows

    - [x] npm run

prs.title: fix(core): add per-request timeout to MCP OAuth discovery fetches
prs.body:
Fixes #30412

## Problem
`OAuthUtils.fetchProtectedResourceMetadata`, `OAuthUtils.fetchAuthorizationServerMetadata` and the WWW-Authenticate HEAD probe in `MCPOAuthProvider` called `fetch` with no signal. A host that accepts the connection and never answers held discovery for up to 60 s per URL (the global undici headers timeout), and discovery tries many URLs in sequence.

## Fix
Add `OAUTH_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS` (5000, same as the HEAD probe in `mcp-client.ts`) and pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(OAUTH_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS)` to the three fetches. The abort is not an `OAuthSecurityError`, so both fetchers already return `null` and discovery moves on to the next well-known URL.

Not covered: the DNS lookup inside `validateOAuthEndpointUrl` runs before the fetch and is not bounded by this signal.

## Tests
Run from `packages/core`:
`npx vitest run src/mcp/oauth-utils.test.ts src/mcp/oauth-provider.test.ts`

- Before the fix: 5 failed, 104 passed. The two new "never answers" tests time out at 60000ms, the probe test fails with `expected undefined to be an instance of AbortSignal`, and the two existing URL assertions fail once they expect a signal argument.
- After the fix: 2 files passed, 109 tests passed.
- eslint and prettier checks on the four touched files are clean. The TypeScript check shows only the pre-existing missing `generated/git-commit.js` errors.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change.

Release notes

Sourced from simple-git's releases.

simple-git@4.1.0

Minor Changes

  • df13aeb: Add the allowConfig and strict options. Configuration keys outside the built-in list of known-safe keys (SAFE_CONFIG_KEYS) and the keys named in allowConfig now emit a one-off SIMPLE_GIT_UNLISTED_CONFIG warning, or are rejected when strict: true is set. Known-unsafe keys can now be permitted individually through allowConfig, and environment variables through allowEnvironment, deprecating the unsafe.allowUnsafe* options that only covered configuration keys or environment variables (they continue to work as before).

  • 4137780: The custom binary (the first string of the binary option or git.customBinary()) may now contain spaces when it looks like a path to a file, for example C:\Program Files\Git\bin\git.exe. The value must include a path separator and no part of the path may start or end with a space. The prefix (the optional second string) remains limited to the existing restricted character set, as it is passed to the binary as its first argument.

  • df13aeb: Add git.cmd for running commands written as tagged template literals, where every interpolated value is treated as untrusted data that can't add options, set configuration keys or select a remote helper transport. Add the remoteUrl() and refName() value wrappers for stricter validation of interpolated values.

  • a996f0f: Thanks to @​manus-pi and @​eliteaja11-dev for submitting CVE proposals that contributed to these changes.

    When the recommended checks are enabled (with unsafe.recommended: true or strict: true), HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME supplied through .env() with a value other than the one in process.env require allowUnsafeConfigPaths (or naming them in allowEnvironment), as git reads the global configuration from $HOME/.gitconfig and $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config in the same way as GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL. Passing the inherited value through is unaffected, and neither is removed from the inherited environment.

    parseEnv accepts the inherited environment as an optional second argument, used to compare HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME against.

    isGuardedEnvKey is now exported from @simple-git/argv-parser, identifying the environment variables (GIT_* and the others git reads, such as EDITOR and PAGER) that simple-git removes from an inherited environment.

  • 86fadaa: Settle on the use of strict to refer to the simpleGit configuration setting to enable strict controls, applying to both Git impacting environment variables and writing to the Git config.

    Use of the strict mode also implies the use of unsafe.recommended

  • c8ee6bb: Vulnerability reports:

    With thanks to @​manus-pi, @​manus-use, @​ba-am, @​mspiq, @​hoseinenddev, @​freyesperales, @​dalberrt, @​zer0d4y5, @​gamster01, @​humaneBicycle, @​Hama1cco, @​eliteaja11-dev, @​Cone-Tester, @​Figo5, @​MalwareEZ, @​zachariah-mithani, @​shaswata56, @​Akokonunes for submitting CVE proposals that contributed to these changes.

    • closing the loop on any configuration setting ending with .cmd or command under the catch-all allowUnsafeCommandBinaries setting (only enforced with the new unsafe.recommended option, or strict), and blocking gpg.ssh.defaultKeyCommand under allowUnsafeGpgProgram.
    • allowUnsafePager will now catch setting a custom binary in git grep --open-files-in-pager.
    • allowUnsafePager now also covers interactive.diffFilter, the shell command that git add -p and the other --patch commands pipe their diff through.
    • new (deprecated on arrival, prefer allowConfig) allowUnsafeSendEmailConfig option covering the sendemail.* keys that git send-email runs as commands, reads as files or uses to turn off certificate verification (sendmailCmd, toCmd, ccCmd, headerCmd, smtpServer, smtpServerOption, smtpSSLCertPath, smtpSSLClientCert, smtpSSLClientKey, aliasesFile and mailmap.file, including their per-identity sendemail.<identity>.* variants), and the imap.tunnel, imap.host and imap.sslVerify keys used by git imap-send.
    • new (deprecated on arrival, prefer allowConfig) allowUnsafeWebServerConfig option covering the instaweb.httpd, instaweb.modulePath and instaweb.gitwebDir keys used by git instaweb.
    • new (deprecated on arrival, prefer allowConfig) allowUnsafeBrowser option covering the browser.<tool>.path, browser.<tool>.cmd, man.<tool>.path and man.<tool>.cmd keys used by git help and git instaweb to open a browser or man page viewer. browser.<tool>.cmd and man.<tool>.cmd were previously covered by allowUnsafeCommandBinaries.
    • new (deprecated on arrival, prefer allowConfig) allowUnsafeSignatureTrust option covering gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile, gpg.ssh.revocationFile and gpg.minTrustLevel, which decide which signatures pass verification.

... (truncated)

Updates `esbuild` from 0.25.0 to 0.28.2
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.2

  • Fix tree shaking bug due to TypeScript import alias (#4507)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to incorrectly tree-shake imports that are used in a TypeScript type alias under certain circumstances. Affected code uses a TypeScript-specific import assignment and looks something like this:

    import Base from './dep.js';
import Alias = Base.SomeType;

  • Fix CSS minification bug involving & (#4497)

    This release fixes a bug where esbuild's CSS minifier incorrectly removed a & when it was unsafe to do so. Here is an example:

    /* Original code */
.a .b {
  & .b:not(& .c) {
    color: red;
  }
}

    /* Old output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{.b:not(& .c){color:red}}
    

    /* New output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{& .b:not(& .c){color:red}}

    This should match <span class="a"><span class="b"><span class="b">yes</span></span></span> but not <span class="a"><span class="b">no</span></span>. The old output incorrectly matched both.

  • Avoid overwriting input files without --allow-overwrite (#4484)

    For example: esbuild input.js --outfile=input.js tells esbuild to overwrite input.js with the output of running esbuild on it. This was supposed to already be prevented by default, but it accidentally regressed in version 0.17.0 and apparently didn't have any test coverage. The error message was being printed but the input file was still being overwritten. Oops.

    This release puts the original behavior back. With this release, esbuild should now actually avoid overwriting input files unless --allow-overwrite is explicitly present. This is done by not writing out any files when a build error is encountered.

  • Fix incorrect code generated when using top-level await (#4498)

    Previously esbuild could generate code containing a syntax error in complex scenarios involving top-level await used in a dependency cycle. The problem was a missing async on one or more module wrapper closures. With this release, esbuild now uses a fixed-point iteration algorithm to correctly annotate all dependencies in the cycle as needing an async module wrapper.

  • Fix a minification bug with lowered logical assignment operators (#4508)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to generate incorrect code for logical assignment operators when lowering them to an older target environment. Specifically the lowering process requires duplicating the left-hand side, but esbuild incorrectly failed to count the duplicate as a new usage when the left-hand side is an identifier. That then caused the minifier to believe that the left-hand side was only used once and could attempt to incorrectly inline an initializer into the first usage. This bug has now been fixed:

    // Original code
function foo() {
  let x
  bar(x ||= {})

... (truncated)
