Sourced from esbuild's changelog.

Changelog: 2025

This changelog documents all esbuild versions published in the year 2025 (versions 0.25.0 through 0.27.2).

0.27.2

  • Allow import path specifiers starting with #/ (#4361)

    Previously the specification for package.json disallowed import path specifiers starting with #/, but this restriction has recently been relaxed and support for it is being added across the JavaScript ecosystem. One use case is using it for a wildcard pattern such as mapping #/* to ./src/* (previously you had to use another character such as #_* instead, which was more confusing). There is some more context in nodejs/node#49182.

    This change was contributed by @​hybrist.

  • Automatically add the -webkit-mask prefix (#4357, #4358)

    This release automatically adds the -webkit- vendor prefix for the mask CSS shorthand property:

  mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat
}

    /* Old output (with --target=chrome110) */
    
main {
    
mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
}

  • Additional minification of switch statements (#4176, #4359)

    foo()

Updates `express` from 5.1.0 to 5.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from express's releases.

v5.3.0

Highlights

🐞 Bug fixes

  • Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by @​YuryShkoda in #4893

    Fixed the behavior of res.send() to prevent conflicts between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding HTTP headers in responses. The Content-Length header in res.send() is now only added when a Transfer-Encoding header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response. ETag generation is unaffected by the presence of a Transfer-Encoding header - by @​cuishuang in #7459

  • Upgrade qs to ^6.16.0, which fixes CVE-2026-2391 (GHSA-w7fw-mjwx-w883), CVE-2026-82417 (GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g) and CVE-2026-82562 (GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx): arrayLimit bypasses in comma parsing and a denial of service via an attacker-controlled isBuffer - by @​davetashner in #7057 and #7478, and @​cyphercodes in #7305

  • Upgrade proxy-addr to ^2.0.8, which fixes CVE-2026-90711 - by @​lazerg in #7474

🚀 Improvements

  • Allow conditional revalidation for QUERY requests. req.fresh previously only validated freshness for GET and HEAD requests, so QUERY responses never returned 304 despite a matching validator. Since QUERY is a safe, idempotent, and cacheable method that supports conditional requests, it is now included in the freshness check - by @​Cherry in #7366

    // QUERY /reports with If-None-Match: "12345"
app.query('/reports', (req, res) => {
  res.set('ETag', '"12345"');
  res.send(results); // now responds 304 Not Modified
});

  • Improve HTML structure in res.redirect() responses when HTML format is accepted by adding <!DOCTYPE html>, <title>, and <body> tags for better browser compatibility - by @​Bernice55231 in #5167

  • When calling app.render with options set to null, the locals object is handled correctly, preventing unexpected errors and making the method behave the same as when options is omitted or an empty object is passed - by AkaHarshit in #6903

    app.render('index', null, callback); // now works as expected

  • Upgrade content-type to ^2.0.0, bringing a faster parser (~1.5x quicker Content-Type parsing/formatting in res.send()) along with a behavior change: res.send() now keeps any existing parameters when adding the charset and no longer throws on a Content-Type that fails to parse. type-is is upgraded to ^2.1.0 as part of the same change - by @​blakeembrey in #7234

    res.set('Content-Type', 'text/plain; foo=bar').send('hey');
// -> Content-Type: text/plain; foo=bar; charset=utf-8

  • The default error handler now logs the full error object instead of only its stack trace, so nested details such as Error.cause and library-specific properties (e.g. Sequelize's parent/original) are no longer swallowed - by @​Nitin-Mohapatra in #6464

  • Upgrade content-disposition to ^2.0.1, which changes the Content-Disposition header emitted by res.download(), res.attachment(), and res.sendFile(): file names that are valid HTTP tokens are no longer wrapped in quotes. This is equivalent per RFC 6266, but applications asserting on the exact header bytes should update their expectations - by @​blakeembrey in #7233

    res.attachment('user.html');
// before -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="user.html"
// after  -> Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=user.html

prs.title: fix(a2a-server): enforce bearer token authentication and request input validation
prs.body:
## Summary

Configures authentication for the A2A server from the environment and applies consistent request input validation in the HTTP layer, in task creation, and in the `restore` command.

## Details

- **Bearer token authentication.** Replaces the placeholder auth checks in `app.ts` with a bearer token read from `GEMINI_IPC_SECRET`, or from `CODER_AGENT_AUTH_TOKEN` when the former isn't set. The token is read once at startup and compared with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`. Requests without the configured token receive `401`. If no token is configured, every request receives `500`. The SDK user builder now only returns an authenticated user.
- **Host and Origin validation.** Requests must use a loopback `Host` (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or `[::1]`), and a loopback `Origin` when that header is present. Other values receive `403`.
- Both checks live in a new `src/http/auth.ts` and are registered before body parsing and before every route, including the routes added by the A2A SDK.
- **Task creation.** Aligns `CoderAgentExecutor.createTask()` with `reconstruct()` and `execute()`: `workspacePath` goes through `validateWorkspacePath()` and `isTrusted` is ignored, so workspace trust is evaluated from server-side configuration rather than from the request payload. As in `execute()`, settings without a `kind` default to `agent-settings`.
- **Checkpoint restore.** `restore` resolves the checkpoint name against the checkpoint directory and returns an error if the resolved path isn't inside it.
- **Agent card.** Advertises the `bearer` scheme only, to match what the server accepts.
- **Docs.** Documents the two environment variables in the package README.

**Behavior change:** the server now requires `GEMINI_IPC_SECRET` or `CODER_AGENT_AUTH_TOKEN` to be set, and clients must send the token in the `Authorization` header on every request, including the agent card request.

## Related Issues

None.

## How to Validate

1. Build and run the package tests. All tests pass, including the new `auth.test.ts` and the added cases in `endpoints.test.ts`, `executor.test.ts`, and `restore.test.ts`.

   ```bash
   npm run build
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-a2a-server
   ```

2. Start the server with a token. The server also needs model credentials, as before (for example, `GEMINI_API_KEY`).

   ```bash
   CODER_AGENT_AUTH_TOKEN="YOUR_TOKEN" npm run start:a2a-server
   ```

3. Check the responses.

   ```bash
   # 200
   curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" http://localhost:41242/listCommands
   # 401
   curl -i http://localhost:41242/listCommands
   # 403
   curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" -H "Host: external.example.com" http://localhost:41242/listCommands
   ```

4. Start the server without either variable. The startup log reports that no token is configured, and every request returns `500`.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [x] Noted breaking changes (if any)
- [ ] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [ ] MacOS
    - [x] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
    - [ ] Podman
    - [ ] Seatbelt
  - [ ] Windows
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
  - [ ] Linux
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker

  • Security fix for CVE-2026-12590 (GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6)

prs.title: chore(deps): bump source-map-js from 1.2.1 to 1.2.4
prs.body:
Bumps [source-map-js](https://github.com/7rulnik/source-map-js) from 1.2.1 to 1.2.4.
Release notes

Sourced from source-map-js's releases.

v1.2.4

Index source maps

  • Fix originalPositionFor returning nulls at the first column of a section (#99)

    Reported by @​trackoor in #82.

  • Fix a section's column offset being applied to its second line instead of its first (#104)

    This affected sections with both a line and a column offset, in eachMapping, generatedPositionFor, SourceMapGenerator.fromSourceMap and SourceNode.fromStringWithSourceMap.

  • Support allGeneratedPositionsFor (#105)

    It threw TypeError: this._findSourceIndex is not a function. It now returns the same results as for the equivalent map without sections, with positions from every section that has the source. generatedPositionFor on nested index maps threw the same error and works now too.

  • Fix generatedPositionFor returning made-up positions (#115)

    It only searched the first section that listed the source, and when that section had no match, it returned the section offset added to null. It now searches all sections, so bias picks the closest mapping across them, and returns nulls when nothing matches.

  • Add computeColumnSpans (#116)

Other fixes

  • Fix generatedPositionFor, allGeneratedPositionsFor and eachMapping with ORIGINAL_ORDER throwing TypeError when a source has no mappings (#100)

    Reported by @​trackoor in #83. This is common in bundles, where a source can be listed after its code was tree-shaken away.

  • Fix allGeneratedPositionsFor returning positions that belong to a different source (#102)

  • Fix lookups throwing RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded on source maps with about 200,000 or more sources (#113)

  • Fix SourceNode#replaceRight throwing on a node without children (#114)

TypeScript

  • Fix type definitions that didn't match the runtime, without breaking changes (#117)

    • SourceMapConsumer accepts version as a number, null entries in sourcesContent, a missing names, index maps, JSON strings and the sourceMapUrl argument. Reported by @​linsk1998 in #43; a fix for sourcesContent was proposed by @​lahmatiy in #75.
    • SourceMapConsumer.fromSourceMap is declared, and allGeneratedPositionsFor takes an optional column and returns lastColumn.
    • The skipValidation and ignoreInvalidMapping options of SourceMapGenerator are typed.
    • SourceNode accepts nulls and chunk arrays in the constructor, nested arrays in add and prepend, and a RegExp or a replacer function in replaceRight.

    Return types that would need a breaking change, such as the nulls from originalPositionFor (#30), are documented in comments and left for the next major (#118).

Package

    The library already failed to load on older Node versions, so this only adds an install warning there.

prs.title: fix(build): clear bundle/ before esbuild to drop stale chunks
prs.body:
## Summary

Nightly releases have failed every night since 2026-11-05 with
`npm error 413 Request Entity Too Large` when publishing `@google/gemini-cli`
to wombat-dressing-room. The tarball is 25.2 MB, but about 70 MB of the
~106 MB of JavaScript inside it is leftover output from earlier builds that
`bundle/gemini.js` never loads. This PR clears `bundle/` before esbuild runs,
so only the current build is packed. The tarball drops to roughly half its
size.

## Details

`esbuild.config.js` builds with `splitting: true` into `bundle/`, and chunk
file names are content hashes. Nothing clears `bundle/` before a build, so
any build whose output differs (for example after `release:version` changes
`CLI_VERSION`, which is inlined via `define`) adds a new set of
`gemini-*.js` / `chunk-*.js` / `interactiveCli-*.js` files and leaves the old
ones in place. The release job bundles more than once (`npm ci` runs
`prepare` → `bundle`, then the job bundles again after the version bump), so
the stale copies are published.

Evidence from the last successful nightly
(`0.67.0-nightly.20261104.g89e9d25d6`, 25.1 MB):

- 4 full copies of the chunk graph: 4 × ~16.8 MB chunks, 4 × 2.69 MB,
  4 × 1.63 MB, 4 `interactiveCli-*.js`, 4 `gemini-*.js` roots.
- Following imports from `bin: bundle/gemini.js` reaches 40 files (27.2 MB);
  48 files (70.5 MB) are unreachable, and 3 of the 4 `gemini-*.js` roots are
  imported by nothing.

The package grew only from 25.1 MB to 25.2 MB, just enough to cross the
proxy's request limit. The likely reason is App Engine's 32 MiB request cap:
npm sends the tarball base64-encoded, so 25.1 MB becomes ~33.5 MB, just
under the cap, and 25.2 MB becomes ~33.6 MB, just over.

The fix is a single `rmSync` before the builds. It is safe because the only
other writer to `bundle/` is `scripts/copy_bundle_assets.js`, which runs after
`esbuild.config.js` in the `bundle` script and re-creates every non-JS asset
(policies, docs, builtin, bundled, examples, sandbox profiles).

A similar packaging problem was fixed before in #25841 (ripgrep binaries in
the npm tarball).

## Related Issues

Fixes #30203
Related to #30202, #30192, #30167, #30149 (the same failure on earlier
nights)

## How to Validate

```bash
npm ci                                   # prepare runs bundle once
npm run release:version 0.0.0-nightly.test
npm run bundle
ls bundle/gemini-*.js | wc -l            # main: 2, this PR: 1
du -sh bundle                            # main: ~74M, this PR: ~51M
node bundle/gemini.js --version          # prints 0.0.0-nightly.test
```

Results on macOS:

| | `gemini-*.js` roots | chunks | `bundle/` | gzipped |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main, after version bump + rebuild | 2 | 26 | 74 MB | — |
| this PR, after version bump + rebuild | 1 | 17 | 51 MB | 12.7 MB |

`npm run test:scripts` gives the same result with and without this change
(19 failures that already exist locally, unrelated to this change); the
esbuild bundle test `proxy-agent-bundle.test.ts` passes.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [ ] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [ ] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [ ] Noted breaking changes (if any)
- [ ] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [x] MacOS
    - [x] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
    - [ ] Podman
    - [ ] Seatbelt
  - [ ] Windows
    - [ ] npm run
    - [ ] npx
    - [ ] Docker
  - [ ] Linux

prs.title: fix: block project Git environment injection
prs.body:
Summary

Prevent workspace-supplied Git environment variables from influencing internal Git and shell operations through .env loading.

This addresses the environment-injection concern described in #29003 while preserving intentionally configured shell and user-level settings.

Details

The fix introduces case-insensitive GIT_* filtering at three environment-loading boundaries:

  • CLI: Reject file-provided Git variables before copying values into process.env.

  • A2A server: Reject Git variables before returning file-loaded task environment values.

  • Extension settings: Reject Git variables from workspace-scoped extension settings while preserving user-scoped and keychain-provided values.

Unlike the earlier approach in #29008, this change filters file-origin values rather than removing selected variables from all downstream subprocesses.

The fix also covers unknown future GIT_* variable names without requiring a manually maintained list.

Related Issues

Related to #29003.

Earlier implementation: #29008, closed without merging under the repository's contribution-label policy.

How to Validate

The following checks were performed locally:

Validation | Result -- | -- CLI and extension focused tests | 50/50 passed A2A suite | 186/186 passed Git utility and shell execution tests | 106/106 passed Build, typecheck, focused lint and formatting | Passed Regression tests against unmodified baseline | Expected failures reproduced

The regression tests cover workspace and home environment files, inherited Git variables, custom exclusions, mixed-case keys, and extension-setting isolation.

Full preflight limitation

npm run preflight exited with code 1 on the local Ubuntu environment due to CLI folder-trust and core keychain failures. Those failures were reproduced on an unchanged upstream baseline. The patch did not introduce additional failures in the tested environments.

Complete upstream CI validation remains pending.

Compatibility

Git environment variables explicitly provided through the shell, user-scoped extension settings, and keychain remain available.

The change is limited to preventing project-controlled environment files from injecting Git settings.

Review notes

This PR changes six files: three environment-loading implementations and three associated test files. No general Git service or shell execution behavior is modified.

Implementation was developed with AI assistance and reviewed with regression tests and baseline comparisons.

prs.title: fix(core): preserve custom model alias generation settings (#30238)
prs.body:
Fixes #30238

### Problem
When configuring a custom model alias that points to or extends a model tier (such as `flash-lite`), `applyModelSelection()` compares the concrete resolved model (e.g. `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`) against the requested tier name (`flash-lite`). Because they are not string-equal, `applyModelSelection()` falsely treated normal tier resolution as an availability fallback and re-queried `modelConfigService.getResolvedConfig()` with the concrete model name, silently dropping the alias's custom generation parameters (such as `temperature` and `maxOutputTokens`).

### Solution
- Distinguish normal tier resolution from genuine availability fallbacks in `applyModelSelection()` by comparing `finalModel` against the target model resolved for the alias/tier.
- Preserve the alias's configured `GenerateContentConfig` across tier resolution.
- Added unit regression tests for custom aliases resolving tiers and genuine availability fallbacks.

## Summary

Quotes the resolved IDE CLI path on Windows when installing companion extensions. This resolves an issue where `/ide install` fails when VS Code (or Positron / Antigravity) is located in default folders containing spaces (such as `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Microsoft VS Code` or `%ProgramFiles%\Microsoft VS Code`).

## Details

On Windows, `ide-installer.ts` invokes `child_process.spawnSync` with `shell: true` to execute `.cmd` files. When `shell: true` is enabled, Node.js formats arguments for `cmd.exe /d /s /c "<command>"`. Because `cmd.exe` strips the outer quotes when `/s` is present, any unquoted path containing spaces is split at the first whitespace character (e.g. `C:\Program` or `C:\Users\...\Microsoft`), causing execution to fail with exit status 1.

This PR wraps the resolved `commandPath` with `quoteCmdArg` from `packages/core/src/utils/editor.ts` across `VsCodeInstaller`, `PositronInstaller`, and `AntigravityInstaller` on `win32`. Paths without spaces remain unquoted, and non-Windows platforms remain completely unaffected.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30245

## How to Validate

1. Run unit tests verifying path quoting across all IDEs and platforms:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/ide/ide-installer.test.ts
   ```
2. Verify linting and typechecking pass:
   ```bash
   npm run lint && npm run typecheck
   ```
3. On Windows with VS Code installed in the default location (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Microsoft VS Code\bin\code.cmd`), run `/ide install` inside Gemini CLI and verify that the companion extension installs successfully.

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [ ] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed)
- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [ ] Noted breaking changes (if any)

Updates `esbuild` from 0.25.0 to 0.28.2
Release notes

Sourced from esbuild's releases.

v0.28.2

  • Fix tree shaking bug due to TypeScript import alias (#4507)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to incorrectly tree-shake imports that are used in a TypeScript type alias under certain circumstances. Affected code uses a TypeScript-specific import assignment and looks something like this:

    import Base from './dep.js';
import Alias = Base.SomeType;

  • Fix CSS minification bug involving & (#4497)

    This release fixes a bug where esbuild's CSS minifier incorrectly removed a & when it was unsafe to do so. Here is an example:

    /* Original code */
.a .b {
  & .b:not(& .c) {
    color: red;
  }
}

    /* Old output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{.b:not(& .c){color:red}}
    

    /* New output (with --minify) */
    
.a .b{& .b:not(& .c){color:red}}

    This should match <span class="a"><span class="b"><span class="b">yes</span></span></span> but not <span class="a"><span class="b">no</span></span>. The old output incorrectly matched both.

  • Avoid overwriting input files without --allow-overwrite (#4484)

    For example: esbuild input.js --outfile=input.js tells esbuild to overwrite input.js with the output of running esbuild on it. This was supposed to already be prevented by default, but it accidentally regressed in version 0.17.0 and apparently didn't have any test coverage. The error message was being printed but the input file was still being overwritten. Oops.

    This release puts the original behavior back. With this release, esbuild should now actually avoid overwriting input files unless --allow-overwrite is explicitly present. This is done by not writing out any files when a build error is encountered.

  • Fix incorrect code generated when using top-level await (#4498)

    Previously esbuild could generate code containing a syntax error in complex scenarios involving top-level await used in a dependency cycle. The problem was a missing async on one or more module wrapper closures. With this release, esbuild now uses a fixed-point iteration algorithm to correctly annotate all dependencies in the cycle as needing an async module wrapper.

  • Fix a minification bug with lowered logical assignment operators (#4508)

    This release fixes a bug that could cause esbuild to generate incorrect code for logical assignment operators when lowering them to an older target environment. Specifically the lowering process requires duplicating the left-hand side, but esbuild incorrectly failed to count the duplicate as a new usage when the left-hand side is an identifier. That then caused the minifier to believe that the left-hand side was only used once and could attempt to incorrectly inline an initializer into the first usage. This bug has now been fixed:

    // Original code
function foo() {
  let x
  bar(x ||= {})

Changelog

Sourced from esbuild's changelog.

Changelog: 2025

This changelog documents all esbuild versions published in the year 2025 (versions 0.25.0 through 0.27.2).

0.27.2

  • Allow import path specifiers starting with #/ (#4361)

    Previously the specification for package.json disallowed import path specifiers starting with #/, but this restriction has recently been relaxed and support for it is being added across the JavaScript ecosystem. One use case is using it for a wildcard pattern such as mapping #/* to ./src/* (previously you had to use another character such as #_* instead, which was more confusing). There is some more context in nodejs/node#49182.

    This change was contributed by @​hybrist.

  • Automatically add the -webkit-mask prefix (#4357, #4358)

    This release automatically adds the -webkit- vendor prefix for the mask CSS shorthand property:

    /* Original code */
main {
  mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat
}

    /* Old output (with --target=chrome110) */
    
main {
    
mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
}
    

    /* New output (with --target=chrome110) */
    
main {
    
-webkit-mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
mask: url(x.png) center/5rem no-repeat;
    
}

    This change was contributed by @​BPJEnnova.

  • Additional minification of switch statements (#4176, #4359)

    This release contains additional minification patterns for reducing switch statements. Here is an example:

    // Original code
switch (x) {
  case 0:
    foo()
    break
  case 1:
  default:
    bar()
}

Updates `express` from 5.1.0 to 5.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from express's releases.

v5.3.0

Highlights

🐞 Bug fixes

  • Fixed HTTP header conflict between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in res.send - by @​YuryShkoda in #4893

    Fixed the behavior of res.send() to prevent conflicts between Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding HTTP headers in responses. The Content-Length header in res.send() is now only added when a Transfer-Encoding header is not present, complying with the HTTP specification that states both headers should not coexist in the same response. prs.title: fix(core): do not stringify a non-string part text when appending to a prompt
prs.body:
## Problem

`appendToLastTextPart()` decides whether the last prompt part can absorb appended text with
`'text' in lastPart` and then interpolates `lastPart.text`:

```ts
} else if (lastPart && 'text' in lastPart) {
  newPrompt[newPrompt.length - 1] = {
    ...lastPart,
    text: `${lastPart.text}${separator}${textToAppend}`,
  };
```

`Part.text` is optional in the `@google/genai` schema, so a part may carry the `text` key with a
non-string value (`undefined` after an object spread, `null` from a `JSON.parse`d payload or a
`model_construct` path). `'text' in part` is `true` for those parts, so the interpolation writes the
literal string `undefined` (or `null`) into the prompt text that is sent to the model.

Every other read of `text` in this module and its neighbours already guards the type:
`partToString` (`part.text ?? ''`), `flatMapTextParts` (`'text' in part` followed by
`!== undefined`), `getResponseText` (`part.text && !part.thought`), `isTextPart`
(`typeof part.text === 'string'`), `agent/content-utils.ts` (`'text' in part && part.text !==
undefined`), `utils/historyHardening.ts` (`typeof part.text === 'string'`). `appendToLastTextPart`
was the only consumer that merged unconditionally.

Who hits it: any caller that appends to a prompt whose last part came from a provider payload or an
object spread. In this repo that path is
`packages/cli/src/services/prompt-processors/argumentProcessor.ts` (`appendToLastTextPart(prompt,
context.invocation.raw)` for custom slash commands), so the model would receive
`undefined\n\n<command args>` as the argument block.

## Fix

Use the module's existing type guard instead of the `in` check:

```diff
-  } else if (lastPart && 'text' in lastPart) {
+  } else if (isTextPart(lastPart)) {
```

A part whose `text` is not a string is now handled exactly like any other non-text part: the
appended text becomes a new `{ text: separator + textToAppend }` part. Real text parts still merge
into the same part, so the rendered prompt is unchanged for `{ text: string }` and `string` inputs.
`isTextPart` is declared in the same file, so nothing new is exported.

## Tests

New case in `packages/core/src/utils/partUtils.test.ts`
(`appendToLastTextPart > should not stringify a non-string text field into the prompt`) asserts that
`[{ text: undefined }]` yields `[{ text: undefined }, { text: '\n\nnew text' }]`.

Repro `repro-1.ts` (standard library plus the repository's own TypeScript, no network, no keys, run
through the repository's pinned `tsx`) prints expected/actual for four last-part shapes and exits
non-zero while the defect is present.

With the source change reverted (`git stash push -- packages/core/src/utils/partUtils.ts`),
`before-1.log` shows:

```
FAIL last part { text: undefined }
     expected: [{},{"text":"\n\nnew text"}]
     actual  : [{"text":"undefined\n\nnew text"}]
FAIL last part { text: null }
     expected: [{"text":null},{"text":"\n\nnew text"}]
     actual  : [{"text":"null\n\nnew text"}]
DEFECT PRESENT: appendToLastTextPart writes the string "undefined"/"null" into the prompt.
EXIT=1

=== new regression test on the reverted source ===
 FAIL  src/utils/partUtils.test.ts > partUtils > appendToLastTextPart > should not stringify a non-string text field into the prompt
 Tests  1 failed | 38 passed (39)
EXIT=1
```

With the fix applied, `after-1.log` shows:

```
FIXED: non-string text fields are no longer stringified.
EXIT=0

=== repo's own focused test for the touched module ===
command: cd repo/packages/core && node ../../node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/utils/partUtils.test.ts
 ✓ src/utils/partUtils.test.ts (39 tests) 7ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  39 passed (39)
EXIT=0
```

## Related Issues

None filed. (This section covers the pull request template's *Summary* and *Details*; *Tests* above
covers *How to Validate*.)

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [ ] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed) — not applicable: no documented
      behaviour changes, the guard matches the module's documented `Part` handling.
- [x] Noted breaking changes (if any) — none; only parts whose `text` is not a string change output.
- [x] Validated on required platforms/methods:
  - [ ] MacOS
  - [x] Windows — `npm run` equivalent: repository vitest runner plus the `tsx` repro above
  - [ ] Linux

prs.title: fix(core): mark folders whose contents were never scanned as truncated
prs.body:
## Problem

`getFolderStructure()` promises, in its own summary line and in the `formatStructure` docstring,
that `...` marks "more items not shown, were ignored, or the display limit (N items) was reached".
`readFullStructure()` did not honour that when the `maxItems` budget ran out *on a folder itself*:
the queued folder is skipped with a bare `continue`, and the comment asserted that the parent had
already flagged truncation. That is only true when the parent skipped a **following** entry:

```ts
    if (currentItemCount >= options.maxItems) {
      // If the root itself caused us to exceed, we can't really show anything.
      // Otherwise, this folder won't be processed further.
      // The parent that queued this would have set its own hasMoreSubfolders flag.
      continue;
    }
```

When the limit is reached exactly at the last queued subfolder, nothing is flagged: the tree ends at
that folder, the folder is rendered as if it were empty, and the summary omits the "display limit
was reached" sentence. The existing `should handle maxItems that only allows the root folder itself`
test shows the intended behaviour for the other branch — `maxItems: 1` on a tree with files and a
subfolder prints both `├───...` / `└───...` markers *and* the summary sentence. Observed with
`level1/level2/level3/file.txt` and `maxItems: 3` (`before-2.log`):

```
Showing up to 3 items (files + folders).

<ROOT>\
└───level1\
    └───level2\
        └───level3\
```

`level3` contains `file.txt`, but the output shows neither the file nor any truncation marker, and
the summary claims nothing was cut off. Every consumer of this helper — the model-facing
`directory structure` context — is told an occupied directory is empty.

Who hits it: any repository whose tree consumes the item budget before a leaf directory is read;
the deeper the tree, the more likely the last visible folder hides its contents silently.

## Fix

Mark the folder whose children were skipped, so `formatStructure()` prints the truncation marker
under it and `isTruncated()` turns on the summary sentence:

```diff
     if (currentItemCount >= options.maxItems) {
       // If the root itself caused us to exceed, we can't really show anything.
-      // Otherwise, this folder won't be processed further.
-      // The parent that queued this would have set its own hasMoreSubfolders flag.
+      // Otherwise, this folder won't be processed further, so mark it here: the parent
+      // only sets its own hasMoreSubfolders flag when it skipped a *following* entry,
+      // which leaves the last folder whose contents were never scanned looking empty.
+      folderInfo.hasMoreSubfolders = true;
       continue;
     }
```

The change is display-only: it reuses the existing `hasMoreSubfolders` field and the existing
rendering path, adds no option, and only affects folders whose contents were skipped.

## Tests

Three expectations in `packages/core/src/utils/getFolderStructure.test.ts` encoded the old, silent
output and were updated to the now-accurate trees (they are the regression tests — all three fail on
the unpatched source):

- `should handle maxItems truncation for files within a folder` — `subfolderB\` now ends with an
  indented `...` and the summary reports the limit.
- `should handle maxItems truncation for subfolders` — each unscanned `folder-N\` now ends with an
  indented `...`.
- `should truncate deep folder structure if maxItems is small` — `level3\` now ends with an
  indented `...` and the summary reports the limit.

Repro `repro-2.ts` (standard library plus the repository's own TypeScript, no network, no keys, run
through the repository's pinned `tsx`) builds the `level1/level2/level3/file.txt` tree, asserts that
`level3` is followed by a truncation marker and that the summary reports the limit, and exits
non-zero while the defect is present.

With the source change reverted (`git stash push -- packages/core/src/utils/getFolderStructure.ts`),
`before-2.log` shows:

```
Showing up to 3 items (files + folders).

<ROOT>\
└───level1\
    └───level2\
        └───level3\
---
FAIL level3 hides file.txt behind a truncation marker: child line was ""
FAIL summary reports the display limit: missing "contain more items not shown" sentence
DEFECT PRESENT: a folder whose contents were never scanned is rendered as empty.
EXIT=1

=== updated expectations on the reverted source ===
 ❯ src/utils/getFolderStructure.test.ts (15 tests | 3 failed) 143ms
 FAIL  src/utils/getFolderStructure.test.ts > getFolderStructure > should handle maxItems truncation for files within a folder
 FAIL  src/utils/getFolderStructure.test.ts > getFolderStructure > should handle maxItems truncation for subfolders
 FAIL  src/utils/getFolderStructure.test.ts > getFolderStructure > should truncate deep folder structure if maxItems is small
 Tests  3 failed | 12 passed (15)
EXIT=1
```

With the fix applied, `after-2.log` shows:

```
<ROOT>\
└───level1\
    └───level2\
        └───level3\
            └───...
---
ok   level3 is rendered
ok   level3 hides file.txt behind a truncation marker
ok   summary reports the display limit
FIXED: folders whose contents were not scanned are marked as truncated.
EXIT=0

=== repo's own focused test for the touched module ===
command: cd repo/packages/core && node ../../node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/utils/getFolderStructure.test.ts
 ✓ src/utils/getFolderStructure.test.ts (15 tests) 110ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
EXIT=0

=== neighbouring consumers of the same helper ===
command: node ../../node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/utils/partUtils.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  39 passed (39)
EXIT=0
```

## Related Issues

None filed. (This section covers the pull request template's *Summary* and *Details*; *Tests* above
covers *How to Validate*.)

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Added/updated tests (if needed)
- [ ] Updated relevant documentation and README (if needed) — not applicable: the documented
      meaning of `...` is unchanged; the code now matches it.
- [x] Noted breaking changes (if any) — none; the rendered tree only gains markers where content was

prs.title: fix(a2a-server): enforce HTTP auth, harden createTask trust, and prevent restore path traversal
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes three security vulnerabilities in `@google/gemini-cli-a2a-server`:
1. Enforces Bearer token authentication (`GEMINI_IPC_SECRET` or `CODER_AGENT_AUTH_TOKEN`) and `Host`/`Origin` localhost validation across all HTTP/JSON-RPC and REST endpoints, removing hardcoded credentials (`'valid-token'`, `'admin:password'`).
2. Strips client-supplied `isTrusted` and normalizes `workspacePath` in `CoderAgentExecutor.createTask()`, matching `reconstruct()` and `execute()`.
3. Prevents path traversal in `RestoreCommand` when resolving checkpoint filenames.

## Details

- **HTTP Auth & DNS Rebinding (`packages/a2a-server/src/http/app.ts`):**
  - Reads `expectedAuthToken` from `process.env['GEMINI_IPC_SECRET'] || process.env['CODER_AGENT_AUTH_TOKEN']` before `loadEnvironment()` so workspace `.env` cannot override it, and fails closed at startup if neither is set. Supporting `GEMINI_IPC_SECRET` preserves compatibility with Gemini Code Assist in VS Code.
  - Validates `Host` and `Origin` headers against `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, and `[::1]` on all routes (including `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json`), returning `403` on mismatch.
  - Validates `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` via `crypto.timingSafeEqual` in Express middleware prior to `setupRoutes()` and all REST routes (`/tasks`, `/executeCommand`, `/listCommands`, `/tasks/metadata`, `/tasks/:taskId/metadata`), returning `401` on unauthorized requests.
- **Task Creation Trust (`packages/a2a-server/src/agent/executor.ts`):**
  - `createTask()` now strips client-supplied `isTrusted` (`isTrusted: undefined`) and normalizes `workspacePath` via `validateWorkspacePath()`.

prs.title: fix(core): respect active YOLO mode in taint and build file checks
prs.body:
## Summary

Respect active, trusted YOLO mode (`--approval-mode=yolo` / `-y`) in shell taint/build-file risk checks and `PolicyEngine` build file protection so autonomous interactive and headless YOLO runs are no longer interrupted by confirmation prompts or hard-denied (`POLICY_VIOLATION`) when editing build configuration files or running commands referencing external context.

All indirect prompt-injection protections remain fully enforced in `default` and `auto_edit` modes, in untrusted folders (`!isTrustedFolder()`), when YOLO mode is administratively disabled (`disableYoloMode` / `isYoloModeDisabled()`), and when higher-tier user/admin policy rules explicitly require `ask_user` or `deny`.

## Details

1. **`ShellToolInvocation` (`packages/core/src/tools/shell.ts`)**:
   - Added `isActiveYoloMode()` verifying both `ApprovalMode.YOLO` and `!isYoloModeDisabled()`.
   - Updated `shouldConfirmExecute()` to skip forcing confirmation for `hasTaintedOrBuildFileRisk()` when active YOLO mode is enabled (unless `forcedDecision === 'ask_user'` from an explicit policy rule or hook).
   - Updated `isCommandSubstitutionAllowed()` so active YOLO mode delegates command substitution checks to `PolicyEngine` (`yolo.toml` sets `allowCommandSubstitution = true`) rather than unconditionally blocking on `hasTaintedOrBuildFileRisk()`.
   - Preserved the `hasTaintedOrBuildFileRisk()` guard in `getPolicyUpdateOptions()` so tainted commands never persist permanent `"Always allow"` rules.
2. **`Scheduler` (`packages/core/src/scheduler/scheduler.ts`)**:
   - Skipped escalating `PolicyDecision.ALLOW` to `ASK_USER` (interactive) or `DENY` (non-interactive/headless) for `hasTaintedOrBuildFileRisk()` when active YOLO mode (`!isYoloModeDisabled()`) is enabled.
3. **`PolicyEngine` (`packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.ts`)**:
   - Skipped the hardcoded `Build File Protection` downgrade (`ASK_USER` / `DENY` on `package.json`, `Makefile`, `BUILD.bazel`, etc.) when running in trusted YOLO mode (`this.approvalMode === ApprovalMode.YOLO && this.isTrustedFolder()`). `auto_edit` mode, `default` mode, untrusted workspaces, and explicit user/admin rules remain protected.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29682
Fixes #29680
Related to #29687
Related to #30004

## How to Validate

1. Run targeted unit test suites:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/tools/shell.test.ts src/scheduler/scheduler.test.ts src/policy/policy-engine.test.ts
   ```
2. Run typecheck and lint:
   ```bash
   npm run typecheck
   npm run lint
   ```
3. Manual / headless reproduction:
   - Run `gemini --approval-mode=yolo -p "Update a script in package.json and run npm test"` in a trusted workspace -> executes without `DENY` (`Modifying build configuration files requires explicit user confirmation`) or interactive confirmation prompts.
   - Run in `--approval-mode=auto_edit` or in an untrusted workspace -> build file edits and untrusted flags still require explicit user confirmation.

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Hello,

 I've been using Copilot CLI and had it connected to the official [Jenkins MCP Server plugin](https://github.com/jenkinsci/mcp-server-plugin/) endpoint at `https://jenkins.my-company-domain.com/mcp-server/mcp` using streamable HTTP. Around a month ago, I had a session going in CLI 1.0.92 and started a new session in a separate terminal tab where auto-update loaded up version 1.0.94. In the new session, I started getting errors connecting to the Jenkins MCP endpoint only. Other MCPs do not have issues.

The session where I was still running 1.0.92 was still working fine so I assumed at the time that perhaps I had just loaded too many MCP sessions, and I didn't really look into it.

Today a colleague is scheduled to do a Jenkins and all plugins upgrade and I asked him to look into the logs on the Jenkins server for more details. He did and said none of my requests are getting to the reverse proxy in front of Jenkins, so I started digging into it further.

First I tried creating a new user-level API key in Jenkins, and that didn't work. Next I tried configuring the MCP in Claude Code, and that did work. So then I started another new session where Copilot CLI 1.0.114 was automatically loaded up as the latest release and I still received the same error.

Finally, I started pulling older versions and installing them one by one in a prefix directory:

```
curl -fsSL https://gh.io/copilot-install | COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false PREFIX="/Users/my-user/copilot-debug" VERSION="1.0.92" bash && mv /Users/my-user/copilot-debug/bin/copilot /Users/my-user/copilot-debug/bin/copilot-1.0.92
curl -fsSL https://gh.io/copilot-install | COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false PREFIX="/Users/my-user/copilot-debug" VERSION="1.0.93" bash && mv /Users/my-user/copilot-debug/bin/copilot /Users/my-user/copilot-debug/bin/copilot-1.0.93
```

Then loading each one up with auto-update forced off:

```
/Users/my-user/copilot-debug/bin/copilot-1.0.92 --no-auto-update
/Users/my-user/copilot-debug/bin/copilot-1.0.93 --no-auto-update
```

When starting version 1.0.92, the MCP server is connected successfully and I can use the tools to interact with Jenkins. When starting version 1.0.93, I get the following error:

`failed to initialize MCP client: transport failure during send initialize request: Client error: error sending request for url (https://jenkins.my-company-domain.com/mcp-server/mcp)`



### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.93.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Setup Jenkins
Install the Jenkins MCP server plugin in Jenkins
Configure a user API key in Jenkins
Base64 encode `jenkins-login:<api-key>` and configure the MCP server with a Basic Authentication token:
mcp-config.json

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "jenkins": {
      "tools": [
        "*"
      ],
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://jenkins.my-company-domain.com/mcp-server/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Basic <base64-encoded-token>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```
Start copilot 1.0.92 with `--no-auto-update`, observe that the MCP server connects
Start copilot 1.0.93 with `--no-auto-update`, observe the error
Start copilot 1.0.114, observe the error again

### Expected behavior

MCP server connects as it did in 1.0.92

### Additional context

ARM (Apple M2 Max) on MacOS Golden Gate 27.0

issues.title: Linux x86_64 CLI aborts in bundled cli-native.node on Arch

labels.name: area:platform-linux
labels.description: Linux-specific: Wayland, X11, Ubuntu, Fedora, Alpine, ARM, terminal emulators

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.114 terminated with `SIGABRT` during a long-lived interactive session on native Linux x86_64. The systemd coredump shows the crashing thread calling `abort()` from the bundled native module `cli-native.node`. No explicit fatal message was emitted in the Copilot log.

This appears to be an internal native-module failure rather than an OOM kill, terminal failure, or Omarchy issue.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.114

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

A minimal reproduction is not yet available.

Observed sequence:

1. Start `copilot` normally in an interactive Kitty terminal.
2. Use a long-lived interactive session.
3. After approximately 49 minutes, the process exits and systemd records a core dump with `SIGABRT`.

The command line recorded in the core was simply:

```text
copilot
```

The session was named `Compare AI Model Nuances`. The operation immediately triggering the abort could not be determined from the persisted logs.

### Expected behavior

The CLI should continue running, or report a recoverable error, rather than aborting the native process and terminating the session.

### Additional context

- OS: Omarchy on Arch Linux
- Kernel: `7.2.11-arch1-1`
- Architecture: `x86_64`
- Terminal: Kitty (`xterm-kitty`)
- Shell: bash
- Embedded Node.js runtime: `v24.22.1`
- Crash time: 2026-11-23 18:57:46 MST (coredump record: 18:58:02 MST)
- The process was running from `/home/tjc/.local/share/mise/installs/copilot/1.0.114/copilot`
- The binary was not updated immediately before the crash; its mtime was 2026-11-17.
- Copilot logged that 1.0.114 was current at startup.
- Memory check after the crash: 31 GiB total, 19 GiB available, 62 GiB swap with 315 MiB used.
- The journal contained no OOM-killer event or related system failure.
- No other `copilot` coredumps were found; retained coredumps for other applications were unrelated.

The complete coredump is available locally if maintainers need additional artifacts, but it was not uploaded because it may contain private session data. The relevant backtrace shape is:

```text
#0  abort() from /usr/lib/libc.so.6
#1  ... cli-native.node
#2  ... cli-native.node
#3  ... cli-native.node
...
#18 ... cli-native.node
#19 ... libc.so.6
```

The native modules have no build IDs and the frames remain unsymbolized. The Copilot process log contains startup/session information but no fatal error or panic text.

issues.title: Copilot CLI rg compaction corrupts filenames with multiple numeric suffixes

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When the built-in rg tool compacts search results, it can truncate filenames with multiple numeric suffixes and display part of the filename where the line number should be. It can also group matches from two distinct files under one truncated filename. Standalone ripgrep returns the correct filenames and line numbers.

### Affected version

1.0.114

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Run this in a shell. It creates two files with 32 matching lines each and prints their directory. The long directory path helps trigger compaction.

cd "$(mktemp -d /tmp/copilot-rg-compaction-repro-with-a-long-absolute-directory-path.XXXXXX)"
for file in sample.log.2-3-71-109 sample.log.2-3-73-112; do
  awk 'BEGIN { for (i = 0; i < 32; i++) print "RG_REPRO" }' > "$file"
done
pwd

2. Start copilot in that directory and enter this prompt, replacing <directory> with the path printed above:
Use the built-in rg tool, not Bash, to search for RG_REPRO in <directory>. Use glob sample.log.*, content output, line numbers enabled, and a head_limit of 20. Show the tool output as-is.

The built-in tool reports 40 matches across 1 file. It groups both files under sample.log.2 and displays entries like 3- 71-109:1:RG_REPRO.

### Expected behavior

The tool should report 40 matches across 2 files, preserving both full filenames and lines 1–20 for each. To compare, run rg -Hn -m 20 RG_REPRO sample.log.* in the same directory. Standalone ripgrep returns the same 40 matches with the correct filenames and line numbers.

### Additional context

_No response_

issues.title: Remove or make optional the 100-word response limit

labels.name: area:configuration
labels.description: Config files, instruction files, settings, and environment variables

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

To meet a hard-coded 100-word response target, Copilot generates incomprehensible answers omitting key details.

### Proposed solution

Remove the 100-word instruction from the default system prompt, or expose it as an opt-in setting. Let models adapt based on the task and user wording, while preserving a general preference for concise answers. Individual prompts can still request a 100-word limit, or users can apply such a limit in their local agent instructions if they prefer it.

### Example prompts or workflows

- Diagnose an implementation or deployment failure and explain the evidence and tradeoffs.
- Plan a focused change spanning several files, including why each step is needed.
- Review an existing design and identify risks.
- Ad infinitum

### Additional context

This rigid limit compresses complex answers, omits necessary evidence or code context, and forces users to spend extra turns requesting the detail that should have been included initially. It wastes user time and tokens rather than saving them.

This request follows the context-engineering principle demonstrated by Anthropic's work on Claude Code: periodically remove outdated instructions whose value no longer justifies their cost. Anthropic [removed more than 80 percent of the Claude Code system prompt](https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/anthropic-claude-code-system-prompt-cut) for newer models and reported no measurable loss in evaluations.

A rigid output budget can be an unnecessary restriction for capable modern models and can increase total token and credit use when users need extra turns. Please remove the limit or make it optional rather than hard-coded.

issues.title: Interactive mode fails on invalid MCP output schema while noninteractive mode succeeds; blocks all turns

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

A local MCP tool advertising `outputSchema.anyOf: null` causes interactive Copilot CLI to fail before answering, even when the prompt does not require the tool.

The error identifies only a tool index, not the offending MCP server or tool. Reproduced with one generic dummy tool, without Agency or Transmog.

### Affected version

1.0.115-7, launched through Agency 2026.11.16.5 on Linux/WSL

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Requires Node.js and an authenticated Copilot CLI. Extract the attached reproduction and run commands from its directory. [copilot-mcp-schema-repro.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/35273756/copilot-mcp-schema-repro.json)


1. Start interactive mode:
   ```sh
   copilot --additional-mcp-config @mcp.json
   ```
2. Enter:
   ```text
   Reply with exactly OK. Do not call any tools.
   ```
3. The turn fails before any tool invocation:
   ```text
   400 [MapParam] [tools[25].output_schema.anyOf]
   [invalid_type] Invalid type for 'tools[25].output_schema.anyOf':
   expected an unknown value, but got null instead.
   ```
   The numeric tool index may vary.

4. Exit and restart with only the invalid schema field omitted:
   ```sh
   MCP_REPRO_VALID=1 copilot --additional-mcp-config @mcp.json
   ```
   Submit the same prompt. Result: `OK`.

5. The invalid schema also succeeds in noninteractive mode:
   ```sh
   copilot --additional-mcp-config @mcp.json -p "Reply with exactly OK. Do not call any tools."
   ```
   Result: `OK`.

### Expected behavior

Detect the invalid MCP schema and identify the server, tool name, and offending field with an actionable diagnostic, rather than failing the entire turn with positional indexes.

Interactive and noninteractive modes should handle the same invalid schema consistently.

### Additional context

- The reproduction exposes one generic tool and requires no npm packages.
- Removing only `anyOf: null` makes the interactive test succeed.
- No tool invocation is required to trigger the failure.
- The failure also reproduced with deferred loading, but deferred loading is not required.
- Other Copilot versions and model backends have not been tested.

issues.title: ACP mode no longer emits `agent_thought_chunk` since 1.0.110 (reasoning summaries missing for ACP clients)

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

issues.body:
Since Copilot CLI **1.0.110**, `copilot --acp` no longer sends any `session/update` with `sessionUpdate: "agent_thought_chunk"`. Up to **1.0.109** reasoning summaries were streamed to ACP clients; our ACP client renders them as a live "thinking" block, so users now see the agent silent for long stretches.

### Repro

Same prompt, model `claude-opus-5.5`, `reasoning_effort=high`, each version installed in isolation with `COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=false` and its own `COPILOT_PKG_CACHE_HOME`:

1. `initialize` → `session/new` → `session/set_config_option` (`model`, `reasoning_effort=high`)
2. `session/prompt`: *"Plan step by step: how many weekdays are there between 2026-03-03 and 2026-07-19 inclusive, excluding German public holidays in NRW? Reason it out before answering, then give only the number."*
3. Count `session/update` kinds.

| CLI version | `agent_thought_chunk` count |
|---|---|
| 1.0.87 | 52 |
| 1.0.100 | 46 |
| 1.0.107 | 44 |
| 1.0.109 | 45 |
| **1.0.110** | **0** |
| 1.0.111 | 0 |
| 1.0.114 | 0 |

Same with `claude-sonnet-5.5` and GPT models; macOS arm64 and Linux x64 (Codespaces). On 1.0.114 the update kinds we receive are only `available_commands_update`, `user_message_chunk`, `agent_message_chunk`, `tool_call`, `tool_call_update`, `config_option_update`, `usage_update`, `session_info_update`.

### Tried on 1.0.114 (no effect)

- `copilot config showReasoning on`
- `reasoning_effort=high` via `session/set_config_option`
- `COPILOT_FEATURE_FLAGS` / `COPILOT_CLI_ENABLED_FEATURE_FLAGS` overrides
- `reasoningSummary` / `inference.reasoningSummary` in settings
- `_meta` on `session/new`

`session/new` only offers the config options `mode`, `model`, `reasoning_effort`, `allow_all`.

### Observations

- The 1.0.110 changelog has several reasoning-display changes (empty Thought rows, incomplete reasoning labels, "Thought for" durations), but nothing about ACP.
- The binary contains a flag named `copilot_cli_reasoning_summaries_off_by_default`; it is also present in 1.0.109, so we can't tell whether this is an intended default change or a regression in the ACP mapping.

### Ask

1. Is dropping `agent_thought_chunk` in ACP mode intended?
2. If the new default is "reasoning summaries off", could ACP clients opt in — e.g. a session config option `reasoning_summary` (`none` / `concise` / `detailed`, like the SDK's `reasoningSummary`), or honoring `showReasoning` in ACP mode?

Workaround for now: pinning the CLI to 1.0.109 with auto-update disabled.

issues.title: In prompt mode, an extension tool's permission request waits forever instead of being denied, and `--allow-tool` can't name an extension tool

labels.name: area:permissions
labels.description: Tool approval, security boundaries, sandbox mode, and directory restrictions

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In prompt mode (`copilot -p`), when the model calls a tool that an extension registers, the CLI raises a `custom-tool` permission request that nothing answers, so the run waits until it is killed. Prompt mode's permission handler returns early for that kind (`if (resolvedByHook || kind === "custom-tool") return;` in `cli-main.js`). Other requests that need approval in prompt mode are denied at once with `denied-no-approval-rule-and-could-not-request-from-user`, as the permissions help says they should be.

`--allow-tool` with the extension tool's name doesn't match the request either, and the permissions help documents no rule pattern for extension tools. Only `--allow-all-tools` works, so a scripted check of one extension tool has to allow every tool.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.108-1 (prerelease). The same early return is in 1.0.107.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Install a plugin or user extension that registers a tool, such as `probe_ping`.
2. Run `copilot -p "Call probe_ping once."`. The run waits; `events.jsonl` shows `permission.requested` with `kind: "custom-tool"` and no `permission.completed` until the process is killed.
3. Run it again with `--allow-tool probe_ping`. Same result.
4. Run it with `--available-tools probe_ping --allow-all-tools`. The tool runs.

### Expected behavior

Prompt mode denies an extension tool request that no rule allows, as it does for other kinds, and `--allow-tool` accepts a pattern for one extension tool.

### Additional context

- macOS on Apple silicon (arm64).
- Reproduced on 2026-11-07 with an extension tool. With no rule, the run waited three and a half minutes until it was cancelled. With `--allow-tool` naming the tool, it waited the same way. With `--available-tools` naming the tool and `--allow-all-tools`, the tool ran.

issues.title: Worktrees are nightmare, should be disabled by default

labels.name: area:configuration
labels.description: Config files, instruction files, settings, and environment variables

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body: ### Describe the bug Worktrees must be disabled by default, and enabled only by human user! Right now I found myself in a situation when a session was handed to CLI, and ended up with thousands of new lines of _useful_ code, but impossible to apply back to main worktree for whatever git-related reason. Applying complex subtree patches with AI-generated code causes immeasurable suffering, as there is no reliable merge UI inside VSCode, and whenever worktree fails to merge, user is stuck with hairy git command line options or lottery-like AI-driven resolution, which can render whole branch broken (if you were careful enough to branch out before starting a session): What am I as user supposed to do here?? issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Repository-level  `.mcp.json` files are parsed as strict JSON. Adding a  `//` or  `/* ... */`  comment causes Copilot CLI to reject the entire file and skip every MCP server it defines.
This makes it difficult to maintain a shared repository configuration containing documentation or temporarily disabled server definitions.

### Affected version

1.0.78-0

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Create a trusted Git repository.
2. Add `.mcp.json`:
```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    // Used for browser-based integration tests.
    "playwright": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["@playwright/mcp@latest"],
      "tools": ["*"]
    }
  }
}
```
3. Run `copilot mcp list --json`
4. Copilot reports:
```
Warning: skipping workspace MCP config ".mcp.json" because it is malformed:
Invalid JSON: key must be a string
```

5. Remove the comment and repeat the command. The workspace MCP server is then discovered successfully.

### Expected behavior

Copilot CLI should parse `.mcp.json` as JSONC, supporting  `//` and  `/* ... */` comments while continuing to load valid MCP definitions.

Alternatively, the configuration schema could provide a documented repository-level mechanism such as `"enabled": false` for retaining optional MCP definitions without loading them.

A malformed individual server entry should ideally not prevent unrelated valid servers from loading.

### Additional context

_No response_

issues.title: Local stdio MCP server silently dropped during session-ID swap on startup (resume and  /new )

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
CLI version: 1.0.86 (also reproduced on 1.0.67 in a parallel session)

Summary:
On every session start — both  --resume  and a fresh  /new  session — the runtime briefly creates a placeholder/foreground session, connects all configured MCP servers to it, then swaps in the real session ID. During that swap,  github-mcp-server  (remote) is correctly torn down and reconnected to the new session. A local stdio server ( mas-devops , our custom MCP server) is not reconnected — it remains bound to the discarded placeholder session and never appears in the tool catalog for the real session, even though its process is alive and its one-and-only MCP handshake succeeded. Result: the CLI reports the server as connected in  mcp list , but  tool_search_tool  finds zero tools for it, and any call to it fails with  "MCP server is not connected" .

Reproduction (100% reproducible, 2 independent trials):

1. Configure a local stdio MCP server in  ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json  ( type: local ,  command ,  args ,  env ).
2. Start a session via  copilot --resume=<id>  or  /new  from within an existing session.
3. Inspect  ~/.copilot/logs/process-<pid>.log :
•  Registering foreground session: <placeholder-id> 
•  mas-devops-mcp  →  Service initialized as client  (single occurrence, tied to  <placeholder-id> )
•  Unregistering foreground session: <placeholder-id> 
•  Registering foreground session: <real-id> 
•  github-mcp-server  →  task cancelled  /  serve finished {quit_reason: Cancelled}  → new  Service initialized as client  (reconnected under  <real-id> )
•  mas-devops-mcp  → no further log lines at all — never torn down, never reconnected.
4.  tool_search_tool  with pattern matching the local server's tool prefix → 0 results, even though  ps  shows its process alive and  copilot mcp get <name>  shows  Status: Enabled .

Expected: Local stdio servers should be reconnected (or at minimum re-registered against the real session) using the same teardown+reconnect logic already applied to remote servers during the session-ID swap.

Actual: Only the remote server observed ( github-mcp-server ) gets that reconnect; the local stdio server is silently orphaned, with no error surfaced to the user except a delayed, easy-to-miss  PluginsScreenDetail listMcpTools(<name>) failed: Error: MCP server "<name>" is not connected  line.

Workarounds attempted, none effective:

• Restarting the CLI ( /restart ) — same defect recurs.
• Starting a brand-new session ( /new ) instead of resuming — same defect recurs identically.
•  copilot mcp disable <name>  +  copilot mcp enable <name>  mid-session — no effect (config toggle doesn't force a live reconnect).
• Clearing  ~/Library/Caches/copilot/mcp-tools/*.json  (unrelated stale-cache warnings were also present) — no effect on this specific issue.
• Killing and letting the orphaned child process re-spawn — not possible; per documented behavior, local stdio MCP connections cannot be reconnected mid-session once dropped.

Impact: Any custom/local stdio MCP server becomes permanently unusable for the lifetime of a session, with no user-facing recovery path short of hoping a future session start doesn't hit the race. Remote MCP servers are unaffected.

issues.title: Remote MCP (OAuth): expired access token forces interactive re-auth instead of silent refresh_token grant

labels.name: area:authentication
labels.description: Login, OAuth, device auth, token management, and keychain integration

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
## Summary

When a remote OAuth-protected MCP server's cached **access token** is expired at session start, the Copilot CLI treats the server as needing a fresh **interactive** OAuth login and drops its tools — even though a valid **refresh token** is cached. It never attempts an [RFC 6749 §6](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6749#section-6) `refresh_token` grant. In non-interactive/automation sessions the interactive flow can't complete, so the server's tools silently never load.

## Environment

- GitHub Copilot CLI `1.0.71`, running inside VS Code
- macOS (Darwin); credential store = Apple Keychain (`copilot-mcp-oauth`)
- MCP transport: `rmcp` streamable HTTP (`rmcp::transport::worker` / `::streamable`), `reqwest 0.13.4`

## Configuration

- Remote HTTP MCP server in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`:
  ```json
  "notion": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.notion.com/mcp" }
  ```
- Cached grant in Keychain (`service copilot-mcp-oauth`, account `<hash>`) and `~/.copilot/mcp-oauth-config/<hash>.tokens.json` — contains `accessToken`, `expiresAt`, `refreshToken`.
- Server authorization-server metadata ([RFC 8414](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8414)) advertises refresh support:
  `token_endpoint: https://mcp.notion.com/token`, `grant_types_supported: ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"]`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Authenticate a remote OAuth MCP server (e.g. Notion) so a valid access+refresh grant is cached.
2. Let the **access** token expire while the **refresh** token stays valid (Notion access tokens last ~8h — e.g. leave it overnight).
3. Start a new Copilot CLI session (especially a non-interactive/scheduled one).
4. Observe: the server's tools are absent from the session.

## Observed behavior

From `~/.copilot/logs/process-<...>.log` (redacted):

```
[ERROR] Starting remote MCP client for notion with url: https://mcp.notion.com/mcp
[ERROR] Connecting MCP client for notion...
        -> connects to mcp.notion.com:443 using the cached (expired) access token
[ERROR] [rust:rmcp::transport::worker] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed,
        when Client(OAuthChallenge { www_authenticate_header:
        "...OAuth, resource_metadata=\".../.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp\",
        error=\"invalid_token\", error_description=\"Mis...\"" })
[ERROR] Server notion requires authentication, initiating OAuth flow
[ERROR] OAuth authentication required for notion
```

The runtime then reads the cached OAuth entry from Keychain but still ends at **"OAuth authentication required."**

### Evidence that no refresh was attempted

Grep of the entire session-start process log:

```
POSTs to mcp.notion.com/token : 0
```

Zero `refresh_token` grants were sent, despite a valid refresh token being cached.

## Expected behavior

On a `401` / `WWW-Authenticate: … error="invalid_token"` for a server that has a cached refresh token:

1. Silently POST `grant_type=refresh_token` (+ `client_id`) to the discovered `token_endpoint`.
2. Persist the rotated access/refresh tokens.
3. Reconnect and load the server's tools.
4. Only fall back to the interactive OAuth flow if the refresh itself fails (`invalid_grant`, expired/revoked).

## Impact

- Any remote OAuth MCP server silently loses its tools once the access token expires, until a manual re-auth — even though the refresh token is valid and the whole point of storing it is to avoid exactly this.
- Breaks unattended/scheduled sessions (e.g. a daily automation), where the interactive prompt can never be completed.

## Likely root cause / where to look

- The `rmcp` streamable transport surfaces the OAuth challenge as a **fatal** transport error ("worker quit with fatal … `OAuthChallenge`"), and the CLI's handler maps "auth required" directly to the interactive flow without first attempting a token refresh.
- Secondary: the session's tool list appears to be snapshotted at startup, so even a later successful (re)auth doesn't surface the tools into an already-running session.

## Suggested fix

- Insert a refresh step in the auth-challenge path: if a `refresh_token` is cached for the server, perform the refresh grant against the discovered `token_endpoint`, persist rotated tokens, and reconnect **before** considering interactive auth.
- Optionally refresh **proactively** when `expiresAt` is at/near expiry before the first connect.
- Consider re-syncing tools into active sessions after a late auth success.

## Workaround

- Manually perform the `refresh_token` grant against the `token_endpoint`, write the rotated tokens back into the cache; or re-run the CLI's interactive auth for the server before starting the session.

---

cc @connor4312 (VS Code team)

<sub>Filed with assistance from GitHub Copilot CLI.</sub>

issues.title: MCP client declares the Tasks extension on tools/call but rejects CreateTaskResult

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

The MCP client sends `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks` in `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities"].extensions` on every request, `tools/call` included. When a server answers with a `CreateTaskResult` (`resultType: "task"`), the tool call fails and `tasks/get` is never sent:

```
MCP request failed: expected CallToolResult from tools/call, got CreateTaskResult(CreateTaskResult { result_type: ResultType("task"), task: Task { task_id: "6c618e1b-c5f1-4b21-81e8-b68d05d39753", status: Working, status_message: Some("Working, 90s left"), created_at: "2026-11-18T02:56:24.271Z", last_updated_at: "2026-11-18T02:56:24.273Z", ttl_ms: Some(600000), poll_interval_ms: Some(30000) }, meta: None })
```

The [Tasks extension spec](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-tasks/blob/main/specification/2026-07-28/tasks.md#capability-negotiation) says: "A client that has negotiated this extension MUST be prepared to handle either `CallToolResult` or `CreateTaskResult` in response to any supported request it issues."

### Affected version

1.0.113

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Add a stdio MCP server to `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` that implements protocol 2026-07-28 and the Tasks extension:
   - `server/discover` returns:
     ```json
     { "resultType": "complete", "supportedVersions": ["2026-07-28"], "capabilities": { "tools": {}, "extensions": { "io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks": {} } }, "ttlMs": 0, "cacheScope": "public" }
     ```
   - `tools/list` returns one tool, `slow_probe`, with an empty input schema.
   - `tools/call` for `slow_probe`, when the request's `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities"].extensions` contains `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks`, returns:
     ```json
     { "resultType": "task", "taskId": "<uuid>", "status": "working", "createdAt": "<now>", "lastUpdatedAt": "<now>", "ttlMs": 600000, "pollIntervalMs": 30000 }
     ```
   - `tasks/get` returns the task as `working` until 90 seconds have passed, then `completed` with a `result` holding a `CallToolResult`.
2. Start `copilot` (with or without experimental mode) and ask it to call `slow_probe`.
3. The client's `tools/call` request declares the Tasks extension in `_meta`; the server returns the `CreateTaskResult` above.
4. The tool call fails with the error above. No `tasks/get` request reaches the server.

### Expected behavior

Either:
- the client polls `tasks/get` until the task completes and returns its result to the model; or
- if Tasks v2 isn't supported yet, the client stops declaring `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks`, so servers return a normal `CallToolResult`.

### Additional context

- With the same server, Claude Code 2.1.322 (Tasks v2) and VS Code 1.146.0's default Copilot harness (Tasks v1) both complete the task.
- Same failure with experimental mode on.
- Related: #2538, which added experimental v1 Tasks support for `taskSupport: "required"` tools. This report is about the v2 extension, which the client declares but doesn't handle.
- OS: Windows 11 x64

issues.title: Built-in GitHub MCP read tools are unavailable to custom agents when `gh` is on `PATH`

labels.name: area:agents

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

[HVE Core’s Backlog Manager report](https://github.com/microsoft/hve-core/issues/3458) describes an issue in the GitHub Copilot app’s CLI runtime: when `gh` is on `PATH`, the agent cannot read GitHub issues through the built-in MCP server, even when it explicitly declares `github/issue_read` and `github/list_issues`. For an agent that uses MCP for GitHub access and cannot use a shell fallback, the GitHub workflow stops.

### Affected version

The original report did not capture the Copilot app or CLI build.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

The original report used HVE Core’s Backlog Manager. Here is a smaller test to isolate tool availability; the with/without-`gh` comparison has not been run independently.

1. With the built-in GitHub MCP server enabled, add `.github/agents/github-read-probe.agent.md` to a test repository:

   ```markdown
   ---
   name: GitHub Read Probe
   description: Checks whether GitHub MCP issue reads are available.
   tools:
     - github/issue_read
     - github/list_issues
   ---
   Read the requested GitHub issue using the declared MCP tools only. If the tools are unavailable, report that. Do not use the shell.
   ```

2. Start a fresh Copilot process with `gh` discoverable on its `PATH`. Select **GitHub Read Probe** and ask it to read a known public issue. Check whether the two declared MCP tools are exposed, rather than relying only on the agent’s reply.
3. Start a fresh process with `gh` absent from its `PATH`. Keep the build, authentication, GitHub MCP configuration, agent, and prompt the same, and compare the exposed tools.

### Expected behavior

Explicitly declared GitHub MCP read tools should remain available regardless of whether `gh` is installed, subject to normal policy and permissions. If the omission is intentional, is there a supported opt-out for custom agents that cannot use a shell fallback?

### Additional context

The original report suggests the CLI runtime may start its built-in server with `excludeGhReplaceableTools: true` when it detects `gh`. That mechanism is unverified. The report also names `search_issues`, `pull_request_read`, `list_pull_requests`, and `search_pull_requests` as potentially affected.

[The HVE Core workaround](https://github.com/microsoft/hve-core/pull/3465) adds a `gh` fallback when an MCP tool is absent. It does not restore the tools for agents that cannot use `gh`.

issues.title: Supabase OAuth status probe fails with missing Mcp-Session-Id (HTTP 400) while normal App tool calls succeed

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
### Summary

The separate OAuth/authorization status check for an existing Supabase MCP connection fails with HTTP 400, while a normal GitHub Copilot App session can successfully invoke `get_project_url` through that connection.

The server's actual response body identifies a missing MCP session header:

```json
{"message":"Mcp-Session-Id header is required for non-initialization requests"}
```

Related: #5014 describes the same session-initialization failure pattern for another provider; #5039 describes a different possible cause of a similar HTTP-400 probe error. This report adds a Supabase-specific reproduction and the actual response body; I am not claiming that protocol-version rejection is the cause here.

### Environment

- macOS
- GitHub Copilot App 1.4.3 (in-app updater reported up to date)
- Copilot Business
- Existing project-scoped HTTP MCP server: Supabase hosted MCP
- Passive diagnostic used the SDK bundled with the App and the installed CLI runtime with `--no-auto-update`; no model prompt was sent during that diagnostic.

### Configuration (sanitized example)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "supabase": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp?project_ref=REDACTED&features=docs%2Caccount%2Cdatabase%2Cdebugging%2Cdevelopment%2Cfunctions%2Cbranching",
      "tools": ["*"]
    }
  }
}
```

`REDACTED` is a placeholder, not a real project reference. There are no static Authorization headers.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure one existing project-scoped Supabase MCP server and complete its normal OAuth connection.
2. Verify that a new local Copilot App session can call `get_project_url` successfully. This was observed in the actual App transcript.
3. Open Customize > Installed and the existing Supabase server's configuration/actions UI.
4. Observe the separate authorization check report:

```text
Could not check authorization
WsCommandError: invalid argument: MCP server probe returned HTTP 400 Bad Request
```

The server row can still report `Connected. Enabled.` afterward.

### Passive diagnostic evidence (sanitized)

```json
{
  "probe_status": "failed",
  "http_status": 400,
  "server_response": {
    "message": "Mcp-Session-Id header is required for non-initialization requests"
  },
  "anonymous_checks": {
    "ping_2026-07-28": 401,
    "initialize_2026-07-28": 401,
    "ping_2025-03-26": 401,
    "initialize_2025-03-26": 401
  },
  "normal_app_tool": "get_project_url succeeded in a separate actual Copilot App session",
  "new_login_during_diagnostic": false
}
```

The passive `session.mcp.oauth.probe` result exposed HTTP 400 and the response body above. No stored token was read, exported, or manually inserted into a request. No reauthentication was started for this diagnostic.

The anonymous checks only establish that those unauthenticated requests receive an expected 401. They do not prove which protocol versions are accepted after authentication.

Limitation: a separate attempt to compare `tools/list` in the explicitly created SDK diagnostic session required authentication in that isolated context, so I did not reauthenticate it. The successful normal tool call is independently evidenced by the actual Copilot App session, not by that SDK session. The successful project URL and all private identifiers are intentionally omitted here.

### Expected behavior

The authorization probe should establish an MCP session correctly before issuing non-initialization requests, or otherwise use a protocol-compliant status check. It should not present a missing-session protocol error as a reason to reauthenticate a working OAuth connection.

Please preserve the response detail in the UI and distinguish a protocol/session failure from rejected credentials. A blanket rule treating every HTTP 400 as authenticated would not be appropriate.

### Current safe workaround

Keep the existing OAuth connection and use normal Copilot App sessions. Avoid unnecessary login resets triggered only by this configuration-dialog probe error. This preserves the functioning connection but does not fix the faulty probe itself.

### Privacy

No credentials, account/organization names, real project reference or URL, local paths, database contents, or raw logs are included. Configuration and connection were preserved during diagnosis.
