prs.title: fix(app): stop following when the reader scrolls up by any input
prs.body:
Stacked on #66020. The timeline went on following its end after the reader scrolled up with anything but the wheel, a scroll key the app handles or a held pointer. The next size change (a streamed line, a row measurement, the draft growing) pulled the reader back to the latest message. With middle-click autoscroll in a session that streams, that is the timeline "moving up and down while scrolling". - **Cause:** the follow state learned that the reader left the end only from input events the app handles. Ctrl+Home, PageUp on a control in a row, the scrollbar thumb (portalled out of the element with the pointer listener), toggled middle-click autoscroll (the gesture ends on release) and a wheel over the session title send none. - **Fix:** the timeline learns it from the scroll itself. `readScroll` counts each movement of the offset as the reader's unless one of the timeline's own writes made it or the browser clamped it to a shorter range. Upward movement of that kind stops following, whatever caused it. - **Coalesced events:** each write sits between `readScroll` and `syncScroll`, so the reader's part survives when the browser folds a pin and a reader scroll into one scroll event. - **Slow scrolls:** autoscroll starts at 1 to 3 px a frame while a streaming reply pins the view back each frame. The machine adds the reader's upward movement up across scroll events and stops following past 4 px, the bound of a zoomed range's rounding. It forgets it when the scroll rests. - **Fast path:** the wheel, key, pointer and touch handlers stay. They give the intent before the scroll event arrives. - **One exemption:** a tool group that collapses from its stuck header scrolls the header back into place first. At the end of the timeline that scroll is skipped: the shorter content takes the view to the new end either way. ```mermaid flowchart LR W["timeline write
(size compensation, pin, end probe)"] -- "readScroll · write · syncScroll" --> L[("seen: top, max, reader")] R["reader scrolls
(any device, any shortcut)"] -. moves the offset .-> S C["range shrinks
(browser clamps)"] -. moves the offset .-> S L --> S["scroll event
readScroll"] S -- "reader = movement − own writes − clamp" --> M{"follow machine"} M -- "up, more than 4 px in all" --> D["detached"] M -- "anything else" --> F["following"] ``` ```ts // virtualizer.tsx function readScroll(root: HTMLDivElement) { const max = root.scrollHeight - root.clientHeight const top = Math.min(Math.max(0, root.scrollTop), max) // A scroll range that shrinks takes a view at its end up with it: the browser's clamp, not the reader. const clamped = top < seen.top && max < seen.max && max - top <= ZOOM_SLACK if (!clamped) seen.reader += top - seen.top seen.top = top seen.max = max } // machine.ts, following const away = Math.max(0, (state.away ?? 0) - event.reader) if (away > ZOOM_SLACK) return detached(state.gesture, false) ``` ### Before and after Real session `ses_e74e90e75ffdAlEBM244YOG6ho`, idle, headless Chromium, 3 runs per cell (`key-thumb.ts`, `realkeys.ts`, `intent.ts`). Each row leaves the latest message one way, then grows the draft by 7 to 12 lines without sending. The numbers are how far the view moved back toward the latest message on screen. | Leave the end with | Old, `dev` | Old, this PR | New, `dev` | New, this PR | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Ctrl+Home: pulled back during the scroll | 1,182 to 1,851 px | 0 | 1,358 to 1,876 px | 0 | | Ctrl+Home: pulled back by the draft | 145 to 835 px | 0 | 136 to 694 px | 0 | | Click a tool header, PageUp | 673 px | 0 | 673 px | 0 | | PageUp on "Copy response" | 526 to 532 px, then 130 to 135 px | 0 | up to 491 px, then 162 to 673 px | 0 | | Scrollbar thumb, 65 px up | 421 px | 0 | 424 px | 0 | | Middle-click, release, autoscroll up | 266 to 267 px | 0 | 266 to 268 px | 0 | | Wheel over the session title | 270 px | 0 | 270 px | 0 | | Wheel over the scrollbar thumb | 270 px | 0 | does not scroll | does not scroll | | Wheel in the timeline, held middle button, Home (controls) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | - **Wheel over the session title:** settled as the same cause through a different door. The wheel event goes to the header, a sibling of the viewport, so the timeline's wheel listener never runs, and the browser still scrolls the timeline. - **Ctrl+Home** now reaches the top and loads the older page, which waits for a reader who is not following.

prs.title: fix(tui): deduplicate slash autocomplete and preserve local command execution
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #66019

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Fixes two related issues when a slash command is registered both on the server (`ctx.command.transform`) and locally in the TUI (`context.keymap.layer`):

1. **Deduplicate slash autocomplete**: In `autocomplete.tsx`, `commandNames` was instantiated and populated with server command names, but never checked against `keymapCommands` or earlier entries. Now, local TUI keymap commands add their names/aliases to `commandNames`, and server commands are filtered with `if (commandNames.has(serverCommand.name)) continue`. This eliminates duplicate entries in the popup and ensures local TUI commands take precedence.
2. **Preserve non-argument local slash dispatch**: In `component/prompt/index.tsx`, `argumentSlash()` required `command.slash?.arguments === true`. Zero-argument local slash commands (like interactive dialog/modal pickers) returned `undefined`, causing submission to fall through to `isCommand` and route to `client.api.session.command` instead of invoking the local handler. Matching `command.slash` directly allows local zero-argument slash commands to run their local `run()` handler on submit.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Added unit test in `packages/tui/test/cli/tui/keymap-arguments.test.tsx` verifying slash dispatch for zero-argument commands.
- Ran `packages/tui` tests with `bun test test/cli/tui/keymap-arguments.test.tsx` (passed).
- Ran TypeScript checks with `bun run typecheck:tsc` in `packages/tui` (passed with 0 errors).

- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(app): keep the New timeline's rows still when older history loads
prs.body:
## Problem

- In the New timeline, an older page of history lands above rows the reader is looking at, and those rows move down 16, 20 or 32 px.
- Every row drew the gap above itself (`data-timeline-gap` as `padding-top`), chosen from the row before it. The first loaded row had none. When its predecessor loaded, the row grew on top.
- The virtualizer keeps the top edge of the first row in view where it was, so the row's content and everything below it moved.
- It happens at every page boundary: 32 px at a prompt, 16 or 20 px in the middle of a turn. The background pages that complete a turn the newest page cut do the same just after a session opens.
- Also in the New timeline: a group collapsed from its stuck header moves the header 6 px up, away from the pointer.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph before["Before: a row holds the gap above it"]
    direction TB
    b1["Older page lands"] --> b2["First loaded row gets a predecessor"]
    b2 --> b3["Row gains padding-top"]
    b3 --> b4["Virtualizer keeps the row's top edge"]
    b4 --> b5["Rows in view move down 16 to 32 px"]
  end
  subgraph after["After: the row above holds the gap"]
    direction TB
    a1["Older page lands"] --> a2["Its last row, or the turn gap, brings the gap"]
    a2 --> a3["No mounted row changes"]
    a3 --> a4["Rows in view stay"]
  end
```

## Change

- **The row directly above holds the gap**, below its own content. `timelineGaps` keys each gap by that row, and the CSS pads the bottom.
- **A turn's first row gets it from the turn gap row**, which is keyed by the turn and arrives and leaves with it, as in the current timeline. A prompt that is sent, steered or delivered changes no row beside it.
- **A prompt after leading notices has its turn gap before the page above it loads**, so the notice never hands the gap over on screen.
- **The live status row** takes no gap from the row above it (it has its own, `laneGap`) and holds the gap above a queued compaction.
- The layout does not change: the same gaps between the same rows.
- **A group collapsed from its stuck header keeps the header in place.** The header rests 6 px above its group (`margin-block: -6px`). The collapse scrolls first, by how far the header is stuck, and measured that from the group's top: 6 px too little.

```ts
// spacing.ts: before, keyed by the lower row
gaps.set(TimelineRow.key(row), gap(previous, { block, item }, reportsBack(row)))

// after, keyed by the row directly above it: the turn gap for a turn's first row, else the row before
gaps.set(TimelineRow.key(rows[index - 1]!), gap(previous, { block, item }, reportsBack(row)))
```

```css
/* timeline-next.css */
[data-timeline="next"][data-timeline-gap="l"] {
  padding-bottom: var(--timeline-gap-l); /* was padding-top */
}
```

```ts
// context-group.tsx: how far the header is stuck, from where it rests
const stuck =
  trigger.getBoundingClientRect().top -
  root.getBoundingClientRect().top -
  parseFloat(getComputedStyle(trigger).marginTop) // new
```

## Before and after

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![The prompt in view moves 32 px when the older page lands](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0a838f6d-d287-47b9-9c64-cbf0566b4ffd) | ![The prompt in view stays where it was](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e2b4882b-f79f-4f21-a025-001da153cf41) |

Real sessions, production builds, the older page held back until the reader is in place. "Moved" is where rows are on screen, not `scrollTop`.

| New timeline | `origin/dev` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reader 300 px below the top, one landing, 3 runs | +32, +32, +32 px | 0, 0, 0 px |
| Reader 200 px below the top, one landing, 3 runs | +32, +32, +32 px | 0, 0, 0 px |
| Reader at the top, 24 landings in 4 sessions: a mounted row changed height | 24 of 24 | 0 of 24 |
| Reader at the top, 24 landings: rows in view moved | 24 of 24, 16 to 32 px | 0 of 24 |
| Reader 300 px below the top, 24 landings: rows in view moved | 5 of 24, 20 to 32 px | 0 of 24 |
| Keeper: page lands in a turn, then above a prompt | +20 px, +32 px | 0 px, 0 px |
| Group collapsed from its stuck header, 4 collapses | -6, -6, -6, -6 px | 0, 0, 0, 0 px |
| Keeper: collapse from the stuck header | header at 93, then 87 px | 93, then 93 px |

- **Same layout:** the distance between the content of neighbouring rows is equal on both builds for 113 pairs in 2 sessions, and a screenshot at the end of a session is identical pixel for pixel.
- **Same tail:** content sits at the same place on both builds through a steer, its delivery, the reply and a queued compaction.
- The current timeline is not changed here. Its stuck header already stayed in place: 0 px in 6 collapses on both builds.

## Tests

- `e2e/regression/timeline-history.spec.ts`: "keeps the New timeline's rows fixed while older pages land in a turn and above a prompt".
- `timeline-next/spacing.test.ts`: rows keep their gaps when older rows load above them; the turn gap and the live status row hold the gap for what waits below.
- `timeline-next/projection.test.ts`: a prompt after leading notices has its turn gap before older history loads.
- `e2e/regression/patch-sticky-header.spec.ts`: "collapsing a group from its stuck header leaves the header where it was", for the current and the New timeline.

prs.title: feat(core): add Driver.lazy combinator and pull-mode Worker client
prs.body:
Stacks on #66024 (`environment-options`). Extracts the shared per-operation `EnvironmentDriver.lazy` combinator, adds KV-backed `Identity` for Cloudflare Durable Objects (`workerd`), and adds pull-mode (`WorkerClient.dial`) and pipe-mode (`WorkerClient.stdio`) worker clients that reuse the existing `opencode-link-v1` Noise XX and `wire.ts` protocol.

**Before:** `Workspace.connect` and `Environment.unavailable` duplicated manual 8-method file + spawn wrappers, `Identity.node` required `node:fs` (failing on Cloudflare Durable Objects), and `Link.serve` only authenticated reverse-dialed connections against `Machines.Service`.

**After:**

```ts
// 1. Shared per-op lazy driver (collapses Workspace.connect & Environment.unavailable)
EnvironmentDriver.lazy(acquire, { module: "Workspace", spawnDescription })

// 2. Pull-mode Noise XX worker client (pairs with `opencode-worker serve`)
const driver = yield* WorkerClient.dial(id, carrier, { peerKey })

// 3. Pipe-mode 4-byte BE length-prefixed wire.ts client (pairs with `opencode-worker stdio`)
const driver = yield* WorkerClient.stdio(id, { stdin, stdout })

// 4. Diskless DO home key persisted in KV.Service
Identity.node.replace(Identity.kvNode) // wired into ServerWorkerd.replacements
```

- **O(N) bounded stdio framing:** `createStdioFrameDecoder` allocates each payload once with zero quadratic copying, bounded by `Queue.bounded(1)` inbound backpressure and `1..Frames.MAX_MESSAGE` frame checks.
- **Strict security invariants:** `Environment.make` locks `local: options?.local === true` after spreading `driver.options` so remote drivers can never claim host privileges; `Identity.kvLayer` enforces exact `base64url` round-trip verification; `Link.serveDirect` validates `peerKey` length, rejects secret-bearing handshakes, and preserves interruption.

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Base | Stacked on #66024 (`environment-options`) |
| Companion Rust PR | https://github.com/kitlangton/opencode-worker/pull/1 (`opencode-worker serve` + `stdio` + 45s idle WS ping) |
| Verification | `bun typecheck`, `tsc -b`, `probe:workerd`, `bun run lint`, 87 core tests + 4 `workerd` tests pass |
| Feature flag | No new user-visible behavior yet; cross-environment navigation remains behind `machines` |

**Read:** `packages/core/src/environment/driver.ts`, `packages/core/src/machine/identity.ts`, `packages/core/src/machine/link.ts`, and `packages/core/src/machine/worker-client.ts`.

prs.title: fix(core): log skipped plugin discovery
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Refs #58647

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

Plugin discovery silently dropped a configured plugin directory when it had no server/GUI/TUI entrypoint, or when its entrypoint resolved outside the directory (the NixOS/home-manager symlink case). The plugin never loaded and nothing was logged.

This adds two warnings in `ConfigPluginSource.scan`:

- no server, GUI, or TUI entrypoint: log the configured target, but only for explicit plugin entries;
- entrypoint resolves outside the plugin directory: log the configured target, resolved root, and resolved entrypoint.

Behavior is unchanged: GUI-only directories still list for their GUI part, TUI-only directories remain the TUI's own, and the containment rule still skips the directory. The only difference is that the skip is visible. prs.title: fix(app): keep the command list and session header steady while the transcript changes
prs.body:
### Summary Every change to the transcript rebuilt the whole command list, registered every keybind again and rebuilt the review toggle in the session header, which made the header fit itself again with a forced layout. It happened once for each history page that landed while the reader scrolled, and for each prompt and tool update while a reply streamed. ```mermaid flowchart LR T["Transcript changes
(history page, prompt, tool update)"] --> S["Session command list
reads visibleUserMessages(), canUndo(), blocking()"] S --> O["command.options
every command rebuilt"] O --> K["Keymap
all layers registered again"] O --> C["Command catalog
reconciled and encoded for storage"] O --> P["command.keybindParts()
every reader runs again"] P --> I["Review toggle
icon rebuilt"] I --> F["Header MutationObserver
fit(): forced layout"] ``` ### Changes - **The session command list reads the transcript through values that change only when a command does** (`use-session-commands.tsx`). `visibleUserMessages()`, `revert.canUndo()`, `revert.canRedo()` and `background.blocking()` return a new value on every transcript change, so the list now reads four boolean memos instead. - **Keybind labels no longer depend on the option list** (`command.tsx`). `keybind()`, `keybindParts()` and `matches()` read a map from command id to keybind that keeps its value until a keybind changes. A command that becomes enabled or disabled (Move to background, when a shell starts) no longer re-renders the controls that show a keybind. ```ts // use-session-commands.tsx const hasMessages = createMemo(() => actions.session.history.visibleUserMessages().length > 0) const canUndo = createMemo(actions.revert.canUndo) // command.tsx: the first option of an id wins, as `options().find(...)` did const keybinds = createMemo( () => new Map(options().map((option) => [actionId(option.id), option.keybind] as const).reverse()), undefined, { equals: (a, b) => a.size === b.size && [...a].every(([id, keybind]) => b.has(id) && b.get(id) === keybind) }, ) ``` ### Counts 5 s of middle-button autoscroll up through history that has not been visited, in a long real session, production build against the live server. 3 interleaved runs for each build, old timeline / new timeline. Counted with V8 precise coverage and a MutationObserver on the header. | In 5 s of autoscroll | `dev`, old timeline | This PR, old timeline | `dev`, new timeline | This PR, new timeline | | :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | History pages that landed | 10, 12, 12 | 12, 12, 12 | 11, 11, 12 | 12, 12, 12 | | Command list rebuilds | 10, 12, 12 | 0, 0, 0 | 11, 11, 12 | 0, 0, 1 | | Keymap layers registered again | 10, 12, 12 | 0, 0, 0 | 11, 11, 12 | 0, 0, 1 | | Header DOM mutations | 10, 12, 12 | 0, 0, 0 | 11, 11, 12 | 0, 0, 0 | | Header fit passes (each forces a layout) | 20, 24, 24 | 0, 0, 0 | 22, 22, 24 | 0, 0, 0 | - One rebuild also ran 65 commands through the keymap parser, reconciled 65 catalog entries, encoded the catalog for storage and reloaded the composer's slash list. - With 4× CPU throttling, the header fit took 13% of the tasks in which a history page landed (93 of 704 ms in one profile), because it is the first layout read after the page's rows are in the DOM. ### Regression test - `e2e/regression/session-header.spec.ts`, "the header keeps its controls while the transcript changes": the review toggle's icon is the same element after a shell starts running and after older pages load. - It fails on `dev`, and with only the command list change (a running shell enables Move to background, so the list changes and the header must not care). It passes with the keybind lookup change. The command list change has no visible contract of its own; the counts above are its evidence. ### Not in this PR - A keymap layer that is registered again drops a key sequence in progress (`ensureValidPendingSequence` in `@opentui/keymap`). A custom chord can therefore still fail when a command changes between its strokes, for example when a shell starts. This PR removes the transcript as a cause; the keymap effect in `command.tsx` still registers every layer again on any change.

prs.title: fix(app): keep a finished reply where it is when its turn goes back to work
prs.body:
## Problem

- A reader follows the end of a session whose last turn has finished. Background work reports back, or anything else starts a new step in that turn, and the reply in view moves down 28 px (31 px in the New timeline).
- The last reply of a finished turn shows a footer: Copy, model and duration. While its turn works the reply is not final, so the footer was removed and the row lost its height. The scroll range shrank under the reader and the browser pulled the offset back.
- An execution that starts and ends without a step moved the view down and back up.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph before["Before"]
    direction TB
    b1["Finished turn goes back to work"] --> b2["Footer removed from its last reply"]
    b2 --> b3["Row shrinks 28 to 31 px"]
    b3 --> b4["Scroll range shrinks under a reader at the end"]
    b4 --> b5["Everything in view moves down"]
  end
  subgraph after["After"]
    direction TB
    a1["Finished turn goes back to work"] --> a2["Footer keeps its place, hidden"]
    a2 --> a3["Row keeps its height"]
    a3 --> a4["Nothing in view moves"]
  end
```

## Change

- **The footer keeps its place while the turn works again**, hidden, so the row keeps its height. Both timelines.
- **It stays on the reply that had it.** Only the steps the turn finished before the session last went idle count, so text from the running step does not take the footer.
- **A turn in its first run reserves nothing**, as before. When the turn finishes again its last reply takes the footer, as before.

```ts
// Where the session last went idle. The steps before it belong to runs that finished.
const lastIdle = createMemo(() => turns().messages.findLastIndex((message) => message.type === "idle"))

const copyContentID = (messageID: string) => {
  const steps = input.projection.assistantMessagesByParent().get(messageID)

  const message = (
    phase(messageID).hideCopy ? steps?.filter((step) => turns().indexes.get(step.id)! < lastIdle()) : steps
  )?.findLast((message) => message.content.some((content) => content.type === "text" && !!content.text.trim()))
  // ...
}
```

```css
/* message-part.css */
[data-component="text-part"][data-copy-held] > :is([data-slot="text-part-footer"], [data-slot="text-part-copy-wrapper"]) {
  visibility: hidden;
}
```

## Before and after

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![The reply moves 28 px down when its finished turn goes back to work](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9a0c5d2-290a-4df2-a698-3bff8fe14573) | ![The reply stays where it was](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a18806e-db89-4164-980e-314cc74b6943) |

Real session, production builds, reader at the end, a new step injected into the finished turn. "Moved" is where the reply's text is on screen.

| | `origin/dev` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current timeline: a new step starts, 3 runs | +28, +28, +28 px | 0, 0, 0 px |
| New timeline: a new step starts, 3 runs | +31, +31, +31 px | 0, 0, 0 px |
| Current timeline: an execution starts and ends without a step, 3 runs | 28 px down, then back | 0 px |
| New timeline: an execution starts and ends without a step, 3 runs | 31 px down, then back | 0 px |
| Keeper, current and New timeline | +28 px, +31 px | 0 px, 0 px |

- A prompt sent into an idle session was already steady on both builds, and still is.
- A reader near the end or deep in history sees no movement on either build.

## Tests

- `e2e/regression/timeline-stream.spec.ts`: "keeps a finished reply where it is when its turn goes back to work", for the current and the New timeline.

Simplifies `Environment` by replacing `Environment.Facts` (`hostsServer`, `searchable`) with `Environment.Options` (`local`, `path`, `shell`, `home`, `rg`), deleting the leftover `MachinePath` wrapper, decoupling `FileAccess` from `Machines` and `Workspace`, and fixing remote `Ripgrep` invocation.

// packages/core/src/environment/environment.ts
export interface Options {
  readonly local?: boolean                   // true only on the server's own OS process
  readonly path?: PlatformPath
  readonly shell?: string
  readonly home?: Effect.Effect<string, unknown>
  readonly rg?: Effect.Effect<string, unknown> // local uses bundled RipgrepBinary; remotes spawn rg
}

- **Fixed remote `Ripgrep`:** spawns `binary.filepath` only when `environment.local` is true and uses `environment.rg` (`"rg"`) on remote workspaces.

prs.title: fix(core): preserve audio and video prompt attachments
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #54600

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Audio and video prompt attachments were dropped before reaching the model: `attachmentContent` only lowered text, directories, images, and PDFs. This keeps `audio/*` and `video/*` attachments as media parts using the existing conversion. Models that declare those input modalities receive them, while other models keep the existing unsupported-input message instead of losing the attachment silently.

The MIME detection also identifies WebM from the `DocType` inside its EBML header. Matroska shares the EBML signature but names its `DocType` `matroska`, so `.mkv` keeps its previous behavior instead of being sent as WebM. MP4 and QuickTime detection was already present.

This is a focused implementation for current `dev`, following the prompt-attachment approach in #54601. Credit to @mweinbach for that direction; this patch adds the WebM `DocType` check and broader coverage. It relates to openchamber/openchamber#3058 and does not attempt the read-tool scope of #54496.

No read-tool changes, frame extraction, Provider production-code changes, or new dependencies are included. The change is a bug fix, so no feature flag is added.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `packages/core`: `bunx bun@1.4.4 run script/test.ts test/mime.test.ts test/session-runner-message.test.ts test/session-model-request.test.ts test/session-prompt.test.ts` — 103 pass, 0 fail.
- The tests cover MP4, WebM, and QuickTime admission, a real WebM EBML header, Matroska remaining unrecognized, audio retention, unsupported models, and Gemini `inlineData` lowering.
- `packages/ai`: `bunx bun@1.4.4 test --timeout 30000 --only-failures test/provider/gemini.test.ts` — 61 pass, 0 fail.
- `bunx bun@1.4.4 typecheck` in `packages/core` and `packages/ai` — passed.
- `git diff --check` and Prettier checks for the changed files — passed.

No real Gemini request was sent and no full end-to-end test was performed. Validation covers prompt admission, canonical conversion, `unsupportedParts`, and Gemini `compileRequest` lowering.

prs.title: feat(tui): footer agent activity panel (#65680)
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR
Closes #65680

### Type of change
- [x] New feature (non-breaking; adds `session.child.activity` keybind, default ctrl+g)

### What does this PR do?
Adds an expandable footer activity panel in the mini TUI so you can see what each running subagent is doing — its label, active tool, and elapsed time — without leaving the footer.

**How it works:**

- While a subagent is running, the footer status line shows a `ctrl+g  agents` hint.
- Press `ctrl+g` to expand: activity rows appear **above** the status line. The status line stays fully visible (spinner, model, `ctrl+p` menu, and the `ctrl+g hide` hint).
- Each row shows `<label> · <tool>   <N>s` + spinner — one row per subagent currently calling a tool.
- `ctrl+g` always toggles. Expanded is the user's choice: the panel stays open across a subagent's think/tool cycles and only auto-collapses when no subagents are running at all. Between tool calls the rows block simply has nothing to show, so you see the status line with the `hide` hint — never a blank footer.
- The 1 s elapsed-time ticker only runs while the panel is open.

**ctrl+g — no collision:** `session.first` (also ctrl+g default in `keybind.ts`) is never registered in the mini TUI, only in the full TUI. `session.child.activity`'s layer guard (`active().type === "prompt" && route().type === "composer" && activeTabs().length > 0`) means the binding is only active in the mini context with live subagents. No collision in practice.

**Relationship to #65343:** Stacked on #65591. Until that merges, the diff also shows #65591's changes.

prs.title: fix(app): refresh browsed directories and reopened files
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #52941

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Watch the immediate entries of directories when they are listed. Directory changes now invalidate loaded trees, including the workspace root, whose normalized path is empty. This avoids recursively watching the whole workspace.

Directory watches are bounded so they cannot degrade open tabs: they take from their own per-location budget (`MAX_CHILDREN_PER_LOCATION`), never evict file watches, keep a shorter one-hour expiry (`CHILDREN_TTL`) that is reset on every listing, and coalesce (`CHILDREN_COALESCE`) so churn such as a continuously written file re-lists a browsed directory at most once per 250 ms window. The native children watch also ignores content writes, since a directory's entries only change on creation, deletion, and renames. This addresses the review concerns about the shared watch budget and uncoalesced directory events.

Force a fresh read when opening a file: closed tabs stop watching, so their cached content can be outdated.

No public API change or feature flag; this restores expected refresh behavior.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun run check` and `bun run lint:changed`.
- Core suite: 7,960 passed, 28 skipped; app unit suite: 2,869 passed.
- Native filesystem/watch tests: 38 passed after rebasing onto current `dev`.
- Verified the native children watch on Linux: content writes and appends to a file emit no directory events, while creates still do.
- Built Chromium regressions for browsing, reopening, and changes during reads: 9 passed across three repetitions.
- Official TypeScript checks passed in core, app, and gui-plugins. The separate E2E typecheck still reports existing fixture/Vite declaration errors outside the added case.
- Confirmed the new regressions fail without the fixes. Manually verified desktop updates on Ubuntu 24.04; the reporting user also tested and confirmed the fix.

To reproduce: keep the file browser open while creating, renaming, or deleting files. Also close a file tab, edit its file, and reopen it. Neither case should require reloading the window.

prs.title: fix(core): resolve sandbox Location paths with the sandbox's own path rules
prs.body:
## What failed

`check-test / unit (windows)`: `CdTool > exempts host-local project worktrees from external_directory, but not sandbox paths` (packages/core/test/tool-cd.test.ts).

This is not flaky. It has failed on Windows every time the core tests actually ran there since the test was added in #65938 (`6d04312b7`, first failing run 11776). The "passing" Windows runs in between took about 1.7 min instead of about 6 min, which suggests the core tests didn't run. The listed suspect #66000 (web-fetch permission saving) is unrelated.

## Root cause

The second half of the test uses a sandboxed workspace Location (directory `/workspace`, a memory-backed POSIX sandbox) and runs `cd /outside-wt`. For a path in the Location's own environment, `FileAccess.place` resolved it with `resolvePath`, which uses the host's `node:path`. On Windows, `path.resolve("/workspace", "/outside-wt")` gives `C:\outside-wt`. The sandbox's memory driver then looks up `/C:\outside-wt`, finds nothing, and `cd` fails with "Working directory does not exist". On POSIX hosts the two rules agree, so Linux passes. The same bug would hit a real sandboxed workspace Location on a Windows server.

## Fix

In the same-environment branch of `FileAccess.place`, resolve with the environment's own path rules (`environment.path`, POSIX for sandboxes) when it has them, and keep `resolvePath` for the local environment. This matches how the other branches of `FileAccess` already choose path rules (`environment.path ?? path`). One side effect: in a sandbox Location, `~/…` is no longer expanded to the server's home folder. Sandboxes don't expose a home folder, so that expansion was wrong.

## Verification

- `cd packages/core && bun run script/test.ts test/file-access test/tool-cd.test.ts test/tool-read test/tool-shell-target-environment.test.ts test/session test/codemode test/location`: 1091 pass, 0 fail (Linux).
- Full `bun run script/test.ts` in packages/core: 7702 pass. The 15 failures (flock, tool-output, MCP descendants, GitLab OAuth) fail the same way without this change; they look like quirks of the local sandbox, which runs as root.
- `bun run typecheck` could not run locally (this Bun build has no `check` script).
- Windows can't run in this sandbox. The fix was checked by tracing the code: with POSIX resolution the target stays `/outside-wt`, which exists in the memory driver, and `external_directory` is still asserted because the sandbox doesn't host the server. The existing failing test is the regression test.

---

**CI failure:** `check-test / unit (windows) / CdTool > exempts host-local project worktrees from external_directory, but not sandbox paths` failed 3 runs in a row on `dev`.
- Failing run: [run 11873](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/45342352197) at `b5948e5` (first failing: [run 11869](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/45341639519))
- Last green run: [run 11867](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/actions/runs/45340819099) at `f824eb3`
- Culprit: [`6d04312`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/commit/6d04312b71ac33e7c150234d7087da01388ff2ab)

Opened by the CI fix job: it does not merge or push to `dev`.

prs.title: feat(plugin): let plugins attach files to a skill
prs.body:
Follow-up to https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65836. Plugins can now ship extra files with a skill, the same way built-in and Console skills do, so the built-in skill plugin goes back to using `ctx.skill` instead of reaching for the core skill service.

```diff
 interface SkillEditor {
-  add(skill: Skill.Info): void
+  add(skill: Skill.Info, files?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>): void
 }
```

```ts
yield* ctx.skill.transform((editor) =>
  editor.add(skill, { "reference/api.md": "..." }), // read as skill://<id>/reference/api.md
)
```

- **What files do:** the core skill registry already supported them (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60921); the plugin editor just didn't pass them through. The read tool opens them at `skill://<id>/<path>`, and loading the skill lists them.
- **Plugin API:** one new optional parameter on `SkillEditor.add`, in both the Effect and Promise plugin types. Existing plugins are unaffected.
- **`SkillPlugin`** in packages/core registers `opencode` and `report` through `ctx.skill` again, with the API reference files attached when `opencode_api` is on.

Files are plain strings, read when the skill is added. Skills whose files have to be fetched lazily, such as skills served by an MCP server, would need a loader instead (`files` as a function, say). I left that out until there's a caller, and the optional parameter can grow that way without breaking this one.

No flag: it only adds an optional parameter.

## Checks

- packages/core `plugin/skill.test.ts`, `skill.test.ts`, `opencode-api-skill.test.ts`; typecheck in core and plugin
- By hand: a dev server with `opencode_api` on, through the real plugin host, and an agent that loads the skill and reads `skill://opencode/api.md` gets the file

prs.title: fix(plugin): leave serverUrl undefined without an HTTP listener
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Fixes #39561

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`PluginInput.serverUrl` no longer invents `http://localhost:4096` when the process has no HTTP listener. It mirrors `Server.url` and is `undefined` in that case. The `PluginInput` type marks the field optional and documents that `client` is the in-process route when it is absent.

A TUI started without `--port` has no listener, yet every plugin was told the server is at `localhost:4096`. Plugins that make raw HTTP calls to `serverUrl` (wake-ups, status probes, session prompts) then reach whatever else holds port 4096: another opencode instance, a leftover `opencode serve`, or an unrelated service. We hit this in practice: a plugin probed a stranger on 4096 (`/global/health` 200), posted a `prompt_async` there (204), and the wake meant for the local session was silently lost.

The SDK `client` handed to plugins was already correct: with no listener it fetches the in-process app directly. Only `serverUrl` misreported the situation.

Compatibility: `serverUrl: URL` becomes `serverUrl?: URL`. Plugins that read it unconditionally get a type error pointing at the case they were already mishandling; at runtime they see `undefined` instead of a URL that may belong to another process. Plugins that need to talk to this process should use `client`.

### How did you verify your code works?

`packages/opencode/test/plugin/server-url.test.ts` loads a real plugin through `Plugin.Service`:

- with no listener, `serverUrl` is `undefined` and `client.project.current()` still resolves the instance in-process;
- with `Server.listen({ port: 0 })`, `serverUrl` equals the listener URL and the client works over HTTP.

The first test fails on the previous code with `http://localhost:4096/`. `bun test test/plugin` 212 pass; `bun typecheck` clean in `opencode`, `plugin`, `sdk/js`, `tui`.

prs.title: fix(opencode): keep snapshot cleanup from failing and leaking packs
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #59766

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The hourly snapshot `git gc` can fail on every run for a store, and every failed or killed run leaves a `objects/pack/tmp_pack_*` behind that is about as large as the store. On one machine that was 600+ failures and several 650 MB leftovers a day.

Three causes, all reproduced on copies of real stores:

1. **Zero-byte loose object** (crash or full disk): gc fails with `object file ... is empty` / `unable to add cruft objects`. `git add` never rewrites it because the object looks present, so the store never recovers. Fix: when gc reports an empty object, delete zero-byte loose objects, reseed the index and retry once. On the real store this took it from 1.4 GB to 74 MiB.
2. **Alternate whose repo was deleted or moved**: gc fails with `bad tree object`, because the snapshot index still references trees that only existed in the alternate. Fix: drop alternates whose path no longer exists and reseed the index. The index is just a cache of the last staged state.
3. **Short-lived processes**: every process that opens a project runs cleanup a minute after start. A gc on a 650 MB store takes over 20 s, so processes that exit sooner kill git mid-repack. Fix: keep the schedule in the store (`opencode-cleanup.json`), so a store is collected at most once an hour across processes. Failures back off by doubling the interval, capped at a day.

After a failed or interrupted gc, cleanup also deletes the `tmp_*` files that appeared during that run. It never touches older ones, and it skips a store when another gc holds `gc.pid`.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New tests in `test/snapshot/snapshot.test.ts` cover each cause, the interrupt leak, backoff and the schedule. All 5 fail on current `v1` and pass with this change; the full snapshot suite passes (60/60) and `bun typecheck` is clean.
- Ran gc against copies of the failing stores: both failure modes reproduce on `git 2.55.0` and gc succeeds after the repair.

### Screenshots / recordings

prs.title: fix(app): open a shell's call from its notice when the call is on an older page
prs.body:
- **Before:** a click on `Shell finished · bun serve.ts` did nothing when the call that started the shell was older than the loaded messages. A route that names such a shell opened the session at latest. `revealPart` searched only the rows that were loaded.
- **After:** the timeline pages older history until the call loads, then scrolls to it and opens it, once.
- **Bounded:** the search ends where the call would be, so a shell without a call does not load the session.
- **No flag:** a fix.

| `dev`: the click leaves the view at latest | This PR: the call, four pages back, opens under the header |
| --- | --- |
| ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e85e609d-0a52-4786-855e-585a00f38419) | ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d18f726b-5e3c-4fa2-bd85-a2224f795ef4) |

## How it works

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant Row as Notice row / route
  participant V as virtualizer
  participant S as reveal-machine
  participant H as history-machine
  Row->>V: revealPart(sh_…)
  V->>S: reveal.requested (found: false)
  loop until found, or the loaded messages reach back past the shell
    S->>H: seek.requested
    H-->>S: older page landed
    S->>V: revealPart(sh_…) again
  end
  V-->>Row: call opened and held under the header
```

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  direction LR
  idle --> seeking: reveal.requested · not loaded · shell ID
  seeking --> seeking: history ready / history.seek
  seeking --> idle: found
  seeking --> idle: an assistant message older than the shell is loaded
  seeking --> idle: history exhausted or failed
  seeking --> idle: reader scrolls or presses in the timeline
  seeking --> idle: another call is revealed
```

- `reveal-machine.ts` is the pure transition. `interaction.ts` drives it: one effect looks again when an older page lands or paging changes phase, and paging goes through the history machine's existing `seek.requested`, so its failure cooldown and stalled-cursor stop apply.
- Each session gets a fresh seek, as it gets a fresh follow state, so a seek never continues in the session opened next.
- The route and the rows share one path (`revealOrSeekPart`). The route still counts as attempted once per history entry.

## Why the bound is the shell's ID

```ts
// A shell's call runs in the newest assistant message created before the shell, and IDs ascend with creation.
oldestAssistantID.slice("msg_".length) < shellID.slice("sh_".length)
```

A shell that a Code Mode script starts has a notice but no `shell` call. Without a bound, a click on its notice would load the whole session, one page of 20 messages at a time. Four real sessions (18,183 messages, 265 shell notices):

| | Notices | Where the search ends |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| The call exists | 225 | At the call, which is in the newest assistant message older than the shell: 225 of 225. Median 9 messages before the notice, 99th percentile 672, farthest 1,241 |
| No call (Code Mode shell) | 40 | Where the call would be. Median 10 messages before the notice, farthest 327 |

- Assistant messages were in ID order in all four transcripts (11,676 messages, 0 out of order).
- A call named by its own ID (`toolu_…`) is still looked for among the loaded messages only. Nothing says how far back it is, and no code path asks for one.

## Real sessions, lab build, 3 runs each

| Scenario | `dev` old / new timeline | This PR old / new timeline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Route to a shell whose call is 4 pages back (9,756 messages) | 0 pages, no call on screen, view at latest: 3 of 3 / 3 of 3 | 4 pages in 192 to 241 ms / 176 to 222 ms. Call 84 px / 92 px below the viewport top, open: 3 of 3 / 3 of 3 |
| Route to a shell whose call is in the first page (control) | Call at 84 px / 92 px, open | The same |
| Click the notice of a shell a Code Mode script started (no call, 723 messages) | 0 pages | 3 pages in 58 to 90 ms, then none. The view moved 0 px |

- e2e keeper: "a shell notice opens its call from an older page, paging back only as far as the call" in `timeline-history.spec.ts`. The call is five pages back; the fixture has ten more pages before it that stay unloaded.

## Not changed

- No link in the app produces a route reveal today: the activity pill opens a shell's output in its own panel since #59496. The route path is covered by the lab runs above, not by an e2e case.
- A shell notice whose shell came from Code Mode stays a dead click. It now costs the pages back to the shell's start.

prs.title: feat(core): generate the opencode skill's API reference from openapi.json
prs.body:
With `opencode_api` on, the built-in `opencode` skill now ships a reference for the HTTP API, generated from `packages/protocol/openapi.json`, so an agent can find the right `opencode:///api/...` call without guessing. Follow-up to https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/65725.

```text
skill://opencode/api.md            index: a few lines on opencode://, then every endpoint by group
skill://opencode/api/session.md    one file per first path segment (experimental/ skipped)
skill://opencode/api/model.md ...
```

`api.md` sorts first, so it's always among the skill's listed files. With the flag off, the skill is unchanged.

An entry looks like this:

```md
## POST /api/session/{sessionID}/prompt

Durably admit one session input and schedule agent-loop execution unless resume is false.

Body:
- `id?: string`
- `text: string`
- `delivery?: "steer" | "queue"`
...

Returns: `{ data: Session.Inbox.User }`
```

## How it's generated

`packages/core/script/generate-api-skill.ts` (`bun run generate:api-skill` in packages/core) reads openapi.json and writes the markdown plus a small `api.ts` that imports it as text. Everything comes from the spec except:

- **An allowlist** of the endpoints the reference documents, in `SHOWN`: the session hand-off flow (create, prompt, wait, interrupt, messages, inbox, answering forms, reading permission requests), automations, location, projects, worktrees, VCS, agents, commands, skills, models, providers and generation. Everything else, including any new route, stays out until someone adds it. Left out on purpose: voice, jobs, media, machines, server setup (config, credentials, integrations, MCP, plugins), terminals, files and shells (Code Mode has tools), events, pairing, debug, and session extras like import/export, revert and stats. This only keeps them out of the docs; it doesn't block them.
- **Trimming for tokens:** error responses are dropped (the index says once that failures return `{ _tag, message }`), `T | null` on optional fields renders as `field?: T`, the "Infinity"/"NaN" number encodings are dropped, the repeated "Experimental: ..." sentence becomes an `(experimental)` tag, path params are listed only when they have a description, and named types are written out once per file in a Types section (big ones list just their fields), with the type's own description. A description on a type that's inlined as a primitive, like steer vs queue on `Session.Inbox.Delivery`, shows on each field that uses it instead.
- **The index header,** three factual lines about `current`, the default directory and errors. The skill's own text is untouched apart from its API section (below).

Protocol's `bun run generate` now also runs the generator, so changing a route is still one command. `test/opencode-api-skill.test.ts` regenerates and fails when the committed files are stale, in case someone writes openapi.json another way.

Size: 68 endpoints in 17 files, about 11k tokens total (o200k tokenizer). The index is about 1.2k and `session.md` about 4.5k, the largest. An agent reads the index and then one file.

## The skill's API section

With `opencode_api` on, the skill's API section (which today says to use `opencode api get /api/...` in the shell) is swapped for `packages/core/src/plugin/skill/opencode-api.md`: use `tools.opencode.*` first, otherwise `fetch("opencode:///api/...")`, and read `skill://opencode/api.md` for the endpoints. It's a short first draft meant to be reworded. The troubleshooting line that checks the service with `opencode api get /api/info` stays, since that's about the CLI. With the flag off, the skill is unchanged.

## Notes

- The plugin API's skill editor can't attach files, so `SkillPlugin` now registers its skills through `Skill.Service` directly, the same way the OpenCode provider plugin registers Console skills.
- Most descriptions are still written for whoever implemented the endpoint, and almost no parameters or body fields have descriptions. Separate PRs add those in the protocol source; the reference picks them up on regenerate.
- Generated files are in `.prettierignore` so the generator's output is the source of truth.

No new flag: it's behind `opencode_api` (local and dev builds only).

## Checks

- `bun run check`
- packages/core: `opencode-api-skill.test.ts`, `plugin/skill.test.ts`, `tool-skill.test.ts`, `skill.test.ts`

- **Archived is a list, not a button + dialog.** Archived sessions are a collapsible **Archived** section at the end of the list (collapsed by default, remembered). The Working shelf stays attached to the bottom. A current archived session still shows at the top while the section is collapsed.

prs.title: fix(core): save the site, not every URL, when always allowing a web fetch
prs.body:
Fixes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/64429 for the common case: choosing **Allow always** on a webfetch prompt saved `webfetch: * → allow`, so one click allowed every URL on every site for the project. It now saves the URL's site.

```diff
 approve https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions → Allow always
- saves  *                                         every URL, every site
+ saves  https://opencode.ai, https://opencode.ai/*  that site only
```

This applies everywhere a webfetch approval is saved: the webfetch tool, Code Mode `fetch`, and the URLs the image and video tools download or hand to a provider. They all go through a new `Permission.site(url)`.

- **Why the site and not the path** (what the issue asks for): other coding tools scope saved web approvals by domain, and a path rule for `/docs/permissions` would prompt again for `/docs/agents`, which defeats "always". Path- or host-wide choices in the prompt itself are https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/64430, which this doesn't touch.
- **Two patterns, not one.** Rules match the URL as written, and `https://opencode.ai/*` doesn't match a bare `https://opencode.ai`. Saving both avoids a second prompt for the same site, which is the trailing-slash question the issue raises.
- **As written.** The site is taken from the URL as the agent wrote it, not normalized, for the same reason: `https://OpenCode.ai/x` saves `https://OpenCode.ai/*`, which matches the next fetch written the same way.
- **Redirects** are unchanged: each hop is still only checked for deny rules, so a saved site doesn't widen what a redirect can reach.

- **Unusual URLs save only themselves.** A URL with credentials in its site (`https://opencode.ai@evil.com/x` goes to evil.com) or that isn't http(s) saves just that exact URL, never `*`, so the saved rule can't name a misleading site. The site ends where URL parsers end it, including at `\`, so `https://evil.com\@opencode.ai/` saves `https://evil.com/*`. Rules treat `*` and `?` as wildcards, so a site containing one (`https://*/x` parses, and would otherwise save a pattern for every site) gets no pattern, and neither does an unusual URL containing one: those prompts offer no "Allow always". The regex is linear (no backtracking), and 200k characters take about 1 ms.

Existing saved `webfetch: *` rules are left alone.

The permissions docs now mention that web fetches propose the URL's site.

No flag: this narrows what a click saves and changes no other behavior.

## Checks

- packages/core: `tool-webfetch.test.ts`, `tool-execute.test.ts`, `tool-image-generate.test.ts`, `tool-video-generate.test.ts`, `permission.test.ts`, `codemode.test.ts`, `generate.test.ts`, `session-generate.test.ts` (the webfetch and Code Mode tests now expect the site patterns)
- `bun run check`

prs.title: fix(desktop): show the update pill while an update downloads
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #62238

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The updater's titlebar pill only appears once an update is `ready`, so while it downloads there is no sign anywhere in the window that an update was found.

A check that finds a release starts downloading it at once (`downloading`), so that gap is the whole download: minutes to tens of minutes on a slow connection, and longer when the feed has no `.blockmap` and the app falls back to the full ~300 MB package, which is every build I tested.

This shows the pill from the moment the download starts: busy, with the existing `action.downloading` title, and with no install to run until the update is on disk. Finding, downloading and installing an update are unchanged: main still checks on launch, downloads in the background, and installs on quit or on click. No new strings, so no locale files change, and no flag: this only surfaces a state that already exists.

The state-to-pill mapping moves into `updaterPill()` next to `updaterAction()`, because the renderer factory needs a plugin context and the mapping itself is what regressed.

### How did you verify your code works?

`bun test src/updater/action.test.ts` from `packages/gui-plugins` (6 cases): hidden for no state, `idle`, `checking`, `up-to-date` and `error`; busy and not installable for `downloading`; installable for `ready` and `download-required`; busy for `installing`.

I did not build a packaged app on this machine and did not run `bun install`, so `bun typecheck` did not run here. On 2.3.2 and 2.4.1 I confirmed the state the pill now covers from `main.log`: `Found version 2.4.1` → `checking` → `downloading`, with no transition until `ready`.

### Screenshots / recordings

_None: the pill only shows in a packaged build. It is the pill that already appears for `ready`, with `busy` set._

prs.title: fix(app): line up settings with home and keep home steady at medium widths
prs.body:
## Summary

Settings and Home now share one layout, so switching between them no longer moves the sidebar or content sideways. Home also stops jumping at its medium breakpoint.

```diff
 Settings (panel ≥ 800px)
-  centred 1048px · sidebar 328px (items 240px) · content ≤ 720px
+  centred 1056px + 24px gutters · sidebar 256px (items 244px) · content 720px
 Home (≥ 1024px)
-  centred 1080px · projects column 280px
+  centred 1056px · projects column 256px
 Home (768–1023px)
-  projects list stacked above sessions · search bar 24px lower than at ≥ 1024px
+  project picker inside the search field · search bar at the same height as ≥ 1024px
```

- Settings sidebar items match Home's rows: 6px corners, 8px icon gap, `bg-layer-01` hover with darker text. Same for "Back to app".
- Settings search icon moves 2px left to line up with the tab icons; its text doesn't move.
- Picking or adding a project from the in-field picker clears the search, like the projects column does. Without this, the typed query stayed in the box while the list showed the project unfiltered. With the Consolidated experiment, search filters in place, so the query carries over.
- Below 768px (phones) Home is unchanged.

## Evidence

Measured in the story lab at 1440 / 1200 / 1050px (x, width):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Home project row / Settings tab | 204, 268 / 220, 240 | 216, 244 / 216, 244 |
| Home search field / Settings card | 516, 720 / 528, 712 | 504, 720 / 504, 720 |

New e2e regressions, each failing with its fix reverted:

```text
settings.spec.ts  "settings lines its sidebar and content up with Home's columns"
  before: tab width ≠ Home row width      after: pass
home.spec.ts      "picking a project from the picker in session search clears the search"
  before: Received "Finished", expected ""   after: pass
```

Ran `home`, `settings`, `settings-search`, `shell-panel-spacing` and `mobile-session` specs in built mode: 126 passed. The 9 failures all press Ctrl shortcuts, which fail on local macOS (Windows UA) and are untouched by this change. Checked by hand in the desktop app.

No feature flag: these are layout fixes. The in-field picker at 768–1023px is the one new behaviour.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

CSS and one optional callback; reverting restores the old layout.

**Blast Radius:** layout

Settings and Home at desktop widths, and Home at 768–1023px. Settings shown beside an open side-tabs sidebar can still pick a different layout than Home, since Home follows the window width and Settings its own panel width.
