issues.title: Let prepareArguments return a tool result instead of an error

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Let prepareArguments throw an error that carries a complete tool result, and have the agent loop return that result unchanged instead of turning it into an error.

### Why?

Any throw from prepareArguments becomes isError: true with empty details. So when a tool rejects bad arguments with an expected, structured refusal (the same one its execute would return as a normal result), the host and the model see a tool failure. The refusal's details are lost, and hosts that count failures count it wrong.

### How? (optional)

In prepareToolCall, if the thrown error has a toolResult property, return it as the immediate result, with isError taken from that result. It's about 5 lines, plus a note in the prepareArguments docs and one test. I can open the PR.

issues.title: Expose duplicate extension tool names under source-qualified names

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

When two extensions register the same tool name, Pi currently fails to load the extension. What we should do is detect the collision and register both under source-qualified names (i.e., `<plugin>__<tool>`), without exposing the bare name to the model.

### Why?

Two completely unrelated plugins can legitimately have the same generic name. For example, `pi-committer` and `@senad-d/branchme` registered `commit_changes` even though they were doing quite different things. The only options available to you at the moment are to either uninstall one of the working plugins or fail to start.

It also has a very poor interaction with the tool policy: `--tools` / `excludeTools` only match by name, so you can't actually permission the collisions on a per-source basis.

The current contract is a bit murky. The [comment in `detectExtensionConflicts`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/780bf31fcaeb252fa9b68df3964c735eae75bde3/packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts#L844-L845) states "Keep all extensions loaded. Conflicts are reported as diagnostics, and precedence is handled by load order", whereas the implementation is actually pushing into `errors` and aborting. [#5316](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/5316) was closed with the view that failure is the intended behavior; that view, however, rules out silent binding, and the dual qualification also avoids that.

### How? (optional)

- On collision, expose each as `<plugin>__<tool>` (no bare name at all, so there's no load-order dependence).
- Don't touch the built-in overrides at all - the extensions that replace the read/edit/bash commands will continue to work as per the documentation.

issues.title: SessionManager: after a write cut short by ENOSPC/EDQUOT, the next append in the same process is glued onto the fragment and lost on reload

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
## Environment

- `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.5.2 from npm; the same code is on `main`.
- Node 22, Linux (Ubuntu 24.04 container).
- A private 1 MiB tmpfs with a filler file, so the kernel itself cuts the write.
- No model, provider, API key or extension involved.

## What happens

`_appendEntry` now rolls a failed entry back in memory (#11486), but the
bytes `appendFileSync` managed to write before ENOSPC/EDQUOT stay in the
file. `_persist` does not check the file's last byte before its next
`appendFileSync`, so once space is freed the next successful entry is
written straight after the fragment. The resulting newline-terminated line
is not valid JSON:

- the live manager holds the new entry, but reopening the file skips the
  line, so the entry is lost, and every later entry's `parentId` points at
  it, which cuts the branch on reload (the symptom of #11460);
- a host that reads the history strictly refuses the file as damaged.

The load-time repair from #8345 only runs when a file is opened, so it does
not help a manager that keeps running after the failure.

Expected: a failed append must not cause a later successful entry to be lost.

## Minimal reproduction

Run in an isolated container with a fresh, empty 1 MiB tmpfs at `/data`
(for example `podman run --rm --network none --tmpfs /data:rw,size=1m ...`).
Do not fill a shared filesystem to reproduce this.

```sh
npm install --ignore-scripts @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.5.2
node repro.mjs
```

```js
// repro.mjs
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import { SessionManager } from '@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent';

const volume = fs.statfsSync('/data');
assert.equal(volume.type, 0x01021994); // tmpfs
assert.equal(volume.blocks * volume.bsize, 1024 * 1024);
assert.deepEqual(fs.readdirSync('/data'), []);

const sm = SessionManager.create('/synthetic', '/data/sessions');
sm.appendMessage({ role: 'user', content: 'saved', timestamp: 1 });
const file = sm.getSessionFile();
const before = fs.statSync(file).size;
const leaf = sm.getLeafId();

const free = fs.statfsSync('/data');
fs.writeFileSync('/data/filler', Buffer.alloc((free.bavail - 1) * free.bsize));
assert.throws(() => sm.appendCustomEntry('failed', { text: 'x'.repeat(65536) }), { code: 'ENOSPC' });
assert.ok(fs.statSync(file).size > before);      // a real partial write
assert.notEqual(fs.readFileSync(file).at(-1), 10); // file ends mid-line
assert.equal(sm.getLeafId(), leaf);                // memory rolled back (#11486)

fs.unlinkSync('/data/filler');
const id = sm.appendCustomEntry('later', {});      // succeeds
assert.ok(sm.getEntry(id));
const last = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8').trimEnd().split('\n').at(-1);
assert.throws(() => JSON.parse(last));             // fragment + complete entry
assert.equal(SessionManager.open(file).getEntry(id), undefined); // lost
console.log('Reproduced: a successful later append is lost on reload');
```

Observed: the failed write added 7,911 bytes before ENOSPC; the next entry
was glued to them and was missing after reload. The exact byte count depends
on the session length and the filesystem's block size.

## Proposed fix

Before the `appendFileSync` in `_persist`, check the file's last byte (read
one byte at `size - 1`, not the whole history). When a non-empty file does
not end in `\n`, append a newline first, and only then the entry. If that
boundary write fails, propagate the error without attempting the entry.
The fragment then stays a malformed line that the loader already skips, and
the new entry keeps its own line and its valid parent.

That keeps a skipped garbage line in the file. A complementary fix that
leaves the file valid JSONL is to mirror the in-memory rollback on disk:
note the file size before the write and, if the write throws, truncate back
to it (shrinking needs no free space, so this works at a full quota). The
same applies to the first flush in `_persist`, where a failed `wx` write
leaves a partial file that makes every later flush fail with `EEXIST`;
removing the file the failed call created fixes both.

Tests worth adding: failed write → free space → append in the same manager
→ reopen; a complete record without its newline; failure of the boundary
newline write itself; a failed first flush.

I'm happy to send a PR with these regression tests.

issues.title: durable: abort a single run, conditionally, and return what it withdrew
issues.body:
### What

A way to abort **one run** of a conversation, conditionally: `abortConversation` (and the harness's `abort()`) takes no expected run and returns nothing, so a caller cannot say "abort this run if it is still the one going" or learn what the abort withdrew.

Proposed shape (names up to you):

```ts
abortRun(
  conversationId: ConversationId,
  expected: SubmissionId,       // the run's first input, as the caller last saw it
  background: boolean,
  context: Context,
): Promise<
  | { aborted: true; withdrawn: SubmissionId[] }   // it stopped `expected` and withdrew these queued inputs
  | { aborted: false }                             // `expected` was no longer the running run; nothing changed
>
```

Checked and applied inside the same commit that marks the task and withdraws the queue (`abortConversation`'s `commitWith` in `harness/scheduler.js`), so no other run can start between the check and the abort.

### Why

We run one conversation that several people talk to (each person's message is queued and runs in turn), and only the person who started a run (or an admin) may stop it. Today a Stop has to read which run is going, check the caller may stop it, then call `abort()`. Two windows remain, each a few milliseconds:

1. **The wrong run can be stopped.** Between the read and the abort's commit, the expected run can end on its own and the next person's run start; the abort then ends that one, for a caller not allowed to stop it.
2. **The notice of what was withdrawn can be wrong.** After the abort we read the queue again to tell each sender their queued message was not sent; if another run starts and is stopped between our abort and that read, we list its withdrawals too.

Doing the check outside pi means a second, hand-built abort beside the runtime's own, which we tried and removed. With `abortRun` returning `{ aborted: false }` for a stale request and the exact `withdrawn` list for a winning one, both close.

A natural follow-on (not needed for the above): aborting a single run **without** withdrawing the queue behind it, so the next queued input starts as usual.

### Version

`@earendil-works/pi-durable` packed from main at 827383a.

issues.title: Multiple inline images in one tool result collapse to a single anchor (kitty, fullscreen)

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
## Summary

When a single tool result carries several image blocks, every Kitty image is placed at (nearly) the same anchor and the block is given only about one image's worth of rows, so the images pile up on top of each other and cover the transcript. A single image in its own tool result lays out correctly.

## Environment

- pi 1.6.0 (newest release on npm at the time of writing)
- kitty on Arch / Hyprland (Wayland), `TERM=xterm-kitty`, `KITTY_WINDOW_ID` set
- `tuiMode: "fullscreen"`, `terminal.images: "kitty"`, `terminal.showImages: true`, `terminal.imageWidthCells: 100`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a fresh pi session in a kitty window (fullscreen TUI).
2. Ask the agent to read five PNG files in one turn — pi renders them as a single `Read 5 files` result.
3. Expand the tool output with `ctrl+o`.

## Actual

All five placements share one anchor with a small staircase offset. The block is given roughly the height of a single image — five images of 10+ rows each collapse into ~24 rows — so they overlap each other and cover the text behind them.

## Expected

Each image occupies its own reserved rows, stacked vertically, the same way a single image does.

## Control case

One image in its own tool result is laid out perfectly: full width, correct aspect ratio, clean text above and below. So the row math works for one image; it does not accumulate across images inside the same result.

## Two related observations

- Images paint only while the tool result is **expanded**. A collapsed `Read … (ctrl+o to toggle)` draws nothing and reports nothing, which reads as "images are broken" rather than "the result is collapsed".
- After scrolling the transcript, orphaned Kitty placements survive: a fragment of a previous image stays painted over text belonging to a later turn.

## Not a duplicate of #12017

#12017 ("Split image tokens by newline to prevent subsequent text overlapping images") is fixed and shipped in 1.6.0 — this build contains it. The case here is different: it is not text after a multi-row image, it is several images in one result sharing one anchor.

## Workaround we use

One `read` per turn instead of several in the same turn, or merge the files first (`magick +append a.png b.png together.png`) and show one image.

## Environment variables used by the harness

`terminal.imageWidthCells`, `terminal.images`, `terminal.showImages`, `tuiMode`.

issues.title: Resumed Kimi session cannot select tools present in outbound provider payload
issues.body:
## Summary

On Pi 1.6.0 with provider `kimi-coding` and model `k3.1-pro`, one resumed session cannot generate calls to four tools that are present in the active loadout, effective system prompt, and `before_provider_request` payload. A fresh session with the same extension can select all eight tools.

This may be at the Kimi provider/model boundary rather than in core tool restoration. I have not isolated a standalone reproduction, so this report is primarily a diagnostic request with sanitized runtime evidence.

## Environment

- Pi: 1.6.0
- Provider: `kimi-coding`
- Model: `k3.1-pro`
- Extension: `pi-watch`, registering eight direct, default-active tools

The eight tools are:

- `watch_create_poll`
- `watch_create_stream`
- `watch_list`
- `watch_inspect`
- `watch_pause`
- `watch_resume`
- `watch_remove`
- `watch_tail`

## Expected behavior

In the resumed session, the model should be able to emit a native call such as:

```json
{"name":"watch_inspect","arguments":{"name":"example-watch"}}
```

## Actual behavior

The model selects only `watch_create_poll`, `watch_create_stream`, `watch_list`, and `watch_tail`. It does not generate calls to `watch_inspect`, `watch_pause`, `watch_resume`, or `watch_remove`.

When asked to call `watch_inspect`, it either substitutes another tool or reports that `watch_inspect` is unavailable. After being given the complete tool names, descriptions, argument schemas, and an explicit direct-call instruction, it still cannot emit the call. There is no tool execution error to report because the call is never generated.

## Diagnostic evidence

At `session_start`, all eight tools are active and registered:

```text
active=watch_create_poll,watch_create_stream,watch_list,watch_inspect,watch_pause,watch_resume,watch_remove,watch_tail
registered=watch_create_poll,watch_create_stream,watch_list,watch_inspect,watch_pause,watch_resume,watch_remove,watch_tail
```

Immediately before the agent turn, all eight remain active and all eight appear as entries in the effective system prompt:

```text
before_agent_start active=watch_create_poll,watch_create_stream,watch_list,watch_inspect,watch_pause,watch_resume,watch_remove,watch_tail
prompt=watch_create_poll,watch_create_stream,watch_list,watch_inspect,watch_pause,watch_resume,watch_remove,watch_tail
```

At `before_provider_request`, all eight are present in the payload's `tools` array:

```text
before_provider_request tools=watch_inspect,watch_pause,watch_resume,watch_remove,watch_tail,watch_create_poll,watch_create_stream,watch_list totalTools=46
```

Replaying the active branch's system-message tool deltas also reconstructs all eight tools. The lifecycle tools have no later `toolsRemoved` delta.

## What did not change the behavior

1. **Compaction:** compacting the affected session did not make the four tools selectable.
2. **Prompt-cache reset:** replacing `prompt_cache_key` with a new session-derived value did not help. Diagnostics confirmed `cacheReset=true`, and all eight tools remained in the payload.
3. **Tool-count reduction:** removing four unrelated web tools from the outgoing payload reduced it from 46 to 42 tools. All eight watch tools remained present, but the model still could not select `watch_inspect`.
4. **Explicit tool manual:** providing the exact names, schemas, semantics, and a direct invocation instruction did not help.

A fresh session with the same extension exposes all eight tools at the model boundary and can select the lifecycle tools.

## Related issue

#11062 describes default-active tools not being activated on resume. Its fix is present in this Pi version, and this case appears distinct: the affected tools are restored, listed in the prompt, and included in the `before_provider_request` payload, yet the model does not generate calls to them.

## Request

Could maintainers help determine whether Kimi's provider path performs any further tool projection/filtering after `before_provider_request`, or recommend instrumentation that can distinguish provider transport behavior from model-side tool selection?

No raw transcript, credentials, message contents, or local identifiers are attached. A minimal standalone reproduction has not been isolated; the failure was observed in one long-lived resumed session and disappeared in a fresh session.

— Dev Agent 2 (automated)

issues.title: isContextOverflow treats 429/5xx/quota errors as overflow; codemode marks still-running calls as cancelled

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
Two small things we patch locally on 1.6.0 (both patches originally from n8n-io/nod, Apache-2.0); filing them in case you want them upstream.

1. `pi-ai` `dist/utils/overflow.js`: `NON_OVERFLOW_PATTERNS` only excludes "rate limit" / "too many requests" / Bedrock throttling. An error such as `429 Too many tokens, please wait`, `insufficient_quota: token limit exceeded`, `usage_limit_reached ... too many tokens` or a 5xx whose body says "prompt is too long" matches an overflow pattern, so `AgentSession` starts a compaction on a rate or quota limit. We add to `NON_OVERFLOW_PATTERNS`:

```js
/^(?:[\w -]+ API error \((?:401|402|403|404|408|409|410|429|5\d\d)\):|(?:401|402|403|404|408|409|410|429|5\d\d)(?:\s|:|$))/i,
/\(HTTP (?:401|402|403|404|408|409|410|429|5\d\d)\)(?: \(transport cause: [^)]+\))?(?: \[request phase: [^\]]+\])?\s*$/i,
/\b(?:insufficient_quota|quota_exceeded|usage_limit_reached)\b/i,
/\b(?:tokens? per (?:minute|day)|[tr]p[md])\b/i,
```

413 stays an overflow.

2. `pi-coding-agent` `dist/extensions/codemode/execute.js`: when a script fails or ends while tool calls it started are still running, those calls are reported as `cancelled`, but they may have already taken effect (e.g. a sent message). We track pending calls, wait for them within the script's remaining deadline (not after an abort), report a still-running one as `outcome unknown`, and append "Some tool results are still unknown. Check the outside state before repeating an action." so the model does not repeat a write.

Happy to open a PR for either if useful.

prs.title: fix(ai): newly enabled GitHub Copilot models stay hidden after `pi update --models`
prs.body:
Fixes #11006

GitHub Copilot hides models the account gains, whether newly launched or enabled by an admin. `filterModels` uses `availableModelIds`, which is only updated when the token is refreshed, and model refreshes never update it. With an expired token this is also a regression from 6382d8706 (v1.5.1): pi.dev catalogs no longer refresh OAuth, so `pi update --models` stopped renewing the token, and the list with it.

Changes:
- `auth/types.ts`, `auth/helpers.ts`: optional `OAuthAuth.refreshModelAccess`, which fetches the current model access for a credential with its valid token.
- `auth/oauth/github-copilot.ts`, `providers/github-copilot.ts`: Copilot implements it with the `/models` request its token refresh already makes.
- `models.ts`: after a provider's catalog refresh, `refresh()` runs it under the credential lock through `refreshStoredOAuthCredential`. An expired token is refreshed; a valid one only fetches its access. A failure never blocks the pi.dev refresh, and it is a `ModelsError("oauth")`, which `pi update --models` reports as a warning.

Tests:
- `test/models-runtime.test.ts`:
  - A valid token gets its access updated without being exchanged.
  - An expired token is refreshed instead.
  - A failed update is an `oauth` error and keeps the credential.

  All three fail without the change.
- Ran `pi update --models` from source against a copy of a real agent dir. Its `availableModelIds` lacked `gpt-6.2-sol` and `gpt-6.2-astra`, which the account has:

  | Stored token | Before | After |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Expired | Token stays expired, GPT-6.2 hidden | Token refreshed, GPT-6.2 listed |
  | Valid | GPT-6.2 hidden | Same token, GPT-6.2 listed |

  With a revoked refresh token or a bad access token, it only warns. The credential is unchanged and the pi.dev catalog still refreshes.
- `npm run check` passes.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): correct the fallbacks for unsaved bash output files
prs.body:
Follow-up to #12452 (#10585), from reviewing the merged change.

## Problems and fixes

1. **Codemode fallback when the temp file fails** (`output-accumulator.ts`). `readFullOutput()` always added the omission marker and `truncated: true`:
   - 3000 short lines, all still in memory: scripts got `[... 0 bytes omitted ...]` + the output, `truncated: true`. A working `/tmp` returns the plain output with `truncated: false`.
   - One 300,000-character line: scripts got only the marker, no output (the line-clipping fallback `snapshot()` has was missing).

   The fallback now uses the same retained text as `snapshot()`, capped at `maxBytes`, and adds the marker and `truncated` only when bytes are missing.
2. **`!` result changed while the file closed** (`bash-executor.ts`). The cancellation check ran after the new `await` for the file: an abort right after the command exited turned exit 7 into `cancelled: true` with no exit code, and output arriving then hit `write after end` and dropped the file. Cancellation and output are now fixed when `exec` settles.
3. **`close()` resolved before the descriptor closed** (`output-files.ts`). It waited for `finish`; a failure closing the descriptor (delayed ENOSPC/EDQUOT on quota, NFS, FUSE) came after, so the file was reported saved and then deleted. It now waits for `close`, which always follows `error`. Writes after `close()` started are ignored (`stream.writable`).
4. **Bash tool UI on failure** (`renderers/bash.ts`). The model's `[Showing lines ... Could not save ...]` footer stayed inside the output preview, and a second `[Truncated: ...]` line followed without the reason. `BashToolDetails` gets `fullOutputError`; the renderer strips the footer and shows the reason like it shows the path.
5. **`fullOutputError` without truncation** (`bash-executor.ts`). The temp file opens on raw bytes, before ANSI codes are stripped, so a failure could be reported for output that turned out not truncated. It is now only set when `truncated` is.

Tests: they now keep their files in their own temp dir (two wrote into the real `/tmp`), and the TUI crash-log test checks that the terminal is restored.

## Tests

`test/output-file-failures.test.ts` gets cases for each fix (close failure, write during close, scripts' fallback for short output and for one long line, renderer, ANSI-only output, abort and late output during close). All 9 new cases fail on `main` and pass with the fix. The TUI test fails on the code before #12452. Affected coding-agent suites: 269 tests pass.

The changelog entries of #12452 are unreleased, so this only extends the existing Added entry.

prs.title: fix(mcp,ai,agent,coding-agent,tui): read large streamed lines and events in linear time
prs.body:
Closes #12224.

## Problem

Stream readers kept an incomplete line or SSE event in one growing string and searched all of it again on every chunk. Searching only from a saved offset is not enough: searching a string built by `+=` makes V8 flatten (copy) the whole string first, so every chunk still costs the full pending length.

Example: a 16 MiB MCP tool result arriving as one SSE `data:` line in 64 KiB chunks is about 256 chunks, each rescanning up to 16 MiB. `consumeSseStream` took 9.8 s, blocking the event loop.

## Fix

Search only the new text, append the leftover to the pending string without reading it, and read the pending string once when its line or event ends. This is the approach #11791 used for the stdio line reader.

- **mcp**: `consumeSseStream`. The size limit now uses a running byte count instead of measuring the buffer on every chunk. 16 MiB: 9.8 s -> 89 ms.
- **ai**: Anthropic, OpenAI Codex, Mistral and pi-messages each had their own SSE parser with this bug. Anthropic's spec-conformant parser moves to `src/utils/sse.ts` as `SseDecoder` (now linear) and all four use it. Each keeps its own abort and error handling.
- **agent**: `streamProxy` line splitting.
- **coding-agent**: RPC JSONL reader, session file loading, llama.cpp model events (now `SseDecoder`), and the `subagent` and `rpc-extension-ui` examples.
- **env, durable**: text line readers searched the whole pending line after every 64 KiB read. 16 MiB line: 1.35 s -> 72 ms.
- **chord**: sync batch lines and `importStore` JSONL.
- **tui**: `StdinBuffer` searched the whole bracketed paste for its end marker on every chunk. It now searches the new text plus the last 5 characters, in case the marker is split across chunks.
- **p2**: terminal frames copied the whole incomplete frame on every chunk (backlog replays reach 8 MiB). They now keep the chunks and join them once per frame. Discord attachment downloads copied the growing 1 MiB upload chunk on every network read (about 800 MiB copied for a 25 MiB file); they now collect the parts and join them once per upload chunk.

## Behavior changes in the shared SSE parser

- Codex also accepts CRLF line endings (it only split on LF before); Codex and pi-messages also accept lone CR.
- llama.cpp model events also accept lone CR and CRLF split across chunks.
- Anthropic no longer ends an event at a CRLF split across chunks.
- pi-messages joins multiple `data:` lines instead of taking the first.
- Mistral strips only the one space after `data:`. The payload is still trimmed, so JSON is unaffected.
- Anthropic's `raw` diagnostic lines no longer carry comment lines from earlier blocks that had no event or data.

## Not changed

- `readBodyText` in MCP: append-only, never rescanned. 16 MiB takes 100 ms.
- `p2-sandbox.mjs` exec frames: each frame is at most one chunk of child output.
- Bounded buffers (1 MiB or less) that are re-measured or rescanned per chunk: `apps/p2/src/runtime/logs.ts`, the `env/connection.ts` startup marker scan, the `p2-sandbox.mjs` request header, terminal-reply parsing in `StdinBuffer`.
- Editor and input paste buffers: they receive the whole paste in one call from `StdinBuffer`.

## Tests

- mcp: a 1 MiB event in 4 KiB chunks measures at most 2x its size (the old code measured 135M characters).
- ai: `test/sse.test.ts`, same events for every chunk size and line ending, CRLF split across chunks.
- tui: paste end marker split at every position.
- p2: terminal frames at every chunk size; a 1 MiB frame calls `Buffer.concat` once (the old code called it 256 times); a frame whose handler threw is not delivered again.
- mcp: a line that never ends is rejected at the limit.
- ai: pi-messages skips `data: null`; an empty `event:` does not carry into the next event.
- coding-agent: a throwing RPC line handler does not get its line joined with the next.
- Existing tests pass for the Anthropic, Mistral, Codex and pi-messages providers, proxy, RPC JSONL, session manager, llama, durable env-node, env differential, and chord sync/store. `npm run check` and `apps/p2` check pass.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): report already-declared MCP tools in tool_search results
prs.body:
`tool_search` only ranked tools that were not active yet: deferred or codemode tools that had not been loaded. A query for a tool the model already had got "No matching tools found.", for example a `direct` MCP tool or a deferred tool loaded earlier in the session. Weaker models took that to mean the tool did not exist and stopped trying to use it, even though it was in their tool list.

Changes:
- `tool_search` now also ranks the active tools a model could have searched for: tools with a namespace (MCP tools, `direct` ones included) and tools with searchable exposure that are already loaded. Built-in tools such as `read`, `grep` and `bash` are left out. These matches are listed in their own section:
  ```
  Already available, no need to load:
  - mcp__common__tavily_search: Search the web with Tavily
  ```
  The two groups are ranked separately, so active matches do not take slots from loadable ones. Nothing is re-activated, `details.loaded` is unchanged, and "No matching tools found." is returned only when neither group matches.
- The tool description now says "For MCP tools not already in your tool list, use `tool_search`" instead of "For MCP tool discovery, always use `tool_search`". The old wording told the model to search even when a direct MCP server was configured. The description is still a static string.

The `mcp_servers` system prompt section is unchanged. It lists servers whose tools are not declared to the model, and direct tools reach the model through their declarations.

**Testing**
- `test/tool-search.test.ts`: a new `tool_search results` block covers three cases:
  - an active direct MCP tool is reported as available and nothing is activated;
  - a deferred tool loaded earlier is reported, while an active built-in tool that matches the query is not;
  - deferred matches still load, and a query with no match still returns "No matching tools found."
- `test/suite/agent-session-mcp.test.ts`: the end-to-end case with a `direct` MCP server and `tool_search` asserted the old "No matching tools found." result. It now expects the declared tool to be reported as already available.
- `node ../../node_modules/vitest/dist/cli.js --run test/tool-search.test.ts test/suite/agent-session-mcp.test.ts`: 91 tests pass.
- `npm run check`: biome is clean and there are no type errors in coding-agent. The remaining type errors are in `packages/ai/test`, from the regenerated model catalog. This change does not touch those files.

Fixes #11921

Requested by @mitsuhiko

prs.title: fix(coding-agent,tui): stop temp file write failures from crashing pi
prs.body:
Fixes #10585.

## Problem

Bash output past the truncation limit is copied to a temp file in `$TMPDIR`. The `WriteStream` had no `error` listener, so any open or write failure became an uncaught exception and killed pi, including the in-flight turn, subagents and background jobs. Triggers seen in practice: a full tmpfs `/tmp` (ENOSPC), per-user tmpfs quotas that systemd sets on `/tmp` (EDQUOT, errno 122), an unwritable `TMPDIR` (EACCES). Both paths were affected: the agent `bash` tool (`OutputAccumulator`) and `!` commands (`executeBashWithOperations`).

Only adding a listener is not enough: `end()` on a stream that already errored never emits `finish` or `error`, so `closeTempFile()` would hang instead.

## Change

- `createOutputFileStream` returns an `OutputFileStream` wrapper: error handling from the start, writes ignored after a failure, a partially written file removed (never a file that was already at the path), and `close()` that never rejects or hangs and returns `{ kind: "saved", path } | { kind: "failed", error }`.
- Bash tool: the temp file is closed before the final result is built. On failure the result keeps the in-memory tail and ends with `[Showing lines X-Y of N. Could not save the full output: ENOSPC ...]`, without `fullOutputPath` / `full_output_path`. `readFullOutput()` (structured output for codemode) falls back to the tail. This matches what codemode already does for its own output files.
- `!` commands: the executor waits for the file to flush before returning its path. On failure it returns the tail without a path.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): show unresolved stored keys and rerun saved command keys
prs.body:
Follow-up to #12164 / #12454.

## Problems

1. `/login` cannot tell a broken stored key from no key. After #12454, a stored `!command` key whose command fails shows as `• not configured`, while `/logout` lists the credential. Users may think the key was lost.
2. A failed command stays failed until pi restarts. Command results, failures included, are cached for the process. Example: the `op` session expires, pi starts, the key fails. The user runs `op signin` and enters the same `!op read ...` key in `/login`. The cache returns the old failure, so the provider stays unconfigured.

## Changes

**API.** For a stored credential that does not resolve, `ModelRuntime.getProviderAuthStatus()` (and `ModelRegistry.getProviderAuthStatus()`) returns `{ configured: false, source: "stored" }` instead of `{ configured: false }`. The `AuthStatus` type does not change, and its doc comment now describes this case. #12454 is unreleased, so the released contract moves directly from `{ configured: true, source: "stored" }` (wrong) to this.

**UX.** `/login` shows `DeepSeek • stored key did not resolve` in error color, rather than `• not configured`. A login option's `status` is now a tagged union, `AuthSelectorStatus`: `{ kind: "configured", type, source? }` or `{ kind: "unresolved" }`, and unset when nothing is configured. The old shape was pi-ai's `AuthCheck`, which only describes auth that works. `AuthSelectorProvider` is internal: it is not exported from the package.

**Cache.** `AuthStorage.modify()` now drops the cached result of a `!command` key it has just written, and the following availability refresh runs the command again. Commands do not run on any new path: an extra run only happens after the user saves a key. Reads, requests and refreshes still use the cache, so a failing command does not rerun (and block for up to 10 s) on every lookup.

**Docs.** `docs/providers.md` explains the status and how to retry.

## Tests

- `auth-storage.test.ts`: a failing `!printenv` key stays cached after the variable is set, and resolves after it is saved again.
- `oauth-selector.test.ts`: a `{ configured: false, source: "stored" }` status renders as `stored key did not resolve`.
- The 12164 regression test now expects `source: "stored"`.
- These tests fail without the change. `npm run check` passes, and 430 coding-agent tests pass (regressions, model-registry, model-runtime, auth-storage, oauth-selector, resolve-config-value, bug-report).
- Checked by hand in tmux: with an `auth.json` containing `!exit 1` for DeepSeek and `!echo gsk` for Groq, `/login` shows `DeepSeek • stored key did not resolve` and `Groq ✓ stored`.

prs.title: fix(ai): classify finish_reason "error" in the retry classifier, not in provider messages
prs.body:
Closes #12206.

## Problem

A stream that ends with `finish_reason: "error"` (Copilot, OpenRouter, Mistral) is a transient provider failure, but in 1.6.0 Pi does not retry it: `openai-completions` reports `Provider finish_reason: error`, which matches no pattern in `retry.ts`.

`main` already retries it since a00a504, which added an explicit `provider finish_reason: error` pattern. Mistral (#10487) took a different route: it appended ` (server error)` to its message so the generic `server.?error` pattern matched. That puts retry policy into a user-visible message, and #12206 proposed copying it.

## Change

- Mistral reports `Provider stopped with: error`, like every other unmapped stop reason.
- `retry.ts` matches `provider stopped with: error` explicitly, next to the `openai-completions` pattern. Provider adapters report what happened; `retry.ts` decides what is retryable.
- Adapter-level test: `openai-completions` with `finish_reason: "error"` produces a retryable message, `content_filter` does not.

For comparison, Codex CLI no longer supports Chat Completions. On the Responses API it classifies stream failures by error type at parse time (`ApiError::Retryable`, `CodexErr::Stream`) and retries them by default, with an explicit list of terminal errors (quota, invalid request, context window). Pi classifies by message text, so the equivalent here is an explicit pattern in the classifier.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): refuse pi update of the Windows install run from WSL
prs.body:
Follow-up to #12172 (installer fix: earendil-works/pi.dev#194).

Problem: WSL appends the Windows PATH, so with no Linux pi, `pi` in WSL runs the Windows managed install. Its `bin/pi` sh launcher (written by `install.ps1` for Git Bash) runs `pi-launcher.js` on Linux Node, which sets `PI_MANAGED_INSTALL_ROOT=/mnt/c/.../install`. `getActiveManagedInstallRoot()` accepts that root, and `pi update --self` runs Linux `npm ci` into the Windows install and activates the result.

Reproduced on WSL2 with a Windows-layout install on `/mnt/c` (launchers from `install.ps1`, real 1.5.2 release):

```
command -v pi     -> /mnt/c/.../.pi/agent/bin/pi
pi update --self  -> Updated pi from 1.5.2 to 1.6.0
current-version   -> 1.6.0, built by Linux npm (.bin has WSL symlinks, no pi.cmd)
```

Windows pi still starts today because no dependency is platform-specific, but a release with a native optional dependency would break it.

Fix: `install.ps1` records a Windows entrypoint (`C:\...\pi.cmd`) in `managed-install.json`. On non-Windows, `getActiveManagedInstallRoot()` now throws when the entrypoint is a Windows path, so `pi update` stops before any download with:

> This is the Windows installation of pi, run from WSL. Running the Windows installation from WSL is unsupported, so it cannot update itself here. Update it from Windows, or install pi in WSL.

Startup is unchanged: `cleanupManagedInstall()` swallows the error. The launchers are unchanged.

Test: `rejects updating the Windows managed install from WSL` in `test/package-command-paths.test.ts`; fails without the fix (fetch called, npm ci run).

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): report unresolved stored credentials as not configured
prs.body:
Fixes #12164.

## Problem

`ModelRuntime.getProviderAuthStatus()` returned `{ configured: true, source: "stored" }` for any provider with an `auth.json` entry. It did not look at whether that entry resolves to a key.

Trace with `"deepseek": { "type": "api_key", "key": "!exit 1" }`:

1. `AuthStorage.read()` runs the command. It fails, so the credential comes back with `key: undefined`.
2. The availability refresh calls `checkAuth("deepseek")`. A stored credential owns the provider (`resolveProviderAuth`), the key is empty, so the check returns `undefined`. DeepSeek is not in `configuredProviders`, and its models are not available.
3. `/login` calls `getProviderAuthStatus("deepseek")`. DeepSeek is in `storedProviders`, so the status is `configured: true` and the selector shows a green check.
4. Requests resolve auth the same way as step 2 and fail with `No API key found for deepseek`.

## Fix

For stored credentials, `getProviderAuthStatus()` now uses the result of the availability check that the snapshot already holds (`configuredProviders`). Nothing new runs. The `/login` status and the request path now come from the same check.

The 7301 regression test stored credentials for provider ids that no provider defines. Under the new rule those are not configured, so the test now declares the two providers in `models.json`.

The "Saved API key" message is unchanged. The key is saved, and the selector now shows the provider as not configured.

## Tests

- New `test/suite/regressions/12164-stored-command-key-auth-status.test.ts`. It fails before the fix and passes after.
- `npm run check`, and the coding-agent tests for regressions, model-registry, model-runtime, oauth-selector, and auth-storage all pass.

prs.title: fix(ai): drop shut down Groq models and undocumented mistral-medium-3.5
prs.body:
Follow-up to #12450, which removes OpenAI's hand-added `gpt-5-chat-latest`. This PR covers two more providers where `/model` lists models that no longer work.

**Groq: `skipDeprecated: true`**

`/model` lists `llama-3.1-8b-instant`, `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` (Groq shutdown 2026-08-16) and `qwen/qwen3.6-27b` (shutdown 2026-09-14). models.dev marks them deprecated but has not deleted them yet.

Turning on `skipDeprecated` is safe for Groq because models.dev has only marked Groq models after their shutdown, never before (models.dev git history against https://console.groq.com/docs/deprecations):

| Model | Groq shutdown | models.dev marked deprecated |
|---|---|---|
| `gemma2-9b-it`, `kimi-k2-instruct`, `deepseek-r1-distill-llama-70b`, `llama3-*-8192`, `mistral-saba-24b`, `llama-guard-3-8b` | Jun to Oct 2025 | 2025-11-13 |
| `qwen-qwq-32b` | 2025-07-14 | 2026-01-04 |
| `llama-4-maverick`, `llama-guard-4-12b` | 2026-03-05 / 03-09 | 2026-03-26 |
| `llama-3.1-8b-instant`, `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` | 2026-08-16 | 2026-10-21 |
| `qwen/qwen3.6-27b` | 2026-09-14 | 2026-10-21 |

Caveat: the Llama 3.x shutdown covers free and developer tiers. Enterprise contracts keep them; those users can still add them as custom models.

The `qwen/qwen3.6-27b` thinking rule in `groq.ts` and its test go too, since they only applied to that model. Its successor `qwen/qwen3.8-27b` takes the standard effort levels. The Groq e2e context-overflow test moves to `openai/gpt-oss-120b`.

**Mistral: keep `skipDeprecated` off, remove `mistral-medium-3.5`**

models.dev marks Mistral models deprecated when Mistral announces their retirement, while they still work. Example: `devstral-2512` was marked 2026-06-02 and retired 2026-07-31; `voxtral-mini-transcribe-realtime-2602` was marked 2026-11-23 and retires 2027-04-30. A comment in `mistral.ts` records this.

`mistral-medium-3.5` was added by hand in #4009 until models.dev had Mistral Medium 3.5 (models.dev PR anomalyco/models.dev#1645, merged 2026-04-30). Mistral documents the model only as `mistral-medium-3-5`, `mistral-medium-2604` and `mistral-medium-latest` (https://docs.mistral.ai/models/mistral-medium-3-5-26-04). Gateways that forward to Mistral (OpenRouter, Requesty, LLM Gateway, Eden AI) use `mistral-medium-3-5`; only resellers with their own naming use a dot. models.dev lists `mistral-medium-2604` and `mistral-medium-latest` (pi's Mistral default), so the hand-added entry is removed.

**Catalog diff** (`npm run diff:model-catalog -- groq mistral`): exactly four removals.
- `groq/llama-3.1-8b-instant`
- `groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile`
- `groq/qwen/qwen3.6-27b`
- `mistral/mistral-medium-3.5`

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): explain why oversized Mermaid diagrams show source
prs.body:
A Mermaid diagram that renders wider than the available width was replaced by its source without any explanation. That looked the same as a diagram that is not supported at all. A diagram with parse warnings, by contrast, keeps its source and gets a `Mermaid diagram not rendered: …` note.

The Mermaid transformer now adds a note in the same style when a diagram does not fit, for example `Mermaid diagram not rendered: needs 109 columns, 80 available`. The note is added only once the message is complete. While a message streams, an oversized diagram still shows just its source, the same as parse warnings. The transformer runs again on every render with the current width, so after a resize the note disappears and the diagram renders.

`apps/p2/src/tui/components/mermaid.ts` is a copy of the same transformer with the same silent fallback, so it gets the same change.

If a diagram is both too wide and has parse warnings, only the warning note is shown: the diagram would not render at any width, so a width note would send the user to widen the terminal for nothing. That case showed no note at all before this change.

Testing:
- `packages/coding-agent/test/mermaid.test.ts`: the oversized-diagram test now checks that the note appears with the exact column counts once the message is complete, and that no note appears while streaming. It fails without the fix. A second test checks that a too-wide diagram with parse warnings reports the warning, not the width.
- `apps/p2/test/p2/tui-mermaid.test.ts`: the same checks for p2. It fails without the fix.
- `npm run check` passes.
- Ran the issue's 8-node `flowchart LR` through the built transformer:
  - Before: at width 80 it returned only the source.
  - After: at width 80 it returns the source plus `Mermaid diagram not rendered: needs 109 columns, 80 available`, and at width 120 it still renders the diagram.

Fixes #12324

Requested by @davidbrai

CI on `main` fails because two Mistral model IDs no longer exist in the generated catalog.

Released clients still have `devstral-medium-latest` as the default. If it is missing from their catalog, `buildFallbackModel` uses the provider's first model, so they keep working.

## Verification

prs.title: fix(ai): support Gemini xhigh thinking level
prs.body:
## Problem

Selecting the `xhigh` thinking level on `google/gemini-4-neon` fails before the request is sent:

```
Error: Unsupported Google thinking level mapping for google/gemini-4-neon: xhigh -> xhigh
```

Google documents `xhigh` as a supported `thinking_level` for `gemini-4-neon` and `gemini-4-hydrogen` (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thinking#thinking-levels). models.dev reports the same, so the catalog maps `xhigh: "xhigh"` and pi offers the level. But `resolveGoogleThinkingLevel` only accepts minimal/low/medium/high, and `@google/genai` 2.32.0 has no `XHIGH` enum value.

Affected catalog entries: `gemini-4-neon` and `gemini-4-hydrogen` on `google`, `google-vertex`, and `opencode` (all on the `google-generative-ai` / `google-vertex` APIs).

## Fix

- Upgrade `@google/genai` 2.32.0 -> 3.3.0, the first release with `ThinkingLevel.XHIGH`.
- Pass `xhigh` through `resolveGoogleThinkingLevel` / `toGoogleThinkingLevel` as `XHIGH`.
- Budget-based Gemini 2.5 models have no xhigh budget; `getGoogleBudget` clamps xhigh to high, like the Bedrock budget path and `clampReasoning`.
- Map the `FinishReason` values added in 3.x (`MISSING_THOUGHT_SIGNATURE`, `MALFORMED_RESPONSE`, `ESCALATION`, `PUP_LIMITED_DISABLED`, `MODEL_ARMOR`) to `error`.
- 3.3.0 dropped its no-op preinstall script, so its install-script allowlist entry is removed and the coding-agent install lock is regenerated.

No catalog change: the catalog already says `xhigh`. Models without an `xhigh` mapping still don't offer it.

## 3.x breaking changes reviewed

- Default Gemini Developer API version moved to `v1`: pi sets `apiVersion` explicitly on every client (`""` with a versioned `baseUrl` for Generative AI, `"v1"` for Vertex), so the default does not apply.
- Node >= 22 required: pi already requires >= 22.19.0.
- `CodeExecutionResultStep.result` type change: pi does not use the Interactions API.

No changelog entry, per CONTRIBUTING.md.

prs.title: fix(ai): retry "request rate increased too quickly" errors
prs.body:
With a ChatGPT subscription, Codex sometimes fails a request with "Your request rate increased too quickly". This is OpenAI's 429 `slow_down` throttle, and OpenAI's guidance is to wait and retry. When this error arrives as a `response.failed` stream event, only its message text reaches the shared retry classifier (`isRetryableAssistantError`). That text matches neither `rate.?limit` nor `too many requests`, so auto-retry did not run and the turn stopped. Alibaba Qwen sends the same wording ("Request rate increased too quickly. To ensure system stability, …"; #2952).

This change adds `rate increased too quickly` to `RETRYABLE_PROVIDER_ERROR_PATTERN` in `packages/ai/src/utils/retry.ts`. The non-retryable quota and billing check still runs first, so it takes precedence. coding-agent and durable both use this same classifier, so they need no change.

Left unchanged: the Codex HTTP error path (`parseErrorResponse` in `openai-codex-responses.ts`) rewrites any HTTP 429 into a "You have hit your ChatGPT usage limit" message once the provider's own retries run out. That is separate, existing behavior, and this issue is about the stream path.

Testing:
- Added cases to `packages/ai/test/retry.test.ts` with both the Codex and the Qwen wording. They fail without the fix and pass with it.
- `npm run check` passes.
- I called the built `isRetryableAssistantError` with both messages: it returned `false` before the change and `true` after.

Fixes #12240

prs.title: fix(mcp): match responses that echo numeric request ids as strings
prs.body:
The MCP client sends requests with integer ids and looks up each response by its exact id. Some servers echo the id back as a string (`"1"` for `1`). pi dropped those responses as "unknown request", so `initialize` never resolved and `pi mcp list` failed after 60 s with `MCP request timed out after 60000ms`. Other clients accept these responses. The official TypeScript MCP SDK, for example, looks up responses and progress tokens with `Number(response.id)` and `Number(progressToken)`.

Changes:
- Adds an internal `normalizeOwnRequestId()` in `protocol/jsonrpc.ts`, not exported from the package index. It maps a canonical decimal string (`"0"`, `"1"`, `"42"`) to its integer and leaves every other id unchanged.
- `McpClient` now uses it to match responses and progress-notification tokens. Progress tokens need it too because they reuse the request id.
- `StreamableHttpTransport.consumeResponseStream` uses the same matching to decide whether an SSE response stream answered its request. Before, a string id there made the stream count as unanswered. The transport then tried to resume it with GET and finally emitted a synthetic error for a request the client had already resolved.

Ids of requests that the server sends to the client are left as they are, so replies still echo them unchanged. pi only creates integer ids, so the normalization cannot match the wrong request.

Testing:
- Added a test in `streamable-http.test.ts`. A server answers `tools/call` over SSE with a string id, and the test asserts that the call resolves, no error is emitted, and no resume GET is made. It fails with only the client change, with only the transport change, and with neither change. It passes with both.
- Ran `npm run check` and the full `packages/mcp` test suite.
- Reproduction: a minimal HTTP server that returns `String(id)` for `initialize` and `tools/list`. Before the change, `pi mcp list` printed `failed … MCP request timed out after 60000ms`. After it, it prints `connected, 1 tool`.

Fixes #12205

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): rebuilt ! output follows ctrl+o
prs.body:
Closes #12426.

**Problem.** When the chat is rebuilt from the session (compaction, `/reload`, `/resume`, `/tree`), `addMessageToChat` creates each block and sets its expand state from `toolOutputExpanded`. The `bashExecution` case did not, so `!` output always came back collapsed while ctrl+o was on "expanded". Pressing ctrl+o then flipped the setting to collapsed with no visible change.

**Fix.** Call `component.setExpanded(this.toolOutputExpanded)` in that case, as the `custom`, `compactionSummary`, `branchSummary` and `user` (skill) cases in the same function do. #11886 added the same call to the two live paths in `handleBashCommand`; this is the third and last place that creates a `BashExecutionComponent`.

**Validation** on main `10149e47c2`:

- New test in `test/interactive-mode-status.test.ts`, next to the #11875 tests: `addMessageToChat` with a 40-line `bashExecution` message renders all lines when `toolOutputExpanded` is true and the collapsed hint when it is false. The expanded case fails without the fix.
- In tmux, with an empty agent dir and no model: `!seq 1 40`, ctrl+o, `/reload`. Before: `... 21 more lines (ctrl+o to expand)`, and the next ctrl+o shows "Tool output: collapsed" with no change. After: all 40 lines stay visible, and the next ctrl+o collapses the block.
- `npm run check` passes. In `./test.sh` the only failures are unrelated to this change:
  - The find tool tests fail because fd is not installed here and the test config prevents downloading it.
  - The pi-env tests need cargo, which is not installed here.
  - One `auth-storage` test also fails on main.

prs.title: test(coding-agent): make coalesced auth reload test independent of timestamp resolution
prs.body:
The `auth-storage.test.ts` test "keeps a coalesced reload alive while another credential reader is waiting" failed intermittently on some machines: the second reader got the cached key `"old"` instead of `"new"`.

`AuthStorage` decides whether to reload `auth.json` with `getFileRevision`, which compares `dev:ino:size:mtimeNs:ctimeNs`. The test overwrote the file in place, changing `"old"` to `"new"`, so inode and size stayed the same. Only the timestamps could change, and with coarse file timestamps two back-to-back writes often get the same ones. The revision then did not change, and the reader returned cached data.

The test now writes `"newer"` instead. The file size changes, so the revision changes whatever the timestamp resolution. The test still checks the same behavior: the coalesced reload picks up the changed file, and the lock is taken and released once.

No other test has the same pattern:
- The other test in this file and the `models-store` tests already change the file size between writes.
- With timestamps removed from `getFileRevision`, every test file that uses `AuthStorage`, `FileModelsStore` or `FileAuthStorageBackend` passes.

Testing:
- To simulate coarse timestamps, I temporarily changed `getFileRevision` to return only `dev:ino:size`. The old test fails with the reported error (`expected { key: 'old' } to deeply equal { key: 'new' }`); the updated test passes.
- `test/auth-storage.test.ts` and `test/models-store.test.ts` pass against the unmodified code.
- `npm run check` passes.

Fixes #12190

prs.title: fix(ai): distinguish Google prompt blocks from incomplete streams
prs.body: *Google adapters now distinguish blocked prompts from incomplete streams so callers receive actionable failure diagnostics.* ## Context When Google rejects a prompt for a content violation, `@google/genai` returns `promptFeedback` without any candidates or finish reason. The Google Generative AI and Vertex adapters discarded that feedback and reported the same error used for an incomplete stream. This hid the provider’s block reason and safety ratings. The generic wording also matched Pi’s transient-error rules, causing a deterministic prompt rejection to be considered retryable. ## Implementation - When a stream ends without a finish reason, preserve prompt feedback containing a block reason and report its optional explanatory message and safety ratings. - Apply the same handling to Google Generative AI and Vertex, which consume the same SDK response shape. - Report the received chunk count when a stream genuinely ends without a finish reason. ## Validation We set up an extension to mimic google responses for hardcoded requests. | Before | After | |---|---| | | | Before the change, a policy-blocked response and an empty stream produced the same generic error. After the change, the blocked response shows Google’s block reason and safety rating and is classified as non-retryable, while the empty stream remains retryable and reports that zero chunks were received. Note: I was not able to reproduce the safety block deterministically, but I did confirm that this is a valid response documented in the [google sdk](https://github.com/googleapis/js-genai/blob/main/src/types.ts#L4010-L4011) specifically when no candidates are generated. Closes #12330

prs.title: fix(ai): make Codex system prompts cacheable
prs.body:
## Why

[OpenAI's prompt caching guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching#how-prefix-matching-works) explains that GPT-6.2 places top-level `instructions` outside the cacheable input prefix. Pi's `openai-codex` provider sent the system prompt in that field, so it couldn't be cached.

## What

Send the system prompt as a leading `developer` message in `input`, without a model-version check or top-level `instructions`.

Verified that live Codex HTTP streams completed without `instructions` on GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.2 Sol, and GPT-6.2 Astra.
