prs.title: fix(web-shell): show scroll-to-bottom control in Split View panes
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Split View panes now render the same floating "scroll to bottom" button the main session view already has. When the reader scrolls up inside a pane, the button appears just above that pane's composer; clicking it scrolls the pane's transcript back to the bottom and resumes following live output.

The pane previously received no scroll-position signal from its transcript, so it could not know when to offer the control. It now subscribes to the existing callback that the transcript list already reports, keeps the state locally, and reuses the pane's existing imperative scroll handle for the click. The button's styling is copied from the main view's so the two controls look identical.

## Why it's needed

In Split View, scrolling up in a pane stops its auto-follow — the same behavior as the main view — but a pane had no way back to the live tail except manual wheel/trackpad scrolling. With several panes running at once, the pane whose autoscroll you broke is exactly the one you cannot easily jump back into. The main view solved this long ago; panes just never wired the same callback.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Run the new unit test: `cd packages/web-shell && npx vitest run client/components/ChatPane.test.tsx -t "scroll-to-bottom control"`. It asserts the button is absent before the pane reports a detached scroll position, that it appears once reported, that clicking it invokes the pane's scroll handle, and that it disappears when the pane reports being back at the bottom.
2. Manually: open a session in Split View (Add to Split View on a session), send a prompt long enough to overflow the pane, then scroll the pane up. Expected: a round chevron button appears above that pane's composer. Clicking it returns the pane to the bottom and re-engages autofollow. Before the change, no button appears and the only way back is manual scrolling.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: after scrolling a split pane up, no control appeared above the composer.
After: the same round scroll-to-bottom button the main view uses appears above the pane composer and returns the pane to the live tail.

No screenshot was captured in this run — the change was verified through the unit test above, not through a live browser session.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   N/A  |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only (`npx vitest run` in `packages/web-shell`); no dev server or browser session was run.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the pane footer gains one absolutely-positioned overlay element when the button is visible. It is `pointer-events: none` except on the button itself, and mirrors the main view's layer, so it should not intercept composer input.
- Not validated / out of scope: not verified in a live browser (see Evidence). The `packages/web-shell` typecheck reports one pre-existing error on `main` (`session-catalog-store.ts`: `liveOnly` missing on `DaemonSessionListPageOptions`); the same error appears with this change stashed, so it is unrelated.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #16569

prs.title: feat(generated-ui): let a click copy or download through the host
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Lets a Generated UI card copy text and download a small text file from a click, with Web Shell performing both outside the card. This is step 1 of the copy and download half of stage 8 in #14019; step 2 teaches the skill and flips the two acceptance checks.

- **Card API.** Cards gain `ui.copy(text)` and `ui.download(filename, mimeType, text)`. They work only while a click handler runs (its promise chain included), once per round. A wrong type, an empty value or an unsupported MIME type throws a `TypeError`, a value over its limit a `RangeError`, and a call outside a click or a second one in the round an `Error`; like saved state, the card can catch all of them. A call during initialization therefore throws, and the pre-display check reports an uncaught one as `VIEW_ERROR`.
- **Which clicks run.** The App performs a round's effect only when its own request for that round was a click and the round applied to the current input values. A round with no patches counts, which is the usual case for a copy or export button. When the values changed while the round ran, nothing is copied or downloaded and the card says so and asks for another click. This differs from saved state on purpose: a copy or export of values the user no longer sees would be wrong.
- **Host.** Web Shell performs both for the bundled card only, never in the transcript view, and never for a hidden card. It validates every request itself. Copy is a private request with at most 16 KiB of text. Download is the standard MCP Apps download request with exactly one embedded text resource of at most 64 KiB, one of CSV, plain text, JSON and Markdown; links and binary content are refused, and the file name is sanitized and given the extension of its type. The App adds that extension too, so another host that implements the standard request cannot save the text under a different type. One effect runs at a time per card.
- **Outcome and fallback.** The bar above the card shows each outcome (copied, download started, not copied) on its own attribute with an increasing count, so a repeated outcome is still a new observation and the save status is unaffected. When the browser refuses the clipboard write, for example because the click's activation expired while the round was queued, the bar keeps the text and shows its own Copy button, which copies on its own click.
- **Design.** A new design document in English and Chinese covers the API, the round rule, the wire contract, host validation, limits, risks and the rollout.

## Why it's needed

The #14019 acceptance evaluation (#16811) fails `bill.copies-current` and `comparator.exports-current-csv` with both the reference documents and the gating model: a card's JavaScript runs in a Worker without clipboard or download access, and its frame's sandbox allows neither. After persistent view state (#17448, #17522, #17922), these two and extending an earlier card are the only checks that still fail, and all three belong to stage 8. Copy and download come first; card revisions follow.

Design: [English](https://github.com/qqqys/qwen-code/blob/feat/generated-ui-copy-download/docs/design/generated-ui-copy-download.md) · [中文](https://github.com/qqqys/qwen-code/blob/feat/generated-ui-copy-download/docs/design/generated-ui-copy-download.zh-CN.md)

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- In Web Shell with Generated UI enabled, show a card whose button calls `ui.copy` with a value from an input. Click it: the bar above the card says the text was copied, and pasting gives the current value. Change the input and click again: the new value is copied and the bar shows a fresh outcome.
- Show a card whose button calls `ui.download('plans', 'text/csv', …)`. Click it: a `plans.csv` download starts and the bar names it.
- Block clipboard writes for the page (for example revoke the site's clipboard permission) and click copy: the bar says the browser blocked the copy and offers Copy. Allow writes and click it: the text is copied and the button goes away.
- Call `ui.copy` during initialization: the tool returns a `VIEW_ERROR` naming the call. Call it from an input handler inside `try`: the card catches an error and nothing is copied.

### Evidence (Before & After)

The bar above the card after a copy, next to the save status, and after the browser refused the write, with the bar's own Copy button (real daemon, Chromium):

![Copied](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qqqys/qwen-code/b0a4ff099e7e4eed7d5e565ae2c63135d7b19a69/copied.png)

![Copy blocked, with the bar's Copy button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qqqys/qwen-code/b0a4ff099e7e4eed7d5e565ae2c63135d7b19a69/copy-pending.png)

Browser check on a real daemon with a hand-written card, Chromium, through the bundled CLI:

| Step | Outcome shown | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Copy with the initial value | `copied`, count 1 | clipboard `Total: 12.30` |
| Edit the value, copy again | `copied`, count 2 | clipboard `Total: 15.00` |
| Export | `downloaded`, count 3, "Download started: plans.csv" | `plans.csv` with the current value |
| Clipboard permission revoked, copy | `copy-pending`, count 4, Copy button shown | nothing copied |
| Permission granted, the bar's Copy | `copied`, count 5, button gone | clipboard `Total: 16.00` |

A separate experiment with the same frame nesting across three origins measured the click's activation: WebKit allowed the clipboard write after a click with a 300 ms relay delay and refused it after 1.2 s or without a click, which is why the bar offers its own Copy button. Headless Chromium refuses writes without a granted permission, so its activation rule was not measured.

Locally: all generated-ui App tests plus the pre-display check, contract and packed MCP tests 300/300; Web Shell host module, card, retained runtime, transcript, artifact and i18n tests 307/307; both packages typecheck clean; the opt-in acceptance replay passes 4/4 with every pin unchanged. The App bundle is 976,762 bytes, under its 1 MiB limit.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Linux, Node 22, bundled CLI, real daemon, Playwright Chromium; WebKit for the activation experiment.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: generated code can now replace the user's clipboard and start downloads. Only a click can, once per click, with text from the card's current values, text-only files with a forced extension and size caps, and the host shows every outcome.
- Not validated / out of scope: whether a real Chrome needs the bar's Copy button (headless Chromium refused the write without a granted permission even after a real click, so the activation rule there is unmeasured); WebKit on the real daemon, where Playwright input reached neither the view nor the App, so only the activation experiment covers WebKit; Firefox, Safari and the desktop app; macOS and Windows; the skill, the reference documents and the two acceptance pins (step 2); copy or download for other MCP Apps.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The bundled card now advertises the standard download capability and a private copy capability.

## Linked Issues

Part of #14019.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

让 Generated UI 卡片在点击时复制文本、下载小的文本文件，由 Web Shell 在卡片外执行这两个动作。这是 #14019 阶段 8 中复制与下载这一半的第 1 步；第 2 步会在 skill 里教这两个调用，并翻转两项验收检查。

- **卡片 API。** 卡片新增 `ui.copy(text)` 和 `ui.download(filename, mimeType, text)`。它们只在点击处理函数运行期间可用（包括它返回的 promise 链），每轮一次。类型错误、空值或不支持的 MIME 类型抛出 `TypeError`，超过限制抛出 `RangeError`，不在点击中调用或同一轮第二次调用抛出 `Error`；和保存的状态一样，卡片都可以捕获。因此初始化时调用会抛错，显示前检查会把未捕获的调用报告为 `VIEW_ERROR`。
- **哪些点击会执行。** 只有当 App 为这一轮发出的请求是点击、并且这一轮应用在当前输入值上时，App 才执行这一轮的动作。没有补丁的轮次也算，复制或导出按钮通常就是这样。如果这一轮运行期间值变了，就不复制也不下载，卡片会说明原因并请用户再点一次。这和保存的状态有意不同：复制或导出用户已经看不到的值是错的。
- **宿主。** Web Shell 只为内置卡片执行这两个动作，转录视图和隐藏的卡片都不行。它自己校验每个请求。复制是一个私有请求，文本最多 16 KiB。下载是标准 MCP Apps 下载请求，只能带一个最多 64 KiB 的内嵌文本资源，类型只能是 CSV、纯文本、JSON 或 Markdown；链接和二进制内容会被拒绝，文件名会被清理并按类型设置扩展名。App 也会加上这个扩展名，所以其他实现了标准请求的宿主也无法把文本存成别的类型。每张卡片同一时间只执行一个动作。
- **结果与兜底。** 卡片上方的栏在独立的属性上显示每次结果（已复制、已开始下载、未复制），并带一个递增的计数，所以重复的结果也是一次新的观测，保存状态不受影响。当浏览器拒绝写剪贴板时（例如轮次排队期间点击带来的激活已经过期），宿主栏保留这段文本并显示自己的“复制”按钮，点击它时在这次点击里完成复制。
- **设计。** 新增中英文设计文档，覆盖 API、轮次规则、线路契约、宿主校验、限制、风险和推进步骤。

## 为什么需要

#14019 的验收评测（#16811）中，`bill.copies-current` 和 `comparator.exports-current-csv` 在参考文档和 gating 模型下都失败：卡片的 JavaScript 运行在没有剪贴板和下载能力的 Worker 里，卡片帧的 sandbox 也不允许这两者。持久视图状态（#17448、#17522、#17922）完成后，只剩这两项和扩展前一张卡片还失败，三项都属于阶段 8。先做复制和下载，卡片修订随后。

设计文档：[English](https://github.com/qqqys/qwen-code/blob/feat/generated-ui-copy-download/docs/design/generated-ui-copy-download.md) · [中文](https://github.com/qqqys/qwen-code/blob/feat/generated-ui-copy-download/docs/design/generated-ui-copy-download.zh-CN.md)

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

- 在开启 Generated UI 的 Web Shell 中显示一张卡片，它的按钮用 `ui.copy` 复制一个输入框里的值。点击后，卡片上方的栏显示已复制，粘贴得到当前值。修改输入后再点一次：复制的是新值，栏里显示一次新的结果。
- 显示一张按钮调用 `ui.download('plans', 'text/csv', …)` 的卡片。点击后开始下载 `plans.csv`，栏里显示文件名。
- 禁止页面写剪贴板（例如撤销站点的剪贴板权限）后点击复制：栏里显示浏览器阻止了复制，并提供“复制”按钮。允许写入后点击它：文本被复制，按钮消失。
- 在初始化时调用 `ui.copy`：工具返回指明这个调用的 `VIEW_ERROR`。在 input 处理函数里用 `try` 调用：卡片捕获到错误，什么都没有复制。

### 证据

复制后的宿主栏（与保存状态并排），以及浏览器拒绝写入后带“复制”按钮的宿主栏（真实 daemon，Chromium）：

![已复制](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qqqys/qwen-code/b0a4ff099e7e4eed7d5e565ae2c63135d7b19a69/copied.png)

![复制被阻止，宿主栏提供复制按钮](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qqqys/qwen-code/b0a4ff099e7e4eed7d5e565ae2c63135d7b19a69/copy-pending.png)

在真实 daemon 上用手写卡片做的浏览器检查，Chromium，通过打包的 CLI：

| 步骤 | 显示的结果 | 实际效果 |
|---|---|---|
| 用初始值复制 | `copied`，计数 1 | 剪贴板 `Total: 12.30` |
| 修改值后再复制 | `copied`，计数 2 | 剪贴板 `Total: 15.00` |
| 导出 | `downloaded`，计数 3，“Download started: plans.csv” | 带当前值的 `plans.csv` |
| 撤销剪贴板权限后复制 | `copy-pending`，计数 4，显示“复制”按钮 | 没有复制 |
| 授予权限后点宿主栏的“复制” | `copied`，计数 5，按钮消失 | 剪贴板 `Total: 16.00` |

另一个实验用同样的帧嵌套、跨三个 origin，测量了点击带来的激活：WebKit 在点击后经过 300 ms 的中转延迟仍允许写剪贴板，延迟 1.2 s 或没有点击时则拒绝，所以宿主栏提供了自己的“复制”按钮。无头 Chromium 在没有授予权限时拒绝写入，所以没有测出它的激活规则。

本地：generated-ui 全部 App 测试以及显示前检查、契约和打包后的 MCP 测试 300/300；Web Shell 的宿主模块、卡片、保留运行时、转录、产物和 i18n 测试 307/307；两个包类型检查都通过；需手动开启的验收 replay 4/4 通过，所有固定项不变。App 包体积 976,762 字节，低于 1 MiB 上限。

### 测试平台

Linux ✅；macOS、Windows ⚠️ 未测试。

### 环境

Linux、Node 22、打包的 CLI、真实 daemon、Playwright Chromium；激活实验用了 WebKit。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：生成的代码现在可以替换用户的剪贴板并开始下载。只有点击能触发，每次点击一次，内容来自卡片当前的值；文件只能是文本，扩展名被强制设置，大小有上限；宿主显示每次结果。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：真实 Chrome 是否需要宿主栏的“复制”按钮（无头 Chromium 在没有授予权限时，即使真实点击也拒绝写入，所以那里的激活规则没有测出）；真实 daemon 上的 WebKit，那里 Playwright 的输入既没有到达视图也没有到达 App，所以 WebKit 只由激活实验覆盖；Firefox、Safari 和桌面应用；macOS 和 Windows；skill、参考文档和两项验收固定项（第 2 步）；其他 MCP App 的复制或下载。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。内置卡片现在会声明标准下载 capability 和一个私有复制 capability。

## 关联 Issue

Part of #14019.

prs.title: feat(web-shell): idempotent prompt auto-retry and message-level resend
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Replaces the blocking uncertain-delivery banner and confirmation dialog in Web Shell with idempotent prompt submission, silent automatic retry for transient admission failures, and a chat-style message-level resend indicator.

- Every daemon prompt submission now carries a per-submission idempotency key so the daemon deduplicates retried admissions instead of starting a second turn.
- When a prompt submission fails with an uncertain or transient error while carrying an idempotency key, Web Shell silently retries twice (after 400 ms and 1200 ms) with the same key and already-uploaded attachment references before surfacing an error. Definite rejections such as invalid input, auth failures, payload-too-large, rate limits, and queue limits skip retries immediately and clean up uploaded attachments.
- If delivery remains uncertain after retries or fails outright, the composer is no longer locked and no banner or confirmation prompt is shown. Instead, a compact circular red exclamation button appears to the left of the affected user message bubble with a hover tooltip indicating either resend or uncertain delivery, and clicking it resends the message in place with the same idempotency key across the main composer, inline message edits, and split-view panes.
- The resend indicator hides automatically while a turn is active and clears permanently once the message receives a server prompt ID or a subsequent user message, assistant reply, thought, or tool step arrives (ignoring background notifications). Post-turn error retries mint a fresh retry key and reuse it only while that retry admission itself is uncertain.

## Why it's needed

Previously, when a prompt submission succeeded or dropped in transit without returning its acceptance response, Web Shell displayed an intrusive banner above the composer with technical "restore local copy" and "discard local copy" buttons, locked the composer until the user dismissed it, forced a browser confirmation popup, and never cleared the banner even after the reply visibly streamed in. Most client-side rejection statuses were also misclassified as uncertain. Using the daemon's existing idempotency-key deduplication together with bounded silent retries makes transient drops invisible and turns remaining failures into a familiar, non-blocking message-level resend flow.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Simulate a transient gateway timeout or dropped response (such as HTTP 503) on prompt submission: confirm three attempts are sent automatically (~400 ms and ~1200 ms apart) with the exact same idempotency key, the composer stays editable with no banner or confirmation popup, and a red circular exclamation button appears to the left of the user bubble with a hover tooltip explaining that the message may not have been sent.
- Restore the prompt endpoint and click the exclamation button: confirm the resend carries the same idempotency key, the server deduplicates without creating a duplicate user bubble or second turn, and the indicator disappears once the reply arrives.
- Simulate a definite rejection (such as HTTP 413): confirm only a single request is sent (no automatic retries), uploaded attachments are cleaned up, and the exclamation button tooltip reads Resend rather than uncertain delivery.
- Verify the same non-blocking message-level resend and auto-clear behavior in inline user message edits, split-view panes, and post-turn error retries, and confirm background notifications do not prematurely clear the indicator.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Verified against the local Web Shell dev server in Chromium (light theme, zh-CN locale) with mocked daemon responses using synthetic data, plus full workspace build, typecheck, lint/format checks, and 10 targeted Web Shell unit suites (2,692 / 2,692 tests passing).

- **Before**: uncertain admission (HTTP 503) displayed a blocking banner above the composer ("恢复本地副本 / 丢弃本地副本") and locked composer input.
- **After — Uncertain delivery (3× HTTP 503 auto-retries, 422 ms & 1204 ms gaps, identical idempotency key)**: no banner, unlocked composer, red circular `!` left of the user bubble with hover tooltip "可能未送达，点击重发".
- **After — Click `!` to resend (4th request reuses same idempotency key, `deduplicated: true`)**: indicator auto-clears, single user bubble preserved, assistant reply streams cleanly.
- **After — Definite rejection (HTTP 413)**: single request only (no retry), left red `!` hover tooltip reads "重发".

| Before (blocking banner & locked composer) | After (uncertain delivery: left `!`, hover tooltip, unlocked composer) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: blocking banner and locked composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a74187f-f5f8-4daf-b315-ac62c346e564) | ![After: uncertain delivery with left exclamation button and hover tooltip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b760c283-3248-476f-9d83-af886d8ce60b) |

| After (click `!` idempotent resend recovery) | After (definite HTTP 413: single request, tooltip "Resend") |
| --- | --- |
| ![After: deduplicated resend recovery](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b4139b09-1d89-4455-9c04-c2c2311e6426) | ![After: definite 413 rejection with Resend tooltip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b2140281-2af1-4fbd-9beb-7d50b00fbf8b) |

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ⚠️ not tested |

### Environment (optional)

macOS arm64; Vite dev server + headless Chromium (Playwright) against mocked daemon routes, plus Vitest (`2,692` passing tests across 10 test files), `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, ESLint, and Prettier.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the daemon's prompt idempotency ring is in-memory, so clicking resend after a full daemon restart may execute the prompt again (matching prior manual resend behavior); older daemons that ignore the idempotency key preserve at-least-once semantics on manual resend.
- Not validated / out of scope: daemon server code changes, managed-agent flows, Windows/Linux browser runs, and full Playwright E2E suite.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. See the design docs: [English design](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/3f07f3127f9f6633cfee99beed09dda296a91dc0/docs/design/web-shell-idempotent-prompt-resend.md) | [中文设计](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/3f07f3127f9f6633cfee99beed09dda296a91dc0/docs/design/web-shell-idempotent-prompt-resend.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

None.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 改动内容

将 Web Shell 中阻断输入框的“送达不确定”横幅和确认弹窗，替换为端到端幂等提交、瞬时异常静默自动重试以及类聊天软件的消息级重发标记。

- 每次 daemon 消息提交都会携带本次专属的幂等键，服务端在收到重试时直接去重，不会重复触发第二轮执行。
- 当携带幂等键的提交遇到不确定或瞬时网络/网关错误时，Web Shell 会自动沿用同一幂等键与已上传附件引用静默重试两次（间隔 400 ms 与 1200 ms），仅在连续失败后才向用户呈现状态。对参数错误、鉴权失败、请求体过大、限流和队列已满等明确拒绝状态，直接跳过重试并清理已上传附件。
- 当送达结果仍不确定或发送明确失败时，不再锁定输入框，也不再展示顶部横幅或浏览器确认弹窗；改为在对应用户消息气泡左侧展示紧凑的红色圆形感叹号按钮，鼠标悬停提示“重发”或“可能未送达，点击重发”，点击后在原消息上携带同一幂等键原地重发，主输入框、消息内联编辑与分屏面板行为保持一致。
- 回合运行期间自动隐藏感叹号；一旦原消息绑定到服务端消息 ID 或后续出现新的用户消息、助手回复、思考过程或工具调用，感叹号自动彻底清除（后台通知不会误清除）。回合错误后的重试会生成新的重试幂等键，仅在该重试本身结果不确定时复用。

## 改动原因

此前消息提交响应丢失时，Web Shell 会在输入框上方弹出带有“恢复本地副本 / 丢弃本地副本”等生硬术语的横幅，强行锁定输入框，点击恢复还要经过浏览器原生确认弹窗，且即便对话已明显开始回复，横幅也不会自动消失；同时大部分客户端明确拒绝状态也被误判为不确定。结合 daemon 已有的幂等键去重能力与有界静默重试，大多数瞬时波动可对用户完全无感，剩余异常则自然回归直观、不打断输入的微信式消息级重发体验。

## 评审测试计划

### 验证步骤

- 模拟提交消息时返回瞬时超时或网关异常（如 HTTP 503）：确认前端自动发出 3 次请求（间隔约 400 ms 与 1200 ms）且携带完全相同的幂等键；输入框保持可编辑、无顶部横幅与确认弹窗；消息气泡左侧出现红色圆形感叹号，悬停提示“可能未送达，点击重发”。
- 恢复接口正常响应后点击感叹号：确认重发请求复用同一幂等键，服务端去重不会产生重复用户气泡或第二轮回复，助手回复到达后感叹号自动消失。
- 模拟明确拒绝（如 HTTP 413）：确认只发出 1 次请求（不触发自动重试），已上传附件被清理，感叹号悬停提示为“重发”而非送达不确定提示。
- 验证消息内联编辑、分屏面板与回合错误重试均保持不锁输入框和一致的重发/自动清除行为，且后台通知不会误清除感叹号。

### 前后对照

已在 macOS 上使用本地 Web Shell 开发服务 + Chromium（浅色主题、简体中文）与全合成脱敏 mock 数据完成端到端模拟验证，并完成全仓构建、类型检查、代码格式与 Lint 检查以及 10 个 Web Shell 单元测试套件（2,692 / 2,692 全部通过）。

- **改动前（Before）**：送达不确定（HTTP 503）会在输入框上方弹出阻断横幅（“恢复本地副本 / 丢弃本地副本”）并锁定输入框。
- **改动后（After — 送达不确定）**：连续 3 次 503 自动重试（实测间隔 422 ms、1204 ms，同一幂等键）后，无顶部横幅、输入框保持可输入，气泡左侧出现红色 `!`，悬停提示“可能未送达，点击重发”。
- **改动后（After — 点击 `!` 幂等重发恢复）**：第 4 次请求复用同一幂等键并命中去重响应，`!` 自动消失、会话流仅保留唯一用户气泡并正常输出回复。
- **改动后（After — HTTP 413 明确拒绝）**：仅发 1 次请求（不自动重试），左侧红色 `!` 悬停提示为“重发”。

| 改动前（阻断横幅 + 锁定输入框） | 改动后（送达不确定：左侧 `!` + 悬停提示 + 输入框不锁） |

prs.title: fix(cli,core): preserve ACP transport error cause and replay cut tool calls
prs.body:
## What this PR does

ACP sessions can now replay a retryable transport stream cut after the model has emitted reasoning, opaque thought signatures, and one or more function calls, provided no visible user output was delivered and no tool call has executed. The behavior is opt-in through a send option forwarded across the client, turn, and client-initiated continuation paths; other consumers retain their existing retry behavior. Errors crossing the ACP boundary also retain the underlying error cause, such as `UND_ERR_SOCKET: other side closed`, in the JSON-RPC error message, error details, and recorded turn result instead of reducing them to a bare `terminated`.

## Why it's needed

A peer-closed socket during a daemon-backed ACP session interrupted a Gemini turn that had streamed reasoning and a file-read tool call before the stream finished. The existing replay gate treated any function call as delivered content, while the continuation gate correctly refused to insert a user turn after a function call. Consequently neither recovery path ran and the entire turn failed. ACP buffers tool calls until the model round finishes, discards pending tool preparations on retry, and never executes a discarded call, making tool-call-only cuts safe to replay. Separately, the raw transport error survived in model telemetry but lost its underlying cause when propagated across the ACP JSON-RPC boundary.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Verify a tool-call-only transport cut recovers automatically in ACP: stream reasoning, an opaque thought-signature chunk, and a file-read tool call with no visible prose and no finish reason, then close the underlying TCP connection. Expect the session to retry cleanly without executing or persisting the cut call, execute the recovered file read once, pass the real file contents to the next model round, and finish with a normal end turn.
2. Verify a visible-text plus tool-call cut does not replay and preserves the error cause: stream visible text followed by a tool call with no finish reason, then close the TCP connection. Expect a single model request with no replay and no tool execution, and expect the ACP JSON-RPC `-32603` error message, details, and recorded turn result to include `terminated (cause: UND_ERR_SOCKET: other side closed)`.
3. Verify exhausted tool-call retries fail cleanly: close the TCP connection after reasoning and a tool call on three consecutive attempts. Expect three model requests total (initial plus two replays), zero tool executions, a `-32603` error preserving the socket cause, and only the final partial assistant turn persisted in the session transcript.
4. Verify non-opt-in callers keep their existing behavior and cause-less long errors are not wrapped into internal JSON-RPC errors.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Real bundled ACP CLI A/B comparison against a disposable loopback Gemini SSE gateway (`origin/main` base vs this PR head `b67f32575e6`):

- Tool-call-only cut (reasoning + unsigned thought signature + file-read call, no finish reason): **Before** — failed on attempt 1 with `-32603` and bare `terminated`, 0 tool executions. **After** — recovered in 3 model requests (cut, replay, tool-result completion), 0 executions of the cut call, 1 real file read, normal end turn, and no cut partial persisted in the transcript.
- Visible text + tool-call cut: **Before** — failed on attempt 1 with bare `terminated` (cause dropped). **After** — still made 1 request (no unsafe replay, 0 tool executions) and returned `-32603` with `terminated (cause: UND_ERR_SOCKET: other side closed)` in both error message and details.
- Three consecutive tool-call-only cuts (budget exhausted): **Before** — failed on attempt 1 with bare `terminated`. **After** — made 3 requests, 0 tool executions, returned `-32603` with `terminated (cause: UND_ERR_SOCKET: other side closed)`, and persisted only the final attempt's partial turn.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

macOS, Node.js 24, isolated worktree and runtime directories, disposable loopback Gemini SSE gateway (`--auth-type gemini`), bundled ACP CLI built separately for base and head. No live external model API was called and the ambient daemon was not restarted.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Replaying a tool call that had already produced a user-visible side effect would be unsafe. The new option is therefore opt-in and enabled only for ACP sends, which buffer tool calls until stream completion and discard pending preparations on retry. Any non-empty visible output (text, inline data, file data, or executable code) still blocks replay, the function-call continuation veto is unchanged, and non-opt-in consumers keep their existing behavior.
- Not validated / out of scope: Full CLI test suite was not rerun after the final audit commit (all affected core suites — 1,515 tests — plus targeted ACP session tests, full workspace build/typecheck, ESLint/Prettier, and the base-vs-head Gemini SSE A/B E2E were run). Other frontends and eager tool-execution paths were not opted into tool-call replay.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None. The new send option defaults to off. Existing JSON-RPC error codes are unchanged, while cause-bearing ACP errors now preserve their underlying cause in error messages, details, and turn results.

## Linked Issues

None.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本次 PR 做的改动

ACP 会话现在可以在模型已经流式输出思考内容、不透明思考签名以及一个或多个工具调用后，对可重试的传输层断流执行自动重放，前提是尚未向用户输出任何可见内容且工具调用尚未执行。该能力通过显式发送选项开启，并在客户端、轮次以及客户端发起的续轮路径中透传；未开启该选项的调用方保持原有行为不变。跨越 ACP 边界的错误现在也会在 JSON-RPC 错误消息、错误详情与落盘的轮次结果中保留底层原因（例如 `UND_ERR_SOCKET: other side closed`），而不再退化为裸 `terminated`。

## 为什么需要这个改动

在一次常驻守护进程驱动的 ACP 会话中，Gemini 流式响应在已经输出思考与文件读取工具调用、但整条流尚未结束时遭遇对端关闭连接。原有的重放门控把所有工具调用都视为已输出内容，而续传门控又必须禁止在工具调用之后插入用户消息，导致两条恢复路径同时关闭、整轮对话直接失败。ACP 本身就会在模型轮结束前缓存工具调用、在重试时撤回未执行的工具准备状态且不会执行被撤回的调用，因此仅含工具调用的断流可以安全重放。此外，原始网络错误原因在遥测日志里存在，但在穿过 ACP JSON-RPC 边界时丢失。

## Reviewer Test Plan

### 验证步骤

1. 验证仅含工具调用的断流在 ACP 下自动恢复：在无可见正文、无结束标记的情况下依次流式下发思考内容、纯思考签名分片和文件读取工具调用，随后硬断 TCP 连接。预期会话自动重放，不执行也不落盘被切断的调用，恢复后的文件读取恰好执行一次并把真实文件内容带入下一轮请求，最终正常结束。
2. 验证含可见正文加工具调用的断流不会误重放且保留错误原因：先流式下发可见文本再下发工具调用（无结束标记），随后硬断 TCP 连接。预期只发起 1 次模型请求、不重放且不执行工具，同时 ACP JSON-RPC `-32603` 的错误消息、详情和轮次记录均保留 `terminated (cause: UND_ERR_SOCKET: other side closed)`。
3. 验证连续断流耗尽重试预算后的清理：连续 3 次在思考与工具调用后硬断 TCP 连接。预期共发起 3 次请求（首次 + 2 次重放）、工具执行 0 次，返回携带底层 socket 原因的 `-32603` 错误，且会话转录仅保留最后一次尝试的残缺记录。
4. 验证未开启该选项的调用方保持原有行为，且不带底层原因的长错误不会被误包装为 JSON-RPC 内部错误。

### 前后对比证据

使用隔离的本机回环 Gemini SSE 网关对打包后的 `origin/main` 基线与本 PR 最新提交 `b67f32575e6` 做了真实双臂 A/B 对照：

- 仅含工具调用断流（思考 + 无标志思考签名 + 文件读取调用，无结束标记）：**改动前**在第 1 次尝试即失败，返回 `-32603` 与裸 `terminated`，工具执行 0 次；**改动后**经 3 次请求自动恢复（断流、重放、带真实读取结果收尾），被切断调用 0 次执行且不入转录，恢复调用成功读取文件 1 次并正常结束。
- 可见正文 + 工具调用断流：**改动前**在第 1 次尝试失败并返回裸 `terminated`（丢失原因）；**改动后**同样只发起 1 次请求（不误重放、0 次工具执行），但 `-32603` 的错误消息与详情均完整返回 `terminated (cause: UND_ERR_SOCKET: other side closed)`。
- 连续 3 次工具调用断流（预算耗尽）：**改动前**第 1 次即失败返回裸 `terminated`；**改动后**精确尝试 3 次、0 次工具执行、返回完整 socket 原因，且转录中仅落盘第 3 次残缺记录。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### 测试环境（可选）

macOS、Node.js 24、隔离 worktree 与 runtime 目录、本机回环 Gemini SSE 网关（`--auth-type gemini`），分别构建基线与本 PR 打包产物对照运行；未访问外部真实模型接口，也未重启常驻守护进程。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险与权衡：如果对已经产生副作用的工具调用执行重放会引发重复执行，因此新选项采用显式开启，仅对流结束前不执行工具且在重试时撤回准备状态的 ACP 路径启用。任何非空可见输出仍会阻止重放，工具调用的续传禁令不变，未开启该选项的调用方不受影响。
- 未覆盖范围：最终审计提交后未全量重跑整个 CLI 单元测试套件（已运行全部受影响的 core 套件 1,515 项测试、聚焦 ACP 会话测试、全仓构建与类型检查、ESLint/Prettier，以及基线与改动双臂 Gemini SSE A/B E2E）。其他前端与流中提前执行工具的链路未启用该选项。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。新选项默认关闭，现有错误码不变，带底层原因的 ACP 错误消息与详情信息量更完整。

## 关联 Issue

无。

</details>

issues.body:
## What happened?

After using CodeWhale in GNOME Terminal and exiting, the terminal profile keeps CodeWhale’s Nord light colors instead of restoring the previous profile colors. The background becomes `#ECEFF4` and the foreground `#2E3440`, while the palette remains Solarized. The terminal looks inconsistent outside CodeWhale.

Expected: CodeWhale restores the terminal’s previous background, foreground, and palette on exit, or leaves the existing profile colors untouched.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In GNOME Terminal, use a profile with the Solarized palette and a non-Nord background/foreground (for example Solarized Dark).
2. Configure CodeWhale with `theme = "custom:nord"` and a theme file containing `surface_bg: "#ECEFF4"` and `text_body: "#2E3440"`.
3. Run `codewhale` in that GNOME Terminal profile.
4. Exit CodeWhale normally.
5. Observe that the GNOME Terminal profile background/foreground remain the CodeWhale Nord colors instead of the previous colors.

## Codewhale version

`codewhale 0.10.2 (ff466b2ed0bf)`

## Where did it happen?

- TUI (terminal interface)

## Operating system

- Linux

## How did you get Codewhale?

- npm

## Provider and model

`deepseek / deepseek-flash`

## Terminal and shell

GNOME Terminal 3.44.0 using VTE 0.68.0; `TERM=xterm-256color`; `COLORTERM=truecolor`; `/bin/bash`.

## `codewhale doctor` (optional)

Not included; no relevant failure was observed.

## Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

- CodeWhale theme: `~/.codewhale/themes/nord.json` defines `surface_bg: "#ECEFF4"` and `text_body: "#2E3440"`.
- GNOME Terminal profile currently reports:
  - `use-theme-colors=false`
  - `background-color=rgb(236,239,244)` (`#ECEFF4`)
  - `foreground-color=rgb(46,52,64)` (`#2E3440`)
  - palette still Solarized (`#002B36`, `#FDF6E3`, etc.)
- CodeWhale’s binary contains OSC 11 handling (`crates/palette/src/osc11.rs`), and its logs show terminal probes for `\x1b]11;?` and `\x1b]10;?`.
- OpenCode 2.2.5 was also used under the same GNOME Terminal profile and has an identical Nord light background/foreground, so the exact writer is not fully isolated. Cross-reference: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/63977
- The request is that the application setting OSC 10/11 restores the previous terminal colors on exit, or preserves the existing profile colors. A regression test for terminal color restoration would help.
- Workaround: reset the GNOME Terminal profile colors with `gsettings`.
- I searched existing issues and did not find a duplicate.

## Isolation steps not yet completed

1. Test whether `printf '\033]111\007'` and `printf '\033]110\007'` restore the dynamic background/foreground.
2. Reproduce with CodeWhale alone, then OpenCode alone, to identify which process writes the profile colors.

issues.body:
## Problem

API Route users can access its OpenAI-compatible endpoint, but there is no built-in provider entry for discovering and configuring it. I maintain API Route and would like to ask whether you would welcome an optional integration.

CONTRIBUTING.md requires prior maintainer sign-off for AI-assisted changes to provider policy or credentials, so I am opening this issue before preparing a PR.

## Proposed solution

Following the recent Cheaper Inference provider in #6761, add a narrowly scoped API Route provider descriptor and setup documentation:

- Base URL: `https://global.api-route.com/v1`; use the existing OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions transport.
- Independent, opt-in `API_ROUTE_API_KEY`; preserve the existing credential and provider-selection behavior.
- Exact unprefixed model IDs from the API Route catalog, including `deepseek-v4-flash`.
- Keep unknown pricing/capability metadata unset until verified, and follow the current route/offering schema instead of copying another provider's model facts.
- Focused descriptor/configuration tests; no changes to global prompts, authentication architecture, sponsorship, or default provider selection.

Would you approve this direction? What endpoint/model discovery evidence or acceptance checks would you require before a PR?

## Use case

Someone who already has an API Route key can choose the provider directly and run a model through their own paid account.

## Alternatives considered

A documented custom OpenAI-compatible provider recipe would be suitable if you prefer to limit new built-in entries.

## Impact

This would reduce setup steps for API Route users. I do not have usage statistics for Codewhale users of the service.

## Additional context

Documentation: https://www.api-route.com/docs/overview. API key management: https://www.api-route.com/tokens. Public model catalog: https://www.api-route.com/pricing. The authenticated `/v1/models` endpoint requires the user's own key.

This issue was prepared with AI assistance; I am responsible for the proposed integration.

issues.body:
# app-server, app-server-protocol: 6 verified defects from R7 (baseline bc58781ba)

## How to read this document (terms used below)

- **R<number>** — review unit, one area of the codebase; this document is about R7.
- **L<number>** — one of twelve review lenses (themes) applied to every unit; the table below names each lens.
- **P0 / P1 / P2** — priority rank: P0 highest, P2 lowest. It orders the work, not the severity of a finding.
- **Stage D** — the verification step: every cited line was opened at the baseline, the reachability was traced, and severity was re-scored. **Stage E** — the drafting step that produced this report.
- **Baseline `bc58781ba`** — the exact commit every quote refers to; re-check before acting if `main` has moved.
- **Confirmed** — a verifier opened the cited line, traced a reachable path and kept the finding; rejected and uncertain findings are not here.
- **Public** — this issue contains only findings cleared for a public report; security-class findings are handled through a separate private channel.
- **needs-test** — the written proof is static; a focused test named in the finding would settle the remaining question. No test was run in this audit.
- **Cell** — one audit cell: a review unit crossed with one lens; finding IDs keep the cell number, so a gap in numbering means a candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.
- **NOT READ** — a scope marker in a cell: that region was not opened, so no claim is made about it.
- **not-applicable / sampled-rescan-passed** — negative-check outcomes: the lens did not apply to that cell, or a sampled rescan found no new signal.
- **Refs #N / UPSTREAM REFS** — existing tracked issues related to the theme or to the exact code site; they are cross-links, never a claim to close or fix those issues. A 500-issue open/closed sweep found no exact duplicate of these findings at the same file and line.
- **CALL PATH, TRIGGER, MECHANISM, IMPACT, EVIDENCE, FIX, REGRESSION CHECK** — copied verbatim from the verified finding file. CALL PATH = how a user reaches the code; TRIGGER = the condition that fires it; MECHANISM = what the code actually does; IMPACT = what the user sees; EVIDENCE = the supporting lines; FIX = recommended change; REGRESSION CHECK = the test that should be added.

Unit R7 (P0 — highest priority is P0, then P1, then P2), runtime API, authz, ACP, control socket, remote setup and OAuth. Confirmed unique findings: **9** — **6 public** in this draft and **3** withheld as private-advisory or held. Finding IDs keep their original cell numbers; a gap means the candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.

## Coverage

- Files scanned: all 75 paths in the unit manifest were covered by at least one of the twelve theme scans; per-cell detail was recorded during the audit.
- Files read: every signal-matched production region was opened and quoted by the capturing and verifying agents; the exact per-theme counts and regions are in those cell files.
- Files not read: full sequential line-by-line reads of all files were not performed. Each cell records its own `NOT READ` scope; no claim is made beyond the matched regions.
- Themes applied: all twelve, L1–L12 — bugs, logic, edge cases, error handling, security, ordering, process lifecycle, fail-closed behaviour, resource limits, durable writes, async blocking, platform and Unicode. Each theme section below names its lens and its related tracked issue.
- Baseline: `bc58781ba` for every quote and every verification.
- Negative checks: failed 1/12 cells, not-applicable 6/12 cells, sampled-rescan-passed 5/12 cells.
- needs-test items: none in this unit. No test or product run happened in this audit.

## Related upstream issues

These are cross-links found in a sweep of 500 open and closed issues; none is a duplicate at the same file and line.

| Issue | State | Title |
|---|---|---|
| #6310 | CLOSED | ACP follow-up: empty terminal responses and Full Access discovery |
| #7071 | CLOSED | zh-Hans and other locales: common TUI strings hardcoded English |

## Contents

| finding id | final severity | theme | one-line problem | confirmation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R7-L11-01 | minor | L11 | sync session store io in async | static |
| R7-L11-02 | minor | L11 | server mutex held across async handler with blocking io | static |
| R7-L11-03 | minor | L11 | skills canonicalize and scan inline in async handler | static |
| R7-L12-01 | minor | L12 | hardcoded english acp full access hint | static |
| R7-L2-01 | minor | L2 | underflow zero menu selection | static |
| R7-L4-02 | minor | L4 | swallow active index rollback failure | static |

## Planned-work issue card

- **Status:** verified at baseline `bc58781ba`; not fixed in code by this audit.
- **Ways to help without Rust (do these first):**
    - Reproduce or confirm a finding on the baseline by following its `TRIGGER` in the exact file listed below; report whether you see the described result.
    - Review the `IMPACT` wording for accuracy and add a real-world example where you have seen this happen.
    - Check the related tracked issue listed under each theme and report whether this finding is already covered there.
    - Improve the documentation or user-facing message for the locale and wording findings.

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
let n: usize = input
    .parse()
    .map_err(|_| anyhow::anyhow!("Invalid input: {input}"))?;
options
    .get(n.saturating_sub(1))
    .map(|_| n - 1)
    .ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("Selection out of range"))
}
```

**CALL PATH:** interactive remote setup -> resolve_cloud/resolve_bridge/resolve_provider (mod.rs:164,185,219) -> prompt_choice (mod.rs:250) -> plain `n - 1` (mod.rs:270) -> array index (mod.rs:171,192,220)

**TRIGGER:** At the interactive "Enter a number" menu (mod.rs:256), the user enters `0`.

**MECHANISM:** `prompt_choice` prints options with 1-based labels (`idx + 1`, line 254) and parses the answer into `n`. The bounds probe deliberately uses `n.saturating_sub(1)` (line 269), which maps `n = 0` to index 0 and passes whenever the option list is non-empty. The value actually returned then uses plain `n - 1` (line 270): for `n = 0` this underflows — a debug-build "attempt to subtract with overflow" panic, or `usize::MAX` with release overflow checks off. The caller immediately uses that value as an index into a static array (`CLOUD_TARGETS[idx]`, `BRIDGES[idx]`, `providers[idx]`).

**IMPACT:** Entering `0` at any of the three setup menus crashes the `remote setup` wizard — an arithmetic-overflow panic in debug builds, an index-out-of-bounds panic in release builds. `0` is a plausible response to a numbered menu (off-by-one from the displayed 1..N), and the wizard must be restarted; no setup work is committed before the crash.

**EVIDENCE:** Bounds check uses `saturating_sub` at line 269 but the returned index uses `n - 1` at line 270 — the two operations are inconsistent for `n = 0`. Callers that index arrays with the result are at lines 171, 192 and 220. The `#[cfg(test)]` module (lines 282-321) tests token generation and unknown flags only; there is no test feeding `0` to `prompt_choice`.

**FIX:** Reject zero before the bounds probe and keep one subtraction: `let n = n.checked_sub(1).ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("Selection out of range"))?; options.get(n).map(|_| n).ok_or_else(|| anyhow::anyhow!("Selection out of range"))`. This makes 0 the same error as any out-of-range entry.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** A unit test that drives `prompt_choice` with stdin `"0\n"` and asserts it returns `Err("Selection out of range")` rather than panicking; a companion test that `"1\n"` maps to index 0. No such test exists today.

**CORRECTION:** Severity reduced from major to minor per §6; mechanism and impact otherwise as reported.

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened crates/app-server/src/remote_setup/mod.rs at baseline bc58781ba (HEAD == baseline). The QUOTE is verbatim: line 269 `    .get(n.saturating_sub(1))` followed by line 270 `    .map(|_| n - 1)`. For `n = 0` the probe reads index 0 and passes on any non-empty list, while the returned value uses plain subtraction. Reachability is a real user path: `remote-setup` is registered in crates/cli/src/lib.rs:549 and dispatched at crates/tui/src/lib.rs:2913 to `run_remote_setup` (mod.rs:62); with no `--cloud`/`--bridge`/`--provider` flag and default interactive mode, it calls `prompt_choice` at lines 164, 185 and 219 and immediately indexes `CLOUD_TARGETS[idx]` (171), `BRIDGES[idx]` (192) and `providers[idx]` (220). The menu prints 1-based labels (`idx + 1`, line 254) and "Enter a number: " (256), so `0` is an out-of-range entry. Effect confirmed: dev builds (overflow-checks on by default) panic with "attempt to subtract with overflow" at line 270; release/dist profiles (Cargo.toml:133-148, no `overflow-checks` override) wrap to `usize::MAX` and panic with index-out-of-bounds at 171/192/220. There is no test feeding `0` (test module lines 282-330 covers only token generation and unknown flags). 640:        if let Err(error) = self.persist(pending) {
641:            *self.classic_lease.lock() = previous.clone();
642:            let _ = self.write_active_index(previous.as_ref());
643:            return Err(error);
644:        }
645:        if lease.is_none()
646:            && let Err(error) = self.write_active_index(None)
647:        {
648:            *self.classic_lease.lock() = previous.clone();

**CALL PATH:** start/finish classic lease -> RuntimeEventJournal::set_classic_lease (626) -> journal.persist fails (640) -> compensating write_active_index(previous) at 642 -> `let _ =` discards the result -> Err(error) returned to controller (2225/2241)

**TRIGGER:** `journal.persist(pending)` fails and the compensating `write_active_index(previous)` also fails (e.g. disk full or permission loss on the journal directory).

**MECHANISM:** On a persist failure the in-memory lease is rolled back, but the rollback write to `active_index` is discarded with `let _ =`. If that write also fails, the on-disk `active_index` still describes the new lease while the journal file still describes the previous state. The caller receives only the original `persist` error and has no signal that the two durable files now disagree.

**IMPACT:** After the failed start/finish, remote control is marked Failed and ownership is locked for `OWNERSHIP_LOCK_AFTER_FAILURE` (2228/2244). On a later start, `open()` reads the stale `active_index` lease (441-443) without any equality check against the journal, so recovery can synthesize a terminal event against a lease whose events were never persisted — a silent divergence with no log of the second failure.

**EVIDENCE:** Guards checked — `read_active_index()` (584-609) and the equality checks at 632-635 and 669-671 detect divergence only on a *later* `set_classic_lease`/`advance` call, not at `open()` (441-447). The failure-injection hook `take_journal_persist_failure` covers `active_index_path` (613), but tests at 8484/8509 inject failures only into `journal_path` (1 or 2), never into the rollback write; grep shows no test asserting divergence handling.

**FIX:** Log the rollback failure explicitly, e.g. `if let Err(rollback) = self.write_active_index(previous.as_ref()) { tracing::error!(%rollback, %error, "active-index rollback failed; durable lease state may be inconsistent"); }`, and surface that in `status_detail`. Prefer writing `active_index` last, after a successful persist, so a failed persist never leaves the index advanced.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** Test injecting a persist failure followed by an active-index write failure, asserting the controller records the inconsistency and refuses to resume from the stale lease.

**CORRECTION:** none

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Quote at remote_control.rs:640-650 verified verbatim. Reachable path confirmed: start/finish classic lease (2225/2241) -> set_classic_lease (626). At entry the equality guard 632-635 proves active_index == in-memory lease; for a Some lease, line 637 writes the NEW lease to active_index before persist (640). If persist fails, the in-memory lease is rolled back and the compensating `write_active_index(previous)` at 642 discards its Result with `let _ =` — a swallowed failure with no log. A second I/O failure on that rollback (injectable via the hook at 613, or genuine disk-full/permission loss) leaves active_index = new lease while the journal and in-memory lease hold the old state, and the caller sees only the original persist error. `open()` (441-443) then loads active_index into classic_lease with no equality check against the journal, so recovery can synthesize a terminal event against a lease whose events were never persisted; guards 669-671 catch divergence only on a later advance, not at open. Genuine silent-divergence / no-durable-trace defect; minor because it requires two failures and normal operations contain it.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/app-server/src/runtime_api.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


## Theme L12 — Platform, Unicode, display width, locale

Refs: #7048, #6953, #7093, #7071 (platform and Unicode).

### R7-L12-01 — hardcoded english acp full access hint

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 8 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/app-server/src/acp_server.rs:713` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/app-server/src/acp_server.rs:713:hardcoded-english-acp-full-access-hint` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | #6310 (CLOSED) |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | stage-d-verifier |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
594:         use codewhale_localization::{MessageId, resolve_locale, tr};
595:         let settings = codewhale_runtime::settings::Settings::load().unwrap_or_default();
596:         let locale = resolve_locale(&settings.locale);
619:             acp::SessionMode::new("plan", tr(locale, MessageId::AppModePlan).to_string())
695:             acp::SessionConfigOption::select(
697:                 tr(locale, MessageId::SettingSubjectPermissions).to_string(),
702:                         tr(locale, posture_name).to_string(),
710:             .meta(codewhale_meta(json!({
713:                 "enableFullAccess": ACP_FULL_ACCESS_HINT,
840: const ACP_FULL_ACCESS_HINT: &str = "Start the server with `codewhale serve --acp --full-access` (alias `--yolo`), or set `yolo = true` in config.toml. Full Access also turns off Codewhale's own sandbox unless sandbox_mode tightens it; Plan stays read-only.";
```

**CALL PATH:** ACP `session/new` handler (crates/app-server/src/acp_server.rs:594-596 resolves `locale` from `Settings::locale`) -> config option `permission` `.meta(codewhale_meta(json!({...})))` at :710-714 -> `_meta.enableFullAccess` = `ACP_FULL_ACCESS_HINT` (:840) sent verbatim to the ACP client.

**TRIGGER:** Any ACP client starts a session with a non-English `settings.locale` (e.g. `zh-Hans`) while the server permission posture is not Bypass. The session config response is localized except this one hint.

**MECHANISM:** The `session/new` config response resolves a locale at :596 and passes every user-visible string through `tr(locale, ...)` — mode names and hints (:619-636), setting subjects (:680-697), posture names and descriptions (:702-704). The sibling `_meta` field at :713 instead injects the module-level `&'static str` `ACP_FULL_ACCESS_HINT` defined at :840, bypassing `tr` entirely. No code path localizes or post-processes `codewhale_meta(...)`.

**IMPACT:** A Chinese- or other non-English-locale ACP client (for example an IDE plugin rendering `_meta.enableFullAccess` as a click-to-enable tooltip) shows a fully localized permission selector with a long English-only instruction beside it. The mixed-language hint is misleading precisely for users who need the Full Access explanation most; no data loss, and the literal commands remain usable, so this is minor locale drift.

**EVIDENCE:** Guards checked — `resolve_locale` is called once at :596 and reused for all `tr`/`tr_key` calls in this handler; no `tr` call wraps :713. `ACP_FULL_ACCESS_HINT` is referenced only at :713 and :840 (grep over acp_server.rs), so no localized variant exists there. `MessageId::HomeYoloModeTip` at :628 shows a localized tip string already exists for the same `--yolo` subject, confirming the localization channel is available at this call site. No test asserts the locale of `_meta.enableFullAccess` (grep for `enableFullAccess` in the unit finds only :713 and :840).

**FIX:** Add a `MessageId` variant carrying this sentence to `codewhale_localization`, add its translations to each shipped locale pack, and replace line :713 with `tr(locale, MessageId::<new>).into_owned()` (or `.to_string()`), matching the neighboring fields. Keep the literal `codewhale serve --acp --full-access` / `yolo = true` tokens verbatim inside the translated string.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** Extend the existing locale-parity test for `session/new` config options (the `tr`-based assertions near :619-704) with one assertion that `_meta.enableFullAccess` equals the translated message for every `Locale::shipped_complete()` entry, so an untranslated constant fails the gate.

**CORRECTION:** none

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened bc58781ba:crates/app-server/src/acp_server.rs myself. session_view (:590) is reached from `session/new` -> new_session (:318) -> session_configuration (:360,:584-588) -> session_view; it resolves `let locale = resolve_locale(&settings.locale)` at :596 and routes every user-visible config string through `tr(locale, ...)` (:619-620, :680, :687, :697, :702-704). But the `_meta` field at :710-714 passes the module-level `const ACP_FULL_ACCESS_HINT: &str = "Start the server with ..."` (:840) verbatim. `codewhale_meta` (:1108-1112) only wraps fields under the "codewhale" key and performs no localization; grep shows ACP_FULL_ACCESS_HINT referenced only at :713/:840 and `enableFullAccess` only at :713/:840, so no localized variant or post-processing exists. The hardcoded-English-in-a-locale-driven-response mechanism is a reachable fact; the exact client rendering is inferred (cell GAP 4), matching the finding's own minor/impact framing.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/app-server/src/acp_server.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.

issues.body:
# engine/src/core/engine/: 3 verified defects from R1 (baseline bc58781ba)

## How to read this document (terms used below)

- **R<number>** — review unit, one area of the codebase; this document is about R1.
- **L<number>** — one of twelve review lenses (themes) applied to every unit; the table below names each lens.
- **P0 / P1 / P2** — priority rank: P0 highest, P2 lowest. It orders the work, not the severity of a finding.
- **Stage D** — the verification step: every cited line was opened at the baseline, the reachability was traced, and severity was re-scored. **Stage E** — the drafting step that produced this report.
- **Baseline `bc58781ba`** — the exact commit every quote refers to; re-check before acting if `main` has moved.
- **Confirmed** — a verifier opened the cited line, traced a reachable path and kept the finding; rejected and uncertain findings are not here.
- **Public** — this issue contains only findings cleared for a public report; security-class findings are handled through a separate private channel.
- **needs-test** — the written proof is static; a focused test named in the finding would settle the remaining question. No test was run in this audit.
- **Cell** — one audit cell: a review unit crossed with one lens; finding IDs keep the cell number, so a gap in numbering means a candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.
- **NOT READ** — a scope marker in a cell: that region was not opened, so no claim is made about it.
- **not-applicable / sampled-rescan-passed** — negative-check outcomes: the lens did not apply to that cell, or a sampled rescan found no new signal.
- **Refs #N / UPSTREAM REFS** — existing tracked issues related to the theme or to the exact code site; they are cross-links, never a claim to close or fix those issues. A 500-issue open/closed sweep found no exact duplicate of these findings at the same file and line.
- **CALL PATH, TRIGGER, MECHANISM, IMPACT, EVIDENCE, FIX, REGRESSION CHECK** — copied verbatim from the verified finding file. CALL PATH = how a user reaches the code; TRIGGER = the condition that fires it; MECHANISM = what the code actually does; IMPACT = what the user sees; EVIDENCE = the supporting lines; FIX = recommended change; REGRESSION CHECK = the test that should be added.

Unit R1 (P0 — highest priority is P0, then P1, then P2), turn loop, tool catalog, approval. Confirmed unique findings: **5** — **3 public** in this draft and **2** withheld as private-advisory or held. Finding IDs keep their original cell numbers; a gap means the candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.

## Coverage

- Files scanned: all 28 paths in the unit manifest were covered by at least one of the twelve theme scans; per-cell detail was recorded during the audit.
- Files read: every signal-matched production region was opened and quoted by the capturing and verifying agents; the exact per-theme counts and regions are in those cell files.
- Files not read: full sequential line-by-line reads of all files were not performed. Each cell records its own `NOT READ` scope; no claim is made beyond the matched regions.
- Themes applied: all twelve, L1–L12 — bugs, logic, edge cases, error handling, security, ordering, process lifecycle, fail-closed behaviour, resource limits, durable writes, async blocking, platform and Unicode. Each theme section below names its lens and its related tracked issue.
- Baseline: `bc58781ba` for every quote and every verification.
- Negative checks: child-attested 1/12 cells, not-applicable 5/12 cells, sampled-rescan-passed 6/12 cells.
- needs-test items: none in this unit. No test or product run happened in this audit.

## Contents

| finding id | final severity | theme | one-line problem | confirmation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1-L4-01 | major | L4 | accounting error hardcoded none | static |
| R1-L4-02 | minor | L4 | approval decision error cause discarded | static |
| R1-L9-01 | major | L9 | server tool deltas exempt from content cap | static |

## Planned-work issue card

- **Status:** verified at baseline `bc58781ba`; not fixed in code by this audit.
- **Ways to help without Rust (do these first):**
    - Reproduce or confirm a finding on the baseline by following its `TRIGGER` in the exact file listed below; report whether you see the described result.
    - Review the `IMPACT` wording for accuracy and add a real-world example where you have seen this happen.
    - Check the related tracked issue listed under each theme and report whether this finding is already covered there.
    - Improve the documentation or user-facing message for the locale and wording findings.
    Exact files for this unit:
    - `crates/engine/src/core/engine/child_host.rs`
    - `crates/engine/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs`
- **Ways to help with Rust:** add the regression test named in `REGRESSION CHECK`, make the minimal fix described in `FIX`, then run the focused test.
- **Local test command:** `scripts/dev-test.sh <path-from-LOCATION>`; the script maps a source path to the fastest crate test and refuses a green run when a filter matches nothing. Each finding also has its own `LOCAL TEST` line.
- **Done-when:** every finding here has a regression test that fails without the fix and passes with it; the focused area test is green; no compiler warning is silenced and no error is hidden to make a test pass; `scripts/preflight.sh --check` is green for the area you touched.
- **What maintainers already hold:** stage-D verification for every finding (quote opened at baseline, reachability traced, severity re-scored), the dedup decision, the private-advisory routing and this draft. Nothing has been fixed in code by this audit.
- **How to claim:** claim a finding by commenting on this issue with its finding ID; one finding per PR keeps the change reviewable. The maintainer resolves conflicts with `main` so contributors never rebase around our churn.


## Theme L4 — Error handling — swallowed cause, wrong fallback

Refs: none — new finding in this audit.

### R1-L4-01 — accounting error hardcoded none

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | major |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 7 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs:6009` |
| FINGERPRINT | `turn_loop.rs:6009:accounting-error-hardcoded-none` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | verifier-R1-L4 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
        let accounting_error: Option<String> = None;
        let accounting_record = if pending.primary && !pending.accounting_owned_elsewhere {
            ...
            crate::cost_status::record_runtime_usage_async(
                pending.accounting_scope,
                pending.accounting_origin.as_ref(),
                &record,
            )
            .await;
            Some(record)
        } else {
            None
        };
        let _ = self.send_event(Event::ProviderRequestReceipt {
            receipt: json!({
                "accounting_error": accounting_error,
                ...
        }).await;
        Ok(accounting_record)
```

**CALL PATH:** provider response completes -> Engine::settle_provider_request_receipt (turn_loop.rs:5960) -> record_runtime_usage_async (cost_status.rs:2263, discards owner_work error via `let _ =`) -> Event::ProviderRequestReceipt emitted with accounting_error: null -> TUI event_loop.rs:5086 / engine manager.rs:19777 gate on `receipt["accounting_error"].as_str()` and never fire.

**TRIGGER:** any provider request where usage settlement fails (owner_work returns Err in record_runtime_usage_async); the receipt still reports accounting_error: null, so no warning or uncertain-usage state is raised.

**MECHANISM:** `settle_provider_request_receipt` initializes `accounting_error` to `None` and never assigns it again; the function's `Result<_, String>` error type is likewise never used (only `Ok(accounting_record)` is returned at line 6060). Usage recording is fire-and-forget: `record_runtime_usage_async` discards the `anyhow::Result` from `owner_work` with `let _ = ...` (cost_status.rs:2272-2278), so a settlement failure cannot reach this receipt. The `accounting_error` key is therefore structurally always null.

**IMPACT:** Two consumers treat a non-null `accounting_error` as the signal that usage settlement is uncertain — the TUI calls `app.mark_usage_uncertain("usage_settlement_unacknowledged")` and shows a status warning (event_loop.rs:5086-5091), and the engine logs `"provider usage settlement failed; the turn continues"` (manager.rs:19777-1979). Because the field is never set, a real settlement failure produces no warning, no uncertain-usage mark and no log line: cost/usage accounting can be silently wrong while the diagnostic receipt looks clean (false success).

**EVIDENCE:** Assignment searched crate-wide: only `turn_loop.rs:6009` defines the variable; `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs:5086` and `crates/engine/src/runtime_threads/manager.rs:19777` consume the field. `cost_status.rs:2263-2279` swallows `owner_work`'s Result. No test asserts a non-null `accounting_error` on a failed settlement.

**FIX:** Make `record_runtime_usage_async` return the `owner_work` Result (or an `Option<String>` error) and have `settle_provider_request_receipt` capture it into `accounting_error` instead of the hardcoded `None`; propagate the same cause through the function's `Err` path and the `ProviderRequestReceipt` field so both consumers fire.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** smallest test — force `owner_work` to return Err during a provider request and assert `Event::ProviderRequestReceipt.receipt["accounting_error"]` is a non-null string and that `mark_usage_uncertain` is reached.

**CORRECTION:** none

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened baseline turn_loop.rs:6009 — `let accounting_error: Option<String> = None;` with no later assignment; `git grep accounting_error` shows only line 6009 (definition) and 6036 (serialize into receipt). Both consumers gate on `receipt["accounting_error"].as_str()` — manager.rs:19777 emits `tracing::warn!("provider usage settlement failed; the turn continues")` and event_loop.rs:5086 calls `app.mark_usage_uncertain("usage_settlement_unacknowledged")` — so both branches are dead while the field is null. cost_status.rs:2263-2279 `record_runtime_usage_async` returns `()` and discards `owner_work`'s Result via `let _ = ...await`, so no settlement Err can reach the receipt. `owner_work` (runtime_control.rs:13-40) can return Err on the 60s permit timeout, which is silently dropped: a real settlement failure produces no warning, no uncertain-usage mark, and no log — silent false success, major under the L4 "log/receipt" rubric row.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


### R1-L4-02 — approval decision error cause discarded

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 7 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/core/engine/child_host.rs:614` |
| FINGERPRINT | `child_host.rs:614:approval-decision-error-cause-discarded` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | verifier-R1-L4 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
                    Some((id, decision)) = approvals.next(), if !approvals.is_empty() => {
                        if runtime.cancel_token.is_cancelled() || handle.is_cancelled() {
                            handle.cancel();
                        } else {
                            let handle = handle.clone();
                            approval_deliveries.push(Box::pin(async move {
                                match decision {
                                    Ok(reply) => handle.accept_child_approval(id, reply).await,
                                    Err(_) => handle.deny_tool_call_unavailable(id).await,
                                }
                            }));
                        }
                    }
```

**CALL PATH:** probe_child_tool_batch loop (child_host.rs:601) -> approvals.next() yields (id, decision) at line 606 -> approval_deliveries future matches `Err(_)` at line 614 -> handle.deny_tool_call_unavailable(id) sends ApprovalDecision::Unavailable (handle.rs:1138).

**TRIGGER:** a child approval's decision receiver resolves Err (e.g. the host drops the approval request before a decision is returned); the code maps it to an Unavailable approval with no log of the underlying error.

**MECHANISM:** The `decision` value is a `Result` returned by the approval receiver (registered at child_host.rs:628, awaited at 629). On `Err`, the binding `Err(_)` discards the error without logging it and maps the outcome to `deny_tool_call_unavailable`, which merely sends `ApprovalDecision::Unavailable` (handle.rs:1138-1141). The surrounding `approval_deliveries` branch at lines 619-622 does log errors from the *delivery* future, but that future resolves to the `Result<()>` of the send — it never sees the discarded decision cause.

**IMPACT:** An operator or the user sees the tool reported as "unavailable" with no record of why the approval decision failed. Because the fallback is fail-closed (the tool is denied), this is a diagnostic gap, not a permission bypass: the lost cause makes post-mortem of a dropped or failed approval decision impossible from logs, and presents a misleading reason to the user.

**EVIDENCE:** `handle.rs:1138-1141` shows `deny_tool_call_unavailable` only sends `ApprovalDecision::Unavailable`; no tracing call on the Err branch at child_host.rs:614. The sibling `Err` handling at child_host.rs:620-621 logs a different error (the delivery Result), confirming the decision cause is not logged elsewhere in this loop.

**FIX:** Change `Err(_)` to `Err(error)` and add `tracing::warn!(%error, %id, "child approval decision failed; denying as unavailable")` before calling `deny_tool_call_unavailable`, so the cause is durably traced while keeping the fail-closed denial.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** smallest test — drive a child approval whose receiver yields Err and assert a warning event containing the error is emitted (or a log-capture assertion that the cause string appears).

**CORRECTION:** none

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened baseline child_host.rs:614 — `Err(_) => handle.deny_tool_call_unavailable(id).await,` discards the decision cause. The receiver is a `tokio::sync::oneshot::Receiver<ChildApprovalReply>` (subagent/mod.rs:4394-4428), whose `.await` yields Err when the sender drops without a reply — reachable when an approval is cancelled or the host drops the request before deciding. The sibling branch at child_host.rs:619-622 logs only the delivery future's `Result<()>`, not the decision cause, and handle.rs:1138-1141 confirms `deny_tool_call_unavailable` merely sends `ApprovalDecision::Unavailable` with no tracing. Denial is fail-closed (no permission bypass); the defect is a missing durable cause in logs, minor under the L4 "log/receipt" rubric row.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/core/engine/child_host.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


## Theme L9 — Resource limits, bounded buffers

Refs: #6554, #6560 (unbounded reads and missing limits).

### R1-L9-01 — server tool deltas exempt from content cap

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | major |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 7 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs:8057` |
| FINGERPRINT | `turn_loop.rs:8057:server-tool-deltas-exempt-from-content-cap` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | stage-d-verifier-R1-L9 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
8052:             Delta::ThoughtSignatureDelta { thought_signature } => thought_signature.len(),
8053:             Delta::RefusalDelta { refusal } => refusal.len(),
8054:             Delta::ReasoningStateDelta { .. }
8055:             | Delta::CitationsDelta { .. }
8056:             | Delta::WebSearchCallDelta { .. }
8057:             | Delta::ServerToolCallsDelta { .. } => 0,
8058:         },
8059:         _ => 0,
8060:     }
8061: }
```

**CALL PATH:** Engine stream loop (`turn_loop.rs:6140`) -> `stream_event_content_bytes` (`turn_loop.rs:8003`) -> `server_blocks` update (`turn_loop.rs:6634`/`6681`) -> `StreamOutcome.server_blocks` (`turn_loop.rs:6851`) -> assistant message `content_blocks` (`model_step.rs:919`) -> persisted in session history and replayed on later turns

**TRIGGER:** A provider stream emits `WebSearchCallDelta` (with large `sources`/`action`/`page`/`error` JSON) or `ServerToolCallsDelta` (with a large `steps` vector), or a large `CitationsDelta`. Each such delta is counted as 0 bytes toward `stream_max_content_bytes`, so the configured content cap never fires no matter how large the payload.

**MECHANISM:** The stream guard at turn_loop.rs:6256-6258 adds `stream_event_content_bytes(&event)` to `stream_content_bytes` and breaks when it exceeds `max_content_bytes`. But `stream_event_content_bytes` returns 0 for `CitationsDelta`, `WebSearchCallDelta` and `ServerToolCallsDelta` even though the `Delta` variants carry arbitrary-size `serde_json::Value` / `Vec<serde_json::Value>` payloads (models/src/lib.rs:684-705). The handlers at turn_loop.rs:6634-6679 and 6681-6688 write those payloads into `server_blocks` (replacing, not appending, so a single large delta or progressively larger replacements are stored whole), which is returned in `StreamOutcome.server_blocks` at turn_loop.rs:6851 and appended into the assistant message at model_step.rs:919. Thus content that would breach the cap if delivered as `TextDelta`/`InputJsonDelta` is admitted uncounted and persisted.

**IMPACT:** A buggy or hostile provider (or a compromised upstream tool-result source) can inject arbitrarily large server-tool-result payloads into the conversation without tripping the operator-configured `stream_max_content_bytes` cap. Once persisted, the oversized blocks are replayed to the model on every later turn — unbounded memory growth in the session and runaway input-token cost, exactly the failure mode the cap is meant to prevent. No other bound on `server_blocks` size was found in this unit.

**EVIDENCE:** Cap invocation at turn_loop.rs:6256-6258; zero-byte mapping at turn_loop.rs:8054-8057; `WebSearchCallDelta` field replacement at turn_loop.rs:6634-6679; `ServerToolCallsDelta` replacement at turn_loop.rs:6681-6688; initial-block accounting at turn_loop.rs:8031-8044 counts only `id/status/kind/action` for `WebSearchCall` (omits `sources/page/error`) and counts `steps` only at block start, not on deltas; commit to history at turn_loop.rs:6851 and model_step.rs:919. Guard tests `stream_event_content_bytes` coverage (turn_loop.rs:9050+) exercise only `RedactedThinking` block-start counting, not these zero-byte deltas. No test in this unit asserts a cap on server-tool-result deltas.

**FIX:** In `stream_event_content_bytes`, account for the serialized size of the payloads these variants carry, mirroring the `WebSearchToolResult`/`ServerToolCalls` block-start arms: for `WebSearchCallDelta` sum `action`, `sources`, `page`, `error` (`to_string().len()`) plus `status`/`kind`/`signature`; for `ServerToolCallsDelta` sum `steps[].to_string().len()`; for `CitationsDelta` use `citation.to_string().len()`. Alternatively, cap the accumulated `server_blocks` byte size explicitly before accepting each delta.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** Add a unit test for `stream_event_content_bytes` asserting that a `WebSearchCallDelta` with a multi-kilobyte `sources` value and a `ServerToolCallsDelta` with large `steps` return a byte count greater than zero and proportional to the payload; extend the stream-loop guard test so such a delta at the cap boundary triggers `StreamError::Overflow`.

**CORRECTION:** Two narrowings to the child's TRIGGER/IMPACT. (1) `Delta::CitationsDelta` is not an impact: the turn_loop handler at 6630 discards it entirely (`Delta::CitationsDelta { .. } => {}`), as recorded in this cell's rejected.md; no payload is accumulated or persisted for that variant. The finding stands on `WebSearchCallDelta` (and the Deserialize-tagged `ServerToolCallsDelta`). (2) `ServerToolCallsDelta` has no in-tree client emitter (only the enum, the turn_loop handler, the TUI conformance serializer and the responses.rs non-streaming accumulator); it is reachable only through a stream decoder that deserializes the serde-tagged `Delta` from JSON. The delta handlers require a matching `ContentBlockStart` to already exist in `server_blocks` (6634-6688 use `iter_mut().rev().find`), which is satisfied by the `WebSearchCall`/`ServerToolCalls` starts at 6519-6543. Path reference `model_step.rs:919` resolves to `crates/engine/src/core/engine/turn_loop/model_step.rs:919`. No change to severity or confidence: major/7 is consistent with rubric §6 (a real resource-limit failure, not the direct cost-runaway/exploit threshold for critical).

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened the cited lines at baseline bc58781ba (HEAD == baseline; turn_loop.rs clean). turn_loop.rs:8054-8057 matches the QUOTE verbatim: `Delta::ReasoningStateDelta { .. } | Delta::CitationsDelta { .. } | Delta::WebSearchCallDelta { .. } | Delta::ServerToolCallsDelta { .. } => 0,`. The guard at 6256-6258 adds `stream_event_content_bytes(&event)` and breaks on `> max_content_bytes`, so these events are admitted with zero cost. The payloads are arbitrary-size: models/src/lib.rs:688-703 defines `WebSearchCallDelta` with `action/sources/page/error: Option<serde_json::Value>` and 705 defines `ServerToolCallsDelta { steps: Vec<serde_json::Value> }`. Reachability is shown in-tree: crates/engine/src/client/responses.rs:731-745 emits `Delta::WebSearchCallDelta { sources: event.get("sources").cloned(), action: event.get("action").cloned(), page, error }` for real `response.web_search_call.in_progress|searching|completed` SSE events, and :756-779 emits it again on `response.output_item.done` with an `action/sources` fallback — all provider-controlled JSON. The handler at turn_loop.rs:6634-6679 writes those fields into `server_blocks` by whole replacement (`if sources.is_some() { *existing_sources = sources; }` at 6667-6669; `*existing = steps;` at 6687), so a delta can enlarge a stored block arbitrarily while the guard charges 0. The block-start arms at 8031-8044 count `id/status/kind/action` and `steps` only at start, omitting `sources/page/error` and later delta replacements. Commit path verified: `StreamOutcome.server_blocks` (6851) -> `content_blocks.extend(server_blocks)` (turn_loop/model_step.rs:919, correction to the cited path `model_step.rs:919`) -> persisted assistant message. Test gap confirmed: the only guard test at 9049-9062 (`redacted_block_start_counts_its_payload_as_content_bytes`) exercises a block-start, not these zero-byte deltas. Reachable scenario: an OpenAI Responses stream carrying a web-search result with large `sources` inflates session history with no cap, contradicting the operator-configured `stream_max_content_bytes`.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.
