issues.body:
# engine/src/fleet/, work_graph, hooks: 8 verified defects from R10 (baseline bc58781ba)

## How to read this document (terms used below)

- **R<number>** — review unit, one area of the codebase; this document is about R10.
- **L<number>** — one of twelve review lenses (themes) applied to every unit; the table below names each lens.
- **P0 / P1 / P2** — priority rank: P0 highest, P2 lowest. It orders the work, not the severity of a finding.
- **Stage D** — the verification step: every cited line was opened at the baseline, the reachability was traced, and severity was re-scored. **Stage E** — the drafting step that produced this report.
- **Baseline `bc58781ba`** — the exact commit every quote refers to; re-check before acting if `main` has moved.
- **Confirmed** — a verifier opened the cited line, traced a reachable path and kept the finding; rejected and uncertain findings are not here.
- **Public** — this issue contains only findings cleared for a public report; security-class findings are handled through a separate private channel.
- **needs-test** — the written proof is static; a focused test named in the finding would settle the remaining question. No test was run in this audit.
- **Cell** — one audit cell: a review unit crossed with one lens; finding IDs keep the cell number, so a gap in numbering means a candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.
- **NOT READ** — a scope marker in a cell: that region was not opened, so no claim is made about it.
- **not-applicable / sampled-rescan-passed** — negative-check outcomes: the lens did not apply to that cell, or a sampled rescan found no new signal.
- **Refs #N / UPSTREAM REFS** — existing tracked issues related to the theme or to the exact code site; they are cross-links, never a claim to close or fix those issues. A 500-issue open/closed sweep found no exact duplicate of these findings at the same file and line.
- **CALL PATH, TRIGGER, MECHANISM, IMPACT, EVIDENCE, FIX, REGRESSION CHECK** — copied verbatim from the verified finding file. CALL PATH = how a user reaches the code; TRIGGER = the condition that fires it; MECHANISM = what the code actually does; IMPACT = what the user sees; EVIDENCE = the supporting lines; FIX = recommended change; REGRESSION CHECK = the test that should be added.

Unit R10 (P1 — highest priority is P0, then P1, then P2), fleet lifecycle, work graph, hook dispatch. Confirmed unique findings: **10** — **8 public** in this draft and **2** withheld as private-advisory or held. Finding IDs keep their original cell numbers; a gap means the candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.

## Coverage

- Files scanned: all 42 paths in the unit manifest were covered by at least one of the twelve theme scans; per-cell detail was recorded during the audit.
- Files read: every signal-matched production region was opened and quoted by the capturing and verifying agents; the exact per-theme counts and regions are in those cell files.
- Files not read: full sequential line-by-line reads of all files were not performed. Each cell records its own `NOT READ` scope; no claim is made beyond the matched regions.
- Themes applied: all twelve, L1–L12 — bugs, logic, edge cases, error handling, security, ordering, process lifecycle, fail-closed behaviour, resource limits, durable writes, async blocking, platform and Unicode. Each theme section below names its lens and its related tracked issue.
- Baseline: `bc58781ba` for every quote and every verification.
- Negative checks: not-applicable 7/12 cells, sampled-rescan-passed 5/12 cells.
- needs-test items: R10-L6-01. No test or product run happened in this audit.

## Related upstream issues

These are cross-links found in a sweep of 500 open and closed issues; none is a duplicate at the same file and line.

| Issue | State | Title |
|---|---|---|
| #6555 | CLOSED | [audit] Durable writes not crash-atomic (tmp+rename without fsync) |
| #6559 | OPEN | [audit] Fail-open paths, swallowed errors, and false-PASS gates |
| #7071 | CLOSED | zh-Hans and other locales: common TUI strings hardcoded English |
| #7328 | OPEN | Provider failures: diagnostic log has no cause, typed code dropped |

## Contents

| finding id | final severity | theme | one-line problem | confirmation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R10-L10-01 | major | L10 | append flush without fsync | static |
| R10-L10-02 | minor | L10 | webhook retry without idempotency key | static |
| R10-L12-01 | minor | L12 | store error bypasses locale translation | static |
| R10-L4-01 | minor | L4 | home error empty path fallback misclassifies fleet scope | static |
| R10-L6-01 | minor | L6 | cached seq recovery two process duplicate | needs-test <static proof shows recovery is cached once and a second process is acknowledged by the code; demonstrating duplicate seq end-to-end needs an interleaved two-writer test, which is not run here> |
| R10-L8-01 | minor | L8 | flush acks after failed durable append | static |
| R10-L8-02 | minor | L8 | lane load error collapsed to owner missing | static |
| R10-L9-01 | minor | L9 | oversized batch error fan out | static |

## Planned-work issue card

- **Status:** verified at baseline `bc58781ba`; not fixed in code by this audit.
- **Ways to help without Rust (do these first):**
    - Reproduce or confirm a finding on the baseline by following its `TRIGGER` in the exact file listed below; report whether you see the described result.
    - Review the `IMPACT` wording for accuracy and add a real-world example where you have seen this happen.
    - Check the related tracked issue listed under each theme and report whether this finding is already covered there.
    - Improve the documentation or user-facing message for the locale and wording findings.
    Exact files for this unit:
    - `crates/engine/src/fleet/members.rs`
    - `crates/engine/src/fleet/store.rs`
    - `crates/engine/src/rlm/bridge.rs`
    - `crates/engine/src/work_graph/runtime.rs`
    - `crates/hooks/src/lib.rs`
    - `crates/hooks/src/lifecycle_outbox.rs`
- **Ways to help with Rust:** add the regression test named in `REGRESSION CHECK`, make the minimal fix described in `FIX`, then run the focused test.
- **Local test command:** `scripts/dev-test.sh <path-from-LOCATION>`; the script maps a source path to the fastest crate test and refuses a green run when a filter matches nothing. Each finding also has its own `LOCAL TEST` line.
- **Done-when:** every finding here has a regression test that fails without the fix and passes with it; the focused area test is green; no compiler warning is silenced and no error is hidden to make a test pass; `scripts/preflight.sh --check` is green for the area you touched.
- **What maintainers already hold:** stage-D verification for every finding (quote opened at baseline, reachability traced, severity re-scored), the dedup decision, the private-advisory routing and this draft. Nothing has been fixed in code by this audit.
- **How to claim:** claim a finding by commenting on this issue with its finding ID; one finding per PR keeps the change reviewable. The maintainer resolves conflicts with `main` so contributors never rebase around our churn.


## Theme L4 — Error handling — swallowed cause, wrong fallback

Refs: none — new finding in this audit.

### R10-L4-01 — home error empty path fallback misclassifies fleet scope

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 8 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/fleet/store.rs:881` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/engine/src/fleet/store.rs:881:home-error-empty-path-fallback-misclassifies-fleet-scope` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | stage-d-verifier-R10-L4 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
877:     let fleet = FleetFile::parse(&text).map_err(|e| FleetStoreError::Parse {
878:         path: path.display().to_string(),
879:         message: e.to_string(),
880:     })?;
881:     let scope = if path.starts_with(personal_fleets_dir().unwrap_or_default()) {
882:         FleetScope::Personal
883:     } else {
884:         FleetScope::Workspace
885:     };
886:     Ok((fleet, scope))
```

**CALL PATH:** codewhale_config::codewhale_home() -> Err -> personal_fleets_dir() (store.rs:592-603) -> Err -> load_fleet_at() (store.rs:881) -> unwrap_or_default() = empty PathBuf -> path.starts_with(empty) = true -> FleetScope::Personal -> callers: exact.rs:155-156 freeze_saved_fleet -> QualifiedFleetId.origin (exact.rs:355) -> cost_status::record_runtime_usage_async(origin.scope()) (exact.rs:797); members.rs:334/379 save_fleet; tui/src/lib.rs:8275 scope.label()

**TRIGGER:** HOME is unset/invalid (or CODEWHALE_HOME cannot be resolved) so codewhale_config::codewhale_home() returns Err, while load_fleet_at() is asked to classify a workspace-scoped fleet file.

**MECHANISM:** personal_fleets_dir() (store.rs:592-603) returns Err(FleetStoreError::Io) when codewhale_config::codewhale_home() fails to resolve a home. At line 881 the error is swallowed by unwrap_or_default(), which for PathBuf yields an empty path. Path::starts_with returns true when the base has no components, so an empty PathBuf is a prefix of every path; any fleet file, including one under the workspace store, is classified FleetScope::Personal. No log or error reaches the caller — load_fleet_at returns Ok with a wrong scope.

**IMPACT:** In a headless/container session where HOME is unset, a workspace Fleet is silently classified Personal. That value flows into freeze_saved_fleet (exact.rs:155-156) and becomes QualifiedFleetId.origin = scope.label() (exact.rs:355), which drives cost attribution via record_runtime_usage_async(origin.scope()) (exact.rs:797) — runtime spend is recorded under the wrong scope. TUI fleet pickers display the wrong "personal" label (tui/src/lib.rs:8275), and save_fleet/member-edit callers receive the wrong scope (members.rs:334/379). The underlying home-resolution error is lost with no durable trace.

**EVIDENCE:** personal_fleets_dir() signature and error path at store.rs:592-603. Every other call site in this file handles the Result rather than defaulting it: line 630 uses the Result directly, 652/837/947/1248 use `?`, 689/984/999 use `if let Ok(dir)`, 764/1066/1088 use `.ok()`. Line 881 is the sole unwrap_or_default() in the file. exact.rs:355 sets origin from scope.label(); exact.rs:797 uses origin.scope() for cost. Existing test store.rs:1797-1805 asserts Workspace scope only while home resolves; no test covers codewhale_home() failure. RISK NOTE: save_fleet re-calls personal_fleets_dir()? (store.rs:947) and will fail cleanly in the same broken-home condition, so no misdirected write occurs; the silent damage is the wrong scope label/receipt origin and its cost attribution.

**FIX:** Propagate the resolution error instead of substituting an empty path: `let scope = match personal_fleets_dir() { Ok(dir) if path.starts_with(&dir) => FleetScope::Personal, Ok(_) => FleetScope::Workspace, Err(e) => return Err(e) };` This makes load_fleet_at fail loudly when scope cannot be determined, matching every other call site in store.rs.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** Unit test that unsets HOME/CODEWHALE_HOME, saves a Fleet at FleetScope::Workspace in a temp workspace, then calls load_fleet_at on that path and asserts it returns Err (not Ok with FleetScope::Personal). The existing store.rs:1797-1805 test does not cover the failure path.

**CORRECTION:** EVIDENCE overstatement corrected — line 881 is not the file's only `unwrap_or_default()` (store.rs:722 file_stem and 1201 provider also use it); it is the only one on the home-resolution path, so the mechanism is unaffected. IMPACT narrowed — the cost-attribution leg (`cost_status.rs:797 origin.scope()`) is not fully traced: `accounting_origin` is a separate parameter built from a saved-operation lease (tui/src/lib.rs:15769-15770 `usage_origin(scope_token())`), not directly from QualifiedFleetId.origin; confirmed downstream effects are the label at exact.rs:355 and tui/src/lib.rs:8278. Severity kept out of major for these reasons.

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened at baseline bc58781ba. store.rs:881 reads exactly `let scope = if path.starts_with(personal_fleets_dir().unwrap_or_default()) {` followed by `FleetScope::Personal` / `FleetScope::Workspace`; store.rs:597-602 shows personal_fleets_dir() maps a failed `codewhale_config::codewhale_home()` to `FleetStoreError::Io`. The error premise is real: crates/paths/src/lib.rs:144-149 returns Err for a relative HOME and crates/config/src/state_dirs.rs:17-21 turns Ok(None) into Err via `.context(...)`. The `starts_with(empty)==true` premise is confirmed from the toolchain stdlib: path.rs:2816 `iter_after(self.components(), base.components()).is_some()` and path.rs:315-316 return Some on `(Some(_), None)` / `(None, None)`, so an empty base prefixes every path. Reachable: load_fleet_at has production callers (exact.rs:155, members.rs:334/379/497, identity.rs:51, tui/src/lib.rs:8275/11213, config_policy.rs:255) and home-resolution failure is tolerated at startup (tui/src/lib.rs:4672 `unwrap_or_else(|_| PathBuf::from("~/.codewhale"))`), so execution reaches the site. Impact is genuine but bounded: members.rs:358/386 pass the wrong Personal scope into save_fleet, which calls ensure_fleets_dir -> personal_fleets_dir()? (store.rs:652/897) and fails cleanly in the same broken-home state, so no misdirected write; no data loss, crash or cost runaway. The confirmed silent harm is the wrong scope label in QualifiedFleetId.origin (exact.rs:355, "user" vs "folder" per store.rs:91-95) and in the diagnostic owner string (tui/src/lib.rs:8278). Trigger is a broken-home misconfiguration with a direct workaround (fix HOME/CODEWHALE_HOME), matching the minor row. Existing test store.rs:1792-1805 exercises load_fleet (by name) with a resolved home only; no test covers load_fleet_at under home failure.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/fleet/store.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


## Theme L6 — Ordering, generation, TOCTOU

Refs: #6557 (ordering and generation fences).

### R10-L6-01 — cached seq recovery two process duplicate

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 7 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/hooks/src/lifecycle_outbox.rs:356` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/hooks/src/lifecycle_outbox.rs:356:cached-seq-recovery-two-process-duplicate` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | needs-test <static proof shows recovery is cached once and a second process is acknowledged by the code; demonstrating duplicate seq end-to-end needs an interleaved two-writer test, which is not run here> |
| VERIFIER | stage-D-verifier-R10-L6 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
356:         if !self.recovered {
357:             self.next_seq = recover_last_seq(&self.path).await?;
358:             self.recovered = true;
359:         }
360:
361:         let mut lines = Vec::with_capacity(events.len());
362:         let mut webhook_posts = Vec::new();
363:         for event in events {
364:             let seq = self.next_seq;
365:             self.next_seq = self.next_seq.saturating_add(1);
```

**CALL PATH:** LifecycleOutbox::emit (hooks/src/lifecycle_outbox.rs:179) -> OutboxInner::enqueue -> WriterState::run (312) -> WriterState::deliver_batch (348) -> recover_last_seq once (357) -> cached next_seq (364) -> append_lines (419)

**TRIGGER:** Two live Codewhale processes configured with the same outbox file path emit lifecycle events concurrently. Each process's writer task lazily recovers next_seq once from the same on-disk last line (both see the same value), then caches it; both assign identical seq values to distinct events.

**MECHANISM:** `next_seq` is recovered exactly once per writer (`self.recovered` latch at 356-359) and thereafter advanced only in local memory (364-365). `append_lines` uses `crate::open_private_append` (O_APPEND) with no lock spanning recover+append (419-420). The module doc at lines 20-23 promises "seq is monotonic per outbox file", and the append comment at 421-424 explicitly acknowledges "a second process appending to the same file can interleave lines" — so the two-writer case is a designed scenario, not hypothetical. Two concurrent writers recover the same last-line seq and emit duplicate seq values, breaking the documented per-file monotonicity and collapsing distinct events onto the same ordering key.

**IMPACT:** An operator running two Codewhale processes that share an outbox path (e.g. same workspace/config) gets a JSONL audit log in which two different lifecycle events carry the same `seq`. Any downstream consumer that uses `seq` as the ordering/idempotency key for `RuntimeEventEnvelope` (the exact `(binding, seq)` idempotency pattern used in work_graph/runtime.rs:837-840) will treat the second event as a duplicate no-op and silently drop it, or mis-order events from the two writers. The failure is silent: both appends succeed and the file looks well-formed.

**EVIDENCE:** `recover_last_seq` (448-491) reads the last complete line once and returns `seq+1`; no exclusive file lock is taken across recovery and append. Tests `seq_is_monotonic_and_recovers_across_reopen` (840-875) and `missing_and_empty_files_start_at_seq_1` (877-884) cover only sequential reopen of a single writer — no test exercises two live writers on one file. The `[fact]` claim of a second-process appending scenario is from the code's own comment at 421-424.

**FIX:** Either (a) document and enforce a single-writer-per-file contract (per-process outbox path, e.g. include PID in the path) so `next_seq` caching is valid, or (b) drop the `recovered` latch and re-read the last committed seq under an exclusive advisory file lock immediately before each batch append, assigning seqs while the lock is held so two processes cannot recover the same value.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** Add a test that spawns two `WriterState` instances pointed at one temp path, interleaves emits between them, and asserts the resulting seq column is globally unique and strictly increasing (1..N). This fails on the current code because both writers start from the same recovered value.

**CORRECTION:** none

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened baseline bc58781ba directly. `crates/hooks/src/lifecycle_outbox.rs:356-359` is the verbatim recovered-once latch (`if !self.recovered { self.next_seq = recover_last_seq(&self.path).await?; self.recovered = true; }`); `364-365` then advances `next_seq` only in local memory. `append_lines` at `419-420` opens via `crate::open_private_append`, which is `options.create(true).append(true)` at `crates/hooks/src/lib.rs:38-43` with no advisory lock spanning recovery and append. The module doc at `lifecycle_outbox.rs:20-23` promises "seq is monotonic per outbox file", and the append comment at `421-424` explicitly contemplates "a second process appending to the same file". Reachability shown in production construction: both `crates/app-server/src/exec_agent.rs:883-893` (headless exec) and `crates/tui/src/tui/app/init.rs:648-658` (interactive) build the outbox from the user-configured `[lifecycle_outbox].path` with no PID/session suffix (`crates/config/src/extension_toml.rs:22-25`), so two live processes sharing that config both lazily recover the same last-line seq and emit duplicate seqs. Mechanism and trigger confirmed; impact stays inference — no in-repo consumer of this outbox's `seq` was found in the rescan, so collapse of a downstream seq-keyed idempotency check is conditional, exactly as the finding's IMPACT states. Severity kept minor per the rubric row "narrow edge case with a workaround" (per-process outbox path); confidence 7 per "confident pattern match in read code; quote still required".

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/hooks/src/lifecycle_outbox.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


## Theme L8 — Fail-closed, gates, receipts, contract drift

Refs: #6559, #7435, #7434, #7328 (fail-closed, receipts, contract drift).

### R10-L8-01 — flush acks after failed durable append

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 8 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/hooks/src/lifecycle_outbox.rs:339` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/hooks/src/lifecycle_outbox.rs:339:flush-acks-after-failed-durable-append` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | stage-d-verifier-R10-L8 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
            if let Err(error) = self.deliver_batch(&events, &mut webhooks).await {
                tracing::warn!(
                    target: "lifecycle_outbox",
                    %error,
                    path = %self.path.display(),
                    "lifecycle outbox write failed"
                );
            }
            if !replies.is_empty() {
                while webhooks.join_next().await.is_some() {}
                for reply in replies {
                    let _ = reply.send(());
                }
            }
    /// Wait for events queued before this call to finish their delivery attempt.
    /// Local writes are flushed before the writer acknowledges this barrier.
```

**CALL PATH:** LifecycleOutbox::flush(timeout) [lib.rs:194-204] -> enqueue OutboxCommand::Flush(oneshot::Sender<()>) [lib.rs:199,209] -> writer task run loop [lifecycle_outbox.rs:315-342] -> deliver_batch() returns Err [324] -> tracing::warn! only [325-330] -> reply.send(()) [339] -> flush() returns Ok(()) [200-204]

**TRIGGER:** The durable JSONL sink cannot be written (disk full, permission change, path became a directory) while lifecycle events are queued and a caller uses flush() as a shutdown/durability barrier.

**MECHANISM:** deliver_batch() returns the append_lines() error (lifecycle_outbox.rs:411, 419-438), but the writer task only emits a warn-level log and discards it (324-330). The Flush command carries a oneshot::Sender<()> with no error slot (lib.rs:209), so the writer unconditionally calls reply.send(()) (339) after joining webhook tasks; flush() then awaits that unit and returns Ok(()) (lib.rs:200-204). The ack therefore reports success even when the durable audit append never completed.

**IMPACT:** A caller using flush() to guarantee lifecycle events were durably recorded before shutdown receives Ok(()) while the JSONL audit file is missing those events. The only trace is a tracing::warn! that is commonly filtered in production and is not written into the outbox itself, so after a crash or audit the loss cannot be reconstructed. This is the #6559 false-success / missing-durable-receipt class: a failed gate is presented as passed.

**EVIDENCE:** Contract quote at lib.rs:190-193 promises "Local writes are flushed before the writer acknowledges this barrier" — contradicted by the unconditional ack at 339. OutboxCommand::Flush is Sender<()> (lib.rs:209), so no error can cross the barrier. append_lines() propagates write/flush failures via context (419-438) and deliver_batch returns it (411). Webhook delivery failures are likewise dropped to a warn (400-406). The only flush test (lifecycle_outbox.rs:583) asserts the success path with expect("flush"); no test exercises a failed append followed by flush.

**FIX:** Change OutboxCommand::Flush to carry oneshot::Sender<Result<(), String>>. In the writer, capture the deliver_batch() error and send Err to every queued reply (and record a durable failure envelope if the append itself failed); make flush() return that error. Keep webhook failures best-effort but include them in the ack result so a barrier acknowledgement cannot claim success when the durable write failed.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** Add a test alongside members.rs:1047 building `FleetModelError::Store(FleetStoreError::NotFound(...))` and asserting `err.message(Locale::ZhHans)` differs from `err.message(Locale::En)` and contains no English literal from store.rs:267-280. (No test is run in this pipeline.)

**CORRECTION:** Two minor evidence imprecisions, mechanism unchanged: (1) the EVIDENCE cites a second `message(Locale::En)` test at members.rs:1138, but that line asserts on `change_receipt(Locale::En, ...)`; only members.rs:1047 calls `message(Locale::En)`; (2) `Display` (members.rs:136-139) calls `self.message(Locale::En)` rather than directly `error.to_string()` — still the English log form, so the Store branch's locale-ignoring behavior is unchanged.

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened at baseline bc58781ba. members.rs:117 documents message(locale) as "The person-facing explanation in `locale`" and the doc on the enum states the surface "picks the person's locale; `Display` is the English form for logs". Every sibling branch uses tr(locale, MessageId::...); line 131 reads `Self::Store(error) => error.to_string(),` ignoring locale. store.rs:266-281 confirms all six FleetStoreError `#[error("...")]` formats are hardcoded English with no locale parameter (e.g. "fleet file not found: {0}", "failed to parse {path}: {message}"). Reachability confirmed: toggle_fleet_model (members.rs:369) propagates FleetStoreError via `?` from resolve_selected_fleet/load_fleet_at/save_fleet through From<FleetStoreError> to FleetModelError::Store, and handlers.rs:130/143-145 wraps `error.message(locale)` inside tr(locale, MessageId::FleetToggleFailed) -> set_sticky_status. Locale files confirm FleetToggleFailed is genuinely translated (zh-Hans.json:1844 "无法更新 Fleet：{error}"), so only the injected {error} stays English — the drift is real. apply.rs:3030/3049 pass ui_locale the same way. crates/tui/AGENTS.md:25 requires "User-visible prose uses `tr(locale, MessageId::...)`". No security/data-integrity effect; operation fails closed.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/fleet/members.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.

# engine/src/tools/subagent/: 7 verified defects from R2 (baseline bc58781ba)

## How to read this document (terms used below)

- **R<number>** — review unit, one area of the codebase; this document is about R2.
- **L<number>** — one of twelve review lenses (themes) applied to every unit; the table below names each lens.
- **P0 / P1 / P2** — priority rank: P0 highest, P2 lowest. It orders the work, not the severity of a finding.
- **Stage D** — the verification step: every cited line was opened at the baseline, the reachability was traced, and severity was re-scored. **Stage E** — the drafting step that produced this report.
- **Baseline `bc58781ba`** — the exact commit every quote refers to; re-check before acting if `main` has moved.
- **Confirmed** — a verifier opened the cited line, traced a reachable path and kept the finding; rejected and uncertain findings are not here.
- **Public** — this issue contains only findings cleared for a public report; security-class findings are handled through a separate private channel.
- **needs-test** — the written proof is static; a focused test named in the finding would settle the remaining question. No test was run in this audit.
- **Cell** — one audit cell: a review unit crossed with one lens; finding IDs keep the cell number, so a gap in numbering means a candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.
- **NOT READ** — a scope marker in a cell: that region was not opened, so no claim is made about it.
- **not-applicable / sampled-rescan-passed** — negative-check outcomes: the lens did not apply to that cell, or a sampled rescan found no new signal.
- **Refs #N / UPSTREAM REFS** — existing tracked issues related to the theme or to the exact code site; they are cross-links, never a claim to close or fix those issues. A 500-issue open/closed sweep found no exact duplicate of these findings at the same file and line.
- **CALL PATH, TRIGGER, MECHANISM, IMPACT, EVIDENCE, FIX, REGRESSION CHECK** — copied verbatim from the verified finding file. CALL PATH = how a user reaches the code; TRIGGER = the condition that fires it; MECHANISM = what the code actually does; IMPACT = what the user sees; EVIDENCE = the supporting lines; FIX = recommended change; REGRESSION CHECK = the test that should be added.

Unit R2 (P0 — highest priority is P0, then P1, then P2), delegation, budgets, delivery, ledger. Confirmed unique findings: **7** — **7 public** in this draft and **0** withheld as private-advisory or held. Finding IDs keep their original cell numbers; a gap means the candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.

No finding in this unit is withheld as a private security advisory or held item.

## Coverage

- Files scanned: all 15 paths in the unit manifest were covered by at least one of the twelve theme scans; per-cell detail was recorded during the audit.
- Files read: every signal-matched production region was opened and quoted by the capturing and verifying agents; the exact per-theme counts and regions are in those cell files.
- Files not read: full sequential line-by-line reads of all files were not performed. Each cell records its own `NOT READ` scope; no claim is made beyond the matched regions.
- Themes applied: all twelve, L1–L12 — bugs, logic, edge cases, error handling, security, ordering, process lifecycle, fail-closed behaviour, resource limits, durable writes, async blocking, platform and Unicode. Each theme section below names its lens and its related tracked issue.
- Baseline: `bc58781ba` for every quote and every verification.
- Negative checks: not-applicable 4/12 cells, sampled-rescan-passed 8/12 cells.
- needs-test items: none in this unit. No test or product run happened in this audit.

## Related upstream issues

These are cross-links found in a sweep of 500 open and closed issues; none is a duplicate at the same file and line.

| Issue | State | Title |
|---|---|---|
| #6559 | OPEN | [audit] Fail-open paths, swallowed errors, and false-PASS gates |
| #7071 | CLOSED | zh-Hans and other locales: common TUI strings hardcoded English |

| R2-L11-02 | minor | L11 | artifact mutex held across await | static |

## Planned-work issue card

- **Status:** verified at baseline `bc58781ba`; not fixed in code by this audit.
- **Ways to help without Rust (do these first):**
    - Reproduce or confirm a finding on the baseline by following its `TRIGGER` in the exact file listed below; report whether you see the described result.
    - Review the `IMPACT` wording for accuracy and add a real-world example where you have seen this happen.
    - Check the related tracked issue listed under each theme and report whether this finding is already covered there.
    - Improve the documentation or user-facing message for the locale and wording findings.
    Exact files for this unit:
    - `crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/coord.rs`
    - `crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/delivery.rs`
    - `crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/engine.rs`
    - `crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs`
    - `crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/worktree.rs`
- **Ways to help with Rust:** add the regression test named in `REGRESSION CHECK`, make the minimal fix described in `FIX`, then run the focused test.
- **Local test command:** `scripts/dev-test.sh <path-from-LOCATION>`; the script maps a source path to the fastest crate test and refuses a green run when a filter matches nothing. Each finding also has its own `LOCAL TEST` line.
- **Done-when:** every finding here has a regression test that fails without the fix and passes with it; the focused area test is green; no compiler warning is silenced and no error is hidden to make a test pass; `scripts/preflight.sh --check` is green for the area you touched.
- **What maintainers already hold:** stage-D verification for every finding (quote opened at baseline, reachability traced, severity re-scored), the dedup decision, the private-advisory routing and this draft. Nothing has been fixed in code by this audit.
- **How to claim:** claim a finding by commenting on this issue with its finding ID; one finding per PR keeps the change reviewable. The maintainer resolves conflicts with `main` so contributors never rebase around our churn.


## Theme L4 — Error handling — swallowed cause, wrong fallback

Refs: none — new finding in this audit.

### R2-L4-01 — discard usage publish result without trace

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 8 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/engine.rs:94` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/engine.rs:94:discard-usage-publish-result-without-trace` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | stage-d-verifier-R2-L4 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
    pub(super) async fn publish_auxiliary_usage(
        &self,
        record: &crate::cost_status::RuntimeUsageRecord,
    ) {
        let _ = self.publish_async(record).await;
        let _ = self.project_settled(record).await;
    }
```

**CALL PATH:** mod.rs:17996 / mod.rs:18055 `record_return_check_usage` -> mod.rs:17924 `accounting.publish_auxiliary_usage(&record).await` -> engine.rs:90-96 `publish_auxiliary_usage` -> engine.rs:57-72 `publish_async` -> engine.rs:35-55 `publish` -> `cost_status::record_runtime_usage`; second discarded branch engine.rs:74-88 `project_settled` -> manager.blocking_write() -> `record_worker_source`

**TRIGGER:** An auto-review return-check reviewer call completes with `Some(usage)`; `record_return_check_usage` builds a `RuntimeUsageRecord` with `UsageSpendOwner::Auxiliary` and calls `publish_auxiliary_usage`. If the disk-backed cost-status write or the subagent-manager state projection fails, both `Result`s are silently discarded.

**MECHANISM:** `publish_async` returns `std::io::Result<Option<u64>>` and `project_settled` returns `std::io::Result<()>` (engine.rs:57-88); both can fail in `owner_work` when `record_runtime_usage` or the synchronous manager write fails. `publish_auxiliary_usage` binds each awaited result to `_`, so neither failure is propagated to `record_return_check_usage` nor written to `tracing`. No other code observes the outcome (the sole caller at mod.rs:17924 ignores the unit return).

**IMPACT:** When the accounting store is briefly unavailable (disk error, poisoned/contended store authority), the reviewer-model spend for the return check is neither persisted to cost status nor projected into the worker's settled source, and no log record exists. Cost/usage reports silently under-count the auxiliary review; an operator reading the durable trace cannot tell the record was lost. This is the concrete "failure with neither cause nor durable trace" the L4 card asks about; severity is minor because a single auxiliary record does not by itself break a user session.

**EVIDENCE:** engine.rs:35-55 `publish` is fallible and its `io::Result` is the value lost at line 94; engine.rs:61-71 `publish_async` maps the failure through `std::io::Error::other`; engine.rs:81-87 `project_settled` maps `record_worker_source` failure. Contrast the sibling settlement paths engine.rs:1624-1627 and engine.rs:1651-1654, which discard `publish_async` at the same time but DO log the `project_settled` failure with `tracing::warn!(%error, ...)` — confirming the missing trace here is an inconsistency, not a house rule. No test exercises a failing accounting store on this path (no `#[cfg(test)]` assertion references `publish_auxiliary_usage`).

**FIX:** Replace the two `let _ =` with explicit logging, e.g. `if let Err(error) = self.publish_async(record).await { tracing::warn!(target: "subagent", %error, "auxiliary review usage not recorded"); }` and the same for `project_settled`, matching engine.rs:1625-1627; alternatively change `publish_auxiliary_usage` to return `io::Result<()>` with `?` and have `record_return_check_usage` log it.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** A unit test that injects a failing cost-status store into `record_return_check_usage` and asserts that a tracing warning is emitted (or an error is returned) would catch reintroduction.

**CORRECTION:** Impact narrative overstates the cost-status write path — `record_runtime_usage` returns `()` and already discards its own error internally at cost_status.rs:2255-2260 (`let _ = record_interactive_runtime_usage(...)`), so `publish`'s `io::Result` is not a disk-write error channel. The outcomes actually lost at line 94-95 are `project_settled` Err (worker-source projection) and `owner_work` failures (permit timeout / JoinError) on both calls. Sibling-path citations engine.rs:1624-1627 / 1651-1654 are off by one line (actual 1625-1627 / 1653-1655).

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened engine.rs:90-96 at bc58781ba: `let _ = self.publish_async(record).await; let _ = self.project_settled(record).await;` with no log. `project_settled` (engine.rs:74-88) can Err via `manager.record_worker_source(...)?`; `publish_async` (57-72) can Err via `owner_work` permit timeout / JoinError (runtime_control.rs:32-47). Sole caller mod.rs:17924 ignores the unit return. Sibling paths engine.rs:1625-1627 and 1653-1655 do log the `project_settled` failure with `tracing::warn!`, so the missing trace is an inconsistency, not a house rule. Reachable: auto-review return-check branches at mod.rs:17996 and 18055 with `Some(usage)` reach `record_return_check_usage` (17902-17925) -> `publish_auxiliary_usage`.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/engine.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


### R2-L4-02 — discard failed state rollback reconcile

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 7 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs:10462` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs:10462:discard-failed-state-rollback-reconcile` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | stage-d-verifier-R2-L4 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
                if let Some(lifecycle) = agent.work_lifecycle.as_ref() {
                    let _ = lifecycle.reconcile_state(OwnerState::Failed, 1, None);
                }
                return Err(anyhow!(
                    "failed to durably register write-capable sub-agent before launch: {error}"
                ));
```

**CALL PATH:** `spawn` write-capable sub-agent (durable_registration branch) -> mod.rs:10444-10446 persist_state_synchronously -> Err branch mod.rs:10451 -> mod.rs:10461-10463 `let _ = lifecycle.reconcile_state(OwnerState::Failed, 1, None)` -> mod.rs:3737-3750 `reconcile_state` -> work_graph/runtime.rs:313-320 `reconcile_operation` -> `reconcile_observation` (returns Err on session mismatch / pre-registration observation)

**TRIGGER:** A write-capable sub-agent's durable registration succeeds but `persist_state_synchronously()` fails (disk/store error). In-memory state is rolled back, then the lifecycle owner is supposed to be moved to `Failed`; if `reconcile_state` itself returns `Err` (for example, the active work graph belongs to a different session or has no registered snapshot), that error is discarded.

**MECHANISM:** `reconcile_state` returns `Result<bool, String>` (mod.rs:3742) and `reconcile_operation` returns `Err` for a session mismatch or an observation that arrives before graph registration (work_graph/runtime.rs:329-341). The rollback branch binds that `Result` to `_`, so a failure to mark the external operation owner as `Failed` is neither logged nor added to the error returned to the caller. The only error the caller sees is `error` from the persist step.

**IMPACT:** After a failed durable launch, the external work-graph owner can remain in a non-terminal state (e.g. `Running`) while the in-memory agent has been rolled back and the launch aborted. A later recovery or progress reader sees an owner that never settled, and the durable trace has no record of why — precisely a lost failure with no cause and no receipt. Severity is minor because the launch is aborted and the persist error is still reported.

**EVIDENCE:** mod.rs:10451-10466 shows the surrounding error handling: the persist error IS propagated with `format!(... {error})`, and the earlier snapshot rollback uses `.expect(...)` on invariants, so the discarded reconcile result is the lone untraced outcome. `reconcile_state` (mod.rs:3737-3750) has no internal logging; `reconcile_operation`/`reconcile_observation` (work_graph/runtime.rs:313-349) return `Err` without logging. No test asserts a tracing event on this rollback path.

**FIX:** Capture the result and attach it to the returned error, e.g. `if let Err(reconcile_error) = lifecycle.reconcile_state(OwnerState::Failed, 1, None) { tracing::warn!(target: "subagent", %reconcile_error, "failed to mark aborted write-capable launch as Failed"); }` (or append `; additionally failed to settle lifecycle owner: {reconcile_error}` to the `anyhow!` message), matching the cause-preserving style at coord.rs:1333-1335 and mod.rs:6922-6924.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** A unit test that forces both `persist_state_synchronously` and `reconcile_state` to fail and asserts the logged/returned diagnostic contains the reconcile cause would catch reintroduction.

**CORRECTION:** none

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened mod.rs:10451-10466 at bc58781ba: the persist error is propagated with `return Err(anyhow!("...before launch: {error}"))`, but line 10462 `let _ = lifecycle.reconcile_state(OwnerState::Failed, 1, None);` discards a `Result<bool, String>` (signature mod.rs:3737-3750) with no log. `reconcile_state` -> `work.reconcile_operation` -> `reconcile_observation` (work_graph/runtime.rs:313-349) returns Err on session mismatch (334-336) or observation before graph registration (341), with no internal logging on that path. Reachable: write-capable spawn with durable_registration where persist_state_synchronously fails and the reconcile also fails; a two-failure edge case with the launch aborted, hence minor.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


## Theme L8 — Fail-closed, gates, receipts, contract drift

Refs: #6559, #7435, #7434, #7328 (fail-closed, receipts, contract drift).

### R2-L8-01 — git failure skips claim mismatch verification

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 7 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/delivery.rs:648` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/delivery.rs:648:git-failure-skips-claim-mismatch-verification` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | stage-d-verifier-R2-L8 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
643:     if !write_capable {
644:         return None;
645:     }
646:     let claimed = explicit_change_paths(summary);
647:     let missing = changed
648:         .map(|changed| claimed.difference(changed).cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>())
649:         .unwrap_or_default();
664:     if missing.is_empty() && undeclared.is_empty() {
665:         return None;
666:     }
```

**CALL PATH:** worker settle -> ensure_worker_delivery_verified (mod.rs:8159) -> compute_delivery_verification (delivery.rs:694) -> DeliveryEvidence::changed_paths (delivery.rs:217) -> verify_changes (delivery.rs:636) -> claim-mismatch check skipped at :647-664 -> default verification stored at mod.rs:8167

**TRIGGER:** A write-capable worker settles in a workspace where `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`/`git status` fails, is absent, or exceeds MAX_BASELINE_PATHS, and its result summary claims file changes it did not make (without matching declared deliverables).

**MECHANISM:** `DeliveryEvidence::capture_for_handle` (delivery.rs:192-210) propagates `?` through `git(...)` (delivery.rs:54-57, which uses `.output().ok()` and `.then_some(...)`), so any git failure sets `baseline: None` with no log. `changed_paths` (delivery.rs:217-218) returns `None` when `baseline` is absent. `verify_changes` then computes `missing` with `.unwrap_or_default()` at :649, mapping "no change data" to "empty missing set" (the success-looking value), so the `claim_mismatch` verdict at :663-672 is never produced for false change claims. `compute_delivery_verification` falls back to `default_agent_run_verification` (`self_report_only`, mod.rs:1355-1362) and may upgrade it to `deliverables_present` at :729-730; `store_delivery_verification` (mod.rs:8159-8169) stores this verdict with `checked = true` and no note that git evidence was unavailable.

**IMPACT:** A write-capable worker that falsely claims source changes avoids the `claim_mismatch` receipt that exists to catch exactly that. The parent sees a bounded verification object whose status is `self_report_only`/`deliverables_present` with no field indicating the claim check was skipped, so the verification surface silently stops doing its job while looking normal. Blast radius is the delivery-verification diagnostic for any worker whose workspace git probe fails; the filesystem `check_deliverable` check still runs, so declared non-empty deliverables are not faked, and docs already warn that `present` does not prove a gate.

**EVIDENCE:** Guards checked — `check_deliverable` (delivery.rs:485-518) independently verifies declared deliverables on disk and is not bypassed; `verify_changes` early-returns `None` for non-write-capable workers at :643-645 (expected). No `tracing::warn!`/`error!` exists on the `capture_for_handle` `?` chain (delivery.rs:192-215) or in `git()`/`git_output()` (delivery.rs:50-57); `checked` (mod.rs:8168) is an idempotency flag, not a "git available" receipt. Relevant test `delivery_tests.rs:659-776` covers `checked` idempotency, not git-unavailable verification.

**FIX:** Give `DeliveryEvidence` an explicit signal for "baseline unavailable" (e.g. keep `checked` but add a `verification_note`/status field at capture time) and have `compute_delivery_verification` emit a `verification_incomplete` status with a summary naming the failed git step instead of letting `changed = None` collapse to "no mismatch". Concretely, branch on `let Some(changed) = changed else { ... }` at delivery.rs:647 and, when `baseline` was expected but could not be captured, log `tracing::warn!(target: "subagent", ...)` in `capture_for_handle` and surface it in the stored summary.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** Smallest test: a write-capable worker in a non-git temp workspace whose summary claims `src/lib.rs` changed but declares no deliverables; assert stored `verification.status` is a degraded/incomplete value (not `self_report_only`/`deliverables_present`) and its summary names the missing git baseline. Today `delivery_tests.rs` has no such case.

**CORRECTION:** Precision only: with changed = None, the `undeclared` half still fires via `changed.is_none_or(|c| c.contains(*path))` (delivery.rs:657) when observed_writes exist, so only the "declared but unchanged" half of claim_mismatch is silently skipped, not the whole verdict. The stored status is `self_report_only` (or `deliverables_present`), never a PASS — this is a degraded diagnostic, not a false success; severity stays minor per rubric (narrow edge case, no data loss/authz/secret/panic, surface does not claim success).

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened all cited lines at baseline (HEAD == bc58781ba). delivery.rs:54-56 `git()` = `git_output(root,args)?` + `output.status.success().then_some(output.stdout)` — any spawn failure or non-zero status yields None with no log; delivery.rs:192-210 `capture_for_handle` threads that `?` through `rev-parse --show-toplevel` / `status_paths` / fingerprint collection so a write-capable worker's `baseline` becomes None silently. delivery.rs:217-218 `changed_paths` opens with `let baseline = self.baseline.as_ref()?;`, confirming changed = None on absent baseline. delivery.rs:647-649 `let missing = changed.map(...).unwrap_or_default();` maps None to an empty missing set; delivery.rs:663-664 `if missing.is_empty() && undeclared.is_empty() { return None; }` then produces no claim_mismatch verdict for a summary that declares `src/lib.rs` (parsed at :542-633) when no observed writes exist. Stored verdict: mod.rs:1355-1362 `default_agent_run_verification()` → `self_report_only`; mod.rs:8159-8169 stores it with `checked = true` and no note. DeliveryEvidence has no baseline-unavailable field (delivery.rs:27-35) and no `tracing` call exists on the capture `?` chain, so the claim-check skip leaves no durable trace. Reachability confirmed via mod.rs:8215-8254 → 17369-17415 → delivery.rs:694-705; TRIGGER (write-capable worker, failing/absent git probe, false change claim, no deliverables) is a real system path even if narrow. Guard checked: check_deliverable (delivery.rs:485-518) runs independently, so declared deliverables are not faked — consistent with the finding's own IMPACT.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/delivery.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


## Theme L9 — Resource limits, bounded buffers

Refs: #6554, #6560 (unbounded reads and missing limits).

### R2-L9-01 — followup message no byte cap unbounded queue

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 8 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/coord.rs:441` |
| FINGERPRINT | `coord.rs:441:followup-message-no-byte-cap-unbounded-queue` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | stage-d-verifier |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
coord.rs:441:        let message = input
coord.rs:442:            .get("message")
coord.rs:443:            .or_else(|| input.get("text"))
coord.rs:444:            .and_then(Value::as_str)
coord.rs:445:            .map(str::trim)
coord.rs:446:            .filter(|value| !value.is_empty())
coord.rs:447:            .ok_or_else(|| ToolError::missing_field("message"))?;
mod.rs:8533:        let queue = self.queued_mail.entry(agent_id.clone()).or_default();
mod.rs:8534:        if queue.len() >= MAX_QUEUED_PARENT_MESSAGES {
mod.rs:8535:            return Err(anyhow!(
mod.rs:8536:                "Agent {agent_id} already has {MAX_QUEUED_PARENT_MESSAGES} queued parent messages; wait for it to read them before sending more"
mod.rs:8537:            ));
mod.rs:8538:        }
mod.rs:8539:        queue.push_back(entry);
```

**CALL PATH:** AgentsFollowupTool::execute (`coord.rs:440`) -> `followup_one` (`coord.rs:316-378`) -> `SubAgentManager::followup_child_for_session` (`mod.rs:8729`) -> `followup_child` (`mod.rs:8586`) -> `queue_parent_message` (`mod.rs:8516-8539`) -> `queued_mail` VecDeque (`mod.rs:4061`) and `mpsc::UnboundedSender<SubAgentInput>` (`mod.rs:10098`, sends at `mod.rs:8632-8637`) -> `drive_child_actor` `input_rx` (`engine.rs:2006`, `engine.rs:2070`) -> injected as a User block into the child's next model round.

**TRIGGER:** A caller invokes `agents/followup` with a `message` (or `text`) string of arbitrary size. `execute` only trims it and rejects empty; no character/byte cap exists anywhere along the path. The only bound on the queue is a count of 64 entries (`MAX_QUEUED_PARENT_MESSAGES`, `mod.rs:480`), so 64 arbitrarily large messages can be admitted.

**MECHANISM:** The follow-up path enforces a count limit on `queued_mail` (`mod.rs:8534`) but never measures `text`. `QueuedParentMessage.text` (`mod.rs:8528-8532`) is stored verbatim, then cloned into `SubAgentInput.text` and pushed through an `mpsc::UnboundedSender` (`mod.rs:8632-8637`). The child actor receives it at `engine.rs:2070` and forwards it into a steer, which becomes a User content block in the next model round. No `bytes()`/`chars().count()`/`take()` guard exists on this path; contrast `advisor.rs:217-236` (per-pair truncation) and `mod.rs:219-244` (byte cap before read) elsewhere in the same unit.

**IMPACT:** A large `message` is retained in the manager's in-memory `queued_mail` and duplicated into the per-child unbounded channel; with `all_parked=true` (`coord.rs:479-484`) or `agent_ids` up to 32 (`coord.rs:458-464`) the same payload is cloned across many children. The payload is then fed wholesale into each child's model round, so its size directly drives input-token cost and memory — the exact "cap on the wrong axis" pattern L9 targets. In practice the string originates from a model tool call and is bounded by that model's output tokens, which is why this is minor rather than major; the code itself imposes no bound.

**EVIDENCE:** Guards checked — `coord.rs:441-447` (trim + non-empty only), `coord.rs:458-464` (batch size 1..32), `coord.rs:479-484` (`all_parked` fan-out), `mod.rs:480` (`MAX_QUEUED_PARENT_MESSAGES = 64`), `mod.rs:8516-8539` (count-only queue guard), `mod.rs:8630-8647` (unbounded `tx.send`), `mod.rs:10098` (`mpsc::unbounded_channel()`), `engine.rs:2006`/`2070` (consumer). No test in the 15-file manifest asserts a byte cap on follow-up message text.

**FIX:** Validate `message` in `AgentsFollowupTool::execute` (or in `queue_parent_message`) against a fixed byte/character budget before constructing `QueuedParentMessage`, e.g. `let max = 16 * 1024; if message.len() > max { return Err(ToolError::invalid_input(...)) }`, mirroring the `MAX_RESIDENT_CONTEXT_BYTES` pre-check at `mod.rs:219-226`. Optionally cap the aggregate byte depth of a `queued_mail` queue, not just its entry count.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** Add a unit test calling `AgentsFollowupTool::execute` with a `message` larger than the chosen limit and asserting `invalid_input` before any `queued_mail` entry is created; a second test should assert that 64 small messages still queue (count cap unchanged).

**CORRECTION:** none

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened the cited code at bc58781ba and traced the whole path. `coord.rs:441-447` on `message` reads only `.get("message").or_else(|| input.get("text")).and_then(Value::as_str).map(str::trim).filter(|value| !value.is_empty())` — trim and non-empty only, no byte/char cap; the tool schema at `coord.rs:425` is `"message": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1}` with no `maxLength`. Batch fan-out is real: `coord.rs:458-464` accepts `agent_ids` 1..32 and `coord.rs:479+` handles `all_parked`, and `execute` loops `for target in targets { ... self.followup_one(&target, message, context) }` cloning the same `message` to each. Downstream, `mod.rs:8528-8531` stores `QueuedParentMessage { text, ... }` verbatim; `mod.rs:8533-8539` guards only `if queue.len() >= MAX_QUEUED_PARENT_MESSAGES { ... }` (count, defined at `mod.rs:480`) before `queue.push_back(entry)` — no size check. `mod.rs:8632-8637` clones `mail.text` into `SubAgentInput` and `tx.send(...)` on the `mpsc::UnboundedSender` (`mod.rs:10098` `mpsc::unbounded_channel()`); the consumer `drive_child_actor` at `engine.rs:2070` forwards `input.0.text.clone()` into `permit.send_with_outcome(...)` as a steer into the child's next model round. No `bytes()`/`chars().count()`/`take()` guard exists on this path, while the same unit does cap bytes elsewhere (`mod.rs:219-226` `metadata.len() > MAX_RESIDENT_CONTEXT_BYTES`), confirming the "cap on the wrong axis" is real. Mechanism and reachability both confirmed; severity stays minor because the payload originates from a model tool call and is therefore bounded in practice by that model's output tokens — the code itself imposes no bound, exactly as the finding states.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/coord.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


## Theme L11 — Async blocking and budget discipline

Refs: #6553 and the #6149 blocking-call rule.

### R2-L11-01 — artifact mutex held across blocking transcript io

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 8 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/engine.rs:1360` |
| FINGERPRINT | `engine.rs:1360:artifact-mutex-held-across-blocking-transcript-io` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | verifier-R2-L11-2026-11-22 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
        let output = {
            let mut artifact = self.artifact.lock().await;
            let writer = artifact
                .as_mut()
                .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!("child transcript writer is unavailable"))?;
            writer.append_messages(&[], true)?;
            let messages = super::load_subagent_transcript_artifact(
                &writer.state_root,
                &self.authority.owner_agent_id,
            )?;
```

**CALL PATH:** drive_child_actor (engine.rs:2002) -> job.capture_activation_output (engine.rs:2286) -> self.artifact.lock().await (engine.rs:1360) -> writer.append_messages (engine.rs:1364) -> load_subagent_transcript_artifact (engine.rs:1365) -> fs::OpenOptions::open + read_to_string (mod.rs:13400-13403, 13383-13386)

**TRIGGER:** A child turn completes while other sub-agents are active; capture_activation_output runs on a Tokio worker thread for every child that produced streamed text.

**MECHANISM:** capture_activation_output is an async fn invoked directly from drive_child_actor, which runs on the Tokio runtime (engine.rs:2286 has a plain `.await`, not spawn_blocking). It holds the tokio Mutex guard `artifact` across several synchronous `std::fs` operations: writer.append_messages (lines 1364 and 1393) and load_subagent_transcript_artifact (line 1365), the latter opening a state file with fs::OpenOptions::new().open() (mod.rs:13400-13403) and reading up to MAX_SUBAGENT_STATE_BYTES (16 MiB) with read_to_string (mod.rs:13383-13386). These blocking calls execute inline on the Tokio worker while the mutex is held.

**IMPACT:** When several children finish turns concurrently, multiple Tokio worker threads block on disk I/O instead of polling other tasks. The engine's async runtime is starved for the duration of each transcript open/read (up to 16 MiB) and append, delaying tool-result delivery, UI events and cancellation across the whole session. This is the "sync work inline on Tokio" class tracked by #6553; no data is lost, so severity is minor.

**EVIDENCE:** No spawn_blocking wraps this call path — grep for spawn_blocking in engine.rs returns no hits. The sibling callers of the same blocking helpers DO use spawn_blocking (mod.rs:16254 DeliveryEvidence::capture_for_handle; mod.rs:17312 changed_paths/checkpoint_uncommitted; mod.rs:17395 compute_delivery_verification; mod.rs:16361 spawn_prep_blocking), which shows the codebase treats this I/O as blocking elsewhere. load_subagent_transcript_artifact is a plain sync `fn` (mod.rs:13396-13409), confirmed blocking. No test covers the threading of this path; existing tests only assert the resulting output value.

**FIX:** Move the synchronous transcript work off the Tokio runtime: capture the needed inputs (writer state_root, owner_agent_id, streamed_text, admission index, stop reason), run the append + load + selection inside tokio::task::spawn_blocking, and return only the derived ChildActivationOutput to record_child_output. Do not hold `artifact` across the spawn_blocking await; serialize the writer mutation inside the blocking closure or use a blocking mutex confined to that closure.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** A test that spawns a task holding a deliberately slow/blocking transcript read and asserts that an unrelated tokio task makes progress would catch reintroduction; none exists. Static check: grep that capture_activation_output body contains no `.append_messages`/`load_subagent_transcript_artifact` outside a spawn_blocking closure.

**CORRECTION:** Child EVIDENCE line "grep for spawn_blocking in engine.rs returns no hits" is inaccurate — engine.rs:1196, 1746, 2311 do contain spawn_blocking. Correct statement: none of those sites wraps capture_activation_output or its two blocking helpers; the substantive mechanism is unaffected.

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened engine.rs:1348-1424 at baseline bc58781ba (HEAD == baseline). At 1360 `let mut artifact = self.artifact.lock().await;` acquires the tokio Mutex; within the same block `writer.append_messages(&[], true)?;` (1364) and `super::load_subagent_transcript_artifact(&writer.state_root, &self.authority.owner_agent_id)?;` (1365) run while the guard is live (held until the block ends at 1412). append_messages (mod.rs:12827-12841) calls append_private_subagent_transcript (mod.rs:13436-13451): fs::OpenOptions::open (13465) and `file.sync_all()` (13448) — synchronous fs. load_subagent_transcript_artifact (mod.rs:12902-12907) -> load_subagent_transcript_projection (12921-12928) -> read_subagent_state_file (13371-13393): open_subagent_state_file (fs::OpenOptions::open, 13400-13403) and `file.take(MAX_SUBAGENT_STATE_BYTES + 1).read_to_string(&mut raw)?` (13385-13386, 16 MiB cap at 13369). Both are plain sync `fn`s, so blocking disk I/O runs inline on the Tokio worker under the artifact mutex. capture_activation_output is `async fn` (1348) reached with a plain `.await` at engine.rs:2286 in drive_child_actor's settle path (drive_child_actor defined 2002), with no spawn_blocking around this call path. Fact (blocking fs under a held tokio Mutex) and impact (worker starvation/contention, no data loss) confirmed independently. Severity minor and confidence 8 unchanged per §6.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/engine.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


### R2-L11-02 — artifact mutex held across await

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 8 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/engine.rs:1446` |
| FINGERPRINT | `engine.rs:1446:artifact-mutex-held-across-await` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | verifier-R2-L11-2026-11-22 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
        let mut artifact = self.artifact.lock().await;
        if self.authority.runtime.cancel_token.is_cancelled() {
            // `project` has durably synced this exact Core Session and updated
            // the captured worker. Return that checkpoint rather than discarding
            // it while projecting the cancellation result.
            let checkpoint = self
                .authority
                .runtime
                .manager
                .read()
                .await
                .get_result(&self.authority.owner_agent_id)?
```

**CALL PATH:** drive_child_actor (engine.rs:2002) -> job.finish (engine.rs:1437) -> self.artifact.lock().await (engine.rs:1446) -> insert_subagent_full_transcript_handle(...).await (engine.rs:1484-1498) -> budget_work_preservation_note(...).await (engine.rs:1538-1543) -> write_digest_artifact(...).await (engine.rs:1548-1553)

**TRIGGER:** A child reaches a terminal state (done, interrupted or budget-exhausted) and finish() finalizes it.

**MECHANISM:** ChildJob::finish acquires the tokio Mutex `artifact` at line 1446 and holds that guard across at least seven subsequent `.await` points: manager.read().await (1455, 1503, 1527), insert_subagent_full_transcript_handle(...).await (1498), budget_work_preservation_note(...).await (1543), and write_digest_artifact(...).await (1553). The guard is not dropped until finish returns at line 1568. budget_work_preservation_note internally runs spawn_blocking and write_digest_artifact performs a spawn_blocking file write (budget_handback.rs:72), so a Tokio mutex is held while the runtime dispatches blocking work and waits.

**IMPACT:** Holding a tokio Mutex across await serializes all access to the same child's transcript artifact for the whole finalization window. Any concurrent task needing that artifact (for example capture_activation_output on the same job, F-01) blocks until finish completes, including the duration of the budget-handback blocking I/O. Under many finishing children and a saturated runtime this extends cancellation and delivery latency. This is the "lock across .await" anti-pattern named in the L11 card and tracked by #6553; it is a contention/scalability defect, not data loss, so severity is minor.

**EVIDENCE:** The lock acquisition (1446) and all cited awaits are in the same function body as read from the file; no explicit `drop(artifact)` occurs before the return at 1568. Awaited helpers that receive `artifact` take `&mut` (lines 1469, 1492) and do not re-lock it, so this is contention rather than a proven self-deadlock. No test asserts lock scope; existing finish tests assert result/status values only.

**FIX:** Scope the artifact guard to the synchronous mutations only: perform insert_subagent_full_transcript_handle's artifact write under a short-lived lock, drop it, then run the manager reads and budget-handback awaits without the guard. If artifact must be passed to a helper that awaits, clone the minimal owned state out under the lock and drop before awaiting.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** A test with a task waiting on `artifact.lock()` that must acquire within a bounded time while finish() is suspended on a slow awaited helper would catch reintroduction; none exists. Static check: assert no `.await` appears between the line 1446 lock and an explicit drop.

**CORRECTION:** Child CALL PATH names drive_child_actor (engine.rs:2002) as the direct caller of job.finish, but finish() is never invoked in engine.rs; the actual callers are core/engine/child_host.rs:238/322/368. The finding's site and mechanism are unaffected by this corrected hop.

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened engine.rs:1437-1569 at baseline bc58781ba (HEAD == baseline). At 1446 `let mut artifact = self.artifact.lock().await;` acquires the tokio Mutex; the guard is held across awaits at 1455-1456 (manager.read()), 1474 (cancelled_subagent_result(...).await), 1498 (insert_subagent_full_transcript_handle(...).await), 1503-1504 and 1527-1528 (manager.read().await), 1543 (budget_work_preservation_note(...).await) and 1553 (write_digest_artifact(...).await). The guard is passed as `&mut artifact` (1469) and `artifact.as_mut()` (1492); no explicit `drop(artifact)` occurs before the function returns at 1568. write_digest_artifact itself does `tokio::task::spawn_blocking(...).await` while this mutex is held (budget_handback.rs:65-78, specifically 72 and 78) — the documented "lock across .await" anti-pattern (L11/#6553). Reachability shown through the three terminal finalizers in core/engine/child_host.rs:238 (cancelled), 322 (budget exhausted) and 368 (normal completion), each calling `job.finish(...).await`; ChildJob::finish is defined at engine.rs:1437. Contention rather than proven self-deadlock: awaited helpers take `&mut artifact` and do not re-lock it; no data loss, so severity minor. Confidence 8 unchanged per §6.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/engine.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


## Theme L12 — Platform, Unicode, display width, locale

Refs: #7048, #6953, #7093, #7071 (platform and Unicode).

### R2-L12-01 — sanitize nonascii branch slug collision

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 8 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/worktree.rs:526` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/worktree.rs:526:sanitize-nonascii-branch-slug-collision` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | stage-d-verifier-R2-L12 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
528     for ch in input.chars() {
529         let normalized = if ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {
530             ch.to_ascii_lowercase()
531         } else if matches!(ch, '-' | '_' | '.') {
532             ch
533         } else {
534             '-'
535         };
536         if normalized == '-' && slug.ends_with('-') {
537             continue;
538         }
539         slug.push(normalized);

544     let slug = slug.trim_matches(['-', '.', '_']).to_string();
545     if slug.is_empty() {
546         "task".to_string()
547     } else {
```

**CALL PATH:** create_isolated_worktree (worktree.rs:104) -> resolve_worktree_path (worktree.rs:389) -> branch_worktree_slug (worktree.rs:501) -> sanitize_worktree_slug_within (worktree.rs:526)

**TRIGGER:** two workers spawned with distinct caller-supplied non-ASCII branch names that sanitize to the same short ASCII slug and no explicit worktree_path, e.g. branch "功能A" and "功能B" both become "a"; branch "功能" alone becomes "task".

**MECHANISM:** `sanitize_worktree_slug_within` maps every non-ASCII character to `-`, and the consecutive-dash suppression at 536-538 collapses a whole CJK or Cyrillic branch name into a single dash; `trim_matches` at 544 removes it and line 546 substitutes the literal `task`. The hash disambiguation added for long branches (`branch_worktree_slug`, lines 501-516) only runs when the sanitized slug differs from the `usize::MAX` cut, which never happens for a short all-non-ASCII name, so distinct Unicode branch names map to the same worktree directory.

**IMPACT:** A user working in a non-Latin script who delegates two workers on branches such as `功能A` and `功能B` gets the same default worktree path; the second `ensure_worktree_path_unlinked` / `provision_worktree` call fails on the existing checkout or reuses the first worker's directory. The user sees a spawn failure with no explanation that the branch name was the cause, and has no way to express the branch in their own script.

**EVIDENCE:** `resolve_worktree_path` (worktree.rs:420) uses `branch_worktree_slug(branch)` when no path is supplied; `create_isolated_worktree` (worktree.rs:111-115) takes `request.branch` from the caller and only validates git branch syntax, which permits UTF-8 names. The collision test at worktree.rs:626-645 covers two long ASCII branches sharing a prefix and explicitly asserts a short branch keeps its plain slug; no test covers non-ASCII input. Byte slicing in this file (`worktree.rs:470`, `:475`, `:514`) is guarded by `str::get`/ASCII sanitization and is not the mechanism here.

**FIX:** When the sanitized slug has no ASCII alphanumeric content, still append the short hash of the full branch name (the same suffix path used for long slugs at lines 506-516), e.g. detect `slug == "task"` with a non-ASCII original and feed the hash suffix; alternatively derive the slug from the branch's Unicode characters with a reversible ASCII encoding so distinct scripts cannot collapse.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** Extend `long_explicit_branches_sharing_a_prefix_get_distinct_paths` (or add a sibling test) asserting `branch_worktree_slug("功能A") != branch_worktree_slug("功能B")` and that `feature/短名` keeps a stable non-colliding path.

**CORRECTION:** The TRIGGER example is wrong: `sanitize_worktree_slug_within("功能A")` -> `"a"` and `("功能B")` -> `"b"` (the trailing ASCII letters survive), so those two do NOT collide. The collision is real for (a) all-non-ASCII names — "功能", "構造", "таск" all -> "task" — and (b) distinct non-ASCII prefixes with the same ASCII tail — "功能A" and "構造A" both -> "a". Core mechanism and impact stand; only the illustrative example is corrected.

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened worktree.rs:501-548 at bc58781ba. `sanitize_worktree_slug_within` maps every non-ASCII char to '-' (`else { '-' }` at :534), collapses consecutive dashes (:536-538), trims (:544), and substitutes `"task"` when the result is empty (:545-546). `branch_worktree_slug` appends a hash suffix only when `slug != sanitize_worktree_slug_within(branch, usize::MAX)` (:503-505); an all-non-ASCII name yields `"task"` under both caps, so no hash is added and distinct Unicode names collide. Reachability shown: `branch` is caller-supplied via `worktree_branch`/`branch` (mod.rs:22030-22040), `validate_git_branch_name` uses `git check-ref-format --branch` (worktree.rs:346-360) which accepts UTF-8, and with no explicit `path` `resolve_worktree_path` returns `default_root.join(branch_worktree_slug(branch))` (:420). Two such branches share one path; `provision_worktree` runs `git worktree add -b <branch> -- <path>` (lane/src/worktree.rs:103-113), which fails when the path is already a worktree. Mechanism + impact independently confirmed.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/worktree.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.

# config: 6 verified defects from R15 (baseline bc58781ba)

## How to read this document (terms used below)

- **R<number>** — review unit, one area of the codebase; this document is about R15.
- **L<number>** — one of twelve review lenses (themes) applied to every unit; the table below names each lens.
- **P0 / P1 / P2** — priority rank: P0 highest, P2 lowest. It orders the work, not the severity of a finding.
- **Stage D** — the verification step: every cited line was opened at the baseline, the reachability was traced, and severity was re-scored. **Stage E** — the drafting step that produced this report.
- **Baseline `bc58781ba`** — the exact commit every quote refers to; re-check before acting if `main` has moved.
- **Confirmed** — a verifier opened the cited line, traced a reachable path and kept the finding; rejected and uncertain findings are not here.
- **Public** — this issue contains only findings cleared for a public report; security-class findings are handled through a separate private channel.
- **needs-test** — the written proof is static; a focused test named in the finding would settle the remaining question. No test was run in this audit.
- **Cell** — one audit cell: a review unit crossed with one lens; finding IDs keep the cell number, so a gap in numbering means a candidate was rejected, marked duplicate or routed to the private index.
- **NOT READ** — a scope marker in a cell: that region was not opened, so no claim is made about it.
- **not-applicable / sampled-rescan-passed** — negative-check outcomes: the lens did not apply to that cell, or a sampled rescan found no new signal.
- **Refs #N / UPSTREAM REFS** — existing tracked issues related to the theme or to the exact code site; they are cross-links, never a claim to close or fix those issues. A 500-issue open/closed sweep found no exact duplicate of these findings at the same file and line.
- **CALL PATH, TRIGGER, MECHANISM, IMPACT, EVIDENCE, FIX, REGRESSION CHECK** — copied verbatim from the verified finding file. CALL PATH = how a user reaches the code; TRIGGER = the condition that fires it; MECHANISM = what the code actually does; IMPACT = what the user sees; EVIDENCE = the supporting lines; FIX = recommended change; REGRESSION CHECK = the test that should be added.

Unit R15 (P1 — highest priority is P0, then P1, then P2), typed config, credentials, fail-loud defaults.
