### R15-L4-01 — legacy migration error dropped false receipt

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 7 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/config/src/legacy_root.rs:900` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/config/src/legacy_root.rs:900:legacy-migration-error-dropped-false-receipt` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | needs-test — static proof establishes the dropped error and the plan-derived false receipt; a focused unit test would settle whether the false notice is emitted in a config that still reaches typed loading. |
| VERIFIER | stage-d-R15-L4 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
    let segments: Vec<&str> = path.iter().map(String::as_str).collect();
    if let Some(value) = toml_value_to_edit(&value) {
        // An error means a non-table sits where a table belongs; the typed
        // parse reports that shape, so the document is left as it is.
        let _ = crate::set_config_document_value(doc, &segments, value);
    }
```

**CALL PATH:** ConfigStore::load / migrate_legacy_root_config (config_document.rs:218) -> apply_to_document (legacy_root.rs:766) -> apply_op_to_document (legacy_root.rs:869) -> set_config_document_value (config_document.rs:272) -> Err discarded at legacy_root.rs:900

**TRIGGER:** config.toml carrying a legacy root `api_key` / `base_url` plus a non-table value at the migration destination (for example `providers = "legacy"`), so `set_config_document_value` bails with "`providers` in config.toml must be a table" (config_document.rs:606).

**MECHANISM:** `apply_to_document` builds its receipt from `plan()` before applying anything (legacy_root.rs:773), while `apply_op_to_document` discards a failed `set_config_document_value` with `let _ =` (line 900). For `Op::Move` the source key is removed only when the target set succeeds (lines 876-880), so a failed set leaves the original key in place but the plan-derived receipt still records the move as applied. `changes_file()` reads only those notes (legacy_root.rs:136-140), so `migrate_legacy_root_config` treats the unchanged document as migrated and creates a credential-free backup plus a user-facing notice (config_document.rs:233-238, config_backup.rs:164-165).

**IMPACT:** the user is told legacy keys were moved and a backup is written even though the file is unchanged. Because the typed model has no root `api_key`/`base_url` field (config_toml.rs:18-19), the root credential is never loaded; a later normalized save serializes a model without it and can drop the key from disk. Blast radius is narrow: a scalar at a provider path typically makes typed deserialization fail loudly first, so in many configs the false notice is the only visible effect.

**EVIDENCE:** `changes_file()` (legacy_root.rs:136-140) derives from `notes`, not an applied-document diff; `set_config_document_value` really errors on a non-table parent (config_document.rs:603-608); no post-apply check re-validates the document against the receipt. The sibling `Op::Remove` at line 892 also drops its error, but that path only errors on an empty segment list and is effectively benign. Tests at legacy_root/tests.rs:334-399 exercise migration; whether this exact type-conflicted destination is covered was not checked (no test run in this cell).

**FIX:** have `apply_op_to_document` return `Result<()>` and propagate the `set_config_document_value` error (naming the conflicting path) to `apply_to_document`; emit `Moved`/`GuessedProvider` notes and set `changes_file()` only for ops that actually landed. In `migrate_legacy_root_config`, do not queue the "moved" notice when an op failed.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** unit test in crates/config/src/legacy_root/tests.rs feeding a document with a root `api_key` and a scalar at `providers`, asserting the applied document still holds the root key and that the receipt does not claim a move (no test run here).

**CORRECTION:** (1) The child's QUOTE at legacy_root.rs:900 is in the Op::Set/Op::SetIfAbsent arm; the failure governing the claimed Op::Move trigger is at lines 876-880 — the error is not literally dropped with `let _ =`, it is collapsed into `landed = false`. The false-receipt consequence is the same. (2) The literal TRIGGER as written (top-level `providers = "legacy"` plus root `api_key`) is NOT reachable via `codewhale config migrate`: `pub providers: ProvidersToml` (config_toml.rs:64) makes typed deserialization fail, `ConfigStore::load` propagates that error (config_store.rs:164-170), and the CLI exits at cli/src/lib.rs:2517-2532 before `Commands::Config` dispatch at 2858. The child's CONFIRMATION: needs-test is therefore resolved from code: typed load rejects EARLIER at startup, not later. (3) The reachable case is profile-scoped legacy keys with a scalar at `profiles.<name>.providers`; impact there is a false "moved" notice plus a spurious credential-free backup and identical-content rewrite — NOT the claimed key-drop on a later normalized save (a typed save would drop the whole unknown `profiles` section, a separate behavior not established by this site). Narrowed accordingly; severity stays minor.

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened at baseline bc58781ba (HEAD = baseline). Mechanism is real: `let (ops, receipt) = plan(&table, Mode::Document(prefer));` (legacy_root.rs:773) builds the receipt BEFORE any op is applied; the Op::Move arm at legacy_root.rs:876-880 does `let landed = written.is_some_and(|value| crate::set_config_document_value(doc, &segments, value).is_ok()); if landed { apply_op_to_document(doc, Op::Remove(from)); ... }` — a failed set only flips `landed`, emits no note and surfaces no error; `changes_file()` (legacy_root.rs:136-140) reads only `notes`; `set_config_document_value` really bails on a non-table parent with ``PathLookup::Create => bail!("`{segment}` in config.toml must be a table")`` (config_document.rs:606). With a false `changes_file()`, `migrate_legacy_root_config` still writes the backup and persists (config_document.rs:233-238), and the CLI prints every receipt line (cli/src/lib.rs:5829-5831) — `LegacyRootNote::Moved` renders "moved top-level {}{} to [{to}]" (legacy_root.rs:219-224). Reachability: `plan()` iterates `profiles` (legacy_root.rs:452-469) and `ConfigToml` has no `profiles` field and no `deny_unknown_fields` (config_toml.rs:16-17), so a config with `profiles.<name>.api_key` plus a scalar `profiles.<name>.providers` survives typed loading, `config migrate` reaches the site, the set fails at the scalar parent, yet the receipt claims the move landed.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/config/src/legacy_root.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


**CALL PATH:** crates/tui/src/lib.rs:15483 migrate_config_if_needed -> config_migration.rs:44 -> :52 reject_path_symlink -> :53 primary.exists() -> :62 std::fs::read(&legacy) -> :63 persistence::atomic_write(&primary, &contents) -> persistence.rs:75 tmp.persist(path) (replacing rename)

**TRIGGER:** first launch with legacy ~/.deepseek/config.toml present, primary ~/.codewhale/config.toml absent and CODEWHALE_HOME unset. Two instances start concurrently (the codebase acknowledges shared homes at persistence.rs:68), or a user/agent writes the primary config in the window between the exists() check and the replacing rename.

**MECHANISM:** the `primary.exists()` guard at :53 and the publish at :63 are not atomic with each other — no lock, `create_new` or generation fence spans them. `persistence::atomic_write` publishes with `tmp.persist(path)` (persistence.rs:75), a replacing rename that clobbers any file created at `primary` after the check. `reject_path_symlink` (:52) only refuses a symlink; it does not fence a concurrent creator. The doc invariant at :43 ("Never overwrites an existing primary config") is enforced solely by the racy `exists()` check. This is the check-then-use / two-process migration race that L6 (#6557) explicitly names.

**IMPACT:** a second first-launch instance, or a user/agent write landing in the window, can have its freshly created `~/.codewhale/config.toml` silently replaced with the legacy bytes. On first-run this can drop a just-added credential or model setting. Bounded: both racing migrators write identical legacy contents, the window is the few instructions between :53 and :63, and explicit `CODEWHALE_HOME` skips the path entirely, so minor rather than major.

**EVIDENCE:** `tmp.persist(path)` with retry loop in persistence.rs:73-104 (replacing rename, not no-clobber); no `create_new`, `OpenOptions::create_new`, lock file or generation counter anywhere in config_migration.rs (full file read); call site `migrate_config_if_needed()` at crates/tui/src/lib.rs:15483; shared-home acknowledgement at persistence.rs:68 ("Two Codewhale instances share one home"). HEAD equals baseline bc58781ba; file read from the baseline tree.

**FIX:** make the check and publish one primitive — add a no-replace mode to `atomic_write` that maps the destination-`AlreadyExists` error to a no-op ("already migrated"), or hold the config write lock across `exists()` and publish. Do not rely on `exists()` alone.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** a test that pre-creates the primary config between the `exists()` check and the write (or races two `migrate_config_if_needed()` calls) and asserts the primary is not overwritten with legacy contents.

**CORRECTION:** none

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened baseline config_migration.rs:44-74 directly. `if primary.exists() { return Ok(None); }` at :53 is followed by `persistence::atomic_write(&primary, &contents)` at :63 with nothing atomic between them. Opened persistence.rs:40-128: `atomic_write` creates a temp file then `match tmp.persist(path)` at :75 — a replacing rename that overwrites an existing destination (retry loop :73-104, fallback `rewrite_in_place` :100). Reachability confirmed at crates/tui/src/lib.rs:15483 (TUI startup, first launch after config load). This is the L6 check-then-use / two-process migration race; the only guard (`reject_path_symlink`, :52) does not fence a concurrent creator, and the `:43` "Never overwrites" invariant is unsupported under concurrency. Severity kept minor: both racers write identical legacy bytes and the window is short; impact is a static inference, not a reproduced loss.

The temp file's bytes are fsynced and the rename succeeds, so the caller receives `Ok(())`; if the machine loses power or crashes before the parent directory's metadata is flushed, the rename can be lost and the file keeps its old contents (or the new file vanishes) even though success was reported.

**MECHANISM:** `atomic_write` fsyncs the temp file's contents (64-66) but never fsyncs the parent directory after `tmp.persist(path)` performs the rename (75). A rename becomes durable only once the directory entry is flushed; returning `Ok(())` at 76 is therefore a receipt that can outlive its own effect. The same gap is present in the independent writer at permissions.rs:474-485 (file `sync_all` at 477-480, `persist` at 481-484, no directory sync).

**IMPACT:** This is the shared write primitive for setup-owned config state (setup_state.rs:685, user_constitution.rs:712, config_document.rs:517, config_backup.rs:76/104/182/219, redaction.rs:256, config_migration.rs:63). After a crash in the window following a successful save, a user can see their setup progress, permission grants, notification edits, or scrubbed backup revert to the pre-write state while the UI/log reported success — a silent false success with config-level blast radius.

**EVIDENCE:** The whole `atomic_write` body (persistence.rs:39-105) was read; its only `sync_all` is on the temp file. The correct pattern exists in the same crate: private_directory.rs:928-930 calls `self.directory_handle.sync_all()` immediately after its `renameat`/`linkat` publish (and again at 2194 and 3026). Tempfile's `persist` performs only the rename — no directory flush. Tests at persistence.rs:395-422 check retry classification and permissions; no test exercises directory-entry durability. Relation to #6555 ("Durable writes not crash-atomic") is thematic only: the CANDIDATES slot carried only issue numbers, with no per-file candidate ids checked in under docs/audit, so no CLASS known:#N mapping was possible.

**FIX:** After `tmp.persist(path)` succeeds, open the parent directory and `sync_all()` it before returning `Ok(())`, propagating any error (mirror private_directory.rs:928-930). Apply the same step in permissions.rs after line 484. Use the repository's parent-sync helper if the dependency direction permits (codewhale_util::files::sync_parent, used at engine/src/session_manager.rs:3088-3098); otherwise a local `File::open(parent)?.sync_all()` is sufficient. The fallback `rewrite_in_place` (persistence.rs:114-128) already fsyncs the file and should flush the directory too.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** None available in scope — no crash/power-loss harness; existing tests assert only content, permissions and retry classification. Smallest useful guard is a static assertion that both write paths sync the parent directory after publishing, or a fault-injection test that drops the directory flush and asserts the write is not reported as committed.

**CORRECTION:** none

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened crates/config/src/persistence.rs at baseline bc58781ba. Lines 64-66 read `tmp.as_file().sync_all()` — this flushes only the staged file's bytes; lines 75-76 read `match tmp.persist(path) { Ok(_) => return Ok(()) }`, publishing the rename and immediately returning success. A grep of persistence.rs finds `sync_all` only at 65 (temp file) and 125 (fallback in-place write); no parent-directory `sync_all`/`sync_parent` exists anywhere, and tempfile's `persist` is a rename with no directory flush (same primitive verified from tempfile 3.27.0 source in sibling cell R16/L10). On POSIX a rename is crash-durable only after the containing directory is fsynced, so the `Ok(())` receipt can outlive its effect. Reachability traced through production callers: SetupState::save_to (setup_state.rs:683-686) and UserConstitution::save_to (user_constitution.rs:711-713) call atomic_write_json (persistence.rs:160-164) -> atomic_write; config_document::persist_locked (513-517), config_backup (76), redaction (256) and permissions.rs:477-485 call it directly. No caller supplies the missing directory sync; the correct in-crate pattern is private_directory.rs:928-930 (`self.directory_handle.sync_all()` after publish). Severity held at major under the rubric's "silent false success" row: a user-visible config save reports success while a crash can revert it; not critical because the impact is durability of local config state, not a secret leak, corruption of existing data, authz bypass or injection. Confidence 8 kept — motivating lines quoted and mechanism traced, with the residual that the loss window depends on filesystem crash semantics.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/config/src/persistence.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.


### R15-L10-02 — migration backup written without fsync before durable migration

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| FINAL SEVERITY | minor |
| FINAL CONFIDENCE | 7 |
| VENUE | public |
| LOCATION | `crates/config/src/user_constitution.rs:957` |
| FINGERPRINT | `crates/config/src/user_constitution.rs:957:migration-backup-written-without-fsync-before-durable-migration` |
| DUPLICATES | none |
| UPSTREAM REFS | none |
| CONFIRMATION | static |
| VERIFIER | verifier-R15-L10 |
| DATE | 2026-11-22 |

QUOTE — copied from the verified finding file (baseline `bc58781ba`; code lines are verbatim):

```text
956:                 let backup = backup_path_for(path);
957:                 std::fs::write(&backup, raw.as_bytes()).with_context(|| {
958:                     format!("failed to write migration backup to {}", backup.display())
959:                 })?;
960:                 constitution.save_to(path)?;
961:                 receipt.backup_path = Some(backup);
962:                 Ok(MigrationOutcome::Migrated {
```

**CALL PATH:** user constitution migration -> UserConstitution::migrate_file (user_constitution.rs:936) -> std::fs::write(backup, raw) (user_constitution.rs:957) -> constitution.save_to(path) (user_constitution.rs:960 -> 711-713 atomic_write_json) -> MigrationOutcome::Migrated receipt with backup_path (user_constitution.rs:961-965)

**TRIGGER:** A legacy constitution file is migrated. The rollback backup is written with a plain `std::fs::write` (no fsync), then the constitution is persisted fsync-first through `atomic_write_json`, and a `Migrated` receipt advertising the backup path is returned. If power is lost or the machine crashes after the new file is durable but before the backup's page-cache contents reach disk, the new constitution survives while the backup is empty/missing; `rollback_file` (975-983) can no longer restore the pre-migration bytes.

**MECHANISM:** The backup is the sole rollback artifact for a migration, but at line 957 it is written without `sync_all` and without atomic publish, so its durability is not established before line 960 persists the migrated file and line 961 attaches it to the success receipt. The two writes have opposite durability guarantees: the migrated file is fsynced by `atomic_write_json` (711-713), the backup is not. A crash between them inverts the intended safety contract — the state that changed is durable, the state that would undo it is not.

**IMPACT:** A user who accepts a constitution migration and then wants to roll back (for example, the migrated bounded form dropped fields they cared about) discovers the advertised backup is missing or truncated. The migration receipt said the rollback path existed; after a crash it does not, which is a silent false success for a data-recovery mechanism. `rollback_file` also restores with non-atomic `std::fs::write` (979) and discards the backup with `.ok()` (981), compounding a partial-restore window.

**EVIDENCE:** Lines 936-983 were read in full. `save_to` at 711-713 delegates to `persistence::atomic_write_json`; `atomic_write` fsyncs the temp file (persistence.rs:64-66) but not the parent directory (F-01). No fsync, `sync_parent`, or atomic-write wrapper exists around line 957. Relation to #6555 ("Durable writes not crash-atomic") is thematic only: the CANDIDATES slot carried only issue numbers, with no per-file candidate ids checked in under docs/audit, so no CLASS known:#N mapping was possible.

**FIX:** Write the backup through `crate::persistence::atomic_write` (which fsyncs the file before returning) instead of `std::fs::write`, and flush the parent directory after publishing so the backup entry is durable before `save_to` runs. In `rollback_file`, restore through `atomic_write` as well and log — do not silently drop — a failed `remove_file` so a failed cleanup does not masquerade as a completed rollback.

**REGRESSION CHECK:** None available in scope — no crash-injection harness. Smallest useful guard is a test that fails if the backup write path is not the fsyncing `atomic_write`, plus a fault-injection case that drops the backup flush and asserts the migrated file is not reported as committed with a usable backup.

**CORRECTION:** none

**VERIFICATION (reviewer's own check):** Opened crates/config/src/user_constitution.rs at baseline bc58781ba. Line 957 is `std::fs::write(&backup, raw.as_bytes())` — no sync_all, no temp file, no atomic publish; line 960 `constitution.save_to(path)?` persists the migrated file (save_to at 711-713 -> atomic_write_json -> atomic_write, which fsyncs the temp file at persistence.rs:64-66 but not the parent directory, see F-01); line 961 `receipt.backup_path = Some(backup)` attaches the backup to the success receipt. The backup is the sole rollback artifact, so a crash between 957 and 960 can leave a durable migrated file with an empty/absent backup. rollback_file at 975-983 compounds it: line 979 restores with plain `std::fs::write` and line 981 discards cleanup failure via `.ok()`. Reachability confirmed through the user-facing `/constitution migrate` and `/constitution rollback` commands: constitution.rs:82/:84 dispatch to migrate_text/rollback_text, which call migrate_file (299) and rollback_file (370). Severity held at minor: the trigger needs a power loss in a narrow window plus a later user rollback attempt, and the migrated constitution itself stays intact — a narrow edge case with a workaround rather than a general config break. Not a security class (no secret leak, authz bypass, injection or SSRF), so public venue. Confidence 7 kept — quote and call path confirmed statically; no crash-injection harness exercises the window.

**LOCAL TEST:** `scripts/dev-test.sh crates/config/src/user_constitution.rs` — run after adding the regression test named above.

prs.title: feat(workflow): verify sealed candidates with an isolated host oracle
prs.body:
Refs #7250
Extracted from #7262

This is the maintainer-requested, opt-in verified evaluator slice. The evolutionary Draft PR remains separate and unchanged.

## Evaluator

- Freeze a versioned host spec, clean Git baseline, authorized write/protected scope, trusted public and held-out cases, executable identities, and a Linux bubblewrap capability probe.
- Accept completed Workflow worktrees; seal added/modified/deleted/binary/mode changes and replay from the sealed artifact after the writer worktree is gone.
- Run candidate commands in isolated processes and compare actual JSON output with the host oracle. Receipts bind spec, baseline, oracle, artifact/tree, sandbox and native binary identities. Public PASS requires public-plus-held-out replay.
- Wire the evaluator into the existing `operate_best_of_n` search Workflow only when `args.evaluator` is supplied. Results are `proposal_only`; there is no candidate apply, push, merge, policy genome, or mutation operator.

## Maintainer review fixes

- **Normal-user namespace creation:** the evaluator-specific `RLIMIT_NPROC` is 4096, and the probe reports that effective value. The old 32 limit counted all tasks owned by the Linux user. PID namespace isolation, `--die-with-parent`, cancellation, CPU/time bounds, filesystem/network restrictions and process cleanup remain in place.
- **Published-crate source identity:** the evaluator hashes the actual loaded Workflow source and compares it with a checked-in SHA-256 constant. The repository script path is referenced only by excluded test source. Exact checked-in content is accepted; a modified script fails closed. The update procedure is documented.
- **Evaluation deadline:** the aggregate budget counts active candidate evaluation and replay time, starting after generation. Receipts record effective start, elapsed time, deadline and stop reason; the delayed-generation regression passes.
- **Artifact capture:** a frozen policy records and excludes untracked root `target/` and `__pycache__/` outputs. Tracked and protected files remain checked, legitimate new source remains captured, and out-of-scope writes still fail. Exclusions appear in artifact and receipt provenance.
- **Descendant test and macOS:** the lifecycle test uses a writable in-sandbox marker, a surviving negative control, and timeout/cancellation cleanup checks. The non-Linux `UNSUPPORTED_ISOLATION` branch no longer has the unnecessary-return warning.

## Final validation at `61b889cf6ec10df5c048ef15715dbb272ccacf77`

- [Upstream PR CI](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/actions/runs/43344788042): 10 successful jobs, 12 path-skipped, 0 failed. Workspace format, strict Clippy and Windows all-targets check passed. The PR view also counts the successful triage check.
- [Hosted final-head build](https://github.com/axobase001/DeepSeek-TUI/actions/runs/43345093377): Rocky Linux 8 full CLI build, 9 focused Rust tests, evaluator crate checks and package file listing passed; Windows focused check and 5 tests passed; macOS focused check and strict Clippy passed. The hosted Linux runner lacked bubblewrap, so real isolation was validated separately.
- **Real non-root Linux isolation:** on the 47 VPS, `nobody` (uid 65534) owned 40 preflight tasks. A 32-limit bubblewrap control reproduced the namespace error; 4096 succeeded. All 9 evaluator tests then executed under bubblewrap and passed (113.64 s), including cancellation and descendant cleanup.
- **Native Workflow E2E:** the exact final-head CLI ran a local scripted provider. A false PASS claim failed 2 public cases; the isolated candidate passed 2 public and 3 public-plus-held-out replay cases, ending `proposal_only`. No-evaluator and modified-source rejection controls passed. An independent verifier recomputed 7 case outcomes and 2 sealed tree hashes.
- **Package file set:** [independent run](https://github.com/axobase001/DeepSeek-TUI/actions/runs/43345093627) compiled the exact listed engine files with the repository Workflow script removed, using local sibling 0.10.3 crates. The artifact records this final SHA.

## Evidence and release gate

The [final-head validation report](https://github.com/axobase001/DeepSeek-TUI/blob/experiment/7250-native-evidence/evidence/7250/PR7294_final_61b889c_validation_2026-11-13.md) and [100 KB evidence bundle](https://github.com/axobase001/DeepSeek-TUI/blob/experiment/7250-native-evidence/evidence/7250/CodeWhale_PR7294_Final_61b889c_Evidence_2026-11-13.zip) contain raw non-root/native receipts, the independent verifier, package file-set proof, and the standard package failure log. Historical failures remain in the [earlier evidence bundle](https://github.com/axobase001/DeepSeek-TUI/blob/experiment/7250-native-evidence/evidence/7250/CodeWhale_PR7294_Review_Fixes_Evidence_Lite_2026-11-13.zip). The [final Linux binary artifact](https://github.com/axobase001/DeepSeek-TUI/actions/runs/43345093377/artifacts/14001504445) binds the CLI and Rust test executable used on the VPS.

`cargo package --locked -p codewhale-engine` still exits 101 during dependency resolution: crates.io offers `codewhale-agent` up to 0.10.2, while this workspace requires 0.10.3. The [raw failure artifact](https://github.com/axobase001/DeepSeek-TUI/actions/runs/43345093377/artifacts/14002692655) is preserved. Standard package verification awaits the sibling crate release; the independently compiled package file set validates the removed out-of-crate source reference.

Adds AtmoRouter as a bundled compatible-host descriptor row, in the same shape as the WorldRouter (#7488) and LLMTR (#7450) rows. prs.body: ## What and why Local specialist whales in the Engine, plus two fixes that `main` needs right now. - **`feat(engine)` multi-whale runtime.** The Runtime API serves `/v1/whales`, `/v1/whales/{id}` and a non-destructive `/v1/whales/{id}/recycle`. Each whale lives in `~/.codewhale/whales//{whale.toml,SOUL.md,MEMORY.md}` under `PrivateDirectory` confinement, with `If-Match` revision fencing; `/v1/whale/soul` keeps working. A thread created with `whale_id` loads that whale's SOUL.md, MEMORY.md and model/posture defaults. Write, maintenance and connector-auth tool results carry a structured `metadata.whale_card`, with secrets redacted. The TUI's blocked whale state reads "Failed" (§274 vocabulary). Linear: CW-8276, CW-8277. - **`fix(engine)` Windows whales folder.** On Windows, saving the default whale created the parent `whales` folder without an owner-only ACL, so listing or creating any named whale failed the ownership check. `create_whale` now repairs that folder with `PrivateDirectory::open`; `list_whales` inspects first and repairs only when inspection refuses. Route-test paths are compared by component. `whale_soul.rs` gets a blocking-call budget of 11: it is a synchronous helper, and every async caller reaches it through `owner_work`, which runs it in `spawn_blocking`. - **`chore(credit)`.** Version drift has been failing on `main`: `check-contributor-credit.py` found seven contributors since v0.10.4 missing from the credit surfaces. They are now in the Unreleased CHANGELOG block, a CONTRIBUTORS.md band and `UNRELEASED_CONTRIBUTORS`: @WTFitsmemyself, @NieZhuZhu, @luochen211, @Serendo, @deosiree, @gaord and @Goldloli. `AUTHOR_MAP` maps the unlinked "Hermes-10" commit identity to deosiree. - **`chore(hooks)`.** The landing preflight has been failing on `main` since PR 7500 (`main-landing.yml` 45352584468, 45353470377): the hooks outbox added five `std::fs` sites. All five sit in synchronous helpers that run only inside `spawn_blocking` (`deliver_batch` and `recover_last_seq`), so the budget records them. The Desktop and Platform halves are already on their mains. ## How I tested it - Exact-SHA `ci.yml` on this branch before the last rebase: run 45342192337 on `6adc77ca47`, 50 passed and 3 skipped by design (Windows sharded tests and hosted macOS included). It and the earlier run 45330497586 on `59dc7833e0` were green, but `main` moved during each. On the rebased head: `dev-test.sh engine whale` 54 passed, `dev-test.sh app-server whale` 8 passed. - An independent read-only review of the Windows fix returned LAND. ## Checklist - [x] One focused change per commit, started from current `main` - [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior - [ ] Feature registry: the full suite, including `feature_registry`, passed on this branch; no new `[features]` flag or command is added Written by Claude Opus 5.5 (AI), working with Hmbown. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---

prs.title: perf(engine): cache the item index across processes
prs.body:
## What and why

Opening a thread is every client's first read, and the store can only answer it after a pass over the whole items directory: an item's filename carries only its item id, never its turn. The in-memory index made that a one-time cost per process — the server already warms it at startup — but nothing about the answer outlived the process, so a restarted engine (or any other client) paid it again. Against this store that is the entire open time of the first conversation.

The index is now cached beside the directories it describes (`item-index.json` at the store root) and rebuilt from a directory listing plus only the entries the cache does not hold. The listing decides membership, so a missing, unreadable or out-of-date file costs one full read — what every process used to pay — and never a different answer.

Measured on a 56,132-item store, first index build in a process:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| before | 4.5s |
| after | 102ms |

Four deliberate choices:

- **Ownership is checked where it can change.** A filename is an item id either way, so a record written again under a second turn is invisible to the listing. `save_item`, `save_items_batch` and `remove_item` drop the cache when an id changes hands, reading the record's current owner only when a cache exists. Keeping a stale cache meant a turn that listed an item it no longer had and a turn that could not find one it did.
- **Reading never writes.** Caching is `RuntimeThreadStore::cache_item_index`, called only by the startup warm-up. A `GET` that created a file would break what those routes promise.
- **The cache is not fsynced.** Losing it to a crash costs the next process one full read. The write is a rename over a per-process temporary, so a reader never sees a partial file.
- **The cold pass no longer materializes records** — that part is split into #7522, which this PR is built on.

## Where this came from

A bug fix with no issue: reopening a long conversation after a restart sat on the previous conversation for seconds, with the delay growing with the store.

Split at @Hmbown's suggestion: #7522 carries the one-field projection (mergeable on its own); this PR carries the persisted index and the ownership check that the review asked for.

## How I tested it

```
cargo fmt --all --check                                   # clean
cargo clippy -p codewhale-engine --lib                    # no new warnings
cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib -- runtime_threads::tests
                                                          # 348 passed
cargo test -p codewhale-app-server --lib -- \
  thread_summary_search_does_not_scan_the_whole_store_per_thread \
  thread_summary_listing_never_walks_the_items_directory \
  turn_operation_lookup_is_authenticated_read_only_and_survives_restart
                                                          # 3 passed
```

Regression tests, all in `runtime_threads::tests`: the cache survives a process; it learns only ids written while it was closed; it forgets a deleted item; a damaged or foreign-version file falls back to the directory; a read-only handle never writes; a read leaves the store byte-identical (snapshot before/after); and the two ownership cases — overwritten under another turn, and deleted then recreated under one. Disabling either ownership hook makes its test fail.

`bench_item_index_against_a_real_store` (ignored, takes `CODEWHALE_BENCH_STORE`) reproduces both numbers.

One pre-existing failure, unrelated: `runtime_threads::tests::engine_withdrawal_retires_approval_and_unblocks_queued_events` is flaky on `main` (it fails 2 of 3 runs there and 1 of 3 here; it passes alone). Two other cases in that module need `RUST_MIN_STACK` raised in a debug build, also on `main`.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [x] No user-facing docs or `docs/features.toml` row: this changes how fast a thread opens, not what it does

prs.title: perf(engine): read only the owner field when indexing item records
prs.body:
## What and why

An item's filename carries its id and not its turn, so the store learns which items a turn owns by opening every item record. That pass deserialized each record into `TurnItemRecord` — every string in `detail` and `metadata` included — to read one field, and a single tool result can be hundreds of kilobytes of output.

It now deserializes into a one-field reference (`ItemTurnReference`). The pass still reads the same bytes from disk; what it no longer does is build and drop a full record to answer a question about an id.

Measured on a 55,572-item store, one pass: **~3.9s, unchanged** — the cost is the per-file read, not the parse. The saving is allocation, which matters most on the stores where that pass hurts. This is the extractable, behaviour-preserving piece of #7446.

## Where this came from

Split out of #7446 at @Hmbown's suggestion, so the part with no correctness question can land while the persisted index waits for its ownership check.

## How I tested it

```
cargo fmt --all --check                       # clean
cargo clippy -p codewhale-engine --lib        # no new warnings
cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib -- runtime_threads::tests
                                              # 340 passed
```

`bench_item_index_against_a_real_store` is included (ignored) so the number can be reproduced on any store root:

```
CODEWHALE_BENCH_STORE=/path/to/runtime cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib -- \
  runtime_threads::tests::bench_item_index_against_a_real_store --ignored --nocapture
[bench] index=4.525688709s items=56132 turns=469
```

`engine_withdrawal_retires_approval_and_unblocks_queued_events` fails intermittently in the full-module run on `main` as well (it passes when run alone); that is not this change.

prs.title: fix(hooks): harden lifecycle outbox locking, torn-tail recovery, fsync, and rotation-safe webhook keys
prs.body:
## What and why

Reworked lifecycle outbox split from #7489 per maintainer feedback on #7466:

- **Cross-process seq locking with graceful degradation**: Serializes seq recovery and append under a sibling `<outbox>.lock` file (preventing Windows mandatory byte-range lock `Os { code: 33 }` errors on concurrent readers of the JSONL file). On Unix filesystems without advisory locks (HarmonyOS hmdfs, FUSE, some network mounts), errors classified by `codewhale_util::lock::advisory_locking_unavailable` (and not `is_contention`) degrade cleanly to unlocked append instead of failing.
- **Torn trailing line recovery**: `recover_tail_state_sync` scans backwards past torn or corrupt trailing lines to recover the last valid envelope, and prepends a leading `\n` when EOF does not end in a newline so new records are never glued onto a partial line or wedged permanently.
- **Durability without breaking webhook fan-out**: Calls `file.sync_all()` after flushing the outbox batch, while preserving the existing behavior that webhooks still fire even if local outbox append/fsync fails.
- **Rotation-safe `Idempotency-Key` header**: Uses `codewhale_paths::stable_hex` plus a per-file random UUID nonce (`outbox_nonce` in envelope `extra`, recovered across restarts and rotated to a fresh nonce when the file is missing/rotated), sent as `Idempotency-Key` across retries. Dropped `fnv1a_64`, `default_idempotency_key`, fallback counters, and the `include_str!` source-grep test.

## Where this came from

Part of #7466

## How I tested it

- `cargo test -p codewhale-hooks --lib` — all unit tests pass (including interleaved multi-writer monotonic seqs, torn trailing line recovery, webhook delivery on local write failure, and retry/rotation idempotency-key behavior).
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `python3 scripts/check-dead-code-budget.py`, `python3 scripts/check-blocking-calls-budget.py` — all pass.

prs.title: fix(tui): let a session switch adopt a populated Runtime store
prs.body:
## What this changes

A session switch can now open a conversation whose Runtime store already holds history.

Before, `apply_loaded_session_with_goal` refused any target store with a non-empty `threads/` directory. The check was aimed at the wrong store. A switch never abandons the target — that store stays on disk for whichever process opens it next — and the host keeps holding the one it already has until the switch explicitly releases it. What a switch must not do is release a store that still needs *this* process, which is a property of the store being **left**.

So the check moves:

- `HasDurableWork` stops being a refusal. Only conditions that make the target unusable from here still refuse: a live process holding its lock, an unconfined or non-directory path, or a scope-pinned automation.
- `current_store_is_disposable` (async) asks whether the store being left has work in flight: a loaded engine with an active turn, or a request waiting on a decision that lives only in memory (`has_unsettled_requests`). Finished history is not work.
- A binding whose recorded scope no longer matches its own owner file is stale, not adoptable — that stays on the recover-onto-this-host path.
- `LoadedSessionOutcome` reports the store to adopt; `adopt_runtime_store` settles the old engines, releases the process-owner lock, and starts a new manager with the saved binding.
- The abandoned store goes through `retire_unbound_store_in_background`, which moves an unbound store to `.set-aside/` and refuses one any document still names.

### Why the first version of this was wrong

The initial patch reused `adoption_refusal` to judge the *current* store. That predicate answers "may a host take this store over?", and opening a store writes `owner.json`, `state.json` and the work directories — so a store that has never run a turn already reports `HasDurableWork`. Every switch out of a freshly started host would have been refused. Three existing tests caught it; `ee28d088f` is the correction.

## Verification

```
runtime_store_binding   15 passed, 0 failed   (default 2 MiB test stack)
tui::ui::tests::       941 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored
```

`main` (05a9a62e0) at the same point: 939 passed, and `picker_adoption_keeps_a_store_another_document_binds` overflows at the default stack — that group only passes with `RUST_MIN_STACK=32MiB`. This branch runs all 15 at the default stack.

`52fb7e9d4` fixes that: `adopt_runtime_store` returns a boxed future (it contains `TaskManager::start`, whose state machine inlined into the session-load path), and the exit test boxes each of its two `TaskManager::start` calls separately.

Two new tests:

- `switch_adopts_a_store_holding_finished_history` — a populated target is adopted, and the returned binding names it.
- `switch_allows_leaving_a_store_with_finished_history` — history in the store being left does not block a switch.

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes. Clippy reports pre-existing findings in `client.rs`, `compaction.rs`, `config.rs` and `runtime_threads.rs:13523` — none in the files this PR touches.

## Known limitations

- A turn active on *another thread* in the store being left is not visible to `session_transition_blocked` (it reads the current conversation's panel). `shutdown_and_wait` interrupts it, and the record is marked `Interrupted by process restart`. Naming the switch as the cause would need `interrupt_turn` to take a reason.
- The failure path in `adopt_runtime_store` (manager set to `None`, user told to run `codewhale resume`) has no test coverage.

Refs #6207, #6225, #6418

prs.title: fix(bridges): move Feishu and WeCom turn observation onto bridge-core
prs.body:
## What and why Feishu and WeCom each kept a copy of the turn event loop. The new `observeTurn` in `integrations/bridge-core` now handles that loop for both. It fetches the stream, detects the terminal record (`turnTerminalStatus`), builds the outcome text (`turnOutcomeText`) and saves the cursor. Each bridge passes only its own effects: the progress flush, the approval message and the final reply. - The cursor and the accumulated reply are saved only after a record's effect succeeds. This fixes WeCom, which saved `lastSeq` before sending approvals and replies and never saved `responseText`, so a reattach lost the partial reply. - WeCom now clears `responseText` when a turn starts, the same as Feishu. - DingTalk is unchanged. It already reads events through its durable outbox, which keeps a per-record cursor. ## Where this came from Refs #7477 (R21: "move dingtalk, feishu and wecom onto bridge-core"). Lane 6 of the 0.10.5 audit. This follows #7498, now merged, and is synced to main with a merge commit. Not in this PR: - **R5-L11-04** (#7461), the MCP pool lock held across network awaits. A real fix needs a redesign. `McpConnection::call_method_decided_inner` changes connection state (`state`, `transport`, reply routing) while it waits on the network, and the catalog accessors return `&McpTool` borrowed from the pool. Releasing the outer lock would need a per-connection slot with a catalog snapshot that can be read without that lock. That redesign is still open. - **Audit tracker pass against main `24fb0fa38`**, for the items that earlier comments left open: - #6557 P01-01: still present. `PetLiveTape` in `pet-native.js` rejects only `sequence <= previous`, so it still accepts a forward jump. - #6559 R06-06: fixed on main. `WorkflowPlan::from_config` checks `EmptyWorkflow`, self or missing phase dependencies, and task-result ordering. `Expand.source` and path scopes were not rechecked. - #6559 U01-m2: fixed on main. A malformed history line is kept as text, and loading continues past it. - #6558 R03-05 and #6559 R01-06: the code looks changed (`capture_thread_operation_key`; `auth print-api-key` now uses the runtime resolver), but neither was confirmed end to end. - #6561: covered separately in #7515. ## How I tested it - `bridge-core`: `node --test test/*.test.mjs` ran 80 tests after the main sync: 79 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (a Windows-only test). A new test shows that a failed approval send does not advance the cursor past that record. The same suite runs the WeCom shipping-source SSE and approval test. - `feishu-bridge`: 21 passed, 0 failed. `wecom-bridge`: 23 passed, 0 failed. - Before the sync, `telegram-bridge` passed 40 and `weixin-bridge` passed 59. I did not rerun them after the sync. ## Checklist - [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves) - [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior - [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) ---

prs.title: fix(update): one install-ownership check, one-line update answers, honest rollback
prs.body:
## Summary Lane 2 of #7486 (CW-8377 items 2-5): one install-ownership check, a one-line answer to "can this copy update itself?", honest rollback, and installers that defer to the binary. The release signing key (item 1) is not in this PR. **One ownership check.** `InstallMethod` gains `System` (`/usr/bin`, `/bin`, `/nix/store`, `/gnu/store`, Windows/Scoop/Chocolatey dirs) and `WindowsInstaller` (NSIS layout: `/bin/codewhale` + `Uninstall.exe` + `update-user-path.ps1`). They replace `protected_update_path` (cli/update.rs) and `windows_installer_uninstaller` (cli/update/uninstall.rs), so update, `--check`, stage, auto-update, rollback, doctor, `/update` and uninstall all read `InstallMethod::detect`. `InstallMethod::owner(exe)` is the same check without the `CODEWHALE_INSTALL_METHOD` override; `detect` no longer lets that override claim a package-managed or system copy is self-updatable. The install inventory (`installs::classify`) now uses `owner`, keeping the Cargo receipt check. **One-line answer.** `installs::update_answer(method, exe)` is the single string for `codewhale update`, `doctor`, and the TUI `/update`: ``` This copy updates itself: `codewhale update`. This copy belongs to Cargo, so it cannot update itself; update it with `cargo install codewhale-cli --locked --force --root "/home/u/.cargo"`. ``` `installs::manager_update_command` adds the exact Cargo `--root` / npm `--prefix` (the doctor/update Cargo wording from the inventory). **Honest rollback.** `replace_command_paths` returns whether a previous binary was kept; `Undo: codewhale update --rollback` is printed only then, and only when the newly installed binary's `--rollback` would accept the kept version (the hint is judged against the installed version, not the updater's own; on Hunter's Windows PC a 0.10.3 → 0.10.4 update printed the hint and rollback then refused it). `autoupdate::rollback_blocker` holds the v0.10.3 boundary check once, used by `--rollback` and by doctor (which now says when a kept version cannot be rolled back to). **Installers follow the binary.** `install.sh` (web + archive) and `install.ps1` no longer print "Updates install automatically" unconditionally. `doctor --installs --brief`, which they already run, now prints the installed binary's own update mode from config. **Checked against CW-8377 (Linear).** Items 2-5 and the smaller items are covered; item 1 (release signing key) waits on Hunter. Added after reading the ticket: - pnpm, Bun, Yarn, Volta and mise copies get their own manager's command instead of npm's. - A self-updating layout in a folder this account cannot write is `ReadOnly`: no update offer, no background staging. - Background-stage and start-up apply failures are stored in update state (`last_failure`) and shown by `doctor` and the update notice until an update succeeds. - `doctor` reuses the terminal's cached latest tag instead of `latest: unknown`, and says it is cached. - Update notices use the same changelog link as What's new and `codewhale update`. - What's new shows the release summary paragraphs, rolled up across skipped versions. - Release bodies open with an `### Upgrade notes` block when the changelog section has one. - `docs/INSTALL.md` states the v0.10.3 rollback floor and no longer shows an impossible v0.10.4 → v0.10.3 rollback. - The package-managed answer test no longer hardcodes `/` separators (failed on Windows CI). - Launch-card PTY tests overflowed the 32 MiB `codewhale-main` stack on resume because the `doctor --installs` config load widened the dispatch future's debug frame; it now lives in an out-of-line helper. Locally `launch_card_pty` went from 0 passed, 2 failed to 11 passed, 0 failed. **Tests (local).** - `cargo test -p codewhale-release --lib`: 60 passed, 0 failed. - `cargo test -p codewhale-cli --lib update`: 114 passed, 0 failed; `undo_hint` regression test: 1 passed, 0 failed. - `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib -- update doctor`: 228 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `dsh_packages_import_through_the_reviewed_install_and_update_flow`, which needs bwrap, and bwrap is not on this VM. These runs set `RUST_MIN_STACK=16MiB` because a `doctor_fix` test overflows the default debug stack. - After the CW-8377 additions: `codewhale-release --lib` 61 passed, 0 failed; `codewhale-cli --lib update` 115 passed, 0 failed; `codewhale-tui --lib -- update_notice whats_new doctor` 153 passed, 0 failed; `generate-release-body.test.sh` passed; clippy on release and CLI clean. - `node --test scripts/release/install-safety.test.js`: 88 of 89 passed. Test 5, "output ends with the PATH command", also fails on main. - Nothing has been run on Windows or macOS. Refs #7486 ---

prs.body:
## Summary One PR for the 0.10.5 TUI audit reports, bundled so they get one review. **Group C: ui, commands and views** (b8c61f7ca) - Refs #7464 (R8 `tui/ui`): approval-routing deny/cancel errors are logged, not discarded behind a "resolved" receipt. Skill mutation fails loudly when config won't load (it used to fall back to defaults). Recovery-snapshot and checkpoint failures use typed toasts instead of `status_message`. Provider balance errors keep their cause. The staged updater child process is reaped. Session loads are capped at 256 MiB. `rx_event` is locked per `try_recv`. Runtime preset writes run under `block_in_place`. The sandbox auto-elevation line is localized. - Refs #7468 (R12 `commands`): `/config` lookups report config-load errors instead of "unknown setting". Command and workflow files go through `read_command_file`, which caps reads at 1 MiB and logs a warning when it skips a file. Failed import report or bundle writes are shown to the user. New exports fsync the parent directory on Unix. `/update` and `/init` run under `run_owner_blocking`, which is now `pub(crate)`. `/config allow_shell` is localized, and its key hint comes from `shell_key_routing` (`PermissionCycle`). - Refs #7469 (R13 views and work surface): Fleet list scans, entry summaries, detail loads and stale-source checks run under `run_owner_blocking`. Summaries are worked out once when the list opens instead of on every render. Fleet setup headers, the Fleet save pager text and the Skills Manager empty state are localized. The terminal dock truncates commands by grapheme cluster. - Adds 24 `MessageId`s, translated in all 15 complete packs. **Group D: session, pickers and app** (280cd1c66, f588d861f) - These cover stdin, review, clipboard init and the follow-up queue. The follow-up queue is capped at 64: an overflowing message goes back to the composer and a toast is shown. - Not covered here: the Wayland and PowerShell paste waits (R17-L11-02/03) need an async paste pipeline. ## Verification - `cargo test -p codewhale-localization`: 54 passed; 0 failed. - `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib` (filters for fleet, user_commands, config_main, skills_manager, terminal, import, export, approval_routing): 287 passed; 0 failed before the rebase. After the rebase onto group D: 334 passed, 1 failed. - That failure, `fleet_draft::workspace_fingerprint_runs_no_repository_fsmonitor`, also fails on `main` (4477e3a61) on this VM (git 2.34.1). This PR does not cause it. - New regression test: `oversized_command_file_is_skipped_not_loaded`. - `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-localization --lib --tests -D warnings` is clean. `cargo fmt --check` is clean. The blocking-call budget is within limits; the `user_commands.rs` entry drops from 5 to 3. - Group D: one plugins test also fails on `main`, because the VM has no `bwrap`. ---

prs.body:
## Summary This is the single bundled PR for the 0.10.5 **engine** audit fixes. Group A (R4 #7460 and R5 #7461) lands first, in commit 1fa6548ce. Groups E (R16/R22) and B's engine follow-ups push onto this branch without force-pushing. **R4: runtime_threads and session_manager** - `external_agent.rs`: `push_bounded` reserves `TRUNCATED_MARKER`, so detail stays at or under `MAX_DETAIL_BYTES`. `bounded_json` counts bytes with a capped `io::Write` instead of building the whole string. `drop(active)` runs before the replay `spawn_blocking(..).await`. `label` and `clean_text` drop `is_title_format_char` (bidi and zero-width) characters. A closed settlement channel now returns an error instead of `Ok(false)`. - `manager.rs`: a failed grant-event append is logged. `sanitize_agent_mail_text` stops at `max_bytes` and matches schemes without lowercasing whole tokens. Permission and plugin receipt text uses `runtime_receipt_locale()` (resolved under `spawn_blocking`, outside the active-thread lock) instead of `Locale::En`. The `from`/`to` labels on `thread.permissions_changed` and its item metadata stay English, as before, because API clients may match on them. - `permission_rules.rs`: a failed standing-rule redelivery is logged instead of `unwrap_or(false)`. - `pack.rs`: the README excerpt is read with `read_prompt_text_bounded`. **R5: tools** - `tasks.rs`: `gate_run` now sets `result.success = status == "passed"`. - `verifier.rs`: a gate pipe read error is written into the captured output instead of being treated as EOF. - `terminal_session.rs`: `load_durable` now returns `Result>`, so a corrupt or unreadable record is reported instead of "does not exist". Kill and persist failures during cleanup are logged and no longer counted as ended. - `search.rs`: the grep worker gets a child token whose drop guard cancels it on timeout. `max_results` is clamped to 1000, and the schema says so. - `scrape.rs`: DuckDuckGo snippets are dropped when the title and snippet counts differ, instead of being attached to the wrong result. - `journal.rs`: `sync_all` after each append. `session_manager.rs`: the parent directory is fsynced after session and goal deletion (unix). - `review.rs` and `verify.rs`: file size is checked or bounded before reading. `repository_tool_workspace` and `gather_files` run under `spawn_blocking`. `github/actions.rs`: `git_status_porcelain` also runs under `spawn_blocking`. **Deliberately not changed** - R4-L11-02 and R4-L11-03: the per-thread projection lock is what orders appends and dedupe. - R5-L11-04: `McpPool` calls take `&mut self`, so releasing the pool lock needs a pool redesign. **Tests** Ran the `codewhale-engine` lib tests with filters covering every touched module: `test result: ok. 720 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored`. This includes the new regression tests for detail cap, JSON cap, bidi labels, snippet pairing, corrupt terminal record and gate success. They need `RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216`, as in CI. Refs #7460 #7461 --- ### Group B follow-up: R6 #7462 and R19 #7475 (commit c1b868578) The rest of R6/R19 is in the approved #7499; this commit takes the findings left over from it. - **R6-L11-02** `app-server/runtime_api/plugins.rs`: marketplace list/get/add/remove/install routes run the sync `MarketplaceStore` and catalog work through a `with_marketplace_store` helper under `spawn_blocking`. - **R19-L4-01** `cli/lib.rs`: when lane start fails and marking the lane terminal also fails, both errors are returned instead of the second being dropped. - **R19-L9-01** `cli/lib.rs`: workflow source reads are capped at 1 MiB. - **R19-L8-02** `cli/update.rs`: a failed save of a declined update is logged and the user is told it was not saved. - **R19-L7-01/02** `snapshot/delta.rs`: `cat-file --batch` is bounded by `GIT_COMMAND_TIMEOUT`; on timeout or error the child is killed and reaped and the writer thread joined. `git_output` uses `run_bounded_git_with_timeout`. - **R19-L8-01** `release/installs.rs`: recovery pruning treats only `NotFound` as a missing record; other metadata errors are returned. - **R19-L10-02/03** `release/installs.rs`: release writes and recovery manifest rewrites fsync the temp file before rename and the directory after. **Left out: R6-L12-01/02** (bwrap/seatbelt denial detection matches English stderr). Neither sandbox gives a locale-stable denial signal other than stderr text, and forcing `LC_ALL=C` on sandboxed commands would change the user's command output. **Tests:** `codewhale-snapshot` delta `5 passed; 0 failed`; `codewhale-release` `59 passed; 0 failed`; `codewhale-cli` workflow source `1 passed; 0 failed`; `codewhale-app-server` marketplace `3 passed; 0 failed`; `codewhale-plugins` marketplace `45 passed; 0 failed`. `scripts/preflight.sh --check`: OK. Refs #7462 #7475 --- ### Group E: R16 #7472 and R22 #7478 (commit 37d55ac96) **R16: runtime, models, cloud-facts, dependencies** - **L11-01/L11-03** `cloud-facts/lib.rs`, `registry.rs`: cache and local-source reads in `refresh_using` and `refresh_registry_using` now run under `spawn_blocking`, through a shared `off_runtime` helper. - **L10-01/L10-02** `config/persistence.rs`: new `sync_parent_dir`. `atomic_write` now fsyncs the directory after a rename, and settings saves call it too. Continual-harness `save_state` now uses `atomic_write` instead of its own unsynced write-and-rename. - **L3-01** `model_context/fragment.rs`: when only the marker fits, it is cut on a char boundary within `max_bytes`. - **L8-01** `session_diagnostics.rs`: a log whose lines are all malformed now reads "failure status unknown" instead of "No session failure signals detected." - **L8-02** `stall_report.rs`: a failed record write is logged with its path. - **L9-01** `working_set.rs`: resident reads stop at the remaining per-file and total byte caps instead of reading the whole file first. - **L7-01** `dependencies/lib.rs`: `run_bounded_git_with_timeout` spawns through `spawn_contained_std`. On timeout it kills the whole process tree; on a normal exit it releases the tree, so `gc --auto` can still detach. **R22: MCP** - **L3-01** `runtime_mcp.rs`: a server name that sanitizes to an empty string is rejected. - **L4-01** `external_import.rs`: skipped import sources and skipped entries are logged. - **L4-02** `extension_host/mcp.rs`: the error that stops the stdio reader is logged. - **L8-01** `mcp_registry.rs`: an entry is kept only if its status is `active` or absent; any status this client does not know retires it. - **L8-02/L9-02/L11-01** `mcp_registry.rs`: cache reads use `read_bounded_mcp_config_file` with a 64 MiB limit and run under `spawn_blocking`. A corrupt cache is logged and rebuilt, and `start_registry_mcp_server` reports it as corrupt instead of missing. - **L9-01** `mcp_registry.rs`: pagination is capped at 500 pages, 50,000 entries and 1 KiB cursors, and a repeated cursor stops it. - **L9-03** `app-server/mcp_server.rs`: the config loads through the bounded MCP config reader, which is now `pub`. - **L10-01** `project_authority.rs`: if the approval receipt can't be saved after an MCP config write, the error is returned and tells the user to re-approve. **Left out** - **R16-L11-02:** `REFRESH_LOCK` still covers the whole read-fetch-write cycle, because it serializes cache updates. With I/O now off the runtime it only delays other refreshes. Merging the two refresh functions, as planned for 0.10.5, is not done here. - **R16-L8-02:** the status line still shows the record path before the background write finishes; a failed write is now logged. - **R22-L11-02:** the TUI setup scans still run in setup-view constructors. Moving them off the UI thread means making setup facts async, which is a separate change. **Tests:** `codewhale-cloud-facts` + `codewhale-dependencies` + `codewhale-config` `946 passed; 0 failed`; `codewhale-runtime` lib (diagnostics, fragment, working_set, continual_harness, settings, stall) `166 passed; 0 failed`; `codewhale-engine` lib `mcp` `465 passed; 0 failed` (`RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216`, bwrap installed); `codewhale-app-server` `mcp_server` `19 passed; 0 failed`. New regression tests cover the tiny byte cap, the all-malformed summary and an unknown lifecycle status. prs.title: test: two load-sensitive test ceilings; flake triage (CW-8368)
prs.body:
## Summary Lane 10 of 0.10.5 (CW-8368): CI speed and top flakes. Net diff: two test files. **Two load-sensitive tests get ceilings above runner jitter.** - `automation_manager::scheduler_wakes_within_one_second_for_subminute_trigger` → `scheduler_wakes_for_subminute_trigger_before_its_tick`: failed on Windows at `1.0510622s` against a `< 1s` assert. The contract is that `Notify` wakes the scheduler before its 60 s tick, so it now polls to a 10 s deadline. - `persistence_actor` tests: `handle.flush(Duration::from_secs(2))` wraps real disk writes and timed out under load (`session persistence flush timed out`); now 10 s. **Windows sccache: tried and reverted.** Windows `Build` makes 0 sccache requests (40–49 min, against Ubuntu's 35–37 min with 78/86 hits) because `ci-test-suite.yml` clears `RUSTC_WRAPPER` on Windows. Re-enabling it here failed with `sccache: error: failed to spawn rustc` for `codewhale_runtime`. sccache re-spawns rustc with the expanded argument list (hundreds of `-L dependency=…` paths), which passes the Windows command-line limit that cargo avoids with an argfile. The revert is in this PR, so the bypass stays. **Health digest #7505 triage (not changed here).** - Ranks 1–6 and 9 (`creator_gate`, `creator_loop`, `extension_host`, `extension_host::mcp::http`) are one PR branch (`devin/dsh-qual-0103`) failing on every push: a host bundle digest mismatch (`creator=dacda4ed321` vs pinned `41bf97f29fad`) and a missing `plugin_manager` tool. Those are deterministic failures on that branch, not flakes on main. - `adaptive_evidence_acceptance` (rank 8) and the runtime/task-ownership timeouts were already addressed on main by 0b7594afc2 and 3256d2faf1. - Already on main, so no change: deduping the duplicate main run (`main-landing.yml` + `require-full-ci-receipt.sh`), the nightly RC dispatch (`nightly-candidate.yml`), and the macOS self-hosted switch (`CW_SELF_HOSTED_MAC` / `macos_runner`; the Mac runner work is CW-8375). - crates.io trusted publishing is deferred. It needs each crate's trusted publisher configured on crates.io first, and the OIDC token lasts 30 min, which may be shorter than the sequential `publish-crates.sh` run. The `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` path stays. ## Checks - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: OK - `node .github/scripts/release-workflows.test.js` and `python3 scripts/test_ci_migration_wiring.py` (19 tests): OK ---

## Summary Four low-risk simplifications picked from #7486 for 0.10.5, bundled as one PR. **One credential resolver (#6559 R01-06).** `[providers.] api_key_env` is now a typed `ProviderConfigToml` field, and the shared `codewhale-config` resolver reads it with the same precedence the TUI resolver already uses: CLI key → config key → route-bound env → secret store → ambient env. Like the runtime reader, the binding stays with its file-owned endpoint (an env-selected custom host does not receive it), an unset binding on a built-in provider falls through to the saved key, and Xiaomi endpoint selection sees the bound key. `auth get` / `auth print-api-key` and the credential handoff now agree with the TUI for bound routes. Regressions: `resolver_reads_the_route_bound_api_key_env`, `route_bound_api_key_env_does_not_follow_an_env_selected_custom_host`. **One provider/model fact table (#7194).** `catalog_corrections.json.reviewed` is the only owner of reviewed model facts. The 131 KB byte-identical `_reviewed` copy is gone from `models_dev.bundled.json`; the seed renderer no longer embeds it, the engine fills `ModelsDevCatalog.reviewed` from the corrections file, and the web facts/model-catalog readers (`facts-lib`, `release-baseline-lib`, `facts-drift`, `model-catalog`) read the corrections file (present with `reviewed` at every v0.10.x tag). `bundled_asset_parses` and the seed unittest now fail if the seed regrows a reviewed copy. **Dead code (#7270, #5587).** - #7270 items 1–4 (`SidebarRowAction::PrefillCommand`, `FleetListOutcome::{OpenDetail,None}`, run/verification receipts, `SkillMutationReceipt` digests): **remove** — landed in #7491 (thanks @luochen211), not duplicated here. - #7270 item 5 (test-only fleet methods): **keep, gated**. `FleetLedger::{claim_next, record_alert, mark_task_terminal_status_if_unchanged}`, `FleetScheduler::cancel_run` and `FleetExecutor::all_terminal` are only called by tests and now compile under `cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))`; `TaskSpec::record_verification_receipt` and `roster::shadowed_for` were already gated. They stay as the test surface for ledger/scheduler invariants. - #5587: removed the module-level `#![allow(dead_code)]` from `core/protocol_parity.rs` and `llm_client/mock.rs`; both are public modules, so the parity guards still compile in normal builds and the mock surface stays usable downstream with no warnings. Dead-code budget on main 101 → 99 after merging current main (which includes #7491). **Skills `listing_*` knob (#7432).** Removed `[skills] listing_max_description_chars` / `listing_budget_fraction` (config, validation, profile merge, docs). The preview keeps its fixed 120-char / 0.2% defaults, so `/context` and `doctor --context-json` reporting is unchanged. `prompt_index` is not added. prs.title: fix(acp): reap escaped agent descendants, report sign-in state, type external refusals
prs.body:
## What and why These are the three parts of CW-8373 that [#7504](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/7504) left open (ACP qualification of v0.10.3). **Leftover agent processes (item 3).** On stop or interrupt, the worker host only signalled processes in the worker's own session. A child that calls `setsid` or detaches, such as `npm exec chrome-devtools-mcp` started by antigravity, escaped that and ran on after shutdown. Before signalling, the host now takes a snapshot of the worker's descendant tree. It reads parents from `/proc` on Linux and `ps -A -o pid=,ppid=` on other Unix systems. Descendants that left the session get the same graceful signals, then SIGKILL once the session is gone. Before each signal the host checks that the process is still in the session recorded in the snapshot, and it never signals its own session. **Sign-in state (item 4).** `auth_status` in `GET /v1/agents/external` was always `unknown`. It now reads `signed_in` after a turn completes for that agent and `needs_sign_in` after the agent refuses with auth-required. Otherwise it stays `unknown`. Known limitation: the state is kept in memory for this app-server process only, so a restart resets it to `unknown`. **Refusal codes (item 5).** These refusals on a session run by another agent used to return a bare 400. They now return 424 with `code: "unsupported_control"`, the same as the per-turn controls already do: - changing model or folder (thread update) - fork (all four fork paths) - compact - steer - creating a session with Codewhale model, provider, tool or prompt controls ## Where this came from Refs CW-8373 (follow-up to #7504). Item 6 (Grok reporting itself as `agent` 0) is a vendor issue and is not changed. ## How I tested it - `cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib -- fleet::host fleet::agents runtime_threads::tests::external_agent`: `test result: ok. 54 passed; 0 failed`. This includes the new `stop_reaches_a_descendant_that_left_the_worker_session` (Linux: a `setsid sleep` child is found and killed) and `sign_in_status_follows_what_the_agent_last_showed`, plus fork and compact asserts added to `per_turn_controls_an_agent_cannot_honor_are_typed_refusals`. - `cargo test -p codewhale-app-server --lib -- external_agent`: `test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed`. - `cargo check -p codewhale-engine -p codewhale-app-server --tests` and `cargo fmt --all` are clean. - Not run: real installed agents (antigravity, devin, grok), or the `ps`-based parent lookup on macOS. ## Checklist - [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves) - [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior - [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) ---

prs.title: fix(model): split /model use-now from default (CW-8370)
prs.body:
## Summary CW-8370: in `/model`, Enter is "use now" and Shift+D is "make default". Three places broke that split: - **`codewhale model resolve` hid the project model.** With no query it reported the global/saved route even when `/.codewhale/config.toml` sets `model`, which the TUI actually launches with. It now loads the project overlay (honoring `--workspace` and `--no-project-config`), resolves that model on the configured provider, skips the saved selection the overlay disables, and prints `model_source: project config model`. An invalid project config fails loud, as the TUI does. - **Shift+D could write a project's model globally.** The overlay now records `Config::project_model` (runtime-only, `serde(skip)`). `save_picker_route_as_default` refuses to save when the live model is the project's pinned model, so one repo's choice doesn't become every workspace's default. prs.title: fix(skills,plugins,secrets): R6/R19 staging, durability and async-blocking audit fixes
prs.body:
## Summary Fixes the skill-install staging race shared by R6 and R19, plus the R6 plugin/secrets/sandbox findings. **Skill staging (R19-L6-01, R6-L11-03, R19-L11-01)** - `stage_tarball` (skill-install) and `place_package` (skills) used a shared `.tmp` path: remove-if-exists, then reuse. Two concurrent installs could delete each other's staging. Both now stage into a fresh hidden `tempfile` dir (`..staging-XXXX`). Discovery already skips dot-dirs. `place_package` also re-checks that the destination is still absent before the rename. - `stage_tarball` runs in `spawn_blocking` (install + cache sync). `install_remote` and `update_skill` run their filesystem phases through a new `off_runtime(ctx, |ctx| ..)` helper that rebuilds an owned `MutationContext` on the blocking thread, so the existing sync bodies stay unchanged. **Plugins (R6-L8-01, R6-L11-01, R6-L4-04)** - Before: remote and DSH `update` returned `NoChange` whenever the source digest matched, even if the installed copy had been altered. Now they stage and compare the installed tree with `installed_matches_staged`, the same check local updates already did, and repair on mismatch. - Install/update staging and `finalize_install` run off the Tokio workers (`off_runtime`, `publish_staged`). `install_prepared_remote` is now `async`; its one caller is updated. - The DSH dependency scan reads non-UTF-8 files lossily instead of skipping them. **Durability (R6-L10-01/02, R6-L9-01, R6-L4-03, R6-L4-01)** - The secrets store fsyncs the parent dir after `persist` and caps reads at 4 MiB. - `.installed-from` and `.trusted` are written with `codewhale_util::utils::write_atomic`. - A failed skill cache-meta write now returns `Failed`. - OpenSandbox parse errors include the serde cause. Not in this PR: R6-L12 (locale-dependent sandbox denial strings), R6-L11-02 (marketplace canonicalize), and R19's CLI, snapshot and release findings. Tests: the touched crates pass (290/204/107/58/56/3/1, 0 failed). Three new regression tests: `remote_update_with_unchanged_archive_repairs_altered_install`, `concurrent_stages_of_one_skill_use_distinct_hidden_dirs`, `file_store_rejects_an_oversized_secrets_file`. `clippy -D warnings` is clean and `scripts/preflight.sh --check` passes. Refs #7462 Refs #7475 ---

prs.title: fix(tui): one paste path; clipboard reads off the UI thread (0.10.5 lane 1)
prs.body:
## Summary 0.10.5 lane 1 (GH #7486 area 1 / CW-8360, plus R17-L11-02/03 from #7473). The 0.10.4 duplicate Windows paste (CW-8354) came from several paste routes each doing their own clipboard read, dedupe and SSH handling. They now all go through one function: ```rust pub(crate) enum PasteSource<'a> { Terminal(&'a str), Shortcut, ReleaseOnly } paste::handle_paste(app, source) -> bool ``` - `Event::Paste`, Cmd/Ctrl+V (composer, onboarding picker, modal stack), the release-only Ctrl+V edge, Windows Terminal's empty paste for an image clipboard, and the mouse menu's Paste all call it. - It works out the target once (terminal panel → provider picker → other modal → history search → composer) and reads the clipboard at most once. - Removed: `handle_bracketed_paste`, `paste_provider_picker_from_clipboard`, `paste_text_into_provider_picker`, `App::paste_from_clipboard`, `attach_clipboard_image`, `apply_clipboard_content`. - What it doesn't do, same as before: a Shortcut aimed at the terminal panel or a non-credential modal returns `false`, so that surface's own key handling takes the chord. **Clipboard reads no longer block the event loop.** - `ClipboardHandler::read(workspace, prefer_markdown)` now returns `ClipboardRead::{Ready, Pending(Receiver)}`. The blocking read (`read_native_clipboard`: `wl-paste`, then arboard with its own handle, then PowerShell's image fallback) runs on a `clipboard-read` thread. - `paste::poll_pending_paste` runs every loop tick, and the poll timeout drops to 16 ms while a read is pending. - The `wl-paste` waits (R17-L11-02), PowerShell's 10 s image wait (R17-L11-03) and the backend open no longer freeze the UI. **Rules while a read is pending:** - Only one read runs at a time. A second edge of the same chord that arrives while it runs is absorbed. The existing 600 ms window still starts when the read finishes. - If focus moved before the clipboard answered (for example the picker closed), the result is dropped, so a credential can't land in whatever replaced the picker. - A reader that never answers is abandoned after 15 s, so the next paste can start a fresh one. **First image paste with no `~/.codewhale` (bug already on main, found by the live test):** - Pasted images are saved under `$HOME/.codewhale/clipboard-images`, even when `CODEWHALE_HOME` points elsewhere. - The no-follow writer creates `clipboard-images` but not a missing state root, so the first image paste said "Nothing to paste". - The `clipboard-read` thread now runs `create_dir_all` on that root before it reads. That keeps the blocking-calls budget for `clipboard.rs` at 0. The arboard handle used for writes is now `cfg(not(test))`: tests never read the host clipboard. Unrelated audit fixes stay in #7502. Refs #7486, #7473. GH #7485 stays open until its reporter confirms. ### Evidence **Local, Linux:** - `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --lib --locked -- -D warnings`: clean. `cargo fmt --check`: clean. - `scripts/check-blocking-calls-budget.py` (Python 3.12): exits 0 at 086a3bd35. - `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib -- paste clipboard_ release_only ssh_direct`: `test result: ok. 100 passed; 0 failed`. - Filters `provider_picker`, `credential` and `image_`: 158, 58 and 20 passed, 0 failed. - Filter `clipboard`: one failure, `tmux_load_buffer_w_reaches_attached_client_with_default_passthrough_disabled`. It tests clipboard writes through this VM's tmux 3.2a; this PR doesn't touch the write path. **End to end, X11 Konsole** (fresh `HOME`, separate `CODEWHALE_HOME`, real `xclip` clipboard, no credentials), recorded at 09b837f8e: - One Ctrl+V in the API-key field put the key in once, masked, and the composer draft was unchanged. - Ctrl+V, Konsole's bracketed paste and right-click Paste each inserted their text once. - Empty clipboard showed "Nothing to paste" and left the draft as it was. - With the X11 clipboard owner paused, typing still showed in the composer. When the owner resumed after 3.2 s, the paste landed once. First image paste rechecked at 086a3bd35 with no `~/.codewhale`: one `[Attached image: …]` and one 0600 PNG. ![First clipboard image attached in a fresh home](https://app.devin.ai/api/presigned_proxy?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..HugxsIqv5qNCgVPYhTt6NldVYFVpZW-ifuVx5FIYJMI) Not run: Wayland, Windows and macOS (CI covers the cfg paths), and the release-only Ctrl+V edge. ---

prs.title: refactor(tui): route every TaskManager consumer through the App's slot
prs.body:
## What this does

Makes the App's `runtime_services.task_manager` the one place every `TaskManager` consumer reads.

This is the first half of what @Hmbown scoped for the store-adoption work (#7451): the manager was reachable four ways — the App field, a local in `run_tui`, a clone captured by `spawn_scheduler`, and a `&SharedTaskManager` parameter threaded through the UI call chain. A session switch could update one and leave the rest pointing at a closed manager. This removes the threading; the release question (when the last handle drops so the owner lock frees) stays in #7451.

**No behaviour change.** Eighteen signatures stopped taking the manager:

```
event_loop.rs       4 composer dispatchers + 3 call sites
handlers.rs         3 + boxed variant
apply.rs            apply_command_result(_inner)
ui.rs               execute_command_input
external_catalog.rs apply_external_catalog_change
task_projection.rs  refresh_active_task_panel
session_state.rs    sync_runtime_workspace_state, switch_workspace
automation_routing.rs handle_action, run_now
router_setup.rs     handle_router_request
```

Net −63 lines.

### Where a `None` slot is now visible

The slot is `Option`, and the old shape made "no manager" impossible at these call sites. Each consumer reports the failure it already had for an unavailable manager rather than swallowing the command:

- task panel refresh → `LiveRefresh::Unchanged`
- `/task add` → `TaskInventoryUnavailable`
- `/task list` → empty list; `/task show` and `/task cancel` → the same "Task not found"
- automation run → `AutomationManagerUnavailable`
- `/router save` → `TaskInventoryUnavailable`

`apply_command_result_inner` reads the slot once and passes `None` through, so `/quit` and other non-task actions still run on a host between managers. An earlier revision returned early for the whole dispatch; that would have been a behaviour change and is not in this commit.

### Two readers keep their captured handle

- `run_event_loop` uses `task_manager` once at startup to subscribe to runtime events, before the caller installs the slot.
- `spawn_scheduler` lives in `codewhale-engine` and has no `App`. That is the piece #7451 still has to solve.

## Verification

At `70d7fe417` on `main` (`4477e3a61`):

```
tui::ui::tests::   943 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored
tui::views::       371 passed, 0 failed
automation          52 passed, 0 failed
task_projection      4 passed, 0 failed
router_setup         7 passed, 0 failed
cargo fmt --all -- --check   clean
cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets   clean
```

Note on the test environment: `tui::ui::tests::adopting_a_local_model_closes_the_connect_picker_and_names_it` overflows the default 2 MiB test stack on `main` as well — it is a pre-existing condition, unrelated to this change, and the runs above used `RUST_MIN_STACK=32MiB` as `main` requires.

Three test fixtures now install their manager in the slot (`conversation_mode`, `conversation_undo` ×2), because the code under test reads it there. Nothing else in the tests changed.

## What this does not do

Adoption still swaps the App field only; the scheduler's clone and the owner-lock release are #7451. Rebased on top of this, that PR gets a single place to swap and a single place to release.
