prs.title: fix(rlm): return bounded RpcResponse::Single error for batch guards
prs.body:
## What and why

Resolves **R10-L9-01** split from #7489 per maintainer feedback on #7466:

- Previously, `batch_guard` in `crates/engine/src/rlm/bridge.rs` allocated `prompt_count` error entries when `prompt_count > MAX_BATCH` or `dependency_mode` was invalid, allowing unbounded response allocation on huge batches.
- Returning a 1-element `BatchResp` broke the Python REPL helpers (`llm_query_batched` / `rlm_query_batched` in `crates/repl/src/runtime.rs`), which check `len(results) != len(prompts)` and surfaced `"size mismatch (1/20)"` instead of `"batch too large: 20 > 16"`.
- `batch_guard` now returns `RpcResponse::Single` with the top-level `error` (since `RpcResponse` is `#[serde(untagged)]`), keeping the wire response O(1) while both Python helpers expand top-level `resp["error"]` to one `"batch too large"` message per prompt.
- Added an end-to-end Python REPL test (`oversized_batch_guard_surfaces_batch_too_large_text_in_python_repl`) verifying both `llm_query_batched` and `rlm_query_batched` surface `"batch too large: 20 > 16"` and never `"size mismatch"`.

## Where this came from

prs.title: fix(tui): a running background shell job no longer keeps the ambient scene drawing (#6728)
prs.body:
## Summary Lane 11 (0.10.5 small user bugs: #7344, #7347, #6728, #6184). Only #6728 still needed code. **#6728:** the underwater ambient scene is supposed to settle 6 s after the shell goes idle. But `ambient_busy` counted every queued, running or waiting jobs-panel row, including `TaskPanelEntryKind::Shell`. So a backgrounded `sleep 900` kept the scene redrawing at ambient cadence for the job's whole life. ```rust // before let durable_tasks_active = app.task_panel.iter() .any(|t| matches!(t.status.as_str(), "queued" | "running" | "waiting")); // after: only Background (agent) tasks keep the scene awake let durable_tasks_active = has_live_durable_tasks(app); ``` The jobs panel's 1 Hz elapsed tick for a visible running shell is unchanged. This brings back what the superseded `boat/issue-6728` branch meant to do, rebuilt on the current `IdleClock` code. Measured on Linux x86_64 with a dev build in tmux 160x45, default theme, after allowing a background `sleep 900`. Draws are counted as `/dev/tty` opens, which happen once per frame via crossterm `size()`: | state | draws/s | CPU | |---|---|---| | main, job running | ~25 | 15.5% | | main, job killed | 0 | 0.43% | | this PR, job running | 1 | 1.02% | On main, the idle composer (0.46%) and the approval wait (1.00%) were already quiet. The FreeBSD measurement is still the issue's acceptance step. Tests: `RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib --locked` with the new regression test plus the existing jobs-panel motion and silent-shell quiet-poll tests: `test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed`. `cargo fmt --check` is clean. **No code change for the others:** - **#7344:** Codewhale only sends a read-only OSC 11 query; the GNOME profile colours come from another program. - **#7347:** the narrower pre-scan landed in v0.10.3 (`016fd567f5c`). This is waiting on the contributor's benchmark and PR. - **#6184:** the bounded-wait and watchdog fixes are on main; the original long freeze is still unreproduced. Refs #6728 ---

prs.body:
## Summary

This is a pass over the #6561 component-hardening backlog against `main` @ `642239fed`. It covers all 138 findings in 37 zones. Each finding was checked against current source and the commit that fixed it (`git log --grep=<ID>`, plus `merge-base --is-ancestor` for every cited commit).

| Result | Count |
|---|---|
| fixed on main | 123 |
| fixed in this PR | 3 |
| still open | 10 |
| not a defect | 2 |

**Fixed here**

- **U07-12** — `is_copy_shortcut` now compares exact modifier masks, so Cmd+Alt+C and Ctrl+Shift+Alt+C no longer count as copy (`crates/tui/src/tui/key_shortcuts.rs`).
- **U06-06** — the macOS notification banner runs `/usr/bin/osascript` instead of resolving `osascript` through `PATH` (`crates/tui/src/tui/notifications.rs`).
- **U08-m1** — the user-input modal records option hitboxes when it renders. Left-clicking an option selects it, and Enter submits it. Test: `clicking_a_painted_option_submits_it` (`crates/tui/src/tui/user_input.rs`).

**Still open.** Each of these needs a design or release decision, or touches files an open PR owns:

- **R02-01 / O01-m3** — release signing. `TRUSTED_RELEASE_KEYS` is empty and there is no publisher attestation. This needs a signing-key decision.
- **R06-10** — fail-fast `parallel()` / `Promise.all` does not cancel running sibling tasks. This needs per-task cancel on the workflow drive.
- **T07-07** — the bounded read is fixed. The project-context capture still runs synchronously from `refresh_system_prompt_from_context_with_reason`.
- **U02-12** — `prepare_user_dispatch` still runs mention, filesystem and git preparation on the event loop.
- **U04-m6** — narrow tables still overflow because of `min(share.max(4))`. This needs a layout decision, such as a stacked fallback.
- **U06-02** — pet live events are stamped with the time they were processed, not when they originated. `live.rs` is in #7502.
- **U06-m4** — pet export still runs synchronously on the owner world.
- **U07-02** — native arboard reads are unbounded. `clipboard.rs` is in #7502.
- **U07-10** — the provider picker still matches `wire_model` with `eq_ignore_ascii_case`. `provider_picker.rs` is in #7502.

Tests:

- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib key_shortcuts`: 9 passed; 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib copy_shortcut`: 1 passed; 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib tui::user_input`: 18 passed; 0 failed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.

Most of the 123 findings marked fixed on main were confirmed by reading the source and the fixing commits, not by running their tests.

prs.title: fix(acp): enforce Ask through the agent's mode, harden discovery, keep agent error detail
prs.body:
## What and why For Claude's review before 0.10.4 — please do not merge without that review. **CW-8372 (Ask posture not enforced by the external agent).** Before every prompt the ACP session now switches the agent through its offered mode control (`session/set_mode` / config option) to a mode that asks before edits (`default`, `manual`, `suggest`) or cannot edit (`read-only`, `readonly`, `plan`, `ask`) whenever the Codewhale posture is Ask/Auto, Never, or plan. Devin (`accept-edits` → `ask`), Claude (`default`), Codex (`read-only`). Each turn records `turn.agent_posture` with `posture`, `agent_mode`, `enforced`; an agent with no suitable mode reports `code: "posture_not_enforced"` so receipts are truthful. If the agent refuses the mode change, the turn fails instead of running unprotected. AcceptEdits/Bypass leave the agent's mode alone. **CW-8371 (discovery marks working agents unavailable).** Handshake probe 8s → 30s and version probe 5s → 30s; at most 4 agents probed at once (process-wide semaphore); when no version can be read and the handshake is unreachable for an agent with a minimum, the reason code is `version_unknown` instead of `no_acp`; the retired Gemini CLI row is removed. **CW-8373 (follow-ups), partial.** - Structured ACP error `data` (`message`/`details`/`error`, else compact JSON) is kept in the turn error instead of a bare `Internal error` (e.g. the 402 balance message). - The external active turn is cleared before `turn.completed` is emitted, so a client starting a new turn right after a failure no longer gets 409 `Thread already has an active turn`. - Not in this PR: child-process lingering after shutdown (the host already spawns workers in their own process group and stops the tree; the shutdown path needs a repro), sign-in state `unknown`, and 400 vs 424 refusal-code consistency. Known limit: an agent switching itself to a permissive mode mid-turn is only re-corrected at the next prompt. ## Where this came from Refs CW-8372, CW-8371, CW-8373 (Linear, Codewhale 0.10.4 project; ACP qualification survey of v0.10.3). ## How I tested it - `cargo test -p codewhale-engine --lib -- ask_posture_picks agent_error_detail_survives fleet::agents fleet::acp` → `test result: ok. 18 passed; 0 failed` (includes the two new regression tests) - `cargo test -p codewhale-app-server --lib external_agents` → `test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed` - `cargo check -p codewhale-engine -p codewhale-app-server --tests`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean - Not run: live agents (Devin/Claude/Codex) under Ask end to end. ## Checklist - [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves) - [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior - [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) ---

prs.title: fix(r21): bound VS Code buffers, gate workflow results, harden bridges
prs.body:
## What and why Fixes the R21 audit findings that don't wait on the bridge-core migration, plus the bridge findings that are one-line fixes. - **VS Code (L9-01, L9-02, L12-02):** - `SseParser` drops an unterminated frame once it passes 2 MiB (bridge-core's `readSse` cap), and `openEventStream` reports that through `onError`. - `requestJson` refuses bodies over 64 MiB, checking both `Content-Length` and streamed bytes. The cap is above bridge-core's 8 MiB because thread detail returns a thread's whole history in one response. - Code-block titles are now cut by code point. - **catalog-refresh (L8-01):** every catalog check now counts toward `ok`. Before, only the last command's exit status did. - **web-maintainer (L8-02):** `publish` writes an error and a summary line, then fails, when `derived` or `lane` didn't finish. Before, the run looked like a clean "no lane proposed a change". - **bridge-core / Feishu / Telegram:** new `splitAtCodePoint` for progress flushes, so a reply is never split in the middle of a surrogate pair. - **Feishu:** - `lastSeq` is now saved together with `responseText`, after the record's effect, the way Telegram already does it. A restart can no longer skip text that wasn't sent yet. - `FEISHU_MAX_REPLY_CHARS` is capped at 30000, both in validation and at runtime. - The leftover DeepSeek strings now say Codewhale. - **WeCom:** - If the reopened stream is also rejected, the error is now rethrown. Final text then falls back to a plain reply. - Approval expiry follows `CODEWHALE_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_MS`, and startup fails if that value isn't a positive number. - Media writes use `fs/promises` and are exclusive (`wx`). An upload whose name already exists is saved under a new timestamped name, so an existing attachment is never overwritten. - **DingTalk:** dropped transport work now logs its key and the error. - **verifiers harness:** staged files are synced before rename, and the bin directory is synced after. ## Where this came from Refs #7477 ## How I tested it - `extensions/vscode`: `npm run compile && npm test`: 50 passed, 0 failed. - `integrations/bridge-core`: `npm test`: 78 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped. - `integrations/feishu-bridge`: 21/21 passed. - `integrations/wecom-bridge`: 23/23 passed. - `integrations/telegram-bridge`: 40/40 passed. - `integrations/verifiers-codewhale`: `python3 -m unittest tests.test_harness`: 9 OK. - New WeCom, Feishu and harness tests fail with the source fixes stashed. The new VS Code tests don't compile without the `SseParser` limit. - The workflow YAML parses, and CI's workflow lint passes. - `scripts/preflight.sh --check` reported 2 failures, both from this VM's environment and not from this change: - the blocking-calls budget script needs Python 3.11 `tomllib`; - `web/scripts/check-facts.mjs` fails without `web/node_modules`. ## Checklist - [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves) - [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior - [x] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) ---

prs.title: fix(config): resolve 6 verified defects from audit R15
prs.body:
## What and why

Fixes all six verified defects reported in audit R15 for `crates/config`:

- **R15-L4-01 (`legacy_root.rs`, `config_document.rs`)**: Pair each planned migration op with its receipt note and propagate `set_config_document_value` / `unset_config_document_value` errors (naming the conflicting path) from `apply_op_to_document`. Only emit receipt notes for ops that actually landed, keep `preview_document` consistent with `apply_to_document`, and have `migrate_legacy_root_config` use `try_apply_to_document` so a non-table destination parent fails loudly without writing a backup or false notice.
- **R15-L6-01 (`config_migration.rs`, `persistence.rs`)**: Add `persistence::atomic_write_if_absent` backed by `NamedTempFile::persist_noclobber` (mapping `AlreadyExists` to `Ok(false)`) and use it in `migrate_config_if_needed`, closing the `exists()`-then-replacing-rename TOCTOU race.
- **R15-L9-01 (`redaction.rs`, `path_io.rs`)**: Add shared `path_io::read_bounded_file_to_string` (checking `metadata().len()` up front and bounding reads via `.take(max_bytes + 1)`) and reuse it in both `read_string_no_follow` and `redaction::config_binding` with the 1 MiB ceiling before TOML parsing.
- **R15-L9-02 (`user_constitution.rs`)**: Enforce a 1 MiB file-byte ceiling (`MAX_USER_CONSTITUTION_FILE_BYTES`) before reading or deserializing in `load_from`, `migrate_file`, `rollback_file`, and `migrate_raw`, and pass `value` directly to `serde_json::from_value(value)` instead of cloning the full JSON graph.
- **R15-L10-01 (`persistence.rs`, `permissions.rs`)**: Sync the parent directory on Unix (`sync_parent_dir`, no-op on non-Unix) after `tmp.persist`, `tmp.persist_noclobber`, `rewrite_in_place`, and `write_permissions_atomic`, propagating sync failures instead of returning false success.
- **R15-L10-02 (`user_constitution.rs`)**: Write the migration rollback backup and rollback restore via `persistence::atomic_write` (file + parent directory fsync) before `save_to` runs, and log cleanup errors with `tracing::warn!` instead of dropping them with `.ok()`.

## Where this came from

Closes #7471

## How I tested it

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passed (0 diff)
- `cargo test -p codewhale-config`:
  - unit tests (`src/lib.rs`): `test result: ok. 863 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 3.23s`
  - integration tests (`tests/configured_models.rs`): `test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.07s`
  - doc-tests: `test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.10s`
  - 9 new focused regression tests covering all 6 defects all passed.
- `cargo clippy -p codewhale-config --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed (0 warnings, 0 errors)
- `python3 scripts/check-dead-code-budget.py`: `PASS: 105 suppressions (allow=75, expect=30), exactly at budget.`

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it)

prs.title: fix(engine,commands): fix 3 R9 audit defects in termination and debug commands
prs.body:
## What and why

Fixes all three verified defects from audit unit R9:

- **R9-L2-01** (`crates/engine/src/core/runtime_contract/termination.rs`): Move the `approval_required` fallback inside the `None` branch of `classify_turn_termination` so every typed `ErrorCategory` (`Budget`, `Timeout`, `Network`, `Tool`, `State`, `Internal`, `InvalidInput`, etc.) takes precedence over historical approval evidence as documented, while keeping `ApprovalRequired` ahead of `ToolError`/`Unresolved` when `error_category` is `None`. Removes the now-redundant `InvalidInput` special-case arm.
- **R9-L12-01** (`crates/commands/src/debug/tokens.rs`): Report `prompt_text.chars().count()` instead of `prompt_text.len()` in `/system`'s `(truncated, {} chars total)` notice so multibyte UTF-8 prompts report character counts rather than byte lengths.

prs.title: [Fix] Handle find -delete as destructive action in execution policy
prs.body:
## Overview

This PR adds support for detecting `find -delete` as a destructive action equivalent to `find -exec rm {} +` in the execution policy expander.

## Motivation

The execution policy's `record_find_exec` function in `crates/execpolicy/src/shell_expand.rs` only handled `-exec`, `-execdir`, `-ok`, and `-okdir` predicates, but not `-delete`. Since `find -delete` deletes files matching the find criteria (equivalent to `-exec rm {} +`), it was bypassing the deny rules for destructive actions.

## Changes

### 1. Core Fix (`crates/execpolicy/src/shell_expand.rs`)
- Added `-delete` to the match arm in `record_find_exec`
- Added special handling for `-delete` since it has no command payload (unlike `-exec` which has a `CMD` argument)
- When `-delete` is encountered, it now creates a synthetic `rm` payload that gets recorded and checked against deny rules

### 2. Test Coverage (`crates/execpolicy/tests/shell_parse_policy.rs`)
- Added `"find . -delete"` to the `HIDDEN_RM` test array to verify the deny rules catch this pattern

## Commit-by-Commit Breakdown

**Commit: 3a4e5e5** - fix: handle find -delete as destructive action in execution policy
- Files modified:
  - `crates/execpolicy/src/shell_expand.rs`: Added `-delete` handling in `record_find_exec`
  - `crates/execpolicy/tests/shell_parse_policy.rs`: Added test case for `find . -delete`
- What changed: The expander now treats `find -delete` as equivalent to `find -exec rm {} +` by creating a synthetic `rm` payload
- Why necessary: Without this fix, `find -delete` could bypass deny rules for `rm`

## Technical Implementation

The fix works by detecting the `-delete` predicate in `find` commands and creating a synthetic `Line` payload representing an `rm` command. This payload is then recorded at a nested depth and subjected to the same deny rule checking as explicit `rm` commands in `-exec` predicates.

## Testing

All existing tests pass (260+ tests in the execpolicy crate). The new test case `find . -delete` is now covered by the `HIDDEN_RM` test array and verified to be denied by both prefix and typed deny rules for `rm`.

## Compatibility

This change is backward compatible - it only adds detection for a previously unhandled case. No existing functionality is modified.

## References

- Issue: #7412 (referenced in commit message context)
- Related: `find -exec rm {} +`, `find -execdir rm {} \;` (already handled)

releases.name: Codewhale v0.10.4
releases.body:
## What's in v0.10.4


Codewhale v0.10.4 is a hotfix release. Ctrl+V no longer pastes text twice in Windows Terminal, which also doubled API keys pasted into `/provider`; the fix was checked on a real Windows Terminal. `codewhale update` no longer refuses a release binary because an unrelated `cargo install` left a Cargo record beside it. The refusal happens inside the installed 0.10.3, so an install it affects cannot update itself to 0.10.4: rerun the installer once (`curl -fsSL https://codewhale.net/install.sh | sh` on macOS and Linux, or `install.bat` from the 0.10.4 Windows archive), and later updates work. `/provider` now works for projects on a second Windows drive such as D:, Computer Use installs from the Marketplace, and every terminal draws the dot whale in `/pet`. `url` is updated to 2.5.9 for RUSTSEC-2026-0592. DeepSeek Harness compatibility is limited: of 32 published packages tried unmodified, 2 activate in the terminal; [DSH compatibility](docs/DSH_COMPATIBILITY.md) lists each one.

## Install

### Recommended — official GitHub release

New macOS/Linux install (checksummed binaries from this release):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://codewhale.net/install.sh | CODEWHALE_VERSION="v0.10.4" sh
"$HOME/.local/bin/codewhale" --version
```

For Windows, use the matching installer or archive below. For an existing
direct install, run `codewhale update`; it prints the executable path and
keeps newer builds. If the install directory is occupied by a different build,
use the fresh-directory migration in [the installation guide](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/CodeWhale/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md).

### Secondary packaging — npm and Cargo

```bash
npm install -g codewhale
# or build from source
cargo install codewhale-cli --locked
```

The wrapper downloads the matched `codewhale` and `codew` command assets
from this Release. Both contain the same compiled runtime.

### Docker / GHCR

```bash
docker run --rm -it \
  -e DEEPSEEK_API_KEY="$DEEPSEEK_API_KEY" \
  -v codewhale-home:/home/codewhale/.codewhale \
  ghcr.io/codewhale-hq/codewhale:v0.10.4
```

The image exposes the same runtime as both `codewhale` and `codew`. The
`latest` tag is also updated on release.

### Cargo (Linux / macOS)

```bash
cargo install codewhale-cli --locked
```

The Cargo package installs `codewhale`. Cargo cannot create a second command
alias from one binary target; users who want the shorter spelling can add a
`codew` symlink to that installed executable. The npm, Homebrew, archive,
shell-installer, and container channels install both command names directly.

### Manual download — platform archives (recommended)

Each archive below contains the same runtime under the `codewhale` and
`codew` command names, plus an install script:

| Platform | Archive | Install script |
|---|---|---|
| Linux x64 | `codewhale-linux-x64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| Linux ARM64 | `codewhale-linux-arm64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| Android ARM64 (Termux) | `codewhale-android-arm64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| HarmonyOS ARM64 (native) | `codewhale-ohos-arm64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| macOS x64 | `codewhale-macos-x64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| macOS ARM | `codewhale-macos-arm64.tar.gz` | `install.sh` |
| Windows x64 (installer) | `CodeWhaleSetup.exe` | NSIS setup |
| Windows x64 | `codewhale-windows-x64.zip` | `install.bat` |
| Windows x64 (portable) | `codewhale-windows-x64-portable.zip` | — |
| Windows ARM64 | `codewhale-windows-arm64.zip` | `install.bat` |
| Windows ARM64 (portable) | `codewhale-windows-arm64-portable.zip` | — |

**Unix (Linux / macOS):**
```bash
tar xzf codewhale-<platform>.tar.gz
cd codewhale-<platform>
./install.sh
```

**Windows:**
- For the installer path, run `CodeWhaleSetup.exe`; it installs
  `codewhale.exe`, `codew.exe`, and `codewhale.bat` under
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\CodeWhale\bin`, adds that directory to the
  current-user PATH, and creates a Start Menu shortcut that prefers
  Windows Terminal (`wt.exe`) when it is installed.
- Extract the archive for your machine: `codewhale-windows-x64.zip` or
  `codewhale-windows-arm64.zip`
- Double-click `codewhale.bat` (not the raw `.exe`) to launch
- Run `install.bat` to copy the binaries and launcher to `%USERPROFILE%\bin`
- Add `%USERPROFILE%\bin` to your PATH

The **portable** Windows archive skips the install script — extract and run `codewhale.bat` from any directory. The NSIS installer is currently unsigned and may trigger Windows SmartScreen until a signing certificate is wired into the release pipeline.

Each platform also has **bare, unarchived** `codewhale-<platform>` and
`codew-<platform>` assets. The seven `codewhale-tui-<platform>` filenames
attached to v0.9.5 are byte-identical compatibility copies used only to let
already-installed v0.9.4 clients discover and cross this single-binary
transition; current installers do not expose a third runtime. The legacy npm
package `deepseek-tui` is deprecated and is not republished. For migration
from v0.8.x legacy binary names, see `docs/REBRAND.md`.

### Verify (recommended)

Download the checksum manifests from this Release and verify:

```bash
# Linux — archive bundles
sha256sum -c codewhale-bundles-sha256.txt --ignore-missing

# Linux — individual binaries
sha256sum -c codewhale-artifacts-sha256.txt --ignore-missing

# macOS
shasum -a 256 -c codewhale-bundles-sha256.txt --ignore-missing
shasum -a 256 -c codewhale-artifacts-sha256.txt --ignore-missing
```

<details>

<summary>Full release notes</summary>

### Added

- Added WorldRouter, an OpenAI-compatible gateway, as a bundled provider (`WORLDROUTER_API_KEY`, base URL `https://inference-api.worldrouter.ai/v1`). Thanks [@Opgeek-1](https://github.com/Opgeek-1). (#7488)

### Changed

- **Minified imports count at DSH import review:** imports written without spaces (`import{x}from"zod"`, `import"pkg"`) are now found when the importer looks for npm dependencies to fetch. A minified package that imported offline before may now ask for npm network approval; without it the plugin would have failed when it loaded. (CW-8369)

### Fixed

- **Computer Use installs from the Marketplace:** in 0.10.3, adding Computer Use from `/plugins` fetched the pinned 0.16.3 archive, passed its checksum, and then stopped with "archive must contain exactly one plugin bundle root … found 2", because the DeepSeek Harness `package.json` that Computer Use ships in `integrations/dsh/` was counted as a second plugin. A Harness `package.json` inside a plugin's folder is now part of that plugin: Computer Use installs as one plugin, disabled and untrusted, with the same skills, commands and MCP server in its review as a directory install of that release, and the nested Harness bundle is neither converted nor enabled. Two plugins side by side in one archive are still refused, and the message now says a Harness `package.json` counts as a plugin.
- **Ctrl+V pasted text twice on Windows Terminal:** the terminal pastes text itself and also forwards the key release, which read the clipboard a second time. A release with no key press now only attaches a clipboard image, which is the case the terminal cannot deliver, and a held Ctrl+V no longer pastes again on release. Thanks [@diegovskytl](https://github.com/diegovskytl) for the report. (Refs #7485)
- **`/provider` failed for projects on a second drive on Windows:** on a drive such as D: or E:, where Windows gives your account Modify but not Full control by default, Codewhale could not make the project's `.codewhale\state` folder private, so `/provider` and starting a session showed "The Engine session acknowledgement does not match this UI". Codewhale created that folder and you own it, so it now applies the owner-only permissions without asking Windows for the right to change the folder's owner. A folder owned by another account is still refused, now with a message that names it and says how to fix it.
- **`codewhale update` refused a release binary in `~/.local/bin`:** any `.crates.toml` beside the `bin` directory, left by an unrelated `cargo install --root`, made the updater treat the binary as Cargo-managed. It now checks that Cargo's record lists this executable, as `codewhale doctor` already did.
- **The installers accept a directory with an unrelated Cargo record beside it:** `install.sh` from the website and the release archives refused any directory with a `.crates.toml` or `.crates2.json` beside it, so rerunning the installer failed for exactly the installs the `codewhale update` refusal affected. They now refuse only when that record lists `codewhale` or `codew`, or cannot be read, and the message says to use `cargo install` or `cargo uninstall` or a fresh directory.
- **Every terminal draws the dot whale in `/pet`:** terminals whose session is not the shared pet companion's source no longer show the old whale with `whale needs /pet source · showing cove`. Each draws the dot whale and its activity forms (editing, reading, waiting, done and so on) from its own session. The source still decides what the companion records and plays sound for. (CW-8359)
- **Resumed reasoning opens a card below tools:** when a gateway continues sending `thinking_delta` chunks after a tool card has already appeared beneath the active thinking card, Codewhale finalizes that earlier card (preserving any unrevealed thinking text and clearing stalled translation placeholders) and opens a fresh thinking card below the tool instead of growing the card above it. Thanks [@SparkofSpike](https://github.com/SparkofSpike). (#7455, Refs #7454)
- **A model request that gets no response is retried once:** when a provider sends no response headers within `stream.open_timeout_secs` (180 seconds by default), Codewhale sends the request again instead of ending the turn, and the transcript says so (`Retry attempt: stream-open-timeout 1/1; provider sent no response headers in 180s; sending the request again`). If the retry also times out, the turn fails with the same error, which now says a retry was already attempted, as soon as the retry times out rather than up to 30 seconds later while a background connection check waits on the provider's model list. `stream.open_retries` sets the count (default `1`, `0` turns it off, at most `3`). The provider may have processed and billed the first request, so its usage stays recorded as unknown. Agents a session starts follow the configured `[stream]` retry counts too. In the turn log, `bound_secs` for "waiting for the model's first response" is now the timeout that request is under, and the watchdog ceiling is logged separately as `stall_after_secs`. (CW-8323)
- **Reasoning stays in the thinking card:** when a gateway opens a text block in the middle of a thinking stream and keeps sending thinking deltas, the reasoning no longer spills into the assistant's answer. Each streamed delta now goes to the cell its own kind owns. Thanks [@SparkofSpike](https://github.com/SparkofSpike). (#7452)
- **A refused Telegram reply no longer stalls the bridge:** when Telegram permanently refuses a reply (the user blocked the bot, a group removed it or took away its right to post, or the chat no longer exists), the Telegram bridge logs it once and moves on to the next message. It used to retry the same update thousands of times a second while every later message, including the owner's, waited behind it. Temporary failures (rate limits, Telegram server or network errors, the Runtime being down) still deliver the same update again, now after Telegram's `retry_after` or 3 seconds instead of immediately. Thanks [@thejesh23](https://github.com/thejesh23). (#7479)
- **Long WeCom replies keep their code blocks:** when a reply is split to fit WeCom's byte limit, which happens to almost every long Chinese reply, each part now ends at a line break and closes and reopens any code block it cuts, so the rest of the message no longer renders as code. Bridges that split only by characters (Telegram, Feishu, Weixin, DingTalk) send the same messages as before. Thanks [@thejesh23](https://github.com/thejesh23). (#7480)
- **Clearer import errors, notification sounds that recover, sturdier telemetry files:** `/import-claude` now says where a Claude settings file stops being valid JSON (line and column) instead of only "invalid JSON". A notification sound player that hangs is stopped after 15 seconds, so later notifications play again. The local telemetry buffer is written to disk before it replaces the old file, so a crash or power loss cannot leave it empty or half-written, and an oversized telemetry ID or state file is ignored instead of read whole. The telemetry service now rate-limits each endpoint as a whole, so changing install IDs cannot get around the limit. Thanks [@NieZhuZhu](https://github.com/NieZhuZhu). (#7482, Refs #7476)
- **Narrow terminals keep the working clock:** at 80 and 60 columns the status row under the composer keeps `working 3s` / `using tool 12s` while a turn runs. The `Shift+Tab to change` hint, then `Esc to interrupt`, stand down first, and a connector notice shortens (`MCP · 1 failed · /mcp`) instead of taking the clock's place. (CW-8264)
- **The Underwater ocean moves while the model works, not while you type:** sea life keeps swimming through a running turn even when the terminal window is not focused, and about six seconds after the session goes idle it holds still, so typing a draft no longer nudges it along and an idle session stops redrawing for it. Reduce motion and Hold still keep the ocean still as before. (CW-8264)
- The Resume confirmation no longer draws its border over the composer on a 60x20 terminal, and the Plugins panel footer always keeps `Esc close`, dropping the per-row hints first at 80 columns.
- **The website no longer calls shipped 0.10.3 features unreleased:** Automatic updates, Installation cleanup, Receipt-owned uninstall and the other features 0.10.3 shipped now show `v0.10.3` (or the release that first shipped them) instead of "In source, not yet released", and the install guide shows `codewhale uninstall` for 0.10.3. Suggested tasks (Desktop only) and the merch interest list stay marked unreleased. The release checklist now has a step to stamp the feature registry, and `prepare-release.sh` lists rows still unstamped.
- **One more DeepSeek Harness plugin activates, and failed ones say what they are missing:** a plugin that reads `settings.describe()` while it loads, outside a tool call, now gets the refusal at once and can fall back, instead of an unhandled rejection that unloaded it. `@michengai/dsh-code-review` 1.0.9 now activates in the extension host with its `dsh_code_review` tool and its `/review-status` and `/review-cancel` commands; its `/review` command is listed as `/plugin-dsh-code-review-review` because Codewhale has a built-in `/review`, and its text is Chinese because Codewhale exposes no host language setting. Against a scripted local model its tool ran end to end in a terminal turn and returned its report; review quality with a real model has not been tested. Plugins that still cannot activate now name the real cause: the services a waiting plugin lacks (only those, with a reason for `webServer`, `connection` and `agentPresets`), the import error behind a composition row that failed, and the services a composition row requires. (CW-8369)
- **npm approval for imported DSH plugins says how to give it:** the message now names the command for the terminal UI and the `[network]` `allow` entry in `config.toml` for the command line, the import review lists every npm package it fetched (`name@version`, sha512-verified, install scripts not run), and `CONVERSION.md` no longer says no network request ran when one did. (CW-8369)
- **The 0.10.3 notes overstated DeepSeek Harness compatibility:** of 32 published DSH packages tried unmodified, 2 activate in the terminal with the default network policy and the rest fail at activation or stop at import review. [DSH compatibility](docs/DSH_COMPATIBILITY.md) lists each package, what it is missing and where it belongs. (CW-8369)
- **Ctrl+V on Windows no longer attaches an image behind onboarding, the redaction gate or a focused panel:** the release-only Ctrl+V that Windows Terminal, conhost and the VS Code terminal forward now attaches a clipboard image only when the composer owns the keyboard. Before, a screenshot on the clipboard could be attached to a composer hidden behind the welcome, language or trust screens, the redaction gate or a focused work panel, and sent with the first prompt.
- **Typing `∫` or `√` no longer switches voice on:** these characters were taken as a voice hotkey, so the character never appeared, voice turned on and the status line said `Recording` while nothing was recorded. They now type as text. `Alt+V` (and `⌥V` on macOS) keeps opening tool details, which already took that chord; start voice input with `/voice` or the hotbar voice button.
- **The OrcaRouter top-up offer ends with its campaign:** the `/provider` and `/model` pickers no longer recommend the Codewhale × OrcaRouter offer, and F7 no longer opens it, after the campaign ended at 2026-11-21 12:29:57 UTC, the same moment the website stopped showing it. The README promo is removed and the providers guide says the offer has ended.
- **The README describes the permission dial that shipped in 0.10.3:** it said `Tab` switched between Plan, Work and Operate and that Ask, the default, applied edits without asking, with the dial described as "coming in 0.10.3". It now describes the `Shift+Tab` dial, Accept Edits as the default, Ask asking before every edit and command, and links the current modes guide; the Simplified Chinese README matches.
- **The roadmap lists only unreleased milestones:** the website's `/contribute` milestones and `docs/ROADMAP.md` no longer show released versions (0.10.3 was still marked in progress) and show 0.10.5, the release that simplifies the whole product, as the one in progress. The release checklist now has a step to drop the shipped release from both lists before tagging.

### Security

- Updated `url` to 2.5.9 for RUSTSEC-2026-0592: a deeply nested `blob:` URL could overflow the stack in `Url::origin()` and end the process. Codewhale computes origins for redirect targets, OAuth endpoints and MCP servers.

</details>


## Contributors

- **[@thejesh23](https://github.com/thejesh23)** — first contribution: stopped one permanently refused Telegram reply from wedging the bridge's poll loop, with a mock Bot API repro that counted 27,520 redeliveries in 15 seconds ([#7479](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/7479)), and kept code fences balanced when the bridges split a long reply by UTF-8 bytes for WeCom ([#7480](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/7480)).
- **[@NieZhuZhu](https://github.com/NieZhuZhu)** — fixed eight audit findings: JSON error detail in `/import-claude`, a timeout on hung notification sound players, durable and size-bounded telemetry files, server-keyed telemetry ingest rate limiting, and release-doc gates that fail closed without the published tag ([#7482](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/7482), [issue 7476](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/7476)).
- **[Sh1Zuku / @SparkofSpike](https://github.com/SparkofSpike)** — kept streamed reasoning in the thinking card when a gateway opens a text block mid-stream ([#7452](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/7452)) and opened a fresh thinking card below tools when reasoning resumes ([#7455](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/7455)).
- **[@Opgeek-1](https://github.com/Opgeek-1)** — first contribution: added WorldRouter as a bundled OpenAI-compatible provider descriptor with its docs, pricing coverage and model-resolution rows ([#7488](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/7488)).
- **[@diegovskytl](https://github.com/diegovskytl)** — reported Ctrl+V pasting text twice in Windows Terminal ([#7485](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/7485)).

See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/CodeWhale/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) for full notes and [docs/CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/CodeWhale/blob/main/docs/CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) for older releases.

## Problem

After an install is converted to the resident launcher, `openclaw gateway install` writes a service entry that bypasses the launcher. Later updates then never activate.

Observed on Linux (systemd user service), `main` 5454c0e62e plus a qualification fixture, 2026-11-24:

1. The install was converted by a release-path update. The launcher is at `<state>/git-install/openclaw-launcher.mjs`.
2. The service definition was removed, then reinstalled through the `openclaw` forwarding entry on PATH (`<state>/bin/openclaw`):
   `openclaw gateway install --runtime node --port <port>`
3. The new `ExecStart` points at the npm package tree, not the launcher:
   `node --max-old-space-size=… <npm-prefix>/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js gateway --port <port>`
4. `gateway start` warned that the service command points at a temporary path.
5. A following `openclaw update` prepared a trial that stayed at `activating`, because the Gateway no longer starts through the launcher that applies trials. [INFERENCE from the trial state; not traced in source yet.]

## Expected

On a converted install, `openclaw gateway install` writes the launcher entry, so updates and rollback keep working.

Evidence: Crabbox runs `run_c23776094a368fd5f61e506cc0158554` (build) and `run_31b93cc9d0cb5193eb9afe01083a8969` (setup). Found while proving #204276.

issues.title: [Feature]: Per-edit checkpoints with undo for agent file changes

labels.name: clawsweeper:intake:feature
labels.description: Preliminary submission classification; full source review pending.

issues.body:
# [Feature]: Per-edit checkpoints with undo for agent file changes

## Summary

Give every agent file edit (write / edit / apply_patch) a lightweight, per-edit checkpoint so a user can undo the changes an agent made in the current run, one edit at a time, without discarding the whole worktree.

## Problem to solve

When an embedded agent performs a multi-file task, each edit lands directly on disk (`src/agents/sessions/tools/write.ts:227`, `edit.ts:183`, `src/agents/apply-patch-file-ops.ts:104-137`). If the agent takes a wrong turn halfway through, there is no way to roll back a single edit:

- **Scenario**: an agent edits five files for a refactor; edit 3 is wrong but edits 1, 2, 4, 5 are fine. Today the user must either keep the bad edit, reconstruct the original bytes by hand, or discard the entire workspace.
- **Frequency**: every long coding run that touches more than one file — the common case for agentic coding, not an edge case.
- **Existing workaround and why it is weak**: managed worktrees give per-session isolation plus whole-worktree `snapshot`/`restore` (`src/agents/worktrees/snapshot-host.ts:39-52`, `src/cli/worktrees-cli.ts:87-90`), and reconciliation journals keep old bytes for rollback. But the project docs explicitly state these journals are "the old bytes of changed paths needed for rollback, **not a history of accepted checkpoints**" (`docs/concepts/managed-worktrees.md:313-315`). The granularity is the entire tree, not one edit. Undoing edit 3 means undoing everything.
- **Confusing naming makes it worse**: the word "checkpoint" already appears in the codebase, but none of it is about file edits — `cache-ttl-checkpoint.ts:5-8` is an LLM prompt-projection snapshot, `cli-backends.ts:257` is native-session fork support, `session-tool-checkpoint.ts:24-39` pins tool definitions. A search for "checkpoint" suggests the capability exists; in practice there is no edit-level undo control surface.

Prior art: Cline exposes a checkpoint for every edit and terminal command, shows each change as a reviewable diff, and lets the user undo the agent's work to any checkpoint. That safety net is what makes long autonomous runs practical.

## Proposed solution

Record a checkpoint at the tool-execution boundary for mutation tools (`write`, `edit`, `apply_patch`), and expose a control to list and restore them.

### CLI/API changes

```bash
openclaw agent checkpoints <session>            # list checkpoints taken this run
openclaw agent checkpoints undo <checkpoint-id> # revert changes after that checkpoint
```

### Design details

- **Capture point**: the single tool-execution choke point `runAgentHarnessToolInvocation` (`src/agents/harness/tool-invocation.ts:17-40,76-86`) already has a `beforeExecute` hook and is the only `tool.execute(...)` call site. Filtering by tool name avoids touching each tool implementation.
  - Note: `src/agents/host-file-write.ts:38` is **not** a universal choke point — default `write`/`edit` call `fsWriteFile` directly (`write.ts:44`, `edit.ts:53`); only `apply_patch` goes through `writeHostFile` (`apply-patch-file-ops.ts:112`). Capturing at the harness level covers all three.
- **Checkpoint payload**: the pre-edit bytes of the target path (plus file-existence flag for newly created files), a monotonic sequence id, timestamp, tool name, and the diff already computed for the tool receipt (`write.ts:220` `planFileWriteDiff`, `edit.ts:168-183`). Store under the session/worktree scope so restarts do not lose them; scope the history to the current run to keep retention bounded.
- **Restore semantics**: restoring checkpoint N rewrites each affected path back to its captured pre-edit bytes and truncates checkpoints after N. Restoration itself should be single-file atomic using the existing authority-aware overwrite path (`src/agents/host-file-write.ts:59`).
- **Config**: `agent.checkpoints.enabled` (default `true`), `agent.checkpoints.maxPerRun` (default e.g. 50). Adding a config key needs the usual compatibility/migration note; `openclaw doctor --fix` remains the migration owner.
- **Non-goals (MVP boundary)**: no undo of terminal command side effects, no rollback of state outside the worktree, no cross-run checkpoint history. One PR = one capability: capture + list + undo of file edits only.

## Alternatives considered

- **Rely on managed worktree whole-tree snapshot/restore**: rejected — granularity is the whole tree; undoing one edit discards good edits too, and docs explicitly deny a checkpoint history.
- **Use git to undo agent edits**: weaker — not every worktree run commits, `git checkout` cannot reconstruct an uncommitted pre-edit state of a single path, and it creates commit-history noise.
- **Ask the agent to undo its own edits**: unreliable — depends on the model remembering exact original bytes; no deterministic guarantee.
- **Persist checkpoints inside the agent's own memory/state**: rejected — prompt/projection state (`session-prompt-state.ts:37-40`) is not a file-system control surface and is not durable against context compaction.

### Why not a plugin?

This is genuinely a core API question: per-edit capture must sit at the single tool-execution boundary (`tool-invocation.ts:83`) and write files through the authority-aware host primitive (`host-file-write.ts:59`). A plugin can wrap tool definitions via `wrapToolDefinition` (`src/agents/sessions/tools/tool-definition-wrapper.ts:27-43`), but it cannot guarantee interception of every mutation path (default `write`/`edit` bypass `host-file-write.ts`), cannot own the trusted restore of pre-edit bytes, and would have to reimplement worktree-scoped durable storage. This is a shared concern across every coding agent harness and every channel, not a niche extension — it belongs in core.

## Impact

- Affected users / systems / channels: all users running the embedded coding agent (CLI, TUI, and channel-driven runs); no channel-specific behavior.
- Severity (annoying / blocks workflow / ...): blocks safe recovery — a single bad edit currently costs the whole run's work.
- Frequency: intermittent to frequent on multi-file tasks.
- Consequences: without it, users either manually reconstruct original bytes or discard good work; with it, recovery is one command.

## Evidence/examples

- Code-level evidence that the capability is absent (current `origin/main`):
  - `src/agents/sessions/tools/write.ts:227` and `edit.ts:183` land edits on disk with no checkpoint persistence.
  - `src/agents/worktrees/snapshot-host.ts:39-52` and `src/cli/worktrees-cli.ts:87-90` provide only whole-worktree snapshot/restore.
  - `docs/concepts/managed-worktrees.md:313-315`: reconciliation journals are rollback bytes, "not a history of accepted checkpoints".
  - Existing `checkpoint` identifiers are unrelated: `cache-ttl-checkpoint.ts:5-8` (prompt projection), `cli-backends.ts:257` (session fork), `session-tool-checkpoint.ts:24-39` (tool pinning).
  - No per-edit undo design exists in `CHANGELOG.md`, `CHANGELOG/*.md`, or docs.
- Prior art: Cline's per-edit checkpoints and undo (`https://github.com/cline/cline#edits-code-across-your-project`).

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

- [ ] Yes, I plan to implement this myself
- [ ] Maybe, with maintainer guidance
- [x] No, proposing the idea only

## Additional information

- This is a capability-gap proposal from competitor feature analysis, not a request to display an existing field. It adds a new control surface (checkpoint list + restore) that does not exist today.
- Open questions for maintainers: should checkpoints be scoped to a run or to a session? Should terminal-command side effects be included later? Would a plugin-level `wrapToolDefinition` be acceptable if core declines?
- Compatibility: checkpoints are additive; when disabled, current behavior is unchanged. Restoring is confined to worktree paths and uses the existing authority-aware overwrite primitive.

issues.body:
### Summary
OpenClaw Share (iOS) is rejected with `reason=token_mismatch` while the main app on the same iPhone is connected with `auth=device-token`. Relaunching the app does not help; only re-pairing the iPhone with a Control UI setup code restores sharing.

### Environment
- iOS app 2026.11.40, iOS 26.6.2
- Gateway 2026.11.7 (macOS), `gateway.auth.mode: token`, Tailscale Serve (loopback bind)

### Gateway log (redacted)
```text
client=OpenClaw Share node v2026.11.40 role=node scopes=0 auth=token device=yes platform=iOS 26.6.2 ua=OpenClawShareExtension/2 reason=token_mismatch
```
3 attempts, 10:42–10:46 KST. At the same time the main app was connected: `client=openclaw-ios name=iPhone role=node/operator auth=device-token`.

After re-pairing via setup code (10:50 KST), `OpenClaw Share ... auth=device-token` connects.

### Likely cause (source on main)
- With no explicit token, the stored Share device token is sent as `auth.token`, so the Gateway reports `token_mismatch` (same mechanism as #190145).
- `ShareGatewayRelaySettings.prepareDeviceAuth` returns early whenever a Share token is stored, including a rejected one (intentional since #191820, to avoid undoing a revoke). Nothing clears or replaces it, so the extension stays broken until a full re-pair.

### Expected
Either:
- (a) after a non-revocation rejection, a Full-access app reconnect re-enrolls Share, or
- (b) the share sheet and app clearly say "Sharing access was rejected — re-pair Sharing", ideally with a one-tap re-enroll that does not require re-pairing the whole iPhone.

Related: #162011, #191820, #190145 / #191424

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Summary

When `openclaw.json` cannot be parsed and `openclaw doctor --fix` cannot repair it, Doctor tells the user to run `openclaw doctor --fix`. That is the command they just ran. The concrete way out added by #126757 (inspect the error, hand-edit the file, or move it aside and re-run `openclaw onboard`) no longer appears on this path.

A config can become unparseable after a truncated write, an interrupted editor or a bad merge. `openclaw config validate` sends the user to `doctor --fix`, and `doctor --fix` sends them back to itself, five times, then exits 2.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use an isolated state dir with a truncated config:
   ```sh
   export HOME=/tmp/oc-home OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/oc-home/.openclaw
   mkdir -p "$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR"
   printf '{\n  "gateway": { "port": 18789 },\n  "agents": { "defaults": { "model": { "primary": "openai/gpt-5.4" } } }\n' > "$OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR/openclaw.json"
   ```
2. `openclaw config validate` prints the parse error and "Run `openclaw doctor --fix` to repair, or fix the keys above manually."
3. `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes`

### Expected behavior

After `doctor --fix` has tried and failed to recover the file, Doctor says the config cannot be repaired automatically and names the next steps, as #126757 made it do:

- inspect the exact parse error with `openclaw config validate`;
- then hand-edit the file, or move it aside and run `openclaw onboard` to generate a fresh config.

It does not suggest running `doctor --fix` again.

### Actual behavior

On current `main` (53e05828a99, OpenClaw 2026.11.7), exit code 2:

```
◇  Config
│  Config invalid; doctor will run with best-effort config.
│  /tmp/oc-home/.openclaw/openclaw.json
│  - <root>: JSON5 parse failed: SyntaxError: JSON5: invalid end of input at 4:1
│  Run `openclaw config validate` to inspect the parse error.
◇  Shared state
│  unknown: config could not be parsed; fix config (or run `openclaw doctor --fix`), then rerun
◇  Agent state
│  unknown: config could not be parsed; fix config (or run `openclaw doctor --fix`), then rerun
◇  Sessions
│  unknown: config could not be parsed; fix config (or run `openclaw doctor --fix`), then rerun
◇  Credentials
│  unknown: config could not be parsed; fix config (or run `openclaw doctor --fix`), then rerun
◇  Cron
│  unknown: config could not be parsed; fix config (or run `openclaw doctor --fix`), then rerun
└  Doctor blocked. Database checks remain unknown; no state migrations were performed.
```

The file is left unchanged, which is correct.

Plain `openclaw doctor`, without `--fix`, prints the same lines. There the `doctor --fix` suggestion is still useful, because `--fix` can strip a non-JSON prefix.

### Cause

#175069 (2026-10-17) routes Doctor through `prepareDoctorEngineSelection` before any storage opens. It runs config recovery with `databaseAccess: "none"`. In that mode, `prepareDoctorConfigRecovery` skips both last-known-good recovery and the #126757 refusal message, which are gated on `databaseAccess !== "none"`. When the file is still unparseable, `reportDoctorUnresolvedEngine` (`src/commands/doctor-engine-selection.ts`) prints a fixed message that always includes "(or run `openclaw doctor --fix`)". It prints that even when the user passed `--fix`, `--repair` or `--yes` and recovery has already been tried.

### OpenClaw version

2026.11.7 (main 53e05828a99)

### Operating system

macOS 26 (arm64). The code path is not platform-specific.

### Install method

Source checkout (`pnpm openclaw`)

## Summary

After conversion to the release launcher, a plain global npm install of a newer OpenClaw leaves the shell CLI and managed Gateway on different versions. `openclaw update status` reports **up to date**, does not show the active release, and gives no next step. `openclaw gateway restart` keeps the older release. A subsequent `openclaw update` refuses and names a long, release-specific command. That named command does work.

This is a user-visible update-status and recovery-guidance defect, not a Gateway outage.

## Environment and inputs

- Linux AWS Crabbox, native systemd user service; Node 24.22.1, npm 11.19.1.
- Main T: `2e90b7627631580126dd43b3f006eb6be8aa88f1`.
- Corrected update proof kit, full AWS source builds. T schema 41; T+1 source `42eb73a4fbb92dfabb6c981de9132540bf7ba69d`, schema 42, normal generated predecessor catalog/migration.
- Genuine published `openclaw@2026.11.7` installed first, followed by `gateway install`.
- T was labeled `2026.11.8-first-hop.0`; T+1 was labeled `2026.11.9-next.0` for conversion. The newer npm case used the **same qualified T+1 code/build/schema**, relabeled with the kit's `stampFixtureVersion` as `2026.11.10-manual.0`. These are test versions, not published release claims. The relabel isolates version/installation selection; it is not an additional migration proof.
- T+1 build ID retained by both labels: `2026.11.8-beta.1-42eb73a4fbb9-2026-11-23T22-45-02.616Z`.

## Reproduction

1. On a fresh Linux lease, globally install the genuine published 2026.11.7 archive with npm; configure an isolated profile and install/start its managed Gateway.
2. With the kit registry serving T, run `openclaw update --yes`. The published updater performs its legacy in-place hop to T.
3. With the registry serving T+1, run `openclaw update --yes` from T. Confirm conversion: systemd `ExecStart` uses `<state>/git-install/openclaw-launcher.mjs`; its active release is `2026.11.9-next.0`.
4. Run plain `npm i -g /tmp/manual-npm-fixtures/next-manual.tgz` (archive version `2026.11.10-manual.0`). No package-spec environment override, `--tag`, `--no-restart`, hand-written service, or code repair is used.
5. Run `command -v openclaw`, resolve its symlink, and run `openclaw --version`, `openclaw gateway status --json`, and `openclaw update status`.
6. Run `openclaw gateway restart`, then repeat the observations.
7. Run `openclaw update --yes` once, then execute its named recovery command once.

## Actual results

Paths below use `<prefix>`, `<state>`, and `<node>` in place of disposable guest paths.

| PATH before and after npm install | `<prefix>/bin/openclaw` → `<prefix>/lib/node_modules/openclaw/openclaw.mjs` |

To update that installation, run: <node> <state>/git-install/releases/3f0f9681-97ba-4158-958b-ca71ac88707b/openclaw/openclaw.mjs update

`openclaw update status` should show both the invoking npm installation and the active Gateway release, explain a version difference, and name **one** next step. Recovery should use a short, stable command, for example through the forwarding entry created during conversion, not a long UUID-specific release path. The user should finish on a consistent working version without first being told the split installation is up to date.

issues.body:
## What happens

The iOS Share Extension treats every timeout/lost response as retryable, but each attempt mints a fresh random request key and Gateway `agent.request` has no logical idempotency owner for it. If the first request was accepted but its response was lost, tapping retry starts a second agent turn.

## Root cause

Current `main` (`3376c29800166a3151cbca6b8ab204964e97ac39`) retains:

- `ShareViewController` re-enables Send on every thrown error.
- every attempt constructs a new UUID in the request payload and uses a 25-second RPC timeout.
- Gateway parses the current `key` but does not reserve/dedupe it; agent work is detached from node RPC response settlement.
- session/run identity is not turn idempotency; existing tests intentionally permit multiple turns in one session.

Targeted live issue/PR search found no exact duplicate; PR #51079 concerns Gateway-generated run IDs, not Share Extension retry identity.

## Impact

One user share can incur duplicate model/provider cost, duplicate tools/side effects, and duplicate routed delivery after an ambiguous response loss.

## Repair direction

Add an explicit logical idempotency key for node `agent.request`. Retain it across ambiguous retries of unchanged Share content and rotate only after definitive acceptance or content/new-share change. Gateway should reserve/dedupe within node + pairing generation, release on admission rejection, and let concurrent duplicates join/observe the same pending/accepted state.

Regress accepted-first/lost-response retry dispatching once, admission rejection retry, edit/new share rotation, concurrent duplicate coalescing, and pairing-generation isolation.

This changes Gateway ingress/wire semantics and requires maintainer review.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Regression (worked before, now fails)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

after upgrade from 2026.10.10 to 2026.11.2, After a few minutes of normal use or idle time, the Control UI page enters a busy loop. The page's own JavaScript repeatedly calls `Element.getAnimations()`, and each call forces a full style recalculation. One renderer core sits at 100% or more, and the UI stops responding to clicks and typing. The window can still be moved. Quitting and reopening the app clears it.

It happens in two different engines at the same time, the macOS app's WebKit WebContent process and a Microsoft Edge renderer, so it looks like a problem in the Control UI page code and not in one browser.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (gateway, CLI and macOS app all on the same release)
- macOS 27.0.1, MacBook Pro (Mac14,6, Apple M2 Max, 32 GB)
- Gateway running locally as the app-managed service, Control UI loaded from it
- Also seen in Microsoft Edge 152 against the same gateway
- Custom theme plugin enabled (the same plugin on a second gateway, running on mac mini, same version 2026.11.2, does not show the problem)

## Observed

- The hot process is the WebKit WebContent process hosting the Control UI (about 100% of one core, around 600 MB resident). A Chromium renderer for a tab on the same gateway shows the same pattern.
- The gateway process stays quiet (roughly 10% CPU) while this happens.
- System load stays low (about 18%), but WindowServer rises to roughly 50% CPU while the loop runs.
- A second gateway on the same release, used from the same app, does not show the problem.

## Stack (WebKit `sample`, main thread, 1,423 of 1,423 samples)

```
WebCore::Page::updateRendering()
  WebCore::AnimationTimelinesController::updateAnimationsAndSendEvents()
    JSC microtask checkpoint
      page JavaScript (microtask)
        WebCore::jsElementPrototypeFunction_getAnimations
          WebCore::Element::getAnimations()
            WebCore::Document::updateStyleIfNeeded()
              Style::TreeResolver::resolve()
                Style::TreeResolver::resolveComposedTree()
                  resetStyleForNonRenderedDescendants()
                    Node::isComposedTreeDescendantOf()
```

All time is in style resolution reached from `getAnimations()` inside a microtask during the rendering update. No other thread is busy.

## Suspected code

`dist/control-ui/assets/control-ui-boot-shared-Ihze6w_j.js` contains an overlay controller that polls animations on an element and reschedules itself while any are still running:

```js
function oe(){return a.getAnimations().filter(...)}
function ce(){return oe().length>0}
function le(e,t){
  ... requestAnimationFrame(()=>{
    ... Promise.allSettled(oe().map(e=>e.finished)).then(()=>{
      ... if(!i.isOpen(a)&&ce()){le(!1,t);return} ...
```

If an animation on that element never finishes or is replaced on each pass (for example, a looping or infinite animation, or one restarted by the theme), the condition `!isOpen && ce()` stays true. `le` then schedules itself again from a resolved promise on every frame. Each pass calls `getAnimations()`, which forces style recalculation. That matches the stack above. I did not run the page under a debugger, so this is the most likely loop and not a confirmed one.

## Expected

An idle Control UI should use no CPU. A loop that waits on animations should be bounded, or should stop when the element is hidden or the animation is infinite.

## Workaround

Quit and reopen the app.

## Not the cause (checked)

- Reduce Motion is off, so that setting does not explain it.
- The gateway is not busy, and its log shows nothing unusual during the spin.
- Page load alone does not trigger it. A normal load peaks briefly at about 84% CPU and then settles to idle.

### Steps to reproduce

The freeze is intermittent and I do not have a deterministic recipe. It has happened several times, each time in this pattern:

1. Run a local gateway as the app-managed service and open the macOS app with the Control UI connected to it ("Local Gateway").
2. Configure a second, remote gateway in the same app. Switch the app from the remote gateway to the local one.
3. Ask a question in an agent, or leave the app idle for a few minutes.
4. Switch to a different group or conversation, then choose **New session**.
5. The UI stops responding to clicks and typing. The window can still be moved. The WebContent process sits at about 100% CPU until the app is quit.

Notes on reliability:

- Two runs that stayed on the local gateway the whole time, including a group switch and **New session**, did not freeze. A two-hour watch with normal use also did not freeze. The failing runs followed a gateway switch or idle time, and the freeze appeared within about a minute of a new WebContent process starting.
- Using the same app on the remote gateway on the same release has not frozen.
- To confirm it, watch the web process while you follow the steps: `ps -axo pid,pcpu,rss,command | grep WebContent | sort -k2 -nr | head`. A process at 100% for more than a few seconds is the loop. Then run `sample <pid> 3` and look for `Element::getAnimations` on the main thread.

### Expected behavior

An idle Control UI should use no CPU. A loop that waits on animations should be bounded, or should stop when the element is hidden or the animation is infinite.

### Actual behavior

he Control UI page enters a busy loop. The page's own JavaScript repeatedly calls `Element.getAnimations()`, and each call forces a full style recalculation. One renderer core sits at 100% or more, and the UI stops responding to clicks and typing. The window can still be moved. Quitting and reopening the app clears it.

2026.11.3

### Operating system

macOS 27.0.1 (both Macbook and Mac mini)

### Install method

mac app

claude-sonnet_5.5, claude-opus_5.5, ChatGPT_6/Sol_5.5

openclaw (local gateway). openclaw (remote gateway)


## Summary

`openclaw configure --section workspace` accepts a regular file, or a path below a regular file, as the workspace directory. Provisioning then fails after the user leaves the prompt. The interactive setup wizard already has a shared path validator that can explain the problem while the user is still editing.

Reuse `validateSetupWorkspacePath` in the configure prompt, applying the same normalization and fallback used when consuming its value. This allows correcting the path in place while preserving the existing protection against persisting a failed workspace.

## Reproduction and expected behavior

The regression runs `runConfigureWizard` with its prompt adapter and real temporary filesystem entries. It checks a file and a child of that file, verifies that neither provisioning nor persistence has started, supplies a corrected directory, and verifies the selected agent receives that directory while the original file remains unchanged.

On base `59b74af7e1ae8cbe1ca664a0fe16b93fd44af5ca`, the prompt has no validator and the new regression fails. With the fix, all 17 cases pass, including the existing persistence-on-provisioning-failure control:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs   src/commands/configure.wizard.test.ts   --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       17 passed (17)
```

This exercises the wizard handler and filesystem boundary with a simulated prompt adapter; it is not a terminal screen recording. The validator introduced for setup in #160373 is reused unchanged.

issues.body:
## Environment
- openclaw 2026.10.x (gateway, systemd user unit)
- Node v24.22.3 (linux x64), Ubuntu 24.04 (kernel 6.8.0-147)
- NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096, MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=4
- 8GB RAM host, no swap; ~25 agents/workspaces, Telegram channel
- Happens on every gateway start, reproducible for weeks (since ~2026.11)

## Symptom
Gateway process RSS grows from ~3.5GB (minutes after start) to 5.5GB+ within 1-2 hours, forcing watchdog restarts (threshold 5.5GB). OOM-kills also observed (journal: 8 events in 4 days) when heap snapshot serialization triggered near the cap.

## Evidence that JS heap is NOT the problem
Diagnostic reports (SIGUSR1, `--report-on-signal`), node 24.22.3:

```
heap.totalCommittedMemory = 1370603520   (t+13min, RSS 4.6GB)
heap.usedMemory          = 1076358408
heap.availableMemory     = 3416612480
heap.memoryLimit         = 4496293888
heap.mallocedMemory      = 4538752
heap.externalMemory      = 46914245

heap.totalCommittedMemory = 1053MB        (t+33min, RSS 4.85GB — heap DROPPED after GC)
```

JS committed heap stays flat around 1.0-1.4GB and shrinks on GC, while RSS keeps climbing. Heap snapshot (2026-11-04, RSS 3.5GB): only ~410MB used.

## Evidence for the native leak
`/proc/<pid>/smaps` histogram of anonymous rw mappings (by Rss):

```
chunk ~256KB:   3623808 KB rss   <-- 3.6GB in EXACTLY 256KB (262144B) mappings
chunk ~240452KB:  236676 KB      (one big mapping)
chunk ~65536KB:  5 chunks ~64MB   (glibc arenas — normal for 53 threads)
```

- ~15,400 rw mappings total; the count of 256KB mappings grows over uptime (6,462 on 11-04 → 16,370 on 11-15).
- Not V8 pages: V8 reports only 1.3GB committed, and V8 regions appear as large mappings.
- Not glibc arenas: MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=4; only ~6 arena-sized (64MB) mappings present.
- Not sqlite mmap: those are 4KB-page multiples.
- Uniform 262144-byte mmaps = a systematic native allocator in a dependency.

## Request
Which component performs fixed-size 256KB mmaps (candidates: some native module / TLS / streaming buffer pool)? Any known workaround? We can provide smaps, diagnostic reports, and heap snapshots on request. Host lacks ltrace/gdb/bpftrace, so we cannot capture the allocation callstack ourselves.

---

*Prepared by: Andrey (agent), 2026-11-24. Data gathered 04-24 Nov 2026 on sashkarobot host.*

issues.body:
## Problem

On the PostgreSQL database engine, a release-path update whose new version crashes after its migration leaves no Gateway running.

1. The new version migrates the PostgreSQL schema (41 → 42), then crashes.
2. The launcher records `rolled-back` and restores the previous release's files. PostgreSQL has no data rollback (documented in `docs/install/updating.md` and #203497), so the schema stays at 42.
3. The previous version refuses to start against schema 42: `Cannot read shared state for discovery … Error: Missing PostgreSQL source schema for inspection`.
4. Nothing serves. The Control UI is unreachable. `openclaw update status` exits 0 but prints `Pending migration status unavailable` and `Update run status unavailable` with the same error and no next step.

The launcher's `rolled-back` result is a file outcome, not a recovered service. SQLite installs are not affected (the launcher restores the SQLite originals).

## Evidence

Linux, PostgreSQL 16.15, `main` 2e90b76276, kit fixtures with a PostgreSQL schema 42 step:

- Healthy `T → T+1`: committed, PostgreSQL at 42, row counts unchanged.
- Crash after migration: the state above. Port refuses connections; `/readyz` fails.

## Expected

After a failed trial on PostgreSQL, the user ends with a serving Gateway and a clear next step. A rolled-back result must not leave the install down.

Related: #203497 (release-path cutover: "PostgreSQL migrations do not have data rollback").

### Summary

In the Control UI's shared text-entry dialog, Enter used while an IME composition is active submits the native form. For example, confirming a partially composed group name immediately renames the group and closes the dialog instead of keeping the edit open.

### Current-main reproduction

Base: `b3ee20852674e20f80cfc72c903de204f2bb17f7`. Chrome 152 on Linux, real Control UI served by the repository's `scripts/control-ui-mock-dev.ts` with the official external mock Gateway and synthetic groups.

1. Open Chat, hover the Research group, choose its options menu, then **Rename group**.
2. Focus **Group name**, clear it, and begin an IME composition.
3. Press Enter while the browser reports `isComposing=true`.

I drove Chrome's actual composition through CDP, rather than calling a component or dispatching an untrusted keyboard event:

```js
await cdp.send('Input.imeSetComposition', {
  text: '\u306b', selectionStart: 1, selectionEnd: 1,
});
await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
```

The recorded browser keydown is `{key: 'Enter', isComposing: true, keyCode: 13, isTrusted: true}`. The mock Gateway recorder receives `sessions.groups.rename` with `{name: 'Research', to: '\u306b'}`. The dialog closes and the sidebar renders that unfinished name. Separate ordinary-Enter and explicit-Save controls each successfully rename exactly once.

This proves the browser keyboard contract through the actual UI and its Gateway request boundary. It does **not** claim a native operating-system IME candidate-window test or a real production Gateway mutation; only synthetic mock state was changed.

### Expected behavior and scope

Composition-confirm Enter must leave the shared text-entry dialog open without a rename/create request. A subsequent ordinary Enter or explicit Save should still submit normally.

The shared owner is `ui/src/components/input-dialog.tsx`, used by group creation/renaming, Sessions-page rename, and device aliases. Its native form has no composition-aware Enter guard. Fixing that owner covers its callers together; no per-dialog variants, config/default, protocol/schema, permissions, styling, or new feature are needed.

Merged #129341 established preserving IME composition in inline session renaming. That earlier inline owner does not guard the shared native-form dialog demonstrated here. I plan a focused shared-dialog fix with failing regressions and the same browser workflow rerun on the fix.

### Summary

On a Linux host running systemd 239, the supported source CLI cannot build its initial artifacts and exits before `--version`. The native manager confirms that the Gateway unit is absent, but the busctl reader treats its unprefixed missing-unit reply as an inspection error.

### Reproduction on current main

Base: `b3ee20852674e20f80cfc72c903de204f2bb17f7`, Node 26.12.1, systemd `239-58.0.4.zncgsl6_6.8.t8.0`.

In a clean checkout with dependencies available, run the normal source CLI with a fresh temporary HOME/cache:

```sh
pnpm openclaw --version
```

It exits 1 before building. The error is `UpdatePreMutationError: Runtime artifacts changed, but the affected Gateway is running or its offline state could not be verified`. Its cause includes:

```text
ServiceInspectionError: busctl --user call: exit 1; Unit openclaw-gateway.service not loaded.
```

Read-only native probes on the same host show the legacy format directly:

```sh
busctl --system call org.freedesktop.systemd1 /org/freedesktop/systemd1 \
  org.freedesktop.systemd1.Manager GetUnit s openclaw-gateway.service
# exit 1; stderr: Unit openclaw-gateway.service not loaded.

busctl --system call org.freedesktop.systemd1 /org/freedesktop/systemd1 \
  org.freedesktop.systemd1.Manager GetUnitFileState s openclaw-gateway.service
# exit 1; stderr: No such file or directory
```

These are actual native replies, not stub executables. No service was installed, stopped, restarted, or modified. The native system-manager probe and the CLI's failing user-manager observation are recorded separately; they are not claimed to be the same manager.

### Expected behavior

The existing systemd-239 compatibility reader should recognize the exact missing-unit replies in both legacy and modern busctl formats. Access-denied, timeout, wrong-unit, and other uncertain replies must still refuse inspection/publication. Existing lock, port, ownership and publication checks must remain active.

### Scope

`src/daemon/systemd-busctl-query.ts` already negotiates legacy output but only recognizes missing-unit text beginning with `Call failed: `. The loaded system-ownership reader has a separate JSON-only transport; it should consume the same bounded busctl query instead of retaining a second version-dependent parser.

This is distinct from #190061/#194018: this host has a running systemd manager, so the non-systemd-host exception does not apply. #184501/#184505 addressed ANSI coloring in systemd 245; stripping ANSI does not repair the missing prefix in systemd 239. The earlier #146022 established support for legacy busctl output.

I plan to fix this in the shared native reader and cover its loaded system-ownership consumer, with focused regression and native-manager controls before opening a PR.

issues.body:
## Summary

On Linux cloud workers, the node enrollment/resume replay script (`extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-node-process.ts`) crashes with a raw errno when the saved `node.pid` no longer refers to our worker:

1. **PID reused by another user's process (deterministic, no race needed).** The liveness probe only exempts `ESRCH`:
   ```js
   try { process.kill(pid, 0); } catch (error) { if (error.code !== "ESRCH") throw error; alive = false; }
   ```
   `kill(pid, 0)` on a process owned by another user throws `EPERM`, which is rethrown. Every resume attempt dies with the bare message `kill EPERM`, the stale receipt is never replaced, and the worker stays stuck until it is manually released and reprovisioned. POSIX `EPERM` means the process *exists* — it should be treated as alive and left to the identity fence, which already refuses mismatched processes with the actionable `release and reprovision the worker` message.

2. **Worker exits between the liveness probe and the identity reads (race).** The Linux branch reads `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`, `/proc/<pid>/environ`, and `/proc/<pid>/cwd` outside any local `try`/`catch` — the only platform branch without one (win32 and darwin both wrap their identity reads). A worker that exits in that window produces a raw `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/proc/<pid>/cmdline'` instead of reaching the dead path that would allow a clean replay. Cloud worker nodes exiting and being reclaimed is normal operation for this module (cf. #188981 "recover cloud sessions after their node process exits").

## Real error output (deterministic reproduction, zero mocks)

Isolated `HOME` with a saved runtime layout and a stale receipt `node.pid` containing `1` (on this host PID 1 is root-owned; the runner is uid 1000). The resume launcher script generated by `createCrabboxNodeResumeScript(request, "launch")` was executed as real `bash` + `node` heredoc bytes against the real procfs, twice:

```
attempt 1: exit=1  stderr: kill EPERM          node.pid after: "1\n"
attempt 2: exit=1  stderr: kill EPERM          node.pid after: "1\n"
```

The receipt is never replaced and every attempt fails identically. The operator sees an errno string, not the `release and reprovision the worker` guidance the rest of this file gives.

The race variant was exercised with the same synthetic-procfs preload pattern already used in `crabbox-worker-warm-image.test.ts`: with the recorded PID alive at `kill` time but gone by the identity reads, the script exits 1 with raw `ENOENT`/`ESRCH` on `cmdline`, `environ`, or `cwd`, and the dead-path replay never runs. An unreadable-but-live identity (`EACCES` on `environ`) likewise crashes with a raw errno instead of the fence refusal.

## Relation to #193653

#193653 (merged 2026-11-05) landed exactly these semantics on the warm-image scrub sibling site: `ENOENT`/`ESRCH`/`EACCES` handled consistently across procfs reads, a gone process treated as dead, and "a readable live process with mismatched ownership still blocks capture". The enrollment/resume replay site in `crabbox-worker-node-process.ts` was not covered and remains asymmetric: its Linux branch still rethrows `EPERM` at the liveness probe and leaves the three identity reads unprotected.

## Impact

- A stale or reused `node.pid` wedges the worker: every resume/enrollment replay crashes before it can either reuse the live process or clean up and relaunch, forcing manual release/reprovision and cold starts.
- The failure surface is an opaque errno (`kill EPERM`, `ENOENT … /proc/<pid>/cmdline`) rather than the actionable message used everywhere else in this flow.

## Suggested direction

Mirror #193653 at this site, without weakening the fence:

- `EPERM` from `kill(pid, 0)` ⇒ treat as alive; the existing identity verification decides (mismatched/unreadable identity still refuses with `release and reprovision the worker`).
- Wrap the Linux identity reads; `ENOENT`/`ESRCH` ⇒ the recorded process is gone ⇒ take the existing dead path (receipt cleanup / resume replay). Any other error ⇒ verification fails closed, never authorizes replay.
- win32/darwin branches unchanged.

A minimal fix (+7 net production lines) with a folded regression matrix is ready locally, following the same semantics as #193653.
