issues.body:
### Summary
`tools.github` with `kind: "app-installation"` gives an agent a GitHub App installation identity for explicitly admitted session reads only. The docs (gateway/config-tools/github-identity, "Session GitHub App reader") say: "Existing publication, background, and shell execution paths do not acquire App tokens." So an agent's writes (`gh` in exec, `github_publish`, background runs) can use only a person's OAuth account or fine-grained PAT.

### Problem
An organisation that wants its agents to commit, open pull requests or file issues has to hand them a person's token. Every write then appears as that person, takes on that person's reach, and stops when the token expires or the person leaves. GitHub's own guidance is to automate with a GitHub App instead: it acts as itself, its permissions are fine-grained, its tokens last an hour, and it takes no seat (GitHub Docs, "Deciding when to build a GitHub App").

### Proposal
Extend the existing `app-installation` selection, with the same `app` object (`appId`, `installationId`, `repositories`, `permissions`, `privateKey` SecretRef, `keyVersion`), to the write paths:
- exec with `host=gateway`: mint an installation token before each launch and place it in `GH_TOKEN`, as managed profiles do today;
- `github_publish`: verify and pin the installation token for each child operation;
- background runs and workers: the same launch-time binding.

Also:
- `gitAuthor` defaults to `<app-slug>[bot]` with the bot's noreply email;
- `github_identity_status` reports the bot account, and `configured_unavailable` when the key is missing or minting fails, failing closed.

### Why
The App's permissions and repository list are set once by the organisation owner, actions appear as the bot, and no person's credential is shared with an agent. The reader already does the verification; this reuses it for writes.

Docs: https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/authenticating-with-a-github-app/authenticating-as-a-github-app-installation

## Summary

In a multi-select `ask_user` question, typing a custom answer highlights the custom row but its checkbox has no tick. The regular options show a check mark when selected; the custom answer row does not.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Ask a multi-select question that includes an own-answer row.
2. Type a custom answer.
3. The custom row gets the selected styling; its checkbox stays empty.

## Expected

The custom answer row shows the same check mark as the other selected multi-select options.

## Cause

`ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-question-answer-controls.tsx` (`QuestionFreeText`): the regular option marker renders `{implicit() ? "−" : selected() ? "✓" : ""}`, but the custom-answer branch renders an empty `<span class="chat-question-panel__option-marker" aria-hidden="true" />` for `multiSelect`. The selected class is applied, so the box lights up without a mark.

## Fix

Render `{props.selected ? "✓" : ""}` inside the custom marker span, matching the option branch.

## Environment

Control UI 2026.11.3 (847611d), webchat. Screenshot available.

issues.body:
### Summary

Give Sessions boards the same view options cards boards have: a **list layout** (rows grouped by column) and the board toolbar's **filtering/search/display options**.

### Problem to solve

Cards boards in the Workboard Control UI can switch between columns and a list layout and have the board toolbar (filters, search, display options). Sessions boards (`kind: "sessions"`) render only as columns and offer just the agent and people filters.

We use a Sessions board as the primary way to organize conversations by topic, replacing sidebar groups: one column per topic (System, Health, Finances, Side Projects, ...), every session pinned into its topic, with ~50 sessions on the board. With 10+ columns this is a wide horizontal scroll, especially on a phone, and there's no way to search or filter the board. A list grouped by column, which cards boards already have, would make the same board readable at a glance.

### Proposed solution

1. Add the list layout to Sessions boards: one section per column (respecting column order and colors), one row per session tile with its title, agent, run state / observer health, and last activity; click a row to open the session. Remember the layout per viewer and board, as cards boards do.
2. Bring the cards-board toolbar to Sessions boards where it applies: text search over session titles, filters by column, run state, health, and agent, plus sort (last activity, title).
3. Allow collapsing column sections in list layout, so empty or low-priority topics take no space.

### Alternatives considered

- **Sidebar custom groups:** they give a grouped list, but we're deliberately moving organization out of the sidebar and onto boards, so pins, columns, and the Board agent live in one place.
- **Fewer columns:** that defeats the purpose of topic columns.
- **The Sessions page:** it's a flat list with no topic grouping.

### Impact

- Affected: anyone using a Sessions board with more than a handful of columns or sessions, and anyone on mobile.
- Severity: annoying, and it limits Sessions boards as an organizing tool.
- Frequency: every time the board is opened.
- Consequence: horizontal scrolling and manual scanning instead of a grouped, searchable list.

### Evidence/examples

- OpenClaw 2026.11.3, Control UI on macOS and iOS Safari.
- The cards boards Rookery and Incidents are in list layout; the Sessions board "Topics" (11 columns, ~54 sessions) has no layout toggle or toolbar filters.
- Related: #196884 (show only pinned/listed sessions), #196794 (per-board visible statuses), #199974 (per-card URLs).

issues.body:
### Summary

On 2026.11.6 (06afb10, npm global, Linux x64, node 24.22.3, one systemd-user gateway, SQLite state) a Telegram DM whose first delivery fails transcript persistence is never recovered: its staged pending input is left `state=cancelled`, and every spooled redelivery (every ~3 min) is refused with `Pending input idempotency key conflicts with the accepted input`. The ingress event stays `pending` and blocks every later update on the same lane until the retry limit dead-letters it (~478 attempts, ~24 h). Gateway restarts do not clear it, and there is no operator command to discard a *pending* ingress event (`openclaw channels dead-letters` only lists/resubmits failed ones).

The first failure looks like #199155 (CLI `openclaw message send` from a scheduled script commits a row in the destination session; the gateway's resident actor then fails the next append with `UNIQUE constraint failed: transcript_events.session_id, transcript_events.seq`). That issue is closed; this report is about the **recovery path**, which turns a one-off write race into a lane outage of up to 24 h.

### Observed (times UTC, 2026-11-21 → 23)

- DM A: a 9-photo media group received 11-21 09:20 → 8 updates dead-lettered after 478 attempts at 11-22 09:19 (`turn-abandoned`). Then a 2-character text received 11-22 17:57 → first attempt `SQLite session write failed: SQLite session entry changed before lifecycle upsert for agent:main:telegram:direct:<id>` + `UNIQUE constraint failed: transcript_events.session_id, transcript_events.seq`; since then 267+ redeliveries, each `Pending input idempotency key conflicts with the accepted input`, event still `pending` after two gateway restarts.
- DM B (owner, main session): UNIQUE failures at 16:21, 16:44, 17:13, 21:08 on 11-22; the 17:13 message needed 31 attempts and every message sent in that chat for 81 minutes waited behind it (completed together at 18:34).
- `sessions_history` for DM A shows the pending inputs as `state: "cancelled"` with no consumed event.
- Writers present: scheduled scripts that call `openclaw message send` into both chats (Hostaway/guest-inbox notifications), a 30-min heartbeat agentTurn into the main session.

Log counts over ~31 h: 1464 `spooled update N failed; keeping for retry: turn-abandoned`, 495 `telegram dispatch failed: Error: Pending input idempotency key conflicts with the accepted input`, 25 `SQLite session write failed`, 8 `dead-lettered`.

### Expected

- A redelivery whose pending input is `cancelled` (no consumed event) should be re-admitted or failed fast, not refused forever as an idempotency conflict.
- One poisoned event should not block the rest of the lane for 24 h.
- An operator command to inspect/discard/requeue a *pending* ingress event.

### Related

#199155 (and fix PR #199365), #96837 (same lane-blocking shape on Telegram DM, 2026.6.11-beta.1), #196219, #197792, #201012.

## Summary
Separate shared Android data and policy from feature-specific owners, consolidating demonstrated duplicate implementations while preserving app behavior.

## Problem to solve
Generic JSON accessors live beside node invocation helpers even though chat, Gateway parsing, settings, voice and Wear consume them. Chat model identity policy also lives in a Compose picker but is used by controllers. Talk route parsing imports a model predicate from setup readiness while readiness imports that parser back. These dependencies make otherwise independent app logic harder to change and test.

## Proposed solution
Use the existing shared data owners, migrate every affected caller, and remove replaced implementations. Deliver narrow PRs with source/history evidence, focused Android validation and independent review.

Initial candidates:
- Move unchanged generic JSON accessors to the existing shared JSON owner.
- Move cron list parsing and summary contracts from runtime orchestration into the existing cron data owner.
- Consolidate model identity policy outside the picker.
- Remove the Talk config/readiness dependency cycle.

## Rejected consolidation candidates

Wear text projections accept different malformed-input shapes, so merging them directly would change behavior. Installed-skill readiness predicates are already shared; an additional classifier would add complexity for a negligible reduction.

## Impact and compatibility
Internal maintenance work; no intended user-visible behavior, protocol, permission, credential, persistence or dependency changes. Releases and deployments are outside scope.

## Alternatives considered
Keep feature-local helpers when their semantics differ. Avoid broad extraction-only rewrites, duplicate compatibility aliases and new abstractions without a concrete responsibility.

## Implementation intent
Maintainer-requested cleanup campaign. Each PR will link this issue and record its own validation and compatibility evidence.

## Delivery status

Remote-verified merges: 0. Eleven reviewed candidates are published; the original delivery target remains unchanged pending scope review.

| Lane | PR | Local proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contracts/chat | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202840 | JSON owner; 108 tests per phone flavor |
| Voice/Wear | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202843 | Talk route policy; 138 tests per phone flavor |
| Settings/domain | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202848 | Cron summary owner; 41 tests per phone flavor |
| Contracts/chat | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202870 | Model policy owner; 216 tests per phone flavor |
| Voice/Wear | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202876 | Wear model state; 24 tests and unchanged picker captures |
| Settings/domain | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202877 | Cron text adapters; 32 tests per phone flavor |
| Settings/domain | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202892 | Installed-skill owner; 88 tests per phone flavor |
| Contracts/chat | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202903 | Runtime fixture lifetime; 41 tests per phone flavor and failing/passing teardown controls |
| Contracts/chat | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202967 | Paired-device token counts; 32 tests per phone flavor and identical render controls |
| Contracts/chat | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202898 | Connection state owner; 87 tests per phone flavor |
| Settings/domain | https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204466 | Explicit Channels/Dreaming inputs; 41 tests per phone flavor, original diary layout assertions retained |

Compilation, focused tests, Kotlin lint, staged-content guards and independent source reviews passed for each candidate. Together they remove 69 production lines while removing duplicate state, an obsolete wrapper, cross-layer dependencies and compatibility adapters. The ninth closes previously unowned runtime fixtures using the existing teardown helper, adding 24 test lines without changing assertions.

Local proof is separate from PR-head CI. Ten runs now pass: Talk, cron summary, model policy, Wear, cron text, installed skills, connection state, runtime fixtures, paired-device counts and read-only settings inputs. Talk, cron summary, fixtures, model policy and skills recovered on attempt 2 at unchanged heads after matching-input infrastructure recovery was observed; token counts passed on its first attempt. The JSON helper run retains its original setup failure and existing auto-merge request; it has not been retried. Original failure evidence is preserved. The read-only settings-input PR passed its first CI attempt at the unchanged reviewed head, including both Android test flavors, 4K/16K Access jobs and Kotlin lint.

Native preparation is complete for all eleven. Merge verification remains pending for all eleven.

Deeper ownership audits identified the installed-skill wrapper and duplicate connection state after the initial six candidates. Other sampled opportunities did not justify a substantive cutover: history/session extraction overlaps active contributor work, and attachment, speech and settings adapters retain distinct contracts. issues.body:
## What happened

Running the modern inference-gated onboarding with an explicitly empty agent name completes setup successfully and creates the default `main` agent. The empty name is neither rejected nor used — it disappears, and the roster/session bind to `main` while the command reports success.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start from a fresh isolated profile with a working default model configured (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; the setup inference check passes against it).
2. In an interactive terminal run:

   ```
   openclaw onboard --modern --agent-name ""
   ```

3. Wait for the welcome plan ("Say yes and I'll set all of that up now."), then reply `yes`.

## Observed behavior

Setup applies with no error and exit code 0:

```
Workspace OK: <profile>/workspace
Sessions OK: <profile>/state/agents/main/sessions
Updated <profile>/openclaw.json
Gateway: service install skipped — say start gateway when you want it running.
Default model: loopback/proof-model (verified and kept)
[openclaw] done: openclaw.setup
Your agent is hatching — handing you over now. Use /openclaw to come back.
```

The written config contains `agents.entries.main` with `name: "main"` and `identity.name: "main"`, and the TUI status line reads `agent main | session main`. The explicitly requested empty name never reaches validation.

## Expected behavior

The classic branch rejects the same input before writing anything:

```
$ openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --agent-name ""
Invalid --agent-name: Agent name is required.
```

The modern path should surface the same validation error instead of silently substituting the default identity and reporting success.

## Control runs (same build, same profile shape)

| Invocation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `onboard --modern --agent-name ""` | silently creates `main`, exit 0 |
| `onboard --modern --agent-name helper` | creates `helper`, exit 0 |
| `onboard --modern` (flag omitted) | creates `main` (default), exit 0 |
| `onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --agent-name ""` | rejected: `Invalid --agent-name: Agent name is required.`, exit 1 |

Only the explicit empty string is dropped; omission and non-empty values behave correctly.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (f7aa7e3), Linux x64, Node 24, built from source at that commit.
- Isolated state/config dirs; loopback OpenAI-compatible provider for the live inference check (2 completion requests per run: the setup probe and the apply-time revalidation).

## Summary

Move the shared iOS session presentation contract out of the Overview view into one app-internal owner.

## Problem to solve

Chat, Sidebar, and Sessions depend on `CommandCenterTab` for the session work-item type and title, detail, and relative-time formatting. These are shared presentation rules, but their owner is a separate screen.

## Proposed solution

Move the existing `WorkItem`, factory, and formatting implementation into an iOS-internal `SessionPresentation` owner. Migrate every production and test caller together and remove the old members without forwarding aliases. Keep the existing fields, defaults, colors, title priority, copied-key rejection, redaction, snooze behavior, and time formatting unchanged.

The cutover excludes routing, grouping, filtering, layout, refresh, mutations, and connection/permission policy. Regenerate the native string inventory for the five moved localized call sites.

## Alternatives considered

The shared chat formatter has different title fallback and redaction behavior. Substituting it would change the product contract. Keeping forwarding aliases on the Overview view would retain the dependency this change is intended to remove.

## Impact

No intended user-visible change. This reduces coupling for developers maintaining the shared session presentation rules. The small import/type-wrapper growth is justified by one explicit owner used by all four surfaces.

## Evidence and validation plan

The current source has the shared implementation in `apps/ios/Sources/Design/CommandCenterTab.swift` and consumers in `ChatProTab`, `RootSidebarSessionButton`, `CommandSessionsScreen`, and `CommandSessionRow`.

The owner of the overlapping Sessions PR approved a separate cleanup and will update its one factory call if this lands first: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192521#issuecomment-7085734637.

Validation will compare the moved bodies and fields, confirm no old member references remain, run native i18n generation/verification, and exercise the existing presentation/filter tests through the iOS app-hosted target. Existing Gateway connection test code will change only its helper receiver. No passing implementation result is claimed yet.

## Implementation intent

Yes, implementation and a focused PR are planned under the maintainer-requested iOS cleanup campaign.

issues.body:
### Summary

The shipped `codex_session_read` supervision tool offers only `endpoint_id`, `thread_id`, and `include_turns`. A completed child's final answer can be near the end of a large thread. The full-thread response is then front-truncated by the native dynamic-result converter. There is no narrower final-only, turn selector, or cursor argument with which to follow the truncation notice's advice.

### Environment and qualification

Observed installed OpenClaw 2026.11.3 on macOS arm64, locally modified `@openclaw/codex` 2026.11.3-goal.2, bundled native Codex 0.164.0. This is not a pristine-package or current-main reproduction. No claim that Codex itself deleted a result. Native saved completion records retained the answers.

### Observed behavior and source join

1. Three native children completed successfully. Their automatic announces failed separately (matching #196199).
2. Owner-authorized temporary transcript supervision could identify the original children, but full-history responses were truncated before their final answers. The temporary policy was subsequently restored.
3. Installed `extensions/codex/src/supervision-tools.ts` bundle passes `thread/read` output directly to `jsonResult`. Its read schema has no bounded selector.
4. Installed `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-content.ts` `convertToolContents` retains a front prefix under the weighted output budget, then appends `OpenClaw truncated dynamic tool result ... rerun with narrower args`.
5. Local exact-ID completion records recovered the final answers without rerunning the work or changing access controls.

The converter behavior and unbounded reader are source-confirmed; this report does not claim a fresh complete Gateway/provider trace or that all truncation occurs at only one layer.

### Smallest repair

Add opt-in bounded final-result reading before the dynamic-result conversion, keeping all existing owner, raw-transcript, live policy and endpoint checks. Use the native paginated `thread/turns/list` with `itemsView: notLoaded`, then `thread/items/list`, newest first, joined to the exact completed turn. Project only a declared `agentMessage` with `phase: final_answer`. Preserve independent turn/item cursors and chunk long answer text with a stable content hash. Do not raise global budgets or silently fallback to full-thread reads.

### Local repair evidence (not live deployment)

A local release-adapted implementation passed 12 focused tests, including exact-turn isolation, Unicode/control-character reassembly under an 8,000-byte serialized result bound, policy revocation between requests and before return, owner denial, and unsupported-method failure without fallback. The policy tests exercise the installed handler/guard functions with endpoint infrastructure mocked.

A separate isolated real **Codex 0.164.0** app-server read copied projection rows for only the selected completed thread plus its rollout, recovered its 3,743-character final answer in three bounded chunks, and matched the saved task-complete text byte-for-byte. No production socket/config, inference request, native resume, service reload, or Gateway end-to-end delivery was involved. The initial rollout-only fixture returned zero turns because this installation uses paginated SQLite history; copying the thread-scoped native projection enabled the native protocol proof.

### Related, distinct issues

- #196199: completion authority/runner lifecycle failure, which creates the need for recovery.
- #196803: finalization context and retained-result accessibility; no shared root cause established.
- #197352: persisted trajectory preview truncation, not this dynamic read-tool response.
- #194547: 64-KiB settled projection rejection, not the front-truncated read response.
- #204147 / #204152: plugin diagnostic omission/budget, not completed-result retrieval.

### Acceptance

An owner with transcript access can retrieve the exact completed turn's final message without receiving its earlier tools/reasoning and without losing its tail. Pagination and long-answer continuation must remain bounded and loss-aware. Owner/policy revocation and endpoint changes must refuse subsequent effects. Existing disabled supervision/write controls remain disabled. Completion handoff is a separate repair and must not be described as fixed by this reader change.

issues.body:
# Bug report: auto-compaction ignores the explicit reasoning-off UI setting; guard_blocked failure loop on thinking-enabled backends

**OpenClaw version:** 2026.11.7 (e31bbf0) — first hit; behavior differs from v2026.11.3 (see "Regression history")
**OS / runtime:** Linux x64 (Ubuntu, kernel 7.0.0-44-generic), Node v24.22.3
**Surface:** webchat dashboard sessions, auto-compaction
**Provider:** custom OpenAI-compatible provider (model `Qwen3.8-Flash-Event`), 128K context

## Summary

When the reasoning/thinking selector in the UI is set to **off** (the default), normal agent turns honor it, but **compaction (session summarization) requests do not**. The compaction path applies the `thinkingLevelMap` mapping only if the model definition declares `reasoning: true`. For any model that does not declare this flag, no thinking-off signal is sent at all, and the server's default applies.

On backends that **default to thinking enabled server-side** (common for Qwen-style models behind OpenAI-compatible proxies), the hidden reasoning output consumes the whole completion budget. The summary comes back truncated, and since v2026.11.6+ compaction rejects truncated summaries, every auto-compaction attempt fails with `guard_blocked`. The session is then permanently stuck once it reaches the compaction threshold — it can neither compact nor continue.

This is a product-level sync defect, not a model misconfiguration: the user explicitly chose "off" in the UI, and that choice must reach the request on **all** completion paths. Asking every user to add `reasoning: true` + `thinkingLevelMap` to each of their (potentially many, arbitrary) models to work around the defect is not acceptable as the primary resolution.

## Reproduction

1. Configure a provider/model that:
   - is **not** declared with `reasoning: true` in `models.providers.<id>.models[n]`, and
   - defaults to thinking **enabled** server-side (and, in my case, ignores `max_tokens`, so thinking is not bounded by the output budget).
2. Leave the UI reasoning level at its default **off**.
3. Use the session normally until it approaches the compaction threshold (128K context here).
4. Wait for auto-compaction, or trigger `/compact`.

### Observed

- Gateway log (sanitized, 2026-11-24): **22/22 compaction attempts** failed:
  `outcome=failed reason=guard_blocked`
- The session cannot recover: every retry fails identically while the UI still shows reasoning = off.
- Normal (non-compaction) turns with the same model and the same UI setting succeed — the difference in behavior between the two paths is what isolates the defect to compaction.

## Root cause (from the shipped dist bundle)

- **Agent-turn path** (`dist/attempt-*.mjs`) explicitly passes `openclawThinkingExplicit` (the user's explicit UI choice) down to the transport, so "off" is emitted as a real signal even for proxy-like endpoints.
- **Compaction path** (`dist/compaction-*.mjs` → `resolveAgentReasoningOption`, reached from the summarization completion via `resolveAgentCoreCompleteFn` / `runSummarizationCompletionFromSource`) only applies `thinkingLevelMap` (e.g. `{"off":"none"}`) **when the model declares `reasoning: true`**. If the flag is absent, no thinking parameter is attached at all.
- Verified by grep over the installed bundle: `openclawThinkingExplicit` appears in the agent-turn/transport modules but **does not appear anywhere in the compaction modules** — the explicit-user-choice marker is simply dropped on this path.

Net effect: compaction silently falls back to the server default (thinking on), the summary is truncated by the token budget, and the truncated-summary guard turns a recoverable quality problem into a hard, repeating failure.

## Regression history

- **v2026.11.3:** same missing sync, but truncated summaries were accepted, so compaction "worked" (with degraded summaries) and the defect was invisible.
- **v2026.11.6+ (incl. 2026.11.7):** the strict rejection of truncated summaries is a good change, but it exposes the sync defect as a permanent compaction failure loop. The guard is not the problem; the un-sent reasoning-off signal is.

## Expected behavior

The UI reasoning selector is an explicit user intent and must be honored on **every** completion path, including compaction/summarization, regardless of whether the model definition declares `reasoning: true`. If the user selected "off", OpenClaw should emit the corresponding provider signal (or, at minimum, a documented per-provider off-control) whenever it makes a compaction request.

## Suggested fix

1. Thread the same explicit reasoning option (`openclawThinkingExplicit`, or an equivalent "user explicitly chose X" marker) from agent-turn options into the compaction completion path, and apply the thinking control based on that explicit choice — not only on the model's declared capability flag.
2. For models without a declared reasoning control: either (a) still send the provider-standard off signal where one exists (e.g. `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false` / `thinking: disabled` shapes already used elsewhere), or (b) log a clear one-time warning like "model <id> has no declared reasoning control; UI setting may not apply to compaction", so the failure mode is visible instead of mysterious.
3. When compaction fails repeatedly with `guard_blocked`, surface an actionable message in the session UI (today it is only visible in gateway logs).

## Workaround applied (confirms the diagnosis, but is not the fix)

Added to `openclaw.json` for the affected models:

```json
"reasoning": true,
"thinkingLevelMap": { "off": "none" }
```

After this, one previously stuck session compacted successfully (`131648 -> 15312 tokens`). This proves the "off" signal reaches the backend when the mapping is enabled. However, it requires every user to hand-edit each model definition to compensate for a system rule — which is exactly what should not be necessary. (One session continued to fail after the change; whether that was an in-flight guard/state issue or a remaining path gap was not fully isolated.)

## Impact

- Any user on a thinking-enabled-by-default model without `reasoning: true` declared can be locked out of auto-compaction entirely once their session grows past the threshold.
- The failure is silent in chat and opaque in the UI (log-only `guard_blocked`), with no hint that the UI reasoning setting was never sent.

labels.description: Good issue quality with a plausible reproduction path needing some confirmation.

issues.body:
## Summary

When `agents.defaults.model.primary` is `ollama/minimax-m3.1-flash:cloud` (and `agents.defaults.compaction` is unset / inherits the primary), compaction fails deterministically: minimax burns the entire 6553-token summary budget on hidden thinking and produces no visible summary text. The user then sees:

> ⚠️ This conversation is too long, and OpenClaw couldn't shorten it. Try again, use /compact, or use /new to start a fresh session.

The log line on the failure is:

```
summary output budget (6553 tokens) was exhausted without visible text; reduce thinking or increase the selected model's maxTokens
```

This did not happen with `ollama/muse-spark-open:cloud` (same gateway, same session, same compaction settings — compaction worked for ~7 weeks on muse). It reproduced twice in a row after switching to minimax.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set `agents.defaults.model.primary` to `ollama/minimax-m3.1-flash:cloud` (no `agents.defaults.compaction` override — compaction inherits the primary). No explicit `thinkingDefault`/`thinking` override.
2. Use a main session long enough to trigger compaction (overflow / safeguard). In my case: ~17.6k transcript events on the main session.
3. Trigger compaction (either via overflow when the conversation is too long, or `timeout-compaction`). It fails with the budget error above. Retrying still fails.

## Observed

- Compaction failed 2/2 times on `ollama/minimax-m3.1-flash:cloud`, then succeeded on `ollama/muse-spark-open:cloud` in the same session.
- The error is that minimax's thinking consumes the entire `maxTokens` / summary budget, leaving nothing for the summary text.
- No file log for the failure beyond what the gateway surfaces as the user-facing warning (nothing matching `summary output budget` in `~/.openclaw/logs/` — it appears to be an in-turn error surfaced to the client).

## Config (before / after)

**Before (failing):**

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "model": {
        "primary": "ollama/minimax-m3.1-flash:cloud",
        "fallbacks": ["ollama/muse-spark-open:cloud", "ollama/glm-5.3-flash:cloud"]
      },
      "compaction": { "mode": "safeguard" }
    }
  }
}
```

**After (working) — two changes, either the first or the second alone would fix it:**

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "model": { "primary": "ollama/muse-spark-open:cloud", "fallbacks": [] },
      "compaction": { "mode": "safeguard", "model": "ollama/muse-spark-open:cloud" }
    }
  }
}
```

## Workaround

Pin compaction to a model that doesn't blow the budget on thinking:

```json
{ "agents": { "defaults": { "compaction": { "model": "ollama/muse-spark-open:cloud" } } } }
```

Or keep the primary on muse-spark.

## Suggested Fix

- When OpenClaw dispatches a compaction turn on an Ollama-routed reasoning model (minimax at least), force `thinking: off` or cap it to `low`/`none` for that turn, or give compaction its own `maxTokens` budget that isn't consumed by thinking. Compaction is an internal maintenance turn — it shouldn't need the model's full reasoning effort.
- Alternatively, document that `agents.defaults.compaction.model` should be set explicitly when using minimax (or any reasoning-heavy Ollama model) as primary.

## Relation to Other Issues

- Closest is #177387 (bundled MiniMax catalog keys M3.1 thinking on `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview` only). That's the *direct* MiniMax provider via `minimaxi.com`; this bug is the *Ollama* path (`ollama/minimax-m3.1-flash:cloud`). The root cause is related — thinking not being capped for the compaction turn — but the provider path is different, so filing separately.
- The session that hit this is the long-lived MAIN session from #154482 (~17.6k events, save cost growing 2.3s → 3.5s over 7 weeks). That issue is about lifecycle/bounding; this one is about compaction failing on minimax regardless of session size.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)
- macOS 27.0.1 (arm64), Node v24.18.0, single gateway under launchd
- Provider: Ollama (`http://127.0.0.1:11434`), model `minimax-m3.1-flash:cloud` via Ollama
- `thinkingDefault: off` globally (no explicit per-model thinking override)

issues.body:
## Problem

On `main`, a fully green scheduled CI run does not prove that every test file passes. Some test files are executed by no scheduled lane. When one of them breaks, no scheduled run shows it. It shows up only when a PR's changed-file selection happens to pick it.

Example: 9 `*.e2e.test.ts` files were red on `main` at 7cbf1585. They showed up only because the wider PR selection from #204292 put them into PR runs (first seen in run 45313132755). The 312 job logs of scheduled run 45305041178 mention none of them.

## Inventory (main a21974cd, from the plan, not from logs)

Method: the scheduled-main node plan (`createNodeTestShards` with the main-validation options of `ci-build-manifest.mjs`), with each config resolved through `vitest list --filesOnly`. Then the UI shard plan, the plugin and channel contract shards, the Windows shards, and literal targets in `ci.yml` are subtracted.

- Tracked test files: 23,066.
- Not in any lane of the scheduled `CI` workflow: **5,601** (upper bound).

| Area | Unit | e2e | Live | Integration | Other | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `extensions/` | 4,221 | 24 | 81 | 44 | 53 | 4,423 |
| `src/` | 651 | 95 | 68 | 13 | 14 | 841 |
| `test/` | 19 | 213 | 16 | 2 | 0 | 250 |
| other | 69 | 7 | 10 | 0 | 1 | 87 |

Where they go:

1. **Plugin shards** (`extensions/`, and probably most of the 511 `src/plugins/` unit files) are excluded from the `CI` plan on main: `includeReleaseOnlyPluginShards: false` (`scripts/ci-build-manifest.mjs:966`). The separate hourly workflow `plugin-prerelease.yml` ("Hourly Extension Tests", cron `37 * * * *`) runs them.
   - **Every one of the last 40 scheduled runs of that workflow failed.** The last success was 2026-11-22T07:39Z.
   - No watcher covered it. It now has an owner.
2. **Release-only runtime files** (95, `RELEASE_ONLY_RUNTIME_TEST_FILES`) are excluded on main: `includeReleaseOnlyRuntimeTests` is false under main validation (`scripts/ci-build-manifest.mjs:644`). Only release validation runs them.
3. **Live files** (175 in total, 94 outside `extensions/`) need provider credentials.
4. **The rest:** about 478 files outside `extensions/` and `src/plugins/`, including 307 `*.e2e.test.ts` files. No vitest config used by a scheduled shard includes them. Nothing on `main` ever runs them unless a PR changes them.

The file list is attached to the owner's handoff. The fix below computes the exact set from both workflows' plans.

## Fix

1. **Every-file lane:** add a scheduled lane that runs every test file that no other scheduled lane covers. Daily, or in the hourly run if the runtime fits.
   - Live files stay credential-gated, but they must be listed under a named owner with an explicit reason.
   - Release-only files run there too, or move to an explicit list that the plan test checks.
2. **Plan test:** add a test that fails when a tracked test file is in no scheduled lane of `ci.yml` or `plugin-prerelease.yml`, and is not on an explicit, reasoned exception list. That makes "never runs on main" unrepresentable.
3. **Sizing:**
   - Measure the runtime of the uncovered set with the existing timing data before choosing daily or hourly.
   - `ci.yml` is 465,817 bytes, so only about 14 KB remains under the 480 KB limit.
   - **Design:** make the lane a generated plan. A planner step computes the uncovered set from the existing plan modules and emits a matrix. One matrix job reads that output and runs it through the existing shard runner (`scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts`). No literal targets go in YAML; the YAML cost is one job.

## Definition of done

- One fully green scheduled `main` run.
- The every-file lane green once.
- "Hourly Extension Tests" green.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

`openclaw audit --agent ""` (or `--agent "$UNSET_VAR"`) exits 0 and returns **every agent's** audit records — byte-identical to running `audit` with no filter — instead of rejecting the blank value. An operator who scopes an audit query with an empty shell variable silently gets a report covering all agents, sessions, runs, and channels.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a Gateway and generate at least one agent_run audit record (`main` agent).
2. Run `openclaw audit --agent ""` (empty value; also reproducible with `--agent "$UNSET_VAR"`).
3. Observe: exit 0, and the output includes the `main` agent's record — identical to `openclaw audit` with no filter.
4. Compare: `openclaw audit --agent nonexistent` correctly returns an empty page (a non-empty value is honored).

Sharpest case: `openclaw audit --execution ""` exits 0 and lists activity, while `openclaw audit --execution xyz` correctly fails with `--execution requires --explain.` — a blank value silently bypasses a validation that a non-blank value triggers.

### Expected behavior

An explicitly passed blank value for `--agent`, `--session`, `--run`, `--execution`, `--channel`, or `--cursor` should fail with exit 1 and a "must not be blank" message, before any Gateway call — mirroring the existing blank-value rejection for `--after`/`--before`/`--kind`/`--status`/`--direction` (added in #137335, merged).

### Environment

OpenClaw main as of 2026-11-16. `src/commands/audit.ts:587` builds `AuditActivityListParams` with truthy spreads (`...(options.agentId ? { agentId: options.agentId } : {})`), so `""` never reaches the Gateway as a filter.

### Anything else

The free-string filters are the inconsistent half: the bounds/kind/status/direction filters already reject blank values (merged #137335), but `--agent`/`--session`/`--run`/`--execution`/`--channel`/`--cursor` still silently drop a blank value.

labels.name: issue-rating: 🦪 silver shellfish
labels.description: Thin issue quality; more reproduction proof or environment detail is needed.

issues.body:
**Version:** OpenClaw 2026.11.3, macOS (launchd service).

## What happens
`gmail-watcher` spawns `gog gmail watch serve` with `detached: true` (own process group). Its shutdown path (`stopGmailWatcher` → `killProcessTree`) only runs on an orderly Gateway shutdown. After `openclaw gateway stop --force` (and after crashes / kernel panics) the Gateway exits without logging `gmail watcher stopped`; the `gog` process is reparented to launchd (ppid 1) and keeps listening on 127.0.0.1:8788. The new Gateway then logs:

```
[gmail-watcher] gog serve failed to bind (address already in use); retry 1/3 in 5s
…
[gmail-watcher] gog serve failed to bind after 3 retries (address already in use); stopping restarts.
```

and Gmail push delivery stops until someone kills the orphan and restarts the Gateway. Seen on 7 different days in one month on one host.

## Expected
Any of:
1. On startup, if the port is held by a `gog gmail watch serve` with ppid 1 started by this user for the same account/port (i.e. our own previous watcher), terminate it and take over.
2. Record the watcher pid/pgid in the state dir and reap it on next start.
3. `gateway stop --force` should signal the watcher's process group before exiting.

## Workaround
Before `gateway start`: find `gog gmail watch serve … --port 8788` with ppid 1, SIGTERM it, then start.

## Related
#161467 (closed) made the watcher recover when the conflicting listener disappears shortly after a restart. Here it never disappears: the previous Gateway's `gog` is orphaned and keeps the port indefinitely, so the watcher stays down until someone kills it by hand.

issues.body:
### Summary

Chinese IME punctuation (fullwidth `，。？！：；` etc.) typed into the OpenClaw **terminal TUI composer** is committed but never rendered in the input box — it appears invisible. The same punctuation typed under the ABC/English input method renders correctly. Output/assistant text containing punctuation renders fine, so the terminal font and display layer are healthy; the problem is isolated to composer input echo during IME composition.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the OpenClaw built-in terminal TUI and focus the message composer.
2. Switch to a Chinese IME (pinyin), e.g. macOS built-in Pinyin.
3. Type Chinese characters, then type a fullwidth punctuation mark (e.g. `，` or `。`).
4. Observe the composer: the punctuation does not appear (no glyph, no caret advance), even though it is committed and sent with the message.

Control comparison:
- Switch to the ABC/English input method and type halfwidth punctuation (`,` `.` `?`) — it renders correctly in the composer.
- Assistant output containing punctuation renders correctly — so the terminal font has the glyphs.

This indicates the characters ARE reaching the buffer (they arrive in the sent message) but are not echoed back into the composer's rendered state during/after IME composition.

### Expected behavior

Fullwidth Chinese punctuation typed via the IME appears in the composer input box immediately, exactly like ASCII punctuation does under the ABC input method.

### Actual behavior

The punctuation is silently dropped from the composer's visible/echoed value. It is not shown while typing and (in observed cases) not shown after commit either, yet it is included in the message that gets sent.

### Environment

- **OpenClaw version:** 2026.11.3 (847611d)
- **Operating system:** macOS (Darwin 27.3.0)
- **Install method:** npm (global): `openclaw@2026.11.3`
- **Model:** sensenova-6.8-flash
- **Provider / routing chain:** SenseNova (direct)

### Impact and severity

Chinese users cannot type punctuation normally in the terminal and must frequently switch to the ABC input method just to enter punctuation, significantly degrading the Chinese input experience. This is a medium-high priority usability defect for CJK input.

### Additional information

- This is the **terminal TUI composer** (Ink-based stdin input), NOT the Control UI / webchat composer. The existing IME fixes (e.g. #194136, #195087, #195356, #196741, #199872) all target the web/Solid `ui/` composer and do not cover this path.
- Likely root cause: the TUI `TextInput` only handles plain keypress/`data` events and does not correctly handle the IME composition commit — fullwidth punctuation goes through the composition path and is never written into the component's echoed state, while ABC halfwidth punctuation arrives as a plain keypress.
- Environment detail: observed with the macOS built-in Pinyin IME; punctuation is visible when pasted elsewhere, confirming it is an echo/render issue rather than a font issue.

## Ask

- Make the portal plugin sqlite-native for `resetSession` and `pushContextStats`, or at minimum stop deleting the legacy index and handle its absence gracefully on sqlite-era stores.

issues.body:
## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (b556fdf), running as a Docker container
- Model: `google/gemini-4-carbon` via `google-generative-ai` (direct API)
- Session store: sqlite (post-migration), portal-channel plugin for message dispatch
- Workload: long agentic turns — 8+ model requests per turn, 300k+ token context, tool-result images staged into requests

## Symptoms

1. `[prompt-cache] cache read dropped 328513 -> 0` on most requests within a single turn: one request reads the full prefix from cache (usage reports ~330k `cacheRead`), the next request reads zero and re-processes everything.
2. `[model-fetch] LLM idle timeout (300s): no response from model` — a 300k-token uncached prompt plus ~7 images regularly exceeds the 5-minute first-byte window; the automatic same-model retry then re-pays the full uncached input cost, and is sometimes killed again. Observed turns running 40-50 minutes that should complete in minutes.
3. Cost impact: ~7.6M tokens re-read uncached in one evening on one agent ($2/M uncached vs $0.10/M cached on this model).

Drop reasons logged by prompt-cache-observability during these turns:

```
cache read dropped 293218 -> 0 ... for google/gemini-4-carbon via provider;
historyRewrite(message 164 (assistant) differs from the previous request; history must be append-only;
changed fields: content.length, content[1].id, content[2].id, content[3].type, content[3].text)

cache read dropped 328513 -> 0 ... via provider;
runtimeContextCarrier(runtimeContextCarrier changed provider history)

message 199 (assistant) differs from the previous request; history must be append-only;
changed fields: content.type, content, envelope.role, envelope.timestamp, envelope.runtimeContext, envelope.runtimeContextCarrier
```

The content-block rewrites correlate with `[agents/tool-images] Image resized to fit limits: 2048x2048px ... -> ...` firing per request for the same images.

## Analysis

- `isGooglePromptCacheEligible` intentionally excludes `gemini-4*` (source comment: "Gemini 4 supports implicit caching only"), so there is no managed `cachedContents` resource and no explicit cache checkpoints on this path — caching depends entirely on Google's implicit caching, which requires a byte-identical request prefix.
- The mutations that the observability layer flags appear to be bookkeeping-level rather than intentional conversation edits: media re-staging (new content-block ids/types per request), envelope metadata back-fill (`runtimeContext`, carrier flags, timestamps written onto stored messages after they were sent), and transient runtime-context carrier position shifts as history grows.
- On the Anthropic boundary-aware path these same mutations are mostly harmless: volatile runtime context stays outside the cached prefix and stable boundaries are checkpointed, so an old-message mutation after the last checkpoint doesn't invalidate the read. On Gemini 4 there is no such armor: a divergence at message ~164 of a 300-message history invalidates the entire cached prefix, so every affected request re-reads the full context.

## Suggestions / asks

- Stable media projection: resize/encode tool-result images once and replay identical bytes and block identity, instead of re-staging per request.
- Keep envelope metadata (runtimeContext, carrier flags, timestamps) out of the wire-history identity used for implicit prefix continuity (or out of the wire payload entirely).
- Pin the runtime-context carrier at a stable position, or move the volatile suffix out of the message prefix, so history growth doesn't shift carrier positions.
- If/when the Gemini API supports explicit cachedContents for gemini-4, extend the managed path to it.
- Consider documenting that `models.providers.google.timeoutSeconds` should be raised for agents running 300k+ uncached contexts on gemini-4 until prefix stability improves (we raised 300 -> 900 to stop the kill-retry churn).

Happy to provide fuller logs or a repro if useful.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
`normalizeAttachment` (src/gateway/chat-attachments.ts), which strips the `data:...;base64,` prefix from chat attachment `content`, only matches a bare media type. An RFC 2397-legal data URL whose media type carries parameters (e.g. `data:image/png;charset=utf-8;base64,...`) keeps its prefix and is then rejected by the strict attachment base64 validator, so the whole attachment fails with `invalid base64 content`.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Check out openclaw `main` at `ad09e3821` (2026-11-16).
2. Call the production entry point `parseMessageWithAttachments` from `src/gateway/chat-attachments.ts` with an image attachment whose `content` is a parameterized data URL, e.g. `{ type: "image", mimeType: "image/png", fileName: "dot.png", content: "data:image/png;charset=utf-8;base64,<1x1 PNG>" }`.
3. Observe it throws `attachment dot.png: invalid base64 content`.
4. The identical payload with a plain `data:image/png;base64,<1x1 PNG>` content parses successfully (inline image returned).

### Expected behavior
Per RFC 2397 the media type may include parameters (`data:image/png;charset=utf-8;base64,<data>` is a valid data URL). The agent image/media tool path accepts that form since #195652 (`decodeDataUrl` in src/media/image-data-url.ts), and the repo's other data-URL parsers (`packages/media-core/src/inline-image-data-url.ts`, `src/gateway/managed-image-attachments.ts`) also accept parameters, so the gateway chat attachment path should accept it the same way instead of failing the upload.

### Actual behavior
The attachment fails hard: `attachment dot.png: invalid base64 content`. The prefix-strip regex `^data:[^;,]+;base64$` requires `;base64` immediately after the media type, so a parameterized header is left in place; `inspectBase64` (attachment dialect) then rejects the whole string because of the `:`, `;` and `,` characters. Observed on base `main`: adding cases for the parameterized form to `src/gateway/chat-attachments.test.ts` fails 2/2 new tests (39/39 pre-existing tests pass unchanged).

### OpenClaw version
Source checkout of `main` at ad09e3821 (2026-11-16, post-2026.11.2)

### Operating system
Linux x64 (reproduced on the source checkout; parser behavior is OS-independent)

### Install method
source / pnpm dev

### Model
Any — deterministic parser path, no model involved

### Provider / routing chain
openclaw local gateway path — no provider involved

### Logs
```
FAIL src/gateway/chat-attachments.test.ts > persistInboundImagesForTranscript > parses data URL attachment content with media type parameters
Error: attachment dot.png: invalid base64 content

FAIL src/gateway/chat-attachments.test.ts > persistInboundImagesForTranscript > parses data URL attachment content with uppercase BASE64 token
Error: attachment dot.png: invalid base64 content
```

### Impact and severity
Affected: gateway API clients (and any entrypoint that builds `ChatAttachment` records, including node events and companion-ask flows) that attach inline images as data URLs with media type parameters. Some exporters and Windows tooling emit `;charset=utf-8` or `;name=` parameters on otherwise standard data URLs.
Severity: blocks workflow when hit (the attachment fails hard and the send errors).
Frequency: edge case (requires a producer that emits media type parameters).
Consequence: a client cannot attach an inline image that the agent tool path and other sibling parsers accept; the misleading `invalid base64 content` error points users at the wrong fix.

### Additional information
The regex intentionally inspects only the header (never the payload). The fix is to allow parameters before the `;base64` marker and to match the marker case-insensitively, mirroring `decodeDataUrl` from #195652: `/^data:[^,]*;base64$/i`. The payload still flows through the unchanged strict base64 validation, size limits, and MIME sniffing.

### Steps to reproduce
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Actual behavior
The November 13 update attempt staged the candidate but failed during candidate-state-snapshot, reported runtime-verification-failed, and recovered to 2026.10.3. The requested target is 2026.11.3; it is not installed.

These observations come from the operator's on-machine diagnostic reports and receipts summarized in the linked support conversation, not a clean-install reproduction or an attached raw-log bundle. Exact invocation and complete environment capture are not available in this report.

Installed: 2026.10.3 (59cb447). Requested target: 2026.11.3, not activated.

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Logs
Reported error strings:
```text
candidate-state-snapshot
SQLite worker queue capacity reached
runtime-verification-failed
```
No unredacted logs, databases, credentials, private paths, or conversation content are attached.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
Existing support discussion: https://community.openclaw.ai/t/safe-update-from-2026-10-3-sqlite-worker-queue-capacity-reached-during-snapshot/385

Related reports found before filing: #178059 (closed snapshot-progress failure) and #183744 (many-agent queue saturation). This report does not establish either root cause locally.

### Impact and severity
Affected: one existing installation.
Severity: blocks completing the requested update through the attempted route.
Frequency: one official update attempt documented in the reconciled timeline; no minimal reproduction.
Consequence: installation remains on 2026.10.3. Gateway and Telegram responses have since recovered. No confirmed saved-history loss.

### Additional information
Please treat this as an escalation of the unresolved upgrade/recovery path, not a claim that the 2026.11.3 installed updater still has the defect fixed by #178126.

Relevant reported state:
- Approximately 22 GB agent database; two unusually large histories around 1.2 GB compressed each.
- Existing external rollback databases, history archives, and older state/workspace archives are preserved. A current coherent application restore has not been demonstrated; a hash alone is not being represented as recovery proof.
- An external TMPDIR reportedly passed a snapshot preflight requiring approximately 109 GiB. Internal storage did not meet that requirement.
- Support advised the fixed release and an external-state/manual-install route. That complete manual route has NOT been carried out and verified, so this is not evidence that the advice failed.

Important separation from later troubleshooting:
- A subsequent sessions compaction attempt on a large history exhausted an 8 GB Node heap ("JavaScript heap out of memory"). This was NOT an active updater run. A continuation retried after readiness alone; that retry is not proof of a new snapshot defect.
- A separate isolated 2026.11.3 probe rejected the schema-24 copy before migration/archive testing. It therefore did NOT establish that supported target migration or history retrieval fails.
- Telegram restart recovery subsequently stalled and was restored by /reset. Earlier claims of lost saved transcripts were retracted after bounded pre-reset history retrieval succeeded.
- No further compaction, deletion, swap, or update retries are being performed.

Maintainer guidance requested:
1. Is stopping the Gateway and manually installing the fixed official package, followed by the documented Doctor migration/startup flow, the supported way past this older updater's snapshot failure? What specific checks/rollback conditions are required for this size of state?
2. Can the released 2026.11.3 migration/startup path preserve and serve these intact oversized histories without first compacting/archiving them? Local source inspection reported 64 MiB cold-decode and 256 MiB archive-candidate limits, but their applicability to these records has NOT been proven. The documented schema-37 chunked path appears unreleased.
3. Which bounded, redacted diagnostics would let maintainers distinguish progress-write backlog from another snapshot failure without another destructive or all-day trial?

If this belongs on an existing issue, please identify the canonical one. We are seeking a supported, evidence-based route, not permission to delete valuable histories.

issues.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a local (stdio) MCP server's sign-in expires, the user has no way to sign in again from OpenClaw. The Connect card from #200538 only covers HTTP servers that use OAuth (`<server>__connect` and `connectMcpServer` are built only for `kind === "http"` with `auth: "oauth"`). A stdio server manages its own credentials, so OpenClaw can't run OAuth for it.

The MCP spec has a route for this: URL-mode elicitation (2025-11-25). The client declares `capabilities.elicitation.url`. The server then sends `elicitation/create` with `mode: "url"`, `url`, `elicitationId` and `message`, or fails the call with `-32042` (URL elicitation required). Later it can send `notifications/elicitation/complete`.

On main, OpenClaw does none of this by default:

1. **Default config:** the bundle MCP client sends `capabilities: {}` (`buildMcpClientCapabilities` in `src/agents/mcp-metadata.ts` returns `{}` unless `mcp.apps.enabled` is true). A server that follows the spec can't ask, so all it can do is fail. If it returns `-32042`, OpenClaw drops `data.elicitations[].url`; the agent gets only the error message, as untrusted text. The user sees a failed tool and no card.
2. **With `mcp.apps.enabled: true`:** OpenClaw declares `elicitation: { form: {}, url: {} }`. A URL request then shows up as a generic "Browser step" question (`compileStructuredInputUrl` in `src/agents/harness/structured-input.ts`):
   - The server's own URL appears in the question text.
   - The options are "I've completed this step" and "Decline", so the user has to report that they finished.
   - It is not the Connect card. The link isn't tied to the user and server, isn't single-use and doesn't expire.
   - Nothing handles `notifications/elicitation/complete` or `-32042` (no match for either in `src/`).

## Repro (main at 0956e14e6814)

- An isolated Gateway (own HOME, state and config, channels off) with a stand-in OpenAI-compatible model that calls `tracker__list_issues`.
- `tracker` is a tiny stdio MCP server, about 50 lines of raw JSON-RPC. On `tools/call`:
  - If the client declared `elicitation.url`, it sends `elicitation/create` with `mode: "url"`.
  - Otherwise it returns `-32042` with the URL in `data.elicitations`.
- The Control UI was driven in headless Chromium: "List my Fixture Tracker issues."

| Config | Capabilities the server got | What the user sees |
| --- | --- | --- |
| default | `{}` | "Tracker List Issues failed", the error text only, no link, no card |
| `mcp.apps.enabled: true` | `elicitation: { form: {}, url: {} }` plus MCP Apps extensions | "Waiting for your answer" question showing the raw server URL, with "I've completed this step" / "Decline" |

Default:

![Default config: the tool fails and the sign-in link is dropped](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/07b9d45e926918561cd36d9ee83073fe7376b362/images/2026/11/2cd2bacd-8054-410f-ad27-990e53c37417.png)

With `mcp.apps.enabled`:

![MCP Apps flag on: generic browser-step question with the raw server link](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/bcb21dabb4ccf58438c9559a7a1ddf5e70d22d56/images/2026/11/512f7a41-443c-4fd0-8539-c1d070f64b26.png)

## Expected (spec route)

- The bundle MCP client declares `elicitation.url` for agent turns. This doesn't depend on MCP Apps, and form mode can stay behind that flag.
- An `elicitation/create` with `mode: "url"`, or a `-32042` with `data.elicitations`, becomes the same Connect card as #200538:
  - Shown to the owner only. Group chats and non-owner turns get no link, and the request is declined as `cancel`, not `decline`.
  - Delivered with no link previews.
  - Sent as a Gateway link bound to the requester and the server. It is single-use and expires. It redirects to the server's URL only on first use by that user.
  - The card shows the target domain, as the spec asks. The client never opens or prefetches the URL by itself.
- `accept` means "the user chose to open it". Completion comes from `notifications/elicitation/complete` (or a retry of the call), not from a "done" button.
- Servers that never send URL elicitations behave exactly as today. Declaring the capability changes nothing for them.

## Not the spec route (workarounds to avoid)

- Turning on `mcp.apps.enabled` just to get URL elicitation. It's an unrelated opt-in, and it gives the generic question above, not the Connect card.
- Moving a stdio server behind HTTP OAuth so that #200538's `<server>__connect` applies.
- Letting the agent copy a URL out of the server's error text into its reply. The link goes through model text, gets channel link previews, and isn't bound to anyone.
- Having the server open a browser on the Gateway host, which doesn't reach a user on another device.

## Open questions

- Should the capability be declared for every agent turn, or only for turns that can present the card (owner, untainted direct chat)? If only for some turns, a server sees different capabilities depending on the turn.
- Claude CLI turns: #164510 (open) reports that `claude-cli` declines every MCP elicitation, so that runtime would need the same handling.

## Related

- #200538: Connect card for HTTP OAuth servers
- #164510: `claude-cli` auto-declines MCP elicitations
- #58161 (closed): MCP elicitations in the embedded MCP client

# Follow-up: await post-ready maintenance in pending-install lifecycle fixture

The first case in `src/gateway/server-plugins.lifecycle.channels.test.ts` (hot-applies pending installs without restarting a sibling whose package metadata keys were reordered) can reach `plugins.reload` while real post-ready maintenance holds the plugin/config lifecycle lease. Its startup/config-reload readiness checks do not cover that owner. The later webhook cases already observe and await real maintenance.

## Release evidence
- Frozen candidate/qualification: `d843d6af39a42cd3c30084edbeabeece732fd93a`; FRV 43770476915/1.
- Original failure: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43770968712/job/132986918056 — `echoed` false, 1 failed / 530 passed. The original assertion did not print the RPC response, so its exact refusal cause remains unobserved.
- Same exact candidate passed this test in prior CI 43759963756/1, job132952700432. A local whole-file replay passed all3 cases; an original-shard replay passed this target but timed out on unrelated HTTP cases, so is not green-shard evidence.
- A bounded private Node24.22.1 diagnostic delayed the REAL `runGatewayPostReadyStartupMaintenance`, held the REAL registry refresh while it owned its lifecycle lease, and invoked the real `plugins.reload` RPC. This reproduced `echoed=false` with `UNAVAILABLE`, retryable=true, retryAfterMs=1000, mutationAccepted=false. No fake RPC/lease response or production change.
- Controlled comparison: release the same real refresh and await the real maintenance promise before the RPC. The unchanged target assertions then passed (1 passed / 2 unselected siblings, 26.16s wrapper; target 11.506s). This changes no production code and is not CI qualification.
- That controlled reproduction proves a missing fixture-readiness boundary; it does not retroactively establish the unlogged original RPC error.

## Requested main fix
Reuse the existing real-maintenance observation helper for the first case, await completion before the explicit reload, and expose the RPC refusal before asserting downstream metadata effects. Add bounded regression proof at the real owner boundary, retaining all sibling ownership/channel assertions. Do not relax the live lifecycle lease or add retries/sleeps to hide contention. Check current main for equivalent fixes before editing.

This is the fix-in-parallel tracking item for a bounded same-SHA release retry, not a waiver. The release candidate and P remain frozen; an unwaived CI failure still blocks publication.

issues.body:
### Summary
On 2026.9.8, `sessions_send` from a parent session to a native subagent session intermittently fails with
`session writer claim changed before transcript persistence` (`SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError`) when the target subagent is starting or finishing a turn. The tool result reports the failure, but the parent gets `status: "accepted"`/`queued` on the immediate retry while the message is still not persisted. Re-sending once the target is idle succeeds.

### Environment
- OpenClaw 2026.9.8 (fc23bc8), Linux, Gateway system service
- Target: native subagent (runtime claude-cli), queue mode `followup`, long-lived (~19 h) session
- Sender: main Telegram direct session

### Steps observed
1. Subagent X is active (running turns that announce back to the parent).
2. Parent calls `sessions_send(sessionKey=X, message=..., timeoutSeconds=0)`.
3. Parent receives an inter-session notice: `sessions_send delivery to X failed: session writer claim changed before transcript persistence. The target may not have received the message`.
4. Immediate retry fails the same way.
5. After the target's turn ends (session_status shows it idle), the same send succeeds and the message appears in `sessions_history`.

### Expected
A message addressed to an active session is queued (followup mode) and persisted once the writer claim settles, rather than dropped. If dropping is intended, the error should be retried internally, since the claim rebind is transient and not caused by the caller.

### Related
#159531 (completion handoff after the same error), #163466, #152659: same error class, different paths.

issues.body:
### Summary / Problem statement

Two CLI commands print only the generic failure plus a doctor hint when their already-composed operator remedy should reach the terminal. Both guards raise plain `Error`s **outside `runCommandWithRuntime`**, so the shared JSON-mode diagnostics fix (#199970) does not cover them — even though the earlier per-command PRs for exactly these two commands were closed with the note that the shared wrapper "covers this command too".

### Affected commands

**1. `openclaw models auth login --device-code --method password`**

`src/cli/models-cli.ts:586` throws a plain `Error` when `--device-code` is combined with an incompatible `--method`:

```ts
if (deviceCode && typeof opts.method === "string" && opts.method !== "device-code") {
  throw new Error(
    "--device-code cannot be combined with --method unless method is device-code.",
  );
}
```

This throw sits in the Commander `.action` callback, **before** `runAuthModelCommand`/`runModelsCommand` (`runCommandWithRuntime`) is entered. It bubbles to the root renderer, which only prints `humanOutput` for expected CLI errors — so the remedy collapses to:

```
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
```

The already-composed remedy line `--device-code cannot be combined with --method unless method is device-code.` never reaches the operator.

**2. `openclaw attach <url> --url <other-url>`** (and colliding prefixes / no-session cases)

`src/cli/session-target.ts` raises four operator remedies as plain `Error`s:

- `:153` — `pass one target: use either the session URL or --url, not both`
- `:199` — `Gateway returned a session without a consistent agent identity.`
- `:213` — the formatted "Session reference is ambiguous:" table + `Pass a longer reference.`
- `:222` — `No session found.` + the sessions-list hint

The `attach` command does **not** go through `runCommandWithRuntime` at all (`src/cli/attach-cli.ts` uses `defaultRuntime` directly and never imports the wrapper), so the same generic-failure collapse applies. Note that `attach` already uses `throwExpectedCliError` for its own `--session`/positional conflict at `src/cli/attach-cli.ts:81`, so the canonical path is established in this exact command — only `resolveSessionTarget` was left behind.

### Why these are not per-command duplicates of the closed fix

The shared fix #199970 ("retain command diagnostics in JSON failures") changed `runCommandWithRuntime` to print the diagnostic in both modes. Its body explicitly names these two commands as uncovered:

> Not covered: #198333 and #198345 fail outside `runCommandWithRuntime`. They remain closed; this change deliberately does not expose arbitrary root/startup errors.

And the two per-command PRs were closed with:

> We're fixing that once in the shared wrapper instead, which covers this command too. Please don't open more per-command variants of this fix; **if you find a case the shared fix doesn't cover, open an issue with a reproduction.**

The shared fix does **not** cover these two commands: the `models auth login` guard throws before `runCommandWithRuntime`, and `attach` never enters it. This issue is that "case the shared fix doesn't cover."

### Reproduction

Both on current `main` (`f8649312`), isolated `HOME`/`OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, no Gateway:

```sh
# 1) models auth login flag conflict
openclaw models auth login --provider openai --device-code --method password

# 2) attach target conflict
openclaw attach "https://gw.example/dashboard/main/abc123" --url wss://other.example
```

Observed (both): stderr shows only

```
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
```

Expected: the remedy line the guard already composed, e.g. `--device-code cannot be combined with --method unless method is device-code.` / `pass one target: use either the session URL or --url, not both`.

### Impact

- Misleading error output for two routine CLI misconfigurations; the doctor hint points at the wrong next step when the remedy is already known at the point of failure.
- Both fixes were already written and reviewed (#198333, #198345); they were closed on the assumption that the shared wrapper would cover them, which #199970 shows is not the case.

### Suggested fix shape

Replace the four/six plain `throw new Error(...)` sites with the canonical `throwExpectedCliError(...)` from `src/cli/expected-cli-error.ts`, keeping message text verbatim. `attach` already imports it, so its change is import-free; `models` needs one import. Same shape as #192127 and the closed #198333/#198345.

### Related

- #199970 — shared fix that explicitly does not cover these commands
- #198333 (closed) — models auth login guard, closed as "covered by shared fix"
- #198345 (closed) — attach resolveSessionTarget, closed as "covered by shared fix"


---

## Systematic root cause: the `showReason` whitelist in `formatCliFailureLines`

Investigation (2026-11-17) shows these two commands are instances of a broader mechanism, not isolated cases.

`src/cli/failure-output.ts:317-324` decides whether the root failure renderer prints the command's own message as `[openclaw] Reason: <msg>` on stderr:

```js
const showReason = isInvalidConfigError(options.error)
  ? !options.error.diagnosticEmitted
  : isUpdateCommand ||                       // update has Reason
    isPluginUpdateCommand ||
    (options.error instanceof Error && options.error.name === "GatewayClientRequestError") ||
    isNodeRunCommand ||                        // node run has Reason
    commandPath[0] === "connect" ||            // connect has Reason
    isForegroundGatewayRunArgv(argv);
```

Only commands in this whitelist get their already-composed message on stderr in the generic failure path. **Every other command** (`models`, `attach`, `backup`, `security`, `directory`, `logs`, `mcp`, `secrets`, …) whose guard raises a plain `Error` outside `runCommandWithRuntime` collapses to:

```
[openclaw] The CLI command failed.
[openclaw] For help, run `openclaw doctor`.
```

The whitelist was introduced with `failure-output.ts` (#198161) and retained by #199970, whose commit message explicitly names these two commands as uncovered:

> "Commands that fail outside the wrapper (for example `models auth login` conflicts and `attach` target resolution) are not covered."

So the decision is not "two commands were missed" but "which commands belong in the Reason whitelist". `update`, `plugins update`, `node run` and `connect` were added one at a time as their owners needed them; the whitelist has not been revisited as a whole.

### Verified on a real build (dist, Node 24.22.1)

| Command | stderr |
| --- | --- |
| `openclaw update --json --admission bad` | `[openclaw] Reason: --admission must be "auto" or "installed".` (in whitelist → remedy visible) |
| `openclaw models auth login --device-code --method password` | blocked earlier by the state-store guard (#198771, now renders its own remedy); the `--device-code` guard sits in the action and cannot be reached on this host |

### Two resolution directions (maintainer decision)

- **Per-site**: convert each affected command's plain `throw` to `throwExpectedCliError` (as #198333/#198345 proposed). Matches the established per-site shape, but means every command's remedy depends on its owner remembering to convert it.
- **Shared**: revisit the `showReason` whitelist as a whole — either widen it to all commands (every command's already-composed message reaches stderr) or replace it with a default-on policy with explicit opt-outs. This is the "fix once in the shared wrapper" direction the earlier closures asked for.

This issue tracks the two concrete commands; the whitelist mechanism above is the shared root cause a maintainer would want to resolve once.

issues.body:
## Summary

Codex exposes the OpenClaw Gateway shell tool as `gateway_exec`, but an automation's `payload.toolsAllow` uses the canonical `exec` capability. This distinction is not explained in the model-facing Gateway exec tool description or automation authoring guidance, making it easy for the assistant to persist the wrong name.

Please clarify the tool definitions and provide actionable validation so models do not have to infer the mapping between runtime tool names and scheduled capability names.

## Observed workflow

1. In a Codex-backed conversation, ask the assistant to create a nightly automation that needs Gateway shell access.
2. The assistant sees and uses `gateway_exec` interactively and saves that name in `payload.toolsAllow`.
3. The saved job runs, but reports that `gateway_exec` is unavailable despite it appearing in its allowed-tools list.
4. The intended maintenance is not performed.

In this case the job's first meaningful result was blocked with that exact mismatch. Later runs returned `no_change`, suppressing a repeat notification even though no successful maintenance was established.

The existing job was subsequently reauthorized with `exec` instead of `gateway_exec`, preserving its other tools. Its verification run returned `no_change`; this alone does **not** establish that the underlying maintenance successfully executed, so this report does not claim a verified end-to-end fix.

## Expected behavior

The assistant should be able to author an automation correctly from its available tool definitions:

- Explain explicitly that the Codex runtime tool `gateway_exec` maps to scheduled capability `exec` (and document the analogous `gateway_process` / `process` mapping).
- Put the guidance where models need it: the Gateway shell description and automation `toolsAllow` authoring/schema documentation.
- Validate known runtime aliases at save/update time and return a precise canonical-name correction, rather than accepting an ineffective grant and leaving the model to diagnose a missing tool at execution time.
- If safe alias normalization is supported, retain the existing creator-authority checks and captured Gateway execution restrictions. Do not broaden permissions or silently turn a pinned Gateway grant into an unrestricted shell grant.

This is a runtime naming distinction, not a claim that GPT models inherently require a different tool name.

## Source context

Inspected checkout: `2910c0de8d7d290f9a82ca388f2893d067c06cb1`.

- [Codex shell dynamic tools](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2910c0de8d7d290f9a82ca388f2893d067c06cb1/extensions/codex/src/app-server/shell-dynamic-tools.ts): `CODEX_GATEWAY_EXEC_DYNAMIC_TOOL_NAME = "gateway_exec"`; `createGatewayExecProjection` projects canonical kind `exec` under that name. Its description covers Gateway access and native-shell preference, but not the scheduled permission name.
- [Creator capability tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2910c0de8d7d290f9a82ca388f2893d067c06cb1/src/agents/tools/cron-tool-creator-cap.test.ts) distinguish canonical `name: "exec"` from `aliasName: "gateway_exec"`.
- [Scheduled tool policy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2910c0de8d7d290f9a82ca388f2893d067c06cb1/src/cron/scheduled-tool-policy.ts) handles canonical exec grants and captured restrictions.

Related: #177182 concerns metadata loss through trusted wrappers. This report focuses on the model-facing naming/authoring UX; the observed run has not been traced to that wrapper defect.

## Acceptance criteria

- An assistant seeing `gateway_exec` knows which value to use in `toolsAllow` without source inspection.
- Invalid known aliases receive an actionable save-time response or safely attested normalization.
- Regression coverage verifies the authoring guidance/validation and preservation of execution restrictions.
