prs.title: fix: stop helper replies failing on Telegram sessions that saved their own key as the chat
prs.body:
Related: #203484

## What Problem This Solves

A Telegram-linked agent session can end up storing its own session key (`agent:<agent>:<name>`) as its Telegram chat. From then on, every helper (subagent) completion announced to that session fails with `Telegram recipient must be a numeric chat ID`, and each retry fails the same way. It happens when a WebChat or inter-session turn lands on a session that already has Telegram as its channel but no stored chat yet: the turn's own address (for WebChat, the session key) is paired with the Telegram channel and saved, and later turns keep it.

## User Impact

User impact: helper completions on these sessions no longer fail at Telegram, including on sessions that stored the bad route before upgrading; the reply stays in the session instead. Sessions with a real stored chat, WebChat's own routes, and turns that arrive from Telegram itself route exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first write happens where an inbound turn's route is resolved. When an internal or inter-session turn keeps a session's established external channel, it already keeps the stored chat; with no stored chat it fell through to the turn's own `to`. The fix takes the target only from the owner of the channel, so that fall-through no longer happens.

Sessions written before this change still hold the session key, so completion delivery also drops a `to` that is an agent session key when it is paired with an external channel (the same `classifySessionKeyShape` check `agent --to` uses). A session key is never an external chat target, so no intended destination is affected; an internal route such as WebChat keeps its own session-key address.

## Evidence

Behavior checked: on current `main`, a route written by the old code makes a helper completion fail with the exact host error, and the same stored state on this branch no longer sends it to Telegram. New routes are no longer written that way. Regression tests at both points fail on `main`.

**Real model, upgrading from the latest stable (2026.11.7).** The same Gateway harness as below, with the mock model replaced by a real one over the OpenAI-compatible API (llama.cpp `llama-server --jinja`). Stable 2026.11.7 (e31bbf0) wrote the route itself, from the Telegram DM, the `agent` request and the `chat.send` turn, once with each model below. Each state directory was then started on one build. There, an `agent` request with `channel: telegram` asked the model to start a helper; the model called `sessions_spawn` itself, and the helper's completion was announced back to `agent:main:build` after the parent turn ended.

| | 2026.11.7 (`qwen3.5-9b`) | this PR (`qwen2.5-7b-instruct`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| route of `agent:main:build`, written by 2026.11.7 | `deliveryContext {channel: telegram, to: agent:main:build}`, `lastTo` and `origin.to` the same | the same shape, loaded unchanged |
| model called `sessions_spawn` | yes | yes |
| helper completion | `Subagent completion direct announce failed`: `Telegram recipient must be a numeric chat ID` | `Subagent completion delivery result`: `completion agent did not produce a visible reply`; no Telegram error |
| Telegram `sendMessage` calls | 0 | 0 |

Limits of this run: the two sides used different local models, because the CPU-only one was too slow for the stable side. On both, the helper's own turn ended at once with `No callable tools remain after resolving explicit tool allowlist`, because the harness denies session tools to helpers (a small model otherwise spawns helpers of its own); the completion that reports that ending is what takes the delivery path. The real-model runs had no Telegram DM after the upgrade; that is covered by the mock-model run below.

**Gateway run, before and after, on stored data from `main`.** One script runs a real Gateway (`node dist/index.js gateway`, Node 24.22.3) with the bundled Telegram plugin pointed at a local stand-in Bot API (`channels.telegram.apiRoot`) and the e2e mock OpenAI server. First `main` writes the route: a Telegram DM from an allowed chat, an `agent` request for `agent:main:build` with `channel: telegram`, `deliver` and `bestEffortDeliver` but no target, then a `chat.send` turn on that session. The Gateway stops, and the same state directory is started once on `main` and once on this branch. On each, an `agent` request with `channel: telegram` on that session spawns a helper that finishes after that turn has ended, so its completion takes the external delivery path. Routes are read with `sessions.describe`; the outcome is the Gateway's own `Subagent completion delivery result` log line. The chat id is the stand-in's.

| Step | `main` (3ff1109b0a6) | this PR (8fb32fe103) on that `main` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| route after the `chat.send` turn, written by `main` | `{channel: telegram, to: agent:main:build}`, `lastTo: agent:main:build`, `origin {provider: telegram, to: agent:main:build}` | the same stored state, loaded unchanged |
| helper completion | fails: `Telegram recipient must be a numeric chat ID` | no Telegram attempt; the reply is in the session transcript |
| Telegram `sendMessage` calls | 0 | 0 |

On this branch with a fresh state directory, that route stays `{channel: telegram}`, `lastTo: null`, `origin {provider: telegram}` after the `chat.send` turn (table below). The Telegram DM's reply went to `chat_id 12345` on both builds.

<details>
<summary>Earlier run: the first write, before and after (main adb2f7c4d4b, this PR b395d277417)</summary>

| Step | `main` | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Telegram DM from chat 12345 | `{channel: telegram, to: telegram:12345}` | same |
| `agent` request, Telegram, no target | `{channel: telegram}`, `origin {provider: telegram}` | same |
| `chat.send` on that session | `{channel: telegram, to: agent:main:build}`, `lastTo: agent:main:build`, `origin {provider: telegram, to: agent:main:build}` | `{channel: telegram}`, `lastTo: null`, `origin {provider: telegram}` |

</details>

Host evidence (redacted, `sessions.describe` on 2026.11.6): the affected session shows `channel: telegram`, and `deliveryContext.to`, `lastTo` and `origin.to` each equal its own session key, the shape `main` writes above. Error on the first attempt and both retries: `Failed to route reply to telegram: Telegram recipient must be a numeric chat ID`.

Gaps:

- After the fix, the Gateway classifies that completion as `completion agent did not produce a visible reply`, though the reply is in the session transcript. `main` gives the same result for a Telegram-channel session that never stored a chat (the `agent` request with no target, then a helper, no `chat.send`), so that is how current `main` treats a channel-only external route; this PR does not change it.
- The stored record keeps the session key, and completion delivery ignores it. Nothing rewrites old rows.
- Harness changes, outside the repo: a proxy holds the helper's model turn back 45 s so it completes after the parent turn, and asks for a one-shot helper (the binding fixture's `thread: true, mode: "session"` is rejected for a session with no thread to bind).
- The Telegram Test Server userbot lane needs leased credentials we do not have. The affected host session predates our logs, so the turn that first wrote it there is not recorded.

<details>
<summary>Tests and checks (Node 24.22.3, pnpm 12.15.0)</summary>

- `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/session-delivery.test.ts src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce-origin.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 14 passed. On `main`, 3 fail: both route cases return `{ channel: "telegram", to: "agent:main:build" }`, and the stored-target case keeps `to`.
- `pnpm test src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.format.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 29 passed. The new case runs the announce flow with a requester session storing `lastChannel: telegram` and its own key as `lastTo`; on `main` the Gateway `agent` call gets `deliver: true, to: "agent:main:main"`, here `deliver: false` with no target.
- `pnpm check:changed` (this change on `main` 3ff1109b0a6): every step passed, including typecheck core and core tests, the core test graphs, lint, format, the SQLite worker and mock export ratchets, and the dead export scan.
- Local review: no autoreview or local ClawSweeper could run in this environment; the diff was reviewed by hand.

</details>

Git updates build the Control UI twice: release preparation runs `pnpm build`, which already includes the UI, and then invokes `pnpm ui:build` again. This repeats work inside the same update deadline.

Git updates build each prepared release once, including its Control UI assets. No configuration or migration is required.

Keep the target's full build as the single owner of runtime and UI artifacts. Remove the second UI invocation and align progress accounting. The fixture now models the real full-build contract and counts UI invocations while retaining the existing artifact and unchanged-checkout assertions.

The first release-aware updater commit (`be5f7fad9dfe8e709e454288ee3a7b03ea4b1a3b`) already included UI in `pnpm build`. Older unsupported targets keep their manual-update guidance. Production delta: -1 line; test delta: +1 line.

prs.title: feat(ui): separate dictation and Talk buttons in the chat composer
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

The web composer overloads one microphone button: tap starts realtime Talk, hold starts dictation. iOS and Android separate these: the mic dictates, and a waveform control starts Talk. On the web that gesture is undiscoverable, it's easy to start the wrong mode, and it doesn't match the native apps.

Related: #204271 (same problem; that issue proposes keeping one button).

## What changed

- **Mic = dictation.** Tap to start, tap again to stop and keep the transcript. The mic never starts Talk.
- **New waveform button = Talk.** Tap starts or stops a Talk session in the **configured mode**: realtime, or split STT/TTS when `talk.realtime.mode` is `stt-tts`. It never submits the draft. While active, it animates from the live mic level (and playback level where it can be metered).
- Dictation and Talk are mutually exclusive.
- The device picker stays in the mic menu and applies to both.
- Readiness follows the configured mode: the waveform is hidden when the active mode's providers aren't ready, and the menu shows the reason for what's missing in that mode.
- New Session stays dictation-only.
- The old hold-to-dictate preference is ignored on load and dropped on the next settings save. No voice-note recording was added (the web has none today).

## Evidence

- Unit tests: mic tap start/stop, Talk start/stop in both modes, mutual exclusion, capability hiding, preference migration (74 focused tests pass).
- Rendered on a test Gateway in STT/TTS mode: idle composer with mic and waveform; dictation active; Talk reached Listening about 1.2 s after the tap, and the waveform followed a recorded voice (0.63 to 1.00, then back to 0.28 when speech ended).
- Not yet verified: waveform animation during reply playback.
- UI asset budget compared against the exact base: no regression from this change (pre-existing budget warnings unchanged).

Draft: hands-on test by the requester in progress.

prs.title: fix: tell people how to recover when doctor --fix cannot repair a broken config
prs.body:
Fixes #204504

## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw.json` becomes unparseable (a truncated write, an interrupted editor, a bad merge) and `openclaw doctor --fix` cannot recover it, Doctor tells the user to run `openclaw doctor --fix`. That is the command they just ran. It says so five times, then exits 2. `openclaw config validate` also points users at `doctor --fix`, so a user who follows the advice ends up in a loop with no way out. #126757 fixed this dead end in August. The Doctor path added for PostgreSQL in #175069 brought it back.

## User Impact

User impact: when `doctor --fix` cannot repair a broken config, it says so and names the way out. Inspect the parse error with `openclaw config validate`, then hand-edit the file, or move it aside and run `openclaw onboard`. This is what `docs/cli/doctor/checks.md` already promises.

These cases are unchanged:

- Plain `openclaw doctor` still suggests `--fix`, which can repair some broken files, for example by stripping a non-JSON prefix.
- Configs that `--fix` can repair are still repaired.
- The file is never modified, and the exit code stays 2.

## Why This Change Was Made

Since #175069, Doctor recovers config before any storage opens, with no database access. In that mode the #126757 refusal is skipped, and the blocked-Doctor report printed a fixed hint that always included "(or run `openclaw doctor --fix`)".

The report now uses the same flag check that decides whether recovery runs, and drops that suggestion once recovery has run. It shows the #126757 next steps instead. That wording now has one owner, shared with the existing refusal in `doctor-config-preflight-legacy-config.ts`.

If the recovery attempt itself errors, for example because another process holds the config lock, the old wording stays. Re-running `doctor --fix` can help in that case.

## Evidence

**Real CLI, built from this branch, on a truncated `openclaw.json` in an isolated state dir:**

Before (current `main`, `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive --yes`, exit 2):

```
◇  Config
│  Config invalid; doctor will run with best-effort config.
│  - <root>: JSON5 parse failed: SyntaxError: JSON5: invalid end of input at 4:1
│  Run `openclaw config validate` to inspect the parse error.
◇  Shared state
│  unknown: config could not be parsed; fix config (or run `openclaw doctor --fix`), then rerun
   ... same line under Agent state, Sessions, Credentials, Cron ...
└  Doctor blocked. Database checks remain unknown; no state migrations were performed.
```

After (this branch, same command, exit 2, config byte-identical):

```
◇  Config
│  Config invalid; doctor will run with best-effort config.
│  - <root>: JSON5 parse failed: SyntaxError: JSON5: invalid end of input at 4:1
│  Doctor cannot repair this file automatically; it remains unchanged.
│  Inspect the exact parse error with openclaw config validate, then
│  hand-edit the file; or move it aside and run openclaw onboard to
│  generate a fresh config.
◇  Shared state
│  unknown: config could not be parsed or repaired; fix config, then rerun
   ... same line under Agent state, Sessions, Credentials, Cron ...
└  Doctor blocked. Database checks remain unknown; no state migrations were performed.
```

**Related flows checked on the same build:**

- Plain `openclaw doctor` still suggests `doctor --fix`.
- A config with a non-JSON prefix is still repaired by `doctor --fix`: "Removed non-JSON prefix from openclaw.json." and exit 0.

**Tests:**

- New regression test in `src/cli/database-engine-selection.test.ts`, run through `prepareCliDatabaseEngine`.
  - The `--fix` case fails on `main` because the output still contains `doctor --fix`, and passes with this change.
  - The plain-`doctor` case passes on both, as a control.
- `src/cli/database-engine-selection.test.ts`, `src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.test.ts`, `src/cli/run-main.cleanup.test.ts`, `src/cli/run-main.profile-env.test.ts` and `src/commands/onboard.test.ts`: all 261 tests pass.
- `oxfmt`, `oxlint` and `git diff --check` are clean.
- `tsgo:core` reports no errors in the changed files. My local install reports unrelated `allowDrvfsRenameRecovery` and fs-safe type errors in untouched files, from dependency drift against current `main`. CI's install is authoritative.

prs.title: fix: keep automation turns alive when nothing is pending
prs.body:
Closes #204291

## What Problem This Solves

Automations that call `sessions_yield` stop running mid-task even when nothing is waiting on them. The yield ends the model turn silently, so the automation never produces its final reply. Fix: automation yields now return `nothing_pending` when no child sessions are unsettled, letting the model continue.

- Problem: `sessions_yield` in a cron or in-session automation placement returned `status: "yielded"` unconditionally when there were no wake-armed execs, even if no child sessions were pending. The `sessions_yield` tool mapped `{ schedulerOwned: true }` to `status: "yielded"`, which terminated the turn.
- Solution: In the scheduler-owned branch of `createRequesterYieldCallback`, check `listUnsettledRequesterChildren` when there are no wake-armed execs. Return `false` (maps to `nothing_pending`) when no children are pending.
- What changed: `src/agents/openclaw-tools.requester-yield.ts` — scheduler-owned callback is now async; when `execs.length === 0`, it checks pending children before declaring scheduler ownership. Test files updated to cover the corrected behavior.
- What did NOT change: scheduler-owned yields with pending children still return `{ schedulerOwned: true }` (unchanged). Wake-armed exec in-place resume path unchanged. Interactive (non-scheduler-owned) yield path unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scheduler-owned branch only checked `listYieldAwaitableExecs` (wake-armed commands) and returned `{ schedulerOwned: true }` whenever that list was empty — skipping the pending-children check that the interactive path already does. The fix mirrors the interactive path's `listUnsettledRequesterChildren` check.

- Best fix: Yes — reuses the same `listUnsettledRequesterChildren` API already used by the interactive path, minimal change scope.
- Alternative: A dedicated `hasUnsettledRequesterChildren` boolean could avoid materializing the full list, but the list is already small (subagent children per session) and not worth a new API surface.
- Risk / non-goals: The callback changed from sync to async; callers already `await` the claim result, so no behavior change at call sites. Not tested: scheduler-owned yields in multi-turn cron scenarios where children from earlier turns are pending.

## User Impact

Automations that yield with `sessions_yield` now continue to their final reply instead of stopping silently. No user action or migration needed.

## Evidence

Ran focused tests on the three affected test files. All 96 tests pass, including 3 new test cases covering interactive, cron run session, and in-session automation placements yielding with nothing pending.

```
npx vitest run src/agents/openclaw-tools.requester-yield.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓  infra  src/agents/openclaw-tools.requester-yield.test.ts > requester yield ownership > ends a cron run session execution and releases its child to scheduler-owned delivery 1208ms
 ✓  infra  src/agents/openclaw-tools.requester-yield.test.ts > requester yield ownership > ends a in-session automation execution and releases its child to scheduler-owned delivery 1169ms
 ✓  infra  src/agents/openclaw-tools.requester-yield.test.ts > requester yield ownership > keeps a interactive turn going when it yields with nothing pending 1093ms
 ✓  infra  src/agents/openclaw-tools.requester-yield.test.ts > requester yield ownership > keeps a cron run session turn going when it yields with nothing pending 985ms
 ✓  infra  src/agents/openclaw-tools.requester-yield.test.ts > requester yield ownership > keeps a in-session automation turn going when it yields with nothing pending 1224ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  43 passed (43)

npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.sessions-yield.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓  infra  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.sessions-yield.test.ts > automation yield > keeps the automation turn going when nothing is pending 7607ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  36 passed (36)
```

What was not tested: multi-turn cron scenarios where children from earlier turns remain unsettled at yield time.

Changelog

Sourced from org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on's changelog.

Version 1.87

Release: 1.87
Date: 2026, 11th November.

Defects Fixed

  • PrivateKeyFactory, and so the ML-DSA and ML-KEM KeyFactory services, ignored the tag of the RFC 9881 / RFC 9935 private key CHOICE and applied no length checks, so mislabelled or inconsistent seed, expandedKey and both forms were accepted. Each form is now checked for its tag, exact lengths and consistency; the pre-RFC draft forms are still read.
  • X500Name.equals was quadratic in the number of RDNs for names that are equal but not byte-identical, and is reached from unverified CMS, TSP and S/MIME messages; the CMS signer and recipient stores could also be slowed with colliding ids. Name comparison is now n log n and the stores no longer hash their entries (CVE-2026-103611).
  • Tables keyed on ASN.1 object hash codes, which a sender can make collide - Extensions, X509Extensions, ExtendedKeyUsage, the CMS AttributeTable, the EST CSRAttributesResponse and the CMS digest algorithm sets - made parsing quadratic in the number of entries. They are now ordered maps and sets.
  • CMSSignedData digested the content once for every signer verified. Signers using the same digest algorithm now share one digest, and the new org.bouncycastle.cms.max_digest_algorithms property can bound the number of distinct digest algorithms computed over one message.
  • The verify side of the ML-DSA-CALCULATE-MU signature service, and MLDSASigner.verifyMu, did not absorb the message, so a correct mu was accepted only for an empty message, and the signer was left unusable afterwards. verifyMu now derives mu as generateMu does and compares in constant time.
  • KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("SM2", "BC") was built on the generic EC generator and could draw a private key of n - 1, which GB/T 32918.1 excludes. It now uses SM2KeyPairGenerator.
  • ESTResponse was quadratic in the number of repeated header lines, and a read limit only applied after the header block. Header values are now collected once and the header block counts against the read limit.
  • The C509 encoding of RFC 6955 proof-of-possession signature values and of the RFC 9883 privateKeyPossessionStatement attribute did not follow draft-ietf-cose-cbor-encoded-cert-21 and could not be reconstructed. Both now convert in each direction, and the draft-ietf-cose-c509-test-vectors-02 vectors drive the tests.
  • DANE SMIMEA support: JndiDANEFetcherFactory mangled the owner name of listed records so lookups failed, DANEEntryStore kept only one entry per owner name, and DANEEntrySelectorFactory mishandled addresses with a quoted local-part or no '@'. All three are corrected, and DANEEntry rejects a record that is not a full certificate entry.
  • TimeStampToken accepted a token whose signing-time attribute disagreed with the genTime in its TSTInfo. Such a token is now rejected (org.bouncycastle.tsp.allow_inconsistent_signing_time switches the check off), and TimeStampTokenGenerator sets signing-time from the genTime (CVE-2026-103615).
  • TimeStampToken.validate() accepted an MD5 message imprint and TSPAlgorithms.ALLOWED included MD5. MD5 is removed from ALLOWED, validate() rejects an imprint algorithm outside the allowed set, and TSPAlgorithms.LEGACY and org.bouncycastle.tsp.allowed_imprint_algorithms are provided for callers needing it (CVE-2026-103606).
  • CRL-based revocation checking mishandled a CRL entry reasonCode outside the RFC 5280 set: 11 left the certificate unrevoked and other values threw an unchecked exception. An undefined reasonCode is now processed as unspecified.
  • OERDefinition.enumItem(label, value) discarded the explicit enumerand value. The value is now kept and unnumbered items are numbered as X.680 sec. 20 specifies.
  • OERInputStream did not detect a stream ending inside an INTEGER or BIT STRING value, decoding the zero-padded buffer instead. Length-driven reads now fail with EOFException and do not allocate a declared length up front.
  • The OER codec encoded a signed INTEGER whose upper bound is exactly the maximum of a fixed-size word in the next word up; X.696 sec. 10.4 bounds are inclusive.
  • The ETSI TS 102 941 response code wrappers range-checked a truncated int value, so 2^32 was accepted as "ok". Out-of-range values are now rejected.
  • OERInputStream accepted an empty group of octets as zero in four places where X.696 requires at least one octet. Each now fails with an IOException.
  • OEROutputStream could not encode a CHOICE whose chosen alternative has a tag number of 63 or more.
  • OEROutputStream rejected a required SEQUENCE component as absent when it arrived wrapped in a defined OEROptional.
  • OERInputStream failed with a NullPointerException for an absent optional SEQUENCE component selected through a switch that has a default value.
  • OERInputStream truncated a SEQUENCE OF count to 32 bits. A count that does not fit in 31 bits is now rejected.
  • OERInputStream rejected a valid SEQUENCE OF on streams whose available() reported fewer bytes than the element count. The count is now bounded by the decoder's allocation ceiling instead.
  • OERInputStream could not decode a variable-size BIT STRING, and mis-sized a fixed one that is not a whole number of octets. Both forms of X.696 clause 13 are now decoded, and OERDefinition gains bitString() and bitString(lower, upper).
  • OEROutputStream wrote a negative INTEGER under a type with a non-negative lower bound as a different, positive value. It is now rejected.
  • OERInputStream.uint64() read its value as signed; it now reads unsigned.
  • The OER codec treated an INTEGER with a positive lower bound as signed, where X.696 sec. 10.2 gives it the unsigned encodings.
  • The OER codec encoded and decoded negative ENUMERATED values wrongly; both directions now follow X.696 sec. 11.4.
  • ASN1Enumerated rejected negative values, which X.680 allows. The checks are removed, isNegative() and longValueExact() are added, and valueOf() returns shared instances for 0 to 15.
  • A PBEKey stored in a BCFKS KeyStore was not reported as a key entry, so KeyStore.getEntry() returned null for it.
  • The CMS content-type decoders (SignedData, EnvelopedData, AuthenticatedData, AuthEnvelopedData, EncryptedData) and the streaming CMS parsers let unchecked exceptions escape for short or malformed content. Malformed content is now reported through the declared CMSException or IOException.
  • A KeyAgreement asked for its shared secret before doPhase returned data rather than throwing IllegalStateException - for Diffie-Hellman, the private value itself. Every key agreement in the provider now refuses the request.
  • Mac.getInstance and KeyGenerator.getInstance failed for the HMAC SHA-512/224 and SHA-512/256 object identifiers; both are now aliased.
  • A KTSParameterSpec naming an HKDF with parameters was accepted at Cipher init and failed with an unchecked exception from wrap or unwrap. The KTS Ciphers now report it at init as InvalidAlgorithmParameterException.
  • A DTLS handshake deadlocked when a handshake message ahead of the peer's ChangeCipherSpec was lost while the ChangeCipherSpec and Finished arrived, as retransmissions were discarded as belonging to the old epoch. They are now accepted until the handshake completes.
  • The lightweight key info factories encoded a GOST R 34.10-2012 key on a legacy CryptoPro curve under id-GostR3410-2001. The digestParamSet now decides, and is OPTIONAL on read and write per RFC 9215 (bc-csharp github #707).
  • Name-constraint checking canonicalised a host with an extra empty label, such as "example.com..", into a name that matched no constraint, escaping an excluded subtree. A tested name whose host carries an empty label is now refused where a constraint of that type is in force (github PR #2436).
  • SSLContext.createSSLEngine() from BCJSSE in the 1.86 bctls jar failed with NoSuchMethodError on JDK 9 and later, from a return type mismatch between the base and jdk1.9 copies of SSLEngineUtil. The copies now agree, and a new multiReleaseCheck build task checks every multi-release jar for such mismatches (github #2448).
  • The BCFKS key store derived its scrypt keys with the block size r in place of the parallelization parameter p, so stores with p != r were not RFC 7914 readable. Derivation now follows RFC 7914, older stores are still read, and org.bouncycastle.bcfks.scrypt_p_eq_r (default true) keeps written stores readable by earlier releases.
  • Building an evidence record was cubic in the number of data objects. SortedHashList and SortedIndexedHashList now sort once, with the same resulting order and root hashes (github #2456).
  • ERSDataGroup recomputed its hash on every request rather than using the ERSCachingData cache.
  • ERSArchiveTimeStampGenerator rebuilt its reduced hash tree on every call; it is now built once.
  • Grain-128AEAD returned corrupted plaintext, with no error, from a decryption driven in chunks carrying more than the tag length. One-shot decryption and encryption were unaffected (github PR #2447).
  • The certificate path validators looked up an indirect CRL entry by serial number alone, so where two issuers had revoked the same serial number a revoked certificate could be reported as not revoked. Entries are now matched on issuer and serial number, including for CRLs parsed by the JDK's provider and in the jdk1.4 distribution.

Release notes

Sourced from org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-serialization-json's releases.

v1.13.0

This release is based on Kotlin 2.4.10 and reverts a breaking change introduced in 1.12.0.

Besides that, it improves JsonElement.toString performance.

Exceptions rework rollback

In 1.12.0, Json format started intercepting almost all exceptions thrown by serializers during serialization and deserialization, and wrapping them into a JsonException with additional information about JSON path and input.

The impact of the change was underestimated, and it was decided to revert the change.

Performance improvements

JsonElement.toString was rewritten and its improved twofold on some benchmarks. See #3296 and #3299 for details.

Updates `org.robolectric:robolectric` from 4.17 to 4.18.1
Release notes

Sourced from org.robolectric:robolectric's releases.

Robolectric 4.18.1 is a minor release that fixes several issues and improves the Robolectric simulator.

It fixes data races that ThreadSanitizer reported when several threads link calls to the same shadow method at once (#11784, #11786). It also fixes ShadowServiceManager.waitForService, which never blocked and could throw IllegalMonitorStateException (#11758), and scheduled task time queries on ShadowPausedLooper, which returned wrong times on newer SDKs and could race when called off the Looper thread (#11780, thanks to Brett Chabot). Content providers are now installed for lazily created applications (#11775), and Choreographer display receivers are disposed, which fixes a CloseGuard leak and stale clock callbacks (#11688, thanks to @​utzcoz).

For the simulator, it handles mouse and keyboard input when running headless (#11750) and advances the system clock by the time spent rendering (#11783). It also adds two opt-in system properties, which the simulator Gradle plugin turns on: robolectric.bindRealServices=true binds to the app's own services the way the system does (#11748), and robolectric.installDefaultUncaughtExceptionHandler=true installs an uncaught exception handler that logs crashes the way Android does (#11734).

Full Changelog: https://github.com/robolectric/robolectric/compare/robolectric-4.18...robolectric-4.18.1

Robolectric 4.18 adds Linux arm64 support to the native runtime, supports native resources on SDK 36 and above, and contains many performance improvements and bug fixes.

If you have any issues, please file them here.

Breaking Changes

  • Support for SDK 23 has been removed. The minimum supported SDK is now 24, matching AndroidX (#11604).
  • The shadows-httpclient module has been removed. It was deprecated in 4.17, and org.apache.http is no longer instrumented (#11373, #11544).
  • @TextLayoutMode has been removed. Realistic text layout, the default since 2019, is now always used (#11498).
  • ShadowRemoteCallbackList has been removed, as the real RemoteCallbackList works without it (#11368).
  • HttpResponseCache.install() now also sets ResponseCache.getDefault(), as it does on a device (#11493).

Linux arm64 support

Robolectric's native runtime now includes Linux arm64 (aarch64) native libraries, so tests that use native SQLite (the default) and native graphics (@GraphicsMode(NATIVE)) can run on Linux arm64 environments, such as GitHub's ubuntu-24.04-arm runners, AWS Graviton machines, and arm64 Docker containers on Apple silicon. prs.title: improve(ui): defer sign-in controls until needed
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening Plugins loads sign-in controls and their channel/provider presentation even when no sign-in is active. This adds requests to the first visit and contributes to the route asset budget failure.

## User Impact

Plugins can open without downloading optional sign-in controls. Starting sign-in keeps its dialog and cancellation available while the controls load. A failed download offers guarded Reload; reloading restarts the page and requires starting sign-in again.

## Why This Change Was Made

Defer the controls at the existing wizard view boundary. Keep the wizard controller, draft, dialog, cancellation and retained-step state in their existing owners. Extend the existing focus owner to wait for the controls to mount.

## Evidence

- UI typecheck, translation checks and targeted lint pass. All 49 model-view, wizard-view and login-controller tests pass (1.35 s); the two text-input cases also pass when run alone from a cold process (0.675 s).
- All five model-setup browser scenarios pass across the focused invocations, including cancellation before download release, guarded reload followed by new sign-in, and device-code focus. All four unchanged first-visit asset limits pass. The corrected recovery scenario and all four asset-limit cases pass together; screenshots were captured from that production-bundle run.
- The exact starting revision also reports the five existing CSS/chat asset budget warnings. No budget is raised by this change.

### Performance acceptance rule (recorded before comparison)

Use the committed production route benchmark, settled New Session, Chromium desktop, 100 ms simulated response latency, five serial alternating baseline/candidate pairs and fresh browser contexts. Record completed-by-ready asset counts and route-ready median/p95 separately. Accept fewer Plugins assets with no greater than 5% latency regression. Preserve the route caps: Skills 30, Skill Settings 31, Plugins 56, Plugin Settings 61. Verify idle sign-in controls are not requested; held controls retain loading/cancel feedback, successful loading restores focus, cancellation settles before release, and a failed download has working guarded recovery. Do not extrapolate these measurements to CI billing or real-provider runtime savings.

Local autoreview covered the complete candidate against `a4eb11709489cade65190b963119d447f2d40c35` at P0–P2. Its recovery-message finding referred only to the old indexed version and was resolved by staging the tested correction; it identified no additional defect in the corrected working tree. A separate fresh review of the readiness-test correction is scoped-clean at P0–P2. Local ClawSweeper remains unavailable because its checkout is divergent. The completed hosted review found the recovery-message issue addressed below.

### Measured result at `65704884f28b1c8361cc0f20f631264b02c67868`

Five counterbalanced baseline/candidate pairs, fresh Chromium browser contexts, synthetic Gateway, desktop viewport, settled New Session and 100 ms HTTP/RPC delay. All 10 observations passed with zero browser errors, long tasks or layout shift.

| Metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Assets completed by page readiness, each run | 56 | 52 |
| Encoded asset bytes by page readiness, each run | 295,583 | 291,353 |
| Page-ready median | 1,195.1 ms | 1,095.0 ms |
| Page-ready p95 | 1,206.8 ms | 1,108.3 ms |
| Page-ready range | 1,194.8–1,206.8 ms | 1,093.6–1,108.3 ms |
| Renderer main-thread CPU median | 106.9 ms | 100.2 ms |

The first visit stops loading the channel picker JS/CSS, provider presentation JS and wizard controls JS/CSS, and gains one small English-catalog chunk: a net reduction of four assets. The accepted outcome is four fewer first-visit assets and an 8.4% lower page-ready median under this fixture. One-minute host load ranged from 8.64 to 10.38. This is a local browser comparison, not measured CI billing or real-provider runtime savings. Visible content, eight plugin rows and 15 inputs are preserved. The exact-base build comparison also confirms unchanged CSS sizes and chat request count; candidate chat gzip is 19 B larger. Existing budget warnings remain visible and no limits changed.

Reproduce with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-engines.ts --bundle-dir <base-build> --compare-bundle-dir <candidate-build> --engines chromium --network-profiles rtt-100ms --viewport desktop --steps page-plugins-visit --pairs 5 --fresh-browser --output <proof-directory>`.

[Clean and annotated before/after visual proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204484#issuecomment-7125545628).

### Current CI dependency

The separate release-fixture type errors are repaired by merged [PR #204478](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204478). [Run 45357278639](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45357278639) at `5a9ce0414113418690b3a067f0159264e7431ed2` passes all three UI unit shards, browser E2E and performance checks. Its baseline-ratchet job fails the unrelated release-test mock export at `plugin-npm-prepared-release-retained-producer.test.ts:10`.

The exact mock repair is now merged through [PR #204497](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204497), commit `ca348bee5543338c02e224edf13c9d0175bc640f`. The identical later [PR #204498](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204498) stays closed as a duplicate. Native preparation published signed candidate `fd1bad9d171d0d9db9abd23fda28b6c7c44badc2` with both merged baseline repairs. Its seven UI files and dependency manifests are byte-identical to the tested source head. Fresh independent complete-candidate review against `ca348bee` is scoped-clean at P0–P2. Required fresh CI is pending; no merge is armed.

Landing remains subject to the existing CI and review gates. No rerun, limit increase, skipped assertion, or administrative CI override has been used.


### Corrections after review and CI

The failed controls download now says “Couldn’t load this step. Reload the page to start over.” The guarded reload and normal rendering-error Retry behavior are unchanged. The new browser assertion fails with the original raw module URL and passes with the corrected message. [Clean and annotated recovery screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204484#issuecomment-7125839528).

The original CI UI job also exposed two device-code fixture cases reading controls before their lazy import completed. Both failures reproduce locally. Those cases and the text-input cases now wait for the actual controls before running their original link, clipboard and accessibility assertions. No assertions or time limits were weakened. All 49 related tests pass.

The corrected UI source was tested at `5a9ce0414113418690b3a067f0159264e7431ed2`; the baseline-refreshed candidate is published at `fd1bad9d171d0d9db9abd23fda28b6c7c44badc2`. The performance table above remains the measurement of the earlier implementation; this follow-up changes recovery wording and test readiness, and does not claim a new timing or byte-count result. All existing landing gates remain in force.


The `model-providers-page.login-refresh` test was also observing “configuration refresh started” before the lazy credential input mounted. The exact seven-test file reproduced one failure; waiting for the real input as part of the existing readiness check makes all seven pass. Every disabled-state, refresh-completion and identity assertion remains, with the same timeout. Targeted lint and formatting pass, and fresh local autoreview of this delta against `9159cb06` is scoped-clean at P0–P2. The completed hosted review of `9159cb06` has zero findings; the only later change is this test-readiness correction.

Current candidate CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45359308505 (`fd1bad9d171d0d9db9abd23fda28b6c7c44badc2`).

prs.title: feat: invite someone to help in one session without giving them Gateway-wide write access
prs.body:
Related: #201526

## What Problem This Solves

A session creator needs to let a teammate contribute to one conversation without giving that person Gateway-wide write access. Read-only invitations cannot express the difference between watching, proposing a message, and asking the assistant to do work in that session.

## User Impact

User impact: creators and administrators can invite people at **Can read**, **Can suggest**, or **Can send**, bounded by the invited person's role. A send-level participant can work with the session's assistant without acquiring the creator's identity or general management permissions.

- **Opt in by role, grant access per session.** Set `gateway.roles.definitions.<role>.sessions.others: "invited"` and `maxInvitedAccess: "read" | "suggest" | "send"`. The role ceiling alone grants no membership. Creators select an invitation level in @mentions (default **Can read**) or the sharing menu; stored per-member access cannot exceed the role ceiling. The narrow role can use `operator.sessions.read`, without Gateway-wide write scope.
- **Bounded session actions.** Can send admits sending, aborting the participant's own runs, typing, and permission patches that only tighten the session. It does not grant session creation, sharing management, or approval authority. Participant inputs remain separate turns rather than steering someone else's turn.
- **Configurable permissions, not a fixed Ask me cap.** `sessions.invitedPermission` accepts `read-only`, `guarded`, `workspace` (default), or `full`. Effective permission is the intersection of the invitation ceiling, the session's effective policy, and ordinary agent/host restrictions. File tools and exec's starting directory remain confined to the invited root; process observations stay scoped to the executing session. This is not an OS sandbox for shell commands or arbitrary plugins/MCP tools.
- **Configurable tools.** `sessions.invitedTools` replaces the defaults (`[]` means no tools); `sessions.invitedAlsoAllow` extends them (`[]` keeps the defaults). They are mutually exclusive, require the opt-in invitation policy, and accept ordinary tool names, groups, and wildcards for otherwise offered and authorized core, plugin, and MCP tools. There is no fixed core-tool upper allowlist. Role and agent policy can still deny a listed tool.
- **Self-authority stays denied.** The `openclaw` tool and Gateway configuration, role, membership, and restart mutations remain unavailable even with `"*"`. Plugin install/uninstall/enable/disable/reload cannot be used to acquire new authority. Allowing other tools intentionally delegates their available capabilities; it does not give them the creator's identity.
- **Approvals stay with the creator.** The non-admin session creator can approve a participant's exec request; the card identifies the person whose turn requested it. The participant receives only waiting status, not an approval card or decision controls. Direct-turn admin review remains supported; descendant exec approvals require the original creator, not an unrelated administrator.
- **Participants can stop their own turn.** A send-level participant gets Stop for their own running turn only, via exact-run `chat.abort`; this never grants broad `sessions.abort`. After a reconnect the UI keeps the original run ID and waits for current invitation evidence before offering Stop; a rejected request is discarded.

**Default participant tools:** `read`, `write`, `edit`, `apply_patch`, `ls`, `exec`, `process`, `sessions_spawn`, `sessions_yield`, `github_publish`, `skills_search`, `skills_read`, `web_search`, `web_fetch`, `tool_search`, `tool_describe`, `dispatch_action`, `view_image`, `progress_card`.

**Migration and downgrade:** the agent database advances from schema **43 to 44**, adding nullable `session_members.access`; the state schema remains **41**. This migration applies to every upgraded Gateway, even without Participate opt-in. Older binaries cannot open the newer agent schema: downgrade requires restoring a verified pre-upgrade backup with its matching binary. No main-branch schema collision required renumbering.

**Compatibility:** roles without `maxInvitedAccess` retain existing behavior; ordinary sharing omits empty member-access maps, and ordinary operator recovery retains its existing unversioned representation. The UI requests participant approval subscriptions only when the Gateway advertises support, preserving ordinary subscriptions against older/released Gateways. This is client/protocol compatibility, not database downgrade compatibility.

**Test accounting:** whole-PR test/support growth is **13,274 lines** against the unchanged allowance of **12,328** (400 + 11,928 existing allocation), so the test-line ratchet is **946 lines over and red**. This round removed 72 genuinely redundant lines and added 44 caret regression lines; no allocation was raised. The remaining lines cover distinct boundaries (native child/grandchild, restart, admission, publication, creator/admin approval guards, main-written upgrade, lazy boot, guest owner). Whether to approve the remaining excess is an open maintainer decision.

**UI budget:** Chat startup JS gzip stays under the existing **1,336,683-byte** feature cap without raising it (measured below). The SDK declaration budget is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

One role ceiling and one stored invitation level express “this person may act in this session.” The existing operator-authority owner carries the resulting restrictions into tools, children, automations, approvals, publication, and recovery instead of introducing a second execution authority. Retained work must satisfy both its captured restrictions and current policy: widening a role never silently widens an old input. The rebase keeps main's centralized request admission and lifetime structure rather than restoring duplicate policy fences.

## Evidence

**Pushed head `700d3ec535bd`, tested on merge base `cded11f`.** GitHub reports the PR open and mergeable; hosted checks for this head are running. This is not a claim that every gate is green.

- **ClawSweeper review of `6748433`:** all six items addressed. Participants can stop their own turn (above); all four static import cycles removed (Madge reports zero); participation tests sorted in the canonical inventory; Chat startup brought back under its cap; deployment-specific wording removed from docs; and an upgrade proof added (below).
- **Upgrade from main-written data:** a compressed, unmodified SQLite fixture generated by clean main `a10e4457` through its production writers (agent schema 43, no `session_members.access`) holds ordinary recovery sources, queued input, sharing state and persisted cron work. This branch migrates it to 44 and exercises ordinary authority restoration, queue consumption with transcript persistence, and cron admission through production owners, with final execution handoffs mocked. It is not a live-model or restored-downgrade proof.
- **Participant behavior:** native child/grandchild, descendant approval/restart and ordinary/guest project spawn integration pass (24 tests in 4 files at the final head); the earlier rebased selection passed 143 tests across 8 files including method inventory, schema authorization, upgrade and CLI ownership.
- **Caret fix:** the per-member access picker in the sharing popover now uses the shared select chevron and styles instead of a rotated submenu glyph; vertical misalignment went from 5px to 0px, closed and open. Verified with before/after captures of the real Control UI on synthetic mock fixtures.
- **Static/build checks:** full build; core, UI and scripts types; all 29 core test shards; scoped lint and formatting; generated config/protocol/schema checks; i18n; session identity and lifetime ratchets; zero import cycles. Dead-export scans passed before the final rebase.
- **Reviews:** independent Astra reviews of the repair delta and of the final rebase found no verified P0–P2 findings within their scope; they are not whole-PR approval.

**Chat startup budget (paired against clean `cded11f`):** Chat JS gzip **1,336,287 bytes**, **396 bytes under** the unchanged 1,336,683 cap (+237 versus main). The paired checker reports no violations. Request count is unchanged at 21; the nominal 20-request and CSS-ceiling warnings also occur on main.

**Hosted CI (previous run `45240204446`, 30 failed jobs):** every failure was classified. Branch-caused defects in seven jobs were repaired; the test-line ratchet (above) remains red; the remaining assertion failures reproduce on main with matching evidence; one UI capability-menu failure did not reproduce locally and is unresolved rather than claimed fixed; Android wear was an SDK infrastructure failure; and `ci-gate` is the aggregate. The five SDK public-surface and four max-lines failures reproduce on clean main, and the max-lines files are byte-identical to base.

<details>
<summary>Validation scope and reproducibility</summary>

The broad 65-file run used `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <participation/sharing/approval/recovery files> --maxWorkers=2` with the repository's continue-on-failure runner. Its frozen runtime source was `7336cd6685b0`; the final delta narrows unused exports and repairs worker test admission, not participant runtime policy. Final consumer tests, source/affected-test typechecks, dead-export scans, and `pnpm build` cover the pushed head. The final worker fixture rerun selected `worker-turn-launcher.test.ts -t participating` (3 passed; 34 other cases had passed before that fixture-only correction).

The four pinned-main approval failures are: the native-usage revocation error wording; a legacy caller revoked during policy read; and the legacy get/set rollback expectations after requester authority ends. Their failing source file is byte-identical on the branch and main. The review repair retains main's shared request lifetime rather than restoring removed handler-level liveness fences.

Performance was measured with `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-control-ui-performance.mts --base-dist <clean-pinned-main-dist/control-ui> --json`. Exact expanded test manifests, paired logs, final-head build output, and review evidence are retained with this task's local artifacts.
</details>

### Historical visual proof — November 20, 2026

The following screenshots are retained from the earlier `9f459e5` proof, **not the current rebased head**. They establish the original invitation, composer, requester-attributed approval, and waiting-only presentation. In particular, the pictured **Ask me** chip reflects the earlier fixed ceiling; current roles can configure `invitedPermission` as described above. These screenshots do not prove the newer subagent, automation, or publication behavior.

### Clean comparison: invited member in the creator's session

prs.title: fix(pr): retain protected resources after native squash merges
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native PR landing currently couples a successful merge with removal of the original remote branch, native checkout and eligible local branches. Maintainers who must preserve those resources cannot complete an otherwise qualified merge through the native workflow.

## User Impact

Operators can explicitly select `--retain-resources` for an ordinary, immediate, exact-head squash merge. The original remote branch, native checkout, local refs and workflow binding remain retained. The default cleanup behavior is unchanged.

Admin landing, auto-merge and merge queues are unsupported in this mode and refuse before dispatch. This workflow change is ready for normal hosted CI. Native admission and bootstrap landing remain held; no existing PR has been merged or cleaned up using it.

## Why This Change Was Made

A version-2 outcome records immutable retention/resource identities and truthful merge/completion phases. Recovery inherits the original choice when the flag is omitted, reconciles uncertain responses without redispatch, and refuses contradictory options or changed resources. Completion comments remain idempotent. Capture-independent cleanup guards prevent native GC, stale-worktree repair and finalized-task cleanup from deleting resources protected by a retained outcome.

Retention preflight checks the **head repository's** automatic branch-deletion policy and effective exact-branch protection. Unknown or bypassable protection fails closed; `--delete-branch=false` alone is not a guarantee. Checks run before and after dispatch, but cannot eliminate a concurrent GitHub policy change. A missing or advanced branch leaves an unresolved outcome; the workflow does not recreate or reset resources.

Existing source, exact-head/tree, signature, review, CI and admission gates remain required. This change does not authorize its own bootstrap landing or modify repository protections.

## Evidence

Signed candidate: `cc6fa0c3543bf49afd0fdfc0d6f393d9e6cea34b`, tree `943bc75c0530ac40292539c2fb22e45f7298823c`; parent `637693a5c762626b65a2e9a4e6fa4524df0e9ee8`; reviewed base `8bc8109271dd91aa33bd425503cb829082730fc4`.

- Retention lifecycle suite: **22 passed**, 152.731s command wall time / 150.931s test-file time at parent `dc782db5f3be8aac65998b03d601d06947a4ca61`. Production bytes were unchanged in `637693a5`; the current follow-up fixes the two default-path regressions described below.
- Final follow-up: **14 passed**, 88.496s command wall time: nine real CLI forwarding controls, two lost-response cases and three changed-resource cases. Selected file times: wrapper 40.060s; retention 46.613s. The earlier same-source anchored CLI recovery/contradictory-option case passed in 11.042s; ambiguous-flag controls passed in 21.396s. The initial invalid binding fixture failed before the intended guard, was corrected to a valid changed binding, and passed; no production change was needed.
- Existing default/admission controls: **6 passed**, 47.110s wall time, with 143 unselected cases explicitly unrun. They cover ordinary cleanup, binding retirement, completion, admin audit and queue-body admission.
- Owning tooling and script typechecks, scoped lint/format, shell syntax, helper ShellCheck and assertion-safety checks passed. Full wrapper ShellCheck still reports **SC2071**, reproduced unchanged on the exact frozen base; this is not a passing full ShellCheck claim.
- Local autoreview found no outstanding production P0–P2 issue. Its follow-up lock-recovery finding was declined after checking the actual supervisor and passing lifecycle proof: only drained ordinary failures release locks; interrupted or uncertain operations remain protected. That report retains its finding rather than being relabelled clean.
- Current two-file compatibility repair: the existing worktree-evidence suite first reproduced **9 failures / 10 passes** (33.505s); the unset-safe prior-record probe exposed **5 diagnostic failures / 14 passes** (67.268s). Restoring manual-reconciliation guidance on the same refusal path produced **19/19 passing**, 43.411s command wall / 41.922s file time. Tests and assertions are unchanged.
- Final v2 controls: **8 passed**, 19 unselected, 75.298s command wall / 73.705s file time. These cover retained completion, captureless GC/stale/finalized refusal, conflicting modes and corrupt metadata/phases. Owning tooling types, scoped lint/format, shell syntax, helper ShellCheck, whitespace and the unchanged test budget passed.
- Scoped local autoreview of the compatibility repair against `637693a5` completed in one attempt (25.930s), **scoped-clean at P0–P2**. It confirms absent-safe legacy initialization and preserved v2/refusal behavior; it did not independently execute tests.
- Net test growth is **407 lines = 400 normal allowance + 7 change-specific allocated lines**. The allocation covers the required CLI bootstrap, ambiguous-response and retained-resource identity controls. Real Git refs, wrapper trust selection, process supervision and recovery persistence require process-level fixtures; cheaper helper-only tests miss these boundaries.

Tests ran through the repository runner on macOS arm64 with Node 26.13.0 and the pinned Bun tooling lane. Original [draft CI 45355549022](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45355549022), attempt 1, was skipped and supplies no broad hosted pass.

Original [ready CI 45355831400](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45355831400), attempt 1 at `637693a5`, tested merge `38a7840a087a8e5172d76eefbf878c936116695e` into `1e0c8f8294d4051b49d8499172240898bed7bc39`. It exposed the introduced unset-variable regression in [job 138314707093](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45355831400/job/138314707093), repaired above. Separately, [baseline-ratchet job 138314706687](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45355831400/job/138314706687) rejected an incoming unannotated first-party mock at `test/scripts/plugin-npm-prepared-release-retained-producer.test.ts:10`. That file is absent from both the frozen base and `637693a5`; the actual tested base `1e0c8f8` contains it, and the mock-export guard is byte-identical across those revisions. This is source attribution, not an executed baseline pass or a waiver; the unrelated file was not changed.

The bounded original watch ended at 08:42:22 UTC. Its last CI snapshot had 29 successful jobs, 2 failed, 26 conditionally skipped and one unfinished job (`checks-node-compact-small-12`); the closeout read found [Darwin tooling 45355831314](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45355831314) successful. The unfinished job is not claimed as passing. New-head automatic CI and its observed timings remain pending. Skipped/unselected tests are not passes. Local fixtures do not prove a live GitHub policy race is impossible.

Ready status triggers normal hosted CI only. Native binding/preparation and bootstrap landing remain held; no workflow binding has been created for this PR. No merge, deployment, release, protection-setting change or checkout deletion is authorized by this transition.

prs.title: fix: apply newer npm installs when restarting the Gateway
prs.body:
Closes #204276

## What Problem This Solves

After conversion to resident releases, installing a newer global npm package changes the CLI but leaves the managed Gateway on the old release. Restart keeps that old release, ordinary update refuses, and update status can incorrectly say “up to date.”

## User Impact

User impact: after `npm i -g`, either `openclaw gateway restart` or `openclaw update` applies the installed newer package through the existing release checks and trial. No UUID-specific command or second restart is required.

| State | What the user sees |
| --- | --- |
| Newer npm package | CLI, selected release, and observed Gateway are separate; status recommends `openclaw update`. Restart, or start of a stopped service, applies the installed package through the normal trial. |
| Matching version and build | Forwarding is restored; an ordinary restart remains a restart. |
| Start while already running | No restart or downtime. Output names the old serving version, the prepared new version, and `openclaw gateway restart` to apply it. |
| Same version, different or unknown build | Status names the build difference. Explicit update validates the installed artifact; restart does not assume unknown bytes are identical. |
| Older npm package | The newer resident release stays selected. Output names `openclaw update --tag <version>` for a deliberate downgrade. |
| Pending trial / `--no-restart` | Forwarding follows the selected release; status names the pending version and its next-start activation. |
| Failed preparation | Nothing is published; the same short update command can retry. |
| Failed trial | The command exits nonzero with the update owner's rollback cause and restored serving version. The npm entry follows the recovered release, not the failed package. |
| Read-only npm tree | A forwarding warning does not undo the Gateway update. The npm entry stays separate. |
| Offline or remote Gateway | Running local version is not claimed as verified. Git and Gateway RPC installation identity checks remain in place. |

## Why This Change Was Made

The resident release prepares a retained archive of the installed npm package rather than registry latest. Managed lifecycle commands ask it only to prepare, then use their original native activation once, with the user's restart options. An existing pending trial is reused, including when npm forwarding is read-only. After native readiness, the update owner follows the recorded outcome; a healthy rollback is not a successful update. If idempotent start leaves the old Gateway running, the owner reports the still-pending release without waiting for an activation that did not occur. Status reads existing release/trial facts; there is no new schema, protocol, public flag, install hook, or background updater.

The explicit local package-to-package policy also admits another global npm prefix for this profile. It does not infer that a markerless package is the original converted tree, and it does not grant that admission to RPC callers or Git checkouts.

## Simplification and boundaries

The whole diff was reviewed with pr-simplify. The repair removes a separate native-restart fallback and leaves activation with the existing lifecycle owner, preserving `--force` and `--wait`. The existing outcome formatter is shared rather than copied into native health checks. Packing is retained through preparation, and forwarding uses the existing marker writer. No update/trial manager, installation receipt, RPC field, retry loop, or postinstall action was added.

The remaining growth implements the approved package admission, local delegation, single managed activation, archive lifetime, forwarding warning, and factual text/JSON status. Supervisor-health and legacy-release rendering code was moved unchanged to keep their existing modules bounded; moves cancel in the net count.

Net against `b0678469a4`: **+448 production TypeScript, +432 tests/support, +29 documentation lines**. This is above the design estimate. The final outcome wait and idempotent-start reporting add 46 production lines to the handed-off +402 tree; they close false-success and unactivated-trial hangs rather than introduce another update mechanism. The added tests are required regressions for these update/lifecycle and status boundaries.

## Evidence

### Local review

Two local ClawSweeper rounds were completed. The first found lost restart intent and interception of a pending trial after forwarding failed; both are repaired. The second reviewed `4134b34a13` and found that idempotent start could wait for a trial it had not activated. `46e01ac296` fixes that in the update owner and names the serving version, prepared version, and restart command. No third full review was run under the two-round policy.

### Final-head AWS checks

- Head: `46e01ac2967a60726f7c3b6c6ec25d1633646dc4`; source tree `d99cf21ead0e87765a1c6a821e0a7cfcbcc18657`.
- [AWS owner/static/base run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_d48b583c06661f56539cc824040794d1): 220 tests passed across nine files / four Vitest configurations, 222.83 seconds for the focused test command. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Core and core-test typechecks passed; changed-file Oxlint reported zero warnings/errors; Oxfmt passed.
- Final regression files were copied onto `b0678469a4` in a separately installed baseline. The original npm update cases hit the installation-mismatch refusal, adopted npm forwarding was absent, and resident text/JSON status facts were absent. Missing new internal APIs are not counted as original-bug proof.

- [AWS full-build/package run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_9297457fe50ca3638c219a019a275a87): three full source builds and package preparation passed. T uses state schema 41; source-built T+1 and the separate startup-fault build use schema 42 and distinct build IDs. The fault runs after migration and before listen. These are disposable qualification fixtures, not published releases or a repository schema change.

### Final-head Linux behavior

[AWS run and retained artifacts](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_e30ee8c9954fd4adfe8a415000415ea1) completed the required lanes on the final head. Independent assertions over the saved CLI, status text/JSON, service snapshots, and journals passed:

| Entry point | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Published `2026.11.7` → T → T+1 | First hop reached `2026.11.8-first-hop.0`; conversion committed source-built schema-42 `2026.11.9-next.0`. |
| Newer npm → `gateway restart` alone | CLI and observed Gateway both reached `2026.11.10-manual.0`, with one systemd restart. |
| Separate newer npm → `update` alone | CLI and Gateway both reached `2026.11.10-manual.0`, with one existing supervisor child restart; the stable launcher was not restarted a second time. |
| Older npm → `gateway restart` | `2026.11.10-manual.0` stayed selected/serving; output named `update --tag 2026.11.9-next.0`. |
| Failing newer npm → `gateway restart` | The source-built candidate crashed after migration; exit 1 reported `Update failed: new build failed to start; v2026.11.10-manual.0 is still running`. CLI, selected release, and observed Gateway all followed that restored version. |
| Newer npm → start while already running | Serving version and PID stayed unchanged; output named the old version, prepared new version, and `gateway restart`. A later restart committed the same pending run. |

`openclaw --version`, `update status`, and `update status --json` were captured before and after. This was **not an all-green script**: the later stopped-service start lane failed candidate validation with `unable to open database file`, before publication. The required lanes above remain independently verified; the stopped-service failure is tracked separately below.
The later read-only-prefix / pending-start runtime lane did not run after that failure; its forwarding warning and pending-run reuse retain focused test coverage.

### Related stopped-service failure

The additional stopped-service validation failure matches the error and checker owner in [#204227](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/204227), concerning a cleanly closed WAL database without SHM. This PR does not change that checker. A comparison build from current main `5454c0e62e` completed ([build run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_c23776094a368fd5f61e506cc0158554)), but the [control attempt](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_31b93cc9d0cb5193eb9afe01083a8969) was time-boxed during service-reinstallation setup before its plain stopped-service update command. **No main-control pass/fail result is claimed.** No public comment was added to the other maintainer's issue.

### Coverage limits

Real runtime qualification is scoped to Linux systemd and a task-owned named profile. Remote/custom-service exclusions and restart `--force`/`--wait` intent have focused test coverage; this PR does not claim new macOS or Windows runtime proof. The registry is an isolated fixture: its channel target differs from the newer npm-installed artifact, so adoption must use the installed source, not registry latest.

prs.title: fix(ci): align exec completion fixtures with process identity
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Main CI still expects background exec notifications to use a reusable process name. Notifications now use the registered process instance, so completion, acknowledgement and egress fixtures look for the wrong event. The runtime fixture also lacks the stored destination required by durable notifications.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. This restores the tests for completion delivery, acknowledgement isolation, timeout policy and background egress lifetime.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the existing process-instance identity in the fixtures and preserve the distinct events when a process name is reused. Give the synthetic runtime destination a store path and use the same isolated Owed-store fixture as the sibling cleanup suite. Existing notification, subprocess and timeout assertions remain intact.

## Evidence

- [Scheduled main CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45348156095) reproduced the stale fixtures in `bash-tools.test.ts`, `bash-tools.notify-on-exit-ack.test.ts`, `bash-tools.exec.egress-lifecycle.test.ts` and `bash-tools.exec-runtime.test.ts`.
- Native `scripts/pr review-tests` passed all four changed test files at `d11145a55678c3e689af80a4b17e7c1a26e24453`, using the checkout's frozen dependencies. The [exec runtime shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45354779599/job/138310481056) and [completion-notification shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45354779599/job/138310480645) also pass on Linux/Bun. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Initial baseline-proof preparation rejects a retained reviewed workflow whenever main advances, even when the complete workflow, dependency and policy inputs remain equivalent. This change admits that case without relaxing later publication or merge gates.

## User Impact

Maintainers can reuse an equivalent reviewed workflow for initial baseline proof while preserving authenticated ancestry, source identity, signed evidence and custody. This is maintainer tooling; it does not change the runtime product. No measured speedup or resolution of the macOS test deadlines is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Authenticate current main and compare complete workflow inventories, file types/modes, dependency/install inputs and runtime policy. Carry provenance through native context and signed baseline bindings. Reuse same-commit facts only within each check; preserve fresh admission boundaries.
- Validate custody and preparation inputs before retiring active evidence. Preserve pending-proof acceptance retirement and qualified-baseline rejection. Keep the selected workflow's dependency revision independent of bootstrap, including creator reentry and unbound commands.
- Integrate frozen main `181656c5749804e8584af726d67eebdecaf017a7`, preserving verified-bootstrap completion and expansion order alongside workflow proof verification. Retain main's native Git captured-byte stdin hashing, `--no-filters`, conditional object writes and no-spill ownership. The proposed descriptor batching was removed. Replay, signatures and FD7/8/9 custody retain their existing owners.
- Keep the private fixture adapter's fresh ordered ref reads and remove both the standalone adapter-only suite and lifecycle query-count instrumentation. The final cleanup removes 73 test lines while preserving all 27 native calls, publication/replay outcomes, signed OIDs, receipt bytes and transport-authority refusals.
- Exercise historical six-field signed-proof records through current native consumers, with the optional field absent before signing. Preserve binding/signature identity, retained bytes and tamper refusals. This qualifies a historical format through current code, not an old released binary. Correct operation-scoped archive assertions, custody injection and the creator-reentry FD9 oracle without weakening assertions or deadlines.

The authored difference from frozen main is **21 files**: production **+740/-329 (net +411)**, tests **+1201/-237**, docs **+28/-5**, inventory **+17**, and a three-line allocation record. Production growth owns workflow equivalence, sealed provenance, validation before retirement and consolidated dependency/materialization accounting. The native staged test-line ratchet passed: **945 eligible net lines = 400 allowance + 545 allocation**, with no extra credit. The separate `.mjs` fixture explains the difference from test numstat. Allocation does not waive proof or review.

## Evidence

Current commit: `fdd9ab4aee15fbbfe307be55940311784edfc4a4`; tree `853ccaef3f39e4c4c57b6d7f97ac207186352a7f`; parent `6dd41479d11142b3f213fd4cc1c4e26c7cf56c12`. Preflight log SHA-256: `0cb6da373dacd1539116f5fcf23036279bea6f162dc1994244ef6b2d1c7367b1`.

Earlier macOS campaigns separately produced **22/22** bootstrap/proof-identity passes at `909fa9e1`, and **93 passed / 6 deadline failures** across earlier reviewed trees. The six failures were signing **152.394s**, successor **191.389s**, incoming-source **215.894s**, ordinary replay **206.336s**, historical replay **185.716s**, and workflow publication **134.859s**, all against 120s. Selections overlap and are not added together. Linux/Bun passes do not establish the macOS cause or a cross-host speedup. Instrumented, interrupted and timed-out runs are not clean proof.

An earlier diagnostic at the current `fdd9ab4a` source measured the same baseline-successor publication scenario at **144.579s**, still failing the unchanged **120s** test deadline. All 13 expected outer native calls were observed; children settled, instrumentation was restored, and canonical source/dependency identities were preserved. This was instrumented diagnostic input, not a canonical test pass. Nested timings overlap and cannot be summed or subtracted to claim a speedup. A separate eight-read, balanced Git-launch probe measured about **7ms** additional startup time through the system launcher versus its selected backend; both binaries were hashed before measurement, so this is not cold-cache timing or an explanation of the full-test deadline. These metrics do not distinguish filesystem, scheduling or lock delays and support no concrete owner-level repair. Instrumented-run differences are not a regression or speedup claim. All four overlays were restored, source/install identities verified, children settled and the native lease released.

## Review and Remaining Gates

A fresh attempt at exact `fdd9ab4a` reviewed the preparation/custody assignment, then reported **INCOMPLETE** because `wrapper-components.txt` and `dependency-inputs.json` were missing from that assignment. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #204366.

A green scheduled run on `main` should mean every test file ran somewhere unattended. The issue counted 5,601 test files outside every lane of `ci.yml`. Counted against **all four scheduled owners**, the real gap is **71 of 23,079 tracked test files**:

- `ci.yml`, hourly main validation;
- `plugin-prerelease.yml`, hourly extension tests;
- `openclaw-scheduled-live-checks.yml`, daily repo e2e, UI e2e and the release live shards;
- `full-release-validation-nightly.yml`, 3-hourly: full CI with release-only runtime files, and the plugin phase with `agentic-plugins`.

| Area | Class | Uncovered |
|---|---|---:|
| .agents | mjs / py | 44 / 2 |
| .github | mjs / mts / ts | 1 / 1 / 1 |
| crates | cjs | 3 |
| packages | live | 10 |
| scripts | ts | 1 |
| src | ts / live | 2 / 1 |
| test | e2e / ts / py | 2 / 2 / 1 |

Of the 71: **67** match a reasoned exception (9 patterns, each with a named owner and reason; for example CodeQL query fixtures, standalone `node:test` skill self-tests, native binding suites owned by path-triggered workflows, credentialed live tests not selected by the release live shards). **4** have no scheduled owner and now run daily:

- `scripts/control-ui-retention/dependency-retention.test.ts`
- `src/plugin-sdk/facade-runtime.test.ts`
- `src/plugins/loader.test.ts`
- `test/e2e/qa-lab/plugins/feishu-crabline.real-gateway.candidate.e2e.test.mts`

## Change

- `listUnscheduledTestFiles()` (`scripts/lib/ci-node-test-plan.mts`, next to the canonical inventory it reads) computes tracked test files minus the four scheduled owners' static selections, minus `SCHEDULED_COVERAGE_EXCEPTIONS` (`scripts/lib/ci-node-test-inventory.mts`). Static only: a config without a static file list fails by name.
- Every-file lane in `openclaw-scheduled-live-checks.yml` (daily cron, secretless): one plan job (`scripts/ci-scheduled-test-plan.mts`) packs the uncovered files into rows with explicit include files; one matrix job runs them through `scripts/ci-run-node-test-shard.mts` with `test/vitest/vitest.every-file.config.ts` (explicit-only; its include list comes from the plan). `fail-fast: false`, continue-on-failure, no `continue-on-error`.
- A `workflow_dispatch` input `every_file_only` (default false) runs only the lane, without the credentialed live checks.
- Plan test `test/scripts/ci-scheduled-coverage.test.ts`: every tracked test file is in a scheduled lane, in the every-file lane, or matches an exception; each exception names an owner and reason and matches at least one tracked file.
- `ci.yml`: **0 bytes** changed. `openclaw-scheduled-live-checks.yml`: +3.6 KB.
- Watcher: the orchestrator's scheduled sweep already covers all scheduled workflows, including this one.

## Evidence

- New coverage tests and the full workflow guards: 234 passed, 8 skipped (the worker's run). The two workflow-guard regressions it found were fixed (explicit `cache-mode`, lazy package read).
- Lane dispatch on this branch (`every_file_only=true`): run 45349390666 green. Plan job success; the 4 files ran in one row (success); live checks skipped.
- Accepted risk: the static inventory can claim a file that its Vitest config excludes.
