prs.title: fix: match the web first-run setup to the Mac welcome
prs.body:
Closes #202132

## What Problem This Solves

On a fresh install, the web dashboard on main picks an AI connection by itself: it tests what it finds and saves the first one that answers. People can't choose what to try first, the card looks nothing like the Mac app's **Connect your AI**, and a failed connection shows the Gateway's full error.

## User Impact

The web setup card follows the Mac welcome flow: **Welcome to OpenClaw**, **Where should your assistant run?**, then **Connect your AI**.

- **Where should your assistant run?** is a real choice between **On this computer** and **On another computer**. Picking the other one opens **Gateways** in the Mac app, or the connection settings in a browser.
- **Connect your AI** lists the Mac's entries: **ChatGPT**, **Claude**, **Gemini**, **API key**, and **A model on your own computer**, with **More providers** below. Logins the Gateway found are tagged **On this computer** (or **On your Gateway**), and nothing is tested until you pick one. Sign-ins and keys are usable while the Gateway is still looking for logins.
- Each pick opens its own card: a found login is tested, a sign-in shows its steps, **API key** shows the key form, and **A model on your own computer** lists local models, local servers, Ollama and LM Studio downloads, and **Check again**. A ChatGPT login that fails its test offers **Sign in with ChatGPT**.
- **You're all set!** names the provider, model and Gateway. After reusing a Codex login it says so and offers **Sign in separately**.
- Errors show one short sentence with the Gateway's message under **Show details**. In a browser with nothing to connect, the card points to `openclaw onboard`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The card discovers choices without testing them (`openclaw.setup.options` first, then `openclaw.setup.detect`) and runs the existing Gateway wizard for the one the user picks, as the Mac does. The Gateway still owns detection, sign-in, activation and the test. Main's automatic test is not kept: it saves an AI the user didn't choose, which the Mac flow avoids on purpose. Main's **Open AI setup** button is not kept either: the card now has the full flow, so it would be a second entry point to the same setup. Activation no longer sends a conversation-catalog choice, following main (#202601).

## Evidence

Screenshots: the Control UI built from main and from this head, with a mock Gateway and made-up providers, from the Control UI browser tests.

| Connect your AI | ![main tests an AI on its own while connecting, with Use a different Gateway as a separate button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/43d1c46f823dc4e4de7c69e445b19b9d2699b871/images/2026/11/bf5dd485-f641-4b2a-821c-f91a1093d28d.png) | ![The Mac's list of AI choices, found logins tagged, More providers below](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/43d1c46f823dc4e4de7c69e445b19b9d2699b871/images/2026/11/aba99490-5496-4e76-a2ac-d2d92fa30268.png) |
| Finished | ![main names the provider, model and Gateway and offers Sign in separately](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/43d1c46f823dc4e4de7c69e445b19b9d2699b871/images/2026/11/5d704449-8b10-4103-bd00-5a63a3fbc385.png) | ![You're all set names the provider, model and Gateway and offers Sign in separately](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/43d1c46f823dc4e4de7c69e445b19b9d2699b871/images/2026/11/89fffea1-06e9-45e9-bf3e-0c0395da4c6c.png) |

![Where should your assistant run? with On this computer and On another computer as choices](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/43d1c46f823dc4e4de7c69e445b19b9d2699b871/images/2026/11/42a6df1c-adb1-41e4-b123-326eeb0b8fec.png)

![A model on your own computer card with connect actions and download links for Ollama and LM Studio](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/afc22bdda3ede4be41e3b1477a9c8b4b8bc2e073/images/2026/11/cbe22edd-5dfc-4d4b-983d-759acfdc9047.png)

- The API-key draft regression in `custodian-auto-setup.e2e.test.ts` holds discovery while the user selects Anthropic and types a synthetic key. It waits for a new provider option to appear before checking the selection and draft.

  The same test applied to `7db6681` failed on both fields with the original renderer.

  ```text
  AssertionError: expected 'openai-api-key' to be 'anthropic-api-key' // Object.is equality
  AssertionError: expected '' to be 'sk-test-draft' // Object.is equality
  ```

  On `2b10d03`, the regression passed and the user could retry a rejected key. All 5 Custodian Chromium scenarios passed, covering the welcome steps, testing only the selected AI, a failed local-model test, API-key recovery, and ChatGPT sign-in success and failure.
- Unit tests (`custodian-auto-setup.test.ts`, 19), `native-device-settings.test.ts` (69) and `setup-inference-activate.test.ts` (43) pass. UI typecheck, focused lint, stylelint, formatting and `ui:i18n:verify` pass.
- Not run live against a real Gateway and provider for this head.

prs.title: fix: finish early Git checkout updates automatically instead of asking for a rebuild
prs.body:
Related: #204275, #203608, #203194, #201463, #201906

## What Problem This Solves

Git checkouts whose installed updater was built from `main` between 2026-11-17 and 2026-11-19 (for example a checkout at `8f80fe08cad`) cannot finish an update that migrates the databases. Since #204275 the new release's check stops that update cleanly and prints a one-time rebuild to run by hand. Until someone runs it, the install stays on the old build and every later `openclaw update` stops at the same point.

## User Impact

On Linux with a systemd user service, the update now finishes itself. The old updater still reports this one update as failed (it cannot be patched), but its output says the new release is finishing in the background and names a path-free command to follow it. About five minutes later the Gateway serves the new version from the rebuilt checkout, `openclaw` on PATH reports the new version, the leftovers of the early layout are gone, and later updates run normally.

- Outage: two restarts. The first lasts as long as the boot migration (28 to 33 s in cells with a 512 MiB agent database), the second 6.5 to 7.3 s. The by-hand rebuild costs about 290 s.
- Nothing in the checkout is reset, stashed, cleaned, rebased or forced. A dirty checkout, a branch with local commits, a branch that cannot fast-forward, another installation on PATH or in the service, low disk, macOS, Windows and hosts without a systemd user manager get the printed rebuild with the reason, and nothing changes.
- A node runner started from the checkout keeps its old code; the recorded outcome says to restart it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installed updater (`8f80fe08cad`) runs candidate code only in `pnpm install`/`pnpm build`, the read-only inspection workers, `--version` and the candidate's `update-migrated-finalize.worker --check`. A failing install or build makes it walk back to older commits, so `--check` is the only hook that can stop it cleanly and act. Letting the check pass instead (experiment X1 in #204275) migrates state, then leaves every `openclaw` command refusing the new schema and an old-format trial armed; that was rejected as an end state.

So when `--check` refuses (the #204275 marker: the check runs from `git-install/releases/<id>/build` while `git-install/lib/node_modules/openclaw` is a link, and the release would migrate state), it now also:

1. Checks every precondition before changing anything (checkout found from the release worktree's Git common directory; clean tracked tree; on a branch; HEAD an ancestor of the release's commit; nothing ahead of upstream; the service is a systemd user unit for this state directory and runs this checkout or the early launcher; `openclaw` on PATH runs this checkout's build or the early release; 4 GiB free; `pnpm` and a user manager present; no recovery running).
2. Moves the release the updater just built out of its cleanup path (`git worktree move` to `git-install/recovery/openclaw`), so the target is built once.
3. Starts the runner as a transient user service, `systemd-run --user --unit=openclaw-update-recovery --collect -p Restart=on-abnormal`, from that release's code, and exits 1 so the old updater stops before switching anything.

The runner then:

1. Waits for the old updater to exit, found by walking the check's ancestors (the CLI renames itself `openclaw`).
2. Fast-forwards the branch to the exact release commit (`git merge --ff-only`).
3. Moves the service onto the kept release with its own `gateway install --force --port <current port>` and waits on `/readyz` through the same loopback probe `openclaw gateway start` uses. That release migrates state at boot. The CLI's own start check cannot be used here, because it opens state the booting release holds for its migration.
4. Opens its update run and takes the release updater's lock (`src/update/store.ts`), so an update the new release's Gateway accepts waits until the recovery is recorded.
5. Runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `pnpm build` in the checkout while the release serves. The build's live-service fence no longer applies, because the service no longer runs the checkout's `dist`.
6. Moves the service onto the rebuilt checkout (`gateway install --force`): the arrangement the by-hand rebuild leaves, which current updates continue from.
7. From the rebuilt checkout, removes the early layout's link, its `lib/node_modules` releases, an old-format `.trial`, and the kept release, then runs `git worktree prune` then finishes its update run (existing fields only) and releases the lock.

**Why it survives where #201906's finisher did not.** That finisher ran in a `systemd-run --scope`: the process stays the caller's child, in the caller's process group, and the caller's process-tree cleanup reaps it. The runner here is a transient *service*, forked by the user manager in its own cgroup and session. Neither the old updater's exit nor the Gateway restart touches it; on the Gateway-started route the updater runs inside the Gateway's cgroup and is gone before the runner acts.

**Failure handling.**
- A failed precondition or fast-forward changes nothing; the next `openclaw update` retries.
- Once the service starts the release, the previous build is never put back: the release may already have migrated. A release that does not report ready, a failed build, or a rebuilt checkout that does not start leaves the Gateway on the release. It records a failed run whose next step is the rebuild from the checkout.
- systemd restarts a killed runner (`Restart=on-abnormal`); the restart has stopped that run's whole cgroup. The restarted runner releases the build lock its interrupted build left, resumes at the build (or, once the rebuilt checkout reports ready, at the cleanup), and stops after three restarts with a recorded next step.
- While the kept release exists, the check refuses every early updater, including one that state the recovery already migrated would otherwise let through.

**Update behavior.** Only the early updaters with a pending schema change (or a recovery in progress) take this route. Same-schema updates through them, published npm/pnpm installs and current-main checkouts are untouched; `inspectEarlyGitReleaseSchemaChange` is unchanged for them (unit tests below). No config key, stored field, schema, protocol, dependency, retention or permission change. Removal: delete `update-early-release-recovery.ts` with `update-candidate-check-early-release.ts` once no install can still run an updater from that window.

**macOS.** Not shipped there. The detaching mechanism and service steps are service-manager specific and no macOS proof route ran (see Not proven), so macOS keeps the printed rebuild with the reason.

## Evidence

Cells: Linux containers with systemd as PID 1, a user Gateway service from `openclaw gateway install`, a 512 MiB agent database under 1 MiB/s of writes, 1,000 marker rows checked by count, SHA-256 and `quick_check`, and a node runner started from the checkout. The installed updater is a checkout at `8f80fe08cad`; state is synthetic. The update is plain `openclaw update` from PATH unless noted. Outage is measured by a client polling the Gateway throughout. T+1 and T+2 are throwaway version-bump commits on top of the head (no schema bump).

RED on base `8b167650d70` (main) and GREEN on the head `764d667295d`, same reproduction. These are replays of the cells' raw output, not live screen captures:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/75851988-83c6-445d-9366-22741e106bb0

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66c77179-9c73-41cb-b114-56b2d5b27706

| Cell | Head | Result | Wall: old updater; runner (from its start, including the wait for the updater) | Outage | End state |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RED: clean checkout | base `8b167650d70` | exit 1, printed rebuild | 357 s | 0 | 2026.11.4 serving on 40/42 two minutes later; old link and a 4.6 GiB release left |
| A: clean checkout, `openclaw update` | `764d667295d` | exit 1, recovery ran | 363 s; 350 s | 33.1 s + 6.5 s | PATH and Gateway 2026.11.7 on 41/43; markers intact; old link and release removed |
| A, then T+1, T+2, a no-op, `doctor --fix` | `764d667295d` | 0, 0, 0, 0 | 425 s, 391 s, 7 s, 3 s | 13.3 s, 7.3 s, 0, 0 | current releases layout, markers intact |
| B: same, started by the old Gateway's `update.run` | `2d34ff30daa` | runner started 301 s after the request; survived the Gateway restarts | 301 s until the runner started; 328 s | 32.2 s + 7.0 s | 2026.11.7 on 41/43, markers intact |
| C: already half-switched by older `main` (2 old releases, old-format trial), then `openclaw update` | `cf2cb89a577` | exit 1, recovery ran | 186 s; 362 s | 32.4 s + 7.0 s | trial, link, both releases and the kept release removed |
| C, then T+1, T+2, a no-op, `doctor --fix` | `cf2cb89a577` | 0, 0, 0, 0 | 408 s, 400 s, 10 s, 3 s | 12.8 s, 8.5 s, 0, 0 | markers intact |
| D: service already on the old launcher after a same-schema update | `cf2cb89a577` | exit 1, recovery ran | 194 s; 366 s | 30.3 s + 7.3 s | service moved from `git-install/openclaw-launcher.mjs` to the checkout |
| E: tracked file edited | `cf2cb89a577` | exit 1, printed rebuild: "the checkout has uncommitted changes to tracked files" | 351 s | 0 | nothing changed (2026.11.4 on 40/42) |
| F: local commit | `cf2cb89a577` | exit 1, printed rebuild: "the checkout's branch cannot fast-forward to 92c7e19d4c3" | 134 s | 0 | nothing changed; the commit kept |
| G: build made to fail (`dist` read-only), then a second `openclaw update` | `cf2cb89a577` | build failed; Gateway left on the new release; failed run recorded with its next step; the second update was refused at once while the boot migration held state | 328 s; 62 s | 30.2 s | the recorded next step, run by hand, served the rebuilt checkout (8.0 s outage) |
| H: runner SIGKILLed 75 s into `pnpm build`, then T+1 | `764d667295d` | systemd restarted it after 15 s; it released its own build lock, resumed and finished; T+1 exit 0 | 323 s; 417 s | 28.2 s + 7.1 s | 2026.11.7 on 41/43, markers intact, all leftovers removed |

The cells ran at the heads shown. Code changes after `cf2cb89a577`: review fixes (update lock, port, readiness check before cleanup on resume, build-lock release), a module split, removed type assertions and process exits, and renames. A and H were rerun on the final head `764d667295d`; the others prove paths those changes do not alter.
B ran before the fix that stops the finishing step from counting its own process as a user of the kept release. In B that release was left on disk; C, D, A and H show it removed.

Disk, per directory: the old updater builds two releases into `git-install` (peak +9.5 GiB, as on base). The recovery keeps the target release instead of building it again, and adds +0.6 GiB peak in the checkout. Afterwards `git-install` holds only the launcher, about 0.2 GiB. The boot migration's own originals peaked at +2.4 GiB under the state directory. No other database copy is made.

<details><summary>What the old updater prints (head, automatic)</summary>

```
OpenClaw 2026.11.7 migrates your databases (state schema 40 to 41, agent schema 42 to 43).
The updater in this checkout (a main build from 2026-11-17 to 2026-11-19) cannot finish that: after the migration, neither it nor the checkout's `openclaw` command can open the migrated data.
So it stops here and reports this update as failed, and the new release finishes the update in the background. In about 5 to 10 minutes it moves the checkout to 764d667295d, restarts the Gateway on the new release (which migrates your databases at startup), rebuilds the checkout, and restarts the Gateway on the rebuilt checkout. The first restart lasts as long as the migration; the second takes a few seconds. If it cannot finish, its log and `openclaw update status` say why and name the next step.
Until the rebuild finishes, the checkout's `openclaw` command refuses the migrated data; that is expected.
Follow progress: systemctl --user status openclaw-update-recovery (log: journalctl --user -u openclaw-update-recovery)
```
</details>

<details><summary>Runner journal (A, head)</summary>

```
systemd: Started openclaw-update-recovery.service - OpenClaw update recovery.
[openclaw update recovery] waiting for the update that started this recovery to exit
[openclaw update recovery] fast-forwarding main to 764d667295d4ec9eb53e6c8ab6e847ff36d9d4e9
[openclaw update recovery] restarting the Gateway on the new release; it migrates state at startup
[openclaw update recovery] rebuilding the checkout while the Gateway serves the new release
[openclaw update recovery] restarting the Gateway on the rebuilt checkout
[openclaw update recovery] Rebuilt the checkout at 764d667295d and moved the Gateway onto it. Removed the old release link, releases/git-mwu3pyf1-e9deb65b, recovery. Node runner 2839 still runs the code from before the rebuild; restart it.
```

`openclaw update status --json` afterwards: `status: succeeded`, `reason: early-release-recovered`, `nextAction: restart the node runner that runs from this checkout`, with the step text above.
</details>

<details><summary>Killed and resumed (H, head)</summary>

```
systemd: openclaw-update-recovery.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
systemd: openclaw-update-recovery.service: Scheduled restart job, restart counter is at 1.
[openclaw update recovery] releasing the build lock left by this recovery's interrupted build (PID 11793)
[openclaw update recovery] rebuilding the checkout while the Gateway serves the new release
[openclaw update recovery] restarting the Gateway on the rebuilt checkout
[openclaw update recovery] Rebuilt the checkout at 764d667295d and moved the Gateway onto it. Removed the old release link, releases/git-mwu5i3yk-32b83499, recovery. ...
```
An earlier run of H at `cf2cb89a577` stopped at this point: `pnpm build` refused the dead build's lock. The runner recorded that as a failure and left the Gateway serving the release. That run led to the lock release above.
</details>

<details><summary>Failed build (G)</summary>

```
[openclaw update recovery] The Gateway serves OpenClaw 2026.11.7 from the release the update built. `pnpm build` failed in the checkout (... path: '~/openclaw/dist/.buildstamp', syscall: 'rm' ...).
update status: failed / early-release-recovery-build-failed
nextAction: fix the cause, then from the checkout run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build && openclaw gateway install --force`
second `openclaw update` (old updater): refused in 1 s, "state ... is undergoing offline maintenance by sqlite-maintenance process"
```
</details>

Full raw logs are not attached; the artifact store rejects uploads from this machine (`http 401`).

**Before the final design.** One cell on an earlier head restored the previous build's service definition when the release's `gateway start` failed. That start failed only because the CLI's start check cannot open state during the boot migration. The release had in fact migrated, so the restored 8f80 build could not open the data. Since then the runner never puts the previous build back once the service starts the release, and it reads readiness over HTTP.

**Tests.**
- `src/infra/update-early-release-recovery.test.ts` (new). The `--check` side runs real Git against a real checkout, upstream and release worktree, with systemd, pnpm and the service scripted. It covers:
  - keeping the release with `git worktree move` and the `systemd-run` launch;
  - 14 refusals, each leaving the release where the updater's cleanup expects it;
  - single-flight.
- The runner, with scripted commands, covers:
  - the full sequence, and that nothing moves before the updater exits;
  - resume once the release serves;
  - a failed fast-forward or service move (nothing changed, nothing recorded);
  - a release that never reports ready (the old build is not put back);
  - a failed build (Gateway left on the release, next step recorded);
  - a rebuilt checkout that does not start (back to the release);
  - the restart limit and the update lock held by another update;
  - releasing only its own interrupted build's lock;
  - cleanup of the early layout while a current-layout release is kept.
- `update-candidate-check-early-release.test.ts` gains the messages for the automatic, fallback and running cases, and the in-progress guard. `update-migrated-finalize.worker.test.ts` runs the real `--check` entry for a refused and a started recovery.
- Red on the base: the worker cases and the new test file fail (no recovery is consulted; the module is missing). I audited all three files: nothing was removed, and the earlier refusal cases are adapted to the split inspect/format API.

**Checks on `764d667295d`:**
- PR CI green.
- Local: the focused tests and `update-restart-module-outcome` + `eager-import-closure`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets` (test lines +333 of 400; session identity, assertion safety and mock exports ok), `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`, `pnpm check:docs`, `git diff --check`.

**Review.**
- An independent reviewer and ClawSweeper's local review (one round, overall F) raised these. Fixed:
  - the finishing step counted itself as a user of the kept release;
  - the resume path skipped readiness;
  - readiness ignored TLS;
  - the restart limit could delete a release the service runs;
  - the update lock;
  - port preservation;
  - credentials in `systemd-run` arguments (proxy variables are no longer passed);
  - a recovery that does not finish now exits non-zero;
  - build timeouts kill the process group;
  - message truth.
- Not changed, with reasons:
  - *Node-runner detection is dead because the CLI renames its process.* Every cell reported the runner (`Node runner 2839 ...`).
  - *`git worktree prune` keeps fresh records.* Without `--expire` it prunes every missing worktree, and the cells' worktree lists after recovery show only the checkout.
  - *Leave old releases to the retention owner.* That owner keeps only releases under the current `git-install/openclaw` slot. The early layout's `lib/node_modules` releases are unreachable once the link is gone, so nothing collects them. A release whose path a live process names is kept.
- `autoreview` does not run on this machine.

## Not proven

- **`openclaw update --no-restart`.** From an affected checkout this still ends with the Gateway restarted. The installed updater does not pass the flag to `--check`, and it renames its own process, so the check cannot see it.
- **A service installed with options other than `--port`** (for example `--runtime`) is reinstalled with the defaults `gateway install --force` chooses. An autostart the operator disabled is enabled again.
- **macOS/launchd and Windows** are not shipped and were not run. No macOS route was attempted, because this machine's Crabbox artifact store rejects uploads and the runner is not built for launchd. Containers without a user manager get the printed rebuild (unit-tested, not run in a cell).
- **A reboot during the rebuild.** The transient unit does not survive it. The Gateway comes back on the kept release, and the checkout needs the recorded build command.
- **After the by-hand next step from a failed build**, the kept release and the old link stay on disk until they are removed by hand.
- A Gateway bound only to a non-loopback address: readiness uses the same loopback probe as `openclaw gateway start`.
- Agent stores at different schema versions, and PostgreSQL-backed state (left on the printed procedure by #204275).

prs.title: fix: show provider billing guidance and plan links
prs.body:
Closes #204403

## What Problem This Solves

A provider can explain that a plan does not allow third-party apps, but the failed-reply card replaces that explanation with generic balance and usage advice. The useful recovery link disappears too.

## User Impact

The existing error header, icon, reason, expand chevron, Edit message, Open Models, Try again, and Report a bug stay in place. Providers can opt in to two additional rows underneath: their message, then a compact **View plans ↗** link when a valid URL is available. The message wraps at 390 px. Existing generic copy and actions remain the fallback. No configuration or migration is needed, and billing classification and retries are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

An optional prepared-provider formatter supplies deliberate user-facing copy and an optional HTTP(S) URL. One normalized value travels through the existing failure, fallback, live-event, and saved-notice paths. Raw response bodies and diagnostic previews are not promoted into display copy. Invalid URLs remove only the link; missing, empty, or throwing formatters retain the generic fallback.

## Evidence

Verified through a production Control UI build, a real isolated Gateway, and a local provider returning HTTP 403. No Gateway or DOM replacement was used.

- The provider's sentence and plans link appear below the unchanged header and recovery actions, live and after reload. Opening details and switching through Open Models work.

- The billing classification, missing/invalid guidance, generic fallback, raw-body exclusion, and mixed-fallback attribution retain regression coverage.
- After the main merge and pr-simplify, the focused billing suites, retained-notice readback, both permanent real-Gateway UI cases, and canonical paired performance check pass. The requested runtime suites have the same failure set on clean main and the PR; details are below.
- Earlier Auto Review of the full change against 80180388d04dadb2966c5322d15a14cd7119c8ec was clean at P0 scope. The repair review attempt could not start because the installed helper script was missing. That attempt is not a clean review.

<details>
<summary>Main merge, paired failures, and saved-data compatibility</summary>

Published head **8ac24b71eab9** retains the normal merge **55ba6551b19d**, with parents **ecd91b4433ed** and main **9ac436d29061**. Both new commits have the requested human coauthor. The published tree matches the locally tested tree exactly. No rebase or history replacement was used.

The five files behind the four requested failure areas were run on clean main 9ac436d29061 and the merged PR source, with the same pinned Bun runtime, four-CPU affinity, one worker, and serial scheduling:

- channel-progress-presentation.e2e.test.ts
- cron-forced-after-turn.e2e.test.ts
- bash-tools.exec-gateway-approval.e2e.test.ts
- gateway-yield-restart.e2e.test.ts
- bash-tools.exec.egress-lifecycle.test.ts

Shared failures include the ambiguous Discord settlement timeout, forced-cron timeout, missing exec hook-source name, policy-unavailable child receipt, and both exec egress cases. Eleven Slack cases stopped at a fixture HTTP 500 before their delivery assertions, so those assertions are not verified by this replay. No shared failure, timeout, assertion, or baseline was weakened. Matching main CI job receipts for these five files were not found; this is a direct local main-versus-PR comparison, not a claim based on job names.

The original Swift, cursor-policy, packaged-file inventory, and CSS regressions passed on ecd91b4. The canonical paired performance check was repeated against merged main and passed: **+50 raw CSS bytes, -4 gzip CSS bytes**, with chat-boot JS at **1,336,254 bytes** under its **1,336,272-byte** cap. A latest-stable upgrade fixture is **not verified**: npm refused openclaw@2026.11.7 under the configured package-age cutoff. That policy was not bypassed. The successful retention trace is pre-PR main to the merged candidate, not a released-version upgrade claim.

Ran pr-simplify again before this push. The displayed screenshots are the earlier inspected ecd91b4 captures; the billing component itself is unchanged by this merge.

No live paid provider, external plans-page navigation, or non-Chromium rendering was tested. New-head CI is being watched separately; the local comparison is not an all-green CI claim.

## What Problem This Solves

UI performance checks can compare an unmerged PR checkout with a newer merge-planning base. Unrelated changes already on main then appear as bundle growth in the PR.

## User Impact

Developers get bundle comparisons against the base of the source actually being built. Performance limits remain unchanged; this PR makes no application runtime change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The UI job passes its authenticated checkout ancestor to the existing Git checkout owner and performance command. The shared merge-planning anchor moves unchanged to the baseline-ratchet job, so its other consumers retain their existing comparison. Six later identical values reuse that anchor to keep the workflow below its unchanged byte limit. Tests preserve checkout ancestry and all eight existing task/event combinations.

The candidate incorporates frozen baseline `b8ce8779496a3822162714169020141c6ca4b26b`, including the landed Settings, publication/mobile fixture and cached-parent paint repairs. Their source presence does not establish that the affected runtime failures are fixed.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `7cc66b92995da9dada9ad032a301217b59925869`; tree: `6afc397ed63b5eca7e6c164b2ccb49204173c2b2`. The three-file change is 9 workflow lines added/8 removed and 54 test lines added/11 removed.

It covers the checkout/ratchet owners, authenticated prefetch, report contract and complete performance command. Report SHA256: `201e403ee0fd555a361462a18468886628af81e8e12d448c91afd1359f40aea3`.
- Targeted formatting, whitespace and source privacy checks passed. The six-alias correction preserves the complete parsed YAML value; the workflow is 479,885 bytes under the unchanged 480,000-byte limit.
- This is a **draft publication for proof**, with native recommendation **NEEDS WORK**. R1 (missing baseline source integration) is resolved; R2 (runtime, performance and hosted CI qualification) remains IMPORTANT and unresolved. There is no pending-proof acceptance or inherited-failure waiver.
- Current-head runtime and hosted CI are pending. Required proof includes the whole ratchet and guard files under Node and Bun; whole Settings search, publication, mobile-menu and cached-session snapshot consumers with their original assertions/order; a correctly bound paired UI performance comparison; and required hosted CI. Source review is not execution proof.

Historical evidence only, at prior head `9b0edb3678236ec280da6840cc884adf544c149c`:

- The complete ratchet file passed 5/5 under Node 24.22.1 and Bun 1.4.4; the complete guard file passed 241/241 under each, including the eight prefetch cases. The historical UI performance job reported zero incremental JS/CSS growth.

prs.title: refactor: simplify automation updates in the Control UI
prs.body:
Closes #204490

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI still maintains separate automation-list update paths for current and older Gateways, even though the UI and Gateway ship together. That leaves duplicate membership and runtime-update logic for maintainers to keep consistent.

Maintainer-requested cleanup: https://discord.com/channels/1456350064065904867/1574663637187170425/1574696858972856333

## User Impact

No features, permissions, or supported Gateway contracts are removed. Automation lists, runtime updates, filters, pagination, reconnects, explicit refresh, and post-write reconciliation continue through the existing shared inventory.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the obsolete event-advertisement mode, uncached fallback, and second runtime/membership projection. The current Gateway always registers and publishes `cron.inventory.changed`; definition/access changes still renew membership, while runtime events only update admitted jobs.

Keep explicit reconciliation reads fresh and retire cancelled or superseded readers without letting an old result clear a replacement inventory. Test fixtures now deliver metadata through the production observer before view subscribers instead of exercising the retired server mode.

## Evidence

- Browser automation inventory flows pass before and after: three tabs retain known runtime updates with zero additional `cron.list` or `sessions.list` calls, while definition changes, retargeting, and hover details still update.
- A real isolated Gateway saves exact automation duration edits, reloads them in the browser, and independently reads them back through the CLI. The scheduler is disabled; no agent/provider execution is claimed.
- 312 tests pass across the 16 touched unit/component test files. The broader focused sidebar/overlay run also passes all 180 tests; these counts overlap and are not additive.
- UI typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, and the Control UI controller/ratchet guard pass. Lint retains three existing Solid reactivity warnings in the unchanged subscription callbacks of `chat-summary-automations.tsx`.
- The cancellation/reopen regression fails on base `5454c0e62ec65f7d3ac7eb0a5c323753789a3518` by joining an aborted request and timing out; it passes with this change.
- Production: **160 net lines removed** across 15 files. Tests/support: **11 net lines added**. No generated code, translation memory, features, or substantive coverage are deleted to obtain that reduction. Only unsupported-server test modes are retired.

Native independent review covered all 38 changed files against base `5454c0e62ec65f7d3ac7eb0a5c323753789a3518`, including unchanged owners/callers, Gateway publication, access and pagination contracts. It found no actionable P0–P2 issues and independently passed 51 owner/CI-control tests. Reviewed diff SHA-256: `586bf141f10b19930df6baaf03b60e949fffaee74b5bf6d64dee4ac0e4ca0dc9`.

Qualified hosted review and exact-head full CI remain pending. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable in the existing dirty checkout. Autoreview preparation refused its temporary-directory isolation boundary before starting a review engine; supplied temporary-directory settings were preserved. The native independent review is not represented as a ClawSweeper/autoreview result or completed helper-isolation proof.

<details>
<summary>Focused proof commands</summary>

```sh
# Before committing, the diff selected the 16 touched unit/component test files.
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs $(git diff --name-only | grep -E '\.test\.(ts|tsx)$' | grep -v '/e2e/') --maxWorkers=1
pnpm tsgo:ui
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.ui.json $(git diff --name-only)
pnpm check:control-ui-controllers
pnpm ui:build
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/cron-inventory.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/cron-duration-save.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts -t 'configured duration precision' --maxWorkers=1
```

</details>

## Contributor credit

Requested by @vincentkoc.

prs.title: fix(sdk): keep API comparisons working with runtime-only imports
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204039

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin SDK API comparisons stop when a declaration graph contains a valid runtime-only side-effect import with no declaration symbol. This prevents maintainers from comparing frozen revisions even when neither revision changes the public API.

## User Impact

No product runtime or public API change. Maintainers can compare those revisions while missing modules and unresolved named, re-exported or type-only imports still fail.

## Why This Change Was Made

The declaration-closure owner now uses the compiler's resolved module information for bare side-effect imports without a declaration symbol. Only resolved JavaScript modules without declaration contributions end that edge. Ambient declarations remain part of the closure and its hash.

Three files, 107 gross lines: tooling +9/-0; tests +95/-3; product runtime +0. Regression coverage includes JavaScript extension variants, missing modules, strict import forms, ambient declaration hashes, whole-file fallback and both frozen revisions.

## Evidence

Signed candidate: `5b9a8d6fc36cab3ebd6be278bb94a592380a1d3b`, based on `b8ce8779496a3822162714169020141c6ca4b26b`. Independent source review and the complete native source review passed with no findings. Scoped formatting, syntax and commit checks passed.

Exact-candidate hosted proof in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45160984672 (attempt 1):

- `src/plugin-sdk/api-baseline.test.ts`: all 32 cases passed on Node 24.22.1 and Bun 1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1, with no target skips (job 137646780700). The surrounding SDK suites had nine skips per runtime.
- `test/scripts/plugin-sdk-api-diff.test.ts`: all 11 cases passed on each runtime (job 137646780249).
- The real API comparison independently rendered baseline `b8ce877` and candidate `5b9a8d6` through the repaired renderer and reported no Plugin SDK API changes (job 137646774021). This exercised the historical baseline without editing it.
- `pnpm build:ci-artifacts`, packaging, launcher smoke tests and built-artifact checks passed (job 137646772689). Executed lint, production/test types and guards also passed. This is evidence for those commands, not a claim that every build or platform passed.

This remains a draft. The full run ended cancelled after the required focused evidence completed: 107 successful, 18 failed, 28 cancelled and 12 skipped jobs. `check-dependencies` failed on existing Knip findings; independent source comparison found its reported owners unchanged by this patch. Other failures included SQLite fixture, MCP authority, UI, real-Gateway and published-driver jobs; source inheritance does not establish a passing baseline or waive any gate, and not every remaining failure has an established cause. Cancelled jobs remain unproven. Required failed gates must be resolved before landing; no new CI run is requested by opening this draft.

prs.title: fix(workers): preserve state and repository authority across worker recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The worker runtime and prepared-project PRs depend on schema and repository credential changes that are not on `main`. The original worker recovery migration also used schema v41, which `main` now uses for approval provenance.

## User Impact

Updates can keep approval provenance at v41 and add worker recovery metadata at v42 without replacing existing state. App-authenticated publication retains its observed result when credential cleanup fails, and workers can open their admitted imported checkout to resolve conflicts without gaining permission to publish it. An installed worker credential keeps its original deadline after a configuration change, but fresh issuance cannot use the obsolete selection.

This is the first landing unit for #201025 and #201029. It is not a retarget or merge of either dependent PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep migration, credential, checkout, and cleanup ownership with their existing owners. Receipt-bound reconciliation can read an already admitted upstream result but cannot grant a new write. Await token revocation separately from the durable outcome. Coding uses the admitted branch and origin; publication still requires an imported PR's prepared head to match its recorded head. Historical imports match the layout that actually shipped, before the v42 columns existed.

## Evidence

- **Packaged upgrade on `9c00f764b6bc76d5a13357cc4c39a4059f348d1f`:** An isolated published OpenClaw v2026.11.7 installation upgraded to the exact archive and the candidate returned `/readyz` 200. SQLite advanced **36 → 42**, retained the same disabled cron record, and passed `PRAGMA quick_check`. Package inventory and tarball integrity passed. SHA-256: `b112c8c753e309e993844b0f99800e680fe4ed12e5c555be64410ddf1211efb1`. This records the archive for the named commit, not a package from the current head.
- **Migration and credential behavior:** The v7/v21 historical placement cases and the v26 runtime/Doctor index cases passed. The SQLite worker ratchet stayed **166 → 166**, including an exact local replay after the prior hosted runner lost communication. The **55-case** worker binding suite and independently reviewed delayed-broker regression verify that selection changes cannot mint a replacement and do not extend the installed token’s original deadline.
- **Current integration at `0e3dc9ccab66c71ebeab39ef8e0cae6eec2cdf06`:** The clean merge preview against `main` at `b0c098c2292824d365875ba2018223f37c85484c` has one canonical provider-types alias and one worker SDK alias in each declaration config. Exact-base identity, line and timeout checks passed; **2,260** test lines against **400 + 1,860** allowed. The **193-line** prerequisite allocation covers distinct persistence, issuance, settlement, and revocation checks; the global cap is unchanged.
- **Main-conflict and inherited fixture proof:** The two focused Native Add cases and the two Slack/Discord cases passed on their exact resolved trees, retaining rejection of new work from a revoked device and verifying wire delivery independently of requester settlement. ClawHub remains unverified offline. Exact original base and merge replays reproduced the exec notification and exit-wake failures; the synthetic storage fixture passed **39** focused cases and observing exact process instance IDs passed **4** real-loopback egress and closure cases. The egress tests still require grants to be refused after kill, exit, and timeout while a surviving process retains access. These repairs do not change production permission or revocation logic.
- **Required CI:** The [previous exact head failed `openclaw/ci-gate`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45348648074/job/138312277207). Exact local baseline replay at `53e05828a99d7389e35d4c510c21cafff42095f0` passed all selected checks except a release-tool mock-export violation that also failed on base alone, with identical owner and fixture content. A requester-wake timeout likewise reproduced on the earlier tested main base. The nested restart assertion passed in focused replays of both its base and merge and remains unattributed. No bypass or green gate is claimed; the current head still needs passing hosted checks.

Earlier stack CI independently verified PostgreSQL v41 → v42 with approval provenance and the lazy repository fragment. The isolated updater proof is the explicit-artifact CLI path, not a Gateway-triggered release rollout. This PR does not claim live-provider or real-model proof for the dependent runtime PRs.

Original worker stack by @galiniliev.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/7f724a56-b56f-40a4-8727-b3f26768bbc8)
- [Prerequisite main integration](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/2065ea43-59a0-4e57-8f33-7159b21bb0be)

Updates `actions/setup-java` from 6.1.0 to 6.3.0
Release notes

Sourced from actions/setup-java's releases.

v6.3.0

Behavior change: Java problem matcher is now opt-in

Starting with v6.3.0, setup-java no longer registers the Java problem matcher by default (#1326, fixes #1322). Java compiler warnings, compiler errors, and uncaught exceptions are no longer turned into annotations on pull request diffs unless you opt in.

To keep annotations, set problem-matcher: true:

- uses: actions/setup-java@v6
  with:
    distribution: temurin
    java-version: '25'
    problem-matcher: true

Compiler output still appears in the build logs, and compilation errors still fail the build. Only annotations are affected.

Why: inline annotations cluttered pull request reviews, and GitHub Actions caps annotations at 10 errors, 10 warnings, and 10 notices per step, and 50 per job. Larger Java builds therefore showed only a truncated subset of their diagnostics as annotations. See Java problem matcher (compiler annotations).

prs.title: fix(release): authenticate retained publication artifacts on main
prs.body:
## Problem
The 2026.11.8 qualification reused exact publication bytes from FRV `45303777043` attempt 1. Main could not verify the retained-artifact qualification: the strict verifier rejected the execution-plan schema, and omitting the admitted pin from the manifest had already blocked [FRV 45328729828](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45328729828).

## Solution
Forward-port the release-tested admission, artifact selection, Release Decision, manifest, final verification, and receipt-backed resealing changes. Keep the original producer Q and attempt, bind the admitted selector to the execution plan and manifest, and re-authenticate exact candidate and artifact bytes before publication. Reuse main’s existing cross-Q child-evidence policy and keep its separate receipt-recovery path and historical empty-pin compatibility. The two recovery paths share the same artifact discovery code.

## Impact
A trusted main commit can verify the retained 2026.11.8 evidence without rebuilding the original packages or images, adopting a failed aggregate verdict, or changing the candidate, qualification tooling, or waiver grants. Unpinned, changed, or unauthenticated evidence still fails closed.

## Evidence
- Read-only `node scripts/frv.mjs verify --run 45335843731` failed on the clean base and passed with this port for [the successful FRV](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45335843731), with C `2d4ab292114df2ab9670c91c9b846f701c565bd7`, Q `7e3d39d4920819a167739bb025da74338971d05d`, and original publication artifacts from `45303777043/1`.
- Focused local suites: 600 passing tests; the one recovery-workflow assertion was updated to account for the pinned, lifecycle-disabled dependency install, and all 13 tests in that suite passed on rerun. Includes a retained-artifact fixture through final verification and publication authentication.
- Script and tooling test typechecks, targeted type-aware lint and formatting, actionlint, workflow guards, and `git diff --check` passed. The all-workflow wrapper could not start zizmor with an empty GitHub token; the pinned version passed offline on both changed workflows at the repository's severity/confidence gate.
- No release dispatch, tag, publication, or candidate checkout change. A full candidate checklist invocation at the new trusted P remains a post-landing check.

- @vincentkoc
- @RomneyDa

prs.title: docs(release): let the requesting release manager approve fast-track
prs.body:
## Problem

The fast-track approval rules say the approver must be "another human in the release-managers group, not the requester acting as their own approver." That's not what #201080 meant. The intent is that an **agent** never approves. A human release manager who asks for a fast-track should be able to approve it.

Because of the wording, agents read it as a two-human rule and tell the release owner they can't approve their own fast-track.

## Solution

The wording now says a human release manager must approve, and that human may be the one who requested the fast-track. Agents still may only prepare requests. Updated in all four places the rule appears:

- `docs/reference/fast-track-release-approval.md`: approval model paragraph.
- `.agents/skills/release-openclaw-maintainer/SKILL.md`: "Fast-track approval is human-only".
- `.agents/skills/release-openclaw-ci/SKILL.md`: fast-track approval boundary.
- `scripts/release-publish-preflight.mts`: the instruction printed by `approval request`.

Unchanged: agents never approve, including with a release manager's token. Approval still has to be explicit and bound to the exact request and its digest, with the permalink and evidence recorded. `npm-release` environment approval and receipts are unchanged too.

## Impact

Docs, agent guidance, and one printed string only. Fast-track still has no publisher integration, so no release behavior changes.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/manual-release-approval.config.ts`: 22/22 passed. No test asserts the changed string.
- `oxfmt --check` on the four files and `git diff --check`: clean.

## Worked on by

- @RomneyDa

prs.title: fix: WhatsApp and Discord upload voice notes that audio scope rules deny
prs.body:
Closes #204120
Related: #163746 (the same gap, fixed for chat type on Telegram), #167634

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `tools.media.audio.scope` rules are ignored when WhatsApp or Discord transcribe a voice note early, before checking whether the bot was mentioned. If you deny transcription in WhatsApp groups, a captionless group voice note is still uploaded to your speech-to-text provider, even when nobody addressed the bot. If you do the opposite and allow only groups, a spoken "hey OpenClaw" in a group is never heard.

## User Impact

User impact: audio scope rules now also decide the early transcription, so a "deny" rule keeps the audio on the host and an "allow" rule lets spoken mentions work. Behavior changes only for people who set `tools.media.audio.scope`; without it nothing changes.

Worth knowing if you use a deny rule for groups: WhatsApp group voice notes that used to get through by mentioning the bot out loud no longer will, because the audio is no longer transcribed. That is what the rule asks for.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scope check matches rules on channel, chat type and session key. The early transcription passed WhatsApp's channel but no chat type or session key, and for Discord none of the three, so those rules could never match and the default applied. The later transcription step passes all three, and Slack and Matrix already did so early too. This makes WhatsApp and Discord pass the same facts the later step uses.

Accepted edge case: a group thread with several agents shares one early transcript, so a session-key rule is checked against the conversation's main route, not once per agent.

Not included:

- Telegram's early step already passes the channel and chat type (#163746) but still lacks the session key, so `keyPrefix` rules do not reach it. It is a one-line change, and an earlier revision of this PR carried it. I took it out because Telegram changes need Test Server userbot proof with team-leased credentials, which I cannot run as an outside contributor.
- Feishu's early step already passes the chat type but still lacks the channel and session key. It lives inside a file that is over the line cap, so it needs a small extraction first.

## Evidence

**Running Gateways, real channel plugins.** I built main (`6587c9fd212`) and this branch (`bca3e22dbea`), started each Gateway with fresh state, and connected the real channel plugin to crabline, the provider server OpenClaw's own QA uses (WhatsApp over the Baileys socket with an encrypted voice note, Discord over its gateway with an uploaded `.ogg`). Speech-to-text and the chat model are local stand-ins; the speech-to-text one counts uploads and answers "open claw please reply". Every case is a captionless voice note in a group that requires a mention, with mention pattern `open ?claw`.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| WhatsApp | none (control) | 1 / yes | 1 / yes | 1 / yes |
| WhatsApp | deny `chatType: group` | 0 / no | **1 / yes** | 0 / no |

| WhatsApp | allow only `chatType: group` | 1 / yes | **0 / no** | 1 / yes |
| Discord | none (control) | 1 / yes | 1 / yes | 1 / yes |

| Discord | deny `keyPrefix: discord:channel:` | 0 / no | **1 / yes** | 0 / no |
| Discord | allow only `chatType: channel` | 1 / yes | **0 / no** | 1 / yes |

"Admitted" means the transcript reached the chat model (Discord, where the bot also replied) or the Gateway logged the inbound group message after the mention check (WhatsApp, because crabline drops the WhatsApp socket shortly after connecting and the turn is then cancelled). Discord cells that were not admitted logged `discord: skipping guild message` with reason `no-mention`.

prs.title: fix: allow provider sign-in as the first message
prs.body:
Closes #204418

## What Problem This Solves

A new session without a connected model could not send `/login`: setup hid the composer and the submit gates rejected model-independent commands. Once that path was usable, its proof exposed a pre-existing transcript bug: one sign-in duplicated the progress notices and user input.

## User Impact

Users can start provider sign-in or list models as their first message using Start or Enter. Sign-in progress remains live and is recorded once with the final result. Ordinary prompts and attachments still require model access; owner/admin sign-in, session access, and placement checks are unchanged. No configuration or migration is required; existing historical duplicates are not rewritten.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing composer visible and reuse the existing model-independent command classifier. For local webchat commands, the Gateway already streams progress and persists the final transcript; the channel dispatcher must not also mirror those messages. The correction reuses its existing local-webchat routing fact and preserves external-channel and explicitly owned transcript mirrors. Provider picker context (#204420) is not changed.

Contributor credit: @daniel-lxs.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-t_998fs7)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/62dac9c7-b163-4a53-af7b-326856d327a0)

## Evidence

On pinned main `cb4f301c6bb7e27946f2cb98ef283f4500dcd6fa`, the real UI had no composer or Start control during model setup. The first-message regressions failed there and pass with this change.

**Correction to the earlier capture:** the original after image followed **one Start submission**, before the existing-chat sibling send and before Enter in a separate new session. Per-session request, run, message, and counted auth-handler receipts confirmed one request and one auth invocation nevertheless produced duplicate transcript entries. The same duplication reproduced in an existing chat on pinned main: it was exposed by, not introduced by, the UI repair.

With the correction, real-Gateway browser tests for Start, Enter, and existing chat each observe **one request, one auth invocation, two ordered progress updates then one final, and one persisted user/assistant exchange for that sign-in**. Each notice appears once. Start and Enter create distinct sessions.

The generic installed Audit Provider archive uses no real credentials or paid inference. It proves entry into provider sign-in and transcript delivery, not completion of a third-party OAuth exchange.

### Clean comparison

**Before**

![Before: model setup hides the first-message composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df2be4d8-7a43-4ce2-8375-e2edc80fa882)

**After**

![After: one first-message sign-in with progress recorded once](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/97543e58-1a3f-46d0-b3d8-04f2730ae950)

**After**

![Single-send sign-in notes appear once](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6c5871b3-6321-49d9-9e06-1a58b93d711d)

Real isolated Gateway and built Control UI, Chromium, synthetic provider, 1280×900 viewport with matched 970×900 sidebar-free evidence. Before: pinned main above. Current after: `30ec612c29bb548fbc55e23d37e6da6f1f4658fb`, matching reviewed full local diff SHA-256 `f1c9e4d0eb3d941e82ff15d1e159ecb00e9a56a1a2455450c38bff4b437ead99`.

<details>
<summary>Historical regression capture — not the corrected result</summary>

The [earlier clean image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/98a62f69-0cc8-45dd-a867-e1240bdc2c41) and [earlier annotated image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/32a5faec-76fe-4c7f-abe8-1e94c0734f23) belong to `9f7fc50c85131e293926a369a395eaf6f57a9a9c`. They show the single-send duplication described above, not multiple intentional sign-ins. They are retained for attribution; the primary comparison shows the corrected result.

- Correction: 161 focused routing, login authorization, command-transcript, and integration tests passed. prs.title: improve: keep failed-reply actions together
prs.body:
Related: #194607

## What Problem This Solves

Failed replies show generic explanations above the actual error, and routine sign-in, connection, or usage failures offer the same bug-report link as unexpected failures. The recovery action is separated from the diagnostic controls.

## User Impact

Failed replies now show the actual error and their existing recovery actions, without an added heading or canned explanation. Recognized routine failures do not offer Report a bug; unknown or ambiguous failures, schema/format and replay errors, and failures to save a reply keep it. The same rule applies to the live card and reloaded history. The Help menu always retains reporting.

For reportable errors with more detail, Show details remains a plain, keyboard-focusable label beside Refresh, with a muted chevron and no button surface. Expanded diagnostics group the error, copying, and reporting. The reply card has no floating shadow; existing retry, Models navigation, status checks, redaction, and dismissal remain intact. No automatic retry, configuration change, database migration, or user action is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the failure classifications OpenClaw already records instead of matching words in error messages. Carry those bounded facts through the existing run-error receipt and history projection, and share one UI reporting rule. Unrecognized or conflicting categories keep reporting available; retryability or provider identity alone never hides it. Certified contention still requires checking status before resending.

**pr-simplify completed before the final tests:** removed generic/provider-generated headings, appended provider debug fields, the retired sign-in display category, duplicate summary markup/styles, redundant rendering branches, and JavaScript truncation already handled by the existing ellipsis styling. Reporting stays with the chat failure presentation rather than global navigation links. The retained growth carries classification through live/persisted boundaries and updates their existing consumers; it is one coherent failure-notice change, not a new error-classification system.

## Evidence

Comparison: **main 4708bac523976c1546f84f790ded7db3fa65dcf5 → head 8ae8b163df8c07fae2927c1865af0c5ac49e99df**. This updates the existing branch without rebasing or force-pushing; the earlier main merge and #204397 remain in its ancestry.

- Routine, reportable, and unclassified cases pass live and after a page reload. Identical “Request timed out” text keeps or loses reporting according to the recorded category. Explicit mixed-unknown, schema/format, replay-invalid, storage, and save-failure cases retain it.
- **184 UI unit tests, 11 Chromium component tests, and 69 Control UI E2E scenarios pass.** The two stale prefix assertions exposed by the final simplification were repaired and their two suites rerun: 21/21 pass. Other suites retain their valid final-input results. Coverage includes keyboard/touch disclosure, copying/redaction, refresh, partial-output preservation, provider-review recovery, placement failures, plugin feedback, and history reload.
- **139 core tests pass** across the shared reader, recorder, history sanitation, terminal publication, and durable lifecycle suites after simplification. UI/core production typechecks and selected core/test graphs, focused lint/format, stylesheet lint, i18n verification, controller checks, and build pass.
- Two isolated real-Gateway tests passed with a synthetic local provider: rejected credentials survive persisted reload with Open Models and no report link, and removing credentials prevents a new authenticated provider request. These ran before the last presentation/parser simplification; final core, UI, and browser tests cover that smaller delta. No paid/live provider credentials were used.
- **Red/green proof:** the same three reporting/layout cases fail against main’s production sources and pass on the candidate. Main fails the intended visible-title/reporting assertions, not setup. Main source substitutions were backed up and restored with exact SHA-256 equality.
- **Paired production-build budget check: zero violations.** Chat boot JavaScript gzip is +43 B; total CSS is −131 B raw / +17 B gzip. No budget or baseline changed. Existing main overages remain visible in the report; this does not claim the absolute baseline is below every ceiling.
- Local Auto Review completed at its default **P0-only** scope before the last simplification, with no findings. Refreshing that review was attempted but the supported helper is currently missing; this is not a final full-priority review. The [earlier ClawSweeper verdict](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204337#issuecomment-7120732555) reports no findings on 6e96079 and is not a review of this new head.

Not checked: physical mobile devices, Safari/Firefox, paid/live-provider failures, or the full repository suite locally. Exact-head hosted CI is monitored separately; prior-head green CI is not counted for this update.

<details>
<summary>Scope and performance measurements</summary>

Against selected main, production/docs: +422/−287 lines; tests: +485/−185 lines (including mechanical indentation). Existing consumers were migrated rather than weakening their recovery/navigation/clipboard checks. The smallest coherent scope is the failure notice plus the classification needed to keep its live and reloaded behavior consistent.

| Measurement | Main | New head | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Chat boot JS gzip | 1,336,594 B | 1,336,637 B | +43 B |
| Total CSS raw | 1,783,756 B | 1,783,625 B | −131 B |
| Total CSS gzip | 346,278 B | 346,295 B | +17 B |

</details>

## Visual proof

Real OpenClaw production builds, **main 4708bac → head 8ae8b16**, with synthetic Gateway data. Matched Chromium light-theme 1280×900 viewports; each comparison is cropped to the same 850×360 region. Annotations are separate copies of the original frames, not DOM edits. The second pair shows the materially different reportable-history path.

### Clean comparison

**Routine live failure — Before**

**After**

**Reportable history failure — Before**

Related: #197555

## What Problem This Solves

Rapid-MLX users need a named setup and memory-search provider in OpenClaw.

## User Impact

User impact: choose **Rapid-MLX** during setup, discover local chat models, and use `rapid-mlx/<model-id>` or an explicitly served embedding model for memory search. Rapid-MLX is an open-source local LLM inference server for Apple Silicon, built on MLX.

## Why This Change Was Made

Follows the bundled oMLX provider in #173327, reusing OpenAI-compatible transports with optional authentication and a default URL of `http://localhost:8000/v1`. Includes provider and memory docs, navigation, generated inventories, tests, official app/onboarding icons, and an existing generic activity glyph. No new external dependencies or changes to oMLX.

## Evidence

Before/after: real Control UI → Models → Add account → On this Gateway, with isolated local state. The before capture uses the same shared build with the new Rapid-MLX plugin omitted; the after capture includes the provider and its official-site onboarding icon. Both images were inspected and contain no personal data.

![Before: local provider list without Rapid-MLX](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raullenchai/openclaw/rapid-mlx-pr-assets/before.png)

![After: Rapid-MLX entry, official icon, and Connect server action](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raullenchai/openclaw/rapid-mlx-pr-assets/after.png)

- Fix pass: onboarding metadata/auth-choice tests passed (25 tests); the browser capture asserts Rapid-MLX is absent before and present after, with a decoded icon and a Connect server action. Inventory/config-baseline and scoped format checks passed.

prs.title: fix(ui): point gateway-token errors at the secret source and #token= link
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This replaces advice to run `openclaw doctor --generate-gateway-token` in the Control UI auth-required step, its English string, and the CLI and gateway error messages. The new text points at the configured secret source and the `#token=` fragment link already supported by the Control UI.

The old advice is destructive in practice: it rotates the gateway token, disconnecting other session pages and daemons that still hold the old one. The common cause of 'unauthorized: gateway token missing' is simply that this browser has no token saved in session storage. The supported fix is a `#token=<token>` fragment link, which the UI accepts and strips. No token is printed and no query parameter is used.

## Changes

- `ui/src/components/login-gate-feedback.ts`: remove the `--generate-gateway-token` command from the auth-required step.
- `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-login.ts`: `login.failure.authRequired.stepGenerate` now distinguishes 'this browser has no token saved' from 'no token configured', points at `gateway.auth.token` and the `#token=` link, and warns that generating a new token disconnects other sessions.
- `src/commands/gateway-auth-token.ts`, `src/flows/doctor-gateway-auth.ts`, `src/gateway/auth.ts`, `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/auth-messages.ts`: the same non-destructive guidance in the CLI, doctor, startup and WebSocket close messages.
- Three tests updated to assert the new strings.

Generated translation caches are intentionally excluded: the repo's i18n tooling says to commit only the English source and let the post-merge refresh translate.

## Evidence

- Targeted unit tests on head `139c94c9f`: `gateway-auth-token.test.ts` 10/10, `doctor-core-checks.test.ts` 14/14, `auth-messages.test.ts` 11/11 (35 passed, 0 failed). Commands: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts src/commands/gateway-auth-token.test.ts`, `--config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts src/flows/doctor-core-checks.test.ts`, `--config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-core.config.ts src/gateway/server/ws-connection/auth-messages.test.ts`.
- `pnpm exec oxlint` is clean on the eight files changed in this revision.
- The WebSocket `token_missing` close message is 109 bytes, under the 120-byte limit.
- The CLI no-token error now names the conditional Doctor recovery path; the command test asserts the exact message.
- On the submitted revision: 11 of 11 login-gate UI tests passed; spec, security and lint reviews were clean.
- A built-CLI or browser capture was not produced: building a modified gateway locally is disallowed by the contributor read-only constraint, so the evidence above is test and lint output from the changed code.
- Follow-up commit `139c94c9f` restores the runnable `openclaw doctor --generate-gateway-token` command and restart instruction in the WebSocket hint while keeping the `#token=` link; `auth-messages.test.ts` 11/11 and `oxlint` pass on the new head.
## Scope note

Other copies of the phrase remain in the wizard, security audit, known-weak secret path, macOS probe and docs. They are deliberately outside this patch to keep it small and reviewable; a follow-up can cover them.

prs.title: fix: publish a valid gateway hostname for long hostnames
prs.body:
Closes #202665

## What Problem This Solves

When a machine's hostname is longer than 63 characters, OpenClaw truncates it for the wide-area DNS-SD zone. The truncation can leave a trailing `-`, so the advertised SRV target (and its `A` owner) is not a valid hostname, violating the LDH rule the module already enforces for configured domains.

## User Impact

The gateway now advertises a well-formed hostname, so clients that validate the SRV target as a hostname (TLS/SNI, strict HTTP clients) are not handed an invalid name.

## Why This Change Was Made

`dnsLabel()` stripped leading and trailing hyphens before truncating to the 63-character limit, so truncation could re-expose a trailing `-`. The label is now re-trimmed after truncation.

## Evidence

**Launched Gateway (shipped entry point), not a test harness.** I built this head with `scripts/build-all.mts cliStartup` and ran:

```
node dist/index.js gateway run --allow-unconfigured
```

with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `discovery.wideArea.domain = openclaw.internal`, and a `--require` preload that sets `os.hostname()` to a 68-character name (`aaa…a-bbbbb`) and reports a Tailscale IPv4 interface. The Gateway logged:

```
[discovery] wide-area DNS-SD updated (openclaw.internal. → …\dns\openclaw.internal.db)
```

and wrote this zone (truncated host label is `aaa…a`, 62 chars, no trailing hyphen):

```
$ORIGIN openclaw.internal.
aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa IN A 100.64.0.1
_openclaw-gw._tcp IN PTR aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa._openclaw-gw._tcp
aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa._openclaw-gw._tcp IN SRV 0 0 18789 aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
```

I served that exact file with CoreDNS 1.15.0 and resolved it with a real DNS client:

```
PTR ["aaa…a._openclaw-gw._tcp.openclaw.internal"]
SRV [{"name":"aaa…a.openclaw.internal","port":18789,"priority":0,"weight":0,"type":"SRV"}]
A   ["100.64.0.1"]
```

Base comparison: the same 68-character hostname through `startGatewayDiscovery()` on `HEAD~1` (a base `dist` build was not available on this host) publishes `aaa…a-` (63 chars, trailing hyphen) as the SRV target and `A` owner — not a valid hostname.

Scope note: CoreDNS also serves the trailing-hyphen label from the base zone (DNS wire format allows any octet in a label), so this is not a hard resolution failure. The defect is that OpenClaw advertises a name that is not a valid hostname.

- Red on base, green on head: `keeps truncated host labels as valid DNS hostnames` in `src/infra/widearea-dns.test.ts` asserts the SRV target matches `^[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$` and that its `A` record exists (selected via the SRV target, not the `ns1` nameserver record). Full file: `10 passed | 1 skipped`.
- `oxlint` on both changed files exits 0; formatter check is clean.

Known environment limitation, unrelated: `src/infra/widearea-dns.boundary.test.ts` fails on this Windows host with `EPERM: operation not permitted, rename …` inside `@openclaw/fs-safe`'s atomic replacement. I reproduced the same failure against the base source with this change reverted.

Not run here: full `pnpm check` / repo-wide typecheck. Required CI workflows on this external PR are waiting on maintainer approval, which I cannot grant.

This change was AI-assisted and verified against the evidence above.

## Result

`check-additional-extension-package-boundary` and `check-lint-core-4` pass again on `main`. Since #204415 (b4cc3bc1) both fail on `extensions/google/transport-stream.ts`:

```
transport-stream.ts(159,32): error TS7006: Parameter 'type' implicitly has an 'any' type.
'ProviderCallStreamOptions' is an 'error' type that acts as 'any' ... (no-redundant-type-constituents)
```

## Cause

#204415 correctly changed `src/plugin-sdk/llm.ts` to import `resolveProviderContext` and its types from the package specifier `@openclaw/ai/provider-types`, so packaged builds share one symbol. The root `tsconfig.json` maps that subpath. The opt-in extension package boundary (`extensions/tsconfig.package-boundary.paths.json`, and xai's derived copy) maps every other public `@openclaw/ai` subpath to its emitted declaration, but not `provider-types`. ## Change

- Map `@openclaw/ai/provider-types` to `packages/plugin-sdk/dist/packages/ai/src/provider-types.d.ts` in the shared boundary paths and in xai's derived paths. The declaration is already emitted.
- New contract test: every public (non-`internal/`) `@openclaw/ai` alias in the root `tsconfig.json` has a boundary alias to its own declaration. The next public subpath an SDK file imports cannot silently degrade to `any` in plugins. It fails on `main` with `@openclaw/ai/provider-types: expected undefined`.

No suppressions, no product code changes.

## Evidence

- `tsc -p extensions/google/tsconfig.json --noEmit` after the boundary prep: 1 error on `main` (the TS7006 above), 0 on this head.

prs.title: fix(skills): detect inline child_process exec in security scanner
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the skill security scanner misses shell-command execution when a skill file calls `child_process` through an inline module load, so a malicious skill containing `require("child_process").exec(...)` can be published to the skill library without the critical security block firing.

## User Impact

User impact: the `dangerous-exec` critical finding now fires for inline `child_process` loads (`require("child_process").exec(...)`, `process.getBuiltinModule("child_process").exec(...)`, and computed-member forms), so skills that run shell commands are blocked at publish time and flagged in workspace audits as intended. Skills that use the module through a proven local namespace alias were already detected; behavior for those is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`isBenignMemberExecMatch` suppresses `dangerous-exec` matches whose receiver cannot be read as a bare identifier, on the theory that they are `RegExp.exec`-style calls. That suppression also matched `require("child_process").exec(...)` because the receiver (`require("child_process")`) does not end in an identifier, so the match was classified as benign and never reported.

The fix only classifies an unreadable receiver as benign when the receiver expression does not itself load `child_process` inline. It checks the receiver text for `require`/`import`/`getBuiltinModule` calls ending at the method access, preserving the `RegExp.exec` exclusion and keeping provenance scoping (a `child_process` load elsewhere on the line does not attribute a later `.exec` on a different receiver).

## Evidence

- Reproduced before the fix: `require("child_process").exec(...)`, `require("node:child_process").exec(...)`, `process.getBuiltinModule("child_process").exec(...)`, and the computed-member forms each produced **0** `dangerous-exec` findings, while `const cp = require("child_process"); cp.exec(...)` produced 1.
- After the fix, all inline-load forms produce the `dangerous-exec` critical finding; the `RegExp.exec` exclusion and plain-object `.exec` calls still produce 0 findings.
- Real behavior proof via the actual deep-audit runtime behind `openclaw security audit --deep`: a regression test in `audit-workshop-skills.test.ts` runs `collectInstalledSkillsCodeSafetyFindings` against a Workshop skill whose support file is `require("child_process").exec("node server.js")` and asserts it now surfaces a critical `skills.code_safety` finding. The same runtime also backs the Workshop library write block (`scanSkillBundle` → `POLICY_BLOCKED` in `src/skills/library/service.ts`).
- Added scanner regression tests for the previously-evaded inline forms (positive) and a provenance-scoping case (negative).
- Branch updated: merged current `main` (`d31463cc`) and resolved the conflicts in `src/skills/security/scanner.test.ts` / `src/security/audit-workshop-skills.test.ts` by keeping `main`'s refactored test bodies and re-adding only this PR's inline-receiver cases. The effective diff vs `main` is still exactly `src/skills/security/scanner.ts` plus the two regression files.
- On the merged head: `scanner.test.ts` and `audit-workshop-skills.test.ts` pass (6/6 in the audit suite, including the new inline-exec case); `pnpm tsgo:core` exits 0; `run-format.mts --check` and `oxlint` are clean on the three changed files.
