prs.title: fix(agent): keep replayed images whose bytes changed but source still loads
prs.body:
Fixes #204387

## What Problem This Solves

On the embedded runtime, an image sent with `chat.send` reaches the model on its own turn but disappears from every later turn. The user sees: *"1 image attachment could not be loaded; their image contents are unavailable. Tell the user and ask them to resend the image."* — even though the image is still loadable.

- Problem: `resolvePromptImageDecisions()` replay branch kept only images whose sanitized output hash matched the pinned set. The inline block and the stored original re-encode to different JPEG bytes for the same image, so the hash never matches.
- Solution: keep an image whose media fact was included before (`previous.hashes.has(part)`) and still loads on replay, instead of requiring its sanitized bytes to match exactly.
- What changed: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/prompt-image-decisions.ts` — added `wasIncluded` check before hash comparison; `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/images.test.ts` — regression test.
- What did NOT change: sanitization pipeline, image loading, media reference resolution, provider image preparation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Same source re-sanitizes to different output bytes because JPEG encoding is not deterministic across different input encodings (PNG inline vs JPEG stored original). Pinning by output hash is fundamentally fragile when the same image can arrive through different code paths.

- Best fix: yes — the fact index is the stable identity across turns, not the sanitized bytes.
- Alternative: hash decoded raw pixels instead of sanitized bytes — rejected because decoding every image to raw pixels is too expensive for the hot path.
- Risk / non-goals: if an image is genuinely deleted between turns, `wasIncluded` is true but the image won't appear in `result.images` (load fails), so it won't be retained — `failedMediaCount` still increments correctly.

## User Impact

Images sent earlier in a conversation no longer disappear from context with a "could not be loaded" notice. The model retains full visual context across turns without asking the user to resend.

## Evidence

Replay comparison before and after the fix:

```
$ pnpm vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/images.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/prompt-image-decisions.test.ts

 ✓ images.test.ts (41 tests) 348ms
 ✓ prompt-image-decisions.test.ts (1 test) 12ms
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  42 passed (42)
```

Regression test "keeps a resent remix of an already included source" verifies: first turn pins image by fact index, second turn loads different bytes for the same fact → image kept (not reported as failed), `failedMediaCount === 0`.

| Turn | Before fix | After fix |
|------|-----------|-----------|
| Turn 1 (inline block) | image pinned by output hash | image pinned by fact index |
| Turn 2 (replay, different bytes) | hash mismatch → failed, notice appended | fact was included + still loads → kept, no notice |

What was not tested: end-to-end gateway replay with real `media://` URI resolution (requires workspace media store setup).

prs.title: fix: let scheduled automations use Claude on Vertex with gcloud sign-in
prs.body:
Fixes #203575

## What Problem This Solves

Since 2026.10.10, people running Claude on Google Vertex with gcloud application default credentials (ADC) cannot use scheduled automations. Every scheduled turn on an `anthropic-vertex/*` model is refused with "Automation has no recorded inference account", and creating a new automation is refused too. Neither suggested recovery works: there is no stored account to record, and `openclaw doctor --fix` skips the job. Gemini on Vertex, using the same gcloud login on the same install, keeps working.

## User Impact

User impact: Claude-on-Vertex automations that use gcloud ADC run again, and new ones can be created. Doctor no longer needs to touch them. Interactive chats are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gemini on Vertex declares its gcloud credentials file in its plugin manifest, so OpenClaw counts that login as a configured key. Claude on Vertex did not declare it, so its login was classed as "known only at runtime". Scheduled runs, automation creation and Doctor all refuse that class. The `anthropic-vertex` manifest now declares the same credentials file the plugin already reads, mirroring `google-vertex`. Core scheduling policy is unchanged.

Accepted edge case: a Gateway that relies only on the GCP metadata server (`ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_USE_GCP_METADATA=1`, no credentials file) has no file to declare and keeps today's behavior. `google-vertex` has the same limit.

<details>
<summary>Technical detail</summary>

- Without manifest evidence, `anthropic-vertex` falls through to the setup-provider fallback in `resolveProviderDirectAuthPlanningEvidence`. `prepareAgentRuntimeAuth` turns that into `runtime` evidence, which `isConfiguredKeyAuthSource` rejects.
- The new `setup.providers[].authEvidence` entry (`local-file-with-env`) uses `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` when set, with no fallback. Otherwise it uses `${HOME}/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json` or `${APPDATA}/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json`, matching `region.ts`. It returns the same `gcp-vertex-credentials` marker and `gcloud adc` source as the existing fallback.
- The entry declares no `authMethods` or `envVars`, so setup choices, startup activation and provider discovery are unchanged.

</details>

## Evidence

- **Reproduced on current main through the real auth planner and bundled manifests,** with a synthetic credentials file and no network:
  - Before: Claude on Vertex is classed `runtime`, which is refused, while Gemini on Vertex is classed `environment`.
  - After: both are classed `environment`.
- **New regression test** in `src/cron/inference-binding.test.ts` creates a Claude-on-Vertex automation with a gcloud credentials file.
  - On main it fails with the reporter's exact error: "Automation requires a stored inference account or a key in the environment or provider config".
  - With this change it passes.
- **Related suites:** 594 of 601 tests pass across auth planning, provider discovery, automation binding, the automation auth-continuity integration test, the Doctor migration, `extensions/anthropic-vertex`, and the plugin manifest and setup tests. The 7 failures are in `src/plugins/manifest-registry.test.ts`. They fail identically on main because the test expects `/var/...` while macOS reports temp folders as `/private/var/...`, so they are unrelated to this change.
- The `services-cron` typecheck shard, `plugins:inventory:check`, format, lint and `git diff --check` are clean.

**Gap:** this was not run as a live scheduled turn against Vertex. That needs a Google Cloud project with Claude enabled and real gcloud credentials, which I don't have. The reporter showed that skipping this exact check makes their refused job return `ok`. If someone with a Claude-on-Vertex ADC setup can run `openclaw automations run <id> --force` on this branch and share the redacted output, that would close the gap.

prs.title: fix: recover completed Codex answers without truncation
prs.body:
Closes #204197

## What Problem This Solves

When a completed Codex session has a large transcript, an authorized supervision read can cut off before the final answer. The tool tells the agent to narrow the read, but the legacy arguments can't select the answer.

## User Impact

User impact: Agents with transcript access can recover a completed answer, including a long one, without reading the rest of the conversation. Existing reads and access controls are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`codex_session_read` accepts an opt-in `final_answer` selector. It uses Codex's paginated history to select the newest completed turn or a pinned `turn_id`, then returns only its `agentMessage` marked `final_answer`. Long text continues in UTF-16-safe chunks of at most 4,096 units, tied to the full answer's SHA-256. The bounded path uses the same policy-guarded native requests as every other supervision read and adds no new authority checks. It does not increase the shared output budget or fall back to the full transcript.

## Evidence

**Built Gateway, before and after:** The OpenClaw Codex harness called the real supervision tool through the plugin-managed native Codex 0.169.0 App Server, with a fresh Gateway state directory and an isolated `CODEX_HOME` per run. The fixture came from two completed native Codex turns driven by a deterministic loopback Responses provider; only the single thread's rollout and SQLite history projection were copied into each proof home. No Codex login or external inference was used.

- **Before (`e2973f933`):** 102,873 characters of earlier history preceded the stored final answer. The legacy read exceeded the 32,000 weighted budget and ended with `0123456789abcd` plus the truncation notice. `END-OF-ANSWER-204197` never reached the model-facing tool result.
- **After (`236ff59ba`):** Starting with `final_answer: {}` returned 3 chunks (3,964 / 3,964 / 1,992 UTF-16 units), totaling 9,920. The joined answer ended with `END-OF-ANSWER-204197`. Its SHA-256 matched both the returned `textSha256` and the independently read native answer: `d8dbced5227a9c1062db244125f0118133755c36a1edd7c077e15d9a186c8ed7`.
- **Controls:** A pinned earlier turn returned `PINNED-ANSWER-204197`; a wrong `text_sha256` was rejected at offset 3,964; omitting `final_answer` reproduced the same legacy truncation behavior.

Focused validation: 96 tests passed across 3 files. Extension typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, whitespace, and `pnpm check:changed` against the candidate parent all passed. Local Auto Review on `236ff59ba` reported no P0 findings (static, P0 scope).

### What was not verified

This change does not fix the separate wrong-home/endpoint selection bug that can return `thread not found` for an existing session. Automatic completion delivery was not exercised.

Thanks to [@jamesdwilson](https://github.com/jamesdwilson) for the [report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/204197) and the [native history procedure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/204197#issuecomment-7114372466). Patch by [@MertBasar0](https://github.com/MertBasar0).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/4a64cdb7-19d1-4844-846c-b31611836835)

## Worked on by

- @MertBasar0

prs.title: fix(onboard): reject an explicitly empty --agent-name in every flow
prs.body:
Closes #204454

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw onboard --modern --agent-name ""` silently creates the default `main` agent instead of rejecting the empty name, while the classic flow rejects the same input with `Invalid --agent-name: Agent name is required.` (reported in #204454 with a full reproduction). This change forwards the explicitly empty value through the whole modern onboarding chain so the existing owner validator rejects it in every flow.

- Problem: seven truthiness-guarded hand-offs (`opts.agentName ?`, `params.agentName ?`, `operation.agentName ?`, ...) drop an explicitly empty `--agent-name` before it reaches `validateFirstOnboardingAgentName`, so the setup apply falls back to `?? { name: "main" }` and writes a default identity the user never asked for. The owner validator already returns "Agent name is required." and throws before any config read/write — it simply never receives the value.
- Solution: replace the truthiness guards with `!== undefined` checks at all seven hand-offs (register.onboard.ts x2, tui-backend.ts, onboarding-welcome.ts, operations-execution-helpers.ts, onboard-interactive.ts, onboard-interactive-runner.ts), following the merged forward-original-value precedent #192726. The explicit empty string now reaches the owner validator and is rejected; an omitted flag still means "use the default".
- What changed: the seven conditionals above; one row added to the existing `routes inference-gated onboarding for %s` `it.each` table in register.onboard.test.ts (plus a `readonly` widening of the local `runCli` helper so the table's array row type-checks); the `--agent-name` bullet in docs/cli/onboard.md now states that an explicitly empty value is invalid in every flow.
- What did NOT change: the omission default (`?? { name: "main" }` in setup-apply stays — omitting the flag keeps today's behavior); the owner validator and its error text; the classic non-interactive rejection; workspace/accept-risk forwarding (still truthiness-guarded, out of scope); no new config options, no schema changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Best fix: forward the original value and let the single existing owner (`validateFirstOnboardingAgentName` / `ensureOnboardingAgent`) decide validity, rather than adding a second rejection policy at the CLI parse layer. The owner already rejects an empty name before touching config, and the classic flow already surfaces that rejection; the modern chain only needed to stop discarding the value. This is the same shape as merged PR #192726 (forward original option values instead of truthiness-filtering them).

Alternative(s) considered: (1) reject empty `--agent-name` at command registration — rejected because it duplicates the owner's policy in a second place and still leaves the conversational/handoff paths (onboard-interactive, guided handoff) dropping the value; (2) coerce empty to undefined explicitly at each site — rejected because it is the bug itself (silently substituting the default for an explicit user value).

Risk: low. The only behavior change is for an explicitly empty `--agent-name`, which previously produced a silent default identity and now produces the owner's existing rejection before any config write. Omitted flags, valid names, and the classic flow are byte-for-byte unchanged in the shipped matrix below. The empty string is now carried through operation objects that previously omitted the key; all consumers read it through the same owner validation path.

## User Impact

Users who pass an explicitly empty `--agent-name` now get a clear "Agent name is required." rejection in the modern interactive onboarding (and the conversational handoff), matching the classic flow, instead of discovering later that a default `main` agent was created under an identity they never chose. Omitting the flag keeps the existing default behavior. No migration or config change is required.

## Evidence

| Case (built launcher, isolated state) | Before (frozen base f7aa7e3) | After (this head 35dc8fb) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onboard --modern --agent-name ''` | exit 0; default agent `main` silently written to config | exit 0; chat reports `That did not go through: Agent name is required.`; no agent written |
| `onboard --modern --agent-name helper` (control) | exit 0; agent `helper` created | exit 0; agent `helper` created (unchanged) |
| `onboard --modern` (flag omitted, control) | exit 0; default agent `main` | exit 0; default agent `main` (unchanged) |
| `onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --agent-name ''` (classic control) | exit 1; `Invalid --agent-name: Agent name is required.` | exit 1; identical rejection (unchanged) |
| register.onboard.test.ts (cli shard) | new empty-name row FAILS (keys dropped): `1 failed \| 28 passed` | `29 passed` |

Both arms are real `cliStartup` builds (`OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts cliStartup`) run through the shipped launcher in a fresh chmod-700 scratch HOME/state dir with no credentials. The interactive cells run under a real PTY; the inference gate is satisfied by a loopback OpenAI-compatible fixture (non-streaming completion), so no third-party provider or token is involved. Each cell is a full user command; the roster is read back from the written `openclaw.json` (`agents.entries`).

Arm identity (`node openclaw.mjs --version`):

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs --version   # base arm
OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (f7aa7e3)
$ node openclaw.mjs --version   # head arm
OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (35dc8fb)
```

Built-bundle form self-attestation — head `dist/register.onboard-*.mjs` carries the forwarded value:

```js
// head built chunk
...e.agentName!==void 0?{setupAgentName:e.agentName}:{}
// frozen base source (built into the base arm)
...(opts.agentName ? { setupAgentName: opts.agentName as string } : {})
```

Shipped matrix, verbatim harness RESULT lines (base arm):

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs onboard --modern --agent-name ''
RESULT label=base-empty3 classic=false agentNameArg="" exit=0 why=process-exit elapsedMs=37084 inferenceRequests=2 roster=[{"id":"main","name":"main"}]
$ node openclaw.mjs onboard --modern --agent-name helper
RESULT label=base-name classic=false agentNameArg="helper" exit=0 why=process-exit elapsedMs=36106 inferenceRequests=2 roster=[{"id":"helper","name":"helper"}]
$ node openclaw.mjs onboard --modern
RESULT label=base-omit classic=false agentNameArg="__OMIT__" exit=0 why=process-exit elapsedMs=36456 inferenceRequests=2 roster=[{"id":"main","name":"main"}]
$ node openclaw.mjs onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --agent-name ''
RESULT label=base-classic-empty classic=true agentNameArg="" exit=1 why=process-exit elapsedMs=11827 inferenceRequests=0 roster=null
```

Shipped matrix, verbatim harness RESULT lines (head arm):

```console
$ node openclaw.mjs onboard --modern --agent-name ''
RESULT label=head-empty2 classic=false agentNameArg="" exit=0 why=process-exit elapsedMs=31633 inferenceRequests=2 roster=null
$ node openclaw.mjs onboard --modern --agent-name helper
RESULT label=head-name classic=false agentNameArg="helper" exit=0 why=process-exit elapsedMs=35943 inferenceRequests=2 roster=[{"id":"helper","name":"helper"}]
$ node openclaw.mjs onboard --modern
RESULT label=head-omit2 classic=false agentNameArg="__OMIT__" exit=0 why=process-exit elapsedMs=59042 inferenceRequests=2 roster=[{"id":"main","name":"main"}]
$ node openclaw.mjs onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --agent-name ''
RESULT label=head-classic-empty classic=true agentNameArg="" exit=1 why=process-exit elapsedMs=11138 inferenceRequests=0 roster=null
```

The head empty-name cell's PTY transcript shows the owner's rejection surfaced in the chat, and the written config contains no `agents.entries`:

```text
That did not go through: Agent name is required.
```

The classic control prints the same rejection on both arms:

```text
Invalid --agent-name: Agent name is required.
```

Regression test (folded into the existing `it.each` table, no new test file). Pre-fix RED with the production change reverted and the test kept:

```console
$ vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts src/cli/program/register.onboard.test.ts
FAIL  cli  src/cli/program/register.onboard.test.ts > routes inference-gated onboarding for --modern,--agent-name,
AssertionError: expected [ [ { yes: false, …(3) }, …(2) ] ] to deeply equal [ [ { yes: false, …(4) }, …(2) ] ]
- Expected
+ Received
-       "setupAgentName": "",
-     {
-       "agentName": "",
-     },
+     {},
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 28 passed (29)
```

Post-fix GREEN on the head:

```console
$ vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts src/cli/program/register.onboard.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  29 passed (29)
```

Sibling suites of every touched file also pass on the head: onboard-interactive.test.ts + onboard-interactive-runner.test.ts (commands shard, 14 passed), tui-backend.test.ts, chat-turn-router.operations.test.ts, config-write-validation.test.ts (53 passed across the three). `check-test-lines-ratchet` reports `Net test lines: +5; allowance: 400` and `check-line-cap-ratchet` reports no new violations; oxfmt check is clean on all changed source files.

Honesty note: on a host with `LANG=zh_CN.UTF-8`, five onboarding-welcome.test.ts label assertions fail identically on the frozen base and on the head (the wizard i18n resolves the host locale); with an English locale the file passes 14/14 on the head. This is a pre-existing environment artifact, not a behavior change of this patch.

What was not tested: a real third-party model provider (the loopback fixture stands in for the inference gate only); macOS/Windows terminals; the non-interactive modern path, which prints an overview and never applies setup, so it has no harm path here.

Open PR collision check: searched the open-PR snapshot by changed files for all eight touched paths and by anchor keywords (`agent-name`, `setupAgentName`, `firstAgent`, `modern agent-name`); no open PR touches these files. #202108 (first-agent native activation) is in the same domain but its file list is disjoint from this patch.

prs.title: fix: keep Feishu sessions active during Doctor repairs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

During an OpenClaw upgrade or `doctor --fix`, a Feishu direct chat can disappear from the active session list even though its saved history is intact. A temporary transcript read failure can trigger archival, and an upgrade can run the old repair before the updated Feishu plugin is installed.

## User Impact

Doctor leaves history and session overrides intact when it cannot verify a transcript. During upgrades it defers these channel repairs until the owning plugin is ready; it still handles verified problems and continues repairs for other available channels.

## Why This Change Was Made

The host already knows which plugins are waiting for package convergence. Apply that decision to channel repair sequences so an old adapter cannot run a repair while its package is pending. Separately, Feishu reports an unsuccessful transcript read without passing it to the repair path. A malformed row that prevents a complete read does not authorize removal of the whole session. No config or database migration is needed.

## Evidence

- In a disposable install of `2026.11.6`, the real Doctor archived one healthy synthetic Feishu session when the transcript read returned an injected `SQLITE_BUSY`. The other session was untouched.
- An unpatched `2026.11.5` → `2026.11.6` package update with only the fixed Feishu plugin available to the updater still archived both healthy fixtures. The archive timestamps were inside the first activation Doctor, before the plugin update.
- Repeated the complete npm upgrade from published `2026.11.5` with the original Feishu plugin to release-matched `2026.11.6` builds carrying both fixes in a disposable macOS profile. Verified the installed core bytes and the updated plugin, both original session IDs, exact message contents, model pins, thinking overrides, and zero archives for either fixture.
- Ran the installed `doctor --fix` again with the same injected `SQLITE_BUSY`. It warned and preserved both fixtures. Config validation and the isolated Gateway's readiness and RPC checks passed before and after the upgrade.
- Both regressions failed on the unpatched source. All 26 targeted tests passed with the fix (14 channel Doctor, 12 Feishu Doctor), along with targeted formatting and type-aware lint.

The packaged replay used the release-matched backport and synthetic chats; it did not connect to a Feishu tenant. The PR also extracts the unchanged transcript validator to satisfy the file-length check. Both focused suites were rerun on the final source.

### Captured behavior (redacted)

These excerpts are from the original disposable macOS runs, not a reconstruction. The commands used installed packages and isolated state with synthetic Feishu DMs; no Feishu tenant was contacted. Unrelated terminal lines were omitted, terminal box formatting was removed, and the Feishu session key was redacted. The `fixture-healthy-*` IDs are synthetic.

**Published 2026.11.6: `doctor --fix` with an injected transcript read failure.** The test hook recorded the failure at the transcript read boundary. The installed Doctor removed one active entry:

```text
$ openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions
Feishu local state repaired.
- Removed 1 Feishu-scoped session entry from 1 session store.
- Archived 0 session artifact files.
Doctor complete.
```

Fault-injection receipt (selected fields) and the original SQLite-backed fixture check:

```text
{"phase":"control","code":"SQLITE_BUSY","isolatedState":true}
$ node session-fixture.mjs inspect-control
```

prs.title: fix(agents): treat a message send batched with other tool calls as progress
prs.body:
Closes #204148

## What Problem This Solves

When the agent sends a message to the current conversation (for example "On it, checking now…") and, in the same step, calls another tool to do the actual work, OpenClaw treated that message as the finished reply and ended the turn. The other tool's result was saved but never handed back to the model, so the work the user asked for was silently dropped.

## User Impact

User impact: a progress message the agent sends alongside other tool calls no longer ends the turn; the agent receives its tool results and finishes the request. Sends with an explicit `final`, and a send that is the only thing the agent did in that step, behave exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

When `final` is omitted, a `message(action=send)` now counts as progress if the assistant message that issued it also called a tool other than `message`. The same rule is applied everywhere that decides whether a send completes the turn (the turn-ending check, the delivery mirror and the subscriber's delivery state), through one shared resolver, so they cannot disagree. An explicit `final: true` or `final: false` still wins.

Since the first revision the branch was rebased onto current `main`, and:

- The model-facing contract now matches. The `message` tool's `final` description, the message-tool-only system prompt line and the shared harness guidance tell the model to set `final` explicitly when the same response also calls a tool other than `message`. That wording is true on every runtime: the exception itself is implemented in the OpenClaw (embedded) runtime only, and the CLI, Codex and agentsapi harnesses still treat an omitted `final` as completing. `docs/concepts/messages.md` describes the exception.
- The message tool's part of the check lives in a small helper (`src/agents/tools/message-tool-send-final.ts`) to keep `message-tool-execution.ts` within the repository's file-length limit; no behavior change.
- New QA scenario `group-batched-send-progress` covers the regression through a real Gateway and qa-channel.

## Evidence

Checked on head `90e78d4d57` (base `e2973f933f`), Linux, Node 24.22.3, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`:

- New regression tests: a send batched with another tool call does not end the turn (`message-tool-terminal.batched-send.test.ts`); the resolver, subscriber and message tool treat it as progress; explicit `final` and send-only messages are unchanged.
- All related suites pass (unit and integration):

| Test file | Result |
|---|---|
| `message-tool-terminal.batched-send.test.ts` | 2/2 |
| `message-tool-terminal.test.ts` | 45/45 |
| `message-tool-terminal.tool-authored.test.ts` | 19/19 |
| `embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts` | 104/104 |
| `embedded-agent-message-tool-source-reply.test.ts` | 82/82 |
| `tools/message-tool.test.ts` | 98/98 |
| `tools/message-tool-execution.test.ts` | 68/68 |
| `tools/message-tool.source-reply.test.ts` | 25/25 |
| `tools/message-tool.internal-source-reply.integration.test.ts` | 16/16 |
| `tools/message-tool.local-source-reply.integration.test.ts` | 14/14 |
| `code-mode.source-reply.loop.test.ts` | 8/8 |
| `embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session.test.ts` | 26/26 |

- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on all touched files: clean. `pnpm tsgo:core`: clean.

### End to end: isolated Gateway, real model, qa-channel (head `90e78d4d57`)

QA Lab drives a real Gateway child through the synthetic `qa-channel` group transport in `message_tool` visible-reply mode with `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` (code mode off, so the model calls `read` directly). The prompt asks for a progress `message(action=send)` with no `final` plus a `read` in the same assistant message, then a final reply containing a code from the file. Retries disabled.

| Run | Model's first step | Posted to the group | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| base `e2973f933f` #1 | `message {action: send}` + `read` | progress only | **fail**: turn ended, the read result never reached the model |
| base `e2973f933f` #2 | same | progress only | **fail** |
| fix `90e78d4d57` #1 | same | progress, then `QA-GROUP-BATCHED-OK EVIDENCE-7Q4K` | pass |
| fix `90e78d4d57` #2 | same | progress, then final with the code | pass |

When the model sets `final: false` itself, base and fix both continue, so the bug needs an omitted `final`. With code mode on, the model batched `message` with `exec` and base and fix both continued.

Deterministic version on the mock provider (committed): `pnpm openclaw qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario group-batched-send-progress` fails on base (1 provider request, no final reply) and passes on the fix (2 requests, progress then final).

### Upgrade from the latest stable (`openclaw@2026.11.7`)

The Docker `published-upgrade-survivor` lane could not pull its pinned base image (Docker Hub rate limit), so the same steps ran natively with an isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME`: install `openclaw@2026.11.7`, onboard non-interactively, set non-default config (`messages.groupChat.visibleReplies=message_tool`, default model, agent identity name), start the Gateway and run a real-model turn that stores a code, stop the Gateway, install the candidate package (packed with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs`) over it, run `openclaw doctor --non-interactive`, start the Gateway, then compare and continue the conversation. The same run with a package built from `main` (`e2973f933f`) serves as the control.

| Check | candidate `90e78d4d57` | control `main` `e2973f933f` |
|---|---|---|
| Gateway `/readyz`, `/healthz` after upgrade | ready, 200 | ready, 200 |
| Non-default config values | all retained | all retained |
| Config keys removed or changed | none (only `wizard.lastRunAt`/`lastRunCommand`) | same |
| Session history (10 messages) | identical before and after | identical |
| Same conversation after upgrade | `RECALLED UPG-4417` | `RECALLED UPG-4417` |
| First `doctor --non-interactive` | stops at `session-entry-state` (step-refused) | same |

The first-run Doctor refusal happens identically on `main` without this change, so it is a pre-existing upgrade-path issue rather than something this PR introduces; it is worth its own follow-up. This change adds no config, state, schema or migration, so nothing persisted depends on it.

prs.title: fix(agents): stop a per-block assistant replay from duplicating a thinking summary
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #204256.

With the `claude-cli` backend and `--include-partial-messages`, a thinking block that is not the first content block of a Claude message is emitted **twice** in the `thinking` snapshot (`text` becomes `<summary><summary>`), so clients that render the snapshot show every such thought duplicated.

Claude Code's `stream-json` output re-emits every finished content block as an `assistant` record whose `message.content` contains **only that one block** (same `message.id`, `stop_reason: null`). The stream path keys thinking by the provider's content-block `event.index`, but the record path keyed it by the block's position inside that one-element `content` array — which is always `0`:

```ts
for (const [index, block] of content.entries()) { // index is always 0 for per-block records
  const previous = tracker.streamedByIndex.get(index) ?? "";
```

For a message that is `thinking` (index 0, empty / signature only) followed by a thinking summary at streamed index 1, the summary is stored under `1` by the stream path. The per-block record then finds nothing under `0`, stores the summary there, and `assembleThinkingTextByIndex` yields `{0: S, 1: S}` → `S + S`.

## Why This Change Was Made

A one-element `assistant` thinking record whose text is already covered by a streamed block is a **replay**, not new progress. Skip it instead of opening a second slot:

```ts
const perBlockRecord =
  content.length === 1 &&
  isRecord(content[0]) &&
  content[0].type === "thinking" &&
  typeof content[0].thinking === "string";
...
if (perBlockRecord && isPerBlockThinkingReplay(tracker, block.thinking)) {
  // Already covered by a streamed block: a replay, not new progress.
  continue;
}
```

`isPerBlockThinkingReplay` treats the record as a replay when any streamed block already `startsWith` its text — the same prefix-snapshot rule the surrounding code already uses for multi-block records, applied here across indexes because a per-block record carries no index of its own.

**Fix classification:** `behavior-preserving` for every existing path. Multi-block records keep their local-index behavior; single-block records whose text is **not** already streamed (snapshot-only reasoning) still create their slot as before. Only the duplicate case changes.

## User Impact

A summarized thinking block that is not the message's first content block now renders once instead of twice in the thinking snapshot. Final answers, tool calls and agent execution are unaffected.

## Evidence

### Base fails, head passes

Same command on both sides:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/cli-output-reasoning.test.ts
```

| | Result |
|---|---|
| Base (`ba2046d48e1`, fix stashed) | `Tests 1 failed \| 21 passed (22)` — `keeps a per-block assistant replay from duplicating a summary streamed at index 1` |
| Head (`8606fc94392`) | `Tests 22 passed (22)` |

The new regression reproduces the reported record sequence exactly:

```ts
claudeMessageStart("msg-1"),
claudeBlockStart({ type: "thinking" }, 0),
claudeAssistantSnapshot("msg-1", [thought("")]),
claudeBlockStart({ type: "thinking" }, 1),
claudeThinkingDelta("Summary of the reasoning.", 1),
claudeAssistantSnapshot("msg-1", [thought("Summary of the reasoning.")]),
// expected: [reasoning("Summary of the reasoning.")]  — once, not S + S
```

### Shipped-parser run (BASE duplicates, HEAD once)

The production entry every `claude-cli` turn builds is `createCliJsonlStreamingParser` (`src/agents/cli-runner/execute-process.ts:198`). Driving that exact function with the issue's record sequence reproduces the user-visible snapshot the callback hands the UI. The harness replays the reported frames verbatim; it does not stub the parser or the thinking path.

```sh
# frames: message_start(msg-1) -> block_start(thinking,0) -> assistant[thinking:""]
#      -> block_start(thinking,1) -> thinking_delta(SUMMARY,1) -> assistant[thinking:SUMMARY] -> result
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs <harness>.mts
```

**BASE** (`perBlockRecord` guard short-circuited to `false`, same tree, same frames):

```
thinking snapshots observed:
  - "The reasoning summary the user should see exactly once."
  - "The reasoning summary the user should see exactly once.The reasoning summary the user should see exactly once."
final snapshot: "...exactly once....exactly once..."
summary occurrences in final snapshot: 2
RESULT: FAIL (summary duplicated)
```

**HEAD** (`8606fc94392`):

```
thinking snapshots observed:
  - "The reasoning summary the user should see exactly once."
final snapshot: "The reasoning summary the user should see exactly once."
summary occurrences in final snapshot: 1
RESULT: PASS (summary appears exactly once)
```

The BASE run is the same tree with only the guard expression forced off, so the two runs differ by exactly the one variable under test (the commit is unchanged; the working copy was `dirty` only for that one expression during the BASE capture).

### Shipped CLI turn via stub-claude subprocess (BASE duplicates, HEAD once)

The shipped parser entry is driven here through a **real subprocess on PATH** that replays the issue's exact frame sequence — the same bytes a `claude --print --output-format stream-json --include-partial-messages --verbose` process would emit. No mocks: the parser is the production compiled code (`dist/`), the bytes come from a real subprocess, the callback is the same `onThinkingDelta` the CLI wires to `emitCliThinkingDelta`.

```sh
# /usr/local/bin/claude is a stub that replays the issue's frames verbatim;
# the proof script spawns it with the real CLI args, captures stdout,
# then feeds those exact bytes through createCliJsonlStreamingParser.
node /tmp/proof-head-final.mjs   # HEAD chunk (guard active)
node /tmp/proof-base-final.mjs   # BASE chunk (guard=false, same tree)
```

**HEAD** (`8606fc94392`, guard active):

```
HEAD final snapshot: "The reasoning summary the user should see exactly once."
HEAD occurrences: 1 PASS
```

**BASE** (guard short-circuited to `false`, same tree, same frames):

```
BASE final snapshot: "The reasoning summary the user should see exactly once.The reasoning summary the user should see exactly once."
BASE occurrences: 2 FAIL (duplicated as expected)
```

The stub-claude subprocess replays all 10 frames byte-for-byte (mismatches: 0), confirming the frame sequence is exactly what the issue reported. The parser is the production `createCliJsonlStreamingParser` exported from the compiled `dist/` chunk — the same function `execute-process.ts:198` builds for every `claude-cli` turn.

### Adjacent suites

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  src/agents/cli-output-events.test.ts \
  src/agents/cli-output-snapshots.test.ts \
  src/agents/cli-output-jsonl.test.ts \
  src/agents/cli-output-partial-messages.test.ts
```

`Test Files 2 passed | 47 passed` and `Test Files 2 passed | 40 passed` — 87 tests green, including the multi-block snapshot-only ordering, prefix-replay, tool-interleaved and message-reset cases that share this tracker.

### Mechanical gates

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-line-cap-ratchet.mts
# Line-cap ratchet OK: 2 changed source files; no new violations or over-cap growth.

node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts
# Test lines OK. Net test lines: +14; allowance: 400; allocation credit: 0.

node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/agents/cli-output-events.ts src/agents/cli-output-reasoning.test.ts
# All matched files use the correct format.
```

### Impact surface

| File | Change | Risk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/agents/cli-output-events.ts` | New `isPerBlockThinkingReplay` guard on the `assistant`-record thinking path | Scoped to one-element thinking records whose text a streamed block already covers; all other record shapes unchanged |
| `src/agents/cli-output-reasoning.test.ts` | One regression case | Test-only |

## Not tested

- **No live model turn.** A real `claude --print --output-format stream-json --include-partial-messages` turn needs working Claude credentials, which this environment does not have (the CLI fails auth and retries). The shipped-parser run above drives the production parser entry with the issue's exact frames; it is not a live authenticated turn. Evidence tier: **producer-chain** (the parser is the real production code path; the frames are the reporter's, replayed, not synthesized from the fix).
- Not verified against a non-Claude backend; the guard is inside the Claude JSONL thinking path only.

## Cleanup

The work ran in an isolated worktree against `origin/main` (`ba2046d48e1`). No Gateway, session, token or config on this host was touched.

Precedent for the shape: the surrounding prefix-replay rule (`previous.startsWith(block.thinking)`) already treats repeated snapshots as replays; this extends the same rule to per-block records that carry no index.

prs.title: refactor(ios): give session presentation an independent owner
prs.body:
Fixes #203831

## What Problem This Solves

Maintaining iOS session titles and row details currently requires other screens to depend on the Command Center view. The chat header, sidebar, and session rows all reach into that screen for shared presentation rules.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Session naming, snooze descriptions, activity times, row flags, and colors stay the same. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move the existing presentation type and functions into one app-local `SessionPresentation` owner and migrate every caller. The Command Center keeps its screen behavior and special default-chat row. No forwarding aliases remain. The seven net additional Swift lines provide the independent owner and explicit existing main-actor isolation.

This is part of the requested iOS architecture cleanup; coordination with the ongoing Command Center work is recorded in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192521#issuecomment-7085734637.

prs.title: fix(release): bind retained npm producers to admitting qualification
prs.body:
## Problem

`openclaw@2026.11.8` publication ([run 45349229685](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45349229685/job/138293136383)) failed in `Dispatch publish workflows` before any npm writes:

```
Prepared npm Q != P adoption requires live candidate-owned qualification.
```

The Full Release Validation run reused plugin npm bytes from an earlier qualification through the supported `publication_artifact_source_json` pin. So the validation commit (Q `7e3d39d4`) differs from the retained artifact producer commit (`de69e842`, run `45304470567`). Both are bound in the authenticated manifest. `authenticatePreparedNpmArtifactEvidence` required the authenticated qualification SHA to equal the **producer** SHA. For a selected retained source, the qualification that admitted this validation is Q.

## Solution

Mirror the existing binding owner (`validateCandidateOwnedArtifactBinding` in `validate-full-release-validation-evidence.mjs`). For a manifest with `publicationArtifactSource`, the authenticated qualification must equal the manifest's own `workflowSha` (Q). Otherwise it must still equal the producer SHA, which keeps receipt recovery unchanged. Candidate SHA, live revalidation authority, descriptor/producer and policy-source checks are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Regression test `test/scripts/plugin-npm-prepared-release-retained-producer.test.ts`: both cases fail on `origin/main` and pass with the fix. One accepts a Q-admitted retained producer; the other rejects a qualification that does not own the validation.
- Read-only replay of the publisher's `authorize` command against the real sealed evidence (FRV `45343386282/1`, P `673b65f0`, the exact retained artifact descriptor). On main it reproduces the exact CI error; with the fix it prints `AUTHORIZE_OK`, using 166 of 256 requests.
- Sibling suites `plugin-npm-prepared-release`, `plugin-npm-receipt-recovery`, `openclaw-release-ready` plus the new test: 169 passed. An initial narrower version broke receipt recovery, which this revision preserves.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `git diff --check` pass.

## Impact

Unblocks 2026.11.8 npm publication on the normal route without changing the frozen candidate, validation, or package bytes.

## Worked on by

- @vincentkoc
- @RomneyDa

prs.title: feat: let administrators manage roles in Settings → Team → Roles
prs.body:
Related: #202552

## What Problem This Solves

Administrators of a shared OpenClaw Gateway can only manage operator roles (`gateway.roles`) by editing raw config. They can't easily see what a role allows, who has it, or give one person different participant tools without hand-writing JSON. The Remote access page shows each member's role but has no way to see what it means.

## User Impact

User impact: administrators get **Settings → Team → Roles**. It lists every role with the people who have it, explains in plain language what each role allows in a person's own sessions and in sessions they're invited to, and lets them edit, create, duplicate and delete roles and assign people. Remote access links each member's role and the invite form to this page. Nothing changes for non-administrators.

## Why This Change Was Made

Roles are core Gateway config that the core Gateway enforces, so the editor is a core Settings page rather than a plugin. It uses only existing Gateway methods:
- **Reads:** `config.get` and `users.list`. The people counts come from `users.list`.
- **Saves:** one `config.patch` per change, sending the hash the page loaded. A role edit also checks that the role hasn't changed since the editor opened, so a concurrent change is reported instead of overwritten.
- **Assignments:** `users.setRole`.

Writing still requires `operator.admin`, as before. Deleting a role first moves its people (and repoints its GitHub mappings) to a role the admin picks. The default role can't be deleted. The participant tool list moves to `src/shared` so the page offers exactly the Gateway's list.

Design and placement were reviewed with Josh on a mockup before implementation. Base is the Participate branch (#202552), because the invited-access settings depend on it.

## Evidence

Mock Gateway fixtures in the real Control UI (dark, 1280×860). Before = `origin/openclaw-2b7/participate` 5672d417181d, after = this branch c056c927e938. Same fixtures for both.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Settings has no Team group or roles page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7124b308-4839-452e-b820-da93e81a366e) | ![After: Settings → Team → Roles lists roles and their people](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b8a7ce9-3c22-4525-a5bd-ae47e516d808) |
| ![Before: Remote access shows role chips only](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e4e823e3-21a3-4d66-9c19-61b7760e132f) | ![After: each member has an Open role link](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b135e4b-1703-420c-80b4-91cb0a84ef17) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![No place to manage roles highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d24d18b-61e7-403c-9170-d2efdbc6391d) | ![Team group and role list highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/99c6e01e-3269-4544-8d18-fdd05ec0e3bd) |
| ![Role chip without explanation highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/040b1a2f-1d78-4e5c-8cc2-0901ea9a5936) | ![Open role link highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/19acbbe4-cf09-40e2-8fd3-7b97005de5c7) |

Role editor (after): ![Role editor showing what the role allows, its people and session settings](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9de1844-68c5-4862-9e71-f3a996bf34ea)

**What was checked:**
- **Mocked-Gateway browser tests** (`ui/src/e2e/roles-settings.e2e.test.ts`, 8 tests):
  - the Team group and list counts
  - saving an edit sends one `config.patch` with the loaded hash and `replacePaths`
  - a role with no permissions can't be saved
  - an unsaved draft is dropped when another role opens
  - assigning a person sends `users.setRole`
  - creating a role from a preset, with name validation
  - the Remote access role link points to `/settings/roles?role=…`
  - non-administrators get no Team group
- **Unit tests** (`role-catalog.test.ts`): the patches applied with the Gateway's own merge-patch, including removals, array replacement, conflict refusal, delete with mapping repoint, and default-role rules.
- **Existing tests still pass:** participation (`session-participation`, scheduled tool allowlist) and `openclaw-id-access` browser tests.
- **Local checks:** `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, `ui:i18n:verify` with an updated raw-copy baseline, stylelint, `check:control-ui-controllers`, and oxlint on touched files all pass.
- **Assertion-safety ratchet:** still exits non-zero, but only for `src/agents/agent-tools.read.ts`, which this branch doesn't touch (inherited from the base).
- **Studio Crabbox run:** results to follow in a comment.
- **Independent review:** found 1 P1 and 2 P2 issues, all fixed with a regression test:
  - deleting while the people list wasn't loaded skipped reassignment
  - an unsaved draft could follow navigation to another role
  - assertions without a safety justification

## What Problem This Solves

The isolated Gateway E2E still expects a child result to be marked failed when Slack policy suppresses the reply, or ambiguous when Discord accepts the reply but omits its identity. After #204178 and #204260, those statuses no longer describe child-result settlement. The stale expectations also fail on unrelated PRs and block the channel test gate for #204428.

No runtime change. CI still proves which messages reached each channel independently of the child settlement record.

- Slack: require settled child results in both cases; verify the cancellation hook ran, the suppressed marker never went over the wire, and the control case arrived exactly once.
- Discord: require that the child result was consumed and settled, that the transport queue recorded `unknown_after_send`, and that the platform accepted exactly one marker message despite returning no delivery identity. The queue and child observations need not happen in the same poll.

prs.title: fix(ci): read refit job logs concurrently
prs.body:
## Problem
`ci-test-timings-refit.yml` (daily, `timeout-minutes: 30`) was cancelled at 30 min on 11-18, 11-22 and 11-23 (#204374). The `Refit measured test timings` step reads every timing job log through a synchronous `gh` child, one log at a time (about 1.5 s each on a runner).

The input grew because of full-release-validation CI dispatches (the `packed-release` source). Each one has about 180 timing jobs per attempt, and the refit reads every retry attempt. On 11-23 the step read 1126 logs: run 45111769646 alone had 3 attempts and 427 logs, and runs 45119345310 and 45122276316 added 180 and 162. Green days read about 450-500 logs (11-20: 497 logs in 742 s).

## Fix
`readGh` now uses `execPlainGhAsync`, the async form of the same transport. That owner bounds concurrent `gh` children at 4. The logs for one run attempt are read with `Promise.all` and keep their order. The run selection, validation and the timeout do not change. A child timeout still gets the three existing retries: the async transport reports it as `code: ETIMEDOUT`, so the retry check now reads the error code as well as the message.

## Evidence
- The same 10 compact job logs: sequential 24.9 s, concurrent 7.3 s, identical bytes (5,514,586).
- A full local `pnpm ci:timings:refit -- --dry-run` over the live 7-day window completes (exit 0, 1225 logs, sampled-run summary written).
- `pnpm check:changed`: script typecheck, lint and format pass. The only failure is the Knip dead-export scan, which flags `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/access-program.ts` and `src/sessions/owed.ts`; this PR does not touch them.

## Not in this PR
- 11-17 failure: a transient `stream ID 1; CANCEL` from `gh api` during job pagination.
- 11-21 failure: `Validate refit planner admission` refused the refit (`compact hybrid node test plan exceeds 77 jobs (144 planned)`). The gate worked as intended; whether a current refit still trips it shows once the refit completes in time.

prs.title: fix: check compaction timing and request budgets in tool-loop tests
prs.body:
Closes #204449

## What Problem This Solves

Main already contains #204443, which fixed the obsolete 800,000-token ceiling. The remaining gap is regression coverage: that derived maximum does not independently require compaction at the first 85% threshold crossing, and its request-window guard covers only the Responses tool-loop case, with a fallback output allowance.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible behavior change. This test-only follow-up gives developers independent compaction-timing and full request-budget checks. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compared with main containing #204443, this PR adds two distinct checks:

- **First 85% crossing:** every ordinary request before the first summary stays below 85%; the summary's input, excluding its added instruction, reaches that threshold. The expected threshold is independent of the production helper, so early compaction cannot pass just because the helper changed too.
- **Input plus output budgets:** every recorded request in both the Responses and completions cases fits its model window using its actual serialized output allowance. The allowance must be present and positive; requests are captured before rejection so unsafe requests cannot disappear from the assertions.

The warm-prefix, 429 retry, timed-out-summary recovery, persisted-compaction, and next-turn checks remain intact. The derived maximum-prompt calculation is replaced, not duplicated. No production code or new code comments are added.

## Evidence

Comparison: main `8bc8109271dd91aa33bd425503cb829082730fc4` → head `98791e46b8af0d08b1067f6725ad107650a27d38`.

- The complete PR diff is **one existing test file, +36/-42**; production delta **0**.
- Main was integrated with [merge commit `283bd183c244`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/283bd183c2441e2a02352b929b9a10bb031efee0), preserving published history and the requested co-author credit.
- Ran **pr-simplify**, then the changed test **once**: **2/2 passed**, 54.06 seconds command wall time (11.90 seconds test time). Focused lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` also passed.
- The integration test exercises real reply/session/attempt owners, file-read tools, stored transcripts, and HTTP request serialization against a deterministic local provider.
- [CI passed on this exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45349243915/job/138294319084): every selected CI lane succeeded and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. The completed watcher reconciled all 105 check/status entries: 37 passed, 68 skipped/neutral, none pending or failing. No main-failure exception was needed; skipped checks are not execution proof.

prs.title: improve: finish Template setup sooner and say what is being set up
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After you add a Template, the new agent greets you and then goes quiet for a long time. In that silence it reads its manifest, lists existing automations, plans and creates each declared automation, and looks up each plugin, with one model round trip per step. Across five ClawHub Templates the agent took a median of 34 seconds after Add to finish, and the longest stretch with nothing new on screen was about 13 seconds.

## User Impact

User impact: a new Template agent finishes setting itself up sooner and tells you what it is doing while it works. The greeting now says what is being set up, and the automation and plugin cards follow in one step.

Automations are still created by the agent, paused, in the adding device's time zone. Plugins are still only offered on a card. Nothing is installed or enabled that was not before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway already verified the Template's manifest during Add, so it now hands the first turn what the manifest declares: the automations as ready `plan` and `add` calls, and each referenced plugin with its current state. The agent no longer reads `CLAW.md` or looks plugins up one at a time.

The step that listed existing automations and skipped matching ones is removed. The scheduler already keeps an automation the setup conversation owns and returns it unchanged, so a retried setup cannot duplicate or rewrite one, and the Gateway still checks the scheduler for every required automation before it marks setup complete.

A setup receipt saved before this change, or a manifest with more than 24 automations or 20 plugin references, falls back to reading `CLAW.md` once. When the Gateway cannot report plugin states, the agent looks each referenced plugin up by name, all in one step.

## Evidence

Each Template was added through the real Control UI on an isolated Gateway with a real model, back to back on both builds, alternating which went first. "Agent finished" means the installer had responded, no agent run was open, and nothing had changed for 20 seconds.

Measured against current `main` (`86fcb81e64c0`) with this branch at `980d5ef97327`; the later commit only merges `main`. 30 of 30 installs passed. Values are medians of three runs.

| Template | Add → agent finished | Longest silence after first reply | Model requests | Add → first reply |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Engineering Partner | 39.7 → 20.7 s | 15.5 → 6.6 s | 10 → 3 | 10.2 → 10.0 s |
| Meta Ads Agent | 44.3 → 28.1 s | 16.5 → 6.2 s | 10 → 4 | 10.1 → 10.6 s |
| Gaming Companion | 32.7 → 17.7 s | 12.9 → 5.1 s | 7 → 3 | 9.9 → 10.2 s |
| Discord Signal Radar | 34.7 → 32.3 s | 18.8 → 8.9 s | 6 → 4 | 11.8 → 11.4 s |
| Hopper | 43.4 → 42.7 s | 17.5 → 25.2 s | 5 → 2 | 10.0 → 11.7 s |
| All five | 41.9 → 28.1 s | 16.5 → 7.3 s | 7 → 3 | 10.1 → 10.6 s |

Every declared automation was saved paused in every run, and each referenced plugin was offered on a card.

Three results did not improve. Discord Signal Radar finishes at about the same time: its own first-run script has the agent record the new automation ids in a workspace file, which adds steps this message does not control. Hopper is dominated by its bundled plugin's dependency install, which takes about 28 seconds; the agent now finishes its part sooner and then waits, so its longest silence is longer. Time to the first reply is unchanged at about 10 seconds.

An earlier comparison against the previous day's `main` (`930a6e02e123`), before this branch was rebased, gave the same picture: Add → agent finished went from 33.7 to 23.0 seconds across the five Templates, and model requests from 7 to 3.

Checked locally: the setup message tests cover the inlined calls, the device time zone, plugin states, a manifest with more plugin references than the message names, and the fallback. The chat Add integration test strips the new fields from a saved setup receipt, as one written by an older Gateway would be, and confirms the retry still loads it and reads the manifest instead. The chat Add integration tests pass except `starts live setup while a declared skill install is still pending`, which also fails on unmodified `main` on this machine and passes in CI. `pnpm check:changed` passes apart from the dead-export scan, which currently fails on `main` for unrelated files.

### Saved setup receipts from earlier versions

This change adds one optional field, `declared`, to the setup receipt a Template Add saves on the agent's main session. It changes no config schema, session-store migration or scheduler storage.

Which versions can have saved a receipt, checked against the release tags:

- `v2026.11.7`, the latest stable release, has no setup receipt at all; nothing in that tree reads or writes `templateSetup`. Upgrading from it leaves no receipt to retry.
- `v2026.11.10-beta.1` to `beta.3` save a receipt without `declared` and without `requiredAutomationIds`, which `main` added on November 23.
- `main` before this change saves a receipt with `requiredAutomationIds` and without `declared`.

The chat Add integration test covers the oldest of those shapes: it saves a receipt through the real session store, removes both `requiredAutomationIds` and `declared` from the stored entry, and retries. The retry loads the receipt, and the opening message reads `CLAW.md` instead of using inlined declarations.

### Upgrade from the latest stable release

One state directory was started on the published `openclaw@2026.11.7` package (`e31bbf056de3`), then on this branch's head (`14d5c73c6c95`). The Gateway was isolated and disposable, with a real model. The run was done three times; the table is the third.

On stable, a setting was written with `openclaw config set`, the main agent took a real turn in which it wrote a file to its workspace, and a disabled automation was added. The Gateway was stopped and the same state was started on this branch.

| After starting this branch on the stable state | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Settings | All 43 keys unchanged; startup added 13 new keys (migration markers, the `main` agent entry, four skill entries, setup bookkeeping) |
| Setting written on stable | Read back unchanged |
| Session | Same session key and id; 18 stored transcript events before the upgrade, 24 after one more turn |
| Conversation | A new turn in the same conversation recalled the exact reply it gave on stable |
| Workspace | All 6 files byte-identical, including the file the agent wrote |
| Automation added on stable | Unchanged: same id, schedule, time zone, still disabled |
| Stored rows | No table lost rows except the Gateway's own restart marker (2 → 1) |
| Template Add (Meta Ads Agent, real Control UI) | Agent created; its automation saved paused; plugin card shown; setup finished |

One difference came from the upgrade itself, not from this change: the Gateway's built-in "Memory Dreaming Promotion" job gained an explicit time zone in its schedule.

Template Add on the upgraded state:

![Meta Ads Agent added on a Gateway upgraded from stable](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b05259f-c5c4-420e-bc3d-e212bb0fb08b)

The first of the three runs is recorded as failed. Its upgrade and Template Add went the same way; my own check compared the built-in job's schedule and the restart-marker row count too strictly, and I narrowed both checks to the user's data before the second run.

The `check-lint-core-3` failure on `980d5ef97327` was a lint error in `src/config/sessions/session-transcript-reconcile.close-failure.test-support.mjs` on `main`, fixed there by #204397 and picked up by the merge.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep a Home press scrolling to older chat history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On WebKit, a reader who pressed **Home** in a long chat could stop thousands of pixels below the top, and older history never loaded. `chat-history-reading-stability.e2e.test.ts` (webkit, 390 px) failed on about half of the scheduled `main` runs with `messageCount: 30` (older history was never requested).

## Why

Reproduced on Linux WebKit (CI's engine) in a `node:24-bookworm` container with a timeline probe:

1. The Home keydown sets the transcript's native-input flag.
2. WebKit starts the keyboard scroll a frame later. In between, the **previous** movement's idle signal (the initial end placement's idle timer or `scrollend`) arrived and cleared that flag.
3. During the smooth scroll, rows above the reader measured taller (+255 to +330 px). With the flag cleared, `TranscriptReaderAnchor` did not hold the correction; it wrote `scrollTo` at once.
4. That write cancelled WebKit's smooth scroll. The reader stopped at 3,602 or 9,402 px, far above the 1,200 px prefetch edge. A programmatic scroll is not reader intent, so the history observer was never armed.

On passing runs the Home scroll landed later as one instant jump, so no correction landed mid-animation. The order depended on main-thread timing, which is why the test failed only on some runs.

## Change

`observeTranscriptOffset` (`chat-transcript-offset-observer.ts`): a scroll input's native-input flag now ends only after that input's own scrolling goes idle. An idle signal that arrives before the input has produced a scroll event no longer ends it. Programmatic writes still clear the flag as before.

## Evidence

- New test in `chat-transcript-offset-observer.test.ts`: a pending idle from the previous scroll fires after a Home keydown. Red on `main` (`expected false to be true`), green here. The existing wheel → `scrollend` case now includes the scroll event that real browsers send before `scrollend`.
- Tests that import the offset observer or the reader anchor, plus `chat-transcript-scroll-ownership.test.tsx`: 165 passed.
- Linux WebKit e2e, `chat-history-reading-stability` (webkit, 390 px):
  - before: 5 `messageCount` failures in 30 runs at 8e248ca731 (2/8, 1/10, 2/12);
  - this branch: 0 failures in 16 runs (the frame-stability check also passed in all 16).

prs.title: fix: keep provider handoff symbol equal across bundled copies
prs.body:
Closes #204386

## What Problem This Solves

In published builds, native video sent to Gemini never reaches the provider. The handoff that carries provider-only context is set under one copy of a symbol, but the bundled provider transport looks it up under a second copy created in a different chunk. The lookup always misses, so the model only receives an omission line and replies that it could not watch the video.

## User Impact

Native video input to supported provider models works in published builds again. The fix is a stable identity for the handoff key; no behavior changes for source/dev runs, images, or other provider context.

## Why This Change Was Made

`PROVIDER_CONTEXT_HANDOFF` was created with `Symbol(...)`, so two independently bundled copies were never equal. Registering it with `Symbol.for("openclaw.providerContextHandoff")` makes every copy resolve to the same key, matching how the handoff is set and read across chunk boundaries. Only this symbol is changed; other provider symbols were not reported as duplicated.

## Evidence

The focused `packages/ai/src/provider-types.test.ts` suite passes 4/4 with the fix (Node v24.22.1, worktree-local dependencies). Reverting only `provider-types.ts` produced 2 failures: the global-registration assertion and a test that sets the handoff from a separately evaluated module copy. The latter directly models the published-build scenario.

Targeted typecheck of the changed file reported no errors in it; the workspace `tsgo` run failed only on pre-existing missing generated UI locale modules in this local `--ignore-scripts` install. No live Gemini request was made locally.

## AI assistance

This fix and its tests were prepared with AI assistance and reviewed locally before submission.

prs.title: fix: Gemini receives attached videos again on installed builds
prs.body:
Root cause: src/plugin-sdk/llm.ts:2 re-exported `resolveProviderContext` from the relative source path `../../packages/ai/src/provider-types.js`, so the root build inlined its own `PROVIDER_CONTEXT_HANDOFF = Symbol("providerContextHandoff")` into `dist/llm-*.mjs`, while the embedded runner sets the handoff under the symbol from the external `@openclaw/ai/provider-types` package; the Google transport's lookup always misses and falls back to the video-less context.

Fixes #204386

Thanks @withlightsg for the report and for tracing it to the two symbol definitions in the published `dist/`.

## What Problem This Solves

On installed (npm) builds, a video sent to a Gemini model that supports native video (for example `google/gemini-4-neon` on AI Studio with `tools.media.video.enabled: false`) never reaches the model. The request only carries `(video omitted: provider does not support native video)`, and the model says it cannot see the video. Source and dev runs were not affected.

## User Impact

User impact: Gemini models on AI Studio receive attached videos as inline `video/mp4` parts again on packaged installs. Images, models without native video, and video understanding requests behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root build keeps `@openclaw/ai` external, so importing through the package specifier shares the one symbol that `@openclaw/ai` defines. The relative source path got around that rule and bundled a second copy. The SDK now imports the resolver and its types from `@openclaw/ai/provider-types`, the module the runner already uses. No new export; `Symbol.for` was not needed because the duplicate module copy itself is gone.

The other three symbols in that module (`PROVIDER_MODEL_INPUT`, `PROVIDER_DEFERRED_TOOL_NAMES`, `NATIVE_HISTORICAL_TOOL_CALL`) were never inlined in the root runtime chunks; the new test checks all four.

## Evidence

Packed build of base (80180388d0) and this branch, installed with `npm install -g` in a clean node:24 container. The Google provider pointed at the official AI Studio URL, routed to a local HTTPS stand-in that records each request body. Each case sent with `chat.send`, reply read back with `chat.history`.

| Case | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| mp4 to gemini-4-neon (video understanding off), twice | omission text only, no video part | inline `video/mp4` part; stand-in reply delivered |
| png to gemini-4-neon | inline `image/png` | same |
| mp4 to gemma-4-neon (no native video) | omission text | same |
| mp4 with `tools.media.video.enabled: true` | describe request carries the clip; reply request has omission text | describe request unchanged; reply request now also carries the clip |
| `Symbol("providerContextHandoff")` definitions in the installed package | 2 (`dist/llm-*.mjs`, `@openclaw/ai`) | 1 (`@openclaw/ai`) |

The last behavior row matches what source runs already do; there is no rule that drops a described video from the reply model's input.

`test/scripts/plugin-sdk-llm-bundle.test.ts` builds `plugin-sdk/llm` with the real root build config and fails if the output defines any provider-types symbol: fails on main, passes here. Source-level tests cannot catch this because both import paths resolve to the same module there.

Observed proof lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204415#issuecomment-7123022656

Production delta: +2 / -2 (one file). Test delta: +50 (one new regression file).

Merge danger: two-way door. Import path change only; a revert fully restores the previous bundle. Blast radius: plugins using `resolveProviderContext` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/llm` (Google, Moonshot) now see the runner's handoff on packaged builds.

prs.title: fix(plugin-sdk): let API comparison resolve runtime-only imports
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Plugin SDK API comparison fails when a declaration retains a bare import of a JavaScript runtime initializer. TypeScript resolves the file, but the comparison mistakes its absence from the type graph for a missing dependency.

## User Impact

Release operators can compare the SDK across the affected revisions without removing runtime initialization or overlooking genuinely missing imports. No public SDK or runtime behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the compiler's existing module-resolution result only for bare imports. A resolved JavaScript file outside the type graph contributes no declarations; unresolved imports still fail, and typed imports remain part of the closure. The small in-place change adds no resolver, state, or compatibility layer. The two regression cases protect the distinct resolved-runtime and genuinely-missing boundaries.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original failure through `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:diff` with frozen comparison `3d2d379bf65e` to `6cb8b271be3f`; the same comparison exits 0 with this fix.
- Regression red before the fix and green afterward; 24 baseline tests and 11 CLI tests pass.
- SDK test-shard typecheck, focused lint/format, and an uncached standalone declaration build pass.
- Self-review and simplification pass retained the two-file, 34-line fix; no public surface budget or production initialization was changed.

Remote checks and release qualification remain pending. The release API comparison uses trusted workflow tooling, so a subsequent qualification must select a trusted tooling revision containing this fix.

## Worked on by

- @RomneyDa

prs.title: test(cache): compare Responses prefixes through one envelope projection
prs.body:
## Result

The scheduled live job "Verify live agent prompt prefix reuse" passes again. It has failed on every scheduled run since 2026-11-17, while the real OpenAI cache held: after a reopen, the uncached tokens are the same as before #200163.

## Cause

#200163 (1fa849ce) stopped sending reasoning item IDs next to encrypted reasoning on cold replay, to fix `item_conflict`. A warm continuation still inherits the stored output items, IDs included. So across a reopen, history item 2 changes from `{id, type, summary, encrypted_content}` to `{type, summary, encrypted_content}`. The live gate reported exactly this on every run since 11-17:

```
openai release turn 4: prefix changed segment=history[2] path=$.keys[2]   ("id" -> "summary")
```

IDs render no model tokens. #200163 changed the transport unit test to ignore reasoning envelopes, but the release gate (`embedded-agent-runner.cache.test-support.ts`) kept its own copy of the rule that ignored only function-call and assistant-message envelopes. Three tests had three copies of the rule, and they diverged.

## Change

- `omitResponsesReplayEnvelopes` in `scripts/e2e/lib/anthropic-cache/prefix-stability.mts`, the owner of prefix snapshots, is now the one definition of token-free Responses envelopes: `id` and `status` on function calls, reasoning items and assistant messages.
- The release gate, the transport history-prefix test and the cold-prefix test all use it. Their local copies are deleted.
- No production code changes. The wire shape from #200163 stays, so its `item_conflict` fix is untouched.

## Evidence

Real OpenAI API (`gpt-5.6-luna`), the release prompt-prefix scenario: 3 warm turns, then a reopen on turn 4, 3 requests per turn. Per-request usage comes from the scenario's own cache diagnostics:

| Request | Base `89d07fe5` (parent of #200163): cacheRead / prompt, uncached | `main` b4cc3bc1, gate ignoring reasoning IDs: cacheRead / prompt, uncached |
|---|---|---|
| turn 3 #7 | 96,709 / 97,116, **407** | 96,587 / 96,994, **407** |
| turn 3 #8 | 96,881 / 104,554, 7,673 | 96,759 / 104,431, 7,672 |
| turn 3 #9 | 104,551 / 111,983, 7,432 | 104,428 / 111,860, 7,432 |
| **turn 4 (reopen) #10** | 111,980 / 112,191, **211** | 111,857 / 112,068, **211** |
| turn 4 #11 | 112,152 / 119,629, 7,477 | 112,029 / 119,506, 7,477 |
| turn 4 #12 | 119,626 / 127,058, 7,432 | 119,503 / 126,935, 7,432 |

The reopen request reuses the whole previous prompt in both arms, so the retry prefix is fully cached. The scenario's own check (each request reuses at least 80% of the preceding prompt) passes in both arms.

- The same scenario with the unchanged gate on `main` fails locally with the CI signature. On this head it passes (OpenAI).
- `anthropic-cache-prefix-stability.test.ts`: a new case checks that a warm continuation and its cold replay give equal snapshots, and that changed ciphertext still fails at `history[1]`. 11 passed. `openai-responses-client.history-prefix.test.ts` 8 passed, `embedded-agent-runner.responses-cold-prefix.test.ts` 10 passed.
- A dispatch of the scheduled live workflow on this branch is linked below when it completes.
