prs.title: fix(openai): offer only the speed tiers an API key's account advertises
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On team.openclaw.ai (API-key route, Team project), a chat on `openai/gpt-6-cyber` with Speed set to Ultrafast logged `rejected ultrafast tier; retrying with priority` on every turn, while the effort/speed popover kept offering Ultrafast. Speed tiers were the last per-model option in that popover not derived from what the model actually supports.

## User Impact

API-key chats offer only the speed tiers the account can use for that model. GPT-6 Cyber shows no Speed row, and a saved Ultrafast preference stops paying a rejection and retry on every turn.

## Root cause

For OpenAI API keys, the Gateway's `models.list` projection always published `serviceTiers: ["priority", "ultrafast"]` for every model on the Platform Responses route (`models-list-public-projection.ts`), so the Control UI offered both for every model. The account already says otherwise: the Codex model listing that OpenClaw fetches with the same API key for Daybreak access programs carries a `service_tiers` list per model — the list Codex itself uses to decide which tier to send (`ModelInfo::service_tier_for_request`). OpenClaw read only `available_access_programs` from those rows.

Live check on 2026-11-23 with a Platform key that has GPT-6 Cyber access:

| Model | Account `service_tiers` | `service_tier: "ultrafast"` | `service_tier: "priority"` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| gpt-6-cyber (Red) | `[]` | 400 `Invalid service_tier argument` | 200, **served `default`** |
| gpt-6-sol | `["priority"]` | — | — |
| gpt-6.2-sol | `["priority", "ultrafast"]` | 200, served `ultrafast` | — |

So the advertisement is accurate; the Gateway just ignored it on the API-key route. The "retry at priority" recovery also bought nothing for GPT-6 Cyber: priority is served as default.

## Change

- **Owner: the OpenAI plugin's Platform discovery.** `discoverOpenAIPlatformModelCapabilities` reads `service_tiers` from the same rows (no extra request) and publishes `modelServiceTiers` for the Platform API-key route and the embedded `openclaw` runtime, next to the existing `modelAccessPrograms`. Only listed models are kept, as before.
- **Consumer: the `models.list` projection.** On the API-key route it now uses the selected credential's advertised tiers (profile or configured key, matched by account/model/route like access programs). When the listing is missing, failed or pending, it keeps today's default of every tier. The UI is unchanged: it already shows Standard only for a recoverable route without Fast/Ultrafast, and hides Ultrafast when only Fast is advertised.
- **Runtime: a rejected tier is remembered per account/model route, not per run.** The existing cooldown (two Ultrafast rejections → Fast for 10 min / 20 requests, then probe) was keyed by run, so a chat with a saved Ultrafast preference paid the 400 again on every turn. It is now keyed by account/model route across runs, bounded to 256 routes, and in memory only.

The shared cooldown key includes the agent's auth store (agentDir) as well as the credential identity, because profile ids are per store: two agents holding different keys under the same profile id never share a cooldown (Codex/ClawSweeper P2 on fc8da94b).

Accepted edge case: a configured key replaced in place keeps the same `direct:openai` route identity, so it can inherit a cooldown for at most 10 minutes / 20 requests before the next probe.

Not in this PR: making the runtime cap requests to the advertised tiers (Codex parity) so a saved Ultrafast never reaches the wire. That needs the attempt-time account-capability reader that #204325 is reshaping for access programs, and should reuse it once that lands.

## Evidence

- Regression (red on `main`, green here): `models-list-result.service-tiers.test.ts` › "offers profile/direct API keys only the tiers their account advertises for each model" — `[]` and `["priority"]` rows project as advertised, an unlisted model keeps the default, and another account's listing is not borrowed. On `main` both cases get `["priority", "ultrafast"]`.
- Regression (red on `main`, green here): `openai-service-tier-observation.test.ts` › a later run on the same account/model route goes straight to `priority`; another account still probes Ultrafast.
- Regression (red without the scope key, green with it): the same test › the same profile id under another agent's auth store probes Ultrafast again instead of inheriting the cooldown.
- Plugin: `platform-access-programs.test.ts` asserts the Platform rows publish `modelServiceTiers` from the same request (fetch count unchanged).
- `pnpm check:changed` green; touched suites green: `models-list-result.service-tiers`, `model-catalog-service-tiers`, `platform-access-programs`, `model-access-programs`, `openai-provider.codex-catalog`, `openai-api-key-catalog`, `provider-fast-mode`, `openai-model-discovery-auth-order`, `openai-service-tier-observation`.

### Popover (mocked Control UI, synthetic data)

GPT-6 Cyber chat with a saved Ultrafast preference. Before = the row `main`'s Gateway publishes for an API key (`serviceTiers: ["priority","ultrafast"]`); after = the row this branch publishes from the account listing (`serviceTiers: []`). The Control UI code is identical on both sides; captured with the Control UI e2e harness at 1280×820.

#### Clean comparison

**Before** — Speed row offers Standard, Fast and Ultrafast; the saved Ultrafast is selected and the trigger shows the Ultrafast badge.

![Before: GPT-6 Cyber popover offers Standard, Fast and Ultrafast with Ultrafast selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94543eeb-9a9d-40ee-b166-8060db78d9e8)

**After** — no Speed row; the trigger shows only the effort level.

![After: GPT-6 Cyber popover shows Daybreak and Effort only, no Speed row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1a3556f4-d208-466d-adb9-9c6089b5f1bd)

#### Annotated comparison

**Before**

![Before, annotated: the Ultrafast option is outlined as offered although the API rejects it](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e56bb681-22f6-4cd6-aba7-598f5d88382d)

**After**

![After, annotated: the popover is outlined, showing no speed tiers because the account advertises none](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6d4073b0-9470-41f9-8eab-2e0463e97f90)

## Docs

`docs/providers/openai/advanced.md`: API keys now offer only the account-advertised tiers; the rejection cooldown spans later turns and runs on the same account/model route.

prs.title: fix: stop status checks from rolling back healthy legacy Git installs
prs.body:
Closes #204192

## What Problem This Solves

Git installations retaining the launcher from development build `d44f263` can count `gateway status` as a Gateway start. Repeated status checks can exhaust an armed trial and roll back an otherwise healthy Gateway.

## User Impact

User impact: after the updated candidate performs post-ready maintenance, status checks through the affected legacy launcher no longer consume trial attempts. Admitted `openclaw update repair` also refreshes that launcher. Genuine-start rollback remains available; this does not settle an unresolved trial or repair unrelated update failures. Custom, resident, other-installation, and read-only launchers remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both entry points share one narrowly scoped repair that recognizes the exact legacy launcher bytes in the selected, account-owned installation. It reuses the existing legacy launcher writer rather than introducing another trial owner or switching a phase-less trial to the resident protocol. The next normal release update installs the resident launcher.

## Evidence

- Fresh focused proof on Linux / Node 24.20.0: 158 tests passed across seven files, with no failures or skips. Coverage includes status checks leaving trial bytes and release selection unchanged, genuine-start rollback, CLI repair admission, and excluded launcher scopes. The maintained runner completed in 189.73 seconds with one worker per shard; CI timings are not yet available.
- Targeted format check passed for eight supported files; lint passed for seven TypeScript files with no warnings or errors. Core production and the gateway-server, cli-update, and other core-test typecheck graphs passed. `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh `pr-simplify` inspection retained the existing shared repair and fixture. Supported base reconciliation resolved one additive documentation conflict while preserving both notes; the eight implementation/test/fixture files remain byte-identical to the pinned patch. Fresh bound Auto Review (OpenClaw engine, P0-only) reviewed the local nine-file candidate against `86fcb81e64c02b29e64892ed8549a639ecd6dc0d` and reported no P0 findings. This is not a claim of broader-priority review.
- Dan (@daniel-lxs) reports that this patch passed its own pinned-`d44f263` Git upgrade lane and his combined run. Those real-VM results are reporter-provided evidence, not an independently observed run by this worker.

The earlier full canonical `pnpm build` (including declarations) and package-integrity check passed on commit `87fdaac718323e350243dcb520c913971e1e9e18`, whose full source tree exactly matches the pinned recreation `2767f4613086d62d4fbe3567645480ebf9f1b5ad`. That is prior pinned-source evidence, not a fresh build. Publication required reconciliation with the current base, so the refreshed whole tree is different: its full build, exact-head PR CI, and cross-platform upgrades remain unrun. No stable-release or universal upgrade claim is made. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; local autoreview was P0-only, with normal hosted review and CI still applicable.

Contributor credit: @daniel-lxs reported and reproduced the issue and supplied the pinned-Git validation; the commit preserves his co-author credit.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @daniel-lxs](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-t_scdvyj)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/e33ad202-0f23-40fa-beb2-7329f01ee7e0)

## Worked on by

- @daniel-lxs

prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body:
## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Before this change, persistent OpenClaw agents were externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation custody store** in the per-agent database persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts, and hands each delegate off to the subagent run registry before spawn (RFC `docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md` §5.4). The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **Durable custody**: delegates and their replay state live in the continuation custody store, with one transactional authority for replacement and a pre-spawn handoff to `subagent_runs` (upstream has removed the Tasks/TaskFlow runtime, #159179) - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → custody record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially host Cron plus / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A tool adapter over durable flow records is also not a lifecycle host, and upstream has since removed the Tasks/TaskFlow runtime (#159179) that such an adapter would have called. Marking a stored record as running neither reacquires a session lane nor invokes the model; continuation needs the turn machinery itself to own which session runs next, how child results return, and what survives finalization. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. prs.title: fix(cli): reject non-decimal tool usage limits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The tool-usage CLI accepted hexadecimal and exponent notation as bounded integers, so inputs such as `0x10` and `1e1` could silently select a range even though these options are documented as integer day/count values.

## User Impact

Decimal integer values within the existing bounds continue to work, while non-decimal, fractional, zero, and out-of-range values are rejected before any Gateway request is made.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both `tools usage import --since` and `tools usage status --limit` now use the shared strict positive-integer parser. The parser stays private to the CLI owner, the help text keeps plain ASCII ranges, and the two tracked CLI files are stored as LF again so the diff only contains the behavior change.

## Evidence

At head `a6927a4ffc072bb42c151e41e9b4d0904a551df8`, the shipped CLI rejects non-decimal arguments before any Gateway request, and a valid decimal value still reaches the transport stage.

Real CLI transcript from `node scripts/run-node.mjs` (the build reports `OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (a6927a4)`), isolated config and state directory, no Gateway running:

```text
$ openclaw tools usage import --since 0x10
OpenClaw could not parse this command: option '--since <days>' argument '0x10' is invalid. Expected an integer between 1 and 90.
Try: openclaw tools usage import --help
exit: 1

$ openclaw tools usage import --since 1e1
OpenClaw could not parse this command: option '--since <days>' argument '1e1' is invalid. Expected an integer between 1 and 90.
exit: 1

$ openclaw tools usage status --limit 0x10
OpenClaw could not parse this command: option '--limit <count>' argument '0x10' is invalid. Expected an integer between 1 and 100.
Try: openclaw tools usage status --help
exit: 1

$ openclaw tools usage import --since 14 --dry-run
gateway toolUsage.import requires credentials before opening a websocket
exit: 1

$ openclaw tools usage import --help
  --since <days>         Days of retained history (1-90) (default: 90)
exit: 0
```

The `--since 14` case fails at the Gateway credential check, which is after argument parsing, so decimal input is still accepted.

Focused regressions:

- Base `1a0a24dcd2c` with the fix reverted: `pnpm test src/cli/tools-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` reports `Tests 3 failed | 14 passed (17)`. The failures are `rejects invalid import days 0x10 before RPC`, `rejects invalid status limit 1e1 before RPC`, and `rejects invalid status limit 0x10 before RPC`.
- Head `a6927a4ffc07`: the same command reports `Tests 17 passed (17)`. The cases assert the rejection happens before the Gateway RPC is called.

Checks: `run-format.mts --check` passes on both files, and `git -c core.whitespace=cr-at-eol diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passes.

Boundary: the CLI transcript proves argument rejection and help text with an isolated config and no Gateway, not a successful admin import. The open question stays maintainer-owned: whether stricter rejection of hexadecimal and exponent notation is the wanted product behavior without a reported harmful outcome.

prs.title: fix: keep the session observer running when a small model copies the previous digest
prs.body:
Closes #203956

## What Problem This Solves

On 2026.11.6 the session observer disables itself for good ("returned invalid JSON twice") when the utility model is a small one such as `anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`. The answers are syntactically valid JSON, but the model copies a `revision` field out of the `previousDigest` block in the user payload, and the strict response schema rejects the whole digest. The status surface then stops updating for that run.

The trigger is any secondary digest: the prompt for the next observation contains the previous digest, so a model that mirrors the shape of its input has a field to copy.

## User Impact

User impact: the session observer keeps updating `/status` with small utility models instead of disabling itself after two rejected answers. The prompt now contains only the fields the answer is allowed to use.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildSessionObserverPrompt` stripped only `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` before serializing `previousDigest`, so `sessionKey`, `agentId`, `runId`, `revision`, and `updatedAt` were offered to the model as examples even though the response schema rejects them.

The fix is at the producer: the prompt now sends only the model-facing fields (`headline`, `assessment`, `health`, `planProgress`). The strict response schema is unchanged, so a model that invents fields still gets rejected rather than persisted.

## Evidence

An observation prompt no longer contains bookkeeping the response schema would reject.

- Baseline, `69ce03a3` (before the fix): the new test failed — the prompt carried all seven digest keys (`sessionKey`, `sessionId`, `lifecycleRevision`, `runId`, `revision`, `updatedAt`, plus `headline`/`assessment`/`health`), and the assertion reported `expected { …(7) } to deeply equal { headline: 'Checking files', …(2) }`.
- With the fix: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-observer-model.test.ts` → 14 passed.
- Adjacent observer tests: `src/gateway/session-observer-completion.test.ts` and `src/gateway/session-observer-persistence.test.ts` → 13 passed, including the invalid-schema failure path that disables observation.
- Prompt produced by the shipped builder for a digest carrying identity and bookkeeping fields:

```text
{"previousDigest":{"headline":"Checking the fix","assessment":"Tests are passing.","health":"on-track"},"newNotes":["ran pnpm test"],"planProgress":{"completed":2,"total":3}}
```

- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on both changed files: clean; `git diff --check`: clean.

Proof boundary: this proves the payload the observer sends, not a live Haiku completion — no utility-model call was made here, and the response validation path is covered by the existing tests rather than by a new live model run.

`src/gateway/server-templates-add-authority.e2e.test.ts` fails on `main` in all three cases (skill, plugin, ClawHub plugin). No scheduled CI lane runs this file, so the failure was not seen.

## What Problem This Solves

Refresh stale CI shard weights from successful jobs in completed scheduled main CI workflows, successful release-check runs, and exact compact selectors and tooling files from successful pull-request CI runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

The daily refit uses independent-run medians, rejects outliers and single samples, and keeps existing weights within the 15% replacement band. Failed main workflows contribute successful timing jobs without supplying pruning evidence. Pull-request measurements describe the merge-ref: exact compact selector keys, runtime inventory observations, and native tooling file costs can update, but partial plans never reprice unqualified compact parents or prune absent measurements. Worker timing identities must agree with observed admission. Main compact keys absent from every contributing run are removed only after three successful contributing workflows for that profile. The complete artifact report lists every change and removal.

## User Impact

Only shard balance changes; test discovery still determines the complete test inventory. This standing branch is updated automatically and never pushes to main.

## Evidence

prs.title: fix(docs): accept annotated front matter terminators in MDX checks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`docs:check-mdx` rejects valid Markdown/MDX pages when YAML front matter uses an annotated `--- # comment` or `... # comment` closing delimiter.

## User Impact

Docs checks now accept the same annotated front matter delimiters already supported by `docs:list`, so valid pages are not reported as malformed MDX.

## Why This Change Was Made

The MDX checker, publishing parser, and release mirror now use the established delimiter grammar: `---` or `...`, followed only by horizontal whitespace and an optional YAML comment. The matcher remains anchored, preserves source line numbering, and does not accept lookalike content.

## Evidence

- Final real behavior proof at exact head `1f29c6f2067d679f589e0ae5e1a4f714c51174b2`: the public MDX checker accepted LF `--- # end` and CRLF `... # end` fixtures and returned `Docs MDX check passed (2 files, 36ms)`.

  ```text
  command: node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mts <fixture-dir> --max-errors 5
  output: Docs MDX check passed (2 files, 36ms).
  ```

- Final release-mirror proof at the same head: `renderReleaseDocsMirror` generated both annotated LF and CRLF pages without `unterminated frontmatter`, producing `### Release title` and preserving `Exact prose.` for each.

  ```text
  LF: {"name":"LF","output":"### Release title\n\nExact prose.\n\n"}
  CRLF: {"name":"CRLF","output":"### Release title\n\nExact prose.\n\n"}
  ```

- Regression coverage exercises both annotated forms through the release mirror test, in addition to the existing public parser and MDX checker cases.
- Supporting checks: 30/30 focused parser and MDX checker tests passed; 3/3 annotated release-mirror tests passed; `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Proof boundary: this aligns front matter parsing across validation, publication, and release mirroring; it does not change published documentation content or Mintlify rendering.

### P2 follow-up on the publishing parser (head `ea74843`)

The maintainer finding asked for the publishing parser to accept the terminators the MDX checker already accepts, with regression proof for metadata/body boundaries, diagnostic line numbers, and rejected/unterminated delimiters. Covered now:

- `scripts/lib/docs-markdown.mjs`: `parseFrontmatter` closes on `---`/`...` with an optional trailing `# ...` comment, LF and CRLF, matching `scripts/check-docs-mdx.mts`.
- Public parser boundaries: metadata and body asserted for `--- # end` (LF) and `... # end` (CRLF) in `test/scripts/docs-markdown.test.ts`.
- Rejected/unterminated cases: unterminated frontmatter and `--- not a comment` stay unfrontmattered; a `---` line inside the body stays in content (same file).
- Real MDX CLI: both annotated fixtures pass through `scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs`, and original diagnostic line numbers are unchanged (`test/scripts/check-docs-mdx.test.ts`).
- Docs-sync closure: the release mirror renders a page with both annotated closers (`test/scripts/release-changelog.test.ts`, filtered run: 2 passed; that file's 2 Windows symlink/path-traversal cases also fail on `upstream/main` in this environment, so they are pre-existing and unrelated).
- Focused runs on this head: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/docs-markdown.test.ts test/scripts/check-docs-mdx.test.ts` -> 18 + 15 passed; `oxfmt --check` clean; oxlint 0 warnings / 0 errors; `git diff --check` clean.
- Proof boundary: docs pipeline contract only; no published content or Mintlify rendering change. The workflow run for this head is awaiting maintainer approval.

prs.title: improve(gateway): reduce redundant work when session rows refresh
prs.body:
Related: #204274

## What Problem This Solves

During bursts of session updates, the Gateway copies equal row facts, republishes transcript previews in two objects, and compares entire decoded entries even when a projected lineage key or common metadata already establishes a difference. This adds work to chat and session-list refreshes.

## User Impact

Reduces session-row lineage work during bursts of Gateway updates. The wire output and delivery order are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Row fact publication copies the frozen row on the first actual patch change and freezes changed nested values. The frozen row alone carries the transcript preview fields used for materialization, which lets transcript updates retain the source object. Lineage checks the projected keys before comparing the rest of the entry and keeps structural equality for distinct worker snapshots that may still represent the same facts.

The existing sparse builder preserves optional-field omission and property order. A dense candidate increased sampled allocation under full materialization by 47%, so the patch keeps the established construction and child-link reuse. The one-pass patch loop and early lineage decisions add 11 net production lines.

## Evidence

The regression assertions went red for equal patch identity, an unnecessary comparison on reparent, and a replacement source on a real transcript preview backfill. All 138 focused tests passed with the change. Codex autoreview found no actionable issues through P3.

The 15,000-session synthetic surge delivered the same 28,200 FIFO frames and the same ordered event and final-page digests across both arms. Lineage deep-equality samples fell from 1.23 to 0.34 ms per 1,000 events. Lineage allocation fell from 3.66 to 3.34 MB per 1,000 events in the median, with a decrease in all five pairs. Resident-read sampling was 72.24 → 71.00 ms and 18.14 → 18.27 MB per 1,000 events. The overall resident path was within baseline variation. Whole-replay main CPU was 1,658 → 1,690 ms per 1,000 events against A/A readings of 1,654 and 1,754. Event-loop p95 was 3.66 → 3.72 ms and p99 was 15.22 → 15.12 ms. Two candidate synchronous slices took 15.67 and 18.87 ms. A diagnostic repeat captured a 32.40 ms baseline spike in a prepared-read callback, with candidate maxima of 4.87 and 5.17 ms.

The 5,000-session mixed replay includes real transcript commits. Both fixture digests match. Sampled allocation moved from 402.84 to 400.98 MB per 1,000 operations. In the longer 3,000-operation timing series, p95 moved from 4.39 to 5.05 ms, compared with baseline controls of 6.44 and 6.03 ms. Mixed-replay CPU and tail differences varied by pair.

The production dead-export scan in `pnpm check:changed` reproduces on main for `prepareAttemptAccessPrograms`, introduced by #204325. The check is outside the changed Gateway owners.

CI scripts typecheck reproduces the same ten release-test diagnostics on exact main parent `d31463cca15f5`. The same check passes one commit before #204438, which introduced the test and contract changes. See [the exact-head CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45346678471/job/138284348306).

prs.title: fix: offer a new chat when OpenClaw runs out of memory loading a conversation
prs.body:
Related: #192839

## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw's storage worker runs out of memory while loading a large conversation, the chat says only "Couldn't finish this reply", offers **Refresh**, and the details advise reopening the conversation or restarting OpenClaw. Every one of those loads the same conversation again and hits the same out-of-memory failure, so the person is stuck in a loop with no hint of the real cause or a way out.

## User Impact

User impact: an out-of-memory failure now says what happened, that the last change may not have been saved, and that sending here will keep failing, and its primary action is **Start new chat**: a new conversation that never loads the failed one, with the unsent message waiting in its composer (not sent automatically). Every other storage or reply error keeps today's message and Refresh.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The worker OOM is classified before the generic "couldn't confirm" outcome, so it gets its own message. It stays a terminal, non-retryable failure: the uncertain write is never replayed by the client, the Gateway dedupe cache, or automatic continuation.
- The chat error event carries a new `storage_worker_memory` error kind. The Control UI uses it to swap Refresh for Start new chat. Other clients still get the full message as text.
- The new chat is created without a parent or current-session reference, so creating it does not touch the failed conversation. Keyboard focus moves to the new composer.
- The Gateway runs on Bun, where native worker errors inherit `code` from their prototype. The earlier classifier (#192839) only read own properties, so in a real Gateway this OOM still fell through to the generic message. The classifier now reads the inherited code without invoking accessors, and the tests use the Bun-shaped error.

Out of scope: bounding hydration so the OOM does not happen (RRI-658, #172970), and restoring unrelated read authority after an uncertain write (P0-2 of the same report).

## Evidence

Isolated Gateway (own state dir and port), real Control UI, a real model reply seeded in the conversation, and an OOM forced inside session-actor hydration for that conversation only (a temporary local patch, not in this PR). Before = `main` at `3091ba81dfce`; after = this branch. Both start from the same copied state.

**Light, 1280px**

![Before: the toast says "Couldn't finish this reply", offers Refresh, and the details say to reopen or restart](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28385f49-97c5-4614-9fae-6982cbddcee8)
![After: the toast says OpenClaw ran out of memory loading this conversation, offers Start new chat, and the details explain the unconfirmed save](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/87c0e904-641f-4386-bbba-d2b67c8f6a9e)

**Dark, 1280px**

![Before, dark theme: generic failure toast with Refresh](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48db9271-1eec-49e9-b5fc-631f6fda7f89)
![After, dark theme: out-of-memory toast with Start new chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05777679-0e03-427d-bb52-b929a936673b)

**Light, 420px**

![Before, narrow: generic failure toast with Refresh](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e00b9f7-bab9-4fc0-9ab5-de44253ca591)
![After, narrow: out-of-memory toast with Start new chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3e06cd4-fc39-4f81-ac90-f3a365751ef9)

**Annotated** (narrow: 1 summary, 2 action, 3 details)

![Before, annotated: 1 generic summary with no cause, 2 Refresh reloads the failed conversation, 3 the details advise reopen or restart, which repeat the failing load](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3bce97f3-43b2-4ff6-83d3-8199fca79843)
![After, annotated: 1 names the out-of-memory cause, 2 Start new chat opens a conversation that never loads the failed one, 3 the details say the save is unconfirmed, sending again fails even after a restart, and the operator should check memory](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/713e939f-7d96-42ca-9151-47939e266bb7)
![Before, narrow, annotated](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2517f8c4-bb61-4559-b743-515a31999519)
![After, narrow, annotated](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/589ce837-0991-4462-9640-992be435bfae)

**Next step after recovery:** the new chat opens with the unsent text in a focused composer, and sending it gets a real reply.

![After Start new chat: a new empty conversation with the unsent message in the composer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e379ac64-16bc-4fc1-a20c-83a63a0c97af)
![The carried message sent in the new chat and answered by the model](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d1e9b84b-5530-4b5b-8b30-e78bd062dd22)

Checked end to end in the after build (counts of `JS heap out of memory` in the Gateway log):

| Step | OOMs |
| --- | --- |
| Send in the failing conversation | +1 (expected) |
| Reload and read the failing conversation | +0 |
| Press Enter on **Start new chat** | +0; focus lands on the new composer, the draft is there, nothing is sent |
| Send in the new chat | +0; the model replies |

Tests (red on `main`, green here):
- `src/infra/sqlite-worker-contract.test.ts`: a Bun-shaped worker OOM under an unconfirmed write, and the session-actor fence that wraps it, classify as `storage-worker-memory` and stay non-replayable.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-dispatch-errors.test.ts`: `chat.send` responds `UNAVAILABLE`, `retryable: false`, `details.code: storage-worker-memory`, caches that refusal for dedupe, and broadcasts `errorKind: storage_worker_memory`.

Also green: UI notice and gateway-event tests, the session failure-row test, error-shape/stream/retry/cron/terminal-resolution consumers, `tsgo` core and UI, oxlint, format, `protocol:check`, `ui:i18n:verify`.

Known gaps:
- After a page reload, the conversation shows the saved failure row with the new text but no Start new chat button. Today the kind is not persisted on the lifecycle row; the regular New session button still works.
- macOS, iOS, and channel clients show the new text without a dedicated button.
- `src/agents/failover-error.test.ts` has 3 failures that also fail on `main` (auth/Gemini cases, unrelated).
- The OOM was forced in hydration. A real 80k-message heap exhaustion was not reproduced.

<details><summary>Reviews</summary>

- Copy review: tightened the long message and the toast description; kept "Start new chat".
- Design review: the new button now wraps on phones like Refresh, and focus moves to the new composer instead of being lost when the toast closes.
</details>

prs.title: feat(ios): filter sessions by attention and work
prs.body:
Related: #162814

## What Problem This Solves

On iPhone, finding conversations waiting for an answer or approval requires checking individual session rows.

## User Impact

Sessions gains All, Needs you, and Working filters with conversation counts for the selected Gateway, agent, and existing status scope. One conversation counts once even when it has multiple requests. Working includes active or queued runs and active child work; it can overlap Needs you. Request badges reuse the existing native preview and approval flow.

All preserves offline browsing. Live activity filters are disabled while disconnected, and incomplete rosters retain a + count qualifier.

This is a draft for the initial iOS design review. Physical Duo and VoiceOver checks remain before readiness. Android parity is a separate follow-up using the same filter meanings.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Sessions screen consumes the existing live roster instead of keeping a second nonarchived snapshot. The existing owners retain question/approval matching, expiry, navigation, grouping, mutations, and Gateway policy. No server, protocol, schema, permission, or persistent setting is added.

Android's native SessionsScreen already has the needed roster and attention/run-state contracts. This PR does not modify or claim validation of Android.

## Native Sessions proof with a real Gateway

Captured on the Mac Studio with an iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator running iOS 27.0. The comparison uses upstream `ed3230dd29d1` and published draft head `5c8b666d53e5`. Both apps used the same three fictional conversations from an isolated OpenClaw `2026.11.4` Gateway. The agent ran Qwen3 4B locally through llama.cpp. A test operator created and answered the ordinary question through the Gateway API, and the model generated the separate work turn.

### Clean comparison

| Upstream Sessions | Draft Sessions |
| --- | --- |
| ![Upstream Sessions shows three rows with no activity filter](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e28e8bf-83a1-4663-b9a6-20923b75021e) | ![Draft Sessions shows the same three rows, with All 3, Needs you 1, and Working 0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee20cc17-e197-439d-a1c0-984f26e77384) |

### Annotated comparison

| Upstream | Draft |
| --- | --- |
| ![The rows start immediately below the status scopes](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2e07899-2d29-4309-b46e-9541c2e72b3c) | ![Activity controls and counts appear between the status scopes and the rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad6e8492-764d-4e94-866c-2401e19d519e) |

### Live updates

| Needs you selected | Working selected | After both settle |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Needs you shows only Color review with a pending question](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e9f2873e-da2d-4a86-8442-6b27f3315369) | ![Working shows only Launch checklist during a real model run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd7b47fe-cea3-49e2-9fe2-3a98893e1d4e) | ![After the question and run settle, All stays at 3 and both activity counts are 0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad309f62-7f9f-45ce-af63-cf17e4183e86) |

The native Sessions screen stayed open during the transition. This trace records the visible filter values and the corresponding Gateway state.

```text
Pending question in Color review     All 3   Needs you 1   Working 0
Needs you selected                  Color review is the only row
Qwen starts on Launch checklist     All 3   Needs you 1   Working 1
Separate capture with Working open  Launch checklist is the only row while the model runs
Gateway accepts Fern                Question status: answered
Model finishes                      All 3   Needs you 0   Working 0
Gateway final state                 Launch checklist: done, no active run
```

The captured proof covers this simulator and the published Sessions screen. The broader design previews below are from separate work.

## November 17 draft update

Merged upstream `ed3230dd29d1` into the existing activity-filter branch. Resolved the four conflicts while retaining upstream session grouping, collapsed sections, and the partial-load retry. The Sessions clock now refreshes when the roster changes and continues to refresh when request or snooze deadlines expire.

Verified on the iOS 27.0 iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator at `5c8b666d53e5`:

- 19 focused Swift tests passed (3 activity logic and 16 typography).
- Both native Sessions flows passed against an isolated synthetic Gateway. The activity flow verified filter counts and live request/run updates. The recency regression verified that a planning row aged past “just now” when a different row changed, with no pending requests or snoozes.
- Native localization verification, SwiftFormat, app-target SwiftLint, and diff checks passed.

The layout images below are from the earlier design prototype. This draft is still asking for an iOS design decision on the focused activity filters.

## Layout prototype for design feedback

The latest local prototype puts a compact filter dropdown beside **Sessions** in the sidebar, with compact icon-and-count cards on the full Sessions screen. Both locations offer **All**, **Needs you**, and **Working**.

On the full Sessions screen, attention rows have one tappable hand or shield on the left. The hand means **Waiting for answer**; the shield means **Waiting for approval**. Both use amber status text and a subtle warning tint because both need a user response. Working rows and the Working card use informational blue. Text and distinct symbols convey the state as well as color. Status labels consistently use sentence case, including Recent, Working, Waiting for answer, and Waiting for approval. The existing native request previews remain available. The sidebar keeps its native attention badges and work indicators.

These images show eight fictional conversations: two waiting for an answer or approval, three working, and three idle. Each image compares **All / Needs you / Working**, with no before/after panels. They are native standard-iPhone simulator captures with synthetic Gateway state. No personal conversations, private Gateway addresses, or real agent tasks appear.

Feedback requested: does keeping the sidebar control beside Sessions make its scope clear? Do the compact cards and the attention-row styling feel clear without adding clutter? Feedback on wording, spacing, colors, and selection styling is welcome. Android parity remains a separate follow-up using the same filter meanings.

**Sessions screen: All / Needs you / Working**

![Latest local Sessions prototype with amber question and approval rows, blue Working states, and compact filter cards](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/04f3b1a7-059a-4c8e-80d0-7aa24a343e14)

**Sidebar: All / Needs you / Working**

![Latest local sidebar prototype with filtering beside the Sessions heading and fictional conversations](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49b52069-9ba1-41c3-b259-5b3b8bf28392)

These are design previews from uncommitted local refinements atop local prototype `4650e6cf067c249871fa7ee7871c466a450b6d01`. The sidebar placement, card styling, status-row cleanup, and adaptive scope control shown here have not been pushed to this draft's published head, `cbb83f9eff100aa5437f15c19c9c3383ee4657d4`. They are not exact-head merge proof. The PR remains a draft for design feedback.

Local refinement checks: 24 typography tests and four activity-owner logic tests pass, as do the native filter flows at standard and largest accessibility text sizes. The sole leading hand and shield were each tapped to verify that the correct native preview opens without leaving Sessions. Light and dark appearances were inspected. The latest local prototype, including sentence-case status labels, was installed and launched on the physical Duo as the separate OpenClaw Sessions build 10. The installed version was read back from the device. A fresh physical visual/interaction check of this revision and a full VoiceOver audit are still pending. The Evidence section below describes the earlier published implementation separately.

## Evidence

- Base: 42aab1ce38cdde59eaa3f2babc3eef488ea9db2c. The native baseline reaches All Sessions and fails because the activity filter is absent.
- Three focused native logic tests pass: distinct conversation counts, overlapping work/attention, terminal and explicit run-state precedence, resolution/expiry/agent matching, and offline/partial data. Test execution: 0.016 seconds; runner setup/execution: 20.805 seconds.
- Native iPhone UI flow passes with synthesized screen taps at rendered targets, selected-state and membership assertions, 44-point targets, and live count changes after run completion and question/approval resolution. Standard-size run: 53.400 seconds; largest system accessibility text: 47.326 seconds. The filters stack vertically at the largest size. Existing session-row text still elides at that size; this is not a full accessibility audit.
- XCTest AX hit-point lookup reports no hit point for the activity filters and existing status picker on this simulator. The test explicitly synthesizes screen touches rather than relying on AX activation, then checks the resulting state. VoiceOver is not covered by this result.
- 23 focused typography tests pass. Targeted SwiftLint/SwiftFormat, Node syntax, native i18n verification, docs formatting/MDX, link audit, and diff whitespace checks pass.
- Fresh independent source review has no actionable P0-P2 findings. It caught an offline-cache cold-open regression and incomplete archive counts, both repaired before the final run.
- Full-app local qualification: unchanged base strict SwiftLint fails in the Apple review demo fixture, also tracked by #191296. Both UI comparison builds use an independently written, local-only extraction of two unchanged fixture branches, preserving guards, payloads, and timestamps. The synthetic Gateway path never enters those branches. No guard or lint configuration is weakened. That qualification and unrelated generated Info.plist changes are excluded from this PR. These results are not exact-tree full-app CI.
- Evidence uses the native app and an isolated synthetic Gateway. No live agent, provider, command, or account is used. Physical Duo, VoiceOver, exact-head CI, ClawSweeper, and maintainer approval are not claimed.

prs.title: test: size compaction fixtures from the shared 85% trigger
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Four test files were red on every scheduled `main` run since #204111 and #204180/#204210 moved compaction to the request boundary and to the 85% trigger (checks-node-compact-large-20/22/25/40; for example scheduled run 45312791464, jobs 138173038133, 138173031811, 138173031998):

| File | Failure on `main` |
|---|---|
| `agent-runner-compaction-fallback.test.ts` (tool rounds: true) | `expected 851264 to be less than 800000` |
| `session-context-accounting.gateway.integration.test.ts` | `expected 853432 to be less than 800000` |
| `agent-runner-required-maintenance.pending-input.test.ts` (two archives) | `compactionCount`: expected 0 to be 1 |
| `session-run.session-model-strictness.integration.test.ts` (preflight watchdog) | `summaryRequests`: expected 0 to be 1 |

## Why (test-only change; no product change)

- **The 800,000 bound was a test constant.** It came from #190017, when the trigger was 75% ("one compaction before 80%"). No product code enforces a limit near it. The product limits are the shared trigger (`packages/ai/src/utils/compaction-threshold.ts:16`, 85%, used by the request boundary at `request-boundary-compaction.ts:169-176`) and the window (`request-boundary-compaction.ts:205`). Both tests now derive the bound: `min(window, resolveCompactionThreshold(window, 0) + largest tool round + summary instruction)`, with the round and the instruction measured from the test's own requests. The largest request is the warm summary request: the request that crossed the trigger plus one instruction.
- **Strictness is fixture sizing, not a product bug.** The fixture stored `totalTokens: 125,000` as fresh, but its transcript was about 14k tokens; the only request was 19,094 tokens. Since #204111 the request boundary measures the outgoing request, so it correctly did not compact a 19k request in a 128k window. The history is now sized from the 85% trigger, and summaries are counted with the shared cold/warm helper (`test/helpers/compaction-summary-request.ts`).
- **Pending-input: the window is the threshold that matters here.** Reply-level maintenance compacts by itself only when projected usage exceeds the window; below it, it defers to the request boundary (`agent-runner-memory-runtime.ts` `defersTokenCompactionToRequestBoundary`), which measures the rendered request (~26k). Prior usage is now `window − 4,152` (the fixture's original margin), so the approved input pushes the projection over the window and reply-level maintenance runs.
- **Accounting mock:** a bare `GET /` without a body sometimes reached the provider mock, which then threw `Unexpected end of JSON input`. The mock now answers non-POST requests with 404.

## Evidence

- `main` (4d99cbb8): all four files red locally with the failures above.
- This branch: all four files green locally (fallback 2/2, pending-input 2/2, accounting, strictness preflight).

prs.title: fix(release): compare advisory jobs structurally
prs.body:
## Problem

The 2026.11.8 candidate checklist rejected a successful Full Release Validation ([45343386282](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45343386282)) at the publisher `selected-lanes` gate with `Release advisory jobs differ from the release policy evidence`.

Authenticated manifests are canonicalized with `sortJsonValueKeys`, but `validateReleaseAdvisoryJobs` compared recorded and recomputed advisories by hashing their JSON. The sealed Windows preview advisory ([job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45306802553/job/138154118844)) matched field-for-field; only its property order differed, so the gate failed closed on equal evidence.

## Solution

Compare advisory jobs with `isDeepStrictEqual`. This drops key-order sensitivity while keeping list order, every field value, and missing or extra advisories strict.

## Evidence

- New regression in `full-release-validation-state.test.ts`: key-sorted manifests are accepted, and a changed advisory conclusion is still rejected. Red on base in all four Windows-node cases with the exact error, green with the fix.
- `full-release-validation-state`, `release-publish-gates`, `validate-full-release-validation-evidence` and `render-github-release-notes` tests: 176 passed.
- Read-only replay against the exact sealed FRV 45343386282/1 manifest: all eight publisher readiness gates pass.
- oxfmt check and `git diff --check` clean.

## Impact

Unblocks stable 2026.11.8 publication with publisher tooling on trusted main. It changes no candidate bytes and weakens no gate.

## Worked on by

- @vincentkoc
- @RomneyDa

prs.title: fix(ollama): uncurated cloud models fail every request with a window-sized max_tokens budget
prs.body:
Fixes #199928

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every reply through an uncurated ollama-cloud model is rejected with HTTP 400 (`max_tokens ... exceeds model's maximum output tokens`) when the model's context window exceeds its real output cap.

## User Impact

User impact: uncurated cloud models (any whose context window exceeds the endpoint's output cap, e.g. the 1M-window lineup) become usable again on 2026.11.3+ instead of failing every request with a misleading "lower its reply limit" copy. Curated cloud models keep their curated budgets; authored `maxTokens` caps are unchanged. Both Ollama output-budget docs (`docs/gateway/local-models.md`, `docs/providers/ollama/troubleshooting.md`) are updated to match.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ollama's API reports no per-model output limit, and a context window is never a safe output budget — hosted endpoints cap output far below the window. The old fallback chain resolved uncurated cloud budgets to `params.contextWindow ?? OLLAMA_DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW`; this drops those two fallbacks so uncurated cloud models return `undefined` and take the shared conservative default (`resolveDefaultModelMaxTokens`) that local models already use. Worst case is again a truncated reply, never a rejected request.

A follow-up could consult the hosted catalog's per-model output limits (already refreshed from models.dev) before falling back, restoring full output headroom for catalogued models; that wiring is intentionally out of scope here.

## Evidence

### 1. Real-cloud before/after (fresh state)

Gateway built from source at each head against live `https://ollama.com`, model `ollama-cloud/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, one-shot turn via `openclaw agent -m "Reply with exactly: OK" --model ollama-cloud/deepseek-v4.1-flash --json` (API key redacted; appears in no log):

| Head | Wire budget (live discovery) | Gateway turn |
|---|---|---|
| main `8e481bae` | `contextWindow=1048576 maxTokens=1048576` | fails: `"ok": false`, error `"The reply length is set too high for this model. ... \| 400"`; gateway log `provider-error ... status=400`, `failoverReason=format`, `decision=surface_error` |
| this PR (`865d2086` / `8d806934`) | `contextWindow=1048576 maxTokens=16384` | succeeds: `"finalAssistantVisibleText": "OK"`, `winnerProvider: "ollama-cloud"`, `result: "success"` |

Wire budgets were printed by driving the real discovery path (`buildOllamaProvider("https://ollama.com", { apiKey })`) at each head — the same derivation that shapes the request.

### 2. In-place upgrade proof (`v2026.11.4` and latest stable `v2026.11.6` → PR head)

No schema or stored-config shape changes are introduced by this PR. Verified end-to-end against live `https://ollama.com` while reusing the exact same `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` (pre-seeded with a saved authored model cap `models.providers.ollama` → `custom-authored-cap`, `contextWindow=262144`, `maxTokens=2048`, plus a workspace sentinel file `workspace/upgrade-sentinel.txt`):

- **`OpenClaw 2026.11.4 (d843d6a)` → PR head (same `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`)**:
  - **Before upgrade (`v2026.11.4`)**: after catalog refresh (24 models discovered), `openclaw agent --agent main -m "Reply with exactly: OK" --json` failed with raw server HTTP 400 (`400 {"error":"max_tokens (1048576) exceeds model's maximum output tokens (393216) for model deepseek-v4.1-flash"}`, `failoverReason=format`, `decision=surface_error`), leaving `session_nodes=1`, `transcript_events=9`.
  - **After in-place upgrade to PR head + catalog preparation (`openclaw models list --all --refresh`)**: SQLite `plugin-model-catalog-v1` persisted 23 discovered `ollama-cloud` models and 1 configured `ollama` model:
    - `ollama-cloud/deepseek-v4.1-flash`: `contextWindow=1048576`, `maxTokens=16384`

prs.title: feat: install Git skills and plugins from repository directories
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Git-hosted skill and plugin repositories may contain multiple packages, but native installation currently selects only the repository root. This prevents callers from choosing an individual package while retaining the Git source and revision through update/removal.

## Changes
- Accept an optional repository-relative `--directory` for Git skill and plugin installs and carry it through the native protocol, install records, updates and uninstall.
- Share Git source parsing and directory validation between the existing lifecycle owners; keep non-Git directory requests rejected.
- Preserve pinned revisions and selected-directory provenance. Root-level Git installation remains supported.
- Preserve literal absolute recorded paths across normalization, discovery, index ownership, payload verification, capability inspection/consent, update and uninstall; retain legacy relative/tilde resolution.
- Add focused CLI, validator, lifecycle, update and uninstall regressions. Extract existing uninstall fixtures/assertions rather than introducing another installation owner.
- Repair the existing plugin-turn-handover model fixture to parse its JSON result separately from the runtime's appended repeat-call note. Runtime guard behavior and test assertions are unchanged.

This is the foundational CLI layer. Template Git dependencies are a separately committed dependent layer and are not included here. No Template catalog admission, package release, manual deployment or live-state change is requested.

## Evidence
A paired comparison loaded the actual generated Gateway validators from baseline `59b74af7e1ae8cbe1ca664a0fe16b93fd44af5ca` and candidate `7353cb2621683a2c04e8c16b2baab171a5399fc9`, without mocks or network:

| Request | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Git repository root | accepted | accepted |
| Git selected directory | rejected | accepted |
| npm with directory | rejected | rejected |
| Git with empty directory | rejected | rejected |

All four paired assertions passed. This proves the public protocol boundary, not successful upstream installation.

Successive real local-Git lifecycle regressions reproduced meaningful whitespace being lost in selector normalization, derived install paths and startup payload verification. The repaired scenario preserves leading-space and POSIX trailing-space selections through record round-trip, discovery, payload checks, update to a new commit and uninstall. It retains an older-shaped root install record without `gitDirectory`: that record round-trips unchanged, survives removal of the selected package, and still updates and uninstalls through the existing owners. This is data-model compatibility evidence, not an executed upgrade from a released v2026.11.4 binary.

Managed capability inspection trimmed `plugins/nested ` before publication. Extending the existing real-Git regression through the actual managed consent callback reproduced `ENOENT` at `resolvePluginArtifactManifests` before the fix. Changing the artifact/current/configured-path consumers to the existing recorded-path resolver also exposed configured discovery's eager trimming; removing that trim made both real-Git selections pass. The regression now records actual capability acceptance and passes the same callback through an update using round-tripped records.

A separate consent-owner regression reproduced an incorrect acceptance transfer between sibling paths `package` and `package `: the pre-fix update silently accepted the sibling's prior review. Literal recorded-path comparison now requires fresh consent for the different path and correctly selects the actual owner when both records exist. No new resolver, policy bypass, runtime hook or consent exemption was introduced. Consent repair local `014e9e974f18c3ff8dd9c7a1ca2df1ac3bfcc0fe` and published `e7c582482b5fb4cc612e3accd3c2436c1f8d7cf0` had independently verified identical trees `0f52b65e1c581639011560e46a12c134a3feb3f1`.

Exact-head CI on `e7c582482b5f` then failed in [checks-node-changed-2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43988956212/job/133725326646). Permitted check annotations identified JSON parsing failures in the existing plugin-turn-handover test. A bounded isolated replay reproduced the same failure at line 222, with subsequent client-stop cleanup errors. A diagnostic probe showed two valid JSON results followed by JSON plus the normal third-identical-call `[System note: ...]`. The test's synthetic model had incorrectly treated the entire model-facing output as JSON.

The fixture now parses the JSON text before that appended annotation. All five existing scenarios pass: declared, undeclared, mixed reload, context-engine handover and bundled Knowledge. The repeat guard still runs; its thresholds, runtime behavior, six-step scenario and all handover/once-only assertions are unchanged. Temporary instrumentation was removed. This is a repaired test fixture, not substitute shipped-CLI or released-upgrade evidence.

Latest local commit `a83a0bdf0891ae4ccbaa48a8c0354a27e875b260` and published head `f53c6c94242ad7b8a943401eabec4c8511f0dcd7` have independently verified identical trees `79a064dabf9cf89955a193e93a20942222142cc9`.

## Validation
- Latest fixture repair: the unchanged isolated undeclared scenario failed in 28.18 seconds before repair. After the parsing repair, all five existing scenarios passed in 96.97 seconds (88.22 seconds test time; command wall time 101.45 seconds), with no unhandled errors. These existing long tests exercise real Gateway turns, reload and generation ownership; no new Gateway boot, sleep, retry or test was added. CI seconds for the new head remain pending.
- The one-file staged `check:changed` completed with exit 1 solely on repository-wide dead-export diagnostics. Core graph boundary, test-root types, changed-test lint, script lint, formatting, line caps, mock-export and all other reported guards passed. `git diff --check` and commit hooks passed. No export was deleted, scan skipped/suppressed or exception applied; no all-green result is claimed.
- Consent repair: 115 affected tests passed across real-Git lifecycle, capability consent, discovery, path inspection, management consent and Template consent integration suites. After extending accepted-surface persistence and update consent, all 13 Git lifecycle tests passed again. Its five-file staged changed gate exited 1 for formatting and repository-wide deadexports; the formatter repaired one expression and a fresh five-file format check passed. Types, lint, cycles and other reported guards passed.
- Payload repair: 39 payload/lifecycle and 56 Doctor tests passed. The incomplete Doctor path-module mock was repaired by retaining actual unmocked exports. An unchanged Gateway trusted-plugin approval timeout scenario passed without timeout or behavior changes. An initial combined build/replay timed out at 240 seconds; a subsequent higher-bound replay passed. The initial timeout remains failed.
- Earlier literal-path repair: 275 affected tests, canonical core/config-cli/plugins-platform types and focused checks passed. Selector-persistence repair: 186 tests passed. Initial CLI layer: 181 affected tests, protocol generation/validator checks and affected type/lint/format gates passed.
- The earlier source-contract export-name collision was reproduced and repaired by renaming only the plugin-update assertion helper to `expectUpdateFields`. Four local contract leaves, 90 plugin-update tests and the hosted source-contract job passed. An initial invocation inherited `OPENCLAW_PROFILE=work` and failed two command-string assertions; the isolated profile-unset rerun passed. The initial failure is not counted as passing.
- Main was integrated once for an actual conflict, retaining physical symlink-parent/`..` semantics after a failing-then-passing preflight regression: 66 integration tests passed (14 skipped), plus 55 contract tests. The integrated 35-file changed gate and later three-file gate each exited 1 on repository-wide deadexports. Another invocation exited 143 during Gateway restart and is not counted as green.
- A full native runtime build passed during the earlier isolated disposable-profile CLI attempt. Fresh exact-head hosted CI/review remain necessary for the latest fixture repair.
- Previous head `39f104fae0088567dea053766f4a72a83f3d33ae` failed Android third-party unit tests and the CI gate. A permitted uploaded report identified `ChatComposerLayoutTest.unavailableDictationOffersExplicitVoiceNoteRecoveryWithoutChangingTheDraft`, Kotlin line 1511, with a 1000 ms Compose timeout. Root cause/inherited status is unproven; no rerun, timeout change or waiver. The subsequent `e7c582482b5f` Node-shard and gate failures remain prior-head failures, not current-head conclusions.

Git/npm/filesystem operations in lifecycle regressions are real; the repository is a synthetic local fixture. These are not shipped-CLI, successful upstream-network or released-binary upgrade proof.

## Remaining proof limitations
The real pinned upstream installation attempt reached Git cloning, then failed with `SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate`. The installer intentionally sanitizes Git CA overrides from its host execution environment. TLS verification, environment policy, egress routing and publication guards were left intact. Successful upstream installation and installed provenance remain unverified; protocol and regression evidence are not substitutes.

The released-binary upgrade attempt is blocked too: ordinary `npm pack openclaw@2026.11.4 --ignore-scripts` returned ETARGET, reporting no matching version before November 9, 2026, 00:01:58. Metadata/integrity lookup succeeded, but no released artifact was admitted or executed. No artifact-date override or direct-tarball workaround was used. Local source reporting version 2026.11.4 is not released-binary proof. Shipped-CLI nested-source lifecycle and an actual released-binary upgrade remain unverified.

ClawSweeper reviewed `e7c582482b5f` with no actionable code findings and confirmed the prior capability repair, but retained the data-model/shipped-CLI/released-upgrade proof requirements. Review/CI and any required owner approval must be reconciled against the new published head before landing.
