prs.title: docs(skills): update bundled himalaya skill for Himalaya 2.x
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The bundled `himalaya` skill documents the 1.x CLI and the pre-2.1 config schema. On Himalaya 2.x every example fails:

- `himalaya folder list` → renamed to `himalaya mailbox list`
- `himalaya envelope list from a subject b` → `himalaya envelope search 'from a and subject b'`
- `himalaya template send` → gone; `message compose` emits RFC 5322 and `message send` takes it
- `backend.*` / `message.send.backend.*` → `imap.server` + `imap.sasl.*`, `smtp.server` + `smtp.sasl.*`

This PR rewrites the skill against 2.x.

## Changes

- **SKILL.md**: 2.x command set for read, search, compose, reply, forward, move, copy, delete and flags; `-m/--mailbox` and `-a/--account`; localized mailbox names; note that 2.x leaves MML to an external composer.
- **references/configuration.md**: rewritten for the 2.x schema — server URLs, one SASL mechanism per backend, password from `password.command`, Gmail app passwords, iCloud, and the NetEase 163/126 requirements (`imap.sasl-ir = false`, `imap.id.auto` plus `imap.id.fields`, otherwise `BAD Request not ending with` then `SELECT Unsafe Login`), multiple accounts, mailbox aliases.
- **references/message-composition.md**: keeps the MML syntax, adds a note that himalaya no longer parses it and it belongs to a standalone composer piped into `himalaya message send`; rewrites the CLI section for the 2.2.1 flag-based `message compose`/`reply`/`forward` commands and restores `himalaya message read <id> --raw` for raw MIME inspection.

## Evidence

Ran against Himalaya 2.2.1 (linux musl aarch64):

- `himalaya mailbox list`, `envelope list`, `envelope search 'subject …'`, `message read` on a Gmail account and a 163 account
- `message compose` to stdout; `message move/copy --to`; `flag add/remove --flag`
- The configuration examples parse and connect: Gmail via app password, 163 via LOGIN plus `imap.id.auto`/`imap.id.fields`
- `himalaya account check -a gmail` and `-a net163`: imap OK, smtp OK

### Real behavior proof

Himalaya 2.2.1 on Raspberry Pi OS (aarch64), run against my configured Gmail and 163 accounts.
Addresses, message ids, IPs and endpoints are redacted; no credentials are included.

### Version

```text
$ himalaya --version
himalaya v2.2.1 +imap +maildir +msgraph +sieve +gmail +smtp +pimdir +jmap +rustls-ring +mbox
build: linux musl aarch64
```

### NetEase 163 with `imap.sasl-ir = false`

Account block, secret values omitted:

```toml
imap.server = "imaps://imap.163.com:993"
imap.sasl-ir = false
imap.sasl.login.username = "<account>"
imap.sasl.login.password.command = "<password-manager>"
imap.id.auto = true
imap.id.fields = { name = true, version = true, vendor = true }
```

```text
$ himalaya mailbox list -a net163
┌────────────┬────────────┬───────┐
│ ID         ┆ NAME       ┆ ROLE  │
╞════════════╪════════════╪═══════╡
│ Inbox      ┆ Inbox      ┆ inbox │
│ 草稿箱     ┆ 草稿箱     ┆       │
│ 已发送     ┆ 已发送     ┆       │
│ 已删除     ┆ 已删除     ┆       │
│ 垃圾邮件   ┆ 垃圾邮件   ┆       │
│ 病毒文件夹 ┆ 病毒文件夹 ┆       │
│ 广告邮件   ┆ 广告邮件   ┆       │
│ 订阅邮件   ┆ 订阅邮件   ┆       │
└────────────┴────────────┴───────┘

$ himalaya envelope list -a net163 -s 2
ID          FLAGS  SUBJECT                                                    FROM                DATE
<id>        *      Re: [openclaw/openclaw] docs(skills): update bundled…    "clawsweeper[bot]"  2026-11-22 01:47 -08:00
<id>        *      Re: [openclaw/openclaw] docs(skills): update bundled…    "clawsweeper[bot]"  2026-11-22 01:42 -08:00
```

Authentication and SELECT both succeed on Coremail with `imap.sasl-ir = false` present in the
account block. The key is documented in the versioned `config.sample.toml` because 126.com and
163.com falsely advertise SASL-IR; the recipe now carries it so an agent copying the block gets the
supported combination.

### Raw read (replaces `message export --full`)

```text
$ himalaya message read -a net163 <id> --raw | head -4
Received: from out-41.smtp.github.com (unknown [<ip>])
	by <host> (Coremail) with SMTP id <redacted>;
	Sun, 22 Nov 2026 17:32:39 +0800 (CST)
DKIM-Signature: v=1; a=rsa-sha256; c=relaxed/relaxed; d=github.com;
```

### Compose from flags

```text
$ himalaya message compose --to <addr> --subject Proof --body "flag-based compose"
From: "Rebine Lee" <addr>
To: <addr>
Subject: Proof
Message-ID: <...@raspberrypi>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 06:36:31 +0000
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset="utf-8"
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 7bit

flag-based compose
```

No `--send` was passed, so the command only printed the message.

### Reply from flags (Gmail)

```text
$ himalaya message reply -a gmail <id> --body "proof reply"
From: "Rebine Lee" <addr>
To: <redacted>
In-Reply-To: <...@google.com>
References: <...@google.com>
Subject: <redacted>
Message-ID: <...@raspberrypi>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 06:36:35 +0000
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset="utf-8"
Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64
```

`2.2.1` has no `--all` flag. `--to` replaces the recipients derived from the source, so an extra recipient goes through `--cc`: with `--cc team@example.com` the output kept the derived `To:` and added `Cc: team@example.com`.

The same reply command against one 163 message failed with `FETCH returned no body for the
requested message`, a server FETCH behaviour unrelated to the documented flags; reply is evidenced
above against Gmail.


## Relation to open PRs

Supersedes #192685 and #192690: this covers the mailbox command, the search/compose/send examples, the configuration schema and the MML disclaimer in one change.

Fixes #192675.

prs.title: test(update): drop the wall-clock exit deadline from the launcher IPC test
prs.body:
## Problem
Scheduled main CI run 45326636554, `checks-node-changed-compact-large-5`, fails `src/update/gateway-trial.test.ts > lets a launcher child exit naturally while its IPC peer remains connected` with `AbortError: The operation was aborted` (`Caused by: TimeoutError`). The abort also escapes as an unhandled rejection.

The test (added in #204224) puts a 10 s `AbortSignal.timeout` on the child's `exit` event, and that timer starts before spawn. So the budget also covers the child's `tsx` import of the `gateway-trial.ts` module graph. On that runner every test in the file took 3-6 s, and this one took 11.1 s. Locally the child loads in 1.2-2.9 s and exits immediately after, so it does not hang. This failure is not related to #204426.

## Fix
- Remove the wall-clock deadline. This follows the rule in `test/helpers/promise.ts`: a gate that is never reached fails at the Vitest test timeout, so healthy work on a loaded runner cannot lose a race.
- Wrap both waits in `withinTest(..., signal)` with the test context signal, so a timeout reaches `finally` and kills the child.
- No product change, and no timeout raise.

## Evidence
- With `process.channel?.unref()` removed from `src/update/gateway-trial.ts`, the test fails (`Test timed out in 15000ms`) and leaves no child process.
- Head: `src/update/gateway-trial.test.ts` 15/15 pass. CI is green on f41fb41ccabf.

prs.title: fix: let local MCP servers ask you to sign in again
prs.body:
Closes #204401

## What Problem This Solves

When a local (stdio) MCP server's sign-in expires, there is no way to sign in again from OpenClaw. The tool just fails. MCP has a standard way for a server to ask the user to open a sign-in page (URL-mode elicitation), but by default OpenClaw tells servers it doesn't support it, and drops the sign-in link when a server returns it as an error.

## User Impact

User impact: when an MCP server needs a new sign-in, the owner sees a **Sign in** button showing the server's domain, right in that tool's row in the Control UI (or the existing `Connect <server>` button on the reply in channels like Telegram). They sign in and ask again. Servers that never ask for a sign-in are unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

- OpenClaw declares URL-mode elicitation on every MCP connection. MCP capabilities are fixed when the connection starts, so this can't depend on the turn. Form-mode questions and the OpenAI form extension stay behind `mcp.apps.enabled`.
- A URL request from the server, or a URL-elicitation error (`-32042`), becomes the same sign-in action the OAuth Connect card from #200538 uses. It is only shown to the owner in a direct chat that hasn't handled untrusted content. Group chats and other senders get no link.
- The link stays out of the model's text, and OpenClaw never opens it by itself. The request is answered `cancel` right away: the button only reaches the user with the reply, so a server that waited for an answer would block the turn. Signing in, then asking again, completes the flow.
- The Gateway passes the sign-in action through chat history (web addresses only), and the Control UI tool row shows it as a pill next to the tool name. The rest of the row still expands the tool details.

## Evidence

Live run in the real Control UI on an isolated Gateway. Same prompt and same small stdio MCP server on both sides: on any tool call, it asks for a sign-in if the client supports URL mode, and otherwise returns `-32042` with the link. The model is a local stand-in that calls the tool. The user avatar is blurred.

Before (main): the tool fails and there is no way to sign in.

Also checked in the browser: the button links to the server's address with `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and opens a new tab; clicking elsewhere on the row still expands the tool details; it reads correctly in dark mode.

prs.title: fix: warn before uninstalling the default model's provider
prs.body:
<!-- Keep Allow edits by maintainers enabled for a personal-account fork PR. For a same-repository PR this checkbox is not applicable; repository permissions govern edits. -->

Closes #204419

## What Problem This Solves

Uninstalling a provider plugin can leave its model selected as the default without warning. The next chat then fails because that model is no longer available.

## User Impact

The removal confirmation now warns when the saved default model uses the plugin and offers **Choose another model**. That choice keeps the plugin installed and opens **Models**; Cancel changes nothing, and Remove preserves the saved model selection and existing disable markers. OpenClaw never chooses a replacement provider automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the plugin's package-wide inspection, the current saved configuration, the shared confirmation dialog, and the existing Models page. An inspection still loading is awaited; unavailable metadata or an unqualified model reference gets an explicit uncertainty warning rather than being treated as a safe mismatch. No CLI or runtime uninstall behavior changes.

## Evidence

A real isolated Gateway and production Control UI reproduced the missing warning on main cb4f301c6bb7e27946f2cb98ef283f4500dcd6fa. Removing the synthetic **Audit Provider** preserved audit-provider/audit-chat and its disable marker; a new browser chat failed with “This model was not found.” The candidate warns before removal and the explicit reselection choice opens Models without uninstalling or changing the saved model.

After

After

Matched 1280×900 Chromium viewport, same 760×450 crop and synthetic archive provider. No real credentials or paid inference. The chat failure after explicitly choosing Remove remains intentional because the saved selection is preserved.

Focused proof: 67 tests across six removal/page/lifecycle/config and i18n suites passed (3.32 s runner wall time), followed by the final focused three-test regression (1.36 s). Immediately before publication, simplification was repeated with no source changes and all 67 focused tests passed again (4.08 s). UI and UI-page test typechecks, targeted lint/format, docs MDX, controller guard, and i18n verification passed. Real-Gateway final proof passed in 75.88 s. CI seconds and WebKit coverage are not yet available.

### CI follow-up

The [original ratchet failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45338749699/job/138257653987) on 85931c1b4b9627ae1e953040eac95c6b5e1f8f09 was PR-caused: the new removal test used a closed first-party mock without preserving real exports. It was not a bundle-budget failure. The exact mock-export guard passed on the pinned main index, reproduced the same file/line failure on the published candidate, and passed after the fixture used typed importOriginal pass-through. No baseline, suppression, limit, or production behavior changed.

Repair 30bcd0224d2057d0819afecb7ab2b1aa47d21630 changes only that mock (+2/−1 lines). Simplification was repeated before pushing; 27 focused tests, the mock-export ratchet, targeted lint/format, and UI-page test typecheck passed. Existing independent production review and real-Gateway/screenshots remain applicable because production inputs are unchanged. [CI passed on this repaired head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204435/checks): 48 checks passed and 46 were skipped or neutral at verification. The failed old run remains recorded as failed.

Bound autoreview (openai/gpt-6.2-sol, full local snapshot against cb4f301c6bb7e27946f2cb98ef283f4500dcd6fa, P0–P2) identified saved-versus-draft and unavailable-read gaps, now fixed. A subsequent conditional stale-cache P2 was declined after verifying the existing config.changed refresh owner; concurrent external changes/retained draft conflicts remain a recoverable, non-transactional warning limitation. The review status is findings, not scoped-clean.

Build commands succeeded. Existing CSS ceilings and the 21-versus-20 chat-request budget still warn on main and candidate. Normalized chat boot JS gzip is 1,336,628 B on main and 1,336,886 B on candidate (+258 B); this delta is not labeled baseline. No budget or unrelated source changes were made. Test tooling hit transient worker/thread exhaustion before a bounded passing retry; an existing catalog-focus stderr warning also appeared on main, and was not repaired here.

Simplification: full change inspected after review fixes; production +71 lines, regression/support +157, docs +5 against the base. No new recovery state, mutation manager, fallback provider, or config writer. The removal decision is a focused page helper so the existing page stays within its line budget. prs.title: fix: keep a stopped reply in history when the turn started from the queue
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

If you press Stop on a reply and send your next message right away, the next reply can no longer be stopped cleanly. When you press Stop on that second reply, OpenClaw shows "Stopped, but a reply could not be saved to history." The partial reply on screen never reaches history, so it disappears once you leave the chat. This was seen in a Claude CLI session on the macOS app and reproduced in the Control UI.

## User Impact

When you press Stop, the partial reply stays in history and is marked Interrupted, including for replies started from a message sent while the previous reply was still stopping.

## Why This Change Was Made

A message sent while the previous reply is still stopping waits in the queue and starts its run later. Unlike a message that starts its run immediately, it recorded that the new run was active but left the session's writer claim with the stopped run. Runtimes that do not take the claim themselves, such as Claude CLI, kept that stale claim for the whole reply. Stop then refused to save the partial reply because the claim belonged to a different run.

Queued input now takes the writer claim in the same commit that records the run as started, matching fresh chat input. The writer check in the transcript store is unchanged; other writers are still fenced.

## Evidence

**Live reproduction (isolated Gateway, Control UI, Claude CLI runtime with Haiku 5.5).** Scenario: start a reply with a tool call, press Stop, send a long essay request about 1.5 s later, press Stop while the essay is streaming, then reload. Before is `main` at `3091ba81dfce`; After is this branch (code at `d1175d734597`; only comments and docs changed since). Same data, theme, and viewport.

- Before: the Gateway logged `chat.abort transcript append failed: session writer claim changed before transcript persistence`, the banner appeared, and the transcript had no assistant row for the stopped reply. A session-entry watcher showed the second run active with `activeWriterRunId` still set to the first, stopped run.
- After: the second run took the writer claim when it started, no warning appeared, and the transcript gained exactly one assistant row with `openclawAbort: { aborted: true }`. After reload, the reply shows as Interrupted.

### Clean comparison: right after Stop

Before:

![Before: after Stop, the chat shows "Stopped, but a reply could not be saved to history." with Refresh and Report a bug](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1fb02e2e-4106-4ef2-9e1e-b372c5dafe5f)

After:

![After: after Stop, the partial reply shows Interrupted and no warning appears](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/821ae643-1543-4f74-905a-dd699d6acab0)

### Clean comparison: after reloading the chat

Before:

![Before: after reload, the partial text shows without an Interrupted mark because history has no row for it](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8e870a7c-6978-4bce-bb51-6419bf0a48aa)

After:

![After: after reload, the partial reply loads from history marked Interrupted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e10bba9-dd02-40bc-8c83-6a04543ea856)

### Annotated comparison

Before (Stop, then reload):

![Annotated before: the save warning outlined](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d5d31dc9-5315-4ac9-a858-5cb6eb75126b)

![Annotated before: missing Interrupted mark outlined after reload](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d786883-fc47-458a-bbfc-7bc03b083ea4)

After (Stop, then reload):

![Annotated after: Interrupted mark outlined, no warning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/adc0ca4f-fa7d-44fe-b23f-22605e935841)

![Annotated after: Interrupted reply loaded from history outlined](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/90d0f9c8-c1a1-4f75-b435-e9e8b8414e1d)

**Regression test.** `agent-runner-source-identity.test.ts` now seeds a stopped run's writer claim and requires queued admission to take it over. It fails on `main` (`activeWriterRunId` stays `"stopped-run"`) and passes with the fix.

**Focused checks.** Affected consumer suites pass: reply runner, chat send queue and prestart lifecycle, `chat.abort` persistence and save warning, transcript reports, restart recovery, CLI steering, and the embedded runner's writer claim. `pnpm check:changed` (format, lint, core typecheck) passes.

**Review.** Local autoreview (Codex, `gpt-6.1-sol`) on `3091ba81dfce..d1175d734597` (before the comment and docs wording pass): no actionable findings. It only reviewed the diff, without the surrounding writer-fence, steering, and recovery code. Local ClawSweeper was not available.

**Gaps.** The live run used the Control UI and Haiku 5.5, not the macOS app or the original model. The save warning itself is unchanged: it can still appear when saving fails for another reason, such as a session reset during Stop.

prs.title: fix(i18n): translate the conversation People label as participants
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In the Control UI session details, the "People" section is rendered as an HR department in eight locales: zh-CN `人力资源`, zh-TW `人力資源`, ja-JP `人事`, ko `인사`, fr `Ressources humaines`, tr `İnsan Kaynakları`, id `Sumber daya manusia`, fa `منابع انسانی`. The English source is just `People` — the participants of a conversation — and the sibling key `chat.sessionHeader.peopleParticipants` already reads `参与者` in zh-CN. Fixes #204347.

## User Impact

The session People heading now reads as the conversation's participants (`成员`, `成員`, `メンバー`, `구성원`, `Personnes`, `Kişiler`, `Orang`, `افراد`), matching the participant rows directly below it. Five locales that were already correct (es, pt-BR, it, pl, hi) are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI catalogs are generated from the `.i18n/<locale>.tm.jsonl` translation-memory entries, so the wrong value was in the memory record that covers both `chat.sessionHeader.people` and `chat.mobileDetails.people`. Correcting that record per locale fixes every surface that renders the key.

## Evidence

Catalog values read from the translation memory the UI build consumes (before = `upstream/main`, after = this branch):

| Locale | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| zh-CN | 人力资源 | 成员 |
| zh-TW | 人力資源 | 成員 |
| ja-JP | 人事 | メンバー |
| ko | 인사 | 구성원 |
| fr | Ressources humaines | Personnes |
| tr | İnsan Kaynakları | Kişiler |
| id | Sumber daya manusia | Orang |
| fa | منابع انسانی | افراد |

![People heading before/after per locale](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/204347/people-label-proof.png)

Rendered A/B of the shipped Control UI (real Gateway on 127.0.0.1:28792, mock provider, session details drawer opened, headless Chromium, `--lang=zh-CN`). The two bundles were produced by `pnpm build:runtime` from `upstream/main` and from this branch respectively, and each screenshot shows the People row directly above 共享选项:

| Build | People heading |
| --- | --- |
| `upstream/main` (`6a8b47c8`) | 人力资源 |
| this branch (`9d6eeaaa`) | 成员 |

![Rendered Control UI People heading before/after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/204347/people-rendered-ab.png)

`check:line-cap-ratchet` OK, `check:test-lines-ratchet` net 0.

## What was not tested

- Only zh-CN was rendered; the other seven locales come from the same shared record and are verified by their translation-memory values in the table above.
- The ui Playwright/vitest project still produces no output on this machine (`ui/vitest.config.ts` never settles), so the rendered A/B above uses headless Chromium against the built bundle instead of the in-repo browser suite. No source test is shipped either: the earlier static-value test was removed per review because generated translation memory and source tests must not share a PR.
- No local typecheck: `run-tsgo` cannot resolve the workspace `@openclaw/proc-safe` package on this machine (fails the same way on clean `upstream/main`).

prs.title: feat(apple): add status chimes for hands-free Talk
prs.body:
Related: #204311

## What Problem This Solves

When using Talk hands-free on iPhone or Mac, people may have to look at the screen to know when a call is listening, ready for another reply, or ended.

## User Impact

Three independent, device-local **Status chimes** default on when unset: **Listening**, **Call end**, and **Ready for reply**. Each can be turned off separately.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cues mark when Talk first becomes ready, when a call ends cleanly, and when native speech recognition resumes after a completed reply. Realtime stays always-listening and does not play a reply cue; switching routes does not overwrite the saved preference. The microphone input is gated around cue playback where it could feed the cue back into Talk.

## Evidence

- R7: macOS app build passed, 4 OpenClawKit tests passed, and 66 iOS simulator tests passed. Both localization checks, both Swift format checks, and iOS lint passed.
- Device: main004 build 4 was installed and verified; hands-on iOS testing confirmed the chimes work and are audible at an acceptable level with earphones.
- Not yet verified: macOS hands-on audio and before/after screenshots, the focused macOS runtime regression test, and iPhone speaker-level parity. R7 macOS lint exited 2 with one pre-existing `file_length` violation in `OnboardingAISetup.swift` (1,546 lines against a 1,500-line limit). This PR does not change that file. Build lint phases were bypassed.
- AI-assisted. Codex found that macOS native fallback still reported the reply cue as unavailable; the fix now follows the active route. A separate cross-family review of the shared lifecycle, player, defaults, and capture gate reported no blocking findings.

### Visual proof
Automated iOS simulator UI capture of the Device Settings rows was attempted repeatedly but the UI test harness did not reach the Device Settings screen reliably (it landed on Quick Setup). Visual verification is therefore a hands-on device check: the chimes and the **Status chimes** settings were reviewed by hand on a physical iPhone running main004 build 4. The macOS fallback runtime regression test is left to PR CI, per the native test guide's disposable-runner requirement.

Second review: Marvin (claude-opus-5-5), no blocking findings.

prs.title: fix: show subagent launches as launched while a Claude CLI turn runs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent on the Claude CLI runtime starts a subagent, the chat shows "Subagent launch outcome unknown" next to the subagent's name for as long as the parent turn runs, even though the subagent started and is working. People who watch a turn live see this on every launch, so a working subagent looks like it may have failed.

## User Impact

User impact: while a Claude CLI turn is running, an accepted subagent launch now reads "Launched" with a link to the subagent, the same as after the turn ends or the page reloads. Real launch failures still show as failed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Claude CLI reports a tool result as a bare list of content blocks. The live tool event passed that list on unchanged, while the rest of OpenClaw (and the Control UI) reads results as `{ content: [...] }`. The UI pretty-printed the list as JSON, could not read the launch receipt, and fell back to "unknown". The CLI adapter now wraps bare block lists as `content` before publishing, which it already did for browser results only. The same change makes live output for every OpenClaw tool called through Claude CLI show the tool's text instead of a JSON dump, and lets the existing result sanitizer strip inline images and cap text in those results.

History reload was a separate cause (Claude omits `is_error` on success) and was already fixed by #203877. Other runtimes are not affected: embedded and Codex tool results already carry `{ content }` with an explicit error flag.

## Evidence

Real Control UI on an isolated Gateway with the real Claude CLI (Opus 5.5), asking the agent to call `sessions_spawn` once. Captured while the parent turn was still running.

Before (current `main`, 3c4bab6bca63):

![Before: while the turn runs, the accepted launch shows "Subagent launch outcome unknown Probe child"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cfdc82b7-8eeb-49ed-b048-5df51e4d9804)

After (this branch):

![After: at the same moment, the launch shows "Launched" with the Probe child subagent link](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/018261b9-c57a-48ec-9aaa-2efe9c05828c)

Annotated:

![Before, annotated: the launch row is marked as reading unknown while the turn runs](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b2e209c-67e4-48bd-8058-23710e67b67c)

![After, annotated: the launch row reads Launched and links to the subagent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4ebaa608-0c19-49e8-b4e1-1af103e5f2c7)

After reload on this branch, the launch still reads "Launched":

![After reload: Launched Probe child, followed by Probe child finished](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7077990e-7a7f-46f5-833a-8d596bc53ed8)

- The live `tool` event for the spawn changed from a bare block array to `{ content: [...] }` (captured from the WebSocket).
- New test in `execute-events.tool-result-args.test.ts` fails on `main` and passes here. The `src/agents/cli-runner` tests pass, except two `prepare.test.ts` credential cases that also fail on `main` on this host.
- Local autoreview of the commit: no findings.

## What Problem This Solves

The scheduled preflight-compaction test stopped exercising compaction and failed with `0` summaries instead of `1`.

## User Impact

prs.title: docs: diagnose HTTPS timeouts in the macOS managed browser
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a Mac running managed Chrome, OpenClaw could list tabs and Chrome could display a local page, yet a public HTTPS page timed out. The guide directed operators to the navigation policy or the target page. In this incident Chrome was waiting for macOS to load certificates. [Original troubleshooting step](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f7aa7e363b2bedf06394cdd4635337550f0e5703/docs/tools/browser/troubleshooting.md#L83)

## User Impact

An operator can check the login keychain on the Mac running Chrome and verify that HTTPS works again by reading the returned tab in the affected profile. For a signed-in task, the final check is whether the expected workspace opens.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tab ID returned by `open` gives the existing troubleshooting sequence an exact target for `snapshot`. The guide now gives an explicit policy denial and a public HTTPS timeout different follow-up steps. The macOS branch includes Apple's instructions for sampling the affected Chrome process while it is stalled.

## Evidence

**During the incident** (macOS 26.4.1, OpenClaw 2026.11.6), Chrome displayed `chrome://version`, public HTTPS navigation stalled, and the desktop showed a login-keychain unlock prompt. The following lines are from the same Chrome process sample. The number at the left is the sample count. Addresses, thread IDs and intervening frames are omitted.

```text
1372  DispatchQueue_151: copy_certificates_from_keychain  (serial)
1372  __SecTrustSettingsCopyCertificates_block_invoke_2  (in Security)
1372  Security::SecurityServer::ClientSession::activate()  (in Security)
```

**After the operator unlocked the keychain**, the managed browser opened a public HTTPS page and a snapshot of that exact tab contained the page text and its IANA link. I repeated the check during this review. On the saved application URL, one profile showed a sign-in screen and the intended profile displayed the saved workspace. The original trigger for the wait is unknown.

Local `autoreview` (Codex) reviewed the complete one-page change against base `f7aa7e363b2` before it was committed as `b0c1d4b60c2`. It reported no actionable P0–P2 findings. The hosted [PR context and evidence check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45343288358) passed on that head. The [fork CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45343291215) requires repository approval before its jobs can start.

<details>
<summary>Repeat the recovery check and inspect the result</summary>

Use the affected profile for both commands and substitute the target returned by the first command.

```sh
openclaw browser --browser-profile openclaw open https://example.com
openclaw browser --browser-profile openclaw snapshot --target-id TAB_ID
```

Two excerpts from the successful snapshot:

```text
This domain is for use in documentation examples without needing permission.
https://iana.org/help/example-domains
```

The changed page passed oxfmt and Markdown lint with the repository configurations, compiled as MDX, and resolved the SSRF policy fragment with OpenClaw's publishing parser. `git diff --check` passed.

</details>

prs.title: feat(signal): let a group reply to the bot count as a mention
prs.body:
Closes #161781.

## What Problem This Solves

Replying directly to OpenClaw’s message in a mention-gated Signal group leaves the follow-up unanswered unless the sender adds an explicit mention. Signal’s native Reply gesture is a common way to address someone in a group.

## User Impact

Quote-only replies stay quiet by default. To let an allowed sender’s native quote-reply count as a mention, set `channels.signal.implicitMentions.quotedBot: true` for the `default` account or `channels.signal.accounts.<id>.implicitMentions.quotedBot: true` for a named account. Named accounts opt in individually. `channels.defaults.implicitMentions.quotedBot: false` disables Signal quote activation across accounts.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Signal adapter matches the quoted author’s phone number or UUID to the configured account and passes that match to the shared mention gate after sender admission. A human and OpenClaw can send under the same account identity, so opting in can also wake OpenClaw when someone quotes a human-written message. The opt-in applies to linked personal accounts and dedicated bot accounts.

## Evidence

- On the previous PR head `4cc1a65f`, four regression cases dispatched a turn unexpectedly. The cases cover the unset default, a shared default set to `true`, an explicit shared disable, and isolation between Signal accounts.
- On `33342fa7aa357640fbfebad9b76835a964bffb2f`, all 64 tests passed across the Signal mention-gating, account-resolution, and schema suites in 49 seconds wall time. They exercise synthetic signal-cli events through the production handler and verify which events dispatch a turn.
- Signal type checking, targeted lint and formatting, MDX validation, base and bundled config schema checks, config documentation baselines, and the import-cycle check passed. Hosted CI is pending. The live validation below covers the revised policy.

### Conflict refresh — 2026-11-24

Merged upstream `9a39176f4d7ea6808df5fc8f891306142e571df6` and regenerated the three conflicting config metadata and baseline files from the merged source. The final head is `409c40970fe1db070bc77bb2cc72d38bc06acdb4`.

All 93 focused tests passed in 79 seconds wall time across Signal mention gating, inbound context, account resolution, and config schema. Signal type checking, formatting, MDX, config schema and metadata checks, and the import-cycle check passed.

### Live Signal upgrade and opt-in proof

Validated on November 24 against the published `v2026.11.7` Gateway and Signal plugin, then against the built PR head `409c40970fe1db070bc77bb2cc72d38bc06acdb4` using the same isolated Gateway state. All inputs were sent from Signal Desktop to a private two-member Signal group. Native quote metadata was verified at the Signal relay. Positive cases ran a real model, had recorded output tokens, and were observed in the same group.

**Upgrade and data:** The candidate opened the saved stable state and kept the Signal channel configuration, group admission settings, and selected model. Startup refreshed metadata and added plugin and skill defaults. The stable reply was retained under the same persisted session, and the candidate’s explicit-address reply extended that session.

**Account controls:** Two logical Signal accounts used independent Gateway account streams backed by one registered Signal identity. A is the default account. B is the named test account. The first candidate phase used the stable config with no opt-in. The opt-in phase set the shared flag to `true` and opted in only B. The final phase kept B opted in and set the shared flag to `false`.

```text
stable A QR7BASEOK | explicit address | reply accepted and displayed, +9.6s, output_tokens=8
stable A QR7BASEQUIET | native quote | quiet 25s, outbound_attempts=0, transcript_rows=unchanged
upgrade A QR7UPQUIET | native quote | quiet 25s, outbound_attempts=0, transcript_rows=unchanged
upgrade A QR7UPMENTION | explicit address | reply accepted and displayed, +5.0s, output_tokens=9
opt-in B QR7OPTIN | native quote | reply accepted and displayed, +4.4s, output_tokens=8
opt-in A QR7OTHERQUIET | native quote | quiet 25s, outbound_attempts=0, transcript_rows=unchanged
shared-disable B QR7VETOQUIET | native quote | quiet 25s, outbound_attempts=0, transcript_rows=unchanged
shared-disable B QR7VETOMENTION | explicit address | reply accepted and displayed, +5.2s, output_tokens=10
```

Four replies and four quiet controls were verified. A send that lacked a relay receipt was retried and is excluded from the eight measured inputs. The isolated Gateway and relay were stopped after verification.

### Prior-head live Signal and stable-upgrade proof

The live test below ran on `4cc1a65fa2da8d6cc52c668dbcd94fb1e15a1abb`, before the policy change to account-scoped opt-in.

Used Signal Desktop in a private two-member test group, an isolated Gateway, and a real OpenAI API model. Started with the published OpenClaw and Signal plugin v2026.11.5, then switched the Gateway and plugin to the earlier candidate on the same test state. The group allowlist, `requireMention`, recent-history limit, and explicit `quotedBot: false` were preserved and checked. After testing the explicit opt-out, removed only that override in the test configuration to exercise the default.

```text
Stable v2026.11.5: explicit mention replied; quote-only stayed silent.
Candidate after upgrade, quotedBot=false: quote-only stayed silent; explicit mention replied.
Candidate with default policy: ordinary message stayed silent; quote-only replied.
Totals: 6 real Signal inputs, 3 expected same-group replies, 3 quiet controls.
OpenAI assistant turns with recorded output tokens: 3 of 3 delivered replies.
```

The live ingress receipts confirmed that the three quote inputs targeted the configured Signal account and contained no explicit mention. The positive quote reply was also observed in Signal Desktop.

prs.title: feat: prepare worker placements for recovery after restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After a worker is confirmed lost, Codex recovery needs to know which placement it is replacing, even if the Gateway restarted. The shared database has no field for that fact yet. Upstream v41 is reserved for approval requester metadata; this independent migration uses v42.

## User Impact

This prerequisite adds storage only; it does not enable recovery or change existing placements. Shared state advances from v41 to v42 (the agent schema is unchanged). Older builds require restoration of the verified pre-upgrade backup before downgrade.

Related: #201026, #201032. The existing shared branch and both PRs are untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing placement row and migration owner: one nullable field on SQLite and PostgreSQL, no backfill, no automatic loss inference, and no reader or writer for the new field in this PR. The placement owner can later record the predecessor with its existing placement update; a separate store would add another write and rollback boundary. No repository reset, permission change, or new retention policy is included. [Maintainer design acceptance](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2d5e4b6d-a60b-4a09-a054-d919b7a422c0).

## Evidence

- After merging `main` at `4708bac52397` into this branch, the v42 patch was unchanged. On `4cc53aa0b423`, the SQLite migration, schema catalog equivalence, and CI inventory tests passed locally. [Both v42 PostgreSQL migration cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45337805942/job/138254787843), three of four PostgreSQL conformance shards, and PG16 smoke passed. Security and dependency review passed, but the [required CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45341662435) did not.
- [PostgreSQL shard 3/4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45337805942/job/138254787865) failed two cron restart cases because the Gateway did not report a new ready boot in time. Both cases passed in an isolated replay on the exact `main` base. Both timed out in an isolated replay on the PR head with frozen dependencies and the CI-pinned Node and PostgreSQL image, but that replay did not reproduce CI's exact HTTP 503 assertion. The cause is not established.
- The [Google transport lint errors](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45337805942/job/138256533137) and [Slack/Discord announcement test failures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45337805942/job/138254790554) reproduced on the exact `main` base. A [runner download](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45337805942/job/138254791313) timed out before tests started. The [Twilio test timeout](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45337805942/job/138254796286) was not reproduced on the base and remains unattributed.
- SQLite fixtures from published stable v36, beta v40, and current-main v41 all preserved their original rows and markers on commit refusal, then upgraded to v42. The existing v41 approval requester was preserved and the new placement field remained NULL. This was a migration-owner replay, not a packaged updater run.
- Isolated PostgreSQL 18.6 passed 17 focused migration and owner cases plus two existing first-use regression cases. Historical catalogs and optional repository fragments were preserved. The CI artifact build, focused typechecks, lint, formatting, generated checks, and test-line budget (+302 before the compatibility follow-up; 400 allowed) passed. The build reported two nonfatal UI budget notices; no UI code changed. Local independent review tooling could not start inside its required sandbox.
- The published npm 2026.11.6 updater activated an explicit tarball built from the tested v42 source tree in isolated, offline Podman. The candidate Gateway startup check passed; the update ledger recorded `succeeded` / `finished` and the activation journal reached `anchor-retired`. SQLite advanced v36 → v42; `quick_check` passed, and all original placement and worker fields matched. The synthetic approval survived with its transport reference normalized by existing Doctor behavior; the new nullable fields remained NULL. No managed service restart was requested.
- The follow-up at `d650a99b8c6f` registers the migration in the extracted PR wrapper and keeps v8 and v21 placement repairs on their historical layouts. The v42 migration alone adds the new field to those stores. The local repair run passed 66 selected storage and provisioning cases, including rollback, live-claim refusal, and cold extracted provisioning. The wrapper source-closure check passed; one additional extracted-package assertion was blocked locally by a mismatched installed `undici` version. [CI for the repaired head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45066136506).
- The fixture-only follow-up at `9291b3c580d0` makes the copied registry, first-use, preflight, and Doctor databases genuinely pre-v42. All four selected suites passed, including the packaged CLI Doctor repair followed by fresh Gateway readiness for the copied v2 state. Local database dialect and worker ratchets passed before this test-only delta; the previous hosted ratchet job was interrupted by its runner. [CI for the fixture follow-up](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45067587314).
- The `prepare-state` PostgreSQL command suite now checks the canonical current schema for both `prepared` and `ready`. Its stale v41 assertion reproduced on the prior v42 head (1 failed, 2 passed); isolated PostgreSQL 18.6 passed all 3 cases with the test-only follow-up at `7ac3e3df12e2`. [CI before merging main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45070683884).
- In the prior run, [models-auth](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45067587314/job/137347873950) matched the [scheduled-main failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45060721787/job/137326224598). On its exact base `128d31793346`, isolated replay reproduced both the [packaged worker revocation timeout](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45067587314/job/137347870205) and the [Codex native-config rejection mismatch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45067587314/job/137347874035) without this PR. This is baseline attribution, not a passing CI gate.
- [Hosted CI on `7ac3e3df12e2`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45070683884) passed all four PostgreSQL conformance shards and PG16 smoke. The worker revocation, models-auth and Codex native-config failures matched the baseline evidence above. [The CI planner mismatch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45070683884/job/137358763804) reproduced on the exact main checkout base `948c233eaedf`: both report the same six deleted update test paths retained in the inventory after #203497. [The separate lint job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45070683884/job/137359697455) hit its 15-minute limit. The required CI gate did not pass.
- **Upgrade cost:** one nullable ALTER on `worker_session_placements`, no backfill or row rewrite; SQLite retains existing idempotent index checks and quick/placement integrity checks. The scoped SQLite backup copies placement rows and publication metadata; the package updater retains its existing full rollback capture. PostgreSQL takes its normal DDL lock and publishes the version. Largest-deployment row counts and backup/lock timings were not available; managed-service restart and a Swift build are still unverified.

Original implementation: @galiniliev, selectively ported from `a1b9b73924b6`.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @galiniliev](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2d5e4b6d-a60b-4a09-a054-d919b7a422c0)

prs.title: refactor(github): migrate repository integration to a plugin
prs.body:
## Summary

Depends on #192349. Review and merge the SDK foundation first.

GitHub repository integration spans account connections, repository discovery, execution identity, publication, and browser presentation. This PR moves the vendor implementation into the bundled `github-repositories` plugin using [the Plugin SDK foundation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192349).

The plugin supplies the existing GitHub workflows. OpenClaw retains sessions, approvals, local Git custody, durable account/publication records, and recovery. Generic SDK additions belong to the foundation; this consumer supplies GitHub registration, lifecycle, configuration migration, and presentation.

**Upgrade:** run `openclaw doctor --fix` to move legacy native GitHub settings into `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`. Explicit plugin allowlists and deny rules remain authoritative; include `github-repositories` to use this integration.

The independent `github` plugin continues to own `github_read`, `github_search`, public link previews, and reader views. GitHub Copilot, Gateway sign-in, and verified profile identity remain separate owners.

## Ownership

| Capability | `github-repositories` supplies | OpenClaw retains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts and OAuth | Credential selection, GitHub transport, refresh policy, and connection presentation. | Canonical managed/personal account records, profile authority, config writing, and refresh settlement. |
| Repository sources | Discovery, URL admission, authenticated clone/fetch, repository/object identity, and worker adapters. | Picker/session admission, checkout storage and leases, worktree placement, accepted checkpoints, and recovery. |
| Execution identity | Identity facts, credential scrubbing, private child-launch adapters, and supported sandbox preparation. | Command policy, approvals, final launch, and sandbox provisioning/permission. |
| Publication | GitHub targets/content, remote operations, and author/coauthor policy. | Local Git/index custody, verified participant/consent facts, exact receipts, accepted-operation settlement, and live effect authority. |
| Agent tools | `github_identity_status`, `github_publish`, and their policy descriptions. | Caller-bound dispatch, workspace access, tool/child-policy ceilings, handoff, and cleanup. |
| PR/check presentation | Reads, subscriptions, plugin read store, badges, actions, Settings, and session accessories. | Session/audience admission, layout, navigation, captured requests, and retained operations. |
| Board and Doctor | GitHub Actions binding, secret/config metadata, migration, and health checks. | Grant preparation, config persistence/migration orchestration, managed service scheduling, and cleanup. |

The plugin entry registers repository and execution contributions, tools, Board data, Gateway methods, and a V2 managed account service. The manifest declares startup activation, Settings views, secret exclusions, and Doctor participation. Heavy handlers load when invoked. The host keeps its existing stores and lifecycle owners. The released `GatewayRequestContext.githubOAuthService` lookup remains a guarded projection of the canonical plugin-owned service through the documented December 31, 2026 compatibility window; it does not create a second account service.

### Repository and execution

The qualified source `github-repositories/repositories` feeds the repository picker and follows `sessions.create` into session, checkout, and worker preparation. Default worktree preparation uses source-owned `resolveBase()` to observe authenticated remote HEAD, hydrate the selected commit, and follow a renamed default branch. Explicit selectors preserve their Git namespace and literal branch names; missing refs remain actionable. The host verifies the commit locally without ambient-origin fetches, retains safe local branch updates under checkout custody, and pins ref/commit before setup. Retries retain that accepted pin. The isolated Fake Forge plugin uses the same contract with a local transport and an HTTPS canonical origin. GitHub callbacks perform authenticated transport; the host retains destinations, cancellation, pinned commits, and recovery.

Worker preparation returns immutable repository/object identities and a nonsecret cache partition. The host revalidates the lease around Git-pack preparation; the plugin asserts caller and credential authority at effects. Cache identity is not access authority. Admitted credential readers retain the original dispatch actor and request; issued credentials register cleanup with the host.

Execution uses the SDK environment provider. Local wrappers enclose the reviewed command after policy/approval. Sandbox preparation explicitly selects backend and scope rather than copying local identity. Declared exclusions keep bearer credentials out of nonsecret environment facts and prepared repository snapshots.

### Publication and lifecycle

The plugin consumes `native-github-account-host`, `native-github-publication-host`, and `native-github-session-read` to work with the existing native records and receipts.

- `github_publish` uses caller-bound Gateway operations and the existing publication/handoff owner. Session and approval checks remain in force. PR preparation retains the selected requester through the existing host continuation; publication keeps its existing accepted-operation settlement.
- The plugin supplies typed provenance and Git author facts. Core records and compares existing receipt fields for replay and uses the author for source-integration commits. Live request/account assertions authorize effects; verified participant/consent facts stay host-owned.
- PR automation reads the session’s own publication without an import-authorship preflight. A different captured target retains its existing authenticated read workflow. The recipe retains jobs after authentication, inspection, network, and checkout blockers and after successful remediation; cleanup is reserved for a verified merged/closed result.
- Plugin-owned `session-pr:v1` declarations retain their SHA256 identity bytes. Wire/storage DTOs and accepted publication records retain their contracts.
- Refresh, publication-provider installation, and session presentation use managed scheduler, Gateway, and plugin-instance lifetimes. The legacy service projection shares its existing exact-Gateway lookup across native and compiled module graphs. Native source loading and compiled SDK consumers use the same canonical owner and installed publication-host lookup. Accepted publication and checkout transfers remain one-use operations under that owner; cleanup, replacement, and revocation end stale capabilities.

### Browser presentation and reader independence

Control UI V2 contributions provide Profile connections, Agent tools Settings, session PR/check accessories, actions, and retained publication operations. They reuse host controls, responsive layout, serialized config mutations, and captured requests. Plain host-owner subscriptions feed plugin-local reactive state across the separately bundled Solid runtimes. The plugin read store owns PR presentation. Hovercards preserve the compact ten-PR limit and remaining count; branch/diff metadata occupies an adjacent row in the existing accessory layout. Branch and publication controls stay in the native Environment section through the generic `session-environment` slot; published PRs use the separate context section.

Explicit shorthand such as `owner/repo#123` names `reader: { pluginId: "github", id: "github" }`. Both contributions must be admitted and active; the reader owns URL filtering and remote reads. Checkout names, project aliases, and adjacent links never infer a destination, so formatting needs no background project-catalog read.

Public `github.preview` and `github.detail` use the reader's data path directly, so disabling `github-repositories` leaves public reading operational. Enabled managed identity retains its current-selection checks; disabled integration skips that managed selection and uses the existing service/environment/anonymous public path. GitHub App installations verify identity with a temporary installation token and support public reads/search scoped to the requested repository. Temporary tokens are revoked before delivery; App access does not broaden the public-only reader or enable shell execution/publication. Request authority is checked during reads and before delivery. Session/Enterprise readers retain their admitted session-specific path.

Disabling repository integration removes its operations, managed service, tools, and browser contributions. Disabling `github` removes public reading without changing repository ownership. Neither operation broadens allow/deny policy.

Session rows render passive plugin badge facts through the native row renderer. The same bounded, data-only facts join the existing scoped sidebar snapshot, so PR indicators survive a reload before plugin reconnect. Pending results retain facts only for the same complete session target and current registration; ready-empty results and retirement clear them. No plugin code, catalog, new storage manager, or capture timer is persisted.

## Configuration and upgrade

Canonical settings live under `plugins.entries.github-repositories.config`:

| Setting | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `system` | Shared managed GitHub execution identity. |
| `agents.<id>` | Complete per-agent identity override and optional sandbox permission. |
| `host`, `apiBaseUrl` | Matching GitHub or Enterprise endpoint pair. |
| `service.host`, `service.token` | Gateway-side discovery and reader service credential. |
| `repositorySearch.useNativeCredentials` | Explicit opt-in for native-credential repository search. |

`openclaw doctor --fix` invokes the plugin-owned transform for `tools.github`, per-agent `tools.github`, `gateway.github`, `gateway.controlUi.github`, and `gateway.projects.nativeGitHubSearch`. Explicit canonical values win, identities remain atomic, and unknown legacy fields remain available for explicit repair. Normalization is idempotent; conflict warnings omit credential values.

Managed OAuth records, personal connections, and accepted publication state retain their existing storage owners. Runtime reads canonical configuration; migration does not add a legacy runtime reader or rewrite receipts. Explicit allowlists, deny rules, disabled entries, and independent-reader policy are preserved.

See `docs/plugins/github.md` and `extensions/github-repositories/config-migration.test.ts` for configuration and migration details.

## Test scope

Native contracts remain with their host owners. GitHub unit and integration suites live with the plugin; native UI fixtures activate its declared public browser entry and consume protocol events. Coverage includes canonical configuration migration, serialized writes, account selection and retirement, publication handoff, worker credentials, execution approvals, browser freshness and independent reader admission. A standalone fixture allocation covers real provider setup, typed public adapters, lifecycle cleanup and passive-badge reload proof; the shared scalar is unchanged. A separate exact allocation covers App status/read lifetime, automation target/blocker guidance, and App capability presentation regressions.

## Validation

- Full local `pnpm build` passes, including SDK declarations, all 102 bundled plugins, all 167 public SDK subpaths and Control UI. Core, Gateway, agent-execution, extension and UI typechecks pass for the affected scopes. The supported local package passes tarball inventory and import-graph integrity checks.
- The intervening handoff and worker-recovery owners pass 98 targeted cases. Publisher installation rollback passes eight host/loader cases; native-menu error isolation and plugin-owned live/persisted badge parity pass 31 UI cases, with affected production/test typechecks and scoped lint.
- A supported local CLI turn with both GitHub plugins disabled executes successfully with the independent Fake Forge identity and no GitHub token in its child environment.
- Published 2026.10.9 state survives Doctor migration, a second idempotent Doctor run and restart, preserving its project, managed worktree, session and published request. Explicit deny remains authoritative when both GitHub plugins are also allowlisted: two Doctor runs and a restart leave both plugins unloaded and absent from UI/repository catalogs while OpenAI remains active. A separate real Gateway interruption during an accepted publication resumes the same request/account/destination through idempotent replay and produces exactly one PR with the expected commit. A crash after a remote effect with its response lost remains synthetic-fault coverage.
- Focused native checkout/publication, RPC, execution identity/approval, sandbox, App/OAuth/Git transport and browser suites pass. Cached badge reload and cross-tab deletion proof includes actual persisted badge facts; capture cadence is unchanged.
- Real isolated Gateway checks verify App identity, public PR reading/search, and refusal to disclose a private PR despite installation access. Native identity also publishes to disposable public/private repositories, resumes an advanced private head, refreshes the base, and uploads/associates sandbox evidence.
- A real scheduled auto-fix occurrence reads the selected PR's feedback, verifies the requested edit, and publishes to the same PR while retaining its job. The 14 recipe contract cases pass; repeated fresh-observation behavior remains unqualified as described below.
- Focused repair suites pass: 63 App/reader/RPC cases, 15 connections cases, 14 automation cases, and the SDK readiness regression.
- Targeted account lifecycle proof verifies unavailable selection and exact-config recovery with real reads; seven credential/profile retirement and cleanup cases pass. Nineteen publication response-loss, duplicate replay, authority, and restart-recovery cases pass through the real host/plugin adapter with synthetic GitHub faults.
- Fresh isolated Fake Forge proof passes: plugin transport supplies the advanced remote commit, the host owns the managed worktree, and one real successful agent `exec` receives `FAKE_FORGE_IDENTITY=sdk-trial`. The Gateway remains available locally; the model is a synthetic loopback fixture.
- Production and test compiler-boundary guards pass without exemptions. English catalogs load through the declared public artifact and retain Vite dependency watching and fresh reloads; source localization verification passes.
- Startup JavaScript gzip passes its unchanged cap: 90,661 bytes against 90,687 bytes. Startup/auth behavior, native Agents settings, browser subscription cleanup and reconnect have focused passing proof.

Interactive OAuth issuance, distinct-account isolation, native Codex-harness execution, Enterprise endpoints, real cloud provisioning, factory-native proof issuance/redemption, and migration from the newer 2026.11.1 release remain unqualified. Reliable full recurring auto-fix monitoring also remains unqualified: the complete recipe can return quietly without reading fresh feedback, and that failure mode is reproduced on untouched upstream as well. Live feedback-to-publication execution is verified separately.

prs.title: feat(gateway): admit sessions_send wake starts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_send` can fan out wake-starting work through the gateway `agent` RPC. Before this change, concurrent senders could bypass sender-local batching and rate limits. This adds an optional gateway-owned admission boundary for typed `sessions_send` wake traffic. It intentionally does not affect `mode:notify`, which does not create recipient work.

## Summary

- add a disabled-by-default `gateway.sessionsSendWakeAdmission` policy (six starts per 15 minutes by default)
- enforce it at the common gateway `agent` admission boundary only for typed `inputProvenance.kind=inter_session` / `sourceTool=sessions_send`
- persist one idempotent per-recipient decision in a separate SQLite database, atomically, and fail closed if state is unavailable

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/sessions-send-wake-admission.test.ts`: 4/4 passed (default-disabled, seven-recipient load, restart/idempotency, fail-closed state error)
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm format:check`, and `git diff --check` passed locally
- implementation is based on released OpenClaw `v2026.10.9` / `8b18b557`, matching the runtime that exposed the issue

## Rollout

Feature remains off by default. This PR contains no config enablement, runtime rollout, or gateway restart. Rollback is retaining the disabled flag or reverting this commit; the receipt database remains as audit evidence.

Tracking: cbire880/the-roost#2473, OP#1548

prs.title: fix(release): validate both update receipt formats and pin beta channel fixture
prs.body:
## Problem
The initial `2026.11.15-beta.1` full release validation run failed two update QA fixtures. Neither failure was in the updater itself.
- **Upgrade-survivor receipt checks** accepted only the historical command receipt (`status: "ok"`). The release updater now writes a native lifecycle record (`phase: "finished"`, `status: "succeeded"`), so a real successful recovery, captured in Actions artifact `14890042643`, was reported as a failure.
- **Update channel switch (stable to beta)** set a bare `openclaw` package override. The release updater packs that override, and with no tag npm resolved it to `latest`, which has schema 40, instead of the loopback beta candidate, which has schema 41. The real preflight then correctly refused the 41→40 downgrade.
- **Package-to-Git dirty checkout.** Once the lane is pinned to the candidate, it uses the candidate's detached package-to-Git switch. [#200578](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200578) intentionally removed the dirty-checkout refusal from that route; the docs say it "does not require a clean source checkout or overwrite its local edits". The lane still asserted the old in-place refusal.

## Solution
- `requireCompletedUpdate` accepts both receipt formats and holds each to its own contract:
  - Historical receipts must be `ok`, with any wrapped run succeeded and finished.
  - Lifecycle records must be finished and succeeded, with a run id, matching target and after versions, and only completed or skipped steps that exited cleanly.
- Running, failed, malformed and rejected receipts still fail. The admission, warning and artifact checks are unchanged.
- The first-hop admission check moved from an inline `node -` heredoc into `assertions.mjs` as `assert-first-hop-admission`, so it shares that receipt parser. Admission ownership and missing-load-path assertions remain fail-closed.
- The beta channel switch now sets `npm_config_tag=beta` alongside the guarded package override. A new `assert-beta-registry` check verifies the loopback beta manifest before the update: one manifest, the same version and schema versions as the installed candidate, a loopback tarball origin, and an exact sha512 tarball digest.
- The beta update assertion expects the native `already-current` channel-switch receipt, including its exact step outcomes, empty repair and no next action.
- The channel-switch lane is now qualified by the frozen target's package-to-Git route (`in-place` or `detached`):
  - **In-place route:** still requires the `dirty` refusal.
  - **Detached route:** checks that the source checkout's HEAD, tracked edit and untracked notes are byte-for-byte unchanged, and that the installed release is the selected commit without either local edit. A failed switch still fails the lane.
  - `src/update/preflight.ts` and all production updater code are unchanged.
- The parent frozen-admission fixture includes the Git route source `update-command-git.ts`, which the route check reads.

## Evidence
- Recovery receipt: the real artifact receipt fails before the fix and passes after it. 10 CLI cases cover supported, rejected, malformed and nonterminal receipts.
- Registry: running the real resolver, the bare override with default `latest` selects schema 40. With the corrected invocation it selects exactly `2026.11.15-beta.1`, schema 41, and the fixture digest matches. In a separate isolated run, the real preflight still refused 41→40 and left database and config bytes unchanged.
- Detached switch: the old assertion reproduced the CI failure. In a minimal isolated fixture, the real Git release runner published the selected commit and passed the new preservation and exclusion checks.
- Parent admission fixture: the missing-file error reproduced before the fix. After it, 122 evaluations and 112,739 bytes, under the 262,144-byte limit.
- 38 focused tests, lint, typecheck, format, ShellCheck and `git diff --check` pass.
- **Not yet proven:**
  - The full Docker channel-switch lane has not run locally (no Docker daemon). The previous CI attempt failed before the lane, in `npm pack` ("Exit handler never called!"); nothing in this PR touches packing.
  - First-hop and missing-load-path lanes stay fail-closed. The frozen candidate's native updater does not write the historical candidate-admission receipt, so they need new candidate evidence or a decision on where that contract is proven.

## Impact
This fix covers part of the `2026.11.15-beta.1` release repair. It will be backported to `release/2026.11.15` after landing.

## Worked on by

- @RomneyDa

prs.title: fix(sessions): use the requesting person's saved pin order across tools and clients
prs.body:
## What changes

Ask the assistant for “my pinned sessions” and it returns the same ordered list as the signed-in user's web sidebar. Updated Mac and Android clients use that list when the Gateway supports it. Pins come from the admitted profile's ordered `session:` entries in `ui.railShortcuts`. A `session-rail:` shortcut is not a pin. Pinning grants no access, wakes no thread and does not write another person's preferences. Visibility and eligibility are applied before pagination. Without a verified requester, the embedded tool rejects either pin filter and omits unknown pin fields from ordinary inventory.

## Scope: pin parity, not a new Archive contract

This candidate removes the proposed native personal Archive/Restore/Undo feature, its Gateway capability, receipt fields and preference cleanup. It adds no suspended legacy pin store. The original Mac Undo implementation and its regression suite, plus the Gateway lifecycle field handling and store-RPC regression suite, match the PR merge base byte-for-byte. That source match alone does **not** establish end-to-end compatibility: the same Mac row can now mean a personal rather than a shared pin.

**Landing blocker — explicit Mac Undo is not base-equivalent.** The original Gateway deliberately clears the active shared `pinnedAt` on Archive. Ordinary Restore only restores the thread. Explicit Mac Undo used to send `{archived:false,pinned:true,expectedSessionId}` for a captured *shared* pin; it recreated a pin with a **fresh** timestamp, not the old timestamp or necessarily the old rank.

On the split Gateway, signed old/new connections for the same synthetic person sent exactly those fields to the same archived mixed-pin thread. The negotiated connection got `INVALID_REQUEST` (“Send pinned separately…”). SQLite confirmed no restore and no preference change. The unnegotiated connection then restored and re-pinned that exact row with a fresh timestamp. An ordinary Restore on the negotiated connection succeeded and both profiles recovered their personal order; no historical shared pin was recreated. Two controls rule out superficially simple fixes: a personal-only row also failed combined Undo (sending its personal flag to the legacy writer incorrectly created a shared pin), and a shared-only row was restored without its former shared pin because the negotiated Mac saw `pinned:false`. Never infer the shared flag from the personal one.

**Rollout proposal:** ship the Gateway with the negotiated Mac/Android adoption. Historical shared pins have no recorded pinner and are not imported: updated users must re-pin the threads they want. Updated clients show shared pins read-only on old Gateways. Existing authorized, unnegotiated direct RPC retains shared pin semantics; restricted web navigation stays device-local. iOS is separate (#199685). Native rollout is proposed, not approved for landing.

## Behavior exercised

- **Tools and web:** a real `sessions_list` call returned two saved pins one per page. A tool batch removed both pins without removing a rail shortcut or changing another person's list. The unrestricted server window ranks personal pins before pagination; on a restricted device, a remote pin no longer displaces ordinary row 50. A signed stopped chat did not publish a paused pin write. At the 4 KiB limit a rejected two-target write preserved all 4,051 existing bytes; retrying after an explicit unpin succeeded.
- **Mac Threads:** Main and Research sheets both received Alpha before the more recently updated Beta. The baseline reversed them. The repair renders **Alpha → Beta → Recent** even after a lifecycle update; another signed profile keeps Beta first. No preference write on open. Ordinary picker and offline-cache ordering stay unchanged.
- **Mac Pages:** against released Gateway `2026.11.7`, moving a shared-pinned thread to another group sent one guarded category-only patch and retained the historical pin. On a modern Gateway, a rejected reorder restores the last confirmed order; an acknowledged reorder keeps its saved order when a subsequent read times out. Neither needs a second write.
- **Android:** after a same-person reorder moved the open Cedar chat from #1 to #104, tapping **Load more sessions** requested offset 100, limit 100. Baseline put Cedar at #101. The repair displayed Birch → Maple → Spruce → **Cedar** → Aspen in Gateway order. Across 14 native views per install, all 105 pins appeared exactly once. History stayed open; Android made no preference or session-patch write after the reorder.
- **Upgrade (retained proof):** a released `2026.11.7` fixture upgraded schemas 38→43 and 36→41. All five sessions, both profiles, historical pin timestamps and four preference rows survived. No historical pin was imported as a personal pin. This was an upgrade check, not an Archive test.

On the previous draft, four signed clients and SQLite showed personal Archive removed Alice’s saved slot, kept Bob’s, and cleared the historical shared timestamp (200 → null). Neither ordinary Restore nor explicit Mac Undo recovered the historical shared position. A later, legitimate shared write remained visible on the archived record. Separately, exact-candidate review traced a >100-row Mac Undo: a failure in a later chunk could invalidate earlier, successful pin-restoration receipts. There was no 101-row device reproduction. Those findings and their traces apply to the removed implementation, not to this split.

## Verification and limits

Split source: `d2d0d7decb010d7acb0d8e787c02fd9fad5b3d3c` (tree `47874f22fba90ca7ed713d5b7c46a900645e82df`); merge base `c237dbd5bf18fbdad8d73d3de18693e23196c0b6`.
