prs.title: fix: send slash commands mentioned in prose as one message
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in Control UI, pressing Enter on ordinary prose that mentions a slash command runs that command and leaves the rest of the message unsent. For example, `Please explain /goal prompt` sends `/goal prompt` alone and leaves `Please explain` in the composer.

## User Impact

User impact: messages such as `Please explain /goal prompt` are sent intact as one message. Leading commands and inline commands picked from the slash menu keep their existing behavior. Typing a complete inline command mid-draft without picking it from the menu no longer runs it (see Scope below). No migration or configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only an explicit slash-menu selection should start a separate inline command. The change removes the Enter-time scanner that guessed commands inside prose, plus the dashboard-only metadata that existed just for it. Explicit selection, permission checks, leading commands and Gateway directive handling are unchanged.

## Scope: typed inline dispatch from #122425 and #137685

This PR narrows behavior that #122425 and #137685 added on purpose. This section lists exactly what changes. It is a recommendation based on the public history linked here, not a recorded maintainer decision. A maintainer confirmation on this PR settles it either way.

What those PRs set out to do:

- #122425 made slash completion work inside a draft that already has prose, so a recognized inline command dispatches through the normal command path while the surrounding prose stays as an unsent draft. Its proof covered both a fully typed command (`Keep this /exec gateway` + Enter) and menu selection (`/reset`, `/weather` to `$weather`).
- #137685 added `/dashboard [request]` as a first-class command. Its commit "dispatch multi-word dashboard requests" let `/dashboard release health` dispatch from a prose position. That served the Side panel Dashboard launcher, which appended `/dashboard ` to an existing draft.

Kept:

- Inline commands picked from the slash menu mid-draft. For example `hello /thin`, Enter selects `/think`, type `high`, Enter runs `/think high` and leaves `hello `. The existing test "preserves typed inline argument mode across command hydration" is unchanged and still passes.
- Skill selection from the menu inserts `$skill-name` (#122425 step 3).
- The same connection, permission and confirmation checks for inline commands (#122425 step 2).
- Leading commands, including `/dashboard release health`, `/goal ...` and `/loop` in front of pasted prose.
- Everything else from #137685: the first-class `/dashboard` command, its namespace transfer, icon and `control-ui` skill routing.
- Gateway directive handling. This PR changes no Gateway code.

Dropped:

- Running a fully typed inline command on Enter without menu selection. `Keep this /exec gateway`, `hello /think high` and `Please explain /goal prompt` are now sent as one message.
- The multi-word prose path for `/dashboard` (`Review @Alex /dashboard release health` + Enter), with its `allowsInlineMultiWordArgs` flag and `INLINE_MULTI_WORD_COMMANDS` set.

Recommendation: retire typed inline dispatch and keep menu selection as the only inline trigger. The evidence:

1. The scanner cannot tell a command from a mention. `Keep this /exec gateway` (the #122425 example) and `Please explain /goal prompt` have the same shape: prose, whitespace, a known command, then one argument. Any rule that keeps the first also fires the second. When it guesses wrong, it runs a command the user did not ask for (Goal mode, a settings change) and drops the rest of the message.
2. The reason for the multi-word `/dashboard` path is gone. #138713 (merged 2026-09-05, commit `08dacc15c9a` on main) replaced the Side panel composer-prefill bridge with a direct panel open and states that manually entered `/dashboard` commands continue to work. They still do as leading commands.
3. The Gateway already follows this rule. #200458 (merged 2026-11-18 as commit `748d6f8cda9` on main, co-authored by @Patrick-Erichsen) recognizes commands, directives and shortcuts only when the sender text starts with `/`, and names this PR as the Control UI companion needed for consistent behavior on every surface. The published slash-command docs already say that a mid-sentence mention such as `Please explain /status` does not run a shortcut. Without this PR, Control UI is the only surface where a mid-sentence `/think high` still runs, because the composer cuts it out and sends it as a leading command.

Tradeoff: someone who types a complete inline command without using the menu (`hello /think high` + Enter) now sends it as prose. To run it they pick the command from the menu, which opens while they type `/thi`, or put the command at the start of the message. Nothing in the product hints at this beyond the menu itself.

Narrower option considered: keep typed dispatch for an allowlist (for example only `/dashboard`, or every command except `/goal`). Not taken, because the same data loss remains for every allowlisted command (`Please explain /dashboard release health` would still run), and it would contradict the Gateway rule from #200458.

How to reverse: revert this PR. The change is limited to the Control UI composer (`findDirectInlineSlashArgumentInvocation`, `beginDirectInlineSlashArgument` and the `allowsInlineMultiWordArgs` metadata), with no config, state or protocol changes and no migration. To restore only the `/dashboard` case, bring the scanner back gated on the `INLINE_MULTI_WORD_COMMANDS` set.

## Evidence

Real Gateway capture: the built Control UI served by a real `openclaw gateway run` (isolated state dir, loopback, no channels, no model), driven by Chromium at 1280 x 900, light theme. Same input, `Please explain /goal prompt`, then Enter.

| | Base `f24c2097` | This PR `bf0fe53c` |
|---|---|---|
| WebSocket frame sent | `chat.send` with message `/goal prompt` | `chat.send` with message `Please explain /goal prompt` |
| Transcript | user bubble `/goal prompt` | user bubble `Please explain /goal prompt` |
| Composer after Enter | `Please explain` left behind | empty |

<details>
<summary>Capture details</summary>

Gateway config: `{"gateway":{"mode":"local","bind":"loopback","auth":{"mode":"none"},"controlUi":{"root":"<ui build of the commit>"}}}`, started with `node openclaw.mjs gateway run --bind loopback --allow-unconfigured`, using `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` in a temp dir. The base UI was built at `f24c2097` with `pnpm ui:build`. The head was built with `pnpm build`. The capture recorded every outgoing WebSocket frame for `chat.send` and `sessions.goal*`.

Recorded frames:

```
base: {"method":"chat.send","params":{"sessionKey":"agent:main:main","message":"/goal prompt","deliver":false}}
head: {"method":"chat.send","params":{"sessionKey":"agent:main:main","message":"Please explain /goal prompt","deliver":false}}
```

</details>

### Before

Enter sends `/goal prompt` on its own and leaves `Please explain` in the composer (built UI, same 1280 x 900 light-theme flow).

![Before: slash command extracted from ordinary prose](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b69bb2eb-b2a7-46e5-befa-bd1761ea6331)

### After

Enter sends the complete sentence as one message and clears the composer.

![After: complete sentence sent intact](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d89de961-ff3d-470f-a98b-90d68b0f9d4d)

Tests:

- New Chromium e2e cases (`chat-slash-leading-command.e2e.test.ts`) cover space, newline and tab before `/goal`. Each asserts exactly one `chat.send` with the full draft, no `sessions.goal` call and no Goal mode.
- Unit coverage asserts that the composer never calls the inline command handler for unselected prose, including Enter and the send button with history loading or ready for `Review @Alex /dashboard release health`. The mention offsets are unchanged.
- The menu-selection inline path keeps its existing coverage in `chat-view.test.ts`.
- CI on `bf0fe53c` is green, including `checks-ui` 1/3 to 3/3, `checks-ui-e2e`, types, lint and docs.

### Contributor credit

Mitchell Etzel reported and requested the fix.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/6ea520fe-72fa-4683-9298-4e03e89c3826)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/cd63ae13-6492-467a-a79e-15cb45d23646)
- [Publication preparation](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/af6ab7d7-03e8-423d-9f03-fb106c44f7df)

## Worked on by

- @Patrick-Erichsen
- @etzelm

prs.title: fix: keep Granola meeting import running after a meeting is deleted
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Knowledge plugin's Learn from Granola scribe retries any meeting it left pending, such as one that was still recording during a run. If that meeting is later deleted or unshared in Granola, the retry fails on every run, and the scribe stops before importing anything newer. Meeting import then stays stuck until someone edits the scribe's checkpoint page by hand.

## User Impact

User impact: deleting a Granola note no longer stops Knowledge from importing your other meetings. The scribe records the deleted meeting as `gone` and continues.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scribe's run instructions retried a pending meeting until it was `done` or `no transcript`, with no outcome for a meeting Granola can no longer return. This adds a terminal `gone` checkpoint state: when `get_meetings` reports a pending meeting as not found or inaccessible, the run records it `gone`, skips it from then on, and goes on with the other meetings. Only the instructions change. No code reads the checkpoint's per-meeting states, and the run's closing status rules are unchanged.

## Evidence

Live on the affected Gateway:
- Before: four scheduled runs in a row (Nov 18 18:00 to Nov 19 18:00 PST) ended `Scribe status: failed` because Granola returned `not_found` for one pending meeting. Granola still returns `not_found` for that ID, and the meeting is absent from its meeting list.
- After hot-patching this wording into the installed skill reference, a manual run recorded `gone · Granola get_meetings returned not_found on November 20; deleted or no longer shared.` and finished `Scribe status: on — 5 meetings ingested; 16 already in Knowledge; 1 duplicate recording; 0 pending; 0 without transcript; 12 content pages written or updated; 37 claims written.`

- Later scheduled runs honored the saved outcome: six scheduled runs since (Nov 20 10:00 through Nov 23 18:00 PST) all ended `Scribe status: on`, ingesting 6 more meetings. The checkpoint still holds the meeting as `gone` and no run retried it.

Compatibility with existing checkpoints: `gone` only adds a line state. Existing `done`, `no transcript` and `pending` lines keep their meaning, and no code parses these states. The live checkpoint above was a pre-existing page with 40+ older entries, and the runs read and extended it without rewriting them.

Checks: `oxfmt --check` on the edited file and `git diff --check` pass. A separate reviewer agent found no issues.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

Closes #204420

## What Problem This Solves

<!--

Choosing **Set up** in a provider tab of the chat model picker forgets that provider and opens the generic Models catalog. Users must find the same provider again before connecting it.

## User Impact

<!--

User impact: provider-specific setup opens that provider’s existing connection flow for the source agent. Generic setup and settings-only links retain their behavior; no defaults, credentials, or model selections are changed by opening the flow.

<!--

Carry the active provider through the picker callback and existing provider-aware Settings navigation. The existing connection owner resolves aliases and consumes the route intent; no second dialog or setup owner is introduced.

prs.title: fix: reject special-use IPv6 destinations consistently
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Outbound URL checks can accept special-use IPv6 destinations when the address library assigns them a range name missing from the policy blocklist. Filtering then differs across special-use ranges.

## User Impact

Outbound checks consistently reject these non-global IPv6 destinations. Global unicast, supported IPv4 transition checks, and existing unique-local and benchmark opt-ins remain available. Deployments relying on newly rejected special-use destinations will now see rejection; no configuration migration is required. Inbound Gateway locality retains its established classifications, so the broader outbound rejection grants no additional local pairing trust.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep both decisions in the shared policy owner: an allowlist for outbound IPv6 classification and a separate established range set for inbound locality. Remove the growing outbound blocklist, redundant site-local fallback, and obsolete type-assertion allowance. The earlier review's pairing-locality regression and stale assertion allowance are both repaired.

## Evidence

All evidence below covers `cfdd443b9d86a12837b65c6af9e32fc09006b25f` on Linux with Node 24.20.0. The source and pushed head are unchanged since the 459-test focused validation.

**Real shipped CLI → Gateway → Chromium:** started a task-owned, authenticated loopback Gateway and isolated headless Chromium profile with strict browser SSRF policy. Actual `pnpm openclaw browser` calls rejected newly blocked IPv6 destinations, then the same browser tab successfully loaded a public HTTPS IP-literal endpoint. No mocked Gateway, DNS, HTTP transport, or browser was used in this run.

```text
pnpm openclaw browser --browser-profile proof --json start
  running=true cdpReady=true pageReady=true
pnpm openclaw browser --browser-profile proof --json open https://1.1.1.1/cdn-cgi/trace
  targetId returned
pnpm openclaw browser --browser-profile proof --json navigate 'http://[2620:4f:8000::1]/' --target-id <owned-tab>
  exit 1: browser navigation blocked by policy
pnpm openclaw browser --browser-profile proof --json navigate 'http://[2001:3::1]/' --target-id <owned-tab>
  exit 1: browser navigation blocked by policy
pnpm openclaw browser --browser-profile proof --json navigate 'http://[5f00::1]/' --target-id <owned-tab>
  exit 1: browser navigation blocked by policy
pnpm openclaw browser --browser-profile proof --json navigate https://1.1.1.1/cdn-cgi/trace --target-id <owned-tab>
  ok=true
pnpm openclaw browser --browser-profile proof --json snapshot --target-id <owned-tab>
  actual page marker h=1.1.1.1 observed
```

The owned browser/Gateway were stopped and port claims released afterward. Strict browser mode's existing hostname restriction required the IP-literal positive control; it was retained throughout the run. The temporary Chromium profile used headless/no-sandbox operation in this container and imported no user browser profile.

**Guarded HTTP runtime:** called production `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without a `fetchImpl` or `lookupFn` override. Six special-use literals (`2001:3::1`, `2001:4:112::1`, `2001:10::1`, `2001:30::1`, `5f00::1`, `2620:4f:8000::1`) each threw `SsrFBlockedError` with zero `beforeRequest` transport admissions. A real DNS/TLS request to `https://example.com/` returned HTTP 200 and `Example Domain`, with one transport admission. This also passed using the existing destination exceptions read by the candidate CLI from the stable config.

**Pairing and settings:** the production pairing-locality and silent-approval decisions classified those six supplied remote addresses as `remote`/`silent=false`, while `172.17.0.1` retained `browser_container_local`/`silent=true`. This uses supplied connection metadata, not a real remote IPv6 socket. ULA opt-in remained effective while cloud metadata stayed blocked.

The integrity-verified published `2026.11.7` package was installed in an isolated proof directory. Its real CLI accepted a config containing the existing `allowRfc2544BenchmarkRange`, `allowIpv6UniqueLocalRange`, and `allowedHostnames` settings. The candidate CLI validated and read that existing config and a fresh identical config. Both retained the same values and exact config SHA-256 `2b5a5e98e5cf0b39fa85b4ba3d04cd1d34d11a552fd8fe98533b826ba15131ca`. This proves settings compatibility across runtime replacement; it does not claim the full package-updater lifecycle.

**Focused checks:** seven files, 459 tests passed in 33.62 seconds. The added policy and pairing regressions failed before their respective repairs and passed afterward. `pnpm tsgo:core`, focused oxlint with `--openclaw-focused-config`, five-file format check, `git diff --check`, and the native assertion-safety ratchet passed. Changed test-file durations: policy 12.62 seconds; handshake is within the 6.81-second Gateway group. CI time for the seven focused files is not reported separately.

The current-head UI shard failure is unrelated: three `sidebar-complete-roster` cases time out in an unchanged browser DOM-scrolling helper under a mocked Gateway. UI production/fixture code is byte-identical to the base; no changed network-policy decision runs in the failing loop. prs.title: fix(release): simplify validation waiver policy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An approved release-validation waiver could still require a run or a particular outcome. The old matcher also required releases to encode failure-log signatures and aggregate causes.

## User Impact

- A frozen-Q grant has `targetVersion`, optional `targetSha`, `childRole`, and `reason`. Omit `jobName` to waive the whole role and its descendants before dispatch, lookup, or reuse, with no required run identity or receipt.
- Specify `jobName` to waive only that job regardless of whether it ran or how it concluded. Add `step` to require an exact match on the first incomplete or failed step of a non-success job. Missing or mismatched step evidence does not waive it.
- Waived is not passed: raw conclusions stay unchanged. Unwaived job coverage, release lineage, inputs, and receipt integrity remain required. No grants are added to main.

## Implementation and retained evidence

One matcher evaluates authenticated frozen-Q grants across dispatch, Decision/Drain, publication, reuse, and recovery. Recovery authenticates the applicable policy before looking for child witnesses and receipts. Passing jobs no longer record unused exceptions. Retained composites must match either the exact current projection or the exact v1 projection without step names, including its digest; exact-step waivers still use authenticated live attempt evidence.

Frozen v1 ledgers remain readable. A plain historical failure-only grant remains failure-only; historical aggregate-, run-, step-, or signature-bound approvals are not promoted to broad grants. Recovering work that requires one of those old selectors under this evaluator needs a newly approved grant and separate Q admission. Qualification exemptions remain distinct.

## Evidence

- The real dispatch shell with a GitHub stub called GitHub on main and skipped the child without calling GitHub on the patch. The focused workflow tests exercise both admitted-P and legacy evaluator routes. No live workflow was dispatched.
- The original pass verified 707 core cases and 39 targeted workflow cases across focused runs, with overlap. The broad package workflow run did not complete; the affected dispatch cases passed separately.
- The [hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204382#issuecomment-7122021186) prompted regressions for frozen ledgers and manifests, exact retained child receipt hashes, and undispatched whole-child recovery. The affected suites passed 500 cases locally; 123 focused cases were rerun after fixture-only lint and typing edits. Scripts and both test typechecks, changed-file lint and formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The published tree matches the local tree.

prs.title: fix(gateway): record Tailscale Control UI sources without a paired browser key
prs.body:
## Problem

A durable `exec` (background) completion that ends after a Gateway restart wakes its chat as a session-principal system turn. For a person who uses the Control UI through Tailscale Serve on a Gateway without named roles, that wake was refused with `Session principal has no current run authority.`. The completion never reached the chat (`exec: completion delivery failed`). A new message from the same person in the same chat was admitted.

## Root cause

- A session-principal turn after a restart has no live socket. It is admitted only through the person's recorded source (`session-operator-sources.ts`: `recordSessionOperatorSource` on each `chat.send`, `restoreSessionOperatorSource` on the wake). If no source was recorded and the profile has no role, `readScopes` refuses.
- Tailscale Serve skips Control UI pairing (`connect-policy.ts`: `shouldSkipControlUiPairing` → `"tailscale-device"`). So a desktop browser presents a device key that is never paired.
- `captureGatewayOperatorRecoverySnapshot` looks up that key in the pairing store for tokenless proxy/Tailscale sources. If it found no row, it returned `unavailableReason: "device-no-token"`. So every message from such a browser had no recovery snapshot, and the session never recorded a source.
- Evidence from the incident Gateway (read-only): 180 of 180 recorded sources are `tailscale` with no `device`. The affected chat (used only from a desktop browser) had no `operatorSources` at all, after 12 prompts.

The brief's hypothesis (an OpenClaw ID linked-owner device, `isLinkedOwnerDevice`) is disproved: OpenClaw ID is disabled on that Gateway. The person connects with Tailscale identity auth.

## Change

Delete the `sourceDevice && tokenlessIdentity && !device` refusal (production −3). A tokenless Tailscale/proxy source whose key has no pairing row is recorded like a device-less Tailscale source, as #202513 already specified: "Device-less proxy/Tailscale scopes use the current grant." Restore checks the auth method, identity grant and browser origin against the current config, the same checks a new connection gets. A paired key is still recorded and still re-checked (revoke/remove → refused). A pairing-store read failure still yields no snapshot.

No new flag, token, stored field or guard.

## What the user sees

A durable exec that finishes after a Gateway restart now posts its completion turn to a Tailscale Control UI chat, as it did before the restart. A person with no recorded source and no role is still refused (unchanged; `admits an untiered person's session work only through their recorded, current source`).

## Accepted edge case

A trusted-proxy Control UI key removed from pairing between connect and the first `chat.send` admission records a device-less source. Removing a device invalidates its live sockets, and admission checks `client.invalidated`, so this needs a race inside one request.

## Why not Tailscale-only

A tokenless trusted-proxy key has no pairing row at capture only when (a) its connection skipped pairing (`skipLocalBackendSelfPairing`), so its live admission did not depend on pairing either, or (b) the device was removed after connect. Removal invalidates its sockets (`invalidateClientsForDevice` → `readGatewayDeviceSourceAuthority`), so admission refuses before capture. In both cases a device-less record admits the wake exactly when a new message would be admitted. Limiting the change to Tailscale would need a new `authMethod` guard, so I did not add one.

## Tests

- New, red on base, green on head: `session-operator-sources.test.ts` › "admits a restart wake for a Tailscale Control UI person whose browser key was never paired". It admits a new message through `prepareGatewayOperatorRunAuthority`, records it with `recordSessionOperatorSource`, then admits the wake with `prepareSessionPrincipalRunAuthority({ sessionPrincipal: true })`. Base fails at the wake with `Session principal has no current run authority.`; disabling Tailscale auth still refuses the wake.
- `bash-process-durable-notify.test.ts`: unchanged. It covers only target preparation (`prepareAdoptedDurableProcessNotification`), which never reaches admission, so changing its principal could not catch this.

## Evidence

- Red on base, green on head: the new test (see Tests).
- Pre-push, one `ocx test` call, 12 files (touched + importers of the changed source + test-support importers): 410 tests passed. Typecheck core + core tests, oxfmt and oxlint pass. `check:changed`: only the dead-export scan fails, on `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-read-aloud-status.tsx` (not in this diff).
- E2E `one-admission-e2e/run.sh` on head `780f7d648c7e`: Q (queued input refused visibly), R (running turn finishes), S (Stop cancels) all pass. The `verdict.json` and `results.jsonl` are attached below.
- Gap: a scratch-Gateway Tailscale reproduction needs Tailscale Serve to proxy to it, which would change the host's live Serve route. The red-on-base test drives the real admission path instead: new-message admission → record → session-principal wake.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

The exec outcome should be written to the session history before the wake, so a refused or failed wake cannot lose it. This needs more than the admission fix; it belongs to the owed-result slice (W4, #204265).

## What Problem This Solves

Context compaction adds a prominent system divider to the Control UI transcript. In longer sessions, repeated dividers interrupt the conversation for something that belongs with the agent’s work.

## User Impact

Compaction appears inline with tool activity. A collapsed turn can read “Read and changed files, ran commands, compacted context,” without operation counts. Manual compaction while the agent is idle gets its own quiet row. A standalone compaction beside a tool uses the same row spacing without gaining a run owner. Expand a row to see token savings when available.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Control UI presents existing compaction events with the existing 16 px Layers icon for both phases, without changing how the Gateway compacts context or adding messages to history. It retains the current count-free summary rules and keeps compaction visible in the OpenAI Worked rollup.

prs.title: fix: let finished background commands reach the agent before an active goal advances
prs.body:
Closes #204187

## What Problem This Solves

With an active Goal, a background command that finishes during a turn can lose its place to the Goal's automatic "Advance the active goal" turn. The agent then advances the Goal before it has read the command result. A Gateway restart between a command's exit and its completion turn also loses the result, because the result exists only in memory.

## User Impact

User impact: a finished background command always reaches the agent before an active Goal advances, and a Gateway restart no longer loses a command result that was waiting for its turn.

- After a restart, the completion turn runs with the session principal's current authority. The original channel owner's owner-only tools do not carry across the restart; durable outcomes already behave this way.
- Completions that arrive while an earlier completion turn runs still share one turn (#199113).

## Why This Change Was Made

The exec result becomes stored state when the command exits (first slice of the owed-result model):

- New `src/sessions/owed.ts`. `owe(item)` is the only writer of new owed rows. It stores the result in the existing `session_pending_inputs` table, with `kind: "exec"` and `originFacts` (requester, command owner, operator profile id) as additive JSON in the row message. There is no schema change. `shouldWake(chat)` reads stored rows: it is true while the chat has owed rows that no live turn holds. Consumption does not read `originFacts` yet; a later slice intersects it with current policy without a migration.
- The exec wake turn adopts its owed row by id (the turn's input idempotency key) and writes its own bytes into it. Before a shared batch turn starts, `fold` writes the joined text into the first member's row and consumes the other members' rows in one transaction, so a restart at any point replays each result once. If the fold fails, the shared turn is refused and each member retries its own row. The transcript append consumes the row in the same transaction, so a second consumer or a retry after restart appends nothing.
- Goal continuation calls `shouldWake` and does not advance while an owed result is pending. The completion turn runs first, and its end continues the Goal.
- One wake path, `wakeOwedExec`, serves the live wake, its single retry and restart recovery. A wake that fails before it becomes a turn, or is refused at enqueue, retries once from the stored row; the live retry keeps the captured target, so admission revalidates the requester's authority. A stop, or a second failure, ends the row with a visible cause. Restart recovery wakes owed rows, which it used to refuse as queued human input.

| Part | Files | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| Deleted in-memory exec path | `bash-tools.exec-notify.ts`: the `pendingExitWakes` set and its reads, `enqueueExecExitNotification`, and the separate settle/log block (`hasExecYieldWake` and the yield sweep now read stored rows) | −46 |
| Shrunk to stay under the line cap | `session-accessor.pending-inputs.ts`: two duplicated "already consumed" receipts become `consumedPendingInputReceipt` (moved to `session-pending-input-value.ts`) | +26 −33 |
| Owed primitive | `sessions/owed.ts` (`owe`, `fold`, `shouldWake`, `readPendingOwed`, `withhold`: +200); `session-pending-input-value.ts` (`readOwedKind`, owed restage, moved receipt: +44); owed-row adoption in `session-accessor.pending-input-request.ts` (+18 −2); absorbed-row consumption in both pending-input kernels and the mutation type (+32) | +294 −2 |
| Glue | `bash-tools.exec-notify.ts` (`wakeOwedExec`, settlement, owed row with origin facts: +104); `session-event-batch.ts` (fold before a shared turn, one refusal path: +68 −15); `queued-chat-inputs.ts` restart wake (+22 −1); `goal-continuation.ts` (+11); `session-yield-sweep.ts` (+4 −1) | +209 −17 |
| **Production total** | 12 files | **+529 −98 (net +431)** |

No parallel in-memory exec-completion path is left. Every exec completion, live or after restart, is an owed row delivered by `wakeOwedExec`. What remains in memory is the shared session-event admission that runs the turn for every producer (cron, hooks, plugins). Its occurrence still carries a copy of the text; that copy can go when session-event admission reads stored rows for all producers, in later owed-result slices. The cron yield-resume path (`execYieldResumes`) is a different consumer and stays out of this slice.

## Evidence

- **Race, deterministic:** a new `server.chat-goal.test.ts` case holds the real exec wake in target preparation until the first turn's Goal check runs. It is red on the merge base (Advance overtakes the completion) and green on head.
- **No deadlock:** a new case makes the first wake fail in preparation; the stored row wakes the completion turn and the Goal then advances. The existing "keeps pursuing after … exec completion" cases end every completion turn before a model call; they stay green.
- **Shared turn:** a new case refuses a shared completion turn before admission; both results are still delivered afterwards. A storage case shows `fold` leaves exactly one row carrying both results; it is red when the absorbed rows are not consumed (both rows remain, so a restart would deliver the second result twice).
- **Storage:** a new pending-input case is red without the kind-preserving restage (restart recovery would refuse an adopted row) and green on head.
- **Touched suites:** exec background follow-up (28/28, shared-turn cases included), yield sweep (6/6), and the pending-input, queued-input, Goal continuation, session-event and restart-resume suites (19 files, 284 tests).
- **Real Gateway, scratch port and state, real model:** an exec result pending in `session_pending_inputs` across a Gateway restart is appended to the transcript exactly once after the restart (5 runs). On head `0abfb478`, which differs from the final head only in the batch's fold-failure path, the same run also shows `Exec completed` before `[System] Advance the active goal` (with #204327 merged).
- **Repeat runs (final head `4b887e10`, frozen copy):** `server.chat-goal.test.ts` as a whole file, 20 separate runs: 20/20 passed with 72/72 each (1,440 test executions). Both "keeps pursuing after … takes the next turn" variants passed in every run (40/40).

Separate bug, fixed and merged in #204327 (issue #204319): on a real Gateway, a Goal did not advance after a background command's completion turn. Post-turn session maintenance waited in the mailbox and the Goal check deferred to it. This happens on `main` too. A plain Goal advances normally on `main`; an earlier note here that it never advanced came from a bad test prompt. With #204327 the real-Gateway transcript reads: Goal request → `Exec completed …` → `[System] Advance the active goal …`.

prs.title: fix: show a Template's image as soon as its new agent's chat opens
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When you add a Template, OpenClaw opens the new agent's chat straight away, but for about five seconds the sidebar shows a generated placeholder face for that agent. It then swaps to the agent's real avatar once setup has written it. The agent you just picked from the catalog looks like a different agent while you wait.

## User Impact

User impact: the Template's catalog image appears as the new agent's avatar as soon as its chat opens, and stays until the agent's own avatar is ready.

Templates that have no image on ClawHub are unchanged: they still show the generated face until their own avatar is saved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog has already loaded and decoded the Template's image by the time Add is clicked. The pending chat now carries that image, and the sidebar shows it for that one agent until the agent has an avatar of its own. Nothing new is fetched, and no other agent's avatar is affected.

## Evidence

The same Template (Meta Ads Agent 0.1.1) was added through the real Control UI on an isolated Gateway with a real model. Both frames are two seconds after clicking Add. Before is `main` at `86fcb81e64c0`; after is this branch at `b79ff995b186`; the later commit changes only how long the image is retained.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: sidebar shows a generated pink face for the new agent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/442f753e-93a8-4cf0-b2aa-1c9c6767dcd8) | ![After: sidebar shows the Template's own image for the new agent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bfa46303-1786-4433-bab7-bfe3626f4825) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Generated face highlighted in the sidebar](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3e1f26cf-4920-44bd-9182-13a6545d5cd8) | ![Template image highlighted in the sidebar](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a2d4ba89-f961-4fba-aab2-0168eab48a89) |

Across the recording, the generated face was visible for about 4.8 seconds before this change and not at all after it. A single-frame flicker at the moment the agent's own avatar loads is still there, as it was before.

The image is offered for as long as its catalog card is mounted, so a card that is still on screen keeps its image however many others load after it.

Checked locally: the card-Add browser test now asserts that the sidebar shows the Template's image while the agent is created. It fails on `main` (no image appears) and passes on this branch, along with the other 28 catalog browser tests. The sidebar display tests cover the handoff to the agent's own avatar and that another agent's chip never borrows the image. `pnpm check:changed` passes apart from the dead-export scan, which currently fails on `main` for unrelated files.

The earlier `checks-ui (3/3)` failure on `b79ff995b186` was `model-control.test.ts > does not borrow a provider for an ambiguous draft target`, in code this change does not touch.

prs.title: feat: transcribe voice notes through Vercel AI Gateway
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

People who use Vercel AI Gateway for their models have no way to transcribe voice notes or audio attachments through it. OpenClaw's Vercel AI Gateway plugin only handles chat models, so voice notes need a separate OpenAI, ElevenLabs or other transcription key. If that separate account runs out of credit, voice notes quietly stop working, even though the AI Gateway key is still fine and AI Gateway already serves transcription models.

## User Impact

People who already use Vercel AI Gateway can transcribe voice notes and audio attachments with the same key they use for chat. Any AI Gateway transcription model works, for example `openai/gpt-transcribe` (the default), `openai/gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, `elevenlabs/scribe-v2` or `microsoft/mai-transcribe-2`. When no audio model is configured, AI Gateway joins the automatic provider order next to OpenRouter. Nothing changes for anyone who doesn't use AI Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

AI Gateway has no OpenAI-style `/v1/audio/transcriptions` route; it returns 404. It does serve transcription through its native endpoint, `POST /v4/ai/transcription-model`, which is the one `@ai-sdk/gateway`'s `GatewayTranscriptionModel` calls. The plugin now registers an audio media-understanding provider that sends that same request: the same headers, a body of base64 `audio` plus `mediaType`, and a response read from `text`.

`language`, `prompt` and per-entry options go in AI SDK `providerOptions`, keyed by the model's provider prefix: `elevenlabs/scribe-v2` → `elevenlabs`.

Accepted edge case: an option name has to match what that provider's AI SDK integration accepts. Unknown names are sent through unchanged, with no per-provider renaming.

Text-to-speech through AI Gateway's native `speech-model` endpoint will be a separate follow-up PR.

## Evidence

- The new provider tests check:
  - the exact request: URL, headers including `ai-model-id`, and body
  - WhatsApp-style `audio/ogg; codecs=opus` being normalized to `audio/ogg`
  - the media type inferred from the file name when no mime type is given
  - options keyed by provider
  - a refusal to call the Gateway when the media type can't be resolved
  - missing `text` and 401 errors surfacing as failures
- All plugin tests pass (17/17), and so do the plugin contract suites (1036 + 62).
- Clean: extension typecheck (source and tests), oxlint, plugin SDK boundary lints, docs formatting, and the pre-commit hook.
- I checked the wire protocol against `@ai-sdk/gateway@4.0.154`: the headers `ai-gateway-protocol-version: 0.0.1`, `ai-transcription-model-specification-version: 4` and `ai-model-id`, plus the `{ audio, mediaType }` body and `{ text, ... }` response.
- `/v1/audio/transcriptions` on `ai-gateway.vercel.sh` returns 404 today. `/v4/ai/transcription-model` returns 401 to a request without a valid key, so the route exists.
- **Live, real key (OpenClaw 2026.11.1, this adapter loaded as a local plugin, `tools.media.models` = `vercel-ai-gateway/openai/gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`):**
  ```
  $ openclaw infer audio --agent main transcribe --file voice.ogg --json
  { "ok": true, "capability": "audio.transcribe", "provider": "vercel-ai-gateway",
    "model": "openai/gpt-4o-mini-transcribe",
    "outputs": [{ "text": "Hello, class. Good morning.", "kind": "audio.transcription" }] }
  ```
  An inbound WhatsApp voice note (`audio/ogg; codecs=opus`) then went through the normal reply pipeline and reached the agent as `[Audio transcript]: "Testing, one, two, three."`.
- **Review follow-up (a5eebf9a6):**
  - **Token Pass / scoped keys:** the provider now uses `transcribeAudioWithContext`. It resolves the key, then checks that the transcription model is in that key's own `/v1/models` list (cached 5 min, keyed by credential) before uploading. Missing key, unlisted model, or an unreadable list returns the pre-upload rejection, so automatic selection moves on to the next transcriber. Upload/HTTP failures still throw. `isAudioConfigured` reports readiness from credential resolution only, with no network call.
  - **ElevenLabs language:** the standard `language` hint maps to `languageCode` for `elevenlabs/*`, and stays `language` elsewhere.
  - **Tests:** removed the 401-only case. Added `media-understanding-provider.eligibility.test.ts`, which covers an eligible upload, a scoped key rejected before upload, a same-id non-transcription row, an unreadable list, a missing credential, and readiness.
  - **Gates:** 23/23 `extensions/vercel-ai-gateway` tests, `test:contracts:plugins`, `tsgo:extensions` (+test), oxlint, oxfmt, `format:docs:check`, all `lint:extensions:no-*`, `plugins:inventory:check` (reference page regenerated).
- **Review follow-up 2 (151c1d20a):**
  - **Every rotation key is preflighted:** `collectProviderApiKeysForExecution` can add environment-configured keys after the primary. Each collected key now goes through the same `/v1/models` eligibility check before rotation starts. The primary key must be eligible, or the call returns the pre-upload rejection as before. Secondary keys that are scoped or whose list can't be read are dropped, so a 429 on the primary rotates straight to the next eligible key instead of uploading with a Token Pass key and stopping on its 403. Upload failures still throw.
  - **Tests:** two new cases. One has an eligible primary, then a scoped key, then an eligible key: a 429 on the primary rotates to the third key and never uploads with the scoped one. This test fails on a5eebf9a6 and passes now. The other has only the primary scoped, and it is rejected before upload.
  - **Gates:** 25/25 `extensions/vercel-ai-gateway` tests, `test:contracts:plugins`, `tsgo:extensions` (+test), oxlint, oxfmt, all `lint:extensions:no-*`, `plugins:inventory:check`.
- **Still open:** no real Token Pass key on hand, so the scoped-key skip and rotation filtering are proven by unit tests only. Automatic audio enrollment (priority 35, no explicit media model) needs a maintainer decision, as ClawSweeper notes.

prs.title: fix(plugin-sdk): keep bundled runtime and control helpers private (forward-port)
prs.body:
## Problem
Two plugin-SDK fixes shipped on the previous beta release line (v2026.11.10-beta.2/.3) but were never forward-ported to main:
- `38174c247574` (from `ee62d322efa7`)
- `af33507cf50e`

The `2026.11.15-beta.1` cut came from main, so it exposes five helpers again as public SDK exports. They are unshipped and only bundled plugins use them. They add to the plugin-SDK surface-budget failure in the initial beta full release validation run.

## Solution
I cherry-picked both fixes with `-x`, keeping original authorship and provenance.
- **`38174c247574`:** moves the agent-harness runtime-update error and the command-menu catalog loader to their existing private facades.
- **`af33507cf50e` (partial):** moves three agent-control helpers to a private facade. It migrates their callers on main in the Discord, Slack, Telegram, Feishu, LINE, Mattermost and MS Teams plugins, and regenerates package exports and declaration aliases.
- **Intentionally excluded:** the reply-conflict classifier part of `af33507cf50e`. `reply-runtime.isReplySessionInitConflictError` ships as public API in stable v2026.11.7, so it stays public.

Feature behavior is unchanged, no shipped public API is removed, and the docs are updated for the moved entrypoints.

## Evidence
- The owning surface check shows public exports going from 3,919 to 3,914 and callables from 2,255 to 2,251. Entrypoints stay at 164, deprecated exports at 222, and deprecated `agent-runtime` exports at 16. The check reports no unauthorized shipped API removals.
- The surface check still exits nonzero on the same five budget categories that already fail on base. No limits were changed; the remaining overage is a separate owner decision.
- 277 tests pass across 20 focused files, including the Telegram HTTP model-callback loopback.
- Targeted typecheck, lint and format pass, along with the package registration and import-subpath guards, the generated SDK boundary declarations and `git diff --check`.
- **Gaps:**
  - The Telegram native-pipeline suite did not run locally. It needs packaged-runtime preparation, which this host refused because it could not confirm isolation from managed Gateway artifacts, and the Podman runner was unavailable.
  - No full package build was verified locally.
  - PR CI must cover both.

## Impact
This reduces the SDK surface-budget overage for the `2026.11.15-beta.1` release repair. It will be backported to `release/2026.11.15` after landing.

## Worked on by

- @RomneyDa

prs.title: improve: simplify failed replies above the chat composer
prs.body:
Related: #204337

## What Problem This Solves

When a reply fails and its in-thread notice is unavailable, the banner above the composer replaces the actual error with a generic title and subtitle. Reading what happened takes a separate **Show details** control, and the card takes three rows above the composer.

## User Impact

The composer shows the redacted error itself on one line, with no generic copy. A long error is cut off with an ellipsis; select the line, or the chevron beside it, to read all of it in place, and select again to close it. The chevron appears on hover or keyboard focus and stays visible on touch screens. A short error that already fits has no chevron. **Refresh** reloads history without resending or changing the draft, and sign-in failures still offer **Open Models**.

## Why This Change Was Made

The notice renders the received error once instead of inventing a summary for it. One line keeps the card as small as the other cards above the composer, on phones too. Opened text wraps beside the actions and then uses the full card width, so it stays readable on a narrow screen while Refresh and dismiss keep their place in the card. Selecting the text to copy it does not close it.

Rewording individual upstream errors is out of scope. In-thread failures, Stop errors, and request or startup notices are unchanged. Reporting a bug remains available from Help.

The card sits above the composer, so it grows upward when opened. An opened error has no height limit of its own; the composer's context area already scrolls as one stack.

## Evidence

The bundled Control UI was exercised in Chromium with synthetic Gateway data at 1280 px and at 400 px with touch emulation. The checks cover the one-line cut-off, the chevron hidden until hover and always visible on touch, opening by click, tap and keyboard, actions keeping their position in the card, Refresh preserving the draft without resending, and redaction. Component checks in Chromium at 820, 400 and 300 px cover a short error with no control, opened text using the width under the actions, text selection, and a replacement error closing the line.

62 browser flow tests across the nine affected suites, 7 Chromium component tests, and 33 unit tests passed. UI typecheck, lint, stylesheet lint, locale verification, the controller guard, formatting, and diff checks passed. Full CI, the paired UI performance budget, Safari, Firefox, physical phones, and live-provider failures were not run.

## Visual proof

Chromium light-mode captures of the actual Control UI with synthetic Gateway data, cropped around the composer. Baseline: `4708bac523976`; candidate: `be578e0dc5cdc`. The candidate uses a longer synthetic error to show the cut-off; the baseline hides the error either way, so its capture is unaffected.

### Clean comparison

**After**

prs.title: fix(cli): keep input-validation remedies visible for guards outside the runtime wrapper
prs.body:
Closes #200142

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw models auth login --device-code --method password` fails with only `The CLI command failed.` and `For help, run \`openclaw doctor\`.` — the guard's actual remedy ("--device-code cannot be combined with --method unless method is device-code.") is computed but never shown, so the user cannot tell what to change. This routes all six input-validation guards that sit outside the runtime wrapper — every guard site enumerated in #200142 — through the existing expected-error contract so their remedy text reaches the terminal.

The reported symptom and reproduction are consolidated in #200142 (reproduction comment covers the three commands shown in the Evidence table below). #199970 fixed the shared wrapper for commands registered through `runCommandWithRuntime`; these guards run before that wrapper (argument parsing / target resolution), so they still threw plain `Error`s whose messages the failure renderer hides. #200167 was a prior attempt at this same narrowed scope.

- Problem: `SessionTargetParseError` extended plain `Error`, and the double-target, inconsistent-ownership, ambiguous-session, missing-session, and device-code/method-conflict guards used `throw new Error(...)`. The CLI failure renderer treats these as unexpected errors and prints only the generic failure line plus a doctor hint, hiding the remedy the guard already wrote.
- Solution: classify these guards as expected CLI errors using the existing contract — `SessionTargetParseError` now extends `ExpectedCliError` (message/humanOutput/machineOutput all set to the existing help text), and the five `throw new Error(...)` sites in `session-target.ts` and `models-cli.ts` now call `throwExpectedCliError(...)` with the same strings.
- What changed: `src/cli/session-ref.ts` (error base class), `src/cli/session-target.ts` (4 throw sites), `src/cli/models-cli.ts` (1 throw site); regression coverage folded into the existing `session-ref.test.ts` and `models-cli.test.ts` cases (test delta -1 lines).
- What did NOT change: no guard message text, no exit codes (still 1), no stdout, no validation logic or accepted inputs; `shapeTargetError` (Gateway-side request errors such as "No session found: <id>") is deliberately untouched — those are server-reported failures, not local input-validation remedies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Best fix: reuse the expected-error contract that #199970 already established as the owner for "user-facing remedy must survive the failure renderer", instead of adding a second printing path. The guards keep their exact messages; only the error classification changes, which is the smallest diff that makes the remedy visible on the real shipped CLI.

Alternative(s) considered: (a) teaching the failure renderer to print `error.message` for all errors — rejected because it would leak internal stack reasons for genuinely unexpected failures, which the renderer hides on purpose; (b) moving these guards inside `runCommandWithRuntime` — rejected because they must run before runtime setup (target parsing happens before a runtime exists).

Risk: expected errors print `humanOutput` directly even under `OPENCLAW_DEBUG=1`, so these six guards no longer emit the debug `Reason:`/`Error:` lines they previously produced (shown in Evidence). This matches how every other expected CLI error already behaves. No config, schema, or protocol change.

## User Impact

Users who hit these six guards now see the actionable remedy instead of a generic failure: the device-code/method conflict rule, the "pass one target" rule, the accepted session-target forms, the inconsistent-ownership message, the ambiguous-session candidate table, and the missing-session hint. Exit codes, stdout, and all valid inputs are unchanged. Under `OPENCLAW_DEBUG=1` these specific failures now print just the remedy line (same as other expected errors) rather than a debug reason block.

## Evidence

| Case | Before (base 766f615) | After (this head 35b6f01) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `models auth login --device-code --method password` | stderr `The CLI command failed.` + doctor hint; remedy hidden; exit 1 | stderr `--device-code cannot be combined with --method unless method is device-code.`; exit 1 |
| `attach <session-url> --url <gateway-url>` (two targets) | stderr `The CLI command failed.` + doctor hint; remedy hidden; exit 1 | stderr `pass one target: use either the session URL or --url, not both`; exit 1 |
| `attach http://127.0.0.1:18789` (no session ref) | stderr `The CLI command failed.` + doctor hint; accepted-forms help hidden; exit 1 | full accepted-session-targets help printed; exit 1 |
| `models list --agent typo` (control) | `Unknown agent id "typo". Use "openclaw agents list" to see configured agents.`; exit 1 | byte-identical stdout+stderr (`cmp`), exit 1 |
| `models list --agent ""` and `--json` variant (control) | `--agent must not be blank`; exit 1 | byte-identical (`cmp`), exit 1 |
| `attach x --session y` (control) | `pass one session target: use either the positional target or --session`; exit 1 | byte-identical (`cmp`), exit 1 |
| `tui --history-limit 10x` (control) | `--history-limit must be a positive integer.`; exit 1 | byte-identical (`cmp`), exit 1 |

All six control cells (four commands, `--agent ""` and `--agent typo` each in text and JSON modes) are byte-identical across arms after filtering two environment-inherent warning lines described below; the three harm cells have byte-identical stdout and differ only in the stderr remedy (c4/c4b stdout is empty; the login cell prints the same 173-byte installed-service-paths-unverified warning on both arms, a consequence of the isolated scratch environment).

### End-to-end shipped proof (both arms built from source)

prs.title: fix: let Ask OpenClaw show channel guides on multi-agent gateways
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a gateway with several agents and none marked as the default, asking Ask OpenClaw for `channel info slack` or the channel list fails with "Multiple agents are configured… Select an agent explicitly". This happens even when `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId` names the owner, and naming the agent in chat doesn't help because the channel read tools take no agent.

## User Impact

User impact: Ask OpenClaw lists channels and shows channel setup guides (including the Docs link) on multi-agent gateways that set `agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId`. Single-agent gateways behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The system agent's channel reads called channel discovery without an owner workspace. Discovery then fell back to the deprecated default-agent lookup, which ignores the configured system agent and throws when there are multiple agents. These reads now pass the workspace from `resolveChannelSetupWorkspaceDir`. That is the resolver the in-chat `connect <channel>` flow already uses (`setupChannels` via hosted setup), so the list and info output match what `connect` will set up. It resolves the owner from `systemAgent.agentId` first, then the legacy owner or the sole agent, and it is the same ambient-owner rule the system-agent overview uses.

The shared discovery and CLI owner fallbacks are left unchanged on purpose. They serve CLI paths with different semantics and are being audited separately.

## Evidence

- New regression test `src/system-agent/operations.channel-reads.test.ts` keeps the real owner and workspace resolution. It checks channel info (Docs line) and channel list for (a) a multi-agent explicit-ownership config with `systemAgent.agentId: main` and no default marker and (b) a sole agent, plus channel info for (c) an invalid config snapshot. On the base commit, case (a) fails with `AgentSelectionRequiredError`. With the fix, all 3 pass, and the test asserts that discovery received the owner's workspace.
- Existing `src/system-agent/operations-parse.test.ts` and `src/agents/tools/system-agent-tool.test.ts` pass (122 tests).
- Live check against a real multi-agent gateway config (4 agents, explicit ownership, `systemAgent.agentId: main`): `channel-info slack` and `channel-list` used to fail with `AgentSelectionRequiredError` and now succeed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck core and core tests, lint, format, architecture and boundary guards all pass. The mock-export ratchet flagged the new test's mocks at first; that is fixed with per-mock isolation notes and the ratchet now passes.
- Autoreview (subagent review): no P0–P2 findings.

### Inherited CI failure

CI run 45313405578 (attempts 1 and 2) fails only `checks-node-changed-1`, and `openclaw/ci-gate` reports that same failure. The cause is 6 timeouts (~121s each) in `src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry.requester-wake.e2e.test.ts`, all under "requester settle wake product flow > settles requester receipts": visible final, transition drift, outcome drift, reply replacement, delivery replacement, empty reply. The same 6 cases fail identically when run locally on this PR's base commit (7cbf1585ed73), which doesn't contain this change. `src/agents/subagents` is untouched by this PR and unchanged between that base and the CI merge base (86fcb81e64c0). This PR lands through the authorized pre-existing-failure route.

prs.title: fix: allow sign-in commands before new-session model setup
prs.body:
Closes #204418

## What Problem This Solves

In New Session, entering an authorized sign-in command such as `/login <provider>` as the first message cannot be sent. The model-setup gate treats it like an ordinary draft and disables Send, so a user with a not-yet-connected provider cannot connect it from a new session. Existing chats already allow model-independent commands.

## User Impact

Model-independent commands (including `/login`) can now be sent before a model account is connected in a new session. Normal drafts still require model setup when needed; the destination and all other submit gates are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveNewSessionSubmitBlock` applied the `model-setup` gate unconditionally when the draft required model setup. The UI already has a single shared predicate, `isModelIndependentChatCommand`, that resolves a command's declared `modelIndependent` policy (the Gateway registers `/login` as `always`). Reusing that predicate here keeps new-session and existing-chat behavior consistent.

## Evidence

The focused `ui/src/pages/new-session/submit-gates.test.ts` suite passes 29/29 with the fix using the repo's UI vitest config. Reverting only `submit-gates.ts` produced one failure: the new test saw `{ gate: "model-setup" }` where no block was expected. The test registers `/login` as a model-independent command and stubs the model-setup requirement, so it isolates exactly this gate.

Limitations: UI typecheck (`tsgo:ui`) reported only pre-existing missing modules in an unrelated package that was not installed in this filtered local environment; no errors referenced the changed files. No browser-based end-to-end run was performed.

## AI assistance

This fix and its tests were prepared with AI assistance and reviewed locally before submission.

prs.title: fix(memory): start default index managers at Gateway boot
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#194164 asks for memory indexing to be fresh right after a Gateway restart:
with the current demand-driven cold start, an agent's index opens on its
first search, flush, or turn, and until then `memory_index_sources`
receives nothing — the reporter observed roughly ten hours of stopped
indexing after an app relaunch.

The original draft of this PR restored eager boot-time indexing for every
configured agent. Review and history showed why that is the wrong default:
#167756 started Memory Core's index service eagerly on every Gateway start,
and #174718 (`6c050f8043`) deliberately reverted it after startup peak RSS
rose from ~1.1 GB to ~1.8 GB (startup catch-up touches every
session-transcript read lane, each spawning its own worker isolate). This
revision keeps that policy intact and adds an explicit operator opt-in
instead:

```jsonc
// memory.search.coldStart
"demand" // default — exactly today's behavior, unchanged
"eager"  // open every configured agent's index at boot and on later service starts
```

Each agent can override the global default with
`agents.entries.<id>.memory.search.coldStart`; the per-agent value wins over
the global setting in both directions, matching how the memory config
resolver treats other `memory.search` fields. Operators who need fresh
indexes immediately (the reporter's local-GGUF fleet) pay a known,
self-inflicted cost; everyone else sees zero change. The demand default, the
`liveIndexing` retention semantics, and the worker/RSS characteristics of
#174718 are untouched.

## The Change

- `memory.search.coldStart` (`"demand"` default | `"eager"`), registered in
  the config schema, field labels/help, and `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`.
- `memory-core-index` service start resolves the opt-in per agent:
  `resolveAgentConfig(cfg, agentId)?.memory?.search?.coldStart ?? global`.
  `"demand"` (effective) keeps `retainMemoryIndexingAgents` exactly as
  before; `"eager"` opens the agent's index through the existing host-aware
  runtime (`memoryRuntime.getMemorySearchManager`, which supplies the host's
  local-service acquisition — resolving the Revision 1 P2 finding). Manager
  construction marks each agent live, so later reloads retain them like any
  watched index.
- Boundary tests on untouched agents (so acquisition cannot be explained by
  prior demand): a per-agent eager override under a global demand default
  opens only that agent; a per-agent demand override under a global eager
  default keeps that agent lazy. Both fail against the previous
  global-only selector.

## Evidence

- **Unit/boundary tests** (worktree, committed source): `extensions/memory-core/index.test.ts` — 35 passed (2 new per-agent cold-start boundary cases; the previous single eager case was rewritten on untouched agents per review), and `src/config` schema regressions (config.schema-regressions, dead-config-keys, schema.hints) — 263 passed after registering the new field.
- **Regression check:** the two new boundary cases fail on the previous
  global-only selector (2 failed | 33 skipped) and pass with the per-agent
  resolution (35 passed).
- **Live redacted output, built from the committed source** (isolated
  state/workspace, local Ollama `nomic-embed-text`, synthetic data; the same
  state is upgraded in place between scenarios):

  ```text
  ===== SCENARIO 1: coldStart demand (default) =====
  gateway ready (demand)
  # memory file written + chat.send delivered, 45s watcher window, no consumer opens an index
  demand: memory_index_sources rows = 0

  ===== SCENARIO 2: upgrade in place -> coldStart eager =====
  gateway ready (eager)
  # same state, settings and sessions intact, 45s after boot, no consumer call
  eager: memory_index_sources rows = 2
      memory|memory/proof-demand-note.md
      sessions|sessions/main/34d590f2-28ad-4c95-91df-bda672a78c92.jsonl
  eager: memory_search -> {"ok":true,"results":[{"path":"memory/proof-demand-note.md",...
  ```

  Scenario 1 confirms the demand default is byte-for-byte unchanged
  (untouched agents stay lazy). Scenario 2 is the reporter's requested
  behavior, available under the explicit opt-in.

- **Latest-stable → candidate upgrade trace (redacted live output):** a
  dedicated run upgrades a state directory created by released
  **v2026.11.3** (npm, `847611d`) to the candidate built from this PR's
  head, covering both the upgrade-compatibility and data-model items:

  ```text
  ## PHASE S — stable v2026.11.3 (847611d), config without any coldStart key
  [stable] consumer memory_search -> {"ok":true,...}   # demand: index opens on first consumer
  [stable-final] memory_index_sources rows: 2          # memory/upgrade-note-a.md
  [stable-final] memory_index_chunks rows: 2           # + sessions/main/ff028686-….jsonl

  ## PHASE C-MIG — candidate refuses unmigrated DB (documented admission guard), then migrates
  "…uses schema version 27; … run openclaw doctor --fix to upgrade it to
   schema version 42 …" | gateway.maintenance_required
  $ openclaw doctor --fix --yes    ->  schema_meta primary = 42
  [post-migration] memory_index_sources: 2  memory_index_chunks: 2   # data survived

  ## PHASE C-A — candidate on migrated stable state, config UNCHANGED (demand default)
  booted healthy; memory_search retrieves the stable-era note
  [candA-final] memory_index_sources: 2                 # demand unchanged: no boot-time growth

  ## PHASE C-B — only delta: memory.search.coldStart = "eager"
  # new file written, then boot with NO consumer call
  [candB] rows BEFORE boot: sources=2 chunks=2
  [candB] rows AFTER eager boot: sources=3 chunks=3     # note B indexed at startup
      memory|memory/upgrade-note-a.md                    # stable-era data intact
      memory|memory/upgrade-note-b.md                    # newly indexed at boot
      sessions|sessions/main/ff028686-….jsonl            # stable-era session intact
  consumer memory_search("Post-upgrade synthetic") -> upgrade-note-b.md
  ```

  Existing settings are preserved (the stable-era config carries no
  `coldStart` key; the candidate boots it unchanged under the demand
  default), the stable-written database migrates via the documented
  `doctor --fix` path and loads/works (schema 27 → 42, index rows,
  session transcript, and provenance intact), demand semantics are
  unchanged after upgrade (no growth without a consumer), and the opt-in
  eager mode works on the upgraded state.

  Data-model note: this change adds an optional config field only — no
  stored index, session, or state format changes; the trace above
  demonstrates the stable-release upgrade end to end.

### November 24 conflict refresh

Integrated upstream main `4708bac52397` into `04af0f2c2c3`. Only the two generated config baselines conflicted. Regenerated both using `pnpm config:docs:gen`.

- `pnpm config:docs:check`, scoped formatting, and `git diff --check` against the integrated main passed.
- Memory Core startup and config schema suites passed, 64 tests across two files.
- The live upgrade traces above are from earlier revisions. This refresh validates the integration with current main. The opt-in startup policy remains open for maintainer review.

prs.body:
Closes #204192

## What Problem This Solves

Git installations retaining the launcher from development build `d44f263` can count `gateway status` as a Gateway start. Repeated status checks can exhaust the startup attempts for a new release and roll back an otherwise healthy Gateway.

## User Impact

User impact: after the candidate performs post-ready maintenance, status checks through the affected legacy launcher no longer consume startup attempts. Admitted `openclaw update repair` also refreshes that launcher. Genuine-start rollback remains available. Custom, resident, unrelated-installation, and read-only launchers are unchanged; this fix does not rewrite update history.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing post-ready maintenance and explicit repair paths share one repair owner. It recognizes the exact legacy executable in the selected, account-owned installation and reuses the existing launcher writer, preserving the old trial and rollback protocol. The next normal release update installs the resident launcher.

The repair remains on this PR's original branch. The earlier incorrectly sourced snapshot has been removed from the main-versus-head diff; this PR now contains only the #204192 fix.

## Evidence

- **Main versus head:** the PR comparison against main uses merge base `766f6157f4d36e7338df8cd7f6934a711bfb1f4b`, which was integrated into the existing branch. Head `8a1c747d41bee220868971fd4bcee826bb167aa6` contains exactly nine intended files, **+406 / -5**, with no unrelated changes. The eight code/test/fixture files retain the existing repair; its documentation note is preserved alongside main's newer notes.
- **Fresh focused tests on the reconciled candidate:** 158 passed across seven files, no failures or skips, Linux / Node 24.20.0. The maintained runner completed three serial shards in 241.69 seconds. Coverage includes diagnostics preserving trial bytes and release selection, genuine-start rollback, admitted CLI repair, and excluded launcher scopes.
- **Fresh static checks:** format passed for eight supported files, lint passed for seven TypeScript files, and the core production, gateway-server, cli-update, and other core-test typecheck graphs all passed. The main-relative diff has no whitespace errors.
- **Simplification and review:** the current complete diff was manually reviewed and pr-simplify retained the single shared repair owner and two existing callers; no extra architecture was added. The earlier P0-only automated review covered the unchanged implementation on its prior base, not a fresh review of this merged head. No broader-priority or completed hosted-review claim is made.
- **Real macOS rollback proof on this exact head:** @daniel-lxs reports that `8a1c747d41bee220868971fd4bcee826bb167aa6` passed on roobook: a real candidate failure exhausted its trial attempts, the updater restored fallback release `2026.11.5` / `d44f263`, removed the trial, and an authenticated RPC succeeded on the fallback. This is supplied live-machine evidence, not an independently executed run by this agent. The earlier own-lane and combined pinned-Git successes remain prior evidence.

The supplied rollback proof covers the requested macOS failure-and-fallback scenario. It is not a full cross-platform release matrix. Exact-head CI and hosted review are recorded separately; no new VM campaign was started here, and #204344 is a separate draft.

Contributor credit: @daniel-lxs reported and reproduced the issue and supplied the pinned-Git validation; the commits preserve his co-author credit.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): carry provider-native chat id into session-event turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#199701: while a backgrounded task runs, a human correction sent from the
same conversation sits queued (observed 95-153 seconds) and the running
assistant never receives it — it keeps acting on superseded instructions.
Steering was rejected with `tool_authority_mismatch` even with
collaborative steering enabled, and an `@mention` retry did not help.

Root cause: session-event turns (background completion finalization,
restart recovery, scheduled automation prompts) are injected through
`buildSessionEventContext`, which never set `MsgContext.ChatId`. Run
assembly copies `conversationId` from that field, so the
same-conversation authority projection compared against an empty
conversation id and rejected the correction. The reporter confirmed
supplying the matching conversation id re-enables the unchanged
authority snapshot.

## The Change

- Session-event targets retain the host-captured `nativeChannelId`
  alongside permission settings (`SessionEventTarget["settings"]`,
  destination settings, and the narrowing function — identity is a fact
  that follows current, never an intersected authority).
- The captured id is read through the canonical origin reader
  (`sessionDeliveryOrigin(entry)?.nativeChannelId` via
  `resolveSessionEventDestinationSettings`), not a route address.
- `buildSessionEventContext` populates `ChatId` from that captured id
  **only**: route addresses (`channel:<id>` for guild channels,
  `user:<id>` for DMs) are not the native conversation identity and do
  not substitute for it; the field stays absent when no identity was
  captured.
- Revocation, route, and thread checks are untouched: they read the same
  snapshot and now receive the identity they were already checking for.

## Evidence

- **Regression-first**: the ChatId case asserts the captured id flows
  through while a prefixed route address (`channel:<id>`) stays out of
  `ChatId` (it remains on `OriginatingTo`) and the field stays absent
  without a captured identity. First revision failed exactly as the
  projection would (`expected undefined to be '123456789012345678'`).
  Full file: **8/8** (capture case covers a real-shaped session entry — `delivery.origin.nativeChannelId` — through destination settings into context construction) (`session-event-context.test.ts`).
- **Sibling suites stay green**: session-event handoff, automation
  result, permissions, policy, config re-admission, and webchat-route
  files — **40/40**; authority and steering suites
  (`agent-runner-execution-message-authority`, `queue.authority`,
  `agent-runner-fallback-steering`) — **23/23**.
- Focused command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run
  src/auto-reply/reply/session-event-context.test.ts` on head
  `28790983e82` (Node 26, isolated worktree).
- **Isolated Gateway A/B, reviewed head:** At base `b601a4b206c` and head `a2dd7462a14`, the same synthetic channel ingress and scripted model exercised a background-exec completion followed by a same-conversation correction. The base rejected the correction with `tool_authority_mismatch` and deferred it as `followup`; the head dispatched it as `steer` and reported `active_run_injected`. The harness used a local `proof-channel` plugin and scripted model endpoint, not a real third-party channel or external model. Both runs used isolated state and loopback endpoints. See the [captured A/B output](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200345#issuecomment-6943968237).
- **Live Gateway trace through a real Telegram channel** (isolated profile,
  fix build; model endpoint held open so an inbound turn stays active):

  ```text
  [routing] resolveAgentRoute: channel=telegram accountId=core
            peer=direct:<tg-user-id> ...
  [model-fetch] start ... sessionKey="agent:main:telegram:core:direct:<tg-user-id>"
            runId="<run-uuid>" requestNumber=1
  [model-fetch] response ... status=200 contentType=text/event-stream ...
  [diagnostic] steering rejected; applying follow-up policy
            reason=requester-mismatch disposition=followup-policy
            channel=telegram sessionKey=agent:main:telegram:core:direct:<tg-user-id>
            activeRunId=<run-uuid>
  [diagnostic] message processed: channel=telegram
            chatId=telegram:<tg-user-id> ... outcome=completed
  ```

  This exercises the same authority-projection stack end to end on a real
  channel: inbound identity capture, an active run with the conversation
  session key, and a same-conversation correction reaching the steering
  decision. The correction shown is rejected one gate earlier
  (`requester-mismatch`: the active run was restored by gateway restart, so
  its requester origin differs from the live Telegram user) — the
  conversation-identity comparison this PR repairs sits one gate below that
  check, which requires requester origins to match first; reproducing that
  exact gate pair needs a Discord-style session where the background
  completion and the correction share one requester origin.

## Risk / compatibility

Additive field population on internal event turns only. The field's
consumers either want it present (authority projection, run assembly,
hook identity context) or treat it as optional template context. No
permission expansion: the id is the host-captured conversation identity
the session already stores, and the revocation and route/thread checks
are unchanged.

### November 24 integration and persisted-session regression

Integrated upstream main `4708bac52397` into `2cec73c1a6d`, retaining the current upstream requester and owner-admission logic. The native conversation ID is read from the canonical persisted delivery origin when capturing the event target.

The regression writes a Discord-shaped delivery record to the isolated SQLite session database, captures it through the session-event target owner, and passes it into completion context construction. The same test fails on `4708bac52397` because `ChatId` is undefined. On `2cec73c1a6d`, it preserves the native ID as `ChatId` and the prefixed address as `OriginatingTo`.

- 183 tests passed across eight suites covering context, handoff, permission bounds, readmission, steering, and tool authority.
- Core typecheck, scoped formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- This regression covers the persistence-to-completion boundary with synthetic Discord data. The earlier Gateway comparisons above used the previously reviewed revision.

## What Problem This Solves

Closes #204267. The QA smoke scenario `subagent-empty-completion-recovery` asserted the child delivery failure notice that #204178 removed. #204299 already replaced that notice assertion with "the parent's completion turn consumes the failed child outcome exactly once" (provider-request count). The scenario still did not check the new contract where it lives: the parent's history.

- no `run-failed-before-reply` row and no displayed `subagent-*` row (the removed "System" dump of the child's raw result and the "delivery delayed" row);
- the restart does not change any of this.

The existing checks stay unchanged: failed terminal outcome, one real write, two tool-free finalizations, no fabricated result, one parent completion request, and no replay after the restart.

- Parent transcript on head (synthetic run): the child status is one hidden `openclaw.runtime-context` entry carrying `[Internal task completion event]` with the child session key. There is no `subagent-completion` entry (the completion turn consumed it) and no `run-failed-before-reply` row.
