prs.title: fix(update): report an already-installed artifact as current
prs.body:
## Problem
The scheduled Install Smoke has been red since 2026-11-24 (run 45318966120, step "Verify candidate already-current no-op without a Gateway service"). The last green run was on 2026-11-23. #203497 moved package updates to the release path in `src/update/`. On that path, `prepareUpdate` treats an explicit artifact (`--tag <tgz>`) as already current only if it is a registry target (`isPackageTargetAlreadyCurrent`). An artifact with the same version and the same build identity as the installed package was staged, validated and started as a trial, and the update ended `running` (phase `activating`). The user asked for the build that is already installed, but got a new release and a trial.

## Fix
- `src/update/run.ts`: after preparation, an explicit package artifact is current when its version and its known `buildId` are the same as the running install's. The run records `skipped` / `already-current`. It publishes no release and starts no trial. A missing build identity does not count as a match, so a rebuilt artifact at the same version still updates (the #144894 contract).
- `scripts/docker/install-sh-smoke/run.sh`: the no-op validator now reads the release update record: `skipped`/`already-current`, artifact staged (`prepare:pack`), no `validating`/`activating`, installed `build-info.json` buildId unchanged. The legacy JSON branch stays for shipped updaters.

## Evidence
- `src/update/prepare.test.ts`: new cases `build: installed` (current, no release, no trial) and `build: rebuilt` (still pending). On base 689d524b-descended main, `build: installed` fails (`expected { status: 'pending' } to match { status: 'current' }`). On head, 33/33 pass.
- Local Docker install smoke, update group (`OPENCLAW_INSTALL_SMOKE_GROUP=update`), from latest stable 2026.11.7 to this candidate: the update completes, and the already-current no-op prints `Verified already-current no-op: artifact staged, installed build unchanged, no activation`. The record is `phase: finished, status: skipped, reason: already-current`.
- `pnpm check:changed`: clean.

## Risk
This changes the update path only when an explicit artifact carries the installed build identity. Every other target goes through preparation and the trial as before.

prs.title: fix(gateway): report removed worktrees before diff baseline capture
prs.body:
## Problem
For a session bound to a managed worktree whose checkout was removed, `sessions.diff` returned an empty diff instead of telling the user the worktree was removed and how to restore it. This happened when the session's first turn had not yet captured its diff baseline (`sessionDiffBaselineCapture.status === "pending"`). The initial `2026.11.15-beta.1` full release validation run caught it: `server.chat-removed-worktree.product.test.ts` line 235 expected an incognito `sessions.diff` to reject with "worktree was removed", but the call resolved with no changes.

Cause: the pending-baseline early return ran before the local worktree owner check (`readLocalWorkspaceReviewBase`), so the removed-checkout error never surfaced.

## Solution
For sessions with a local managed worktree binding, `sessions.diff` now checks the worktree owner first. It returns the empty pending-baseline result only after that check passes.
- A removed checkout returns the usual Restore guidance.
- A healthy checkout still hides pre-session changes until the first turn captures the baseline.
- Sessions without a managed worktree, and named-commit reads, behave as before.
- The read never restores or provisions a checkout.

## Evidence
- The new regression case (managed worktree, pending baseline, then removed) returns an empty diff on base and rejects with the Restore guidance after the fix.
- All 3 reset/baseline cases pass, as do all 5 real-Gateway removed-worktree product cases, including incognito and explicit restore.
- All 16 repository cases and 5 live-read sibling cases pass.
- The broader diff suite has two failures (native revision, untracked-cache refresh). Both fail the same way on unpatched main.
- Core and Gateway-methods typechecks, targeted lint and format, and `git diff --check` pass.

## Impact
This fix unblocks the `2026.11.15-beta.1` release repair. It will be backported to `release/2026.11.15` after landing; both changed files are identical on the release branch.

- @RomneyDa

prs.title: chore(release): raise fast-track limits to 20 commits and 15k lines
prs.body:
## Problem

The proposed `approved-fast-track-v1` policy allows at most 10 commits and 10,000 added/deleted lines since a published, fully validated release. Every commit counts, including the release prepare/version-bump commit. For a stable patch built on 2026.11.8, the prepare commit alone takes one slot and about 650 counted lines (changelogs and the channel catalog; `package.json` files are excluded). That leaves too little room for a useful set of P0/P1 backports.

## Solution

Raise the eligibility ceiling to **20 commits and 15,000 total added/deleted lines**. This changes only the numbers:

- `scripts/lib/release-fast-track-contract.mts`: limit checks and the error message.
- `docs/reference/fast-track-release-approval.md`: policy description.
- `test/manual-release-approval.checks.ts`: boundary cases move to 20/21 commits and 15000/15001 lines. The manifest and lockfile exclusion fixture is resized so it still crosses the new line limit.

Unchanged: what counts (every commit, generated files, deletions), the manifest/lockfile exclusions, the binary/submodule/shallow-history refusals, the "previous fast-track cannot reset the baseline" rule, and the requirement for explicit approval from another human release manager.

## Impact

- Fast-track is still request preparation only. No publisher accepts it yet, so this changes no live release behavior.
- The policy ID stays `approved-fast-track-v1`. No approved fast-track requests exist under the old limits, so there are none to invalidate.
- This loosens a proposed validation-skip safeguard, which is a release-policy decision. Requested by Dallin Romney (release owner).

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/manual-release-approval.config.ts` (manual suite, outside CI): 22/22 passed.
- `oxfmt --check` on the three files and `git diff --check`: clean.

prs.title: fix: let session writers run read-only plugin helpers in their own chats
prs.body:
Closes #204405. Companion plugin change: [Better Prompt #1](https://github.com/obviyus/openclaw-better-prompt/issues/1).

## What Problem This Solves

People who can write to their own chat can still get “Ask an admin to grant write access” when a plugin tries to run a helper on that conversation. The Gateway admits the plugin’s session-scoped request but then treats the helper as a new, sessionless agent launch.

## User Impact

A plugin that opts into own-session writes can now run a helper in that same existing chat without asking for general Gateway write access. For these callers the allowed local tools are `read` and `ls`; shell and plugin tools stay unavailable. The Better button also needs the separate plugin change. No role change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the exact session already authorized by the Gateway and pass it through the existing own-session run check. A session key by itself is not a grant. For a tool-bearing fork, the source WebChat turn must belong to the caller. General writers and sessionless agent launches keep their previous paths.

## Evidence

**Live runtime proof on `d07fa2731d20` (2026-11-24 UTC).** A disposable Gateway ran the OpenClaw agent against [Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 Q4_K_M](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-GGUF/tree/a06e946bb6b655725eafa393f4a9745d460374c9), served by [llama.cpp b10809](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/b10809) on CPU. These were actual model generations, not scripted HTTP responses. The scoped helper was asked to read a fixture file; only the file contained the randomly generated reference. The assertion checked the returned reference **and** observed a real `read` tool event for that helper run.

Redacted trace (identities, addresses and private endpoints omitted):

```text
WebChat/TLS → sessions.create: session writer, own chat; no operator.write
chat.send → OpenClaw agent → Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507: completed (stop)
ordinary plugin RPC → denied: missing operator.write
session-scoped RPC, tools=[exec] → refused: tool_policy
session-scoped RPC, tools=[read] → read notes.txt once → settled
returned reference matched file-only marker PINE-41703: true
proof exit: 0; disposable Gateway and local model server stopped
```

The test runner orchestrated startup and assertions; it did not mock the Gateway, agent, model, or file read. This exercises the OpenClaw host path, not the separately maintained Better button.

On the unpatched base, the new limited-writer Gateway case failed after the outer plugin RPC was admitted. With the fix, an authenticated WebChat client created its own chat, sent a message, and ran a helper that read a real fixture file and returned the expected text. The same client was refused the broad-write RPC and the scoped helper refused `exec`. That separate automated regression uses a scripted model for deterministic CI; the live run above does not.

All eight real-Gateway fork tests passed, including the new regression. The revised fork uses the Gateway session resource’s existing lifetime check rather than comparing transcript identities itself. The `check:session-identity-ratchet` failure reproduced on the first head (6 pins vs. 2 allowed) and passed after the repair without changing the allowlist. Focused TypeScript, lint, formatting and diff checks passed. Local Auto Review of the complete candidate against `0956e14e6` found no P0 issues; it did not run tests. CI and hosted review are separate.

Reported by @etzelm in [the downstream issue](https://github.com/obviyus/openclaw-better-prompt/issues/1).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/eab7267b-75cc-4a12-82c0-0f8ef3bdca4f)

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

prs.title: fix: deliver images sent during a Claude CLI turn instead of queueing them
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When someone sends an image while local Claude CLI is working, the composer shows “Queued” until the turn ends. On a long turn that can take more than ten minutes, even though a text message sent at the same time can reach Claude at its next step.

## User Impact

Claude can see an image before it finishes the current turn. If an installed `before_agent_run` hook needs to inspect new input, the image still waits for the next turn. The hook sees it before Claude does. Other runtimes that do not support image steering keep their existing queue behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin CLI input path previously supported text only. Claude CLI accepts native image blocks on its existing stream, so it can read the pixels rather than a note containing a file path. Plugins explicitly opt in with `acceptsImages`. The shared CLI adapter loads images with the same scoped roots and limits as the first prompt, sends them in order, and records the message only after the native runtime acknowledges it. An image-only message does not add an empty text block.

The existing admission check decides whether to steer or queue. A sink without image support, a permissions mismatch, or an installed run-policy hook keeps the input on the normal followup path. Node-placed Claude CLI sessions are unchanged. This PR does not change the “Queued” label or add a protocol field to explain why an input is waiting.

## Evidence

Two isolated Gateways ran the actual Control UI and Claude CLI 2.1.311 on the tree published as `3416af6467dc`. Each received one synthetic two-color PNG while Claude was using a timer tool:

| Scenario | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| No run-policy hook | Claude identified blue and yellow before its next tool call. The answer appeared about 13 seconds after upload and before the original turn ended. The composer never showed “Queued.” |
| Run-policy hook installed | The composer showed “Queued.” After the original turn ended, the hook inspected one PNG and Claude identified red and green on the next turn. |

Both runs recorded one image-bearing model input and one durable user message with the attachment. Reloading the chat showed it once, with no input left pending. In the original baseline run, the image waited about 36 seconds for the turn to finish.

- The installed-hook regression failed on the incoming PR head and passed on the corrected tree. The unsupported-sink and native `[text, image]` / `[image]` cases also passed.
- 131 affected tests and 16 prompt-prefix tests passed, along with targeted type checking, type-aware lint, formatting, and SDK export sync. Runtime builds passed on the candidate and its main ancestor; the paired Control UI budget check found no new violation. No budget was raised.

prs.title: improve: make pull requests easier to read in the link reader
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves The link reader that opens pull requests, issues and commits beside the chat does not read like a finished surface. On a pull request with one failed check it opens the whole check list (85 rows on a typical OpenClaw PR) in its own scroll box, so the description starts about 450 px lower, below the first screen on a laptop-height window. The header spreads its facts across a grid, the section bar gives no sign of where you are, each changed file and each comment sits in its own bordered box, diffs have no line numbers, and authored images shrink to thumbnails. When checks arrive a second after the page, everything under them jumps. ## User Impact Opening a pull request shows what it is, whether CI is green, and what it says on the first screen, and nothing moves while the rest loads. - **Header:** state badge, repository reference and time on one line, then the title, the author with their picture, the branch, and the signed totals. It follows the hover preview's order, so the reader looks like that card opened up. - **Section bar:** Overview, Checks, Files and Discussion mark the section you are reading. The Checks tab carries a state dot from the first paint. - **Checks:** one summary with a fixed height. A ring and a legend count failed, in-progress, passed and skipped runs, and the failed runs are named beside the title. Expanding it, or selecting Checks, lists the runs grouped by state. A partial list says "Checks incomplete", leaves the ring open and counts the runs it could not show, instead of reading "Checks unavailable" above known results. - **Description and comments:** one reading scale for authored Markdown, framed full-width images with their description as caption, restyled tables, code, quotes, task lists and disclosures. - **Changed files:** one list with the file name first and its directory after it, signed totals, a status word for added, removed or renamed files, and a header that stays in view while its diff scrolls. Diffs have line numbers from their hunk headers; copying a diff still yields the patch text. - **Discussion:** a thread with authors, relative times, review location and collapsible diff context, not a stack of boxes. - **Loading:** the first-load skeleton has the document's geometry, the checks placeholder has the height of the loaded summary, and changed files reserve one row per expected file. ## Why This Change Was Made The first revision of this pull request kept the description on the first screen. Vyctor's review was that the reader still did not look like part of the product, so this revision rebuilds the document. Decisions worth a reviewer's attention: - **Nothing moves when late content arrives.** The first revision listed failed runs under the summary, which pushed the description down when checks loaded. The summary now has one height from loading to loaded: failed runs are named on its title line, long lines fade and never wrap, and the Checks tab shows a state dot, not a late count that would move the tabs after it. - **Counts come from the passive check items.** The host already grouped items by state for the open list; the legend is that grouping, collapsed. The source's own summary stays as the legend's tooltip and still speaks when there are no items. The GitHub summary now says "in progress" where it said "pending", matching the reader. - **The section bar is still one scrolling page.** Find-in-page, comment anchors and the lazy file load keep working; the bar reads the scroll position and reuses the product's tab look. - **GitHub plugin:** the overview now carries the author's picture, the same cached public avatar bytes the hover preview already sends. It loads beside the content reads with a 500 ms budget, so a slow avatar host cannot hold the document, and section requests never read it. It ships here because only the new header shows it. - **Authored emphasis tags:** bare ``, ``, ``, ``, ``, ``, `` and `
` in reader Markdown now render, without attributes and through the existing sanitizer. Review bots write `…`, which showed as literal tags. - **No contract change.** The reader document, the plugin SDK types and the Gateway protocol are untouched. Known limits: the relative date does not tick while the reader stays open. The GitHub plugin reads at most 100 check runs, so a pull request with more reports "Checks incomplete"; raising that bound is a separate change. Diff syntax highlighting is not part of this pull request. Size against the merge base: production TypeScript +995 −529, styles +1023 −340, tests +221 −34. The growth is the redesign's styles and the checks, files and thread components. Reader chunks are lazy: the paired performance comparison against `origin/main` reports chat boot JS −3 B, new-session boot JS −3 B, and no CSS asset change. ## Evidence Same reader panel in the Control UI shell, same document (openclaw/openclaw#203950 as returned by the GitHub plugin, with the check states from the original report: 1 failed, 9 in progress, 30 passed, 45 skipped; one synthetic review comment), dark theme, 795 px panel, mocked Gateway. Before is `origin/main` at `862c71e4cda9`; After is this branch. **Before** ![Before: a plain header with a facts grid, and one failed check opening all 85 checks above the description](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c296a9d-cd18-46bc-8f24-97ab138c7ce7) **After** ![After: a compact header with the author's picture and branch, a section bar, and a one-line checks summary above the description](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f9f8b2ef-5c42-4815-8ed1-37881c18f1c5) Changed files with one diff open: **Before** ![Before: each file in its own box with a native disclosure triangle and an unnumbered diff](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e609dc37-6c84-4f36-a8f4-2a020b93547a) **After** ![After: one file list with names first, signed totals and a numbered diff](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c440eae-ace4-4afe-8341-fecd0d7df7e9) Discussion: **Before** ![Before: comments as bordered boxes with link-colored timestamps and literal strong tags](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd546d33-8e0c-4b36-980d-c3daede2ca79) **After** ![After: comments as a thread with authors, relative times and a review location](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/69d8bb37-9d82-4e88-a63b-fd3a3618448a) Annotated: ![Before, annotated: the facts grid repeats the tabs and the open check list pushes the description down](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5bbc3057-4d76-49e6-a94b-77cfc426debe) ![After, annotated: one header, a section bar that follows the reading position, and a fixed-height checks summary](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f5a2218-f646-41dc-9c75-fc25bab05cbb) Layout stability: a `layout-shift` PerformanceObserver on the reader with a simulated Gateway, at 400, 820 and 1280 px, while the overview, checks (about 1.4 s later) and discussion arrive, recorded no shift inside the document for three documents (1 failure, 5 failures, 14 files with incomplete checks). The only entry is the panel's tab title, 0.0001 to 0.0002. The loading browser test now asserts that the description and the tabs keep their position through a failed check load, a retry, and the arrival of 85 checks with five failures. Gap: this was not measured against a real isolated Gateway, as the UI guide asks for layout work. Checked: reader content, panel, hovercard and page-preview tests; the GitHub plugin tests; the checks, loading, refresh and GitHub panel browser tests. Lint for the touched files, the style lint, the controller guard, UI and extensions typecheck and the i18n check are clean.
Commands ``` pnpm test ui/src/components/link-reader-content.test.ts ui/src/components/link-reader-panel.test.ts ui/src/components/link-reader-hovercard.test.ts ui/src/components/link-reader-page-preview.test.ts ui/src/components/link-reader-metadata.test.ts pnpm test extensions/github/src pnpm test ui/src/e2e/link-reader-checks.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/link-reader-loading.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/link-reader-refresh.e2e.test.ts ui/src/e2e/github-panel.e2e.test.ts pnpm tsgo:ui && pnpm tsgo:extensions pnpm check:control-ui-controllers && pnpm ui:i18n:verify pnpm exec stylelint --config config/stylelint.config.mjs "ui/src/components/link-reader-*.css" pnpm ui:check-performance:base 862c71e4cda915f9d0548117b7d38d86755f27ff ```

prs.title: refactor(gateway): check the cron creator grant's issuer once
prs.body:
## Problem

AGENTS.md says to check authority once, when work starts. The MCP cron creator grant (`src/gateway/cron-creator-authority-grant.ts`) still re-read its issuer's state each time it was used:

- Gateway `agent` and `chat.send` turns passed the client's `hasCurrentClientAuthority` (the issuing device's live revocation state) into the run scope's `isCurrent`.
- Channel-owner turns put a live command-owner check (`isConfiguredCommandOwner` on current config) into `managementEntitlement.isCurrent` and `requesterOwner.isCurrent`.

Grant mint, consume, provenance, stream exec policy, management redemption, tool construction and requester continuations all called those callbacks. A device revoke or an owner removal during a run refused the started run's next automation write with "This run's MCP cron access has ended" (R6z, #204249, named this follow-up).

## Fix

- `CronManagementEntitlement` is now one shape, `{ source }`. The channel-owner variant loses `isCurrent`. `requesterOwner` keeps only its identity fields (`senderId`, `channel`, `accountId`).
- Deleted every use-time read of those callbacks: grant mint, provenance and `assertCronGrantCurrent`; `bindCronManagementToolConstruction`, `captureActiveCronManagementAuthority`, `bindRequesterOwnerIdentity`, `bindCronManagementGrant`; the requester continuation's `isCurrent`.
- The direct operator admission (`resolveDirectOperatorAuthority`) no longer takes or copies `isCurrent`. Removed `isCurrent` from the admission params, `GatewayChatUserTurn`, the chat external-admission contract and both call sites. The `agent` turn keeps `hasCurrentClientAuthority`: the operator-run retention (`retainGatewayOperatorRun`) still reads it at turn start.
- The channel reply factory checks the owner once when it creates the run's capability. On the fresh path this happens at turn start. A queued `/followup` start passes its own owner check, so a revoke while queued still starts the turn without cron management.

Kept, because they are run liveness or grant identity data, not issuer state: scope `active`/`signal` (Stop and run close), the operation signal, `scope.isCurrent` from requester continuations (session reset/archive, cohort and new-user-turn fences), the grant's `isCurrent` from the MCP loopback grant (grant replaced) and `validateAgentRunDelegatedAuthority` (run occurrence), the run/job identity compares and the 60 s management grant expiry.

Production code: 9 files, +18 / −43. No new lint allowlist entry.

### Decisions

- A yielded requester's continuation (child completion back to the parent) is part of the started task. It keeps the owner identity captured at the parent's admission. A channel-owner removal between yield and continuation no longer drops the continuation's cron management. Session reset/archive and a new direct user turn still retire it.
- Accepted edge: a channel owner removed while their message is queued still gets their turn, but without cron management (the factory returns no capability), as before for other caller-scoped turns.

## User impact

A started run can finish its automation writes after its device is revoked or its channel owner is removed mid-run. The next turn uses the new state. Stop and run close still end the grant.

## Tests

Deleted, because each asserts a refusal after a mid-run device, owner or entitlement change:
- `cron-creator-authority-grant.test.ts`: "channel owner" retained-creator row and the owner-revoked mint case.
- `cron-creator-authority-context.test.ts`: owner-revoked construction case.
- `requester-cron-authority.test.ts`: "rejects an owner revoked before dispatch" and the owner toggles in "retains %s across yields".
- `run.bind-parent.test.ts`: "refuses the stored write when the owner loses authority while bind waits for the store".
- `cron.ownership-matrix.test.ts`: the `revoked` caller.
- `sessions-send-owner-continuation.test.ts`: the "owner revoked" row.

Flipped to prove the new rule (revoke mid-run does not refuse; run close does):
- `agent-run-local-operator-authority.test.ts`: device revoked mid-run → the grant is consumed; after run close an unspent grant is refused.
- `cron-creator-transports.integration.test.ts`: real CLI/embedded/remote/chat/template creator mutations succeed after the issuing device is revoked; the session-data fence (skill selection) still refuses.
- `mcp-cron-management.integration.test.ts`: a channel owner's MCP update succeeds after owner removal; revoking the MCP grant still returns 401.
- `server.sessions-send-owner-continuation.test.ts`: the "owner revoked" row's plugin write now lands.
- `sessions-send-followup-revalidation.test.ts`: the "revoked" row now resolves.

## Evidence

- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: clean. oxfmt and oxlint on the changed files: clean.
- Pre-push `ocx test`: the 94 touched and importer test files (direct importers of every changed source and `*.test-support.ts`). All ours green after one repair round (the `agent` turn still needs `hasCurrentClientAuthority` for `retainGatewayOperatorRun`, so that plumbing is kept). `service.pr-automation*.test.ts` (32 cases) fails the same way on merge base `04ddd0ebe84e`.
- `pnpm check:changed`: all lanes pass except the dead-export scan, which flags `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-read-aloud-status.tsx: RecordingApiKeyNotice` (not in this diff).
- E2E `one-admission-e2e/run.sh` on head `882bbde7cecf`: Q (revoke while queued → refused visibly), R (revoke while running → finishes) and S (Stop → cancels) pass. `verdict.json` and `results.jsonl`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204395#issuecomment-7122442814
- Local review on this head: ready, no findings. CI reds are not ours: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204395#issuecomment-7123270269

prs.title: feat(a2a): implement the A2A protocol v1.0 specification
prs.body:
## Summary

This PR upgrades the `extensions/a2a` channel plugin from partial 0.3-era support to a **conformance-validated implementation of the A2A protocol v1.0 specification**, tested against the official [a2a-tck](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-tck) conformance suite (remaining failures are limited to scripted-reference-SUT-only scenarios — see Evidence). All configuration remains backward compatible with the original plugin.

## What Problem This Solves

The `extensions/a2a` plugin currently implements only a partial, 0.3-era subset of the A2A protocol. A2A has since shipped **v1.0** with breaking changes and new requirements:

- **New method surface**: `SendMessage`/`GetTask`/`ListTasks`/`CancelTask`/`SendStreamingMessage`/`SubscribeToTask` replace the 0.3 dotted methods, plus push notification config CRUD and `GetExtendedAgentCard` — v1.0 clients calling a 0.3-era server get `Method not found`
- **HTTP+JSON (REST) binding** at `/a2a/v1/rest` (spec §5.4) with gRPC-transcoding-style path bindings — required for REST-native clients, previously absent
- **Revised error model**: codes `-32001..-32009` with `google.rpc.ErrorInfo` details, and new HTTP status mappings (`TASK_NOT_CANCELABLE` → 409, `CONTENT_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED` → 415, `INVALID_AGENT_RESPONSE` → 502) — the old mappings no longer conform
- **Capability, media-type, and required-extension validation** (spec §3.3.4, §3.1.1, §4.6) — previously not enforced
- **Agent Card caching** (ETag/304, §8.6.1) and the **Extended Agent Card** — previously absent
- **Push notification webhooks** with idempotent delete (§3.1.10) and SSRF protection — previously absent

In short: without this change, the plugin cannot interoperate with A2A v1.0 clients and fails the official conformance suite. With it, it passes (see Evidence below) while every pre-existing config key keeps its name, semantics, and default.

## Evidence

### a2a-tck conformance suite (official, black-box against a live instance)

Round 10 (latest, HEAD `086867253` — the stream-order fix — both declared transports `jsonrpc` + `http_json`, Bearer auth; [full rendered report](https://gist.github.com/beeven/d00d70490e12cea4d1450b26f472da37)):

- **Overall: 70.0% / MUST: 71.2%** — the only MUST requirements still failing are the two scripted reference-SUT contracts (`DM-ART-001`/`DM-MSG-001`)
- Per-transport: `agent_card` 10/10; `jsonrpc` 62P/5F; `http_json` 57P/5F — every remaining failure is a scripted-contract case
- `STREAM-ORDER-001` (round-9 finding: state-sequence regression when a reused messageId lands on a completed task) **passes on both transports** after `086867253`, with a regression test in the suite
- Round-to-round: 51.3% -> 65.8% -> 67.9% -> 69.1% -> 73.9% -> 75.0% -> 73.9% -> 71.4% -> 71.2% MUST. Round-over-round variance is coverage, not behavior: the real LLM returns COMPLETED or INPUT_REQUIRED non-deterministically for TCK's fixed prerequisite text, so requirements move in and out of the denominator between runs
- Round-9 confirmation traces (live gateway, token redacted):

```
# REST push-config list route — the round-8 regression, now fixed
GET /a2a/v1/rest/tasks/<uuid>/pushNotificationConfigs
-> 200 {"configs":[],"nextPageToken":"","pageSize":0}

# STREAM-ORDER-001 reproduction (reused messageId on a completed task)
jsonrpc  first stream : ok     [WORKING, WORKING, COMPLETED]
http_json reuse       : regress [COMPLETED, WORKING, COMPLETED]   <- before fix
http_json reuse       : ok     [WORKING, COMPLETED]               <- after 086867253
```

- Reproduction (public repo layout, local plugin injects Bearer auth which upstream TCK lacks):

```
cd a2a-tck && PYTHONPATH=$PWD .venv/bin/python ./run_tck.py \
    --sut-host http://localhost:38789 --transport jsonrpc,http_json -- \
    -p tck_local_openclaw --timeout=45 --timeout-method=signal
```

Artifacts: `reports/compatibility.json` / `compatibility.html` / `junitreport.xml`.

### Behavior proof over the real transport

Captured against a real Gateway built from this branch (`19e3466d0`) — real HTTP/SSE on the wire, real agent dispatch to a live model backend, real webhook POSTs to a local receiver (localhost endpoints and placeholder tokens throughout, nothing to redact). Full traces in [#issuecomment-6659323864](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179380#issuecomment-6659323864); summary:

- **Allowed delivery**: three ordered webhook POSTs (WORKING → artifact → COMPLETED), all 200, per-task ordering held
- **Foreign peer refused**: unknown bearer → HTTP 401, no task, zero webhook POSTs
- **No POST after deletion in the real retry window**: registration deleted via REST inside the 250 ms backoff → receiver saw exactly one failed POST, no retries
- **No POST to the old URL after replacement in the retry window**: same config id re-registered to a new URL during backoff → old receiver silent, new receiver got the retries
- **No POST after shutdown**: SIGTERM while a delivery chain was live → terminal update delivered while the account was still stopping, then zero POSTs after `shutdown completed` with the receiver healthy for 17 s
- **Disabled extended card**: authenticated peer gets `-32004` UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION pointing at the config
- **Stream ordering (v4 contract)**: `SendStreamingMessage` = opening Task snapshot (WORKING) → updates → terminal close; subscribing to an INPUT_REQUIRED task folds all pre-subscription transitions into the snapshot and streams only post-subscription events
- **Follow-up retry identity**: identical messageId retry while the resumed turn was running resolved to the same task, history contains the answer exactly once
### Unit tests and typecheck (this repo)

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run extensions/a2a
Test Files  13 passed (13)
     Tests  151 passed (151)

$ pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test   # typecheck: green
```

New coverage added alongside the review fixes: REST binding HTTP tests (push-config create/list, shared per-peer rate limit -> 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, malformed body -> INVALID_ARGUMENT), per-subscriber stream queues each observing the full event sequence, replay-before-subscribe, interrupt-released blocking sends, `statusTimestampAfter` filtering, task-eviction observers expiring push registrations, 429 webhook retry, and the stream-order regression above.

### Config compatibility

- All pre-existing config keys verified unchanged (name/semantics/default) — existing deployments upgrade without touching config
- New keys are opt-in; `src/config/bundled-channel-config-metadata.generated.ts` regenerated via `pnpm config:channels:gen` and the metadata sync check passes

## What's implemented

### Core protocol (§3)
- All **11 JSON-RPC methods** defined in v1.0: `SendMessage`, `GetTask`, `ListTasks`, `CancelTask`, `SendStreamingMessage`, `SubscribeToTask`, the four push notification config CRUD methods (`SetTaskPushNotificationConfig`, `GetTaskPushNotificationConfig`, `ListTaskPushNotificationConfig`, `DeleteTaskPushNotificationConfig`), and `GetExtendedAgentCard`
- Backward-compatible **0.3-era dotted method aliases** (`message/send`, `message/stream`, `tasks/get`, `tasks/list`, `tasks/cancel`, `tasks/subscribe`, ...) so existing clients keep working
- **Agent Card** served at `/.well-known/agent-card.json` with ETag / Last-Modified / Cache-Control caching and `If-None-Match` → 304 handling (§8.6.1)
- **Extended Agent Card** served behind the `extendedAgentCard` capability

### Transports
- **HTTP+JSON (REST) binding** at `/a2a/v1/rest` per §5.4, with gRPC-transcoding-style URL path bindings (path parameters take precedence over body fields)
- **SSE streaming** with resumable task updates
- **gRPC-style HTTP status mappings** per §5.4: `TASK_NOT_CANCELABLE` → 409, `CONTENT_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED` → 415, `INVALID_AGENT_RESPONSE` → 502

### Error model
- Full v1.0 error codes **-32001..-32009** with `google.rpc.ErrorInfo` details (reason / domain / metadata); JSON-RPC reserved codes (-32700..-32603) carry no ErrorInfo, as required

### Push notifications (§3.1.10)
- Full config CRUD with **idempotent delete** (repeated deletes succeed silently, per spec)
- Webhook delivery with **SSRF protection** (private-network targets blocked unless explicitly allowed)
- Configurable authentication schemes (bearer, basic, apikey)

### Validation
- **Capability validation** (§3.3.4): calling a method whose capability is disabled returns `-32004` `UnsupportedOperation`; enabling `extendedAgentCard` without configuring it returns `-32007`
- **Media-type validation** (§3.1.1): raw/url part media types checked against `inputModes` (with `type/*` and `*/*` wildcard support) before text-part checks, returning `-32005` with ErrorInfo metadata
- **Required extensions** (§4.6): extensions declared with `required: true` that are not activated via the `A2A-Extensions` header return `-32008`

### Outbound agent-to-agent client
- Full `Message | Task` oneof parsing with ErrorInfo reason surfacing in thrown errors

## Configuration compatibility

- **No breaking changes**: every pre-existing config key keeps its name, semantics, and default
- New v1.0 features are **opt-in** via new keys: `capabilities.*` (skill discovery, extensions, push), `pushNotifications.*` (auth, webhook options), `rest.enabled`, `extendedSkillDescriptions`
- `src/config/bundled-channel-config-metadata.generated.ts` regenerated via `pnpm config:channels:gen` so core startup validation accepts the new keys
- Config-surface budget: this consciously raises the `channel` baseline by **+30 entries** (`docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json`, channel 3975 → 4005) — exactly the new opt-in A2A v1.0 keys (`capabilities.*`, `pushNotifications.*`, `rest.*`, `extendedSkillDescriptions`, and peers/auth knobs); no existing keys changed

## Notes

- Rebased onto latest `main` (`65fc2f00d`); the diff is limited to `extensions/a2a/` + the regenerated config metadata file, and upstream's `wait()`/`buildContext` refactors from #178508 are integrated
- Happy to split into smaller commits or adjust scope per maintainer feedback

prs.title: fix: run unconfigured cyber models at Daybreak Red outside the Control UI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cyber models such as GPT-6 Cyber and GPT-5.6 Cyber can only run under Daybreak Red; OpenAI rejects them at Standard with 400 `invalid_access_program`. Without an explicit `params.accessPrograms.cyber` setting, OpenClaw sent Standard for every OpenAI turn, so any turn on an unconfigured cyber model that did not start in the Control UI failed: channel chats, cron jobs, CLI runs and `sessions_spawn` children. The model picker also listed Standard as those models' default.

openclaw/openclaw#204302 fixed the Control UI flows client-side and left this runtime default as a follow-up. Simply omitting the field is not a fix: OpenAI's own defaults differ by model (omitted, GPT-6 Sol runs Blue and GPT-6.2 Sol runs Standard), which is why OpenClaw sends an explicit program.

## User Impact

An unconfigured cyber model now runs at Daybreak Red on every entry path, and the model picker reports Red as its default. Models that advertise Standard (GPT-6.2 Sol and other mainline models) keep Standard. Explicit configuration (including `accessPrograms: {}`) and saved session choices still win. Role ceilings still apply to the resolved program, so a role limited to Standard gets the existing "operator role cannot use this Access level" error on a cyber model instead of a provider 400.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Owner of the advertised list.** The prepared model runtime's catalog already owns "which programs does this account advertise for this model, route and runtime": the gateway catalog projection reads it through `resolveModelCatalogAccessPrograms`, and the embedded submission guard reads it, account-scoped, before every physical request. This change reuses that owner rather than adding a model-name heuristic.

- `resolveModelCyberAccessProgramDefault` (one default policy for presentation and requests) takes the advertised list. Configuration wins; otherwise a list with exactly one entry selects that entry, and an unknown or Standard-capable list keeps Standard.
- `projectModelCatalogAccessPrograms` passes the list it already resolves, so the catalog default and the physical request agree.
- The account-scoped read inside `prepareEmbeddedAccessProgramGuard` moved into `prepareAttemptAccessPrograms`, which the guard and dispatch now share. Harness-owned auth (native Codex) reads that runtime's native observations, matching the projection.
- Dispatch reads the list once per attempt (`readDispatchAccessPrograms`) and hands it to the runtime plan as `cyberAccessPrograms`. It reads only on routes that send a program (`consumesCyberAccessPrograms`, now shared with the default resolver), skips the read when the session already has a choice, and treats a superseded prepared runtime as unknown, so non-OpenAI turns do no extra account-catalog work and ordinary turns cannot fail on the read.
- The embedded guard validates the resolved program with the same reader, and the Codex harness keeps validating non-Standard programs against its live `model/list` before `turn/start`; both apply role ceilings to the resolved program as before.
- `run-attempt-dispatch.ts` sits at its 700-line cap, so the read lives in the Access module and dispatch drops its redundant `modelApi` argument (the builder derives it from `model.api`).

Accepted limits: an unknown list (cold or failed account discovery) keeps Standard and fails visibly as before. Standalone compaction builds its own plan without the list, as it already does without the session's saved choice; in-turn compaction reuses the dispatch plan.

`buildAgentRuntimePlan` is exported through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`; the new optional `cyberAccessPrograms` parameter is additive.

## Evidence

Regression proof at the production boundary: `subagent-spawn.production-boundary.test.ts` now runs two `sessions_spawn` children with no saved choice and no `accessPrograms` config through the real embedded runner, prepared catalog, Access guard and OpenAI provider, and asserts the captured physical Responses body.

- `default-red`: unconfigured `gpt-6-cyber`, account advertises `["daybreak_red"]`. On `main` (92c476640812a) it fails exactly on the bug: the physical request carried `access_programs: { cyber: "standard" }`. With this change it sends `daybreak_red`.
- `default-standard`: unconfigured `gpt-6.2-sol`, account advertises `["standard", "daybreak_blue"]`. Sends `standard` before and after.

Unit contracts for the other consumers: `model-catalog-access-programs.test.ts` (projection default for Red-only, Standard-capable, empty, and configured lists), `runtime-plan/build.test.ts` (plan default for both `openclaw` and `codex` runtimes, configuration still wins), `access-program.test.ts` (harness-owned auth reads that runtime's native observations; forwarded credentials do not).

Also run and passing: `run-attempt-dispatch.{owner,input,media,sandbox-baseline}`, `run-entry.cyber-failover`, `harness/host-model-execution`, `subagent-spawn.access-program`, `gateway/session-access-program`, `models-list-result.{access-programs,openai-routes}`, Codex `run-attempt.native-config` and `harness.cyber-failover`, and the full spawn production-boundary file. `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, oxlint and format on touched files, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` (+95 of 400).

CI follow-ups on this PR: the first run exposed test-only type errors (fixed in `436c5f3`) and a shared overflow-compaction runtime fixture that omitted the type-required `isCurrent` (fixed in `8f64190`; `run.shared-integration` and `run.harness-auth-failover` pass, 158 tests). `3dfbabc` then limits the dispatch read to Access-consuming routes. Gateway e2e failures in that run (`gateway-restart-resume`, `gateway-plugin-turn-handover`, `cron-one-shot-run`) reproduce identically locally with the merge-base production code, so they are inherited from `main`.

Local review: autoreview (Codex engine), branch mode against `origin/main`, P0 threshold: scoped-clean, no findings.

Known gaps: no live OpenAI request was made; the physical-request proof uses a fixture fetch at the OpenAI provider boundary. The Codex runtime is covered at the plan and reader level, not through a `turn/start` capture. `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:diff` currently fails while rendering the base commit (`src/infra/worker-cpu.ts -> ../../worker-heap-flag.mjs`), independent of this change.

Pre-existing flake seen while testing: `preserves routed native Stop authority and existing receipts (consumed-session)` failed 1 of 4 runs on unmodified `main` and 0 of 4 with this change (one earlier failure on this branch before that comparison).

Release note context: Unconfigured OpenAI cyber models (GPT-6 Cyber, GPT-5.6 Cyber) now default to Daybreak Red on every entry path (channels, cron, CLI, subagents) instead of failing with `invalid_access_program`; models that support Standard keep Standard.

prs.title: fix: open older session links without reloading chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Clicking an older session link in a chat message opens the right session, but first the whole Control UI disappears behind “Connecting to OpenClaw.” The browser treats the click as a new page load instead of a change of conversation.

## User Impact

Links for this Gateway with a full session key now look like other session links and open in place. Back returns to the original conversation without reloading it. Links to other Gateways still use normal browser navigation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Chat and startup use the same parser for older session links. Chat hands a qualified destination on its own Gateway to the existing session router. It preserves the mounted path, dashboard or chat destination, other query parameters, and fragment. If the link does not identify its agent, startup resolves it. Native authentication and Gateway reconnect behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

On the source tree published as `018d8923562f`, Chromium and WebKit each connected to two separately paired, isolated Gateways with synthetic conversations. On the historical base (`2545889fe860`), clicking a same-Gateway link loaded a new document and opened a new WebSocket in Chromium. With the fix, both browsers opened the requested conversation, kept `?view=full#latest`, and restored the source URL and transcript on Back. Neither action loaded a document or opened a WebSocket.

A link to the second Gateway opened in a new tab. It showed that Gateway’s conversation, not the different conversation with the same key on the first Gateway. These checks cover browser navigation, not macOS authentication. Related: #203918 fixes a separate Knowledge link.

On the same base as the original CI run, the correction reduced gzipped chat startup JavaScript from 1,334,754 to **1,334,445 bytes**, 35 below the limit. On a newer paired `main` (`0956e14e6814`), it used 85 fewer bytes than the base. Both official comparisons passed locally with unchanged chat CSS and 21 JavaScript requests. The 181 focused tests, UI typecheck, lint and formatting checks passed locally. No budget was changed. The screenshots below show the original before/after comparison in Chromium with a simulated Gateway; the two-Gateway check above exercised the same interaction on the corrected tree.

prs.title: fix: report channel plugin download failures to scripts without prompting
prs.body:
Closes #201990

## What Problem This Solves

When `openclaw channels add` cannot download a required plugin, it can find a local copy and ask whether to use it. A script has nobody to answer, so the prompt can hide the download error. The [earlier fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5c9389a5ba9c21efa4b0c97dd55c57d0bc9c3112) already stopped the command from reporting success after a failed install.

## User Impact

Scripts see the download error once, exit with status `1`, and leave channel configuration unchanged. People running the command at a terminal can still choose the local copy. No migration or new flag is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The installer used to offer the local copy even when the command had already determined that it could not ask questions. The [five-file follow-up against `main`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/918d2f59ee155556aa6e89343233c4d6f44fec0e...01b4da6fd317b45b1d168c93288bd85f6a680d9c) ties that one question to terminal input and output. Guided setup, source selection and capability consent are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Integration verification

The [current head `01b4da6f`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/01b4da6fd317b45b1d168c93288bd85f6a680d9c) incorporates [main `918d2f59`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/918d2f59ee155556aa6e89343233c4d6f44fec0e). The four installer regression cases and all four current Chromium route benchmark cases passed locally on the published tree. The PR still changes only the original five installer files. The [hosted CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45333547069) is separate from that local proof.

The current route benchmark is not the historical one: upstream replaced the Skills reader dialog with a page and repaired Skills/Plugins loading. No benchmark assertions were changed by this PR.

### Earlier installer behavior proof

Ran the built `openclaw.mjs channels add --channel fixture-chat --name Example` at [the previously reviewed head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4a13c9dc3faf3fabba7b7454c04363fc5dc72d60) with a local copy present and a loopback registry returning HTTP 404. With stdin closed there was no prompt. In a real terminal the local-copy prompt appeared; answering **No** preserved the same error. Each run made one registry request, printed the cause once, exited `1`, and left the config byte-for-byte unchanged. The public registry was not contacted.

```text
Closed stdin:
Could not install the plugin for channel "fixture-chat". Install the plugin manually or verify the install source, then retry.
Package not found on ClawHub.

Real terminal:
Use local plugin path instead? ([fixture workspace]/plugins/fixture-chat)  → No
Could not install the plugin for channel "fixture-chat". Install the plugin manually or verify the install source, then retry.
Package not found on ClawHub.
```

The CLI regression test failed against the original implementation because it asked one question instead of zero. On that earlier head the command, setup-adapter and installer suites passed, as did scoped typecheck, lint and formatting. Independent autoreview of the complete five-file range found no actionable P0–P2 issues. The [hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202091#issuecomment-7024309261) verified the terminal proof on `4a13c9dc` and listed no findings or before-merge actions.

[Required CI on the earlier `4a13c9dc` head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44804403623) **failed**. The [failing UI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44804403623/job/136525382964) timed out waiting for rows on Skills and Plugins; Skill Settings loaded 33 assets against a limit of 31. The tested merge changed no UI or benchmark files. The [Skills and asset-count failures](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44803148089/job/136521248000) and [Plugins timeout](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44796218464/job/136497502162) also occurred on independent runs. Related upstream work: [#202694](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202694) and [#202687](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202687). Those historical runs are not evidence that CI passed on the new head.

An independent replay on `4eb94c89`, the first parent of the [tested merge](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5a0796342287836329eacfc8f6c85dfa1a93c95e), reproduced all three failures without the installer change. Skills and Plugins timed out on the same selectors. Skill Settings requested the same 33 asset URLs against the 31-asset limit. Plugin Settings passed on both. The base push skipped this UI suite; the comparison was run locally with Chromium and Node 24.22.1.

Contributor: Mitchell Etzel (@etzelm). Reported by Anmol (@anmol0b).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @etzelm](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2edc3159-c613-4611-ac1c-48d712e40c67)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/e22c0f1b-d725-4148-b4d3-3a6437d47641)
- [Local fallback correction and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/d7d74ff2-50f8-4b78-a6d7-f10ac7918e37)
- [Landing discussion and verification with @VACInc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/dfbb8805-b4f2-4c40-ac84-ea5b941703a5)

- [Exact-base CI comparison, integration and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/3e4c57f3-2562-41a7-b38e-85e9d34c1285)

## Worked on by

- @etzelm

Browser split Talk can stay silent after the Gateway returns a reply. A stalled silent unlock clip prevents the reply from playing and keeps the microphone from resuming.

With the fix, all 26 focused speech playback and split Talk tests passed, including the never-settling and late-settling cases. Scoped lint passed. Two independent code reviews found no blockers. prs.title: feat(ui): hear when hands-free Talk is listening or ends
prs.body:
Closes #204311

## What Problem This Solves

People using Talk hands-free have to look at the screen to tell whether the call is listening or has ended. In turn-based calls, they also have no audible cue that they can reply after the assistant speaks.

## User Impact

Browser Talk plays short status chimes by default. Users can turn off Listening, Call end, or Ready for reply individually under Settings → Talk → Status chimes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The listening cue plays when the call becomes ready, and the end cue plays on a clean end, not on an error or background abort. In STT/TTS mode, Ready for reply plays when capture resumes after the assistant speaks. Live mode does not play that cue because its microphone is already listening; the disabled control leaves the saved preference intact.

## Evidence

- 129 focused tests passed across five files. Both new stop cases pass; before the fix, a background abort incorrectly requested the end cue. Scoped lint, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- The approved scratch build showed all three controls available in STT/TTS and Ready for reply disabled in Live. The final review changes do not alter the visuals. Realtime cue playback was checked on an earlier scratch build; split-mode Reply audio has automated coverage but no hands-on signoff.
- Local review against `92c47664081` through the working changes: Codex found that a failed asset download silenced a cue until reload. Fixed and covered with a fail-before/pass-after test.
- Second review: Marvin (claude-opus-5-5), findings above, addressed. The review covered cue loading, the session lifecycle, split capture, and Talk actions. A user stop now requests the end cue explicitly, independently of the transport abort disposition. Preloading only enabled cues was optional and left out.

prs.title: fix: retry the primary after a local dispatch failure
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A 30-second primary-model recovery probe exists to check whether a cooldowned provider has recovered. A worker failure before provider handoff consumes that probe today, so immediate turns remain on fallback even though no provider request was made.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The worker-turn launcher marks `WorkerRunnerUnavailableError` only when it knows the provider handoff never happened. Harness preflight failures also happen before dispatch.
- The fallback runner releases only the exact reservation for those known pre-dispatch failures. It keeps the throttle after provider outcomes and after coordination errors that may happen after a request.
- Probe reservation now happens synchronously with the cooldown decision, before the async observer can let a concurrent turn pass the same decision.
- The broader `isNonProviderRuntimeCoordinationError()` classification still prevents unsafe provider fallback. It does not prove that no provider request started.

## User Impact

After a local worker dispatch failure, the primary model can be tried again immediately. Failures after provider dispatch keep the existing 30-second throttle.

Related #127649

## Evidence

The committed runner `node src/gateway/worker-environments/repro-cooldown-probe.mjs` starts a local Gateway and sends real WebSocket `agent` and `agent.wait` RPCs. A controlled placement provider routes the first Gateway turn through the production worker-turn launcher fixture. That launcher registers a Node Host fixture through the production `NodeRegistry`, `NodeWorkerTunnelManager`, and launch adapter over a real loopback WebSocket, then disconnects the socket immediately before dispatch. The Gateway reports the pre-dispatch `WorkerRunnerUnavailableError`; the next Gateway turn reaches the primary through the loopback OpenAI-compatible HTTP provider. The placement provider and Node Host are test fixtures; no physical Node Host, external provider, or real credential was used.

Output captured on exact head `a2c2150a9c6edc768137ac6502434943ebfadf63`:

```text
[gateway-proof] rpc=agent/agent.wait pre-dispatch=WorkerRunnerUnavailableError transport=node-registry-websocket disconnected-before-handoff=true recovery=ok provider_requests=1
[gateway-proof] post-dispatch=loopback-429 then transcript-coordination retry=throttled provider_requests=2 no-extra-request=true
```

The post-dispatch control receives actual loopback HTTP 429 responses, then the test placement callback injects `SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError`. The second Gateway RPC remains throttled and sends no additional provider request. The coordination error is injected by the test callback, rather than produced by the transcript writer itself.

At the pinned validation base `86fcb81e64c02b29e64892ed8549a639ecd6dc0d`, the earlier worker-boundary control observed `retry=throttled provider_requests=0` after the same live NodeRegistry disconnect. That base capture used the direct worker-boundary harness, while the exact-head capture above enters through Gateway RPC.

Focused checks passed on the exact head: `model-fallback.personal-cooldown.test.ts` (9/9; 9.76s local wall time), `worker-turn-launcher-failure-recovery.test.ts` (18/18; 47.48s local wall time), and the committed Gateway proof runner (1 passed; 17 unrelated cases filtered out; 14.63s local wall time).

The test-line ratchet reports +526 net test lines against its 400-line allowance. Allocation `config/test-lines-allocations/203469-gateway-recovery-proof.txt` covers the remaining 126 lines for the Gateway transport proof, its no-extra-request control, and the distinct preflight, provider-error, concurrency, and reservation-identity contracts. The two redundant mock-only local-worker retry and post-dispatch coordination cases were removed. Hosted CI seconds are pending for this head.

prs.title: ci(perf): run the plugin-pressure Kova scenario on its own runner
prs.body:
## Problem

The `Kova mock provider performance` job in `OpenClaw Performance` takes 35–40 minutes on release validation (for example run 45329409933, job 138226987907). That job runs the whole matrix one entry at a time (`--parallel 1`), and one scenario takes most of the time.

Timings per record from run 45324941412 (release profile, repeat 3):

| Scenario:state | Per repeat | 3 repeats |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gateway-performance:many-bundled-plugins` | 470–543 s | ~25 min |
| `fresh-install:fresh` (includes the local build on the first repeat) | 201 / 23 / 23 s | ~4 min |
| `fresh-install:onboarded-user` | ~23 s | ~1 min |
| `bundled-plugin-startup:fresh` | ~29 s | ~1.5 min |
| `agent-cold-warm-message:mock-openai-provider` | ~29 s | ~1.5 min |

Most of the `gateway-performance` time goes to harness setup, not measurement. The `many-bundled-plugins` state installs 80 synthetic plugins one at a time through `ocm @env -- plugins install`, at 5–6 s per plugin. That is about 7.5 minutes before every repeat. The measured phases take about 25 s (cold start 7 s, API latency 7 s, warm restart 12 s). The installs can't run in parallel: I ran concurrent `openclaw plugins install` calls locally and all but one failed on the exclusive state lease.

## Change

- Split the mock lane in two:
  - `mock-provider` keeps `fresh-install`, `bundled-plugin-startup` and `agent-cold-warm-message`.
  - The new `mock-plugin-pressure` lane runs `gateway-performance` on its own runner.
- Measurement isolation stays the same: each lane is still `--parallel 1` on a dedicated runner.
- Add the new lane to the `publish` matrix, so it gets its own clawgrit report and `latest-mock-plugin-pressure.json` pointer. The mock-provider source-probe attachment and baseline pointer don't change.
- Calibration mode is unchanged. Only `mock-provider` runs there.
- Update the lane list in `docs/ci/scheduled-workflows.md` and the workflow contract test.

## Coverage

`kova matrix plan` at the pinned Kova ref (`7c162a32`) confirms the two filter sets select exactly the entries of the old combined filter:

- release profile: {fresh-install:fresh, fresh-install:onboarded-user, bundled-plugin-startup:fresh, agent-cold-warm-message:mock-openai-provider} + {gateway-performance:many-bundled-plugins}
- diagnostic profile: {agent-cold-warm-message:mock-openai-provider} + {gateway-performance:many-bundled-plugins}

## Expected impact

Release wall time for the Kova jobs should fall from about 37 min to about 30 min. The plugin-pressure lane is now the slowest job. The other mock scenarios finish in about 10 min. The cost is one extra runner with its own checkout, install and local build.

The bigger remaining cost is the 80 serial plugin installs, which repeat three times. Fixing that belongs in the Kova fixture (`states/many-bundled-plugins.json` / `support/install-many-plugin-pressure-state.mjs`), and I'll do it as a separate follow-up.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test test/scripts/openclaw-performance-workflow.test.ts`: 50/50 passed
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` are clean. `pnpm check:workflows` reports no findings for `openclaw-performance.yml`. Its only failure is existing zizmor findings in other workflows.
- I compared `kova matrix plan` filter selection against the old filter (see above).

## Worked on by

- @RomneyDa
