prs.title: improve: resume cold-history navigation after update readiness
prs.body:
Related: #182616

This addresses only reconstructible cold-history navigation in the stopped update window, not the issue's other copy/hash or repeated-Doctor costs.

## What Problem This Solves

Updates can keep the Gateway stopped while Doctor builds navigation for old cold-history archives. Those archives remain restorable without the navigation, so this work need not delay readiness.

## User Impact

Update Doctor leaves reconstructible SQLite navigation pending for post-readiness maintenance. Required migrations, integrity and recovery checks remain before activation. Standalone Doctor and PostgreSQL retain their existing behavior. No schema, configuration, retention or permission changes.

**Still a draft: foreground-latency acceptance and five interleaved update/downtime samples are incomplete.** Preparation now runs outside the canonical writer and outside the foreground discovery-reader pool, but complete-archive publication remains atomic. A single diagnostic pair at prior head `471ff839a604` exceeded the declared 20% investigation threshold in tail latency; this is not an accepted regression or a no-regression claim. The test host also reproduced long hot-write COMMIT stalls on unchanged baseline code. Controlled comparative measurement is required before this PR can be marked ready.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing pending SQL predicate and post-readiness transcript-facts scheduler. A cancellable, lifecycle-owned reader prepares verified archive navigation in disposable SQLite. A separate lazy maintenance reader lane prevents foreground discovery cleanup from waiting for the whole archive. The canonical writer rechecks the source/archive identity and pending state, then copies the complete projection in one transaction. No incomplete canonical rows or new durable progress store are published; unused preparation is discarded and restart rediscovers pending archives.

Typed archive-read failures leave the affected archive pending while healthy later archives progress. Authority, cancellation, SQL and lifecycle failures are not swallowed. Ordinary foreground reader deadlines remain unchanged.

## Evidence

### Bounded qualification attempt — 2026-11-18 21:28–21:29 UTC

Stopped before expensive work because sustained host qualification failed. Sixty one-second observations spanning 59.11 seconds used the declared quiet-host limits of I/O full-pressure avg10 <=1% and one-minute load/CPU <=0.25. **48 of 60 observations exceeded the I/O limit**: range 0.69–6.89%, ending at 1.56%. Maximum load/CPU was 0.08094 (128 CPUs), so load was within its limit. The earlier low-pressure snapshot did not hold throughout the window. This is host evidence, not a fresh baseline-write stall or a candidate regression measurement.

Source and publication remain `a078fd677795d17d6633a9c2a189e96c024039ea`, with no local delta. The retained qualified candidate package digest was rechecked as `90fbb6b12768052a4af4262cae161745c0bf1e2567366739b60a3bb2b8c9f5e9`. The admitted base `0aafe6691b818c24ac00a2172e57819b21632554` has state40/agent43; retained historical control has agent42 and was not reused. A matching-base package is not retained. Its supported route is a task-owned detached worktree from that exact admitted Git object and the existing canonical `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mts` build/integrity workflow, not rebuilding the candidate or altering the shared checkout.

Because the host capacity gate failed, that missing baseline was not built. A qualifying committed-runner manifest/preflight and unchanged-baseline RPC control therefore remain unrun, as do all five interleaved pairs. No package installs, Gateway launches, source/review changes, retries for green, threshold changes or native-downtime claims were made. Required next condition: a sustained qualified quiet host, followed by the missing matching-base artifact and the unchanged committed sampler.

### Workload-only follow-up (`a078fd677795d17d6633a9c2a189e96c024039ea`)

This follow-up changes only the performance entrypoint/helper, its README, one plan test and the test-line allocation. Product runtime remains identical to `9901fa77f855c0cf2eecaa0b0032a0086d699f77`; the package/update/restore/automatic-rollback proof below stays bound to that runtime artifact, not a newly built package.

The existing update-performance entrypoint now owns the rerunnable installed-Gateway foreground procedure. Read-only plan/preflight checks artifact and Node SHA-256, fixture-producer bytes, schema compatibility, a fresh owned scratch root and at least five serial A/B pairs. It preserves qualified source/build receipt references as declarations, not inferred provenance. A matching schema-43 baseline package is required; the historical schema-42 control is not qualified for this composition.

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/update-doctor-generation-measure.ts \
  cold cold-navigation-runtime plan .openclaw/tmp/cold-runtime-input.json
```

The manifest and controlled-host requirements are documented in `scripts/perf/README.md` under **Installed cold-navigation foreground workload**. Change only `plan` to `run` after artifact and quiet-host qualification. The fixed workload is three 4,096-event archives, an independent hot session, two `chat.inject` loops and one `chat.history` loop for 60 seconds with 50 ms after responses. Receipts retain all RPC IDs/errors, readiness request intervals, pending/atomic-publication observations, archive hashes/FK checks, host/IO pressure and joined cleanup. The command stops on failures or >=20% adverse paired tail movement rather than retrying for green. It leaves TOTAL UPDATE and native-service GATEWAY DOWNTIME **unmeasured/null**; the separate real native handoff remains required.

Validation: two focused tests passed (570 ms tests, 1.73 s wrapper): real-entrypoint plan/schema refusal and the measured-overlap qualification regression, including mismatched package/Node/fixture/schema and pre-existing-root refusal before fixture mutation. Scripts and tooling-test typechecks, targeted lint/format, script erasability (1,949 files), both Knip unused-file scans (zero findings), scoped diff checks and the official test-line ratchet passed. Net test lines are now 577 with a justified 177-line excess allocation; this includes the prior 435-line runtime regressions plus 142 workload-test lines. CI seconds are not yet available. No packages were installed, Gateways started or full timing samples run for this workload-only addition.

A bounded workload-delta narrative review found a real P2: backfill could finish during unrecorded warmup, allowing a false performance pass. The completion-only gate reproduced that failure. Warmup is now recorded/correlated and compared separately; both measured writes and history must complete with pending work at both request boundaries, followed by eventual completion. Missing overlap is explicitly inconclusive. Request/transition/completion clocks share Gateway launch origin. The report distinguishes sampled pending-window overlap from exact writer-lock occupancy. Targeted supplied-source verification resolved the finding with no new actionable P0–P2 findings. The reviewed workload-only patch SHA-256 is `4aa874f63a498042b7d285c2ed3fc222e01a10e96d061a29cd6ec1aa9d967bbe`; review was narrative, without independent checkout/hash custody or test execution. This does not replace helper-validated review or an end-to-end run of the newly committed sampler.

### Current refreshed-base integration

Source: `9901fa77f855c0cf2eecaa0b0032a0086d699f77`, integrating main `0aafe6691b818c24ac00a2172e57819b21632554` through the managed base-refresh workflow because the PR conflicted. This resolved the reported conflict at that runtime head.

- The sole manual conflict resolution preserves upstream agent-creation alias checks, claim capture and cleanup reservation before the caller-owned maintenance deadline. Dispatch/settlement claim assertions and native witness propagation remain intact. Whole-archive atomic publication and off-writer preparation are unchanged.
- **61 tests across four affected suites passed** in 103.13 s: session-transcript worker lanes, active-facts backfill, cold-storage worker and usage-worker environment/recreation coverage. Core and affected agents/sessions test types, targeted runtime lint/format and scoped diff checks passed. A whole cached diff against the old guest base flags an upstream release-note blank EOF; that release-owned file was not changed by this repair and is not in the PR diff.
- A bounded independent narrative review of the resolved runtime and claim/scope owners found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Runtime-file SHA-256: `234e4249a1e951f802bad47558cffc62ff49c9e7070a5bceb81cf0c41bc2fb24`. This is not helper-validated Auto Review or a review of unrelated upstream changes. No unbounded helper retry was launched.
- The refreshed base carries upstream version/schema and cold-body maintenance changes; this PR adds no new schema or partial canonical navigation contract. Installed-package/update/rollback correctness is now requalified for `9901fa77…` below. The performance measurements remain prior-head diagnostics; no new latency or downtime-distribution claim is made.

### Current artifact and latest-stable functional qualification

- A new canonical package was built once from the accepted source for `9901fa77f855c0cf2eecaa0b0032a0086d699f77`; full package integrity passed. SHA-256: `90fbb6b12768052a4af4262cae161745c0bf1e2567366739b60a3bb2b8c9f5e9`. The managed staged-source snapshot stayed unchanged through build and execution (`b3647cf94ea2d16dc701a2ba23f329d17b4631e201fce42feae71e7d6708846f`); the older `471ff839…` package was not reused.
- The live npm latest-stable tag resolved to **2026.11.5**, and that exact released driver installed under the existing age/script policy without an override. Its Doctor imported real synthetic legacy input and produced agent schema **38**. The correctly bound actual package entrypoint performed a successful real update to the source candidate, also version 2026.11.5 but agent schema **43**. All three 4,096-event archives were pending immediately after update. Node 24.22.1 was used throughout.
- Public `chat.history` opened an old archive before its navigation existed. The existing legacy fallback restored that archive; **all 4,096 original event payloads, sequence values and creation timestamps matched the independent pre-update digest**, including after reopening in another process. The two remaining archives stayed byte-identical. Separate installed Gateways reached HTTP readiness with pending counts **2**, then **1**, and resumed background completion to **0**; foreign-key checks were empty.
- The initial fixture expected history to leave zero navigation rows and therefore stopped after observing 4,096 restored rows. Source inspection confirmed the supported missing-navigation restore fallback. The incorrect fixture oracle and its failure were retained; exact restored bytes were verified independently, and execution continued from the existing state without replaying the successful update or history mutation. No production code or acceptance timeout was changed.
- The maintained, exact-state-bound failing-Doctor package caused a real post-activation failure and **automatic rollback succeeded**. Config, installed finalize-worker hash, six agent-table hashes, schema and remaining archive payloads matched the pre-failure oracle exactly. The restored installed Gateway reached readiness with zero pending navigation. Update run: `2609fcae-bfcb-48c6-b4b0-048d3923af79`; rollback run: `31b95910-bb4b-4ad5-94d0-b90a80d56e7b`.
- This is the same isolated foreground-process `--no-restart` workflow with managed stop/relaunch, not native-service automatic-restart or performance acceptance. No five-pair timing runs, architecture changes or Auto Review retry were performed.

### Prior-head implementation proof (`471ff839a604`)

- Focused repair validation: 46 tests across three affected suites passed (65.44 s wall), followed by two exact-restore/resume regression cases after the final test-only assertion (49.42 s wall). Prior unchanged codec/Doctor and reader-adapter evidence is retained. The foreground-pool routing regression was red before the isolation repair and green afterward. Cold restore before/after completion, missing/corrupt archive progress, cancellation/recreated pass, concurrent restoration, atomic rollback and exact archive preservation are covered.
- Core and affected agents/sessions test typechecks, targeted six-file lint, formatting, docs/script formatting and diff checks passed. The test-line gate passed with 435 net lines and a justified 35-line allocation for the distinct update/restore/corruption/preparation/lifetime/cleanup boundaries.
- Canonical package build and full tarball integrity passed. Candidate SHA-256: `ed3935063014a778e765b27fc6c4d111b7369a45b51dfe5c769180013238e390`. The installed preparation dependency was inspected to verify the isolated lane and private schema transaction, rather than relying on an unchanged worker entrypoint hash. Packaging's UI warnings were also present in the pinned baseline build.
- **Actual update and rollback passed for prior head `471ff839a604`**, using Node 24.22.1 and a fresh published 2026.11.2 installation. Released Doctor imported real synthetic legacy input and created schema 27. A dry run verified the actual package entrypoint, isolated installation root and npm-global mode. The real CLI update succeeded to the rebuilt candidate/schema 42 with all three cold archives still pending.
- Two separate installed-candidate Gateway processes reached real HTTP readiness with pending counts 3 and 2. The first stopped after one complete archive; the second completed the remaining two. Three archives × 4,096 events (12,288 events; approximately 150.9 MB raw envelope bytes) retained exact payload hashes and checked archive metadata, with no foreign-key failures.
- The maintained state-scoped failing-Doctor package caused an actual post-activation failure. Automatic rollback reported succeeded. Config, installed finalize-worker hash, six agent-table hashes, schema and archive payloads exactly matched the pre-failure oracle; the restored installed Gateway reached readiness. Update run: `79d9bfed-a7de-422a-941b-bb183e9abdef`; rollback run: `1c59e044-3cbc-4bbf-8acb-5e2a73d87a26`. This is an isolated foreground-process, `--no-restart` fixture with manual supervised relaunch, not native-service automatic-restart or downtime-distribution proof. All owned Gateway processes were stopped, joined and verified absent.

### Performance qualification is not complete

The prior-head 60-second pilot uses two public `chat.inject` loops plus one `chat.history` loop, with 50 ms between responses and the same archive shape. The following is **one diagnostic pair, not five-pair acceptance**:

| Observed metric | Pinned baseline | Prior candidate (`471ff839a604`) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Successful foreground writes | 2,083 | 1,999 |
| Write median / p95 / p99 (ms) | 7.02 / 9.88 / 14.11 | 7.30 / 11.55 / 38.83 |
| Write p99 after first 3 seconds (ms) | 13.37 | 16.95 |
| Successful history reads | 1,100 | 1,095 |
| History p95 / p99 (ms) | 6.22 / 7.27 | 6.26 / 8.80 |
| Canonical cold publication | Completed before startup | 3 atomic commits; 48.0 ms maximum admitted execution, 137 ms total |
| Cold preparation outside writer | Not applicable during runtime | 3,025 ms total |
| Host I/O full pressure, avg60 start → end (%) | 6.90 → 2.12 | 1.73 → 0.88 |

The measured prior candidate reached readiness with all three pending and finished navigation after 47.5 s. Those timings are diagnostic observations, not a gain claim. The largest remaining write delays were not all archive-overlapping, so atomic copying has not been established as their sole cause.

An earlier prior-candidate pilot failed when a hot-session COMMIT took 14.3 s after backfill had completed. A bounded unchanged-baseline diagnostic then reproduced a 17.9 s COMMIT and the same RPC timeout with no cold backfill running; host I/O pressure rose to about 22% full avg10. Both failures are retained. This demonstrates a baseline problem under those conditions, but does not explain away every candidate tail-latency difference. No timeout, safety or acceptance threshold was increased. Comparative runs stopped rather than retrying for green.

Remaining performance gates: a controlled environment without these baseline stalls, matching-base/current runtime artifacts, execution of the committed foreground sampler, and five interleaved baseline/candidate real-update/native-handoff samples separating TOTAL UPDATE, observed GATEWAY DOWNTIME, eventual background work and foreground latency. The new runtime sampler does not provide updater/native-service measurements. Latest-stable functional upgrade/rollback is now qualified for `9901fa77…` using the newly admitted 2026.11.5 driver. Earlier age-policy refusals and the 2026.11.2 run are historical evidence only. Performance acceptance remains open despite functional correctness passing. The reported main conflict is resolved at `9901fa77…` against `0aafe669…`. The historical installed proof used base `b255cc584…`; refreshed-base acceptance must not be inferred from that older artifact.

### Review and prior-head evidence

The previous published head `54795095a26a7f08b064cee7246395ab19d6eec7` decoded/projected archives while holding the canonical writer. Its prior update/rollback proof remains prior-head evidence, and its measured roughly 540–570 ms archive-overlapping RPC waits prompted this repair. Its [hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200908#issuecomment-6966703854) does not cover the new implementation.

Independent narrative supplied-source reviews resolved two real P2 findings: corrupt-first-archive starvation and inheritance of the foreground 60-second deadline. The pre-refresh targeted review found no new actionable P0–P2 in lane isolation, scratch transaction, cancellation or cleanup. It reviewed runtime snapshot `111da2db5296df74b7e844b9d064220ddec3c391fbf92dd4dfde99da59497f9e`; the final local snapshot `1177095149ebe6c5794513e7812ee7eb44e6cba8c902deb2432e447424a6f1f0` differs only in test/line-allocation metadata. This was not live-checkout or helper-validated review. A newly available bound Auto Review was attempted on the current complete candidate, then interrupted by Gateway shutdown; no validated report was recovered and it was not rerun. Local structured review and current-head CI remain incomplete.

Requested by Jacqueline Henriksen.

prs.title: improve: prepare plugin downloads before updates stop the Gateway
prs.body:
Related: #182616

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin archives can still be downloaded after an update stops the Gateway, even though the core candidate is already prepared. Slow registry transfers can extend that unavailable window.

## User Impact

Real updates attempt script-free preparation of selected exact-version npm plugin archives while the old Gateway serves. Failed preparation, changed selection or an unavailable cache falls back to normal installation. Dry runs stay metadata-only; no configuration change is required.

**Draft: forward-update and cancellation behavior are proven, but comparative timing and automatic post-startup-failure rollback acceptance remain incomplete. No downtime improvement is claimed.**

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse existing plugin target selection, the npm archive owner and npm’s integrity-addressed transport cache across the fresh-process finalization boundary. Packs use private disposable workspaces with scripts disabled and their selected version/integrity checked. No new persisted manifest, cache owner, configuration option or update protocol is introduced.

The normal installer independently re-resolves source/release cohort and retains compatibility, trust, integrity, capability-consent and recovery checks. An enabled operator install policy keeps downloads in that installer. Prefetch does not install, migrate or execute plugins.

A real timeout test exposed a missing cancellation boundary: candidate admission bypasses ordinary CLI startup, allowing its detached npm download to outlive admission. The repair uses the existing CLI signal gate and command-process scope to abort and join those children before exit, without granting updater authority or changing timeouts.

## Evidence

- **Actual installed update passed on the final repaired candidate.** Released 2026.11.5 accepted native foreground handoff, parked before activation and restarted into the canonical candidate. Terminal verification confirmed boot, running version/build match, healthy readiness, no plugin errors and loaded plugin 2.0.0 with matching archive integrity.
- **One archive GET before shutdown; zero duplicate GETs through post-core convergence.** The old Gateway was ready before and after that transfer. Real npm tests also cover changed selection/cache eviction (normal fallback, two total GETs), unchanged selection/environment-only cache (one total GET), metadata-only dry runs, operator-policy exclusion and advisory preparation failure. The original prefetch regression was red on the base.
- **Actual released-driver cancellation, red → green.** Before repair, timed-out admission left an orphan npm process and held HTTP request. After repair, the request closed before fixture teardown, the observed npm process exited and its private workspace was removed. The run correctly ended failed/update-activation-timeout while the original Gateway stayed ready on 2026.11.5 with plugin 1.0.0. No custody or permission safeguard was relaxed.
- **Consent was preserved.** A widened-capability plugin archive was downloaded without activation; plugin 1.0.0 stayed loaded. The real candidate CLI subsequently refused the same update without consent (exit 1, “requires capability consent”). Initial explicit-consent installation passed. The normal installer is unchanged by the later cancellation repair.
- **181 focused consumer cases passed**, covering admission and its heartbeat/workshop consumers, executor, preflight and real-registry behavior. The cancellation regression failed before repair and passed after it. Targeted CLI/update typecheck, scoped lint/format and diff checks passed. The final canonical self-contained runtime-only package build, tarball integrity and import-graph checks passed.
- **Fresh independent static P0–P2 review found no concrete actionable defect** in the original change, cache-selector test addition or cancellation repair. Reviewers did not execute code or mount the checkout; runtime receipts are separate evidence. Two earlier local AutoReview attempts were interrupted without validated receipts. A new bounded review of the full workload/source snapshot prepared one complete pass, then timed out during native execution without a validated report. None is a clean local review. Hosted ClawSweeper found no actionable findings on preceding head 81ddd2b78c96338f50b014efc7bed07de958558b, not the later signal repair.

<details>
<summary>Validation detail and the original custody failure</summary>

The native forward test was repeated after the signal repair, against the rebuilt canonical artifact. The target is the private source candidate (package version 2026.11.4), not the older official 2026.11.4 release. Runtime-only packaging is not full declaration/release qualification.

Cache fixtures clear both the explicit cache and task-private HOME cache after packing sources, so setup cannot seed the observed download. All four real-registry cases passed. The signal regression was moved unchanged to a focused file to respect the existing test-file line limit and passed again; the original admission test file is unchanged. The previous 149-case receipt is retained as prior evidence, not substituted for the affected-consumer reruns.

The initial raw-CLI/foreground failure was a fixture/lifecycle mismatch: unmodified released Doctor refused the same database custody and named the exact serving Gateway PID. After stopping/joining that owned Gateway, baseline Doctor and the actual stopped --no-restart update passed. Correct native handoff then passed. This is not evidence of a prefetch database-handle leak; the stopped control is not managed-downtime proof.

</details>

### Predeclared paired timing acceptance

Before measurements: extend the committed update-generation workload with an installed-plugin-prefetch mode. Compare the canonical package built from baseline b255cc584c9b5b31de7f89df56357bdfe4b317f9 with the already-qualified repaired candidate (SHA-256 385a8aae406c57fda8ae4b362ea269aabd0f6191f75aa03b9687a6427a7bc554); both are driven by the same released 2026.11.5 installation. Run five serial AB pairs, not separate baseline/candidate batches.

Fixed workload: four npm plugins, each with 128 payload files of 8 KiB; plugin 1.0.0 is installed before each run and 2.0.0 is selected during update. Delay each selected archive response by 3 seconds (12 seconds of serial controlled transport wait). Seed 128 MiB shared and 64 MiB agent synthetic SQLite payload plus 4,096 ordinary 1-KiB files. Each case has a fresh private prefix, state, HOME and npm cache; installed-driver/setup dependencies may be warm within that case, selected plugin archives start cold. Record artifact hashes, actual host load, visible cgroup CPU/IO/pressure and harness resource counters; do not describe uncontrolled host work as absent.

Required counts/outcomes: four selected archive GETs per run, zero candidate GETs after readiness is lost, identical final plugin versions/integrities, verified new serving build and intact synthetic state. TOTAL UPDATE is native run creation to terminal verification; separately report request-to-observation wall time. GATEWAY DOWNTIME is the observed readiness-loss/recovery interval, sampled every 200 ms with a 500-ms probe deadline (report that observation uncertainty).

A win requires median downtime to remove at least 70% of the controlled archive wait (8.4 seconds), with no extra archive downloads and no regression in total-update median/p95. Report median, nearest-rank p95, min/max and paired deltas for both metrics. Any worse metric is disclosed for owner acceptance; a 20% regression stops further performance acceptance. This rule is recorded before the first timing run; no result is implied.

### Remaining acceptance — keep draft

- **Paired benchmark blocked before measurement (0 valid samples).** The first synthetic plugin install correctly required explicit source trust; the new workload omitted the force confirmation already used in the qualified fixture recipe. This is a setup error, not a product regression. The failed run then encountered a sandbox artifact-synchronization size limit on its private npm cache, requiring operator recovery before retry. No latency result or gain is available. The committed workload and fixed acceptance rule are retained.
- Workload safety review identified uncertain-request cleanup and unjoined replacement-process teardown; both were repaired before execution. The revised static review found no remaining concrete P0–P2 issue. Script typecheck, lint, format and import checks passed. This is separate from the unavailable helper-validated local review.
- **Automatic rollback after candidate startup failure remains unproven.** A controlled pre-readiness SIGKILL left the isolated run at restarting after its owners exited. Recovery state/artifacts were preserved, without forced downgrade, custody override or manual restore. This failure is not baseline-attributed and is not claimed as a prefetch regression. Earlier package/config restoration plus a manual healthy restart is not automatic recovery proof.
- **Comparative timing remains outstanding:** at least five interleaved baseline/candidate samples on representative plugin/state shape under serialized same-host/cache conditions. Report archive counts first, then TOTAL UPDATE and GATEWAY DOWNTIME median/p95 and spread separately. The functional native ledger supplied no downtime value; no measured or universal speedup is asserted.
- The execution marker covers plugin entry evaluation, not an independent lifecycle-hook fixture; script suppression uses existing explicit npm flags. Broad exact-head CI, full declaration packaging, the incomplete local review route and enforced owner/security approvals remain outstanding. No merge, release or deployment requested. Production state was untouched.

Simplification: existing selection, archive, cache and cancellation owners remain authoritative. Only the signal bridge required by the observed timeout failure was added; there is no parallel cache or recovery protocol.

Prepared with Jacqueline Henriksen.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with Jacqueline Henriksen](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/0883b476-2af0-4f4f-9bc7-593c230557af)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/ef3e6f69)

## Worked on by

- @jjjhenriksen

prs.title: improve: avoid scanning unrelated agent files during updates
prs.body:
Related: #182616

## What Problem This Solves

Update database discovery walks default-agent files to inventory temporary directories even when those trees cannot contain a selected plugin database. Installations with large agent trees pay for this unrelated traversal during update preparation.

## User Impact

Updates avoid scanning agent subtrees outside retained plugin resource roots while keeping the same database selection and backup coverage. Full backup archives retain their complete temporary-directory inventory. No user configuration or migration is required. An older installed updater retains its own shipped discovery behavior on the first hop.

This is a draft implementation PR: real installed upgrades, a latest-stable native foreground handoff, documented explicit operator rollback, recovered-Gateway readiness, and retained-data checks pass. The structured local-review checkpoint and broad CI remain incomplete. No total-update or Gateway-downtime speedup is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The resource-inventory owner can limit temporary-root discovery to the plugin paths that database discovery already selects, including their ancestors. Explicit nested includes and custom agent roots keep their existing policy; ordinary archive callers keep the complete default inventory. This removes unrelated traversal rather than introducing a cache or another database-discovery owner.

Simplification: 18 net production lines, 74 net test lines, plus a rerunnable discovery phase in the existing update I/O workload. The remaining test/workload growth protects scoped exclusions and records counts independently of wall-clock noise.

## Evidence

- Regression reproduced against `b255cc584c9b5b31de7f89df56357bdfe4b317f9`: the real discovery owner selected the correct core database but issued three unrelated agent-directory reads; the fixed regression issues zero.
- 20 focused tests pass across database resources, resource inventory, and backup ownership. Coverage includes every retained account/token database beneath a disabled plugin resource, snapshot payload rows, custom roots, protected children under temporary exclusions, privacy markers, aliases, restore, and refusal paths. The targeted command took 70.39 s including a 37 s compiler-cache preparation; actual test bodies were about 26 s. CI seconds are not yet available.
- A complete candidate package build and package-tarball integrity check pass. The build reports UI asset-budget warnings; no UI source is changed.
- The actual installed `2026.11.2` CLI successfully updates to the built `2026.11.4` candidate through ordinary `update --yes --json --tag <tarball> --no-restart`. Real foreground Gateways pass HTTP readiness before and after; WebSocket probes confirm their actual serving version/build IDs. The basic probe's privileged diagnostics are scope-limited; a separate configured-auth CLI `update.status` call succeeds. No auth configuration or grants were manually changed. Seeded Unicode rows in two core and three disabled-plugin databases, full integrity checks, and 2,000 ordinary files survive the update.
- This single functional CLI invocation takes 174.99 s including launch/cleanup. It is not a before/after full-update benchmark. Gateway downtime is unmeasured: this fixture externally stops/restarts foreground processes with `--no-restart`, so no managed-downtime value or zero-downtime claim is inferred.
- Scoped TypeScript validation and workload lint pass; changed-file format and `git diff --check` pass. Core lint reports one inherited `max-lines` violation in `backup-sqlite-snapshot.ts`: baseline 720 counted lines, candidate 721, existing limit 700. No limit or baseline was weakened.

Acceptance declared before measurement: exact selected database set, zero unrelated agent-tree reads, and no discovery median/p95 regression. Five warm interleaved baseline/candidate samples use 200 nested directories, 2,000 ordinary files and one existing core SQLite database. Both changed baseline production modules are frozen from the base; other dependencies and fixture state are shared. Linux, Node 24.20.0; starting load averages 8.44/12.70/11.92.

| Discovery-owner measurement | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Unrelated directory reads, every sample | 201 | 0 |
| Median | 94.48 ms | 90.13 ms |
| p95 (maximum of 5) | 94.83 ms | 92.44 ms |
| Range | 92.57–94.83 ms | 85.35–92.44 ms |

Rerun: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/update-state-io-measure.ts --baseline b255cc584 --phase discovery --samples 5`. A separate CPU-profile run is attribution evidence, not part of the timing table. These are owner-only observations, not installed CLI-update or downtime measurements.

**Recovered fault fixture — explicit operator path, not automatic package rollback:** the controlled post-activation Doctor failure reports all seven pre-migration databases restored but initially leaves the failed package installed. The first repair used a `bin/openclaw` symlink nested beneath the source checkout and correctly failed the installation check: root discovery selected the enclosing checkout rather than the admitted fixture package. Artifact-preserving inspection confirmed the saved cohort/state/config binding. The four root-discovery/recovery owner files are byte-identical in the reviewed base and this PR. Retrying through the originally admitted absolute public launcher completed normal repair (exit 0). The documented `update --tag <known-good-tarball> --yes --no-restart` rollback then completed (exit 0), restored the known-good package, and its real Gateway passed HTTP readiness and serving version/build checks. Independent private-image reads verified all five seeded databases and full integrity, plus all 2,000 ordinary files. The original failure and stopped receipts remain preserved. No journal, identity marker, permission check, or product source was changed to force recovery. Automatic package restoration in the initial fault case is **not** claimed.

**Latest-stable native foreground update — passed:** a clean installation of live-checked stable `2026.11.5` ran public `gateway call update.run` with the real detached update owner and reached native status `succeeded`. The replacement Gateway passed HTTP readiness and verified its actual version/build identity. The local registry served a version-only `2026.11.6` fixture made with the maintained fixture-stamping helper, not a published release: all 21,166 package members were audited, only the three version/inventory metadata files changed, and both changed production bundles retained their original hashes. This exercises the built candidate without patching its modules or bypassing admission. Five seeded database payloads/full integrity and all 2,000 ordinary files were preserved.

This one functional run took **118.52 s request-to-observed-terminal**, separately from the HTTP readiness interruption. Across 1,219 readiness probes (100 ms polling, 1 s request timeout), the last pre-update ready observation to first replacement ready observation was **58.84 s**; failed observations spanned 58.63 s. This is an observed availability window, not an exact downtime counter: the native receipt has `downtimeMs: null`. There is no comparative total-update/downtime timing claim. The verified foreground successor was stopped through its exact native ownership identity; the original Gateway exited 0, and no fixture process remained.

An earlier foreground proof attempt failed in its observer when the released updater temporarily removed `package.json` during publication. Its cleanup stopped the foreground owner while settlement was pending. That original attempt is retained as failed, not counted as a pass or timing sample. Native `update repair` reconciled it; after repair, the actual installed candidate passed readiness, serving-build and retained-data checks. A transient duplicate-column startup error before repair is preserved rather than masked; it did not recur in the clean native handoff. The only observer correction tolerates `ENOENT` for that exact manifest during accepted publication, retaining the original deadline and every other read/parse failure. No product schema, journal, grant or guard was edited.

The maintained Docker runner is unavailable in this sandbox; both successful installed package/process paths above are real product execution, not the synthetic lifecycle driver.

Two bound Auto Review attempts were interrupted around Gateway restarts. A later same-route attempt failed in response handoff (`FileNotFoundError` for its response JSON); no validated local report or clean Auto Review result is claimed. Hosted ClawSweeper independently reported no actionable source findings on this head ([review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200916#issuecomment-6967036005)); that advisory review does not replace the real proof or broad CI. A fresh independent OpenClaw subagent (separate context) performed a P0–P2 static review of the complete five-file frozen delta and requested dependency/caller context against `b255cc584c9b5b31de7f89df56357bdfe4b317f9` (diff SHA-256 `a701791945d56673e2e0791f3f90da11981776781150f6a1c7c2e7413e1b73db`); no P0–P2 regression or remaining material source-context gap was found. It is a source-snapshot review, not checkout-based execution or helper-validated Auto Review. Directory counts are asserted by the workload; timing acceptance is checked against the printed sample table rather than enforced by a timing assertion. Statistical full-update baseline/candidate timing, a managed downtime comparison, and broad current-head CI remain outstanding. Draft-skipped CI jobs are not passing evidence.

Contributor credit: Jacqueline Henriksen.

prs.title: fix(codex): recognize native completion handoff after explicit yield
prs.body:
## Current status — November 18, 2026

Published head: `6ee8cd7c7a9f3423de0ed2783a0c6af1fe38c0d7`. This is an empty CI-retry commit on `797ff4a87384a94144ffd63d3124ee3c5630d6a9`; both have tested tree `19fafe8d4e49f0ffe2180172b5d8ecba6c842c2e`. Current-head CI, OpenGrep and the central CI gate pass, and GitHub reports the PR mergeable. The previous OpenGrep download outage is resolved. The historical runtime proof below remains attributed to its named source revisions.

Related: #188224

## What Problem This Solves

Completed native Codex child work can lose its completion acknowledgment when the requester accepts more native work and explicitly yields without a visible final reply. Core previously ignored native-only acceptance, allowing completion delivery to report `visible_reply_missing`.

## User Impact

A successful explicit yield can acknowledge the handoff to accepted native work, whose result can subsequently resume the requester. Released custody, a replaced requester, or a revoked Gateway cannot authorize new requester effects.

Core and the bundled Codex plugin must ship together: the plugin consumes a new helper on the existing private-local `agent-harness-completion` SDK surface. No public SDK type becomes required; there is no schema change or older-host fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing host completion owner records accepted native assignments against the exact operational run and revalidates retained requester custody at settlement. Pending-to-active promotion refreshes the registration with the surviving assignment handle. Only explicit successful yields settle native handoffs; failed, aborted, implicit and wrong-run cases remain excluded.

## Evidence

Historical test-allocation head (before the integrations below): `4fd2784ecac6b726a42fa5e326ddb4486bf30576`. This adds only the regression-test allocation below; production and test source are unchanged from runtime-proven head `5b50c82b96bf63a964b80240acaf04fceb7acd14`, tree `d2c9a30a95c99c1dd9b002a0323fbf413b7a1b21`.

### Regression-test growth allocation

`config/test-lines-allocations/codex-native-completion-handoff-pr188229.txt` grants exactly **362** lines, matching this PR's literal-newline growth: custody regression **+41**, direct authority **+1**, execution-boundary authority **+144**, and handoff settlement **+176**. These regressions protect native-only acknowledgment, the surviving promotion handle, and distinct release/replacement/revocation boundaries that existing core-spawn tests do not cover. The allocation is limited to these regression contracts.

The shared `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` is unchanged; no inherited main debt is allocated. The repository checker passes against base `68fbe4ac429cdac7a54541df40367d66defd0161`, including the exact staged snapshot: **6,294,619** test lines; effective ceiling **6,332,151**; slack **37,532**. `git diff --check` passes. The package-script equivalent used on this host is `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base 68fbe4ac429cdac7a54541df40367d66defd0161`.

### Running Gateway and native execution

**Four candidate Gateway scenarios pass.** These use the built Gateway, authenticated WebSocket RPC, bundled Codex **0.164.0**, real native tool execution, requester storage, admission, settlement and delivery classification on Linux / Node **26.12.1**. Model responses come from an isolated local HTTPS Responses fixture with synthetic authentication.

| Scenario | Observed behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Allowed handoff | Native child A completes; its real requester receives `CHILD_A`, accepts native child B and explicitly yields with **zero payloads**. Real settlement records `requesterContinuationSettled`; A's delivery is acknowledged as `delivered:true, path:direct`. |
| Later result and effects | The requester receives B's actual `CHILD_B` completion input, executes native `exec_command` to write `REAL_REQUESTER_EFFECT`, and persists assistant final `PR188229_FINAL_CHILD_B`. B's delivery is also acknowledged. |
| Custody released while paused | Real delivery returns `source_owner_changed` / `intentional_non_delivery`; **0** new requester model requests, **0** new transcript messages, and no requester file. |
| Physical requester replaced while paused | The real in-Gateway storage owner persists a different session ID and lifecycle revision, independently verified through `sessions.describe`. The old delivery returns `source_owner_changed` / `intentional_non_delivery`; **0** new requester model requests, **0** new transcript messages, and no requester file. |
| Canonical Gateway owner revoked while paused | Real retained custody becomes noncurrent and its signal aborts. Delivery returns `delivered:false, path:none`; **0** new requester model requests, **0** new transcript messages, and no requester file. |

The three negative controls first reach an awaited barrier **inside the real requester `startTurn`, before its real routing/preparation**. They then invalidate the selected owner and resume the actual production path. The load-time instrumentation only observes results, introduces that barrier, and invokes the real revocation/replacement owners. It does **not** replace `startTurn`, seed delivery receipts, fabricate a settled flag, or substitute an array append for an execution effect.

Physical replacement is an injected mutation through the real storage owner, not a claim about concurrent public delete/recreate RPCs. Gateway revocation targets the canonical host lifetime captured by retained custody, rather than a bound resolver wrapper.

Candidate wrapper wall times: allowed flow **64.01s**, release **50.35s**, physical replacement **54.93s**, Gateway revocation **52.82s**, including Gateway startup and cleanup.

<details>
<summary>Redacted and normalized Gateway/native-path output</summary>

```text
candidate / initial native assignment:
  yielded=true payloads=0 requesterContinuationSettled=true
candidate / completion-A requester:
  received=CHILD_A accepted=native-child-B
  yielded=true payloads=0 requesterContinuationSettled=true
  delivery={delivered:true,path:direct}
candidate / completion-B requester:
  received=CHILD_B
  native-file=REAL_REQUESTER_EFFECT
  persisted-assistant-final=PR188229_FINAL_CHILD_B
  delivery={delivered:true,path:direct}

released:
  barrierReached=true
  delivery=false reason=source_owner_changed disposition=intentional_non_delivery
  newRequesterModelRequests=0 newTranscriptMessages=0 requesterFileExists=false
requester-replaced:
  barrierReached=true differentSessionId=true differentLifecycleRevision=true
  delivery=false reason=source_owner_changed disposition=intentional_non_delivery
  newRequesterModelRequests=0 newTranscriptMessages=0 requesterFileExists=false
gateway-revoked:
  barrierReached=true custodyCurrent=false custodySignalAborted=true
  delivery=false path=none
  newRequesterModelRequests=0 newTranscriptMessages=0 requesterFileExists=false
```

</details>

### Regression comparison

The same Gateway/native sequence was replayed with the complete original `settleRequesterRun` function from PR base `68fbe4ac429cdac7a54541df40367d66defd0161` (compiled from that Git source) substituted at module load. Both initial and completion-A yields had zero payloads but **no settled handoff**; the actual classifier returned:

```text
original settlement owner / completion-A:
  yielded=true payloads=0 requesterContinuationSettled=false
  delivery={delivered:false,path:direct,reason:visible_reply_missing}
  error="completion agent did not produce a visible reply"
candidate settlement owner / completion-A:
  yielded=true payloads=0 requesterContinuationSettled=true
  delivery={delivered:true,path:direct}
```

The original-owner replay also receives B's actual completion and executes/persists its later final, isolating the missing acknowledgment from a setup failure. The differential's expected-failure assertions pass; wrapper wall time **57.91s**. This is a production settlement-owner differential inside the running candidate Gateway, not a claim of a whole original-main build.

### Build identity and supporting validation

- The reused build was produced before the final commit, so its metadata labels producer head `e90278c646e2`. The repository's canonical `resolveRunNodeInputSignature` independently matches **both** build and runtime-postbuild stamps against the current candidate inputs. Build signature: `451850e044a352b3e8f2924f68b4c30c0b48e685551300abaa13b813ff8a4477`; runtime signature: `b6a3f8b7c38074f2d4eb919c7333d235a56c6eb21404334ba5e79cdbdc61a367`. This is a staged-source build identity check, not a claim that the producer stamp already named the later commit.
- Existing promotion regression: the new custody case fails on prior PR head `e90278c646e2` because the active handle is stale, then passes with this repair; the custody suite passes **22/22**, including result delivery and surviving-handle release.
- Existing focused suites: **118 passing tests**, including the host authority, native custody/completion delivery, requester settlement, and Codex follow-up attempt controls. The older four-case authority composition still simulates requester execution; it is supporting coverage, distinct from the running-Gateway evidence above.
- Both regular core/extensions typechecks, scoped oxlint/oxfmt, and `git diff --check` pass. Original-base mock-export, max-lines and test-line ratchets pass. The shared scalar remains unchanged; the only additional test credit is the exact 362-line allocation described above.
- Full candidate build passed, exit **0**, **13m 19.9s**: runtime/packages, bundled plugins, unified declarations, CLI bootstrap guard, UI and postbuild. All **161 public SDK subpaths** pass export validation; the built host exports `registerAgentHarnessCompletionHandoff`. Earlier installation/readiness evidence remains package-loading evidence.
- Existing external shared Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) was `scoped-clean` for base `68fbe4ac429c` through the final staged snapshot. Additional independent source/evidence inspection checked the actual requester path, physical replacement, canonical Gateway revocation, and the real child-completion inputs. These are supporting reviews, not maintainer approval.

**Prior-head CI limitation remains visible:** the [test-line budget job on `5b50c82b96bf`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41657963914/job/125994397263) compares against newer main `850bdb1c8e5a`: **6,434,597** test lines versus ceiling **6,433,074**; this PR adds **362** lines. The arithmetic attributes **1,161** over-ceiling lines to comparison main plus this PR's 362. This is not a passing CI claim, and the earlier review could not independently download that job's log. The new commit allocates only this PR's 362 lines and does not absorb the inherited 1,161-line deficit. No broader baseline increase is included; CI for the allocation commit is separate and is not claimed green here.

### Proof limits

The new replay proves real Gateway/native execution with deterministic external model I/O, not hosted-model behavior, channel delivery or restart recovery. It uses **two distinct native children**; same-thread promotion retains its separate committed regression. An attempted same-child follow-up on this candidate was rejected at native receiver lookup; no successful same-child reuse is claimed. [#189344](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/189344) tracks a separate collected-receiver restoration repair.

The base comparison swaps the original settlement owner into the same built replay; it is not a complete original-main binary build. No UI changes are included.

### Existing focused reproduction commands

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-subagent-monitor.custody.test.ts -t 'refreshes accepted completion custody' --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts src/agents/agent-harness-completion-authority.test.ts -t 'revalidates native completion at the requester execution boundary' --maxWorkers=1
```


## Current-main integration — November 9, 2026

Integrated main `34f7aa1425d293f819254ecd0a9da2ef4d1083b2` into this branch to remove the GitHub merge conflict. The sole conflict was the imports in `native-subagent-model-input.ts`; both the existing native-run identity helper and main's agent-path helper are retained. No behavioral repair, test allocation, or baseline change was introduced by this integration.

Validated integrated tree `19fafe8d4e49f0ffe2180172b5d8ecba6c842c2e`, published as `797ff4a87384a94144ffd63d3124ee3c5630d6a9`: all four selected suites / **71 tests** passed through the canonical wrapper (526.04s, including cold preparation); core typechecking, typed lint on the conflict file, formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Earlier runtime proof and CI above remain evidence for their named revisions. Hosted CI for this new head is separate; it is not claimed passed here.

The release-adapted fix remains active in the locally deployed 2026.11.2 combined package; see the operational follow-up in the conversation.

prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): avoid search timeouts during source refresh
prs.body:
Related: #187429, #132296

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway-hosted Wiki searches wait for source import and compilation even when existing Markdown is already searchable. Large imports can consume the complete search deadline.

## User Impact

Search existing Wiki pages while source refresh and compilation continue in the background. After publication, subsequent searches find the imported content. No configuration or data migration is required.

Search reads live Markdown, so individual imported pages may appear before the entire refresh is published; results are not a snapshot of a whole refresh. Explicit imports, standalone callers without an active service, and `ingest.autoCompile: false` retain their existing behavior.

**Maintainer decision requested:** approve the shared 60-second successful-refresh window and service-owned retries with 5–60-second backoff. These freshness/recovery defaults remain an owner decision; local use and the correctness repair below do not supply that approval.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both `wiki_search` and Gateway `wiki.search` use the existing service-owned refresh coordinator shared with dashboards. Queries initialize the vault and use existing candidate selection and scan fallback without waiting for maintenance.

Current-head Gateway verification also exposed a lifetime defect in the original PR: a cold 6,000-source import could enumerate beyond the search response, then fail its lazy plugin-state opening with an `AsyncWorkScope` AbortError inherited from the completed caller. This reproduced in a fresh isolated namespace before any source pages were imported.

The repair uses the existing host service scheduler, including its async-resource ownership, for both demand admission and retries. Its child scope replaces the separate abort controller; shutdown closes admission, cancels pending work, and joins active synchronization. Existing coalescing, freshness/backoff limits, and stale-service guards remain. No core SDK, configuration, or schema surface is added.

This extends the signal-lifetime fix already merged in #187429 and consolidates the dashboard maintenance from #132296.

## Evidence

Validated revision: `875805b71957ff7a63b193cf492da25fbdb0a2ff`. The uploaded Git tree `dc7c6b5c782fd6687df5da9c54968f48d20e8337` exactly matches the reviewed and tested local tree.

- Four focused files / 48 tests passed, including real query/compiler cases that close the caller's public async-work scope before releasing a paused importer, and service restart, retry, cancellation, and shutdown controls.
- Production and test typechecks, canonical type-aware lint with pinned-runtime parity (zero warnings/errors), formatting, whitespace, assertion safety, and the test-line ratchet passed. The existing 196-line allocation and ceiling are unchanged.
- Fresh independent review found no actionable P0–P2 defects.

### Built Gateway proof

**Inspectable current-head evidence:** [Captured Gateway terminal output, HTTP response bodies, durable publication event, shutdown process logs, and client harness](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188256#issuecomment-6640716126). Captured 2026-11-03 08:39–08:41 UTC; on 2026-11-04 the production-source build hashes were rechecked against GitHub head `875805b71957ff7a63b193cf492da25fbdb0a2ff` and matched exactly. IP addresses, endpoint URLs, host identifiers, and the synthetic authentication token are redacted where present. This supplies the inspectable artifacts for the behavior-proof request; the separate maintainer policy decision remains open.

Linux / Node 26.13.0, synthetic Markdown only, isolated filesystem/state and network namespace, no real credentials, models, paid keys, importer/compiler mocks, clock changes, or artificial work delays.

The unchanged host runtime was built from parent `86401535f4ef0579933241dfd82de8a980364651`; the Wiki package was rebuilt with the canonical package builder from the repaired source. The loader explicitly selected the candidate package over the bundled baseline. The only changed production files are [index.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/875805b71957ff7a63b193cf492da25fbdb0a2ff/extensions/memory-wiki/index.ts) and [source-sync.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/875805b71957ff7a63b193cf492da25fbdb0a2ff/extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-sync.ts).

| Real Gateway observation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Cold query with 6,000 pending source files | Existing Cobalt entity returned, HTTP 200, 1.310s; 96 real imported pages observed and no publication. |
| Another query during the same import | Same existing entity returned, HTTP 200, 0.887s; imports advanced 96 → 296 while publication count remained zero. |
| Real import and compiler completion | Accepted publication contained 6,000 source pages, one entity, and nine reports. |
| Query after publication | Newly imported Zirconium source returned its evidence snippet, HTTP 200, 3.710s. |
| Separate fresh 6,000-input shutdown control | Search returned during import as imported pages advanced 2 → 122; zero publications. SIGTERM exited cleanly with code 0 in 679ms; no publication appeared and the journal remained unchanged after exit. |

Selected assertion/output summary, with machine identifiers and fixture paths omitted:

```json
{"query":"cobalt","phase":"before-publication","httpStatus":200,"elapsedMs":1310,"resultPath":"entities/cobalt.md","importedPagesObserved":96,"publications":0}
{"query":"cobalt","phase":"during-refresh","httpStatus":200,"elapsedMs":887,"importedBefore":96,"importedAfter":296,"publications":0}
{"phase":"published","sourcePages":6000,"entityPages":1,"reportPages":9}
{"query":"zirconium","phase":"after-publication","httpStatus":200,"elapsedMs":3710,"snippet":"Zirconium publication evidence."}
{"phase":"shutdown-during-refresh","exitCode":0,"elapsedMs":679,"noPublication":true,"journalStableAfterExit":true}
```

Package/source identity used for those runs:

```text
index.ts sha256 44bdbf83fec848e777c8f25222878681d0dd9aa2e88490b38bd9a95fadce0435
source-sync.ts sha256 e739012c2115dbf76aa84f7367ac9fa97496831d469038820a9771a7c70b4b87
```

The original 6,000-source failure and repaired run exercise real Gateway tool HTTP dispatch, source import, compilation, durable publication, query, and service shutdown. These are completion observations, not latency guarantees or a comparison benchmark.

The host runtime and candidate Wiki package were built successfully. The full host build's unrelated UI stage stopped at Vite temp-cache setup on a read-only dependency mount; UI was disabled for this runtime proof. No full UI build or full-repository test pass is claimed. Hosted CI for the new head has not yet completed.

## Operational relevance

I have used the combined Wiki release backports for several days in my own deployment, and they made Wiki usable for my daily work. That operational report concerns the combined backports; the pinned candidate proof above is separate, isolated evidence for this PR.

## Merge Danger

Reverting restores awaited search synchronization and the previous refresh lifetime. No schema, configuration, protocol, or stored-data migration changes are introduced. The owner decision about the freshness window and autonomous retries remains explicit above.

prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): avoid repeated full scans during compilation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Wiki compilation rereads and reparses the entire vault after updating related blocks and again after updating generated reports, even when almost every source page is unchanged.

Related: #186881

## User Impact

Compiles do less file-reading and parsing work while preserving generated pages, counts, projections, and compiled-cache source identity. No configuration, storage schema, package version, or migration changes are required. This change is independent of diagnostic snapshot PR #186883.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep scan entries only for the current compile and refresh compiler-written paths before deriving the next projection. The sibling scan module owns reading, scanned-byte fingerprints, projections, and discovery ordering together; the compiler retains publication ownership. Invalid/ignored page digests and title-tie ordering remain intact. There is no persistent cache, watcher, or additional state owner.

The compiler extraction fixes the grandfathered file-size violation. Shared test fixtures and parameterized concurrent-edit cases keep the entire PR's test-line delta at zero without raising either baseline or dropping the distinct behavioral checks.

## Evidence

The real main-branch Gateway comparison uses baseline compiler `d7349d9395e2bde0f42882a9f7ef8afab59e19c3` and this candidate on the same built main host. It is separate from the earlier 2026.10.8 release-backport measurements. Synthetic fixture: 1,000 sources, one changed entity, nine generated reports; no production state or model calls.

Instrumented real `wiki.compile` RPC proof:

| Measured page reads | Main baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Unchanged source | 3 | 1 |
| All fixture pages | 3,030 | 1,014 |

These count Gateway main-thread `fs.promises.readFile` calls for wiki page paths, not all filesystem I/O. Both arms produced identical page counts and generated-content digest `55b74cdc731f37d00c75461bcab3a13754c9927ef308fc523619adb489d8eae6` after normalizing only generated `updatedAt` clocks. Each publication's source-generation hash matched an independent hash of that arm's actual final bytes. Raw source hashes differ between arms because their generated timestamps differ; they are not falsely normalized for the identity check.

The committed real-Gateway runner has an opt-in read counter (`WIKI_BENCH_COUNT_READS=1`); timing runs omit it. It waits for plugin sidecar readiness before invoking Wiki methods. Packaged plugin fingerprints include hidden setup artifacts. The host fingerprint covers its broader checkout, including generated tooling files; both arms within each run use the identical built host.

A separate uninstrumented run alternated five warm compile calls per arm after entity edits, with task-owned builds/checks paused:

| Warm `wiki.compile` RPC | Main baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median | 1,725.0 ms | 1,110.0 ms |
| p95 (nearest rank, n=5) | 2,134.0 ms | 1,331.6 ms |
| Range | 1,317.1–2,134.0 ms | 867.7–1,331.6 ms |

All five candidate samples were faster; median decreased 35.7%, p95 37.6%. Every pair retained matching generated output/counts and independently validated source identity. The predeclared 20% warm median/p95 regression guard passed. Cold initial compiles are separate single observations: 7,668.5 ms baseline versus 8,626.7 ms candidate (+12.5%); no cold improvement is claimed. This shared host had one-minute load 5.36–5.98. These results describe the synthetic workload, not a predicted production-vault speedup. Profiling did not yield a usable main-thread profile, so no CPU/RSS conclusion is claimed.

The focused regression is red on the actual main baseline (three unchanged-source reads, expected one) and green on the candidate. The consolidated compiler suite passes 10/10 tests, including ordering, import projections, malformed input, source preservation, cancellation, and both initial-scan/dashboard-write external edits. prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): avoid diagnostic timeouts on large vaults
prs.body:
Closes #186881

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes wiki status and doctor timing out on large bridge vaults when diagnostic requests synchronize sources and count every page before returning.

## User Impact

The updated CLI and `wiki_status` read the last published wiki snapshot without importing or compiling. Missing counts are unknown (`null`), not zero. Doctor warns when no readable publication exists. Refresh bridge sources with `wiki bridge import` and publish fresh counts with `wiki compile`.

Remote compatibility is negotiated: the new CLI requests `statusMode: "snapshot"`; callers omitting it retain the released live behavior and numeric counts. Old clients therefore remain compatible, including before the first post-upgrade compile, but keep the potentially slow synchronization path. The new CLI also accepts responses from old Gateways.

**Maintainer decision requested:** approve snapshot-mode health as configuration/publication availability, rather than current exporter health or source freshness. This is the remaining product-contract decision, including the default CLI/tool change; released remote compatibility alone does not resolve it.

| Diagnostic contract | New default CLI / `wiki_status` | Remote clients without snapshot negotiation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source synchronization / live exporter checks | Not performed by diagnostics | Existing live behavior retained |
| Counts | Last readable publication; unavailable metadata is `null` | Live numeric counts |
| Publication missing or unreadable | Unknown counts; doctor warns and reports unhealthy | Existing live behavior retained |
| Publication readable but inputs newer or exporter currently failing | Can report healthy if configuration/publication checks pass; does not establish current exporter health or source freshness | Existing live checks retained |

The explicit tradeoff is prompt, observational diagnostics versus an up-to-date exporter/freshness assessment. Operators refresh inputs with `wiki bridge import` and publish updated counts with `wiki compile`. The requested owner acceptance covers the changed default health/count semantics and nullable unknowns. The docs state the limits; local use, green CI, and bot review do not supply that approval.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing durable compile publication instead of doing expensive work on every diagnostic read. Compile adds optional provenance counts and a timestamp; legacy publications remain readable with unknown provenance/time. Active owners retain restoration/quarantine decisions, and offline diagnostics read the journal-selected publication without activating the vault. No extra count cache, storage namespace, schema bump, or background loop is introduced.

Related: #170553 optimized live counting while preserving output; #170611 was a separate, closed cache proposal. This change addresses diagnostic synchronization and scanning. It does not claim to accelerate compilation or eliminate snapshot-blob loading.

## Evidence

Actual CLI/Gateway upgrade proof passed on Linux / Node 26.12.1 using latest stable v2026.10.8 and the built candidate host. The committed [upgrade proof script](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/338b6b93fd010ae6fe49e8e30d2a68a93530e764/scripts/prove-memory-wiki-diagnostics-upgrade.mts) reproduces the scenario in isolated state:

- Released memory-wiki compiled 12,000 synthetic source pages plus one genuine memory-core bridge input. Its legacy publication, 12,001 source-page count, and plugin settings survived the upgrade.
- Before this repair, the unmodified released CLI against the snapshot Gateway failed with `Invalid Gateway response for wiki.status.` (exit 1).
- After repair, released CLI → candidate Gateway status and doctor both exit 0 with numeric counts. Candidate CLI → released Gateway status and doctor both exit 0.
- Candidate CLI → candidate Gateway status and doctor both exit 0; legacy provenance/timestamp remain honestly unknown. A pending real bridge input is not imported. Wiki-file/journal SHA-256 remains `5b4ed31d3aae58c99ba5882a72ed2b73ef0a70f5ebcdfbd671b54e32af598c20` across upgrade and both snapshot diagnostics. The subsequent legacy live call imports the pending input, demonstrating that the unchanged result was not a disabled bridge.
- Without a publication, candidate status returns unknown counts; doctor returns `healthy: false` and exit 1. Released status remains accepted.

The 11 CLI calls include startup. Candidate snapshot status/doctor took 14.757s/13.882s; these are completion observations, not a latency comparison. This is a 12,000-page compatibility fixture with small real exports, not a 37-workspace throughput benchmark. The digest covers wiki files/journal; it does not hash all external blob storage. No production installation, version, or data changed.

Focused tests: 110 passed across the five consolidated test files and the compiled-cache/prompt helper consumers. Extension production/test and script typechecks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and the assertion-safety ratchet passed. The original assertion-safety failure was corrected without a baseline change. The later merged-tree test-line failure is also addressed: the entire PR now has zero net test-line growth, using shared lifecycle/FIFO/page fixtures while retaining the asserted contracts. Its existing ceiling is unchanged.

Canonical plugin packaging and full candidate runtime build passed. The final consolidation commit changes tests/fixtures only; the production bytes exercised by the real upgrade proof are unchanged. Hosted CI for revision `0623d2cc408b2a915b254a2ce443673537ba66f1` [passed the CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40766312661/job/123111720682); the full repository suite was not run locally. This result applies to that pinned head; the new main integration is validated separately below.

Independent local review found no remaining actionable code/proof findings. It is not a maintainer approval or ClawSweeper verdict. The owner decision above remains explicit.

## Integration validation — 2026-11-03

Locally validated integration revision: `a3d384d5f5512877862660582d1eb7fb0645d0a8`, integrating main `31ad71a8addc1d42fbc5478f7e114860f5cbf6c7`. The compiled-cache conflict is resolved while preserving main's forced persisted-cache reload and this PR's shared publication reader and owner/quarantine checks.

The existing cache-retention regressions also exposed a semantic integration issue: a newly generated diagnostic timestamp prevented reuse of unchanged publications. The existing publication owner now ignores only that attempted timestamp when comparing otherwise identical diagnostic snapshots. Reused publications keep their original time; changed publications receive the new timestamp, and legacy snapshots can still acquire diagnostics metadata. Existing regressions failed before this correction and pass afterward.

- 109 distinct tests passed across seven diagnostic, Gateway, and cache suites; the final fixture replay passed all 19 cache lifecycle and 42 Gateway tests. Shared Gateway fixtures retain current-main request-agent/app-config-once assertions and snapshot routing assertions.
- Scoped production typechecking with exact dependencies, canonical type-aware lint and pinned-runtime parity, formatting, whitespace, and the test-line ratchet passed. Net test-line delta against pinned main is -1; no ceiling or exception changed.
- Fresh independent review found no actionable P0–P2 defects. Uploaded tree `1a3417fe58a1d7be50cee48f18d162a156dfa453` exactly matches the reviewed/tested local tree. The earlier release-upgrade proof remains evidence for its pinned revision; no new full-repository suite or upgrade matrix is claimed. Hosted CI for the later head is recorded below; these local results remain pinned to the tested integration revision.

A subsequent main merge advanced the branch to `4eaa353e2c5b09f137b4c5373c8596eeac7496f4` without changing Wiki files or this PR's diagnostics docs/runner. [Hosted CI passed for that exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41604304974), verified 2026-11-04. The six other returned workflows also completed successfully. The local results above remain pinned to their tested integration revision.

The maintainer decision about diagnostic health semantics remains open; this integration does not substitute for that approval.

## Operational relevance

I have used these Wiki fixes together for several days in my own deployment, and they made Wiki usable for my daily work. This reports experience with combined release backports; it is not an isolated measurement of this PR or proof that the exact PR head has been exercised.


## Current-main integration — November 9, 2026

Integrated main `34f7aa1425d293f819254ecd0a9da2ef4d1083b2` to remove the GitHub merge conflict. The CLI test conflict uses main's newer spawn/FIFO helpers and fixture naming while preserving this PR's snapshot negotiation and legacy-client assertions. Production code needed no manual conflict repair. The documented maintainer decision on diagnostic-health semantics remains outstanding.

Validated tree `556c07a0ebe2d819478a15afe34b5ff96270bdc0`, published head `36d035d993e3ed863d83e6880fc2b7c711f48818`. **89/89 CLI/status/Gateway/tool tests** passed. The conflict resolution is confined to test integration; prior behavior proof remains pinned to its recorded revision. Formatting, `git diff --check` against pinned main and the canonical test-line ratchet pass. No ceiling or allocation was raised.

**Local tooling limitation:** canonical `prepare-extension-package-boundary-artifacts` failed with `Incomplete plugin-sdk native declaration inventory`. Local typed lint therefore did not complete; local typechecking is also not counted as passed. No artifact/guard bypass or unrelated tooling change was made. Fresh hosted CI for this head is required; older green CI above remains older-head evidence.

The release-adapted fix remains active in the deployed 2026.11.2 combined package; the operational follow-up distinguishes that experience from candidate validation.

## Current-main integration — November 18, 2026

Published head: `84441a0386d7042f140929f4d4218c418b155a8a`; validated tree: `b8099175751f27ccdc262a9eabbf5d428fbe3ddb`. Integrated official main `2f658fce2596a82459efccbe84a471b077600633` to resolve three actual conflicts in the Wiki CLI, its regression fixture and CLI documentation.

The resolutions preserve snapshot negotiation for status/doctor, ordinary bridge-import parameters, upstream interrupted-read cancellation and exit semantics, generic response validation, and the documented diagnostic-health limits. Existing publication-retention behavior remains covered.

- **109 focused tests passed** across five files and two canonical shards. Wrapper: 378.11s, including 124.65s cold worker preparation.
- Scoped Memory Wiki production typecheck and focused CLI production/test typecheck passed. The test selector inherited the canonical extension-test configuration and ambient declarations; it did not weaken compiler options.

- Fresh independent local Autoreview (Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, medium; default **P0** scope) assessed the complete resulting PR delta and the cancellation/snapshot integration: one complete pass, scoped-clean. No broader-priority clean result is claimed.

Earlier runtime and stable-upgrade evidence remains attributed to the source revisions named above; it was not rerun for this mechanical integration. New-head hosted CI is separate and must pass after any required fork-workflow approval.

I can document carrying this release-adapted correction since **OpenClaw 2026.11.2**, through **2026.11.3, 2026.11.4 and the currently deployed 2026.11.5**. It has remained stable in my use. The current combined release installation passed package-byte verification, native Doctor/migrations, Gateway health and active-plugin checks. This is operational experience with the combined adaptation, separate from a pristine runtime proof of the upstream head.

The remaining owner decision is unchanged: whether publication/configuration availability with nullable historical counts should be the default snapshot diagnostic-health contract. Passing checks and local stability do not supply that upstream policy approval.


**New-head hosted CI status (November 18):** [CI run 44261159964](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44261159964) is `action_required` with no jobs. prs.body:
Related: #39127, #168186. Preserves the paused-child distinction discussed in #186387.

## What Problem This Solves

A parent conversation can appear idle after `sessions_yield` while its native Codex child is still executing.

## User Impact

The existing working indicator remains available through `hasActiveSubagentRun` during observed running or waiting native execution, then clears when execution becomes unknown or ends. This changes server-side activity metadata only.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native children are owned by the harness monitor rather than OpenClaw's subagent-run rows. Their host-issued event sink now contributes display-only activity to the existing run-registry snapshot. Independent tokens retain concurrent child observations; requester identity and lifecycle revision keep activity from moving to a replacement conversation. The existing registry revision and row publisher invalidate cached projections. Settlement, custody release, and Gateway closure remove the observation independently of result delivery.

## Evidence

Historical pre-integration head: `60bab48c06b0d7d5141919ba1403fc6da49610e9`. Its only change from the reviewed production commit `2738b9d7aa1223ed3f689bdbac027a97b3d6eef6` is the requested test-line allocation.

- **Real main-targeted Gateway/model proof:** [redacted method and live observations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196256#issuecomment-6770721732). A fresh, isolated Gateway built from this PR's main-targeted source runs a real parent that spawns one native child and yields. While yielded, `sessions.describe` reports `hasActiveRun=false`, `hasActiveSubagentRun=true`, `activeRunIds=[]`. After native execution ends, the parent receives the automatic completion and finishes `PROBE_DONE`; both describe and the sidebar's list projection clear the activity. This replay uses no stable overlay, mocked execution, or injected events. It proves server-side behavior, not browser rendering.
- **Exact source:** The built checkout plus allocation has tree `bb621456c7526a4f16d7f4321dff2cc051b040a7`, exactly matching the published head. Canonical `build:runtime` completed successfully (exit 0, 4m38s). It reported Control UI size-budget warnings; no UI sources or budgets are changed here.
