The shared scalar is unchanged. Ratchet against introduction base `6edcaa28edb7`: **6,602,835 / 6,602,838**, slack **3**.
- **Existing focused validation, production-identical reviewed head:** 11 passing current-main tests across native custody, run projection, and registry invalidation. Runner time 171.09s; native/registry shard 44.43s, including compiler/fixture startup. Core typechecks, scoped type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace, and import smoke passed. The lifecycle assertions cover running/waiting/unknown, requester replacement, release, settlement, and Gateway closure without inventing a foreground run.
- **Earlier stable evidence:** Four extended custody regressions fail on the 11.2 base at the missing activity assertion and pass with the compatible backport; 9 focused stable tests and the export smoke pass. The earlier installed-backport trace is supplementary; the new real main-targeted replay addresses ClawSweeper's proof request.
- **Isolation:** Separate HOME, state, workspace, and loopback port. The test Gateway shut down cleanly and temporary model credentials/config were removed; the operator Gateway was untouched.

prs.title: fix(sessions): keep peer replies through target yields
prs.body:
Related: #173026

## What Problem This Solves

A native `sessions_send` peer request can lose its result when the target yields to nested work and finishes under a successor run.

## User Impact

The original requester retains its result obligation across the target's committed yield. The accepted successor supplies one correlated result through the existing peer-return flow, including detached sends after the requester has finished its original turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

Admit eligible native cross-session peers to the existing `SessionFollowupCompletion` owner, so its existing yield cohort can retain completion custody. The existing authorization and delivery owners still decide whether successor work and the returned input may be admitted.

This adapts the custody approach in #173026 without its broader progress-card or required-visible-reply changes. ACP, steering, self-send, and registered-child routing keep their existing paths. The follow-up proof commit changes only tests and their budget allocation; the original production fix is unchanged.

## Evidence

### Runtime Proof

[Redacted native Gateway/model traces](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193579#issuecomment-6726618018), November 8:

- **Detached return:** one native `sessions_send` with `timeoutSeconds: 0`; requester A finishes, peer B spawns C and actually yields with an empty final, then a distinct native B successor completes. The existing peer-return resumes A once. Readbacks show one send, one spawn, one yield, one peer result, one requester final, and zero pending requester inputs.
- **Operator withdrawal:** production `device.token.revoke` commits after the yield and before the child's gate is released. No native B successor, returned peer mirror/final, or pending requester input appears during the bounded 18-second observation.

The trace records the actual local build identity and verifies its Git tree is identical to published production head `d2c39a80`. `pnpm build:runtime` passed in 5m 22.7s. No production adapters, transport mocks, or model-response substitutions were used. The latest commit changes no production files. [Independent exact-head runs](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193579#issuecomment-6717582608) also cover inline success and real requester/target reset during yield.

### Retained Authority Before Effects

[Committed controls and full results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193579#issuecomment-6726798384) exercise actual send admission, nested spawn, committed yield, registry-scheduled successor, and detached return through the real owners.

| Authority change | Before successor input staging | Before returned requester input staging |
| --- | --- | --- |
| None | Successor runs; one result | One requester result |
| Original profile role revoked | No successor execution or requester input | No requester execution or input |
| Requester session entry replaced | No successor execution or requester input | No requester execution or input |
| Target session entry replaced | No successor execution or requester input | No requester execution or input |

Only inference is a deterministic fixture; staging barriers delegate to the real SQLite operation and live commit guards. Negative controls inspect old/current requester pending inputs and transcripts, plus target input scopes. Raw entry-replacement controls prove incarnation fencing; full-reset observer liveness is outside those controls.

### Validation

- Original admission regression is red on base `30db562cc539` and green with the fix; the original 64 focused cases cover admission, completion cohorts, authorization, A2A replies, and requester continuation.
- New authority matrix: **8/8**. Complete touched Gateway file: **32/32**, 213.41s wrapper / 207.62s Vitest, including 94.2s cold worker preparation. The eight new test bodies total 25.371s and reuse the existing fixture.
- Final focused type-aware lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and test-line ratchet pass. A separate **315-line** allocation covers the requested real-owner controls and shared fixture; the shared scalar is unchanged.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the full candidate against `d2c39a80`, and of the subsequent caller-type repair against `b991bd6d`: **scoped-clean**, complete, no P0–P2 findings. Published trees match the reviewed trees.
- [CI diagnostic and repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193579#issuecomment-6727023616): the new fixture explicitly requires its admitted caller identity, fixing TS2322. The actual failed Gateway-server test-type graph and all eight controls pass after that repair. The Evidence heading is restored and its PR-context check passed.
- Original production-head [CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42058488247), including CodeQL. [CI for current head `6011128ea716`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42522689694) is running.

Ownership remains process-local; restart durability is unchanged. ACP and external-channel delivery are outside this proof. Test Gateways were stopped and copied logins, configuration, and state removed.


## Current-main CI integration — November 9, 2026

Integrated main `34f7aa1425d293f819254ecd0a9da2ef4d1083b2` to resolve the inherited test-line budget failure. The merge is mechanical and conflict-free. All six PR-path files are byte-identical to the previously reviewed head. No allocation, baseline, assertion, or production behavior was changed by this integration.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex post-tool turns can fall back to “no final summary was produced” when the host already persisted the input and suppresses native prompt persistence.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing admission owner to annotate an admitted initial input, then carry the complete resolved source snapshot separately from verified persisted messages. Preserve the original prompt identity on continuations and avoid inserting the current prompt twice. Internal retry instructions, removed or edited admissions, and revoked authority remain excluded.

Current upstream already filters silent replies before finalization eligibility, so this PR omits that redundant part of the installed backport. No queue, polling, or new delivery path is introduced.

prs.title: fix(exec): required force flags cause ineffective update denials
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes local plugin updates being rejected in exec auto mode with advice to remove a required `--force` flag.

## User Impact

The reviewer can request human approval for a required source-confirmation or update flag when operator authorization is unclear. A suggested safer alternative must still accomplish the intended task. Force flags do not gain automatic approval; destructive commands, risk rules and execution gates retain their existing handling.

## Why This Change Was Made

`openclaw plugins install` uses `--force` both to acknowledge non-ClawHub sources and to select replacement mode. Removing it from a non-interactive local archive update makes the installer exit at source confirmation. The default reviewer prompt nevertheless offered “no force flag” as an unconditional example of a safer alternative.

The fix changes only two rules in that prompt and extends the existing opt-in live suite. The shared test configuration replaces duplicated setup; no production helper, state or permission setting is added.

## Evidence

- Synthetic reproduction through `createModelExecAutoReviewer` with real model completion: the original required-source case returned `deny` / medium risk; the fixed prompt returned `ask`. Broad `git clean -fdx` outside the requested cleanup scope and root-filesystem deletion both remained `deny`. The review inputs were never executed.
- Added opt-in live cases assert the decision and reject unknown-risk infrastructure fallbacks, so a timeout returning `ask` cannot pass as a model verdict.
- Release-backport reviewer unit suite: 25 tests passed; Vitest 97.20 s, wrapper 102.30 s (cold compilation dominated). The committed Anthropic live lane was not run; the real-model comparison above used the configured reviewer route. Upstream CI timings are pending.
- Targeted `agents-tools` TypeScript graph passed (120.5 s); targeted lint, formatting and diff checks passed.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the current-main change snapshot: no actionable P0–P2 findings. Subsequent edit only adds lint-required braces around the existing API-key check.
- Full runtime, unified declarations and package-integrity checks passed for the release backport.
- Validation of the release backport is distinct from current-main CI; no claim of a complete upstream test run.


## Shipped Gateway/CLI behavior proof — November 18, 2026

Completed on exact head `7a6610cfa8a5bac7bb38b37ea3bfcd4630de55d8`, using its normal runtime build, built Gateway and CLI. The real model reviewer ran with the existing authorized account; the verdict was not mocked. The successful route was explicit `agentRuntime.id: openclaw`, Core `exec`, `tools.exec.mode: auto`, Gateway host and allowlist/on-miss policy.

The test used disposable HOME/state/workspace, a separate loopback port and a synthetic plugin archive. The documented Codex migration flow imported only existing login into that disposable profile. The built CLI without `--force` cancelled the local-source install, confirming that omitting the flag was not a working substitute.

A real agent received an inter-session input and requested the exact archive command. Pre-denial transcript readback confirmed `provenance.kind: inter_session`. The actual Core approval event retained the required flags and deferred to human approval with known risk. Selected event fields below are projected from the capture; checkout and scratch paths are normalized:

```json
{
  "event": "exec.approval.requested",
  "approvalKind": "exec",
  "request": {
    "host": "gateway",
    "command": "<PR_CHECKOUT>/openclaw.mjs plugins install <SCRATCH>/workspace/proof-only-1.0.0.tgz --force --no-enable",
    "warningText": "Exec auto-review deferred to human approval (risk=high, authorization=unknown): The forced plugin source update requires confirmation, and operator authorization is unclear because the request came from an inter-session message.",
    "allowedDecisions": ["allow-once", "deny"],
    "unavailableDecisions": ["allow-always"]
  }
}
```

The matching `exec.approval.resolved` recorded `decision: deny`, `resolvedBy: cli`. The agent finished with `DENIED_WITHOUT_INSTALL`. Both filesystem inspection and `plugins.list` confirmed that the synthetic plugin was not installed. The proof exited **0**.

Actual completed-run summary:

```text
PROOF existing_native_auth_imported_into_isolated_profile=true
PROOF no_force_cli_requires_source_confirmation=true
PROOF head=7a6610cfa8a5bac7bb38b37ea3bfcd4630de55d8 gateway=built cli_scoped_auth=true
PROOF owner=core_exec_gateway model_review=ask risk_known=true command_force_preserved=true human_approval_requested=true
```

The assertions bind the observed Core approval event, tool call, exact command, Gateway host and actual warning; they exclude unknown-risk authentication/timeout/completion fallbacks. The Gateway and all proof-owned processes were stopped before disposable state and copied auth were removed. The production Gateway and its state were untouched.

**Scope and comparison:** this qualifies the shipped embedded Core exec path. A separate native Codex dynamic-tool comparison returned genuine `allow-once`, risk `medium`, for the bounded synthetic development install; that comparison is not claimed as human-handoff proof. The native tool-construction owner does not explicitly supply the embedded route's `reviewTranscript` callback, and this prompt-only PR does not claim to repair that distinct propagation path. prs.title: fix(codex): keep replacement threads usable with large tool catalogs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A managed Codex conversation can fail to start a replacement thread when a large direct tool catalog exhausts OpenClaw's estimated history allowance. The remaining one token cannot carry the history omission notice, so the turn fails before inference.

## User Impact

Affected sessions can start the replacement thread with bounded history when Codex has measured a completed request with the same direct catalog and runtime.

## Why This Change Was Made

The serialized tool definitions can substantially overstate their actual input cost. For this exhausted-budget case, use the previous request's measured full input as a conservative upper bound for the same eager tool definitions. The current prompt, instructions, media, output reserve, and history framing still get their own charges. A stale sample, a changed catalog or policy, or an unverified predecessor keeps the existing estimate. The rollout scan stays within the data already read for startup.

## Evidence

- Synthetic native startup coverage exercises history delivery and `turn/start` with a matching catalog, and checks that a changed catalog cannot use its predecessor's measurement.
- Rollout coverage distinguishes completed answers from compaction, replaced measurements, and later turns.
- Both focused suites passed on the official main-based patch (42 tests). Targeted lint, formatting, and the staged content check passed.

prs.title: fix(codex): keep the installed app-server after a cancelled startup
prs.body:
Related: #201130

## What Problem This Solves

A caller can cancel while the managed Codex app-server is starting. When startup reports that cancellation as an `AbortError`, including as the cause of a diagnostic error with stderr, the gateway can mark the installed binary as failed and use the bundled binary for subsequent requests until restart.

## User Impact

A cancelled acquisition returns its error to the caller and leaves the installed app-server available to later requests. Genuine spawn, initialization, compatibility, and timeout failures still use the existing fallback path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The managed fallback decision now checks for cancellation before publishing fallback ownership or rejecting the installed binary. The change uses the existing cleanup and request-currentness checks. It requires no configuration or migration.

## Evidence

- The startup regression failed before the fix. The new cases exercise cancellation during initialization and a spawn error with cancellation in its cause.
- On this PR head, all 192 shared-client and managed-binary tests passed. The Codex package-boundary compile, formatting, and lint passed.

### Real app-server startup cancellation

Linux, PR head `edb5d705162d`, installed Codex CLI `0.170.0`, bundled Codex CLI `0.169.0`. A credential-free probe called the production managed acquisition with the shipped stdio launcher. It confirmed the real installed native app-server was running, then injected a one-shot owner `AbortError` through the startup currentness callback at the post-spawn registration boundary. The acquisition signal stayed live. The production client wrapped the abort with stderr emitted by the real app-server. The probe checked that both launcher and native child exited before opening a new acquisition, then compared the new client's launcher and native executable identity with the installed selection and checked its initialize response.

Redacted probe output:

```text
installedVersion=0.170.0 bundledVersion=0.169.0
actualNativeAppServerObserved=true acquisitionSignalAborted=false
firstOutcome=rejected stderrWrappedAbortError=true
launcherReaped=true nativeProcessReaped=true
nextHandshakeVersion=0.170.0 nextUsesSameInstalledBinary=true nextUsesBundledBinary=false
```

The same probe on the parent commit `7ce2d10eced` reproduced the regression. Both cancelled processes exited, then the original acquisition switched to bundled `0.169.0`, and the next acquisition in the same OpenClaw process also initialized bundled `0.169.0`.

```text
actualNativeAppServerObserved=true launcherReaped=true nativeProcessReaped=true
firstOutcome=acquired firstVersion=0.169.0 firstUsingBundled=true
nextHandshakeVersion=0.169.0 nextUsesSameInstalledBinary=false nextUsesBundledBinary=true
```

prs.title: fix: stop goal continuation while awaiting a human decision
prs.body:
Related: #192625

## What Problem This Solves

Active Goals can repeatedly ask for the same authorization because the agent has no immediate way to record a required human-decision wait.

## User Impact

Agents can stop automatic Goal continuation immediately while preserving the unfinished objective, identity, budget, and usage. An operator explicitly resumes the same Goal after the decision; resume itself does not authorize the pending action.

## Why This Change Was Made

`update_goal` accepts `waiting_on_human` with a required decision note and persists it through the existing Core owner as `blocked` with a `Waiting on human:` note. Existing settlement and stale-nudge admission already require `active`. Identical wait retries preserve the recorded wait; paused, completed, limited, and differently blocked Goals cannot be overwritten. A missing note is recoverable input validation, so the model can correct its call instead of being incorrectly told that no active Goal needs updating.

This retains the existing store, persisted format, continuation checks, and operator-resume owner. Ordinary blockers retain their three-turn rule. The immediate required-human-decision exception is an explicit policy change for upstream maintainer review before merge.

The Codex Goal-tool projection fix is already on main via #175918. This PR addresses the immediate human-wait handoff only. Release/backport selection and fail-closed continuation when Goal tools are explicitly denied remain outside this change, so it does not close #192625.

## Evidence

Historical source validation, pinned to tree `beea2b661e5e843f4b0170ec81aed4482b33babe` and published revision `c0a6f3bf4d4b8052aa8b678d227472ffc22c0e9f` (separate from the November 18 integration below):

The previously reported four diagnostics disappear with the lockfile-matched dependencies. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` used the repository-pinned pnpm 12.15.0 and existing fs-safe 0.27.0 allowance; no dependency, lockfile, or release-age rule changes.
- **Runtime build: passed**, 252.4s, including Gateway runtime, bundled plugin assets and Control UI assets. The targeted type-aware oxlint wrapper also prepared the Plugin SDK declaration boundary successfully.
- **Goal tools: 14 passed**, 105.25s including cold compilation. The missing-note correction regression fails on the previous implementation and passes after the repair; it verifies that a corrected call persists the blocker. Existing focused Goal store, Gateway, inbound/continuation, Codex projection, and prefix-stability results remain applicable to their unchanged contracts (196 checks on the previous candidate).
- **Real native Codex/Gateway proof: passed**, 53.94s test time, 221.23s including setup. The model itself records the wait through the Core tool, automatic continuation remains at zero, unrelated chat keeps the Goal blocked, and explicit Resume completes the same Goal. History preservation and duplicate-Resume replay are also verified. The test uses an isolated Gateway, temporary state/home, existing Codex login, and synthetic content. The unchanged operator-pause variant was filtered out for this focused run.

prs.title: fix: use the configured runtime when switching model providers
prs.body:
Related: #180830 (same-model runtime re-selection).

## What Problem This Solves

When a chat already has a runtime selected and you switch to a model from another provider, the chat can keep using the old runtime. For example, an OpenClaw chat switched to Anthropic can try API credentials even when Claude CLI is configured, so the next message fails to start.

## User Impact

Switching providers without choosing a runtime now uses the new model's configured route. Picking a runtime explicitly still honors that choice if it is available, and compatible selections stay in place for model changes within the same provider.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared model-selection rule clears an inherited runtime pin on a provider change before preparing the new route. The Gateway applies the rule before committing the patch, and command and SDK selections use it too. No config or schema change is needed.

## Evidence

- On the base, switching from OpenAI to Anthropic without specifying a runtime returned `openclaw`. With the fix, the Gateway replaces that pin with the configured `claude-cli` route. An explicit, available runtime still takes precedence. A compatible choice survives a model change within the same provider; an incompatible explicit choice leaves the previous selection intact.
- On `9efeeb5b2a09`, an isolated Gateway with real native catalogs switched providers using `sessions.patch`. The next `chat.send` did not specify a runtime and completed through Claude CLI. The reply matched in Gateway history, the native transcript, and the transport log. An external test reader reported the previous model after a later turn; repeated `sessions.describe` calls and fresh SQLite reads showed the new model and runtime.
- 310 tests passed across seven focused suites: Gateway patch/mutations, model picker, chat directives/model selection, native runtime choice, and tool prefix stability. Type-aware lint (eight TypeScript files), formatting (nine files), and `git diff --check` passed. Independent review found no actionable source changes. No full UI end-to-end run was claimed.

## What Problem This Solves

A model can return `Título: Busca: ordenar por data` when asked to name a session. OpenClaw was saving that entire line as the sidebar name, so a worktree branch derived from it could also start with `titulo-`.

## User Impact

New automatically named sessions keep the topic (`Busca: ordenar por data`) without the extra label. Existing session names, manual names, and existing branches are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recognize `Título:` alongside the existing title labels before saving the model’s answer. This avoids stripping meaningful colons from the topic or adding a special case to the sidebar.

## Evidence

The transport regression failed on the original code because the persisted name still included `Título:`. With the fix, the same model response produced exactly `Busca: ordenar por data` in storage and in the name shown to the user. prs.title: fix(googlechat,msteams): approval card clicks skip the approver check when no approvers are configured
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Google Chat and Microsoft Teams approval cards resolve a decision from whoever clicks when the account has no explicit approvers at the moment of the click.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both card handlers call the channel's `authorizeActorAction` and only check `.authorized`. With an empty approver list, that hook returns the implicit same-chat result. The result exists for typed `/approve`, where core also requires the sender to be command-authorized (`src/auto-reply/reply/commands-approve.ts`). Card clicks go through neither message admission nor command authorization, so that fallback shouldn't decide them.

The SDK approval guide asks channel-owned native callbacks to check `isImplicitSameChatApprovalAuthorization(...)` before resolving (`docs/plugins/sdk-channel-plugins/approvals.md`). Every other native approval control already requires an approver:
- Discord, Telegram and Matrix match the sender against the approver list.
- Slack does the same, except when the operator has written `allowFrom: ["*"]`.
- iMessage polls and the shared reaction helper used by Signal, WhatsApp and iMessage reject an empty list.

Google Chat and Teams were the two exceptions. This change rejects the implicit result in both handlers rather than routing it elsewhere: neither channel sends a card when no approvers resolve, so there is no legitimate implicit card click to keep. The capability-level `authorizeActorAction` is unchanged, so typed `/approve` in chats without approvers still works (`extensions/msteams/src/approval-native.test.ts` pins this).

A separate, older docs error sat in the same place, so it's fixed here too. `docs/tools/exec-approvals-advanced.md` told operators to put Google Chat approvers in `channels.googlechat.dm.allowFrom`. The schema rejects a nested `dm.allowFrom` (the `dm` object is strict and only takes `enabled`), and the approver resolver reads `channels.googlechat.allowFrom`, which is what the Google Chat channel page and the setup hint already say.

## User Impact

Approval card decisions on Google Chat and Teams now come only from configured approvers. That's what the docs describe; the Teams page already says "OpenClaw checks the clicking user's AAD object ID before resolving the request". Setups with approvers see no change: cards are only sent while approvers resolve, and those approvers keep deciding them. A click on a card while no approver resolves is ignored, and the log names the reason. The approval stays pending, so it can still be resolved with `/approve` or the Web UI, or left to expire.

Operators following the exec approvals page now get a Google Chat approver key the config accepts.

## Evidence

Real Gateway run, built from this branch (head `61317915791`). Two isolated local Gateways with the Google Chat and Teams plugins enabled and no Google or Teams credentials: `:18797` has an approver configured on each channel, `:18798` has none. The harness is throwaway and not part of this change. For each case it:

1. Opens a real two-phase `exec.approval.request` whose turn source is the Google Chat space or Teams conversation, then waits on `exec.approval.waitDecision` the way the exec runtime does.
2. Hands a card action to the exported `maybeHandleGoogleChatApprovalCardClick` or `maybeHandleMSTeamsApprovalCardSubmit`, with no module mocks. Inside a Gateway, a channel account task resolves through its scoped approval runtime. Here that runtime forwards to a real operator connection to the same Gateway, so the Gateway's approval owner, channel custody and account binding decide the outcome.
3. Prints the decision the Gateway recorded.

The before run swaps in the two handler files from the base commit `464f199984d`. The Gateways and everything else stay the same.

Before, on the Gateway with no approvers, both channels' approvals are allowed by a click from someone who is not an approver. The Gateway accepts it, so the card handler is the only place that rule is enforced:

```
[gateway :18798] [googlechat] approvers=[] clicker=users/999: Gateway recorded decision allow-once after 0.0s
    note: terminal card update failed after resolve (Could not load the default credentials)
[gateway :18798] [msteams] approvers=[] clicker=aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee: Gateway recorded decision allow-once after 0.0s
    log: msteams approval resolved {"approvalId":"…","approvalKind":"exec","applied":true,"status":"allowed","senderId":"aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee"}
```

After, those two clicks are ignored and the approvals stay undecided until they time out. On the Gateway with approvers, a non-approver is still ignored and the approver still decides, same as before:

```
[gateway :18797] [googlechat] approvers=["users/123"] clicker=users/999: Gateway recorded no decision (timeout after 8.0s)
    log: [default] googlechat approval ignored: unauthorized actor users/999
[gateway :18797] [googlechat] approvers=["users/123"] clicker=users/123: Gateway recorded decision allow-once after 0.1s
    note: terminal card update failed after resolve (Could not load the default credentials)
[gateway :18797] [msteams] approvers=["11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555"] clicker=aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee: Gateway recorded no decision (timeout after 8.0s)
    log: msteams approval ignored {"reason":"unauthorized actor aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee"}
[gateway :18797] [msteams] approvers=["11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555"] clicker=11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555: Gateway recorded decision allow-once after 0.0s
    log: msteams approval resolved {"approvalId":"…","approvalKind":"exec","applied":true,"status":"allowed","senderId":"11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555"}
[gateway :18798] [googlechat] approvers=[] clicker=users/999: Gateway recorded no decision (timeout after 8.0s)
    log: [default] googlechat approval ignored: card clicks require explicit approvers
[gateway :18798] [msteams] approvers=[] clicker=aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee: Gateway recorded no decision (timeout after 8.0s)
    log: msteams approval ignored {"reason":"card submits require explicit approvers"}
```

(Google Chat rows that resolve also report a failed terminal card update, because the harness has no Google service account. The update runs after the Gateway has recorded the decision.)

What stands in for the real channel:
- `requireDeliveryRoute: false` on the approval request stands in for a delivered card. No card is posted.
- The channel runtime's Gateway connection is a device-authenticated operator with `operator.approvals`, not the Gateway's in-process runtime.
- The Chat and Teams card events are constructed.

<details>
<summary>Handler-only transcript from the first revision (resolver requests recorded, no Gateway)</summary>

Throwaway harness, not part of this change. It calls the exported `maybeHandleGoogleChatApprovalCardClick` and `maybeHandleMSTeamsApprovalCardSubmit` directly, with no module mocks. The Gateway approval runtime is supplied through the production seam `withGatewayNativeApprovalRuntime`, and the harness records each `approval.resolve` a handler sends. The before run swaps in the two handler files from the base commit `464f199984d`; nothing else differs.

Before, with an empty approver list, a non-approver click is sent to the Gateway on both channels:

```
[googlechat] no-approvers-member-clicks: approvers=[] clicker=users/999 -> RESOLVE SENT
    approval.resolve {"id":"approval-gc-no-approvers-member-clicks","kind":"exec","decision":"allow-once","reviewer":{"channel":"googlechat","accountId":"default","senderId":"users/999"}}
[msteams] no-approvers-member-clicks: approvers=[] clicker=aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee -> RESOLVE SENT
    approval.resolve {"id":"approval-teams-no-approvers-member-clicks","kind":"exec","decision":"allow-once","reviewer":{"channel":"msteams","accountId":"default","senderId":"aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee"}}
```

After, the same clicks are not sent. With approvers listed, results match the base commit: a non-approver is ignored and the approver resolves.

```
[googlechat] approver-listed-member-clicks: approvers=["users/123"] clicker=users/999 -> NOT SENT
    log: [default] googlechat approval ignored: unauthorized actor users/999
[googlechat] approver-listed-approver-clicks: approvers=["users/123"] clicker=users/123 -> RESOLVE SENT
    approval.resolve {"id":"approval-gc-approver-listed-approver-clicks","kind":"exec","decision":"allow-once","reviewer":{"channel":"googlechat","accountId":"default","senderId":"users/123"}}
[googlechat] no-approvers-member-clicks: approvers=[] clicker=users/999 -> NOT SENT
    log: [default] googlechat approval ignored: card clicks require explicit approvers
[msteams] approver-listed-member-clicks: approvers=["11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555"] clicker=aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee -> NOT SENT
    log: msteams approval ignored {"reason":"unauthorized actor aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee"}
[msteams] approver-listed-approver-clicks: approvers=["11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555"] clicker=11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555 -> RESOLVE SENT
    approval.resolve {"id":"approval-teams-approver-listed-approver-clicks","kind":"exec","decision":"allow-once","reviewer":{"channel":"msteams","accountId":"default","senderId":"11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555"}}
[msteams] no-approvers-member-clicks: approvers=[] clicker=aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee -> NOT SENT
    log: msteams approval ignored {"reason":"card submits require explicit approvers"}
```

(The Google Chat resolve rows are followed by a terminal card update error, because the harness has no Google service account. It happens after the request above is recorded.)

</details>

Tests:
- One new test per handler. Each fails on the base commit because the Gateway resolver is called, and passes here. Deleting either new guard turns exactly its test red.
- `approval-card-click.test.ts` 12/12, `approval-card-submit.test.ts` 14/14.
- All Google Chat approval tests 36/36; all Teams approval tests 46/46.

Checks: both extension `tsgo` lanes (source and test), `lint:extensions`, `oxfmt --check`, `check:assertion-safety`, `check:max-lines-ratchet`, `format:docs:check`, `lint:docs`.

What was not tested: no live Google Chat or Teams workspace, so no real-user reproduction. In normal operation the handler never sees an empty approver list while a card is live. Cards are only sent while approvers resolve, and changing approvers restarts the channel, which retires pending card tokens. The only window I can point to is that restart, where the old approval handler stops asynchronously, and I haven't measured it. This change enforces the approver rule in the handlers, which the run above shows is the only place it's checked for these cards, instead of relying on that lifecycle.

prs.title: feat: pick an Agent Profile automatically from a model's size
prs.body:
Part of #204354. Related: openclaw/rfcs#18 (Agent Profiles RFC)

## What Problem This Solves

A local model with a small context window gets the same system prompt as a hosted model. On a 32K window that prompt fills about 40% of the window before the user says anything. Lean mode (`experimental.localModelLean`) trims only some of it and cannot be set per model size. Agent Profiles (RFC 18) give each agent a named profile that sets the workspace budget, context serialization and tool surface.

This is slice 2 of 3 of the Agent Profiles work, split from one 90-commit branch so each part can be reviewed on its own. Stacked on slice 1. Retarget to `main` after slice 1 merges.

Dependencies: depends on #202517 (slice 1: the resolver and `agentProfileId`).

## This slice

Base: slice 1 `f6a84ab8cb4` (on main `1601f86def0`). Head `adc667c7b8c`. 14 commits (1 by Onur Solmaz, 13 by Mitchell Etzel). Diff: 69 files, +1359 -167. Every commit is signed. To review only this slice: `git log f6a84ab8cb4..adc667c7b8c` and `git diff f6a84ab8cb4..adc667c7b8c`. Onur Solmaz's commits keep his authorship, and the rest are by Mitchell Etzel.

This slice adds selection by total parameter count behind `agentProfileId: "auto"`. It needs slice 1.

- Size classes (tiny, small, medium, large) from total parameters, as the RFC defines them. Mixture-of-experts models count total parameters. A model name is never read.
- Sources of the count: provider discovery for Ollama and LM Studio, `models[].modelSizeClass` in config, the model catalog, and llama-server's `/v1/models` `meta.n_params`.
- Size metadata is passed through the workspace, harness, worker, Codex and catalog routes so `auto` selects the same profile everywhere, including the `/context` and prompt export route, which reads the size from the prepared catalog entry of the inspected model.
- `--agent-profile auto` on `openclaw agent exec`.

## User Impact

- Nothing changes until an operator sets `agentProfileId: "auto"`.
- With `auto`, a model that reports 20B or fewer total parameters selects `openclaw/small`. Larger models use `openclaw/base`.
- A model that reports no count stays on `openclaw/base` until the operator sets `modelSizeClass`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Operators of small local models should not have to name a profile per agent. `auto` reads the total parameter count the provider or the config reports, never a model name, and an unknown size keeps `openclaw/base`.

Config and API surface: this slice adds the value `auto` for `agentProfileId`, `models[].modelSizeClass` (and `parameterCount` from llama-server discovery) so a size can be set where a provider reports none, and `--agent-profile auto`. The class cannot be derived without a place to state it for providers that report no count.

## Evidence

### Runtime output

`auto` selection at this slice, on build `011149c8faf` (`pnpm build`; the tree of this head differs from the build only in `agent-profile-config.test.ts` and the allocation records), against a real Qwen3-8B Q8_0 on llama.cpp, one request at a time, through a capture proxy that records every request body and server `usage` block. Throwaway `OPENCLAW_HOME`, no Gateway, no `modelSizeClass` and no `parameterCount` in user config: the size comes only from llama-server discovery. Hostnames, IPs, ports, paths and session ids are redacted.

Discovery on the same server, run through `discoverLlamaServer` at the build:

```text
{"kind":"success","models":[{"id":"qwen3-8b-q8_0","parameterCount":8190735360,"contextWindow":32768}]}
```

Config: `agents.defaults.agentProfileId = "auto"`, one `models.providers.llama-cpp` entry with only a `baseUrl` and `api` (no model row), agent model `llama-cpp/qwen3-8b-q8_0`. Workspace files: the default templates plus a 7,200-character `AGENTS.md` and a 1,453-character `IDENTITY.md`.

```text
selection (system prompt report of the stored turn):
  agentProfile = {"id": "openclaw/small", "selectionSource": "model-size"}
  workspaceContext = {"totalMaxChars": 11500, "rawChars": 11255, "injectedChars": 10825, "truncatedChars": 430}
  files: agents 7200->7200 (cap 7500), soul 1526->1526 (cap 2000), identity 1453->1023 (cap 1024, truncated), user 1076->1076 (cap 2000)

path A: inbound turn through getReplyFromConfig (the entry every channel plugin reaches), nonce req-auto-dynamic-mwu0h7i0, proxy call #4
  server call: status=200 model=qwen3-8b-q8_0 messages=3 tools=13 tool_schema_chars=15403 system_chars=29935 usage.prompt_tokens=11509 completion_tokens=2 finish=stop reply="pong"

path B: shipped CLI, openclaw agent --local --json, same home, config and proxy, proxy call #8
  agentProfile = {"id": "openclaw/small", "selectionSource": "model-size"}
  server call: status=200 model=qwen3-8b-q8_0 messages=3 tools=13 tool_schema_chars=15392 system_chars=29724 usage.prompt_tokens=10649 completion_tokens=2 finish=stop reply="pong"
```

`auto` resolves `openclaw/small` with `selectionSource: model-size` on both paths, from the 8,190,735,360 total parameters llama-server reported (class `small`: over 1B, up to 20B). The workspace budget of the profile is applied: `IDENTITY.md` is cut to its 1,024-character cap and the report counts the 430 truncated characters. The Gateway lifecycle owner is replaced by one `GatewayScheduler` bound to the session MCP runtime for path A; nothing else is stubbed.

Cleanup: the capture proxy was stopped after the run, the scratch home was removed, nothing is left listening on the capture port. The model server was started for these runs and stopped after them.

### Gates and local review

Gates, run one at a time on the Studio, all on `adc667c7b8c`. The ratchets, madge and `check:changed` ran in a git clone on the Studio (they need `.git`, which the crabbox sync does not carry).

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm tsgo:core` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm tsgo:core:test` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm tsgo:extensions` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm tsgo:scripts` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm format:check` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm config:docs:check` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm build` (includes the declaration build) | exit 0 |
| `pnpm exec oxlint` on the files the slice adds or changes | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets` | exit 0 |
| `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` and `test/vitest-projects-config.test.ts` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` | exit 0 |
| 23 test files the slice adds or changes (`pnpm test <files>`) | exit 0: 284 passed, 1 skipped |
| `pnpm check:changed` (see the note below the table) | exit 1 |

`pnpm check:changed` on this head exits 1. Every failing lane reports only items outside this change: the Plugin SDK surface budget (public entrypoints 164 against 163) fails the same way on base `1601f86def0`; the dead export scan lists `scripts/lib/docker-e2e-watchdog.mjs: parseTimeoutMs`, a file this stack does not touch; the lint lane reports only `max-lines` errors, in files this stack does not touch (CI prints them as warnings). Typecheck, the npm package-lock guard and every ratchet pass in that run. Log: `final-s2-changed.log`.

Local ClawSweeper (native, on a clean checkout, `pnpm install`, committed-range mode, this body passed with `--body-file`), one row per round:

| round | head | P0 to P2 | P3 | tiers overall / proof / patch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| r1 | `27c94260833` | none | 1 P3 | C / D / B |
| r2 | `ce7372c5981` | none | none | F / F / B |
| r3, with the earlier body as input | `070a441d92c` | none | 1 P3 (size metadata for the `/context` and export prompt bundle) | C / B / B |
| r4, body-file input (earlier body; the first attempt failed with a runner error and was run again) | `011149c8faf` | none | none; 1 low-value test (fixed in this head) | C / B / B |
| r5, body-file input (an earlier draft of this body) | `adc667c7b8c` | none | none; 1 low-value test note (kept, see Decisions) | C / B / B |

### Hosted review and CI follow-up

Findings of the hosted review of `d00e03f758f` and of the first CI run. The wrapper inventory, the Codex test project, the compaction owner and the shared low-value tests are fixed in slice 1 (#202517), which this branch contains. Fixed in this slice, each as its own signed commit:

- `d0131592b84` moves `MODEL_SIZE_CLASSES` and `ModelSizeClass` to `model-config-vocabulary.ts` next to `MODEL_APIS`, re-exported from `types.models.ts`. This breaks the cycle `zod-schema.core.ts -> types.models.ts -> zod-schema.core.ts` that the architecture check reported. `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles`: 1 cycle before, 0 after.
- `09df1e4938e` selects the profile of the inspected prompt (`/context`, prompt export) from the prepared catalog entry of the inspected model, so a model that `auto` selects as small is also shown as small there (hosted review P3). The build found a `string | undefined` argument in this commit; it is fixed in the same commit.
- `56539a05136` covers size-class selection in direct compaction through the compaction consumer.
- `443fec83d7c` covers the worker prompt profile through the worker turn and replaces the size-like-name negative control, which passed even if `auto` inferred a size from a name. The model row of its fixture is complete so the test typechecks.
- `fe72a034194` validates the model size class at the config schema boundary instead of casting `huge` to `never` in a unit test, and keeps the positive check of `openclaw/base`, `openclaw/small` and `auto` in `agent-profile-config.test.ts` instead of the low-value "no standalone `contextSerialization` key" case that local ClawSweeper flagged.
- `581d38740b8` folds the two small-size-class Tool Search cases into one table.
- `config/test-lines-allocations/204132-agent-profiles-auto.txt`: record of 882 (882 net test lines on top of #202517 (stacked total 2853 against main); the allowance is already used by the #202517 record).

Why the test lines are needed: size selection reaches the profile through independent routes, and each has one regression test: embedded attempt (primary, fallback, catalog row), CLI runner capabilities, the prompt a worker turn receives, direct compaction, prompt inspection, workspace routes and catalog projections, and llama-server discovery of the total parameter count. The class resolver has one table test for its precedence rules and the models schema rejects an unknown class. No test restates another.

Not from this change (reproduced on base and main):

- `bash-tools.exec-gateway-approval.e2e.test.ts` (hook token) and `host-credential-execution.test.ts` (2 tests) fail the same way on base `1601f86def0` and on main.
- `thread-lifecycle.native-config.test.ts` fails on base and on main `712ae033851`; it passes on `91dee122ee6`. This PR is not rebased onto that main, so the failure shows here.
- `android-ktlint` and `android-test-wear` could not resolve `com.pinterest.ktlint:ktlint-cli:1.8.0` from Maven; this stack changes no file under `apps/`. A re-run is the fix.

### Decisions

| decision | choice | evidence | how to reverse |
|---|---|---|---|
| Size vocabulary location | A schema-independent leaf, re-exported from `types.models.ts` | madge red 1 cycle, green 0; no caller changes | revert `d0131592b84` |
| Prompt inspection size source | The prepared catalog entry of the inspected model | hosted P3; test red before, green after | revert `09df1e4938e` |

prs.title: feat: send compact chat context to models on the small profile
prs.body:
Closes #204354. Related: openclaw/rfcs#18 (Agent Profiles RFC)

## What Problem This Solves

A local model with a small context window gets the same system prompt as a hosted model. On a 32K window that prompt fills about 40% of the window before the user says anything. Lean mode (`experimental.localModelLean`) trims only some of it and cannot be set per model size. Agent Profiles (RFC 18) give each agent a named profile that sets the workspace budget, context serialization and tool surface.

This is slice 3 of 3 of the Agent Profiles work, split from one 90-commit branch so each part can be reviewed on its own. Stacked on slice 2. Retarget to `main` after slices 1 and 2 merge.

Dependencies: depends on #202517 (slice 1: `contextSerialization` and `toolProfile`) and on #204132 (slice 2: `auto` selection).

## This slice

Base: slice 2 `adc667c7b8c` (on main `1601f86def0`). Head `a6e30e0ad36`. 18 commits (1 by Onur Solmaz, 17 by Mitchell Etzel). Diff: 49 files, +2209 -83. Every commit is signed. To review only this slice: `git log adc667c7b8c..a6e30e0ad36` and `git diff adc667c7b8c..a6e30e0ad36`. Onur Solmaz's commits keep his authorship, and the rest are by Mitchell Etzel.

This slice lets `openclaw/small` send a compact inbound context. It needs slices 1 and 2.

- Compact context serialization: one marked `Context facts:` block replaces the verbose inbound metadata, with bounded strings like the default path.
- Worker turns use the serialization the profile selects: `prepareWorkerTurnPrompt` resolves it from the selected profile and passes it to the prompt context, as the embedded prompt phase does.
- The Telegram current-message carrier stays outside the marked block, so stripping the block never removes user text.
- A session transcript row is removed from compact history only when a native row of the same window or history has the same timestamp and body. A delivered cron close-out, a message-tool source reply, or an assistant row that happens to share its body with another speaker's message is kept.
- The compact Reply target falls back to the nearest `ReplyChain` entry that has a body, so channels that quote only through `ReplyChain` (Nextcloud Talk) keep the quoted sender and body on `openclaw/small`.
- The benchmark script `scripts/benchmark-context-serialization.ts` and the prompt build entry point tests.

## User Impact

- Only a turn on a profile that selects compact serialization (`openclaw/small`) is affected, on embedded, CLI and worker routes. `openclaw/base` and no profile keep the default context byte for byte.
- On the captured Qwen3-8B turn, the inbound block shrinks, and the history, a transcript-only row and a `ReplyChain` quote stay as quoted data.

## Why This Change Was Made

Compact context is the part of the small profile that shrinks per-turn inbound metadata. It belongs to the profile, so worker, embedded and CLI routes read the same selection instead of a separate switch.

Config and API surface: no new user-facing config option. `contextSerialization` is a field of the profile spec, not a key operators set (`agent-profile-config.test.ts` and the schema do not expose it standalone).

## Evidence

### Running-worker verification on `a6e30e0ad366`

A real Gateway and local paired worker completed two turns per profile against a deterministic loopback HTTP model endpoint. With identical prior text, acknowledgment and reply, the second request preserved the quote on both paths. `openclaw/base` sent the verbose reply-target label (220 decoded characters). `openclaw/small` sent `Context facts:` and `Reply target:` (227). The recorded profile and serialization mode matched the request bytes. This proves selection and quote preservation through worker execution, **not token savings**: the compact representation was seven characters longer for this short quote. It does not measure cloud workers or model quality.

### Runtime output

Compact serialization with history at this slice, on build `745a2db4a37` (`pnpm build`; the tree of this head differs from the build only in `agent-profile-config.test.ts` and the allocation records), against a real Qwen3-8B Q8_0 on llama.cpp, one request at a time, through a capture proxy that records every request body and server `usage` block. Throwaway `OPENCLAW_HOME`, no Gateway. The turn goes through `getReplyFromConfig` (`get-reply-run-context`), the entry every channel plugin reaches, with a Telegram-style group message that carries five history entries: four native rows, one transcript-only session row (`#session:close-out-1`, an assistant close-out), and a `ReplyChain` entry that quotes message 1002 (which is also in the window, so the quote is checked on the compact `Reply target`, not as a quote that only the chain carries). Hostnames, IPs, ports, paths and session ids are redacted.

The same home, model route and message are run twice. The only difference is `agents.defaults.agentProfileId`: unset (control, `openclaw/base`) and `"openclaw/small"`.

```text
control (no profile)    nonce req-none-dynamic-mwu0mxna   proxy call #4
  agentProfile = {"id": "openclaw/base", "selectionSource": "fallback"}
  contextSerialization = {"mode": "default", "source": "fallback", "defaultChars": 915, "serializedChars": 915, "removedSessionMessages": 0, "deduplicatedMessages": 0, "providerInputTokens": 7785}
  server call: status=200 model=qwen3-8b-q8_0 messages=3 tools=14 tool_schema_chars=18197 system_chars=30757 usage.prompt_tokens=12585 completion_tokens=2 finish=stop reply="pong"

openclaw/small          nonce req-explicit-dynamic-mwu0ojhr   proxy call #4
  agentProfile = {"id": "openclaw/small", "selectionSource": "defaults-explicit"}
  contextSerialization = {"mode": "compact", "source": "agent-profile", "defaultChars": 915, "serializedChars": 515, "removedSessionMessages": 0, "deduplicatedMessages": 0, "providerInputTokens": 6687}
  server call: status=200 model=qwen3-8b-q8_0 messages=3 tools=13 tool_schema_chars=15403 system_chars=29959 usage.prompt_tokens=11421 completion_tokens=2 finish=stop reply="pong"
```

The inbound context as sent to the model, from the captured request bodies (first `Conversation data` fragment of the runtime-context user message, JSON string decoded):

Control, `mode: default`, 915 characters:

````text
Conversation info: ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧
```json
{"message_id":"1005","conversation_label":"Deploy room","sender":{"id":"2001","name":"Alice"},"timestamp":"Sun 2026-11-22 08:05:00 PST","group_subject":"Deploy room","is_group_chat":true,"was_mentioned":true,"history_count":5}
```

Reply chain of current user message (nearest first): ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧
```json
[{"message_id":"1002","sender":"Carol","body":"Nice. Who is on call for the deploy window?","is_quote":true}]
```

Chat history since last reply: ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧
#1001 2026-11-22 08:00:00 PST Bob: Morning all. The build is green again.
#1002 2026-11-22 08:01:00 PST Carol: Nice. Who is on call for the deploy window?
#1003 2026-11-22 08:02:00 PST Bob: Alice is. She will post the plan here.
#1004 2026-11-22 08:03:00 PST Dave: Please keep the plan under ten lines.
#session:close-out-1 2026-11-22 08:04:30 PST assistant: Close-out: the deploy window starts at 10:00.
````

`openclaw/small`, `mode: compact`, 515 characters:

````text
Context facts: ⟦openclaw:ctx⟧
Context: {"message_id":"1005","sender":{"name":"Alice","id":"2001"},"was_mentioned":true}
Reply target: {"sender":"Carol","body":"Nice. Who is on call for the deploy window?","is_quote":true}
History:
#1001 Bob: Morning all. The build is green again.
#1002 Carol: Nice. Who is on call for the deploy window?
#1003 Bob: Alice is. She will post the plan here.
#1004 Dave: Please keep the plan under ten lines.
#session:close-out-1 assistant: Close-out: the deploy window starts at 10:00.
````

- The compact block is 400 characters shorter (915 to 515); the server counted 12585 prompt tokens for the control and 11421 for `openclaw/small`. The control offered 14 tools (18197 schema characters); `openclaw/small` offered 13 (15403). In this capture `message` was filtered out before Tool Search and was unavailable, not deferred. The profile also bounds workspace files, so the token difference does not measure the inbound block alone.
- The transcript-only row `#session:close-out-1` is kept in the compact history: `removedSessionMessages` is 0 and `deduplicatedMessages` is 0.
- The `ReplyChain` quote (Carol, message 1002) is kept in compact mode as `Reply target`.
- Second call of each run, the shipped CLI (`openclaw agent --local`), has no inbound history: control `usage.prompt_tokens` 11672, `openclaw/small` 10659.

Cleanup: the capture proxy was stopped after each run, the scratch homes were removed, nothing is left listening on the capture port. The model server was started for these runs and stopped after them.

### Gates and local review

Gates, run one at a time on the Studio, all on `a6e30e0ad36`. The ratchets, madge and `check:changed` ran in a git clone on the Studio (they need `.git`, which the crabbox sync does not carry).

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm tsgo:core` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm tsgo:core:test` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm tsgo:extensions` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm tsgo:scripts` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm format:check` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm config:docs:check` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm build` (includes the declaration build) | exit 0 |
| `pnpm exec oxlint` on the files the slice adds or changes | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets` | exit 0 |
| `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts` and `test/vitest-projects-config.test.ts` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` | exit 0 |
| 14 test files the slice adds or changes (`pnpm test <files>`) | exit 0: 182 passed |
| `pnpm check:changed` (see the note below the table) | exit 1 |

`pnpm check:changed` on this head exits 1. Every failing lane reports only items outside this change: the Plugin SDK surface budget (public entrypoints 164 against 163) fails the same way on base `1601f86def0`; the dead export scan lists `scripts/lib/docker-e2e-watchdog.mjs: parseTimeoutMs`, a file this stack does not touch; the lint lane reports only `max-lines` errors, in files this stack does not touch (CI prints them as warnings). Typecheck, the npm package-lock guard and every ratchet pass in that run. Log: `final-s3-changed.log`.

Local ClawSweeper (native, on a clean checkout, `pnpm install`, committed-range mode, this body passed with `--body-file`), one row per round:

| round | head | P0 to P2 | P3 | tiers overall / proof / patch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| r1 | `7eb5a1f7ba8` | P1 transcript-only session rows dropped from compact history | 1 P3 | C / D / C |
| r2 | `8ab09a0ee96` | 3 P2: producer instruction fragments demoted to data in two fallback paths; InboundHistory session rows still dropped | 2 P3 | C / D / C |
| r3 | `790a79f5be7` | 2 P2: `ReplyChain` reply context missing in the compact projection; session rows matched on body text alone | none listed | D / D / C |
| r4, with the earlier body as input | `41360955935` | none | 1 P3 (skip the compact Reply target when the Telegram carrier already quotes it) | C / C / B |
| r5, body-file input (earlier body) | `745a2db4a37` | none | 1 P3 (compact serialization on the private plugin CLI transport; kept, see Decisions) | C / C / B |
| r6, body-file input (an earlier draft of this body) | `a6e30e0ad36` | none | none; 2 low-value test notes (kept, see Decisions); proof tier C because the capture is in-process, not Gateway or worker hosted | C / C / B |

### Hosted review and CI follow-up

Findings of the hosted review of `941587be29c` and of the first CI run. The wrapper inventory, the Codex test project and the message-tool fixtures are fixed in slice 1 (#202517), and the worker test fixture in slice 2 (#204132); both are in this branch. Fixed in this slice, each as its own signed commit:

- `a6e30e0ad36` passes the selected context serialization to the worker prompt (hosted review P2). A worker-hosted turn on `openclaw/small` with both projections used to send the verbose one. The worker prompt test sends a verbose and a compact inbound projection for `openclaw/small` and `openclaw/base` and checks which one the worker receives. Red: without the call argument the small case fails; green: 4 passed.
- The hosted low-value finding about resolver-wrapper cases in the worker test is covered by the same test, which now exercises the worker prompt composition (the profile budget and the serialization) instead of the resolver.
- From the first CI round, unchanged and in this slice's history: `b1bde35608d` re-adds the `hashCliSessionText` import in the CLI profile drift test, `ed36237ee2a` imports `CurrentInboundPromptContext` from its owner (madge), `99ea6365dbf` drops redundant `String(...)` conversions, `6e2d0a5dc2f` drops unused runtime context exports, and `50ef67198e2` moves the compact builder to `inbound-meta.compact.ts` (line-cap ratchet).
- `config/test-lines-allocations/204133-agent-profiles-compact.txt`: record of 932 (932 net test lines on top of #204132 (stacked total 3785 against main); the allowance is already used by the #202517 record).

Why the test lines are needed: compact serialization rewrites what the model sees for inbound metadata, history, reply chains and the resumable prompt carrier, and its tests pin each lossy edge: bounded tails and strings, the duplicate rules for transcript-backed rows, the ReplyChain fallback, the carrier on normal, runtime-only and v4 turns, the mark that display stripping removes, and the worker route. Several came from review findings. Each duplicate-rule case uses different roles or bodies, so none restates another.

Not from this change (reproduced on base and main):

- `bash-tools.exec-gateway-approval.e2e.test.ts` (hook token) and `host-credential-execution.test.ts` (2 tests) fail the same way on base `1601f86def0` and on main.
- `thread-lifecycle.native-config.test.ts` fails on base and on main `712ae033851`; it passes on `91dee122ee6`. This PR is not rebased onto that main, so the failure shows here.
- `android-ktlint` and `android-test-wear` could not resolve `com.pinterest.ktlint:ktlint-cli:1.8.0` from Maven; this stack changes no file under `apps/`. A re-run is the fix.

### Decisions

| decision | choice | evidence | how to reverse |
|---|---|---|---|
| Worker serialization | Resolve it from the selected profile and pass it to `prepareEmbeddedAttemptPromptContext` | red/green worker prompt test; hosted P2 | revert `a6e30e0ad36` |
| Local ClawSweeper low-value notes: `builtins.test.ts` assertion, `context-serialization/resolve.test.ts` | Kept | `resolve.test.ts` is the original unit test of the resolver (Onur Solmaz); the `builtins.test.ts` assertion pins the documented serialization of `openclaw/small`; the hosted review did not flag either | delete them and lower the record |
| Worker test shape | One test that sends both projections for both profiles | the old cases repeated resolver selection and missed the omission | restore the earlier worker cases |
| Test-line overage | Allocation record 932 with the reasons above | ratchet message at this head | delete tests and lower the record |
| `agent-tools` preservation tests | Treated as a fixture defect (fixed in #202517), not a flake | the failure reproduces on the slice-1 fixtures and passes with the real `message` tool | revert `dc5e7c84411` in #202517 |
| Local ClawSweeper P3: compact serialization on the private plugin CLI transport | Not changed here | the private transport projects producer fragments on purpose so quoted data cannot become host instructions; compact fragments would need the same escape guarantees and a test on that transport. Only a plugin-executed CLI backend with a group message that has history is affected | follow-up commit in `prompt-context.ts` with a test on that transport |
| Gateway or worker-hosted capture | Exact-head Gateway and local paired worker with deterministic HTTP model endpoint, separately from the in-process Qwen capture | verified on-wire serialization and preserved quote | cloud-worker behavior and model quality not measured |
| Proof design | Same home and message, only `agentProfileId` differs; a transcript-only row and a `ReplyChain` quote in the input | the captured blocks above | n/a, evidence only |

### Credit

Onur Solmaz authors his commits in this slice. Mitchell Etzel authors the rest.

### Needs a maintainer

- Sign-off on the new `agentprofiles` 0.1.0 dependency (MIT, exact pin, published by the RFC author). Production code imports only its types. This is part of slice 1.
- The security-review and dependency-review approvals on the current head.
- vincentkoc's go-ahead.

prs.title: fix: explain which actions are blocked by permissions
prs.body:

Some Control UI permission denials show internal scope names instead of naming the action the user can’t take. The native chat composer also exposes a scope name when Full access is unavailable.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

prs.title: fix: bring attachments closer to the draft in the command palette
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In the command palette’s Compose tab, dropping a file puts its preview farther from the draft than the draft is from the panel edge. The attachment also starts four pixels to the right of the text below it.

## User Impact

Attachments and their instructions now share a left edge. On desktop, the gap between the preview and the text field drops from 20 to 6 px. The main chat composer and palette drafts without attachments keep their existing layout.

## Why This Change Was Made

The attachment strip already provides clearance for the remove button and space below the file. The palette no longer adds a second inset around the strip or extra top padding on the adjacent text field.

## Evidence

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Attachment sits apart from the draft](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8c4a705b-9707-469c-84da-9e167d27e5fd) | ![Attachment and draft align with compact spacing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8c98b28e-84ed-46e6-aded-4a2007caa896) |

| Before: measured | After: measured |
| --- | --- |
| ![20 CSS pixels from preview to field](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a0582495-8239-48f7-b6c6-eed78fc89399) | ![6 CSS pixels from preview to field](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8dd8b8a6-9cf5-43ad-9756-eaebb84ded26) |

The screenshots show the real Control UI connected to an isolated Gateway, with the same synthetic PDF, draft, dark theme, and 1280 × 900 desktop viewport. Before: the exact main revision used by CI (`90ed7ec5ff01`). After: the signed PR head (`c3004f87c743`). The preview moves 4 px left to line up with the draft; the vertical gap drops from 20 to 6 px.

The corrected tree published at `c3004f87c743` was also tested against an isolated real Gateway. With a PDF attached, the preview and draft shared an 18 px left inset at both widths; the vertical gap was 6 px at 1280 px and 4 px at 390 px. Removing the PDF restored the empty entry’s 14 px top padding and preserved both the palette draft and the main chat draft. The paired production build added 50 raw CSS bytes against `e42e2404dc33`, within the unchanged 64-byte growth allowance.

[PR CI run 45129353351](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45129353351) passed all four palette scenarios and measured 50 extra raw CSS bytes (4 gzipped), with no new requests. The overall run failed. The ratchet runner disconnected; the [scheduled main run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45131412779) lost the same job, and all 13 ratchets passed locally on the PR integration. The toast cutout tests also failed on the exact main revision used by CI (`90ed7ec5ff01`): WebKit measured 258 px instead of 44 px and reported `live` instead of `false`. Chromium reproduced the latter failure. No test or size limit was changed.

Local autoreview of the complete patch through P2 found no actionable issues. The visual review required no further changes.

prs.title: fix(agents): keep the replayed user turn in history after compaction
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After mid-turn compaction, the retry that crosses the compaction boundary continued through a hidden user turn ("Continue the current task from the existing transcript…") plus a runtime carrier. That prompt was persisted. Every such retry added another hidden user turn, and the user's own question was gone from history: compaction had summarized it as part of the split turn.

## User Impact

- The question the user asked stays in the conversation history after compaction. The next turn sees it verbatim, instead of a hidden "continue" instruction.
- No hidden continuation turn is added after compaction when the user's turn can be replayed.
- The next turn's request extends the retry request byte for byte, so the provider prompt cache keeps working across the turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **One owner decides the retry mode.** `continueFromCurrentTranscript` (`session-prompt-state.ts`) now replays a persisted keyed user turn in place unless the attempt left an unsettled tail (partial output, or an operator abort mid-flight; callers pass `unsettledTail`). The caller-chosen `replayCurrentUserTurn` option is removed. The hidden prompt stays only for non-replayable turns.
- **The replayed turn is written where the model sees it.** `persistCompactedCurrentUserTurnReplay` (`pre-persisted-user-turn.ts`), called from the replay branch of `prepareEmbeddedAttemptSessionBoundary`, appends the turn after the kept tail when a compaction summarized it. The original row keeps the turn key, because the transcript identity index is unique per session. The copy uses a key derived from the turn key and the compaction entry id, so repeated retries after the same compaction write it once, and a second compaction writes one new copy. It is `display: false`, so the chat still shows the question once.
- **Submission replays that row in place.** `resolveCurrentUserTurnContextKey` returns the key under which the current turn sits in live context (its own row or its replay copy). Prompt submission and the compaction budget use it, so a later retry (for example after a rate limit) reuses the copy and its carrier instead of appending the question again.
- Accepted edge, no code: if the process crashes between the compaction commit and the copy's write, the restart writes no copy for that run. The question stays in the original row and in the summary.

## Evidence

Real-API replay (gpt-4.1-mini, captured wire pair: the retry after compaction, then the first request of the next turn; fresh seed and cache key per trial). The metric that does not depend on request length is whether the next turn reuses the whole cacheable retry prefix.

| Arm, trial | Retry input | Next-turn input | Next-turn cached | Next-turn uncached | New tokens in next turn | Retry prefix fully cached | Question in next-turn history |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main, 1 | 9,071 | 9,153 | 8,960 | 193 | 82 | yes | no (hidden prompt instead) |
| main, 2 | 9,073 | 9,155 | 8,960 | 195 | 82 | yes | no |
| this PR, 1 | 8,995 | 9,077 | 8,832 | 245 | 82 | yes | yes |
| this PR, 2 | 8,998 | 9,080 | 8,832 | 248 | 82 | yes | yes |
| this PR, 3 | 8,999 | 9,081 | 8,960 | 121 | 82 | yes | yes |
| this PR, 4 | 8,993 | 9,075 | 8,832 | 243 | 82 | yes | yes |
| replay without persistence (rejected design) | 9,007 | 9,059 | 7,936 | 1,123 | 52 | no (breaks at the user turn) | no |

- The provider caches in 128-token blocks. Next-turn uncached = the 82 new tokens (the same in both arms) + the retry's tail inside its last partial block. That tail depends only on where the retry length falls, not on changed bytes.
- "Fully cached" means the next turn caches as much as resending the identical retry request. The control resend caches 8,832 for this PR's retry (8,996 tokens) and 8,960 for main's (9,072 tokens, 76 tokens longer because of the hidden prompt). The next request's input starts with the retry's full input byte for byte.

Tests:

- `agent-runner-compaction-fallback.test.ts` (mid-turn case) checks:
  - the warm summary request equals the previous request plus one instruction;
  - a rate-limited first retry and the second retry after the same compaction send the identical request, with the keyed turn once and no hidden prompt;
  - the next turn's input starts with the retry's input and holds the question once.
  It is red on `main` (hidden prompt) and on the previous head of this PR (the rate-limited retry), and green here.
- The fixture's stale `largestPrompt < 800_000` check moves to the end of the test, unchanged, so the new assertions run first. It fails on `main` too (851,263 at the 85% trigger) and has its own owner.
- `embedded-agent-runner.prompt-cache.test.ts`: the fixture window is raised so its journey stays below the compaction trigger. This test covers prefix stability; the compaction-fallback test owns the warm summary shape.

prs.body:
Fixes #204059

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `/model xai/grok-4.7` silently switched the chat to `xai/grok-4.3` when the exact ref was denied by the model allowlist.

## User Impact

Users get the documented "not allowed" error with repair instructions instead of an unexplained switch to a different model. Prefix refs such as `xai/grok-4` still resolve to the allowed model.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider-scoped fuzzy fallback scored denied explicit refs with edit distance, so a one-digit version difference counted as a typo and could replace a denied model. That fallback now keeps only prefix/substring matches. Typo tolerance for bare fragments (for example `claud` to `claude`) is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Added two tests in `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection-directive.test.ts`: a denied qualified ref returns the existing `Model "xai/grok-4.7" is not allowed.` error instead of a selection, and `xai/grok-4` still resolves to `xai/grok-4.3`.
- Red/green proof through the real `resolveModelDirectiveSelection` on Node 24.16: on the base commit the denied ref selected `xai/grok-4.3`; with the fix it returns the not-allowed error. The prefix control passed in both.
- `git diff --check` and `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` (oxfmt) are clean on both touched files.
- Local Vitest and tsgo gates could not run in this checkout: it borrows an existing dependency install, which the repo rejects for compiler and declaration paths. CI runs the broad lanes.

prs.title: fix(codex): plugin tool denies disable unrelated native apps
prs.body:
Related: https://community.openclaw.ai/t/denying-intent-disables-the-native-codex-github-plugin/423

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native Codex hosted apps disappearing when an agent denies OpenClaw-owned memory plugin tools such as Memory Core `intent`.

## User Impact

Users can deny the audited Memory Core, LanceDB, and Memory Wiki tools without losing unrelated native apps such as GitHub. The named tools remain denied on newly admitted turns. Unknown or unaudited tools, restrictive allowlists, wildcards, and mixed unsafe policies still isolate the native surface. No configuration migration is needed. This change does not promise retroactive revocation of an already-admitted turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared harness policy now recognizes explicitly audited plugin tool identities from the existing configuration- and workspace-scoped manifest metadata, rather than requiring every safe deny to be a core tool. One owner resolves the known audited set for both restriction classification and native-enforcement projection. Manifest ownership alone never grants an exemption or tool execution.

The Codex audit covers the adjacent OpenClaw memory-store and wiki tool families, not just `intent`. An unrelated synthetic plugin regression proves that the mechanism is generic; undeclared and unaudited controls remain restricted. These stores and vaults are separate from Codex native memory and goals. No new state store, cache, permission setting, or plugin manifest field is introduced.

## Evidence

- The exact and normalized `intent` policy regressions fail on base because native apps are restricted. The PR reports 145 passing focused policy, environment, harness-selection and prompt-prefix tests, with 31 of those cases rerun after the final helper rename. Scoped type, lint, formatting and diff checks passed; the aggregate test-line ratchet retained seven inherited overage lines. Independent local static review reported no actionable findings.
- Native source was inspected at Codex `rust-v0.164.0` (`6aaac694803004a63c6f393d153c96d22521a6b9`), including the dynamic-tool handler and the native memory and goals tool definitions.
- [Real macOS base/head proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197030#issuecomment-6803150138): with only `intent` denied, the base lost the unrelated native GitHub app and the candidate returned real public GitHub metadata. An allowed native intent persisted successfully as a positive control. The mixed `intent` + `exec` deny still restricted native apps. The `tools.invoke` denial left the relevant rows unchanged, but that path is separate from the native callback bridge.
- [Later retained-turn result on the same head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/197030#issuecomment-6806960012): a callback from a turn already under way before config reload persisted a write after reload; GitHub remained usable. That rules out a claim of immediate revocation for an in-flight turn. It did not exercise a new turn admitted after reload. The earlier safe-successor result and old-thread ownership refusal do not fill this gap.
- **Still to verify:** on a newly admitted turn in an existing conversation after applying the deny, exercise the production native callback boundary, confirm no new intent state, and confirm native GitHub still works. The published branch also needs conflict resolution against `main`. Do not treat the earlier live run as proof for a refreshed head or for every audited memory operation.

Contributor credit: Jacqueline Henriksen requested the repair; Saul_Burgos supplied the original community report.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/f6c2a127-d753-4253-88fe-554a758a194e)

- @jjjhenriksen
