prs.title: fix(sqlite): TEMP views invalidate sibling readers and worker logs lack timestamps
prs.body:
Related: #188274

## What Problem This Solves

Creating a connection-local TEMP VIEW unnecessarily invalidates other SQLite readers, while worker console lines lack the emit time needed to attribute stalls accurately.

## User Impact

TEMP views preserve sibling MAIN-reader admission. Worker diagnostics carry emitter-side timestamps, and slow transaction-hold warnings include the hold start time. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing TEMP-object classifier to views without suppressing subsequent MAIN DDL. Enable the existing timestamp mechanism in the two worker logging entry points and expose the already-measured hold start.

The worker registration fixture now keeps the real console exports and stubs only the two process-wide setters. The mock-export checker removed one obsolete baseline entry. The branch also incorporates the tested `main` revision and resolves the SQLite store worker conflict.

This does not address the exec-retry, proof-publication, or invalidation-message concerns in issue items a–c.

## Evidence

### Running-Gateway comparison on the reviewed head

Two isolated Gateways took the same `projects.register` request. The probe held a real SQLite store-worker commit and stalled the Gateway main thread for 2.2 seconds without changing its clock, logger or response.

| Observation | PR base `0828443372be` | PR head `a0f86c30cf59` |
|---|---|---|
| Worker stderr write to external receipt | 2,193 ms | 2,194 ms |
| Timestamp on worker warning | None | 04:51:49.124 UTC (worker write); received at 04:51:51.318 UTC |
| Transaction hold | 1,270 ms; no start time | 1,270 ms; started at 04:51:47.853 UTC |

Both registrations returned the expected JSON. On both builds eight readiness probes timed out during the stall, and `/readyz` returned 200 before and after. This shows **when the worker emitted its warning**, not that the fix prevents stalls. TEMP-view behavior has its own two-connection proof below. [Running-Gateway proof session](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/8e56ede9-fd3a-4fa4-a7fe-b847436e50dd).

### Tests

- Before the fixture update, `src/state/openclaw-agent-execution.registration.test.ts` failed at import (`sqlite-store.worker.ts:74`, missing `setConsoleTimestampPrefix` on the mock) with all 11 cases skipped. This is the `checks-node-changed-compact-large-27` failure.
- On `a0f86c30cf59`: 101 focused tests passed across nine files, including timestamped SQLite worker stderr and clean JSON stdout through the real broker, plus worker lifecycle and close coverage. The mock-export guard, targeted lint, formatting, focused typechecks and `git diff --check` passed. [Repair and verification session](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/46408351-32b5-4056-b4d0-1bdd6090fc21) · [exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45225057226).

### Earlier runtime evidence (built `dist/`, base 7ecd67ccfd5 vs the handoff branch)

Both sides were built with `pnpm build` and exercised through the compiled output only, with an isolated state directory and HOME. This earlier capture was not repeated on `a0f86c30cf59`.

**TEMP view admission.** Two connections to one SQLite file, opened and admitted through the compiled `openNodeSqliteDatabase` and `admitSqliteSchema`. The writer runs `CREATE TEMP VIEW`, then `CREATE TABLE`.

| step | base sibling admission / revision | branch sibling admission / revision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| before | 5c4329e6... / 1 | 0dc08831... / 1 |
| after CREATE TEMP VIEW | 932793a6... / 2 (invalidated) | 0dc08831... / 1 (kept) |
| after CREATE TABLE (MAIN) | abf765f1... / 3 (invalidated) | 20f50f70... / 2 (invalidated) |

**Worker timestamps.** The shipped SQLite store worker and the shipped worker task server, run through the compiled `openSqliteWorkerStore` and `WorkerTaskPool`:

```
base:   [state/sqlite] SQLite read-only snapshot for synthetic.sqlite: 4.0 KiB, budget 301 seconds
branch: 2026-11-22T19:05:15.683-08:00 [state/sqlite] SQLite read-only snapshot for synthetic.sqlite: 4.0 KiB, budget 301 seconds
```

Stdout stays `{"value":"ready"}` and parses as JSON on both sides. The stock CLI (`openclaw sessions --json`) emits no worker log line at any level, so the worker entry points are the closest shipped seam.

**Slow hold start time.** The compiled `runSqliteImmediateTransactionSync` with `slowTransactionHoldMs: 20` and a real 60 ms hold. The "slow SQLite transaction hold" warning has no `startedAt` on base and `"startedAt": "2026-11-23T03:06:16.974Z"` (`elapsedMs: 60`) on the branch.

The earlier harness evidence is separate from the running-Gateway comparison above. Harness scripts and full redacted logs are in the attached evidence bundle.

Original patch by Mitchell Etzel.

- @Patrick-Erichsen
- @etzelm

prs.title: chore(ui): cover selected-agent scope across owner filters
prs.body:
Related: #199621. Regression coverage for the selected-agent contract merged in #201207.

## What Problem This Solves

Changing sidebar owner filters used to change which agents' conversations appeared. #201207 fixed that behavior, but this PR's original real-Gateway diagnostic still expected the old cross-agent results and would fail when integrated with current main.

## User Impact

**Test-only: no shipped behavior or permission changes.** This PR now protects the already-merged rule that the selected agent scopes My sessions and All owners. It does not choose a new membership policy, claim a new product fix, or reproduce the reporter's installation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The regression uses the existing isolated Gateway/browser fixture to select My sessions → All owners → My sessions while keeping the chat URL and selected agent unchanged. Every sidebar request must retain agentId=main. My sessions shows Main mine; All owners shows Main mine + Main other; the Research mine conversation stays excluded throughout.

The cross-agent session remains seeded and included in the three-key locator, so the test catches leakage rather than ignoring that row. The narrow locator also preserves coexistence with the preceding request-rate test. No new production helper, test server, schema, configuration option, or real provider call is introduced.

The product decision is no longer open: #201207 landed as [5d106ddc20f8](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5d106ddc20f8fc5176f4048fb24ee9c2ddd93790). Related #198985 covers a different navigation-triggered transition.

## Evidence

- **Reproduced the review finding through the real browser/Gateway flow:** on refreshed main base `39c3099189516d374bc1a74cd625b9ceaa5494e3`, the original full file produced **1 passed / 1 failed**, with the diagnostic failing at its agent assertion: expected undefined, received main. The sibling request-rate test passed.
- **After the assertion repair (published head `74b8ae4d37b7da3d1611fe153275fbbb48b33b86`): 2 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 0 unhandled errors**, together in the complete file with no test-name filter. Command wall time 58.25 s; Vitest 53.89 s; file duration 19.73 s; rate scenario 12.547 s; owner-filter regression 1.635 s. Gateway, contexts, and Chromium cleaned up successfully.
- Rebuilt the current source's QA runtime before testing. Chromium 156.0.8078.4, built Control UI, real disposable Gateway, synthetic owners/sessions, and the existing loopback provider were used. An initial setup attempt could not find the expired temporary Chromium executable and skipped both cases; installing the same browser into task-owned storage resolved setup before the recorded red/green proof. No live service or real provider credentials were used.
- Owning UI E2E typecheck, targeted lint, final formatting, and diff whitespace checks passed. Initial formatting found a wrapping issue; the repository formatter corrected it, and the final check passed.
- **Simplification/test audit:** production delta 0; total PR test delta **+90/−0**, one file. The repair removes the obsolete conditional agent expectation and cross-agent personal membership expectation; it adds no machinery. The existing rate/ownership-refresh scenario and the real owner-filter round trip protect distinct boundaries. The three-key shared-fixture repair and unchanged-chat checks remain.
- **Review:** the [completed ClawSweeper re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199634#issuecomment-6896440582) names repaired head `74b8ae4d37b7da3d1611fe153275fbbb48b33b86`, confirms the prior findings are resolved, and reports **no actionable findings**. Its [completion receipt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199634#issuecomment-7056046194) is terminal. Earlier local Auto Review of the complete candidate against the exact refreshed base timed out after 180 seconds without a validated report; no clean local review is claimed.
- **Exact-head CI:** the [full CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44856820941/job/136703606988) and [aggregate/security gates](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44857706163) succeeded on repaired head `74b8ae4d37b7da3d1611fe153275fbbb48b33b86`. The complete observed inventory was 35 passed / 64 skipped or neutral / 0 pending or failing. The full gate used no known-main-red exception. Hosted real-Gateway E2E was not selected; the local full-file red/green above supplies that proof. Earlier CI and the November 20 pass covered historical head `492700bc5c7f23aa1473d7cdbfad0a2f6e9baa34`, not this repair.
- **Remaining scope:** mobile layouts, Show all, and alternate owner-policy/legacy-ownerless configurations are not exercised by this focused case; #201207 carries its own broader coverage. No visual product change or before/after screenshot claim is made.

<details>
<summary>Focused commands and local proof receipts</summary>

QA runtime: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime`.

Full-file red and green command:

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/session-roster-request-rate.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

Red invocation: `d7fb99fb-c930-440b-a146-ce5b23a65f16`. Green invocation: `9ab03d34-f90b-4aab-9100-2737704c6949`. Formatting afterward only collapsed the unchanged membership comparator expression.

</details>

prs.title: fix: retry the primary model when a recovery check never started
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the primary model is in cooldown, OpenClaw periodically checks whether it has recovered. If a worker goes offline before sending that check, the next turn can skip the primary for 30 seconds and use a fallback or suspend the session.

Closes #127649

## User Impact

As soon as the worker is available, the next turn can retry the primary. The 30-second limit still applies when a request reached the provider or a worker disconnected after accepting it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fallback runner reserves the check before it yields to observers. Local admission and worker launch can release that reservation when they can establish that execution never started, including an explicit capacity refusal from the worker supervisor. Each release belongs to one reservation, so a late failure cannot clear a newer check.

A transcript write can fail after the model has already replied. The execution boundary lets OpenClaw preserve throttling in that case and when result processing discovers missing tool output. Related work includes #128616 and #203469.

## Evidence

### Captured Gateway and model output

Two `agent` RPCs ran in separate sessions of one isolated Gateway with the same cooled-down auth profile and no fallback. `probe-model` was local Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct served by llama.cpp. A forwarding HTTP proxy counted completion POSTs in `modelCalls`. The placement fixture counted entries in `admissions`.

**Worker offline before dispatch.** The placement fixture raised `WorkerRunnerUnavailableError` before running the first turn. The next RPC followed immediately. The following lines are from the terminal capture.

Base `7a570c41bc2`

```text
ISSUE_PROBE first {"offline":true,"admissions":1,"modelCalls":0}
ISSUE_PROBE retry {"status":"error","admissions":1,"modelCalls":0}
ISSUE_PROBE baseline: primary skipped before admission
```

Fixed runtime `f7dcf12e72b`

```text
ISSUE_PROBE first {"offline":true,"admissions":1,"modelCalls":0}
ISSUE_PROBE retry {"status":"ok","model":"probe-model","hasReply":true,"admissions":2,"modelCalls":1}
```

**Transcript failure after the model replied.** The fixture awaited a nonempty model reply and then raised `SessionTranscriptWriterClaimReboundError`. Success had cleared the synthetic profile’s cooldown (`profileStillCooling` was `false`), so the fixture reapplied it before the retry. The retry began 21,298 ms after the first turn began. The request count stayed at one.

```text
ISSUE_PROBE post-provider {"modelAnswered":true,"writerFailure":true,"profileStillCooling":false,"retryAfterMs":21298,"skipped":true,"admissions":1,"modelCalls":1}
```

**Late completion of an older probe.** The fixture advanced the clock past the probe interval and admitted a newer probe. The older pre-dispatch failure arrived after the newer model call. A third attempt observed the newer reservation.

```text
ISSUE_PROBE overlap {"olderFailedAfterNewer":true,"newerModelCalls":1,"third":"MODEL_FALLBACK_SKIPPED","clockAdvancedMs":30001}
```

### Committed regression on base and head

I copied only the [committed worker test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9c0da2ee43b585bd5ab9f62b64f85f2cc88c22bb/src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-launcher-failure-recovery.test.ts#L519-L576) into a clean worktree at `7a570c41bc2`. The test holds the clock across both attempts so a slow worker cannot outlast the 30-second interval. Without that clock control a cold baseline run took 54 seconds and the pre-dispatch case passed.

To select the two disconnect cases in either checkout, run

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/worker-environments/worker-turn-launcher-failure-recovery.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1 -t 'retries a cooled-down primary only if'
```

Base output, with the common file prefix omitted and the fixture model name redacted

```text
× retries a cooled-down primary only if the worker disconnects before dispatch (disconnect: before) 50570ms
✓ retries a cooled-down primary only if the worker disconnects before dispatch (disconnect: after) 3875ms
Caused by: FailoverError: All models failed (1): [fixture model]: Provider openai is in cooldown (overloaded)
Tests  1 failed | 1 passed | 16 skipped (18)
```

Worker test on `9c0da2ee43b`, including all 18 cases in the file

```text
✓ retries a cooled-down primary only if the worker disconnects before dispatch (disconnect: before) 5981ms
✓ retries a cooled-down primary only if the worker disconnects before dispatch (disconnect: after) 4316ms
Tests  18 passed (18)
```

The original runtime change passed 289 focused tests in 16 files, the build, production and affected test typechecks, lint, formatting, and docs link checks.

### Model policy and placement admission on `016703f257b`

After #204155 and #204249, fallback candidates use the operator model policy admitted for the run. In a merge that skipped cleanup when the model policy denied dispatch, the immediate retry failed with `Provider fixture is in cooldown (overloaded)`. On this revision the rejected turn makes zero candidate calls and the next permitted turn makes one. [Model-policy regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/016703f257b98218e394917db17611082d40770c/src/agents/model-fallback.operator-model-policy.test.ts#L64)

A Gateway lifecycle change can also reject placement before execution starts. The local and remote admission tests both reproduced a missing release. Both now release the unused reservation. The worker disconnect after dispatch still keeps its throttle. [Placement regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/016703f257b98218e394917db17611082d40770c/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/lane-controller.test.ts#L962)

In an isolated Gateway, the placement fixture rotated the lifecycle on the first authenticated `agent` RPC. The Gateway withdrew that input before execution. The next RPC reached placement 11,349 ms after the first began and got a reply from local Qwen. The forwarding proxy counted completion POSTs across both RPCs.

```text
ISSUE_PROBE first {"status":"timeout","stopReason":"restart","timeoutPhase":"gateway_draining","admissions":1,"modelCalls":0}
ISSUE_PROBE retry {"status":"ok","model":"probe-model","hasReply":true,"admissions":2,"modelCalls":1}
ISSUE_PROBE admission {"retryAdmissionAfterMs":11349,"operatorAdmissions":2}
```

All 227 focused tests in nine files passed on this revision, along with the full build, production and affected test typechecks, lint, and formatting. CI for `016703f257b` is awaiting approval. [Upstream CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45328721026)

<details>
<summary>Review, test timings, and change size</summary>

- Local Codex autoreview covered the runtime change in `f7dcf12e72b` against `7a570c41bc2`. A second pass covered the test-clock change in `9c0da2ee43b`. Both reported no actionable findings through P2. A fresh local review against `ad2f629e55f` found a placement-admission issue. The final pass on the complete `016703f257b` tree reported no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- On `016703f257b`, Vitest recorded 64.5 s for worker launch recovery, 33.5 s for runtime refresh, 2.9 s for personal cooldowns, 1.0 s for fallback model policy, and 0.2 s for the lane controller. The integration files exercise worker handoff and runtime admission.
- Relative to the merge base, production code adds 123 lines and removes 62, tests add 152 and remove 9, and documentation changes one line. The existing cooldown owner holds the reservation. The runtime wiring carries its release callback to the code that observes dispatch.
- Maintainer edits, including workflow edits on this fork branch, are enabled.

</details>

prs.title: fix: count settled model tokens toward Goal budgets
prs.body:
Closes #203350

## What Problem This Solves

A built-in Goal could keep running past its token budget when its context size stayed flat or shrank. The budget counted growth in the conversation, not the model tokens used to do the work.

## User Impact

Budgeted built-in Goals now count tokens from settled turns and stop scheduling more work once the budget is reached. Turns served by a CLI backend count the usage the CLI reports. If a turn reports no settled usage, the Goal records why pursuit stopped instead of assuming zero. This is a continuation limit, not a cap on the cost of an in-flight model call.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing turn settlement records the token total for the Goal that was active at admission. Retries of the same settlement do not count twice. Existing Goals keep their recorded tally; no historical usage is backfilled. Unbudgeted Goal behavior and native Codex accounting are unchanged.

## Evidence

- **Published head `33b8ef2680e7`:** Both new CLI regressions failed without the fix. With it, 195 focused tests passed, covering Goal accounting, persistence, continuation, Gateway requester authority, and the Gateway budget stop. The session-identity ratchet, core and four targeted test typechecks, lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Local Auto Review found no P0 issues. [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/4d05a3e4-7d3d-4b98-abe1-b4c5d8e24333) · [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45274833548) · [required gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45274832852).
- The branch incorporates `main` at `7866e72c5d82`. The resolved authority test preserves the revoked-requester outcome: the Goal stays active without continuing, and the completed turn still records its 28 tokens. GitHub readback confirmed both the original PR head and the pinned `main` in the new merge history.
- **Stable upgrade on this head:** [2026.11.7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.11.7) created three Goals in SQLite. Doctor migrated a disposable copy from schema 38 to 43. The first read preserved Goal/session IDs, objectives, timestamps, statuses and budget windows: active 17/80, paused 9/50, exhausted 55/50. Resuming only the exhausted Goal preserved its ID and reset it to 0/50; the other two did not change.
- **Gateway → local CLI executable on this head:** Two explicitly submitted turns each reported 45 tokens. The Goal moved 0 → 45 → 90 and reached `budget_limited` at a budget of 75. A successful CLI response with no usage instead recorded `usage_limited` at 0/75 with a reason and no successor. This was a deterministic executable, not live Claude. Automatic continuations were separately observed on the embedded loopback path (135,000/100,000), not in the direct CLI capture.
- **CI attribution:** The failing assertions from shards 2, 33 and 39 also failed on exact base `7866e72c5d82`. Shard 28 passed five repeats on both revisions; its assertion also failed on an unrelated PR ([tracking issue](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/204187)). This does not turn the red hosted gate green.

<details>
<summary>Earlier real-model and upgrade evidence</summary>

- An isolated real-model Gateway created a Goal with a 30,000-token budget. After five successor turns the recorded usage reached 32,142, the Goal became `budget_limited`, and no further model calls occurred during two more minutes of observation. The baseline remained `active` after model-reported usage had already exceeded the budget.
- The earlier CLI fallback run on `bc3049ff6f86` ended `usage_limited` with zero metered tokens after one CLI turn. With the CLI fix from the handoff, live Claude CLI turns against a 40,000-token budget recorded 11,709, 24,099, 37,200, and 51,002 tokens; the fourth turn moved the Goal to `budget_limited`. Two more user turns did not change the tally.
- The 2026.11.6 stable-upgrade run migrated a disposable SQLite store from schema 38 to 43 and preserved three Goals, their recorded usage, and the configured budget. Resume reset only the exhausted Goal tally.

</details>

prs.title: fix: avoid raw errno on stale cloud worker PID probes
prs.body:
Closes #200021

## What Problem This Solves

On Linux cloud workers, a resume attempt with a stale `node.pid` crashes with bare errno text: `kill EPERM` when the PID now belongs to another user, or a raw `ENOENT` for `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` when the worker exits between the liveness probe and identity reads. The stale receipt is never replaced, so the worker stays stuck instead of reaching the existing actionable "release and reprovision the worker" guidance or a clean replay.

## User Impact

A PID owned by another user is now treated as a live foreign process and rejected by the normal identity fence, with its actionable message. A process that disappears during identity reads is treated as dead, allowing the stale receipt to be replaced safely. Other probe errors still fail closed. No change for healthy worker replay.

## Why This Change Was Made

The liveness probe only exempted `ESRCH`, so POSIX `EPERM` (which means the process exists) escaped as a raw error. The Linux procfs identity reads were also the only platform branch without error handling. The probe now normalizes `EPERM` to "alive", and procfs `ENOENT`/`ESRCH` fall through to the dead-PID path while other read failures leave verification failing closed at the fence. This matches the handling already used by the warm-image scrub sibling.

## Evidence

Two new regression cases were added to `crabbox-worker-node-enrollment-replay.test.ts` and pass with the fix. Reverting only the source file and rerunning those cases produced two failures showing the raw `kill EPERM` and raw `/proc/.../cmdline` ENOENT output. The full replay file has 8 pre-existing failures in this local Windows environment (unrelated native/lsof and interrupted-launch cases); the two new cases were verified in isolation with `-t "EPERM|procfs race"` (2 passed, 41 skipped). No live Linux cloud worker was available locally.

## AI assistance

This fix and its tests were prepared with AI assistance and reviewed locally before submission.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep session status badges compact beside wrapped titles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a session status badge grows tall beside a wrapped handoff session title, and on phone-width chat views the resumed handoff list runs off the screen so its badges cannot be seen.

## User Impact

Status labels stay compact and readable beside wrapped session titles, and the resumed handoff list fits on narrow screens with every badge visible. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each list row now aligns to its top edge, and status text stays on one line. Long titles still wrap. The resumed handoff block is capped at the width of its chat group. Before this change the block grew to the list's fixed 560 px width, so the list's own maximum width never took effect on narrow views. Desktop layout is unchanged, and the list stays 560 px wide so status badges still line up. Session links and the disclosure behave as before.

Contributor credit: Mitchell Etzel reported the visual defect and requested the fix.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren't public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/2741a181-9bfc-48e1-bc46-f6bfe403279b)
- [CSS budget repair and integration verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1a7911fa-25cb-453b-baeb-84c90fa320d0)

## Evidence

Built Control UI (production bundle, mocked Gateway, synthetic sessions), resumed handoff with three child sessions. One session has a long title that wraps and is still Running.

| Viewport | Before (main CSS) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| 1280 x 900 | Running badge 55.8 px tall, the height of the wrapped title | Running badge 19.0 px tall, one line, top-aligned |
| 390 x 844 | List right edge at 598 px, past the 390 px screen; no badge visible | List right edge at 357 px; all three badges visible, 19.0 px tall |

Status line height is 17.05 px in every case.

### Clean comparison, desktop 1280 x 900

#### Before

#### After

prs.title: fix(ci): model every Solid lazy named-export loader in the UI for Knip
prs.body:
## Result

The `check-dependencies` job on `main` passes again. It has been red since #204200 (first red: scheduled run 45319833099 on a21974cd). Knip reported a false unused export:

```
Unused exports are not allowed:
  ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-read-aloud-status.tsx: RecordingApiKeyNotice
```

## Cause

`RecordingApiKeyNotice` has one real production consumer: `chat-message-bubble-view.tsx` loads it with `lazy(() => import("./chat-read-aloud-status.tsx"), { export: "RecordingApiKeyNotice" })`. Solid selects the export by a string, which Knip cannot see. `config/knip-vite-consumers.mjs` modeled that pattern for exactly one hard-coded loader (`settings-sidebar-lazy.tsx`). Every other lazy named-export loader either had an ignore entry or broke the gate, as this one did.

## Change

The consumer model now derives a named import edge from every non-test UI source file that contains a `lazy(() => import("…"), { export: "…" })` loader. A new loader needs no registration, and deleting a loader still removes its edge, so a truly unused export is still reported.

## Evidence

- `check-deadcode-exports.test.ts`: 36 passed. The updated case (two loaders in different directories, test files excluded, deleted loader dropped) fails on `main`.
- `pnpm deadcode:report` on this head: script, production and full-tree Knip reports all pass. On `main`, the production and full-tree reports fail with the error above.

prs.title: fix: preserve profiles when Linux onboarding cannot install the Gateway service
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Linux without a working user-systemd session, `openclaw onboard --non-interactive --install-daemon` can write config and create a workspace before exiting with a service-install error. If `--reset` is also requested, the reset can run before the same error is reported.

## What Changes

Check user-systemd availability before dispatching reset or setup, only for local, non-interactive Linux onboarding that explicitly requests daemon installation. Keep the installer's check in case availability changes after preflight. The error tells users to rerun with `--skip-daemon` or retry from a working user-systemd session.

## Evidence

### Behavior proof: real Linux CLI

Ran the CLI from this patch in an isolated Linux container with Node 24 and no working user-systemd session. The run used a disposable home, explicit config and state paths, and a dedicated workspace. Common options were `--non-interactive --accept-risk --mode local --auth-choice skip --skip-channels --skip-skills --skip-health --workspace "$workspace" --json`.

Captured terminal output from the Linux run (outer test script exited 0):

```text
ISOLATED_DEPS_READY
REFUSAL_EXIT=1
Cannot install the Gateway service: systemd user services are unavailable. Rerun with --skip-daemon for setup without a background service, or retry from a working user-systemd session.
FRESH_NO_CONFIG_OR_WORKSPACE
SKIP_DAEMON_CONTROL_OK
REFUSAL_EXIT=1
Cannot install the Gateway service: systemd user services are unavailable. Rerun with --skip-daemon for setup without a background service, or retry from a working user-systemd session.
RESET_CONFIG_AND_WORKSPACE_UNCHANGED
```

The harness parsed the CLI's JSON and printed the actual `message` only after asserting `ok: false`, `phase: "options"`, and `--skip-daemon` guidance. It asserted CLI exit 1 in both refusals. The named markers came from the harness, not the CLI; each printed only after these shell assertions passed:

| Scenario | Assertions behind the output |
| --- | --- |
| Fresh profile, `--install-daemon` | `test ! -e "$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH"` and `test ! -e "$workspace"`. |
| Same environment, `--skip-daemon` | CLI exit 0, then `test -s "$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH"` and `test -d "$workspace"`. |
| Existing profile, `--install-daemon --reset --reset-scope full` | Copied the config and added a workspace sentinel before invoking reset. `cmp` confirmed the config was byte-for-byte unchanged, and the sentinel still contained `sentinel`. |

For comparison, an earlier isolated Linux CLI run on unpatched `v2026.11.10-beta.3` reproduced the fresh-install bug: onboarding reported unavailable user systemd, but both the config and workspace were created. The runtime checks above cover the specified paths, not every possible filesystem side effect.

### Regression checks and limits

- On unpatched `main` (`5754fac480d8`), the new focused suite had **3 failures and 4 passes**: the probe was never called in the two refusal cases or in the supported local Linux case. With the patch, **45 tests across four focused onboarding suites passed**.
- The tests assert that neither reset nor setup is called on refusal. They also verify normal setup dispatch with a mocked working probe and no preflight for remote mode, daemon opt-out, an omitted daemon flag, or the covered macOS case.
- Core TypeScript, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Successful installation under a real user-systemd session was not exercised; the working-probe path was covered with mocks. The live Gateway was not touched.

Prepared with OpenClaw assistance.

prs.title: fix(sessions): clear stale compactionQualityDegraded on rewind/branch switch
prs.body:
Fixes #204060

## What Problem This Solves
After a lossy compaction, `compactionQualityDegraded: true` is written to the session entry. Rewinding to before that turn (or switching branches) cleared `compactionCount` but not the degraded flag, so `/status` kept showing `Compactions: 0 · degraded history (details may be lost)` even though the context was fully restored — a false "degraded" warning on a healthy session.

## Change
`buildMessageCutSessionEntry` now derives the degradation flag from the selected transcript path on every rewind / branch-switch / fork commit: the flag is cleared when the new path contains no quality-degraded compaction, and kept (recomputed from the active path's compaction events) when it does. No change to the status formatter's zero-count warning logic, and no unconditional clearing — switching back to a still-degraded history restores the warning.

Also fixed while testing: fork planning only saw navigation-projected compaction rows (no `details`), so the planner could not see degradation info; the fork read path now exposes `hasDegradedCompaction(prefix)`, which reads only the selected prefix's compaction payloads one at a time instead of hydrating every summary.

## Evidence
- 5 new regression tests: SQLite (rewind clears, switch away/back restores, fork prefix) and memory (rewind clears, switch away/back restores).
- SQLite message-cut file: 17/17 passed; memory fork file: 8/8 passed; `sessions-rewind` (+incognito): 30/30; `status-message`: 28/28.
- Failing-first verified for the rewind + switch SQLite tests (failed on base with "expected true to be undefined", green with the fix).
- Rebased onto current upstream main (b647c1be) and re-ran both targeted suites after the rebase: 17/17 and 8/8 green.
- Not verified locally: `pnpm tsgo:core` (typecheck) could not run on my machine (OOM; the repo's own docs note tsgo peaks at ~8.4 GiB). Please let CI run it. The fork test was not run red-on-base separately (its red state follows directly from the base code never setting the flag).

### Update: ClawSweeper rework (2026-11-24)

Both P2 regressions are fixed; the flag-derivation behavior is unchanged (rewind clears, switching back to degraded history restores).

**Fork read budget.** `readSessionMessageCut` no longer hydrates every compaction payload before the planner picks the prefix. The read result now exposes `hasDegradedCompaction(prefix)`, which reads only the selected prefix's compaction payloads one at a time (per-event budget guard, no retention, no charge to the cumulative 8 MiB navigation budget). This preserves the streaming intent of b62210f: only navigation, header, and editor data stay resident while copied payloads stream.

**Ordinary rewind scan.** `selectedPathHasDegradedCompaction` now fast-paths via the active-path projection for targets on the active path with no reset after them (compaction seqs from `session_transcript_active_events` up to the target position, payload reads one at a time; `targetId === null` returns false immediately). Canonical tree resolution is reserved for off-path targets (branch switch) and post-selection resets. This preserves the indexed in-place rewind intent of d59fe05.

**Real behavior proof (in-process harness, real entry points).** The test `proves /status clears and returns across navigation and fork` seeds a session through the production append owner (pre-change stored shape: `compactionQualityDegraded: true`, `compactionCount: 2`), then drives the real SQLite accessor (`rewindSessionToMessage`, `switchSessionBranch`, `forkSessionAtMessage`) and the real /status renderer (`buildStatusMessageParts`). Rendered Compactions line at each step:

```text
/status before:             Compactions: 2 · degraded history (details may be lost)
/status after rewind:        [no Compactions line]
/status after branch switch: Compactions: 0 · degraded history (details may be lost)
/status on clean fork:       [no Compactions line]
/status on degraded fork:    Compactions: 0 · degraded history (details may be lost)
```

**Data-model compatibility.** The harness above loads the exact rows the stable release writes (seeded through the production append owner, untouched by this PR) with the changed code; the 2 → 0 count across navigation is the compatibility evidence.

**Failing-first.** The fork-budget regression test fails on the pre-fix code with `Session history editor/header content exceeds the 8 MiB navigation budget` and passes after. The rewind-scan regression test fails on the pre-fix code (the precheck issued the canonical navigation scan twice) and passes after (no `identity_count` query). Fork-flag assertions fail on base b647c1be (degraded fork: flag undefined instead of true) and pass after.

**Test results (direct vitest, `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=2048`):**

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| SQLite message-cut (infra) | 20/20 (17 existing + 3 new) |
| Memory fork (runtime-config) | 8/8 |
| sessions-rewind + incognito (gateway-methods) | 30/30 |
| status-message (unit-fast-isolated) | 28/28 |

Format clean, oxlint 0 warnings/errors, `git diff --check` clean.
`pnpm tsgo:core` was not run locally (OOM on this machine, peak ~8.4 GiB vs 6.1 GiB cgroup) — CI must run it.

prs.title: docs(release): keep parallel release lines ledger-only and coverage explicit
prs.body:
## Problem
We often run beta, stable, and extended-stable releases at the same time, in separate sessions that shouldn't message each other. The only thing they share is the hotfix ledger. In 2026.11.10-beta.3 that ledger quietly dropped work:
- Fixes with no assessment for the release never showed up anywhere. That covered 87 candidates cut by a capped review batch and 12 high-severity fixes added after the last sweep.
- `blocked` was used to mean "no test environment", and nobody rechecked those fixes once Testbox and PostgreSQL became available.
- Decisions that needed the operator were never put to them.

## Change
Guidance only, kept short.

`hotfix-ledger-management.md`:
- New **Parallel release lines** section. Each release owner works only from the shared hotfix records and its own release record. Another release's assessment is evidence, not this release's decision. Anything a later owner needs goes into the ledger, not a message to another session.
- The checkpoint now also looks for eligible fixes that have no assessment yet. A capped review batch writes its remaining fixes as `unknown` instead of skipping them.
- `blocked` now means a named decision is needed (schema, config, public contract, permission, or policy). A missing test environment is recorded as a deferral, with a note on what would let it resume.
- A destination counts only if it is on the release branch. A partial `-x` pick is `adaptation_required`.
- Before freezing, tell the operator how many fixes are still unassessed and which decisions are blocked.
- At closeout, unshipped `needed` fixes get a `deferred` or `policy_excluded` reason and are added to the next release record on the same line.

`backport-discovery.md`:
- Freezing with an unfinished inventory is the operator's call. Report how much is still unreviewed first.

## Impact
No product change, no scripts, and no new gates or validators. The rules just make it clear what each release owner records and reports.

## Evidence
- The beta.3 ledger was reconciled against the shipped `3d2d379` (865 assessments).
- The missed-backport report for 11.10 is done: 36 added, 23 excluded with reasons.
- `git diff --check` passes.

## What Problem This Solves

Pressing Command-R while working in the macOS Dashboard reloads the current page. That interrupts the active view even when the user did not intend to leave it. It does not restart the Mac app or the Gateway.

## User Impact

Command-R no longer triggers Dashboard reload. Use Shift-Command-R or choose **Navigate → Reload** to reload the active Dashboard, including its recovery page.

## Why This Change Was Made

The native menu already owns this command. Requiring Shift there makes reload deliberate without adding a keyboard handler in the web view or changing browser shortcuts or theme persistence.

## Evidence

AppKit dispatched real key events to the SwiftUI Navigate menu in an isolated macOS test app. Before the change, Command-R invoked Reload and Shift-Command-R did not; after, only Shift-Command-R invoked Reload. Option-Command-R did not invoke it in either version. With a text area focused in a nonpersistent WKWebView, Command-R previously loaded a new document. On the candidate it preserved the document and the typed text; Shift-Command-R loaded a new document exactly once. This exercises native menu dispatch and WebKit, not the installed OpenClaw app.

A separate check used the production Dashboard window and Navigate menu in an isolated macOS guest. With a local editor page focused in the Dashboard, a synthesized Command-R kept the same document, the text `draft`, and keyboard focus without navigating. Shift-Command-R navigated exactly once. The macOS code matched the CI integration (`371057e866c1`).

prs.title: fix: keep hidden macOS dashboards connected until closed
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Hiding the macOS app made an open dashboard look closed to the code that handles Gateway reconnections. If the SSH tunnel recovered while the app was hidden, the native app could reconnect while the existing dashboard kept its outdated connection. On the base build (`fb629723a4f3`), both the Gateway and its tunnel were healthy, but the same window's controls stayed unavailable for more than 50 seconds after returning. Explicitly reopening the dashboard restored access.

## What changed

The native dashboard window now records whether it has been preloaded, opened, or closed. Hiding or minimizing an open window changes its presentation, not its lifetime. Replacing the document keeps the lifetime of its window; closing the window ends it. The existing connection and native authorization handlers read that same state. There is no unhide observer, retry timer, or change to Gateway admission.

## Verification

Using a signed debug build of the integrated commit (`b94a516938d2`) and synthetic profiles in a macOS VM, we hid the macOS app while the dashboard window was open and interrupted the app-owned SSH tunnel twice. On both runs the Gateway accepted the dashboard connection, separately from the native operator and node, **before the app was unhidden**. Back in the same window, pressing **Check again** completed `openclaw.setup.detect` on that same connection. Neither run required a reopen or reload. After explicitly closing the window, we interrupted the tunnel a third time: the native transport recovered, the dashboard did not reconnect, and no window reappeared.

The focused Swift regression failed on the previous PR revision (`1caf60ace18f`): an already-open but hidden window did not receive its updated native binding. With this change it followed two updates while still hidden, preserved an unsent draft in the same document, and stopped receiving updates on close. All 61 tests in eight macOS suites passed on the integrated commit, including preload, close/reopen, fullscreen, profile replacement, the native authorization bridge, and the upstream favicon refresh when a hidden dashboard is shown again.

SwiftFormat and SwiftLint reported no violations in the changed files. Local source review found no actionable findings. System sleep was not tested because the macOS VM refused the sleep request.

### Models page before and after

The before images are from the base build. The after images are from the second live macOS VM run with the fix (`d8c4d7424718`).

**Before:** Add account was disabled and Check again was not shown. The controls stayed in this state for more than 50 seconds after returning to the app.

![Models page with Add account disabled and two placeholders](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40246c9f-5c18-4074-bbfd-0efdd6948ea5)

**After:** Add account is enabled, Check again is available, and the model picker has loaded. Use stays disabled until a model is selected.

![The same Models controls available on the fixed build](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b428dc77-42f3-4019-b801-27bc44a0f539)

The purple outline below is an annotation around the same button, not a focus ring. The screenshots show the controls; the live connection and its timing were checked separately.

![Add account disabled on the base build](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e33a615c-33dd-486a-86c8-b430a01a73c1)

![Add account enabled on the fixed build](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fb59ace6-f7d1-4f1e-8848-70989fda4a56)

prs.title: fix(ui): clarify pending guest suggestions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A guest who submitted a suggestion saw a bare name and “Pending.” Long suggestions wrapped above the composer, and the status moved to another line on narrow screens. During verification, an Inbox test also exposed an Escape interaction: a sidebar tooltip could finish loading after the user had already moved on to the Inbox and consume the first Escape.

## User Impact

Guests now see the author's avatar and name, one line of prompt text, and “Awaiting approval.” Owner actions and resolved suggestions are unchanged. A tooltip that never appeared can no longer take Escape away from the focused Inbox.

## Why This Change Was Made

The guest preview uses the existing person-reference label with the author's profile ID and shares its frame with neighboring composer cards. The full prompt remains in the row for assistive technology; only its visual presentation is shortened. No permission or approval behavior changes.

The tooltip owner now cancels a pending reveal when the pointer leaves. A visible rich tooltip still provides time to move the pointer into its contents.

## Evidence

The real Control UI ran against synthetic Gateway data in Chromium. The new guest-row regression failed on the base, then passed at 1180 px and 400 px. All 10 suggestion browser scenarios, 3 component tests, and 20 surrounding layout and corner tests passed. UI typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, and English catalog verification passed.

The [initial performance failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45319117785/job/138193898645) was PR-caused: raw CSS grew by 563 bytes where only 64 were allowed. Sharing the card styles reduced that growth to 10 bytes (+20 bytes gzip). The full local differential gate passed against base 63125678512d without a budget change. The repaired row and composer crop is pixel-identical to the After image below.

The [Inbox shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45320739299/job/138199122293) captured the dialog still open after Escape, but not the pre-key event target. Holding the sidebar tooltip's first render reproduced that outcome on the previous head with the Inbox list focused. With the fix, a single real Escape closes the dialog and restores focus to its trigger. The original shard selection passed locally (33 files, 142 tests), including the original navigation case and the new controlled regression. The tooltip and Inbox owner suites also passed.

prs.title: fix: keep agent work moving past recoverable setup failures
prs.body:
Related: #204343 (reported during review; no Telegram changes).

## What Problem This Solves

A reviewer failed to start even though the correction had passed its tests. The agent handed setup back to the requester before trying supported recovery. Skipping that handoff left the requester having to ask again for work that did not depend on it.

## User Impact

The agent now has explicit instructions to try recovery it is already allowed to perform before asking for help. Skipping a manual step or letting it expire leaves dependent actions blocked, not the rest of an active request. Choosing **Stop this task** still means stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Direct tools and Code Mode share the pre-handoff guidance. The existing `action_unresolved` result now carries the next action for its actual reason, so Code Mode does not lose the distinction when it returns structured data rather than display text. No approval, review, sandbox, or tool permission changes.

## Evidence

Two unscripted turns on an isolated Gateway exercised the outcome. When the primary review-record path was missing, the agent used the documented mirror and wrote the verified decision and the independent tracking file without asking for help. After one Skip, it wrote the independent file, left the device-confirmation file absent, and did not ask again.

Terminal output from that run (each line is emitted only after checking the real files and question count; no transcript or credentials):

```jsonl
{"kind":"setup","model":"openai/gpt-5.6-luna","skipped":0,"independentWork":"completed","dependentWork":"verified"}
{"kind":"skip","model":"openai/gpt-5.6-luna","skipped":1,"independentWork":"completed","dependentWork":"not performed"}
```

The new handoff and result assertions failed on the base. All 74 focused tests passed with the fix, including cancellation, expiry, explicit Stop, recheck, and prompt stability. Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, and docs checks passed. Local Codex autoreview could not start in its read-only sandbox. The [completed hosted re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204353#issuecomment-7121309564) accepted the live proof and found no actionable code issues on `82dec2b8174d`.

**Required CI is red.** [Attempt 1 on this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45319110530) finished with 14 failing test jobs. All 39 distinct failure diagnostics matched earlier runs without this patch, by source path, test case, and error—not just job name. The three CSS-size messages were warnings, not failed tests.

- The nine `checks-node-changed` jobs (2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11, 12, 13) have matching diagnostics in [earlier independent CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45312232532). prs.title: feat: add opt-in Agent Profiles for small local models
prs.body:
Part of #204354. Related: openclaw/rfcs#18 (Agent Profiles RFC)

## What Problem This Solves

A local model with a small context window gets the same system prompt as a hosted model. On a 32K window that prompt fills about 40% of the window before the user says anything. Lean mode (`experimental.localModelLean`) trims only some of it and cannot be set per model size. Agent Profiles (RFC 18) give each agent a named profile that sets the workspace budget, context serialization and tool surface.

This is slice 1 of 3 of the Agent Profiles work, split from one 90-commit branch so each part can be reviewed on its own. Base of the stack. Slices 2 and 3 are stacked on this branch.

Dependencies: none. This PR does not depend on slice 2 or slice 3.

## This slice

Base: main `1601f86def0`. Head `f6a84ab8cb4`. 24 commits (5 by Onur Solmaz, 19 by Mitchell Etzel). Diff: 122 files, +3948 -668. Every commit is signed. Onur Solmaz's commits keep his authorship, and the rest are by Mitchell Etzel.

This slice adds the profile object and everything that applies it. It does not select a profile by model size.

- Agent Profiles: the `agentprofiles` dependency, the OpenClaw profile extension, the built-ins `openclaw/base` and `openclaw/small`, the resolver, and `agents.defaults.agentProfileId` with the per-agent override.
- The workspace budget: `openclaw/small` caps `AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `IDENTITY.md` and `USER.md` at 11,500 characters together, on embedded, CLI, compaction, harness, Codex, Copilot, agentsapi, acpx, Muse and worker routes. Compaction takes the profile through the shared `resolveBootstrapContextForRun` owner; there is no second budgeting adapter.
- The tool surface: `openclaw/small` filters seven heavy tools out by default before building the Tool Search catalog. Explicitly preserved tools still follow normal tool policy. The compact filter does not remove `automations` or `exec`.
- Diagnostics: `/context` and the system prompt report show the selected profile and budget; `openclaw agent exec --agent-profile` picks one for a run.
- Lean retirement: `openclaw doctor --fix` turns `experimental.localModelLean: true` into `agentProfileId: "openclaw/small"`, and an explicit `false` under an enabled default into `openclaw/base`; `--local-model-lean` stays as an alias for `--agent-profile openclaw/small`.

## User Impact

- With no `agentProfileId` set, every agent uses `openclaw/base`: the prompt and tool list are the same as on `main`.
- An operator picks `openclaw/small` by hand, per agent or in defaults.
- An operator who set `experimental.localModelLean: true` keeps the small profile after `openclaw doctor --fix`. `openclaw/small` also applies the 11,500-character workspace budget.
- `auto` and size classes are not in this slice (slice 2). Compact context serialization is not in this slice (slice 3); here `openclaw/small` keeps the default serialization.

## Why This Change Was Made

The workspace budget, the tool surface and the Doctor migration all read one resolved profile, so they land together: split apart, a profile would select nothing. Selection by model size (slice 2) and compact serialization (slice 3) build on this resolver.

Config and API surface: this slice adds `agents.defaults.agentProfileId` and the per-agent `agentProfileId`, the `openclaw agent exec --agent-profile` flag, and the `agentProfileApplied` harness option (`localModelLeanApplied` stays as a deprecated alias). A persisted selector is needed because the profile has to survive restarts and be set per agent; Doctor retires `experimental.localModelLean` into it, so there is one setting, not two.

## Evidence

### Runtime output

Shipped entry points at this slice, on build `f6a84ab8cb4` (`pnpm build`, the head of this branch), against a real Qwen3-8B Q8_0 on llama.cpp (`qwen3-8b-q8_0`), one request at a time. A capture proxy sits between OpenClaw and the model server and records every request body and every server `usage` block. Every response reports model id `qwen3-8b-q8_0`. Throwaway `OPENCLAW_HOME`, no Gateway, from a clean environment. Hostnames, IPs, ports, paths and session ids are redacted.

#### (a) Over-budget workspace truncation

`agents.defaults.agentProfileId = "openclaw/small"`, an `AGENTS.md` of 12,000 characters and an `IDENTITY.md` of 3,000 characters, one shipped CLI turn: `openclaw agent --local --agent main --session-key <key> --message "Reply with one word: pong (<nonce>)" --json --timeout 300`.

```text
config validate: Config valid
turn exit: 0   request: req-1.json (the captured turn that carries the nonce trunc-mwu0b0vs)
workspace files on disk:        AGENTS.md 12000 chars, IDENTITY.md 3000 chars
in the system prompt:           AGENTS.md section 4626 chars, IDENTITY.md section 1035 chars
truncation markers in the prompt: ["[...truncated, read AGENTS.md for full content...]", "[...truncated, read IDENTITY.md for full content...]"]
server call: status=200 model=qwen3-8b-q8_0 messages=3 tools=13 tool_schema_chars=15392 system_chars=27146 usage.prompt_tokens=10357 completion_tokens=2 finish=stop reply="pong"
```

The profile bounds the four injected files to 11,500 characters together (per-file caps 7,500 for `AGENTS.md` and 1,024 for `IDENTITY.md`), and the prompt tells the model to read the file for the rest. Without a profile the default limits (20,000 per file, 60,000 total) inject the same files whole.

The same captured request offers 13 tools: `apply_patch`, `dispatch_action`, `edit`, `exec`, `ls`, `openclaw`, `process`, `read`, `session_project`, `sessions_yield`, `tool_describe`, `tool_search` and `write`. #### (b) Doctor upgrade from the latest stable release, explicit Lean choices kept as profiles

prs.title: fix(tts): deliver OpenAI-compatible speech as it arrives
prs.body:
Fixes #204368

## What Problem This Solves

The OpenAI speech provider does not expose incremental audio to streaming TTS callers, even when the configured endpoint sends audio in chunks.

## User Impact

Callers of `textToSpeechStream` can receive OpenAI-compatible speech before synthesis finishes. Browser Talk still uses the buffered `talk.speak` RPC. This PR does not reduce browser Talk latency.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider now forwards audio as it arrives and releases the guarded HTTP request when the stream ends, fails, or is canceled. Raw PCM assumes 24 kHz. Endpoints with a different sample rate can use WAV if they support it. Buffered synthesis keeps its current behavior.

## Evidence

- Phonon, three warm paired trials with matching text and voice: median **25 ms** to the first PCM chunk versus **443 ms** to the complete buffered WAV. This measures provider delivery, not playback.
- **79 focused tests passed** across five files. The regression failed on stock because the streaming hook was absent. Tests cover mid-stream cancellation and explicit release, followed by a successful next request.
- The compiled TTS SDK delivered WAV before EOF. Gateway playback was not measured, and no authorized OpenAI Platform key was available for a live OpenAI test.
- Runtime bundles built. The full local build stalled during declaration generation. This draft leaves that check pending.

AI-assisted. Second review: Marvin (claude-opus-5-5). The Codex review attempt returned HTTP 429.

prs.title: test(browser): forward lstat options in install-layout ownership mocks
prs.body:
## Result

`extensions/browser/src/browser/extension-install-layout.test.ts` "installs from a package-shaped root-owned tree into user-owned state" passes again. It is the last red file in the scheduled **Hourly Extension Tests** workflow (`plugin-prerelease.yml`, `checks-node-extensions-shard-7`). That workflow has been red on every scheduled run since 2026-11-22T08:39Z; the other causes are already fixed on `main`.

## Cause

#203860 (`efe7b7f5`, fs-safe 0.28.2) made `RootHandle` verify file identity with bigint `lstat` results (`inspectFileIdentity` rejects numeric `dev`/`ino`). The test's two `fs.lstat` spies called the real `lstat(target)` without the caller's options, so fs-safe got numeric stats. It then reported "file identity changed", then "root path changed during operation", and the chromium registration came back `invalid`. Product code is unaffected.

## Fix

Both spies forward `options` to the real `lstat`. The `foreign-owner` case used the same pattern. It passed only because a refusal was expected, and it now refuses for its own reason.

## Evidence

- `efe7b7f5^`: 22/22 pass. `efe7b7f5`: 1 failed (this case). Current `main`: 1 failed. Head: 22/22 pass.
- Scheduled runs 45127204974 .. 45314013064 (21 runs): `AssertionError: expected 'invalid' to be 'owned'` at `extension-install-layout.test.ts:90`.

prs.title: fix(ci): install the Android SDK for scheduled Android CodeQL on Boat
prs.body:
## Result

Scheduled Android CodeQL critical-security scans have failed every day since 2026-11-12, so no critical Android scan reached code scanning. This change makes them build again.

## Cause

#196904 routed scheduled `main` runs of `codeql-android-critical-security.yml` to `boat-xlarge`. Boat runners have no preinstalled Android SDK. The workflow only installed Java, so the Gradle build failed before CodeQL could analyze:

```
Could not determine the dependencies of task ':app:compilePlayDebugJavaWithJavac'.
> SDK location not found. Define a valid SDK location with an ANDROID_HOME environment variable ...
```

Manual runs still go to Blacksmith, which has an SDK, so they kept passing (for example the 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-23 dispatches). Scheduled runs failed from 11-14 to 11-23; the one green scheduled run on 11-17 happened while the Boat backend was not selected.

## Change

- Replace the bare `setup-java` step with the repository's `setup-android-toolchain` action. That action already installs the pinned Java and Android SDK for the Android Store Release job on `boat-xlarge`.
- Run Gradle with the toolchain's pinned Gradle Java (`gradle-java-home`), the same way the `android` CI lane does.
- Add a guard test: the toolchain step must come before the CodeQL build, and the build must use the pinned Gradle Java. It fails on `main` and passes with this change.

## Evidence

- `ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` (Android CodeQL cases): 12 passed. The new case fails on the base.
- Manual dispatch of this workflow on the branch (Blacksmith runner, new toolchain step): https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45323653484 succeeded through Build and Analyze.
- PR CI on 086bf631: green.

CI can schedule a runtime build for tests that were filtered out. It can also schedule the transcript reconciliation lifecycle suite without the compiled worker the suite launches.

prs.title: fix(tests): stop recovery and output checks racing lazy UI loads
prs.body:
Closes #204312

## What Problem This Solves

PR CI intermittently fails the login recovery and inline command-output tests while their real UI modules are still loading. The assertions start a one-second DOM poll before the lazy import finishes, so a slower cold import reports missing recovery text or stdout even though the component has not loaded yet.

Related failure evidence: [login recovery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45072487555/job/137362837106) and [inline stdout](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45089601050/job/137416552128).

## User Impact

No user-visible product change. Developers get tests that wait for the actual module-loading boundary before checking the existing recovery and output behavior. No retries, longer timeouts, weaker assertions, or production workaround are added.

## Why This Change Was Made

Await dynamic-import completion after requesting the recovery toast. Move the existing expanded-output import wait ahead of the stdout assertion instead of after it. The immediate no-reload check, warning/action checks, output checks, composer-preservation checks, and rendering budgets remain intact.

Simplification: two test files, two added lines and one removed line (net +1); zero production lines, helpers, or permanent fault-injection machinery.

## Evidence

Both exact reported assertions were reproduced on unchanged source by holding the REAL lazy module's Vite transform for 1,500 ms. Each failed **3/3** without the fix and passed **5/5** with it under the same conditions. Removing the fixes after the passing runs restored both failures twice. This is controlled cold-import scheduling proof, not a replay of the original full CI shard or an estimate of the natural flake rate.

- Login recovery: unchanged failure at line 315, undefined/string assertion; fixed full-file runs passed all 24 cases each.
- Inline output: unchanged failure at line 212, expected undefined to be 'First stdout line.'; fixed browser runs passed.
- Stock UI config, changed files plus login-gate-refresh and chat-tool-expanded-lazy siblings: **49/49 passed**; 9.13s Vitest / 10.96s wrapper. Hosted checks on c272bb292055b5c0adc37599b9488d74f2d76490 are now green, including all three UI shards, UI E2E, and openclaw/ci-gate; 27 passed, 47 skipped/neutral.
- Production UI typecheck plus canonical UI components/chat test typecheck leaves: passed. Targeted oxlint, formatting, and diff check: passed.
- Auto Review, OpenClaw engine, effective model openai/gpt-6.2-sol, local candidate against ba2046d48e1784b79121a3de358534df73622760: **scoped-clean at default P0 coverage**, no findings. Not a P0–P3 review; the reviewer did not independently rerun tests. The committed patch is identical to the reviewed candidate.

<details>
<summary>Controlled reproduction and remaining investigation gaps</summary>

Use the existing UI config with this temporary plugin appended to every inline project's plugins:

```ts
{
  name: "ci-flake-delay-lazy-view",
```

prs.title: fix: read GitHub previews with the connected GitHub CLI account
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the Gateway's GitHub CLI login is the shared agent account, **Settings → Profile → GitHub accounts** shows it as Verified for every agent's dashboard data. But GitHub link previews, the side reader, and `github_read`/`github_search` skipped that login and read anonymously. Anonymous reads share GitHub's 60 requests per hour per IP, so after a few previews every PR failed with "GitHub API rate limit exceeded (HTTP 403)", even though a working account was already connected.

## User Impact

GitHub previews and the reader now use the same account Settings shows for the agent, including a shared account that is the Gateway's GitHub CLI login. Nobody has to connect the same account a second time just for reading. An explicit `gateway.controlUi.github.token` still takes precedence, and managed accounts behave as before. When there is no CLI login, or it cannot be verified, reads fall back to anonymous access as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reader already shares identity preparation with the rest of the Gateway's GitHub reads, but it called it only for OpenClaw-managed accounts. Without a managed account, it now also prepares the detected GitHub CLI login through the same owner, with its existing 60-second token cache and per-request selection checks.

The change keeps the existing fallbacks:

- `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` and an explicit `gateway.controlUi.github.token` keep their existing path, including the anonymous retry when GitHub rejects or rate-limits the token.
- The CLI login is used only when the Gateway's periodic GitHub CLI sample (about every 60 seconds) reports a configured login, so hosts with no login do not start `gh` on every read.
- A rejected or rate-limited CLI login retries public reads anonymously, like environment tokens. If the login cannot be prepared, reads stay anonymous as before. A failure of a managed account still surfaces as an error.

## Evidence

- **Real Gateway, same request as the user:** in an isolated Gateway on the base, `controlUi.githubDetail` for a public PR used up the anonymous quota and then returned `GitHub API rate limit exceeded (HTTP 403)`. On this head, reader requests for two public PRs succeeded through the host's `gh` login, and the anonymous quota stayed at 20 before and after.
- **Regression tests:** five `shared GitHub CLI account` cases in `control-ui.test.ts`. The CLI-login preview, detail, and rate-limited anonymous retry fail on `main`. The rate-limited retry, signed-out no-probe, and `GH_TOKEN`-path cases failed on this PR's first head and pass now.
- The affected Gateway suites (`control-ui`, `tools-github`, `control-ui.github-preview-refresh`, 74 tests) pass. `tsgo:core`, lint, and format pass. Local autoreview of the final change found no P0–P2 issues.
- Gap: the signed-out and environment-token paths are proven with unit tests at the request handler, not with a live signed-out host.

prs.title: fix: recognize valid Git plugin installation provenance
prs.body:
Closes #204324

## What Problem This Solves

Installing a plugin from Git at a full commit SHA succeeds, but inspection and the loader incorrectly report `provenance-invalid` even when the saved source information agrees. This produces a misleading warning that OpenClaw cannot verify where the plugin came from.

## User Impact

Valid Git installations are reported as `third-party-git` instead of invalid provenance. Pinning a commit does not grant official-plugin privileges or hook agent-turn authority. Conflicting metadata and unrelated installation paths still produce diagnostics; no configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared classifier handled official and third-party npm installations but lacked a Git case. It now checks the recorded spec, URL, ref, and full resolved commit, including equality for a full-SHA pin.

Git parsing lives in a small dependency-leaf module shared directly by installation, source planning, and metadata inspection. It does not depend on bundled-source discovery or installation orchestration. The old parser exports are removed, all consumers use one parser, and parser behavior, installed-content verification, and authority checks are preserved. No cycle suppressions or dependency configuration changes are used. The trusted PR wrapper inventory also includes the parser so extracted tooling retains this runtime dependency.

## Evidence

### Real CLI before and after

Fresh public-CLI runs compare main at `766f6157f4d36e7338df8cd7f6934a711bfb1f4b` with this PR head `949eab8910242300b707b7e477ea2c1b6c2ddbd2`. Both complete source trees were verified against those revisions, then rebuilt through supported project commands (main: `pnpm build:runtime`; PR head: `OPENCLAW_BUILD_CACHE=0 pnpm build`). Runtime input fingerprints matched the selected source before the CLI runs.

Both runs used the same dependency-free, no-op local Git fixture, pinned to the full commit below, in separate temporary OpenClaw home/config/state directories. No existing Gateway or user state was used. Node 24.20.0, pnpm 12.15.0, and the pinned Bun 1.4.4 CLI runtime were used. These are real CLI commands, not calls to an install helper.

```sh
pnpm openclaw plugins install "git:file://<FIXTURE_SOURCE>#9229999c6612b90aa0515bdf1ec0944600df0234" --force --accept-capabilities
pnpm openclaw plugins inspect git-provenance-cli-fixture --runtime --json
```

Both install and inspect exited **0 on each revision**. `<FIXTURE_SOURCE>` and `<STATE>` replace temporary filesystem paths only. The pin and generic plugin ID are actual values.

**Install stdout, identical on main and PR head (complete, path-redacted):**

```text
WARNING - Installing plugin from Git repository: git:file://<FIXTURE_SOURCE>#9229999c6612b90aa0515bdf1ec0944600df0234
This source is outside ClawHub review and trust metadata. Only continue if you trust the publisher, package contents, and install source.
Cloning <FIXTURE_SOURCE>...
Installing plugin dependencies with npm…
Installed plugin: git-provenance-cli-fixture
Saved for the next Gateway start.
```

The normal warning that a Git source is outside ClawHub review remains on both revisions. It is separate from the incorrect invalid-provenance diagnostic.

**Before: main `766f6157f4d36e7338df8cd7f6934a711bfb1f4b`. Selected fields from the actual inspect stdout JSON:**

```json
{

      "message": "OpenClaw can't verify where this plugin came from. Review it with 'openclaw plugins inspect git-provenance-cli-fixture'. Adding it to plugins.allow lets it load, but does not make it trusted. If it's an official plugin, reinstall it from its official npm package or its official ClawHub listing to enable trusted features. reason=provenance-invalid; registryPath=\"<STATE>/state/openclaw.sqlite\"; origin=\"global\"; installSource=\"git\"; installSpec=\"git:file://<FIXTURE_SOURCE>#9229999c6612b90aa0515bdf1ec0944600df0234\"."
    }
  ],
  "install": {
    "source": "git",
    "spec": "git:file://<FIXTURE_SOURCE>#9229999c6612b90aa0515bdf1ec0944600df0234",
    "gitRef": "9229999c6612b90aa0515bdf1ec0944600df0234",

```

**After: PR head `949eab8910242300b707b7e477ea2c1b6c2ddbd2`. Selected fields from the actual inspect stdout JSON:**
