prs.title: feat(agents): keep idle prompt caches warm with read-only prewarms
prs.body:
## Problem

When an interactive session with a large prompt goes idle past the provider's prompt-cache lifetime, the user's next turn rewrites the whole prompt at the cache-write price (1.25× or 2× input) instead of reading it (0.05–0.1× input). On dashboard sessions with a 30-minute OpenAI cache and a ~280k prompt, people return after p50 60 min / p90 140 min, so most returns pay that rewrite. A 12-hour cache costs more, because every write doubles.

## Fix

Shortly before a known cache lifetime ends, the Gateway sends one read-only **prewarm** of the session's own next request. It reads the cached prefix, which restarts the lifetime, and generates nothing.

- **Request form** (`StreamOptions.cachePrewarm`):
  - Anthropic Messages: `max_tokens: 0` without streaming. The trailing placeholder item gets no cache checkpoint, and the empty `max_tokens` reply settles as an ordinary `stop`.
  - OpenAI Responses: `prompt_cache_options.prewarm: true`, keeping the lifetime the session already sends.
  - The request is refused before sending when it would change the cached prefix: Anthropic budget thinking, a forced tool, or structured output.
- **Who sends it:** a tool-free session fork (`runSessionFork` with `cachePrewarm`). It reuses the session's pinned system prompt and tools, history, cache key and thinking level, and it keeps the session's `tool_choice` instead of forcing `none`. It runs detached: nothing is written to the transcript, it never dispatches to a CLI backend and never compacts. It refuses to send without the session's pinned prompt or while a run is live. Its usage is the fork's internal `model.usage` diagnostic.
- **Which routes:** decided by capability, never by provider ID.
  - Anthropic-style routes use the cache-write tier their own responses reported (5m or 1h). This also covers a proxy that forces 1h on a 5m request.
  - OpenAI Responses on the native API uses the documented 30-minute lifetime (GPT-5.6+), or the requested `30m`.
  - No pings for unknown or no lifetimes (ChatGPT sign-in, xAI, Gemini, Chat Completions, local models), or for 12h, where a read does not restart the clock.
- **Which sessions:**
  - Interactive only: a person started the turn that made the last request. Cron runs, subagents and ACP sessions are excluded.
  - Prompt at least 50k tokens.
  - The last reply is settled on the session's current route, with no compaction, reset or model change after it.
- **Timing:** the cron maintenance loop gains a third deadline. Transcript changes note a candidate in memory, and the row and transcript are read only when the earliest ping could be due. Ping k is due one lead (`clamp(TTL/10, 60 s, 120 s)`) before the lifetime of the previous request ends. A late wake, checked again just before the request is sent, sends nothing.
- **Stop rules:**
  - Budget `floor((write − read) / (2 × read))` in route prices (at most 24, or 3 when unpriced), so the pings never cost more than half of one rewrite.
  - Ends 12 hours after the last human interaction.
  - Stops on a miss (read 0, wrote more than it read, or read under half the prompt).
  - An error pauses that provider for 15 minutes.
  - A user message cancels the in-flight fork and re-anchors the schedule.
- **Durable state:** one additive optional session-row field, `promptCacheKeepWarm { anchorEntryId, provider, model, lastPingAt, pings }`. It is JSON in the entry, with no column and no schema-version bump, and readers accept its absence. It lets a series resume after a Gateway restart, and it moves the cache-TTL pruning clock (`readLastCacheTtlTimestamp`), so a prewarmed cache is not pruned as expired on the next turn. Forks pass their source's record. Readers use it only when the reply it warmed is in the transcript they read and the route matches; no session ids are compared.
- **Config:** on by default; `agents.defaults.promptCacheKeepWarm: false` turns it off. Docs: Prompt caching → Idle keep-warm.

## User impact

An idle interactive session on a route with a known cache lifetime keeps its cache warm, so the next turn reads the prompt instead of rewriting it. Each prewarm costs about one cache read of the prompt and no output. Nothing changes in the transcript or the UI. Routes without a known lifetime behave as before.

## Evidence

### Paid probes (raw HTTP, ~91k-token prefix; ping at lifetime − margin, follow-up after the lifetime)

| Route | Ping read / write / output | Follow-up with ping | Control (no ping) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anthropic API 5m (Sonnet 5.5, adaptive thinking) | 91,437 / 0 / 0 at 4.5 min | read 91,437 at 6.5 min | read 0, wrote 91,338 |
| Anthropic API 1h | 91,573 / 0 / 0 at 55 min | read 91,573 at 62 min | read 0, wrote 91,186 |
| Claude proxy (requests 5m, writes 1h) | 91,745 / 9 / 0 at 55 min | read 91,745 at 62 min | read 0, wrote 91,637 |
| OpenAI API 30m (gpt-6.1-sol) | 56,958 / 14 / 0 at 28 min | read 56,958 at 33 min | read 0, wrote 56,769 |

OpenAI also accepts `prewarm` on a streamed request (read 56,918 / write 14 / output 0).

### Isolated Gateway, base (`9a39176f4d7e`) vs head, dist builds, Anthropic API 5m

Rerun on the final head (820599411fb7) gave the same result: ping 1 after the restart at 21:33:12, ping 2 resumed from the row at +4m01s after a mid-series restart (both read 70,808 / write 33 / output 0), and the user message read 70,808.

One session with a ~70.7k-token prompt; the user message comes 8 minutes after the last turn.

| | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| Restart 1 min after the turn | — | ping 1 at T+4m02s from the transcript: read 70,708 / write 33 / output 0 |
| Restart 30 s after ping 1 | — | ping 2 at ping 1 + 4m03s, resumed from the row: read 70,708 / write 33 / output 0 |
| User message at T+8m | read 1,591, **wrote 69,184** | **read 70,708**, wrote 112 |

User message during a ping (two runs, Anthropic 5m): the user's request started 84 ms after ping 2 in one run and 40 ms before it in the other. Both pings completed (read 70,666 / 70,696, output 0), and both user requests read the warm prefix (70,666 / 70,696). The user turns took 5.8 s and 5.1 s end to end, CLI start included, so the user did not wait. The next prewarm re-anchored to the new reply 4 minutes later (read 70,778 / 70,808).

Longer cache lifetimes, base vs head (dist builds, one session each):

| Route | Head prewarm | User message | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OpenAI API 30m (gpt-6.1-sol, ~64k prompt) | T+28m01s: read 64,017 / write 80 / output 0 | T+33m | read 0, **wrote 64,141** | **read 64,017**, wrote 131 |
| Claude proxy, 5m requested, proxy writes 1h (~71k prompt) | T+58m04s, tier observed from usage: read 71,203 / write 113 / output 0 | T+62m | read 0, **wrote 71,074** | **read 71,203**, wrote 192 |

OAuth routes:
- **ChatGPT sign-in:** no lifetime is documented, so no ping. Observed: no model request in the 7 minutes after the turns.
- **Claude setup-token:** not run. The subscription is rate-limited for 4 days (429).
- **GitHub Copilot:** not run. Its token is a write-only secret-store reference that cannot be copied into a scratch Gateway.
- **Gemini:** not run. The OAuth token was expired, and copying it would need a refresh that rotates the live token. Gemini runs on the CLI runtime, which gets no pings by design.
- **xAI:** not run. Under 2 h of access-token life was left. No lifetime is documented, so no pings.

Live Gateway pid and live config hashes were unchanged after every run; scratch states and credential copies were deleted.

Tests:
- Anthropic prewarm request equals the normal request except `max_tokens`, `stream` and the trailing item's checkpoint; the reply is an empty `stop`; budget thinking is refused before sending.
- OpenAI documented lifetimes and the prewarm flag.
- Fork keeps `tool_choice`.
- Cache-TTL clock with the row record.
- Stored-record rules: resume, budget kept across automation turns and renewed on human turns, other route ignored; the cache-TTL clock ignores a record whose reply is not in the transcript.
- Tier observation and ski-rental budget.
- Cron maintenance wakes keep-warm after start and after an interactive transcript change, never for a cron run.
- `agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts` green; `pnpm check:changed` green.

## Decisions recorded

- The stored row field was approved in advance, conditional on a design consult confirming it is needed and correctly shaped; the consult confirmed it. Its proposed `sessionId` was dropped: the session-identity ratchet forbids comparing session ids, and the reply entry id plus the human-turn rule already identify the transcript.
- Default on, one opt-out key. The core config budget rises by one (2670 → 2671 after merging `main`).
- The 50k minimum prompt, the 12-hour cap and the 15-minute provider pause are conservative defaults chosen from the replay data, not tuned values.
- Ping usage is filed under the fork's internal session, as every session fork's is, not in the session's transcript cost.
- Edge cases accepted without extra code:
  - A user turn that starts while a ping is in flight: the fork cancels on the transcript change, and a request already sent may still bill one read.
  - Two Gateways on one store: last writer wins.

Related: [Lobster Packs #160093](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/160093) is a separate proposal, not implemented here.

## What Problem This Solves

Lobster visitors, the collection, Memory artwork, and tab icons are built into the Control UI. Operators cannot turn them off together. Moving them behind the private plugin catalog would instead hide the visitors from people who can open the UI but cannot read that catalog.

## User Impact

Lobsterdex is on by default. Disabling it removes the visitors and collection without erasing discoveries, dates, familiarity, visit and sound preferences, or the chosen tab icon. Re-enabling it restores them without replacing the current draft. The 52-card collection keeps saved links and main’s mobile alignment; it does not restore per-card Copy link buttons.

## Why This Change Was Made

One bundled plugin owns the collection and visitor rendering. The Gateway confirms enablement without disclosing private catalog data or granting Gateway access to the renderer. Once the app has cached its assets, a fresh offline tab uses only that Gateway’s last confirmed decision. An unknown decision waits.

## Evidence

All 14 affected Chromium scenarios passed. The packaged UI with a real Gateway verified a sessions-only reader, a saved Taylor Pinch link, fresh offline opens after enable and disable, and the same draft and textarea through live changes. The phone layout passed at both 100% and 140% text as a second tab recorded the tenth visit.

prs.title: fix(release): reuse child evidence across release tooling changes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Full Release Validation discarded already-executed child results when qualification tooling (Q) changed and the old and new workload trees were not equivalent. That could require rerunning sealed work after a tooling fix, even with the same release candidate and inputs.

## Solution

Remove the cross-Q workload tree comparison and its orchestration-path exception. Keep selection and exact inputs, authenticated producer lineage, live run/attempt, artifact identity and digest, receipt authentication, candidate descriptor binding, and reevaluation under current Q waivers. Reuse retains the original producer Q; whole-parent reuse and publication artifact rules are unchanged.

## Impact

Release operators can reuse eligible sealed child results after a Q change. The accepted tradeoff is that changes to child workflows or test harnesses no longer force fresh execution: operators set `reuse_evidence=false` when they need the new harness to run. Reused receipts attest to execution at the original Q, not the new one.

## Evidence

- The cross-Q regression failed on the base at the old Git-tree read and passed with the fix. It also rejects diverged lineage and receipt digest mismatches. Candidate identity, exact inputs, and current-Q waiver reevaluation remain covered.
- 417 tests passed across eight focused suites after rerunning the execution-plan suite with its obsolete tree-rejection assertion removed. Targeted lint and formatting, scripts and tooling-test type checks, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Author simplification pass: one evidence verifier remains. Production scripts: +2/−175; tests: +46/−302 against the base, removing workload-tree scaffolding while retaining authenticated-evidence checks.

## Worked on by

- @vincentkoc
- @RomneyDa

prs.body:
Related to #203271, #197510, #204134, and #204336.

## What Problem This Solves

Two test fixtures fail main CI before they can verify their intended behavior. The worker placement fixture omits the now-required model selection, and the node-host fixture can cancel a child before the parent finishes process admission. Supplying the model also exposed stale failed-recovery expectations left behind when explicit recovery policy moved to request entry.

## User Impact

Main CI can verify destination preparation, pending-result settlement, failed-placement recovery, and real POSIX signal diagnostics. Both changes are test-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The destination fixture declares a synthetic model and still throws if a model turn is attempted. Failed-placement recovery now checks that a policy-denied request preserves the failed placement and blocks a Gateway worktree and local turn. A second request after lifting the policy restores the accepted checkpoint.

The cancellation fixture uses guarded stdin EOF as its parent-side admission signal. The child installs its SIGTERM handler before sending readiness after EOF, so the test still requires a real SIGKILL diagnostic.

## Evidence

- Linux arm64 OrbStack with the repository-pinned Bun fork. Two plain baseline runs failed all three destination cases with the missing-model diagnostic. The repaired file passed all three. [Original CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45315132500/job/138180908159)
- The same 150 ms delay after the real Linux PID stat read reproduced stdout `ready` with a null diagnostic twice on the baseline. Both delayed runs passed after the repair, and the full node-host file passed 16 cases with two platform skips. [Original CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45315132500/job/138180908141)
- macOS with pinned Bun passed all three destination cases and all 15 applicable node-host cases. The model-only replay isolated the old failed-recovery assertion before the admission fixture was corrected. Full-file macOS wall time was 50.67 s for destination authority and 32.72 s for node-host.
- Codex autoreview of the full two-file patch against `a21974cdddd19` found zero actionable findings through P2. Production LOC delta is zero.

prs.title: fix(cron): re-prepare script runtimes when the plugin inventory changes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An existing script automation kept reporting `ReferenceError` for a plugin tool after online enablement, although a new automation could call it in the same Gateway. Restarting the Gateway restored the old job (#199478).

## User Impact

Existing automations can use newly enabled plugin tools on their next invocation without a Gateway restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cron preparation now includes the existing active plugin registry version in its cache identity. Registry publication invalidates an unchanged job even when its previous registry was retained. Gateway-owned cron runs read the current Gateway config, not the startup config, before preparing plugin tools; standalone cron retains its existing config fallback. The duplicate registry-version export and its mocked call-count test were removed in favor of a real plugin-loading regression.

## Evidence

An isolated Gateway with a synthetic plugin was started once; the same disabled script job was run before and after `plugins.setEnabled`. The following is terminal output from `pnpm exec tsx .artifacts/199492-gateway-proof.mts`, selecting only the status, error, and returned marker fields from its CLI/RPC JSON records (identifiers and local paths omitted):

```json
{"step":"BEFORE","status":"error","error":"cron script payload failed (internal_error): ReferenceError: inventory_probe is not defined"}
{"step":"INVOKE","ok":true,"details":{"marker":"plugin-online-ok"}}
{"step":"AFTER","status":"ok","completionStatus":"succeeded"}
{"step":"NEW JOB","status":"ok","completionStatus":"succeeded"}
{"step":"JOB","lastRunStatus":"ok","triggerState":{"marker":"plugin-online-ok"}}
```

`BEFORE` and `AFTER` are the same pre-existing job. `JOB` is the stored state of that job; its `triggerState` contains the actual plugin tool return marker, beyond the completion status. `NEW JOB` is a separate job created after enablement. This proof uses no live account or external model.

The committed real plugin-loading regression also checks a registry-only publication with an unchanged config object, followed by live config publication with the updated plugin generation. Focused cron suites: 37/37 passed. Core TypeScript, changed-file oxlint and oxfmt, line-cap ratchet, test-line budget, and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh review identified and resolved a registry-only invalidation proof gap before this push.

No config migration or user action is required.

prs.body:
Closes #204271

## What Problem This Solves

The desktop chat microphone starts a voice conversation on a click, when people expect it to dictate text. Dictation instead requires a hold, and a saved preference can disable that gesture entirely.

## User Impact

Click the idle microphone to dictate into the unsent draft; hold it for about half a second to start Talk. The old **Hold to dictate** setting is removed and its saved value is ignored. Mobile web keeps its separate controls, and New Session and Side chat remain dictation-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing gesture owner now routes clicks to dictation and holds to Talk without submitting the existing draft. A waveform and progress ring identify the pending Talk action. **Start Talk** in the microphone menu supplies a keyboard-accessible route without another composer button.

Talk waits for pending dictation to finish so late transcripts stay in the draft. Unavailable Talk keeps its configuration guidance open.

## Evidence

Real Control UI browser checks verify click/hold dispatch, release-click suppression, draft preservation, cancellation, microphone-menu behavior, and the mobile/direct-dictation siblings. The captures use a synthetic conversation/Gateway and Chromium synthetic microphone devices; the complete composer controls remain visible in every crop.

**A live microphone and provider audio were not tested.** The requester explicitly accepted the browser gesture proof for this PR; the transcription and Talk audio implementations are unchanged. The issue records the requester's separate live-provider reproduction of the original behavior.

- Focused dictation, direct-dictation and microphone-menu checks: 76 passed after the review fixes; other affected composer/action/picker checks also passed.
- Browser Talk regressions: 20 passed across five suites. Dictation, pending-transcript preservation, unavailable-Talk guidance and composer-layout browser checks passed after correcting old gesture expectations.
- Saved-preference regression and settings checks passed, including ignoring an old saved false value. Chromium settings/Appearance checks: 27 passed.
- UI typecheck, changed-file lint, CSS lint, capture-script lint, English copy verification, formatting and UI ownership guards passed.

prs.title: fix(codex): keep Model Setup probes out of chat history
prs.body:
Root cause: packages/session-url-contract/src/session-key.ts:8 the incognito key pattern lists only `dashboard`, `subagent` and `internal-session-effects`, so the Model Setup check key `agent:<id>:setup-inference:incognito-…` (src/system-agent/setup-inference-turn.ts:90) is treated as a normal session and the Codex harness leaves `ephemeral` off its `thread/start` (extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-requests.ts:252).

## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw shares its Codex home with Codex Desktop or the CLI, a tool-free Model Setup probe can appear in chat history. If a user reopens that thread and asks it to run a command, the probe's saved instructions can still cause a tool refusal.

## User Impact

New Model Setup probes use temporary Codex threads and stay out of saved chat history. Normal chats still save their Codex threads.

## Why This Change Was Made

Model Setup creates keys in the `setup-inference:incognito-…` namespace. Add that namespace to the shared incognito key classifier so the existing Codex `thread/start` logic sends `ephemeral: true`. The setup turn still runs with `disableTools: true`. Ordinary keys in the same namespace stay non-incognito; Model Setup is the only producer of `setup-inference` keys.

Doctor side effect: each check's audit rows (`agent.run.started`/`finished`) carry its session key. With this change, `openclaw doctor` reports those rows as keys in the reserved incognito namespace, and `openclaw doctor --fix` rewrites their `session_key` to a `legacy-incognito-` key. That applies to rows from earlier checks and from new ones. Control UI incognito chats already get the same Doctor finding today. This PR is on hold until Doctor's reserved-key repair skips `audit_events`.

The regression test covers a probe-shaped key and an ordinary key in the same namespace.

## Evidence

Isolated Gateway run with the real bundled Codex app-server and a local ChatGPT backend: on `main` the Model Setup check starts a saved Codex thread (`ephemeral` unset, one rollout, listed by Codex `thread/list`). On this head it sends `ephemeral: true`, writes no rollout, Codex lists no thread, and the check still succeeds. A normal chat afterwards still saves one thread. Output and Codex source references: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/199452#issuecomment-7026472339

Focused test `src/shared/incognito-session-key.test.ts`: the setup-check key case fails on the merge base and all 10 cases pass on this head.

Thanks @pimalaispaphuket-debug for the fix.

Merge danger: two-way door for the Codex thread behavior; reverting restores saved probe threads, and no config or schema changes. Not fully reversible for audit history: after this change, `openclaw doctor --fix` rewrites the session key on Model Setup check audit rows, and a revert does not restore those rows. Blast radius: Model Setup checks on the Codex runtime, Doctor runs on installs that have run a check, and the other incognito-key consumers, which now treat these probe-only keys as incognito.

prs.title: feat: let plugins finalize streamed speech without provider-specific code
prs.body:
Closes #187368

## What Problem This Solves

Voice-integration plugins need to upload audio during capture, then end input and obtain a complete transcript without implementing each speech provider's WebSocket protocol.

## User Impact

Plugins can use optional `api.runtime.mediaUnderstanding.transcribeAudioStream` through the existing typed plugin runtime, with ElevenLabs Scribe v2 Realtime as the first adapter. Existing continuous sessions keep synchronous `sendAudio` and their close/VAD behavior. Older hosts without the optional runtime method retain batch behavior.

Streaming requires an explicitly selected supported model and format. Omitted models, CLI selections, and unsupported batch-only profile/request/header/prompt/provider options return unsupported **before input is consumed**. Once admitted, failure throws instead of automatically replaying audio or changing provider. This does not make every existing batch provider realtime-capable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing session exposes callbacks and close, but no end-of-input acknowledgment covering every accepted sample. Add awaited finite writes/finalization, and let the runtime reuse media selection, policy, credentials, secret admission, and configured limits. The finite helper owns bounded completion/cancellation; ElevenLabs owns framing and acknowledged manual commits.

The consumer no longer imports a private-local SDK facade: the new operation is declared on the already-published `OpenClawPluginApi.runtime.mediaUnderstanding` type and lazily bound by the host. The private-local transcription/provider helpers remain private and official-provider-only. No new public subpath, package export, or blanket promotion of private SDK internals is introduced. Registered-plugin projection preserves optional absence and applies the existing selected plugin scope/revocation guard.

**SDK-owner decision requested before merge:** accept this optional extension of the existing typed runtime capability. This PR proposes that direction; neither the linked issue nor source review is represented as upstream owner approval.

## Evidence

### Branch refresh — 2026-11-16

Current head: `e1f81d130eaa93d960a237ffc0d1d1a4dbeb0f6f`, incorporating upstream main `ec025eba2df15ab949239fa17dfd99ac4286b50c` to resolve merge conflicts. The finite-input contract and no-replay-after-admission behavior remain unchanged.

The refresh follows upstream's split provider-context types and `PluginCapabilityCatalogHostContext`, preserves lazy saved-key lookup on both continuous and finite connections, and carries the upstream caller-authority callback through finite completion. Existing tests now cover direct/saved credentials and revoked caller authority before final commit. Upstream proxy, reconnect, backpressure and continuous-session behavior remain intact. No new retry loop, dependency or public SDK subpath was added.

Source review found no actionable defect; exact-file formatting and diff whitespace checks passed. The current test-line budget passed: +1468 test LF, 400-line allowance, 1068 allocation credit (reduced from the old record). The added growth protects progressive input, acknowledged completion, cancellation and live ownership at separate boundaries; no unrelated test allowance changed.

Fresh executable validation is **pending**, not passing. The local lint attempt could not initialize because this checkout lacks `eslint-plugin-solid`; this is an incomplete-tooling result, not a code verdict. No local full dependency installation, test/typecheck run, paid provider call, deployment or restart occurred. [Current-head GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43930692011) is `action_required`, waiting for upstream approval to run. Please approve the run; no test pass is claimed. Current test wall time and CI seconds are not yet available.

SDK-owner acceptance of the optional runtime contract remains required before merge. All proof below belongs to the explicitly named earlier revisions; it does not establish a pass for this refreshed head.

<details>
<summary>Historical evidence and review context — prior heads only</summary>

### Branch refresh — 2026-11-03

The only textual conflict was adjacent import additions in `src/realtime-transcription/websocket-session.ts`. The resolution retains both `createNodeProxyAgent` from merged proxy fix #187369 and the finite-runtime `getPluginRuntimeGatewayRequestScope` import. Main's environment-proxy routing and provider-shutdown queued-audio cleanup (#191761), and this PR's finite lifecycle and final-effect ownership checks, are preserved. The feature diff remains 28 files, +2347/-38 against the incorporated main.

Executable validation for this refreshed head is owned by [GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41663533787). The run completed **failure**: all 108 scheduled jobs finished, with **76 passed, 28 skipped and 4 failed**. ### Stronger process-boundary proof — executed on this head

The new `test/e2e/qa-lab/media/finite-transcription.e2e.test.ts` replaces the duplicate mocked happy-path test with a real Gateway process. [Exact-head build and execution job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40886048121/job/123490837973) **passed**:

### Executed lifecycle and transport proof on `351cad743` (unchanged production code)

prs.body:
Closes #189041

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes speech integrations losing structured provider failure details when TTS returns a failed synthesis attempt.

## User Impact

Callers can inspect optional HTTP status, provider/transport error code, WebSocket close code and retry delay without parsing human-readable messages. Existing messages, provider selection, fallback and retry policies are unchanged. No configuration migration or new dependency.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider HTTP owner already creates structured errors, but the shared TTS attempt projection drops those fields. Preserve a bounded subset on the existing result contract and document it. Numeric fields are range-checked; codes must be bounded machine tokens. No response bodies/headers are copied, no message parsing or nested-cause flattening is added, and ordinary logging is unchanged. Metadata is not a guarantee that retry is safe.

## Evidence

### Branch refresh — 2026-11-16

Current head: `25aee5199a37a3d0f0cd0e845fc0936be61a7374`, incorporating upstream main `ec025eba2df15ab949239fa17dfd99ac4286b50c` to resolve a real modify/delete conflict.

Closes #204323

## What Problem This Solves

First-run setup mentions verifying an API key or token even when the selected provider supports only browser and device-code sign-in. The introduction describes a credential that the dialog does not offer.

## User Impact

Users signing in with an account now see method-neutral setup instructions. Available connection methods and model-selection behavior are unchanged; no migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared introduction now says: “Choose how to connect. Setup can also verify and select a model for this agent.” One generic browser regression covers the sign-in-only provider, absence of an API-key control, and the browser sign-in request. The existing first-run picker assertion uses the same updated copy.

## Evidence

The regression fails on the old API-key wording and passes with the change. All eight provider-login browser tests passed against the completed production build (10.93 seconds wall time; CI timing not yet available). Before/after captures use the real Control UI built with `pnpm ui:build`, served through the production-build preview contract, with identical synthetic Example Cloud Gateway data, Chromium 156, a 1280×900 viewport, and light theme. All 77 fetched JavaScript assets in each capture were byte-compared with `dist/control-ui`; no DOM edits or source-dev serving were used.

Both baseline and candidate UI builds passed. Focused format, lint, UI E2E typecheck, keyless i18n verification, and `git diff --check` passed. The i18n baseline generator produced no tracked changes.

Author simplification reviewed the complete change against `29bc3e3ee37076e9aa256c83ca5f9e02c609fd9a`: the shared copy owner remains unchanged, with no added production branching or state. Production delta: +1/−1 line; test delta: +80/−3 lines. Auto Review covered the same complete local delta at its default P0 scope and reported no findings; this is not a broader-priority review.

Limitations: real provider authentication, translated copy, and other browsers were not tested. The ordinary test harness's nested build hit a process-resource error and then a native runtime abort; the same unchanged test file was run through the repository test runner using the completed production assets instead. An early run overlapped atomic build publication and still served baseline assets; its new wording assertions failed, and one existing account-picker case timed out. The bounded replay after build completion passed all eight cases, without a code or test workaround. Both builds also reported the same nonfatal CSS/chat-boot size-budget warnings.

prs.title: fix: session lookup rejects a database created during discovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes session entry lookup failing with “SQLite database path identity changed” when the agent's first database is created during ordinary discovery.

Related: #197510, #199862.

## User Impact

Session lookup can read the first-created database without rejecting a stale observation that the path was absent. Retained mutation plans and artifact-preserving inspection keep their existing identity checks. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker lookup introduced in #197510 captured a database-path identity even for an ordinary read. A legitimate first creation between preparation and reading then invalidated that captured absence. Use the existing `captureIdentity: false` option only for ordinary, non-retained, non-inspection discovery; the reader still owns physical-source custody.

Production growth is one line selecting the existing mode at the common lookup owner. The regression extends the existing real first-creation interleaving test to entry lookup; no new production seam, retry, or timeout.

## Evidence

- The new entry regression fails on the base with the exact absence-identity error. Restoring only the pre-#197510 worker module makes it pass, establishing the introducing change. With the fix, nine selected tests pass under both Node and Bun, including retained-plan refusal, revoked custody, retargeted locators, and inspection behavior.
- The original provider-reload real-Gateway case passes under Node (11.004 s) and Bun (10.083 s). Its unchanged-base local replays also passed, so this does not uniquely identify the failed CI RPC; the deterministic owner regression supplies causal proof.
- Browser history passes (1/1); the real-Gateway browser flow creates and reopens an empty persistent child (1/1, 4.582 s), with no agent run or chat.send. Canonical UI build succeeds.
- `pnpm check:changed --base 6aae38f36ee8152c2294fb52f9b91bb174e146e3 --timed`: all typechecks, storage audits, format, lint, and remaining guards pass; the full-tree export scan fails only on the separate rollback test-support export `resolveRollbackWorkerInputs`. That export regression was introduced by #198268 and is being repaired separately in #199897. Production and script export scans report zero entries.
- Independent Codex review: no actionable findings through P2.
- Existing synthetic 35 GiB database / 5,000-session / 62,000-file measurements apply to the byte-identical shared qualification owner and the same capture-mode operations. On btrfs, per-operation median wall time was 15.132 → 8.150 µs, CPU 20.279 → 12.786 µs, sampled JavaScript allocation 15,985 → 10,950 bytes. A/A ranges were 1.94%, 11.94%, and 0.15%. These measure qualification, not end-to-end entry lookup; btrfs used a loop image over ext4.

A separate Bun xAI case still reports `SESSION_MUTATION_AUTHORIZATION_CHANGED` on the base. Its pending-registration cause has not been correlated to the current failed request, and its introducing commit remains unknown. This change does not claim to repair it or treat it as an inherited-CI exception.

prs.title: fix(ci): bound agent owner PR selection to same-directory importers and a declared behavior set
prs.body:
## Result

PR CI for agent, compaction, prompt and transport owners goes from a full-suite plan back to a bounded one, about 13x smaller. It still selects the four tests that #204252 was about.

| Replay (PR planner, hybrid, 130-row cap) | Before (#204292) | After |
|---|---|---|
| #204111 (31 files) | 12,562 tests / 131 jobs / 36,859 s | **967 tests / 21 jobs / 2,881 s** (max job 271 s) |
| #204180 (9 files) | 12,405 / 131 / 36,673 s | **302 / 14 / 1,393 s** (max job 250 s) |

Both replays select `embedded-agent-runner.prompt-cache.test.ts`, `agent-runner-required-maintenance.pending-input.test.ts`, `agent-runner-compaction-fallback.test.ts` and `session-context-accounting.gateway.integration.test.ts`.

## Change

For a changed source file under `src/agents/`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner*`, `packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/` or `packages/ai/src/transports/`, the aggressive PR plan now selects:

1. the normal two-import walk, as for every other file;
2. every transitive importer test **in the changed file's own directory**. A file directly in a package root (for example `src/agents/compaction.ts`) skips this step, because that directory is the whole package (1,795 tests for `src/agents/`);
3. a **declared behavior set**: every `*prompt-cache*` and `*compaction*` test under `src/` and `packages/` (118 files), plus `agent-runner-required-maintenance.pending-input.test.ts` and `session-context-accounting.gateway.integration.test.ts`.

A test-only edit under these owners runs itself and does not pull in the declared set.

Full mode (manual and hourly) is unchanged and still walks every importer.

## Decision recorded

The follow-up asked for "importers within the same package". With the package root as the scope, #204111 selects 2,424 tests / 7,519 s, which misses the target of about 1,200 tests / 3,700 s. I used the changed file's directory instead, which meets the target. Coverage given up: cross-directory transitive importers, outside the declared set, of a file under these owners. The hourly full plan still runs them. This is reversible: widening the scope is a one-line change.

| Variant | #204111 | #204180 |
|---|---|---|
| Declared set only | 369 / 1,888 s | 135 / 1,035 s |
| **Same directory + declared (this PR)** | **967 / 2,881 s** | **302 / 1,393 s** |
| Same package root + declared | 2,424 / 7,519 s | 308 / 1,393 s |
| #204292 (unbounded) | 12,562 / 36,859 s | 12,405 / 36,673 s |

## Evidence

- `ci-changed-node-test-plan.integration.test.ts`: for 7 owners from #204111 and #204180, the plan selects the four named tests and every same-directory importer test.
- `ci-changed-node-test-plan.selection.test.ts`: the fixture case again expects the two-import stop for a distant consumer in another directory (the pre-#204292 expectation).
- Planner, project and workflow tests (11 files): 1,322 passed. `pnpm check:changed`: pass.

**PERFORMANCE HOLD — not ready for review.** Exact-head CI and ClawSweeper passed, but [two newer fully drained traces](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202894#issuecomment-7116725613) model this change adding **83s and 12s** to total FRV versus the landed 64-slot baseline. Those replays supersede the earlier disposition and gate status below. No hosted post-change savings were measured.

## Problem and smallest repair

Unconditional priority also produced modeled regressions at smaller capacities. #202688 merged as `877dd67f20347872f494d3b0af2c8ae4781cbdc2` on November 23; this branch includes that exact merge and preserves its 64/32 capacity decision.

- Evaluate the existing capacity decision exactly once in the planning step's internal `MAX_PARALLEL`, export `max_parallel`, and consume it via `fromJSON` in matrix admission.
- Parse capacity with the existing positive-integer owner, default32. Only64 prioritizes `acpx-openclaw-tools-bridge`, after `plugin-update` and before `legacy-operator-state`; otherwise it remains unprioritized.
- Preserve complete rows, baseline/scenario identities, timeouts, independent failures/retries, fresh containers, capacity selection and stable remainder order. No new user configuration/input, timing planner, release/version exception, cache, jobs or allocation.

This extends #198925 and #199911 while preserving recovery-first ordering. Self-simplification retained one capacity owner and removed the consumer-side expression. Against integrated main: five files; production/workflow +15/-3, tests +69/-52 (mostly indentation; whitespace-insensitive +23/-6), docs +6/-0.

prs.title: fix(ci): keep bundled npm retries within their deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A stalled npm download while packing bundled plugin dependencies can make Docker seed validation miss its existing three-minute attempt limit. In one fully drained release-validation run, that wait held up the entire run even though the next install attempt completed promptly.

## User Impact

On Linux, the bundled-plugin installer can retry once the existing deadline expires instead of waiting for npm to finish a blocked download. No installed-product behavior or validation coverage changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use a hard termination signal only when the existing Linux npm ci attempt reaches its timeout. Node's synchronous subprocess runner otherwise waits for npm to finish handling SIGTERM. Keep the same command, 180s deadline, retry count, partial-staging cleanup and error handling. Keep non-Linux behavior unchanged. A hard-killed timed-out attempt may not finish writing its own debug log; the timeout and attempt index still report. The package install already disables lifecycle scripts and the existing cleanup discards the timed-out attempt's partial dependency tree before another attempt. No timeout reduction, other-packager policy change or new runner allocation.

## Evidence

- [Fully drained FRV 45268128383](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45268128383): [Docker seed job 138025096695](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45269228243/job/138025096695) ran 83m31s. The registry phase ran 28m53s, including a 28m05s outer gap before the first Codex bundled dependency install logged SIGTERM. It reported a timeout and packed on retry 2.67s later. The rotated npm diagnostic is absent; this does not establish the upstream cause or attribute every second to SIGTERM. The parent was not a passing release qualification.
- **Whole-FRV upper bound: 7m03s on that trace**, not 28 minutes. Normal CI sealed at 22:49:26 UTC; the independent candidate child sealed at 22:42:23. Faster npm cannot move the parent past that next barrier. This is a trace-derived ceiling, not a measured improvement or a claim about healthy installs.
- **Real npm 11.20.0 loopback proof:** controlled 3s tarball stall, 700ms deadline. Five interleaved baseline attempts 3,127–3,140ms vs 704–707ms with the proposed signal; ETIMEDOUT in both. With the production helper patched, a two-attempt run completed in 832ms vs 3,324ms on base: same locked tarball integrity, one partial-tree cleanup, exact dependency installed, status 0. This does not rely on changing registry retry settings in production.
- Existing retry regression goes red on base and checks the bounded Linux attempt alongside normal failures and exhausted-retry cleanup. No new production owner, fixture dependency or test suite. Hosted full-FRV A/B not run.
- Focused manifest, npm runner and consuming registry-artifact suites: **86 passed**. The baseline also failed an endpoint teardown assertion when this host proxied loopback; with `NO_PROXY` restricted to local fixture endpoints, all assertions passed without test edits or exceptions. Type-aware lint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed. Local tooling typecheck returned byte-identical failures on the base and patch because the host dependency store has `@openclaw/fs-safe` 0.27.1 versus the pinned 0.28.2. Exact-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper remain pending.

prs.title: feat: preview cross-thread messages with sender descriptions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An incoming message from another chat shows only a generic update count until you open it. That hides the sender’s context and makes the receiving conversation harder to scan.

## User Impact

Cross-thread messages appear in a native left-aligned bubble with a link to the source conversation. The optional sender description flows as one paragraph and wraps to the available width. Long previews fade at the bottom. **Show more** opens the card to the full incoming column and reveals the original; **Show less** sits below the whole message and restores the compact preview. Without a description, the original message is shown directly.

## Why This Change Was Made

The optional `sessions_send.description` accepts up to 280 characters and stays separate from the message. Each entry keeps its own timestamp, disclosure, reply, and copy actions. Passive notifications and automation messages behave as before.

## Evidence

A real model sent a migration receipt on an isolated Gateway with the rebuilt Control UI. The sender description wraps naturally as one paragraph. The original still has two paragraphs, and **Show less** follows the last one in visual and keyboard order. The native expanded width, left avatar, and source link are unchanged.

### Clean comparison

Before — hard line breaks split the preview, and Show less appears above the original.

![Before: hard-broken preview and Show less above the original](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/240b3de7-ffff-4bca-bee1-45622c2ecada)

After — the description flows naturally, and Show less appears after the complete original.

![After: a flowing preview and Show less at the bottom](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f9d80f2b-f0f4-47d1-a851-2d2f3f7e1a3d)

### Annotated comparison

Before

![Before annotated: description and original separated by the control](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac3809e3-b355-4d6f-a79f-3fa900e4a186)

After

![After annotated: paragraph description and control at the bottom](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/21e4d26f-e5de-4dcc-891c-15fb30af3ee8)

Matched synthetic receipts at 1280 × 800 in dark mode. Baseline: `14cc0da5dce1`. After: `5a1b4b2404da`, whose tree matches this PR head. Mobile light mode was also checked.

### Current preview and Show less demo

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/39f01816-b4b4-4957-b5ef-133a70284748

Focused checks passed: 23 send-admission, 16 prompt-prefix, 58 renderer/attribution, and four bundled Chromium cases. Desktop and mobile cases cover Tab into the original, bottom collapse with later transcript content, legacy line breaks, search, and automation. Runtime and UI builds, targeted typechecks, lint, styles, and formatting passed. Keyboard expansion focuses the original before its links (the outline in the capture is the native focus ring). A tap that does not focus its button leaves platform focus unchanged; native iOS WebKit was not exercised. No broad CI pass is claimed.

Earlier feature proof: [original update count](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3dd3e794-e7cc-4983-8c6f-0849e72ba12b), [annotated original update count](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b990d6e2-c216-4371-b8af-a0a6bf805663), and [full-width behavior before this revision](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d69a5b5-9711-4110-abb6-19e8112f1506).

## Contributor credit

Co-authored with [@Patrick-Erichsen](https://github.com/Patrick-Erichsen).

prs.title: fix: make Daybreak one toggle that follows the chat's model
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Each OpenAI model supports exactly one Daybreak program: mainline models (GPT-6.2 Sol and similar) take Daybreak Blue or Standard, while cyber models (GPT-6 Cyber, GPT-5.6 Cyber) take Daybreak Red only. The chat speed menu still offered a Blue/Red chooser, so GPT-6 Cyber showed "Blue (unavailable)" next to "Red", which reads as if access were missing. Worse, a chat that turned on Blue with GPT-6.2 Sol kept `daybreak_blue` after switching to GPT-6 Cyber. Every send then failed with "This Daybreak program is not advertised… Select Standard", and Standard cannot run a cyber model either. New chats on an unconfigured cyber model also started at Standard.

## User Impact

Daybreak is one on/off toggle per chat. The model decides Blue or Red and the toggle shows it as a caption. Cyber models show the toggle locked on with "Required by this model". Switching models carries Daybreak along, so Blue becomes Red on a cyber model (and back to Blue on a mainline model) in the same update as the model change. A chat that already stores the wrong program shows the toggle off, and turning it on repairs it in place. Runtime errors now name what the model supports and the next step.

Behavior note: choosing a cyber model turns Daybreak on, and it stays on (as Blue) when the chat switches back to a mainline model. It is visible there and can be turned off.

## Why This Change Was Made

- One UI resolver (`ui/src/lib/chat/daybreak-access-program.ts`) derives the program, locked state, checked state, and model-switch remap from the model's advertised `availableAccessPrograms.cyber`. Chat controls, chat model switches, and new-session drafts all use it.
- The chat model switch sends `model` and the remapped `cyberAccessProgram` in one `sessions.patch` (also through native-runtime recovery). New-session drafts submit the model's required program.
- The remembered Blue/Red preference (`daybreakAccessProgram`) is removed; legacy stored drafts and preferences still decode and drop the field. It was never part of the Gateway protocol.
- The embedded runner and the Codex harness error text names the supported programs and says "Turn on Daybreak for this chat to use Daybreak Red" (or "Turn Daybreak off" when the model has no Daybreak program). Codes, failover reasons, and control flow are unchanged.

Out of scope, named on purpose: sessions created outside the Control UI on an unconfigured cyber model still get the server's `standard` default (`resolveModelCyberAccessProgramDefault`) and fail until `params.accessPrograms.cyber` is configured; that runtime default is a separate follow-up. A remap that an operator role ceiling rejects fails the model switch; restricted roles get Standard only, so this is not reachable with default roles.

## Evidence

Synthetic Control UI E2E fixtures (mocked Gateway, synthetic models and chat), dark theme, 1440×900, speed popover open. Before = `main` at 34c8570c297ab, after = this branch.

### Clean comparison

GPT-6 Cyber chat that still stores Daybreak Blue (the reported failure):

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Daybreak chooser on GPT-6 Cyber lists Blue (unavailable) and Red](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3020c7fd-a1f4-4bf2-8454-6d752e5a8467) | ![After: single Daybreak toggle shown off with the hint Required by this model](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/085df0b2-eae0-45d6-8ae6-36fdb77ff4cd) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Blue/Red chooser outlined; saved Blue shows as unavailable](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/828a0122-02a2-43fd-832f-e988e2ed09aa) | ![Single Daybreak toggle outlined; stale Blue shows off and turning it on saves Red](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f133f4f7-a4ca-49e6-8516-f14370e7877d) |

### Other states

| State | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GPT-6.2 Sol, Daybreak on | ![Before: toggle on with a Blue option row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec219510-1a4d-468a-96d3-5435254aa26c) | ![After: toggle on with caption Blue](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0c1f2ab0-031e-4120-94f8-352d27843c90) |
| GPT-6 Cyber, Red saved | ![Before: toggle on with a Red option row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/70ef9faa-f3b6-4a9b-be40-4fa6a889df7e) | ![After: toggle locked on with caption Red](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f60ba3c-643b-4030-ab85-6c3e0100e46e) |
| GPT-6.2 Sol, Daybreak off | ![Before: toggle off](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/120be126-4fa1-4c41-91a3-33d37276a8c8) | ![After: toggle off](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a102ea45-40ad-4096-a62e-7915f6426e07) |

Behavior proof:

- `ui/src/e2e/chat-daybreak-controls.e2e.test.ts` (4 cases): mainline toggle writes `daybreak_blue`; cyber model renders locked Red; switching GPT-6.2 Sol (Blue) → GPT-6 Cyber through the model picker sends one `sessions.patch` with `model` and `cyberAccessProgram: "daybreak_red"` (this case fails on `main`: the patch carried only the model); a stale Blue on GPT-6 Cyber renders unchecked and turning it on sends `daybreak_red`, after which it is locked with caption "Red" (fails on `main`).
- `ui/src/e2e/chat-daybreak.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` (3 cases) passed against a built, isolated Gateway with synthetic provider I/O.
- Resolver, model-preferences, new-session model-control/preferences, draft codec, settings materialization and effort-picker browser tests pass (Chromium and WebKit for the picker).
- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/access-program.test.ts` and `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.native-config.test.ts` cover the new error guidance.
- `pnpm tsgo:prod`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, oxlint and format on touched files, stylelint on `composer.css`, `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline`/`verify` (no baseline drift), `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` (net −170 test lines), `git diff --check`.
- Local review: autoreview (Codex engine), local change snapshot on base 34c8570c297ab, P0 threshold: scoped-clean, no findings.

Review follow-up (head 245be295):

- ClawSweeper P2: a new draft on a Red-only model displayed the catalog default (Standard) while submission normalized to Red. Drafts now render `accessProgramForSubmission()`, the same value they submit, so the toggle shows locked Red before sending. The restored test `commits the displayed first-use Access as daybreak_red` failed before this fix and passes now. Existing chats keep the separate stale-program repair.
- Stored data compatibility: `ui/src/lib/chat/composer-draft-store-codec.test.ts` loads an IndexedDB draft that still carries the retired `daybreakAccessProgram`, keeping `cyberAccessProgram` and dropping the old field. `ui/src/pages/new-session/preferences.test.ts` does the same for authenticated new-session preferences. No Gateway protocol, config, or server-side state changed, so there is no Doctor or upgrade migration.

CI notes (head 3598443c):

- Chat boot JS budget: the model-switch remap and stale-program repair add +451 B gzip to chat boot (1,334,559 → 1,335,010 B vs the paired base). `chatBootJsGzipBytes` is raised by exactly that measured cost plus 64 B headroom, with a provenance comment in `scripts/check-control-ui-performance.mts`. New-session boot grew +151 B and stays within its limit.
- Fixed a test-only type import (`CyberAccessProgram` now comes from the gateway-protocol schema module) that broke `check-test-types-core-2`.
- Not caused by this PR: with this PR's runtime and Codex changes reverted to base, the same five `extensions/codex` app-server tests (host credential execution, compaction model policy, parent continuation) still fail locally. `test/vitest-projects-config.test.ts` failed because `src/shared/session-unread.test.ts` (from #204281) had two owners; main fixed that in #204316, so head 1a3e659a merges current main and the test passes locally (42/42). `boot-module-boundaries`, `session-catalog-backoff`, and `signed-call-boundary` pass locally. The gateway e2e shards that failed don't involve the touched code, and main's hourly full CI is red across similar shards.

Live context: the reported failure reproduced on a real Gateway (GPT-6.2 Sol with Blue → GPT-6 Cyber); this PR's flow was verified with mocked/isolated Gateways, not yet on that deployment.

Release note context: Control UI: Daybreak is now a single per-chat toggle; the model picks Blue or Red, cyber models show it locked on, and model switches carry Daybreak over instead of failing with an unavailable-program error.

prs.title: fix(ci): drop an unselected whole group's timeout from selected Node jobs
prs.body:
## Result

A selected (PR) Node job no longer inherits the 120-minute whole-config timeout from a group it does not run. `test/scripts/ci-changed-node-test-plan.test.ts` "retains precise process ownership and independent timing keys (github)" passes again.

## Cause

`createSelectedNodeTestShardBundles` projects each job of a subset compact plan onto the selected files, and copies the job's fields with `...shard`. When that subset job also held a whole-config group (no `includePatterns`), it carried `COMPACT_WHOLE_NODE_TEST_TIMEOUT_MINUTES` (120). The projection drops the unselected whole group but kept its 120-minute timeout. So an exact-file job could run with twice its canonical owner's deadline.

It is latent and depends on packing. #204178 (`cded11f81d55`) added a test to `databaseWorkerCoreTestFiles`, which changed the subset packing for the GitHub profile. After that, `agentic-agents-embedded-base-3` (canonical owner timeout 60) shared a subset job with the whole `agentic-agents-embedded-run` group and got 120. A planner replay of the test's two targets shows it: at `dae98a63` (parent) the selected job has timeout 60; at `cded11f8` it has 120. The canonical owner jobs are the same at both commits. #204292 did not change this path: `main` fails the same way before and after it.

## Fix

The projection keeps the whole-config timeout only when a retained group is still a whole group (`!includePatterns`). Every other timeout, such as the long-unfitted 90 minutes or a cron minimum, is copied as before.

## Evidence

- Planner replay (GitHub profile, the test's two embedded targets): before, `checks-node-changed-compact-large-35` has `timeoutMinutes: 120`; after, no override (60 default). The single-file `embedded-run` job no longer gets 120 either, which matches its canonical owner, since its whole group is not selected.
- `test/scripts/ci-changed-node-test-plan*.test.ts`, `ci-node-test-plan.test.ts`, `ci-workflow-planning.test.ts`: 11 files, 1,285 tests pass on the head. The named case fails on `main` (`expected 120 to be less than or equal to 60`), the same as scheduled run 45288712101 (small-18).

prs.title: fix(telegram): keep numbers on ordered lists in rich messages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With `channels.telegram.richMessages: true`, numbered lists in agent replies can arrive as bullets. The author saw this twice in a Telegram group. A numbered list nested inside a bullet loses its numbers too, and an HTML list starting at 3 is sent as though it started at 1.

## User Impact

Ordered items keep their numbers in Telegram rich messages, including nested Markdown items and HTML lists with an explicit start. Bullet lists, task-list checkboxes, plain-text fallback, and the legacy non-rich sender are unchanged. No configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram selects a list marker **per item**, not per list. A numeric `value` alone does not request a number; the [Bot API](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#inputrichblocklistitem) also needs `type: "1"` for a decimal label. The Markdown and HTML builders now supply both fields for ordered items. The HTML builder honors a non-negative `<ol start>` when every resulting label fits Telegram’s signed 32-bit integer field. Otherwise, the list starts at 1. Alphabetic and Roman styles are out of scope.

## Evidence

The receiver on Telegram’s Test Server reported these labels. The **before** message came through the unpatched Gateway. The **after** message replayed the exact `sendRichMessage` payload captured from the corrected, registered HTTP adapter; it was not a live run of the patched Gateway.

| Items in the same message | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parent bullet | `•` | `•` |
| Nested Markdown ordered items | `•`, `•` | `1.`, `2.` |
| HTML `<ol start="3">` items | `•`, `•` | `3.`, `4.` |

The [HTTP regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/25b2348fd55f5cf38f36f5914e9afa0dc79bd5c5/extensions/telegram/src/outbound-adapter.telegram-http.test.ts#L170) failed on the PR parent `86fcb81e64c0`: the nested items lacked decimal types and the HTML values were 1 and 2. On [the corrected head `25b2348fd55f`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204343/commits/25b2348fd55f5cf38f36f5914e9afa0dc79bd5c5), all 154 focused tests passed across four files. The [two-item boundary tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/25b2348fd55f5cf38f36f5914e9afa0dc79bd5c5/extensions/telegram/src/rich-blocks-html.test.ts#L129-L130) verify that a start of `2147483646` retains `2147483646, 2147483647`; a start of `2147483647` would overflow, so the list falls back to `1, 2`.

prs.title: fix(github): keep named updates on the original pull request
prs.body:
Related: #204293, #204300.

## What Problem This Solves

When an agent tries to publish a fix to an existing PR, an ordinary publish from an unrelated checkout can create a second PR. Until now, an agent couldn’t tell the publisher to update the named PR or leave the work unpublished.

## User Impact

Fixing CI and publishing again from the same checkout stays one step, even if the agent includes the PR URL. A workspace prepared for that PR also works. If the PR is closed or the checkout can’t be matched to it, OpenClaw keeps the work and does not push to a different target or open a replacement. New PRs and ordinary publishes without a URL are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The URL is a target assertion, not permission to import or update any PR. OpenClaw checks the workspace’s prepared PR or its existing publication record, then uses the same publishing path. The accepted request’s existing idempotency digest retains the target across recovery. No new settings, storage schema, or permission changes.

## Evidence

- The named CI follow-up regression failed before the fix when the publisher rejected `workspacePath` with a PR URL. Seven focused real-Git Gateway cases passed with synthetic GitHub transport, including both checkout paths, refusal without writes for a closed named PR, and recovery of the named update after restart. The ordinary no-URL path still opens or reuses a PR as before. No live update was attempted against the incident PRs.
- The CI follow-up removed a redundant session ID comparison; the receipt reader already verifies session ownership, and the checkout ID and branch checks remain. Five focused Gateway regressions, core typecheck, formatting, and the local ratchet passed after the change. The [hosted ratchet also passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45312232532/job/138171600724) on the corrected head.
- [CI on `23d61a2`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45312232532) remains red. All 15 failing test shards were accounted for: 29 end-to-end failures reproduced in targeted runs on the exact [unmodified main parent, `7cbf158`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7cbf1585ed737dd0b42fb28ea82082dc851ed4e3), and 10 other test failures matched test names and error signatures across [scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45305041178) and [the earlier scheduled main run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45299031361). The [required gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45312232532/job/138191193217) is still red: it did not map the differently named PR and main shards. No bypass or rerun was requested.

prs.title: fix(gateway): keep workspace Git imports off the main thread
prs.body:
Related: #204217

## What Problem This Solves

When the Gateway imports a cloud workspace snapshot, Git receives an open file as stdin. That path used to launch Git from the Gateway event loop, where Linux can block other Gateway work while the child starts under I/O pressure.

## User Impact

Workspace staging and pack imports use the existing spawn broker when available, keeping the child-launch handshake off the Gateway event loop. File-backed media probes use the same input path. There are no configuration or migration steps.

## Why This Change Was Made

The caller pins the regular file and hands the broker its absolute path and exact device and inode. The broker opens it with no-follow and nonblocking flags, verifies the opened file, and passes that same descriptor to the child. A swap fails with a typed error. The caller keeps the inode pinned through broker admission, including during cancellation.

The SDK still supports numeric descriptors for pipes and shared offsets, including the public media helpers. Git staging and recovery already prepare their files inside private temporary directories. Application source grows by 90 lines across the callers and the process owner, plus one line in the trusted PR wrapper's source inventory. The shared process code adds identity capture, verification and cancellation handling. Callers shed per-command descriptor setup and cleanup.

## Evidence

The workspace regression on the exact main parent reported one staging launch as `native.descriptor`. The candidate records one `broker` launch and preserves the staged bytes and refs. The real broker rejects both a replacement inode and a symlink to the original inode with `ERR_COMMAND_STDIN_FILE`.

The existing `scripts/perf/workspace-reconcile-spawn-measure.ts` runs real workspace staging and recovery. The synthetic Linux fixture contains 62,000 files, 1.14 GB on btrfs, 620 changed files, a 7 GiB parent and concurrent random writes with fio. The acceptance check requires equal output fingerprints, zero candidate main-thread fast-import launches, and lower synchronous child-launch blocking. A/A controls measure host noise. Main-thread spawn measurement uses a separate instrumented run.

Warm staging, median / p95 across 16 observations per arm in the eight-pair controlled repeat:

| Metric | A/A baseline control | Before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Owner wall time, ms | 869 / 1,075 → 942 / 1,413 | 886 / 1,110 → 806 / 964 |
| Main-thread CPU, ms | 55.86 / 67.97 → 61.48 / 75.56 | 65.28 / 82.25 → 21.71 / 36.08 |
| Process-tree CPU, ms | 897 / 1,120 → 971 / 1,204 | 929 / 1,161 → 831 / 1,033 |
| Parent V8 allocation, MB | 2.29 / 4.10 → 2.29 / 5.02 | 2.18 / 4.17 → 1.81 / 3.24 |
| Peak event-loop delay, ms | 57.64 / 68.03 → 62.32 / 80.61 | 73.17 / 84.74 → 5.49 / 15.43 |

The repeat measured **75.91 / 87.21 ms → zero** synchronous main-thread blocking per warm staging fast-import. Staging launch counts shifted from one native and one broker launch to two broker launches, with identical output fingerprints. The first run measured 62.10 / 64.50 ms → zero. The initial empty-patch wall p95 increased from 82 to 221 ms in one candidate observation with higher reaped-child CPU. The controlled repeat measured 142 → 50 ms and retained every observation.

All 99 applicable focused process tests passed under Node, including both file-swap cases. The 71 Gateway tests and 15 update tests passed. Both playback close-error tests passed after fixing the fixture spy, completing focused media coverage. Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings. The full worker-environment suite passed 3,791 tests across 333 files. `pnpm check:changed` passed against the pinned main parent. Control UI browser tests passed 14/14, and the real-Gateway worker setup E2E passed.

The first CI run exposed three destination-authority E2E failures with `No model is configured`. The identical three cases failed on the clean exact main parent `29bc3e3ee3707` and the first head. The parent reproduced under both Node and Bun. The fixture configures a workspace without a model. #203271 removed the implicit model and added the placement error. The fixture and failure site are unchanged by this PR.

[Exact-head CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45310871178/job/138166708563)

The first CI run also found that the new helper was missing from the trusted PR wrapper's extraction inventory. A follow-up commit adds that entry. Both failed wrapper closure tests passed locally under Bun after the fix.

[Wrapper closure CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45310871178/job/138166708567)

ClawSweeper caught the shipped numeric stdin option on the public media helpers. Both helpers now forward it through the same shared command runner. The two new compatibility cases failed before that repair and passed with it. The focused media and process rerun passed 71 tests, including the broker file-swap cases.

The final CI run also exposed a cancellation fixture race from #197510. The child can print its readiness marker before Linux process-identity admission completes. Under a controlled delay of the actual process-identity read, the unchanged test reproduced the same missing SIGKILL diagnostic on both the exact CI main parent and the tested merge. This byte-input invocation takes the existing early-cancellation branch.

The exact final CI run contained these two failed shards and their downstream CI gate failure. The security-fast check passed. The pinned main and candidate both reproduced the destination-authority failures, and the unchanged node-host fixture reproduced the second failure under the same controlled delay. Local qualification and the final-head ClawSweeper review passed.

[Final CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45315132500) · [Cancellation shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45315132500/job/138180908141) · [Final ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204336#issuecomment-7120447073)

prs.title: fix: keep a goal advancing after a background command's completion turn
prs.body:
Closes #204319

## What Problem This Solves

An active Goal stops advancing after a background command's completion turn. It resumes only after the next user message. At the end of the first turn, post-turn session maintenance queues a native task in the session mailbox. When the completion turn ends, the Goal check counts that task as queued work and defers to it. A maintenance task never evaluates the Goal, so nothing continues it.

## User Impact

User impact: a Goal keeps advancing on its own after a background command's completion turn, without a new message.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Goal check defers to queued work because that work's turn continues the Goal when it ends. Only a reply turn does that. `hasSessionControllerQueuedTurn` (in the session controller, next to `hasSessionControllerQueuedWork`) counts bound reply sources and reserved sources still preparing, and leaves out a bare native task: one with a claim request but no reply source. Goal continuation uses it. Other callers (lifecycle drain, idle sweeps, yield sweep, cron cleanup) still count all queued work.

## Evidence

- New unit case in `goal-continuation.test.ts`: with post-turn upkeep queued, the Goal continues; with a reserved reply source queued, it still defers. On `main`'s implementation the upkeep assertion fails (`expected false to be true`); with the fix, the file passes (83/83).
- Real Gateway, scratch port and state, real model (gpt-5.5): a Goal whose first turn starts a background command. On `main` the transcript ends after the completion turn and no Advance runs. With this change the transcript reads: Goal request → `Exec completed …` → `[System] Advance the active goal …`.

prs.title: feat(templates): sign in to ClawHub from a private draft
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Trying to review a private Template draft while signed out of ClawHub led to a `clawhub login` error. **Retry review** repeated it. Creators had to leave the conversation and sign in on the Gateway host.

## User Impact

The card starts with **Sign in to ClawHub**. Select **Sign in** to request a code without leaving the conversation. The code replaces the subtitle and the same button becomes **Copy & open ClawHub**. Select it, paste the code into ClawHub, and approve. Review resumes on the original unpublished draft. A blocked clipboard or popup offers manual recovery; cancellation or expiry leaves the draft private. **Preview** shows the files without publishing. Only **Publish** uploads the draft.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway binds the pending approval to the original person, registry, conversation and draft. It stores the verified credential in the existing private SQLite identity store for that person and registry; another administrator cannot borrow the host account. The card displays the short approval code, never the device credential or API token.

## Evidence

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c1c0ce8-c4bd-423d-a12e-f38f633f2e46

[13.36-second before/after recording](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202013#issuecomment-7028869474). Before, ClawHub opened with an empty field and no code on the clipboard. After, the first click stays on the draft; the second copies the code and opens one approval tab. A keyboard paste fills the field. Approval opens exactly one review of the original unpublished draft. Opening and closing Preview sends neither chat nor a publish request. The card and button kept their dimensions and positions at 400, 820, 1280 and 1440 px.

The recording shows tree `715f2b57bf28`. It uses Chromium, a rebuilt Control UI and Gateway, the [pinned ClawHub approval component](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/blob/63a48631a855dfda27254b4a767962ca7a4ece8b/src/routes/cli/device.tsx), and a local fixture account and authorization backend—not a production sign-in. On later tree `c8956918ccff`, sign-in and review screenshots were pixel-identical and all four layout measurements matched.

### Current integration

Published head `00d3ea4671b9` has the exact tree tested locally: `4058941b50ae101355873333dac6b0f346a5f9b5`. It includes `main` through `34c8570c297a`: the [prerequisite](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202715), the [WebKit paging repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204216#issuecomment-7113545506), the [ready-only review card](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202786), the [submission-view link](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202791), the [screen-routing test repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204257), and the [attachment filename test repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204288). The feature still changes the same 40 paths against `main`.

- **Upgrade from the latest stable release.** The stable-to-candidate test was [rerun from shipped `v2026.11.7` against this exact commit](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202013#issuecomment-7118119926), after [the same run on the previous head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202013#issuecomment-7116903626). The existing owner login and private draft remained byte-identical and mode `0600`, and the stable-written team secret still matched. The new personal credential survived restart and stayed isolated from the other person, another registry and another registry path on the same host. Seven Gateway processes exited cleanly; zero publication requests. This was an application-state upgrade with loopback registries in a sandbox that blocks all other outbound network, not a production sign-in or installer certification.
- A full build of this exact commit completed for that test. Its local Control UI size report listed budget overages, as it did on the previous head, where the hosted `control-ui-performance` check passed.
- Hosted CI on the two previous heads failed only on tests that this change does not touch, and both are now repaired on `main`. Head `bdb724a67f6a` failed three [screen-routing cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45264188693/job/138007616919) in `ui-command.test.ts` that also failed on `main`. Head `fe6023c47093` failed one [attachment layout case](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45283633614/job/138075135026) in `chat-flow.media-files.e2e.test.ts` whose result depended on whether the CI shard had CJK fonts installed; its Android job failed once on a corrupt emulator download and passed on rerun.
- Neither merge of `main` had textual conflicts. One creator-review expectation needed a one-line repair: the submission-view change hard-coded the pending link for `main`'s fixture, so that case failed here (1 failed, 15 passed) until the expectation was derived from this branch's fixture URL with the same `?view=submission` suffix.
- The generated protocol validator matched the merged schema with no drift. Core and UI typechecks and all six focused Gateway, infra and tooling test files passed, including all 20 `ui-command` cases.
- Both creator test files passed (25 cases), including all 16 creator-review cases with the three sign-in handoff outcomes and the upstream retry case.
- All 15 browser cases in the three affected suites passed with synthetic data on loopback: four history-reading cases (including 390 px WebKit), three Template review cases and eight chat media cases.
- Hosted CI for this head is separate from these local results. The real-Gateway browser recording was not rerun on this tree.

### Earlier integration and upgrade evidence

Published head `b9cb09145eec` had the same tree as locally tested `d7522079bc6c`, including the [iPhone Settings fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202634). On that revision:

- 242 focused tests and 12 bundled Chromium cases passed without retries. One opt-in real-Gateway authority case was skipped. A separate real Gateway + Chromium run exercised the two-click sign-in, clipboard handoff, same-draft review, and Preview/Close with no chat or publication.
- The [stable-to-candidate test](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202013#issuecomment-7046623878) started from shipped `v2026.11.6`. The existing owner login and private draft remained byte-identical and mode `0600`; the original team secret still matched. The new personal credential survived restart and stayed isolated from the other person, another registry and another registry path on the same host. Seven Gateway processes exited cleanly; zero publication requests. This was an application-state upgrade with loopback registries, not a production sign-in or installer certification.
- Core/UI typechecks, protocol generation/drift, formatting, lint, i18n and changed-test-line checks passed. Chat boot measured +1 byte JS and +18 bytes CSS gzip against the landed base; no budgets changed.

Both generated the same 349 declaration files byte-for-byte: 5,394,009 bytes against a 5,385,536-byte limit. No exception or budget change. [Hosted CI for that earlier revision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44792697148).
