prs.title: test(qa): expect empty child completions to settle as parent history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QA Smoke CI (profile 3/6) fails on every `main` run since cded11f8 (#204178): scenario `subagent-empty-completion-recovery` reports `empty completion did not produce exactly one system failure notice`. The last green run was on e2973f93.

## Why

#204178 delivers a child's end state as parent history. A completion turn that consumes the child's result is delivered, whatever it replied, and the missing-reply notice ("No answer was returned. Ask again if you still need one.") was removed. The scenario still required exactly one notice. The failing run's outbound shows only the "Working" card and the parent acknowledgement, which is the new behavior.

## Change (test only)

- Replace the one-notice assertion with the new contract: the parent completion turn consumes the failed child outcome exactly once (one provider request with `[Internal task completion event]`).
- The notice text moves to `forbiddenReplies`, so a returning notice fails the existing leak checks.
- After the Gateway restart: no completion request replays (unchanged); the notice-identity checks are removed.
- The child checks are unchanged: failed terminal outcome, one real write, two tool-free finalizations, no fabricated result.

## Evidence

- Failing scheduled run 45259316971, job "QA Smoke CI (profile 3/6)": outbound = `Working` card + `QA-SUBAGENT-EMPTY-PARENT-ACK`, no notice.
- The scenario YAML parses (45 flow actions). The QA Smoke CI shard on this PR is the run proof.

prs.title: docs: clarify macOS minimum version across app releases
prs.body:
Related: #187770

## What Problem This Solves

In `docs/platforms/macos.md`, `## Requirements` lists macOS 26.2 (Tahoe) or later without scoping it to a release version, while `## Download` right below links directly to pinned `2026.10.3` DMG installers whose tagged release metadata declares macOS 15.0. That paragraph also groups Voice Wake and push-to-talk with the app floor instead of keeping their separate macOS 26+ requirement distinct from `2026.10.3`–`2026.10.9`. Readers on macOS 15–26.1 and macOS 26.2+ cannot tell from the guide which `OpenClaw.app` releases fit their Mac or which features require macOS 26+.

## User Impact

User impact: macOS 15–26.1 and macOS 26.2+ users can now tell at a glance which `OpenClaw.app` releases require macOS 26.2 (`2026.10.10` and later, including `main` builds) versus declare macOS 15.0 (`2026.10.3` through `2026.10.9`), see the separate requirement for Voice Wake and push-to-talk, and reach the CLI and Gateway installer script (`/install#recommended-installer-script`) on older Macs.

This is a reversible, docs-only change to `docs/platforms/macos.md` (`+16/-6`) with no source, deployment-target, default, or public API changes. `https://openclaw.ai/install` is maintained in the separate `openclaw/openclaw.ai` repository and is outside the scope of this PR.

#168595 intentionally raised the native macOS deployment target and guide baseline to macOS 26.2 for `main` and `2026.10.10`+, and #171560 added the per-architecture `2026.10.3` download table without qualifying the version split. This PR retains #171560's pinned `2026.10.3` links instead of hardcoding a newer release because releases ship frequently and not every release includes macOS DMG assets; the existing GitHub Releases link already covers newer `2026.10.10`+ builds, while `## Download` now labels `2026.10.3` as declaring macOS 15.0 and notes `2026.10.9` as the last macOS app release declaring macOS 15.0. prs.title: fix(agents): a member on the global session gets a reply again
prs.body:
## Result

A member who sends on the `global` session gets a reply again. Since #204219, the reply turn could end with `status: error, stopReason: "rpc"` and the message "OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply", and no assistant entry was written. This happened even with `agents.defaults.promptCacheKeepWarm: false`.

## Cause

#204219 added a committed-facts listener in `src/cron/maintenance.ts` that calls `notePromptCacheKeepWarmChange` for every transcript change. That function resolved the agent with `resolveAgentIdFromSessionKey(sessionKey)`. Transcript receipts (`publishCommittedSessionTranscriptReceipts`) name no `agentId`, and for the `global` key that resolver **throws** ("Session key does not contain an agent id").

The listener runs inside committed-fact installation (`sessionChanges.emitBatch` → `publishSqliteCommittedState`). A throw there fails the batch, and the publication's `invalidate()` sends every fact listener a copy of the change with `factsInvalidated: true`. The member turn's retained session-sharing facts (`prepareSessionMutationFacts`, followed by `chat.send`) treat that as a foreign change and invalidate themselves. The next `assertTargetCurrent` then throws `SessionMutationAuthorizationChangedError: session changed before chat.send`, and the run settles as a failure.

The listener is registered whether keep-warm is on or off. That is why the switch did not help.

Trace (runtime probes, removed): run error → `agent-runner-error-handler` `SessionMutationAuthorizationChangedError` → `readCurrent` saw `SessionMutationFactsUnavailableError` → facts `invalidate()` on `{ sessionKey: "global", scope: "transcript", factsInvalidated: true }` → `sqlite-post-commit` `invalidate` ← `publishCommittedSessionTranscriptReceipts`. Calling `notePromptCacheKeepWarmChange` directly with `global` throws.

## Fix

`notePromptCacheKeepWarmChange` returns without a candidate when the change names no agent and the key is not an agent key. It no longer throws inside fact installation. Agent keys (`agent:<id>:…`) and changes that carry `agentId` behave as before.

Accepted edge case: a `global` or legacy-key transcript receipt without an `agentId` does not schedule a keep-warm ping. Before this fix, such a receipt failed the commit instead.

## Evidence

- `src/gateway/server.chat-membership-authority.product.test.ts`: fails on `b36ba3fe` (#204219; the parent `2264fd00` passes), passes on this head. The test starts a real Gateway server on a scratch port with a TLS WebSocket and a trusted-proxy member identity, and sends to a provider HTTP server. A member's `chat.send` and `agent` turns on `global` for both agents now get replies.
- New `src/cron/maintenance-lifecycle.test.ts` case: a `global` transcript change installs once, with no `factsInvalidated` re-delivery. It fails on `b36ba3fe` (3 deliveries) and passes on the head.
- #204219's keep-warm tests still pass: `prompt-cache-keep-warm.test.ts`, `maintenance-lifecycle.test.ts` ("wakes keep-warm … when an interactive session's transcript settles"), `session-fork-request.test.ts`, `cache-ttl.test.ts`, `openai-prompt-cache.test.ts`, `anthropic-transport-stream.prewarm.test.ts`.
- Gap: I did not repeat #204219's paid provider prewarm probes. This change touches only candidate noting for agent-less non-agent keys, and that path never produced a ping.

prs.title: fix(telegram): sibling bot's deleted stream previews corrupt group history
prs.body:
Closes #164958

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in a group running two OpenClaw bots, one bot's streamed reasoning preview (the 🧠 draft) is recorded into the other bot's persistent message cache as an ordinary message. Telegram never delivers message deletions to other bots, so when the streaming side deletes the superseded preview, every sibling cache keeps its copy. From then on, each group turn's history window carries that foreign reasoning text, and Anthropic rejects the whole turn with `reasoning_extraction`. The issue's live capture shows the orphaned preview surviving in cache long after it disappeared from Telegram.

## User Impact

User impact: multi-bot Telegram groups stop breaking on streamed reasoning previews. Once a preview is confirmed deleted, every account's history cache drops it, so later turns no longer inherit dead draft text from a sibling bot. No config change or migration is needed. The fix handles deletions observed after deployment and does not claim to clean up pre-existing orphans.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix tracks previews precisely instead of classifying by content, which is the direction the review discussion on the issue called for. The draft stream is the one component that knows the exact message id of a superseded preview, and it already waits for Telegram to confirm the delete. It now reports that id through a new `onPreviewRetired` callback, and the dispatch layer fans the retirement out to every configured account's message cache, including the sender's own (its cache recorded the preview too). Each cache drops the entry from the live map and the persisted store: retained group history through a compare-and-delete loop, bounded private-chat history through a map delete plus store delete. Nothing keys on message text, prefixes, or usernames, so ordinary bot messages are never misclassified. If Telegram rejects or never confirms the delete, nothing is retired, because the preview may still be visible and its history copies are then still honest.

## Evidence

- New `preview-retirement.test.ts`: two accounts each holding the same preview id in group (retained) and private (bounded) history, fan-out retires it from both and keeps neighboring messages; a single-account config with no `channels.telegram` section still covers the implicit default account.
- New cache tests: `retireMessage` evicts from the live map and the persisted store, a reopened bucket does not resurrect the entry, repeat retirement returns false, non-native ids are rejected, and other chats with the same message id are untouched.
- New draft-stream tests: `onPreviewRetired` fires exactly once after a confirmed supersede delete, and never fires when the delete is rejected or returns unconfirmed.
- Review round 4 follow-ups (head 8e35a3e79d5, rebased onto current main a134038ad7f): retirement fan-out now keys on the Bot API chat type carried from the inbound message instead of the `-100` id prefix, so a basic group whose id was recycled into the supergroup space stays account-local; `record()` and `retireMessage` serialize per cache key through a writer chain shared across all cache instances over the same bucket, so a record in flight while retirement lands from a separate fan-out handle can no longer write the preview back; the persisted tombstone settles before retirement reports done, keeping the fence across restarts. New regression tests cover the recycled-id basic group, channel fan-out, unknown chat type staying local, and both store paths racing retirement mid-write.
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/telegram/src/preview-retirement.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/message-cache.retained.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 24 passed. The same command over `message-cache.test.ts` and `draft-stream.test.ts`: 64 passed. oxfmt and oxlint passed on the five touched files.
- Earlier head `c3677719ea19cfb0f1c7461c70a535153adb4634` had green CI. Current head `3afe346625f` merges current main `e3e615b7115d2b1ee0744f1f40e6819cfe8a6005` without conflicts and allocates the PR's actual 592 added regression lines through the repository's test-lines mechanism. The first 14-line estimate from a sparse local tree was insufficient: authoritative CI still reported 543 lines over, so the allocation was corrected to the full 592 and pushed normally. Hosted CI on this new head is required; the live gap below remains open.

- New cross-instance regression in `message-cache.retained.test.ts`: two cache handles over the same bucket, one recording and one retiring the same key. The retire from the second handle completes its fence and delete before the first handle's compare commits; without the shared writer queue the stale observation resurrects the preview. This test fails on the previous per-instance chains and passes after moving `keyWriteChains` onto the shared bucket.
- New persisted-eviction regression: 3,000 rows are seeded with message 1 and preview 2. Reading message 1 makes it newest in memory, then row 3001 evicts preview 2 from the memory LRU while SQLite evicts message 1 by creation order. Retirement previously returned false and left preview 2 persisted; it now deletes the persisted key independently of memory membership and the reopened cache stays empty. Current verification across `message-cache.test.ts`, `message-cache.retained.test.ts`, `preview-retirement.test.ts`, and `draft-stream.test.ts`: 79 passed. oxfmt and type-aware oxlint pass on the changed files.

- Latest-stable data-model compatibility proof: applied this exact PR diff to the `v2026.11.7` source tree. The unpatched stable tree passed 22 cache tests. It then seeded real SQLite history and settings for two accounts in one process; the patched tree reopened them in a second process, found every old record, retired the group preview for both accounts, preserved ordinary group messages, retired only the origin private-chat preview, and preserved the sibling's account-local private message. A third process confirmed the tombstones and surviving records after reopen. The configuration SHA-256 stayed `d3ab6f395d88ac717c6a4d9980788e97aa81468757df7be3cc4ec0b96c46458e`, and the saved history/settings were unchanged. The same stable-plus-diff tree passed all four focused files: 77 tests. oxfmt and type-aware oxlint both passed.

Gap I want to be explicit about: I could not stage the live two-bot Anthropic reproduction locally, so the end-to-end proof rides on the issue's live capture for the failure side and on the cache/draft-layer tests above for the fix side. The retirement path itself is covered at every layer it touches; a maintainer with two bots can confirm in one group turn by watching the sibling's cache stay empty after the preview is deleted. The latest-stable data-model compatibility gap is addressed by the cross-process proof above; the live two-bot workflow gap remains open.

prs.title: fix(stt): retain realtime provider and connection failure codes
prs.body:
Closes #189042

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes realtime speech consumers losing provider error codes and pre-readiness WebSocket close codes from transcription failures.

## User Impact

Callers receive `errorCode` on ElevenLabs protocol Errors and `closeCode` on pre-readiness socket Errors. Error messages, callback delivery, connection lifecycle and provider-owned reconnection are unchanged. No configuration migration, new dependency or retry policy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve classification at the existing error producers: the ElevenLabs helper retains the explicit code, falling back to the event type; the shared transport retains the numeric close code. No raw payload or close-reason metadata is copied. This is independent of finite-utterance STT work and the separate TTS metadata PR.

## Evidence

### Maintenance check — 2026-11-16

This fix remains needed on upstream main `ec025eba2df15ab949239fa17dfd99ac4286b50c`: the ElevenLabs error producer still omits `errorCode`, and the shared transport still omits the pre-readiness `closeCode`. GitHub reports this PR mergeable without conflicts. The patch remains unchanged at `666c2a5e07828b84ecb39740a2b6d2d7d9a80f53`; no unnecessary base merge or empty commit was added.

The existing exact-head CI and before/after transport proof below are historical evidence, not a new current-base test run. The latest review found no actionable defects and marked this ready for maintainer review. No new runtime validation or deployment is claimed.

**Reviewed head:** `666c2a5e07828b84ecb39740a2b6d2d7d9a80f53`. **Pre-fix production base:** `3f2791e7b620d5023877090e56e265df3f3cfa47`.

- [Exact-head upstream CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41170379928), including selected tests, production/test types, lint and guards.
- [GitHub-hosted standalone runtime proof: PASS](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/41175867415/job/124463178906). A plain Node process calls public `getRealtimeTranscriptionProvider("elevenlabs", cfg)` to cold-load the shipped provider through native discovery/registration, then connects its actual WebSocket transport to a controlled loopback endpoint. No provider factory, registry, parser or transport is mocked or manually seeded.
- Three real transport cases pass before and after: explicit protocol code before readiness, event-type fallback after readiness, and pre-ready close 1011. The base omits the fields; the candidate delivers `rate_limited`, `input_error`, and 1011 respectively. Each case makes exactly one connection and one error callback. Rejected connections expose the identical Error to the callback and `connect()` rejection; no raw close reason is retained.
- The existing selected regressions fail on pre-fix production files at the intended metadata assertions (2 provider cases + 1 close case), then all 3 pass after restoring exact candidate files. No fixture/setup failure is counted as an expected regression.
- Regression command wall time, including compiler preparation: 171.585s before / 160.992s after, entirely on GitHub.
- [Download SHA-verified receipts, JSON test results and terminal traces](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/actions/runs/41175867415/artifacts/13033411725). [Immutable harness](https://github.com/lordratner/openclaw/tree/03ab7fba323c7ad2584b9c52bdba1738bfafbeaf/proof/speech-errors). Earlier harness attempts stopped while interpreting abbreviated/redacted Vitest assertion output; the corrected reader verifies the selected metadata assertion and failure count. No product changes or passing-head substitutions were made to resolve those harness failures.

<details>
<summary>Redacted runtime trace excerpt</summary>


prs.title: fix(release): compare changelogs with the previous shipped release
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Release notes can omit unreleased work when the previous shipped release lives on a divergent branch. The stable workflow rejected that release as a baseline and recommended a reachable main-closeout commit instead; work already on main before closeout could disappear from the next release notes.

## User Impact

Release operators can compare against the actual previous published release without losing pre-closeout beta development or counting proven backports twice. Missing legacy evidence produces warnings and conservatively retains uncertain work; malformed selected or canonical historical provenance, duplicate rows, and unsupported exclusions remain integrity errors. No existing release, tag, asset, or live release notes are changed by this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Stable generation captures public npm `latest` before publication; beta preserves its public npm `beta` selector semantics. Both freeze the resolved tag for replay. Extended-stable uses its own line. Local tag ordering is not publication evidence.
- Keep the shipped tag as the semantic base and traverse `base..target`, including side branches. A merge base is informational, never a substitute for the shipped boundary.
- One shared owner loads cumulative shipped records and canonicalizes evidenced release carriers before subtraction. Exact cherry-pick/forward-port origins and unique author/path-supported matches deduplicate backports; contextual references and title-only similarity do not. Stable inventory ignores unshipped beta drafts.
- Generation freezes canonical main history for deterministic alias replay. Candidate validation, checklist, full-release validation, and existing render/publication consumers use the same inventory/provenance contract. Removed duplicate shipped inventory loaders, redundant candidate provenance parsing, and superseded inventory exports.

### Regression provenance

Raw-parent inspection confirms:

- `f684527085ebeeeff0de13e62decb0c5b1bd4457` (June 17, 2026) introduced merge-base traversal.
- `336e43c31482a6ace6764b018293ce68930bef6c` (July 10, 2026, release pipeline convergence) added the strict ancestor requirement and reachable main-closeout guidance.
- `a94074f6a4987ee27796e572be33b8cd1367fdc3` / #166881 (October 8, 2026 UTC) added a divergent-tag exception only for beta, replacing its base with the merge base while subtracting the shipped record. This is a beta-only contributor, not the direct cause of stable closeout substitution. The legitimate renderer, beta-delta, and attribution improvements are preserved.
- `6dd12ab0eeeea8f7462dd990fbc1bd18961a94c1` added the initial 11.5 record on November 16, 2026 with the incorrect main-closeout base; subsequent refreshes preserved it. GitHub returned no associated PR for this commit or the two older introducing commits above.

The observed 11.5 baseline `90a5029e427822745c59e4f1268db08ade257d5b` is the **10.9 main closeout**, not the 11.4/11.5 merge base. The previous tag `v2026.11.4` peels to `d843d6af39a42cd3c30084edbeabeece732fd93a`; its merge base with code cut `e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff` is `459cad76530457e5c0a32bc21d4982920e9991e7`.

## Evidence

- Before editing, the real verifier rejected `--base v2026.11.4 --target e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff --version 2026.11.5 --source-ref e13cf15ece9bbd969b7362927c315362c90c97ff` at its ancestor guard.
- Six real-Git divergent-history regressions fail on the original verifier at that same guard and pass with the repair. They cover pre-closeout beta work, shipped backports, side ancestry, reversals, missing records, and normal merge carriers. Generation-to-candidate replay rejects missing/forged subtraction provenance.
- End-to-end canonical credit tests cover backports and differently titled release-first forward-ports. These address two findings from independent review.
- Final affected core coverage passes: 209 verifier tests, 127 candidate checklist tests, 10 candidate changelog tests, 15 renderer tests, and 17 ledger tests. The verifier was rerun after fixing an old fixture that paired canonical provenance with a nonexact `HEAD` target; integrity validation was not weakened.
- Broader affected pipeline run: 430 tests across seven files passed, including candidate-owned full-release dispatch and publish-closeout preflight. Later historical-record changes are additionally covered by the final core suites and real baseline read.
- Script and tooling-test typechecks, targeted script/test lint, formatting of all ten changed files, docs MDX sanity, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The final shared owner successfully loaded real `v2026.11.4` against code cut `e13cf15...`. It reported the existing stale legacy total in the 2026.6.9 historical section as a warning, preserving explicit rows instead of introducing a blanket failure.
- Final canonical autoreview (OpenClaw engine, P0–P2) of `0ca4e7d3db4b83fd82bd74f43844e25605b52b85..43bf2dd91c1c3d8ad206922047d46b6fa231cafc`, with renderer/parser context, completed **scoped-clean: no actionable findings**. This was static review, separate from executed tests. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; the maintainer fallback uses autoreview plus hosted review on the ready PR.

### Limitations

Explicit ancestral SHA baselines remain accepted for historical replay with a generation diagnostic, not as the default or recommended new-release boundary. Missing legacy evidence can retain duplicates rather than silently lose contributions. Old historical `merged PRs` totals can be stale: these warn and use explicit rows, never the declared total. Ambiguous canonical aliases remain unsuppressed.

The full historical 11.4-to-11.5 live inventory was bounded and stopped after partial GitHub discovery, with a reusable snapshot retained locally. The Git range contains 11,811 commits; that is **not a verified unique-PR count**. No corrected PR count or live-note repair is claimed.

prs.title: fix(diffs): restore PNG and PDF exports on clean installs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a clean Diffs install, the viewer works but PNG/PDF exports can fail because the plugin's patched Playwright copy cannot find Acorn. That duplicate also adds 13.7 MB of unpacked runtime files even though OpenClaw already ships Playwright.

## User Impact

PNG and PDF exports work again without enabling the Browser plugin. File exports still require a local Chromium-compatible executable; viewer-only mode still does not. The updated plugin needs a co-released host that provides the new private runtime entry point.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the host's patched Playwright through a private entry point loaded only for file exports. Diffs still owns browser selection, rendering, request isolation, and cleanup. This removes the plugin-local copy without adding a second renderer or attaching to a browsing profile.

Thanks @RomneyDa for the investigation direction and request.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bc96f145-9330-4d68-a4ad-55c78c715051)

## Evidence

- **Published 2026.11.7 baseline:** an isolated Gateway served the viewer, but PNG and PDF exports returned HTTP 500. Combined mode returned the viewer with a rendering error. Making Acorn resolvable in the diagnostic run restored both formats.
- **Candidate:** installed the release-packer Diffs tarball with `npm-pack:` into a fresh managed plugin project on the built host. Neither the tarball nor the managed plugin project contains Playwright. With the Browser plugin disabled, the Gateway served the viewer, generated valid PNG and PDF files, and returned a viewer plus PNG in default combined mode.
- The package ownership regression failed before the fix and passed after. All 93 Diffs tests and 375 dependency contract tests passed, as did the full build, targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, and SDK export and touched-doc checks.
- Local independent review could not start because the installed reviewer failed its read-only sandbox preflight. Hosted checks are still required.

## Worked on by

- @RomneyDa

prs.title: fix(ci): restore signed Gateway releases and completion-owned Store requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Stable Windows Gateway downloads remain at 11.1 because the release requester selects unsigned Store-only builds. The same requester abandons Store approval after 45 minutes even when packaging subsequently succeeds.

## User Impact

Stable and beta Gateway releases request signed GitHub downloads. Long builds no longer lose the Store handoff merely because a separate polling job expires. Store release-manager approval remains required.

**Dependency:** merge [packaging #273](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-packaging/pull/273), the completion adapter and forward-only Latest safeguard, first. Its new `request_store_publication` input is required; landing this caller first would make GitHub reject both release lanes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core verifies the public signed source, requests the official packaging workflow, records the accepted run, and finishes. Packaging owns build completion and its opt-in Store request; the central publisher owns exact candidate/approval validation. This deletes core's timed polling, duplicate artifact inspection, direct Store dispatch, and unnecessary token access to `releases`.

## Evidence

Head: `60dd109c3d6ceb7a9a3efbce5514a679fd8c2044` (code reviewed at `5275e40b81a02e254ef8a7f69234ffd783b02f3a`; subsequent commit only documents companion safeguards).

- 21 targeted release-handoff tests pass. The new stable/beta regression cases fail against the original owner.
- `pnpm check:workflows`, targeted oxlint/oxfmt and `git diff --check` pass.
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed base `29bc3e3ee37076e9aa256c83ca5f9e02c609fd9a` to the code head. It identified the receiver deployment dependency and forward-only Latest requirement, both addressed by the coordinated packaging change/rollout. The central publisher continues binding human approval to exact attempt/artifact/hash and revalidates before Store I/O; the requester does not authorize packages.
- Simplification: one completion owner replaces timed polling and a second artifact validator; production requester shrinks by 120 net lines. Native receiver growth implements completion eligibility and serialized Latest ordering.
- Hosted CI and a live automatic signed-release-to-approval run remain unverified. The manual 11.7 build is a separate existing-main run, not proof of this patch. No npm or Store release was repeated for validation.

prs.title: fix(ci): select every transitive importer test for agent, compaction and transport owners
prs.body:
## Result

Pull request CI now selects every test whose runtime imports reach a changed file under `src/agents/`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner*`, `packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/` or `packages/ai/src/transports/`, directly or transitively. Replaying the file lists of #204111 and #204180 now selects the four tests that first failed on scheduled `main` (#204252).

**Cost, read this first:** for these owners the transitive closure covers almost the whole runtime suite. A PR that touches them now runs a full-suite-sized Node plan, about 21x to 105x the previous predicted test time. Exact numbers are below. The plan stays inside the existing row cap and per-job time objective. Nothing is capped or dropped.

Closes #204252.

## Why the tests were missed

PR CI uses `selectionMode: "aggressive"` (`scripts/ci-build-manifest.mjs`). In `resolveBoundedChangedTestTargetPlan`, aggressive mode walks reverse imports to **depth 2**, and only to **depth 1** when the changed module has 20 or more direct importers (the hub cutoff). There are no owner-list routes for these files and no shard owner list filters them. The tests are simply too far away:

| Changed owner | Import distance to the missed tests |
|---|---|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.ts` | 3 (agent-runner tests) |
| `src/agents/compaction.ts` | 5 (agent-runner), 7 (prompt-cache) |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/request-boundary-compaction.ts` | 5 (agent-runner), 10 (prompt-cache) |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-submit.ts` | 7 (prompt-cache), 9 (agent-runner) |
| `packages/ai/src/transports/anthropic-messages.ts` | 6 (prompt-cache), 8 (agent-runner) |
| `packages/agent-core/src/harness/compaction/summarization-completion.ts` | 6-7 |

`session-context-accounting.gateway.integration.test.ts` is not reached within 10 imports of any compaction owner. It is reached only through the full closure, which runs through the Gateway into the runner.

## Fix

The PR plan owner (`resolveChangedNodeTestTargets`) passes `transitiveOwners` to the bounded target walk. For a changed file that matches, the walk has no depth limit and no hub cutoff. All other paths keep the two-import walk. `docs/ci/scope-and-routing/node-test-lanes.md` describes the rule.

## Selection growth (replayed through the PR planner, hybrid backend, 130-row cap)

| Replay | Before: tests / jobs / predicted test-seconds (max job) | After |
|---|---|---|
| #204111 (31 files) | 300 / 14 / 1,767 s (228 s) | 12,562 / 131 / 36,859 s (469 s) |
| #204180 (9 files) | 22 / 5 / 351 s (140 s) | 12,405 / 131 / 36,673 s (468 s) |

- The closure is nearly the whole runtime inventory. An unbounded walk from `request-boundary-compaction.ts` alone reaches 12,397 test files.
- 48 of the last 200 first-parent commits on `main` (24%) touch these owners. At the replayed size, each PR push of that kind adds about 35,000 predicted test-seconds.
- Shard budget: the plans stay at the compact Node row cap (130 rows plus one dist row) and below the 480-second per-job objective (max 469 s). They use the full PR row envelope that the registration budget already allows, so concurrent PRs of this kind compete for the same rows.
- I tested no smaller rule that still selects the four tests. A walk depth of 10 already selects 2,401-7,129 tests (13,797-26,905 s) and still misses the Gateway integration test.

## Evidence

- New test in `test/scripts/ci-changed-node-test-plan.integration.test.ts`. For 7 changed owners from #204111 and #204180, it asserts that the plan selects the four named tests and **every** test in the owner's unbounded runtime-import closure. It fails on `main` and passes on this head.
- Replay script results above, on `main` and on this head.
- One existing fixture expectation changed: `ci-changed-node-test-plan.selection.test.ts` used a `src/agents/example` source to pin the depth-two stop; it now expects the distant consumer.
- Planner and workflow tests (13 files, 1,573 tests): all pass except `ci-changed-node-test-plan.test.ts` "retains precise process ownership (github)", which fails the same way on `main` (`expected 120 to be less than or equal to 60`). It is not caused by this change.
- `pnpm check:changed`: pass.

prs.title: feat(voice-call): add optional Telnyx noise suppression for inbound realtime calls
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds an optional `telnyx.noiseSuppression` setting to Voice Call. When it is set, inbound realtime calls run Telnyx per-call noise suppression (`Denoiser`, `DeepFilterNet`, `Krisp`, or `AiCoustics`) on the caller's audio before it reaches the realtime model.

It is off by default. With the setting unset, calls without media streaming and outbound dials send exactly the same Telnyx requests as before.

## What Problem This Solves

Background speech from a TV or another person in the room reaches the realtime model as if the caller had said it. Telnyx can isolate the caller's voice per call, for example with Krisp's telephony voice isolation model.

Voice Call couldn't use that, because it starts streaming inside the `answer` command and Telnyx rejects `suppression_start` while streaming is active (422, code 90045).

## Change

When `telnyx.noiseSuppression` is set and the call streams media, `TelnyxProvider.answerCall` runs these steps in order:

1. `answer` without the stream fields.
2. `suppression_start` with the configured direction, engine and engine config. This step is capped at 5 seconds so the stream token stays valid. If it fails or times out, Voice Call logs a warning and streams without suppression.
3. `streaming_start` with the same stream settings the answer would have carried.

When the setting is unset, the single `answer` still carries the stream fields inline, unchanged from today.

The config is validated in both the manifest schema and `normalizeVoiceCallConfig`; `engineConfig` requires `engine`. The docs in `docs/plugins/voice-call/realtime-and-streaming.md` cover the direction semantics, the engine fields, and the Telnyx number setting below.

**Prerequisite:** set the number's own noise suppression to `disabled` in Telnyx. A number-level setting engages the default engine at answer, and a later `suppression_start` collides with it; Telnyx returns a 500 for that collision.

## Failure handling

| Step that fails | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `answer` (setting on) | Voice Call sends a best-effort hangup, then reports the answer failure. Telnyx may have answered before its HTTP response was lost; that answer carries no stream, so without the hangup the caller would sit on silence until duration cleanup. |
| `answer` (setting unset) | Unchanged. The answer carries the stream inline, so a lost response still connects media, and no hangup is sent. |
| `suppression_start` | Logs a warning and streams without suppression. The call continues. |
| `streaming_start` | Voice Call hangs up the answered call and reports the failure. |

Both hangups share one helper, and a failed hangup is only logged. This resolves the earlier silent-call window when the answer response is lost: the contributor-side cleanup option from the review is implemented in `2df6212`.

## Evidence

The live runs below are real inbound calls to a Telnyx local number through a source build of this branch, loaded as a bundled plugin. The setup used a Call Control app with number-level suppression `disabled`, a Tailscale funnel, OpenAI realtime, and `inboundPolicy: allowlist`.

Hostnames, call control IDs and the caller are redacted. Timestamps are local (UTC-5).

The current head, `50e97a8c67d`, is `2df6212` rebased onto main `24015bf60cb`, plus test-only commits for the review's P3 findings; the two generated config baseline files were regenerated, and `docs/plugins/voice-call/configuration.md` was merged with main's new Twilio call recording section. Since `2df6212`'s base, the only main change to the Telnyx provider, the runtime, the webhook or the media stream is one line in `runtime.ts` from #189687 that passes Twilio's `record` setting to the Twilio provider, so the runs below on `2df6212` exercise the same Telnyx answer path as the current head.

### Upgrade from current stable v2026.10.8, on head `2df6212`

All runs used one profile, one state directory and one config file.

**A. Stock `v2026.10.8` (`dc2523e`), config without `noiseSuppression`.** Four inbound calls were answered and streamed. The first three ended with the model calling `openclaw_end_call` (`endReason=hangup-bot`). The gateway was stopped during the fourth call's setup; v2026.10.8 closed that record as `completed` on shutdown.

**B. Checkout of this branch (`2df6212`), same profile, config untouched.** `openclaw doctor --fix` ran the core state migration for the newer build. That migration belongs to v2026.10.8 to main, not to this plugin. After it, the gateway started and three inbound calls behaved exactly as before:

```
22:12:37.815 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:13:28.983 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=8fea48a4-... endReason=hangup-bot
22:13:34.990 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:13:55.616 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=05f267e5-... endReason=hangup-bot
22:14:01.298 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:14:37.845 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=0a54b7ad-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

**C. `noiseSuppression` added with `config set ... --strict-json`, no other change.** The config was Krisp with `krisp-viva-tel-lite-v1.kef`. The call was a normal conversation with no suppression warning and no answer failure:

```
22:15:40.991 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:15:42.112 [voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call 28ab70e0-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>, initialGreeting=queued)
22:16:14.703 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=28ab70e0-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

**D. Rejected `suppression_start` on the same head.** The model was set to a name Telnyx does not accept, and two calls were placed.

Both calls had `suppression_start` rejected. On the first, Telnyx's own `streaming_start` then failed to reach the media destination, and Voice Call hung the answered call up through the shared helper. The second call streamed without suppression and finished normally.

```
22:24:50.955 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:24:51.486 [telnyx] Noise suppression failed to start for call 70f2a343-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>); streaming without it: Telnyx API error: 422 {
  "errors": [ { "code": "10000", "title": "Invalid request",
    "source": { "pointer": "/noise_suppression_engine_config" },
    "detail": "The 'noise_suppression_engine_config' parameter model must be one of: krisp-viva-tel-v2.kef, krisp-viva-tel-lite-v1.kef, krisp-viva-pro-v1.kef, krisp-viva-ss-v1.kef." } ]
}
22:24:52.886 [voice-call/events] Failed to answer inbound call v3:<redacted>: call answered but Telnyx streaming_start failed; hanging up: Telnyx API error: 422 {
  "errors": [ { "code": "90046", "title": "Media Streaming failed", "detail": "Failed to connect to destination" } ]
}
22:24:53.750 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=70f2a343-... endReason=completed

22:24:57.684 [voice-call/events] Inbound call accepted: caller=sha256:<redacted> allowlisted=true
22:24:58.077 [telnyx] Noise suppression failed to start for call 3e06844d-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>); streaming without it: Telnyx API error: 422 { ...same 10000 error... }
22:24:58.939 [voice-call] Realtime bridge starting for call 3e06844d-... (providerCallId=v3:<redacted>, initialGreeting=queued)
22:25:17.777 [voice-call/lifecycle] Call finalized callId=3e06844d-... endReason=hangup-bot
```

Thirty seconds after the hung-up call, the existing realtime stream watchdog logged `Realtime stream WebSocket never connected within 30s` for `70f2a343`. That call was already finalized, and the warning had no effect on it or on the next call. The watchdog belongs to the stream token issued before the answer; this PR does not change it.

### Stored call history after the upgrade

These records were read back with `openclaw voicecall tail` on `2df6212` after legs B through D. They include the four calls that v2026.10.8 wrote before the upgrade:

| Call | Written by | Started | Answered | Ended | State | End reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 61706121 | v2026.10.8 | 17:46:45 | 17:46:46 | 17:47:32 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |

| 3e06844d | 2df6212 | 22:24:57 | 22:24:58 | 22:25:17 | hangup-bot | hangup-bot |

All 11 records in the store load on the new build with their original timestamps and end reasons, including the four written by v2026.10.8.

`49b062ca` and `c96579c8` are calls that were in setup when the gateway was stopped. Each build closed its record as `completed` on shutdown.

`70f2a343` is the streaming-failure call from leg D. It has no `answeredAt` because the hangup came before Telnyx's `call.answered` webhook was processed.

So on `2df6212`, all three live paths ran against real Telnyx: Krisp on, a rejected `suppression_start`, and a `streaming_start` failure cleaned up with a hangup.

The one path not exercised live is a lost `answer` response, which can't be arranged against Telnyx on demand. The unit tests cover it.

### Earlier runs (head `c1a26c2`, [comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183266#issuecomment-6458928065))

- Krisp in a room with a multi-voice video playing: the model stayed on the caller through English and Korean speech.
- The same rejected-suppression and streaming-failure paths as above.
- An upgrade from v2026.10.7.

### Tests

- `runtime.telnyx-answer.test.ts` starts the real runtime with Telnyx and realtime enabled and POSTs a `call.initiated` webhook to its listener. It mocks only the outbound HTTP edge and asserts the Telnyx commands for three paths: unset, Krisp, and rejected `suppression_start`. It replaces the constructor-forwarding test the review flagged.
- `providers/telnyx.test.ts` covers:
  - the request order and payloads,
  - engine field mapping,
  - the 5 second suppression bound,
  - fail-open on network errors,
  - hangup on a failed stream-less answer (and none on a failed inline-stream answer),
  - hangup on a failed `streaming_start`, even when that hangup fails,
  - unchanged outbound dials.

  The unset-answer case is folded into the existing streaming-answer test.
- `config.test.ts` covers the rejection cases.

## For the voice-call owner

This adds one optional block, with 10 config paths, under `telnyx`. It stays inside the existing Telnyx provider, and the defaults are unchanged. ClawSweeper recommends approving the optional capability. A maintainer decision on exposing it is the remaining item I can't close from the contributor side.

prs.title: improve(workers): reuse admitted prepared project snapshots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Worker dispatch repeats repository admission and content validation that project preparation already completed. Snapshot capture also needs to verify the workspace, toolchains, and runtime it is about to preserve.

## User Impact

A fresh, eligible fork can reuse verified preparation from the same admitted dispatch. Ordinary starts and replays use normal verification, and the shortcut expires before code can change the prepared files. Snapshot inspection does not hydrate the worker or repair its runtime cache.

Depends on #201025 at `07fecaed8f114` and the v42 schema/auth prerequisites at `5eece39dc1a4`. The stack incorporates `main` at `2e8c1ad0aa97`. Related older proposals #193776, #193872 and #194279 remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry fresh-fork provenance from the exact selected checkpoint, and verify expanded package code through the native CLI before inspecting and capturing project caches. Validate prepared output in its owning HOME and account for bootstrap and repository Node installations separately. Keep snapshot invalidation with the workspace and bundle owners, including before fallback prewarm executes code.

The worker-local setup initializer has no supported production provider in this stack; it is not a shipped capability. Existing protected-egress setup still works. Initializer scope remains open.

## Evidence

- [CI at `b8a3bafbadae0` passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45121054062), including the [private thin-pack import, build, and refresh](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45121054062/job/137515434930) and [full worker-launch wire E2E](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45121054062/job/137515434914). The fixture now streams the setup script on stdin like production. PostgreSQL and built SQLite were not selected for this PR; the parent’s database checks passed and [#201025’s unchanged-head retry](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45121053621/attempts/2) cleared its hosted gate.
- The merged prepared-project tree passed **59** focused tests locally across service preparation, prepared dispatch, reserve refresh, and thin packs. Core types, preflight scope, lint, format, and repository ratchets passed. The test allocation is 1,252 above the default 400 (1,652 net test lines).
- Earlier builds and independent reviews are not exact-head proof. The [prior shared-publication shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44412835810/job/135186602579) passed **130/130**. Native CLI fixture evidence is not live-provider proof.

**Remaining proof:** live-provider/real-model integration and a packaged forward upgrade from latest stable. The previous [package acceptance run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44262689778) did not reach state-survival assertions. Both CI gates are for the existing stack bases, not a new merge with current `main`. No operator Gateway was changed and no cloud worker lease was allocated.

Original PR by @galiniliev.

prs.title: improve(workers): start nodes with prepared runtimes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Worker nodes repeat runtime expansion and prewarm, disposable nodes wait for private-computer preparation before connecting, and retained managed nodes can reconnect with an older runtime after a Gateway upgrade.

## User Impact

Nodes reuse verified package-owned worker code and overlap connection with private-computer preparation. Bundle admission and computer use still join readiness and failures. Dedicated Linux nodes, including supported XFCE desktop workers, can install the current runtime and recover the same enrolled device without replacing its workspace. Pending result cleanup retains its saved runtime.

This is the first worker PR in a two-PR stack extracted from `23dcc5f19b1`. It targets `galiniliev/main7-worker-prerequisites` at `5eece39dc1a4`, which incorporates `main` at `2e8c1ad0aa97`. The prerequisite keeps main’s v41 approval provenance and adds the two nullable worker-recovery fields at v42. Fresh-snapshot admission shortcuts belong to dependent #201029. Related older proposals #193776, #193872 and #194279 remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep bundle integrity, package preparation, plugin readiness and runtime recovery with their existing owners. The provider invokes the installed native preparation command before recording runtime completion; read-only inspection uses the same owner without repair, download, enrollment, prewarming or bytecode-cache writes.

Deferred preparation retains its resource disposers through early shutdown. Same-node upgrades verify fresh artifacts before retiring the matching process, preserve canonical saved-runtime selection and rediscover the authoritative XFCE environment. Late preparation is released after provider timeouts. Ordinary bundle reuse still performs integrity validation; no snapshot fast path or additional admission state is introduced here.

Queued deletion now checks current authority when the owning attempt starts. A no-op prepared cancellation does not admit a later deletion, while cleanup already accepted durably can finish after requester removal.

## Evidence

- [Attempt 2 passed on unchanged head `07fecaed8f114`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45121053621/attempts/2). The failed-only retry passed the [full 12-turn wire E2E](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45121053621/job/138169061236) in 79 seconds, including finalization, workspace settlement, Gateway restart, and the post-restart audit. The [aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45121053621/job/138171394285) passed. The [attempt 1 timeout](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45121053621/job/137515248262) did not recur; no source change or root cause is claimed. An isolated same-head replay also passed in about 62 seconds of test time.
- Attempt 1’s successful jobs were retained, including queued deletion, destination model, initial launch and heartbeat credentials, format, test types, and built SQLite session and transcript lifecycle. All four PostgreSQL 17 conformance shards passed, including [v41→v42 with approval provenance and the lazy repository fragment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45121053621/job/137515247447). PostgreSQL 16 covered Gateway cron smoke, not the schema upgrade. Historical SQLite migration fixtures passed locally, not in the observed hosted logs.
- Local focused checks: **99** lifecycle and authority tests, including a red/green regression for the no-op cancellation; core and scoped test types, lint, format, preflight and repository ratchets passed. The build and 163 SDK subpath checks at `eeb7ff91c450` are prior-head evidence.

**Remaining proof:** live-provider/real-model/native-computer integration and a packaged forward upgrade from latest stable. Database migration tests are not a package-updater run. The earlier [package acceptance run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44262689778) did not reach state-survival assertions. The green CI gate applies to this stack base, not a new merge with current `main`. No operator Gateway was changed and no cloud resources were allocated.

prs.title: fix: explain when OpenAI voice needs an API key
prs.body:
Related to #204128

## What Problem This Solves

I can get text replies after choosing Sign in with ChatGPT. When OpenAI voice needs a separate API key, the Control UI can show a provider error or leave me without a next step.

## User Impact

I show which API key is needed for Read aloud, Talk, Dictation, and recordings. Read aloud waits for the voice catalog to confirm the missing key before showing the notice. When the check finds no matching missing-key result, I show the provider error.

Configure opens **Settings → Communications → Text-to-Speech** for Read aloud and split Talk speech output. The existing TTS provider API-key field saves the credential synthesis reads. Transcription continues to open the provider in **Settings → Models** for the agent in that chat. The picker shares one Configure action when Talk and Dictation need the same key.

## Before and after

![Main shows the provider error beside the speaker button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/9514b06dca77c4363fa9ff03514bcd46df89ae72/images/2026/11/3f9f05ea-5c12-4750-a8b7-5e94561c0c66.png)

![The PR names the missing speech API key beside the speaker button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/e0c2f520c3ba39fc040e19c0043184c04ec38a59/images/2026/11/7e65df5d-2cb5-47db-afb3-e299c279b89a.png)

![Configure opens the existing TTS provider API-key field](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/daniel-lxs/screenshots/e0c2f520c3ba39fc040e19c0043184c04ec38a59/images/2026/11/7d615bde-71f9-4a04-95f5-e63446f0f83a.png)

## Why This Change Was Made

I raised the chat startup JavaScript gzip cap from 1,334,623 to 1,335,821 bytes to fit the five voice notices, following the measured-budget approach in #203448. The paired build measured 1,334,559 bytes on main and 1,335,714 bytes with this PR. Both used 21 requests.

## Evidence

- I ran 240 targeted tests, the UI typecheck, the formatter check, and the paired Control UI budget check. The Read aloud navigation regression fails when Configure opens Models and passes with the speech settings route.
- I verified in the production Control UI that Read aloud and split Talk open Text-to-Speech. I used the existing form to save a synthetic key and verified that retrying Read aloud used the key at an isolated speech endpoint.
- I checked that upgrading from published OpenClaw 2026.11.7 preserves existing settings and transcript entries. A new recording’s missing-key notice remains visible after reopening the conversation.
- I did not test a real ChatGPT token or make a real OpenAI speech request.

prs.title: fix: show provider usage for model API key SecretRefs
prs.body:
Closes #150173

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw status --usage` and Gateway `usage.status` can omit a provider when its configured model API key is a SecretRef. A failed credential lookup could also interrupt the entire CLI status report.

## User Impact

Operators can see usage with their existing SecretRefs. If one lookup fails, status keeps reporting available usage and includes a diagnostic without the resolver’s raw error. No configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

CLI status resolves only the configured provider API keys within its existing time budget, keeping the original config available for fallback. Uncertain subprocess cleanup still stops the command. Managed Gateway usage continues to check the captured credential owner at request time.

Thanks to @alex-strattab for the report, @Samay10 for the original investigation in #150192, and @meska for the Z.AI store report.

## Evidence

- On Node 24.22.1, all **74 tests across six files** passed (70.37 seconds across three repository test shards). The new regression failed before the fallback change and passes now; it also verifies that uncertain cleanup still fails the command. Online JSON coverage verifies that scan and usage diagnostics both reach the output.
- Core and command/infra test typechecks, scoped lint and formatting, test-line/timeout/mock guards, the unified runtime build, and the CLI bootstrap import guard passed. The test allocation is exactly 275 net lines for the credential, deadline, cleanup, and output regressions; it uses the upstream budget restored by #196432.
- Independent source review verified the follow-up. Earlier built loopback evidence for [CLI and Gateway usage and the deadline](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187360#issuecomment-6489445493) and [managed credential checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187360#issuecomment-6490298252) remains scoped to the revisions recorded there. Callers that already hold independently resolved plaintext config remain outside the managed snapshot’s revocation guarantee.
- Hosted CI and maintainer review for this head are separate from the local checks.

### Built CLI fallback proof

Node 24.22.1, repository `cliStartup` build, head `ee435a893be7652c4f41c04e86b3f5ebd8423ab5`. The CLI command was `openclaw status --usage --agent main --json` with an isolated config and synthetic credentials.

The missing-env case leaves a configured environment SecretRef unset. A separate loopback Gateway protocol fixture returns a malformed `secrets.resolve` reply to exercise the preparation-error fallback in online JSON (`collection.source=gateway`, `gateway.reachable=true`). The real CLI emits the generic diagnostic and retains healthy OpenRouter usage from two native loopback HTTP requests. The raw resolver error and fixture credentials are absent from CLI output.

```text
malformed-response exit=0 secrets.resolve=1 diagnostics=1 credits=200 key=200 balance=21 USD key_budget=20% credentials_or_fault_marker=false
missing-secret exit=0 secrets.resolve=1 diagnostics=2 credits=200 key=200 balance=21 USD key_budget=20% credentials_or_fault_marker=false
healthy-control exit=0 secrets.resolve=0 diagnostics=0 credits=200 key=200 balance=21 USD key_budget=20% credentials_or_fault_marker=false
```

These three product CLI cases passed locally. A subsequent Node 24.22.1 rerun compiled and verified the full test fixture graph and passed all 72 cases across five files in three repository Vitest shards. The same 72 cases and the required checks passed in hosted CI for this head.

AI-assisted implementation and verification.

### November 24 upstream refresh

- Synced upstream main at `7cbf1585ed7` to resolve the merge conflict. The refresh preserves status usage diagnostics and fallback for ordinary lookup failures. Ctrl+C now reaches the credential Gateway request and owned subprocesses, then stops the status operation before usage collection.
- On Node 24.22.1, commit `00773a43612` passed 100 tests across six files and four repository Vitest shards. Scoped type-aware lint, formatting, the staged test-line budget, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The two new cancellation regressions both failed with signal forwarding removed and passed after it was restored. Independent Codex source review identified the missing Gateway signal and rechecked the transport path after the correction.

## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw gives up delivering a Codex child’s result, it writes the child thread ID, turn ID and session key into the parent conversation. Anyone reopening that conversation sees instructions meant for an operator.

## User Impact

The conversation shows “Couldn’t deliver the result of a background task.” Operators can use the existing structured warning to find the child thread, turn, session key and terminal status.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retirement writer creates the shared system note that clients read from history. Updating its text covers blocked delivery and exhausted retries. The existing receipt, retry and deduplication logic continues to decide when a notice is due. The wider question in #195436 about when retirement should occur remains open.

## Evidence

On v2026.11.7, the existing monitor test read the diagnostic text back from an isolated transcript for both blocked delivery and exhausted retries. With this change, all 40 cases in `native-subagent-inventory.test.ts` passed, including the empty-result case and recovery after retirement.

The two source files matched upstream main before applying the patch. Formatting, targeted lint and the Codex package entry-point typecheck passed. The release pack command produced an installable plugin, and `plugins inspect codex --runtime` loaded it in an isolated v2026.11.7 host. The delivery failure was exercised at the monitor and transcript boundary. No external chat client was used. Local autoreview was unavailable.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): Docker runs fail with "No such container" when another run's cleanup overlaps their start
prs.body:
Related: #178166, #103542

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Docker sandbox run fails with "No such container" when another run's sandbox cleanup removes the same container while the first run is starting it.

## User Impact

User impact: sandboxed runs that start at the same time, such as cron jobs scheduled for the same minute, no longer lose their container to the other run's cleanup. Cleanup still removes containers that are idle or past their maximum age when no run is starting them.

This PR protects a container while a run starts or recreates it. Protection for the rest of the run, when `maxAgeDays` expires mid-run, stays with #131935.

Risk: code only, reverted by reverting the commit. No config, schema, or stored-state change. A Docker or Podman sandbox start now waits for an in-progress cleanup of the same container, and cleanup waits for an in-progress start, including a setup command. An explicit `openclaw sandbox recreate` from another process also waits for a Gateway start already in progress; within one process it already waited behind the start in the container lifecycle queue.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cleanup checked a container's last use, then queued `docker rm` behind the run's start. The run started the container, recorded its use, and got it back, and the queued removal then deleted it. Docker entries never took the per-container registry lock that already protects reserving backends.

Docker and Podman starts now hold that lock for the whole container lifecycle. Cleanup of backends without runtime reservations takes it before it records removal intent, and skips a container whose last use changed since its scan:

```diff
 ensureSandboxContainer
+  withSandboxRegistryEntryLock(container)
     withSandboxContainerLifecycle(container)
       inspect, then start or create and run setup
-      record use (creation reused the timestamp written before allocation)
+      record use (creation stamps the time setup finished)

 removeSandboxRegistryRuntime (backends without reservations)
-  beginRemoval: check expiry, write removal intent
-  remove container
+  withSandboxRegistryEntryLock(container)
+    beginRemoval: check expiry, skip if last use changed since the scan
+    remove container
```

Skipping on changed last use matters for `maxAgeDays`: a container past its maximum age stays expired after a run uses it, so without that check cleanup that waited for the run would still delete it. Reserving backends keep their existing order: removal intent first, then the lock and a re-check.

<details>
<summary>Accepted edge cases</summary>

- `maxAgeDays` ignores activity by design, so a cleanup pass whose scan begins after a run's start has finished can still remove an age-expired container that run is using. This change protects only cleanup that overlaps the start; #131935 tracks protection for the rest of the run.
- The change adds no fallback that recreates the container when `docker start` returns "No such container". With the lock held, OpenClaw's own cleanup can't remove the container between inspection and start; only an external `docker rm` in that window could, and the next run recreates it.

</details>

## Evidence

### Real Docker

Docker Desktop 29.8.2 on macOS, `debian:bookworm-slim` as the sandbox image. A temporary, uncommitted Vitest file calls the real `ensureSandboxContainer` and `maybePruneSandboxes` with no mocks, against an isolated state directory and real `docker` commands, and prints `docker events` for the sandbox container. Two scenarios:

- **Idle reuse:** a stopped container last used 2 hours ago, `{ idleHours: 1 }`. Cleanup and the run's start are launched together.
- **Setup replacement:** a container created 2 days ago and last used 2 hours ago, `{ idleHours: 1, maxAgeDays: 1 }`. The run starts with a changed `setupCommand` (`sleep 4`), so it replaces the container. Cleanup starts once the replacement is running its setup.

Times are seconds after the proof started. In the setup case, the run destroys the old container itself, then creates and starts its replacement; any later `kill`/`destroy` of the replacement comes from cleanup. Redacted runs; regenerated by a local script that copies the proof file in, runs it on this PR's code and on main's production files, and removes only the `oc-proof-*` containers it created.

main `d97b1248689`:

```text
idle: launching cleanup (maybePruneSandboxes) and run start (ensureSandboxContainer) together
  +2.11s start a2af0e080e92
  +2.14s kill a2af0e080e92
  +2.16s die a2af0e080e92
  +2.17s destroy a2af0e080e92
idle: RESULT run got a2af0e080e92; docker inspect after cleanup: No such container (deleted)
setup: run starts with a changed setupCommand (sleep 4), so it replaces the container
setup: replacement 8307e8ec3c05 is running its setup command; launching cleanup now
  +4.92s kill c5062e8f166c
  +4.94s die c5062e8f166c
  +4.95s destroy c5062e8f166c
  +5.03s create 8307e8ec3c05
  +5.10s start 8307e8ec3c05
  +9.19s kill 8307e8ec3c05
  +9.21s die 8307e8ec3c05
  +9.22s destroy 8307e8ec3c05
setup: RESULT run failed: Sandbox runtime was removed or is being removed; retry after sandbox recreate completes.
```

This PR, `75f15d80c88`:

```text
idle: launching cleanup (maybePruneSandboxes) and run start (ensureSandboxContainer) together
  +2.09s start 560c2bcf549e
idle: RESULT run got 560c2bcf549e; docker inspect after cleanup: running=true
setup: run starts with a changed setupCommand (sleep 4), so it replaces the container
setup: replacement 342c2fd70823 is running its setup command; launching cleanup now
  +5.08s kill 6763ba7a6562
  +5.11s die 6763ba7a6562
  +5.11s destroy 6763ba7a6562
  +5.20s create 342c2fd70823
  +5.27s start 342c2fd70823
setup: RESULT run got 342c2fd70823; docker inspect after cleanup: running=true
```

The idle overlap's ordering depends on timing, so on this PR cleanup may also go first. In that case it removes the idle container before the run inspects it, and the run creates a new one; the regression tests below pin both orderings.

### Regression tests

`src/agents/sandbox/prune.docker-start-race.test.ts` drives the real `maybePruneSandboxes` and `ensureSandboxContainer` against a real registry database, with only the `docker` CLI faked. Each case orders the two sides with gates, not timers:

1. Cleanup first: cleanup selects an idle container and pauses before removal, then a run starts it.
2. Run first: a run pauses at `docker start`, cleanup scans the registry, then the run continues. The setup-command container was created 2 days ago and idle 2 hours, under `{ idleHours: 1, maxAgeDays: 1 }`.
3. Recreation, run once for each creation path: the expired container has a stale config hash, so the run replaces it and pauses while cleanup scans. The setup row pauses in the setup command; the managed-worktree row, with no setup command, pauses at the replacement's `docker start`.

| Production code | 1. Cleanup first | 2. Run first | 3. Recreation, setup | 3. Recreation, managed worktree |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main `d97b1248689` | fails: container deleted | fails: container deleted | fails: run errors "Sandbox runtime was removed or is being removed" | fails |
| this PR | passes | passes | passes | passes |

Before, on main:

```text
× keeps a container that a run starts while cleanup removes its idle predecessor
  → the started container must survive cleanup: expected null to deeply equal { …(3) }
× keeps an expired setup container that a run starts before cleanup removes it
  → the started container must survive cleanup: expected null to deeply equal { …(3) }
× keeps an expired setup container that a run recreates while cleanup scans it
  → Sandbox runtime was removed or is being removed; retry after sandbox recreate completes.
× keeps an expired managed-worktree container that a run recreates while cleanup scans it
```

With only the old managed-worktree skip of the completion write restored, just the managed-worktree row fails: "the started container must survive cleanup: expected null".

After:

```text
✓ keeps a container that a run starts while cleanup removes its idle predecessor
✓ keeps an expired setup container that a run starts before cleanup removes it
✓ keeps an expired setup container that a run recreates while cleanup scans it
✓ keeps an expired managed-worktree container that a run recreates while cleanup scans it
```

Other checks, run locally:

- All of `src/agents/sandbox/` plus `src/agents/sandbox.*.test.ts`: 62 files, 644 passed, 15 skipped.
- `pnpm check:changed --base d97b1248689` passes format, lint, core typecheck, the `agents-root` test typecheck graph, import cycles, and the ratchets for the changed files. Its four failures point at files this PR doesn't touch: a `tsgo:ui-e2e` error in `ui/src/e2e/session-scoped-delivery.e2e.test.ts`, max-lines suppressions in three `ui/` files, Knip unused exports in `src/video-generation/types.ts`, `ui/src/pages/chat/talk/audio.ts`, and `extensions/typesafe/src/decisions.ts`, and the advisory test-root budget for the `gateway-root` and `plugins-platform` graphs.
- CI `checks-node-changed-1` fails 3 cases in `src/agents/sandbox-agent-config.agent-specific-sandbox-config.e2e.test.ts` with "JSON Parse error: Unexpected EOF" from `captureDockerPersistentTarget`. The same 3 cases fail on `main` `d85fcb29bec` without this PR: a11879cd40f added a `docker context inspect` call that the test's fake Docker doesn't answer. The test runs here only because this PR changes sandbox files.
- Test cost: `pnpm test src/agents/sandbox/prune.docker-start-race.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` takes about 3.8 s of test time for the four cases and 20 s wall on an Apple M1 Pro. Each case uses a fresh state directory and waits on the real file lock's 100 ms retry.
- `autoreview` (Codex, `--mode branch`, P0 to P1): scoped-clean, no findings. The helper reviewed the diff without the unchanged surrounding source, so it couldn't fully check lock ordering against the lifecycle queue. Four review rounds with full repository access covered that. The first three found three issues, all fixed here and covered by cases 2 and 3; the fourth found none after the managed-worktree row was added.

Gaps:

- The regression tests fake the `docker` CLI. The real-Docker runs call the production functions directly in one process, not through a Gateway with a model-driven agent run. The regression tests run cleanup and the start in one process, where the lock's in-process holder record makes one side wait for the other. A second process, such as the CLI, waits on the lock file instead; `src/plugin-sdk/file-lock.test.ts` covers when a waiter may take over a lock under `remove-if-definitely-stale`.

prs.title: fix(release): pin ClawHub package-publish with trusted publishing error and staging fixes
prs.body:
## Problem

OpenClaw's plugin release workflow pins ClawHub's reusable `package-publish.yml` at `ef56b2cb`. That ClawHub revision predates several fixes that caused or prolonged the 2026.11.10-beta.1, 2026.11.10-beta.2 and 2026.11.7 ClawHub publication failures.

- **CLI error masking:** at `ef56b2cb`, when trusted publishing failed, the CLI fell back to a saved token and reported `Not logged in. Run: clawhub login`. That hid the real reason. It's why the beta.1 diagnostics-prometheus failure looked like an auth problem.
- **Server-side fixes:** the other fixes below are in ClawHub's backend and are already deployed to production. Pinning the commit that contains them keeps the workflow source, CLI and server contract aligned.

## Solution

Bump the pin to `11f935929080ad9ff2fc539154b6521c1b85c123`, which is ClawHub main and contains:

- `596c649b` (CLI): reports trusted-publishing errors as-is instead of falling back to "Not logged in".
- openclaw/clawhub#4939 (server): a running release parent that GitHub reports as `queued` or `waiting` is still treated as active, and GitHub 5xx responses during authorization are retried.
- openclaw/clawhub#4944 (server): large package publishes stay under the 512 MB publish action memory limit. `@openclaw/diffs` previously crashed this step.
- openclaw/clawhub#4945 (server): a check claim held by a stopped worker is released, and retries are dispatched directly instead of waiting for the sweep.

Between `ef56b2cb` and this commit, the reusable workflow's `inputs`, `outputs` and `secrets` are unchanged. The only workflow changes are internal: Bun 1.4.4, and Node set up for plugin validation. The separate `clawhub@0.23.3` npm pin, used by the bootstrap and pre-tag pack paths, is not changed.

## Evidence

- `keeps release publication ownership and artifact boundaries wired`, which asserts the pinned `uses:` ref, passes with the new pin. It fails if the workflow pin and the test disagree.
- `actionlint` passes on `.github/workflows/plugin-clawhub-release.yml`.
- In the same local run of `test/scripts/package-acceptance-workflow.test.ts` (filtered to `package artifact reuse` and ClawHub), main and this branch give identical results: 18 failed, 276 passed. The failures are macOS-local bash errors in release-check shell snippets (`ambiguous redirect`, `wait: pid … is not a child of this shell`), not this change. Hosted CI is the proof for the full file.

prs.title: fix(android): connect through HTTPS proxies requiring Basic login
prs.body:
Related: #162240; related recovery report: #173578.

## What Problem This Solves

Android cannot sign in through an HTTPS reverse proxy that requires HTTP Basic, even when browser access works. A direct-LAN setup code does not supply the proxy-authenticated user identity, and the app can hide the useful rejection behind a generic reconnect message.

## User Impact

Adds a separate proxy-login control to manual and QR/setup-code onboarding and saved-Gateway editing. Credentials are encrypted and limited to the confirmed HTTPS destination. Android CA trust and hostname verification remain required; an existing certificate pin is additional.

For per-user access, the proxy must validate Basic credentials, strip its Authorization header, and forward the authenticated identity on HTTP requests and WebSocket upgrades. GitHub is not required. Gateway roles and pairing remain server-owned. Proxy credentials never enter Gateway token/password fields or setup codes.

Password rotation preserves pairing. Switching proxy usernames requires Forget and re-add; Forget clears local credentials/cache, not server pairing or server history. Image requests retain proxy authentication without falling back to a Gateway Bearer token; an ingress-only proxy that cannot authenticate the upstream HTTP route can leave images unavailable.

This is Basic support, not browser-only SSO/OIDC, per-account proxy Bearer tokens, a new Gateway authentication mode, or a local-account database.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuses the existing ingress-authorization and secure-preferences owners, one shared setup-confirmation component, and the existing image loader. Failed credential writes preserve saved Gateway authentication and drafts. Recovery distinguishes node connectivity from operator sign-in and handles both AUTH_VERIFIED_USER_REQUIRED and AUTH_UNAUTHORIZED with trusted_proxy_user_missing.

The simplification removes decorative assets, duplicate design material, unrelated client-side setup-expiry plumbing, proxy-specific retry/pairing timers, and the separate favicon RPC rewrite. Existing Gateway expiry and reconnect policies remain in charge. The current-main integration preserves fingerprint-entry recovery and structured method diagnostics; the unrelated Doctor repair is already upstream and is no longer part of this diff.

Original implementation by @DonnieFi. Earlier repair and native verification with @IWhatsskill.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/220c0918-a800-4d03-9de9-76bfe07ee90d)
- [Earlier discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/261a2cb8-209d-4eb4-bda3-ae36c5b32e91)
- [TLS repair implementation and source inspection](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/41959a0a-a06c-4e63-9d9f-d917545e3c51)
- [Earlier native Android verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/0c87876b-823a-435d-a74e-59e628d7e6ab)

## Evidence

Published head: `e9112783498b6bcd5329fa88735a01bf3fa85def`.

**Local Android lint and APK assembly passed on this revision; installed-app recovery and upgrade proof remain outstanding.** The follow-up restores the existing changed-pin recovery for Basic-authenticated Gateways without weakening platform trust or hostname verification, and removes the process-wide production test trust override. A test-scoped Robolectric fixture uses the existing explicit-trust-manager builder. Both Basic and non-Basic recovery cases remain covered.

The complete changed-test diff is **494 lines (483 added, 11 deleted)**. The author reported all three focused Gradle suites passed on `8a8209d6` (53 seconds). The second Gradle invocation stopped at `ktlintTestSourceSetCheck`: one expression-body layout in the test fixture. The current commit joins those two lines; production code and test logic are unchanged. `git diff --check` passed; the author then fast-forwarded to `e9112783498` and reported `:app:ktlintCheck :app:lintThirdPartyDebug :app:assembleThirdPartyDebug` passed in 3m 30s (116 actionable tasks: 19 executed, 97 up-to-date). Independent source review of the preceding four-file TLS repair found no actionable issues. Base-red/head-green execution and native recovery/upgrade proof remain outstanding. No custom-CA opt-in is included.

Required follow-up proof: unmodified-app Basic login through an Android-trusted certificate; corrected-login and failed-save/retry recovery; explicit pin replacement or Use system trust after certificate renewal; and same-signer latest-stable source install-over retaining existing credentials, pairing, settings and pins. Latest stable source checked November 24 is `v2026.11.7` (`e31bbf056de321127988ec5c1a36ff1b59297de0`), not the historical `v2026.10.5` upgrade. Maintainer security approval and current-head CI remain required.

- Author-reported clean local validation at prior head `8bdb5fcb566b48cb07be03fb2beb9153e6384e76` passed `pnpm android:i18n:check` (1,901 app keys), `:app:ktlintCheck`, the full `:app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest` suite, `:app:lintThirdPartyDebug`, and `:app:assembleThirdPartyDebug`. The assembly produced the third-party debug APK. [Validation results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162247#issuecomment-7118049057)
- Physical-device verification on a Samsung Galaxy S24 FE used a live Caddy HTTPS reverse proxy with HTTP Basic authentication and an OpenClaw Gateway configured for trusted proxy authentication. The standard trust configuration rejected Caddy's local CA with `PROXY_TLS_FAILURE`. With a local debug-only Android User CA trust override, TLS and hostname verification succeeded, proxy authentication reached Gateway device approval, and the paired device completed a live chat round trip. The override was confined to the device test build. [Device procedure and results](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162247#issuecomment-7117731183)
- ClawSweeper completed its latest requested review. The PR still carries the security review and needs-proof labels. [Review acknowledgment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162247#issuecomment-7118050793)

<summary>Earlier native evidence — historical, not current-candidate proof</summary>

The earlier repair at 952b53fd37484e180ac87b610d977b7e071ae7f2 exercised a real API 35 Android emulator with Caddy TLS/Basic authentication and an isolated Gateway. It covered failed Save/Remove recovery and a same-signer debug upgrade from stable source while retaining pairing, settings and a TLS pin. That was not an official Play APK or a physical-device run.
