prs.title: fix: restore compact failed-reply cards in the Control UI
prs.body:
Closes #204297

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI's persistent "Couldn't finish this reply" card grew after #194607. Stacking Refresh and Report a bug inside the title row left a 39.7px gap above the body, and the report link used larger text than the body.

## User Impact

Failed-reply cards return to their compact layout while keeping Report a bug, Refresh, expandable details, and dismissal. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing card grid now shares its title and body rows with the action group, so reporting no longer stretches the title row. The report link matches the body's scaled typography. The narrow-screen discard action retains its full-width layout.

Scope is limited to the card layout, reused toast typography, and the responsive E2E regression. No production JavaScript, comments, dependencies, or unrelated behavior changed.

## Evidence

### CSS budget repair

Acceptance: no more than 64 B of total generated raw CSS growth versus pinned main `941e80567e600f18f900d27b1f383c67a5f25ae6`, with the compact layout and mobile discard behavior preserved. No budget or baseline changes.

Ran the existing paired production-build check locally before and after the repair, with one toolchain and fixed build identity (Node 24.20.0, Vite 8.3.5, Pako 3.0.3):

prs.title: fix(voice): answer phone, meeting and FaceTime consults on Claude CLI agents
prs.body:
Closes #202208

Related: #188440, #161885, #164229, #199379, #199378; supersedes closed #191683.

## What Problem This Solves

On an agent whose model runs on Claude CLI (or another CLI runtime), a phone call (Voice Call realtime), a meeting bot (Google Meet, Teams, Zoom, Slack huddles) or a FaceTime call cannot get an answer from the agent: every consult fails with `No API key found for provider "anthropic"` or a sign-in error, and the caller hears an error. Typed messages and Discord voice to the same agent work.

## User Impact

User impact: phone, meeting and FaceTime voice consults run on the agent's own runtime, including Claude CLI and its configured fallbacks, like a typed message. Embedded-runtime agents keep working. Tool policy is unchanged: callers and meeting participants are guests, FaceTime owners stay owners, and a phone consult's `voice_call` can still only end the current call.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared helper `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` always ended in `runEmbeddedAgent` with an explicit provider/model, which calls the provider API directly and never selects the agent's runtime. Discord voice works because it runs a normal agent turn through `runCommandFromIngress`.

- `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` gains `runner: "agent-turn"`: after the helper prepares the consult session (fork from the requester, lineage, delivery fields, lifecycle admission), the consult runs as a turn of that session through `runCommandFromIngress` with `deliver: false`. Prompt building, timeout, cancellation, `onRunStarted`, speakable-text extraction and yield acknowledgements are unchanged. The default stays `embedded`, so Talk (which adapts embedded tool context and is being reworked in #164229 / #199379) and third-party SDK callers are untouched.
- Voice Call, meeting-bot and FaceTime opt in. Voice Call passes a model override only when `responseModel` is configured and a thinking override only when `realtime.consultThinkingLevel` is set; otherwise the session's own selection applies. Meeting consults no longer force thinking `high`; they use the session default. A level a bridge does pass (FaceTime always asks for `off`, Voice Call passes `realtime.consultThinkingLevel`) is a one-run choice: a model without that level runs at its closest one, as on the embedded runner (`8711c7b5a`, below).
- Plugin ingress (`runCommandFromIngress` wrapper): a plugin may omit `messageChannel` for a turn on its own surface. Owner authority still needs a bundled or trusted official plugin, and a named channel must still be the plugin's own. `toolBindings` are accepted only for tools the plugin declares in `contracts.tools`. **This widens the plugin ingress capability** (previously only channel plugins could admit turns); it stays narrower than `runEmbeddedAgent`, which any plugin can already call with an owner bit. Flagging for SDK/security owner review.
- The Claude CLI path carries `toolBindings` from the command attempt into the MCP loopback grant, as the embedded runner already does, so `voice_call` stays bound to the live call.
- Voice Call runs the consult in its service context so Gateway-dispatched tools such as `sessions_send` work from webhook handlers.

Not changed: the Voice Call classic (non-realtime) responder (#188440), Talk's Gateway consult path (#164229 / #199379), Discord voice.

## Review fixes (ClawSweeper review of `1fd6919`)

Rebased onto `main` `d7d546f29` (first commit now `1698a745c`, unchanged content). Second commit `503beb2ae`, one focused test per finding, each red on the first commit and green after:

- **[P1] Sender policy at the MCP boundary.** A Gateway-launched CLI run's loopback grant now resolves requester policy like its embedded twin (`senderPolicyMode: "always"`, owner WebChat still exempt), also when a capped tool list drops node exec, which is what switched it to `when-sender-id` before (`src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts`, `tool-resolution-authority.ts`; keyed on the grant's existing `nodeExecAllowed`, which only Gateway-launched CLI grants carry). HTTP `/tools/invoke` keeps `when-sender-id`. Voice Call also passes the remote party's number (`from` inbound, `to` outbound, the identity inbound admission checks) as the consult's `senderId`, so `toolsBySender` entries apply to the caller. Tests: `src/gateway/mcp-http.voice-consult-grant.test.ts` (real MCP loopback, grant built by `buildCliMcpGrantContext`: `tools/list` without `sessions_send`, `tools/call sessions_send` refused, control case with an identified caller), `tool-resolution.exclude.test.ts`, Voice Call `runtime.test.ts`.
- **[P2] Verbose not saved.** New `verboseOnce` command option (like `thinkingOnce`): it sets the run's verbose level and is never written to `SessionEntry.verboseLevel`. Consults use it instead of `verbose: "off"`. Test: `session-preparation.test.ts` (one-shot runs at off and the row keeps `full`; the persistent override still saves).
- **[P2] Workspace.** The agent turn gets the consult's already-resolved `workspaceDir` (restored `spawnedWorkspaceDir`).
- **[P2] Account and reply target.** The turn's run context carries the resolved account, destination (`currentChannelId`) and thread (`currentThreadTs`), with `deliver: false` unchanged. Tests for both: `agent-consult-runtime.test.ts`.
- **[P2] Voice policy surface.** The CLI MCP grant keeps a provider that carries a tool policy (`voice`, `discord-voice`, `node`) when it is not a delivery channel, so the voice filter still drops `tts`. The same surface also hides `ask_user` (no question input on a phone line), as on the embedded route. Other non-channel providers stay unset as before. Test: `mcp-grant-context.test.ts`.
- **Tests.** The mock-echo binding case in `attempt-execution.cli-mcp.test.ts` is removed; the loopback test above covers the grant at the MCP boundary.

## Follow-up fix found by the meeting/FaceTime e2e (`8711c7b5a`)

The first FaceTime e2e (a stand-in plugin with FaceTime's consult parameters, `evidence-e2e-surfaces-red-503beb2ae.log`) failed on `503beb2ae`: FaceTime passes `thinkLevel: "off"`, and on the agent-turn route the command's model selection rejects an explicit level the model lacks, so every FaceTime consult on `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` failed with `Thinking level "off" is not supported for anthropic/claude-opus-5-5. Use one of: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra.` The embedded runner clamps such a level to the closest supported one, so this was a regression for any FaceTime agent on such a model, embedded or CLI. New command option `thinkingOnceClosest` lets a one-run level fall through to the attempt's existing clamp, as subagent spawns already do; consults set it. A persistent `/think` override and other callers still get the error. Test: a new row in `model-selection.configured.test.ts` ("prefers observed max support"), red with `503beb2ae`'s `model-selection.ts`, green after; the helper and Voice Call tests assert the flag. After the fix the FaceTime consult runs at `--effort low` and the Gateway logs `Thinking level clamped to low for anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (requested off; preference retained).`

## Follow-up fix found while tracing a Google Meet e2e failure (`7f72cb5c7`)

Plugin `runEmbeddedAgent` runs its turn as a detached work continuation ("plugin turns can outlive both the triggering request root and its async work scope"); plugin `runCommandFromIngress`, which this PR's agent-turn route uses, did not. A meeting's realtime bridge is opened inside the `googlemeet.join` request, so a consult that reaches the command queue after the request that started it has ended lost its admission with `Gateway is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.`, where the embedded route kept going. `runCommandFromIngress` now runs its turn as a detached continuation, the same way (`src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent.ts`, one wrap). Test: `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent.ingress-continuation.test.ts` (an ingress turn that starts after its parent root and async scope ended), red on `8711c7b5a` with `GatewayDrainingError` at `enqueueCommandInLane` ← `runtime-agent.ts`, green after (`evidence-unit-ingress-continuation-7f72cb5c7.md`); the PR's test-lines allocation goes from 13 to 69 for it. A consult whose tool call itself arrives after that request ended still fails one step earlier, at `beginSessionEffect`, on `main` too; see "Pre-existing" under Evidence.

## Evidence

### Proof status: meeting callback path is blocked by a known bug on `main`

On this PR alone, as on `main`, a meeting consult that arrives through the normal provider callback cannot complete, because of a known bug on `main` that this PR does not touch: a realtime voice consult issued from a callback runs under the already-released root of the request that opened the call (`googlemeet.join` / `googlemeet.create`), and `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` → `beginSessionEffect` refuses it with `GatewayDrainingError` ("Gateway is temporarily unavailable" / "Gateway is draining") before any runner is chosen. It fails the same way on the embedded route on `main`.

- Reported in #142610 (meeting, Google Meet) and #202915 (FaceTime).
- Fixed by #202979 (fresh root admission inside `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent`, covers every voice bridge) and, for meetings only, #142692. Both are open and waiting on maintainers.
- This PR only changes what happens after admission (which runner executes the consult), so it neither causes nor fixes that refusal. Once #202979 (or #142692) lands, the normal meeting callback reaches this PR's agent-turn route unchanged. This is shown below: with #202979 applied **temporarily** on top of `7f72cb5c7` (throwaway local branch, never pushed, not part of this PR), a meeting consult delivered through the normal provider callback after `googlemeet.join` returned was answered by the real Claude CLI; the same run on `7f72cb5c7` alone is refused at `beginSessionEffect` ("Meeting through the normal provider callback").

The proof below is sufficient for the change this PR makes: real Claude CLI answers on the phone route with sender-policy refusal; bundled Google Meet and FaceTime plugins running their own code into the agent-turn route with real Claude CLI answers; a **live FaceTime call on the exact head** by the FaceTime plugin author; and an upgrade from the latest stable release with existing sessions and saved preferences intact. The meeting callback entry is shown too, with the separate fix applied temporarily; without that fix it stays blocked by the bug above, not by this change.

### Real model (Claude CLI 2.1.325, operator's own login, `8711c7b5a`)

Same isolated QA Gateway as the stub runs (private state, own log file, `env -i`), with the real `claude` binary behind a small logging wrapper that gives only the CLI process the operator's `HOME` so its login works, and logs argv, the CLI's `system/init` tool list, `tool_use` names and the final result (no credentials). Twilio and the realtime peer stay simulated; the fixture's consult question is replaced. The `anthropic` provider base URL points at an unreachable local port, so any embedded fallback could not reach the API. Files: `evidence-e2e-real-answer-8711c7b5a.log`, `evidence-e2e-real-policy-8711c7b5a.log` (same runs on `503beb2ae`: `*-503beb2ae.log`).

`safe-read-only`, caller asks "what is 17 times 23?":

```text
[+21.5s] gateway up; mode=answer; toolPolicy=safe-read-only; claude=REAL CLI via logging wrapper
[+25.8s] consult answered in 3606 ms
FINAL TOOL RESULT: {"text":"17 times 23 is 391."}
real claude system/init: {"claude_code_version":"2.1.325","model":"claude-opus-5-5","apiKeySource":"none",
  "tools":["ToolSearch","mcp__openclaw__memory_get","mcp__openclaw__memory_search","mcp__openclaw__read","mcp__openclaw__voice_call","mcp__openclaw__web_fetch"],
  "mcp_servers":[{"name":"openclaw","status":"connected","source":"dynamic"}]}
```

`owner` policy, `tools.toolsBySender["*"].deny: ["sessions_send"]`, `tts` allowed; the caller asks the agent to relay a message with `sessions_send`. The requester's own chat turn (first CLI process) has `sessions_send`, `tts` and `ask_user`; the phone consult (last CLI process) has none of them, the model says so, and a direct call on the consult's own loopback grant is refused:

```text
[+35.3s] consult answered in 10437 ms
FINAL TOOL RESULT: {"text":"No, the message wasn't sent, because a tools-by-sender policy blocks the sessions_send tool for this phone session."}
requester chat turn  system/init: 44 tools, sessions_send: true,  tts: true,  ask_user: true
phone consult        system/init: 39 tools, sessions_send: false, tts: false, ask_user: false
phone consult tool_use: ToolSearch "select:mcp__openclaw__sessions", ToolSearch "sessions_send send message to session", mcp__openclaw__session_status
probe on the consult's grant: tools/list 38 tools, sessions_send: false
  tools/call sessions_send -> "Tool not available: sessions_send"
  tools/call gateway       -> "gateway needs the owner's authority, and this turn was not started by the owner. Do not retry gateway."
"No API key" occurrences: 0
```

(`session_status` inside the consult shows `Runtime: Claude CLI` and `Auth: api-key (qa-mock-anthropic ...)`: the QA harness seeds a placeholder Anthropic profile; the CLI itself reports `apiKeySource: "none"`, i.e. its own login.)

### Meeting and FaceTime through the bundled plugins (Claude CLI 2.1.325, operator's own login, `7f72cb5c7`)

Same isolated QA Gateway and Claude CLI wrapper as the phone run, on a dist built from `095c1ce7e` (the same tree as `7f72cb5c7`, whose commit message was reworded afterwards). Only the `claude` process gets the operator's `HOME`, and the `anthropic` API base URL is a dead local path (0 requests reached it). This time the **bundled** plugins run their own code; a test plugin (`.artifacts/vci-e2e/surface-real-plugin`) stands in only for what has no local equivalent. Three real consults in total (meeting ×2, FaceTime ×1; the meeting log is the second run, which also lists the consult's session row; the first gave the same answer). Files: `evidence-e2e-real-meeting-7f72cb5c7.log`, `evidence-e2e-real-facetime-7f72cb5c7.log`, commands in `commands-e2e-real-surfaces-7f72cb5c7.md`.

**Google Meet.** `googlemeet.join {transport: "chrome", mode: "bidi"}` on the bundled `google-meet` plugin: its Chrome transport, realtime engine and `createMeetingRealtimeEngineBindings(...).handleToolCall` → `consultMeetingAgent` → `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` (`runner: "agent-turn"`) → google-meet's own `api.runtime.agent.runCommandFromIngress` (no `messageChannel`, guest). Faked: `browser.request` (the Chrome tab, in call with mic on and audio routed), `pactl`/`parec`/`pacat` on `PATH` (the meeting audio device), and the realtime voice peer, which emits `openclaw_agent_consult` and records the tool results.

```text
PLUGIN: {"id":"google-meet","origin":"bundled","enabled":true}
googlemeet.join -> {"session":{"id":"meet_...","transport":"chrome","mode":"bidi","agentId":"qa","state":"active",
  "realtime":{"enabled":true,"strategy":"bidi","provider":"vci-realtime","toolPolicy":"safe-read-only"}, ...}}

  "agentRuntime":{"id":"claude-cli","source":"model"},"modelProvider":"anthropic","model":"claude-opus-5-5"}

real claude system/init: {"claude_code_version":"2.1.325","model":"claude-opus-5-5","apiKeySource":"none",
  "tools":["ToolSearch","mcp__openclaw__memory_get","mcp__openclaw__memory_search","mcp__openclaw__read","mcp__openclaw__web_fetch"]}
real claude result: {"subtype":"success","is_error":false,"num_turns":1,"result":"19 times 21 is 399."}
MCP probe on the consult's grant: tools ["memory_get","memory_search","read","web_fetch"]; gateway -> "Tool not available: gateway"
[agent/cli-backend] cli live session start: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 activeSessions=1
[agent/cli-backend] cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 durationMs=1833 outBytes=19
"No API key" occurrences: 0     "cannot admit" occurrences: 0     mock provider requests: 0

```

**FaceTime (owner).** The bundled `facetime` plugin is loaded and registered with `ownerHandles` and a realtime config. A test-side Gateway preload (`surface-real-preload.mjs`, a Node load hook, in memory, no file edited) records the plugin's own `register(api)` argument and exports its bundled, otherwise unexported `startFaceTimeTalkDriver`. The test plugin then starts that talk driver for the owner handle with facetime's own `api.runtime`, config and logger, from its service context (where the `facetime-runtime` service would create its helper RPC server). Everything after that is the plugin's code: talk driver → `createFaceTimeConsultController` → `handleToolCall` → `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent {senderIsOwner: true, runner: "agent-turn", thinkLevel: "off"}` → facetime's `runCommandFromIngress` (bundled-plugin owner admission). Faked: the native helper and carrier (no FaceTime.app, no injected helper, no call events), the capture helper (`facetime-audio-capture` printing its two readiness lines) and `sox` on `PATH`, and the realtime peer. The platform check is not faked: it only gates the `facetime-runtime` service (native helper supervisor), which stays off on Linux; the talk driver and controller do not read `process.platform`.

```text

MCP probe on the consult's grant: 38 tools incl. automations, exec, gateway, plugins, secrets, sessions_send;
  gateway config.get -> "Action not available: config.get"   (passed the owner gate; config reads are off on this surface)
[agent/cli-backend] cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 durationMs=2073 outBytes=19
Thinking level clamped to low for anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (requested off; preference retained).
"No API key" occurrences: 0     "cannot admit" occurrences: 0     mock provider requests: 0
```

Owner admission: a non-owner turn gets `gateway needs the owner's authority, and this turn was not started by the owner` before the tool runs (phone run above); the FaceTime consult's call reaches the tool. The earlier stand-in run (`evidence-e2e-surfaces-8711c7b5a.log`) showed the other side: the same owner consult from a non-bundled plugin is refused with `Plugin "vci-surface-consult" cannot admit authenticated owner authority for channel "unknown".`

**Pre-existing, not changed here.** When the peer delivers its tool call from a timer created in its `connect()` (the async context a provider WebSocket opened by `googlemeet.join` has) after `googlemeet.join` has returned, the consult fails before any runner is chosen: `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` → `beginSessionEffect` throws `GatewayDrainingError` because that request's root is already released. `beginSessionEffect` sits at the same place in the helper on `main` (`src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.ts:352` at `d7d546f29`), so this hits the embedded route the same way; the runs above deliver the peer's events from the test plugin's service context instead. File: `evidence-e2e-meeting-released-root-7f72cb5c7.log` (stub `claude`, no model turn):

```text
FINAL TOOL RESULT: {"error":"Gateway is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly."}
[vci-debug] GatewayDrainingError Error
    at new GatewayDrainingError (dist/gateway-work-admission-*.mjs)
    at beginSessionEffect (dist/session-controller.lifecycle-*.mjs)
    at consultRealtimeVoiceAgent (dist/realtime-session-harness-*.mjs)
    at async consultMeetingAgent (dist/plugin-sdk/meeting-runtime.js)
```

This is the known `main` bug described under "Proof status" above (#142610, #202915), with open fixes in #202979 and #142692; this PR leaves it to those.

### Meeting through the normal provider callback, with #202979 applied temporarily (Claude CLI, `7f72cb5c7` + #202979)

Same isolated Gateway as the runs above (`env -i`, private home, state dir, config and log file). Agent `main` is on `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` with `agentRuntime: claude-cli`, and the `anthropic` API base URL is a dead local path, so an answer can only come from the CLI. In the real-model run only the `claude` process gets the operator's `HOME`, through a logging wrapper on the Gateway's `PATH`. The bundled `google-meet` plugin runs its own code: `googlemeet.join {transport: "chrome", mode: "bidi"}`, its Chrome transport and PipeWire-Pulse backend check, the realtime engine, then `handleToolCall` → `consultMeetingAgent` → `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` (`runner: "agent-turn"`) → `runCommandFromIngress`. Faked, because there is no local equivalent: `browser.request` (a test plugin loaded through `plugins.load.paths`, with the browser plugin disabled, acts as a Chrome tab that is in the call with the mic on and audio routed), `pactl`/`parec`/`pacat` stubs on `PATH`, and the realtime voice provider and peer. **What changed from the meeting run above:** the peer now sends `openclaw_agent_consult` through the normal provider callback. ### Stub e2e (phone)

Isolated Gateway (QA gateway child, private state, mock voice provider, mock realtime bridge that calls `openclaw_agent_consult`), stub `claude` on `PATH` speaking stream-json and calling the real MCP loopback. No real model or provider credential.

| Claude CLI agent, phone consult | embedded run → `anthropic` 401 / "Couldn't sign in to the AI service"; stub `claude` never got a turn | answered by `claude-cli` in 2.0–4.2 s; 0 "No API key" |
| `safe-read-only` tools on the CLI route | n/a | MCP tools exactly `memory_get, memory_search, read, voice_call, web_fetch`; `write` → "Tool not available"; `voice_call initiate_call` → "This realtime consult may only end_call." |
| `owner` tool policy, guest caller | n/a | `sessions_send` to another session accepted; owner-only `gateway` refused ("not started by the owner"); `voice_call` still end_call-only |

Latency (gap called out in the task): the consult now goes through typed-turn preparation (session, model and runtime selection, workspace bootstrap) instead of a direct embedded run. On quiet runs with an embedded (mock) agent, base answered in 2.0 / 2.4 s and this branch in 2.4 / 3.2 s from media start to the final tool result, so expect up to roughly half a second more. Runs on this shared host that hit I/O stalls ranged 5.8–15.9 s on base and 6.6–8.2 s on the branch, so treat the numbers as indicative. Queueing: the turn queues only behind other turns of the same consult session (per call, per meeting, per FaceTime call), not behind the requester's chat, because the consult session is its own key.

prs.title: feat: add per-account proxy credentials with Shellgate
prs.body:
Related: #202751

## What Problem This Solves

Local reverse proxies can give people separate Basic-auth logins, but Bearer-capable automation needs individually revocable credentials too. Sharing the Gateway token/password instead authenticates clients as the shared owner rather than distinct proxy identities.

## User Impact

User impact: enable optional Shellgate to issue, list, rotate, and revoke per-account proxy Bearer tokens while retaining existing Caddy Basic accounts and Gateway profiles. `openclaw shellgate caddy` prints a maintained drop-in; existing Caddy configuration needs two imports inside an ordered route, not a separately maintained authentication service. Bearer-only ingress is supported too.

Keep HTTPS/private ingress and configure Gateway named-role ceilings: stripping client scopes alone is not least privilege. Nothing edits a live proxy or Gateway configuration. Tokens are not Gateway/device tokens, local accounts do not establish verified email/GitHub identity, and proxy revocation does not close already-upgraded WebSockets or revoke paired devices. Normal security/dependency review remains required before merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

Shellgate owns only random-token verifiers and stable subject bindings, using existing asynchronous plugin SQLite storage and administrator-scoped RPCs. Caddy owns Basic authentication/TLS/proxying; Gateway owns profiles, roles, pairing, and session permissions. No new core auth mode, custom database schema, external dependency, credential cache, or background service.

The generated drop-in hides verification, strips client identity/scope claims and consumed credentials, preserves HTTP bodies, and verifies WebSocket requests without upgrading the verification subrequest. Invalid Bearer never falls back to Basic. CLI output is declared machine-readable so diagnostics cannot corrupt redirected Caddy configuration or credential JSON. The complete production implementation is 292 TypeScript lines, including the 39-line Caddy template; this follow-up adds 48 production lines rather than another proxy implementation.

## Evidence

**Real Caddy 2.11.9 → built isolated Gateway passed on the source published as `496a124d3cb1d3edbd5ffe21824426a84aadd7b8`:** actual administrator CLI/RPC issuance; signed-device pairing; Basic and Bearer bind to one human profile; a service gets a distinct limited profile; forged identity/scope headers do not grant admin; rotation/revocation and cold-restart persistence work. The run consumed the exact snippet printed by the real CLI, not a parallel test recipe.

Four focused tests pass (real SQLite/HTTP plus lazy CLI metadata). The committed optional real-Caddy test passes HTTP/body forwarding, custom identity-header handling, WebSocket upgrades, stripping, no fallback, revocation, and a stalled-request abort with process cleanup. Multi-space Bearer parsing and missing machine-output metadata each failed before their fixes and pass afterward. Full build, targeted package typecheck/lint/format, MDX and diff checks pass.

[Hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203178#issuecomment-7066507286) of `496a124d3cb1d3edbd5ffe21824426a84aadd7b8`: **4/6 readiness, 4/6 proof confidence, 4/6 patch quality; no actionable findings.** It accepted the public live output as sufficient. The earlier follow-up `d994e8408304021d96c5fd93558b62ce75eaf80e` changes only the disposable test WebSocket server to an explicit 64 KiB payload bound, addressing the scanner comment; its real-Caddy test and focused lint/format pass. Production code and the live Gateway proof remain exactly those reviewed at `496a124d`—the rating is not relabeled as a fresh review of the test-only follow-up.

Independent source review also identified machine-readable CLI metadata and bounded test cleanup; both were fixed before `496a124d`. Standard Auto Review is unavailable because its installed helper is missing; this is not an Auto Review pass.

<details>
<summary>Actual sanitized Caddy/Gateway output and reproduction</summary>

Run on Node 24.20.0 with Caddy 2.11.9, disposable state and generated synthetic credentials. No production configuration or credentials were used. Published source snapshot: Git tree `9671c04922b61c1116f24519882c12f2d5c63df8`, integrated base `282121402940c47c87a68bf08bb6e66097818884`. Generated snippet SHA-256: `c9acfebb02e7c984e5a43cc3be128e15d9c1224e0de45f88fb5ce501873dc96c`.

```text
PASS offline CLI redirected stdout equals generated snippet; startup warning on stderr
PASS isolated built Gateway ready
PASS real administrator CLI and RPC issue credentials {"cliTokenIssued":true,"rpcTokenIssued":true}
PASS initial Basic sign-in admitted
PASS administrator Basic sign-in admitted
PASS Basic and Bearer preserve one human profile with signed-device pairing {"sameProfile":true,"basicScopes":["operator.questions","operator.sessions.write","operator.admin"],"bearerScopes":["operator.questions","operator.sessions.write","operator.admin"]}
PASS distinct service profile and admin-only credential RPC despite forged claims {"distinctProfile":true,"scopes":["operator.questions","operator.sessions.write"],"adminRpcOk":false,"error":"missing scope: operator.admin"}
PASS HTTP named-role ceiling prevents scope-header escalation {"basicHttp":200,"serviceHttp":500,"error":"missing scope: operator.admin"}
PASS private verifier hidden and invalid Bearer refused
PASS revocation refuses new authentication without claiming existing-socket termination
PASS rotation invalidates old token while Basic remains independent {"oldBearer":401,"newBearer":200,"basic":200}
PASS cold Gateway restart retains rotated credentials and revocations {"rotatedBearer":200,"revokedBearer":401}
CLEANUP owned processes stopped
```

The HTTP admin RPC adapter returned HTTP 500 with the explicit missing-scope error for the limited subject; this is an observed authorization rejection, not a claim of HTTP 403. The same operation succeeded for the administrator. Existing sockets intentionally remained usable after proxy-token revocation, as documented.

Reproducible committed proxy test (locally available Caddy binary):

```sh
pnpm test:extension shellgate --maxWorkers=1
SHELLGATE_CADDY_BINARY=/path/to/caddy node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.live.config.ts extensions/shellgate/src/caddy.live.test.ts
pnpm build
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/shellgate/tsconfig.json --noEmit
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json extensions/shellgate
```

The full isolated Gateway run additionally used the documented setup, real `shellgate issue`, `users.self`, `users.setRole`, signed protocol handshakes, administrator RPCs, token rotation/revocation, and a cold Gateway restart. It did not exercise inference or a real user's browser. All owned listeners/processes were stopped.

</details>

**2026-11-24 maintainer-preparation audit:** reviewed all current discussion (including the complete hosted review) and reconciled all 133 `d994e840` checks/statuses from the public Checks page, rather than relying on the 100-item tool excerpt. There were 60 successful check runs, 69 skipped, one canceled dispatch, plus three policy statuses: security review passed, dependency review pending, and the policy `ci-gate` failed. The separate [full-CI aggregate job passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44932774640/job/136941983691); its complete log records every selected lane succeeding, with no known-main-red exception. The [policy job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44932774104/job/136932877240) explicitly awaited maintainer approval. These are distinct gates, not contradictory test results.

A real main-branch conflict was resolved against `ff9c567e0c30099900c0b9f134abdda488593819` by regenerating only the two configuration-baseline artifacts. Current head: `ef6b7eb9d6770c10de5d86698068444a46572a05`. The baseline now retains main’s 2,671 core and 4,011 channel paths plus 5,714 plugin paths (exactly 24 Shellgate wrapper paths above main). No Shellgate production code, tests, custom schema, dependency choice, permission policy, Android code, or CA feature changed.

The independent `pr-simplify` pass retained the smallest complete stage: credential lifecycle, one verifier, and one generated proxy adapter. Production remains 292 lines; the three test files cover distinct SQLite/HTTP, CLI-output, and real-proxy boundaries rather than duplicate owners. No speculative refactor or proof-invalidating churn was warranted. After base integration, all four focused tests, the real Caddy 2.11.9 test, baseline generation/check, and scoped whitespace check passed. Prior full-Gateway, build, visual, and hosted-review evidence retains its original source binding; no new full-Gateway run is claimed. The November 24 interop comment is deployment context, not new Shellgate execution evidence.

**Remaining merge gates:** fresh-head CI must finish, and a repository administrator or active SecOps member must approve the existing SDK workspace-link manifest/lockfile change. No gate was bypassed or approval self-issued. The user’s additional re-review request is recorded; no duplicate request was posted.

Not claimed: production deployment, Android changes, external EDGE/TLS validation, real-user browser login, or inference.

### Clean artwork comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Shellgate before: missing package artwork](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02ff1644-a369-4683-bd4d-0b952ffd85e8) | ![Shellgate after: packaged identity artwork](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f7a4908a-5437-4b2e-b062-61ca34834567) |

### Annotated artwork comparison

| --- | --- |
| ![Shellgate missing artwork highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8572cfef-32df-42c3-acae-b39682ec2c3e) | ![Shellgate packaged artwork highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a67f398c-190b-4db2-bbed-095907b42613) |

Actual Control UI rendered with synthetic plugin inventory, matched 1200×900 dark-theme viewport. Before reproduces the missing-artwork state at `f092e957`; after uses the asset repair at `94b2790e` (asset bytes unchanged in the final follow-up). The UI source is unchanged between the two captures; these are not production screenshots.

Requested by Donniefi.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @DonnieFi](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/220c0918-a800-4d03-9de9-76bfe07ee90d)

prs.title: feat(vercel-ai-gateway): speak replies through Vercel AI Gateway
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

People who use Vercel AI Gateway for their models can't use it for spoken replies. OpenClaw's Vercel AI Gateway plugin only handles chat models, so text-to-speech (Auto-TTS, `/tts`, voice-note replies) needs a separate OpenAI, ElevenLabs or other speech key, even though the AI Gateway key is already set up and AI Gateway already serves speech models.

## User Impact

People who already use Vercel AI Gateway can turn on text-to-speech with the same key they use for chat. Any AI Gateway speech model works, for example `openai/tts-1` (the default), `openai/tts-1-hd`, `elevenlabs/eleven-v3`, `google/gemini-3.8-flash-tts` or `microsoft/mai-voice-2.1-flash`. When `tts.provider` is unset, AI Gateway joins the automatic provider order next to OpenRouter. Voice-note replies on Telegram, WhatsApp, Feishu and Matrix come out as Ogg/Opus. Nothing changes for anyone who doesn't use AI Gateway.

## Why This Change Was Made

AI Gateway has no OpenAI-style `/v1/audio/speech` route; it returns 404. It does serve speech through its native endpoint, `POST /v4/ai/speech-model`, which is the one `@ai-sdk/gateway`'s `GatewaySpeechModel` calls. The plugin now registers a speech provider that sends that same request: the same headers, a JSON body of `text` plus optional `voice`, `outputFormat`, `instructions`, `speed` and `language`, and a response read from base64 `audio`.

The key comes from `tts.providers.vercel-ai-gateway.apiKey` when set. Otherwise it uses the normal `vercel-ai-gateway` chat credentials: auth profile, `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`, or `models.providers.vercel-ai-gateway.apiKey`. The provider is declared in a capability catalog, so it shows up without loading the full plugin.

The response doesn't say what format the audio is in, and formats differ by upstream model (OpenAI and ElevenLabs default to MP3, Google returns WAV). OpenClaw reads the format from the audio bytes, the way the AI SDK does. For voice notes, Ogg/Opus is passed through and anything else is converted to Opus with `ffmpeg`, the same as MiniMax and Xiaomi. OpenClaw doesn't ask for `opus` by default, because only some upstreams accept that value; ElevenLabs, for example, uses `opus_48000_64`.

Accepted edge cases:

- Voice ids and `responseFormat` values are specific to each upstream provider and are sent unchanged. AI Gateway has no voice listing endpoint (`/v1/voices` returns 404), so the provider doesn't list voices. If no voice is set, the upstream default is used (`alloy` for OpenAI).
- Talk-mode PCM (`synthesizeTelephony`) and streaming aren't included. AI Gateway's streaming speech uses a WebSocket protocol, which can be a later change.

This is a companion to the AI Gateway speech-to-text PR. The two branches change the same manifest and `index.ts` lines, and whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

## Evidence

- The new provider tests check:
  - the exact request: URL, headers including `ai-model-id`, and a body with only `text` by default
  - the base64 `audio` decoded back to the original bytes, with MP3 detected and labeled `.mp3`
  - configured `model`, `speakerVoice`, `speed`, `language`, `instructions` and `responseFormat` sent as Gateway fields, with `[[tts:...]]` overrides taking priority
  - a TTS-specific key used without looking up chat auth, and the chat credential used when no TTS key is set
  - Ogg/Opus kept as a native voice note, and MP3 converted to Opus for voice notes
  - missing or malformed `audio` and 401 errors surfacing as failures
  - readiness from the TTS key, `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`, `models.providers`, or the chat auth profile
- All plugin tests pass (22/22). The plugin contract suites pass too, including the cold capability-catalog check for `vercel-ai-gateway`.
- Clean: extension typecheck (source and tests), oxlint, plugin SDK boundary lints, docs formatting, markdownlint, plugin inventory, config-docs baseline, line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check`.
- I checked the wire protocol against `@ai-sdk/gateway@4.0.154`: the headers `ai-gateway-protocol-version: 0.0.1`, `ai-gateway-auth-method: api-key`, `ai-speech-model-specification-version: 4` and `ai-model-id`, the `{ text, voice?, outputFormat?, instructions?, speed?, language? }` body, and the `{ audio, warnings?, usage?, providerMetadata? }` response.
- `/v1/audio/speech` on `ai-gateway.vercel.sh` returns 404 today. `/v4/ai/speech-model` returns 401 to a request without a valid key, so the route exists. `openai/tts-1` appears in `/v1/models` with `type: "speech"` and v4 spec support.
- **Live, real key (OpenClaw 2026.11.1, this provider loaded as a local plugin; OpenAI account out of credits, so OpenAI could not have served either result):**
  ```
  $ openclaw infer tts convert --provider vercel-ai-gateway --channel whatsapp \
      --text "Hi Nate, this is Clutz, speaking through Vercel AI Gateway." --output tts-test.mp3 --json
  { "ok": true, "capability": "tts.convert", "provider": "vercel-ai-gateway",
    "attempts": [{ "provider": "vercel-ai-gateway", "outcome": "success", "latencyMs": 1349 }],
    "outputs": [{ "format": "mp3", "voiceCompatible": false }] }
  $ ffprobe tts-test.mp3   # codec_name=mp3, duration=3.288000
  ```
  I sent that clip as a WhatsApp voice note, and the recipient confirmed it played. Then, with the active TTS provider set to `vercel-ai-gateway`, the agent `tts` tool synthesized a reply through the running gateway, and it was delivered to WhatsApp as a voice note.
- **Observation (not caused by this PR):** on 2026.11.1, `openclaw infer tts providers --gateway` didn't list the plugin's provider even though synthesis through the gateway worked. That listing seems to come only from runtime-registered plugins.

### Review follow-up (277984457)

- **Raw PCM for voice notes (ClawSweeper P2):** headerless formats (`pcm`, `pcm_*`, `ulaw_*`, `alaw_*`, `raw`, `s16le`) carry no encoding metadata, so MIME sniffing and the shared ffmpeg transcoder can't decode them. For voice-note targets the provider no longer requests them: it omits `outputFormat`, the upstream returns its default container (MP3 for `openai/tts-1`), and that goes through the real Opus transcode path, the same path proven live above. Non-voice targets still get the PCM they asked for, unchanged. Tests cover `pcm`, `pcm_24000`, and `ulaw_8000` on voice notes (no `outputFormat` sent, MP3 transcoded) and `pcm` passthrough on audio-file targets. The behavior is documented in `docs/tools/tts/output.md`.
- **Gates:** 26/26 `extensions/vercel-ai-gateway` tests, `test:contracts:plugins`, `tsgo:extensions` (+test), oxlint, oxfmt, `format:docs:check`, `plugins:inventory:check`, `git diff --check`.

## Result

`test/vitest-projects-config.test.ts` "covers each normal full-suite test file exactly once" passes again. `src/shared/session-unread.test.ts` runs in one project only.

## Cause

#204281 (`7986fe168800`) moved `src/shared/session-unread.test.ts` into `databaseWorkerCoreTestFiles` (it now reads the transcript through the agent database worker). The infra project runs those files. The `shared-core` project (`src/shared/**/*.test.ts`) did not exclude the list, so the file ran in both `vitest.infra.config.ts` and `vitest.shared-core.config.ts`. Every other scoped project that can include a listed file already excludes `databaseWorkerCoreTestFiles`.

## Fix

`vitest.shared-core.config.ts` excludes `databaseWorkerCoreTestFiles`, like the other scoped configs.

## Evidence

- Ownership audit (`auditFullSuiteTestFileOwnership`) on `main`: duplicated `src/shared/session-unread.test.ts: vitest.infra.config.ts, vitest.shared-core.config.ts`. On the head: no duplicates and nothing missing.

prs.title: fix(subagents): keep confirmed cancellations final during delivery
prs.body:
Related: #175837

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a cancelled subagent returning to provisional reconciliation when a duplicate killed callback arrives while its completion notice is still pending.

## User Impact

Once cancellation is confirmed, a late duplicate cannot reopen that cancellation or disturb the pending notice to its parent. This does not change an SDK, storage, or cancellation contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

The terminal-completion guard protected a confirmed cancellation only after delivery cleanup finished. Before that point, a duplicate callback recreated `killReconciliation`. Confirmation and notification delivery are separate facts: keep the confirmed result final and let the existing cleanup owner handle delivery retries. The guard still admits a new explicit kill intent and leaves provisional cancellation reconciliation unchanged.

The regression uses the existing lifecycle owner and starts with a confirmed cancellation whose notice is pending. No new scheduler, retry mechanism, or test-only production interface is added. Production delta: +2/−5 lines; test delta: +23/−0 lines.

## Evidence

- The new owner regression fails on unchanged main: it expects no reconciliation marker, but receives `{ killedAt: 4000 }`. The prepared Linux baseline has the same registry source and original test bytes as the PR's pinned main base.
- Linux focused runtime: lifecycle and sweeper-recovery suites, **288/288 passed** (62.03 s Vitest); wake-retry suite, **7/7 passed** (51.01 s Vitest). The new regression takes 4 ms. These runs use the source-identical main registry with this two-file patch; no timeout, assertion, or baseline was relaxed.
- The original uninstrumented Linux Gateway reproduction also passes with only this production correction applied to the prepared cutover: **12/12** in 277.19 s Vitest (285.75 s including wrapper), previously 9 passed / 3 timed out. Awaited-child passes in 17.517 s, awaited-parent in 16.762 s, and overlapping confirmations in 18.347 s. The command, environment, fixtures, assertions, and timeouts are unchanged. This is additional cutover integration proof; the independent lifecycle regression above proves this repair on main.
- Local and committed-branch independent review: **scoped-clean at P0–P2**.
- Targeted production typecheck (56.07 s), test typecheck (58.81 s), lint (16.17 s), formatting (0.69 s), and `git diff --check` all pass.

Runtime commands (Linux, repository-pinned Bun, one worker):

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-sweeper-recovery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-support.config.ts src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-lifecycle-wake.retry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose
```

The main-side Gateway comparison explicitly advances main's existing five-minute kill-confirmation window. It reaches the parent notification; its stricter cutover-only no-output-polling assertion fails because main polls once. That comparison is not claimed as an all-pass main fixture or as proof that the cutover Stop shard is fixed. The independent lifecycle regression above is this repair's red/green proof.

Gateway integration command (Linux, repository-pinned Bun, two workers):

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-server.config.ts src/gateway/server.subagent-queued-cleanup.product.test.ts src/gateway/server.subagent-stop-followup.product.test.ts --maxWorkers=2 --reporter=verbose
```

prs.title: fix(usage): show model attribution without stored session metadata
prs.body:
Fixes #198488

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing provider and model information in Usage session rows and exports when measured usage exists but session-level attribution is absent or incomplete.

## User Impact

Missing fields now use representative measured attribution without inventing a provider/model pair. Stored values remain authoritative. If one field is stored, the missing field is filled only from matching measured entries; if none match, it stays empty. No configuration, migration, or protocol changes are required.

For mixed-provider sessions, this fallback is representative metadata only—not attribution of every token or cost. Aggregate accounting and provider filters are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Initial row assembly only copied stored metadata. Packed overview summaries arrive later, and metadata restoration replaces report rows with visible rows while retaining their usage. One shared helper fills final response metadata after hydration/restoration and filtering/aggregation.

The helper selects the greatest totalTokens among eligible measured entries, keeping the first on ties. Eligibility preserves an existing provider or model. When neither field is stored, both come from the same dominant entry. Repeated application is idempotent and does not mutate source usage.

The response regression is a sibling test file because usage.sessions-usage.test.ts is at its line cap. It uses the existing isolated Gateway-methods lane. Documentation describes both representative attribution and partial-pair consistency.

## Evidence

- Base: 3ab80aba158a5c5488d9323f4352aa593fb9af1c (tree 7e4dc64cd2172b6045e63b7f35f5d38b5af13a34).
- Final candidate: 3ffbb5d752358a4b3500738ac7cc79fd4789f089 (tree 32cf975c2eb0b50588d8135fc10d5abc23516507).
- The Windows runtime proof below is supplied by @MertBasar0 and bound to afe57af5e5fdd7391263110cc8efd4dbb86a583d (tree 8393447bc9453ff991178b99a42920976a9189c5). Roboclaw did not execute those Windows commands. The final commit adds only 15 lines to one test file; every other repository file, including all production code, is byte-identical to afe57af5. The proof remains labeled with the commit actually built.
- Original RED/GREEN: detail, packed overview, and restoration failed on the pinned base due to absent attribution. Partial-pair consistency cases then failed on f303c818 (eight assertions across two tests) and passed with afe57af5.
- Final Linux verification: 53 tests pass across usage.sessions-usage.test.ts, usage-overview-report.test.ts, session-cost-usage-worker-overview.test.ts, usage-overview.test.ts, and usage.row-attribution.test.ts. Runner wall time: 22.01 seconds including preparation; attribution test bodies: 0.840 seconds. CI time is not yet available.
- Final test-file lint, format check, Gateway-methods test typecheck, and git diff --check pass. Prior core production typecheck and full-candidate review remain applicable to unchanged production code.
- Independent OpenClaw Auto Review: the full afe57af5 candidate was P0–P2 scoped-clean; a fresh review of the final test-only delta against afe57af5 is also scoped-clean, with no findings.

### Reporter measurements and explicit regression coverage

Thanks to @spacenet-Pop-OS for the [follow-up live-store measurements and requested controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/198488#issuecomment-6875408820). Their live-store counts, mixed-provider frequency, and client-workaround observations are reporter-provided evidence, not numbers reproduced by this PR's Windows fixture.

Both controls are in src/gateway/server-methods/usage.row-attribution.test.ts:
- **fills final detail row attribution from dominant measured usage without changing accounting**
- **fills final overview row attribution from dominant measured usage without changing accounting**

The existing **missing** case supplies two providers with 10 and 30 tokens and requires the 30-token entry's provider and model, while independently checking aggregate totals. The new **null-model-usage** case supplies totalTokens=0 and modelUsage=null and requires both row attribution fields to stay empty. Detail additionally asserts that the returned modelUsage is literally null; packed overview represents it as zero model entries and keeps attribution empty. Existing usage=null and modelUsage=[] controls remain. The null fixture is intentionally outside the current optional-array TypeScript summary type, with a localized documented expected type error; no production type was widened.

### Publication status and remaining verification

UI E2E passed locally on Windows as reported by @MertBasar0 below; this is not a passing CI claim. The inherited unused-export failures are documented rather than suppressed. Preflight found no competing #198488 PR. Main b9dacb674914f74b57155edc02cdd13f8f963486 still has the unchanged row assembly, loading, and restoration defect.

### Real behavior proof — Windows, built Gateway

A built Gateway answers the real `sessions.usage` RPC through `openclaw gateway call`. The Claude turns that create the session usage records are served by a **stub Claude CLI**, so no real inference runs. The RPC, the usage pipeline, session deletion and the overview projection are the shipped code.

Setup, identical for both builds:
- Windows 11 Home 26200 x64, Node v24.19.0. `pnpm build` of each commit from a clean checkout: base `3ab80aba` (tree `7e4dc64c`) and candidate `afe57af5` (tree `8393447b`).
- Isolated `HOME`/`USERPROFILE`, state dir, config and workspace. Model `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6`.
- Sequence: `openclaw gateway run` → `openclaw agent` turn in session K (kept) → turn in session D → `openclaw sessions delete <D> --yes` → `openclaw gateway call sessions.usage` with `{agentScope:"all", limit:100, startDate, endDate}`, re-polled until no row reports `computing: true` → the same call with `projection: "overview"`.

| | Base `3ab80aba` | Candidate `afe57af5` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Detail, deleted session D | `modelProvider`/`model` empty; `usage.modelUsage` = `claude-cli`/`claude-sonnet-4-6`, 2 tokens | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
| Detail, kept session K (stored metadata) | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
| Overview, deleted session D | empty | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
| Overview, kept session K | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
| Rows with `modelProvider == null` and measured usage | 1 of 2 (detail), 1 of 2 (overview) | 0 |
| `aggregates.byProvider` | `claude-cli` = 4 tokens | `claude-cli` = 4 tokens (unchanged) |

Notes:
- The deleted row first reports `computing: true` while its usage is summarized; the values above are after it settled, in both builds.
- Mixed-provider, partial stored pair and empty-usage cases are covered by the regression suite, not by this run.
- `pnpm deadcode:exports` reports the same three unused exports on base `3ab80aba` and on the candidate: `REQUIRED_ACTION_STOP`, `mergeNodeRepositoryPublication`, `WorkspaceTransferOperation`. All are in files this PR does not touch, and the new `usage-row-attribution.ts` is not flagged. So the `check:changed` red is pre-existing.
- `pnpm test:ui:e2e ui/src/e2e/usage-overview.e2e.test.ts` passes on Windows: 3 of 3 tests passed in 45.6 s, run with Playwright-managed Chromium (chromium-1248; the runner redirects `USERPROFILE`, so branded Chrome and Edge refuse remote debugging there) on candidate `afe57af5` after a clean build. The final head only adds a test case, so production and UI code are identical.

### Real behavior proof — Windows, real Claude Code

**Real Claude Code CLI 2.1.325 with a real `claude.ai` login and real `claude-sonnet-4-6` inference** serves the agent turns; the `sessions.usage` RPC, session deletion and the overview projection are the shipped code.

Setup, identical for both builds:
- Windows 11 Home 26200 x64, Node v24.19.0; `pnpm build` from a clean checkout of base `3ab80aba` (tree `7e4dc64c`) and of candidate `afe57af5` (tree `8393447b`; the later commits on this PR only add tests).
- Isolated `HOME`/`USERPROFILE`, state dir, config and workspace; Gateway env built from an allowlist, with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` pointing at a dedicated directory that holds the only Claude login. Model `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6`.
- Sequence: `openclaw gateway run` → `openclaw agent` turn in session K (kept) → turn in session D → `openclaw sessions delete <D> --yes` → `openclaw gateway call sessions.usage` with `{agentScope:"all", limit:100, startDate, endDate}`, re-polled until no row reports `computing: true` → the same call with `projection: "overview"`.

| | Base `3ab80aba` | Candidate `afe57af5` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Detail, deleted session D | `modelProvider`/`model` empty; `usage.modelUsage` = `claude-cli`/`claude-sonnet-4-6`, 14,073 tokens | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` (45,760 measured tokens) |
| Detail, kept session K (stored metadata) | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
| Overview, deleted session D | empty | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
| Overview, kept session K | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` | `claude-cli` / `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
| Rows with `modelProvider == null` and measured usage | 1 of 2 (detail), 1 of 2 (overview) | 0 |
| `aggregates.byProvider` | `claude-cli` only (59,546 tokens) | `claude-cli` only (59,919 tokens) |

Token counts differ between runs because they are real inference (cache reads included); the provider breakdown is unchanged by the patch. The captured logs contain no account email or tokens.

### Inherited Gateway CI inventory repair

The [failed CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43642589689/job/132593688319) incorrectly retained `test/plugins/deep-research-recovery.gateway.test.ts` in the methods inventory after [55b5905](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/55b5905ff83aed24f81dee5657e1ed39ac261b2b) moved it to server-isolated ownership. Candidate `a256a71dd8a164a5bb0556a27551835ca2d57640` backports @steipete's exact one-line [upstream repair, 491c2944 / #199304](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/491c2944f56ad7d6d9a561a17dfffcd42cab49e3), using the canonical `gatewayMethodsTestExclude`. Database-worker and server-isolated ownership, the separate execution owner, and coverage assertions remain intact.

Retained, source-bound Linux evidence (not rerun for this update):
- Actual CI base `d4e669de` without the Usage patch reproduces both coverage failures, 591/590. Actual CI merge `6faaf175c` reproduces 592/591. Both turn green with the same upstream line; patched-base planner/routing suites pass 276 tests, and patched-merge focused coverage/routing passes 4 tests.
- The candidate tree passes **278 tests**: 275 planner/routing plus 3 Usage attribution/restoration. Targeted format/lint, scripts typecheck, tooling-test typecheck, and whitespace checks pass.
- Historical replays retained a read-only `skills/github/SKILL.md` overlay; executable source and test inventory matched the named commits. The final candidate has no overlay delta.

This update changes only `scripts/lib/ci-node-test-inventory.mts` (+1/-1) on parent `a03eb8d3`; candidate tree: `0c9323a1b3fc796f22bcd355cdbab4a6e72e981a`. Prior Usage behavior, Windows proof, and credits are unchanged. Upstream authorship is preserved, with MertBasar0's co-author trailer.

**Review qualification:** @MertBasar0 reports a secondary Codex source inspection of this exact candidate, including the complete inventory module, canonical exclusions, Vitest configuration, coverage contract, and upstream repair: no actionable issue found. This is **not a successful native Autoreview report**. The first automated attempt timed out after 600 seconds without a report; the same-route narrowed retry could not start because the installed Autoreview helper was missing. Neither attempt is pending or clean. The earlier Usage review applies to the original patch, not this backport.

## Credits

Thanks to @spacenet-Pop-OS for the report, measured dominant-usage fallback idea, and follow-up live-store evidence linked above, and @MertBasar0 for the partial-pair correction and commit-bound Windows proof. All three candidate commits include MertBasar0's co-author trailer.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/87cebbce-53c0-4f08-93b6-077c21f9ae2b)

prs.title: docs(release): keep retrospective tracking in the ledger
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The release retrospective skill says each operator-default or P0/P1 follow-up becomes a skill, tooling, or issue change, without making the ledger's tracking authority explicit. That ambiguity contributed to opening a redundant beta.2 umbrella issue in openclaw/tideclaw#32. The instruction did not explicitly require that issue; the interpretation was wrong.

## User Impact

Release operators keep one authoritative findings tracker instead of maintaining duplicate release-wide issues. No runtime or published artifact changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Make `release/retrospectives/issue-ledger.md` the canonical tracker and link scoped repairs from its entries.
- Explicitly exclude duplicate release-wide umbrella issues, citing the beta.2 incident.
- Limit the existing shared issue to per-agent coordination linked to ledger entries, preserving its collaboration safeguards.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/tideclaw/issues/32

## Evidence

- Read the full retrospective reference and checked the narrow diff for consistency with its existing ledger and follow-through requirements.
- Author simplification: one existing reference changed; no additional policy file or tracking artifact.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check --threads=1 --config .oxfmtrc.jsonc .agents/skills/release-openclaw-maintainer/references/retrospective.md` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Documentation-only change; runtime tests are not applicable.

Remote ClawSweeper review requested; no local independent review per Tideclaw policy.

- @vincentkoc
- @RomneyDa

prs.title: fix(meeting): answer agent consults after the meeting starts
prs.body:
Closes #142610. Related: #142692 and #202979.

## What Problem This Solves
A meeting can join and speak normally but fail to consult the configured agent after the meeting-creation request finishes. This affects agent-mode talkback and bidirectional voice consults even when the Gateway is healthy.

## User Impact
Meeting participants can get an answer from the configured agent after startup. A genuine Gateway drain still refuses new consultations.

## Why This Change Was Made
All meeting consult paths reach one meeting consult entry point. It now acquires and releases its own independent Gateway work admission instead of inheriting the already-released creation admission. This follows the meeting-scoped approach proposed by @chelsealong in #142692. @LiuwqGit's #202979 proposes a broader shared owner for other voice surfaces as well; choose one owner rather than stacking both approaches. This draft provides independently authored coverage for both meeting modes.

## Evidence
- The owning-boundary reproduction failed on the pre-fix source for agent/native-bidi delegation and the bidi function-tool path, and passed on the fix. The tests exercise the real consult runtime and work admission; the model and session fork are test doubles.
- 35 focused tests passed across the admission, consult, and realtime engine suites at `4703b1588fef`. Core and test typechecks, targeted lint and format, and diff checks passed.
- Live Teams/Meet transport remains untested; the draft does not claim live end-to-end qualification.

## Worked on by

- @RomneyDa

prs.title: fix: deliver finished child results while siblings wait for messages
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Finished subagent results can remain pending indefinitely when a yielded batch also contains children paused to wait for a message. Restart recovery restores the owed results, but the batch never attempts delivery.

## User Impact

Ready results can reach the requester or settle through the existing visible permanent-failure path. Message-waiting children remain resumable and retain their future completion; saved child results remain readable. No expiry, schema, or protocol changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The frozen-batch gate in `src/agents/subagents/announce/subagent-announce.requester-settle-wake.ts:165` on the base required every surviving member to pass `isRequesterSettleMemberReady`, which always rejects `sessions_yield`. An ended message wait therefore blocked every ready sibling without a dispatch attempt. The killed member already follows the intentional non-delivery path.

Keep the existing dispatch owner and select the ready members once every other member is an ended message wait. The lifecycle failure fallback (`subagent-registry-lifecycle-wake.ts:338`) must exclude those waits too, so a preparation failure cannot consume their future wakes. Both paths share the liveness owner's predicate. Running children and pauses waiting on descendants still hold the batch. Overlapping cohorts retain the existing changed-batch permanent-failure handling and saved result payloads.

The change was rebased onto main after #200924 merged before editing the shared dispatch file. The simplification pass retained the two existing settlement boundaries and one integration regression; no new owner, timer, or policy was added. Production delta: +29/-13 lines; regression: +213 lines; docs: +4/-2 lines.

## Evidence

The regression models 89 restored rows, 68 distinct members in overlapping 33-member batches, the success/error/no-outcome mix, prior deliveries and unavailable sinks, nine message waits, and a killed child. It exercises real SQLite persistence/restore, restart custody, the sweeper, lifecycle dispatch, descendant checks, and durable settlement, with fixture session I/O and the external delivery sink replaced.

Red on base `38439333e1f49667c8fc7fe572a10637f36af211`: the first sweep fails with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called at least once`; the owed batch never reaches delivery. The same regression is green with the fix: ready rows clear their wakes through delivery or recorded permanent failure, saved results remain readable, and all nine message waits keep their wakes.

- 211 tests passed across all 18 sweeper/settle and affected lifecycle test files (157.72s wrapper).
- Targeted agents/sessions typecheck, type-aware lint on the four TypeScript files, format on all five files, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Codex autoreview of the full local candidate against the base above, now committed as `3a57f8426e625372c2d53fb3508e1182fb718297`: scoped-clean through P2, no accepted/actionable findings. Supporting owner code was supplied; the reviewer did not execute tests.

Reproduction: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-registry-sweeper-owed-batches.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. PR CI supplies broad proof.

prs.title: fix: show native notification settings in the iOS app
prs.body:
Closes #164557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings → Notifications shows Safari Home Screen installation instructions when opened inside the native iOS app.

## User Impact

User impact: iPhone and iPad app users can see their native notification delivery and permission settings and open the existing device settings pages. Browser/PWA and macOS notification flows remain separate and unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page already observes the native device-settings capability but did not pass its snapshot into the notification view. This repair uses that existing owner, shows a loading state while its snapshot is pending, and keeps missing status values unknown. Device links use application navigation so the native Back history is retained; modified clicks keep normal link behavior.

Upstream migrated the settings UI from Lit to Solid. This update keeps the current Solid renderer and ports the native-notification regression with it. Native notification presentation and capability-to-view props live in focused siblings to respect the existing file-size guards. No notification transport, native permission operation, configuration key, dependency, or generated translation memory changes.

## Evidence

Current tested head: `c326ed5fc8fc63d243f337ff928a9cca42304f5b` (tree `f7d308969f6204e5309accb9137dfac74b82069c`). This is a normal two-parent merge preserving the original PR head `d7bdb5a3c123b1db96eeb9322a42efeb0075df71` and upstream `5584b16af9109db5235f776cb1302093f6bf2f59`.

- The real Notifications route, ConfigPage, capability adapters, and rendered DOM are exercised together. The migrated test fails eight native cases against untouched upstream production; the Safari/PWA/Mac controls pass.
- Final focused run: **140 tests passed in six files, 8.12 seconds wall time**, covering iPhone/iPad, base paths, delayed and changed native snapshots, missing fields, ordinary/modified clicks, absent callbacks, and browser/Mac controls.
- Production Control UI build completed successfully in **18.94 seconds**.
- i18n verification, focused style checks, documentation MDX/link checks, formatting, line-cap/max-lines/assertion-safety guards, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent source review identified missing route-loader result narrowing in the migrated test fixture. Explicit route and result guards address it; the final focused rerun and fresh canonical P0–P2 autoreview passed without remaining actionable findings.

**Outstanding verification:** Physical iPhone QA and inspected before/after screenshots remain unavailable. The DOM tests provide synthetic bridge-contract evidence and do not establish native-device or visual behavior. Production UI typechecking, a reduced focused typecheck, and typed lint were terminated with exit 137/SIGKILL without source diagnostics; those gates are not claimed green. Full repository tests have not run, and current-head hosted CI is not yet verified. This remains a draft pending those checks and the required native/visual evidence.

Checks ran on Node 24.19.0 through the repository wrappers. Dependencies were installed with the frozen lockfile using the environment's pnpm 11.25.0. The pinned pnpm 12.9.0 install was attempted but could not open its store operation lock on this host's read-only filesystem; this tooling limitation remains explicit.

Codex generated the change and performed the code review and automated checks described above; no human review is claimed.

Focused command:

```sh
cd ui
node ../scripts/run-node-package-bin.mts vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/pages/config/config-page.notifications.test.tsx src/pages/config/config-page.test.ts src/pages/config/notifications-section.test.tsx src/app/native-notifications.test.ts src/app/native-device-settings.test.ts src/app/web-push.test.ts --project unit --maxWorkers=1
```

prs.title: fix: let setup verify Codex without a runtime override
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/193115

## What Problem This Solves

I am fixing setup rejecting a successful inference check when the agent uses an implicitly selected Codex runtime. Dan hit this while setting up Gmail reconnect cards with `openai/gpt-6-astra`: setup reported that the verified owner changed even though the runtime had not changed.

## User Impact

Setup can accept an unchanged implicit Codex execution without requiring a runtime pin. Legitimate fallback to OpenClaw remains available, and actual owner or artifact changes still reject verification. No configuration migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

I now prepare the selected runtime plugins before capturing ownership and use the existing availability decision to identify the implicit runtime owner. I apply that ordering to verification and activation. Explicit verified execution stays pinned, and I leave the strict owner and artifact comparisons unchanged.

On main, the initial snapshot omits Codex when no override is present. The successful Codex execution includes it, so the comparison rejects an unchanged runtime. This head captures the effective owner before the probe instead of treating an absent override as an absent runtime owner.

[#193139](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193139) was closed as "not reachable" because the default probe's 256-token cap caused implicit Codex to fall back to OpenClaw. Later that day, [#193467](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193467), commit [7d6167760550](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7d6167760550edb543b7d7be3e7a42ba00669f99), deliberately removed the probe-specific output caps. That removes the reason given for dismissing the mismatch when the probe actually selects Codex.

## Evidence

### Live gateway result

Dan reported the following live check on a real gateway, with real `gpt-6-astra` turns through the agent setup tool path. I did not run these live turns myself.

| Version or case | Configured owners | Selected owners | Observed result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Main baseline `7866e72` | `[openai]` | `[codex, openai]` | Delegated setup tool returned the owner mismatch error |
| Patched `57a0abd` | `[codex, openai]` | `[codex, openai]` | Tool returned no error |
| Patched, Codex runtime off | `[openai]` | `[openai]` | Model call completed; tool returned no error |

The reported patched commit is `57a0abdd81f6cda590000575f13d0a7e91103625`, based on `7866e72c5d82556fb1ea9083a965ac6470329bf7`. Its patch SHA-256 is `097f334172dfe892bed6a7b9a9189026a8d0330a3be35ce0c0dfa909d4680959`. I verified that the source patch is unchanged before publication. These results establish the reported setup-tool flow, not an unreported Gmail reconnect or upgrade test.

### Local checks

I reran 219 targeted tests across eight files before publication: 62 unit tests and 157 infrastructure tests, all passing. The new six-case regression uses production runtime selection, owner discovery, binding comparison, and physical file hashing. It covers warm and cold implicit Codex, unsupported and unavailable runtime fallback, manifest-owner changes, and source-byte changes. Plugin registration, credentials, and model responses in those tests are fixtures.

On unchanged base production code, the final regression produced 4 failures, 2 passes, and 14 skips. The four Codex cases fail the required initial-owner assertion because Codex is missing; both fallback cases pass.

I also reran production and services-test typechecks, changed-file lint, formatting, and `git diff --check`; all passed. Auto Review previously returned `scoped-clean` for the unchanged source patch using `openai/gpt-6.2-sol` at P0 scope. That is not a claim of a broader review or CI result.

<details>
<summary>Targeted test command</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/system-agent/setup-inference-turn.test.ts src/system-agent/verified-inference.test.ts src/system-agent/inference-route-runtime.test.ts src/system-agent/setup-inference.provider-install-owner.test.ts src/system-agent/setup-inference-activate.test.ts src/system-agent/setup-inference-error-reporting.test.ts src/system-agent/inference-route.test.ts src/agents/harness/selection.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

</details>

### Simplification against main

I reran pr-simplify on the complete main-to-head diff. It removed nothing further. The change removes the assumption that no explicit override means no runtime owner, reuses existing preparation and selection owners, and retains the distinct cold-load, fallback, and drift checks. Relative to the main merge base, production changes are +61/-25 lines and tests are +175/-0 lines across four files. I did not run the full repository suite or an upgrade test.

## Contributor credit

Reported and live-checked by @daniel-lxs (Dan Riccio). Earlier investigation is recorded in #193115 and #193139.

Co-authored-by: daniel-lxs <57051444+daniel-lxs@users.noreply.github.com>

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren't public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-t_imb4fi)

prs.title: fix: keep OpenAI account usage rows steady while loading
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening the OpenAI provider card showed a separate loading message for every subscription. The quota rows then appeared as accounts responded, moving the values people were trying to compare.

## User Impact

The grid reserves room for the 5-hour, weekly, and credit readings with neutral placeholders. Accounts fill in independently, and a refresh keeps the last reading visible. A missing credit balance is not shown as zero. No new quota window is implied once loading finishes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The loading layout now follows the shape of the finished grid, with one accessible loading status rather than one per email. Actual errors remain tied to the account. The change is limited to the Control UI and its tests; usage requests, account priority, billing, and fallback are unchanged.

## Evidence

The cold, partial, complete, and refresh states retained identical cell positions and dimensions at 400, 820, and 1280 px for the common 5h/Week case. Seven Chromium cases and 35 focused UI tests passed with synthetic subscriptions, including omitted or additional windows, credits-only readings, zero versus missing balances, partial/all failures, retry, and reduced motion. Typechecks, targeted lint, stylelint, formatting and the base-relative CSS budget passed. The local automated reviewer could not run in its read-only sandbox; no clean automated review is claimed.

Follow-up to #202324.

Contributor: @jesse-merhi

prs.title: fix(release): apply approved waivers during receipt recovery
prs.body:
Supersedes #204293 (same change plus the CI fixes; the publisher opened a new branch instead of updating that one).

## What Problem This Solves

Receipt-only release recovery stopped on a retired empty publication-plan input and had no way to apply later operator-approved waivers without changing the original qualification identity.

## User Impact

Release operators can apply separately admitted, signed waivers to already-retained qualification attempts without rerunning children or rewriting their raw results. Receipt recovery never dispatches qualification jobs as a fallback; missing evidence or unwaived failures block. Fresh qualification stays a separate, explicit operation. No runtime behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original admission still owns candidate, child provenance, coverage, baselines, and artifacts. A separate admission can supply only appended ledger grants scoped to the original candidate version and selected attempts. Recovery and the publisher both verify that relationship and recheck the retained receipts.

The later waiver admission is a second operator grant. Recovery carries it in its authenticated evidence, and the publication authority record retains it next to the original admission, so carrier-backed publication commands (for example plugin `consume`/`authorize`) recheck both operators' current grants when they start, not just the original one.

## Changes since #204293

- Shared release evidence test fixtures implement the new `getCommit` and `resolveQualificationAdmissionDescriptor` client reads (fixes `check-test-types-core-2`/`-3`).
- Recovery test narrows `params.descriptor` before reading `runId`.
- Recovery always passes the selected waiver policy to child reuse; the unwaived-failure test asserts the child-reuse policy error.
- `RELEASING.md` no longer says receipt recovery is retired; `evidence.md` states recovery never dispatches jobs.
- ClawSweeper P1: `authenticateReceiptRecovery` returns `policyAdmission`; `candidateArtifactAuthorityRecord` records `policy: { descriptor, admission }` (and refuses a recovery manifest that names a policy admission it did not authenticate); `revalidateCandidateArtifactAuthority` rechecks it.

## Evidence

- Hosted recovery `45292736951` reproduced the old-plan mismatch against the original attempt.
- A read-only check against the original five receipts matched all 28 exact grants; the original failed attempts remain failed. Separate hosted policy admission `45294805585` passed; it started no qualification or package preparation jobs.
- Regression (distinct original and waiver operators): the publication authority record from strict consumption carries the waiver admission, and revoking only the waiver operator's permission makes carrier revalidation fail. Red without the fix (`expected undefined to deeply equal …`), green with it.
- Affected suites (receipt recovery, release-ci-summary, waivers, evidence consumption, qualification summary, ClawHub postpublish, Docker artifacts, evidence validation): 367/367. `release-publish-preflight-evidence` fails 8 cases locally only because its fake `gh` script is written under this checkout's ESM-typed tmp dir (`require is not defined`); unrelated, hosted shards cover it.
- `tsrs` on `tsconfig.scripts.json`, `tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json`, and `tsconfig.test.root.tooling.json`: no `scripts/` or `test/scripts/` errors (remaining output is shared-install extension module resolution noise). Lint, format, `git diff --check` pass.

## Worked on by

- @vincentkoc
- @RomneyDa
