prs.title: refactor: drop the admitted operator authority re-check and the lifetime ratchet (R6z)
prs.body:
## Problem

AGENTS.md says to check authority once, when work starts. The admitted operator authority (`AdmittedRunOperatorAuthority`) still carried a mid-run re-check member, `assertCurrent`, plus `onModelPolicyChanged`, a mid-run model-policy revocation hook. About 60 production readers called `assertCurrent()` in the middle of started runs, requests and queued work, and the constructor latched any failure into the run's signal. A started run could still be refused after a permission, role or profile change. The lifetime-check ratchet (`scripts/check-lifetime-check-ratchet.mts`) only kept the count from growing; it is now at zero and protects nothing.

## Fix

This is the last one-admission PR (R6z).

- `AdmittedRunOperatorAuthority` loses `assertCurrent` and `onModelPolicyChanged`. `createAdmittedRunOperatorAuthority` no longer composes or latches a re-check: its `signal` is the source signal (Stop) only. `bindOperatorModelExecution` keeps release and Stop, and no longer re-runs the policy on change.
- Every reader the compiler listed is deleted. Stop reads its own signal (`signal.throwIfAborted()`). Data fences keep reading their own data: owner, generation, writer lease, run occurrence, released/closed flags, request lifetime, commit guards, the cron delivery fence (`scheduledAutomation.deliveryAttemptFence`) and the cron control-edit compare (`retainCronControlSource`).
- `SessionControllerSourceAdapter.authority.assertCurrent` becomes optional. Non-operator producers keep their fence there. An operator authority passed there carries only Stop.
- The retired-cron-delivery fence moves off the operator authority. A queued follow-up checks `scheduledAutomation.deliveryAttemptFence` before claim, in the same place where the removed `operatorAuthority.assertCurrent()` was. The follow-up runner withholds a run on `CronDeliveryAuthorityError` itself: it records the run and does not replay it. Before, it learned this only from the authority's latched signal.
- The ratchet script, its test and its `ci-baseline-ratchets` entry are deleted.
- New lint rule `openclaw-boundaries/no-operator-permission-read` (in `config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json`, which the `lint:no-chained-type-assertions` boundary lane runs over `src`, `extensions` and `packages`). Only the files named in `scripts/lib/no-operator-permission-read.mjs` may reference the live permission readers `resolveOperatorRolePolicy`, `resolveOperatorRolePolicyForAssignment`, `resolveOperatorRolePolicyForProfile`, `resolveOperatorRoleSelection`, `authorizeCurrentOperatorRoleScopes`, `onOperatorRolePolicyChanged` and `captureResidentUserProfileAccess`. The allowlist is the owners and the work-start files that use them today (63 files). It only shrinks: new code takes scopes, role and policy from the admitted operator authority. The planted fixture `test/fixtures/oxlint-boundary-guards/operator-permission-recheck-violation.ts` (named import, namespace member, lazy import) fails the rule (4 reports).
- Parked item from R6c4a: the worktree publication message reads "The GitHub publication worktree changed" instead of "...authority changed". The test fixture URL that had fake credentials is now `https://example.test/repo?...`.
- The last three refusal strings in production code are gone:
  - `agent-run-user-turn.ts`: the requester-owner re-read from live config (`assertRequesterCurrent`, "Requester owner authority changed") is deleted, along with its admission-phase and execution-phase plumbing. The owner decision is made once, when the turn starts. The `subagent-spawn.production-boundary` expectation "removing the spawning owner after admission must stop that dispatch" is deleted with it.
  - `acp/runtime/session-meta-resume-authorization.ts`: this is a data fence (the source session's facts changed). It is reworded to "The ACP resume source session changed".
  - `cron-creator-authority-grant.ts`: the run-scoped grant ends with its run, scope, operation or management deadline. It is reworded to "This run's MCP cron access has ended".
- `scripts/perf/*-measure.ts`: removed the `assertCurrent` counters and the source-authority revocation proof, which measured the deleted mid-run re-check.

Production code: 86 files, +82 / −313. Scripts, config and lint test: +138 / −242.

### Decisions

- Lint rule shape (Fable 5.2): an import/reference boundary on the live readers, with exact files listed. A rule that bans the name `assertCurrent` would be wrong, because ~150 data-owner authorities use that name. The refusal-string ban would only bring the deleted ratchet back as a wording check. Accepted risk: an allowed work-start file can still call a reader twice. Review owns that.
- `src/cron/service.restart-delivery.test.ts` "automation=false" row deleted. Only the fixture put the delivery fence on the operator authority. In production the queued authority comes from `decideOperatorAdmission`, whose `assertCurrent` was always a no-op. The real carrier is `scheduledAutomation.deliveryAttemptFence`, and that case stays.
- Accepted edge: a queued chat input's `requesterProfile.isCurrent` is now `true` for the life of the dispatch. Before, it turned false after the admitted source was released. It only selects the requester attribution prefix.
- Accepted edge: if a completion cohort settles between the steering preparation and the queue commit, the human correction now reports `failed` with the policy-mismatch error. Before, it reported `rejected: tool_authority_mismatch`. The message is still refused visibly, and the race window is a few milliseconds.
- Known follow-up, not done here: a cron creator grant can still be refused when consumed after its issuing device or channel owner is revoked during the run, because the grant's `isCurrent` producers still read the device and owner lifetime. Only the wording changed in this PR. Removing those producers is a separate cut in the cron grant plumbing.

## User impact

A started run, request, queued start, tool call, model execution or scheduled job finishes after a permission, role, profile or model-policy change. The next request uses the new permissions. Stop still cancels. Data fences still refuse stale writes.

## Tests

Deleted, because each asserts a refusal after a mid-run permission, role, profile or model-policy change (full list in the PR comment). Stop, run-close and data-fence tests keep their condition. Test fixtures no longer pass `assertCurrent` or `onModelPolicyChanged`.

## Evidence

- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`: clean.
- oxfmt and oxlint on all changed files: clean. `pnpm lint:no-chained-type-assertions` (all focused guards, including the new rule) over the tree: 0 errors. `test/scripts/oxlint-boundary-guards.test.ts`: the planted re-check fixture fails the rule.
- Pre-push `ocx test`: all 215 touched test files and the importers of every `*.test-support.ts` file. The direct-importer set is over the 150-file cap. Then the failed files, plus importers of `followup-runner.ts` and `reply-agent-turn-preparation.ts`, and after the rebase on #204191 its 17 test files. Final reruns are green.
- E2E `one-admission-e2e/run.sh`: see the comment.

prs.title: feat(plugins): let manifest configSignals test a config value
prs.body:
Closes #197882

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin authors cannot hide a tool while its config flag is `false`, because manifest `configSignals` can only test whether a value is present. The tool is still offered to the model.

## User Impact

User impact: plugin authors can list a tool only while a feature is actually on, for example `"equals": { "knowledgeBase.enabled": true }`, so the model no longer sees tools the plugin will refuse to run. Existing manifests behave exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each `configSignals` entry now accepts an optional `equals` map from a dot path to a literal string, number, or boolean. It follows the issue triage: literal equality only, with inequality left out until a plugin needs it. The issue is marked as needing a product decision; this PR implements the recommended contract so that decision can be made on concrete code.

The contract, stated in the docs and covered by tests:

- **Missing value:** a missing or `null` path fails. Comparison is strict, so `"true"` does not equal `true`.
- **Overlays:** paths are read from the same effective config as `required`, after `overlayPath`. With `overlayMapPath`, each map entry is checked on its own, so `equals` and `required` must pass on the same entry.
- **SecretRefs:** never resolved. A path holding a SecretRef does not equal any literal, even when the secret has that value.
- **Older hosts:** they ignore `equals` and drop a signal that has nothing else, so the tool falls back to its other config or auth signals, and with none it stays listed, which is today's behavior. The docs tell plugins that rely on `equals` to set `openclaw.install.minHostVersion`.
- All fields of one signal must pass together. `required`, `requiredAny`, and `mode` are unchanged, so `false` still counts as present for `required`.

Generation provider metadata shares the same evaluator, so it gets the same field. Docs cover the field, its rules and a flag-gating example.

## Evidence

Real agent turns from the shipped CLI: `openclaw agent --local --model claude-cli/claude-sonnet-5-5 --json`, each with a fresh isolated state dir and config, `tools.profile: "full"`, and a small fixture plugin that registers two tools unconditionally:

- `kb_search`: `configSignals: [{ rootPath: "plugins.entries.kb-demo.config", equals: { "knowledgeBase.enabled": true } }]`
- `kb_status`: `configSignals: [{ rootPath: "plugins.entries.kb-demo.config", required: ["knowledgeBase.enabled"] }]` (presence only, unchanged control)

Prompt: list every tool whose name contains `kb_`, then call `kb_search` once if it is available, otherwise reply "kb_search unavailable". The tool columns come from the run's own tool list (`meta.systemPromptReport.tools.entries`, the tools sent to the model):

| Build | `knowledgeBase.enabled` | Tools sent | `kb_search` | `kb_status` | Model |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main (`92e16d25ce01`) | `false` | 62 | sent | sent | called `kb_search`: "kb_search fixture result: ok" |
| main (`92e16d25ce01`) | `true` | 62 | sent | sent | called `kb_search`: "kb_search fixture result: ok" |
| this branch | `false` | 61 | not sent | sent | listed only `kb_status`, replied "kb_search unavailable" |
| this branch | `true` | 62 | sent | sent | called `kb_search`: "kb_search fixture result: ok" |

On main, `equals` is an unknown field, so the signal is dropped and the model can call `kb_search` while the flag is off. The presence-only `kb_status` stays listed in every run, because `false` counts as configured. On this branch the only difference between the two flag values is `kb_search`.

Redacted model reply, this branch, `knowledgeBase.enabled: false`:

```text
kb_status
mcp__openclaw__kb_status

kb_search unavailable
```

(The Claude CLI runtime also exposes OpenClaw tools under `mcp__openclaw__` names, so the model lists each tool twice.)

Regression tests (red on main, green here):

- `src/plugins/manifest-tool-availability.test.ts`: on main 7 failed, 23 passed (30). Covers `true`, `false`, the string `"true"`, `null` and a missing path; `overlayPath`; `overlayMapPath` where `equals` and `required` must pass on the same entry; and a SecretRef that is never resolved.
- `src/plugins/manifest-registry.test.ts`: on main 1 failed, 65 passed (66). Loads a real manifest: the normalizer keeps `false` and `0`, trims paths, and drops non-scalar values, empty paths and a signal whose only `equals` entry is invalid.

Checks run on this branch (based on main `92e16d25ce01`):

- `pnpm test` on the two files above plus consumers (`tools.optional`, `tools.inspection`, `manifest-command-aliases`, `tool-policy`, `tool-policy-pipeline`, `tools-effective-inventory` (6 files)): 13 files, 286 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm check:docs`, `git diff --check`, `pnpm build`: pass.
- `src/plugins/bundled-plugin-categories.test.ts` fails on main `92e16d25ce01` and on this branch with the same message, `perplexity: expected exactly one purpose category`. The perplexity manifest has listed two categories since #195641; this branch does not touch it.

Risks: low. The field is optional and additive, and no existing branch of the evaluator changed. Older hosts drop the unknown field and fall back to the tool's other signals, which is today's behavior; the docs point plugin authors to `openclaw.install.minHostVersion`.

prs.title: feat(update): capture PostgreSQL stores while the Gateway serves
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

On updates that take a pre-migration image, OpenClaw starts capturing PostgreSQL stores while the Gateway serves. It reuses unchanged captures after taking exclusive ownership and captures changed stores again. For a custom service or foreground Gateway, `openclaw update --wait-for-gateway-stop <seconds>` prepares the update first, then asks the operator to stop the Gateway before activation. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/196154

SQLite stores still get their capture after the stop. The default managed-service flow owns its stop and restart. The installed updater must contain this change. The landing scope retains both the stop handoff and default PostgreSQL capture; this is not approval to merge before verification.

### What Problem This Solves

The previous updater required exclusive state ownership to capture PostgreSQL, even though each store can be copied from a repeatable-read snapshot while the Gateway serves. A Gateway with an external owner could therefore require the operator to stop it before staging and validation, extending downtime.

### Root Cause

The updater now records the generation and reuse digest from the same snapshot as each capture. Under exclusive ownership, it compares the current digest and captures any changed or unreadable store again. This usually includes shared state because the updater records its run there. Restore still checks the existing generation fingerprint. The reuse digest has a theoretical collision risk when two row sets have the same count and sum of 64-bit hashes.

The low-space skip runs before the final capture copies any data. An earlier online capture can already have a server schema and manifest, so the skip retires the schema through the existing capture owner before removing files. A failed drop preserves the manifest. Online server copies use the existing PostgreSQL prune marker, keyed to the online capture directory. A later online server capture can reap a marked copy after its directory is gone. Retained captures and restored live schemas stay in place. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201579

## Verification

### Evidence

- **Pushed head `edca9115`:** [all four PostgreSQL conformance shards, `pg16-smoke`, and the required CI gate passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44860715131). The published-driver job was skipped. Static checks passed. Earlier CI on `466ab69d` covered [low-space cleanup and manifest retention](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44853257676/job/136691538342) and [orphaned PostgreSQL schema cleanup](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44853257676/job/136691537808).
- **Pushed head regression:** the mixed-store test failed on `edca9115`. The online pass privately copied the shared SQLite file before deciding whether the PostgreSQL export fit. On a nearly full Gateway volume, a temporary copy is enough to exhaust space.
- **Signed, unpublished correction `2c2f8fd234e639593bddf3e890f2f5c85ad7d063`:** read-only discovery preserves existing PostgreSQL registrations without staging SQLite. The mixed-store regression passed. With an 85,880,832-byte SQLite file and 48,336,896 bytes free, the optional PostgreSQL export was deferred, free space fell by just 4,096 bytes, and SQLite accepted another write. The existing registered agent row survived. Focused PostgreSQL 17 compatibility, retention, and recovery checks passed.

### Real behavior proof

- **Package:** built `2c2f8fd2` with the repository's published-driver CI recipe. The tarball checker passed; the embedded commit matched the signed SHA. Tarball SHA-256: `5ea5bded0703937e3b2568d89d25697aad5f535b79966df8d5ac10df086b609a`.
- **Latest stable → signed candidate:** on a disposable Linux VM, the published `2026.11.6` build (`06afb10d`) used a real systemd user service and PostgreSQL 17.11 for shared state and agent history. Its installed `openclaw update --tag <candidate.tgz> --yes --json` restarted the service onto `2c2f8fd2`. The serving build was checked by authenticated RPC, not by version alone. A pre-existing shared row and durable chat message survived.
- **Signed updater → forced rollback:** the repository's failing-Doctor successor activated, then Doctor exited 1. Database and package rollback both exited 0. systemd served `2c2f8fd2` again; both PostgreSQL store IDs, the shared row, and both acknowledged messages survived in restored namespaces. A separate successful update by that same installed signed updater preserved all three acknowledged messages. On both candidate-driven runs, `/readyz` responded while the original service PID and an online capture directory were present; the stopped-state receipt explicitly recorded reuse of the agent's online capture.
- **Retention:** both retained capture directories had manifests matching the PostgreSQL state and agent store IDs. Rollback retained the replaced namespaces for manual recovery. On the successful hop, Doctor reported an unknown writer after the snapshot; the updater retained the recovery image rather than risking those later writes.
- **Earlier contributor evidence:** the [foreground macOS Git test](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/commit/7da4339c06f71c3ae52f30f67a16168c16cf7e91) reported survival of a write between capture and stop and about 287 seconds of downtime versus 941 seconds on its stopped-first baseline. Those timings were not remeasured on the signed correction.

### What was not tested or remains blocked

The separate full source build still fails `check-plugin-sdk-exports`: **5,396,987 bytes vs. a 5,385,536-byte limit** on the untouched base, the pushed head, and the corrected production code. The published-driver tarball passed a distinct CI recipe; it does not make the full build green. Independent whole-diff review stopped before producing a verdict. The correction is not pushed, so hosted CI and [ClawSweeper's P1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200294#issuecomment-6932530027) are still tied to `edca9115`, not the tested correction.

prs.title: fix(release): apply approved waivers during receipt recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Receipt-only release recovery stopped on a retired empty publication-plan input and had no way to apply later operator-approved waivers without changing the original qualification identity.

## User Impact

Release operators can apply separately admitted, signed waivers to already-retained qualification attempts without rerunning children or rewriting their raw results. No runtime behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original admission still owns candidate, child provenance, coverage, baselines, and artifacts. A separate admission can supply only appended ledger grants scoped to the original candidate version and selected attempts. The recovery and publisher both verify that relationship and recheck the retained receipts. Missing, changed, or unwaived evidence remains blocking.

## Evidence

- Hosted recovery `45292736951` reproduced the old-plan mismatch against the original attempt.
- A read-only check against the original five receipts matched all 28 exact grants; the original failed attempts remain failed. Separate hosted policy admission `45294805585` passed; it started no qualification or package preparation jobs.
- 252 focused tests passed across seven suites, including publisher consumption and the real child-reuse CLI fixture. Targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Standalone typecheck was not run to completion in the prewarmed checkout; hosted checks remain required.

prs.title: fix: Setup reports plugin settings applied while activation is deferred
prs.body:
Closes #197067

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Setup reporting a plugin setting as applied when retained work keeps the previous plugin configuration active.

## User Impact

Approved Setup edits distinguish successful saving from confirmed runtime application. Deferred edits say **“Saved; waiting to apply”** with the runtime owner's reason and application condition. Offline/unconfirmed and restart-required outcomes are explicit. No forced release or interruption of admitted work.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direct writer consumes the existing Gateway runtime-application receipt and preserves request admission. Setup keeps `applied` as persistence success for approval/post-write verification, exposes `runtimeApplication` separately, and records it in the audit. Deferred detail is redacted at egress. No new runtime owner, reload classifier, or model request is introduced.

Production delta: +87/-22 lines across five files. The 985-line regression allocation covers distinct persistence/approval, factory-retention/replacement, and managed-Gateway boundaries; the remainder is test registration/allocation. Independent reviews found no blocking findings.

## Evidence

### Current head: isolated macOS regression verification

At `4a6060fd6d1a4681770e8bc51216d43021e1c6cb`, the repository's official test wrapper on macOS (Node 24.22.2) passed **57 focused tests, with no skips**: 51 planner tests, one managed-Gateway test, one retained plugin reloader test, and four Setup writer tests.

The managed-Gateway run verified that Setup reported “Saved; waiting to apply.” The new setting was on disk while retained work kept the old setting active (three retained references). After the retained work released, the runtime adopted the new setting, with only one startup.

[Hosted CI for this exact head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45155780256) is awaiting maintainer approval to run the fork workflow (`action_required`), not reporting a test failure. The local result is focused coverage, not a full suite, lint/type check, or a fresh real-model run. The historical real-model and build evidence below is for earlier commits.


### Hosted CI follow-up: approval mock contract

Hosted CI run [43060033189](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43060033189) exposed three existing approval assertions that did not expect the new `onRuntimeApplication` callback (two Gateway cases and one chat-router case). Commit `5edc7d0fd3893c51575735901f1e187f1dfe7f4a` updates only those two exact argument expectations and their +2-line test allocation (985 total); no production code or approval behavior changed. Existing authority, refusal and single-write assertions remain intact.

Local proof for this follow-up:
- Before correction, the Gateway file reproduced the same two CI failures (25 passed / 2 failed).
- After correction, both complete approval files passed: **68 tests (41 + 27), exit 0**, through the official Vitest wrapper, 232.06s.
- Changed core test TypeScript graphs `services` and `gateway-methods` passed; scoped type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace and exact test-line ratchet passed.
- The first concurrent lint attempt was killed by SIGKILL, not counted as passing. Sequential retry with `GOMEMLIMIT=2GiB GOMAXPROCS=2` and `--threads=1` passed without rule changes.
- Independent review found no issues. The previous real-model/plugin/Gateway/build evidence belongs to head `03eb4825`; those broader runs were **not repeated** for this test-only follow-up. Hosted CI for the new head remains pending.

Reproduction:
```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/system-agent-approval.test.ts src/system-agent/chat-turn-router.approval.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '["src/gateway/server-methods/system-agent-approval.test.ts","src/system-agent/chat-turn-router.approval.test.ts"]' --concurrency 1
GOMEMLIMIT=2GiB GOMAXPROCS=2 node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --threads=1 src/gateway/server-methods/system-agent-approval.test.ts src/system-agent/chat-turn-router.approval.test.ts
```

Original tested base: `9b0588ab72cca4fedcbc12f64c69d6c38031e13b`; the following original evidence is for head `03eb48259a6e19be1c8cd57a3b424451ab407d8a`. That published tree exactly matched the tested staged tree. Original patch SHA256: `a9f439318ab76c2b22b138c4cc67db3c3518ce4e854e7ef3247c4a01fe198c86`.

### Deterministic regression report

- **Red → green:** the approved Setup writer saved successfully on the base but failed the deferred-outcome assertion, returning only persistence success. The same regression passed with this fix.
- **Focused consumers:** 4 files / 38 tests passed, including approval, final authority, schema validation, SecretRef and secret-store recovery. New feedback tests cover deferred, applied, unclaimed/offline, unchanged and denied cases, including audit.
- **Real plugin replacement:** production external CJS loader, prepared lease and actual tool factory. Unused and allowlist-excluded controls acquire zero plugin work. While a resolved tool holds the old generation, Setup saves the new value and reports deferred; natural release triggers production replacement and a fresh tool reads the new value. Final narrow test passed, body 8.647s.
- **Managed Gateway:** actual `runGatewayLoop`, Gateway client, agent/tool and public Setup command with same-session approval. A local Responses protocol fixture holds the agent turn. Disk becomes new while runtime remains old; release allows automatic replacement and a fresh agent reads new, without restart. Owned Gateway shuts down and child joins. Passed, scenario approximately 24s.
- Targeted production/test TypeScript, scoped lint, formatting, whitespace and exact test-line budget passed. These are focused checks, not a full build/suite.

Reproduce the committed behavioral tests from a qualified source checkout:

```sh
pnpm test src/system-agent/operations.config-application.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test src/system-agent/config-application-reloader.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_TEST_FILE_LOG=1 pnpm test src/gateway/server.setup-config-application.product.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Linux validation used Node 24.22.1, pnpm 12.15.0 and `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`. The standard wrapper prepares compiled subprocesses, so wall time exceeds test-body time.

### Real-model acceptance report (macOS)

An additional isolated acceptance harness ran on macOS 27.2.1, Node 24.22.2, with the same base and patch, a real managed Gateway and external probe plugin. It used **real OpenAI gpt-5.4-mini** through a loopback budget proxy that forwarded Responses API output unchanged; no fabricated model responses.

Procedure and observed results:

1. The model actually calls the plugin with `hold:true`, retaining the old plugin instance.
2. A **natural-language** Setup request, not a typed config shortcut, makes the model call `openclaw config_set` with `approved:false`; the host returns a proposal/needs-approval hash.
3. Same-session `yes` makes the model call the exact operation with `approved:true`; the host executes the approved directive.
4. The host reports **Saved; waiting to apply**. Disk contains the new value, active runtime still contains the old value, with four retention references.
5. Release the actual held plugin call naturally. The production owner applies automatically after approximately **3.36 seconds**; Gateway starts remain **1**.
6. A fresh real-model tool call with `hold:false` reads the new value. Final acceptance: **1 test passed, exit 0, 49.39 seconds**.

The first attempt's cumulative 400 KB budget guard stopped the final fresh probe; it was **not** counted as a complete pass. After replacing that guard with per-request monetary reservation plus actual usage accounting, preserving spend across retries, the complete replay passed. Two attempts made 16 requests total. The live harness was temporary acceptance tooling, not part of this patch; the committed local protocol fixture remains the deterministic replay. The host's status text is not claimed as independent model comprehension.

Its source SHA256 before path-only sanitization was `14958feb358825cb82291ee76cd4aa920ac3b9bf09643073ff01e87be51d66e7`.

Actual OpenAI `gpt-5.4-mini` Responses requests went through a loopback budget forwarder. The `LIVE_TOOL_RESULTS` entries were captured from subsequent actual provider requests, so matching `call_id` values connect tool calls to their consumed outputs. Repeated proposal entries are repeated conversation history, not extra writes. The host deferred receipt is deliberately distinguished from the model's own text.

The harness exercised the public `openclaw.chat` natural-language proposal followed by same-session `yes`, not typed `config set` parsing. After `release-held-turn`, the existing assertions required the held model turn to complete, actual config publication to reach `new`, old-instance retention to drain to zero, `gateway.starts === 1`, a fresh actual model/tool output `{"value":"new"}`, and that new turn to complete. The actual live source retained these assertions:

```ts
expect(activeValue()).toBe("new");
expect(instance.retentionSnapshot().total).toBe(0);
expect(gateway.starts, "Deferred application must not require a restart").toBe(1);
// After starting the fresh actual-model probe turn:
expect(await wait(newValue.promise)).toEqual({ value: "new" });
```

Completion lines observed directly from the same successful terminal run (separately from the selected event export above):

```text
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 39.46s

      Tests  1 passed (1)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 49.39s
```

The process returned exit code 0. First attempt was not hidden: an overly restrictive 400 KB cumulative request-size guard stopped before the final fresh probe, after deferred/release/application assertions had passed. A corrected per-request monetary reservation guard retained previous spend, bounded total measured-plus-reserved cost below $0.90, and allowed the complete second attempt. Across both attempts: 16 actual requests, 205,566 input tokens (156,672 cached), 948 output tokens; usage-rate estimate $0.0526869 including caching, or $0.1584405 at all-input-uncached rates. No recharge/fallback billing was enabled.

Scope: real model + real managed Gateway + real external synthetic plugin/configuration and real active-call/work retention. Not a production CRM plugin, UI/native-app, upgrade, full-build, or hosted-CI claim. No additional claim that the model independently reasoned about the host's deferred receipt. Temporary machine state and local credential file were removed after explicit user approval; this retained trace contains no credential, private local path, IP address, or private endpoint.

</details>

### Latest-stable data compatibility follow-up

**Passed: stable-to-candidate runtime/configuration/audit compatibility. Not passed: complete package updater or Doctor.**

Installed npm stable `2026.11.3 (847611d)` into an isolated prefix, started its real Gateway, and used public Setup proposal + same-session approval to save `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds=117`. This generated a real old audit row with only `details.path`, not fabricated database contents. After stopping stable, preserved its state and backup and tested a separate copy with the built candidate.

The candidate source tree `07906a5c316c19e2afced69c10e2e34eea026ce6` exactly matches this PR's head `03eb48259a6e19be1c8cd57a3b424451ab407d8a`. The checkout was base plus staged patch, so generated build metadata reports the base SHA; no metadata was falsified. Official runtime-only build completed in **3m49.9s** (runtime/plugins/UI, not declaration emission). The patch hash remained unchanged.

Candidate configuration validation passed, its real Gateway loaded the existing settings, and public Setup approved changing the value to 118. Read-only SQLite comparison verified every field of the old audit row, including exact `payload_json`, was preserved. The new audit row contains `runtimeApplication: "applied"`.

Selected original command/check output (isolated paths omitted):
```text

{"phase":"candidate","oldAuditUnchanged":true,"records":2,"newRuntimeApplication":"applied"}
```

Original candidate Setup approval reply:
```text

Updated agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds. Saved and applied to the active Gateway.
[openclaw] done: config.set
```

This compatibility run used a local Responses protocol fixture, no paid API or production state. It is separate from the real-model Mac trace above.

**Retained blockers, not bypassed:**
- The official pack step refused generated dependency-lock metadata: `generated package-lock.json violates pnpm-lock.yaml: node_modules/@openclaw/fs-safe-linux-arm64-gnu libc "<missing>", expected ["glibc"]`, with further fs-safe/proc-safe Linux variants. No dependency edits or lock/packaging-guard bypass was used. Therefore the package updater did not run.
- Candidate `doctor --fix --non-interactive` failed during maintenance snapshot staging: `SpawnBrokerError: Spawn broker failed before readiness: listen EPERM: operation not permitted .../resource.sock [task=sqliteSnapshotStaging.task ... stage=startup]`. One explicitly approved elevated retry hit the same environment limitation; retries stopped. The independent Gateway compatibility test used a **fresh** stable-state copy, not the failed Doctor state.
- Runtime build emitted nonfatal UI CSS budget warnings (gzip 319.3 > 318.9 KiB, raw 1647.1 > 1642.8 KiB). This is not a complete UI-budget, DTS, or full-build pass.

Reproduction outline (all HOME/state/cache/prefix/ports isolated):
```sh
npm install --global --prefix <isolated-prefix> openclaw@2026.11.3 --no-audit --no-fund
OPENCLAW_TSDOWN_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB=2048 node scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs --runtime-only --allow-unreleased-changelog --output-dir <artifacts>
npm_config_cache=<isolated-cache> node scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs --skip-build --runtime-only --allow-unreleased-changelog --output-dir <artifacts>
pnpm openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive
pnpm openclaw config validate
pnpm openclaw gateway run --bind loopback --port <isolated-port> --token <synthetic-test-token>
```

The two packaging commands and Doctor retain the outcomes above, not implied passes. On stable and candidate, the driver uses public `openclaw.chat` to propose the respective config edit and approve on the same connection/session. Both test Gateways stopped accepting connections afterward. No source changes or new commit were needed.


### Local official CI artifact build follow-up

**PASS, exit 0:** `OPENCLAW_TSDOWN_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB=4352 pnpm build:ci-artifacts`, Linux / Node 24.22.1, **7m35.5s**.

The official CI artifact profile completed AI/package declaration generation, runtime/plugins/UI, the canonical SDK declaration graph and public SDK export checks. This extends the earlier runtime-only build evidence. Final source tree remained `07906a5c316c19e2afced69c10e2e34eea026ce6`, exactly matching published head `03eb48259a6e19be1c8cd57a3b424451ab407d8a`; patch hash unchanged, no unstaged source edits.

Selected original output:
```text

[build-all] tsdown-packages done in 1m 8.3s
[build-all] write-plugin-sdk-entry-dts done in 3m 10.9s
OK: All 162 public plugin-sdk subpaths verified.

```

This is a **local run of the official CI build profile**, not a hosted exact-head CI pass or full release/global declaration build. The UI CSS budget warnings noted above remain nonfatal warnings in this successful command. Package-updater and Doctor limitations are unchanged. This follow-up did not change source or rerun hosted CI.


### Boundaries and outstanding proof

**Remaining verification limits:** full release/package build with global declaration emission, hosted exact-head CI, complete package-updater/Doctor upgrade validation, and the original production CRM/native UI remain unverified. The local official CI artifact profile and focused product proof above cover the changed Setup feedback contract; they are not claims that these broader checks passed. The runtime/config/audit compatibility proof above does not remove those limits. No production configuration or external channel was changed. The Mac acceptance was isolated, not the original CRM installation. Credentials, private paths and raw logs are deliberately excluded.

Patch application was checked against newer main `6a411d69ff64bd0f85c55256525cc427c3345e10` with no conflicts; this is not a test replay on that newer base. Existing production owners were unchanged. The expanded plugin/Gateway fixtures were not separately replayed on unpatched production; the original source-red writer regression is the red baseline.

Earlier fixture setup failures were diagnosed rather than bypassed: asynchronous catalog preparation had to settle before zero-retention controls; a direct-server fixture lacked the real managed recovery owner and was replaced with production `runGatewayLoop`. No retention or authority guard was weakened. CI routing/cost of the managed-Gateway proof remains to be assessed.

prs.title: fix: keep prompt-history diagnostics accurate between turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary transient-context turns can produce a false prompt-history rewrite warning after the previous attempt is disposed. Repeated removal of an old context carrier can also be misclassified and conceal an unrelated history edit.

## User Impact

Operator diagnostics and assertion-enabled development runs recognize legitimate replay while still rejecting unrelated history edits. Ordinary model output, provider prompt bytes, stored conversations and permissions are unchanged. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep comparison facts with the existing bounded diagnostic baseline, not disposable attempt state. Weak metadata carries removal facts with the exact converted request, including its first observation, without retaining raw payloads or changing another affinity's baseline.

The current-main refresh preserves the newer provider-prefix owner and project-move replay behavior rather than restoring superseded code.

## Evidence

- On exact pinned-main production `57dd84bd1e0f4b23159dec4e270edc4f6bd094f8`, both the converter regression and actual transient embedded-runner case fail for the original false prefix-change error. The refreshed repair passes **160 tests across eight files**, including all **16 prefix-stability tests**, unrelated-edit controls, affinity/reset/eviction and payload-collection cases.
- Actual `runEmbeddedAgent` acceptance completes four turns across retained and provider-opt-out transient modes, checking real outgoing carrier flags and stable prefixes. External model I/O uses the existing deterministic fixture; no packaged CLI, public Gateway-RPC, paid inference or cache-hit-performance proof is claimed.
- Core/test types, seven-file lint/format, pinned-main guards and whitespace checks pass. Fresh production and full-tree Knip scans each report zero unused files.
- Full `pnpm build` exits zero on source `dd0ea1214a535b5d149e274e312fe1a4163b9969`, with no tracked changes. It reports five nonfatal UI-budget diagnostics; separate baseline attribution was not performed.
- Full local ClawSweeper review completed on `57dd84bd1e0f4b23159dec4e270edc4f6bd094f8..dd0ea1214a535b5d149e274e312fe1a4163b9969` with no correctness or security findings. The source-only reviewer did not execute the validation above; its suggested packaged-session capture remains unclaimed. Earlier incomplete reviews remain recorded as failures, not evidence for this range.
- Published head `4241321333373679348a36d2ea4e17d030a24bf8` is tree-equivalent to that reviewed source, and the actual PR diff contains exactly the seven intended files.
- [Exact-head CI run 45294692944, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45294692944) completed **failed**, not green: `checks-node-changed-1` reports three unique prompt-cache scenarios (four route variants) at an unchanged request-count assertion, expecting 15 and observing 16. `security-fast` passed. The same four failures reproduce after reversing the entire PR delta to exact main `57dd84bd…`; the failed fixture and embedded-runner subtree are unchanged through CI's main parent `7986fe16…`. The scoped repair does not weaken this assertion or claim to fix that baseline issue. The documented protected pre-existing-failure landing route is selected, subject to its live authority, source, security and review checks.
- Simplification retains one comparison owner and removes the old attempt-state copy. Production delta against pinned main is +43/-31; tests net +165, including formatter indentation in the reused runner fixture.

prs.title: fix(templates): avoid descriptor exhaustion with many workspace sources
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw templates validate` and `build` reject a valid project containing many tiny workspace files when its file count exceeds the process descriptor limit.

## User Impact

User impact: projects within the existing file-size and aggregate byte limits can validate and build without raising the system's open-file limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Release each source handle after the metadata preflight, then read each file through the existing bounded safe-reader owner. The aggregate preflight still happens before reading contents; per-file/actual aggregate limits, hardlink and symlink checks, source ordering and digest inputs are retained. This trades a second sequential open per source for bounded descriptor usage.

## Evidence

Real CLI comparison on base `fc7f037d6b97f3156f50437e5bcd06332dfd2343` and the fix, using identical generated project bytes in separate isolated directories:

| Actual CLI invocation | Base | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Validate 16 sources, `ulimit -n 1024` | succeeds | succeeds |
| Validate 1,100 sources, `ulimit -n 4096` | succeeds | succeeds |
| Validate 1,100 sources, `ulimit -n 1024` | fails: `workspace_source_invalid` at source 1005 | succeeds |
| Build 1,100 sources, `ulimit -n 1024` | not separately replayed | succeeds; 1,102 archive entries and all 1,100 source files byte-verified |

<details>
<summary>Reproduction through the shipped CLI</summary>

After preparing the repository CLI build with `pnpm openclaw templates --help`, create the fixture with Node:

```js
// Save as make-project.mjs, then: node make-project.mjs /tmp/template-many
import { mkdir, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { join } from 'node:path';
const project = process.argv[2];
await mkdir(join(project, 'files'), { recursive: true });
await writeFile(join(project, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({
  name: 'many-files', version: '1.0.0', openclaw: { template: 'CLAW.md' },
}));
const files = [];
for (let i = 0; i < 1100; i++) {
  const source = `files/source-${String(i).padStart(4, '0')}.txt`;
  await writeFile(join(project, source), `Reference ${i}\n`);
  files.push({ source, path: `reference/source-${i}.txt` });
}
await writeFile(join(project, 'CLAW.md'), `---\n${JSON.stringify({
  schemaVersion: 1, agent: { id: 'reader-agent' }, workspace: { files },
})}\n---\nReference assistant.\n`);
```

```sh
(ulimit -n 4096; pnpm openclaw templates validate /tmp/template-many --json)
(ulimit -n 1024; pnpm openclaw templates validate /tmp/template-many --json)
(ulimit -n 1024; pnpm openclaw templates build /tmp/template-many --out /tmp/template-many.tgz --json)
```

</details>

The committed process regression sets a real 128-descriptor limit: a 16-source control builds successfully, then the same child process builds 160 sources and verifies 162 archive entries. It fails on the base and passes with this fix. Reader, schema, project and descriptor regressions: 90 passed, 1 skipped. The new test has its own exact 81 LF allocation; the descriptor assertion takes ~1.7 s, while cold runtime-worker compilation dominates the ~231 s focused run. The POSIX limit test skips Windows; Windows runtime behavior and a full declaration build were not replayed locally. Targeted type-aware lint, the official templates typecheck shard, formatter Node/Bun parity and the test-line ratchet pass. Full PR CI provides the broad check.

### Captured CLI output

Actual CLI JSON excerpts, with the large manifest/archive file lists omitted and temporary fixture roots replaced by `/proof/base` and `/proof/fixed`.

```text
exit 0
```

After (e3792884f6b5384d3fc3e59da07fa995c63b95ea):

```text
    "name": "many-files",

  },

PASS: 1100-file validate/build under nofile=1024; 1102 archive entries; all source bytes preserved
```


## Conflict resolution update (2026-11-18)

The branch now merges current `main` at `a6983ed7eeb7848bd744945abc6d2075fb955863` in hosted head `9dd1c1d9b8fe3583e818fb7e6ec457f80841f29f`. The conflict resolution keeps the current Template reader's HEARTBEAT size/UTF-8 validation and bundled dependency handling, while retaining the two-pass workspace-source lifecycle repair: descriptor preflight opens and disposes each source before the content pass reads through the bounded `sourceRoot.read` path.

Isolated Docker checks on this exact merge head passed for formatting, TypeScript syntax transformation, and diff whitespace. The descriptor-limit process regression was also attempted through the shipped `buildTemplateProject` entry point. Its child TypeScript loader reaches `EMFILE` while loading shared modules under the test's real `ulimit -n 128` before product behavior, so that run is recorded as environment/loader-limited rather than claimed as a passing regression. The existing pinned-head before/after CLI and process evidence above remains the behavioral proof for the original repair.

## Descriptor regression follow-up (2026-11-24)

The process regression now prepares a bundled ESM `project-build.ts` entrypoint before applying `ulimit -n 128`. This keeps the TypeScript loader graph outside the descriptor-limited child while the real control and 160-source Template builds still run under the limit. The child produced the expected 162 archive entries in the exact current-head isolated runner.

The prior unprepared command was reproduced at `nofile=128` and failed with `EMFILE` while the loader opened `src/shared/http-error-response.ts`, before product code loaded. The exact current head now passes the focused process test, formatting, and whitespace checks in the secretless bounded runner. The test allocation is updated to its exact 91 lines. Full repository CI remains the broad gate.

prs.title: fix: keep OpenAI account limits aligned while loading
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening Settings → Models with several OpenAI accounts repeats a loading message for every email. As the first account responds, quota rows appear above Credits and push it down, making it hard to follow a particular account.

## User Impact

The account names, common quota rows, and Credits stay aligned while readings arrive independently. Refresh keeps existing readings visible. An account that fails still shows its own error and recovery guidance.

## Why This Change Was Made

The comparison reserves space for the common five-hour and weekly windows, but only labels a window once a provider reports it. One quiet loading status replaces repeated announcements. Unreported windows drop away after all accounts settle; other reported windows are preserved, and a missing balance is not displayed as zero. No requests, retries, permissions, or routing changed.

## Evidence

In Chromium, four synthetic accounts returned deliberately staggered responses. At 400, 820, and 1280 px, the common grid kept the same cell geometry from its first painted frame through partial results and refresh. The original test saw four loading announcements instead of one. Seven Chromium cases and 35 focused UI tests passed, including absent windows, measured zero, additional reported windows, errors, and recovery. Typechecks, scoped lint, formatting and the base-relative CSS budget passed. Local P0–P2 autoreview did not complete: its read-only sandbox could not execute the installed Codex binary.

### Isolated Gateway measurements

**The loading grid passed; the page-wide performance and expanded-panel refresh gates did not.** We compared the unmodified parent (`76b4b183b571`) and PR UI (`98ce1b9792ee`) in Chromium against the same compiled Gateway code. Each run used a fresh loopback Gateway and browser context, four synthetic OpenAI accounts, three other providers with 24 configured models, and staggered upstream quota responses (1.00–2.95 s). No Gateway RPC was mocked.

| Width | Models ready, ms (base → PR) | Entry shift (base → PR) | Grid loading shift (base → PR) | Refresh-to-error shift (base → PR) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 400 px | 532 → 605 | .165461 → .165461 | 0 → 0 | 0 → 0 |
| 820 px | 572 → 573 | .093484 → .093484 | .001432 → 0 | .002864 → .004219 |
| 1280 px | 634 → 718 | .044129 → .044153 | .001495 → 0 | .002842 → .003255 |

Times are from in-browser navigation out of Appearance to the first frame with a laid-out OpenAI row and refresh control and no provider-section placeholder. They exclude the provider delay and are a **lower bound** for full load. Marks came from DOM mutations and animation frames, not Playwright polling. These single paired samples show both revisions miss 200 ms; they do not establish a timing regression. Native layout-shift scores are sums of all entries (including recent input), split at first grid frame and the actual Refresh click. On both revisions the settings-page body and model-picker text moved before the grid appeared. During staggered loading, the base moved account-status text; the PR recorded zero at every width. Both revisions also moved quota/error rows on all-account failure; the two wider error-state scores were higher in this PR sample, not zero. This is not a claim that the whole page is shift-free.

**Repeated refresh-to-error measurements.** Seven expanded-panel refreshes per width and revision (28 total) used the same real Gateway fixture and eight previously successful quota readings. These are ranges of raw frame-shift scores, including recent input:

| Width | Unmodified base | PR |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 820 px | 0.002856–0.004545 | 0.002856–0.004545 |
| 1280 px | 0.001416–0.003316 | 0.002202–0.003259 |

Frame-by-frame DOM measurements found the same movement in both builds: each of the four failed accounts added exactly one named error, and after the last reading failed the two quota rows disappeared, moving Credits upward **88 CSS px**. How many errors had already painted before the last response changed the score: existing error text moved with Credits instead of appearing directly in its final position. No score remained after excluding recent-input entries. The earlier single-run difference did not establish an additional PR-specific displacement. The UI still reports the failures rather than presenting old values as current.

**Refresh diagnosis.** With the grid expanded, all eight readings remained visible immediately after Refresh on both revisions, but all four fresh account RPCs returned credential authority unavailable before reaching the local Codex upstream. The forced catalog refresh and account reads start together; a separate diagnostic trace observed a pending credential publication during each refusal. No real credentials or authority bypass were used. With OpenAI collapsed during the same toolbar refresh and reopened **after** the real catalog response, all four accounts returned updated values at **400, 820, and 1280 px**. This verifies the fixture and recovery, **not** one-click refresh of an expanded grid. Fixing that inherited sequencing issue is separate from this loading-only change.

### Clean comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Four accounts have separate loading messages and no quota rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3f6035b2-0653-42c7-8502-a1732bc66d88) | ![One loading message and reserved quota and credit cells](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac75b47a-a0b8-4780-a2f4-cf995fa87ad8) |

### Annotated comparison

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Four repeated loading messages highlighted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b33080e-4de9-4af3-a486-2c3c0761e8df) | ![Reserved quota cells highlighted below their account names](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84299f0d-9e2f-44d2-8248-8c4a17a32ca1) |

Cold OpenAI account comparison, captured from the actual Control UI at 1280 px using synthetic Gateway responses. Before: `76b4b183b571`; after: `98ce1b9792ee`. Related: #202324.

Requested and co-authored by @jesse-merhi.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @jesse-merhi](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/d1ce1a33-86f6-49f0-9c77-01e4e873398d)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/eae05606-636e-4358-81cb-d1d1301b6816)

prs.title: fix: let update cleanup retry preserved database snapshots
prs.body:
Related: #202591

## What Problem This Solves

A temporary deletion denial can move legacy database snapshots away from the location recorded in update history, making later cleanup miss them. Separately, the new release updater can finish successfully without recording the readiness and plugin observations that historical cleanup requires.

## User Impact

Failed snapshot removals remain discoverable, and successful release updates can qualify as the later verified update for existing cleanup rules. Core success remains immediate; plugin maintenance runs afterward and Doctor remains advisory. No schema, permission or retention-policy change is introduced. Already-relocated copies remain a manual-inspection case.

The snapshot-path guard serves the surviving legacy package `--tag main` and Git-to-package conversion routes. Ordinary owned-install updates use `src/update/` and do not produce these `.databases` snapshots; their separate verification producer is repaired here instead. Repairing the already-executing shipped updater requires a separately scoped **v2026.11.7 backport**, which this main-only PR does not perform.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep failed deletion at its recorded filesystem owner. After successful background plugin maintenance/reload, the existing trial owner records actual core readiness and canonical registry error diagnostics through the existing verification writer. Unknown, pending, failed or canceled observations do not qualify cleanup. The deletion predicate, eligible-update ordering, directory identity and PostgreSQL-capture checks are unchanged.

The readiness observation is one-shot: an unavailable or unready observation can leave a successful update unqualified until a later verified update. No polling loop or new state owner is added.

## Evidence

**Draft: required latest-stable installed-upgrade proof remains unproven.** The observed stable package `2026.11.7` was published November 23 at 01:21:13.567 UTC; under the unchanged seven-day acquisition policy, that pinned package first becomes eligible **November 30, 2026 at 01:21:13.567 UTC**. The maintained Docker endpoint is unavailable. No age override, alternate acquisition or setup mutation was attempted. This is not a promise that the then-current latest package will be eligible on that date.

- The actual legacy cleanup-entry regression is red before the guard and green afterward. Fresh current-main validation passes **132 tests**: 71 successor/adapter tests and 61 legacy tests, with six existing platform skips.
- A second regression runs actual trial settlement, joins its background work, reads the persisted verification and applies the unchanged historical-cleanup predicate. It fails on pinned-main production and passes with the producer repair, without hand-seeding verification. Held plugin work, late failure, cancellation, unknown/error observations and independent Doctor work remain covered.
- Targeted types, lint, formatting, assertion/line/test-budget guards, documentation links and PR-base whitespace checks pass. Full `pnpm build` exits zero on `d068755b008539641ddcb4de98841aed236637fc`, with no tracked changes; five nonfatal UI-budget diagnostics are disclosed without separate baseline attribution.
- Full local ClawSweeper review of `57dd84bd1e0f4b23159dec4e270edc4f6bd094f8..d068755b008539641ddcb4de98841aed236637fc` completed with no correctness/security findings. Its required real-update proof gap remains open. The first invocation stopped on a transient build-generated file; only the subsequent clean-tree completed review is counted.
- Published head `991e1ff0e9600d58131cee5411b2bd0bdedf36df` must match the reviewed source tree and nine-file scope; exact-head CI and the latest-stable upgrade are not claimed complete. Applicable four-platform real-update qualification is also unrun; the update contract explicitly makes missing platform receipts a stable-release blocker.

Requested and scoped by @vincentkoc; builds on Josh Lehman’s database-snapshot cleanup in #202591.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion with @vincentkoc](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/7e40cc6f-f76b-4156-a406-f2952f2a9bcd)
- [Coordination](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/176703a2-b9e8-4c4f-9707-706441873d88)

prs.title: fix: report a missing Windows gateway recovery task
prs.body:
Related: #204233

## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, a logon task can remain after its `openclaw-gateway-recovery.exe` is gone. `openclaw gateway status --deep` reports no extra service, so the broken registration is invisible. `gateway install` only rewrites the canonical task and does not establish ownership of that other registration.

## User Impact

User impact: `gateway status --deep` lists that leftover task and prints a `schtasks /Delete` command only when the missing recovery executable is the task's only action. A task that also does other work stays visible with a query hint. Install still does not delete tasks. A recovery executable that is still present is left alone, because that registration belongs to the Windows package.

## Why This Change Was Made

Command markers only recognize gateway and node arguments, and the recovery executable has neither. Deep inventory now reports a non-canonical task when its recovery executable is missing. Deletion advice requires that executable to be the task's only action, which matches the package task contract. The canonical task and `OpenClaw Gateway (profile)` tasks are unchanged. An unreadable launcher is an inspection error and is not offered for deletion.

Preventing a new orphan during package uninstall stays with the Windows package owner. Companion teardown is drafted in openclaw/openclaw-windows-node#2306 and does not repair a task whose package is already gone. `GatewayPersistenceManager` in openclaw/openclaw-windows-packaging remains the registration owner.

## Evidence

Read-only capture on the reported Windows machine, 2026-11-23. The installed CLI was not replaced, and no scheduled task was deleted. The published text replaces the home directory, user name, host name, user SID, and package-family id. The raw capture is not uploaded.

Installed `OpenClaw 2026.11.10-beta.2` (`bbcf2a4`), Node v26.13.1, Windows AMD64, Atlantic Standard Time. `openclaw gateway status --deep --json` exited 0. The canonical scheduled task was running, RPC was ok, and `extraServices` was `[]`.

The same machine then ran the updated classifier and hint renderer, using the product's Task Scheduler query. That capture is the helper run. The rebuilt CLI proof is in the next section. The live orphan is a single action and receives both hints. A synthetic second action on a missing recovery executable receives the query hint only:

```text
scheduled-task-count 276
task \OpenClaw Gateway state=4 enabled=true actions=1 canonical=true
  action type=0 recovery=false file=cmd.exe
  classify skipped-canonical
task \OpenClaw Gateway {package-family} {sid} state=3 enabled=true actions=1 canonical=false
  action type=0 recovery=true file=openclaw-gateway-recovery.exe
  classify missing sole=true
  hint schtasks /Query /TN "\OpenClaw Gateway {package-family} {sid}" /V /FO LIST
  hint schtasks /Delete /F /TN "\OpenClaw Gateway {package-family} {sid}"
control-present present
control-missing missing sole=true
control-mixed missing sole=false
control-mixed hint query-only
```

A temporary copy of the executable classifies as present. The unreadable branch was not reproduced: denying read on a temporary file still left it readable by its owner, and a protected system path classified as missing.

Focused inventory tests cover the single-action delete hint, the mixed-action query-only hint, a present executable, and an unreadable executable. The Linux runs stub task discovery. The Windows output above is the native scheduler result.

## CLI proof

Rebuilt `70f7c978c00d9192e4caf5ba68c76ed43d5afb5f` (`2026.11.7`) with `pnpm build:runtime`. Exit 0. The proof process was `node openclaw.mjs gateway status --deep` and the same command with `--json`. The global install stayed `2026.11.10-beta.2` and was the base comparison only. No scheduled task was deleted. The state-directory timestamp did not change. Raw status payloads were not uploaded.

Build identity: source archive SHA-256 `4569f519a99d6a02052a27a1b0194311cf64e9bf87e9198aceb7a13ecc899e55`; `openclaw.mjs` SHA-256 `f59773629d9546b5c06aca6e97a566861b0ca976d07aa339af98b0331ce1936e` (24880 bytes); Windows `dist/entry.js` SHA-256 `65657bb2e87651c14b2bc1c4c667c5067b702f0ef75a52e2cd53bdfdfc92f10a` (12944 bytes); build id `2026.11.7-70f7c978c00d-2026-11-23T23-50-56.805Z`.

Candidate human: exit 0 in 20246 ms. One missing-recovery line, one Inspection hint (`schtasks /Query`), and one Cleanup hint (`schtasks /Delete`). The delete line is not labeled inspection. Inspection-failure lines: 0.

Candidate JSON: exit 0 in 19206 ms. `extraServices` length 1, platform `win32`, scope system, detail missing recovery launcher, sole-action deletion true. The managed service is `Scheduled Task` and loaded, with no deletion flag. RPC was ok. Inspection errors: empty.

Installed base, same two commands: human exit 0 in 22256 ms, JSON exit 0 in 21240 ms, `extraServices` length 0, no hints.

The live recovery task is the same user as the inspector. It has one quoted drive-absolute action, the default alias, and the file is absent. The stored path has no `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, so the inspector shell environment does not decide this classification. Both candidate commands returned in about 20 seconds, inside the 60 second inventory deadline.

Boundary tests, not induced on this host: mixed-action tasks, unresolved paths, unreadable paths, side-by-side aliases, profile-named tasks, a present executable, and a probe that never settles. `inspect.startup.test.ts` 43 passed. Hint-label tests 7 passed. Status gather and print 94 passed and 1 skipped. Doctor legacy-service tests 23 passed.

Pull-request workflows for this commit remain `action_required`. That is an approval blocker, separate from this diagnostic result. Offering `schtasks /Delete` remains a maintainer decision.

prs.title: fix(ci): select prompt-cache and compaction owner tests
prs.body:
Closes #204252

## What Problem This Solves

Aggressive PR test selection omits prompt-cache and compaction behavior suites when a change reaches them through runner facades or Gateway fixtures. Both #204111 and #204180 merged without selecting four tests that later failed on scheduled main validation.

## User Impact

Changes to these preparation and compaction owners now run the four existing behavior tests before merge. Their failures can surface in PR CI instead of waiting for hourly validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add bounded owner watches through the existing policy inventory. Include the current shared threshold and provider replay and payload owners. Keep the import traversal and shard planner as they are.

## Evidence

The regression is red on `57dd84bd1` and green on `3977cb51c`. It exercises aggressive PR selection for request-boundary, prompt assembly, prompt-cache history, compaction assembly, provider replay, payload policy and the shared threshold. An unrelated runner fixture selects none of the four behavior suites.

Replayed both historical PR changed-file lists through the production target resolver, shard planner and `scripts/ci-build-manifest.mjs`. Both candidate manifests list all four tests with `policy-watch` provenance. The counts below are tests selected and tests found in one executable shard each.

```text
Changed paths                        Base targets/shards  Candidate targets/shards
Request boundary compaction (1)      0/0                  4/4
#204111 actual changed files (31)    0/0                  4/4
#204180 actual changed files (10)    0/0                  4/4
Unrelated source control (1)        0/0                  0/0
```

- Tooling typecheck, targeted lint and formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- The three planner suites on the exact head reported 194 of 195 tests passed, including the full source-owner and policy suites. The one GitHub runner timing assertion fails with the same `120 <= 60` comparison on the untouched base. It was retained and is disclosed here.
- Independent review caught the moved compaction threshold and neighboring production owners. The patch routes the current threshold location, related payload/replay and prompt assembly paths, and includes representative regressions. The behavior suites themselves are unchanged.

Thanks to Ayaan Zaidi for identifying the missing routes.

prs.title: improve: reduce session row refresh work during bursts
prs.body:
Related: #202883

## What Problem This Solves

During bursts of session changes, refreshes can resolve the same parent once per child and rebuild a frozen child list whose contents have stayed the same. This adds main-thread work for active chats with large child histories.

## User Impact

Reduces the Gateway work needed to keep session rows current during an event burst. The serialized rows and published event order are identical in the synthetic replay.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resident reads resolve the existing logical and physical parent buckets once, using the same store precedence. The indexed lookup returns a single candidate directly. The row builder reuses the frozen compact child list when the relation reader returns its prior identity. Reads that acquire child entries still take a snapshot of the candidate IDs and resolve lineage after acquisition.

## Evidence

The regression fails on the baseline because a committed parent-label update replaces an equal child list. The candidate preserves that identity while still publishing the new label. Existing tests cover logical aliases, duplicate stores, inherited models, and ancestor delivery.

The performance run uses 15,000 persisted synthetic sessions across four physical stores, six loopback recipients, 100-row pages and 4,700 logical events paced at 470/s. The activity mix includes committed metadata updates, chat-delta presentation, live model updates and child activity. The real prepared event and list owners run in process.

In five alternating A/B pairs, median main-thread CPU fell from 1,719 to 1,663 ms per 1,000 events (3.3%, four of five pairs) and sampled allocation fell from 1,174 to 1,124 MB per 1,000 events (4.2%, five of five pairs). Baseline A/A controls were 1,714 and 1,526 ms of main-thread CPU, and 1,191 and 1,193 MB of sampled allocation per 1,000 events. The A/A CPU spread exceeds the whole-burst median change. Median event-loop p95 was 3.98 to 3.82 ms and p99 was 14.41 to 14.97 ms.

A separate stack-attribution pair showed session-row refresh at 89.5 to 69.6 sampled ms per 1,000 events and child-link reads at 38.2 to 21.7. Parent-reference lookups fell from 8.0 to 0.3 sampled ms per 1,000 events. The run includes synchronous synthetic writes and uses prepared Gateway owners in process.

Each matching replay preserved all six normalized event digests, all final-page digests, 28,200 FIFO deliveries and 600 list reads. The 81 focused Gateway tests, one Control UI browser test, nine UI E2E tests and `pnpm check:changed` passed. Codex autoreview found no actionable items through P2 on the complete change relative to `8b17822bec4f`.

## CI on the first head

Both failed test shards in [the first PR run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45286532168) reproduce on its exact main parent, `8eb7c5628a142575a2b2c5109a5ba71aba3ef3e8`. The failing tests and their owners have identical source blobs on that parent and the CI merge.

- The canonical authority profile and scope assertions expected older refusal wording. They fail unchanged on the parent and the candidate. [#204134](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204134) changed the wording and [#204270](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204270) repaired the assertions on main. [CI authority shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45286532168/job/138085005529)
- The owner and guest Goal cases intermittently receive the automatic Advance before the exec completion. Focused unmodified runs pass. On the exact parent, holding async target preparation in the test fixture makes both original assertions fail with the same prompt order as CI. [#167897](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167897) introduced the empty-queue decision while exec wakes could still be preparing. [#204187](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/204187) tracks the race and [#204265](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204265) owns the fix. [CI Goal shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45286532168/job/138085005777)

The first run also lost its baseline-ratchet job result. GitHub ended that job as failed without a terminal step record or available log. The same-head recovery run passed the ratchets and reproduced the inherited authority assertions on the branch checkout. The PR now includes main's #204270 repair. All eight PR files retain the same blobs as before the rebase. [First ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45286532168/job/138085004809) · [Recovery run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45291704038) · [CI on the rebased head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45293927258)

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the synthetic measurements</summary>

Use Node 26.12.1 from the PR checkout. For the baseline, save these six Gateway modules from `8b17822bec4f36582bf5e15743087b32fd3460b1`: `session-row-projection.ts`, `session-row-projection-ancestors.ts`, `session-row-projection-identities.ts`, `session-row-projection-record.ts`, `session-utils-projection.ts`, and `session-utils-row.ts`. Add one `--source-file` argument per saved module to run the same driver against the baseline. Give each process fresh state and output paths.

```sh
scratch="$(mktemp -d)"
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/sidebar-presentation-measure.ts \
  --surge --entry-surge --sessions 15000 --page-size 100 --clients 6 --operations 4700 \
  --state-dir "$scratch/state" --output "$scratch/output.json"
```

Run two independent baseline controls. Use `--repeats 5 --barrier-dir <dir> --side base|fix` with one process per arm. After both `*.ready` files appear, release one arm at a time using `<repeat>.base.go` and `<repeat>.fix.go`, in alternating order. Wait for each repeat's output before releasing the next arm. Repeat the series with `--allocations`. Collect `--cpu-profile` separately for stack attribution. Compare all six normalized event digests, FIFO sequences and final-page digests within each matching replay.

</details>

prs.title: test(ui): make the attachment filename fit check independent of installed CJK fonts
prs.body:
Related: #203711, #204247

## What Problem This Solves

Contributors get a red Control UI browser check from a chat attachment test whenever its CI shard also installs WebKit's system packages, even when their change does not touch attachments. The same test fails on a developer machine that has CJK fonts, such as a Mac.

The case is "exposes an assistant document download with its Unicode filename and ticketed URL" in `ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.media-files.e2e.test.ts`. At a 320 px viewport it expects the filename `测试 market report.pdf` to wrap onto two lines and stay fully visible. It fails with:

```
expected { wraps: true, fullyVisible: false } to deeply equal { wraps: true, fullyVisible: true }
```

## User Impact

User impact: none. This is a test-only change; no product code changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Whether the old filename fits depends on which fonts the host has. The title is 68 px wide at that viewport. With real CJK glyphs, `测试 market` measures 72.83 px, so the first line overflows by about 5 px, the name needs three lines and the two-line clamp truncates it. On a host without CJK fonts the two ideographs render narrower and the name fits in two lines.

In CI, `playwright install-deps webkit` installs `fonts-wqy-zenhei` and `fonts-ipafont-gothic`. A shard that runs the "Install selected Control UI E2E WebKit" step therefore renders real ideographs, and a shard that skips it does not. #204247 added a WebKit suite, which can now share a shard with this test. Example: [shard 7 on #202013](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45283633614/job/138075135026) ran the WebKit step and failed twice with the assertion above, while the same shard on that PR's previous head skipped the step and passed.

This change uses the filename `测试 Q3 notes.pdf`. In the title font, `测试 Q3` is 47.05 px and `notes.pdf` is 58.89 px, so both lines fit in 68 px with real CJK glyphs. `Q3 notes.pdf` alone is 79.41 px, so the name still wraps however narrow the ideographs render. The assertions are unchanged, and the name still exercises the Unicode filename and the encoded download URL.

Not changed here: with CJK fonts, the original filename really is truncated at 320 px by the two-line clamp from #203711. Whether the card should give such names more room is a product question for that card and is left alone.

## Evidence

The case fails on `main` and passes with this change on a Mac that has CJK fonts. Run with synthetic data in a loopback-only sandbox, bundled Chromium, `ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.media-files.e2e.test.ts`:

| | Commit | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Before | `main` at `57dd84bd1e0f` | 1 failed, 7 passed |
| After | this change | 8 passed |

A layout probe on `main` and on the #202013 branch measured the same title (68 px) and card (230.39 px), so the failure does not come from that PR's changes.

`pnpm check:changed` exits 0 on this change.

Limit: I verified this only on a host with CJK fonts. The host without CJK fonts is covered by hosted CI shards that skip the WebKit install step, not by a local run.
