prs.title: feat: watch a running command automation's output live in the Control UI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a long-running command automation shows nothing in Automations, Run history until it finishes, so an operator cannot tell what a multi-hour job is doing. Only Settings, Logs is live, and it does not contain the script's output.

## User Impact

User impact: while a command automation runs, its Run history shows a **Live output** panel that follows the combined stdout and stderr like `tail -f`. It auto-scrolls, pauses when you scroll up (with a **Jump to latest** button), and stops polling while the browser tab is hidden. When the run ends the panel goes away and the recorded run appears in the list as before. Gateway clients can read the same tail with `cron.liveOutput`.

Risks and limits:
- Live text is redacted with the tool-payload policy, so it can be masked more strictly than the recorded summary of the same run. The recorded summary is unchanged. A private key is masked across polls; one whose start was already dropped from a full tail is masked only while its end line is still held.
- Only the most recent output is kept: at most 256 KiB, or `payload.outputMaxBytes` when that is smaller. The panel keeps the last 2000 lines.
- Agent-turn runs have no live panel. Their transcript is still available only after the run is recorded (see Evidence).

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway keeps a fixed-size in-memory ring for the active run. The command runner owns it and discards it in its existing `finally`, so exit, timeout, abort and spawn failure all clean up through one path. `cron.liveOutput` (`operator.read`, same job visibility checks as `cron.get`) returns complete lines from a byte cursor, so a reconnect neither loses nor repeats lines. The panel reuses the existing visible-poll and stream-auto-follow helpers. Cursor polling, like `logs.tail`, keeps the Gateway free of timers and per-chunk broadcasts when nobody is watching. No config key, schema or migration; `cron.history` and `cron.runs` are unchanged.

Size: about 360 lines of new production code across 3 modules, about 560 lines of tests, small edits to existing files, plus regenerated validator files.

## Evidence

Before and after screenshots (Run history of a running command job; Live output panel; paused with **Jump to latest**; hand-off when the run ends) are in the first comment below. The extra Error row in the before shot is from restarting the throwaway Gateway while testing.


- Throwaway Gateway (own state dir, port 28789, loopback, throwaway token) and a real headless Chrome against the built Control UI. A command job printed a line per second for 60 to 90 s. Follow reads returned only new lines, replaying a cursor was idempotent, stderr was interleaved in order, a fake `token=sk-...` was masked, and `active` flipped to `false` exactly when `state.runningAtMs` cleared, including after a job timeout. The recorded run was unchanged.
- Tests: buffer bounds and fixed memory, cursor, drop-oldest, UTF-8 safety, redaction (including a private key across polls) and escape stripping, cleanup on exit, timeout, abort and spawn failure; the gateway method (follow, inactive, validation, visibility, access closed mid-read); the UI line bound and panel (follow, hidden tab, hand-off, still polling before the command starts, jump to latest).
- Review round: fixes covered by focused tests and typecheck; the current-head Gateway run is under Real behavior proof below. `check:changed` passes except the dead export scan, which flags `flattenRun` in `scripts/lib/catalog-compare-released-diff.mts` (already on main, not in this PR).
- Checks run: `pnpm gateway:validators:check`, `pnpm protocol-registry:check`, the protocol since-guard (new method vintage `2026.10`), the native protocol check, scoped core and UI tests (including the existing `command-runner`, `cron.history` and `cron.runs` suites), `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, and `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` (all lanes passed). I re-ran the validators, registry and new tests after the work finished.
- Agent-turn runs: not changed. Run history rows, including the transcript binding `cron.history` needs, are written when the run completes, so an in-flight run has no row and **View transcript** is unavailable. Live agent transcripts need an early binding row from the run owner and a follow protocol for transcript pages, which is a separate change.
- Local review: autoreview and local ClawSweeper were not run. The author read the full diff against the simplify checklist before opening.
- Not covered: hidden-tab pause in a real browser (unit-tested with a mocked `visibilityState`), narrow layout, dark theme and RTL screenshots, Windows and macOS, WebKit, the full test suite.

### Real behavior proof

Current head `1bb85c8a42c`, built with `pnpm openclaw`, against an isolated Gateway (own state dir, loopback, port 28789, throwaway token). A command job (`openclaw cron add --command`, then `openclaw cron run`) printed one line per second for 20 s, including a synthetic token, a synthetic private key split across polls, and one stderr line. I polled `cron.liveOutput` with `openclaw gateway call`, sending back the returned `cursor` and `runAtMs` (trimmed):

```
11:22:28 cursor=0   -> active:true reset:true cursor:14  "line 1 stdout\n"
11:22:31 cursor=14  -> active:true cursor:56  "line 2 stdout\nline 3 stdout\nline 4 stdout\n"
11:22:34 cursor=56  -> active:true cursor:174 "line 5 stdout\napi token=sk-pro…7890 used\nline 6 stdout\nline 7 stdout\nwarn 7 on stderr\n"
11:22:37 cursor=174 -> active:true cursor:310 "line 8 stdout\nline 9 stdout\n-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----…redacted…\n"
11:22:40 cursor=310 -> active:true cursor:381 "…redacted…-----END PRIVATE KEY-----\nline 13 stdout\n"
11:22:43 cursor=381 -> active:true cursor:426 "line 14 stdout\nline 15 stdout\nline 16 stdout\n"
11:22:46 cursor=426 -> active:true cursor:471 "line 17 stdout\nline 18 stdout\nline 19 stdout\n"
11:22:49 cursor=471 -> active:false cursor:0 ""   (run ended, buffer discarded)
```

Each poll returned only new complete lines, stderr arrived in order, the token and the private key (across polls) were masked, and `active` flipped to `false` when the run ended. `cron.runs` then recorded the finished run with its full, unchanged summary. Not re-run on this head: the Control UI panel (the screenshots above are from an earlier head).

prs.body:
<!-- Related: #186966 and #187075 also touch the Browser panel; the three merge cleanly together -->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in screenshot fallback, a Browser panel action waits a fixed 350 ms before the refresh, even when the action itself was slow.

## User Impact

User impact: fallback frames refresh sooner after an action. Typing, clicks, wheel and a live screencast are unchanged. No Gateway, protocol or model-facing tool changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The post-action refresh counts the time the action already took toward the 350 ms settle delay. If a capture is still pending, retries stay 350 ms apart.
- Text input is not batched: each soft-keyboard, composition or paste event stays its own `insertText`, so auto-advancing code fields keep working.

## Evidence

Real run, head db783d6 vs base 54afe28: two isolated Gateways, managed headless Chrome 156, built Control UI, 12 interleaved runs per version, medians in ms. Fallback is forced by replying to `/screencast` with `SCREENCAST_UNSUPPORTED` (the error the Gateway returns for node-hosted browsers) at the operator socket; everything else is real. Only the refresh timing below is in this PR.

```text
                                      base     head
fallback click to updated frame       1013     733
```

- `pnpm test ui/src/components/browser`: 271 tests pass at dcdea95. The slow-action test fails without the refresh change, and the one-insertText-per-event test fails with text batching.
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files: clean. Net test lines vs base: -5.
- Not run: the browser e2e files. Not observed: the native bridge.

prs.title: improve(ui): copy selected text out of the Browser panel
prs.body:
<!-- Related: #187032 and #187075 also touch the Browser panel; the three merge cleanly together -->

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: text cannot be copied out of the Control UI Browser panel. The remote page is drawn as a screenshot, Ctrl/Cmd+C was never handled, a native copy copied the panel's empty input and left the clipboard unchanged, and the actions menu only offered "Copy URL". Text the agent selected, or that a page selected itself, could not reach the user's clipboard.

## User Impact

User impact: press Ctrl/Cmd+C with the page focused, use the browser's Copy, or choose **Copy selection** in the Browser actions menu to put the remote page's selected text on your local clipboard; a "Copied" notice confirms it. An empty selection, a disconnected panel, disabled page scripting (`browser.evaluateEnabled=false`) or a clipboard failure each show a notice naming the next step, and the menu entry is disabled with a reason when there is nothing to copy. Password fields and cross-origin frames are never copied. Mac tabs still copy natively with ⌘C. Known gap: the panel cannot yet create a selection in the remote page (no drag-select, no Ctrl/Cmd+A), so copy works on selections that already exist; the notices tell users to ask the agent to select text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The panel already runs page functions through the existing `act:evaluate` route, so a small page script reads the selection back (input/textarea ranges, open shadow roots, same-origin frames, capped at 1,000,000 characters). No Gateway, protocol or model-facing tool change is needed. The clipboard write needs a live user gesture but the text only arrives after a round trip, so `copyToClipboard` now accepts a pending promise (`ClipboardItem`, then `writeText`, then `execCommand`). The tab and connection are rechecked right before the write so a stale result from another tab is dropped, a read that finishes after a newer copy never overwrites it, and selected text never reaches logs, errors, the local textarea, chat or panel state. Forwarding the key to the remote browser's clipboard was rejected because the Gateway cannot read that clipboard.

## Evidence

Real run, head a5fb8f5 vs base b9251d1: isolated Gateway, managed headless Chrome 156, built Control UI. Text selected via `openclaw browser evaluate`.

```text
                          base                      head
Ctrl+C, text selected     clipboard unchanged       copied + "Copied!" toast
local Ctrl+V paste        "local-clipboard-before"  "Order 4821 shipped to Rotterdam"
Actions menu              Copy URL only             + Copy selection (copies the same text)
nothing selected, Ctrl+C  nothing happens           clipboard unchanged + "Nothing is selected" notice
tab switched 340 ms into a 3 s selection read
                          n/a                       clipboard unchanged, no toast
                                                    (same read without the switch: copied)
```

| before | after |
|---|---|
| ![before: menu has no Copy selection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/867adabe-de77-4830-a000-59755316dee7) | ![after: Copy selection in menu](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9be0888b-c393-458d-a298-7c53e45e9b3d) |
| ![before: Ctrl+C shows nothing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fdf6c8c6-a6fb-4d50-9d4d-11414d006076) | ![after: Copied toast](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9e5613d-7a80-483d-a76d-726cce174b0e) |

![after: Copy selection disabled with nothing selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b19edf76-ca99-4c19-a129-c2ff78a6696d)

- `pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/components/browser src/lib/clipboard.test.ts src/lib/sessions/session-menu-navigation.test.ts` in `ui/`: 28 files, 328 tests pass; 23 of the 24 new tests fail without the production change (the chord guard passes trivially on the base).
- `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:test:ui`, `pnpm check:control-ui-controllers`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, oxfmt check and `git diff --check`: clean. `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets` passes on this head merged with current main. oxlint reports one warning at `browser-panel-toolbar.tsx:220`, the existing Copy URL handler, also flagged before this change.
- Not observed: Safari/Firefox clipboard behavior, the native bridge, `contenteditable` selections (jsdom lacks them).

prs.title: fix: stop Git checkouts on 2026-11-17 main updaters from half-switching on a schema change
prs.body:
Related: #203608, #203194, #201463

## What Problem This Solves

Git checkouts whose installed updater was built from `main` between #199706 (2026-11-17) and #201917 (2026-11-19), for example a checkout at `8f80fe08cad`, cannot update to current `main`. Their `openclaw update` builds the new release, switches the release link and arms a trial. It then fails with "Agent database migration did not finish". The install is left half-switched: the Gateway still serves the old build, and the link points at a release that never started. Later runs report `already-current`, or build another 4.6 GiB release and fail again. Published releases (2026.11.5, 2026.11.6, 2026.11.10-beta.2) keep the in-place Git updater and are not affected.

## User Impact

This is a stopgap, not the full fix. It stops the strand before it happens and prints a one-time rebuild that was proven in cells. It does not recover automatically.

When one of those updaters is about to update to a release that migrates the databases, the release's own check now stops the update before the link is switched. The Gateway is not touched, and the run prints why and one command to run from the checkout:

```sh
git pull --ff-only && openclaw gateway stop --force && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build && openclaw gateway install --force || { openclaw gateway start; false; }
```

After that, `openclaw` on PATH is the new build, the Gateway serves it on the migrated schema, and later `openclaw update` runs work normally. Updates that change no schema still go through the older updater unchanged. No other install sees any change.

What still needs a person, and why:
- **Running the rebuild above, once.** The installed updater runs first and cannot be patched, and the reasons below rule out finishing inside it. Its failure output already offers `openclaw triage`, which hands the step to a repair agent on the machine.
- **Gateway-started updates show only the generic headline.** When the update starts from the Gateway (Control UI, `update.run`), the stored run record and the update report show only the old updater's fixed text, "The update could not load its recovery runtime (exit 1)", plus its `openclaw triage` hint. The full explanation is in the step's stderr, which the CLI route prints and the triage diagnostics carry.
- **The old link and first release stay on disk.** `git-install/lib/node_modules/openclaw` and the release it names (about 4.6 GiB) are no longer used. The docs give the removal steps: delete the release directory the link names, then the link, then run `git worktree prune` in the checkout.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Root cause.** It sits in the installed updater, not in the new release; the release's `--check` output is the same at `8f80fe08cad` and on `main`.
- On this route the updater never stops the Gateway: `servicePrepared = params.gitRelease === true` (`src/cli/update-cli/update-command-execution.ts:418` at 8f80).
- It runs no Doctor. The Gateway that starts from the new release is meant to migrate state at boot.
- After switching the link, though, it runs its own `inspectActivatedUpdateState` (`src/cli/update-cli/update-command-migrated.ts` at 8f80). That function writes a synthetic `openclaw doctor` step (`durationMs: 0`) whenever the on-disk schema differs from the release's, which is every schema change.
- #201463 fixed that check (`!gitRelease`) in the updater, so it reaches only updaters built after it.
- It became visible when `main` bumped the agent schema to 43 (#200533) and the state schema to 41 (#201615).

**Why not recover automatically.** The new release's code runs inside that updater only during `pnpm install` / `pnpm build`, `--check`, the read-only schema inspection workers and `--version`.
1. A refusal or failure in install or build sends the updater back to older commits (the candidate walk in `src/infra/update-runner-git-preflight.ts` at 8f80). Those commits lack any fix, so it would strand anyway. A failed `--check` aborts the whole update instead, so the refusal lives there.
2. None of those hooks may migrate state, because the old Gateway is still serving it.
3. After a migration, the updater's own process and the checkout's `openclaw` on PATH refuse the newer schema. The updater never rebuilds the checkout: `update-runner-git-release.ts` at 8f80 says "The checkout and the running release are never written".

**The experiment that rules out finishing inside the old updater.** Branch `exp/snapshot-strand-y1` made `--check` report the on-disk versions, so the updater's check passed.
- The updater moved the service to the launcher. The Gateway on the new release migrated state to 41/43 and served after one 19 s outage, with marker rows intact.
- The run then exited 1 as `post-update-failed`: "Refused by OpenClaw 2026.11.4 (8f80fe0) … schema version 41; this build supports 40".
- Every later `openclaw` command on PATH refused the same way, and the old-format trial stayed armed (`attempts: 1`).

**The change.**
- `src/infra/update-candidate-check-early-release.ts` recognizes the early updater only by what it alone produces: the release check runs from `<stateDir>/git-install/releases/<id>/build` while `git-install/lib/node_modules/openclaw` is a symlink. Current `main` builds at `releases/<id>/openclaw`, npm and pnpm prefixes at `releases/<id>/lib/node_modules/openclaw`, and published updaters never build Git releases.
- It reads the shared and agent schema versions directly through `readonly_shm` (no writes to the serving Gateway's WAL sidecars), from the shared registry, the `agents/` directory and the agent-dir overrides. It refuses only when this release would migrate them, and never for a PostgreSQL-backed store (its local anchor has version 0; that schema migrates through the stopped-writer Doctor procedure, which this rebuild does not cover).
- `update-migrated-finalize.worker.ts --check` prints the refusal to stderr and exits 1. Any read failure falls through to the normal contract.
- No config, stored field, schema, protocol, dependency or `--check` contract change. Removal note: delete the module once no install can still run an updater from that window.

**Relation to other work.**
- #201463 fixed the same check in the updater for builds after it.
- #203194 replaced this layout; a COMMENT there recorded the same strand.
- #203608 tried a conversion started from the release CLI. It was closed in favor of the by-hand rebuild. This PR makes the updater print a rebuild instead of stranding.
- Correction to the closing comment on #203608: it says the updater stops "before any target code can migrate state or restart the Gateway". Target code does run (the release's `--check` and inspection workers), but nothing restarts the Gateway or stops it, and no Doctor runs in the `openclaw doctor` step.

## Evidence

Cells: Linux containers with systemd as PID 1 and a user Gateway service from `openclaw gateway install`, a 512 MiB agent database under 1 MiB/s of writes, marker rows checked by count and hash, a node runner started from the checkout, and synthetic state only. Installed updater `8f80fe08cad` unless noted.

Recordings: red on the unmodified base `0828443372b`, then green on this exact head `0ccd577bd3e`. Each shows the cell run (sped up), then that run's decisive raw facts.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a1c4b46d-888c-4dfc-a255-e11c1b3bb39f

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2c1c11b1-f31c-4ae1-a049-1b4187b80d77

Green on this exact head: refusal exit 1 after 316 s, with the Gateway untouched; repeat 129 s. Rebuild exit 0 (269 s, Gateway outage 296 s). T+1 389 s and T+2 365 s, both exit 0, with 12.3 s and 7.0 s outages. No-op `already-current` in 7 s. Schema 41/43 and marker rows 1000 with the same hash throughout. `git-install` peaked at 14.7 GiB (the old first release plus T+1 and T+2 releases) and ended at 14.6 GiB.

| Cell | Start state → target | Result | Wall time | Gateway outage | Disk (git-install peak → end) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RED, base `0828443372b` | clean 8f80 checkout → unmodified `main` | exit 1 `openclaw doctor`; half-switched (link on a never-started release, trial armed, service on checkout); repeat `already-current` (false) | 308 s, repeat 124 s | none | 14.1 → 9.5 GiB |
| A, head | clean 8f80 checkout → head | exit 1, refusal shown; nothing switched; Gateway serves 2026.11.4 on 40/42; repeat refuses again (122 s) | 303 s | none | first release 4.7 GiB stays; candidate build removed |
| A, rebuild | the printed command | Gateway and PATH `openclaw` on the new build; schema 41/43; marker rows 1000, hash unchanged | 263 s | 286 s (the build) | — |
| D, T+1 / T+2 / no-op | version-bump builds through the rebuilt checkout's updater | exit 0 / exit 0 / `already-current`; trials committed | 391 s / 381 s / 7 s | 12.8 s / 10.8 s / none | 14.7 → 14.6 GiB |
| C, half-switched | stranded on pre-fix `main` → head | true refusal (no false `already-current`); rebuild then T+1, T+2, no-op as above | 171 s; rebuild 267 s | rebuild 289 s; T+1 12.6 s; T+2 9.1 s | 19.4 → 19.2 GiB |
| Service on launcher | earlier same-schema update by 8f80 (serves 2026.11.5 from the old link) → head, with this exact rebuild command | refusal; rebuild exit 0, service back on the checkout, serves 2026.11.7 on 41/43; T+1, T+2 exit 0; no-op `already-current` | 177 s; rebuild 276 s; T+1 374 s; T+2 361 s; no-op 7 s | rebuild 303 s; T+1 11.8 s; T+2 8.8 s | 19.3 → 19.2 GiB |
| B, Gateway `update.run` | clean 8f80 checkout → head | handed to the installed CLI updater; refused; Gateway untouched | 423 s | none | 9.4 → 4.8 GiB |
| Same schema (falsifier) | clean 8f80 → `6691acae` (schema 40/42) | exit 0; service on launcher; serves 2026.11.5. This change leaves that path alone | 356 s | 7 s + 13 s | — |
| Experiment | clean 8f80 → on-disk versions reported | see the experiment below | 316 s | 19.4 s | — |

The A and C rows ran on heads `a425da8665c`/`2955d62788b`; they differ from this head only in the printed command's last operator (`;` before `openclaw gateway start` became `||`). In those runs the trailing `openclaw gateway start` exited 1 because the rebuilt Gateway was still migrating at boot; everything else matched.
The "service on launcher" row ran this rebuild command without the final `false` (`|| openclaw gateway start`) and it exited 0. The green recording is the clean-checkout cell rerun on this exact head.

<details><summary>RED, unmodified base: the updater's own output</summary>

```
status=error reason=openclaw doctor
step openclaw doctor: exit 1
  Shared state migration did not finish: expected schema 41, found 40.
  Agent database migration did not finish: ~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite; expected schema 43, found 42.
step gateway recovery verification: exit 1  Expected Gateway version 2026.11.7; observed 2026.11.4.
then: legacy link -> never-started release, trial armed, service on the checkout; repeat -> skipped already-current
```
</details>

<details><summary>GREEN, head: the step the installed updater records</summary>

```
status=error reason=runtime-verification-failed
step candidate-recovery: exit 1
  OpenClaw 2026.11.7 migrates your databases (state schema 40 to 41, agent schema 42 to 43).
  The updater in this checkout (a main build from 2026-11-17 to 2026-11-19) cannot finish that: after the migration, neither it nor the checkout's `openclaw` command can open the migrated data.
  The update stopped before switching releases; the Gateway was not touched.
  Rebuild the checkout once from its directory; later updates then run normally:
  git pull --ff-only && openclaw gateway stop --force && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build && openclaw gateway install --force || { openclaw gateway start; false; }
```
</details>

<details><summary>Experiment: report on-disk versions instead (rejected)</summary>

```
managed-service-install 0 ... post-update verification 1
This OpenClaw build cannot open your existing data.
OpenClaw state database ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite uses newer schema version 41; this build supports 40.
Refused by OpenClaw 2026.11.4 (8f80fe0) installed at ~/openclaw.
schema after: state 41, agent 43; Gateway ready; outage 19.4 s; trial {"attempts":1} still armed
```
</details>

Full raw logs are not attached because the artifact store rejects uploads from this machine (`http 401`).

**Tests.**
- `src/infra/update-candidate-check-early-release.test.ts` (new) uses real SQLite files and real release layouts. It covers:
  - the refusal and its path-free command;
  - an older agent store, registered or only on disk;
  - a linked state directory;
  - pass-through when nothing migrates, when state is newer, or when it is unreadable;
  - no refusal for the current Git layout, the package layout, a missing legacy link, or a `build` directory elsewhere.
- `src/infra/update-migrated-finalize.worker.test.ts` gains one case that runs the real `--check` entry against a real state fixture. It fails on base (the contract JSON is printed) and passes on head (empty stdout, exit 1, the refusal on stderr).
- I audited both files in full. Nothing was removed; the existing `--check` case still proves that other callers get the unchanged contract.

**Checks on head.**
- Passed: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` on the focused files and `test/scripts/update-restart-module-outcome.test.ts` plus `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts`; `pnpm tsgo:core`; `pnpm tsgo:core:test`; oxlint on the touched files; `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets`; the session identity ratchet; `pnpm check:docs`; `git diff --check`.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` fails only on dead exports in files this PR does not touch (`subagent-completion-admission.store.ts`, `task-supervisor.ts`, `project-access.ts`).

**ClawSweeper (one round, informational).** Overall D, proof C, patch D. Findings and what changed:
- *A failed in-place build can leave the checkout's build incomplete, and the trailing start hid the failure.* Real. The line now ends `|| { openclaw gateway start; false; }`, so a failure restarts the previous service and exits non-zero, and the docs say a failed `pnpm build` must be fixed and rerun. A service already on the launcher (the old-link release) comes back regardless; a service on the checkout stays down until the rebuild succeeds. Not covered by a cell.
- *PostgreSQL anchors are not schema versions.* Real. PostgreSQL-backed stores now pass through, and the docs point them to the stopped-writer procedure.
- *Plain read-only opens touch WAL sidecars.* Real. The reads now use `readonly_shm`, as `src/update/check-release.ts` does.
- *The docs lost the terminal-route note for the same-schema case.* Real. Restored.

**Review.** An independent reviewer read the diff and the behavior contract. Its findings are fixed:
- the updater redacts state and home paths from the step text, so the command now names no path;
- the pull now runs before the stop;
- every agent store is read;
- a linked state directory is handled;
- the wording is truthful;
- the docs remedy is included.

Its concern that the old link would become the next trial's fallback did not hold: the first update after the rebuild falls back to the rebuilt checkout. `autoreview` does not run on this machine.

**Update proof rules (#203915), from the cells' raw logs.**
- Route: every CLI update step was a plain `openclaw update --yes`, and the installed updater's own runs record trigger `cli`. Row B started the update with `openclaw gateway call update.run`; its RPC `--timeout 120000` is the call's own wait, not an update `--timeout`. The green cell on the exact head (AF3) records trigger `api` for the rebuilt checkout's T+1 and T+2 runs, and its journal has `[gateway] update.run <runId> actor=gateway-client` for T+1, T+2 and the no-op run. No `OPENCLAW_UPDATE_PACKAGE_SPEC`, `--tag`, `--no-restart` or shortened update `--timeout` was used.
- Service: the Gateway unit comes from `openclaw gateway install`, and the rebuild reinstalls it with `openclaw gateway install --force`. In AF3 the rebuild step ended `|| openclaw gateway start` without the `{ …; false; }` group; that group runs only when an earlier step fails, and every step succeeded (rebuild exit 0). After each step the cell saved the unit's `ExecStart` (`systemctl --user cat`), the release link, `.trial` and the checkout worktrees. `NeedDaemonReload` was not captured.
- Freshness: each recording names its commit (base `0828443372b`, head `0ccd577bd3e`). Public `npm view openclaw dist-tags` at landing: `latest` 2026.11.7, `beta` 2026.11.10-beta.2, `extended-stable` 2026.10.33. Published packages do not reach this code path (see Not proven).
- Next build: the refused target itself migrates the schema (state 40 to 41, agent 42 to 43), which is the case under test. T+1 and T+2 after the rebuild are version-bump-only builds, so they prove the later switches and not a further migration or rollback.
- Installed code: the change does not touch `src/update/launcher.ts`, `run.ts`, `preflight.ts` or `convert-service.ts`. The cells still ran T+1 and T+2 through the rebuilt checkout's updater.
- Platforms: only Linux systemd user services ran. A Linux container without a user bus, the macOS LaunchAgent and the Windows Scheduled Task are unproven.

## Not proven

- macOS/launchd. The service stop, start and install steps and the Gateway's boot migration timing are service-manager specific; only Linux systemd user services ran.
- Installs whose agent stores sit at different schema versions run the refusal on the oldest one; not run in a cell.
- Published npm/pnpm updaters were not rerun. The keying cannot match them (unit test), and they never run this code path from a `build` directory.
- Separate defects seen on a pure-`main` checkout, outside this change: listed in the review notes and not fixed here.

prs.title: fix(cron): preserve missing-account refusal diagnostics and repair guidance
prs.body:
Related: #195802, #191637, #189953, #188946

## What Problem This Solves

A scheduled run refused for a missing recorded inference account can lose its actual cause and appear only as "Session event execution failed". Startup diagnostics also missed unbound Codex jobs using stored accounts.

## User Impact

Automation history and diagnostics retain the actionable refusal. Direct chat failure alerts explain the missing account and repair without naming the stored account; webhook failure routes retain their existing raw-error behavior. Startup inspection warns about affected Codex jobs without rewriting them.

Recurring jobs **stay enabled**, following #203106. Normal backoff, alert thresholds/cooldowns, and owner-conversation repair policy remain in charge. This PR no longer introduces first-failure pausing or restores the removed ten-failure auto-disable policy. Account authorization and fallback guards remain unchanged. Existing owner-conversation repair briefs still use the recorded last error; no account-redaction guarantee is made for generated repair replies.

## Design and Persisted State

- Pass the reply owner's recorded failure cause separately from optional chat text. Only recognized account refusals use the new error projection; unrelated wrapped errors keep their existing outer-error boundary.
- Recognize the account guard's error by identity, then project a closed failure detail and permanent run classification through isolated and session-event results. Timeout, cancellation, auth-revoked, operator-admission and session-conflict precedence remain intact.
- Do not confuse missing account configuration with revoked creator authority: an operator-linked recurring job keeps its schedule too.
- Persist the actual refusal in existing history/error fields. Do not write a new account binding, disable the recurring job, introduce a disable reason, or migrate schemas.
- Use credential-neutral alert copy that supports either selecting an authorized stored account or a configured provider key, without adding another metadata variant.
- Remove the auto-disable plumbing and redundant configuration-refusal predicate from the earlier revision. Preserve the current-main run preparation split and operator-admission handling.

## Evidence

- On reconciled candidate `7d3da265064d`, seven focused suites passed: 165 tests covering session events, account propagation, scheduling, lifecycle classification, startup warnings and watchdogs.
- On final candidate `aed3a9904c0b`, the three affected suites passed again: 88 tests, including stored/direct refusal handling, unrelated nested-error non-disclosure and operator-linked jobs remaining enabled. Session-event suite: 104.14s; cron scheduler/notification suites: 5.20s combined. These are boundary integrations; most session-suite time is real isolated state/lifecycle setup.
- Core typecheck, changed-file lint/format and `git diff --check` passed. Dependencies were installed from each branch's frozen lockfile without package manifest or lockfile edits.
- The first local ClawSweeper pass found two P2 issues: generic nested-error disclosure and stored-account-only alert wording. Both were fixed with regression coverage. Final full-range local ClawSweeper completed at `aed3a9904c0b` against `8b17822bec4f` with two later findings dispositioned:
  - **Owner repair account detail:** retained intentionally. The existing trusted owner repair brief needs the actual account selection to repair the job. Documentation now scopes account-free wording to direct alerts, not model-generated repair replies; no new redaction policy is imposed on the owner workflow.
  - **Webhook `Cause: unknown` line:** not retained. It was an incidental projection of the old unknown classification, not a required field. A recognized permanent configuration refusal should not be labeled unknown. Structured raw `error` remains unchanged; the guide's stable-message note concerns omission of chat-only timestamps/links, not freezing an incorrect cause classification.
- Relative to current main: production +141/-51 (**+90 net**); tests +203/-26 (**+177 net**). Compared with the previously reported PR delta, production net growth fell from +108 to +90; additional tests protect the keep-running and disclosure boundaries. No auto-disable machinery was restored.

Current-head CI has an inherited failing shard, reproduced on the unmodified integration base; see the auditable proof index below. Prior-head green runs are not proof of this candidate.

The current tests use synthetic model execution, not a shipped-Gateway/live-model run. No new live Gateway or upgrade proof is claimed.

Reported by @Marvinthebored in #195802.

Evidence is pinned to `c6f663fce6fd3cb55c5a5b4fa99377cc149a761c`. Local results below are retained results from the earlier preparation, not newly rerun tests or additive coverage counts. Hosted CI links are checks attached to this exact PR head (GitHub PR CI may execute its merge ref).

prs.title: fix(sessions): unread advances only when a run ends with a new visible reply
prs.body:
Closes #204164. Replaces #204209.

## Problem

A session went unread with nothing new to read. Example (synthetic): a heartbeat or child-end wake runs in a chat, the model answers `NO_REPLY` (or `HEARTBEAT_OK`), the chat shows no new row, and the sidebar still lights its unread dot.

Cause: the run end stamped unread activity per run, not per content.
- The Gateway's run-end lifecycle projection set `lastActivityAt = endedAt` for every Control UI–visible run (`controlUiVisible`).
- Agent-command post-run set `lastActivityAt = now` for every run without internal events (`touchActivity`), with a special case for a child's `sessions_send` turns (#204143).

Neither knew whether the run added anything a person can see.

## Change

The run end now reads what the run added. Both run-end writers ask the transcript for its newest visible assistant row (`lastAssistantMessage`, the same row projection that feeds the sidebar preview) and advance `lastActivityAt` to that row's time only when it is newer. Silent replies (`NO_REPLY`), heartbeat acknowledgements and hidden coordination replies (`display: false`) are not visible rows, so a run that ends in one of them leaves unread alone.

- One read: `readVisibleSessionActivityAt` (`src/gateway/session-row-transcript-backfill.ts`), a thin wrapper over the existing bounded row-transcript read (`backfillSessionRowTranscriptFields`).
- Gateway run end: `persistPreparedGatewaySessionLifecycleEvent` passes the time into the lifecycle patch (`visibleActivityAt`); `projectSessionLifecyclePatch` applies it on terminal events.
- Agent-command run end (Gateway `agent` runs and `openclaw agent --local`): `updateSessionStoreAfterAgentRun` reads the same fact; a visible reply also ends a snooze, as before.
- Nothing is written in the transcript append path.
- Channel inbound messages and background/cron results keep their existing stamping (they add a visible row themselves).

Removed:
- the run-end `controlUiVisible` stamp and `controlUiVisible` on lifecycle events, which only fed it;
- agent-command `touchActivity`, its internal-event and coordination special cases;
- the lifecycle-event unread recomputation in `buildGatewaySessionSnapshot`;
- `session-store.snooze.test.ts`, which asserted the removed `touchActivity` parameter (snooze is covered in `session-unread.test.ts`).

Production line delta (excluding tests, docs and test inventories): **+44 / −27 (net +17)**. The read is one helper with two call sites; the per-run special cases it replaces were smaller than the read and its plumbing.

## What the user sees

- A turn that ends in `NO_REPLY`, a quiet heartbeat, an internal wake, or a parent answering its child's `sessions_send` no longer lights the unread dot.
- A visible reply, a channel message, or a delivered cron/background result still does. A visible reply still wakes a snoozed session.

## Accepted edge cases

- Incognito sessions: their transcripts stay in the Gateway process, so the run end has no stored row to read and their replies no longer mark them unread. You are usually in an incognito chat while it runs.
- A reply that is only an image (no text) has no row preview, so it does not mark the chat unread.
- CLI-backend runs (`claude-cli` and similar) persist their transcript after the agent-command run end, so `openclaw agent --local` with a CLI backend does not mark unread from that writer. I did not verify whether the Gateway lifecycle run end sees a Gateway CLI run's reply.
- A visible reply whose stored event is over 64 KiB has no row preview, so it does not mark the chat unread (the preview read is size-bounded so it can run at every run end).
- The run end adds one bounded transcript read per terminal run (the same read the sidebar row owner already does).

## Evidence

- `src/shared/session-unread.test.ts` (rewritten) appends real rows to a SQLite transcript and runs the real agent-command run end:
  - stays read and snoozed after a `NO_REPLY` wake turn, a quiet heartbeat, and a parent's reply to a child's `sessions_send` (built through the run writer's display projection). **Red on base** (base stamps every run).
  - turns unread and ends the snooze after a visible reply;
  - inbound channel message unread, internal wake read (unchanged from #204143).
- `src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts`: a visible run that ends without a new visible reply leaves `lastActivityAt` alone. **Red on base.**
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/destination-completion.test.ts` (unchanged): a delivered cron result still stamps the destination.
- PostgreSQL conformance, full suite, locally against PostgreSQL 16 (pgvector pg16 image from CI): `server-database-engine-cron.postgres.test.ts`, which failed on #204209, passes. `client-credential-update.test.ts` and `git-backup.postgres.test.ts` fail locally the same way on the merge base (local environment, not this change).
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck, lint and guards pass. The dead-export scan fails on three exports this PR does not touch (also on `main`).
- Real-Gateway Control UI E2E (throwaway, not committed; only the model provider is scripted; dist build): two chats each get an `agent` turn with a hidden heartbeat input while the browser shows a third chat. The first reply is `NO_REPLY`, the second visible.
  - Base: **fails**, the `NO_REPLY` chat shows an unread dot.
  - Head: **passes**, the `NO_REPLY` chat stays read; the visible-reply chat shows a dot. Screenshots in a PR comment.

prs.title: fix(gateway): grant busy accounts reconnect grace on a validated typed disconnect
prs.body:
Fixes #146800

## What Problem This Solves

A health sample taken milliseconds after a typed Discord disconnect classified a busy account as `stuck` and restarted the whole provider, aborting the account's in-flight reply operations. The busy branch computed `busyAge` from the oldest active run's start age and returned `stuck` before the typed-disconnect branch could validate `lastDisconnect.at` and apply the 120-second reconnect grace, so a long-running but healthy run turned a transient socket blip into an immediate account-wide restart.

## User Impact

A busy channel sampled during a transient transport disconnect now rides out the transport's own reconnect window instead of being force-restarted: no aborted reply operations and no account-wide downtime for blips the client already schedules its own reconnect for. A disconnect that outlives the 120-second grace still reports `disconnected` and restarts. Stale run heartbeats still report `stuck`, and accounts without a validated disconnect keep the run-start-age proxy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Run age is not a disconnect age. `activeRunStartedAt` measures how long a task has been running; only a validated `lastDisconnect.at` measures how long the transport has been down. While the run heartbeat stays fresh, the validated typed disconnect now owns the down clock: reconnect grace applies under `CHANNEL_RECONNECT_GRACE_MS` and `disconnected` is reported at the boundary. The lifecycle-validated disconnect extraction moved into a shared `resolveCurrentDisconnectAt` helper so the busy branch and the disconnect branch keep one owner for that invariant. Accounts without a validated disconnect are unchanged: run start age remains the only down-clock proxy there.

## Evidence

- Pre-fix policy red: with the issue's snapshot (busy, 4 active runs, run started 26 minutes ago, heartbeat 1 second old, `connected=false`, `lastDisconnect` 4ms old), `evaluateChannelHealth()` returned `stuck`; the new tests assert `reconnect-grace` (4ms) and `disconnected` (exactly 120s) and both failed before the fix, while the stale-heartbeat-stuck and patch-merged-disconnect guard tests passed throughout.
- Pre-fix monitor red (production change stashed): the new monitor test observed the monitor calling `stopChannel`/`startChannel` for the busy Discord account on a 4ms-old validated disconnect — the reported incident (`expected stopChannel not to be called, but called 1 times`); with the fix the monitor does not restart. The policy assertions ran through `evaluateChannelHealth()` and the monitor assertion through the real `startChannelHealthMonitor` check loop.
- Real-transport proof inside the grace window (committed test `src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.real-transport.test.ts`, real clock, real TCP transport, no fake timers, no spy mocks on the monitor path): the production `startChannelHealthMonitor` check loop drives a fixture manager whose transport is a real TCP socket to a loopback server. A 26-minute-old run keeps a fresh heartbeat while the real socket is destroyed mid-run; every monitor tick evaluates `reconnect-grace`, the transport really reconnects (`transport disconnected` → `transport connected` ~250ms later), and the run completes intact (`run 1 completed`). With the pre-fix policy checked out, the same harness fails: the monitor restarts the account, aborts the run, and the run never completes (`timed out waiting for run completion`).
- Real-transport proof of grace expiry (temporary harness, real clock, 124s run): after the real socket drop the loopback server stops accepting connections, so the fixture's real reconnect attempts fail with `ECONNREFUSED` 479 times across the window while the run heartbeat stays fresh. The monitor issues no restart until 120032ms after the disconnect, then stops the account (`monitor STOP (active run aborted)`), starts it again, and the account reconnects (`transport connected`) once the transport endpoint returns. A disconnect that outlives the 120s grace still restarts a busy account. Full transcript:
  ```
  [t=0ms] start (run 1)
  [t=16ms] transport connected
  [t=67ms] transport disconnected          <- real TCP drop; monitor evaluates reconnect-grace, no restart
  [t=321ms..119.8s] transport error (ECONNREFUSED) x479   <- fixture reconnect attempts fail; run heartbeat stays fresh
  [t=120133ms] monitor STOP (active run aborted)   <- 120s grace expired (first restart 120032ms after disconnect)
  [t=120133ms] start (run 2)
  [t=120335ms] transport connected         <- recovered after restart
  ```
- Post-fix: `src/gateway/channel-health-policy.test.ts` 58/58, `src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.test.ts` 56/56, `src/gateway/channel-health-monitor.real-transport.test.ts` 1/1, plus sibling consumers `src/gateway/server/readiness.test.ts` 27/27, `src/infra/channels-status-issues.test.ts` 11/11, `src/plugin-sdk/status-helpers.test.ts` 25/25, `src/plugin-sdk/channel-lifecycle.queue.test.ts` 6/6 all green.
- `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` report only the pre-existing `src/gateway/server-startup-finish.ts(416)` TS2741 error on current `main` (unrelated to this change); the changed files introduce no new type errors. oxlint (type-aware, repo shard tsconfig) and oxfmt are clean on the changed files.

Both the `v2026.11.6` base and this PR's head `cc6dac4b097` were built to their own `dist` (shipped `scripts/tsdown-build.mts` + `copy-bundled-plugin-metadata.mts`, Node 24.22.1) and driven as real CLIs on a real SQLite state database. The head change itself is unchanged: the four commits are byte-identical to the previously reviewed head (`23deadb73807`), replayed onto current `main` (`aa2dc6433e1`). Suites re-run on the shipped trees: `doctor-plugin-registry.test.ts` 33/33 and the three records/json-files suites 37/37, both green.

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor` (and the install-record recovery path) silently skips any managed npm plugin whose `openclaw.plugin.json` uses JSON5 — comments, trailing commas, or unquoted keys — because the stale-managed-npm-shadow check (`doctor-plugin-registry.ts`) and the recovery reader (`installed-plugin-index-record-reader.ts`) parse the manifest with a strict JSON reader that returns `null` on such syntax. The plugin is documented as JSON5-capable (`docs/plugins/manifest.md`: "Native manifests are parsed with JSON5"), the main loader accepts it (`manifest.ts:218` `parsePluginCacheJson(file, { json5: true })`), and `openclaw plugins install` installs it. But Doctor's shadow check reads the same file strictly, so a stale managed npm package shadowing a bundled plugin is never reported and never repaired — the user's plugin silently keeps the old version with no hint from `openclaw doctor`.

Fixes #201715

Precedent: #198808 (same shape: a JSON5-capable manifest reread with strict `JSON.parse`; the CLI browser builder was switched to the JSON5-capable reader). This PR applies the shape to the two remaining strict readers of installed-plugin manifests.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two remaining strict readers are the only places that parse a user-installed `openclaw.plugin.json` with plain strict JSON. `package.json` reads stay strict (npm `package.json` is never JSON5). The fix adds one shared reader, `tryReadJson5ObjectSync` in `src/infra/json-files.ts`, that keeps the strict-JSON fast path, falls back to JSON5, and preserves the `null`-on-failure contract of the existing `tryReadJsonObjectSync` — so a malformed manifest degrades exactly as before. Both call sites route their `openclaw.plugin.json` read through it.

Production LOC is `+72/-10` (net +62), two call sites change, one shared helper added in the JSON-reader owner, plus a recovery rekey. No new validator / option / config / persistence.

Classification: `behavior-completing` (a stale shadow that was silently skipped is now reported and repaired, matching the loader's documented JSON5 acceptance).

## User Impact

A user who installed an npm plugin with a JSON5 manifest (comments, trailing commas, unquoted keys) now gets the stale-managed-npm shadow warning and `--fix` repair from `openclaw doctor`, instead of the shadow being silently skipped and the bundled plugin staying shadowed by an old managed copy. Strict JSON manifests and all other doctor behaviors are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Discriminating test (producer-chain, real repair path)

The regression adds a JSON5 variant of the existing `warns about stale managed npm packages that shadow bundled plugins` case in `src/commands/doctor-plugin-registry.test.ts`: it builds the same bundled-vs-managed fixture but writes the managed package's `openclaw.plugin.json` as JSON5 (`{ id: 'bundled-demo', ..., }` with a leading comment), then runs `maybeRepairPluginRegistryState` and asserts the shadow warning and the `@openclaw/bundled-demo@2026.5.2` note are emitted.

- RED on base (`v2026.11.6`, `06afb10d327`): the JSON5 case fails at `expect(notes).toContain("Managed npm plugin packages shadow bundled plugins")` — the strict reader returns `null`, `pluginId` is undefined, and the stale package is skipped.
- GREEN on head (`cc6dac4b097`): the same case passes; the full file stays green (33/33).

Remote proof run (sandboxed runner, docker Node 24.22.1, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/doctor-plugin-registry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`), tree-local md5-pinned base vs head:

```text
RED  (base, strict read):   1 failed | 32 passed  ->  expected '' to contain "Managed npm plugin packages shadow bundled plugins"
GREEN (head, JSON5 read):   Test Files 1 passed (1); Tests 33 passed (33)
```

### Fixup: retain the atomic-writer import

A first revision of the shared reader accidentally replaced the `@openclaw/fs-safe/atomic` import in `json-files.ts`, leaving `writeTextAtomic` with an undefined `writeFsSafeTextAtomic` (ClawSweeper P1). The current head restores the atomic import alongside the new read import; the atomic-writer tests stay green (`src/infra/json-files.test.ts`: 22/22 on head).

### Fixup: rekey persisted package-name recovery records

A released strict reader could already have persisted an install record keyed by the npm package name for a package whose JSON5 manifest declares a different `id`. Reading the JSON5 id then yields the same install path under the manifest id (ClawSweeper P1). `mergeRecoveredManagedNpmInstallRecords` now rekeys the persisted record to the recovered manifest id **before** building recovery candidates — deleting the old key first would discard persisted metadata (`integrity`, `installedAt`, …) and lose the active-path authority. A regression in `src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-records.test.ts` covers the previously persisted package-name case and asserts the persisted metadata is retained:

```text
RED  (JSON5 id read, no rekey):   expected { source: 'npm', …(6) } to match object { source: 'npm', …(8) }  (metadata lost / duplicate key)
GREEN (JSON5 id read + rekey):    Test Files 1 passed (1); Tests 11 passed (11)
```

### Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/doctor-plugin-registry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 33/33 on head (RED on base for the discriminating assertion).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/json-files.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 22/22 on head (atomic writer tests intact).
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-records.test.ts src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-records.managed-npm.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 15/15 on head (reconcile regression included).
- `git diff --check` — clean.

### Shipped proof: real `openclaw doctor` on a JSON5 manifest

Built both trees to a real `dist` and drove the actual CLI binary (`node dist/entry.js doctor --lint --all --only core/doctor/plugin-registry --json`), not the test harness. The fixture is a genuine managed npm plugin install under an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`: `npm/projects/openclaw-a2a-d83b9340a9/` with a `package.json` declaring `@openclaw/a2a`, the installed package's strict `package.json`, and an `openclaw.plugin.json` written as JSON5 (leading comment, unquoted keys, single quotes, trailing comma):

```json5
// Native manifests are parsed with JSON5 (docs/plugins/manifest.md).
{
  id: 'a2a',
  name: 'A2A',
  configSchema: { type: 'object' },
}
```

`@openclaw/a2a` is a real bundled plugin, so the managed copy is a genuine shadow. Four-cell matrix, same fixture, two real builds:

Re-run on the two shipped builds for this refresh — base `v2026.11.6` (`06afb10d327`) and head `cc6dac4b097`, each built to its own `dist` and driven as a CLI:

```text
===== BASE (/w/v2026116) =====
  manifest is JSON5 (leading // comment, single quotes, trailing comma)
  "ok":true
  SHADOW_FINDING=ABSENT
  package exists before --fix: yes
  package exists after --fix: yes
  AFTER_FIX=clean
  CONTROL(strict JSON): SHADOW_FINDING=PRESENT

===== HEAD (/w/head) =====
  manifest is JSON5 (leading // comment, single quotes, trailing comma)
  "ok":false
  SHADOW_FINDING=PRESENT
  finding: Managed npm package @openclaw/a2a@2026.5.2 shadows bundled plugin a2a.
  package exists before --fix: yes
  package exists after --fix: no
  AFTER_FIX=clean
  after-fix ok: "ok":true
  CONTROL(strict JSON): SHADOW_FINDING=PRESENT
```

Four-cell matrix:

| `openclaw.plugin.json` | base `v2026.11.6` (strict reader) | head `cc6dac4b097` (JSON5 reader) |
|---|---|---|
| strict JSON | `Managed npm package @openclaw/a2a@2026.5.2 shadows bundled plugin a2a.` | same — no regression |
| JSON5 | **no finding** (`ok: true`) | **`Managed npm package @openclaw/a2a@2026.5.2 shadows bundled plugin a2a.`** |

The strict-JSON row proves the diagnosis path itself is unchanged; only the JSON5 row changes. On head the repair is real: `doctor --fix` deletes the stale package (`exists after --fix: no`) and the follow-up lint is clean. Raw head output:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/w/s-head2/state node dist/entry.js \
    doctor --lint --all --only core/doctor/plugin-registry --json
{"schemaVersion":1,"ok":false,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":77,"findings":[
  {"checkId":"core/doctor/plugin-registry","severity":"warning",
   "message":"Managed npm package @openclaw/a2a@2026.5.2 shadows bundled plugin a2a.",
   "path":"/w/s-head2/state/npm/projects/openclaw-a2a-d83b9340a9/node_modules/@openclaw/a2a",
   "target":"a2a",
   "fixHint":"Run `openclaw doctor --fix` to remove stale managed npm packages and rebuild the plugin registry."}], ...}
```

Repair path, end to end on the same state:

```text
$ node dist/entry.js doctor --fix --non-interactive
before --fix: package exists = yes
after  --fix: package exists = no
$ node dist/entry.js doctor --lint --all --only core/doctor/plugin-registry --json
ok: true   findings: <none>
```

### Shipped proof: v2026.11.6 → head upgrade keeps legacy keys and metadata

The compatibility question is whether an install record persisted by the **released** strict reader (keyed by the npm package name) survives the upgrade. Both sides here are the real thing: the latest release `v2026.11.6` resolves to `06afb10d327` and that commit was built to its own `dist` and run against the real state database; the head side is this PR's `cc6dac4b097`, built the same way. Both runs used the shipped `scripts/tsdown-build.mts` + `copy-bundled-plugin-metadata.mts` build, Node 24.22.1.

The fixture is a non-shadow managed npm plugin — `@vendor/demo@1.2.3`, not in the bundled set — so the upgrade path exercises the record rekey rather than the shadow repair:

```json5
// JSON5 manifest
{
  id: 'demo',
  name: 'Demo',
  configSchema: { type: 'object' },
}
```

Each phase is a separate process, all against the real SQLite state (`state/openclaw.sqlite`, `config_machine_state.value_json` under `plugins.installedIndex.index.installRecords`). Phase A runs the `v2026.11.6` tree, Phase B and B2 run the head tree in fresh processes.

```text
[A] package dir: /w/state-up/npm/projects/vendor-demo-4e2ce35bbb/node_modules/@vendor/demo
[A] manifest is JSON5 (comment + single quotes + trailing comma)
[A] v2026.11.6 strict reader -> keys: ["@vendor/demo"]
[A] seeding metadata onto key "@vendor/demo": integrity + installedAt
[A] on disk after persist -> keys: ["@vendor/demo"]
[A] on disk record: {"source":"npm","spec":"@vendor/demo@1.2.3","installPath":"/w/state-up/npm/projects/vendor-demo-4e2ce35bbb/node_modules/@vendor/demo","version":"1.2.3","resolvedName":"@vendor/demo","resolvedVersion":"1.2.3","resolvedSpec":"@vendor/demo@1.2.3","integrity":"sha512-legacy-v2026.11.6","installedAt":"2026-05-02T00:00:00.000Z"}

[B] on disk before head read -> keys: ["@vendor/demo"]
[B] head JSON5 reader -> keys: ["demo"]
[B] metadata retained: {"integrity":"sha512-legacy-v2026.11.6","installedAt":"2026-05-02T00:00:00.000Z","installPath":"/w/state-up/npm/projects/vendor-demo-4e2ce35bbb/node_modules/@vendor/demo"}
[B] on disk after persist -> keys: ["demo"]
[B] persisted: {"integrity":"sha512-legacy-v2026.11.6","installedAt":"2026-05-02T00:00:00.000Z","installPath":"/w/state-up/npm/projects/vendor-demo-4e2ce35bbb/node_modules/@vendor/demo"}

[B2] fresh-process reload -> keys: ["demo"]
[B2] reloaded: {"integrity":"sha512-legacy-v2026.11.6","installedAt":"2026-05-02T00:00:00.000Z","installPath":"/w/state-up/npm/projects/vendor-demo-4e2ce35bbb/node_modules/@vendor/demo"}
[B2] VERDICT=PASS
```

The released strict reader keys the record by the npm package name (`@vendor/demo`); head reads the JSON5 `id` and rekeys to `demo`, keeping `integrity`, `installedAt` and `installPath`; the rekeyed state survives persistence and a cold reload.

Note on where the write comes from: `loadInstalledPluginIndexInstallRecords` itself only reads and caches, as the review observed. The rekeyed map reaches disk when a caller that owns registry persistence writes it — the plugin-install commit path, or `openclaw doctor --fix` when its preflight selects `migrate`/`initialize` (with a readable index already present, preflight selects `skip-existing` and doctor intentionally writes nothing). Phase B uses that same production write pair (`withPluginLifecycleLease` + `writePersistedInstalledPluginIndexInstallRecordsWithLease`) rather than inventing a new one.

Result: the identity migrates, the persisted metadata and install path survive, and the state is stable across persistence and a fresh-process reload.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+72/-10` net +62 (one shared helper in `json-files.ts`; two call sites; atomic import retained; recovery rekey)
- Test LOC: `+61`
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses `parseJsonWithJson5Fallback` (the JSON5-capable parser already used by the main loader and `state-migrations.fs.ts`) and the existing `tryReadJsonObjectSync` null-on-failure contract; the reconciliation reuses the existing `recordsShareInstallPath` owner predicate — no new abstraction beyond the shared helper the two call sites need.
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none. `package.json` reads remain strict; the JSON5 reader is used only for `openclaw.plugin.json`.

### Cleanup

The shipped-CLI proof runs used isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` / `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` directories (`/w/s-base`, `/w/s-head`, `/w/state-up`) created for this run, each with `chmod 700`, inside a disposable container. Two separate builds were used: the latest release `v2026.11.6` (`06afb10d327`) and the PR head (`cc6dac4b097`), each built to its own `dist`. No running Gateway, session, token, or production config was touched.

prs.title: fix: explain node restart steps after manual updates
prs.body:
Related: #204266

## What Problem This Solves

On a node-only host, a manual package update can finish successfully while the managed node keeps running its previous runtime. Gateway-only restart output does not explain that the node was left alone or what the operator should do next.

## User Impact

Successful in-place updates identify a running node belonging to the replaced installation and tell the operator to wait for idle, then run `openclaw node restart`. Stopped nodes and nodes belonging to another installation do not receive that claim.

Prepared-release updates explicitly say the Gateway trial is pending and warn that restarting a node alone cannot activate it. This PR does **not** add node restarts, change idle/drain policy, repair legacy launchers, or implement node-only activation of Gateway release trials.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both updater generations use one read-only node-service inspector and retain the notice in update history/JSON. The legacy candidate finalizer supplies the in-place guidance; the current release owner records the staging distinction and the CLI displays it. Native inspection that cannot positively identify the running same-install node remains best effort.

The candidate-side change reaches shipped updaters that delegate finalization. An updater that finishes entirely in its installed code needs a backport to its supported stable line (including the 2026.9 extended-stable line); this main-targeted PR does not perform that backport.

## Evidence

- Missing notices reproduced as failing regressions on base `8b17822bec4f36582bf5e15743087b32fd3460b1`, then passed with the repair. Coverage includes same-package running nodes with no local Gateway, stopped/foreign nodes, persisted warnings, plain CLI output, and prepared-release staging.
- Focused suites: CLI 22 passed; release preparation 31 passed; legacy finalization 98 passed; service maintenance 40 passed. Changed field-report cases were rerun after incorporating the [additional observations](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/204266#issuecomment-7116719559).
- Follow-up verification: the package preparation regression launches a fresh `dist/index.js node run` process through the generated release forwarder, observes the old package, and checks the Gateway trial remains pending. Both touched suites pass (22 CLI and 31 preparation cases). This fixture does not simulate systemd or prove the published update hop.
- Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, docs inventory, and `git diff --check` passed.
- An isolated execution of the actual generated launcher confirmed that `node run` keeps the old selected release and leaves a pending Gateway trial untouched.
- Auto Review (OpenClaw engine, `openai/gpt-6.2-sol`) reviewed the complete local change against the base above: no **P0** findings. This was a P0-only review, not an all-severity clearance.
- Simplification: one shared advisory implementation, with existing update/history owners retained; no additional activation owner, service mutation, or schema.

**Draft / remaining proof:** The real published-updater-to-candidate hop on a Linux systemd node-only host, unchanged-PID/manual-recovery verification, and the release contract's multi-platform and T → T+1 → T+2 runs are **unproven**. This sandbox has no systemd user manager. Unit/integration fixtures and the launcher probe do not replace those runs. No live service or user installation was touched. Full build and exact-head CI are not claimed.

<details>
<summary>Local proof details</summary>

Tests used the repository `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` wrapper with `--maxWorkers=1`. Measured test durations: CLI about 8 seconds; preparation 27.26 seconds; finalization 138.17 seconds; service maintenance 7.19 seconds. CI seconds are not yet available.

An existing unwritable-package fixture initially failed with `target-metadata-unavailable` rather than `package-not-writable`. The same failure reproduced with unchanged base source: the sandbox's workspace-contained TMPDIR let package fixtures discover the parent Git checkout. Bounding Git discovery with `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES=$TMPDIR` made the complete preparation suite pass without changing the fixture assertion or production admission.

The completed [ClawSweeper issue assessment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/204266#issuecomment-7116616245) independently identifies the same two reporting paths and activation distinction.

</details>

Thanks to @DonnieFi for the field report and reproduction details.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b5d66242-4f71-4dd0-8a69-31ea7795a2a0)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/c32c134a-c289-42c3-acbf-37194ea426a6)

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

## Worked on by

- @DonnieFi

prs.title: fix: let signed-in Gateway users connect personal MCP accounts
prs.body:
Closes #138113

Closes #188164 — supersedes the authenticated Webchat requester and OAuth lifecycle fix.

Closes #202434 — supersedes the alternative browser fix, including shared-tool independence when personal authority is denied.

Closes #177356 — supersedes the verified-profile fix for users behind the same Gateway backend and reuses their MCP Apps sign-in.

Closes #189257 — supersedes the verified requester fix for Chat Completions and Responses HTTP callers.

Closes #158852 — supersedes the cached-catalog fix for a missing connect tool when another personal server is already connected.

Contributor credit: @apps3000, @SeveHo, @Canvinus, @tguggenberger-lab, and @chelsealong for the authored commits and proof carried forward; @jacobtomlinson for reporting the HackMD reproduction and directing the combined repair. The original commit authors are preserved; integration is a separate commit.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b88083e9-c798-484b-8632-377bbc5d25b7)

## What Problem This Solves

People signed in to the Control UI can be unable to connect a personal MCP account. Gateway clients behind the same trusted proxy can share a sign-in, and verified OpenAI-compatible HTTP callers can lack a personal requester altogether. A separate catalog bug hides a second server's sign-in tool once another server is connected.

## User Impact

Verified users can use their own OAuth account from browser chat, trusted-proxy Gateway chat, and the Chat Completions and Responses HTTP routes. Their profile uses the same credential namespace as MCP Apps. People previously using a backend's shared requester identity will sign in once as themselves; the legacy credential is not deleted or copied. Shared MCP servers and channel sender attribution are unchanged. Scheduled and spawned work does not inherit a personal account. If another participant steers a turn while a personal MCP write is in flight, the write that already started still returns its result; later personal calls in that turn are refused.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing Gateway-verified identity and admitted turn authority rather than rewriting transport sender IDs. A browser request must match the live participant; personal authorization is checked once when each personal MCP operation starts, reusing the attempt's existing ownership fence, outside the shared partition. Select the cached/live catalog first, then add absent servers' connect entries. The single-use sign-in-link trust model is unchanged; use a private session or a mutually trusted audience. This does not add personal sign-in to Settings or `openclaw mcp login`, nor change standalone Claude Code or OpenClaw's separate `claude-cli` runner.

## Evidence

Current head: `9c19fcee097c35e24385caaf9f9df0a370336399`. It differs from `573fff87e2d762baced3498f43cbd127b3dc98c8` only by test-only commit `c4358072d632`, which consolidates duplicated test setup to fit the test-line budget. All runs were on isolated AWS Crabbox machines with no instance role (IMDS returned `404`), and each pinned its exact head.

- [Review-fix proof at `573fff87`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_501f15b164fb03e7ee27645043b8c312):
  - **Settlement regression:** the new test fails against the prior settlement code (`21afee89`) with `Several people have steered` and passes with the fix. A personal write that was admitted before a second participant steered the turn now returns its result. The next call is still refused.
  - **Focused tests:** 78 passed.
  - **Gateway OAuth tests:** 3 of 3 passed. They cover verified users on backend chat, verified users on browser chat, and the shared-token backend client.
- [Changed test file at `9c19fcee`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_20164beccba6ce4c6df501b6a785a4bd): `src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-webchat-requester.test.ts` passed.
- [Shipped-CLI in-place upgrade at `9c19fcee`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_66d59b9207e89fa35181d9557755587b): passed.
  1. A foreground `openclaw@2026.11.7` Gateway ran with isolated state and a pinned TLS certificate. Its shared-token backend client completed a real consent and callback against the synthetic OAuth server and then used that account.
  2. The shipped Gateway was stopped. The candidate's `doctor --fix --non-interactive` then migrated the agent database from v38 to v43 in place.
  3. A fresh candidate Gateway reused the same account with no new sign-in and exactly one client registration.
  4. Earlier replay attempts failed for harness setup reasons only: TLS session reuse, a missing trusted-proxy entry, and a doctor timeout while building Control UI assets.
- The verified-user cases run only on the candidate. The shipped CLI had no per-profile requester to upgrade from, so verified users sign in once as themselves, as described above.
- Core and affected test typechecks, the session-identity and lifetime-check ratchets, the test-line budget, changed-file lint and formatting, and `git diff --check` passed locally.

### CI attribution

The [comparison run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_364986b683ffeb057cf7bd494b222f90) ran each test file that failed CI at the PR head, at base `36bc0460`, and at current `main` (`57dd84bd1e0f`).

- Every failure reproduces at the PR base with the same assertions. This PR did not cause them:
  - `src/model-picker/apply-session-model-selection.operator-context.test.ts`
  - `src/gateway/session-access-authority.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/command/model-selection.configured.test.ts`
  - `src/gateway/server-methods/themes.test.ts`
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-compaction-fallback.test.ts`
- The first three pass on current `main`. `themes` and `compaction-fallback` still fail there.
- Four jobs are not attributed: `compact-large-4`, `compact-large-17`, `compact-large-27`, and `extensions-bundle-2`. Their logs only show the final `exit 1` within the readable tail.

The proof uses a synthetic OAuth/MCP server and a deterministic model fixture. It does not test live HackMD, Claude CLI, or browser rendering. The source PRs remain open while this replacement is reviewed.

## Worked on by

- @jacobtomlinson

prs.title: fix(ui): resume Logs auto-follow when WebKit delivers a wheel's scroll late
prs.body:
## Result

In Safari (WebKit), when a reader scrolls the Logs stream back to the end with the mouse wheel, Auto-follow turns back on, even when the browser is busy. Before this change, Auto-follow could stay off although the reader was at the newest line. This is the intermittent `logs-scroll.e2e.test.ts` "wheel in webkit (1440 px)" failure: red on 5 of 12 scheduled runs, `expected false to be true` at the Auto-follow check, after the "at the end" and "last row visible" checks had passed.

## Cause

Auto-follow turns back on only for scroll events that count as reader input: a wheel opens a 200 ms window (`READER_INTENT_MS`), which starts at the wheel's first animation frame. WebKit applies wheel scrolling off the main thread. When the main thread is busy, the wheel's scroll event can arrive after that window has closed. Then:

1. The late scroll event does not count as the reader. Rows near the end are measured at that moment, so the view is a little above the end (in the test, 78 px).
2. The next layout measurement moves the view to the end. That scroll does not count as the reader either, so Auto-follow stays off.

The hypothesis "a later layout measurement moves the view to the end after the window closes" is correct, but only together with the late wheel scroll event. When the wheel's scroll event arrives inside the window, the reader reaches the end first and Auto-follow resumes. Probes in 40 local WebKit runs showed the wheel's scroll event 13-20 ms after the wheel, so the failure did not reproduce locally. The new unit test sets the timing directly.

## Fix

`beginReaderScroll` (in `ui/src/pages/logs/view.tsx`, which owns the reader-intent state): a vertical wheel that has room to scroll keeps reader intent until its first scroll event. That scroll event starts the normal 200 ms idle window, so the measurements that follow are counted as part of the reader's own travel. All other input does not change: touch, keys, a horizontal wheel, or a wheel with no room to scroll still start the window at the first frame. No new timer, flag or state.

Accepted edge case: if a vertical wheel with room to scroll produces no scroll on the stream, intent stays on until the next scroll on the stream. The wheel listener is on the stream, and rows do not scroll by themselves, so this does not occur in the current layout.

## Evidence

- New unit test `resumes following when WebKit delivers a wheel's travel to the end after the idle window` (`view.test.tsx`). It sets the scroll event to arrive 250 ms late and makes rows measure 23 px against a 20 px estimate. It fails on the base 78d2f2e70746 (`expected false to be true`) and passes on the head.
- `view.test.tsx` + `logs-page.test.tsx`: 30 passed.
- Control UI E2E on the head: `logs-scroll.e2e.test.ts` (3 cases, including wheel in WebKit 1440 px) and `logs-autofollow.e2e.test.ts` (4 cases): all passed.

prs.title: fix(sessions): charge settled run billing to goal token budgets
prs.body:
Closes #203350

## What Problem This Solves

An explicitly budgeted built-in Goal reported `tokensUsed: 0` for its whole lifetime when the fresh context snapshot stayed flat: the budget only grew from the context-window high-water delta, so runs whose billed input/output outpace context growth (heavy cache reads, compaction, or a constant fresh snapshot) admitted unbounded ordinary continuations at any budget.

## Fix

`projectSessionEntryUsageUpdate` now passes each run's settled billable tokens (`input + output`) into the goal accounting, which accumulates them in a new optional `billedTokensUsed` field and takes the max of the context high-water mark and the accumulated billing. Budgets are enforced against settled consumption regardless of context growth.

## Compatibility

- Baseline adoption and stale-baseline holds keep their existing semantics: the run that establishes the baseline is not double-charged, matching the context window.
- Budget-window resets (`/goal resume` on a budget-limited goal) clear the accumulated billing with the rest of the window.
- Goals persisted before this change keep working: the new field is optional and the context high-water mark remains the floor.

## Evidence

- Pre-fix repro (unmodified main): driving the production `projectSessionEntryUsageUpdate` with a constant 20,000-token fresh context and settled billing of 45k, 45k, then 10.5k left `tokensUsed: 0` and status `active` after every settlement — the 100k budget never engaged.
- Post-fix: the same sequence charges 45,000 → 90,000 → 100,500 into the goal and flips status to `budget_limited` exactly at the cap (`billedTokensUsed: 100500`).
- Regression coverage: a flat-context settlement test in `session-usage.test.ts` asserts the three-step charge and the cap transition; the existing fresh-snapshot accounting test now asserts the settled-billing semantics (`tokensUsed: 130` for a 105-token baseline followed by a 130-token run).
- `tsgo` core typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, and the pre-commit protocol checks pass on this tree.

## Notes for reviewers

- `cacheRead`/`cacheWrite` stay out of the charged amount on purpose: the issue's expectation charges `input + output` only, and cache-heavy runs are exactly where the context delta already undercounts.
- The vitest suite could not run on this constrained environment (OOM, exit 137); behavior was verified by driving the production projector directly via `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs` both pre-fix and post-fix. CI remains the authoritative test run.

prs.title: fix: keep configured agent skills available to automations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled agent runs using a different execution workspace can lose skills installed in their configured agent workspace. A skill available in an interactive conversation can consequently be unavailable to the same agent's automation.

## User Impact

Automations retain the configured agent's skill catalog while still discovering execution-workspace-only skills. Configured skills keep their documented precedence. No configuration changes, skill copies, migration, or permission changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cron snapshot preparation was treating the selected execution workspace as the sole primary skill root. Resolve the configured agent workspace through the existing agent-scope owner and pass the execution workspace separately to the existing reusable snapshot owner. This keeps normalization, precedence, eligibility, library selections, and stale-root refresh in their current owner rather than adding cron-specific policy.

Author self-review and simplification completed: production delta +3/-1 lines, test delta +58/-0 lines; no new helper, state, compatibility branch, or duplicate discovery implementation. Local automated/independent prepublication review was intentionally skipped under the task's review policy; hosted ClawSweeper review is requested after publication.
