prs.title: fix(cron): catch missing account selection before enabling automations
prs.body:
Related: #195802

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: enabling or editing an agent-turn automation could appear to succeed even though every scheduled run would stop with `Automation has no recorded inference account`.

## User Impact

**Before:** the job could be saved as enabled, fail on every run, and eventually be automatically disabled. Simply enabling it again could repeat the same failure.

**After:** when an edit would leave an enabled job without the stored account selection its runs require, OpenClaw rejects the edit immediately and names the model and account to select. Disabling the job is still allowed.

**Existing jobs:** installing this change alone is not a blanket repair of older automations. If a job reports the missing-account error, an authorized user can record the intended account with:

```sh
openclaw automations edit <jobId> --model <provider/model>@<profileId>
```

This also sets the job's model; re-enable the job afterward if it was disabled. The equivalent `openclaw cron edit` repair was [confirmed by a user on 2026.11.2 with an isolated Claude CLI automation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/195890#issuecomment-6778141386). Existing Doctor adoption for eligible accounts is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Having a signed-in model account is not the same as recording which account a scheduled job is authorized to use. The account may be available to interactive chat while the job still lacks that authorization record; the error does not necessarily mean credentials are missing or expired.

**Why this helps:** it turns a misleading successful edit followed by repeated unattended failures into an immediate, actionable account-selection error. The runtime's safety check stays intact: this does not borrow another account, weaken ownership or revocation checks, or add a fallback.

The PR closes two gaps:

- **Editing an existing job:** use the existing account-capture logic to check the job's resulting state, including when an edit removes native runtime authority. An ordinary edit does not silently choose an account for the job.
- **Re-declaring an existing job:** when `cron.add` matches a job by `declarationKey` and that job has no recorded account, save the account already authorized by the declaring context—even when that is the only change. Existing account bindings are not replaced.

**Scope:** this prevents the supported edit/re-declaration paths from preserving this failure state; it does not fix every way a job can lack an account. Template-created jobs, bundled-plugin scheduling, provider-changing declarations and session-event error propagation are outside this patch. The original incident's creation path is still unestablished, so this is `Related`, not `Closes`.

## Evidence

- November 23 revalidation at `d3b6da12cb60`: installed frozen-lockfile dependencies in an isolated worktree; all 50 `cron.inference-binding.test.ts` cases passed (277.20 seconds suite duration). Changed-file format and diff checks passed. Cleanup inspection found no justified production or test deletions; source is unchanged.

- Regression tests cover account-only declaration persistence, inherited and Gmail-hook models, and refusal of unauthorized or replaced accounts.
- An isolated Gateway/CLI run demonstrated the refusal and explicit-account recovery; a separate 2026.11.2 upgrade run checked existing jobs and history.
- The current head passed the CI gates, and ClawSweeper's completed review lists no findings.

Live Codex execution is **not** claimed: Codex coverage uses a harness fixture. The live runtime proof used OpenClaw with a loopback provider.

<details>
<summary>Verification details and sanitized output (November 9, 2026)</summary>

**Upgrade from 2026.11.2 (latest stable at test time) → this branch.** The installer's 7-day package-age policy blocked `openclaw@2026.11.2` from npm, so the stable side was built from the `v2026.11.2` tag source (`b556fdf`). Both sides ran an isolated Gateway on the same temp state with the real CLI, SQLite and a loopback stub provider that logs the Authorization header. On stable: an unbound job and a declared job were created on a provider-config key, then a stored OpenAI key was added, then a job explicitly bound to it was created and both were run. The branch then ran the normal `doctor --fix` and Gateway. The tested checkout was labeled 2026.11.1, so branch commands used `OPENCLAW_ALLOW_OLDER_BINARY_DESTRUCTIVE_ACTIONS=1`, as the repo's own upgrade harnesses do; database compatibility checks still apply.

**Gateway handler tests** (`src/gateway/server-methods/cron.inference-binding.test.ts`, real SQLite, auth stores and capture, registered Codex harness fixture):

**Test-line growth:** `config/test-lines-allocations/195802-cron-edit-inference-account.txt` grants exactly the +171 net lines of these regressions. `check-test-lines-ratchet` passes locally against main.

prs.title: docs: correct Codex catalog diagnostic guidance
prs.body:
Closes #201798

## What Problem This Solves

Operators investigating slow Codex session catalog requests are directed to cache-wait logs and counters that the resident catalog no longer emits. The guide also misstates the scope of request timing fields, making the available diagnostics harder to interpret.

## User Impact

The logging guide now describes the summaries and fields that operators can actually observe, including how background hydration relates to a list request.

## Why This Change Was Made

The resident catalog replaced the earlier per-query cache. The guide now describes its two diagnostic summaries and their current fields, removes retired cache observations, and clarifies the request-loop and projection timing boundaries. It does not change runtime behavior.

## Evidence

- Compared the guide against the current Codex catalog diagnostic field types, emission paths, hydration call sites, and background-context regression test.
- Documentation format: 1,449 files checked; all passed.
- Documentation MDX: 1,449 files checked; all passed.
- Internal links: 16,760 checked; zero broken.
- `git diff --check` passed. Documentation-only change; no runtime reproduction was performed.


### Review follow-up

The shared-budget paragraph now refers to “these summaries,” matching the two supported summaries described above. On the follow-up tree, `docs/logging.md` passed the targeted MDX and formatting checks, and `git diff --check` passed. The broader documentation checks above were run before this one-line follow-up.


### Catalog diagnostics regression

Ran `pnpm test extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-diagnostics.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 9 tests passed. prs.title: fix(sessions): unread follows visible transcript rows, not run ends
prs.body:
Closes #204164.

## Problem

A session went unread with nothing new to read. Example (synthetic): a heartbeat or child-end wake runs in a chat, the model answers `NO_REPLY` (or `HEARTBEAT_OK`), and the chat shows no new row, but the sidebar lights its unread dot.

Cause: unread was stamped per run, not per content.
- The run-end lifecycle projection set `lastActivityAt = endedAt` for every Control UI–visible run (`controlUiVisible`).
- Agent-command post-run set `lastActivityAt = now` for every run without internal events (`touchActivity`), with a special case for subagent coordination turns (#204143).
- Auto-reply `initSessionState` and `commitBackgroundResultToSession` stamped it separately for inbound messages and background/cron results.

None of these knew whether the run added anything a person can see.

## Change

One rule, applied where rows are appended: a session becomes unread (and a snooze ends) only when an appended user or assistant row is one the chat renders with something to read. The decision is `projectVisibleSessionActivity` (`src/config/sessions/session-visible-activity.ts`). It uses the Control UI's own per-message projection (`projectChatDisplayMessage`). Silent replies, heartbeat prompts and acknowledgements, wake inputs, `display: false` coordination rows, tool calls and reasoning do not count.

The rule writes the entry only when it changes something: when a visible row makes a read session unread, or ends a snooze. Appends to a chat that is already unread stay transcript-only writes, so streaming previews keep their no-rematerialize path.

It is applied by the existing append owners, in the same transaction as the append:
- transcript turns (`buildExpectedTranscriptTurnSessionPatch`: chat sends, channel inbound, chat inject, background and cron results);
- SessionManager appends outside a turn (`appendTranscriptMessageSnapshotSync`: embedded run replies, including `openclaw agent --local`);
- the in-memory (incognito) actor's event writer.

Removed:
- the run-end `lastActivityAt` stamp, and `controlUiVisible` on lifecycle events, which only fed it;
- agent-command `touchActivity`, its coordination special case, and its snooze clearing;
- the `initSessionState` and background-result `lastActivityAt` stamps, and `lastActivityAt` in the turn lifecycle patch type;
- the lifecycle-event unread recomputation in `buildGatewaySessionSnapshot`.

Channel inbound messages, background/cron results and `--local` replies still mark unread, because each appends a visible row.

`scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt` gains the projection modules that the session writer now imports (the PR-wrapper import inventory test lists them).

Production line delta (excluding tests, docs and the wrapper/test inventories): **+86 / −43 (net +43)**. The add is the one decision function and its three appliers; the per-run stamps it replaces were smaller.

## What the user sees

- A turn that ends in `NO_REPLY`, a quiet heartbeat, or an internal wake no longer lights the unread dot.
- A visible reply, a channel message, or a delivered cron/background result still does.
- A visible message in a snoozed session still wakes it; a quiet turn no longer does.

## Accepted edge cases

- `lastActivityAt` now marks the visible row that made the session unread. Further rows in a chat that is already unread do not move it. Row order uses `lastInteractionAt`/`updatedAt` as before. Chat prefetch keys on `lastActivityAt`, so it does not re-warm an already-unread chat for each later row; opening the chat still loads its history.
- Imports, forks and other batch installs of existing history do not mark unread: they copy rows the reader already had (older than the read baseline).
- Legacy rows without `createdAt` or `lastReadAt` were never unread and still are not; a visible row still wakes them from a snooze.

## Review notes

- Local ClawSweeper findings and why two are rejected: see the `Rejected review findings:` comment. Round 2 (a snoozed legacy session would not wake) is fixed.
- CI: `model-selection.configured.test.ts` fails on `main` too (`ci-triage`: MAIN-ALSO). Our reds were fixed: per-append entry writes broke the streaming-preview row contract (now only unread transitions write), the wrapper import inventory, and a stale test inventory entry for the deleted snooze test.

## Evidence

- `src/shared/session-unread.test.ts` (rewritten) drives real SQLite appends through `SessionManager` and `persistSessionTranscriptTurn`:
  - stays read after a NO_REPLY wake turn, a quiet heartbeat, a parent's reply to a child's `sessions_send` (snooze kept);
  - turns unread and ends the snooze after a visible reply or a channel message; a batched turn that also writes metadata keeps it.
  - On base: the "turns unread" cases fail (appends never set activity); the "stays read" cases pass (base's bug is in the run-end stamp).
- `src/gateway/session-lifecycle-state.test.ts`: a visible run's end no longer moves `lastActivityAt`. Red on base, green on head.
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/destination-completion.test.ts`: a delivered cron result marks a read destination unread.
- Real-Gateway Control UI E2E (throwaway, not committed; only the model provider is scripted; dist build): two chats each get an `agent` turn with a hidden heartbeat input while the browser shows a third chat. The first reply is `NO_REPLY`, the second visible.
  - Base (merge base): **fails**, the `NO_REPLY` chat shows an unread dot.
  - Head: **passes** on the first head and again on 854cdb36a1be: the `NO_REPLY` chat stays read and the visible-reply chat shows a dot. Screenshots in the PR comment.
- `src/shared/session-unread.test.ts` also covers a snoozed legacy row (no read baseline) waking on a visible reply.
- `pnpm check:changed` on the first head: typecheck, lint, guards and import cycles pass. The PostgreSQL turn-count conformance lane was not run locally (no PostgreSQL); the SQLite turn-count budget is unchanged.

prs.title: fix: long outbound replies stall the gateway while being split
prs.body:
Closes #199440

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the gateway stalls and spikes memory when it splits a long outbound reply that has spaces or non-ASCII text.

## User Impact

User impact: a multi-MiB message no longer blocks other sessions for seconds or allocates GBs of native memory.

## Why This Change Was Made

The grapheme helpers segmented the whole remaining text for every chunk. They now segment a bounded window, so the work is linear.

## Evidence

- New work-volume test fails on `main`, passes here.
- `chunkText` on 4 MiB of spaced text: 2478 ms before, 15 ms after.
- chunk, text-chunking and markdown-core tests pass (286). tsc, oxfmt, oxlint clean.
- Not run: Windows, a live channel send.

## Real behavior proof

Real `chunkText` (`src/auto-reply/chunk.ts`), 4 MiB spaced input, limit 4000, fresh process, Node v24.22.3, Linux x86_64. Run in a checkout of base `918847e` and head `3c0c157`:

```text
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs --input-type=module -e 'import{createHash}from"node:crypto";import{chunkText}from"./src/auto-reply/chunk.ts";const t=("a".repeat(3990)+" ").repeat(1052);const s=performance.now();const c=chunkText(t,4000);console.log(c.length,"chunks",Math.round(performance.now()-s),"ms",process.resourceUsage().maxRSS>>10,"MB peak RSS","sha",createHash("sha256").update(JSON.stringify(c)).digest("hex").slice(0,12))'

base: 1052 chunks 4796 ms 4397 MB peak RSS sha db583116377c
head: 1052 chunks   31 ms  184 MB peak RSS sha db583116377c
```

Non-ASCII spaced text: base 4533 ms, 8623 MB; head ~50 ms, ~200 MB; same output hash. Peak RSS includes ~180 MB of startup.

Base vs head output: identical chunks for emoji, ZWJ, combining marks, flags, CRLF and prepend clusters at boundaries, and 20k random cases through `chunkText`, `chunkMarkdownText` and markdown-core `chunkText`. Only 2 cases differ, where the limit is smaller than one cluster (cut inside it, no text lost). This check also found a CRLF/prepend whitespace bug, fixed in the second commit.

Gateway run: same setup with a 4198532-char spaced reply sent through the Gateway `send` RPC to the IRC channel (local stub IRC server), `/healthz` polled meanwhile. Base `a8a7ce9`, head `720faa7`, one run each:


prs.body:
Closes #204261

## What Problem This Solves

People using Talk with `gpt-live-1` cannot pick the voices OpenAI added to GPT-Live, such as `flitz` (German) or `brise` (French). They never show up in the voice picker, and if you set one in config anyway, the session quietly starts with `marin` instead. There is no warning or log entry.

## User Impact

All 16 voices that OpenAI documents for GPT-Live but OpenClaw was missing can now be selected and actually reach the session: brise, calandria, compas, destello, flitz, halo, harema, hornero, juni, luciernaga, nira, noeul, nuri, pearl, shida, sillage. Unknown names still fall back to `marin` as before, and `gpt-live-1-codex` voices are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The public `gpt-live-1` voice allowlist was out of date compared to OpenAI's "Managing GPT-Live sessions" guide (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/live-conversations, voice options table). This PR only refreshes that list and the matching docs and catalog test. Following the ClawSweeper review, it deliberately does not change the fallback policy or add custom-voice pass-through.

## Evidence

- New regression test in `realtime-quicksilver-wire-profile.test.ts`: `gpt-live-1` with flitz, nuri, juni, pearl, luciernaga and noeul keeps the voice in `audio.output.voice`. An unknown voice still becomes `marin`.
- Base-failing check: with the source change reverted, the 6 new voice cases fail (`Tests 6 failed | 3 passed`). With the fix: `Tests 9 passed (9)`.

- `oxfmt --check` on the touched TS files: clean. `git diff --check`: clean.
- Not run locally: `realtime-voice-browser-auth.test.ts` (it only updates the expected catalog list) plus typecheck and lint, because the local test host has a 1 GiB memory cap. Left to CI.
- Not verified: a live audio session with `flitz`.

prs.title: fix(ci): run MLX proof for frozen targets without a bundled driver
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192782

## What Problem This Solves

The macOS MLX workflow fails before running tests when a frozen target contains the MLX runtime but predates the native proof driver. [The existing frozen-target run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43576909441/job/132393503708) exited because the candidate did not contain `scripts/test-macos-mlx-native.py`.

## User Impact

CI can assess supported frozen MLX targets without copying controller code into them or treating missing proof tooling as a not-applicable result.

## Why This Change Was Made

The platform checkout owner materializes the trusted driver, sandbox policy and bad-lock reference in `.ci-harness`. The driver authenticates the candidate root, commit, tree, tracked modes and complete package inputs. Controller assets retain their independent workflow identity; both sets of inputs are checked again after resolve, build and test.

A target without both config-preflight files must run the six original helper tests. If either file is present, both are required and all thirteen tests apply. Partial, unknown, mutated, symlinked or untracked build inputs fail closed. Extended proof cannot downgrade to baseline; per-method evidence, deadlines and cleanup remain enforced.

The baseline also contained an incompatible role-tool call. Its correction keeps cancellation and authorization before commit, while returning the actual committed result or error when a self-downgrade retires the caller. This uses the existing request contract; other gateway operations are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Current signed candidate `c961eb3543a9253c4e168fc478d1cf3cabe41871`, tree `fc39013a7a18fe3813c79d2a65380378d87efef7`, has ordered parents `e56ad7860ad7938b004105b6c9635f01f77147e1` and frozen baseline `f7558cc8ff82cbcd9c9573d32f175b76e33bfe94`. Native reconciliation resolved exactly the role-tool call conflict. All seven owned MLX/gateway/test blobs remain byte-identical to the prior tested correction, and every other tree entry matches the frozen baseline.
- On this composition, the 55 gateway/storage/request tests and both core and gateway-server test typechecks passed. The four dependency inputs are unchanged from the private frozen installation. Fresh hosted exact-head gates remain required.
- The optional state-reader task-counter assertion is already present in that baseline: unavailable measurement remains an error and zero remains valid.
- Supporting prior correction proof: 55 gateway/tool/storage tests and 127 MLX/workflow tests passed. The new self-downgrade regression fails against the unrepaired baseline and passes with the correction. Precommit cancellation/revocation, next-call denial, original-admin audit and committed-error delivery remain asserted.
- Before this composition, core and gateway-server test typechecks, focused lint/format, whitespace checks, normal signed-commit hooks, and `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` passed. The build includes SDK declarations/export checks and UI assets. Dependencies were installed privately from the frozen baseline inputs.
- [Prior CI 44726749361](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44726749361) tested merge `f73d3dadb99615a499883d01d2f900048507165c` and failed on the obsolete role-tool option; SDK publication then blocked dependent restores. Those failures remain retained. Fresh exact-head hosted checks are pending; no prior result is transferred.
- [Original CI 43604565114](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43604565114) failed the optional counter check and had three setup jobs exhaust the sandbox-start budget before commands. Current capacity is unknown from that historical evidence; no check is waived.

Historical supporting native evidence:

- [Actual Xcode 27 MLX job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43603189598/job/132472522118): controller, trigger and candidate were exactly `f1ddcf9f52852884a684e93f5a3a85a39f329bb2`, tree `bc514485e0e6d3a46bba57cd84a3a171722ed18f`. All thirteen methods passed (six helper plus seven config-preflight). Native proof reports complete=true, processes/pipes retired, platform destinations retired and scratch removed. Extended model inference was not selected. Artifact SHA256: `beb2d50678fe7683aff483d5f7ba2ef0b7b3a0ba277da1b0ca9dd621af64fbc5`.
- That manual run is supporting proof for the unchanged implementation, not CI or a tested merge for the new head. [Its native-i18n failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43603189598/job/132472521820) remains failed: all 100 reported IDs were already in the frozen parent's inventory and absent from its 21 translation files; the nine source files and checker inputs are unchanged. This is source attribution, not a baseline runtime pass or a classification of other jobs.

prs.title: fix(agents): settle every undelivered child completion into history; drop delivery dispositions
prs.body:
## Problem

#204178 made a child's status entry in the parent's history the delivery, but left the old delivery dispositions behind: `permanent_failure`, `ambiguous`, `intentional_non_delivery`, the announce error classifier that produced them, and a 5-minute retry/give-up ladder for announces without an explicit completion mode. Generated-media completion still read the shared dispositions.

One more gap showed up in the live run: when the user pressed Stop on the parent's turn while a finished child's completion was waiting to steer in, the steer was cancelled, the delivery settled, and the child's result was dropped (the session's status was `killed`, and the history append skipped killed requesters). The parent's next turn did not have the result.

## Fix

Deletion only. A child's completion is either delivered, owned by a queue or mailbox, waiting for its requester, or not delivered. "Not delivered" settles into requester history on the first failure; nothing retries it.

- `SubagentAnnounceDeliveryResult` loses `disposition` and `terminal`. "A queue or mailbox owns this" is `path: "queued"`.
- Deleted: `classifyAnnounceDeliveryError`, `isPermanentAnnounceDeliveryError` and the permanent error pattern list, `sourceOwnerChangedResult`, ten never-read failure reasons, `resolveDeferredCleanupDecision`, the optional-announce retry/backoff and its 5-minute expiry (`ANNOUNCE_EXPIRY_MS`, resume-time expiry, `finalizeResumedAnnounceGiveUpInBackground`, the "failed" give-up branch, `logAnnounceGiveUp`), the `delivery_suppressed → failed` branch, the yielded-batch `intentional_non_delivery` marker, and the pause-notice clear on intentional outcomes.
- Announces without an explicit completion mode now settle into history on the first failure, like required ones. Children spawned with `expectsCompletionMessage: false` are unchanged.
- Generated-media completion no longer reads shared dispositions: delivered → delivered; `path: "queued"` → the durable media queue owns it; anything else → not confirmed (no retry, no "ambiguous counts as delivered").
- A Stopped parent still receives a finished child's status entry (one-line guard removal). Stop ends that turn; it does not discard work that already finished. A deleted requester still receives nothing.
- Persisted rows: no schema or DDL change. `delivery.disposition` stays in `payload_json`; old rows that carry a retired value decode unchanged and no reader looks at it. Legacy `suspended` rows keep their sweeper settlement, and legacy `failed` rows (results an older build gave up on) are settled into requester history the same way, once, instead of being removed by session retention.

Accepted edge cases:

- Media: a transient wake failure (for example a transcript conflict) now ends as "completion delivery was not confirmed" instead of retrying for up to 2 minutes; a partly sent wake reply is reported as not confirmed instead of delivered.
- An ended child whose yielded requester re-armed its batch now counts as an unsettled descendant until that batch settles (it was marked settled through the deleted marker). This can only delay an ancestor's own completion until the yielded batch wakes.

## User impact

The parent always gets a child's end state in its history when the wake did not consume it, including after the user stops the parent's turn. No retries, no give-up logs, no user-visible delivery rows.

## Evidence

Scratch Gateway from this branch (`ocx src`, real Claude route via cliproxy, isolated state). The parent spawns a child whose task is `echo zeta-$(date +%N)` (unguessable), then runs `sleep 150` without yielding; the child finishes while the parent is in the shell call; the user Stops that parent turn (`chat.abort`, `userInitiated`); then the user asks "What did the child you spawned report?".

- Before the guard removal (the #204178 rule): the completion steer was cancelled, the row settled `delivered` with no history entry, and the parent had nothing to read (its answer only matched because that child's task text contained the answer).
- After: log `Subagent status appended to requester history`; the parent transcript gets the model-visible entry `Child "…" (session agent:main:subagent:…, run …): completed — zeta-080312000`; the parent's next turn answers `zeta-080312000`, the value the child printed.
- Gateway logs for both runs: 0 `Subagent completion delivery` lines, 0 `delivery discarded`, 0 give-up lines.

Tests: tests that asserted the removed behavior were deleted (classifier and retry tables, optional-announce backoff and 5-minute expiry, permanent/ambiguous/intentional holds, media ambiguous-to-delivered, `logAnnounceGiveUp`); remaining fixtures moved to the new outcomes (`undelivered`, `path: "queued"`, history settlement). `ocx test src/agents/subagents/registry` 1,222 passed (1 failure, `subagent-registry-worker.test.ts` serialized-payload retention, fails the same way on the base); announce, completion, media, cron, gateway and SDK touched files 972 passed (1 Gateway-readiness timeout in `test/gateway-completion-replay.e2e.test.ts` before its scenario ran; it passed in the previous run). `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` clean. `pnpm check:changed`: everything green except the dead-export scan, whose remaining entries (`appendChildStatusToRequester`, two registry test-support fixtures, `runWindowsGatewayTaskSupervisor`, `ProjectGrant`) are unused on the base too; this PR's own leftover (`isReplaySafeTranscriptConflict`, whose only caller was the deleted classifier) is removed.

## Size

Production code (excluding tests and docs): `src/` +193 / −829 (net −636); with scripts +196 / −835 (net −639). Tests +209 / −948. Docs +9 / −9.

## Merge danger

Two-way door; no schema, protocol or dependency change. Blast radius: subagent completion delivery, requester settle, generated-media completion wake.

prs.title: fix(ui): reveal the transcript start when a WebKit reader reaches native zero
prs.body:
## Result

In WebKit, a reader who scrolls to the top of a chat (Home key or a fling) now gets the older history page. Before this change, about half of the runs stopped at the top of the loaded page and never asked for older messages.

## Cause

During native scrolling in WebKit, `TranscriptReaderAnchor` keeps rows that grow above the reader in place by moving the row column up (a negative margin), because a `scrollTop` write stops the scroll. When the reader reached native `scrollTop` 0, that held growth (about 1.3-1.4k px in the failing runs) was still above the reachable area:

- the history sentinel moved with the column, so it sat more than `CHAT_HISTORY_PREFETCH_EDGE_PX` (1200 px) above the viewport and the IntersectionObserver did not report it;
- when the scroll ended, `settle()` folded the shift into `scrollTop` (about 1374), so the reader stayed below the prefetch edge and no request was sent.

Runs where the held growth was under 1200 px passed. This is the `chat-history-reading-stability` "webkit, 390 px" failure in the scheduled `checks-ui-e2e` shard (`expected { messageCount: 30 } to deeply equal { messageCount: 190 }`).

## Fix

`settle()` treats native zero as the reader's start, the same rule `landSize` already applies to first measurements ("Native zero is the reader's start"). At native zero it releases held growth without writing `scrollTop`, so the transcript start (and the sentinel) comes into view and the older page loads. Other cases are unchanged.

## What the user sees

- WebKit, Home key or fling to the top: the start of the loaded history shows, and older messages load.
- The rows that were above the reader appear at that moment instead of after another scroll.
- Chromium and non-zero offsets: no change.

## Evidence

- Unit (`chat-transcript-reader-anchor.browser.test.ts`, new `growth` phase): fails on the base (`expected '-40px' to be ''`), passes on the head.
- Control UI E2E `chat-history-reading-stability.e2e.test.ts -t "webkit, 390"` with `repeats`, local, same machine:
  - base: 10 of 20 and 8 of 10 iterations failed (no `chat.history` older request; sentinel 1278-1352 px above the viewport at `scrollTop` 0);
  - head: 48 of 50 iterations passed (9/10, 19/20, 20/20).
- Remaining rare mode (2 of 50): a row correction applied while not held writes `scrollTop` in the first 100 ms of the Home animation, which stops it at about 8.7k px. This is a different path; it is not changed here.
- Focused UI tests that import the reader anchor or the virtualizer host: 111 passed.

prs.title: fix: add templates without requiring model sign-in
prs.body:
Closes #204207

## What Problem This Solves

Offline `openclaw templates add` can create an agent and then fail because its opening greeting needs a model sign-in. On the tested main commit, this leaves a retained agent, reports `partial`, and exits `1` before the remaining setup finishes.

## User Impact

Users can add a Template before connecting a model provider. If preflight finds no usable model or sign-in, Add skips the optional greeting, prints a short note to stderr (including with `--json`), and continues dependency installation, automations, and first-run instruction files. Successful setup exits `0`.

**Unchanged:** when a usable model is available, the greeting still runs. A model turn that is attempted and fails still reports `partial` and exits `1`; failed setup is not silently reported as success. There is no new setting, schema, or change to online Gateway Add.

## Why This Change Was Made

The greeting is optional, but installing the agent should not depend on having a model account. The preflight reuses the existing model-readiness owner for the effective model, its actual execution backend, and configured fallbacks; it does not accept an unrelated signed-in alternative. Automatically selected native backends can prepare their catalog before readiness is judged. Catalog errors are reported after the installer retains the agent, rather than rolling it back.

## Evidence

The comparison below is **main at `e2973f933f10364471f8d8e470d3c4a7c3d6be96` versus this PR head**, using the real source CLI on Linux x64. Each run uses a fresh isolated home/state directory, a stopped Gateway, `openai/gpt-5.4` configured with the native OpenClaw backend, and no provider credentials. Paths below are abbreviated to `./canary`.

```sh
pnpm openclaw templates create ./canary --agent-id orchard-canary --json
pnpm openclaw templates add ./canary --agent-id orchard-canary --json
```

**Before — main, selected CLI output:**

```json
{
  "status": "partial",
  "agentRetained": true,
  "error": {
    "code": "add_failed",
    "message": "No route-compatible authentication source is configured for openai. The agent was already made available and was kept. Continue setup in this agent; do not add another copy."
  }
}
```

Process exit: **1**.

**After — this PR head, stderr note:**

```text
Opening greeting skipped: no usable model or sign-in is available. Configure a model in Settings → Models, then open this agent's chat.
```

Selected CLI JSON output:

```json
{
  "status": "complete",
  "configCommitted": true
}
```

Process exit: **0**.

Additional checks:

- The no-model and no-sign-in regressions fail on main because it starts the greeting; the fix skips it.
- 83 focused tests passed in 88.52 seconds across the CLI adapter, CLI command, installer, and model-runtime-choice suites. Coverage includes configured fallbacks, automatic/explicit backend selection, catalog-error retention, native-catalog renewal, and failed/silent model completion.
- A bundled skill and package `BOOTSTRAP.md` were installed byte-for-byte after a skipped greeting, and the declared automation was created disabled. These are installed first-run instructions, not a claim that model-driven onboarding ran without a model.
- The real CLI with a **local HTTP provider fixture and synthetic credentials** made one successful greeting request (exit `0`) and one HTTP-rejected model request (`partial`, exit `1`). This verifies the attempted-turn path, not live provider authentication.
- CLI rebuild, targeted TypeScript checking, type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. `pr-simplify` was applied and the affected tests rerun; temporary proof services and fixtures were cleaned up.

**Not checked:** live provider sign-in or live-provider inference, ARM64 execution, or the full CI matrix. Local HTTP responses were synthetic.

<details>
<summary>Focused test command and review</summary>

```sh
OPENCLAW_TEST_PROJECTS_SERIAL=1 OPENCLAW_TEST_WORKERS=1 GOMAXPROCS=2 pnpm test \
  src/cli/templates-agent-conversation.test.ts \
  src/agents/model-runtime-choice.native.test.ts \
  src/cli/templates-cli.test.ts \
  src/templates/add-stateless.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Local Auto Review covered P0–P2 findings against the pinned main base. Its selected-runtime, agent-retention, and native-catalog preparation findings were corrected and covered by focused regressions. The built-in-default concern did not apply: the current selection owner does not invent an unconfigured model. No clean-review or live-provider result is inferred from the fixture checks. CI runtime is not yet available.

</details>

Human contributor: @daniel-lxs (report and requested behavior).

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/task-t_j35vj4)

- @daniel-lxs

prs.title: fix(plugins): stop source-receipt warnings during model refresh
prs.body:
Related: #177882 (source-receipt warning only; the separate memory-search failure is outside this fix).

## What Problem This Solves

Refreshing models can succeed while the Gateway logs “Plugin source receipt was not recorded: Shared-state admission requires the host broker” and fails to save the record of captured native companion files. This still reproduces on main after #200320.

## User Impact

Model refresh saves its captured native-file receipts without the host-broker warning. Receipt-write failures stay advisory, and the existing discovery deadline is preserved. No configuration, schema migration, or operator action is required for the fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog worker forwards publications over its existing task channel to the retained host-owned publisher, rather than trying to acquire shared-state authority itself. Retained artifacts use the current task channel, exchanges are serialized, and pending receipt writes settle before that channel closes.

The adaptation preserves #200320's broker-owned source roots and cleanup, as well as main's sleep-aware admission watchdog. The two receipt regressions move into a dedicated broker-backed test file instead of restoring the native suite retired on main. The task admission owner keeps its existing input-size validation; the duplicate caller check was removed.

Original fix and regression tests contributed by @MertBasar0. This continues the same PR and preserves its authorship.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/18472a57-03bf-47c3-90c6-29f26dfbd442)

## Evidence

**Fresh real-Gateway comparison on 2026-11-18:** both eager and retained/lazy model refreshes succeed in both variants. Host-broker warnings fall from **2 to 0**; persisted receipts rise from **0 to 1**, covering both captured artifacts with independently verified SHA-256 hashes after Gateway shutdown. The synthetic plugin is installed through the real CLI. No model inference or native binary execution was used; both isolated Gateways and their owned children were joined.

**Current validation:** three regression cases fail on the pinned base for the intended missing-receipt/deadline reasons; **66 focused tests across eight files pass** on the adaptation. After the final duplicate-validation simplification, **40 pool tests pass** (20 repeat earlier coverage), and the real-Gateway comparison passes again. Core, agent-test and package-test typechecks, targeted production/test lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass.

**Published head:** `bba64ec693034893bd25b2db9440ef44affdbb4c`; its complete tree matches the validated workspace. Independent source-snapshot review found no actionable defects across all nine changed files. A test comment was clarified afterward without changing executable behavior. The reviewer did not run tests or verify a checkout; the local Auto Review launcher was unavailable and is not claimed as completed. [One hosted re-review was requested](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/198572#issuecomment-6989886602) after the branch and proof were updated; completion is pending. **Required CI is blocked on maintainer workflow approval:** [CI run 44385446283](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44385446283) targets this exact head, reports `action_required`, and has zero jobs started. Other fork workflows also await approval. A repository maintainer must review the fork workflow changes and use **Approve and run workflows** on the pending run(s). Earlier review/CI do not certify this head. The PR remains draft.

<details>
<summary>Inspectable before/after runtime output and exact source binding</summary>

Baseline: `226ebab23543b2677203141b7ce3321b645b7945`.
Tested/reviewed implementation diff SHA-256: `42c0e192f71d8c6a82901a06b39d9c9505c7c55a0ee0c64211d469839ea73781`.

Each variant uses a fresh HOME, configuration, state, workspace and isolated loopback Gateway. The real link installer creates the installed index. Two `models.list({refresh:true, provider:"catalog-receipt-proof"})` calls exercise the eager companion, then the lazy companion through retained plugin code. A read-only SQLite inspection after shutdown checks the actual installed-index receipts and captured-file bytes. Paths and temporary credentials are sanitized below.

### Before: unmodified pinned main

```json
{

  "runtime": "v24.20.0",
```

prs.title: fix(openai): embed system prompt in input on ChatGPT Responses when uncached (#202372)
prs.body:
Closes #202372

## What Problem This Solves

On `openai/gpt-6.2-sol` and other models using the ChatGPT Responses backend (`openai-chatgpt-responses`), top-level `instructions` are not cached by the provider, but the request builder always placed the system prompt in `instructions` and disabled input prompt conversion. This resulted in the entire system prompt being reprocessed uncached on every turn, causing excessive subscription quota usage and avoidable prefill latency.

## User Impact

User impact: Places the system prompt in leading developer input for models declaring `cachesInstructions: false`, making it eligible for provider prefix caching. Authenticated OAuth tests verified backend acceptance, changed-prompt obedience, and cache-token reuse; see live evidence below.

## Why This Change Was Made

The model catalog already configures `cachesInstructions: false` for GPT-6.2, but the ChatGPT Responses adapter hardcoded `includeSystemPrompt: false` and always populated `instructions`. Consulting `cachesInstructions` enables system-prompt input conversion and omits the uncached `instructions` field when `cachesInstructions` is `false`, while preserving existing `instructions` behavior for models that support and cache it.

## Evidence

### Wire Comparison (`openai-chatgpt-responses`)

| Field | Base (before fix) | Head (with fix, `cachesInstructions: false`) |
|---|---|---|
| `instructions` | `"You are an autonomous agent."` (uncached on 6.2) | `undefined` (omitted from payload) |
| `input[0]` | `{ type: "message", role: "user", ... }` | `{ type: "message", role: "developer", content: [{ type: "input_text", text: "You are an autonomous agent." }] }` |
| `input[1]` | Next user turn message | `{ type: "message", role: "user", ... }` |

### Fixture WebSocket Continuation Trace

Verified with the synthetic `installWebSocket()` fixture via `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts`. Responses contain synthetic IDs and empty model output; this checks serialized continuation and prompt-change replay, not backend acceptance, prompt obedience, or actual cache hits:

1. **Turn 1 (Cold request, initial developer prompt)**:
   ```json
   {
     "model": "gpt-6.2-sol",
     "stream": true,
     "input": [
       { "type": "message", "role": "developer", "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "System Prompt 1" }] },
       { "type": "message", "role": "user", "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "turn 1" }] }
     ]
   }
   ```
   *Outcome*: `instructions` omitted; system prompt placed in leading developer input for prefix caching.

2. **Turn 2 (Continuation with unchanged prompt)**:
   ```json
   {
     "model": "gpt-6.2-sol",
     "stream": true,
     "previous_response_id": "resp_1",
     "input": [
       { "type": "message", "role": "user", "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "turn 2" }] }
     ]
   }
   ```
   *Outcome*: `previous_response_id` continues the stored chain. The delta input carries only the new user turn without duplicating the developer prompt. This fixture does not measure provider cache reuse; separate authenticated evidence is below.

3. **Turn 3 (System prompt changed to `System Prompt 2 (Changed)`)**:
   ```json
   {
     "model": "gpt-6.2-sol",
     "stream": true,
     "input": [
       { "type": "message", "role": "developer", "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "System Prompt 2 (Changed)" }] },
       { "type": "message", "role": "user", "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "turn 1" }] },
       ...
     ]
   }
   ```
   *Outcome*: Continuation is safely invalidated (`previous_response_id` omitted) and a full replay is dispatched with the new developer prompt.

### Automated Test Suite Execution

- **Reproduction**: Unit test proved red failure on base (`AssertionError: expected { model: 'gpt-6.2-sol', ... } to not have property "instructions" (received "You are an autonomous agent.")`) and passes green with the fix.
- **Suite Results**:
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts`: **35 passed** (including uncached prompt placement, cached prompt retention, and multi-turn WebSocket continuation).
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.replay.test.ts`: **4 passed**
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses-streaming.test.ts`: **9 passed**
  - `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses-protocol.test.ts`: **5 passed**
  - `packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-uncached-instructions.integration.test.ts`: **4 passed**
  - `packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-payload-policy.test.ts`: **28 passed**
- **Standards & Code Quality**:
  - `oxlint`: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
  - `run-format.mts` & `git diff --check`: Clean.

## Maintainer validation update (November 23, 2026)

Two test-only repairs preserve the contributor production fix and ancestry:
- Shared one existing conversation provider-state claim across the three continuation fixture turns (incoming 34/35 red becomes 35/35).
- Aligned the compaction consumer test with native ChatGPT developer-input placement while preserving managed instructions and full normal/V2 request equality (incoming 13/14 red becomes 14/14).

Candidate: `406329b989cd105ae45252edd757f62438fc38bd`. Related compaction/provider/payload suites: **81/81**; earlier provider/replay/protocol/streaming selection: **85/85**. Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, and diff checks passed. One additional unchanged local abrupt-disconnect fixture cannot reach its loopback WebSocket because the host proxy returns HTTP 502 before handshake; that local environment gap is retained, not represented as passing replay.

### Authenticated live validation

At `8ef8f30f58fb4d65805da1359b0a52460cb18761`, real OAuth requests passed through both SSE and websocket-cached transports. A same-source old-wire-shape control (`cachesInstructions: true`) reported warm `cacheRead: 0` and input 4,877. With false capability, warm requests reported **cacheRead 4,736 / input 141**. A changed developer prompt was honored (`BRAVO-2` rather than `ALPHA-1`), with full-prompt replay and cacheRead 0. This is a controlled wire-shape comparison on the fixed source, **not an actual base-revision run**, and not a measured subscription-quota claim.

The isolated full Gateway OAuth profile suite also passed: selected 1 model, 1 runnable candidate, 0 credential skips; prompt, tool-read, tool-exec, image, and tool-only regression checks completed successfully. One selected test passed; 179 unrelated tests were filtered. The temporary suite copy only added normal auth-store credential provisioning; tracked Gateway/runtime/assertions were unchanged. The settled remote wrapper exited 0. The subsequent candidate changes only a test assertion, leaving this exercised production code byte-identical.

Author self-inspection and simplification retained the existing owner, with no new production machinery or weakened assertions. Required exact-published-head CI/security gates must complete before landing; live proof does not waive them.

prs.title: test(gateway): drop the stale mid-turn revocation step from screen routing
prs.body:
Related: #204155

## What Problem This Solves

Contributors whose pull requests touch Gateway screen routing get a red required CI gate from three test cases that already fail on `main`, so unrelated work cannot merge. The same three cases fail on scheduled full runs of `main`.

The failing cases in `src/gateway/server-methods/ui-command.test.ts` are:

- routes personal screen requests only to the admitted embedded requester (hidden question: false)
- routes personal screen requests only to the admitted cli requester (hidden question: false)
- routes personal screen requests only to the admitted embedded requester (hidden question: true)

Examples: [a scheduled run on `main`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45259316971/job/137990383661) and [#202013's run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/45264188693/job/138007616919). Pushes to `main` stay green because the changed-test shard only runs this file when related files change.

## User Impact

User impact: none. This is a test-only change; no production code changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each failing case revokes the turn owner's access in the middle of a started turn and expects the next screen request to be refused with "Alice's access changed; ask them again". #204155 removed that mid-run re-read from `createReplyTurnParticipants` on purpose: authority is checked once when work starts, so a started turn keeps routing to its owner. That PR updated the matching step in `session-controller.message-join.test.ts`, but this file was missed.

This change removes the revoke step and its refusal expectation (two lines). The cases still assert the refusal that was kept: after `turn.complete()` the same request is rejected.

#204249 contains the identical two-line deletion as part of a larger refactor, so the two changes merge without conflict in either order.

## Evidence

The three cases fail on `main` and pass with this change. Run in an isolated worktree with a loopback-only sandbox, `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/ui-command.test.ts`:

| | Commit | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Before | `main` at `b36ba3fed244` | 3 failed, 17 passed. All three fail at `ui-command.test.ts:239` |
| After | this change | 20 passed |

`pnpm check:changed` exits 0 on this change, including format, lint, core test typecheck and the Knip scans.

prs.title: fix: open the dashboard in a compatible installed browser
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Onboarding and `openclaw dashboard` can open a browser that cannot run the Control UI even when a compatible browser is already installed. Switching browsers using only the clean dashboard URL loses the one-time pairing handoff and creates avoidable recovery work; this is not a failure of normal pairing.

## User Impact

When the default browser is known to lack required features, OpenClaw can open an identified compatible alternative on macOS, native Windows, or Linux for this session only. Supported and unknown defaults keep their existing opening path. No browser is installed, no OS default is changed, and no automation browser profile is selected.

**Draft: native Windows selection and prepared-profile automatic pairing passed on `6f75e6e45291`, but fresh-profile cold pairing failed. The visible-launch and macOS/Linux HTML-handler repairs below still need native confirmation. Earlier-head macOS dashboard validation remains valid only for its recorded scope; onboarding and broader native coverage are incomplete.** Windows Hub is independently released and is not changed here. WSL keeps its existing Windows desktop opener rather than selecting a Linux browser.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing browser opener now accepts an installed-browser target, while the existing private-file handoff still carries each newly issued one-time pairing URL. Browser-version estimates and actual browser feature probes share the same requirements; browser-side verification remains authoritative.

- macOS resolves the default HTML-document handler through Launch Services and reads application registrations/metadata, including `~/Applications`.
- Native Windows queries the Shell for the effective HTML-file handler and reads installed executable versions without running browsers to identify their versions.
- Linux reads the XDG `text/html` association and normal Chrome/Chromium, Firefox, and Edge executables on `PATH`. Custom wrappers, Flatpak-only installations, and `BROWSER` overrides remain conservative unknown cases.
- Selection order is deterministic. Unknown metadata retains the existing fallback, while missing compatible alternatives retain a terminal/recovery path.
- Explicit remote sessions do not launch on the wrong desktop. Cold GUI processes acknowledge startup without waiting for their lifetime; onboarding separately waits for a newly connected Control UI client.

There is no new pairing mechanism, stored browser preference, configuration option, token handling, or installation step. Changes target main only; no backport or older-Gateway compatibility is proposed. Necessary growth is the three platform discovery adapters and their common selection contract; no registry/cache/manager is introduced.

## Evidence

### Native Windows retest and visible-launch / HTML-association follow-up

Follow-up commit: [`1e5e0cb0a861`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/1e5e0cb0a8618ceec47fd2c591bace46e41cc946). Independent source review found no concrete P0/P1/P2 issue in this follow-up; native execution remains unverified.

[@ekinnee’s retest](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200840#issuecomment-6993850519) of `6f75e6e45291` on Windows 11 26H2 confirms **correct selection**, unchanged HTML/HTTPS associations, protected handoff ACLs, credential-free browser arguments, and **60 passing Windows tests, 1 skipped, 0 failed**. Windows assigned HTML to Chrome 124 and HTTPS to Edge 157; the repaired selector correctly chose Chrome 158. With Chrome already visible in a prepared disposable profile, the dashboard opened and established one fresh authenticated Control UI connection.

**Fresh-profile cold launch/pairing still failed:** the selected process remained alive without a visible main window and admitted no Control UI connection, including a repeat launch. A separate harmless-HTML probe showed a window with `windowsHide: false`, but did not show the probe page title. That isolates a visibility problem, not a complete cold-pairing fix.

The follow-up sets `windowsHide: false` only for directly launched user GUI browsers, retaining detached startup acknowledgement and private-file delivery. It does not add first-run bypass flags, change profiles, or equate a process launch with connection/pairing success.

It also addresses ClawSweeper's HTML-handler finding on macOS/Linux: Launch Services resolves `public.html` with the default role, and XDG resolves `text/html`, matching the file actually passed to the opener instead of an unrelated HTTPS association. Unknown HTML handlers retain the existing opening path. Windows already uses the effective HTML association.

- Six visibility/split-association regressions failed before this follow-up and pass afterward. The Mac regression executes the actual JXA discovery program against fixed native-boundary responses; Linux uses real subprocess fixtures with deliberately different HTML/HTTPS defaults. Neither is native GUI proof.
- **102 focused tests across 8 files pass** (17.68 seconds wall time), plus strict affected typechecking, targeted lint/format, and diff checks.
- **Current-head native verification remains pending**, especially fresh-profile Windows visibility and actual handoff redemption. Prepared-profile success on the earlier head must not be reported as a cold-start pass.

### Windows repair after native verification

Repair commit: [`6f75e6e45291`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6f75e6e45291e2769e58df887aabf5fd9cde31c1). Independent source review found no concrete P0/P1/P2 findings in this repair; this was not native Windows execution.

[@ekinnee’s native Windows report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200840#issuecomment-6987294781) exposed a real failure on `cee9b3506c21`: Windows 11 26H2 resolved Chrome 124 as the effective HTTPS/HTML handler, but the legacy `UserChoice` key still named Edge. The PR therefore skipped fallback and opened the unsupported browser, with no admitted Control UI connection. The same run found that the selector suite called POSIX-only `process.getuid()` during shared setup on Windows.

The repair removes legacy default-registration/ProgID command parsing and asks the Windows Shell's `AssocQueryStringW` API for the effective `.html` executable. This is the association used for the private `handoff.html` file; it can differ from HTTPS. Unknown Shell results remain unknown, never fall back to stale default-registration data. Existing application metadata still supplies versions and deterministically ordered alternatives; no browser settings, registrations, installations, or profiles are modified.

Selector fixtures now supply and restore a synthetic macOS UID independently of the native host. Private-file tests run on their real host platform, retaining POSIX permissions versus Windows ACL behavior instead of performing real file operations under a mocked macOS platform.

- Three effective-handler regressions failed before the repair and pass afterward, including unsupported effective Chrome with stale Edge data, a supported effective handler, and an unknown association.
- **100 focused tests across 8 files pass** (16.59 seconds wall time), plus strict affected typechecking, targeted lint/format, and diff checks.
- All **27 selector cases also pass with `process.getuid` removed before the test runner starts** (39.97 seconds wall time, including compilation). This is Linux-hosted portability proof, not native Windows execution.
- **Superseded by the native retest above:** selection, the Windows selector suite, and prepared-profile pairing passed on this repair head; fresh-profile cold launch/pairing did not.

### ClawSweeper repair: inherited SSH variables on macOS

Commit [`cee9b3506c21`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/cee9b3506c218358154da01c7de7bb7ac8afaf75) restores the local-shell behavior protected by [#67088](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/67088) and [#85340](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/85340). SSH environment variables alone no longer reject a local Mac GUI terminal. After verifying the console owner, SSH-marked Mac sessions must identify as the current launchd `Aqua` GUI bootstrap; background, unknown, or failed context checks remain blocked, as do Remote Containers/Codespaces. Linux/Windows SSH and WSL handling are unchanged.

Four inherited-SSH regressions failed on the previous PR head and pass with this repair. **70 focused tests across four affected/consumer files pass** (15.44 seconds wall time), along with strict affected typechecking, targeted lint/format, and diff checks. Independent source review found no concrete P0/P1/P2 issue in this narrow repair. This is fixture/source proof, not a new native macOS run: the earlier report's simulated-SSH result applies to `29dae7868b21`, not the new GUI-context distinction.

### Native macOS dashboard validation — passed

[@jjjhenriksen’s native test report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200840#issuecomment-6966181964) validates head `29dae7868b2139b5829806475c52b1f9076d2138` against comparison build `e9561fb93e23aca2a797ed0cf28593cac45edc17` in a disposable Apple Silicon Tart VM running macOS Sequoia 15.7.7, using a foreground loopback Gateway and disposable state.

- **Before:** the dashboard opened the HTTPS default, Safari 18.6, which displayed the unsupported-browser screen; the Gateway recorded no admitted Control UI connection.
- **After:** with Safari still the HTTPS default, the dashboard selected Chrome 158.0.8127.37 installed only in `~/Applications`. Both a cold launch and a repeat launch into the running Chrome process produced fresh, authenticated Control UI connections at the Gateway. The HTTPS default remained Safari.
- **Additional checks:** removing the compatible alternative produced the recovery notice; `--no-open` suppressed launch; `--json` returned the handoff and expiry fields; a simulated SSH session suppressed GUI launch.
- **Onboarding is partial, not passed:** the browser-handoff helper selected Chrome and the Gateway recorded a separate fresh Control UI connection, but the helper did not return before the test cutoff. This was not a full interactive onboarding run or confirmed handoff completion.

The report includes sanitized terminal/Gateway excerpts, not before/after screenshots. It does **not** establish supported-default behavior, unknown/custom metadata, failed browser startup, a forced expired handoff, or a successful chat reply.

### Automated and source validation

- **Prior-head validation:** 89 targeted tests across 8 files passed on `29dae7868b21` (16.96 seconds wall time). The repair reruns the four affected/consumer suites above; unchanged feature-floor, private-handoff, Linux subprocess, and browser feature-admission proof is retained from that run. Focused tests cover browser feature floors, supported/unknown defaults, user-installed macOS alternatives, deterministic selection, native Windows metadata fixtures, Linux XDG subprocess fixtures, headless/SSH/WSL behavior, selected-launch failure, cold long-lived GUI process startup, private-file delivery, and fresh handoffs on repeated dashboard runs. Existing dashboard/onboarding handoff suites and browser feature admission remain green.
- Selected-launch regressions were red on base `e9561fb93e23aca2a797ed0cf28593cac45edc17` (three intended failures) and green with the target-aware opener.
- Strict typechecking of affected production/tests with repository ambient declarations, targeted lint/format, and `git diff --check` pass.
- `pnpm ui:build` succeeds. Existing advisory size budgets also fail on the pinned base: CSS 57.8 KiB vs 56.9 KiB; chat boot requests 21 vs 20; chat JS 1297.2 KiB vs 1296.8 KiB. The candidate reports 1297.3 KiB chat JS; no CSS/request-budget exception is added.
- Independent read-only source review identified cold-GUI lifetime and kernel-only WSL classification defects; both were repaired with regressions. The follow-up review confirms both repairs with no remaining concrete P0/P1/P2 findings in those repairs. Native platform execution is not established by that review. The structured Auto Review attempts were interrupted by Gateway restarts and did not produce a completed receipt.

Linux-specific proof uses real Linux subprocesses for XDG discovery fixtures and a real long-lived process for cold-launch lifetime; those pass locally. This runner has no installed desktop browser or display, so real Linux desktop opening/pairing and screenshots remain unverified, not claimed as passing.

### Remaining native verification

Use disposable state/profile and a foreground Gateway on an unused port, never normal Gateway credentials.

- Finish a full interactive onboarding run and establish why the helper did not confirm completion in the reported test.
- Verify the new macOS distinction between a local GUI shell carrying inherited SSH variables and an actual SSH/background session belonging to the same console user. Also cover the supported-default and unknown/custom browser paths, failed browser startup, forced expired-handoff recovery, and a separately observed chat reply.
- Rerun fresh-profile Windows cold launch with the visible GUI setting, observe any browser first-run UI, and verify the private handoff actually redeems and admits a new Control UI connection. Repeat with a prepared visible profile and preserve the HTML/HTTPS defaults.
- Verify the new macOS/Linux HTML-handler discovery with differing HTML and HTTPS defaults, including an unknown/custom HTML application. Linux subprocess fixtures and the Mac native-boundary fixture do not establish desktop browser behavior.
- Capture sanitized unsupported-default before/after media with actual OS/browser versions. Do not publish pairing URLs, credentials, or private desktop content.

Reported and scoped with @jjjhenriksen. Native test-box verification is still pending.

## Work sessions

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/bfef40a9-b1b9-4014-a803-f5a73399e554)

## Worked on by

- @jjjhenriksen

prs.title: fix: preserve managed GitHub exec on packaged Windows
prs.body:
Related: #197437

## What Problem This Solves

On packaged Windows installs, managed GitHub exec can refuse to run even after GitHub Identity is connected. The credential reader starts without the native dependency redirect already used by the Gateway.

## User Impact

The private credential reader reuses the package's known startup redirect without changing the requested command's environment. Missing or malformed profiles still refuse execution. No new user configuration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The resolver forwards only the package preload identified by the Gateway's startup arguments and verified against the package layout. It pins the two native redirect roots only for the credential child. Request environment overrides cannot supply those roots or arbitrary startup hooks. Failure diagnostics use fixed stage codes without credential data.

The environment-variable budget increases from current main's **464 to 466** for `OPENCLAW_NATIVE_APP_ROOT` and `OPENCLAW_NATIVE_STAGED_ROOT`. This preserves the two-name increase already reported as owner-approved by the contributor; no formal GitHub review approval is claimed.

## Evidence

### Real installed-package credential-reader comparison — Parallels ARM64

On Windows 11 Pro Dev build 26300, installed the signed ARM64 release `v2026.11.10-beta.1-msix.0` and successfully ran `clawctl setup`. Ran baseline/candidate launch builders through `clawctl pwsh` under the package's isolated agent identity, using its provisioned Node 24.22.1, real immutable installed credential reader, vendor preload, and staged dependency roots. The reader was not mocked; only the token contents were synthetic.

- Baseline `ff4a6c70d6b42`: both `-Command` and `-EncodedCommand` refused with the credential-unavailable diagnostic and empty stdout.
- Candidate launch code from `25dc64eac1978`: both forms ran the requested command, read the selected profile, preserved conflicting request root values, and cleared competing inherited GitHub token variables. Valid-case wall times: 2.830s and 2.342s.
- Missing `hosts.yml` and a regular file instead of a profile directory both refused, through both PowerShell forms. **All six candidate assertions passed.** Synthetic fixture profiles were removed afterward.
- Installed package: `OpenClaw.Gateway_2026.11.999.10_arm64__kaa03rpbbqef6`, not a development registration. Packaging commit `4f6903c877b96dd707f0a996867f4fabc0a56c1d`; installed payload commit `995f9059b6e6fe3ba0865a3354924fd2bcbfceea`.
- **Limits:** this is launch-builder/installed-reader A/B, not an installed candidate-MSIX A/B or a model-driven Gateway E2E run. No real GitHub credential or authenticated API command was used. fs-safe reports `ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED` for its ARM64 native addon and succeeds through its supported .NET-helper fallback; native-addon loading is not claimed fixed. The installed reader remains the signed release, so candidate reader-stage diagnostics are not covered by this native run.

### Conflict repair and review

Merged main `36bc0460f4200` in `fcfdcd4a2c887`. Resolved the budget conflict by retaining both main's launcher names and this PR's native-root names; regenerated both conflicting script bundles with their owner generator. The CLI bootstrap, launch builder, and credential-reader source are unchanged from the Parallels proof inputs.

Local ClawSweeper completed review of `36bc0460f4200..fcfdcd4a2c887`: no blocking production-code or security finding. It identified a P3 Windows-test routing gap, addressed in `daadf5a94c37a` by adding the launcher regression suite to the explicit Windows CI inventory. Its missing-package-proof note did not include the separate installed-reader run documented above. No second hosted review is claimed.

### Focused checks

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/github-exec-launch.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-github-credential.test.ts src/infra/openclaw-cli-invocation.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **36 passed, 11 intentional Windows-only skips**, 48.72s outer runner time.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed.
- Focused oxlint of the four changed agent implementation/test files — passed.
- Explicit format check of the seven changed code/docs files — passed.
- `pnpm runtime:scripts:gen` and `pnpm runtime:scripts:check` — passed.
- `git diff origin/main --check` — passed.
- Environment-name budget check in CI advisory mode — passed with its growth warning; normal mode retains the budget-growth approval gate.
- `pnpm build:runtime` — passed before main integration, 1m45s. This is prior-input build evidence, not a new-head build claim; current-head CI remains authoritative.

The previous head's CI gate passed. Current-head CI is pending after the conflict-repair push; no merge-readiness claim is based on the old green run.

prs.title: fix: remove repeated details after an update rolls back
prs.body:
Closes #204091

## What Problem This Solves

After an update rolls back, Settings → Updates and `openclaw update status` repeat the failure as `Failed: restarting` and `Failing check update (update-failed)`. The CLI also adds an unavailable-health notice above saved facts that say the Gateway started, which makes the outcome hard to read.

## User Impact

The rollback summary keeps the cause and the version still running, then gives one next step: Retry, followed by Report update failure if it fails again. Recorded verification and useful supplemental failures remain visible. Startup output stays in collapsed diagnostics.

Stored rows, JSON diagnostics, support-report content, update execution, and nonrollback reports stay unchanged. No schema, protocol, or configuration change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared report owner now omits the failed phase only when a recorded rollback reason already gives the cause. It keeps failed-phase details for other failures and rollbacks with no recorded reason. An unavailable health probe adds no normal rollback notice; positive current-health observations and all nonrollback health wording remain intact.

On current main, upgrades defer plugin maintenance until the candidate is ready. A downgrade can still record a plugin failure before a later rollback. That supplemental failure remains below the cause and recovery action.

<details>
<summary>Producer and reader trace</summary>

Original producers on main `3b64ff6c6289`:

- `src/infra/update-run-report.ts:487`: failed-phase label.
- `src/infra/update-run-report.ts:498–507`, through `src/infra/update-failure-facts-format.ts:46`: the phase's internal check line.
- `src/infra/update-run-report.ts:392–402` and `:562–569`: normal-report current-health wording.
- `src/infra/update-run-report.ts:640–644`: recovery advice followed the details.

The normal report is consumed by `src/cli/update-cli/status.ts:667–684` and `ui/src/app/update-run-projection.ts:77–83`. `src/infra/update-failure-report-prepare.ts:502–514` separately includes current-health context in Report update failure; that reader and its formatter are unchanged.

The existing repaired-update formatter moved to the existing failure-fact formatting owner, with identical output and its caller migrated. This keeps the report owner below its existing line cap without dropping the CLI's Phases/Total timeline or adding a new module.

</details>

## Evidence

- All three removed-line regressions fail on main for the intended unwanted text. The frozen base run reports 5 failed / 61 passed, including two recovery-order failures: [AWS red-on-main run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_a06e6c79ce907706a21a1275ad886e59).
- Local ClawSweeper reviewed final range `3b64ff6c6289..f1629feee395`: patch is correct, zero findings, security cleared. That review used source-only context; real-path evidence is listed below. The three independent table cases are retained because this issue explicitly requests one test per removed line.
- A real Settings → Updates request on a Linux systemd user service reproduced the duplicate phase/check lines on built main `3b64ff6c6289`; CLI status also showed the unavailable-health sentence above recorded running facts. The unchanged hang fixture rolled back at the normal 20-minute trial ceiling and restored v2026.11.7.
- The restored reporter package was fully built and packed on AWS from head `bd9a5d981431`, shared-state schema 41. Its immutable tarball SHA-256 is `87b3ef2ff8f5a1ac1fe412945fc6223da8cfcf498af4c6299796c6eea0d9d41b`.
- On the built `bd9a5d981431` reporter, a real Settings → Updates request to an unchanged, qualified crash candidate completed two genuine starts after migration and rolled back. The normal report showed headline → Retry/Report → facts, with startup diagnostics collapsed: [AWS runtime evidence](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_4f9519dcefd70a05d8a95f979fb1df60). The candidate was `2026.11.8-beta.3`, schema 42, SHA-256 `a9875749592188cf9adbbba0140a9d1af0d2caf556269fd0e52256064a7eafa5`; the reporter's starting schema was 41. The candidate was not rebuilt from this PR.
- Replaying the original rollback row on an isolated state copy also produced the fixed CLI report; the persisted row remained byte-identical. The copied row's UI selected its intended historical view, so it is not used as the normal-report UI proof.
- All 68 owner tests passed. Completed consumer shards passed 23 files / 479 tests. The combined 37-file run hit its 1,800-second command deadline during the CLI-process shard, with no observed assertion failures; remaining consumer coverage is deferred to PR CI, not claimed green: [AWS consumer run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_61a5ac6e484c21fb463a0a9a5e206388).
- Final targeted lint, format, and both service/update test typechecks passed: [AWS checks](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_f2f54b0d5391a8b4eb239beb86f05833).
- Report update failure title/body bytes were identical between base and head, including its unavailable-health qualification: [AWS comparison](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_ba38435be12c0f8468da93c2a8001143).
- Final commit `f1629feee395` differs from the runtime-tested `bd9a5d981431` only by two callback-variable renames in the relocated repair-summary helper. The rollback renderer is byte-for-byte unchanged. Build/runtime evidence is reused for that unchanged path; targeted static checks cover the final rename.
- All three task-owned AWS leases were released with `--wait`.

### Settings → Updates

Before — built main:

![Settings before: repeated failed phase and internal check](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cee82519-10c2-443b-b326-ca52f6ccea77)

After — real crash rollback, built reporter:

![Settings after: cause, one recovery step, and recorded facts](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d0d329f-ae35-45b2-ada1-c5ec8f27a4eb)

### Captured `openclaw update status` output

These images show the command's unchanged captured stdout, not live Terminal windows.

![CLI before: three redundant lines](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d5f5d8e-8047-44a3-9591-4ffd023bfff3)

![CLI after: one next step and recorded verification](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d9b11625-6ba7-49e2-bb25-2b036b9050e5)

prs.title: fix: release SQLite snapshot disk space after cleanup (backport #201661 to 2026.11.8)
prs.body:
Related: #201588, #201661

Target branch: `release/2026.11.8`. Backport of #201661 (`eb381dceef2`, by @Alix-007, landed on `main` 2026-11-19).

- **Has the fix:** `main` and `release/2026.11.10`.
- **Lacks it:** every published release (2026.11.6, 2026.11.7, 2026.11.10-beta.2) and `release/2026.11.8`, which branches from 2026.11.7. None of them has `captureSqliteDatabaseDescriptorCustodyLocations`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a long-running Gateway keeps every retired read-only SQLite snapshot copy open after its directory is deleted, so the disk fills up until the Gateway restarts.

## User Impact

User impact: Gateways on 2026.11.8 release disk space when snapshot cleanup runs, instead of filling the disk.

Today `du` cannot see the lost space; only `df` or `/proc/<pid>/fd` shows it. On one production host (official 2026.11.6, state database of about 125 MB), the Gateway held **902 deleted-but-open copies, 54 GB, after 2.7 days**. The disk filled and other services on the host failed with ENOSPC.

This is separate from #204066. That issue is about Doctor copying the database during update, which #194042 and #194267 fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the last reader closes, its admission is forgotten but its descriptor custody stays registered. Snapshot cleanup only retired live admissions, so the orphaned descriptor was never closed.

As in #201661, custody now records its location, and cleanup retires admission and custody locations together.

The only difference from `main` is one context line: the 2026.11.8 custody type still has `additionalDescriptors`. The 2026.11.8 `retireDescriptor` also closes those extra descriptors, so retiring a custody releases every descriptor it holds.

## Evidence

**Focused tests** on `release/2026.11.8` (`7df7997a6e4`), Linux, Node 26.12.1:

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| With the fix: `sqlite-readonly-location.cleanup.test.ts` + `sqlite-database-admission.retention.test.ts` | 2 files, **49/49 passed** |
| New regression test only, source change reverted | **fails**: `releases closed readers' descriptors before removing an awaited snapshot` (1 failed, 17 passed) |

**Live observation, same production host** (count of `openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-*` entries in `/proc/<gateway pid>/fd` marked `(deleted)`):

| Build | Held copies |
|---|---|
| Official 2026.11.6 | 902 (54 GB) after 2.7 days |
| Official 2026.11.7 | 8 (485 MB) within 24 minutes |
| 2026.11.7 + this change, running since 2026-11-23 17:20 UTC | **0** at every sample through 21:56 UTC; copies deleted in that window were released |

The 24-hour run is still going, and I will post the final count here.
