prs.title: feat(whatsapp): edit the bot's own messages
prs.body:
Related: #189815

## What Problem This Solves

WhatsApp is missing the `edit` message action that Telegram and Discord have, so an agent cannot correct a message it already sent.

## User Impact

User impact: agents can edit their own WhatsApp messages. Turn it off with `channels.whatsapp.actions.editMessage: false`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `edit` the same way `react` works, behind the host's exact-current chat gate. Editing another user's message is refused when the cache knows the sender. On a cache miss the edit goes out under the bot's own key (`fromMe: true`); WhatsApp applies an edit only when it comes from the original sender, so such an edit has no effect on the other phone. That is provider behaviour, not something this PR enforces. Baileys resolves on the socket write, so the result says `submitted: true, confirmed: false`.

The edit key's chat is pinned to the chat the caller named. The message-cache lookup that quoting uses also matches a message through its sender. Only an entry whose stored peer number is the target's own number counts as this one-to-one chat under its other JID (phone number or LID) and may supply the key's `remoteJid`; anything else (a status update keyed by its poster, a broadcast list, a match through a bare participant JID) is another chat, and the edit is rejected with `message belongs to another chat`.

Caller authority: `edit` is declared in `writeAuthorityActions`, and the host's `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` is passed down the edit chain as a plain parameter. It is checked at the action handler and again inside the queued socket task, right after the socket-identity check and right before the native `sendMessage`. An edit whose originating run lost authority while it waited in the per-socket queue is dropped before any I/O. A revocation is never retried: the caller guard runs at the start of every send attempt, also while the socket is away, so a revoked caller never waits for a reconnect backoff, and the retry path re-checks the caller before classifying an error as a disconnect, so the caller gets the original guard error. Edits now use the ordinary send path, so the separate single-attempt path is gone.

Provider ownership (`fromMe`, the message cache) only scopes which messages are eligible; it does not stand in for caller authority. Both are required.

Scheduled edits stay out on purpose: `edit` is not in `providerOwnedReadGates`, so the host keeps its exact-current chat check and rejects a scheduled edit. A contract test locks that.

Known limitation: for an external install the host compares targets literally (it applies `normalizeTarget` only to bundled plugins), so a delegated edit must name a DM as `+E164`, the spelling the agent's prompt shows, or omit the target; a `...@s.whatsapp.net` spelling is rejected, fail-closed. Changing that is host policy and out of scope here.

## Evidence

### Live proof on 2026.11.1 (latest stable)

**Upgrade.** A real linked WhatsApp install was upgraded from 2026.10.10 to 2026.11.1 with the normal npm install, `plugins update` and `doctor --fix`. Before and after the upgrade, the full config (sorted JSON), the WhatsApp auth creds and the number of files in the WhatsApp auth dir hashed identically, and the cron list count was unchanged. The channel came back `linked, connected, health:healthy` and the agent answered on its primary model. The config has no `actions.editMessage` key.

**Edit.** Then this PR's commit was cherry-picked onto `v2026.11.1`, `extensions/whatsapp` was packed with `scripts/plugin-npm-publish.sh --pack`, and only the plugin's `dist` + manifest were swapped in (same dependency versions; all 94 `plugin-sdk/*` imports exist in the installed 11.1 core). Afterwards the stock 2026.11.1 plugin was put back. The cherry-pick differs from this branch only where 11.1's file layout differs from main (the action list lives in `channel-actions.ts` there, plus import lines); the edit, authority and socket code is the same as the pushed head, including the final same-chat guard and the no-socket caller check.

Phone number redacted; the message id is a random WhatsApp id.

```text
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20)

$ openclaw message send --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --json \
    --message "Proof test for the WhatsApp edit action: meet at 3"
"action": "send", "handledBy": "core", "messageId": "3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8"
[exit 0]

$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --message-id 3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8 --json \
    --message "Proof test for the WhatsApp edit action: meet at 4"
"action": "edit", "handledBy": "plugin",
"payload": { "ok": true, "submitted": true, "confirmed": false, "messageId": "3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8" }
[exit 0]

$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +15555550100 --message-id 3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8 --json \
    --message "must not arrive"
ToolAuthorizationError: WhatsApp edit blocked: chatJid "+15555550100" is not in the
configured allowFrom list for account "default".
[exit 1]

$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --message-id 3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8 --json \
    --message ""
Error: WhatsApp edit rejected: text is empty.
[exit 1]

# a message the other phone sent earlier; after the restart the cache does not know it
$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --message-id 3A7E5B8528B197B3CF6A --json \
    --message "must not arrive (not this account's message)"
"payload": { "ok": true, "submitted": true, "confirmed": false, "messageId": "3A7E5B8528B197B3CF6A" }
[exit 0]
```

**Receiving side.** On the receiving account's WhatsApp Web (read-only IndexedDB lookup by message id), the received message `3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8` carries `latestEditMsgKey`, with the edit's sender timestamp 4.4 s after the original. So the edit reached the other phone; it is not only a socket write. The last command above targets a message the other phone itself sent: the socket accepted the write (`submitted: true`), but on the receiving side that message has no `latestEditMsgKey`. WhatsApp dropped the edit because it did not come from the message's sender, which is the provider behaviour the Why section relies on for a cache miss.


### Delegated edit from a real inbound turn (2026.11.1)

Same install and plugin port, plugin installed under `~/.openclaw/extensions` (origin `global`, so the host treats it as an external plugin, the same trust class as the integration test below). The owner's phone sent the bot a WhatsApp DM asking it to call the `message` tool twice. The group is configured and allowed (`groups` + `groupAllowFrom`, the bot is a member), so the plugin itself would accept it. Gateway log plus the session trajectory from `openclaw sessions export-trajectory`; numbers redacted, times UTC:

```text
14:19:11  CLI (direct operator)  message send -> +<owner>  messageId 3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19  "...: meet at 3"
14:19:43  web-inbound            Inbound message +<owner> -> <bot> (direct, 494 chars)
14:19:49.724  tool.call  message  {"action":"edit","channel":"whatsapp","target":"+<owner>",
                                   "messageId":"3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19","message":"...: meet at 4"}
14:19:49.724  tool.call  message  {"action":"edit","channel":"whatsapp","target":"<allowed-group>@g.us",
                                   "messageId":"3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19","message":"must not arrive"}
14:19:49.762  tool.result (group)  error: Delegated whatsapp:edit requires the exact current conversation and account for this plugin.
14:19:49.789  tool.result (DM)     {"ok":true,"submitted":true,"confirmed":false,"messageId":"3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19"}
14:19:52      web-outbound         the bot's text reply with both raw tool results
```

Receiving side (read-only WhatsApp Web IndexedDB lookup by message id): before the turn the received message had no `latestEditMsgKey`; after it, `latestEditMsgKey` is set with edit sender timestamp 14:19:49.783, the moment of the DM tool result. The group call was stopped in `message-action-dispatch` before the plugin ran (gateway log: `[tools] message failed: Error: Delegated whatsapp:edit requires the exact current conversation and account for this plugin.`); the only outbound socket traffic in that window is the edit and the bot's text reply.

The earlier `openclaw agent --to ...` attempts were rejected for a different reason: a CLI-started run has no host-minted turn capability, so the gateway receives no tool context or requester account and fails closed before comparing targets. That is the host's design, not this PR.

Not covered live: a second linked account and revocation while queued (one linked account; revocation cannot be timed from outside). Both are covered by the host-issued-guard integration test below.

### Tests on this branch, rebased on current main

- Host-issued caller guard, end to end (`test/whatsapp-message-edit.integration.test.ts`, on the shared `createMessageReadAuthority` harness, reaching the plugin only through `api.js` and a new `extensions/whatsapp/test-api.ts`, the same public test surface the Discord and Slack suites use): a really minted turn capability and run claim, the message tool under the gateway caller identity, the in-process `message.action` handler (which builds `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` itself), the plugin registered as an external install, the real WhatsApp handler and the real socket session; only Baileys' `sendMessage` is a mock. The test never supplies a guard. The config allows both the other chat and the other account, so only the host can refuse them. Cases:
  1. the current chat's edit reaches the socket with the edit key and returns `submitted: true, confirmed: false`;
  2. the same run naming another allowed chat is rejected before the socket;
  3. the same run's identity sent straight to the gateway's `message.action` with another allowed account is rejected by the host before the socket;
  4. `revokeMessageActionTurnCapability` (what the reply run calls when it ends), called after the edit's preflight while it waits behind a busy send, drops it with the host's `The message turn has ended. Start a new turn to retry.`; the socket only ever sees the busy send.

  Red checks: with the in-queue re-check removed, case 4 fails (the edit reaches the socket); with the host's account comparison disabled, case 3 fails. The old vertical test with a hand-written guard in `channel-actions.test.ts` is removed; this test replaces it.
- Socket session (unit level, with a test guard): the queued caller check runs after the socket-identity check and before native I/O; a revoked caller is not retried and gets the guard's own error, also when the error text looks like a disconnect; a revoked caller with no current socket is rejected at once, without a backoff wait; a guard rejection leaves no send-ready proof behind for the next send.
- Message cache: ids containing `:` are never cached or found, so the colon-joined cache key cannot collide.
- Contract: a scheduled `whatsapp:edit` is rejected with "requires provider-owned target authorization".
- Through the plugin handler: a target outside `allowFrom`, another account's `allowFrom`, a message cached as foreign, a message cached in another chat (a status update, or another person's chat matched only through a participant JID), and `actions.editMessage: false` all stop before the socket; a message cached under the other spelling of the same chat, with the target's number as its stored peer, keeps its cached `remoteJid` in the edit key.
- Through the host dispatcher: a direct operator's edit reaches the listener, a delegated caller naming another chat stops at the gate, and a chat removed from `allowFrom` stops the next edit.
- Upgrade compatibility: a config without `actions.editMessage` parses and enables edit; the message cache is in memory and its shape is unchanged.

Rebased on `main` at 3cc31b25860 (23 Nov). Conflicts: the generated config baseline (`config-baseline.counts.json`, `config-baseline.sha256`) and `bundled-channel-config-metadata.generated.ts`, regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen` and `pnpm config:channels:gen` (one new channel field, `actions.editMessage`), and `test/message-read-authority.test-support.ts`, where main's new turn assertion and throwing `receiptAuthority` are kept and this PR still only adds the optional gateway-context resolver. One test expectation follows main: since #201697 the host's turn assertion throws `The message turn has ended. Start a new turn to retry.` instead of `agent runtime authority is no longer active`, so case 4 now expects that text; the behavior it proves is unchanged (the queued edit never reaches the socket). No production code changes.

On that head, `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main` passes every lane: typecheck (all lanes), lint, format, config/metadata checks, the dead-export scan and the test-lines ratchet (+1176 net, within the 400 allowance plus the 1152 allocation). The WhatsApp extension, the edit-gate contract, the WhatsApp schema tests and the three integration suites on the shared read-authority harness (WhatsApp edit 4/4, Matrix, Slack) pass: 106 files, 1169 tests.

Earlier rebase on 694224f4432 (18 Nov): `check:changed` passed every lane, including the dead-export scan.

Before that rebase: WhatsApp extension: 101 files, 1107 tests passing; the new integration file 4/4; the extension test-boundary suite 13/13. Contract, dispatcher (`message-action-dispatch.registry`) and schema tests pass; `tsgo` (core, extensions, extension tests, root tests), oxlint, format, `config:docs:check` and `check:baseline-ratchets --base origin/main` are clean.

### Test-line allocation

Duplicated cases were removed (the vertical queued-revocation test with a hand-written guard in `channel-actions.test.ts` and its helpers, now replaced by the host-issued-guard test; the duplicate queued-revocation case in `monitor-inbox.socket-lifecycle.test.ts`; the per-dispatch allowFrom case in `channel-actions.test.ts`; the successful-edit case in `channel-actions.test.ts`, which the host-issued-guard test proves end to end; the cached-foreign case in `send.test.ts`); each contract is still proven at an equal or stronger boundary. The attached-listener setup that `channel-actions.test.ts` and the new test both need lives once in `extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/attached-listener.test-support.ts`, and the shared harness only gained an optional gateway-context resolver. The remaining net growth of 1152 lines is recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/whatsapp-edit-own-messages.txt`, shared scalar unchanged. It is needed because this adds a new write action whose authority has to hold across the host gate, the plugin's account/`allowFrom` checks and the queued socket write, and each of those boundaries has its own test.

prs.title: fix: say how big an oversized reply attachment was and what the limit is
prs.body:
Closes #204236

## What Problem This Solves

When an agent replies with a file that is over the outbound media limit, the person gets `⚠️ report.pdf: Too large to attach. Look for this file in Files.` and nothing else. They can't tell whether the file needs to shrink a little or a lot, or what the limit even is (default 5 MB or a configured `mediaMaxMb`). On text channels there is no Files view to fall back to, so "make it smaller or send a link" is the only way forward, and that needs the numbers. Rich clients have the same gap: the `attachment_error` card has no size or limit to show.

## User Impact

User impact: an oversized reply attachment now says how big it was and what the limit is, e.g. `⚠️ report.pdf: Too large to attach (5.6 MB, limit 5 MB). Look for this file in Files.`, and the `attachment_error` block carries `sizeBytes` / `maxBytes` so clients can show the same. The agent sees the numbers in the transcript and can resize or switch to a link on its next turn. When the size isn't known (a stream cut off at the cap) the receipt shows just the limit; with no facts at all the text is unchanged. Purely additive: no new failure codes, and clients that ignore the new fields behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The size and the limit are already known at the point of rejection (`stat.size`, buffer length, the cap passed to the reader); they just weren't kept on the error. This change records them on the size rejections (`SaveMediaSourceError`, `ImageOptimizationLimitError`, and `FsSafeError.details` from the local media reader), reads them back along the same bounded cause chain the `file-too-large` classifier already walks, and passes them through `ReplyMediaFailure` → `attachment_error` → receipt. Re-reading the file after a failure was rejected as an alternative: it would be a second, racy filesystem access outside the access decision that produced the failure.

To keep `web-media.ts` and `managed-image-attachments.ts` within the line-cap ratchet, the cap-message formatters moved next to `formatMediaSize` in `store.shared.ts` and `buildManagedMediaFailureBlock` moved to its own module; behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- End-to-end webchat reply (`chat-reply-media.test.ts`): with `mediaMaxMb` set to 512 bytes, the oversized ZIP's `attachment_error` block now carries `sizeBytes: 1158, maxBytes: 512` from the real local read path.
- Receipt wording (`reply-payload.test.ts`): size + limit, limit only, a file a few bytes over the limit (`over 5 MB, limit 5 MB` instead of `5 MB, limit 5 MB`), no facts (unchanged text), and other failure codes ignoring the fields. The strip helper still removes the receipt it produced.
- Text fallback projection (`chat-display-projection.test.ts`): a card with byte facts projects to the receipt with numbers and still never leaks the private file name.
- Error plumbing (`store.shared.test.ts`): facts from media errors, from `FsSafeError.details` through a wrapping `Error`, outermost-wins across layers, invalid numbers ignored, cause cycles bounded.
- Focused suites green locally: `store.shared`, `reply-payload`, `chat-display-projection`, `chat-reply-media`, `reply-media-paths`, `store`, `web-media` (7 files, 223 tests). `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck (core, UI, tests, extensions, scripts), format and all ratchets green; oxlint on the changed files is clean (0 warnings), while the whole-tree `oxlint:core` shard is red locally on existing UI warnings unrelated to this change.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```
pnpm test src/media/store.shared.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply-payload.test.ts src/gateway/chat-display-projection.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/chat-reply-media.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-media-paths.test.ts src/media/store.test.ts src/media/web-media.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm check:changed
```

</details>

prs.title: Control UI: lead the sidebar with the selected agent and move Home to the rail top
prs.body:
## Problem

The Control UI sidebar had two agent controls that competed for the top of the rail. The rail opened with an agent card and menu ("Switch agent"). Home, which opens the selected agent's main conversation, sat at the bottom of the rail, far from the agent it belongs to. The main conversation also had no place in the session list itself.

## Solution

- **Home leads the rail.** The agent card and switcher menu are removed. Home moves to the top of the rail as a house with an arched doorway, drawn in the rail's stroke. While the Home dock is open, the house fills and keeps the selected surface. Clicking Home still toggles the dock beside the current page, and `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+H` still works.
- **The selected agent's row leads the session list.** It shows the avatar, the name and the latest reply, and clicking it opens that agent's main conversation. While the session list is closed, the rail Home carries that conversation's activity and attention.
- **One row menu for agent actions.** The **⋯** button, a right-click or Shift+F10 opens the menu. **Show all agents** (or **Show only this agent** when all agents are shown) and **New agent** come first, followed by the agent's own actions: Pin, Sessions, Share or Create template, Settings and Delete. While other agents have unread conversations, the **⋯** stays visible with a dot.
- **Environment identity moves to the agent row.** The `gateway.controlUi.environment` pill and avatar ring now sit on the row of the agent in use. The ring yields to the run ring while the agent works.
- **Removed:** the agent card and menu, the workspace header, the `sidebarRecentlyCreatedAgentId` preference, the unused sidebar snapshot brand fields (`icon`, `iconUrl` and `environment`, which no reader uses anymore) and their CSS.
- **Docs** are updated: Settings, Sessions and sidebar, Panels, the main Control UI page, Main session, and Agents and templates.

Product decision kept from the old menus: the selected agent's menu keeps the agent switcher's **Share {agent}**, and roster rows keep **Create template**. Unifying the two template flows is a separate decision.

## Evidence

Mocked Control UI with a busy sidebar: custom groups, Other, Groups, Coding, sessions owned by several people, running and queued sessions, unread, questions waiting for an answer, a cloud worker and several agents. The standard appearance is used, without an environment label. Left is `main` (`e2973f9`), right is this branch.

prs.title: fix: schedule Template automations in the adding device’s time zone
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A Template that says “Monday at 9 AM” now creates a cron job for **9 AM on the device that adds it**. Before, the job used the Template’s declared zone, which could run it hours earlier or later than expected. New jobs use the adding client’s validated IANA time zone, falling back to the Template’s declared zone if the client supplies no valid one. The source `CLAW.md`, cron expression and interval schedules are unchanged.

Catalog and chat previews show the schedule in the viewing device’s time zone. Viewing or retrying from a second device does not change existing jobs. Retry uses stored job identity and declaration keys to add only missing declarations; it does not move, duplicate, overwrite or re-pause an existing job.

This diff is limited to the time-zone behavior and its tests and docs. The earlier Skills/Plugins route changes were removed in favor of main’s [Skills pages](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202581) and [Plugins route checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202687). Template automations use main’s inline rows unchanged; this PR does not add a dialog.

## Evidence

All five requested local checks passed without waivers. Published `f7af676696ed` and locally tested `6ada1b98a996` have the same tree: `24211f349bb8594f860573bbd3372ac7becaf802`.

| Local check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Bundled Chromium route assets | **4/4 passed:** Skills, Skill Settings, Plugins and Plugin Settings. The previous PR head needed 57 Plugins asset requests before the page was ready. After integrating [the upstream Plugins fix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202795), the same cold visit measured **55 requests**, below the unchanged limit of **56**. |
| Template, cron, subagent and scenario regressions | **244/244 passed**, including deterministic New York Add → Tokyo Retry. Only the missing declaration was created in New York time; existing jobs, including an operator-edited Paris schedule, were preserved. |
| UI owner tests | **278/278 passed.** |
| Device-zone and pending-job fixtures | **35/35 passed.** |
| Default `pnpm check:changed` | **Passed**; all three Knip scans found zero unused exports. |

The three-dot diff against integrated main `150edeea6e0e` is still the same 30-file time-zone patch as on the previous PR head. Of those files, 29 are byte-identical. `docs/cli/templates.md` also contains main’s independently added Template-drafting paragraph; the time-zone and Retry edits are unchanged. No branch-only route, budget, or presentation changes were added. These are local results, not hosted CI or review clearance. The standalone Tools catalog interaction probes and paired startup benchmark were not rerun on this tree.

### Upgrade compatibility on this revision

The isolated upgrade and readback was repeated on November 23, 2026 against this published tree, `24211f349bb8594f860573bbd3372ac7becaf802`. A scratch environment ran the shipped **2026.11.6** Gateway and stored three cron jobs with Template-style declaration keys and three settings. The same state directory was then switched to a release-shaped runtime packed from this tree (`npm pack` of `6ada1b98a996`), started, and read back through the upgraded Gateway.

| Stored by shipped 2026.11.6 | Read back after upgrading to this revision |
| --- | --- |
| Enabled job, `0 9 * * 1` in `Europe/Paris` | Same job ID, declaration key, cron expression, time zone and enabled state. Next run unchanged: 09:00 Paris time on November 30. |
| Paused job, `30 18 * * *` in `Asia/Tokyo` | Same job ID, declaration key, cron expression and time zone; still paused. Enabling it on the upgraded Gateway scheduled 18:30 Tokyo time (09:30 UTC); it was then paused again. |
| Paused job, `15 7 * * 1-5` in `America/New_York`, bound to an agent and session key | Same job ID, declaration key, cron expression, time zone, agent and session key; still paused. |
| `agents.defaults.userTimezone`, `session.dmScope` and the Templates Labs setting | Unchanged. |

All four stored job IDs were present after the upgrade, including the built-in memory job. The job records differ only in fields that main adds on load and this diff does not touch: a recomputed `configRevision`, `reauthorizationRequired: false` and `ownerProfileId`. The built-in memory job, stored without a zone, now records the host zone it already ran in. The config file gained only migration markers and upgrade metadata.

Limits of this run:

- The baseline is 2026.11.6, the release line this branch is built from. The branch’s package version is 2026.11.6, so an upgrade from the newer 2026.11.7 would be a downgrade and was not attempted.
- The jobs were created with `cron add` and declaration keys, not through Template Add. A stored pending-setup record was not part of the upgrade. That record gains only the optional `deviceTimeZone` and `requiredAutomationIds` fields; the integration suite resumes an older record without `requiredAutomationIds` and rebinds it from the pinned Template source.
- No model was configured in the scratch environment, so no agent turn ran.

The earlier upgrade on tree `e3ceec9db23ba955a94541ea5b3f8753eeae0937` showed the same retention; all 30 files in this diff are byte-identical between that tree and this one.

**Real-model two-device Retry remains unproven.** The earlier hosted run did not create the jobs needed to exercise Retry. The deterministic regression above covers job reconciliation, not a completed model-driven setup.

prs.title: fix(models): show provider plugin labels in the Control UI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A provider plugin declares its own label (`ProviderPlugin.label`), but the Control UI replaced it with core text. A plugin whose provider id is `acme` and whose label is `Acme Cloud Plan` showed `Acme` (the title-cased id) in three places:

- the connected provider row in **Settings → Models → Providers**;
- the model-picker group header;
- the chat failure heading (`Acme reports a billing problem`).

The Gateway's provider presentation (`resolveProviderPresentation`) read only the user's `models.providers.<id>.name`, so the plugin label never reached the Control UI.

The bundled Google provider's API-key route was also labeled `Google AI Studio`. This PR renames it to `Gemini API key`.

## What Changed

- **The catalog row carries the declared label.** When `models.list` projects a public model row, it adds `providerName` from the provider plugin's `label` in the plugin registry that prepared the catalog. A models read never loads a plugin only to name it.
- **The provider presentation still decides the final name.** `projectModelsProviderPresentation` uses the user's `models.providers.<id>.name` first, then the row's declared label. If neither exists, the Control UI keeps its existing fallback (brand table, then title-cased id).
- **Chat failure heading** reads the provider name from the chat's model catalog rows. That is the source the model-change notices already use, so the chat boot path does not load the provider-icon module.
- **Bundled Google provider:** the provider label, the API-key method label, the choice label and the manifest `groupLabel` change from `Google AI Studio` / `Google AI Studio API key` to `Gemini API key`. Gemini CLI guidance and the docs that name the setup now say `Gemini API key`. The provider id `google`, the choice id `gemini-api-key`, `--gemini-api-key`, `GEMINI_API_KEY` and all config keys are unchanged. Docs still name Google AI Studio as the website where you create a key, and as the official API endpoint.

## User Impact

- A provider plugin's own label now appears on the Models provider row, the model-picker group and the failure heading. A name that the user sets in `models.providers.<id>.name` still wins.
- Bundled providers whose plugin label is different from the old Control UI brand-table entry now show the plugin label on these surfaces. Example: Google shows `Gemini API key`.

## Evidence

**Red on base, green on this branch** (base `e2973f933f10`, tier vitest-source):

| Test | Base | Branch |
|---|---|---|
| `src/gateway/server-methods/models-presentation.test.ts` › names a plugin provider with its declared label unless the user named it | fail | pass |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-run-failure-notice.test.ts` › names a provider's billing problem with its declared label | fail | pass |
| `extensions/google/provider-contract-api.test.ts` › exposes Gemini API key setup | fail | pass |
| `extensions/google/manifest.test.ts` › offers Gemini API keys without consumer CLI OAuth | fail | pass |

**Consumers:** 72 test files that import a changed source or `models-list.test-support.ts` pass in one `ocx test` run (652 tests; it includes every `extensions/google` test).

**Control UI E2E** (tier dist-nodts). The screenshots below come from the first head `7dd27d006ab7`. The second commit changed where the label is read, so the synthetic `acme` run was repeated on a working tree before the final helper extraction (`readDeclaredProviderNames`, no behavior change), with the same three results. On the exact head `8aa5765ff4d7` (frozen `ocx base` build), a separate scratch Gateway with an external provider plugin showed the plugin's label on the provider row, the picker group and the billing failure heading. two scratch Gateways (base and branch), each with a synthetic `acme` provider plugin loaded through `plugins.load.paths` and a local stub endpoint that returns HTTP 402. Before → after:

- Models provider row: `Acme` → `Acme Cloud Plan`
- Model-picker group: `Acme` → `Acme Cloud Plan`
- Failure heading: `Acme reports a billing problem` → `Acme Cloud Plan reports a billing problem`
- Add a provider: `Google AI Studio · API key` → `Gemini API key · API key`

| | Before (base) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Models provider row | ![Before: Models provider row shows Acme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dbcb5bd6-f2de-4401-a77a-15d612fb19fe) | ![After: Models provider row shows Acme Cloud Plan](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16ad6379-9b1b-4756-ab55-83e0f0338940) |
| Model-picker group | ![Before: picker group Acme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16125107-a428-4597-95cf-6c67fcc916c3) | ![After: picker group Acme Cloud Plan](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d002c3b-ad06-4ff5-8c01-533e2b1c0dd8) |
| Failure heading | ![Before: Acme reports a billing problem](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/47f33c63-3de7-4110-963c-28573208285c) | ![After: Acme Cloud Plan reports a billing problem](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ccbdab97-7e95-4a16-931b-59e99fc87450) |
| Add a provider (Google) | ![Before: Google AI Studio](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0168650b-c616-4eb2-a551-fa12bd7eb76d) | ![After: Gemini API key](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e8014b57-c0c5-49ef-9089-024afa064008) |

## Defaults recorded

- The plugin label wins over the Control UI brand table, because the plugin owns its provider's name. The user's configured name still wins over both.
- The label comes from the plugin registry that prepared the published catalog, when the catalog rows are projected. It does not come from a cold plugin load or an extra catalog read.

## Not in this PR

A provider-written failure message with its own action link is not shown in the chat notice yet. Today the provider error text is reduced to `errorMessage` when the stream turns it into an assistant message (`src/llm/stream.ts`). prs.title: fix: stop iOS Talk from answering realtime speech twice after a mode switch
prs.body:
Closes #197406

## What Problem This Solves

On iOS, if `talk.realtime.mode` changes from `stt-tts` to `realtime` while continuous Talk is on, the next turn starts the realtime voice session but the old on-device silence monitor keeps running. Every realtime utterance is then also sent as an ordinary chat turn, so the agent answers twice and the phone speaks the extra answer with the system voice over the realtime voice. Those duplicate turns also keep the agent busy, so realtime consult calls get rejected.

## User Impact

Changing the Talk mode during a call no longer produces two voices or duplicate agent work. Realtime speech is handled only by the realtime session, and stopping and restarting Talk is no longer needed to recover.

## Why This Change Was Made

The silence monitor belongs to the native capture session and was only cancelled by `stop()`, backgrounding, push to talk, and muting. When `start()` switched to a realtime route it never touched the monitor, and realtime callbacks fill the same transcript fields the monitor reads. `start()` now cancels the monitor before it takes a realtime route. If realtime startup fails, `start()` falls through to native startup, which starts its own monitor as before, so the native fallback is unchanged.

## Evidence

No device or simulator run exists for this change yet, so there is no observed proof that the duplicate answer is gone. What exists is a new test and static checks.

The new test in `TalkConfigRefreshTests` covers the handoff through the real turn path, with no test-only lifecycle helper:

- It starts native Talk against a connected Gateway fixture and confirms the silence monitor is running.
- It switches the served `talk.config` to a realtime route and sends a final transcript through the existing transcript entry point. The turn reaches `chat.send` and ends on a terminal error acknowledgement, and the resume then starts realtime.
- When `talk.session.create` arrives, the monitor must already be gone. On the base commit it is still running at that point.
- The test then fails realtime startup and checks that native capture resumes with a recognition request and its own silence monitor.

Checks run here: `swiftc -parse` on the two changed Swift files (`apps/ios/Sources/Voice/TalkModeManager.swift` and `apps/ios/Tests/TalkModeConfigParsingTests.swift`) and `git diff --check` pass.

Not run here: the iOS test suite (`pnpm ios:test`), because this machine has only the Command Line Tools and no Xcode, so the new test has not been compiled, executed or timed. A device check that switches `talk.realtime.mode` during continuous Talk and confirms no native `chat.send` or system-voice playback is also not run.

prs.title: fix(agents): apply_patch reports earlier hunks it already applied whe…
prs.body:
# fix(agents): apply_patch reports earlier hunks it already applied when a later hunk fails

Related: #127496 (follow-up to #160409)

## What Problem This Solves

#160409 made `apply_patch` check every update hunk before writing, so a missing update target or a context mismatch now rejects the patch with no file changes. Failures that only appear while writing still leave earlier hunks applied, and the error names only the hunk that failed:

- `Add File` onto a path that already exists
- `Delete File` of a missing path
- `Move to` onto an existing file, or a move whose source removal fails after the destination was written
- I/O errors, or cancellation between hunks

The model gets a single error and has no way to tell that earlier files were created, changed, or deleted. It then resends the whole patch from an outdated view of the files.

## User Impact

When a patch fails partway through, the tool error now lists the changes that already landed, using the same `A`/`M`/`D` markers as the success summary, and tells the model to re-read those files before retrying:

```
Cannot create existing.txt: the file already exists. Use "*** Update File: existing.txt" to change it, or delete it earlier in the same patch.
The patch stopped partway; these earlier changes were applied and not rolled back:
A created.txt
M notes.txt
Re-read these files before retrying, and do not resend the hunks already applied.
```

A failure on the first write leaves the error text unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

#127496 offers two options: compensate (roll back with an undo journal) or keep the earlier changes and report them. This PR takes the reporting option:

- It adds no new state, journal, or backend preconditions. #122933 stalled while trying to model those preconditions across the host and sandbox backends.
- It follows the repo guidance to prefer cheap mechanisms, such as best-effort recording with a warning, and to accept rare, visible, recoverable edge cases.
- Rollback can still be built on top of this later if maintainers decide on it. Even then, a rollback that fails would need this same partial-effect report.

Details:

- The error object is kept and only its message is extended. `AbortError`, `ToolInputError`, and the host-root-escape markers survive, so cancellation handling and the containment hint behave as before.
- If a move writes the destination but fails to remove the source, the destination is reported as `A` (a new copy), not `M` (a finished move).
- The summary type and formatting moved to `src/agents/apply-patch-summary.ts`, because `apply-patch.ts` would otherwise go over the 700-line `max-lines` cap. Its one external type import moved with it.

Not changed: there is still no rollback, and earlier hunks stay on disk. If maintainers decide rollback is required, that is a separate follow-up.

## Evidence

New `src/agents/apply-patch.partial-commit.test.ts`, run through the public tool boundary:

| Case | Upstream main | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Add + update succeed, then an add onto an existing file fails (real host fs) | only the failing hunk's error | error also lists `A created.txt`, `M notes.txt` |
| Cancellation after the first write (sandbox bridge) | `AbortError`, no applied paths | still `AbortError`, lists `M a.txt` |
| Move: destination written, source removal fails | no applied paths | lists `A new.txt` |
| Failure on the first hunk | unchanged message | unchanged message |

- `pnpm test src/agents/apply-patch.partial-commit.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 4 passed, about 45 s on a cold shard (mostly worker preparation); the tests themselves take under 40 ms. Without the source change, 3 of the 4 fail.
- `pnpm test src/agents/apply-patch*.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (all 9 apply_patch test files): 158 passed, 2 skipped.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` on the touched files: clean.

prs.title: fix(completion): regenerate core-only caches when setup requests full…
prs.body:
fix(completion): regenerate core-only caches when setup requests full completion

Refs #127450

## What Problem This Solves

Setup asks for a **full** completion cache, meaning core commands plus plugin commands (`ensureCompletionCacheExists(CLI_NAME, { generationMode: "full" })` in `src/wizard/setup.completion.ts`). But `ensureCompletionCacheExists` returned `true` as soon as the cache path existed, whatever mode had built it.

`openclaw update` always rewrites every shell's cache in core-only mode (`tryWriteCompletionCache` sets `OPENCLAW_COMPLETION_SKIP_PLUGIN_COMMANDS=1`). So on a host that has updated before, setup:

1. requests a full cache,
2. finds the core-only file,
3. reports success and installs it unchanged.

Plugin commands then never complete, and setup gives no sign that anything is wrong.

## Change

- **Cached scripts record their mode.** `completion --write-state` adds a final `# openclaw-completion-cache: full` or `# openclaw-completion-cache: core-only` comment to each script. `#` starts a comment in bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell, and the line comes after the script body, so zsh's `#compdef` and the rest of the script are unchanged.
- **Mode is `full` only when plugin commands were actually registered.** A write with `OPENCLAW_COMPLETION_SKIP_PLUGIN_COMMANDS=1`, or one where plugin discovery was skipped because the config is invalid, is recorded as `core-only`.
- **`ensureCompletionCacheExists` checks the mode.** A `full` request reuses the cache only when it is marked `full`. A missing, unreadable, or older unmarked cache is regenerated. A `core-only` request still accepts any existing cache, so the update path behaves as before.
- **Docs:** `docs/cli/completion.md` documents the marker.

Production code grows by about 45 lines across `completion-runtime.ts`, `completion-cli.ts`, and `doctor-completion.ts`. There is no new state file or config key.

## Update behavior

Caches written before this change have no marker. A `core-only` request (`openclaw update`) still accepts them. A `full` request from setup regenerates them once, which is the fix. The next `openclaw update` writes marked core-only caches as usual.

## Deliberately not in scope

The issue's repair direction also suggests build/source identity, config and plugin-inventory identity, fencing for concurrent publication, and keeping the prior generation when a refresh fails. The issue is labeled `needs-product-decision` for those, and each adds ongoing machinery for staleness that is rare, visible, and easy to recover from:

- **Build and plugin changes** are already handled. `openclaw update` refreshes the cache after every upgrade, and `openclaw completion --write-state` rebuilds it on demand. The docs already tell users to run it to pick up plugin commands.
- **Concurrent core/full writers.** Each write is published atomically (`publishOutputFileAtomically`), so readers never see a torn file. If update and setup race, the last writer wins and its marker states truthfully what it contains. The next full request regenerates if needed.
- **Doctor/status health** (`checkShellCompletionStatus().cacheExists`) still checks only that the cache exists. Doctor generates core-only caches itself, so a core-only cache is not a problem for doctor.

## Evidence

- **Regression (`src/commands/doctor-completion.test.ts`):** five cases on a real filesystem, with the generator process mocked:

  | Requested mode | Existing cache | Regenerates? |
  |---|---|---|
  | `full` | `full` | no |
  | `full` | `core-only` | yes |
  | `full` | unmarked | yes |
  | `core-only` | `core-only` | no |
  | `core-only` | unmarked | no |

  With the old existence-only check restored, the `full` over `core-only` and `full` over unmarked cases fail (2 failed, 11 passed). With the fix, all 13 tests pass.
- **Writer (`src/cli/completion-cli.write-state.test.ts`):** a successful plugin registration writes `full`. An invalid config that skips plugins writes `core-only`. The existing byte-exact cache assertions now include the marker line.
- **Real CLI, isolated `HOME` and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`:**
  - `pnpm openclaw completion --write-state --shell bash` ends with `# openclaw-completion-cache: full`.
  - With `OPENCLAW_COMPLETION_SKIP_PLUGIN_COMMANDS=1`, all four shell caches end with `# openclaw-completion-cache: core-only`.
  - The bash cache passes `bash -n`. zsh, fish, and pwsh are not installed on this host, so those shells' syntax was not checked.

## Tests

`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` (Node 24.22.2):

| File | Result | Wall time |
|---|---|---|
| `src/commands/doctor-completion.test.ts` | 13 passed | 43.3 s |
| `src/cli/completion-cli.write-state.test.ts` | 16 passed | 2.7 s |
| `src/wizard/setup.completion.test.ts` | 10 passed | 6.7 s |
| `src/cli/completion-runtime.test.ts` | 29 passed | 2.3 s |
| `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-post-update.test.ts` | 94 passed | 99.2 s |

Most of the wall time is compiler preparation on a loaded host. The new cases take a few ms each and use no timers, processes, or Gateway boots.

Also clean: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, type-aware `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check`.

prs.title: feat: let one room be ambient without changing the agent's other rooms
prs.body:
Closes #197838

## What Problem This Solves

When one agent serves several rooms, every room has to share one unmentioned-message policy, because `unmentionedInbound` can only be set globally (`messages.groupChat`) or per agent (`agents.entries.*.groupChat`). An operator who wants one ambient Slack channel alongside regular Discord channels on the same agent can't have both: turning on `room_event` for the agent also makes every Discord channel quiet, and unmentioned messages there stop getting automatic replies.

## User Impact

Operators can set `unmentionedInbound` on a single room: a Slack channel, a Discord guild or guild channel, or a Telegram group or forum topic. That room becomes ambient (or stays a normal request room) without changing the agent's other rooms. Existing configs behave exactly as before; the new key is optional.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared resolver (`resolveUnmentionedGroupInboundPolicy`) now takes the room's resolved value and uses this precedence: room, then agent, then global, then the `user_request` default. This is the order the issue review recommended. Each channel plugin owns its key and resolves it the same way it already resolves `requireMention`:

- Slack: `channels.slack.channels.<id>.unmentionedInbound`, inheriting from the `"*"` entry, and the same path under `accounts.<id>`.
- Discord: `guilds.<id>.channels.<channel>.unmentionedInbound`, then `guilds.<id>.unmentionedInbound`.
- Telegram: `groups.<id>.topics.<topic>.unmentionedInbound`, then `groups.<id>.unmentionedInbound`. DM topics don't accept it.

There is no per-room `visibleReplies`. Room events already require `message(action=send)` to post, so an ambient room needs nothing more, and other rooms keep their configured reply mode. Classification and `visibleReplies` stay independent, as discussed on the issue. Mentions, commands, aborts, DMs and access or mention gating are unchanged. The enum schema is exported once from `plugin-sdk/channel-config-schema`, so the three plugins share the core definition. The generated channel config metadata and the config doc baseline were regenerated, and the Slack key is listed as a no-op reload prefix, the same as the other per-channel keys.

Docs: ambient room events (new "Room specific policy" section and troubleshooting order), Slack and Discord access control, Slack troubleshooting, and the mention gating config reference.

## Evidence

- New tests cover two rooms on one agent with opposite policies:
  - Core resolver: room beats agent, and agent beats global. A room `user_request` beats a `room_event` agent.
  - Slack prepare: a channel set to `room_event` becomes a room event while a sibling channel on the same agent stays `user_request`.
  - Discord preflight: the same check with two channels in one guild.
  - Telegram message context: a group override beats an agent set to `user_request`, and the group without an override keeps the agent policy.
- The core and Discord tests fail on the base resolver and pass with the change. The runner stops at the first failing shard, so the Slack and Telegram tests were not run against the base separately; they exercise the same resolver input.
- Focused suites pass: `classification.test.ts` (5), Slack `prepare.test.ts` (58), Discord `message-handler.preflight.test.ts` (49), Telegram `bot-message-context.body.test.ts` (46).
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck (core, core tests, extensions, extension tests), lint, format, bundled channel config metadata, config docs baseline, plugin boundaries and import cycles all pass. Two lanes fail the same way on unmodified `main`:
  - Plugin SDK surface budget: with this PR's one added export reverted, `main` reports 3919 public exports against a budget of 3898 and 164 entrypoints against 163. This PR adds one export and no entrypoint.
  - Dead-export scan: unused exports in files this PR doesn't touch (`subagent-completion-admission.store.ts`, `task-supervisor.ts`, `project-access.ts`).
- Released-build check: the same change, applied as a small diff to the published 2026.11.7 core and Slack plugin files, on a gateway where one agent serves one Slack channel and several Discord channels. The new key passes `openclaw config validate`, and the existing config still validates. With the room override set, the resolver returns `room_event` for that Slack channel, and `user_request` for other Slack channels and the agent's Discord channels.
- Gap: I haven't run a channel e2e skill against an isolated Gateway with a live model.

prs.title: fix(normalization-core): restore the dropped one-day rung in relative time labels
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: relative time labels skipped the one-day rung entirely, so anything between 24 and 48 hours old rendered as `24h ago` … `47h ago` and then jumped straight to `2d ago` nearly half a day early.

## User Impact

Only the localized Control UI timestamps change, and only in the 24–48h window:

| Elapsed | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 23.4h | `23h ago` | `23h ago` (unchanged) |
| 23.5h | `24h ago` | `24h ago` (unchanged) |
| 24.1h – 47.99h | `24h ago` … `47h ago` | **`yesterday`** |
| 48h | `2d ago` | `2d ago` (unchanged) |

`ui/src/lib/format.ts` feeds the bucket to `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` with `numeric: "auto"`, which is what renders `-1 day` as `yesterday`. That label was always correct and simply never received a `1`.

Compact CLI timestamps (`src/infra/format-time/format-relative.ts`, which composes `${value}${unit[0]} ago`) now read **`1d ago`** in that window instead of `24h`..`47h` — they never say `yesterday`, because that path builds a unit-initial label. CLI **age** columns (`formatTimeAgo`, used by `openclaw status` and the session table) are unchanged: they still show `30h ago`, since they select their own unit. No configuration change and no migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

`bucketRelativeTimeMs` derived every unit from the already-rounded unit above it: seconds → minutes → hours → days. Two defects followed.

First, error compounded across four rounding steps (23h29m30s became 24 hours).

Second, the day rung required `hours >= 48` **before** `Math.round(hours / 24)`, which made `{ value: 1, unit: "day" }` unreachable. A missing rung is the whole behaviour: values below `2` days could never display as `1` day, so anything from 24h to 48h had to render as `24h`..`47h` and then jump to `2d` at 47.5h — roughly 12 hours early.

Each rung now promotes on its own rounded value (`minutes < 60`, then `hours < 24`) and days floor off the raw duration. Rounding at a boundary stays meaningful — a duration that rounds up to a whole hour promotes to hours instead of being labelled `60m` — while the day count finally reflects whole elapsed days.

The second/minute and the 48-hour boundary are specified contracts (`59_499ms → 59s`, `59_500ms → 1m`, `48h → 2 days`) and are unchanged; all four original cases still pass.

`ui/src/components/session-hovercard.ts` had already worked around the missing rung with its own `days >= 1` guard. That guard stays, because it still supplies the week, month, and year rungs the owner does not own.

## Evidence

Focused tests, red on the base and green with the fix, in `packages/normalization-core/src/format.test.ts`.

**Base (`2fe0a234f29`), test added first, no source change:**

```
FAIL  keeps 86400001ms inside the one-day rung
FAIL  keeps 171000000ms inside the one-day rung
FAIL  reaches the one-day rung somewhere between one hour and two days
      AssertionError: expected false to be true      // units.has("1day")
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  6 failed | 9 passed (15)
```

**After:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/normalization-core/src/format.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  20 passed (20)
Duration  15.04s
```

`src/infra/format-time/format-time.test.ts` — 54 passed.

**Runtime proof through the shipped Control UI formatter** — `ui/src/lib/format.ts` is the module that renders these labels, and it calls `bucketRelativeTimeMs` then `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat(locale, { numeric: "auto", style: "narrow" })`. No mock sits between the owner and the label:

| elapsed | before | after | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 23.4h | `23h ago` | `23h ago` | |
| 23.5h | `24h ago` | `24h ago` | |
| 24.1h | `24h ago` | **`yesterday`** | changed |
| 30h | `30h ago` | **`yesterday`** | changed |
| 36h | `36h ago` | **`yesterday`** | changed |
| 47.5h | `2d ago` | **`yesterday`** | changed |
| 47.99h | `2d ago` | **`yesterday`** | changed |
| 48h | `2d ago` | `2d ago` | |
| 72h | `3d ago` | `3d ago` | |

The `47.5h → 2d ago` row is the half-day-early rounding defect from the report: before this patch four of the seven samples in 24–48h still showed hour counts, and the other two jumped to `2d` about twelve hours early. Both UI entry points agree — `formatTimeAgo(30h)` and `formatRelativeTimestamp(-30h)` both return `yesterday`, and both still return `2d ago` at 48h.

**Owner-level boundary sweep:**

```
[1] minute -> hour promotion
      3570000ms  base=1hour   now=1hour  MATCH
      3599999ms  base=1hour   now=1hour  MATCH
[2] no sub-hour value labelled 60 minutes: offenders = 0
[3] no value labelled 0 across 0..60 days:  offenders = 0
[4] hour rung tops out at 24h, day rung starts at exactly 24h   (7/7 OK)
        86399999ms -> 24hour     86400000ms -> 1day
       172799999ms -> 1day       172800000ms -> 2day
[6] preserved base contracts   (4/4 OK)
RESULT: promotion=true; sixtyMinutes=true; noZero=true; edges=true; preserved=true -> PASS
```

**Gates:** `oxfmt --check` correct format; `oxlint` clean; `tsgo -p packages/normalization-core/tsconfig.json --noEmit` exit 0.

**Known gaps, stated rather than hidden:**

- The table above renders the shipped formatter module in Node. It is not a browser screenshot of a running Control UI; that would additionally cover the DOM/CSS path and needs a `pnpm dev` Gateway plus the Control UI e2e route.
- `ui/src/lib/format.test.ts` reports 1 failure on this Windows host (`expected '30秒后' to match /^in (29|30)s$/`). It is a pre-existing locale-dependent failure: with this change stashed, the same file fails identically on the base commit (`1 failed | 65 passed`).

<details>
<summary>Diff shape</summary>

```
packages/normalization-core/src/format.test.ts | 36 ++++++++++++++++++
packages/normalization-core/src/format.ts      | 36 ++++++++++++++++--------
2 files changed, 63 insertions(+), 9 deletions(-)
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(update): inspect closed or incomplete WAL databases in check-release
prs.body:
### Summary

`checkRelease()` previously opened state and agent SQLite files directly via `resolveReadOnlyShmSqliteFileUri()` (`?mode=ro&readonly_shm=1`), which fails with `SQLITE_CANTOPEN` (`unable to open database file`) when a WAL-mode database has been cleanly closed without a `-shm` file or only has an empty `-wal` file.

### Changes

- `src/update/check-release.ts`: Use `tryInspectSqliteReadOnlyInProcess(..., { preserveSourceArtifacts: true })` to read live complete WAL families in-place without modifying source bytes/sidecars, and fall back to `prepareSqliteReadOnlyCopyInProcess()` when a WAL family is closed or incomplete (missing `-shm`).
- `src/update/check-release.test.ts`: Added regression tests verifying cleanly closed WAL-mode agent DBs (with no sidecars and with an empty `-wal` only) pass without creating sidecars, while live committed WAL frames with newer schemas are still detected and rejected.

### Verification

- `pnpm vitest run src/update/check-release.test.ts` (1 test file passed, 6 tests passed)

Fixes #204227

prs.title: fix(agents): warn when agentDir bootstrap files are silently ignored
prs.body:
Closes #29387

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: per-agent bootstrap files (SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, TOOLS.md, …) are silently ignored when an `agentDir` is configured, so owners believe safety rules are enforced when they are not.

Bootstrap injection only reads from the workspace directory (`resolveBootstrapFiles` → `loadWorkspaceBootstrapFiles(workspaceDir)`). Files placed in a configured `agentDir` have no effect and raise no diagnostic — no warning, error, or log entry.

## User Impact

User impact: owners with per-agent `agentDir` setups now get an explicit, actionable warning naming the ignored files and both directories, instead of silently-ignored safety constraints. No behavior change otherwise: nothing new is injected, no output changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

A new `warnIgnoredAgentDirBootstrapFiles()` runs inside the shared `resolveBootstrapFiles()`: it resolves `agentDir` via the existing `resolveAgentDir(cfg, agentId)`, skips when it equals the workspace, stats the canonical `WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILENAMES` set, and emits the warning through the existing session-scoped dedupe warning sink.

Placing the check in the shared resolver covers every run path (CLI, embedded runner, compaction, preparation/diagnostics) without threading `agentId`/`agentDir` through all call sites — the approach that stalled the earlier attempts (#29450 stale-closed, #29545). The change is purely diagnostic, which keeps the issue's `impact:security` / `needs-security-review` concerns out of scope for now; the behavioral merge ("Option A") remains a product decision as labeled on the issue.

## Evidence

- New tests in `src/agents/bootstrap-files.test.ts` ("agentDir bootstrap diagnostics"): warns for SOUL.md/AGENTS.md in agentDir; silent when agentDir holds no bootstrap files; silent when agentDir resolves to the workspace.
- `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/bootstrap-files.test.ts` — **36/36 pass** (33 existing + 3 new).
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on both touched files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Repo check battery (`scripts/check.mts`) green except a pre-existing, environmental `npm package-lock guard` failure (`ETARGET: no matching version for @openclaw/fs-safe@0.26.14 with a date before 10/28/2026`); no package files touched.
- Example warning emitted:

  `bootstrap files found in agentDir (~/.openclaw/agents/main/agent) are not loaded into the system prompt: SOUL.md, AGENTS.md. Bootstrap files are only read from the workspace directory (~/.openclaw/workspace); move them to the workspace (or set this agent's workspace) to apply them. (sessionKey=agent:main:…)`

prs.title: fix: let Windows updates restart after a rollback
prs.body:
Closes #204196

## What Problem This Solves

After a Windows release update rolls back, another Update click can stop the Gateway and leave it down. Cleanup finishes, but the old process stays alive, so its resident launcher cannot start the pending release.

## User Impact

A Gateway running this fix can exit after cleanup without losing stop or readiness messages. No configuration, dependency, schema, or launcher-format change is needed. The serving release must contain the fix; a newer candidate cannot release a reference held by older running code.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing IPC stop listener references Node's child channel. Release that event-loop reference in the same owner with `process.channel?.unref()`. The channel stays connected while the Gateway serves. This removes the keepalive instead of adding a shutdown hook, forced exit, retry, or timer.

The change adds two production lines, one real-process regression, and the update-contract note.

## Evidence

- **Live cause established:** the stuck Windows Gateway had exactly one active, referenced libuv handle: its launcher IPC pipe. It had no workers or listening server; timers were unreferenced. A ten-minute passive exit observation returned false. Running only `process.channel.unref()` made it exit within 0.3 seconds and advanced the pending trial from zero attempts to one. Details and UTC timestamps are in #204196. This diagnostic intervention is not counted as fixed-build acceptance proof.
- **Regression:** the final test fails against `e2973f933f` with an exit-wait `AbortError` after 10 seconds. It passes on `5e894bb924` in 4.5 seconds. The Gateway trial, launcher, and respawn suites pass on AWS Linux runners; final touched-test typecheck, lint, and format checks also pass.
- **Packages:** full source builds and canonical package creation passed on AWS for the fixed serving release and both frozen healthy/crash successors. The serving package is pinned to `7629c49617`; the later PR commit changes only the regression's exit observation.
- **Known base failure:** `check:changed` passes its other checks but reports the pre-existing Knip unused export `runWindowsGatewayTaskSupervisor` from #204094. That separate cleanup is owned outside this PR. No guard, baseline, or skip flag was added here.
- **Windows acceptance:** native Scheduled Task rollback → healthy-click and plain T → T+1 proof is running against those frozen packages. This PR is not a release qualification sign-off.

prs.title: fix: recover overlapping global chats through Doctor
prs.body: Related: #188165 ## What Problem This Solves Older stored state can contain both `global` and `agent::global` for one agent, with different session IDs and saved conversations. The normal qualified session reader cannot choose between those overlapping bindings, so continuing either conversation can fail even though its history and files still exist. Doctor previously left this pair in place. This change repairs the stored binding once through Doctor. The original ongoing chat keeps `global`; the accidentally created second chat receives a distinct ordinary address derived from its existing session ID. ## User Impact With the Gateway stopped, run `openclaw doctor --fix`, restart, and reopen the recovered conversation from **Sessions**. Both conversations retain their original session IDs, stored titles, history windows, ownership, membership and workspace locations. Files stay where they were. After the repair, both addresses use normal session handling. The old literal review URL requires explicit reopening. A retained view or a fresh visit resolves to the existing missing-session view, which offers navigation choices without silently moving work into the ongoing chat. Ordinary global aliases retain their meaning. Attributable completed cron history follows the recovered conversation. Its stored run identity, timing and outcome remain unchanged, and scheduled-job definitions and enabled states are untouched. Doctor refuses an occupied destination, pending input, linked work or uncertain historical identity rather than overwriting or guessing. The moved review chat must have no repository workspace or persisted worker placement; those bindings remain untouched and their recovery is outside this operation. A binding owned only by the unchanged ongoing chat does not prevent repair. ## Why This Change Was Made The defect is an overlapping persisted binding. Doctor first completes ordinary key normalization. Its existing maintenance lock and session lifecycle writer own offline repair, history-window movement and preservation of session artifacts. They can give the second conversation an ordinary address while retaining its original identity and saved work. The agent database move and the shared historical-reference update use their existing transaction owners. If execution stops between them, the retained run's session ID identifies the existing destination on the next Doctor run. Recovery checks for outstanding references before inspecting a destination, so a completed repair leaves subsequently active conversations alone. It selects the owner of the recorded history windows rather than scanning older recovered chats. The UI change is limited to verifying the old explicit literal address, revalidating it after reconnect and keeping a retired view in place until the user chooses where to go. The canonical session and update documentation explains the repair and reopening step. ## Evidence The original Doctor regression failed on the base because the literal overlapping row remained after repair. The focused tests exercise the real Doctor entry, existing session writers and historical-run producer, including preserved history and ownership, refusal conditions, repeat execution and interruption between the two database commits. Two additional retry failures were reproduced before correcting selection: a completed repair rejected a conversation with restart work, and an interrupted repair inspected an older recovered conversation instead of the recorded session's destination. The candidate in 3cc0cff304505ccdc524ea1487314740480d95cb passed formatting, focused lint and i18n checks, file-size/assertion/test-line guards, the SQLite worker and membership-writer guard, and seven selected type-check groups. Its Doctor-consumer run passed 357 cases in 32 files. Passing evidence for 743 cases in 30 other related files remains applicable on unchanged inputs, including the reconnect tests. These 62 related files cover initial preservation, retry and interruption, refusal conditions, healthy aliases, legacy normalization and explicit old-view handling. A participant preservation case reproduced a doubled contribution count before correction. The lifecycle owner now transfers artifacts once, preserving counts and timestamps through repair and repeat execution. Repository-bound review inputs refuse before rehome while their Files access, identities, history, permissions and binding remain unchanged. Persisted worker placements receive the same protection. Separate controls verify that bindings owned only by the ongoing chat do not prevent recovery. The original affected pair was repaired through the normal offline update/Doctor owner on this head. Independent native readback preserved both original session IDs, all 77 retained messages, ownership, membership, permissions, workspace roots and all three saved files. The disabled schedule stayed unchanged; the historical failed run retained its other facts while following the recovered conversation. Repeating Doctor made no further change. Both original chats then completed one new natural UI turn at their own addresses. The ongoing chat used its saved work to recommend three pickups at capacity 18; the review retained its separate saved plan and kept seven parcels held pending inspection. Native send/acknowledgement/final receipts and rendered answers agree on each original identity. Independent post-turn readback preserved the existing history prefixes, files, authority and workspace roots. The retained and freshly opened old review URLs both stayed at the old address and required explicit reopening, with no sends. A fresh healthy global conversation created by published OpenClaw 2026.10.9 was upgraded through OCM to the release-shaped package built from this head. Full-integrity Doctor completed, and the original address, session ID, six-message history prefix, owner fields, workspace and saved note were preserved. Existing Doctor behavior supplied a previously missing display title from the first message. One new ordinary agent turn then used the saved plan, retaining twelve eligible samples and three held for inspection. Independent readback preserved the original history prefix and note; no background service was introduced. A confirmed blocker remains for an overlapping review conversation with managed attachments: after rehome, normal media cleanup can remove its old-key attachment record and original payload file. The unchanged ongoing-chat attachment control passes. This PR is not ready to land while that recovery contract is unresolved. The current hosted ratchets pass. The published head's remaining Visitor Access and native plugin-spawn CI failures also reproduce on the relevant baseline; their attribution is recorded separately. Focused integration with the selected target, including its landed Visitor fixture repair, and final readiness checks remain pending. This PR remains open and unmerged. ## Visual evidence []() | View | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | Old review address: baseline to repaired runtime | ![Original review at its old address before repair](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad5853bc-f4f6-4daf-9e79-c205965b224f) | ![Old address remains selected and requires explicit reopening after repair](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d01325df-8cd6-43fb-a325-4c284eb02e0d) | | Original ongoing chat: continuation on 3cc0cff | ![New ordinary prompt prepared in the original ongoing chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b36bb512-f9c8-434e-b59c-30423671e275) | ![Original ongoing chat uses its saved work to recommend pickups with capacity 18](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a99969ab-47a9-41d7-b477-c11ede3775cf) | | Recovered review: continuation on 3cc0cff | ![New ordinary prompt prepared in the recovered original review](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5fbb8b05-4eee-46aa-8ae4-8c3caf500461) | ![Recovered review keeps held parcels pending actual inspection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/039493db-1bbd-4780-954f-6581a92e11fd) | ### Original repair and continuation; reconnect wait labeled 8x https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09d44cbc-9200-4182-a8a7-db59b8db34f0 ### Visual verification - Baseline: 199d2967a6a10e91eccb1eb1a5ebfc28d37f00ee \(old address\); continuation pre\-send states use the fixed head - Exact head: `3cc0cff304505ccdc524ea1487314740480d95cb` - Scenario: Repair the original stored pair once, retire the old review address, and continue both original conversations through ordinary UI handling\. The old\-address comparison is 199d296 to 3cc0cff; continuation panels show before and after new turns on 3cc0cff\. - Runtime/build: OpenClaw 2026\.10\.9\-3cc0cff30450\-2026\-10\-31T10\-16\-29\.514Z - Retained and fresh old address: Both stay at the old address and show the missing\-session view; zero sends - Original conversations: Two original session IDs; 77 existing messages preserved; two new prompts finish in their own chats - Saved work and references: Three named files unchanged; disabled schedule unchanged; failed\-run facts retained at the recovered address - Repeat repair: No further history, ownership, authority, membership, workspace or file change - Exact fixed head and Gateway build observed in the real UI\. - Independent native readback checks original history prefixes, files, ownership, authority, memberships and workspace roots\. - Only the held\-view update/reconnect wait is accelerated 8x; new\-turn interactions remain at normal speed\. - The review recording retains its brief scroll through the same saved history\. - Source recordings received every\-frame thumbnail inspection and full\-resolution still/critical\-frame inspection; no normal\-speed playback claim\. - The final 1,147\-frame recording and decisive full\-resolution frames were inspected; captioned waits and joins are measured, and the original recordings are retained\.

OpenClaw users with a JZSTOKEN API key do not currently have a documented provider configuration for its OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

prs.title: improve: identify commands that fall back to in-process spawning
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot tell which shared command callers fall back to in-process spawning when a broker is present, or distinguish that fallback from a missing broker. This prevents targeting the callers behind main-thread spawn stalls.

## User Impact

The existing `openclaw_child_process_spawn_total` counter now identifies the fallback class and main/worker thread alongside its bounded command family and caller-operation labels. It records no argv, command paths, environment values or stacks. Spawn routing and process behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The option translator reports the reason for its existing fallback instead of discarding it. The existing heartbeat aggregates successful launches by that reason, and the Prometheus exporter preserves it. No new worker, dependency, configuration or cache is introduced. Production growth is 33 physical lines net, including comments and the exporter.

The Team perf-loop lead, an agent acting under Peter's standing instruction, rejected the general off-main spawner draft and directed this diagnostic-only landing. This decision was the lead's, not Peter's. The broad draft is parked and is not part of this PR. Follow-up fixes should make only the caller classes identified by production evidence brokerable. This lane did not access Team.

## Evidence

The real-spawn regression fails on exact main `e2973f933f103`: eight launches collapse into one counter without fallback attribution. With this change it distinguishes broker, missing broker, IPC, independent lifetime, numeric descriptors, inherited stdio and native-API stdio fallback; two descriptor launches aggregate together under the same caller. The exporter test verifies that these labels reach the rendered counter. Existing tests cover failed launches, disabled diagnostics, deferred caller attribution and bounded labels.

Validation: all 68 focused Node tests passed (51 spawn-owner, 17 exporter); core and extension/test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting and the line-cap ratchet passed. Independent Codex autoreview is clean through P2. The existing output-option predicate moved unchanged beside its protocol type to keep exec-spawn within its existing file cap.

`pnpm check:changed` completed. Its candidate line-cap failure was fixed and the affected lint/ratchet/type gates rerun successfully. Its remaining deadcode failure is inherited: `runWindowsGatewayTaskSupervisor` became an unused export in #204094 / `e2973f933f103`, which moved its external caller into the same module. The same production Knip command reproduces exactly that one failure on the exact main parent with a separate frozen install. This is a main regression, not ignored noise. No UI-imported module was changed.

<details>
<summary>Measurements from the rejected general-spawner draft</summary>

These are measurements of the parked prototype, not benefits claimed for this diagnostic PR. The draft added 627 production lines and left descriptor retention and native IPC/bootstrap unresolved. No dependency change was approved or made.

Synthetic Linux arm64 Node 26.12.1/libuv 1.52.1; ~7 GiB touched parent RSS; private loop-backed btrfs with 62,000 files (~1.14 GB); concurrent direct random-write/fsync fio. Eight balanced samples per arm, cold first launch separate from 100 warm launches, with unchanged A/A controls. No production data.

| Metric | Native A1 | Native A2 | Worker fallback |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread spawn calls / 100 warm launches | 100 | 100 | 0 |
| Worst main heartbeat ms | 86.27 | 84.06 | 24.10 |
| Main CPU median ms / 100 warm launches | 1914.93 | 1709.60 | 62.17 |
| Process-tree CPU median ms / 100 warm launches | 3715 | 3300 | 3800 |
| Warm wall median ms / 100 launches | 3683.31 | 3271.42 | 3711.41 |
| Cold first-launch wall median ms | 51.00 | 44.19 | 90.82 |

The 90.82 ms measurement is one-time cold initialization, not the latency of every warm spawn. Warm A/A wall spread was 12.6%; Worker warm wall was 0.8–13.5% higher than those controls. The small-process broker arm remained much cheaper (103.15 ms per 100 warm launches). The lead did not accept the broader tradeoff or implementation size. An earlier packaged run had 27.8% A/A spread while a host-side check overlapped; it was not accepted as total-cost proof.

The Linux syscall trace used fork-style `clone(SIGCHLD)` without CLONE_VM/VFORK for the measured invocation. This does not establish the syscall path of every Node/libuv build, and the fixture did not reproduce a multi-second production storage stall.

</details>
