prs.title: fix(ui): inline widgets flash an empty box before loading on warm chat reload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: inline widget cards in a cached chat show an untitled empty box, then "Loading…", then another empty frame before the widget appears, on every warm reload.

## User Impact

User impact: a reloaded chat shows each inline HTML widget's title in its reserved card from the first frame, and the card fills in place with the live widget, with no empty or "Loading…" state and no layout movement.

Risks and required actions, kept visible:

- **CSS budget (approved by Peter, recorded).** The overlay and the canvas-card outline add 137 B of raw CSS to the chat route stylesheet; startup CSS is unchanged (+0 B) and total CSS gzip grows 14 B, within build variance. Main already exceeds `totalCssRawBytes` (1,783,379 B measured on 6b0df8b9 against a 1,740,234 B ceiling), and the gate allows only 64 B of growth over an over-cap base, so the entry resets the ceiling to this PR's measured 1,783,516 B plus 64 B, absorbing main's inherited raw debt as earlier approvals did. The original parked layout cost 335 B; the overlay is the smallest CSS form of an opaque titled cover I found.
- **Security boundary.** `src/agents/sandbox-host.ts` (sandbox proxy shell) is in the `execution` category of `.github/security-review-policy.yml`; no `CODEOWNERS` entry covers it, so it needs an independent maintainer review. The host-facing message, params and validation are unchanged; only the timing moves (details below).
- **Other `onRendered` consumers** now run 3 frames after load instead of at load: board widgets show content and post host state for legacy saved widgets on the presentation signal (which also removes the same empty-frame flash there), and offscreen board widgets acknowledge after the 1 s fallback. HTML previews in strict mode are script-free and keep load timing.

- **Recovery status kept.** Rebasing onto main (6b0df8b9, including #202220) showed that deleting the owner's generic pending notice had also dropped "Disconnected. This view reconnects automatically." for scheduled read retries, an offline Gateway and sandbox proxy restarts. A narrow `reconnecting` flag now carries exactly those states and the titled overlay shows the status, so nothing in flow moves. Still removed on purpose: the 10 s slow-read notice (it said "Disconnected" while connected) and the in-flow notice above an already-rendered iframe (it shifted rows on every revalidation).

Accepted edge cases (not coded): a rendered widget whose Gateway drops shows no per-card status (the app's connection status covers it, and the card is inert until the next validated read); a widget whose main thread stays busy for more than 1 s after `load` falls back before it paints (the previous behavior); a tab hidden during load acknowledges by fallback and may show one empty frame when it becomes visible again.

## Why This Change Was Made

The acknowledgement now means "the document's post-load frames are with the compositor", carried by the existing message:

- The trusted proxy shell prepends one more guard script to scripted widget documents. After the document's `load` (capture, once), it waits three `requestAnimationFrame` callbacks and posts a params-free `sandbox-resource-loaded` to the proxy. A third frame can only begin after the first post-load frame finished raster and activation; two frames only prove a commit.
- The proxy acknowledges the host with the unchanged message and `renderId` only after it observed the inner `load` itself and the witness arrived from the current inner window. Script-free documents keep load timing. Hidden or offscreen frames run no animation frames, so they acknowledge 1 s after load.
- Host validation (`source`, `origin`, `renderId` in `ui/src/lib/widget-sandbox-host.ts`) is unchanged, no message type was added, and inner `ui/notifications/sandbox-*` messages are still never relayed to the host.

On that signal, the Control UI reapplies the parked L315 change in a smaller form: scripted canvas documents show their title in the lazy, admission-held and canvas reservations as one opaque overlay (`.chat-tool-card__reservation`, absolutely positioned over the already-positioned `.chat-tool-card__preview`). The space is held by whatever is in flow beside it (the lazy box, a spacer, or the mounted iframe, which stays paintable and is never hidden), and the overlay retires synchronously on the validated acknowledgement. The generic pending/"Loading…" notice machinery in the canvas owner and the parked two-frame host delay are deleted; only the automatic-recovery status remains, inside the overlay. Only frames that hold a title until the acknowledgement show one (`widgetReservationTitle`); MCP Apps, strict documents, plain frames and script-free canvas documents keep untitled placeholders so they never regress from titled to untitled.

<details><summary>Sandbox boundary analysis</summary>

`src/agents/sandbox-host.ts` matches the `execution` category of `.github/security-review-policy.yml`; no `CODEOWNERS` entry covers it or the UI files.

- The host-facing message, its params and its validation are unchanged; the change is timing only.
- Widget code shares the witness's realm and can post the same witness, but the proxy never acknowledges before the `load` event it observes, so a forged witness can at most restore the previous load-time acknowledgement for its own card. Withholding it only delays the widget's own placeholder by the 1 s fallback; the existing 30 s render timeout is unaffected.
- The witness captures `postMessage`, `requestAnimationFrame` and its `load` listener before stored scripts run (the same pattern as the existing shortcut and scroll bridges), and a superseded render can never acknowledge.

</details>

## Evidence

**Rebased head (5a1ded31 on main 6b0df8b9), Team archived fixture, compositor captures.** Same bench command as below, without the three sidebar flags: on current main, `--sidebar-view online` lands on the People → Activity page during setup, so the chat (and the widget) never shows; that is a bench/fixture follow-up unrelated to this PR. Every delivered frame of the "Team metric 12" card was classified by a pixel classifier over the bench's `frames.json` and the DOM geometry probe, and the transition crops were inspected by hand.

| Reload | First card frame | Empty-outline frames | Card box / scroll while visible | Handoff | Bench anchor (movement / excess / missing) |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| r1 priming | titled (548 ms) | 0 | one signature (525,689 668×220, scroll 17099) | titled → live at 1,331 ms | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| r2 priming | titled (546 ms) | 0 | same single signature | titled → live at 1,346 ms | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| r3 priming | titled (763 ms), after 7 frames of an unpainted transcript column | 0 | same single signature | titled → live at 1,496 ms | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| r4 priming | titled (560 ms) | 0 | same single signature | titled → live at 1,360 ms | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| r4 measured | titled (562 ms) | 0 | same single signature | titled at 1,262 ms → live on the next frame (1,278 ms) | 0 / 0 / 0 |

Six other capture processes stopped on the bench's own setup refusals on this loaded host (load average 20–80): five `Invalid or backward compositor timestamp; no paint verdict` and one paint-holding calibration miss. On current main the Team active fixture requires `--transcript-witness`, which appends fresh live turns and opens at the transcript end, so the "Team metric 12" card is never in the viewport (the geometry probe sees no widget host in any sample; bench anchor excess 0, missing 0; the 209 px movement is the expected end-follow). The active-fixture card evidence below is therefore from the pre-rebase head only.

The mechanism probe and the remaining Team fixture captures below ran on the pre-rebase head (base d2bfdb0d).

"Team metric 12" card on a Team archived warm reload, delivered compositor frames top to bottom (synthetic fixture data):

| Main: untitled box (1,380 ms) → "Loading…" (1,397 ms) → empty box (1,797 ms) → live (1,947 ms) | This PR: unpainted transcript (847 ms) → titled card (863 ms) → still titled (2,147 ms) → live on the next frame (2,163 ms) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Main warm reload card frames](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc5b2491-40bd-44f5-97e1-baf71c34a06b) | ![This PR warm reload card frames](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7371477a-f79b-485f-abbd-747d397c8e93) |

The live canvas card also gains a 1px `--border` outline, so its frame matches the reservation.

**Mechanism probe (compositor).** A standalone harness served the real proxy shell from an isolated sandbox origin and a host page with an opaque titled cover over the iframe, retired on `sandbox-resource-loaded`. Chromium 156 headless with paint holding, CDP screencast of every delivered frame; a trial fails if any frame between the cover and live content shows the empty card. Stress = busy host main thread plus a raster-heavy SVG widget.

| Acknowledgement timing | Trials with an empty card frame |
| --- | ---: |
| Inner `load` (main) | 23 / 80 |
| `load` + 2 host frames (parked L315) | 10 / 80 |
| Proxy-side rAF pair after `load` | 2 / 140 |
| Paint Timing `first-paint` inside the widget | 8 / 80 (an occluded surface gets no presentation feedback, so it falls back) |
| Inner rAF pair after `load` | 15 / 290 (12 / 150 under stress) |
| **Inner third rAF after `load` (this PR)** | **0 / 290** |
| This PR's shell, unmodified, stressed | 0 / 100 |

Offscreen frames run no animation frames; the real shell acknowledged them through the fallback at ~1,027 ms.

prs.title: fix(agent-db): drop orphaned FTS5 shadows before recreating standing_intents_fts
prs.body:
## Problem

An agent database whose `standing_intents_fts` virtual table is gone but whose FTS5 shadow tables remain cannot converge. SQLite refuses to recreate the virtual table:

```
fts5: error creating shadow table standing_intents_fts_data: table already exists
```

`CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` does **not** help here: the guard only covers the virtual table, not its shadows. The schema ensure path therefore fails, and the caller reports

```
SqliteWorkerError: SQLite worker stopped before its result was received
```

which surfaces as `memory-core: standing intent maintenance failed`.

Measured with the SQLite behaviour that produces it:

| state | `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE IF NOT EXISTS x USING fts5(text)` |
|---|---|
| virtual table present | `table x already exists` |
| virtual table gone, shadows present | `fts5: error creating shadow table x_data: table 'x_data' already exists` |

The second row is the one that breaks the ensure path. The guard is absent in the first row too, but that row is not reached here — the ensure path only runs when the virtual table is missing.

## Fix

Drop the orphaned shadow tables before the canonical agent schema is applied, so the ensure path can recreate the virtual table and rebuild its index. When the virtual table is still present, the shadows are left untouched.

## Why this place

`ensureOpenClawAgentStandingIntentsSchema` (`src/state/openclaw-agent-standing-intents-schema.ts`) is the owner that recreates `standing_intents_fts`. It already exports the shadow table list (`STANDING_INTENTS_FTS_SHADOW_TABLES`), so the cleanup needs no new table list.

## Verification

Reproduced the exact failure and confirmed the fix against the same SQLite semantics:

```
OHNE Fix (aktueller Upstream-Code): fts5: error creating shadow table standing_intents_fts_data: table 'st...
MIT Fix (mein Patch):               OK
```

The added test covers both cases: orphaned shadows are cleaned up, and shadows of a present virtual table survive.

## Notes

- No database data is dropped: only FTS5 shadow tables of an **absent** virtual table are removed, and they are rebuilt from the owning content table.
- The same shadow-orphaning shape can occur for the other FTS5 tables (`session_transcript_fts`, `memory_index_*_fts`); this change fixes the standing-intents path that was observed failing. Happy to extend it if the maintainers prefer a shared helper.

prs.title: refactor: drop mid-request authority re-checks in the last gateway, session and node-host refusals (R6d part 4)
prs.body:
## Problem

OpenClaw checks authority once, when work starts (AGENTS.md "Choose good compromises"). The last gateway, ACP, session and node-host files outside `src/agents/**` still re-read a role, scope, profile version, access revision, config or command policy during a request. A started request was then refused with "authority changed" or "authority is no longer active/current". Other checks in the same files are valid Stop, disconnect or data fences, but their text claimed authority.

## Change

R6d part 4. Each string site was classified with one test: can it fire when only a permission, approval or config changes while nothing about the run or the data changes?

- Yes: the check and its plumbing are deleted.
- No (Stop, run close, disconnect, data fence): the check is kept and reworded. The text says what ended and what to do next.
- Start-time checks (admission, made once before work begins) stay. In `factory-github-proof.ts` the role/scope check sat inside a repeated closure whose first call was the admission; it is now a one-time check before the closure.

| Site | Old message | Kind | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `channel-avatar-http.ts` | Channel avatar session authority changed | data fence (session id, lifecycle revision, avatar ref) | reworded |
| `managed-image-session-read.ts` | Managed media session authority changed | data fence (session id, lifecycle revision) | reworded |
| `server-node-event-source.ts` | Node event session authority changed | data fence (harness, delivery) | reworded |
| `human-mention-policy.ts` recipient selection | Committed mention recipients or sender authority changed | admission, repeated at involvement commit | kept once at the start, reworded; repeat removed |
| `human-mention-policy.ts` involvement `assertCurrent` | Committed mention authority changed before involvement commit | mixed: recipient policy re-selection + policy closed | policy re-selection deleted; closed-policy fence kept, reworded |
| `mention-inbox.ts` commit | Mention authority changed before commit | mixed: profile version, access revision, config + session revision | profile/access/config compares deleted; session-revision fence kept, reworded |
| `node-claude-skill-runtime.ts` | Paired-node skill assignment or run authority changed | mixed: live node command allowlist + node/session/placement/claim fences | allowlist re-read deleted (still checked once at invocation start in `node-agent-cli-runtime.ts`); fences kept, reworded |
| `node-mcp-elicitation.ts` | MCP elicitation authority changed | opaque callback (pairing lifecycle mixed with MCP config) | kept, reworded |
| `cron-stream-sandbox-authority.ts` | Sandbox stream authority changed | session/resource fence | reworded |
| `desktop/observe-bridge.ts` | Desktop observer authority is no longer current | opaque connection callback | kept, reworded |
| `factory-github-proof.ts` | Factory GitHub caller authority changed. | mixed: role/scope/operator flag + connection/identity | role/scope/operator check moved to a one-time check at capture; connection/identity fence kept, reworded |
| `repository-dispatch.ts` | Repository caller authority changed | mixed | role, scope, operator-flag and permission-callback re-checks deleted; connection, device-source and identity fences kept, reworded |
| `repository-integration-identity.ts` | Repository operation authority changed | config re-read (integration, host, API URL) | deleted |
| `http-auth-user-profile.ts` (2) | HTTP profile authority changed during acquisition | admission (one acquisition) | kept, reworded |
| `openai-compatible-agent-run.ts` | Gateway requester authority changed | admission (`!admitted` only) | kept, reworded |
| `session-sharing-read.ts` | Gateway requester authority changed | requester identity fence | kept, reworded |
| `skill-library-session.ts` | OpenClaw ID owner authority changed | opaque owner-device callback (Stop fence of `SkillLibraryAuthority`) | kept, reworded |
| `talk/client-run-authority.ts` (2) | Talk caller source authority is no longer active | mixed: release/device source + `hasCurrentClientAuthority` fallback | permission fallback deleted; release and device-source fences kept, reworded |
| `remote-control-ui-ingress.ts` | Remote ingress principal authority changed; … | mixed: person auth policy + role compare + identity/alias/abort | **cut less:** kept, reworded. The role compare retires the binding so the MCP relay rebinds with the current role on the next request. Without it the next relay request fails downstream with `internal` and never rebinds (`remote-control-ui-ingress.integration` "shares real principal authority…" red). |
| `ws-connection/authenticated-request-dispatch.ts` publication transport | publication transport authority changed | opaque token-identity callback | kept, reworded (telemetry reason code unchanged) |
| `ws-connection/authenticated-request-dispatch.ts` expected profile | Gateway requester authority changed | permission re-check (`hasCurrentClientAuthority`) | callback argument deleted |
| `ws-connection/connect-publication-transport.ts` (2) | publication transport authority changed | handshake admission | kept, reworded |
| `server/ws-origin-policy.ts` | OpenClaw ID owner authority changed | opaque principal callback | kept, reworded |
| `config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-reclamation-commit.ts` | SQLite reclamation authority is no longer current | reclamation-state fence | reworded |
| `node-host/openclaw-id-connection.ts` | server authority changed | transport identity (server key) | reworded |

Deleted tests (they asserted a mid-request permission refusal):
- `server.sessions.create.repository-required.test.ts`: the `caller` row (client scopes cleared after ACK, run expected to be refused).
- `mention-inbox.test.ts`: "refuses a pending mention write after the recipient loses access".
- `server-plugins.session-facts.test.ts`: the `role`, `profile` and `same-object config` rows of "retains admitted grants but fences selected disclosure data". They expect a started disclosure to be refused after that change; #204134 removed that re-check, and the rows are red on main `8ea0f17162ab` (3 failed locally). The `grant` row stays: a started disclosure finishes and the next one is refused.

Stop and data-fence tests keep their conditions. Only their expected text changed. `config/session-identity-allowlist.txt` is pruned.

Accepted edge cases:
- A started mention write commits even if a recipient's role changes before commit. The next read applies the new role.
- A started repository operation keeps its admitted role. The next request uses the new role.

## Not in this PR

- `src/gateway/cron-creator-authority-grant.ts`, `src/acp/runtime/session-meta-resume-authorization.ts` and `src/gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-user-turn.ts` (`assertRequesterCurrent`, the requester-owner re-read from live config through the run): tests under `src/agents/**` pin them, and a parallel PR owns that tree. `subagent-spawn.production-boundary.test.ts` line 457 expects the child dispatch to stop after `commands.ownerAllowFrom` is cleared. Delete that expectation first, then the check and its admission/execution-phase plumbing. `src/agents/worktrees/errors.ts` stays parked for R6z.
- Readers of `AdmittedRunOperatorAuthority.assertCurrent` outside `src/agents/**` and `src/auto-reply/**` (41 production files, listed by LSP references): `gateway/operator-role-policy.ts`, `sessions/session-controller.tool-authority.ts`, `gateway/operator-run-authority.ts`, `gateway/operator-admission.ts`, `security/dangerous-tools.ts`, `gateway/expected-profile.ts`, `gateway/session-sharing-policy.ts`, `gateway/session-sharing-read.ts`, `gateway/server-plugin-in-process-authority.ts`, `plugins/runtime/runtime-llm-isolated.ts`, `gateway/operator-invocation-authority.ts`, `plugins/runtime/runtime-llm-operator-authority.ts`, `gateway/github-publication-requester.ts`, `gateway/session-sharing-authorization-async.ts`, `gateway/session-create-existing-selection.ts`, `gateway/session-permission-authorization.ts`, `gateway/session-create-model-selection.ts`, `gateway/operator-session-run.ts`, `gateway/session-access-authority.ts`, `gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-user-turn.ts`, `gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-admission-phase.ts`, `gateway/agent-turn/agent-run-execution-phase.ts`, `gateway/cron-operator-source.ts`, `gateway/github-publication-actions.ts`, `gateway/session-companion-rpc.ts`, `talk/agent-run-control.ts`, `gateway/talk/client-run-authority.ts`, `gateway/question-session-access.ts`, `plugins/requester-models.ts`, `gateway/server-plugin-in-process-dispatch.ts`, `gateway/session-companion-ask.ts`, `gateway/session-activity-summary-authority.ts`, `gateway/cron-command-source.ts`, `gateway/plugin-command-scheduled-run.ts`, `cron/session-run.ts`, `gateway/cron-stream-sandbox-authority.ts`, `plugins/service-session-work.ts`, `gateway/openai-compatible-agent-run.ts`, `gateway/queued-chat-inputs.ts`, `gateway/session-restart-resume.ts`, `gateway/server-instance-runtime.ts`. `server-methods/**` has its own readers. Admission sites (`operator-admission.ts`, `operator-run-authority.ts` constructors) stay.
- Opaque mixed callbacks kept here (MCP elicitation `current()`, desktop observer `isCurrent`, publication transport token check, OpenClaw ID owner principal, skill-library owner device) mix policy with lifecycle inside their producers. Splitting them needs the producer change in R6z.

## User impact

A started request, mention write, repository operation, Talk run or ingress binding is no longer refused because a role, scope, profile, access revision or config changed. The change applies to the next request. Stop, disconnect, session changes and transport identity changes still end work, and the messages now say what ended and what to do next.

## Evidence

- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test`: pass. oxfmt and oxlint on changed files: clean. Lifetime-check ratchet: 0 counted strings in changed production files, no per-file growth.
- Production vs `main`: 23 files, +75/−107.
- `ocx test` (continue-on-failure) on 140 files: every touched test file, every test file importing a changed source, and every importer of the 12 test-support files that import one. Ours fixed: Talk parity expected-text regex, the remote-ingress cut-less above, and the stale session-facts rows. Base comparison on `8ea0f17162ab`: `server.operator-role-scope-matrix`, `server.sessions-send-resume` and `server.agent.gateway-server-agent-a` timed out at host load ~90 and pass on head and base at lower load (one head scope-matrix case failed on a transient `node_modules` module-not-found, file present after). Final reruns of every red or invalidated file: green.
- CI round 1 (`29148535213c`): OURS = `project-github-identity.factory` expected text (fixed) and `local-request-context.session-tools` (passes after the requester-owner revert). Local review round 1 found `subagent-spawn.production-boundary.test.ts` pins the requester-owner mid-run check under `src/agents/**`: cut less, `agent-run-user-turn.ts` and its two phase files restored to `main`.
- Local ClawSweeper review: round 1 (`29148535213c`) 1 real finding (fixed above); round 2 (`5dd4558144b8`) "patch is correct", no findings.
- One-admission E2E on `5dd4558144b8`: verdict pass. R.running-turn-finishes, Q.queued-input-refused-visibly and S.stop-cancels all pass (`verdict.json`, `results.jsonl` kept in the proof directory).
- CI round 2 (`5dd4558144b8`): OURS = `server.sessions.create.repository-required` `caller` row (deleted, test-only push `4ba022722a64`); not ours: `server.talk-consult-history` (#203507), `local-request-context.session-tools` (red on main run 45238720546). The E2E on `5dd4558144b8` covers `4ba022722a64`: production is identical.
- CI round 3 (`4ba022722a64`): OURS = `server.talk-permission-parity.test-support.ts` regex still matching the old Talk wording (fixed, test-only push `711ba27c5b6f`); not ours: `local-request-context.session-tools` (main runs 45238720546 and 45248844963). Local review clean on `711ba27c5b6f`. Production is unchanged since `5dd4558144b8`, where the E2E passed.

prs.title: feat: add bf16.ai official provider plugin for uncensored open-weight models
prs.body:
Closes #204195

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw users who run autonomous multi-step coding, security-research, browser, and desktop workflows with uncensored open-weight models currently have to configure [bf16.ai](https://bf16.ai) manually as a custom OpenAI-compatible provider, losing one-click onboarding (`--auth-choice bf16-api-key` / `BF16_API_KEY`), curated 1M-context model metadata, provider icons, and automatic live `/v1/models` catalog refresh.

## User Impact

User impact: users can install `@openclaw/bf16-provider`, authenticate once with `openclaw onboard --auth-choice bf16-api-key` (or `BF16_API_KEY`), and immediately run bf16.ai's uncensored open-weight models (defaulting to `bf16/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-uncensored`) with automatic live `/v1/models` discovery, keeping OpenClaw's own local approval and sandbox policies as the safety boundary. Existing users who previously configured `models.providers.bf16` manually keep their authored provider models, agent defaults, fallbacks, and aliases intact on upgrade.

## Why This Change Was Made

bf16.ai serves uncensored open-weight models (refusal behavior edited out of the weights rather than papered over with system prompts) with 1M context windows, vision, deterministic tool calling, smart routers (`bf16/auto*`), and ultra-low false-positive refusal rates over a standard OpenAI-compatible API at `https://api.bf16.ai/v1`.

Following the official external provider plugin pattern (`@openclaw/abliteration-provider` / `extensions/abliteration` + refreshable public `/v1/models` discovery like Venice/Cerebras):

- Adds `extensions/bf16/` (`@openclaw/bf16-provider`, `bundledDist: false`) with starter catalog metadata for all 10 live models/routers and `"discovery": { "bf16": "refreshable" }` + `liveModelDiscovery: { authentication: "none" }` (since `https://api.bf16.ai/v1/models` is a public catalog endpoint, discovery never sends inference credentials and automatically surfaces newly published models without waiting for an OpenClaw release).
- Uses `createProviderConnectionPresetAppliers` for connection-only setup so existing user-authored `models.providers.bf16` definitions, fallbacks, and aliases are preserved.
- Registers the plugin in `scripts/lib/official-external-provider-catalog.json`, `package.json` (`!dist/extensions/bf16/**`), `config/knip.config.ts`, `.github/labeler.yml`, `test/vitest/vitest.extension-misc-paths.mjs`, and `test/plugins/bundled-provider-auth-literal-parity.test-support.ts`.
- Adds opaque 512×512 white-tile `assets/icon.png`, single-path monochrome `assets/activity.svg` and `ui/public/provider-icons/ProviderIcon-bf16.svg`, and attribution entries.
- Adds provider docs (`docs/providers/bf16.md`), navigation/index entries, and generated plugin reference/inventory (`pnpm plugins:inventory:gen`).
- **Config baseline justification (`docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json`)**: `plugin` grew from `5690` to `5714` (+24 entries) strictly from registering the new official external `bf16` provider plugin manifest and auth choice.

*(Maintainer ownership note: happy to maintain this either as an official external package here or as a vendor-owned package on ClawHub if maintainers prefer independent distribution.)*

## Evidence

### 1. Shipped CLI onboarding & REAL live `/v1/models` discovery against `https://api.bf16.ai/v1/models`

Ran built `openclaw.mjs` (`OpenClaw 2026.11.7`) in an isolated temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`:

```text
$ openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --skip-health \
    --mode local --auth-choice bf16-api-key --bf16-api-key "<redacted>"
Updated config: /tmp/openclaw-bf16-e2e-.../state/openclaw.json
# Verified: models.providers.bf16.baseUrl = "https://api.bf16.ai/v1", api = "openai-completions",
# agents.defaults.model.primary = "bf16/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-uncensored"

$ openclaw models list --all --provider bf16 --refresh
Model                                      Input      Ctx         Local Auth  Tags
bf16/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-uncen... text+image 1049k       no    yes   default,configured,alias:DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (Uncensored)
bf16/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-uncen... text+image 1049k       no    yes
bf16/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-exl3-2.5bpw  text+image 524k        no    yes
bf16/zai-org/glm-5.3-flash-uncensored      text+image 1049k       no    yes
bf16/zai-org/glm-5.3-uncensored            text       1049k       no    yes
bf16/moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro-uncensored   text+image 1049k       no    yes
bf16/auto                                  text+image 1049k       no    yes
bf16/auto:fast                             text+image 1049k       no    yes
bf16/auto:coding                           text+image 1049k       no    yes
bf16/auto:reasoning                        text+image 1049k       no    yes
# JSON check (`models list --all --provider bf16 --json`): count=10, 10/10 live ID parity with manifest
```

### 2. Upgrade / data-model compatibility proof via shipped CLI

Pre-seeded a pre-upgrade `openclaw.json` with hand-written `models.providers.bf16` (`zai-org/glm-5.3-uncensored`), `agents.defaults.model.primary = "bf16/zai-org/glm-5.3-uncensored"`, `fallbacks = ["bf16/bf16/auto"]`, and custom alias `"my-glm"`:

```text
$ openclaw config validate
Config valid: /tmp/bf16-p2-.../state/openclaw.json

$ openclaw models list --all --provider bf16 --refresh
Model                                      Input      Ctx         Local Auth  Tags
bf16/zai-org/glm-5.3-uncensored            text       1049k       no    -     default,configured,alias:my-glm

$ openclaw onboard --non-interactive --accept-risk --skip-health \
    --mode local --auth-choice bf16-api-key --bf16-api-key "<redacted>"
Replacement credential saved but inactive. Your connection is unchanged. Test and activate it with:
openclaw models auth activate bf16:setup-... --agent main
# Post-upgrade openclaw.json verified intact:
# - models.providers.bf16.models kept exact custom "zai-org/glm-5.3-uncensored" entry
# - agents.defaults.model.primary stayed "bf16/zai-org/glm-5.3-uncensored"
# - agents.defaults.model.fallbacks stayed ["bf16/bf16/auto"]
# - agents.defaults.models["bf16/zai-org/glm-5.3-uncensored"].alias stayed "my-glm"
```

### 3. Shipped CLI embedded agent turn & isolated Gateway turn + live plugin icon HTTP check

Executed through the built `openclaw.mjs` runtime and a live isolated `openclaw gateway run` process against a local loopback OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions server (`127.0.0.1`, streaming SSE + `reasoning_content` + `usage`; `extensions/bf16/bf16.live.test.ts` is also included and gated behind `BF16_LIVE_TEST=1` + `BF16_API_KEY` for live-key inference):

- **Embedded agent turn (`openclaw agent exec --model bf16/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-uncensored --json` with `OPENCLAW_DEBUG_MODEL_TRANSPORT=1`)**:
  - Transport log confirmed provider routing:
    `[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] start provider=bf16 api=openai-completions model=deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-uncensored method=POST url=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1/chat/completions`

- **Isolated Gateway turn (`openclaw gateway run` + `openclaw agent --agent main --json`)**:

prs.title: fix(update): keep a Gateway's own update running when it first reports ready
prs.body:
Related: #203925

## What Problem This Solves

A Gateway that starts a release update takes the preparation lock under its own PID. On its first maintenance tick after it starts, `announceReady` treats any lock with its own PID as a leftover from an earlier Gateway that reused the PID, so it marks the running update `failed` with reason `interrupted` and releases the lock. The update itself continues and succeeds, but the recorded result says it failed.

Observed on Linux: run `90faf5a6-b3a4-4946-bebb-8f9ff903d6b6` was clicked shortly after a fresh Gateway start. The row was finished as `interrupted` at 20:02:00 while the old Gateway (PID 10561) was still preparing; the new Gateway started at 20:03 and served the target through the migration chain.

## User Impact

Clicking Update soon after a Gateway start no longer reports a working update as failed. A lock left by a dead process, or by an earlier Gateway whose PID a restarted container reused, is still settled as `interrupted`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The lock already records `startedAt`. A lock with this Gateway's PID counts as a leftover only when it was taken before this process started. No new state or check.

## Evidence

- `src/update/gateway-trial.test.ts`: the new `own-live` case (this Gateway's own lock, taken during its lifetime) fails on main (the run is marked `interrupted`) and passes here; the `same-pid` case now uses a lock from before the process started; `dead` and `live` are unchanged. All 10 trial tests pass.
- Real Linux proof: pending in this PR (a click within the first maintenance interval after a Gateway start).

prs.title: feat: let MCP servers use pre-registered OAuth clients
prs.body:
Closes #116052 ## What Problem This Solves Operators cannot currently connect OpenClaw to MCP servers whose OAuth provider requires a pre-registered client instead of dynamic client registration. This blocks providers such as Google OAuth deployments even when the operator already has a client ID and SecretRef-backed client secret. ## User Impact User impact: operators can configure a pre-registered OAuth client for an MCP server, keep its secret out of config, process arguments, logs, authorization URLs, and SQLite state, and use the provider-advertised token authentication method for sign-in and refresh. Existing dynamic registration and client metadata document flows, and state written by v2026.11.6, keep working unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made The implementation follows the [posted proposal](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/116052#issuecomment-7062283377). A maintainer encouraged the implementation on Discord; the proposal's open questions remain open, and reviewers can redirect these choices: - Q3 uses a fixed `access_type`, `prompt`, and `login_hint` authorization-parameter allowlist to keep the initial security surface small. Widening it later is additive. - Q5 defers `identity: "per-requester"` because v1 has one operator-owned SecretRef and client binding. Supporting requester-owned clients later is additive. - Q6 fails closed when a configured redirect differs from the callback the Gateway will use, avoiding provider-dependent fallback behavior. Supporting additional explicit callback shapes later is additive. `oauth.clientId` bypasses dynamic registration and client ID metadata documents. An optional `oauth.clientSecret` accepts only a SecretRef, is resolved by the Gateway runtime snapshot or the stopped-Gateway CLI flow, and is supplied to the MCP SDK for both code exchange and refresh. The persisted client binding deliberately omits `client_secret`; changing the configured client ID makes existing tokens unusable. ### Branch update at `a1edfd5` The branch had fallen behind `main` with conflicts only in the generated config-baseline count and hash files. I merged `main` (`4e2e0383d5fa`) without rewriting history and regenerated both files with the generator instead of hand-merging them. The PR diff is otherwise byte-identical to the reviewed `38c95f2` diff. `src/plugins/management-service.inspect.test.ts` auto-merged: `main` added a separate test there, and this branch's change is intact. `main` has since advanced one more commit (`49795c31df01`, ClawHub release scripts). That commit touches none of this PR's files, and a `git merge-tree` check against it is clean, so I did not merge it. ### Changes in this revision (ClawSweeper review of `de6509de`) - **Client binding reaches status and sign-in discovery (P2).** The status owner (`projectMcpOAuthCredentialsStatus`) now takes the configured client ID: stored tokens issued to another client project `requires-authorization`. Every consumer passes the server's OAuth config: `mcp status`/`doctor`, the owner chat connect bootstrap (`agent-bundle-mcp-operator-connect`), Settings plugin status, and the Gateway sign-in link. Requester and Template callers pass none, because those servers cannot configure a pre-registered client. I chose the status-side check over clearing the row in `clearReplacedMcpOAuth`: the status check also covers rows written before this change, the store key stays unchanged, and the next sign-in already replaces the other client's tokens. The sign-in link's stale-callback guard now skips pre-registered clients, because they never reuse a stored registration. - **One unresolvable client secret no longer aborts the probe (P2).** `probeMcpServers` resolves each secret on its own. A failure becomes that server's diagnostic in the documented `diagnostics` shape. The message names the config path, the reference, and the next step, never the value. That server is left out of the runtime, the other servers are still probed, and the command still exits nonzero. `doctor --probe` and `add/configure --probe` share this path. - The docs describe both behaviors (`docs/cli/mcp/transports.md`). A test-line allocation record covers the 91 lines above the 400-line allowance. Out of scope: client credentials (#84294), a default `offline_access` policy (#160611), credential export, `private_key_jwt` or mTLS client authentication, the `env`-on-URL-server Doctor hint, and the Google Home protected-resource-metadata 404 workaround. ### Remaining owner decisions - **Maintainer contract decision:** ship this shared-client contract (SecretRef-only secret, SDK-selected client authentication, three allowed authorization parameters, exact callback matching)? - **`/allow-security-sensitive-change`** is required before landing. ## Evidence All current evidence below was produced at merge commit `a1edfd57f8c900ca1c7b6d92f731369d355620fc`. Evidence from `38c95f2` and earlier is labelled historical. **Built-distribution CLI proof at `a1edfd5`** (redacted excerpts below). The documented no-declarations runtime profile, `pnpm build:runtime`, ran in a separate bounded systemd unit. It exited 0 after 3m53.6s, with a 4.7 GiB memory peak and a 299.2 MiB swap peak. The build stamp, runtime-postbuild stamp, and `dist/build-info.json` all name `a1edfd57f8c900ca1c7b6d92f731369d355620fc`, and the CLI reports `OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (a1edfd5)`. The behavior run used the shipped launcher (`node /openclaw.mjs`), which imports `dist/entry.js`, not tsx or a source loader. The run used a fresh `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` in a disposable directory. `~/.openclaw`, active Gateway state, and real credentials were not used. A synthetic fixture listening only on loopback served the OAuth authorization server and a bearer-protected MCP server. The authorization server offered a registration endpoint, `client_secret_basic`, and PKCE S256. Its access tokens lasted 3 seconds, which forced refreshes. A `curl -L` of the printed sign-in URL stood in for the browser. This is a real local network server and the shipped CLI path, not a live Dropbox or Google sign-in. No Gateway was running for the disposable state, so this is the documented Gateway-stopped CLI path. 1. **Upgrade from v2026.11.6.** The installed **v2026.11.6** CLI (`OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (06afb10)`) created the config and signed in with dynamic registration, storing client `dcr-client-1` in `mcp_oauth_stores`. The built CLI then opened the same directory through the normal database upgrade. `mcp status` reports `authorized`, and `mcp probe` refreshes with the v2026.11.6 client and lists tools. The stored client registration is unchanged. 2. **Client switch.** `mcp configure docs --oauth-client-id proof-app` and `config set …clientSecret --ref-source env …` keep the same URL and stored row. `mcp status` then reports `requires-authorization`. 3. **Pre-registered sign-in, refresh, and MCP use.** `mcp login docs` sends `client_id=proof-app` without calling `/register`. It keeps PKCE S256 and adds `access_type` and `prompt`. The code exchange and every refresh authenticate with `client_secret_basic`. `mcp probe` initializes and lists tools with a token issued to `proof-app`. The stored row holds only `{client_id, issuer}`. Its parsed JSON has no `client_secret` key, and the synthetic secret appears zero times in the disposable state directory and the raw CLI and fixture logs. 4. **Probe isolation.** A second server, `calendar`, references a missing env SecretRef. `mcp probe --json` still probes `docs`, reports `calendar` in `diagnostics`, and exits 1.
Redacted built-entry CLI excerpts (commit a1edfd57f8c900ca1c7b6d92f731369d355620fc) ```text ===== built distribution version ===== $ node /openclaw.mjs --version OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (a1edfd5) [exit 0] ===== built distribution mcp status --json (v2026.11.6 state) ===== "hasTokens": true, "hasClientInformation": true, ... "state": "authorized", ===== built distribution mcp probe docs --json (v2026.11.6 dynamic client refreshes) ===== "servers": { "docs": { "launch": "[LOOPBACK]/mcp", "tools": 1, ... } }, "tools": [ "docs__whoami" ], "diagnostics": [] [exit 0] ===== mcp_oauth_stores rows (after built distribution reused v2026.11.6 state) ===== {"clientInformation": {"application_type": "native", "client_id": "dcr-client-1", ..., "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none"}, "format_version": 1, "hasTokens": true, ...} ===== built distribution mcp configure docs --oauth-client-id proof-app ===== Updated MCP server "docs" in /openclaw.json. ===== built distribution config set clientSecret SecretRef ===== $ ... config set mcp.servers.docs.oauth.clientSecret --ref-source env --ref-provider default --ref-id PROOF_MCP_CLIENT_SECRET Updated mcp.servers.docs.oauth.clientSecret. Change will apply without restarting the gateway. ===== built distribution mcp status --json (client switched, same URL) ===== "hasTokens": true, "state": "requires-authorization" ===== built mcp login docs ===== $ node /openclaw.mjs mcp login docs Open this URL to authorize "docs": [LOOPBACK]/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=proof-app&code_challenge=&code_challenge_method=S256&redirect_uri=[LOOPBACK]%2Foauth%2Fcallback&state=&scope=docs.read&resource=[LOOPBACK]%2Fmcp&access_type=offline&prompt=consent MCP OAuth credentials saved for "docs". [exit 0] ===== mcp_oauth_stores rows (after pre-registered sign-in) ===== {"clientInformation": {"client_id": "proof-app", "issuer": "[LOOPBACK]"}, "format_version": 1, "hasTokens": true, "keys": ["authorizationId", "clientInformation", "discoveryState", "tokenExpiresAt", "tokens", "tokensAuthorizationServerUrl"], ...} ===== built distribution mcp probe docs --json (pre-registered refresh + MCP use) ===== $ node /openclaw.mjs mcp probe docs --json "servers": { "docs": { "launch": "[LOOPBACK]/mcp", "tools": 1, ... } }, "tools": [ "docs__whoami" ], "diagnostics": [] [exit 0] ===== built distribution mcp probe --json (calendar secret unresolved, docs healthy) ===== "servers": { "docs": { "launch": "[LOOPBACK]/mcp", "tools": 1, ... } }, "tools": [ "docs__whoami" ], "diagnostics": [ { "serverName": "calendar", ..., "message": "MCP server \"calendar\": mcp.servers.calendar.oauth.clientSecret (env:default:PROOF_CALENDAR_CLIENT_SECRET) could not be resolved: Environment variable \"PROOF_CALENDAR_CLIENT_SECRET\" is missing or empty. Make the secret available to this terminal, then run the command again." } ] MCP check failed for "calendar" in /openclaw.json: ... [exit 1] ``` Fixture request log (excerpt, one JSON line per request): ```text {"kind":"register","clientId":"dcr-client-1","redirectUris":["[LOOPBACK]/oauth/callback"]} <- v2026.11.6 only; exactly one register event in the full log {"kind":"token","grant":"refresh_token","clientId":"dcr-client-1","clientAuth":"none","authenticated":true} <- built CLI, v2026.11.6 state {"kind":"mcp","method":"tools/list","bearer":"valid","clientId":"dcr-client-1"} {"kind":"authorize","clientId":"proof-app","redirectUri":"[LOOPBACK]/oauth/callback","codeChallengeMethod":"S256","hasCodeChallenge":true,"extra":{"access_type":"offline","prompt":"consent"},"known":true} {"kind":"token","grant":"authorization_code","clientId":"proof-app","clientAuth":"client_secret_basic","authenticated":true} {"kind":"token","grant":"refresh_token","clientId":"proof-app","clientAuth":"client_secret_basic","authenticated":true} {"kind":"mcp","method":"tools/list","bearer":"valid","clientId":"proof-app"} ``` The SDK printed `SEP-2352: stored OAuth credential has no 'issuer' stamp` once, during the client-switch sign-in. That is expected: the stored binding still belonged to `dcr-client-1`. The built CLI also printed `log file append failed; records dropped` for the disposable state's log file. I left both out of the excerpts, along with timestamps and repeated requests. The same isolated-log-sink warning appeared in the historical `38c95f2` run, and this PR does not change logging code. Because the file logger dropped those records, the secret scan covered CLI stdout/stderr, the fixture log, and the whole state directory, but no Gateway file-log content. The published logs replace loopback endpoints with `[LOOPBACK]`. A residual scan found zero tokens, codes, PKCE values, state values, client-secret values, literal IPs, private hostnames, or user paths. Nineteen independent assertions passed against the raw state and the redacted logs, including checks that the cited events survived redaction. Build and proof identities (SHA-256): ```text f59773629d9546b5c06aca6e97a566861b0ca976d07aa339af98b0331ce1936e openclaw.mjs bb4b71168199fbf0ba892b9280473d9077f5737af1ff6519436732249ec7b161 dist/entry.js 6d9624a4a6e250c6945835c62ea1d48a01105fd3199a6c1467a48ba234455a96 dist/.buildstamp 942bd96e480165f62772b90160d0c75af28a33c3e87a9f762fb918a9b3edeaf4 dist/.runtime-postbuildstamp 5e171e70cfe1e6168bd8834fe86d53426b059cb1a2dca09aa26455f0f01019b2 dist/build-info.json 1a9823e96a3d8cb5311802b17bf00ef6956d4870044da4b13521fc5e7e050fc7 redacted/after.log 58436c1386fc57b27e3e06b47d8b65aec2d00ccb365c86a9f95f4e6797fef72a redacted/fixture.log ```
**Focused tests at `a1edfd5`.** The same 31-file regression list passed on the merge commit: **31 files, 443 tests, 8 shards**, 657.22 s, max RSS 3,921,436 KiB, exit 0. The one extra test compared with the historical 442 is the test `main` added to `management-service.inspect.test.ts`. The test-line ratchet against the current PR base passes: net +491, allowance 400, allocation credit 91. The targeted formatter passed on the 34 applicable changed files, the generated config baseline `--check` passed, and `git diff --check` passed. **Historical red/green (before `38c95f2`).** I wrote the red tests first and ran them against the production files at `de6509de`, with the new tests applied: - The client-switch test failed because status did not check the client. - The probe test failed because the whole probe rejected with the `calendar` secret error. Both pass on this revision. The first broad attempt (`green1`) was not green, and I do not count it as a pass. It ran an earlier version of the mixed-probe test, which wrongly expected the Commander promise to reject after partial-success JSON, and stopped after three shards with 1 failed and 141 passed. The corrected test runs through CLI exit finalization and checks exit 1, the healthy server result, and the failed server diagnostic. The pre-merge `green2` run then passed 31 files and 442 tests, and the historical `38c95f2` merge passed the same 442 tests.
Exact commands and counts ```text # historical red, at de6509de production files + new tests node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/mcp-oauth.test.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.oauth-integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t "configured client changes|one client secret cannot be resolved" 2 failed | 28 skipped (30) # current merged head a1edfd5 node scripts/test-projects.mts src/config/schema.test.ts src/agents/mcp-oauth.test.ts src/agents/mcp-oauth-link.test.ts src/agents/mcp-oauth-provider.preparation.test.ts src/agents/mcp-oauth-provider.read.test.ts src/agents/mcp-oauth-redirect.test.ts src/agents/mcp-oauth-refresh.test.ts src/agents/mcp-oauth-refresh-issuer.test.ts src/agents/mcp-oauth-writes.test.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.oauth-integration.test.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.oauth.test.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.login-loopback.test.ts src/cli/mcp-cli.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.reference-values.integration.test.ts src/secrets/runtime.coverage.test.ts src/secrets/target-registry.docs.test.ts src/secrets/target-registry-data.current-snapshot.test.ts src/secrets/target-registry.path-scope.test.ts src/gateway/server.mcp-auth-login.link.test.ts src/gateway/server.mcp-auth-login.test.ts extensions/migrate-hermes/config.test.ts src/secrets/exec-secret-ref-id-parity.test.ts src/plugins/management-service.inspect.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-manager.requester-connect.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-harness.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-acquisition.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-reload.test.ts src/agents/mcp-oauth-requesters.test.ts src/agents/mcp-oauth-refresh-boundary.test.ts src/config/mcp-repair.integration.test.ts src/plugins/management-uninstall.mcp-oauth.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 unit-fast 1/3, gateway-server 2/41, infra 13/142, runtime-config 2/31, secrets 5/90, agents-core 5/72, plugins 2/27, extensions 1/37 passed 8 Vitest shards in 657.22s; max RSS 3,921,436 KiB node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main -> Test lines OK. prs.title: fix(subagents): preserve yield settlement after child cleanup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A requester can yield after accepted children have been delivered or discarded and cleaned up, then fail with “accepted continuation children could not transfer terminal delivery.” Cleanup removes the registry rows but leaves their in-memory accepted completion receipts outstanding. The completeness guard consequently demands deleted rows as witnesses.

## User Impact

Requesters can yield after finished children are cleaned up and receive the remaining results without a false execution-failure message. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Committed registry removal retires the existing accepted completion receipt before releasing custody. Ordinary spawn registration retains the caller's operational instance for this accounting. A requester task-completion claim remains separate and explicit for watched continuations, preserving #195420: ordinary message waits stay session-bound, and claimed waits still close when their requester task finishes. Yield settlement transfers the surviving cohort and continues to reject genuinely unknown missing children. The sweeper's redundant full-batch witness-retention guard is removed.

This incorporates Ayaan Zaidi's merged #204178: unconsumed child status/results now become parent history rather than delivery failure notices. The earlier notice wording and lifecycle-deduplication changes in this branch have been removed because their producer was deleted on main. The remaining cleanup defect reproduces on that new main. #203176's partial yielded-wake policy is preserved.

No schema, configuration, persistent delivery-state or cache change. Production code is +18/−28, net −10 lines against `cded11f81d55cc6f54a971ed347b7259727de115`. Follow-up to #203198.

## Evidence

- Exact main `cded11f81d55cc6f54a971ed347b7259727de115`, with only the cohort regression applied: both delivered/cleaned and discarded/cleaned mixed reused-session cohorts fail at transfer=false; 42 existing cases pass.
- Nine isolated real-Gateway cases pass after integration, including retained live-requester delivery, cleanup followed by yield, and claimed/unclaimed message waits. Runtime proof uses real sessions, tools, registry, lifecycle and SQLite with a deterministic loopback Responses provider. Cleanup cases supply synthetic terminal metadata then run the actual retention sweeper. A separate real-model run uses the same isolated Gateway flow with external `gpt-4.1-mini` inference: eight HTTP 200 calls, two cleaned children, one cohort wake and one result, no false failure notice. Its exact-main replay reproduces the reported “accepted continuation children could not transfer terminal delivery” error. A task-owned relay keeps credentials out of the hermetic test process; synthetic phase instructions and tool selection control the reproduction, while model responses and tool execution are real. The prior 31-minute requester/full synthetic btrfs proof remains historical evidence for #203198, not a new test of main's replacement policy.
- Fresh full remaining-diff Codex autoreview through P2 is scoped clean. The generated identity allowance shrinks from 6 to 2 after guard removal. All 275 distinct focused/consumer tests pass on the integrated candidate: 9 Gateway, 44 yield, 30 self-hold, 3 history, 1 captured-history, 19 requester settlement, 119 registry/receipt consumers and 50 requester-wake cases. Final `pnpm check:changed` completed without skips: every gate passed except the five independently reproduced main unused exports below. ClawSweeper reviewed final head `8ca03c0e527c1c3d66c9589e183634f705d89431` with zero findings and zero open checklist items.
- Fresh memory-owner A/A/B: 5,000 registry rows, 100 completion custodies, five interleaved rounds, 500 samples per arm/mode, 3,000 verified outcomes. Median wall time A1/A2/B: 0.024708/0.0248125/0.030104 ms; CPU: 0.034/0.034/0.040 ms; sampled allocation: 8,128/8,088/8,176 bytes. Receipt retirement adds about 5.3 microseconds wall, 6 microseconds CPU and 48–88 sampled bytes. No SQL/filesystem work is added; the redundant per-row receipt scan is removed. Notice rendering is no longer part of this patch or measurement.

The latter again reproduces on exact current main with two failures and one pass. #204178 (`cded11f81d55cc6f54a971ed347b7259727de115`) also leaves the exported `appendChildStatusToRequester` and two retired fixture helpers unused, and #203470 (`4a775a078bf0b871f3d9f50bce4942913b511cee`) adds the internally used `ProjectGrant` export. prs.title: fix(ui): keep a reader who reaches the top of a chat at the top
prs.body:
After this PR, a reader who scrolls to the top of a chat (for example, with **Home** in Safari) stays at the top, and older history starts loading. Before, the transcript could fold a held layout correction into the scroll offset and leave the reader about 1.2 to 1.4k px below the top. Older history then waited for a second upward gesture.

Part of #204008.

## Problem

`chat-history-reading-stability.e2e.test.ts` (webkit, 390 px) failed on the last two scheduled runs (45227595368, 45238720546) with `messageCount: 30, prefixCommitted: false`: the older history page was never requested after **Home**. Locally it failed in 2 of 4 runs on `main`. A probe of every scroll write showed this (failing run):

```
scroll 1091 ms  scrollTop 0     (WebKit's smooth Home scroll reaches native zero)
anchor 1243 ms  scrollTop 0 -> 1374  (TranscriptReaderAnchor.settle folds a +1374 px held column shift)
chat.history requests: 0
```

Passing runs had the same fold, but it was smaller (+1173 or +1224 px), so the reader stayed inside `CHAT_HISTORY_PREFETCH_EDGE_PX` (1200) and history loaded. The outcome depended on whether the held shift was under 1200 px.

While WebKit animates a scroll, `TranscriptReaderAnchor` holds the native offset and shows row growth above the reader as a negative column margin (`columnShift`). `settle()` then folds the shift into `scrollTop`. At native zero, the reader had reached the start, but folding a positive shift moved them that far down: the rows hidden by the margin ended up above a reader who had asked for the top. `landSize` in the same class already states the rule: "Native zero is the reader's start; newly measured rows must not move it away". `settle()` did not follow it.

## Solution

When `settle()` folds a positive held shift while native `scrollTop` is at zero (`shift < 0 || offset > 0` still scrolls), it removes the margin and moves the virtual rows, but it does not write the scroll. The reader stays at the top and sees the rows that grew above it. All other folds keep the existing `scrollBy`.

## Evidence

- `chat-history-reading-stability.e2e.test.ts` webkit 390 px: `main` 2 of 4 runs fail (fold +1374); this branch 4 of 4 pass, and every run requests `chat.history`. The whole file passes 4/4, including the "visible messages only move with the reader" frame checks.
- 11 test files that import `chat-transcript-reader-anchor`, `chat-transcript-virtualizer-host` or `chat-transcript-offset-observer`, plus `chat-transcript-scroll-ownership.test.tsx`: 219 passed.

prs.title: improve: start automatic compaction at 85% of the window on every route
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw started automatic compaction at three different points depending on the route. Client and request-boundary compaction started at 80% of the context window. Anthropic server compaction (`compact_20260112`) and OpenAI Responses inline server compaction started at 70%. Sessions on server-compacting routes summarized away history earlier than every other route, for no measured reason.

## User Impact

Every route now starts automatic compaction at the same point: `min(floor(0.85 × window), window − reserve)`.

- Client and request-boundary compaction: 80% → 85% (200k window: 160,000 → 170,000; 1M window: 800,000 → 850,000).
- Anthropic `compact_20260112` default trigger: 70% → 85% (200k: 140,000 → 170,000). The 50,000 API minimum is unchanged.
- OpenAI Responses default `compact_threshold`: 70% → 85% (200k: 140,000 → 170,000). The 1,000 floor, the 80,000 fallback without a known window and the service-tier context cap are unchanged.
- Explicit `anthropicCompactThreshold` and `responsesCompactThreshold` overrides are unchanged.
- Small windows still trigger at `window − reserve` when that is lower.

Sessions keep more verbatim history before the first summary. The request shape is unchanged except the threshold number.

## Why This Change Was Made

One owner now holds the trigger formula: `resolveCompactionThreshold` moved from `packages/agent-core` to `packages/ai/src/utils/compaction-threshold.ts` (agent-core already depends on `@openclaw/ai`; the transports cannot import agent-core). Client, boundary, Anthropic and OpenAI thresholds all call it; the two `0.7` literals are gone. Docs that stated 80%/70% and their worked examples are recomputed.

At equal thresholds, the server trigger and the client request-boundary trigger fire at the same occupancy. Whichever check sees the crossing first compacts: the boundary before sending, or the provider inside the request. Both paths already existed and both are safe; previously the 70% server trigger always fired first. The docs no longer claim Anthropic always compacts first.

## Evidence

- On a 200k window, the client threshold, both request-boundary variants (native checkpoint and warm text), the Anthropic `compact_20260112` trigger and the OpenAI `compact_threshold` all equal 170,000 (`request-boundary-compaction.chatgpt-v2.test.ts`, `anthropic-payload-policy.test.ts` in `src/agents` and `packages/ai`, `extensions/anthropic/stream-wrappers.test.ts`, `extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts`). These tests fail on the base (160,000 / 140,000) and pass on this branch.
- Host/transport parity tests (`memory-flush.test.ts`) keep the host preflight floor equal to the wire threshold at 85%.
- Override, minimum and service-tier cap cases keep their existing expected values.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert restores 80%/70% fully. No stored state, config or published contract changes. Blast radius: every automatic compaction start point moves later by 5–15 points of the window.

prs.title: fix: update plugins after the new Gateway starts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Prepared-release updates ran the candidate's plugin maintenance before restarting the serving Gateway. When the candidate needed a newer shared-state schema, that maintenance correctly refused to migrate under the old Gateway. Core activation could succeed while plugins missed their update.

Closes #204035.

## User Impact

The new version reports success as soon as it is ready. Plugin downloads, installs and runtime reloads run afterward, without holding core readiness or disabling Update. Final plugin results reach the open update details; real failures add an attention warning without failing or rolling back the core update.

Stopping the Gateway during maintenance can leave no final plugin result. Work may be incomplete; this is not an atomic all-old/all-new plugin transaction. Published compatible versions load at the next Gateway start, and `openclaw plugins update --all` finishes the rest.

Removed install records do not hot-unload an already-running plugin. As in the existing metadata-only update path, removal takes effect at the next Gateway start. This repair reloads changed records that still exist.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Remove candidate maintenance from pre-restart preparation for equal/newer versions. Downgrades retain the previous pre-trial maintenance because older targets do not run this post-ready job and do not migrate the schema forward.
- Use one existing Gateway-watcher job after success: ten-minute plugin maintenance, release its lease, reload successful changes through the existing runtime lifecycle, then run advisory Doctor inspections.
- Record only final plugin steps. Preserve explicit capability consent in one optional field in the existing trial record; absence never approves widened capabilities.
- The internal `update plugins --json` result optionally carries existing batch-reload targets, captured from the exact published records under the publishing lease. The parent passes their hashes unchanged; the existing batch check refuses a record changed again before reload.
- Bind both commands to existing watcher cancellation and command-process cleanup, so stop/restart does not wait for their work budgets.

No new scheduler, timer, retry, in-progress marker, plugin staging mechanism, SQL, protocol or config change. Already-current updates keep their existing maintenance/restart behavior. An upgrade candidate that crashes before readiness does not start plugin maintenance.

Accepted edge case: a Git target with the same version string but an older revision gets no plugin maintenance if that revision lacks the post-ready job. Run `openclaw plugins update --all` in that case.

Ownership is unchanged: `update plugins` calls the maintenance owner directly, not the offline `plugins update` command. Its plugin lifecycle lease uses ordinary shared-state access. `gateway-state-owner-record.ts:132–134` permits that access while a Gateway serves; schema mutation has a separate exclusive lease and still refuses a foreign owner. The earlier real three-plugin command completed with the managed Gateway up (`run_f97b488afec5a305855aaaf6ba36ff64`, 46.20 s, schema 41). That is same-schema ownership evidence, not the repaired schema-bump proof. Plugin-owned SQL migrations retain their existing refusals.

## Evidence

- Red on main: the preparation regression exercises real candidate plugin lifecycle/schema admission while the old Gateway owns older state and captures the reported schema-mutation refusal.
- Head `37415ace28cf3b98055b6b707115f9dd9566986d`: AWS focused preparation, trial settlement, late ledger receipt, and plugin-record publication suites passed on production-identical `9507eb380c` (`run_21799856ebb39d5a8f48461e3c9fb78e`), with all 14 changed TypeScript files' lint, export collision guard, and TypeScript/docs format. The ledger-only assertion reduction then passed its suite, lint, format and ratchet on the final head (`run_91d5a424ce7fc02ef11e44244d7da329`). Earlier 15-suite/core-typecheck evidence is retained on `550010466eae` (`run_5f88592c54ec96289086157555acda72`); it is not represented as final-head execution.
- Test budget: removed 12 duplicate report-assertion lines; trial settlement remains the report behavior owner. Both downgrade decisions already share `it.each`. Net +465 test lines retain distinct schema-admission, consent, late-receipt, child-cancellation and exact-install reload contracts; the allocation is 65 above the 400-line allowance. The required local ratchet passed before push.
- Design measurement, not fix proof: three real IRC/Matrix/MS Teams updates took 46.20 seconds in one untraced warm-cache run. The separate counted filesystem performance finding is #204046, not part of this repair.
- **Passing Linux Control UI proof on this head:** official IRC `.6 → .7` run `ea01e4df-6fb3-453b-9484-023036b557d6` (AWS `run_d1d3df4f1e0e6e55fcc36bad4826e01f`) and compiled test-registry plugin `1.0.0 → 1.0.1` run `44217221-4196-436f-bb74-3bfd7a09eb12` (AWS `run_6a29d07f27be45d349bb62bc076f8324`). Both core updates succeeded through the real schema 41→42 migration chain, without generic fallback; `plugins` completed and Doctor inspections followed. [Run details and Settings → Updates screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204127#issuecomment-7113622075).
- Official plugins are converged by the new core's own startup: IRC was already current before post-ready maintenance. The separate honest compiled fixture (two real archives in the kit registry, plain JavaScript, no SQL migration) proves the third-party path: after core success, installed/runtime version changed `1.0.0 → 1.0.1` and Gateway generation changed `2 → 3` with unchanged service PID. All 31 sampled readiness probes during that post-success work were healthy; final plugin work took 7.348 seconds, then Doctor finished with informational findings.
- Full T/next builds retained exact source/build/schema provenance. Canonical `stampFixtureVersion` relabeled their package versions to T=`2026.11.6`, next=`2026.11.7`, preserving distinct build IDs, commits and schemas. Both qualified clicks followed two minutes of serving T plus observed maintenance ticks. Earlier live-own-lock interruption is tracked separately in #204215; QQbot package refusal was a published-package missing-compiled-output finding, not an update regression.
- Sampled outages were 65.678 seconds (official IRC) and 44.306 seconds (compiled fixture). An earlier no-plugin sample was 42.706 seconds but hit #204215; it is not a clean controlled latency comparison. Crash rollback was explicitly removed from this PR's proof scope. All AWS leases were released with `--wait`. Local review is owned by the lead; no further proof variants are pending.
- Linux container, macOS and Windows proof is unproven; this PR does not qualify a stable release.

prs.title: fix: keep older chat history reachable when message rows shift
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

At the top of a long chat, the marker that asks for older messages can move out of view while the browser adjusts the positions of measured rows. On a narrow WebKit viewport, pressing Home could leave only the newest 30 of 190 messages loaded.

## User Impact

Older messages can continue loading at the top without changing how the chat preserves the reader’s position. No configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The history marker belongs just after the history header, not inside the column of message rows. Rendering it there lets the existing reader-position correction move rows without moving the paging boundary. This adds no observer, timeout, retry, or scroll handler.

## Evidence

[Before/after WebKit captures and passive runtime trace](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204216#issuecomment-7113545506). On matched 390 px browser runs, pressing Home left the original at 30 messages; its marker moved to −1,330 px when the scroll position reached zero. On the reviewed build the marker stayed at +44 px, and the browser had loaded all 190 messages by the 213 ms sample, while the rows were still shifting. The original paging and reading assertions failed before and passed after. Both runs used the same synthetic history, with no injected margin change.

- A browser regression measured both the row column and the marker. Before the fix, a −1,600 px correction moved the marker from +44 px to −1,556 px relative to the transcript. After the fix the rows still moved the full 1,600 px, but the marker stayed at +44 px.
- All four unchanged history-reading E2E cases passed on their first local candidate run, including 390 px WebKit loading all 190 messages. This used a production UI build and synthetic history, not a live Gateway. The related hosted failure was intermittent; the geometry regression independently reproduced the defect on demand.
- The three affected test files passed (39 tests); after relocating the regression to the pagination suite, that suite passed all three tests. Typechecks, lint, formatting, and line-count checks passed.
- The broad local changed-file check is **not green**: its pinned production unused-export scan reports `runWindowsGatewayTaskSupervisor` in `src/cli/gateway-cli/task-supervisor.ts`. The exact unmodified parent `a1a7893689ac` and candidate tree `2216d749a1b5` produced the same sole finding. Script and full-tree scans were clean on both. No scanner was skipped or suppressed, and the Windows code is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(ui): retry dictation recordings when transcription returns no text
prs.body:
Related: #195982

## What Problem This Solves

A dictation recording that finishes without usable text cannot be recovered, so the user must record it again. Current main now preserves ordered pending transcripts and reports empty results, but still does not retain failed audio for explicit retry.

## User Impact

User impact: **Retry recording** resends the same captured audio without reopening the microphone. Recovered text stays in the editable draft until the user explicitly sends it. Successful retry clears only that recording’s obsolete error; unrelated errors remain.

Recovery is memory-only in the current tab and draft. Discard, Escape, draft replacement, or starting another capture releases failed recordings. Usable preview text keeps its existing recovery behavior. Pending successful recordings continue in recording order; an explicit retry joins the current pending-transcript tail rather than rearranging text already delivered.

## Why This Change Was Made

The November 22 integration preserves merged #200235: the existing lazy ordered-commit queue, preview placement, Gateway-first microphone admission, and typed capacity refusal remain in charge. Failed audio lives in the existing capture session, and its recovery stays with that queue—not the retired single-pending-session implementation. Discard targets the failed recording without cancelling another recording still transcribing.

Retry creates a fresh normally authorized Gateway transcription session. No persistent audio storage, new provider, permission/configuration change, automatic Send, or microphone fallback is introduced. Listening feedback/lazy loading from #198424 and #198643 remains. prs.title: fix: explain why guarded plugin state calls are blocked
prs.body:
Related: #183790

## What Problem This Solves

When operators investigate “Plugin state authority is unavailable,” an overlapping write and an earlier unknown publication outcome currently produce the same diagnostic. That makes it difficult to tell which fail-closed condition stopped a guarded call.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish those two conditions and correlate the same database within one process without exposing its path, plugin scope, or stored values. Each diagnostic gives a branch-specific wait instruction and explicitly warns not to replay a write whose outcome is uncertain. Guard behavior and recovery are unchanged. This addresses diagnostic question 3 only: it does not establish the cause or delivery outcome of the reported Telegram incident, fix worker OOM, or authorize replay.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing publication owner now supplies branch-specific reasons, a process-local keyed identity reference, and conservative publication-state labels. Native commit remains explicitly unconfirmed. The diagnostic key has its own singleton so an already loaded reconciliation owner keeps its existing shape. No new public schema, retry, or recovery path is introduced.

## Evidence

- Both denial states fail the new owning-boundary/caller diagnostic checks before the repair: 5 intended failures, 12 passing tests.
- Final complete reconciliation and native-binding-facts suites: **18 passed**, including real SQLite worker/foreign-writer and unknown-installation cases, old-guard invalidity, later recovery, and synthetic private-data nondisclosure through the real error formatter. Latest test time: approximately 0.64 s and 4.07 s per file; combined Vitest wrapper wall time 43.41 s. These are local suite timings; the separately verified current-head CI result is listed below.
- Core and owning-test typechecks, targeted lint (three TypeScript files), four-file formatting, and diff checks passed on the updated candidate.
- **Current-head CI passed:** [run 44313746337](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44313746337), attempt 1, succeeded for `58e4185df842595a0034b4837d49cb7bcd221892`. The audit at **2026-11-18 13:52:26.840 UTC** verified 68 terminal CI jobs with no bad jobs and successful current `openclaw/ci-gate`, security-sensitive review, and dependency review. This is the recorded audit result, not a claim about later metadata-triggered checks.
- **Current-head hosted review completed:** [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/201189#issuecomment-6979497221) reviewed `58e4185df842595a0034b4837d49cb7bcd221892` at **2026-11-18 13:46:58.201 UTC**, with **zero findings**, “Before merge: None,” and “Ready for maintainer review.” The prior P2 safe-next-action finding is resolved: pending diagnostics say to wait for publication settlement, unknown-outcome diagnostics say to wait for committed-state confirmation, and both prohibit uncertain-write replay. The owning/caller guidance assertions failed before that correction (5 expected failures, 13 passed) and pass afterward.
- Independent provided-source narrative review covered all four changed files and the complete supplied owner/caller/formatter context. It found one P2: an older reconciliation singleton could lack the new key. The suggested separate-key repair is applied; a focused regression failed with the HMAC key TypeError before the repair and passes afterward. No actionable finding remains unaddressed. The reviewer did not re-review that exact recommended correction.
- Review limitation: the human-approved narrative route replaced interrupted/timed-out canonical AutoReview. It has no helper-enforced isolation or frozen-input machine validation; read-only instructions are not enforced isolation. The exact diff was intact, while paginated full-file evidence normalized separating newlines in long files. Hashes are implementer evidence, not reviewer machine attestation. No Telegram/Codex live proof or full-incident resolution is claimed.
- **Built-Gateway proof is partial; the aggregate two-case run failed.** A disposable source-bound QA runtime on Node 26.12.1 started through the maintained compiled-process/Gateway fixture. An authenticated local synthetic-plugin RPC used the real keyed-store owner, read-availability guard, and error formatter. The controlled pending write was denied with the correct reason, guidance, and non-sensitive reference, then became available after settlement. Privacy and actual-Gateway PID correlation checks passed.
- The attempted unknown-outcome stimulus used a public worker-owned operation adding 34 near-limit values. It committed 35 total rows, but **did not produce an observed unknown denial**; that assertion was not weakened. Therefore the built-runtime unknown case and cross-branch same-process identity correlation remain **unproven**. This is an unqualified stimulus, not evidence that the product’s unknown-outcome handling failed. No further fault framework or uncertain-write replay was introduced. The owned Gateway/client/state cleanup completed; no model, live channel, production Gateway, or user installation was used.

<details>
<summary>Sanitized built-Gateway observation and source binding</summary>

```text
Plugin state authority is unavailable (reason=overlapping-publication-pending; identityRef=7e74914d876cbbdd; settlement=pending; committed=unconfirmed; installation=unconfirmed). Wait for the pending publication to settle before continuing. Do not replay the write while its outcome is uncertain.
```

The tracked workspace matched head `58e4185df842595a0034b4837d49cb7bcd221892` before and after execution. The maintained `qaRuntime` build and repository E2E runner produced build ID `2026.11.4-58e4185df842-2026-11-18T13-34-22.599Z`; built entry SHA-256 was `6d90382770a71fd23199aceaf95857c3928d7adaee0f7647210a34a8cd1cf2bc`. Build-info uses the supported explicit commit input; local freshness stamps retain the managed checkout’s older guest HEAD and `inputsClean=false`, so this is content-bound runtime evidence, not a clean-checkout stamp attestation or released-package proof. The first fixture attempt stopped at config validation; removing a retired fixture-only heartbeat setting and running canonical Doctor on disposable config allowed the actual Gateway run. All stimuli were synthetic diagnostic checks, not reproduction of the Telegram/OOM incident.

</details>

- Simplification: one private error-construction helper serves the four existing denial sites; no parallel authority owner or diagnostic registry was added. Production delta is +33/-4 lines; necessary test growth covers the two diagnostic branches, real caller privacy, and the review-found singleton-shape case.

Prior-head CI limitation: head `e6ede3437d2046df482e44b8c05c62e9fdafa3de` failed [PostgreSQL conformance (1/4)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44308164326/job/134816046689): the interactive crestodian setup test expected exit 130 but received 1 after the Gateway reported “Originally observed agent target requires its captured creating reference.” The [failure classifier](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44308164326/job/134829252061) labels this **unknown**, with scheduled-main evidence unavailable. The determining test, onboarding process adapter, and agent-execution throw site are unchanged from the tested base; that source comparison alone does not prove an inherited failure.
