prs.title: docs: explain the Proactive check's cost on shared local model servers
prs.body:
Related: #202146, #134994, #201282

## What Problem This Solves

People who run OpenClaw on a local model server don't learn from the docs that the default Proactive check sends
the main conversation's whole prompt to their model every 30 minutes, even when it has no way to reach them. On a
server with one or two parallel slots it also pushes the conversation they are using out of the prompt cache.

## User Impact

The local models page now says what the job costs on a local server, how to find it, and how to turn it off, run
it less often, or move it to a smaller model. Docs only; no behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The cost shows up only in server logs. On one install with a local llama.cpp server (two 65,536-token slots), the
default job made 344 requests in 6 days with a median prompt of 51,212 tokens: 62% of all prompt tokens the server
processed. No channel was configured, so every run ended with `Owner delivery unavailable (no-route)` (details in
#202146). The section points to the existing commands. If #201282 lands and removes `skipIfScratchEmpty`, the
second bullet should go.

## Evidence

- Docs checks on this branch: formatting clean (`format:docs:check`), MDX check passed, link audit 0 broken links,
  markdown lint 0 issues, pre-commit hook passed. `docs:spellcheck` fails on main already, in other files; nothing
  in `local-models.md`.
- Every flag used exists on main (`src/cli/cron-cli/register.cron-options.ts`: `--every`, `--model`, `--session`,
  `--light-context`); `automations disable` is documented in `docs/gateway/heartbeat.md`.
- The measurement comes from the llama.cpp server log and the Gateway's automation run history over
  2026-11-13 to 2026-11-19 (2026.11.3 source build; the job definition is unchanged on main).

prs.title: fix(cli): refresh profile shims after Git release conversion
prs.body:
Closes #204146

## What Problem This Solves

After a checkout-to-Git-release conversion, the Gateway can start through the resident launcher while an existing managed profile's terminal CLI still runs the checkout. Terminal integration compares the release link path with the physical package path and skips replacing the old shim.

## User Impact

The profile's terminal command follows the selected release and keeps the profile default and Node runtime arguments. Other profiles keep their selected commands.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the verified service command names the profile's managed Git release launcher, validate the physical package entrypoint and keep the resident launcher in the terminal shim. This reuses the release selector for subsequent updates and retains the existing path for ordinary package and standalone installs. A named file without a release launcher header is left alone.

## Evidence

Verified on Apple silicon macOS with Node 26.12.1. A dedicated named profile, separate temporary config and a loopback Gateway isolated this check from the existing installations. I installed the latest stable build through the real Gateway CLI. From an external terminal I then installed the candidate by invoking the actual Git release launcher from the selected release slot with `gateway install --force`.

| Runtime check | Latest stable checkout | Candidate Git release |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Profile shim `--version` | OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (`712ae03`) | OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (`b05be57`) |
| Resident launcher `--version` | — | OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (`b05be57`) |
| Authenticated `gateway status --deep --require-rpc --json` | RPC available, build `712ae0338512` | RPC available, build `b05be5771daf` |

The rewritten profile shim names the resident launcher. The installer reported that the pre-existing default selection was retained. The temporary LaunchAgent was unloaded and its plist and probe profile were removed from the account. This exercises service installation and reconciliation against real builds. The release artifact and link were staged locally for this check.

- The regression fails on `69ce03a30b`, where the executed shim still returns the original checkout output. It passes on `b05be5771d` with the real updater-generated launcher, filesystem links and fixture package entrypoints. It also verifies the next release selection, profile defaults, Node flags, an unrecognized launcher file and preservation of another profile's shim.
- 25 installer-definition tests, 10 resident launcher tests and 56 terminal/service-layout tests passed. One pre-existing login-zsh test selects the host CLI first and fails with the same output on the untouched base. Two tests were skipped by the runner.
- Core typecheck, targeted lint/format, and `git diff --check` passed. Runtime builds completed for both commits and emitted existing Control UI budget warnings on both. Hosted CI is pending.

An independent review of the local change identified the need to distinguish a generated launcher from a different file at the same path. The final patch checks the existing launcher headers and the regression verifies the unrecognized-file case.

### Native shim and subsequent release selection

On the installed candidate service, the generated profile shim kept the dedicated named profile and the service's actual Node argument `--max-old-space-size=8192`. Its command points to the resident Git release launcher. After the authenticated Gateway check and after unloading the test service, I atomically redirected the actual release link to a second built release and ran the same installed shell shim and launcher. Neither command required a shim rewrite.

```text
shim before link switch=OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (b05be57)
shim after link switch=OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (712ae03)
resident launcher after link switch=OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (712ae03)
```

prs.title: fix(agents): deliver a child's end state as parent history, not a turn obligation
prs.body:
## Problem

When a child agent's result could not reach its parent through a parent turn, OpenClaw parked, retried, expired or "failed" the delivery and showed the user artifacts they could not act on: a System row dumping the child's raw result, a "delivery delayed" row, a red "Couldn't finish this reply" lifecycle error, or a failure notice after a 7-day or 30-minute expiry. The parent model often never saw the child's end state at all.

Reproduced on `main` with a scratch Gateway and a real Claude route: a parent yields on two children, its wake turn for child A fails at the provider, and the chat shows a System row `Child <Child A> (run …) ok ALPHA` (log: `Subagent completion delivery result`).

## Fix

The child's end state is history, not a turn obligation:

- A completion turn that consumed the child's result is delivered, whatever it replied (no visible-reply enforcement).
- When the steer or wake does not consume the result (refused, aborted before admission, delivery path failed, media queue not recovered), the child's status is appended once to the requester transcript as a model-visible, non-displayed entry, then the delivery settles. Content: child label, session, run, status (`completed` + result capped at 8,000 chars per child and 32,000 per entry; a truncated result says to ask the child for the rest with `sessions_send`, `failed: …`, `timed out`, `interrupted by Gateway restart`, `killed`) and, for failures, "If you still need this work, resume it with sessions_send or start a new child with sessions_spawn."
- No retry ladder, suspension, 7-day expiry, 30-minute reservation expiry, backlog warning, failure notice, `failed_notice` channel send, expiry farewell or `child_completion_delivery_failed` lifecycle error. A yielded requester whose continuation never ran ends as an ordinary run.
- Rows that older builds parked as `suspended` still decode and are settled once on the next sweep by appending their status (no wake).
- Kept: consumed-input dedupe (no steer + append double context), cron continuation caller, depth≥1 wake skip, `collect`/`expectsCompletionMessage !== true` exclusions, the message-tool-only text fallback, and cleanup's storage write retry (which now also retries a failed append).

Mid-turn: if the status lands between a tool call and its result, the existing replay pairing repair moves it after the result, so provider role order stays valid (covered by the new test).

Accepted edge case: the transcript report owner dedupes against the latest status entry only. If a child's status append commits, its registry write then fails, and another child's status appends before the retry, the retry repeats the first entry. It is a repeated history line, never a lost result; a per-child receipt would need a new transcript identity mechanism.

## User impact

The parent decides whether to tell the user, resume the child or start a new one. The user sees the parent's reply and the child card; no System dumps, delayed rows or delivery error badges.

## Evidence

Scratch Gateway from source on a real Claude route, before (`main`) and after (this branch):

- Wake fails at the provider while the parent is yielded on two children (parent model switched to an unknown model, then restored before the second child finishes). Before: a System row dumping `Child … ok ALPHA`, log `Subagent completion delivery result`. After: no System row and zero `Subagent completion delivery`/`delivery discarded` log lines; the parent's next wake answers `Child A: ALPHA — Child B: BRAVO`. The red "Couldn't finish this reply" in both is the parent's own provider failure (the injected fault), not a child row.
- Child errors (spawned with an unknown model): the parent wakes, sees `failed: unknown provider …`, respawns without the override and reports `PONG`.
- Codex reference (`spawn_agent` with an unknown model): the parent sees the error and respawns; no user-visible delivery rows.

Before:
![Before: System row dumps the child result](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c0b890a4-a96d-42d2-9db3-36e78a6beb37)

After:
![After: no System row](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05a2dd6e-368e-4d7e-b4cc-3fc18793de08)

Tests: new `subagent-child-status-history.test.ts` proves, through the real transcript append and model-context read, that the status entry is model-visible exactly once for an idle parent, survives compaction, and keeps tool call/result adjacent at the provider boundary when it lands mid-turn. Existing suites were updated: tests that asserted notices, suspension, expiry, retry ladders or permanent/ambiguous holds were deleted; ownership, consumption, rollback and write-retry coverage stays.

## Size

Production code (excluding tests and docs): `src/` +264 / −980 (net −716); with the bench/perf scripts that exercised the removed paths, +266 / −1,439. Tests: +539 / −3,166. Docs: about +50 / −100.

Not in this PR (follow-up): removing the `permanent_failure`/`ambiguous`/`intentional_non_delivery` disposition values and the announce error classifier. Generated-media completion delivery still consumes them, so they need their own cut.

## Merge danger

Two-way door for code; no schema change (delivery state lives in `payload_json`). Settled legacy `suspended` rows become `delivered` and are not restored by a revert. Blast radius: subagent completion delivery and requester wake settlement.

prs.title: ci(android): cache Gradle dependencies per lane and version catalog
prs.body:
After this PR, each Android CI lane restores the Gradle dependencies it resolved on its last main run. Lanes no longer fetch the Kotlin compose plugin or JUnit Platform from Maven Central on every run, so a Central HTTP 429 cannot fail them.

## Problem

Scheduled run 45216550182 failed `android-test-wear` with:

```
> Could not download org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.compose.gradle.plugin-2.4.21.jar
   > Could not HEAD 'https://repo.maven.apache.org/maven2/org/jetbrains/kotlin/plugin/compose/org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.compose.gradle.plugin/2.4.21/...jar'.
      > Received status code 429 from server: Too Many Requests
```

The same class hit `android-access-native (16384)` and `android-ktlint` today.

The Android lanes used `gradle/actions/setup-gradle` with `cache-provider: basic`. That provider delegates to `setup-java`'s Gradle cache:

1. **One shared key for every lane.** Every lane restored the same entry: `setup-java-Linux-x64-gradle-077f1986…` (1.3 GB, created 2026-11-18).
2. **The key misses the Android version catalog.** `setup-java` hashes root-relative patterns (`gradle/*.versions.toml`), which do not match `apps/android/gradle/libs.versions.toml`. A catalog change (Kotlin `2.4.21`) does not change the key.
3. **An exact hit never saves.** Each lane logged `Basic caching restored entry with key setup-java-…. Save was skipped.` The lane that first saved the entry fixed its contents. Every other lane fetched its missing artifacts from Central on every run, forever: `android-test-wear` the compose plugin jars, and both `android-access-native` rows 14 Central downloads each (JUnit Platform 1.13.3, Kotlin stdlib).
4. **`android-access-native` was restore-only, even on main**, so it could never save its own artifacts.

## Solution

`setup-android-toolchain` owns the Gradle dependency cache directly:

- `setup-gradle` keeps running with `cache-disabled: true`.
- `actions/cache` (read-write) or `actions/cache/restore` (restore) caches only what Gradle fetches over the network: `~/.gradle/caches/modules-2` and `~/.gradle/wrapper/dists`. The key is `<os>-<arch>-gradle-deps-v1-<lane>-hash(gradle-wrapper.properties, libs.versions.toml, apps/android/**/*.gradle.kts, gradle.properties)`.
- **Per-lane key** (new input `gradle-cache-key`): the `android` matrix passes `matrix.task`, and `android-access-native` passes `access-native`. Each lane saves exactly what it resolves.
- **Restore keys:** this lane's previous entry first, then any lane's. A new or changed lane therefore starts from another lane's set instead of an empty cache.
- `android-access-native` gets `gradle-cache-mode` read-write on main (same `cache_write_allowed` rule as the `android` job). Its Android SDK cache stays restore-only.
- A catalog or wrapper change now makes a new key. The lane restores its previous set, fetches only what changed and saves the new entry. Gradle's own cache cleanup removes artifacts unused for 30 days.

No retries, mirrors or credentials. `ci.yml`: 478,480 → 478,640 bytes.

**Storage tradeoff:** the measured entries are 539 to 873 MB each (`access-native` 539, `test-play` 719, `test-third-party` 720, `ktlint` 873). Five Linux lanes total about 3.5 GB, replacing one 1.3 GB `setup-java` entry, which expires after 7 days without use.

## Evidence

- `test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts`: the Android toolchain guards now pin `cache-disabled: true` and require the key to include the version catalog, the wrapper properties and the build scripts. They also check restore and save gating for off, restore and read-write modes, and for the store-release `gradle-cache-mode: restore`. `android-access-workflow.test.ts` passes. 261 tests passed.
- `actionlint` passes on `ci.yml`.
- **Cache-hit proof** (PR-scoped warm and restore; the temporary write commit d52301f8 is reverted in 567056ce, so the final diff has no PR writes):
  - Warm run 45247973090 saved `Linux-X64-gradle-deps-v1-{test-play,test-third-party,ktlint,access-native}-e054d43e…`. `android-test-wear` started from the `test-play` entry and hit a Central 429 while fetching its own additions, so it saved nothing. This is the one-time first-fill risk; it goes away once each lane has an entry.
  - Restore run 45252292885 (final config, restore-only):
    ```
    android-test-play:        Cache restored from key: Linux-X64-gradle-deps-v1-test-play-e054d43e831e7cb4ad1123229fe14f11bf4f75032927207d62f6f2b0bea1d420
    android-test-third-party: Cache restored from key: Linux-X64-gradle-deps-v1-test-third-party-e054d43e…
    android-ktlint:           Cache restored from key: Linux-X64-gradle-deps-v1-ktlint-e054d43e…
    android-test-wear:        Cache restored from key: Linux-X64-gradle-deps-v1-ktlint-e054d43e…   (restore-key fallback)
    android-access-native ×2: Cache restored from key: Linux-X64-gradle-deps-v1-access-native-e054d43e…
    ```
    All six jobs passed with zero `Downloading https://repo.maven.apache.org` lines and zero 429s. Before, each `android-access-native` row made 14 Central downloads on main (scheduled run 45216550182), and `android-test-wear` fetched the compose plugin from Central every run.
- **Main first fill:** a lane saves only when its job succeeds. A lane that fails while filling saves nothing, which avoids freezing a partial set under the final key (the original bug), and fills on its next successful run.

prs.title: fix: avoid rereading unchanged sandbox files on reuse
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The first reuse of a sandbox workspace cloned from a prepared template reads every unchanged source file again. On the 62,006-file synthetic workspace this adds roughly five seconds to preparation, even though the template producer already established the file contents.

## User Impact

Sessions can reuse the template-derived workspace without that redundant content read. Both live metadata walks, external-edit detection, recent-write safety, and recovery remain. Initial observation of the live canonical workspace is unchanged. No configuration, schema, migration, or operator action is added.

The measured tradeoffs below have separate performance-owner acceptance for this PR, recorded verbatim below.

## Why This Change Was Made

The template manifest producer already visits the immutable files. It now carries their existing fingerprint format through the existing 64 MiB byte-bounded manifest LRU and the existing baseline publication. Btrfs preserves inode and ctime during the native clone; the publication worker rebinds the clone device and the prepared-directory tree root. Other clone backends retain their current behavior. There is no new cache, persistence format, scan shortcut, or retention policy.

Production delta: +84 lines across the existing producer, transport, codec, and publication owners. The growth carries prepared facts across those boundaries; it removes the repeated full-content read rather than creating a second scan owner.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: two baseline A/A controls and five serial counterbalanced pairs on the same native Btrfs rig, using fresh outputs and the same frozen harness. Require identical accepted bytes/types/symlinks/deletions, two live metadata probes, 62,006→0 first-reuse content hashes, and at least 5% lower first-reuse latency. Report cold preparation, every later phase, CPU, allocation and tails. No adverse metric is implicitly accepted.

All twelve runs completed with identical final contents. Baseline first reuse reads 1,142,784,919 bytes; candidate reads zero. A/A first-reuse controls: 4,880.94 / 4,408.98 ms. Five-pair medians:

| Phase | Wall ms baseline → candidate | Main CPU ms | Process CPU ms | Main allocation MiB |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| first | 19,988.58 → 19,939.82 | 1,022.08 → 1,044.90 | 22,095.33 → 22,759.91 | 402.46 → 414.45 |
| unchanged-1 | 4,887.90 → 1,144.19 | 60.81 → 48.32 | 7,015.70 → 1,244.54 | 11.50 → 11.18 |
| unchanged-2 | 845.14 → 988.43 | 42.52 → 49.12 | 925.20 → 1,005.98 | 7.43 → 7.87 |
| guest-export | 3,099.93 → 3,094.12 | 167.29 → 166.25 | 3,562.77 → 3,502.03 | 35.97 → 32.02 |
| host-import | 2,617.42 → 2,769.27 | 211.05 → 225.29 | 2,661.31 → 2,800.58 | 25.59 → 21.07 |
| post-import-reuse | 987.04 → 1,104.78 | 47.56 → 50.10 | 1,181.45 → 1,264.35 | 8.19 → 9.38 |
| post-import-steady | 914.20 → 1,020.66 | 51.06 → 67.35 | 1,089.20 → 1,204.95 | 5.93 → 6.23 |
| sum | 33,139.36 → 30,508.24 | 1,675.93 → 1,689.22 | 38,707.70 → 34,217.13 | 488.56 → 496.70 |

First-reuse median improves 76.6%, process CPU 82.3%, and matched-worker allocation 1,984.0→868.5 MiB. The seven-phase sum improves 7.9% in wall time and 11.6% in process CPU; matched-worker allocation falls 7,542,306,960→6,399,456,144 bytes. Worker deltas exclude newly started/unavailable workers; cold worker allocation is incomplete, not zero. Process CPU excludes native child processes. Main allocation is measured separately.

**Adverse metrics:** total main CPU +0.8%, main allocation +1.7%; cold preparation process CPU +3.0% and main allocation +3.0%. Second unchanged reuse wall +17.0%, host import +5.8%, post-import reuse +11.9%, post-import steady +11.6%. Post-import steady main CPU rises 51.1→67.4 ms (+31.9%). The separately sampled profile pass does not reproduce those later-reuse slowdowns; it does not replace the timing rows or establish acceptance.

First-reuse min–max: 4,608.85–6,375.73 ms → 850.28–1,209.50 ms. With five samples, maximum is nearest-rank p95. Whole-sequence maximum: 36,652.97→31,856.25 ms.

<details><summary>Every phase maximum (nearest-rank p95, five samples)</summary>

| Phase | Wall ms | Main CPU ms | Process CPU ms | Main allocation MiB |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| first | 21,256.56 → 21,112.08 | 1,283.27 → 1,171.57 | 23,110.85 → 24,417.93 | 411.49 → 417.20 |
| unchanged-1 | 6,375.73 → 1,209.50 | 74.20 → 50.90 | 8,871.66 → 1,328.29 | 13.46 → 14.18 |
| unchanged-2 | 909.73 → 1,039.91 | 47.19 → 50.86 | 974.62 → 1,154.42 | 8.78 → 10.76 |
| guest-export | 3,342.44 → 3,592.18 | 234.41 → 182.32 | 4,197.01 → 4,140.92 | 36.28 → 35.57 |

</details>

The separate CPU/heap profiles attribute baseline first-reuse work to file open/read/close and abort bookkeeping. Profiled Git-worker CPU falls 4,995.5→828.3 ms. Both metadata walks remain. Main profiles are dominated by waits, existing spawn/GC, and profiler controls. Timing and profile samples are not pooled.

Focused producer/codec tests and the 118 consumer cases pass (two existing consumer skips); core, core-test and script typechecks, lint, format, database guards pass. Isolated Codex P0–P2 review is clean. Both frozen compiled runtime builds pass. The compiled Gateway completed three real `openai/gpt-4.1-mini` calls per revision with successful terminal events through ordinary WebSocket `sessions.create` / `chat.send`, preserving exact HEAD, clean index, source and installed dependencies. Its history-wide sentinel check also matched the input prompt, so that assertion does not establish exact assistant reply text; the timing and filesystem assertions are independent. The first reuse is the second send in this reproduction: startup **5,342→1,361 ms**, `reuse.reconcile` **4,841→944 ms**, model completion **7,451→4,663 ms**. The initial send still pays the separate canonical observation: startup 10,041→9,946 ms, initial checkpoint 4,015→4,132 ms. Third-send startup 1,129→1,196 ms and reuse 742→794 ms are disclosed unaffected variation, not claimed gains. This PR does not claim to fix the initial canonical scan.

`pnpm check:changed` passed all selected gates except two dead exports in untouched hook owners. A clean detached checkout of the exact parent c6a27e6a3484ad923ff77ced84d76a0ece87cac8, with its own frozen install, reproduces the identical findings under `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mts`:

- `GatewayStartupHookContext` in `src/hooks/internal-hook-types.ts`: introduced at this owner by #203017, commit 25b89de32d511d313809bf623a81f39d97cdf57d.
- `PluginHookExecRequestOwner` re-export in `src/plugins/hook-types.ts`: introduced by #201503, commit d541d8c9ea1ca9039a452417b4f261b19ede86fc.

These are confirmed main regressions recorded for repair, not ignored noise. No skip, allowlist or unrelated fix is included. Exact-head CI and the final ClawSweeper checklist remain landing gates.

<details><summary>Rerun the native workload</summary>

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/local-workspace-checkpoint-measure.ts \
  --freeze-source /owned-proof/base --revision c6a27e6a3484ad923ff77ced84d76a0ece87cac8 --fingerprint-import
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/local-workspace-checkpoint-measure.ts \
  --freeze-source /owned-proof/candidate --fingerprint-import
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/local-workspace-checkpoint-measure.ts \
  --mode preparation --serial-turns --burst 1 --requests 2 \
  --files 62000 --file-bytes 18432 --fixture-source /owned-btrfs/clean-git-export \
  --acceleration --sandbox-backend podman --sandbox-image SYNTHETIC_IMAGE \
  --fingerprint-import --output /owned-btrfs/fresh-arm --report report.json
```

Use the same qualified compiled filesystem worker in both arms when selecting `--filesystem-worker`; retain the worker source identity. The 10,001 session rows and 62,006-file/1.14 GB workspace are synthetic. The rig also retains a 35 GiB synthetic storage allocation, not a copied production agent DB. Full content validation follows measured phases. No production access was used.

</details>


## Performance-owner decision (verbatim)

Performance-owner decisions by the Team perf-loop lead (an agent acting under Peter's standing unattended instruction), NOT Peter.

**#203112: ACCEPTED.** First reuse reconcile goes 4.89→1.14 s and 62,006 redundant hashes are removed. Production saw reuse_reconcile at 5.5–9.2 s today. The +84 production LOC is justified by carrying prepared fingerprints forward, which is a "record the fact once" ownership improvement. Land after #202960, same gates.


## Resumed landing on current main (2026-11-23)

The interrupted November 21 run did not merge either accepted PR. This branch is now rebased onto `e2973f933f10364471f8d8e470d3c4a7c3d6be96` at `02854cb379396724ba8c379d4816317339b2562d`. The rebase is patch-identical by range-diff; the existing clean Codex review and measured-head performance evidence are retained. Main now requires fs-safe 0.28.2, and the task-local frozen install is updated accordingly. The refreshed affected suites pass 178 tests with two existing filesystem-qualification skips. The complete changed-file check finished with only the attributed main regression below; new exact-head CI and ClawSweeper zero open items remain required. No earlier CI result is substituted for this head. The verbatim performance-owner decision above remains unchanged. No Team access.


### Resumed local-check main regression

Both resumed branches and their exact main parent `e2973f933f10364471f8d8e470d3c4a7c3d6be96` fail the production unused-export gate on `src/cli/gateway-cli/task-supervisor.ts: runWindowsGatewayTaskSupervisor`. #204094 introduced this main regression by moving its production caller into the same module while retaining the export. The isolated exact-parent reproduction uses the frozen current lockfile and `pnpm deadcode:exports`; the initial misspelled script invocation ran no scan and is excluded. Every other full changed-file gate passes. This failure is retained and attributed, not ignored, skipped or fixed incidentally in this PR. Hosted CI must be qualified separately.


### Exact-head inherited CI qualification

Scoped lane 2699 landing authority permits a pinned-head admin merge only for proven inherited failures. CI 45249294371 attempt 1 has two root failures. #203271 (265577c4c159bd13057f5e66ece64a7246aeff9e) added a no-model refusal while the three destination-authority fixtures omit a model; unchanged candidate and exact-main-parent E2E runs reproduce those errors. #203126 (ae8155cf5f5434132b578504716a60c62c3de4e6) added a pending-baseline empty return before removed-worktree validation. The original incognito test passed on this candidate and in five local parent executions, so none is claimed as a failing replay. A bounded scheduling probe on the exact main production tree issues the same sessions.diff RPC immediately after removal, before chat can settle the pending baseline, and reproduces the identical empty result; removing only that five-line #203126 branch makes the same probe pass. The diagnostic edits were removed and the parent is clean. Both are main regressions, not noise.

The actual tested merge `f379c909b1a0ddf2088a651bb977986ebd16a851` has ordered parents `e2973f933f10364471f8d8e470d3c4a7c3d6be96` and `02854cb379396724ba8c379d4816317339b2562d`. The failure owners and original tests are unchanged in that merge. All other selected CI jobs, including `security-fast`, pass. The native inherited-failure exception preserves the failed result; CI is not relabeled green. The pending-window probe only adds the same RPC immediately after removal; it does not change production state or create a new baseline claim. Its separate causal check removes just #203126's five-line branch. These are newly observed main regressions requiring their owners' follow-up.

prs.title: fix: notify script webhooks when a Gateway restart interrupts a run
prs.body:
Closes #204194

## What Problem This Solves

When a Gateway restart interrupts a script automation, its run history records an error but its configured webhook receives nothing. Integrations waiting for the usual finished event cannot tell that the run stopped.

## User Impact

Script jobs with webhook delivery now send the usual `finished` / `error` POST by default, explaining that the Gateway restarted during the run and the script was not rerun. The run remains failed and the script stays stopped. No configuration change is required.

The notice is bounded to five seconds during graceful shutdown. It does not survive a hard kill, and an unavailable receiver can still prevent delivery. There is no durable resend queue. Operator cancellation remains silent; a webhook already in progress is not sent again.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scheduler retains the interrupted run's existing delivery authority long enough to send its terminal notice through the normal webhook transport, then persists the delivery outcome. Payload execution remains aborted. Existing destination, outbound-policy, cancellation, and run-owner checks remain in place.

The repository's pr-simplify pass retained this single-owner change: no new schema, queue, manager, or opt-in. Against main, the production delta is +55/-3 lines, tests +86/-4, and documentation +2/-0. This is a product fix, not a workaround.

## Evidence

The comparison below is unmodified main `e2973f933f10364471f8d8e470d3c4a7c3d6be96` versus head `ee88f6024b507add320cffe4b520047e45507fea` (the verified four-file diff on that base).

Detached, logged disposable Linux Gateways ran actual script jobs and delivered to a real local HTTP receiver. prs.title: feat: manage projects and who they are shared with from the Control UI
prs.body:
Builds on #203470 (role project grants), merged as `4a775a07`. This branch is now rebased directly onto `main`.

## What Problem This Solves

Admins have no place in the Control UI to manage projects. Registering one is hidden inside New Session's folder browser, renaming isn't possible, and removing one needs the CLI. People with restricted roles who open the project picker see a folder-browse write-access error followed by "No folders match your search.", which reads like there are no projects rather than "nothing has been shared with you".

## User Impact

User impact: admins get a **Projects** tab in the Sessions hub, between Sessions and Worktrees. There they can see every project, register one (browse folders on the Gateway or clone from GitHub), rename or remove it, and choose which roles it is shared with. People with restricted roles see "No projects are shared with your role. Ask an admin to share one." instead of a misleading empty folder list, and no longer see a Browse folders control they can't use.

Writers see the tab read-only. Share switches are disabled when the Gateway config is read-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The share switches edit the per-role `projects` list added in #203470, through the same config write path the settings pages use (with base-hash conflict handling). Removing a role's last share deletes the field, which returns the role to its previous behavior. The switches present explicit shares only. Roles with write access are shown as locked on, roles that can't start sessions as locked off, and the dialog notes that restricted roles can also use public GitHub repositories. Registering reuses the existing folder browser and `projects.register` / `projects.add`, and renaming uses the new `projects.rename`.

`projects` is added to the Control UI's reserved route segments so `/projects` can't collide with a session share URL.

## Evidence

**Real Gateway:** [proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203472#issuecomment-7108085087). A full Gateway and the real Control UI, with an admin and a restricted guest, both signed in as real identities. The admin registers a folder, renames it, shares it with the guest role (the config gains `projects: ["handbook"]`) and the guest's picker lists it. After unsharing, the field is removed, the picker drops the project, and `sessions.create` for the guest returns `unknown project id`.

**Screenshots** below compare `main` `0828443372be` (Before) with this branch `3705874707ed` (After). They use Control UI E2E against a mocked Gateway at 1280×800, light theme, with the same fixtures on both sides. The fixtures are a restricted connection with only `operator.sessions.write`, an empty `projects.list`, and `fs.listDir` returning the missing-scope error. The Projects shots use synthetic projects (`docs`, `main`, `site`) and roles (`admin`, `contractor`, `operator`, `viewer`).

**After**

![After: the picker says no projects are shared with their role and hides Browse folders](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5844abdf-9dcb-42cc-a257-bedf775d95ae)

### Clean comparison: Sessions hub

**Before**

![Before: the Sessions hub has only Sessions and Worktrees tabs](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7be3325a-bd05-4ef9-9a2a-1c07bde009cc)

**After**

![Before, annotated: the write-access error and misleading empty-list text are outlined](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/92a52369-c2e0-4c84-802f-f2b09a202116)

**Before**

![Before, annotated: only Sessions and Worktrees, no place to manage projects](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/36840b23-7a24-4686-858f-83671555f2cc)

prs.title: feat: let admins share specific projects with restricted roles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a multi-user Gateway, people with restricted roles (for example `guest` or `collaborator`) can only see agent workspaces and projects whose origin is a public GitHub repository. An admin has no way to share a specific private repository with them short of granting `operator.write`, which also unlocks folder browsing, arbitrary working directories and cloning by URL. In practice, a collaborator opening New Session sees no projects at all.

## User Impact

User impact: admins can share chosen registered projects with a named role by adding `projects` to its definition (`"*"` for every registered project, or a list of project IDs). People in that role then see and can start sessions in those projects. Roles without the field behave exactly as before. Sharing or unsharing takes effect on the next request without disconnecting anyone or stopping their runs.

Admins can also rename a registered project with the new `projects.rename` method (admin only).

## Why This Change Was Made

Project access is decided in one place (`project-access.ts`), and roles already carry similar allow lists (`agents`, `workerProfiles`). This adds a matching `projects` list and passes the caller's current grant to every project-access check: project listing, checkout options, project skills, session creation, subagent spawns, inherited worktrees, GitHub publication and PR workspace prep, and project icons.

- **Additive and backward compatible:** a grant is added on top of the existing public-GitHub rule and never widens anything else (folders, `cwd`, cloning by URL, remote search). Hidden projects still look like unknown IDs.
- **Read live, not snapshotted:** grants are not part of the role-policy change that reconnects clients. They are read from current config for the caller's current profile, including runs that were admitted earlier, so revoking a grant denies the next use. A profile that has since been merged into another profile does not inherit that profile's grants.
- **Isolation:** when someone can use a project only because of a grant, their sessions and spawns always get a new worktree, even if the client asked for none.

Known gap, deliberately unchanged for backward compatibility: a restricted caller can still open a public-GitHub project as a direct checkout without a worktree, as on `main` today.

This is the core half of a two-PR stack; the Control UI Projects tab that edits these grants follows on top of this branch.

## Evidence

- New tests cover an unset grant (old behavior), `"*"`, a listed private project, an unlisted private project staying hidden, full access being unchanged, a forced worktree for grant-only access (and none for public access), and `projects.rename` (authorization, validation, kept ID).
- Real `sessions.create`, `projects.list` and `checkoutOptions` integration tests share and unshare a private project. They show revocation denying it again, a retained restricted run following grant edits without a restart, and a merged profile not picking up another profile's grant.
- A reload test checks that a grant-only config edit closes no sockets, aborts no runs and triggers no recovery restart, for both write-scoped and restricted roles.
- Independent reviews found a stale-grant issue with retained runs and a profile-merge widening; both were fixed with regression tests and re-reviewed clean.
- **Real Gateway, upgrade and fresh install** ([proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203470#issuecomment-7106839509)): stable 2026.11.7 state upgrades in place and behaves identically for a role without `projects`. Sharing a private project lists it and opens it in a managed worktree, revoking it denies the next request, rename survives a restart, and a fresh install works.
- **Inherited test fix carried here:** #203488 (`6ff7a062e54e`) stopped re-checking requester authority after a request is admitted, but left four stale mid-request rows in `server.sessions.create.projects.test.ts`. That test fails identically on `main`, and this PR's diff makes CI select it. Commit `6b490a1d` removes those rows the same way #203488 handled its other tests, and keeps the parent-source-change row. Bisect: passes at `e0c7c74ae20d`, fails at `6ff7a062e54e`.
- **Inherited failures from `main`, not caused by this PR:** CI tests this branch merged with current `main`, and this diff makes it select these files. Each fails identically on `main` `515a93c6725b` without our commits, and the first three pass on this branch without #204155:
  - `operator-run-authority.worker.test.ts` (`readCurrentRoleFacts` no longer throws), `ui-command.test.ts` ("Alice's access changed"), and `local-request-context.session-tools.test.ts` (revocation now returns a tool error): stale expectations after #204155 dropped mid-run authority re-reads.
  - `users-personal-file.test.ts` (3 rows): fails on `412df9062d6c` too and is already listed as failing on `main` in #204093.
  - `session-run.session-model-strictness.integration.test.ts` (scheduled preflight compaction): fails on `main` alone.
- Test lines: +455 net against the 400 allowance. The 55-line allocation covers authorization regressions for a permission boundary (retained-run revocation and profile-merge fencing).

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:src` (22 shards): pass
- oxlint on changed files, line-cap ratchet, protocol `since` check, `format:docs:check`: pass
- Rebased onto `main` `1601f86def0c`. `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base origin/main` (12/12), `protocol:check`, `gateway:validators:check`: pass
- Targeted batch (19 files): gateway 276/276, gateway-client 5/5, infra 14/14, runtime-config 64/64, spawn production-boundary 139/139
- Regenerated: gateway validators, protocol, config docs baseline

</details>

prs.title: fix: start sessions from ready templates during background refreshes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A first send at an already accepted repository commit can wait behind a background template refresh for a newer commit, even though its own template is ready. The same cache-wide wait affects managed checkout materialization and sandbox projection preparation.

## User Impact

Startup uses the ready generation for the session's accepted base while a different generation builds. HEAD, index, source files and prepared dependencies stay on that accepted commit. Requests that need an unavailable generation still join or build it normally.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preparation sharing now includes the requested content and backend. The template owner validates an idle exact generation without waiting for a different commit's build lease, then atomically acquires reader custody for the validated generation ID. Managed validation remains read-only. Existing publication, uncertain-process custody and retention owners remain responsible; no new persistence, schema, product configuration or cache.

Scope directed by the Team perf-loop lead (an agent acting under Peter's standing unattended instruction), not Peter. This is the startup-wait follow-up to #202803. Projection reconciliation and pre-attempt storage phase accounting are separate follow-ups; MCP timeout investigation belongs to another owner.

## Evidence

Current source head: `a852ab9f87f8f9f813457d1d33a90db0dbc48874`; performance campaign head: `d9b466b067c8904015041e814de59fb90059a751`; baseline: `ab054758bb2a6eac5c4caab6722437e0da777d12`. Focused owner suites: 31 tests pass. The real-Git regression is red on baseline for both consumers: managed startup falls back to ordinary Git and fails the one-private-clone assertion; sandbox startup waits until timeout. Candidate startup completes while the build gate is held, with exact A HEAD, index, source and dependencies. Existing cancellation, concurrent preparation and unknown-native-outcome custody tests remain green. Full `pnpm check:changed` passes. Isolated Codex review is scoped-clean through P2. Previous-head CI gate was green (run 44884649486; gate publisher 44885786877). Pre-rebase CI run 44900735659 completed successfully at `4d246ad046bc5de32b77c316b81f3a32e3bc2f70`; November 21 pre-resume CI [44935797495](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44935797495) completed successfully for `381949bf9b9da21a082bec88b3d0b392da4acdef`. ClawSweeper revision 4 reported zero open items and no findings on that November 21 head. Native review validation and preparation completed before the interruption; the resumed head requires refreshed native records, exact-head CI and hosted review. Landing uses `scripts/pr`.

The predeclared workload uses two A/A controls and five serial counterbalanced pairs per kind, a synthetic 62,000-file/~1.1 GB Btrfs workspace, a 35 GiB synthetic storage fixture, and real Podman. One idle native clone and directory fsync complete before their return is delayed 30 seconds. This models slow storage completion, not the kernel's metadata-reservation cause. Required outcomes: exact accepted-base contents, zero inline template builds, foreground completion while storage remains pending, lower send latency, and no >20% total CPU/allocation regression. Any other worse metric requires explicit owner acceptance.

Rerunnable committed workload: `scripts/perf/worktree-creation-measure.ts --base-advance --first-send-layout --first-send-image <local-image> --startup-refresh managed|sandbox --repo <synthetic-repo> --output <new-directory> --samples 1`, with the repository TypeScript loader and matching compiled filesystem worker. The warmed case prepares a separate untimed session; the measured retained-A session remains unprepared. It was declared in this body before its first run.

### Warmed-process comparison

Five serial counterbalanced pairs per kind, plus two A/A controls per kind. Resource totals cover the measured B idle pass plus the C refresh/send overlap once; the nested send row is not added again. All ten candidate sends finished while the 30-second storage-completion delay remained pending, with zero inline template builds. All 48 measured/control/warmup projection and installed-skill comparisons matched fresh preparation.

| Metric | Managed baseline → candidate | Sandbox baseline → candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First-send median | 43.84 → 8.38 s (-80.9%) | 45.28 → 9.08 s (-80.0%) |
| First-send minimum–maximum | 43.37–44.62 → 7.70–8.81 s | 43.72–51.41 → 8.31–10.37 s |
| Template preparation median | 30,285 → 167 ms | 33,868 → 86 ms |
| Idle-pass median | 4.62 → 4.43 s (-4.0%) | 4.92 → 5.14 s (+4.6%) |
| Total CPU median | 39,494 → 38,383 ms (-2.8%) | 40,887 → 36,455 ms (-10.8%) |
| Main-thread CPU median | 2,486 → 2,609 ms (+4.9%) | 2,710 → 2,568 ms (-5.3%) |
| Transient main allocation median | 279,659,104 → 287,566,240 bytes (+2.8%) | 250,972,232 → 257,981,672 bytes (+2.8%) |

With five samples, the maximum is also the nearest-rank p95. A/A first sends were 43.45/43.32 s managed and 43.06/44.95 s sandbox. The main-CPU/allocation increases and sandbox idle-median increase are disclosed and covered by the separate performance-owner acceptance recorded below.

### Compiled Gateway, real transport and model

An isolated compiled Gateway used the ordinary idle scheduler, real WebSocket requests, Podman, and a real OpenAI model reply. Both heads reached a successful terminal model event and retained exact A HEAD, clean index, source and installed dependencies, with zero inline template builds. The retained harness searched the entire history for the response sentinel, which also appeared in the input; exact assistant reply text is therefore not claimed by that assertion.

| Delayed-refresh scenario | Baseline → candidate startup | Baseline → candidate model completion | Template preparation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Managed, existing warm slot consumed first | 38.57 → 11.77 s | 41.84 → 14.63 s | 28,557 → 90 ms |
| Sandbox, first chat.send into existing A session | 38.96 → 8.55 s | 40.89 → 10.71 s | 30,249 → 54 ms |

These are one real Gateway pair per scenario, not estimated p95s. Both candidate model replies arrived before the delayed refresh completed; both baseline replies arrived after it. Sandbox projection reconciliation stayed 4.16→4.22 s, separate from the template wait.

The managed flow uses an initial-message create, whose admitted startup owner materializes accepted A. A prior ordinary create consumes the one ready checkout slot in 340/370 ms while C is delayed. On baseline, the following startup waits for C. On candidate, A can also replenish that slot while C is still pending, so startup consumes it immediately. The direct startup-owner regression separately proves one private template clone when no slot is involved. An initial managed qualification with the slot still available completed on both heads (14.62→15.25 s model completion); that unaffected-path observation is retained and is not claimed as a red reproduction.

### Profiles and disclosed costs

Source profiles still include first-idle esbuild work in both arms (maximum consecutive non-idle spans 4.42→4.40 s managed; 5.12→4.51 s sandbox). They are not shipped-runtime blocking claims. The compiled Gateway has no such multi-second spans. Its qualified managed candidate records existing GC spans up to 83.6 ms and a 105.5 ms timer delay during the idle interval: the latter aligns with a 106.5 ms profile sample gap marked `(idle)`, followed by a 78.6 ms timer delay dominated by `(program)`. Those are disclosed native/descheduling observations, not evidence of a newly added synchronous JavaScript section. No >50 ms section was attributed to the new exact-generation selection code. Foreground module-loading/GC pauses remain (maximum observed timer delay 196 ms); reconciliation and pre-attempt storage accounting are separate follow-ups.

prs.title: fix(agents): record a child's message to its parent without a parent turn
prs.body:
## Problem

When a child session calls `sessions_send` to the parent that spawned it (for example, to report progress), OpenClaw starts a new, hidden parent turn for each message. Each parent turn spends a model call, usually replies back to the child, and marks the parent chat unread although the chat shows nothing new. One child that sent 15 progress updates started 15 hidden parent turns.

## Change

A supervised child's `sessions_send` to its completion owner (the parent that the child's end state reports to: hidden, ACP and visible supervised children) no longer starts a parent turn (`mode: "notify"` keeps its existing ephemeral next-turn behavior):

- Parent mid-turn: the message steers into the running turn (the existing active-run injection).
- Parent idle: the message is appended to the parent's transcript as one model-visible, chat-hidden custom entry (`sessions-send-child-message`). The parent reads it on its next turn.
- The child gets `status: "accepted"` with `delivery: { status: "skipped" }` at once. It does not wait for a parent reply, because no parent turn runs.
- Only the child's end state wakes the parent (the existing completion wake).

All other `sessions_send` uses do not change: parent to child, peers, `agentId` targets, self-sends, sends to people's sessions, and sends from unsupervised `sessions_create` sessions to their creator (they have no completion that would wake the creator, so they keep the ordinary recipient turn).

The `sessions_send` tool description and `docs/concepts/session-tool.md` now tell a child that a message to its parent is recorded for the parent's next turn and gets no reply. Prompt snapshots are regenerated.

Codex works the same way: inter-agent progress and completion messages use `trigger_turn: false` and are recorded in history without starting a turn.

## Production line delta

+73 / −1 (excludes tests, docs and snapshots). The new code is one function, `recordSessionsSendForRequester`, which reuses the existing active-run steering and the existing transcript report append. No new tool parameter, config option, state or retry.

## Accepted edge case

If the parent is mid-turn but refuses the steer (for example, the running turn does not accept the child's requester authority), the message is appended to the transcript instead. The parent reads it on its next turn. No turn starts.

## Review

Local review round 1 found that `sessions_create` sessions also carry parent lineage but have no completion owner, so their messages to an idle creator would wait with nothing to wake it. Fixed: the history path now keys on `completionOwnerSessionKey`, and a test proves an unsupervised session's send still starts a creator turn. Round 2 found that `mode: "notify"` entered the new path before its own handling, and that the tool description did not limit the rule to supervised children. Fixed both: notify is handled first, as before, and the description and docs name supervised children only (prompt snapshots regenerated).

## Evidence

- New tests in `src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions-steering.test-support.ts`, through the real `sessions_send` tool path:
  - `a supervised child's send to its parent starts no parent turn` (idle, busy). Red on the merge base: a parent `agent` turn starts and the child gets the parent's reply. Green on this head: idle → one transcript entry and no `agent` call; busy → one steer and no `agent` call.
  - `an unsupervised session's send to its creator still starts a turn`.
  - The existing parent-to-child steering tests in the same file stay green.
- `ocx test` on every test file that imports a changed source, plus `src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts`: 28 files plus the prefix-stability test, 8 Vitest shards, all passed. After the review fix: `openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts`, `sessions-send-tool.admission.test.ts`, `sessions-send-acp-custody.test.ts` passed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck, guards, format and prompt-snapshot drift passed; baseline ratchets (session identity, line cap) pass after the review fix. One Knip full-tree finding is in `scripts/lib/docker-e2e-watchdog.mjs`, a file this PR does not touch.
- `pnpm prompt:snapshots:check` with a clean HOME: current.
- E2E, isolated Gateway from source on a real Claude Sonnet route. The parent spawns a visible child; the child sends the parent 3 progress messages with `sessions_send`, then replies `DONE`. Model requests were counted at a logging proxy:
  - Merge base: the parent ran 4 turns after spawning: 3 hidden turns (one per progress message, each told to reply through the message tool) and the completion wake.
  - This change: the parent ran 1 turn after spawning, the completion wake. Its request contained the 3 progress messages once each, before the completion. Its reply: "The child finished. I received these PROGRESS codes from it, in order: 1. PROGRESS-1-… 2. PROGRESS-2-… 3. PROGRESS-3-…"

prs.title: fix: keep Git-installed plugins working after an OpenClaw update
prs.body:
Closes #204156

## What Problem This Solves

After changing releases, a plugin installed from Git can retain its OpenClaw peer link to the previous release. The new Gateway then refuses to load the plugin, leaving its tools unavailable.

## User Impact

Pinned Git plugins remain usable when the managed installation switches to another release. `openclaw doctor --fix` can repair an existing stale link, and a retry can finish an interrupted repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair path now uses the same source and checkout identity as the Git installer. It checks the registered checkout and Git commit, then targets the serving release. An existing link is replaced only when it points to another release of that installation. A missing link can be recreated without overwriting a file or a package that appears in the meantime.

## Evidence

- On macOS arm64, installed a local Git plugin pinned to one commit in an isolated managed release layout. With the published **2026.11.7** package (`e31bbf0`), its real Gateway tool returned HTTP 200 from release A. After selecting a separate release directory B with the same published package, the persisted peer still pointed to A. The Gateway logged a peer-link audit refusal and the tool returned HTTP 404.
- Built the exact candidate `7b7cad3` with `pnpm build:runtime`. Two independently seeded profiles retained the same Git pin. Starting the candidate Gateway repaired the link and returned HTTP 200 with the candidate SDK path. Running `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` in the second profile repaired its stale link before startup, and the Gateway returned the same successful result.
- The focused peer-link suites passed **53 tests** on the final commit. They cover interruption after unlinking, retry, and preserving a regular package that appears during repair. Core typecheck, changed-file lint, formatting, and the repository commit checks passed.

The reproduction selected real package directories through a disposable release link. It did not run a system service installation, the full self-updater, or an external model. Linux and Windows runtime evidence remains for CI.

OpenAI Codex (GPT-6.2 Sol, xhigh) authored the patch, tests, and verification.


### Named profile replay on `3e8159a`

The real Git release launcher ran `--profile work` on macOS arm64. The launcher and its selected releases were under `home/.openclaw/git-install`. The Git checkout and state were under `home/.openclaw-work`. The checkout commit stayed pinned throughout. The tested profiles and plugin were disposable fixtures.

```text
Stock shared launcher --profile work: OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (e31bbf0)
work pin 642130defa9a HTTP 200 via A/dist/plugin-sdk/core.js
Original PR shared launcher --profile work: OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (7b7cad3)
work pin 642130defa9a after shared host B, peer still A, HTTP 404
Original doctor --profile work: peer still A, Git pin 642130defa9a

Reviewed shared launcher --profile work: OpenClaw 2026.11.7 (3e8159a)
work pin 642130defa9a HTTP 200 via fixed shared release/dist/plugin-sdk/core.js
Doctor updated named profile peer to shared release before startup; pin 642130defa9a
work pin 642130defa9a HTTP 200 via fixed shared release/dist/plugin-sdk/core.js
```

The original change reported this audit failure, with the temporary path replaced by `<fixture>`.

```text
peer link audit failed: <fixture>/home/.openclaw-work/git/git-e17adb066d1bd4e5/repo/node_modules/openclaw points to <fixture>/home/.openclaw/git-install/releases/stock-a/openclaw instead of <fixture>/home/.openclaw/git-install/releases/published-patch-b/openclaw
```

The review revision resolves the serving release from its verified active installation and uses the named profile for the Git checkout. On the preceding commit, the unit reproduction failed both when a named profile was actively serving and when the candidate host was inactive. Both controls pass on this revision. Six affected suites passed 123 tests, including the interrupted-repair retry. Core typecheck, targeted lint and formatting, and the complete runtime build passed.

prs.title: feat(mcp-events): receive MCP events by poll without a public callback
prs.body:
Related: #166586

## What Problem This Solves

MCP Events can only deliver by webhook today, so an Automation can't react to an MCP server's events unless the Gateway has a public HTTPS callback route. Most Gateways run on a laptop or a private network, bound to loopback.

## User Impact

User impact: operators can enable `mcp-events` without `callbackOrigin`, and event Automations receive their events by polling the MCP server (`events/poll` from SEP-3415), with no public route to the Gateway. Each event runs the Automation once, as with webhook delivery.

`callbackOrigin` becomes optional. Configs that set it keep webhook delivery for events that offer it, and webhook subscriptions saved by earlier versions are kept as they are. An event that offers only webhook still needs `callbackOrigin`, and its source reports that. Adding or removing `callbackOrigin` later replaces affected subscriptions with the other mode; as when a source is replaced, events still queued for the old subscription don't run, and the replacement starts from now.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper's review of #166586 recommended starting with polling: extend the existing host capability and plugin, and prove cursor recovery and replay deduplication. It also asked for a maintainer decision on that direction, which this PR still needs. SEP-3415 (status: Accepted) defines the poll profile. This PR implements poll only; push (`events/stream`) is not included.

Poll reuses the webhook path from the queue onward. Webhook callbacks and poll results go through one admission step into the same durable ingress queue, so deduplication by event ID, the `maxPendingEvents` budget, the drain and Cron's `runEvent` handoff are shared. The shared ingress code now lives in `ingress.ts`, which keeps `service.ts` under the line cap. Following the SEP's client guidance, OpenClaw uses webhook when `callbackOrigin` is set and the event offers it, and poll otherwise.

Poll behavior, per the SEP:

- One poll loop per event Automation, on the existing Gateway scheduler. The first poll sends `cursor: null` ("start from now").
- The returned cursor is persisted in plugin state after the batch is queued. A crash re-polls the batch and the queue drops repeated event IDs. After a restart, polling resumes from the saved cursor.
- `hasMore: true` with events polls again at once. Otherwise OpenClaw waits `nextPollMs`, with the SEP's 1-second floor and a one-hour ceiling. Editing other Automations doesn't pull a scheduled poll forward.
- Events in a batch run in the server's order.
- `NotFound` or `Unsupported` rediscovers the event type and starts again from now, dropping events still queued for the old subscription and backing off if the server keeps refusing. Other errors, including `Forbidden`, retry with backoff capped at five minutes while the Automation is enabled, as webhook sources do.
- Events over 256 KiB, or failing envelope or `payloadSchema` validation, are skipped with a warning, so one bad event can't block the Automation's queue.
- Poll keeps no server-side subscription, so removing or pausing the Automation just stops polling.

The host capability accepts `events/poll` only for the Automation's own persisted event name and arguments, the same rule `events/subscribe` follows. Two small SEP alignments also apply to webhook mode: discovery accepts the `io.modelcontextprotocol/events` extension entry as well as the earlier top-level `events` key, and requests that carry an event name send the `Mcp-Name` header (Base64 form for non-ASCII names). The Automation editor's catalog now lists events that offer poll; push-only events stay hidden.

Not included: `maxAgeMs`. After a long outage a saved cursor replays everything the server still retains, one run per event, bounded by `maxPendingEvents`. Webhook refresh behaves the same today.

## Evidence

- Focused tests, all passing with `--maxWorkers=1`: `extensions/mcp-events/src/service.test.ts` (20), `src/agents/mcp-event-request.headers.test.ts` (4, new), `src/plugins/service-mcp-events.test.ts` (27), `src/gateway/server-methods/mcp-events.test.ts` (8). The plugin suite's test time is about 3 s of a 17 s run; the rest is compile time. The 16 existing webhook tests pass unchanged.
- New plugin tests cover: poll without a callback across a restart (cursor resumed, one queue row per event, `hasMore` and `nextPollMs` honored); a cursor write that fails after the batch is queued (the next poll resends the old cursor and the queue keeps one row); a webhook binding stored in the pre-change shape (kept, same binding ID, no new subscribe, and its refresh sends the same callback URL and cursor); and poll errors, rediscovery and its backoff.
- Three defects found while building this have tests that fail with the fix disabled and pass with it: events in one poll batch shared a queue receipt time and could run out of order; any Automation change re-polled every poll subscription at once, ignoring `nextPollMs`; and a restart after a recovered failure waited out the old backoff before polling.
- ClawSweeper found that a full poll batch (100 events at the 256 KiB limit) could exceed the MCP HTTP transport's 10 MiB response cap. The transport rejected it before parsing, the cursor didn't move, and the backlog stalled. Polls now ask for at most 32 events (8 MiB). A test in `src/agents/mcp-event-request.headers.test.ts` sends a full 32-event batch through the real transport, and shows a 100-event batch is rejected with `MCP HTTP response exceeds 10485760 bytes`.
- `pnpm check:changed`: everything this change touches passes, including type checks, format, the line-cap ratchet, the config baseline (regenerated because `callbackOrigin` is no longer required) and lint for `extensions/mcp-events`. Local gaps are listed below.
- Live run on macOS, isolated Gateway (own home, state and profile, loopback), on commit 7408fdf028c (the later commits only clear the stored retry time after a recovered poll, lower the poll batch to 32 events, and add or move tests and docs), against the MCP Events bridge (disclosure below) running in poll mode, with a real model (`anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`). No `callbackOrigin`. The Automation's instruction was "Reply with only the comment_id value from the event data", so each run's reply shows which event it received. A pass-through recorder between the Gateway and the server logged each request:
  - The plugin's requests were `server/discover`, `events/list` and `events/poll` (37 polls). Every poll carried `Mcp-Name: proof.comment.created`. The server also saw `initialize` and `tools/list` once per run: each agent run loading the server's tools.
  - The first poll sent `cursor: null`, and each later poll sent the cursor the previous one returned. The server asked for `nextPollMs: 2000`, and polls ran 2.16 to 2.46 s apart.
  - Two signed test events, `comment_id` `one` and `two`, started two Automation runs. Both completed (`ok`) and replied `one` and `two`.
  - With the Gateway stopped, a third event (`three-while-stopped`) was sent. After restart, the first poll sent the cursor saved before the restart and returned that event. Its run completed and replied `three-while-stopped`. The subscription kept its binding ID.
  - Removing the Automation stopped polling. No subscription remained and nothing was unsubscribed.
- Upgrade from 2026.11.7, the latest stable (installed from npm), with a live webhook subscription, on macOS with an isolated Gateway, the same server and model, and a public HTTPS tunnel as `callbackOrigin` (2026.11.7 accepts only a bare origin). Re-run on 23 Nov on head d714c02dcb3; it replaces the earlier run from 2026.11.3, which had the same results:
  - On 2026.11.7 the Gateway subscribed by webhook, and a signed test event ran the Automation (`ok`, replied `c_stable`).
  - `openclaw doctor --fix` on this branch's build (commit d714c02dcb3) migrated the state databases, with backups, as `openclaw update` does (agent database schema v38 to v43).
  - This branch's Gateway then loaded the subscription 2026.11.7 had saved: same binding, `delivery: "webhook"`, one subscription, and no `events/subscribe` before its scheduled refresh.
  - At the refresh time 2026.11.7 had stored, this branch's build refreshed it: same callback URL and saved cursor; the server rotated the signing secret and extended the same remote subscription.
  - A signed test event after the upgrade ran the Automation (`ok`, replied `c_after-upgrade`).
  - In the saved record only refresh fields changed (`secret`, `previousSecret`, `cursor`, `cursorRevision`, `refreshBefore`, `nextAttemptAt`, `updatedAt`). `bindingId`, `callbackUrl`, `remoteId`, `status` and the stored event `definition` (still without a `delivery` field) were unchanged.
- Gaps:

prs.title: fix(macos): launch alert shows the CLI's schema refusal instead of generic credential steps
prs.body:
Closes #201468

## What Problem This Solves

When the macOS app's bundled CLI refuses a forward schema migration because an older Gateway service still uses the same state, the launch alert hides the refusal. Instead it tells the user to run `openclaw doctor --fix` and restore backup credentials. Doctor meets the same refusal, so that advice cannot work, and the refusal's own remedy appears only in the unified log.

## User Impact

User impact: with an older, separately installed Gateway service (for example a global npm install), the alert now shows the CLI's refusal. The refusal names both versions, the service's install root, and `openclaw update`.

Every other credential startup failure still shows the existing Doctor/backup recovery, unchanged. That includes native credential admission errors, other CLI failures such as an invalid config, timeouts, and the background-only stderr path.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ClientCredentialStartup.prepare` now throws a `PreparationError`. When the CLI exited with the refusal from `assertGatewayServiceSchemaMigrationAllowed` (`src/state/openclaw-state-service-installation.ts`), the error also carries that sentence. The launch handler shows that sentence only for that refusal.

Two cases deliberately keep the generic recovery:

- **Native admission failures**, such as `Local client credential schema does not match version 1`. They carry no next step. This addresses the earlier review finding.
- **The previous build's app-managed service**, the `StaleGatewayServiceReplacement` path. There the refusal names `openclaw update`, which reports `host-managed` on an app-owned install, so it would replace one wrong instruction with another. That variant has a different root cause: replacement stops the service, but the guard reads the installed service definition. It is described in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/201468#issuecomment-7020325845 and belongs in its own fix.

The alert title and the generic text are the existing strings, so the localization inventory does not change. The branch is rebased on main after #201505, so the handler uses `requestTermination()`.

## Verification

### Proven on this revision

- **Regression test** (`ClientCredentialStartupTests`): drives the real `ClientCredentialStartup.prepare` boundary with a child CLI that exits 1 and prints the schema refusal on stderr. It asserts:
  - the recovery is exactly the CLI's refusal sentence for a separately managed older service;
  - generic recovery is kept for the app-managed stale-service replacement path;
  - generic recovery is kept for a native admission error (`Local client credential schema does not match version 1`);
  - generic recovery is kept for an unrelated CLI failure (the existing failed-preparation test).
- **Composition test:** the `ClientCredentialStartupCompositionTests` malformed-config launch keeps its expected `OpenClaw client credentials need recovery.` stderr.
- `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passes (`changed=false`); the alert title and the generic recovery strings are unchanged. `git diff --check` is clean.
- `git merge-tree` against current `main` (91dee12) is clean. #203382 conflicts only in `ClientCredentialStartup.swift`. The compatible resolution keeps #203382's exact-entrypoint replacement admission and applies this PR's refusal classification only on the non-replacement path, so either order of landing works.

### Still required before merge

- `ClientCredentialStartupTests` RED on base `64416d16a2` with the regression-only patch applied, then GREEN on head `8d899626d0`.
- Maintainer-approved `macos-swift` CI on the exact head.
- On a disposable Mac, captures of a locally built packaged app:
  1. the generic Doctor/backup alert before the fix;
  2. the CLI's schema-refusal sentence after the fix, against an older, separately managed Gateway;
  3. the generic Doctor/backup alert still shown for a native credential admission failure.

I have no Mac, so no macOS execution or packaged-app behavior is claimed. A step-by-step recipe for a volunteer is in the comment below.

**Test access** could report **Invalid response** for a working account when the agent had no model configured for that provider and no completed catalog was cached. The check sent a plugin’s manifest model even when the account’s model list did not include it.

## User Impact

Test access uses a listed model when one is available. If discovery fails and there is no usable model, it reports **No model** without sending an inference request. No configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Configured models still take precedence. Only explicit probes without a configured candidate request scoped live discovery from the existing read-only catalog loader. It reuses completed inventory when available and does not publish a refresh. Passive listing, failure messages, and inference timeouts are unchanged.

## Evidence

Both regression cases failed on `4b9faa26d`: the planner queued `manifest-model` instead of the discovered model, including when discovery would return HTTP 503. With the fix, a successful listing selects `discovered-model`; HTTP 503 returns `no_model` with zero inference targets.

prs.title: fix: recover a completed Models sign-in after reconnect
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Models can say a sign-in session ended even though the Gateway saved the account. This happens when the socket drops after the Gateway finishes sign-in but before the dialog receives its final reply.

## User Impact

The same user or paired device can reconnect within five minutes and see success without signing in again. Restarting the Gateway ends that window, not the saved account.

## Why This Change Was Made

The UI already retries by reading the session without resending the answer. Keep successful Models credential sessions readable by their original owner and start one unreferenced purge timer when the runner settles. Reads do not reset the timer, repeat login, or prevent another sign-in. Failed and cancelled sessions keep their existing cleanup.

## Evidence

On unpatched main (`4b9faa26d`), the Gateway returned `done` to the original request, then `WIZARD_NOT_FOUND` to its owner's reconnect read. With the fix, all 60 focused tests passed, including stale-answer rejection, owner isolation, admission release, and expiry at the original deadline.

All three real-Gateway Chromium scenarios passed. The new one withholds an actual successful `wizard.next` response, closes the socket, and observes the same session's successful reply on a new socket. The dialog shows “ready” and the fixture exchanges the code once.

<details>
<summary>Recorded Chromium run: redacted Gateway trace and test output</summary>

From the original successful run on November 23 (UTC). A and B replace two distinct connection IDs; only the relevant fields are shown.

```text
13:15:59.158  [ws] client connected conn=A
13:15:59.911  Auth profile: <synthetic provider account>
13:16:00.901  [ws] client connected conn=B
13:16:01.209  [ws] webchat disconnected conn=B
13:16:01.210  [ws] webchat disconnected conn=A
```

From the test runner in the same run:

```text
✓ recovers success when the final wizard reply is lost 4752ms
```

The Gateway log records the two connections and the account, not the WebSocket payloads or token count. The passing [browser transport assertions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/b4777532e3d91fc1188331587bd681d537eef179/ui/src/e2e/provider-browser-login-leave.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts#L109-L146) required the first real `done` reply to be withheld, a newly opened socket to receive `done` for the **same session**, and the provider to receive **exactly one** `/token` request. The browser baseline stopped before approval because its environment lacked font discovery; the pre-fix failure was reproduced at the Gateway handler, not in Chromium. prs.title: fix: try your next Claude login when one runs out of usage credits
prs.body:
Related: #122010, #177426

## What Problem This Solves

When one saved Claude login runs out of usage credits for a model, the Claude Code CLI says "You're out of usage credits. Switch to another model, or manage usage credits at …". OpenClaw doesn't recognize that wording, so it files the failure as `unknown`. If you have several saved Claude logins, you get an error instead of a reply even when the other logins still have credits. A model you picked by hand (for example Fable) has no fallback model, so the turn just fails.

## User Impact

User impact: when Claude Code says a login is out of usage credits, OpenClaw files the failure as `billing` instead of `unknown`. The reply now says it is a billing problem, and a run on a saved auth profile marks that profile billing-disabled like other billing errors. Tested on 2026.11.10-beta.1: the classification changes as expected. A claude-cli conversation whose run has no selected saved profile still does not move to another login, so this does not fix rotation on its own.

## Why This Change Was Made

The billing list already has Claude's older "out of extra usage" wording. This adds the current CLI wording next to it. #122010 was closed because unknown errors now continue to the next fallback model, but that doesn't switch logins and doesn't help a hand-picked model. #177426 covers a different message ("You've reached your Fable limit"), which is a rate limit, not this one. #122512 tried the same fix and was closed as stale.

## Evidence

- Seen live on 2026.11.10-beta.1 with three saved Claude logins: Fable 5.2 failed on the first login with this message, logged as `reason=unknown`, attempt 1 of 1, and never tried the other two. Running Fable directly on each login showed the other two answer fine.
- With the same one-line pattern applied to the installed build, the failover classifier returns `billing` for this message (it returned unknown before) and still returns `timeout` for an unrelated network error. The compaction variant ("Prompt is too long · automatic compaction failed: You're out of usage credits…") still classifies as context overflow, as before.
- Added a corpus row with the exact CLI message to `failover-classification.billing.cases.ts`. I didn't run the suite locally and am relying on CI for it.

prs.title: fix: stop reporting unknown send IDs as confirmed messages
prs.body:
Closes #199070

## What Problem This Solves

Some channel adapters return `messageId: "unknown"` when they cannot confirm a provider message id. OpenClaw treats that placeholder as a real send identity, records the payload as `sent`, and emits a successful `message_sent` event — even though the receipt contains no platform message ids. Operators and downstream bookkeeping can be told a message was confirmed when delivery is actually ambiguous.

## User Impact

Reserved adapter placeholders (`unknown` and `suppressed`) are no longer promoted into confirmed platform identities. Sends with real ids are unaffected, mixed multi-part sends keep their genuine ids, and deliberately non-sent results stay non-sent. Ambiguous sends retain their existing "no identity" custody behavior instead of being silently confirmed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveReceiptSourceId` accepted any nonblank `messageId`, while the reconciliation code later filtered `"unknown"` and `"suppressed"` out of platform ids. That disagreement let an unidentified attempt become an identified `sent` result. A single shared normalizer now defines what counts as a platform message identity and is used by source-id resolution, receipt construction, receipt reads, and delivery reconciliation.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests for `src/channels/message/receipt.test.ts` and `src/infra/outbound/deliver.test.ts` were run with Node v24.22.1 and worktree-local dependencies. The new receipt tests cover both reserved placeholders with an empty receipt, a bare placeholder result, and a mixed send where real ids must survive. All 11 receipt tests pass, including the new cases.

Limitations: this is a source-verified contract fix. No live Matrix homeserver or full Gateway integration run was performed; the Matrix path was exercised through the shared receipt helpers rather than a live adapter send. A few unrelated long-running delivery tests time out in this local Windows environment (5s default timeout); increasing the timeout and loading the standard test setup is used to separate those from regressions.

## AI assistance

This fix and its tests were prepared with AI assistance and reviewed locally before submission.
