prs.title: fix: recognize missing Gateway units on systemd 239
prs.body:
Closes #200026

## What Problem This Solves

On hosts running systemd 239, OpenClaw's service inspection treats an absent Gateway unit as a hard inspection failure. The native manager correctly reports that the unit is missing, but the busctl reader only recognizes systemd 245's `Call failed: ` prefixed reply, so a first source build can refuse to run with a misleading "runtime artifacts changed / state could not be verified" error.

## User Impact

On systemd 239 hosts, an absent Gateway unit is now recognized as "not installed" instead of "inspection failed", letting normal first-time builds and status checks proceed. Permissions errors, timeouts, and other uncertain replies still fail inspection and keep all existing lock, port, ownership, and publication guards active.

## Why This Change Was Made

Missing-unit replies differ by systemd version: 245 prefixes them with `Call failed: `, while 239 returns the same text unprefixed. The matcher now strips that optional prefix before comparing, so one rule handles both formats. ANSI stripping and method-specific wording are unchanged.

## Evidence

The focused `src/daemon/systemd-busctl-query.test.ts` suite passes 10/10 with the fix (Node v24.22.1, worktree-local dependencies). Reverting only the source file and rerunning the same tests produced 6 failures, all for the unprefixed systemd 239 replies, while the 4 pre-existing prefixed/negative cases still passed. Coverage includes `GetUnit`, `LoadUnit`, and `GetUnitFileState`, plus colored replies and unrelated unprefixed failures that must still throw.

Limitations: verification is unit-level with a stubbed `busctl` process; no live systemd 239 host was available locally. The issue also suggests consolidating the loaded system-ownership reader onto this shared query; that broader refactor is out of scope here and is not attempted.

## AI assistance

This fix and its tests were prepared with AI assistance and reviewed locally before submission.

prs.title: fix: keep npm updates working when TMPDIR is too small
prs.body:
Related: #203913

## What Problem This Solves

An npm update can pass its database rehearsal by moving scratch work off a full `TMPDIR`. Package Doctor and the final state checks can still use the original filesystem after the new package is active. If they run out of space, the update can finish with its database state unverified.

## User Impact

When rehearsal finds a usable fallback for the explicit scratch directory, the package update can finish without the operator changing `TMPDIR` and retrying.

## Why This Change Was Made

Package Doctor, the live schema check, and the migrated finalizer reuse the fallback filesystem selected by rehearsal. They use it for disposable scratch while config, database, and service paths stay the same. This targets the updater on `release/2026.11.7`. The same constrained fixture passed with the newer updater on `main`.

## Evidence

I reproduced the failure in isolated Linux/x64 npm installs with Node 26.13.1, a seeded SQLite database, and a private 1,140 MiB tmpfs. See the [published-release reproduction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/203913#issuecomment-7093624286).

| Updater and scratch | Result updating to 2026.11.10-beta.1 |
| --- | --- |
| Published 2026.11.7, 1,140 MiB tmpfs | Rehearsal selected the state volume. Package Doctor hit ENOSPC and the update ended with `rollback-state-unverified`. |
| Patched 2026.11.7, same tmpfs cap | Rehearsal selected the state volume. The update and migration finished successfully. |
| Patched 2026.11.7, disk-backed TMPDIR | The update and migration finished successfully. |

Both patched runs migrated schema 36 to 40, preserved the seeded row, passed SQLite `quick_check`, and recorded `succeeded` in the update ledger. Both Gateways reported core readiness and RPC served version 2026.11.10-beta.1. These runs used foreground Gateways and synthetic state. Managed service restart, channels, and other operating systems are outside this proof.

<details>
<summary>Commands and review</summary>

- Update: `openclaw update --tag 2026.11.10-beta.1 --yes --json --no-restart`.
- Verification: `openclaw health --json`, `openclaw gateway status --deep --require-rpc --json`, and read-only SQLite schema, integrity, and witness checks.
- The package Doctor regression failed on the release base and passed with the fix. It verifies that the Doctor child gets the admitted scratch directory without changing the parent environment or installation selectors. The 42-line test allocation covers that regression.
- `pnpm test src/cli/update-cli/update-command-{package,migrated,migrated-schema}.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 77 tests. The package test file took 68.73 s in a dedicated local run. The final three-file run took 430.79 s including runtime preparation. CI timing is pending.
- Core typecheck, targeted lint and formatting, runtime build, and npm tarball integrity checks passed.
- Fresh independent Codex review of this patch against the release base found no remaining blocker. Local autoreview was unavailable. The original preflight approach was dropped after review exposed a false-refusal case.
- Base `393b8ffff768d41c9eeb9cb2382d578ad937b808`. Tested source `33a26b693b6ff2637e4c339ceaa65b1fa45079f7`. Upstream contribution guide and PR template rechecked at `6a8b47c86d4b58f88181c084ae72cd19189b8282`.

</details>

prs.title: fix(openclaw-id): refuse inherited member account names
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An OpenClaw ID owner can sign a membership change whose account id is an inherited object name such as `constructor`. Membership state is a normal object, so that lookup reads `Object.prototype.constructor` instead of a missing member. `set_role` and `set_member_recovery_kit` then store a record with no `peer_keys`. Gateway submit commits that state. The next tunnel admission walks every member and throws `TypeError` on `peer_keys.includes` before it reaches owner devices. A peer that belonged to an earlier well-formed member can still be admitted. Every other peer, including the owner's, fails until the row is repaired.

## Evidence

Before this patch, an owner-signed `set_role` for account id `constructor` was accepted. The suite assertion that it must be refused failed on current main:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run packages/openclaw-id-protocol/src/review-regressions-2.test.ts -t "prototype account id"
 FAIL  packages/openclaw-id-protocol/src/review-regressions-2.test.ts
AssertionError: expected { ok: true, status: 'applied', …(2) } to match object { ok: false, code: 'target_mismatch' }
  {
-   "code": "target_mismatch",
-   "ok": false,
+   "ok": true,
  }
```

After this patch, an isolated Gateway refuses the same statement and still admits the owner on the tunnel API. The Gateway is `startGatewayServerCore`, the server `src/gateway/server.ts` starts. The client calls the shipped websocket method `openclawId.authority`. Tunnel admission is HTTP on the Gateway ingress socket, which checks admission before it serves `/_openclaw-id/v1/membership`.

```console
$ cd /tmp/oc-f101
$ NODE_OPTIONS='--require /tmp/capture-ingress.cjs' pnpm exec tsx proof-gateway-member.mts
[ws] res openclawId.authority errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=unknown member
PROOF_JSON {"head":"f8999716dead","submit":{"ok":false,"message":"unknown member","code":"target_mismatch"},"constructorStored":false,"ownerDeviceCount":1,"tunnelAdmission":{"status":200,"code":null,"detail":null},"tunnelSubmit":{"status":403,"code":"target_mismatch","detail":"unknown member"}}
```

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: An owner-signed set_role for account id constructor is refused by the Gateway submit method. The claw store does not gain that member. The owner device remains, and the tunnel API still admits that owner.
Real environment tested: Darwin 27.2.0 arm64, Node v26.13.1, worktree /tmp/oc-f101 at f8999716dead, pnpm 12.15.0. Isolated state from createOpenClawTestState. Gateway bound to loopback with channels skipped and OpenClaw ID enabled.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: NODE_OPTIONS='--require /tmp/capture-ingress.cjs' pnpm exec tsx proof-gateway-member.mts
Evidence after fix: terminal output copied below.

```console
$ NODE_OPTIONS='--require /tmp/capture-ingress.cjs' pnpm exec tsx proof-gateway-member.mts
[ws] res openclawId.authority errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=unknown member
PROOF_JSON {"head":"f8999716dead","submit":{"ok":false,"message":"unknown member","code":"target_mismatch"},"constructorStored":false,"ownerDeviceCount":1,"tunnelAdmission":{"status":200,"code":null,"detail":null},"tunnelSubmit":{"status":403,"code":"target_mismatch","detail":"unknown member"}}
```

Observed result after fix: openclawId.authority submit returns target_mismatch and unknown member. constructorStored is false and one owner device remains. GET /_openclaw-id/v1/membership on the Gateway ingress socket returns 200. POST /_openclaw-id/v1/statements returns 403 target_mismatch.
What was not tested: This checkout has no iroh binding, so the QUIC relay child did not stay up. The Gateway still opened its ingress socket and served the tunnel API. A membership row that was already saved without peer_keys is not repaired.

## Summary

Same own-property rule already used for membership operation names. A real account id that is later stored as an own property is unchanged.

prs.title: fix: keep dictation recording when switching tabs or applications
prs.body:
Related: #197843, #200346

## What Problem This Solves

Control UI dictation stops and starts transcription whenever the browser loses focus or the page becomes hidden. This interrupts people who switch tabs or applications to read reference material while dictating a longer message. Earlier fixes preserve the text on interruption, but still stop the recording.

## User Impact

User impact: once dictation starts, switching tabs or applications, minimizing the browser, or moving the pointer away no longer ends the recording. **Stop and keep text** finishes it; **Escape** still discards it. The first explicit Stop works even if the original held pointer was released outside the window. Nothing is sent automatically.

The microphone remains active in the background. Closing/reloading the page, changing the draft/conversation, microphone loss, and connection failures can still end capture. Browsers and operating systems may suspend background capture, particularly on mobile or screen lock; this change adds no wake lock, automatic restart, or persistent audio retention.

## Why This Change Was Made

Focus and visibility interruptions now belong to the existing unfinished hold gesture, not the lifetime of an already-started recording. The shared dictation owner keeps the existing cancellation and final-transcript paths. Explicit mouse or keyboard Stop is distinguished from the synthetic click produced by releasing the initiating hold.

The reporter explicitly confirmed the requested background-recording behavior. Simplification keeps one existing owner and removes recording-lifetime focus/visibility listeners; no new state owner or compatibility path. Production delta: +20/-15 lines; documentation +6; tests +165/-73.

## Evidence

### Clean comparison

Before

![Before: background event ends capture and starts transcription](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6cf63b6b-1c15-4234-b943-50f1b78a1801)

After

![After: microphone remains listening after background event](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6cbc942a-f099-4b4e-9624-53927259ecdb)

### Annotated comparison

Before

![Before: transcription begins without explicit Stop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a305ca74-09d7-4e5d-8f9f-9df8c3f50169)

After

![After: listening continues until explicit Stop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1054bbb9-3fc2-4b3f-ba1f-13fc72cb3e1d)

Chat composer after synthetic blur/hidden events. Before: base f56171778657c9332e78eda92c4545143be07549; After: published a6f9b7b22af974e2dca86e04b0e9b722c628b727, identical candidate tree. Real Chromium/native audio with a fake microphone and mocked Gateway; not real OS window-switch proof.

- Recording regressions fail on base `f56171778657c9332e78eda92c4545143be07549`: four owner cases fail, and both browser cases issue an unexpected early close. They pass with this change. The transferred candidate is tree-identical to implementation commit `8cf02670b42ad6faf94ee0e4b7643fd86b95ef48` (tree `a02b81af2acd6c79fed9fa45cbb4d22b67cafca1`).
- Implementation verification: 131 tests in six owner/consumer files passed. Publication verification independently passed the 49-test owner suite and all 19 browser dictation scenarios (36.98 s reported duration).
- Chromium uses native getUserMedia and AudioContext with a test microphone. The new browser scenarios verify audio continues reaching the Gateway request boundary after blur/hidden events, with no close until explicit Stop and no chat.send. Gateway responses and platform focus/visibility events are synthetic.
- UI production and relevant chat/E2E test typechecks, scoped lint, formatting, and git diff --check passed in implementation; publication rechecked formatting and whitespace on the identical tree. The UI build exits successfully. Its performance report flags largest CSS gzip 57.2 KiB versus 56.9 KiB and 21 chat-boot JS requests versus 20; those warnings have not been baseline-qualified or waived.
- Native independent source review identified a lost-release click-suppression defect. Mouse and keyboard Stop regressions reproduced it before repair. Follow-up independent owner/session reproduction found no new actionable P0–P3 findings on the complete final patch. This is native-agent review, not helper-validated Auto Review. Bound Auto Review did not produce a validated report: the original attempt was interrupted, and a source-only retry reached its 120-second reviewer deadline with cooperative cleanup. No alternate model, host, or credential route was used.

<details>
<summary>Publication replay recovery and remaining uncertainty</summary>

The first publication browser run was 15 passed / 4 failed, not clean: two hidden Listening-label timeouts and two late-transcript draft-edit mismatches. The container had no system fallback fonts, and its captured failure screen had invisible text. A bounded base comparison reproduced the guest-label timeout and live-edit mismatch; the new-session edit mismatch did not reproduce in that comparison. Installing task-local DejaVu/fontconfig data, without source or assertion changes, restored visible text; the five focused cases and then all 19 scenarios passed. The original failures remain recorded: font repair explains the rendering failures, but a passing replay alone does not establish the cause of the intermittent draft-edit mismatches. Both background cases still fail on base with an early close under the same repaired font environment.

</details>

Not tested: physical microphone, cloud transcription provider, real OS window/tab/minimize actions, or mobile suspension. The code does not change transcription-provider behavior.

Reported and directed by Daniil Karpenko.

Linked for team reference; these sessions aren’t public.

prs.title: fix(sandbox): reject glob allows that admit an unconfined tool
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Workspace confinement decides whether a sandboxed worker is limited to its workspace tools. The check looked only at the shortest allow list and treated a glob such as `sessions_*` as if it were a tool name. A longer policy that names `sessions_spawn` does not allow that literal string, so the glob was skipped. The runtime matcher still allows `sessions_spawn`. Workboard treats a missing confinement error as a confined workspace, so that spawn tool was accepted.

## Evidence

Before this patch, the same configuration produced no confinement error. The suite assertion failed because the error was undefined:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/sandbox/workspace-authority.test.ts -t "glob allow list"
FAIL src/agents/sandbox/workspace-authority.test.ts > rejects a glob allow list that admits sessions_spawn
AssertionError: the given combination of arguments (undefined and string) is invalid for this assertion.
```

After the patch, `resolveSandboxWorkspaceAuthority` reports `sessions_spawn`. This command calls that function directly:

```console
$ pnpm exec tsx proof-confinement-glob.mts
{
  "sandboxed": true,
  "confinementError": "target sandbox allows unclassified tool surface sessions_spawn."
}
```

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Allow globs are expanded against core tool ids and then judged with the same policy matcher the runtime uses. A sandbox allow of sessions_* plus a longer allow that names sessions_spawn is reported as unconfined.
Real environment tested: Darwin 27.2.0 arm64, Node v26.13.1, worktree /tmp/oc-f103 at ad9d29c3c09, pnpm 12.15.0. The script builds the sandbox tool config and calls resolveSandboxWorkspaceAuthority.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: pnpm exec tsx proof-confinement-glob.mts
Evidence after fix: terminal output copied below.

```console
$ pnpm exec tsx proof-confinement-glob.mts
{
  "sandboxed": true,
  "confinementError": "target sandbox allows unclassified tool surface sessions_spawn."
}
```

Observed result after fix: the authority is sandboxed and the confinement error names sessions_spawn.
What was not tested: Workboard's dispatcher was not driven in a browser. The script calls the same resolveSandboxWorkspaceAuthority function that prepareWorkspaceAuthority uses before it accepts a confined worker. A named sessions_spawn allow was already covered by the existing suite and still passes. A glob that names only a plugin tool is not expanded, because those ids are not in the core catalog. An explicit plugin tool name is still judged.

## Summary

Safe allow lists that only name confined tools stay confined. The read alias skills_read is not treated as a separate unconfined tool.

prs.title: fix: voicecall expose --mode off leaves the Tailscale address published
prs.body:
Closes #204118

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw voicecall expose --mode off` says `"ok": true`, but on the default HTTPS port (443) the Tailscale address stays published. After `expose --mode funnel` that means the voice webhook is still reachable from the internet when you think you turned it off. A Gateway that published the webhook itself leaves the route behind the same way when it stops.

## User Impact

User impact: turning the Tailscale exposure off now really removes the voice webhook route on port 443, as it already did on other ports. Only the voice routes are removed; anything else you serve on port 443 (for example the Gateway at `/`) stays up. No config change is needed. A route left over from an earlier version is removed the next time you run `voicecall expose --mode off` for the same path.

## Why This Change Was Made

On port 443 the cleanup ran `tailscale funnel off /voice/webhook`. The Tailscale CLI only accepts `off` as the last argument, so it answered `Error: invalid argument format` and changed nothing, and that error was not shown. The other ports already used the accepted form, `--set-path <path> off`. This removes the special case for 443 so every port uses that one form.

Not changed here: the command still prints `ok: true` without checking the result. It tries `serve` and then `funnel` for each path, and the second one normally reports "handler does not exist" because the first already removed the route, so the exit code alone cannot tell success from failure.

## Evidence

**End to end with the real Tailscale CLI (1.80.0).** The real `voicecall expose` command handler ran the real `tailscale` binary. The only stand-in is tailscaled: a local socket that stores the serve config the CLI reads and writes, so nothing was published and no account was used.

| After | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `expose --mode funnel` | `/voice/webhook` published, Funnel on | same |
| `expose --mode off` | prints `ok: true`; `/voice/webhook` **still published, Funnel still on** | prints `ok: true`; serve config is empty |

A second run with another route on port 443 (`/` on Funnel) removed only `/voice/webhook`; `/` and its Funnel setting stayed.

<details>
<summary>Raw output</summary>

main (`6587c9fd212`):

```
> openclaw voicecall expose --mode funnel
[voice-call] Tailscale funnel active: https://bot.example.ts.net/voice/webhook
   serve-config: {"TCP":{"443":{"HTTPS":true}},"Web":{"bot.example.ts.net:443":{"Handlers":{"/voice/webhook":{"Proxy":"http://127.0.0.1:3334/voice/webhook"}}}},"AllowFunnel":{"bot.example.ts.net:443":true}}
> openclaw voicecall expose --mode off
{ "ok": true, "mode": "off", "path": "/voice/webhook", "streamPaths": [] }
   serve-config: {"TCP":{"443":{"HTTPS":true}},"Web":{"bot.example.ts.net:443":{"Handlers":{"/voice/webhook":{"Proxy":"http://127.0.0.1:3334/voice/webhook"}}}},"AllowFunnel":{"bot.example.ts.net:443":true}}
   tailscale stderr: Error: invalid argument format / try `tailscale serve --help` ... Error: invalid argument format / try `tailscale funnel --help` ...
```

this branch:

```
> openclaw voicecall expose --mode off
{ "ok": true, "mode": "off", "path": "/voice/webhook", "streamPaths": [] }
   serve-config: {}
   tailscale stderr: error: failed to remove web serve: error: handler does not exist
```

The two command forms on their own, with no tailscaled running (so only argument checks apply):

```
$ tailscale funnel off /voice/webhook
Error: invalid argument format            exit=1
$ tailscale funnel --bg --yes --set-path /voice/webhook off
getting client status: failed to connect to local tailscaled ...   exit=1 (arguments accepted)
```

Sibling route check (`/` published first):

```
$ tailscale serve --bg --yes --set-path /voice/webhook off
```

Closes #204186

## What Problem This Solves

A script checking where it can append a JSONL record gets a successful lookup for `+event` or `+0`, even though writing to either location fails. Both lookups report the next line as an insertion point.

## User Impact

`openclaw path resolve` now exits with status 1 for these unsupported JSONL targets. The root `+` still resolves to the next line and accepts an append.

## Why This Change Was Made

The resolver and writer now use the same rule for JSONL insertion: a bare `+` at the root of the file.

## Evidence

Ran the built CLI on a file containing one record, `{"event":"start"}`. Before the fix, both invalid lookups reported line 2 and exited 0, while a dry-run write to `+event` returned `not-writable`. After the fix, both lookups failed as expected. Appending at the root and reading the new record also succeeded.

<details><summary>CLI output (JSON fields abridged)</summary>

```text
$ openclaw path resolve oc://log.jsonl/+event --file log.jsonl --json
{"resolved":false}
exit 1

$ openclaw path resolve oc://log.jsonl/+0 --file log.jsonl --json
{"resolved":false}
exit 1

$ openclaw path set oc://log.jsonl/+event '{"event":"finish"}' --dry-run --file log.jsonl --json
{"ok":false,"reason":"not-writable"}
exit 1

$ openclaw path resolve oc://log.jsonl/+ --file log.jsonl --json
{"resolved":true,"match":{"kind":"insertion-point","container":"jsonl-file","line":2}}
exit 0

$ openclaw path set oc://log.jsonl/+ '{"event":"finish"}' --file log.jsonl --json
{"ok":true,"bytesWritten":37}
exit 0

$ openclaw path resolve oc://log.jsonl/L2/event --file log.jsonl --json
{"resolved":true,"match":{"kind":"leaf","valueText":"finish","leafType":"string","line":2}}
exit 0

```

</details>

Two new regression cases failed on the unmodified base. All 513 oc-path tests passed with the fix. The runtime build, extension and test typechecks, changed-file formatting and lint, and local review passed.

prs.title: fix: let Windows updates replace migrated state databases
prs.body:
Closes #204085

## What Problem This Solves

Every release-path update that changes the state schema fails on Windows today: the startup swap renames over the live SQLite files while retained handles are still open. This also affects a successful migration chain, not only its generic-copy fallback (`state-upgrade.ts:566–584,660–663`). The launcher restores the previous release, but the update cannot complete. Shipped first hops use their existing in-place update route and are not affected by this release-path defect.

## User Impact

The candidate releases its closed databases' retained file descriptors before the startup swap. The Windows task supervisor now skips Gateway state and config bootstrap entirely, so it holds no database connection while its child runs. The child still loads its own dotenv files and selects its database and environment. Migration and rollback keep their existing owners and preserved files. There is no schema change or new user action.

An interrupted Windows swap that already created `.pre-*` hard links can still retain admission custody and roll back; this existing, visible recovery edge is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Closing SQLite leaves the admission owner's identity descriptor open. A native Windows control reproduces the failure with both SQLite connections closed, then permits the same rename immediately after the existing admission-retirement operation runs. The durable swap now performs that retirement for both database paths before it preserves or replaces either file.

The next open must admit the replacement's physical identity again. The launcher, trial budget, attempts, rollback policy, and SQLite file-sharing mode are unchanged. This requires the candidate fix, not a new installed launcher.

The real Windows replay exposed a second holder: the waiting task supervisor had opened the shared database during Gateway pre-bootstrap. Its only job is to launch and wait for the real Gateway. Supervisor dispatch now happens before SQLite runtime, dotenv, database-engine selection, and Gateway environment selection. The late dispatch is removed.

## Evidence

- Original real Control UI failure: run `4adf1716-1734-4ed5-9eee-38083120fdfc`, two starts, schema 41→42 attempt, both blocked at the canonical WAL; the previous release served after rollback.
- Native Windows reproduction on Azure: a candidate with isolated state holds its own live and prepared file descriptors when replacement fails. No supervisor targets that isolated state.
- Product-API causal control on that lease:
  ```json
  {"file":"live.sqlite","nativeClosed":true}
  {"file":"next.sqlite","nativeClosed":true}
  {"beforeRetirement":"refused","code":"EPERM","syscall":"rename"}
  {"afterRetirement":"renamed"}
  ```
- One swap-owner regression checks descriptor release, new database contents, and the preserved old contents.
- AWS Linux run [`run_604041d54425b8c7e03ba43362072ac2`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_604041d54425b8c7e03ba43362072ac2): all 46 focused tests passed; the new regression fails on the base because the two descriptors remain retained (not a setup failure).
- Final-head T, next and crash full distribution builds, repository packing, and archive identity/SHA-256 checks passed in AWS run [`run_60ba70a2d1888c2d832aef9a1c6c3665`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_60ba70a2d1888c2d832aef9a1c6c3665). The corrected fixture declares its predecessor/runtime catalog inputs before generation.
- AWS run [`run_1af4700e569a25502494c17898d4839d`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_1af4700e569a25502494c17898d4839d): all 37 run-main tests passed; both new supervisor cases fail on clean main base `38f4f8fe018c` because the supervisor enters SQLite startup. Final parser consumer replay [`run_e6e98aa9e306b3332caadeefe5a8615c`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_e6e98aa9e306b3332caadeefe5a8615c) passes `cli-root-options` and `run-main`. Final-head local review and CI are owned by the lead.
- Fixed candidate-only Windows click on `3c150b5bfa`, run `36fec6f8-d822-409f-9f00-dfb6633e0d70`, still rolled back after two canonical-WAL `EPERM` failures. Native samples every two seconds show the old task supervisor retaining that WAL across candidate starts. Final head `69f58bc4e8` includes the early, database-free supervisor dispatch, its owner regression, and the preserved ordinary parser result.
- **Windows migrating UI update passed:** run `47295f8d-1098-407b-ac2d-160cdca32158`, committed on its first start, T+1 build `0322afdd098e` serving, shared schema 42 and the new STRICT table present. The startup log explicitly reports `by migration chain`. Across 491 native `openclaw.sqlite` handle samples, task-supervisor PID 404 has zero matching lines; other processes have 12,165 matching lines, confirming the sampler was active.
- **Linux chain-mode UI update passed:** run `137ae66a-ab63-4c64-af4b-9c90ee345278`, committed on its first start, T+1 serving schema 42 with the STRICT table. The startup journal explicitly reports `by migration chain`, not generic copy.
- The retained Doctor log explains the old fixture's generic-copy fallback: its schema-41 predecessor catalog was undeclared. Earlier Linux and macOS proof used that fallback. Those runs are not counted as chain-mode proof; the corrected final-head passes above are.

Crash rollback plus healthy recovery, and reboot-before-candidate recovery remain pending on separate fresh Windows machines. Optional plugin maintenance refused old-Gateway-owned schema mutation in the passing runs; those advisory/plugin/channel checks are not claimed as passed.

The swap repair reuses admission retirement. The supervisor repair removes its unnecessary Gateway bootstrap. There is no new user-facing API, flag, configuration, retry, timer, or stored state.

prs.title: feat: let agents participate selectively in group conversations
prs.body:
## Problem and motivation

When mention gating is disabled in a group, the primary reply model receives admitted messages and decides whether to participate as part of an agent turn. Many of those messages are exchanges between other people, questions that have already been answered, or chatter where another reply would add little value. Starting the primary agent for every such message creates unnecessary work and conversation noise.

Requiring an explicit mention avoids some of that work but misses indirect invitations and useful opportunities to contribute. A configured Decision Model should make the participation choice using the existing group etiquette, while the primary model keeps generating replies in its usual voice.

## Solution

With the existing default-off Decision assistance setting enabled and a Decision Model configured, assess eligible unmentioned text messages in always-on groups and channels before primary generation.

The assessment receives the current message, reply reference, bounded recent model history, and bounded workspace identity text. Recent history uses the same reader as normal generation, preserving native message-tool calls and their actual delivery results. Identity context uses the existing workspace loader and context formatter, preserving heading/prose `IDENTITY.md` files and configured identity precedence.

History preparation runs inside the existing admitted Decision execution, after the selected model’s effective route limits are known. It reserves space for the current message, identity and question, then uses the existing history selector to keep a bounded suffix with complete tool-call/result pairs. In addition to the shared token-pressure estimate, aggregate state/question and request limits set a conservative UTF-8 byte envelope, checked against the complete serialized batch. Provider-specific encoded-input constraints keep their existing handling. It adds no second catalog preparation or provider hook call. If the required input cannot fit, or all prior context would be omitted, the existing ordinary-reply fallback applies. Diagnostics measure the prepared batch rather than its initial placeholder.

- **Reply:** continue through the ordinary agent generation and delivery path. The turn carries approval as the existing result-required completion policy, and turn context tells the primary model to generate its reply in its usual voice.
- **Silent:** record the incoming message through the existing transcript owner and finish the turn without primary generation.
- **Assessment unavailable:** use the ordinary reply path.

The existing admission, transcript, queue, cancellation, permissions, and delivery owners remain responsible for their normal work. A declined queued source is consumed after persistence, so the recorded input is not retried as an abandoned request. The completion owner uses confirmed current-source delivery evidence. `NO_REPLY` after message-tool delivery prevents duplicate output. An undelivered `NO_REPLY` remains an unfulfilled reply and follows existing bounded generation recovery and failure handling. Source-delivery retries retain that requirement; they do not make another participation choice. Exhausted or refused retries record failure through the existing runner, and system notices retain their existing permission.

## Scope and rollout

This uses the existing Decision assistance Labs flag and configured `decisionModel`; there is no separate participation setting. An already-saved enabled preference also enables this capability after upgrade.

Explicit mentions, commands, media inputs, ambient room events, internal events, and generic CLI backends keep their existing paths. When Decision assistance is disabled or unavailable, the primary model retains its ordinary participation behavior.

Assessments use the selected Decision provider and may incur its normal charges. The provider receives the identity and conversation evidence described above. Each assessment is bounded by the turn timeout and a maximum of 30 seconds.

## Validation

The existing approved-text case reproduced approval followed by primary `NO_REPLY` completing without an answer before the fix, then passed with normal generation recovery and delivery. The existing message-tool case still completes without a duplicate reply. A second revised existing case reproduced queued delivery retry being disabled by the stronger completion policy.

Focused validation covered 168 existing cases across five files. After the final source-receipt consolidation, all 73 affected immediate/queued consumer cases passed in 77.02 seconds. The unchanged terminal-resolution and stranded-recovery suites also passed. No test cases or fixture frameworks were added.

The final messaging type-check graph, formatting, syntax guards, whitespace checks, and source/test line ratchets pass. Independent source review is clean. It also traced private transcript receipts, exhausted retry settlement, and refused retry enqueue through the existing owners. The 180-line allocation covers the excess above the 400-line allowance: 580 net test lines retain participation, persistence, source settlement, delivery and prepared-input coverage. The budget repair extends existing cases without adding test cases or a fixture framework.

The history-input repair passes all 11 existing participation/queue cases, the messaging type-check graph, formatting, syntax guards, whitespace checks, and the runtime import-cycle check. An isolated synthetic SQLite transcript reproduces the prior omission and confirms that the shared model-history reader retains the reply text and matching settled source-delivery receipt in order. Independent review is clean; no tests were added for this repair.

A fresh live assessment reached TypeSafe and received HTTP 400 with token-limit wording; the earlier rejection traces remain unattributed. The budget repair passes 102 existing cases across seven focused files (109.38 seconds). After the final interruption correction, all 89 affected Decision host/native cases passed again (46.40 seconds). Messaging and agents-root type checks, formatting, syntax guards, runtime import-cycle and line ratchets pass. Independent source review is clean.

Live validation of that first budget repair still returned unsupported input. A controlled replay through the existing native Gateway Decision tool then compared reconstructed local history with all fields preserved: the approximate selection (85,580 submitted JSON bytes) was rejected; the byte-bounded selection (26,067 bytes, seven messages with complete paired turns) succeeded with 13,990 provider input tokens. A local protocol comparison confirmed HTTP 400 with token-limit wording for the former and HTTP 200 for the latter. These were reconstructed inputs, not captured copies of the original requests; no channel messages were sent.

The follow-up repair changes one production file (+12/-2) and adds no tests. All 13 existing participation/queue/history cases pass, along with the messaging type graph, formatting, focused guards, whitespace and source-line checks. Independent source review is clean. The byte envelope is conservative, not an exact tokenizer guarantee. Exact-commit package installation and live greeting, contextual follow-up and silent-branch validation remain pending.

prs.title: fix: reconcile subagent completion after successful settlement
prs.body:
Related: #201339

## What Problem This Solves

After a requester yield batch successfully hands off a child result, the stored child run can still report a permanent delivery failure. The settle wake is then cleared even though the result reached the requester.

## User Impact

Successful requester handoffs are recorded as delivered, so monitoring and the Subagents list no longer retain a stale permanent-failure result for that run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The requester-batch mutation now reconciles a suspended permanent failure only when the settlement outcome confirms delivery and the row still owns the requester yield batch. Other unsuccessful or ambiguous outcomes keep their existing handling.

## Evidence

Result: on head `b4d0cc993f6612ea0752648da60209c2c24d883f` (rebased onto `main` `feea72c1863`), a permanently suspended completion that still owns its requester yield batch settles as delivered, and the unfixed base keeps `permanent_failure`.

Focused regression:

- Base `feea72c1863` with the fix reverted: `pnpm test src/agents/subagents/registry/subagent-requester-delivery.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` reports `Tests 1 failed | 10 passed (11)`. The new case fails with the stored delivery still at `"disposition": "permanent_failure"`.
- Head `b4d0cc993f66`: the same command reports `Tests 11 passed (11)` in one file, including `marks a permanently suspended completion delivered after its owned yield batch succeeds`.

Existing-data check: a `subagent_runs` row persisted by the unfixed build at `feea72c1863` is reopened by the fixed build and settled through the production requester-batch mutation. Observed output:

```json
{"readBeforeSettle":{"delivery":{"status":"suspended","suspendedReason":"permanent_failure"},"hasWake":true},"mutationStats":{"settled":1},"readAfterSettle":{"delivery":{"status":"delivered","disposition":"delivered","deliveredAt":300},"hasWake":false}}
```

The patch changes no schema or migration, and the pre-fix row loads and resolves with the fixed build.

Gateway handoff regression: `pnpm test extensions/qa-lab/src/plugin-subagent-current-requester.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes 2/2 on this head. That suite runs a real Gateway child with the qa-channel transport and the scripted `mock-openai` provider, covering `sessions_spawn` followed by `sessions_yield` requester delivery to the originating conversation. It is regression coverage for this owner, not the suspended-permanent-failure reconciliation itself.

Checks: targeted `run-format.mts --check` passes on both touched files, and `git -c core.whitespace=cr-at-eol diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passes.

Boundary: this proves the production SQLite mutation, persisted-row readback, and the real Gateway spawn/yield handoff path, not a live-model run that reaches the suspended-permanent-failure settlement. No model provider is configured in this environment, so that specific handoff and the Subagents-list rendering remain unproven here, and fork CI still needs maintainer approval to execute.

prs.title: fix(gateway): apply credential limits to assistant media URLs
prs.body:
## Summary

Apply the Gateway's configured lockout to assistant media reads that use a URL credential on loopback. Local clients can keep using URL previews, authorization headers, and scoped media tickets.

## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI media reader accepts several credential types. Its URL credential path inherited the general loopback exemption, so URL reads and native bearer requests shared a policy despite having different callers. In `src/gateway/http-auth-utils.ts`, the reader now checks a URL-specific budget before validating the credential and records a failure after the applicable credential checks finish.

Same-origin previews have a separate budget from other URL reads at the same loopback address. Failed credentials still count toward the configured IP limit. Bearer headers keep precedence, and scoped media tickets retain their existing reader and source checks.

## Evidence of Fix

| Check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Token and password routing | The original reader accepted a URL credential with a preloaded URL lockout. The updated reader returns HTTP 429. |
| Gateway socket test | A fixture earned a URL lockout. The next URL read returned 429, and the authorized bearer read returned 200. |
| Trusted-proxy local password and IP policy reload | The local password uses the URL budget. Tightening the IP policy enforces previously recorded failures. |

All 209 tests across six Gateway suites passed, as did the separate assistant-media socket test. Core and Gateway-server TypeScript checks, targeted lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.

The socket test can be run with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/control-ui-assistant-media.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. Routing coverage is in `src/gateway/server-http.control-ui.test.ts`.

## Real Behavior Proof

I installed the published stable npm package and started its Gateway. I then stopped it, installed the exact PR head as a self-contained npm tarball into the same prefix, and started the packaged Gateway again. Both runs used the same saved operator profile, credential, and media file. The repository’s package integrity check passed, and the installed build metadata matched the reviewed SHA. With a one-failure limit, the terminal capture was:

```text
Published package: 2026.11.7
Stable existing bearer: HTTP 200
Stable existing URL credential: HTTP 200
Installed candidate build: 24d58503a0a2019e9098be021ad2a7fc21874326
Upgraded existing bearer: HTTP 200
Upgraded existing URL credential: HTTP 200
Retired fixture credential: HTTP 401 | no fixture bytes
Earned URL lockout, known valid credential: HTTP 429 | no fixture bytes
Same-origin preview during lockout: HTTP 200
Authorized bearer during URL lockout: HTTP 200
Scoped ticket during URL lockout: HTTP 200 | fixture bytes match
Same saved credential and media across the install switch: verified
```

prs.title: fix: keep Claude CLI inline widgets on the reply after a chat reloads
prs.body:
Root cause: `src/gateway/chat-display-projection.canvas.ts:302` (`augmentChatHistoryWithCanvasBlocks`) gives pending canvas previews to the next assistant row without tool content. Claude Code history stores the reply's thinking as its own assistant row (empty `thinking` text plus a signature) before the visible reply, so after a reload the widget lands on that thinking-only row instead of the reply.

Related: #203893, follow-up to #203922. Thanks @fonchaves for finding this with real Claude CLI runs, and for the fix.

## What Problem This Solves

After #203922, a Claude CLI agent's `show_widget` widget appears on the live reply. After a reload it often ends up on the wrong message. Real Claude Code history usually stores the turn's thinking as its own assistant row, between the tool rows and the visible reply. The restored canvas block lands on that thinking-only row, so the reply people read has no widget. The iOS app shows the widget as a separate bubble next to the folded thinking. The Control UI shows it twice: once on the thinking row and once from the reply's `[embed]` shortcode.

## User Impact

After a reload, inline widgets from Claude CLI agents stay on the visible reply they belong to, as they do live. Histories without a thinking row are unchanged. A turn that ends without a visible reply keeps the widget on its own thinking row, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

A row whose only content is internal reasoning (`thinking`, `reasoning`, `redacted_thinking`, checked with the existing `isAssistantInternalReasoningContentType`) no longer takes pending previews straight away. It only holds them. If a visible reply follows in the same turn, the reply gets them. If the next user prompt or the end of history comes first, the thinking row gets them, as it does today, so a widget never moves to another turn's answer. Rows that carry tool results don't count as a prompt: Claude history keeps each result of parallel tool calls as its own user row, and those rows belong to the same turn. Codex review found the end-of-history and next-prompt cases on earlier revisions. The last commit fixes the tool-result rows, which on the previous revision put the widget back on the thinking row. All of these show up in the proof below.

Every client that reads `chat.history` treats a thinking-only row as hidden activity. The widget only shows up next to the reply when the block is on the reply row:
- Control UI: `ui/src/lib/chat/message-visibility.ts` `resolveMessageVisibleContent` returns `none` for thinking-only rows and `non-text` once a canvas block is added (checked through the shipped pipeline below).
- iOS (OpenClawChatUI): `thinking`/`redacted_thinking` count as work content (`ChatWorkChunks.swift`) and fold away. A canvas preview with an inline widget path (`hasWorkMedia`, `ChatCompletedWork.swift`) keeps the row visible on its own.
- TUI: assistant history rows with no text are skipped (`tui-session-actions.ts`), and the TUI does not render canvas blocks.

## Evidence

Built Gateway (`pnpm install` and `pnpm build` in a secretless `node:24.22.1` container), `agentRuntime: claude-cli` with a stand-in `claude` that sends Claude Code 2.1.330 stream-json. It calls the Gateway's real loopback MCP `show_widget` and writes the Claude project JSONL that `chat.history` imports, including the thinking-only assistant row before the reply. The client is an iOS-shaped operator (`openclaw-ios`, `inline-widgets`, signed device) plus a Control UI client. Two runs on each side.

| case (`chat.history` after reload) | `main` (d38fed5803) | this head (21e04e5fc7) |
|---|---|---|
| widget turn, thinking row before reply | `2:thinking+canvas 3:text` (6/6 runs) | `2:thinking 3:text+canvas` (2/2) |
| same, Control UI pipeline | widget on the thinking row and again from `[embed]` (twice) | one widget, on the reply |
| thinking row, parallel tool calls, reply | `2:thinking+canvas … 7:text` (2/2) | `7:text+canvas` (2/2) |
| widget turn ending on the thinking row | `4:thinking+canvas` | same (2/2) |
| that turn, then the next prompt | `4:thinking+canvas 7:text` | same (2/2) |

The earlier revisions misplaced the widget in specific cases: 2e4dc45fe7 put it on the previous turn's answer, 77b00ff475 on the next turn's answer, and 3962182ce1 on the thinking row in the parallel-tools case. Every revision is shown in the evidence comment.

Controls: the same widget turn without a thinking row, a plain Claude CLI turn, and an embedded-runtime widget turn give byte-identical `chat.history` on the merge base, both earlier revisions and this head (run-random ids and times normalized). Full output: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204102#issuecomment-7109116215

Regression test: the existing "restores widgets from Claude CLI results coalesced into the tool-call message" case now covers four things: the visible reply after a thinking row (fails on `main`), the same with a parallel tool-result row in between (fails on `main` and on 3962182ce1), a turn that ends on the thinking row (fails on 2e4dc45fe7), and that turn followed by the next user prompt (fails on 77b00ff475).

prs.title: fix: show app update guidance instead of a failing Update button on app-managed Macs
prs.body:
Closes #198506 Prior work: #198562 tried this and was closed without merging because the update handlers it edited have since moved. This PR is written against current main. ## What Problem This Solves On a Mac where OpenClaw.app owns the Gateway, Settings > Updates still shows an enabled "Update Gateway..." button and an "Update status unavailable" row. Clicking the button gets a refusal from the Gateway ("Managed by OpenClaw.app. Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway."). The page then keeps that refusal as an update error with a "Retry update" button, and the error stays until the page is reloaded. A healthy install looks like it failed an update, and Retry cannot succeed because the Gateway marks the refusal as not retryable. ## User Impact User impact: on an app-managed install, Settings > Updates now says "Managed by OpenClaw.app" in the status row and shows the app's own guidance ("Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway.") where the update button used to be. There is no button to click, so no error appears and nothing is left to retry. Other installs (package, Git checkout, separately managed Gateways) look and behave as before. ## Why This Change Was Made The Gateway already knew the install was app-owned, but `update.status` dropped that fact, so the page had no way to tell this install from any other and offered the normal action. The Gateway now sends the owner under `schedule.install.host`, and the Settings page uses it. Ownership comes from the same install marker the Gateway's refusal already uses, so a Mac connected to a separately managed Gateway still gets the normal update flow. The protocol schema gains an optional `install.host` object and a `host` install kind, and the generated validators are regenerated from it. The Control UI adds four English strings. The updating doc notes where the owner is reported. Update behavior: this only changes what `update.status` reports and what Settings shows. Config, the state schema, migrations and the way updates run are untouched. An app-owned Gateway still refuses Gateway update requests with the app's hint, and package and Git installs keep their current update flow. ## Evidence ClawSweeper's last review left two pieces of end-to-end proof open: the built Settings flow, and an upgrade from v2026.11.6 that keeps settings and data. The Settings flow is covered below. The upgrade is not (see Not verified). The current head, `8a511b6`, is `1b71766` rebased onto main `15e5f75`. Apart from the generated `predicates.js`, which was regenerated from the schema, its diff is identical to `1b71766`'s, so the browser run on `1b71766` recorded in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200910#issuecomment-7066419264) applies to this head. That run built fresh Gateways with `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` from the base (`dc6e31a`) and from `1b71766`, both with the Mac packaging ownership marker, and ran the same Settings > Updates steps in Chromium on each. The changed Updating guide was built with `docs:build:preview` on both sides. Before, Settings offered "Update Gateway…", confirming it left the ownership refusal as an update error, and the guide did not mention the Settings display. After, Settings shows "Managed by OpenClaw.app" with the app's guidance and no Gateway update button, and the guide describes that behavior. The screenshots below come from an earlier run of the same steps against Gateways built from `d119c6b` and `0f678cb`, using the exact ownership marker written by the Mac packaging script, with fresh Gateway state and no model or credentials. `0f678cb` has the same hand-written changes as the current head. Before: Settings shows "Update status unavailable" and offers "Update Gateway…". Confirming it leaves "Couldn’t update OpenClaw. Managed by OpenClaw.app. Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway." in the status row. `update.status` returned `schedule.install: null`. After: Settings shows "Managed by OpenClaw.app" and the guidance "Managed by OpenClaw.app. Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway." There is no Gateway update button. `update.status` returned `schedule.install: {"kind":"host","host":{"owner":"macos-app","displayName":"OpenClaw.app","updateHint":"Update OpenClaw.app to update this Gateway."}}`. With main's sources at `dc6e31a` and this PR's tests, the new Settings test fails the way the issue describes: the status row reads "Update status unavailable" where it should say "Managed by OpenClaw.app". The 9 Gateway and schema cases that expect the owner fail the same way. On the current head, all of them pass.
Tests and checks on the current head (Node 26.8, macOS arm64) - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` over the five changed test files: 93 tests pass. That is 43 in `ui/src/pages/config/updates.test.ts`, 28 in `src/gateway/server-methods/update-status-schedule.test.ts`, 12 in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/config.test.ts`, and 10 across `src/infra/update-install-status.test.ts` and `src/infra/update-startup-host-owned.test.ts`. The three new cases took 21 ms (Settings), 283 ms (update status schedule) and 2 ms (schema). - `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:ui` pass. Type-aware `oxlint` on the 11 changed TypeScript files reports no diagnostics. - `pnpm gateway:validators:check` reports no drift, and `git diff --check` is clean. - `oxfmt --check`, the line-cap ratchet, docs markdown lint, `protocol:check`, `ui:validators:check` and `ui:i18n:verify` passed on these same file contents before the final rebase onto `15e5f75`, which left all 13 files unchanged.
Not verified: - No run inside OpenClaw.app itself. The browser runs above used Gateways built from source with the Mac packaging marker. The issue's reporter offered to check a fix on their Mac. - No upgrade from a released version with settings and data kept. I tried one with the published v2026.11.6 in an isolated home, but my test environment blocks the process listing that release uses to verify SQLite ownership, so it could not read its own config there. - A separately managed Gateway was not run in a browser; the existing `updates.test.ts` cases for the "Update Gateway…" action still pass. - The full `pnpm check:changed` was not run.

prs.title: fix: let plugin updates finish for plugins that ship no Doctor artifact
prs.body:
Closes #203604

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw plugins update` can refuse an entire batch with "Plugin config repair could not be inspected: typesafe. Repair the plugin's Doctor artifact, then retry the update." when one of the plugins has no Doctor artifact at all. The trigger is a plugin migration left pending by an earlier update. The reporter's 11.6 batch of five plugins failed until they left `typesafe` out. No user action can fix it, because the plugin has no artifact to repair.

## User Impact

Plugin updates go through for plugins that publish no Doctor contract, such as `@openclaw/typesafe`, and their pending migrations settle. A plugin whose Doctor artifact exists but fails to load still refuses, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The update's config-migration step counts a plugin as inspected only when its config-repair contract reports in. A package with no declared Doctor contract and no `doctor-contract-api`/`contract-api` artifact never reports, so any pending migration that retained its config paths looked permanently uninspected. Published `@openclaw/typesafe` 2026.11.5 and 2026.11.6 both have no Doctor artifact. The step now counts those plugins as inspected with no config repair. The Doctor migration-availability check (`plugin-migration-availability.ts`) already treats such packages as stateless; this applies the same rule here.

The plugin registry was left as it is. Adding empty config-repair entries there would also change the historical-webhook supplement logic for official channel owners.

## Evidence

- New `artifact-free` scenario in `plugins-update-command.migrations.integration.test.ts`. It runs the real update command with real state and a retained pending migration for a plugin with no Doctor artifact. On base (`origin/main` 6837fd38ed4) it fails with the reported refusal text; with this change it passes.
- The whole integration suite passes (38/38). That includes `legacy-contract-failure` and `constructor-failure`, where an artifact that fails to load still refuses.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `tsgo:core` pass.
- Published package check: `npm pack @openclaw/typesafe@2026.11.5` and `@2026.11.6` contain no `doctor-contract-api.*` or `contract-api.*`.

prs.title: fix: say which consent fact is missing when an agent's tool authority can't be verified
prs.body:
Related: #193383

## What Problem This Solves

When OpenClaw cannot confirm the tool permissions a Template-managed agent was installed with, Doctor and agent runs show one fixed line: "Cannot verify the installed tool authority … Repair the OpenClaw state database before running it." The same line appears whether consent was never prepared in that process, the state database could not be read, or a stored schema version was invalid. Reporters on #193383 (10.10 through 11.6) followed the advice, found a healthy database, and had no way to tell which case they were in.

## User Impact

The refusal now names the specific missing fact, for example "OpenClaw state database has not initialized Template consent provenance." Users and maintainers can see which condition blocks the agent. The consent check itself is unchanged: an unverifiable agent still refuses to run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The consent owner already passed the specific reason as the error's `cause`, but Doctor prints only `Error.message`, so the reason was lost. The error now puts its direct cause's message in its own text. Only the direct cause is used, never a walk of the cause chain, so wrappers that redact their message keep that redaction. A first attempt at printing causes generically in Doctor's error renderer was dropped after independent review showed it would bring back the PostgreSQL connection string that `src/infra/database-engine/adapters.ts` deliberately removes from its outer message.

This is a diagnostic, not a root-cause fix for #193383, so the issue stays open. A synthetic manually configured agent (`tools.profile: "full"` plus `alsoAllow`, with empty Template install tables) does not reproduce the refusal on published 2026.11.6 or on current main, with `doctor`, `doctor --fix`, or warm reruns. Empty install tables alone do not trigger it, and the next report will say which branch does.

## Evidence

- New test `tool-policy-runtime.preparation.test.ts` "tells Doctor which consent fact is missing": builds the production refusal (late preparer registration, unprepared consent) and asserts on its Doctor-rendered text. It fails on base (`origin/main` 6837fd38ed4) and passes with this change.
- Consumers: `tool-policy-runtime*.test.ts`, `message.tool-policy.test.ts`, `agent-tools.policy*.test.ts` and `tool-availability-explanation*.test.ts` all pass (6 files, 34 tests).
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `tsgo:core` pass.
- Real CLI, built `qaRuntime` with isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`: no refusal for the synthetic config on main or on published 2026.11.6 (`doctor`, `doctor --fix`).
- Production LOC: +4/−2 in `src/templates/tool-policy-runtime.ts`. Tests: +16.
- Review: autoreview (Codex) scoped-clean. An independent Codex review traced every cause source (fixed provenance diagnostics, worker/open/lifecycle errors, schema-version decoding, `matchTemplateConsent`), found no path that turns redacted content into the new message, and reported no findings at P0–P3.

prs.title: refactor(agents): drop mid-run operator authority re-reads (R6c part 4c)
prs.body:
## Problem

Agent runs still re-read the admitted operator authority (`operatorAuthority.assertCurrent()`) in the middle of the work: before each model fallback candidate, at exec spawn, before each step of a queued compaction, at queued collector launches, at question binding, and when one participant of a steered turn reads or writes personal data. AGENTS.md says to check authority once, when work starts. These re-reads can refuse a started run after only a permission, approval or config change.

## Fix

This removes the last `operatorAuthority.assertCurrent` readers in `src/agents/**` and `src/sessions/session-controller.tool-authority.ts` (R6c part 4c). Start-time admission does not change. Stop, run close and data fences keep working through their own signals or flags.

| Site | Kind | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `admitted-run-context.ts` `readCurrentRoleFacts` wrapper | authority re-check | deleted; the role facts the producer captured are returned as they are |
| `admitted-run-context.ts` `createOperatorModelSelectionAssertion` source composition | authority re-check | deleted; the admitted model-policy check stays |
| `admitted-run-context.ts` `assertOperatorAccessProgramAllowed` | authority re-check | deleted; the admitted access-program check stays |
| `admitted-run-context.ts` `getAdmittedRunOperatorProfileId` | authority re-check | deleted; the active-lease check stays (run close) |
| `admitted-run-context.ts` `readOperatorAuthority` | authority re-check | deleted; the `closed` refusal stays (run close) |
| `bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts` spawn `assertCurrent` + pre-retain read | authority re-check (Stop rode on it) | deleted; Stop now reads `operatorSignal.throwIfAborted()` directly |
| `model-fallback-runner.ts` start + per-candidate (×2) | authority re-check | deleted; the admitted `modelPolicy.allows` filter stays; Stop is `abortSignal` |
| `model-fallback-image.ts` start + attempt error | authority re-check | deleted; `abortSignal` stays |
| `operator-run-recovery-source.ts` `captureScheduledOperatorSource` | authority re-check of the creating request | deleted; each scheduled run is still admitted at its own start (`restoreScheduledAutomationOperator`) |
| `plugin-tool-execution.ts` plugin model execution | authority re-check | deleted; `callerSignal` already includes `authority.signal` (Stop) |
| `plugin-native-subagent.ts` request runtime | authority re-check | deleted; guard, source, abort signal and Gateway binding stay |
| `harness/host-source-authority.ts` `retainHarnessSource` native branch | authority re-check | deleted; `assertRetained` keeps the source signal (Stop) and the lifecycle generation |
| `harness/host-source-authority.ts` `assertCompactionSource` | authority re-check | deleted; `assertActive` (session data) and the host-issued check stay |
| `harness/selection.ts` `assertHarnessModelPolicySupport` | authority re-check | deleted |
| `cli-runner/tool-authority.ts` question bind + `assertActive` | authority re-check | deleted; turn end, source and abort signal stay |
| `embedded-agent-runner/compact.queued.ts` host `assertActive` composition | authority re-check after each await | deleted; the operator signal stays in `abortSignal` (Stop). The queued compaction starts inside a request that was admitted when it started |
| `subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn.ts` collect retain | authority re-check | deleted; `retain` stays |
| `subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn-collector.ts` queued launch | authority re-check | deleted; the registration-ownership fence stays; the queue item still cancels on `operatorAuthority.signal`; the child run is admitted by the Gateway `agent` start |
| `sessions/session-controller.tool-authority.ts` participant `assertCurrent` | authority re-check | deleted; the turn-closed check and the retain failure at acceptance stay |

No ratchet strings were in these files, so no counts change. The `AdmittedRunOperatorAuthority.assertCurrent` type field and its producers stay for R6z.

## User impact

A started agent run, exec, fallback chain, compaction or steered-turn personal tool call finishes after a permission or role change. The next request uses the new permissions. Stop still cancels.

## Tests

Deleted, because each asserts a mid-run permission refusal:
- `model-fallback-image.operator-model-policy`: "stops the chain when the original requester retires".
- `cli-runner/tool-authority`: the "refuses it after its source is revoked" half (the profile carry stays).
- `harness/host-capability.source-lifetime`: the "source assertion" case. The Stop-signal and lifecycle cases stay. They now abort or rotate directly instead of inside the removed source read.
- `session-controller.message-join`: the "access changed" step. It now asserts the kept turn-closed refusal.
- `model-fallback.operator-model-policy`: "rechecks retained authority after asynchronous preparation before starting a model".
- `tools/pdf-tool`: the "retired after extraction" case (the denied-override and permitted-fallback cases stay).
- `harness/compaction.cancel` "source revocation" case: Stop now reaches the model binding through the source's `signal` (the kept path) instead of its `assertCurrent`. The refusal and its text stay the same.

Text only, condition kept:
- `gateway/openai-compatible-agent-run`, `gateway/tools-invoke-http.abort`: after run close the source still refuses, now with the producer's "Operator execution ended" run-close text. Two expectation lines outside `src/agents` changed because this PR changed what they observe.
- `subagent-spawn.participants.test-support`: a new spawn for a revoked participant is still refused at its start, and nothing is written. The refusal now comes from the spawn's own start check.

## Evidence

- Pre-push `ocx test`: 95 targeted files (operator-authority importers of the changed files, over the 150-file importer cap, plus nearby tests). Every red was fixed and rerun. Rerun result: all green except `subagent-spawn.production-boundary`. On the rerun that file cascaded from 120 s timeouts at host load 95. It passed 138/139 in the first run on the same production code, and its 1 red was the participant text fixed above.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test`, oxfmt and oxlint on the changed files: clean.
- E2E `one-admission-e2e/run.sh` on the head: see the comment.

prs.title: fix: compact at 80% on every route
prs.body:
Related: #204111

## What Problem This Solves

Automatic compaction started at two different points. Client maintenance started at 75% of the context window. Since #204111, the request-boundary compaction (ChatGPT V2 checkpoint and the warm text summary on every other route) started at 90%, a side effect of reusing the V2 trigger. No measurement supported 90%. At 90%, the warm summary request (the full window plus an appended instruction and the summary output, thinking included) can run out of room on ~200k windows and silently fall back to the cold summarizer.

## User Impact

All built-in routes now compact at the same point: the smaller of 80% of the window and the window minus the compaction reserve. On a 200k window, compaction starts at 160,000 tokens.

- ChatGPT V2 and the warm text route move from 90% to 80% (180,000 → 160,000 on 200k). The summary request keeps 20% headroom.
- Client maintenance moves from 75% to 80% (150,000 → 160,000 on 200k; 750,000 → 800,000 on 1M).
- The reserve cap is unchanged. Manual `/compact`, overflow recovery and native Codex / Claude CLI policies are unchanged. Request shape is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveCompactionThreshold` already owns the client trigger. It now uses 0.8, and the request-boundary soft trigger calls it (capped by the reserve-based prompt budget, as before) instead of keeping its own `0.9`. One trigger, one owner. Docs that stated 75% or 90% now state 80%, with recomputed examples.

## Evidence

- New test (`request-boundary-compaction.chatgpt-v2.test.ts`, both `native-checkpoint` and `text` variants): on a 200k window the client threshold is 160,000, the boundary sends no compaction request at 159,000, and sends one at 160,000.
  - Red on base (`0828443372be`): the client threshold is 150,000; with that assertion removed, both variants send no request at 160,000 (base triggers at 180,000).
  - Green on this branch.
- Updated threshold tables in the agent-core `shouldCompact` test, `setup.test.ts` and the refusal compaction test (now derived from the owner, not a hard-coded ratio).
- Targeted local run: the touched tests plus every test file that imports a changed source.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert restores 75% / 90%. No stored state, config or contract changes. Blast radius: when every built-in agent session compacts (slightly later for client maintenance, earlier for ChatGPT V2 and warm text compaction).

prs.title: fix(telegram): retry failed draft preview cleanup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram progress streaming now retains a detached preview cleanup target when `deleteMessage` fails. A later `stream.clear()` retries that exact message once, while scheduled/in-flight guards prevent duplicate deletes and successful cleanup releases the retained reply target. Persistent failures stop after two attempts.

Issue #200862 reports that a transient Telegram draft preview deletion failure loses the message ID, so a later clear cannot retry and the stale progress message remains beside the delivered reply. This change keeps cleanup ownership at the draft stream lifecycle where the preview ID is known.

## Evidence

The independent reproduction in [comment #6971892060](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200885#issuecomment-6971892060) drives the shipped transport path instead of mocking `api.deleteMessage`:

- It uses the repository's `useTelegramHttpFixture()`, a real loopback `node:http` server, and a real grammY `Bot` configured with the fixture's `apiRoot`.
- `fixture.bot.api` is passed directly to `createTelegramDraftStream`; requests therefore go through grammY serialization, undici, and HTTP before reaching the fixture.
- The fixture lets `sendMessage` succeed, then returns a real HTTP 400 Bot API response only for `deleteMessage`:
  `Bad Request: message to delete not found`.
- The natural sequence is `update("Preview text")` → `flush()` → wait for the 4-second preview dwell → `clear()` → `clear()`.

The same one-test harness was run against the merge base and this head, changing only `draft-stream.ts`:

**BASE — `3ba6a8402e4^` (without this repair) — FAIL**

```
deleteMessageRequests: [
  { method: "deleteMessage", fields: { chat_id: 123, message_id: 1 } }
]
warnings: [
  "telegram stream preview cleanup failed: Call to 'deleteMessage' failed! (400: Bad Request: message to delete not found)"
]

AssertionError: expected 1 to be 2
```

The preview ID is dropped before detached deletion completes, so the second `clear()` has no target to retry.

**HEAD — `3ba6a8402e44d56eef8697c011fc71e31bf9388a` (this PR) — PASS**

```
allMethods: [ "sendMessage", "deleteMessage", "deleteMessage" ]
deleteMessageRequests: [
  { method: "deleteMessage", fields: { chat_id: 123, message_id: 1 } },
  { method: "deleteMessage", fields: { chat_id: 123, message_id: 1 } }
]
warnings: [
  "telegram stream preview cleanup failed: Call to 'deleteMessage' failed! (400: Bad Request: message to delete not found)",
  "telegram stream preview cleanup failed: Call to 'deleteMessage' failed! (400: Bad Request: message to delete not found)",
  "telegram stream preview cleanup abandoned after 2 attempts (chat=123, message=1)"
]
```

Two `deleteMessage` requests for the same preview ID reach the real transport, and the bounded retry budget then closes the target.

The full standalone test source, commands, and raw trace are available in [the reproduction comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200885#issuecomment-6971892060). The proof uses an isolated loopback Bot API only; it does not contact Telegram production or use a live bot token.

## Other Validation

- `oxfmt --check` passed for both changed files.
- esbuild TypeScript syntax transform passed for both changed files.
- oxlint was attempted but the offline dependency mount lacks `eslint-plugin-solid`; CI should provide that repository plugin.

Closes #200862



## CI context

The current body contains both required authored sections above. The two earlier `PR context and evidence` failures ran on this same head before those sections were present in the workflow event payload. This body update preserves the existing transport evidence and re-triggers the trusted base check for the current body.

prs.title: fix(ui): rich hover cards close while the pointer is on the card
prs.body:
Root cause: ui/src/components/tooltip.ts:193 (base 712ae0338512) tracked rich-content hover on the slotted content wrapper (`.tooltip-rich-content`), not on the visible card surface, so the card's padding and border counted as "outside" and the close delay ran while the pointer was on the card.

Fixes #198048

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the sidebar build card (and other rich hover cards) closes while the pointer is on it, so the build info can't be read or copied. Thanks @changyogpt-code for the report.

## User Impact

Rich hover cards stay open while the pointer is anywhere on the card, including its edge. Plain-text tooltips, keyboard focus behavior and close-on-leave are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`openclaw-tooltip` already keeps rich content open while it is hovered (`handleContentPointerEnter` / `handleContentPointerLeave`). The listeners sat on the inner content wrapper, which is inset from the visible surface by the surface padding and border. Moving the pointer from the trigger onto the card's edge started the close timer and nothing cancelled it, so the card closed under the pointer (300 ms for the build chip). The listeners now sit on the surface itself. Plain-text and `pointerThrough` tooltips keep `pointer-events: none` on the surface, so they get no hover events and still close on leave.

The reporter's suggestion (adding the host to `interactionElements`) would not change this: that list only feeds outside-pointer/focus dismissal, which tooltips turn off. No close-delay change was needed.

## Evidence

Built Control UI served by an isolated built Gateway, Playwright Chromium 156 and WebKit 27.2, real mouse moves: open the identity menu, hover the build chip until the card opens, move up onto the card's lower edge (inside the card), rest 1.5 s, then move into the card.

- Before (base 712ae0338512), both browsers: card closed while the pointer rested on it.
- After, both browsers: card stays open on the edge and in the body, closes after the pointer leaves it.
- Controls, before and after: an icon-only plain sidebar tooltip opens on hover and closes within 150 ms of leaving (surface `pointer-events: none`); keyboard focus on the build item opens the card and moving focus away closes it; the pinned-agent card (the sidebar's other rich hover card) stays open on its edge after the fix.
- `tooltip.test.ts`: the hover-intent test now enters the card surface after leaving the trigger; red on base (`expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0`), green with the fix (40/40).

Screenshots and the observed lines: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/204176#issuecomment-7109380334

Merge risk: two-way door; revert fully undoes it. No state, config or contract change. Blast radius: hover handling of every rich `openclaw-tooltip` card.

prs.title: fix: report a disallowed model instead of switching to a near miss
prs.body:
Closes #204059

## What Problem This Solves

When someone sends `/model xai/grok-4.7` while the gateway's allowlist still only has `xai/grok-4.3`, the chat switches to `grok-4.3` and the reply looks like the requested model was applied. There is no error and no hint that a different model was chosen, so the operator keeps using a model they did not ask for until they notice later.

The trigger is an explicit `provider/model` directive that resolves but is not permitted — most likely right after a model is added to the catalog but before the running gateway's allowlist catches up.

## User Impact

User impact: an explicit `/model provider/model` that is not allowed now reports `Model "..." is not allowed` with the existing instructions for allowing it, instead of silently selecting a different model whose id happens to be one character away.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveModelDirectiveSelection` treats a disallowed explicit ref as a search query: it scores allowed models by prefix/includes matches plus bounded Levenshtein distance. Distance scoring is what lets one version of the same model shadow another.

Typo tolerance stays for bare fragments (`claud` → `claude`), where it is genuinely a search query. For an explicit `provider/model` ref that already resolved, only literal prefix/includes matches may still widen it, so `xai/grok` still finds `grok-4.3` and a one-digit version difference no longer does.

## Evidence

An explicit disallowed ref is reported instead of silently switched; bare-fragment and prefix widening still work.

- Baseline, `8ea0f171` (before the fix): the new regression case failed — `/model xai/grok-4.7` returned `{ provider: "xai", model: "grok-4.3" }` instead of an error.
- With the fix: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection-directive.test.ts` → 14 passed, including the near-miss rejection and the `xai/grok` prefix-widening control.
- Adjacent consumers: `src/auto-reply/reply.directive.parse.test.ts` (35 passed) and `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts` (22 passed), which cover the provider-scoped `fixture-minimax/highspeed` match and the `custom/custom/model` widening.
- Runtime trace through the directive resolver with the real visibility policy owner, allowlist `openai/safe`, `xai/grok-4.3`:

```text
/model xai/grok-4.7 -> Model "xai/grok-4.7" is not allowed. Use /models to list providers, or /models <provider> to list models.
/model xai/grok -> selected xai/grok-4.3
/model xai/grok-4.3 -> selected xai/grok-4.3
```

- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on both changed files: clean; `git diff --check`: clean.

Proof boundary: the trace above invokes the shipped directive resolver with the real allowlist policy but no live Telegram/chat transport, so delivery itself is not re-proven here. The bare-fragment path keeps typo tolerance by design and is unchanged by this PR.
