prs.title: fix(linux): avoid idle watchdog CLI launches
prs.body:
Closes #149253.

## What Problem This Solves

The Linux companion starts several CLI processes on every idle watchdog tick, even while its window is hidden and it already has a healthy Gateway connection. That work continues as long as the companion is open.

## User Impact

The companion checks for pending pairing through its active local Gateway connection. It still shows pairing notifications while hidden and uses existing CLI recovery when the connection drops.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the selected, authenticated Linux route for read-only pairing polls. The watchdog keeps its existing recovery path when the native connection or a pairing request is unavailable. An earlier fix investigated the same issue in #149572.

## Evidence

A source-built Linux companion and real loopback Gateway 2026.11.7 ran on Ubuntu 24.04 arm64. The X11 main window was hidden during both 60-second idle samples. The Gateway and sampler were outside the measured cgroup.

| 60-second idle sample | Upstream `712ae033` | Patched `5ec895b8` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Watchdog CLI invocations | 9 | 0 |
| Companion cgroup CPU time | 13,775.8 ms | 334.8 ms |
| Fraction of one CPU core | 22.94% | 0.56% |

Real device and node pairing requests each produced a desktop notification while the window remained hidden. Neither pairing cycle launched a watchdog CLI command. After stopping the Gateway, the companion attempted CLI recovery and then reconnected the Control UI after the Gateway restarted, with the window still hidden.

`cargo build --locked`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `cargo test --locked --all-targets` passed on Linux. There were 362 passing Rust tests and 9 environment-specific skips. Local validation used a source build on Linux arm64. Release packages and other platforms were outside that run.

### Runtime capture

The same zero-launch assertion was replayed against both captured idle samples. The lifecycle lines are from the candidate run that issued real local pairing requests and stopped and restarted the Gateway.

```text
Upstream 712ae033
{"seconds":60.046,"cgroup_cpu_ms":13775.815,"one_core_pct":22.94,"cli_invocations":{"gateway status --json":3,"nodes pending --json":3,"devices list --json":3}}
AssertionError: Connected hidden companion started watchdog CLI commands: {'gateway status --json': 3, 'nodes pending --json': 3, 'devices list --json': 3}

PR head 5ec895b8
{"seconds":60.053,"cgroup_cpu_ms":334.796,"one_core_pct":0.56,"cli_invocations":{}}
PASS: zero watchdog CLI launches in 60.053 seconds.

PR head 5ec895b8 — lifecycle replay
Device notification arrived via native DBus with the main window hidden.
Node notification arrived via native DBus with the main window hidden.
Both notifications arrived with zero watchdog CLI launches on the native route.
Gateway loss and restart reconnected the Control UI with the main window hidden.
```

prs.title: fix: fill each plugin category preview when installed plugins are hidden
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawHub picks up to eight plugins per category. Control UI then hides installed plugins, including disabled ones. On one real gateway this left Channels with three installable plugins and Models with one, although ClawHub lists more than 200 in each category.

## User Impact

When the registry supplies a continuation cursor, the Plugins page fills short previews with the next installable plugins in the same ranked order (pins first, then downloads). The overview appears immediately. Registries without cursors keep the previous behavior. The [companion ClawHub change](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/4867) is merged; production did not return cursors when checked on November 20.

## Why This Change Was Made

Control UI knows which plugins are installed; ClawHub owns the ranking. The Gateway requests an optional `previewCursor` on each overview category and passes it through `plugins.catalog.browse`. The client asks for the next page only when a category has fewer than eight available entries. Installed IDs never go to ClawHub. Continuations are limited to two concurrent requests, three pages per category, and 32 requests per overview. View all, Search, Featured and Trending keep their existing behavior.

## Evidence

Real Control UI in Chromium against a mocked Gateway and synthetic catalog. The first comparison uses base `5458e9614f17` and the initial fix, with the same fixture, viewport and crop (1440 × 1180, light). This is not a live Control UI–Gateway–ClawHub run.

### Clean comparison

![Before: Channels shows three plugins and Models shows one](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ebcca46c-7b06-4ab4-82ab-3ed1247e429a)

![After: Channels and Models each show eight plugins; Memory is unchanged](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d19dabf7-4918-4842-8d2a-3277c2d5e3e8)

[Annotated before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a66e81e7-35ed-4e35-ac52-161831aaa29e) · [Annotated after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9569b40e-53d6-45aa-9f3c-4b5d627507a6)

### Loading state

A category reserves only the missing card slots while its next page is pending, even if all its initial candidates are installed. Loaded cards stay visible. If the continuation fails or runs out of results, unused slots collapse once and the page keeps the available cards.

[Clean loading state: before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd01e48f-c184-4953-9da8-fedeaf3b3dd5) · [Clean loading state: after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d1070441-5d71-405c-ae8d-09fd5288976f)

![Before the layout repair: Memory begins 320 px above its settled position](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eebd266e-1d13-48ed-adf6-8cbaa91b1243)

![After the layout repair: placeholders reserve the final section positions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6bbcb077-bd14-4ad0-8014-74e4611b4aa5)

Chromium layout-shift scores during two sequential refills. Paired values are for one / zero initial Models. The loading screenshots isolate the layout repair before main's artwork update; post-integration browser checks confirmed stationary headings in all seven cases.

| Width | Before repair | After repair |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 400 px | 0.1237 / 0.1719 | 0 / 0 |
| 820 px | 0.1461 / 0.1846 | 0 / 0 |
| 1280 px | 0.0740 / 0.1114 | 0 / 0 |
| 1440 px | 0.0689 | 0 |

At 1440 px, Memory moved down 320 px before the repair and stayed fixed afterward. At 400 px, reserving two summary lines makes short rows less dense: the settled Models and Memory headings sit about 96 px and 192 px lower, respectively.

### Validation

Published head `b0cab735d344` has the same tree as the tested checkout (`9f2169b1979a`) and includes main `52f945e38e59` with the [settings-search test repair](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/203201).

- 230 Plugins and settings-search unit tests and all 34 bundled Chromium tests passed, including both Plugins route request budgets. Repository changed-file checks passed. The category schema keeps its public export; six cursor boundary cases cover omission, valid strings, invalid type, and length limits.
- The performance comparison against integrated main passed: startup JavaScript remained 90,165 B gzip across three requests. Total raw CSS fell from 1,784,945 B to 1,784,838 B (−107 B). No budget was raised.
- The earlier integration also passed the catalog (37), Gateway plugins (32), and management-service catalog (39) tests. The seven sparse-shelf cases recorded unchanged geometry after redundant responsive visibility rules were removed.
- Live verification is separate: the production overview returned zero cursors across 22 categories at the November 20 check. The browser evidence above uses a mocked Gateway.

prs.title: fix(sessions): exclude hidden coordination and failed children from unread
prs.body:
## Problem

A session went unread with nothing new to read. Example (synthetic): a subagent sends its parent 15 progress messages with `sessions_send`. Each one starts a hidden parent turn that answers only the child. Nothing appears in the parent chat, but every turn lights the parent's unread dot.

Cause: `deriveSessionUnread` compared `lastReadAt` with `max(lastInteractionAt, lastActivityAt)`.
- `lastInteractionAt` is the idle-reset clock. Every non-system turn moves it, hidden turns included.
- Agent-command post-run moved `lastActivityAt` on every non-internal-event run. Unlike the run-end lifecycle writer, it did not skip hidden subagent coordination turns.

Second problem: failed or timed-out hidden subagent runs stayed unread for good. Opening the parent acknowledged its hidden runs but skipped failed ones, and hidden runs have no row of their own to open.

## Change

- `deriveSessionUnread` reads only `lastActivityAt` (plus the manual `markedUnreadAt`). It no longer reads the idle clock.
- Post-run `touchActivity` now also skips subagent coordination provenance (`isSubagentCoordinationInputProvenance`), the same check the run-end lifecycle writer already applies through `controlUiVisible`. A hidden coordination turn no longer stamps activity, and it no longer clears a snooze.
- Auto-reply `initSessionState` stamps `lastActivityAt` for an inbound non-system message, with the same value as the existing `lastInteractionAt` stamp. Channel sessions (for example Telegram) depended on the idle clock for unread, so they still go unread when a message arrives. Internal wakes do not.
- Background and scheduled results committed into a conversation (`commitBackgroundResultToSession`, used by confirmed cross-conversation messages and cron results) stamp `lastActivityAt` with the same message timestamp as `lastInteractionAt`.
- The sidebar tree counts a hidden subagent run toward its parent's unread count only while reading the parent can acknowledge it (`isAcknowledgeableHiddenRun`). Failed and timed-out hidden runs no longer hold the parent dot. They are not acknowledged, so their failure stays on the child card.
- Docs: `docs/web/control-ui/sessions-and-sidebar.md`.

Production line delta (excluding tests and docs): **+27 / −15 (net +12)**.

## What the user sees

- A parent that only answers its child's `sessions_send` stays read.
- A visible reply, or a channel message arriving, still marks the session unread.
- Failed hidden child runs no longer keep a parent's dot or count lit after you open the parent.

## Review notes

- Round 2 found (both fixed): (a) background and scheduled results stamped only the idle clock, so they would stop marking the destination unread; (b) the first head acknowledged failed hidden runs when the parent opened, which stamps `lastReadAt` and hides the failure on the child card. Now failed runs stay unacknowledged and are left out of the parent count instead.
- Local ClawSweeper round 1 found that `openclaw agent --local` has no Gateway lifecycle persister. The first head deleted the post-run `lastActivityAt` write, so visible replies from that path stopped marking unread. Fixed by keeping the write and gating it on coordination provenance instead.

## Not done here (original scope, unfinished)

The goal was that unread follows visible content: a turn that appends nothing visible never marks the session unread. This PR covers hidden coordination turns and failed hidden children only. Unread still follows run visibility, not appended content, so a Control UI–visible run that ends in `NO_REPLY` or a quiet heartbeat still marks the session unread. Fixing that needs one owner that decides from transcript content (the run end has no visible-output fact today). Tracked in #204164.

## Evidence

- `src/shared/session-unread.test.ts` (new) drives the real run-end lifecycle patch and `initSessionState` through `deriveSessionUnread`:
  - hidden turn (idle clock moved, run not visible) → read; visible run end → unread. **Red on base, green on head.**
  - inbound channel message → unread; internal wake → read. Green on both (guards the auto-reply stamp).
- `src/agents/agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts`: through `agentCommand`, an operator turn stamps activity and a child's `sessions_send` to its requester does not. **Red on base, green on head.**
- `ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-tree.test.ts`: an unread finished hidden run counts toward its parent; failed and timed-out ones do not. **Red on base, green on head.**
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/destination-completion.test.ts`: a delivered cron result stamps `lastActivityAt` on the destination. **Red on base, green on head.**
- Real-Gateway Control UI E2E (throwaway; only the model provider is scripted, while Gateway, `sessions_spawn`, `sessions_send` and sidebar are real): a parent spawns a visible child; the operator moves to another session; the child sends the parent a progress message with `sessions_send`; the parent's hidden turn replies only to the child (the child stays running, so no completion wake). Assertion: the parent sidebar row has no unread dot.
  - Base: **fails**, 1 dot. Head: **passes**, 0 dots. Screenshots in the PR comment.

prs.title: fix: MiniMax Talk calls the global server for China-region accounts
prs.body:
Closes #204124

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: with a MiniMax account from the China region, Talk replies are sent to MiniMax's global server instead of the China one, together with that account's token. Normal text-to-speech on the same setup uses the right server.

## User Impact

User impact: Talk now uses the same MiniMax host as normal text-to-speech. People on the global host, and anyone who sets a MiniMax `baseUrl` or `MINIMAX_API_HOST`, see no change. If you have a China `minimax-portal` host configured and no explicit TTS host, Talk moves to that host, which is where normal text-to-speech already goes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The MiniMax provider docs say that when no TTS host is configured, OpenClaw reuses the `minimax-portal` host. Normal text-to-speech does that. Talk built its settings without the OpenClaw config, so it could not see the portal host, fell back to the global default, and then stored that default as if you had chosen it. Talk now passes the config along, like normal text-to-speech. An explicit Talk or TTS `baseUrl` still wins.

## Evidence

**Shipped Gateway, then upgrade.** I installed the released `openclaw@2026.11.7` from npm in its own folder, stored a (made-up) `minimax-portal` token with `openclaw models auth paste-token`, pointed `models.providers.minimax-portal.baseUrl` at a local stand-in for the China host, and started the Gateway. I called `tts.speak` and `talk.speak` with `openclaw gateway call`. Then I stopped it, ran this branch's `openclaw doctor --repair --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions --yes` on the same state (the arguments the updater uses), started this branch's built Gateway and made the same calls. Outside DNS was cut, so the global host was recorded but never contacted.

| Host settings | Call | 2026.11.7 Gateway | same state, this branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| none | `tts.speak` | portal host, audio returned | portal host, audio returned |
| none | `talk.speak` | **tried `api.minimax.io`, failed** | portal host, audio returned |
| explicit TTS host | `tts.speak` and `talk.speak` | explicit TTS host, audio returned | same |
| explicit Talk host | `tts.speak` | portal host, audio returned | same |
| explicit Talk host | `talk.speak` | explicit Talk host, audio returned | same |

The `tts` and `talk` config blocks and the portal host were identical before and after the upgrade in all three cases.

**Tests.** `speech-provider.test.ts` now checks the Talk host: portal host when nothing is set, and an explicit TTS or Talk host still wins. The portal case fails on the old code. Net +17 test lines.

**Checks.** Type check (extensions and their tests), `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, test-lines ratchet.

prs.title: fix: show degraded history only on the selected branch
prs.body:
Closes #204060.

## What Problem This Solves

After rewinding a conversation to before a lossy compaction, `/status` can still say that its history is degraded. It keeps the warning from the branch the user left.

## User Impact

The warning clears on a branch that has no lossy compaction and returns when the user switches back to a branch that does.

## Why This Change Was Made

The history cut derives the warning from the selected transcript path before committing session metadata. Both the database and incognito paths use their existing navigation data. The database reads only compaction payloads on the selected path, one at a time.

## Evidence

- The SQLite and incognito regressions both failed against the base with the degradation flag still set after rewinding.
- 80 focused tests passed across the session stores, Gateway history methods, and status rendering on Node 24.22.1. The expanded SQLite regression passed separately with an added check that rewinding to a point still after the compaction keeps the warning.
- Core typecheck, focused lint/format, and the affected Markdown check passed. A separate Codex review checked the final commit and the active/legacy history paths.
- Local verification covered SQLite and incognito storage. PostgreSQL and external messaging platforms were outside the local checks.

### Live Gateway and stable-data upgrade

The replay compared the [published OpenClaw 2026.11.7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.11.7) (`e31bbf056de3`) and this PR's exact head `94945647ef4dfb8ff6ada4d37635e59f546f3601` on macOS arm64 with Node 24.22.1. The stable Gateway wrote two ordinary conversation turns with a deterministic loopback provider. The test then seeded one synthetic lossy compaction and its follow-up offline through the published release's native SQLite transcript writer. Both runs began from independent, byte-identical copies of that stopped stable database and configuration.

`gateway call sessions.rewind` and `gateway call sessions.branches.switch` went over the real Gateway. The `/status` check used the shipped TUI Gateway client to send the command with `chat.send` and read its final chat event. `/status` made zero provider requests.

```text
latest stable 2026.11.7 (e31bbf0)
/status before                 Compactions: 0 · degraded history (details may be lost)
/status after rewind           Compactions: 0 · degraded history (details may be lost)

PR head 9494564 on the same stable data
/status before                 Compactions: 0 · degraded history (details may be lost)
sessions.rewind                accepted; original first turn restored
/status after rewind           [no Compactions line]
sessions.branches.switch       accepted; exact compacted-branch message IDs restored
/status after branch switch    Compactions: 0 · degraded history (details may be lost)
```

On the candidate, the original session ID, all four old message IDs, label, configured model, and read-only permission persisted. A new ordinary turn also appended its message and reply to the upgraded SQLite session. `PRAGMA quick_check` returned `ok` after both Gateways shut down. Every original config value survived. The candidate added `agents.entries`, `meta`, `skills`, and `wizard` keys. Stable's older rewind path rotated its session ID, so the stable run documents the upgrade source and observed release behavior. This replay used fixture text and a loopback model response, with no live channel or paid model involved.

AI disclosure: developed and verified using Codex (GPT-6.2 Sol, xhigh).

prs.title: fix(voice-call): pace interruptible prepared statements
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An agent calling someone to deliver a long prepared statement can generate audio faster than the telephone plays it. The bounded queue then overflows and closes the stream. The statement must also remain interruptible: the listener should be able to ask a question, continue the unfinished statement, or stop it entirely.

## User Impact

This draft adds paced delivery for OpenAI response-mode prepared openings and later `speak` requests, retaining the interrupted passage for resume. The `say` steering route keeps its existing 500-character limit. Caller speech is not discarded for the duration of a managed statement. Resume repeats the last unacknowledged short passage rather than skipping unheard words; it is not word-exact seek.

**Not ready to merge:** the latest human test resumed and progressed, but also showed unexpected caller-speech detections and unwanted continuation during caller exchanges. A clean human interruption → answer → explicit continuation → complete reading → stop test remains outstanding. The earlier uninterruptible eight-passage success does not validate this revision. Production is unchanged.

Other providers, short openings and continuous/native-delegation paths retain their existing behavior. Arbitrarily long spontaneous model replies are not covered: the host must have prepared text to split. No configuration migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

One plugin-local coordinator supplies bounded, sentence-aware passages and waits for generation completion plus carrier playback acknowledgement before advancing. Caller speech pauses delivery; unique marks prevent cleared/stale acknowledgements from skipping the interrupted passage. The call-bound `openclaw_statement` tool can resume or stop, but cannot start or replace a statement: only the host supplies complete prepared text. Explicit stop, continuity reset and teardown discard it.

The initial revision exposed model `start` as well, and broadly instructed the model to use the tool for prepared statements. A human test then logged repeated tool calls before reading audio. The follow-up removes that recursive route and clarifies that only the quoted Answer text—not internal playback directions—is spoken. Repeating full session instructions inside each passage was also removed. The rejected-start regression attempts replacement while paused and verifies that resume retains the original passage.

The previous proposal to suppress early caller input is withdrawn. There is no longer a request to approve discarding caller speech throughout a long statement. Normal code-owner review and CI requirements remain.

The existing six-line package-build compatibility correction remains: bundle the pure SHA-256 helper for declared supported hosts lacking its SDK subpath. Retire that alias when the declared host floor supplies it. The prepared-statement coordinator is scoped to the OpenAI response-created/done and silent tool-result contract; it is not claimed as a generic continuous-provider capability. Existing overflow protection stays enabled.

## Evidence

- **Deterministic playback:** paced completion, pre-ready caller input, interruption, answer playback before resume, repeating the unacknowledged passage, late cleared marks, explicit stop, later host speech, teardown, and unchanged short/continuous behavior are covered. The 180-second production-composition replay at 4x generation speed still distinguishes unsegmented overflow from paced delivery.
- **Follow-up tests:** 10 passed / 2 files (`realtime-reading` and `realtime-reading-overflow`). After moving the rejected-replacement assertion into the paused-state scenario, the final reading group passed 8 / 8 (9.31 s wrapper; Vitest 7.05 s). Earlier implementation had 48 focused tests / 4 files; these are bounded local results, not broad exact-head CI.
- **Checks:** targeted strict typecheck, changed-file type-aware lint, formatting, docs lint and commit guards passed. Canonical plugin package built; isolated Gateway reload verified the exact compiled candidate path and source digest. No production deployment occurred.
- **Review:** autoreview found the earlier provider-eligibility P2, addressed by restricting registration/coordination to the OpenAI non-native response path. A subsequent scoped review of host-only initiation found no actionable P0–P2 issues. The later prompt clarification has real-model evidence below, not a claim of an additional independent review.
- **Real model, no phone:** an OpenAI realtime probe generated audio, answered the train-colour question, invoked resume, reached the final phrase, and invoked stop on a later statement. It checked that playback directions were not spoken. Caller interruption and carrier acknowledgements were simulated, so this is not telephone timing or human-audibility proof. Earlier probe iterations caught spoken wrapper text and an overlapping probe turn; these were corrected before the final probe.
- **Latest human-answered call (21 November, ~23:29–23:33 UTC):** the corrected candidate started the reading, paused, handled conversation, resumed the retained passage on a continuation request, and progressed through multiple further passages. Unexpected input detections and later unwanted resumptions prevented a clean pass. Possible acoustic echo is only a hypothesis, not an established root cause. The test was ended; full delivery and a caller-directed permanent stop on this revision remain unproven. No more human calls are planned tonight.

The immediate next work is to diagnose the unexpected input/continuation behavior from this call and add the appropriate boundary regression before another human test. Keep the PR draft.

Hosted validation is not complete. The latest PR-context check rejected the previous body because its validation section was titled “Verification” rather than the required “Evidence”; this body corrects that presentation issue. Earlier broad CI was `action_required` with zero jobs, and the author has read-only upstream permissions. prs.title: fix(ui): keep a reader's scroll when an older row remeasures
prs.body:
Reading upward through loaded chat history no longer snaps back. A row measurement that lands between a scroll and its scroll event can no longer undo that scroll.

Part of #204008.

## Problem

`chat-history-reading-stability.e2e.test.ts` (chromium, 1280 px) failed on scheduled run 45205190078 with `visible messages must only move with the reader: expected [ 24 ] to deeply equal []`. The test's own frame trace shows the cause:

| Frame | Before | Reader requested | Painted | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 24 | 62737 | 62713 | 62691 | A row above the reader remeasured (−22 px); the correction is right (residual 0.39 px). |
| 25 | 62691 | 62667 | **62691** | The reader's scroll is undone: residual 24 px. |

`TranscriptReaderAnchor.landSize` returned `true` for a measured row above the reader when the reader holds no native offset. Virtual-core then writes the adjustment itself as `getScrollOffset() + adjustments`. `getScrollOffset()` is virtual-core's cached offset, and it updates only on the next scroll event. When the reader scrolls and a measurement lands before that event, virtual-core writes the old offset (62691) plus a sub-pixel delta over the reader's new position (62667).

This file has failed intermittently on 8 of the last 10 scheduled runs (shard 8).

## Solution

Before `landSize` hands an above-reader correction to virtual-core, it calls the offset observer's existing `syncNativeOffset`, which publishes the native `scrollTop` into virtual-core. Virtual-core then adds the delta to the reader's real position. `syncNativeOffset` does nothing when the offsets already match, and it keeps virtual-core's end-clamp retry (`chat-transcript-scroll-ownership.test.tsx` "preserves reader policy when row measurement clamps a positive adjustment to the end").

The first version of this PR routed the correction through `owedScroll` instead. CI showed that this drops the end-clamp retry, so this version keeps virtual-core's adjustment and fixes only its stale base.

## Evidence

- `chat-history-reading-stability.e2e.test.ts`: 4/4 pass locally (this file also passes locally on `main`; the failure needs CI timing, so the trace above is the reproduction).
- The 11 test files that import `chat-transcript-reader-anchor`, `chat-transcript-virtualizer-host` or `chat-transcript-offset-observer`, plus `chat-transcript-scroll-ownership.test.tsx`: 218 of 219 pass. The one failure (`chat-message-reactions.browser.test.tsx`, hover picker at 320 px) passes 4/4 alone both on `main` and on this branch.

## Not fixed here

The same run also failed the webkit 390 px case with a different symptom: after `Home`, the older history page was never requested (`messageCount: 30`, `prefixCommitted: false`). CI kept no trace or geometry for that case. It needs its own investigation.

prs.title: feat(msteams): send private and shared channel files to the channel's own SharePoint site
prs.body:
Closes #185926

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: bots cannot send files in Microsoft Teams private or shared channels unless an operator configures a single central `sharePointSiteId`, which exposes every private channel's files to that site's members and still shows "request access" to channel members.

## User Impact

User impact: in private and shared channels, file sends now land on that channel's own SharePoint site, where exactly the channel's members already have access, and the file card opens without extra permissions. No organization-wide sharing link is created for those files. Standard channels, group chats and explicit `sharePointSiteId` keep their current behavior. No new Graph permissions and no config changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Builds on #189339. Teams keeps a private/shared channel's site membership in sync with the channel, so the channel's own site is the only upload target that preserves the channel audience. For a non-standard `membershipType`, the resolver reads `GET /teams/{groupId}/channels/{channelId}/filesFolder`, then `GET /drives/{driveId}?$select=sharePointIds` (drive resources spell it `sharePointIds`; driveItems use `sharepointIds`), and builds the site ID `{hostname},{siteId},{webId}`. Results are cached per account, tenant, bot, team and channel, like the team-site cache.

`resolveMSTeamsSharePointSiteId` now returns `{ siteId, memberScoped }`. Member-scoped uploads skip `createLink`: the organization link that channel sends create would let anyone in the tenant holding its URL read a private-channel file, and channel membership already grants access through the file card's `webDavUrl`. An incomplete drive response fails closed before upload.

## Evidence

- **Focused tests:** `vitest` msteams config, 92 files / 943 tests pass. New cases run the real send paths (proactive and reply) against stubbed Graph `fetch`: private and shared channels upload to the channel site, never call `/groups/.../sites/root` or `createLink`, and cache the channel site (one `filesFolder` call across two sends); member-scoped uploads create no link; incomplete `sharePointIds` fails closed.
- **Static:** `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main`: typecheck (extensions and extension tests), lint, plugin boundaries and the other guards pass. The dead-export scan fails only on `src/gateway/control-ui-session-pr-prepared-read.ts` (`retireControlUiSessionPrState`), unrelated to this change.

### Real behavior proof (production)

Multi-team production deployment, private channel, `sharePointSiteId` absent.

**Before** (#189339's behavior; private channels rejected). Gateway file log, redacted:

```
14:00:01Z [msteams] received message — text: "send me a CSV with 3 rows of test data"
          conversation: 19:<private-channel-id>@thread.tacv2;messageid=<id>
14:00:01Z [msteams] dispatching to agent
14:02:57Z [tools] tool_call failed: msteams file send failed: Automatic SharePoint site discovery
          supports standard channels only. Set channels.msteams.sharePointSiteId to upload to a specific site.
14:03:02Z [msteams] dispatch complete — counts: { tool: 0, block: 0, final: 1 }
```

The user received a text-only reply. No file reached the channel.

**After** (this change, backported onto the deployed release). Same private channel, first file send after a gateway restart (empty cache):

```
11:24:17Z [msteams] received message — text: "send me a CSV with 4 rows of test data"
11:24:17Z [msteams] dispatching to agent — sessionKey: agent:main:msteams:channel:19:<private-channel-id>…
11:24:36Z [msteams:send] sent native file card — fileName: <report> 1.csv
```

Graph check after the send (bot application credentials):

- `<folder>/<report> 1.csv` (created 11:24:35Z) sits on the private channel's own site (`/sites/<team>-<private-channel>`).
- Item permissions are only the channel site's Owners / Members / Visitors groups. No `organization` link.
- The parent team site has no entry for this send.
- The requester opened the file card from the channel.

During rollout, the first build read `sharepointIds` from the drive and failed closed ("incomplete SharePoint IDs") without uploading anything; Graph returns `sharePointIds` on drive resources. A later build still created the organization link; Graph showed it on the item, which is why member-scoped uploads now skip `createLink`.

### Access check (member, non-member, removal)

Same private channel. Each person opened the file's direct document URL in a browser, signed in with their own work account. Times are UTC.

| Step | Who | File | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Channel member | `<report-1>.csv`, sent by the bot | Opens (09:14) |
| 2 | Owner of the parent team, not a channel member. Also tried with their admin account | `<report-1>.csv` | Access denied (09:16) |
| 3 | The step 1 member, removed from the channel about 6 minutes earlier | `<report-1>.csv` | "You need access" (09:24) |
| 4 | Bot sends a new file in the same channel. No gateway restart, so the channel site comes from the cache | `<report-2>.csv` | Lands on the channel site (09:23). Inherits the library permissions; no sharing link |
| 5 | The removed member | `<report-2>.csv` | "You need access" (09:26) |
| 6 | A channel owner | `<report-2>.csv` | Opens (09:25) |

The removed user left the channel site's Members group without any bot action (checked 09:18). Access follows Teams channel membership.

Before step 1, an organization link on `<report-1>.csv` was deleted. A manual "Copy link" in the Teams client had created it, not the bot. After that, both files grant access only to the channel site's Owners, Members and Visitors groups (checked through SharePoint REST as a channel owner).

prs.title: refactor: drop mid-request authority re-checks in gateway operator/plugin/MCP App paths, skill library, reclaim and channel reads (R6d part 3)
prs.body:
## Problem

OpenClaw checks authority once, when work starts (AGENTS.md "Choose good compromises"). Gateway operator, approval, plugin and MCP App paths, the skill library, worker reclaim and channel message reads still re-read a permission, role, scope, trust or config mid-request and refused started work with "authority changed" / "authority is no longer active/current". Other checks in the same files are valid Stop, run-close or data fences whose text claimed authority.

## Change

R6d part 3, first half (split rule). Each check was classified with one test: can it fire when only a permission, approval or config changes while nothing about the run or data changes?

- Yes → deleted, with its plumbing.
- No (Stop, run close, disconnect, data fence) → kept, reworded to say what ended and the next step.
- Start-time checks (admission, made before work begins) stay.

| Site | Old message | Kind | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skills/library/store-access.ts` `assertCurrent` | Skill library authority changed | mixed: config roles, role subject and scopes re-read + `authority.assertCurrent()` (run close, claim loss, disconnect) | role/scope/config compares deleted; Stop (`authority.assertCurrent`) and the database admission fence kept |
| `skills/library/store-access.ts` `read` | Profile authority changed during library access / Skill library profile authority changed | profile-row change (includes role) after admission | refusals deleted; a profile change now only keeps the reply out of the read cache (no stale cached role) |
| `server-worker-placement-reclaim.ts` | grant callback refusal (`assertWorkerGrant`) | grant re-check during reclaim preparation | deleted; lifetime + target-generation fences kept |
| `worker-environments/placement-dispatch.ts` `reclaimOnce` | Gateway recovery disabled by required worker profile | config re-read inside the repeated source check | checked once at entry; `reclaimSource`/preparation get the existing `assertWorkerLifetime` branch |
| `channels/plugins/message-action-dispatch.ts` | Plugin X read/alias authority is no longer active | registration lifetime + `trustedOfficialInstall` downgrade | trust term moved to capture time in `plugins/registry-registrars-network.ts` (admission); registration fence kept: "…was reloaded during the read. Retry the action." |
| `shared/channel-read-authority.ts` | Channel read authority is no longer active. | Stop (closed read scope) | reworded: "Channel read ended. Retry the action." |
| `agent-runtime-identity-token.ts` | agent runtime approval authority is no longer active | run/claim fence | reworded |
| `device-revocation.ts` | Gateway caller authority is no longer active. | mixed | permission callback re-check deleted; closed-owner / released-lifetime fences kept |
| `exec-approval-authority.ts` + `exec-approval-manager.ts` | approval resolver authority is no longer active | mixed | repeated caller assertion and its plumbing deleted; store/binding fences kept, reworded |
| `exec-approval-resolution-authority.ts` | approval standing grant authority is no longer active | Stop (run abort) + tool-owner data | reworded |
| `operator-approval-session-events.ts` | Operator approval replay authority is no longer current | mixed | reviewer-permission and scope re-reads deleted; runtime, connection and device fences kept, reworded |
| `operator-invocation-authority.ts` | Gateway caller authority is no longer active. | mixed | caller-permission re-checks deleted; signals and context identity kept |
| `operator-role-policy.ts` | OpenClaw ID membership authority changed | authority | membership re-reads for admitted runs deleted; admission checks kept, reworded |
| `operator-run-authority.ts` `prepareGatewayOperatorRunAuthority` | Gateway caller authority is no longer active. | admission (before the run starts) | kept: "Gateway request could not start. Reconnect and try again." |
| `question-manager.ts` | the question's resolution authority is no longer active | Stop / question lifecycle | reworded |
| `openclaw-id/node-pairing.ts` | OpenClaw ID node authority changed | mixed | membership check moved to admission; connect-policy callback kept (opaque, mixes lifecycle), reworded |
| `openclaw-id/tunnel-principal.ts` | OpenClaw ID membership authority changed | admission / recovery | reworded |
| `server-plugin-github-account.ts`, `server-plugin-user-profile.ts`, `server-plugin-session-facts.ts` (`callerAuthorityError`) | … caller authority is no longer active | request lifetime | reworded (helper has callers outside this PR) |
| `server-plugin-session-facts.ts` `assertAuthority` | Session read authority changed; retry the request | mixed | caller/config/policy/access/profile re-checks deleted; projection replacement fence kept, reworded |
| `server-plugin-in-process-session-read.ts` | Session read authority changed before inference. | mixed | repeated visibility authorization deleted; projection/session/store/generation fences kept, reworded |
| `server-plugin-in-process-authority.ts` | Gateway continuation authority is no longer active | Stop (release, cancellation, Gateway lifetime) | reworded |
| `server-plugins-node-runtime.ts` | Plugin Gateway runtime authority is no longer current. | mixed | plugin permission/config reader deleted; lifecycle signal, binding and run/claim checks kept, reworded |
| `mcp-app-form-resources.ts` | Form upload workspace authority changed; MCP App runtime is unavailable | data fence; config (apps disabled) mid-operation | workspace/session fence reworded; mid-operation enabled/upload-policy re-checks deleted (upload admission kept) |
| `mcp-app-host-files.ts` | App file workspace authority changed; 3 subscription "authority changed" closes | mixed | permission/config/grant re-checks and revocation-retention plumbing deleted; connection, requester, view, session, workspace fences kept, reworded |
| `mcp-app-tool-approval.ts` | MCP App tool approval authority changed | authority (post-consumption re-check) | deleted; admission, decision and allow-once consumption kept |

Deleted tests (they asserted a mid-request permission refusal): skill library role change after preparation (`skill-library-authoring`, `selection-authority`), reclaim "caller changes at transaction/commit completion admission", message-action registry `trust-downgrade` row, form upload "upload policy"/"apps disabled", host-file synchronous grant revocation, fork "session visibility", linked-owner membership revocation for an admitted run, replay waiting-client scope revocation and revoked-requester variant, device-retention permission revocation. Stop and data-fence tests keep their conditions; only their expected text changed. The 21 channel read assertions that matched the generic "no longer active" text were first split so each matches its own producer.

Lifetime-check ratchet: 0 counted strings in every touched production file. `config/session-identity-allowlist.txt` pruned.

Accepted edge cases:
- A started skill-library read or prepared selection keeps its result if the profile role changes; the next request admits the new role. The worker-side publication check is unchanged.
- A started reclaim finishes even if the caller's grant is revoked; Stop and session lifetime still end it.
- A channel read that started keeps going if the plugin install trust drops; the next read is admitted with the new trust.

## Not in this PR (part 4)

- Remaining `src/gateway/**` string files: `agent-turn/agent-run-user-turn.ts`, `channel-avatar-http.ts`, `cron-creator-authority-grant.ts`, `cron-stream-sandbox-authority.ts`, `desktop/observe-bridge.ts`, `factory-github-proof.ts`, `http-auth-user-profile.ts`, `human-mention-policy.ts`, `managed-image-session-read.ts`, `mention-inbox.ts`, `node-claude-skill-runtime.ts`, `node-mcp-elicitation.ts`, `openai-compatible-agent-run.ts`, `remote-control-ui-ingress.ts`, `repository-dispatch.ts`, `repository-integration-identity.ts`, `server-node-event-source.ts`, `server/ws-connection/authenticated-request-dispatch.ts`, `server/ws-connection/connect-publication-transport.ts`, `server/ws-origin-policy.ts`, `session-sharing-read.ts`, `skill-library-session.ts`, `talk/client-run-authority.ts`.
- Reclaim: `sessions.reclaim` passes the unsplit `SessionMutationAuthorization.assertCurrent` (grant + session lifetime) and Move's composed callback reads config policy + signal. Removing the grant there needs the producer to expose its lifetime part (R6z type change).
- Approval replay visibility (`canAccessInvitedApprovalSession`) mixes session-sharing data with role/scope reads; node-pairing's connect-policy callback mixes lifecycle and policy. Both kept.

## User impact

A started read, reclaim, approval replay, plugin or MCP App request is no longer refused because a role, scope, trust or config changed mid-request; the change applies to the next request. Stop, disconnect, plugin reload and data changes still end work, with messages that say what ended and what to do next.

## Evidence

- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test`: pass. oxfmt and oxlint on changed files: clean. Lifetime-check ratchet: 0 counted strings in changed production files; session-identity ratchet OK after prune (6257 → 6239 pins).
- `ocx test` (continue-on-failure) on 204 files: every touched test file, every test importing a changed source or test-support file except the 3 widest modules (`operator-role-policy`, `operator-run-authority`, `tunnel-principal`: 200 importers; CI runs them), plus every test pinning a changed message. OURS reds fixed and rerun. Remaining local reds are not ours: `mcp-http.async-scope`, `agent.test` (2), `question.communication`, `question.recovery` (base-red, see earlier R6 PRs), `server.sessions.create.lifecycle` requester row + `server.sessions.create.durability` (rewritten on main by #203560), `users-personal-file` text (open #204110).
- Production vs `main`: 27 files, +120/−228.
- CI round 1: OURS = 6 text/permission test pins (message-action registry + alias, Telegram history plugin row, skill-library role/alias seed rows, runtime-llm replaced caller), fixed in `8519761ded`. Round 2: only not-ours reds (see the Maintainer override comment).
- Local ClawSweeper review: round 1 `6db0ccd7d01d` and round 2 `8519761ded13` both "patch is correct", no findings.
- One-admission E2E on `6db0ccd7d01d` (production is the same at `8519761ded13`; that diff is test-only): verdict pass; R.running-turn-finishes, Q.queued-input-refused-visibly and S.stop-cancels all pass. `verdict.json` and `results.jsonl` are kept in the proof directory.

prs.title: fix(update): keep updates working after read-only database reads
prs.body:
Closes #204078

## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, opening a read-only SQLite connection during an update's Doctor step can fail the update with “SQLite migration source changed after update capture.” A status reader, backup tool, or database browser can trigger this without writing anything. Users then need `openclaw update status` and `openclaw update repair`.

## User Impact

Read-only readers no longer count as database writes after a WAL checkpoint. A real change to committed content or file identity still refuses migration. This fix is in the candidate's Doctor, so it applies to first hops from published v2026.11.7; the installed updater needs no backport. No schema, stored-field, fingerprint-format, option, or lock changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

A checkpoint can leave an empty WAL with a nonzero shared-memory index counter and commit checksum. A read-only reopen rebuilds that disposable index and clears both values while preserving database bytes and identity. The existing rebuilt-index equivalent covered only nonempty WALs.

Extend that existing equivalent to a reader rebuild completed between capture and source verification. The equivalent still includes the original file identity and committed-content hash. The same-observation guard is unchanged. No new state, hook, retry, or reader lock. Existing native-generation and migration tests keep real-write refusal, including a checkpointed retained index followed by a reader rebuild.

Accepted edge: a reader inside the guard's own observation window can still cause a rare, visible refusal; recover with `openclaw update status`, then `openclaw update repair`. The separate SHM-absent/coarse-metadata rapid-write window in #204101 exists on main and is unchanged here; its fixture and evidence limits are recorded in that issue.

## Evidence

- Controlled original Windows failure: `8c73a489-9f22-4a56-936a-81b2f33182ce`; one read-only connection during Doctor. Clean no-reader control succeeded.
- Native Windows probe: counter `03000000` → `00000000`, checksum `0443775e300eeaf7` → `0000000000000000`, WAL length 0, with identical database SHA-256/device/inode/birthtime. Linux and macOS show the same transition; real-write controls change database hashes.
- Owning migration regression fails on unchanged main at the exact source-changed guard.
- Formatting/lint passed on the narrowed head. An earlier local test attempt failed collection because concurrent packaging rewrote `package.json`; that was setup contamination, not a product verdict.
- Narrowed head `57dc1a001943` built and passed canonical tarball validation on isolated AWS. First-hop archive SHA-256: `9e4fb9cc0fcef5f0e3bcfff94e87c75ebde704e73d41ecc2a1f4ee0ab5856714`. Its build ID remains bound to that exact commit. Node/Bun CI write controls and the serial focused consumer run are still pending.
- Final-head local ClawSweeper review (`4ff5ebdd239a..57dc1a001943`) completed: patch correct, zero findings, security cleared. The offline review did not load execution receipts.
- Windows reader-success and checkpointed-write-refusal first hops remain unproven. This PR is ready for hosted CI/review, but is not merge-ready until those explicit proof gaps are closed.

prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: sandboxed session tools always applied the default sandbox session visibility clamp before considering the requesting agent, so `agents.list[].sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility` could be configured but was not consistently honored.
- Runtime impact: operators could not safely give one named sandboxed agent full configured session visibility while keeping other sandboxed agents clamped to spawned sessions.
- Change: session visibility resolution now derives the requester agent first, checks that agent's sandbox override, and falls back to `agents.defaults.sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility` only when no per-agent override exists.
- Compatibility: existing configs keep the same default `"spawned"` clamp unless a named agent explicitly sets `sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility`.

## User-Visible Behavior

New optional per-agent config:

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "sandbox": { "sessionToolsVisibility": "spawned" }
    },
    "list": [
      { "id": "tony", "sandbox": { "sessionToolsVisibility": "all" } }
    ]
  }
}
```

For sandboxed session tools, precedence is:

```text
agents.list[].sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility
agents.defaults.sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility
default spawned clamp
```

## Security Impact

- Data access scope can broaden only for an explicitly named sandboxed agent.
- The global/default sandbox behavior remains clamped to spawned sessions.
- Existing `tools.sessions.visibility` and `tools.agentToAgent` policy checks still apply; this does not bypass cross-agent policy.
- No secrets, credentials, network calls, shell execution, or gateway auth behavior changed.

## Files in This PR

- `CHANGELOG.md` - records the user-facing runtime/config behavior change.
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md` - documents per-agent sandbox session visibility.
- `docs/gateway/config-tools.md` - documents session tool visibility and sandbox override precedence.
- `docs/tools/multi-agent-sandbox-tools.md` - documents multi-agent sandbox session tool behavior.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts` - wires requester identity into session tool construction.
- `src/agents/tools/session-status-tool.ts` - applies requester-aware sandbox visibility to `session_status`.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-access.ts` - centralizes requester-aware sandbox visibility resolution.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-helpers.ts` - forwards requester context through shared session helper wiring.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-history-tool.ts` - applies requester-aware visibility to `sessions_history`.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-list-tool.ts` - applies requester-aware visibility to `sessions_list`.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.ts` - applies requester-aware visibility to `sessions_send`.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.session-status.test.ts` - covers requester-aware `session_status` behavior.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions-visibility.test.ts` - covers tool-factory wiring for the override.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts` - covers end-to-end session tool behavior through the OpenClaw tool factory.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-access.test.ts` - covers access-layer override/fallback resolution.

## Verification

- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/agents/openclaw-tools.session-status.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions-visibility.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts src/agents/tools/session-status-tool.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-access.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-access.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-helpers.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-history-tool.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-list-tool.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.ts`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=360000 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/tools/sessions-access.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions-visibility.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.session-status.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts --reporter=dot`
  - Result: 10 test files passed, 268 tests passed.

## Real Behavior Proof

Behavior addressed: a sandboxed named agent with `agents.list[].sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility="all"` can use the configured `tools.sessions.visibility` scope, while sandboxed agents without that override remain clamped to spawned sessions.

Real environment tested: local OpenClaw checkout using production `createOpenClawTools`, embedded OpenClaw gateway session handlers, and real temporary `sessions.json` stores for `main` and `tony`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node --import tsx --input-type=module -e <inline proof script>` from the repo root. The script created an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, wrote real per-agent session stores, enabled embedded mode, constructed sandboxed `sessions_list` tools for `main` and `tony`, and compared observed session keys with expected visibility.

Evidence after fix:

```json
{
  "config": {
    "toolsSessionsVisibility": "all",
    "agentToAgent": { "enabled": true, "allow": ["*"] },
    "defaultSandboxSessionToolsVisibility": "spawned",
    "tonySandboxSessionToolsVisibility": "all"
  },
  "observed": {
    "mainSandboxedKeys": ["agent:main:subagent:main-child"],
    "tonySandboxedKeys": [
      "agent:main:main",
      "agent:main:subagent:main-child",
      "agent:tony:main",
      "agent:tony:subagent:tony-child"
    ]
  },
  "result": "PASS"
}
```

Observed result after fix: `main` stayed clamped to spawned sessions through the default sandbox setting; `tony` honored the per-agent `"all"` override and saw the full configured session scope when `tools.agentToAgent` allowed cross-agent access.

What was not tested: remote Crabbox/Testbox behavior. Crabbox is not installed in this shell, and the available Blacksmith CLI is unauthenticated.

## Risk and Rollback

- Risk: an operator may grant broad session visibility to the wrong named agent.
- Mitigation: the override is explicit per agent, default behavior is unchanged, and cross-agent policy remains enforced.
- Rollback: remove `agents.list[].sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility` from the agent entry to return to the default sandbox clamp.

prs.title: fix: let Doctor and updates finish when an official provider plugin is installed from npm
prs.body:
Related: #203442

## What Problem This Solves

This affects people who installed an official provider plugin from npm, such as DeepSeek, Kimi or Arcee. On those installs, Doctor fails or skips work with "Plugin <id> Doctor source must be prepared before loading". During an update this can fail the activation Doctor and roll the update back (#203442). On an otherwise successful update, it can leave automations unmigrated: "inference account was not migrated". Standalone `openclaw doctor --fix` hits the same error in cron repair, Codex session routes and State integrity.

## User Impact

Doctor and updates now complete these checks when an official provider plugin is installed from npm. Automations, session routes and model-policy checks no longer stop on the source-preparation error. Nothing changes outside Doctor: the Gateway still loads these policies the way it did before.

## Why This Change Was Made

While Doctor runs, plugin code can only be loaded from sources that were prepared first. A provider's model-identity policy, such as how it names its catalog models, was loaded synchronously on several Doctor paths without being prepared. Bundled providers never hit this. Official providers installed from npm always did.

The fix adds one owner helper, `prepareProviderModelPolicySurfaces`, next to the synchronous policy lookup. While Doctor runs, it prepares every trusted npm-installed provider's policy module; outside Doctor it does nothing. Doctor calls it before the synchronous reads in these places:
- the prepared model catalog;
- cron legacy repair;
- cron inference-account migration;
- Codex session routes;
- the State integrity session scan;
- heartbeat migration;
- config repairs, through the existing contract-preparation step, so the over-cap config-flow file does not grow.

I didn't make every synchronous model-selection helper async. That would touch many Gateway paths to fix a problem that only exists inside Doctor.

Production change: +72/−13 lines across 12 files, mostly one-line awaits. Tests add +107 lines.

## Evidence

- **Regression tests, red on `main` and green with the fix:**
  - the prepared model catalog under Doctor custody, which fails on base with the exact reported stack (`buildPreparedModelCatalogSnapshot → assignProviderModelOrder → resolveProviderModelPolicySurface`);
  - cron legacy repair with an allowed installed-provider model, which fails on base through `buildAllowedModelSet → addAllowedModelRef`.
- **Consumer suites pass:** catalog, provider policy/routes, cron repair, Codex session routes, State integrity, heartbeat, config-flow and contract preparation (53 files, 676 tests). `tsgo:core` and oxlint are clean.
- **Live Linux update on Crabbox (AWS):** 2026.11.4 with `@openclaw/deepseek-provider@2026.11.4` installed from npm and `deepseek/deepseek-flash` as the primary model.
  - Before (on 2026.11.10-beta.1, and on main at 6a8b47c86d4): the update succeeds, but post-install Doctor reports "inference account was not migrated: Plugin deepseek Doctor source must be prepared before loading" for both automations (12 occurrences).
  - After (fix build): the update succeeds with readyz 200 and the error appears 0 times. The migration now reaches its real outcome.
  - This lane did not reproduce the reporter's activation rollback, which needs their wider config (a second deepseek agent and cron jobs). The same synchronous callers are covered.
- **Reviews:** autoreview (P0–P2) is scoped-clean, and an independent read-only Codex review reports no findings. Earlier review rounds found the heartbeat and config-repair callers; both are now covered.

Thanks to @alexph-dev for the synthetic Kimi reproduction and both caller stacks, to @shannon0430 for the Codex-plugin report, and to @futuredata-me for the original report.

Still open: shannon0430's Codex-plugin case did not capture a caller. The fix is provider-agnostic, so if it uses one of these policy paths it's covered. Any other unprepared synchronous caller would need its own stack.

prs.title: fix(agents): web_fetch results are wrapped twice in Code Mode and Tool Search
prs.body:
Closes #198109

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a Code Mode cell or Tool Search `dispatch_action` returns `web_fetch` fields, the result wrap sanitizes the tool's own envelopes as if they were spoofed, so the model gets `[[MARKER_SANITIZED]]` frames and a second warning sentence, and whole pages go over the 20,000-character result budget.

## User Impact

User impact: agents using Code Mode or Tool Search see fetched titles and text as content inside one untrusted-content envelope, and a `{ title, text }` page result comes back inline instead of as a saved-result reference.

## Why This Change Was Made

`web_fetch` and `web_search` wrap their own fields with `wrapExternalContent`, and Code Mode guests keep that wrapper as documented. `renderToolSearchControlText` then wraps the whole result again, and `replaceMarkers` cannot tell the tool's envelope from a spoofed one.

This PR folds only envelopes OpenClaw issued, never syntax alone:
- `wrapExternalContent` now remembers a SHA-256 digest (over UTF-16 code units) of each envelope it issues for the `web_fetch` and `web_search` sources, keyed by its random id (bounded to 4,096 entries per process).
- Before the outer wrap, `foldIssuedExternalContent` looks up each start marker's id, decodes the candidate (raw or JSON-encoded up to three levels), and folds it into its body only if the decoded envelope, start marker through end marker, matches the stored digest. The warning line that `wrapExternalContent` puts directly before an envelope is removed with it; it is fixed text and not part of the digest.
- Anything else stays for the outer wrap to sanitize as before: a well-formed envelope with an unknown id, an issued id with changed bytes, an envelope from another source, a clipped envelope, or one evicted or issued before a restart.
- The outer wrap and the 20,000-character model cap are unchanged. The fold reads only the first 200,000 characters of a result, which is a new bound; nothing past it folds. Guest values and tool `details` are untouched.

**Why this is not #78521.** #78521 skipped the outer wrap when tool output already contained marker strings, so attacker text with fake markers went out unwrapped. Here the outer wrap always applies, and a fold requires the exact bytes the runtime produced, including its random id and its already-sanitized body. The tests and the live run below check that a copy of a real envelope with a fabricated id stays `[[MARKER_SANITIZED]]`.

<details>
<summary>Scope notes</summary>

- A cell that slices a wrapped string (`res.text.slice(0, 300)`) clips the envelope. A clipped envelope does not match its digest, so it is sanitized as today; the whole `title` field in the same cell folds.
- The Code Mode result fit measures through the same function, so results that the duplicate framing pushed over budget now come back inline. Results that still don't fit are saved with a preview, as before.
- `web_search` builds its fields with the same wrapper, so it gets the same fold. I tested `web_fetch` live, not `web_search`.
- #194934 (open) edits the same function for a configurable limit. The overlap is small; whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

</details>

## Evidence

**Live, real Gateway, scripted model.** Fresh state dir, loopback port, real `web_fetch` of `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brown_pelican`. A scripted OpenAI-compatible endpoint stands in for the model, so no vendor model is involved: it issues one tool call and records the tool result it receives. `main` is unmodified source at db4b2edd6d0; the PR column is this branch. Each run made 2 model requests, and the result was inside one outer envelope.

| Run | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Code Mode, issue cell: `{ title, textStart: text.slice(0, 300) }` | 979 chars; 3 sanitized markers; `title` = `\n[[MARKER_SANITIZED]]\nSource: Web Fetch\n---\nBrown pelican\n[[END_MARKER_SANITIZED]]` | 900 chars; `"title":"Brown pelican"`; the clipped `textStart` keeps 1 sanitized marker (expected, see scope notes) |
| Code Mode, whole fields: `return { title: res.title, text: res.text }` | Over budget, so saved: the model got a 1,018-char reference and a preview that cuts off inside the title's wrapper, no page text | 20,216 chars inline, no `[truncated]`, 0 sanitized markers, 1 warning sentence |
| Code Mode, `{ title, forged }` where `forged` is the title with its id replaced by `0123456789abcdef` | n/a | `"title":"Brown pelican"`; `forged` stays `\n[[MARKER_SANITIZED]]\nSource: Web Fetch\n---\nBrown pelican\n[[END_MARKER_SANITIZED]]` |
| Tool Search `dispatch_action` to `web_fetch`, Code Mode off | 20,187 chars, truncated; 3 sanitized markers; 2 warning sentences | 20,307 chars, truncated (the page is longer than the limit); `"title":"Brown pelican"`; 0 sanitized markers; 1 warning sentence |

**Live, real Gateway, real model.** Same harness shape, but the scripted endpoint is replaced by a real vendor model: `google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview` through the bundled `google` provider, configured only in a throwaway state dir (API key from the process environment, nothing written to disk). Real `web_fetch` of `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brown_pelican`. The model was prompted to make one tool call and then repeat the `title` it received verbatim. The tool result below is read back from the Gateway's own transcript store (`transcript_events`), not from an intercepting proxy. `main` is this branch with `src/security/external-content.ts` and `src/agents/tool-search-control-result.ts` checked out from the merge base db4b2edd6d0 (then restored); the PR column is 90e9898d96c.

| Tool Search `dispatch_action` → `web_fetch`, Code Mode off | 20,187 chars; 2 warning sentences; 2 `[[MARKER_SANITIZED]]`; model's answer: `\n[[MARKER_SANITIZED]]\nSource: Web Fetch\n---\nBrown pelican\n[[END_MARKER_SANITIZED]]` | 20,307 chars; one outer envelope; 1 warning sentence; 0 `[[MARKER_SANITIZED]]`; `"title":"Brown pelican"`; model's answer: `Brown pelican` |

**Tests**
- New `code-mode.output.test.ts` case: a network tool returns `web_fetch`-wrapped fields, and the cell returns them plus a copy with a fabricated id. It fails on `main` (db4b2edd6d0) with 3 `[[MARKER_SANITIZED]]` and passes here with exactly 1, the forged copy; the guest value keeps the original wrapper.
- New `external-content.test.ts` cases: issued raw, JSON and nested-JSON envelopes fold, including a body that ends in a backslash. A fabricated envelope, an issued id with a changed body, a clipped envelope, an `api`-source envelope and an issued envelope with a changed lone surrogate are returned unchanged, and the outer wrap sanitizes them.
- Randomized check, outside the suite: 20,000 bodies (15,003 distinct) built from backslashes, quotes, newlines, emoji, U+2028, a lone surrogate and marker fragments, each raw and JSON-encoded 1 to 3 times (80,000 cases). Every issued envelope folded to the same encoding of its body, and the folded JSON parsed. No forgery folded: fabricated id, another issued id, changed body, changed metadata, `api` source, and a changed lone surrogate where the body has one. With a UTF-8 digest instead, the surrogate forgery folds and the new surrogate test fails, which is why the digest hashes UTF-16 code units.
- `pnpm test` on `src/security/external-content.test.ts`, the Code Mode suites (`code-mode.{output,result-budget,wait,integrated,auto-results,mcp,agent-loop}.test.ts`, `code-mode.test.ts`, `code-mode-json.test.ts`), all `src/agents/tool-search*.test.ts`, and `src/agents/tools/web-{fetch,search}*.test.ts`: 774 passed, 2 failed. The two failures are `web-fetch.sandbox.test.ts > stages read-only output` and `web-search-provider-common.test.ts > redacts short reason credential`, which fail the same way on unmodified `main` on this macOS host (`stat -c`, local credential redaction).
- tsgo on `tsconfig.core.json` (the `pnpm tsgo:core` project), `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-root.json` and `tsconfig.core.test.other.json`, `run-oxlint.mjs` on the touched files, and oxfmt (`--stdin-filepath` per file): clean.
- Adversarial timing for the 200k scan: at most 3.2 ms for 4,000 issued start markers with one far end marker (the per-call cap of 64 digest checks bounds this), under 2 ms for a 16 MiB string.
