prs.body:
## CI repair update (November 19, 2026)

- Published `4e804cab63c15c4a8d7337025e5195daf172d159`, preserving incoming `21d62a5bccc5cf2390894e67d7951488b1952022` as first parent and integrating landed baseline `4aa45837b5dc9139769cfcbadf8fc206a2ba0747`. All five history-product files remain byte-identical to incoming; no replacement PR, merge into main, release, or deployment.
- The [failed PostgreSQL job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44355222346/job/135250463535) polled `/readyz` after its HTTP listener retired, yielding `ECONNREFUSED`. The inherited cron test is absent from the raw incoming head. Integrated the existing upstream fix from #201501: synchronize on completed HTTP shutdown, then retain the same blocked-writer, original-live-process, durable-receipt, restart and no-replay assertions. No extra retries, relaxed timeout, or production shutdown change.
- Fresh independent review of the complete five-file delta and actual integrated candidate found no actionable P0–P3 defects; fresh `git diff --check` passed. [Upstream repaired-test execution](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44427245056/job/135235869774) passed both graceful-stop and crash-recovery cases. This is upstream proof, not current-head proof. Historical 25/25 history-source evidence below remains historical.
- **Current-head CI passed:** [run 44537651916, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44537651916), **53 successful jobs / 29 skipped**, including all four PostgreSQL conformance shards and PostgreSQL 16 smoke. Both required `openclaw/ci-gate` checks passed. [Shard 1/4](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44537651916/job/135608945127) explicitly passed the original graceful-stop/restart case (**52,609 ms**), interrupted in-process restart (**43,520 ms**) and killed-process recovery (**49,888 ms**). No failure was ignored or marked expected.
- CI is attached to exact published head `4e804cab63c15c4a8d7337025e5195daf172d159`; its test checkout was GitHub merge commit `cae14968332079bad2fafe71c7c1c7f32cd3d983`, tree `66e027bcefab6c98ce032b29e27cd6f1daf95b27`, with main parent `a484d2040389674e3a6b4e35b631cf8d29299c16`. This is integrated PR-CI proof, not raw-head-only execution. Initial fork workflow admission required approval; after scoped approval, attempt 2 executed successfully. The old cancelled PR-context check was superseded by its successful replacement. PR remains open and mergeable; no merge was performed. Older readiness sections below retain their dated historical scope.

## Exact-head readiness update (November 15, 2026)

- **R1 resolved; native correction recommendation: READY FOR /prepare-pr.** Product source remains `eb919fb0d0b19dfa86c3e7055145b5a83ae27ef9` (tree `85c33b6fd00340e5b14124706b8d5f3f9004d04b`). No source changes or new source review were needed for this evidence-only qualification.
- Supplemental secretless [hosted run 43771398337, history job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43771398337/job/132987885912) completed **success**, using proof tooling `9838c5239d071ab5845c061da812f2aa76f1db5c` against that immutable product source. Independently inspected original summary, Vitest JSON reports and prefix log show **25/25 passed**: all **14 prefix-stability**, **6 bounded-projector** and **5 persisted SQLite/inbound-context** cases; zero failures. This closes the exact-source prefix execution gap left by the November 14 CI run. The proof workflow's head is the tooling commit, not a new product commit.
- Broad exact-head-attached CI remains [43624048246, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43624048246): **55 successful jobs, 28 skipped**. It executed GitHub's merge checkout, whereas the supplemental proof executed the raw candidate source. The scopes are not interchangeable.
- On November 15, the remote product head was unchanged, the PR was non-draft and **MERGEABLE / CLEAN**, and both checks reported by the required-check query (`openclaw/ci-gate`) were **SUCCESS**. This is readiness evidence, not a merge or an assertion that future main changes cannot require reconciliation.
- Existing independent exact-candidate source review found no actionable P0–P3 defects. The original baseline-red and candidate-only synthetic-channel live evidence below remain **prior-head evidence**. No fresh exact-head baseline/fix A/B or live Gateway/model run is claimed. No autoreview rerun, source rebase, push, merge, release, main change or production-service change was performed for this qualification.

## Historical exact-head proof update (November 14, 2026)

The missing-prefix status in this section records the November 14 observation; it is superseded by the successful November 15 exact-source proof above.

- Current native-published candidate: `eb919fb0d0b19dfa86c3e7055145b5a83ae27ef9`, tree `85c33b6fd00340e5b14124706b8d5f3f9004d04b`, refreshed against baseline `976a4fb8784a326579108e03d0df4356dad501a3` including the landed `d43de8` worker fix. Workflow source: `8e961de3f838e9bc16c37c148c3364ed958ab810`. Independent exact-candidate source review found no actionable P0–P3 defect.
- Secretless [CI 43624048246, attempt 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43624048246) completed **success**: 55 successful jobs, 28 skipped. Runtime setup, build artifacts, production/test types, lint, docs, baseline ratchets and `openclaw/ci-gate` passed. This supersedes the runtime-setup gap for this candidate, not the historical outcome below.
- Actual assertion logs verified: [persisted SQLite job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43624048246/job/132536373207), **5/5** (internal-pair absent/present, aborted false/true reconciliation, delivery-only restart); [projector/consumer job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43624048246/job/132536373205), **6/6** bounded projector, **46/46** transcript facade, **12/12** memory-reader; [inbound-context job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43624048246/job/132536373103), **9/9**. The projector cases cover 250/9,999/10,000 newer physical rows, 0/1-row contiguous suffixes after an omitted oversized barrier, and the shared 64 MiB budget. The executed persisted fixture asserts prepared-channel rendering and retention of edited, attachment-bearing, unseen, incomplete and image-barrier requests.
- **Remaining required proof:** the full available CI log contains no execution of `src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts`. CI success must not be represented as that suite passing; its recorded 14/14 below is prior-head evidence. Native R1 is narrowed to this missing exact-head execution and remains open; recommendation remains **NEEDS WORK**, not READY. No fresh exact-head live baseline/fix A/B or Gateway/model run was performed in this pass; the original baseline and candidate-only synthetic-channel evidence retain their stated scope and source identities.
- No merge, release, backport, main change, local contributor-code execution or production-service change was performed. The earlier CI failure below is retained as historical evidence.

## Historical conflict-repair review update (November 14, 2026)

- Published conflict repair head: `d8caf07f9c97fbfadccf74a24e7649e0bf1c6d32`, preserving original contributor head `9b62025151d3f823522144895d26c17e9c1abfaa` as the first parent and integrating main `7bccde609cbb0eaa054ac07a6d5ccd91ec712a92`. This is a merge into the existing fix branch, not a merge of this PR into main.
- Independent source review found no actionable P0–P3 findings. The adaptation preserves main's delivery-only projection envelope/filter and both the existing and added SQLite regression blocks. `git diff --check` passed.
- Existing live/regression evidence below remains prior-head evidence. This conflict-only adaptation was not executed locally: the supported secretless AWS proof environment could not acquire credentials (no EC2 instance role). Historical CI run [43600201582](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43600201582) completed. Production types, core test-type stripes, lint, and test-line accounting passed; that run was not green. Its failures matched three existing main defects: identity worker build budget (240 evaluated modules versus 220), TS18048 at scripts/perf/state-read-worker-bench.ts:373, and mock export preservation at src/infra/worker-idle-gc.test.ts:13. The exact failure text was independently compared with contemporary [main run 43599691199](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43599691199), specifically [build job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43599691199/job/132461948967), [type job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43599691199/job/132461949721), and [ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43599691199/job/132461948989). Its affected Node test jobs stopped at the inherited runtime-build failure; that historical run remains build-blocked, not runtime proof.
- Attribution and bounded lookup remain separate reviewable fixes under the existing transcript projection/reconciliation owners. Combining them later requires reconciling the shared projector, SQLite append tests, and documentation; neither is represented as testing their combination.

Closes #197995

## What problem this solves

Recent-history reconciliation previously requested `candidate count * 2` projected canonical text rows. Candidate messages, physical platform rows, and projected canonical text rows are different units. An internal user-role runtime input plus assistant `NO_REPLY` can consume that evidence budget without adding a channel-history candidate. A selected, unchanged, previously answered request then resurfaces in later model context because its completion evidence fell outside the lookup.

The conservative behavior on genuinely unavailable evidence is intentional and remains. This is not a missing-final-answer report or a requirement to suppress unproven input. Token cost and answer-quality effects have not been measured.

## What the branch changes

- The recent-history omission owner passes the selected transport message IDs to its existing private canonical turn reader instead of prescribing a two-row ratio.
- The shared SQLite/memory transcript projector follows those IDs until each has been encountered, the active transcript ends, or an existing safety ceiling is reached: 10,000 physical canonical message rows and 64 MiB of captured serialized transcript data.
- Both ceilings are reused from the existing transcript reader constants. The byte count bounds captured payload data, not process heap usage; parsed objects and page metadata add overhead.
- A byte-limited page can contain older sparse rows. Only its newest contiguous suffix is used, and lookup stops at the first omitted physical row. It never bridges a potentially missing user barrier.
- All intervening user rows remain barriers, including image-only/textless users represented as `text: ""` only in the private turn-evidence projection. The public SDK text reader retains its old nonempty-text behavior.
- The private facade captures options and clones candidate IDs before awaiting acquisition. Caller mutation cannot silently change the evidence request after it starts.

The final omission decision still requires exact transport-ID/body equality and completed-answer evidence. Attachment-bearing, changed, unseen, unfinished, and unproven requests remain eligible. Existing active-session/agent scoping and snapshot/worker ownership are retained. There is no new schema, index, configuration, background archive, public SDK option, or arbitrary larger multiplier.

### Performance and bounded fallback

An unseen or too-old selected ID can require searching the whole permitted tail, unlike the old short heuristic. The explicit row and cumulative byte ceilings cap that additional work, and lookup stops early once all selected IDs are found. A missing ID, oversized barrier, unavailable transcript, or exhausted bound can therefore still leave an answered request quoted conservatively. This is an accepted bounded-evidence limitation, not an assertion that every historical answered request will disappear.

The direct projector's 10,000-row synthetic scans ran in 2-3 ms in the supplemental test run. These pages contain already decoded small fixture rows; this is not a SQLite/JSON-decoding benchmark, a production latency guarantee, or a memory measurement.

## Reproduce the original failure independently

The evidence package is attached here: [openclaw-197995-evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34783640/openclaw-197995-evidence.zip)

Use Node 26.12.1+; the portable helper was executed with Node v26.13.0:

```sh
node reproduce.mjs > observed.json
```

No repository checkout, npm install, credentials, network, model, or Gateway is required. The helper resolves its bundled source relative to itself, not the current directory. Copying the package outside the checkout and running it from `/` produced the identical output.

`SOURCE-MANIFEST.json` pins the bundled baseline owner to `489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b` (package version `2026.11.3`) with exact source hashes and its MIT license. `reproduction-output.json` is the fresh baseline result. `current-base-reproduction-output.json` confirms the same baseline owner/behavior at the fix branch's newer upstream base.

The helper's optional checkout argument is for reproducing this baseline contract:

```sh
node reproduce.mjs /path/to/openclaw > checkout-observed.json
```

It prints the actual checkout commit/hash and does not label differing source as the pinned baseline. Its assertions intentionally encode the old behavior, including the bug. It is not a green-on-fix acceptance script; use the branch's real owner tests below for the new reader contract.

The executed fixture has exactly six unchanged ID-bearing channel candidates, each with a directly following completed answer. There is no steering fixture:

1. Six ordinary U/A pairs: 12 projected rows, requested limit 12, retained `[]`.
2. Add one internal U/NO_REPLY pair after the oldest answered pair: 14 projected rows, same candidates and requested limit, retained `[target]`.
3. Give the unchanged algorithm all 14 rows: retained `[]` again. This reader override isolates coverage; it is not a repair.
4. Separate controls retain all candidates without evidence and preserve independently edited text, attachments, and incomplete answers.

These are synthetic production-function probes with an injected chronological reader. They do not exercise the real projector, persistence, channel/Gateway, prompt renderer, or model. Passing them must not be called a live end-to-end result.

## Prior-head evidence

`persisted-baseline-red.txt` records the actual pre-fix SQLite/reconciliation failure on the then-current upstream base: three tests passed; adding the internal U/NO_REPLY pair retained `target` and failed the expected-empty assertion. This was a real owner assertion failure, not the earlier cold-compiler infrastructure failure.

The prior implementation passed:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/coverage-final-cache \
  pnpm test src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.sqlite.test.ts \
  src/config/sessions/transcript-recent-text.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

- SQLite owner: 4/4. Real persistence and `runPreparedChannelTurn` rendering cover the six-candidate control/failure, edited text, attachments, unseen discussion, incomplete output, unrelated internal text users, image-only user barriers, and unchanged public text projection.
- Private projector: 5/5. Covers paging past 250 rows, the exact 10,000-message edge, candidates beyond it, and zero/one-row newest-contiguous suffixes after oversized omissions.
- Provider prefix stability: 14/14, prior head only.
- A supplemental cumulative-byte-budget regression was added after that integration run; the updated projector suite passed 6/6 in 3.36 seconds (7.69 seconds including the wrapper). Production source was unchanged. The new case uses two contiguous pages reporting 32 MiB each, verifies requests of 64 MiB then 32 MiB, and prohibits a third read. Its config-cli test-leaf typecheck, dedicated-core lint, formatting, and diff check also passed. This is a private byte-budget contract, not a SQLite memory benchmark.
- Prior final command: 23 tests passed across three shards, 413.35 seconds including a 160.54-second cold worker compilation. SQLite test bodies totaled about 7.6 seconds; projector bodies about 37 ms. No PR CI was run during that original implementation work; current CI evidence is recorded separately above.
- An earlier candidate passed the unchanged non-recent channel suite, 9/9; that unaffected-path evidence was reused, not presented as an exact-final-head rerun.
- Core production typecheck, plugin-sdk/config-cli test-leaf typechecks, dedicated-core targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. `FIX-VERIFICATION.json` records exact tested source hashes and verification scope.

Independent review found and corrected the textless-user barrier and pre-await request-capture defects. Re-review found no further material findings in the reviewed scope. This is not a claim of an automated scoped-clean review.

## Owner and upstream implementation pointers

Pinned baseline source prefix: <https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b/>

- `src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.runtime.ts`, `omitAnsweredRecentHistory`: selected candidate identities and conservative final omission.
- `src/config/sessions/transcript.ts`, `readRecentUserAssistantTurnsForSession`: private active-session/agent facade; public text projection stays separate.
- `src/config/sessions/transcript-recent-text.ts`, `readRecentTranscriptConversationText`: shared SQLite/memory projection and candidate stopping/coverage.
- `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-visible-cursor.ts`: existing 10,000-message/64 MiB ceilings.
- `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-active-events-read.ts` and `session-actor-memory-history-facts.ts`: byte-bounded page and contiguous-suffix contracts.
- `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.recent-history.ts`: physical platform-row budget, distinct from filtered candidates and canonical rows.
- `docs/channels/discord/threads-and-sessions.md`: bounded completion confirmation and conservative retention contract.

## Evidence and submission files

`LIVE-EVIDENCE.md` indexes the successful November 13 candidate-only run. A real isolated Gateway, native Codex runtime and configured provider produced one older answered request followed by seven non-platform user-source RPC turns with seven `NO_REPLY` responses. These are real persisted turns, not fabricated transcript rows, but they are not internal-system events or scheduled automation. Historical production evidence separately covers the original internal-event example.

With six selected history candidates, core dispatch removed the older answered request and retained all five unrelated unanswered candidates. The newly submitted native input contains each retained candidate once and does not quote the older request again. Independent review matched all nine submitted bodies to native and provider requests, verified the 16-row pre-lookup canonical transcript, and separated eight auxiliary recap calls. Retained native conversation history is intentionally not erased.

The canonical `build:runtime` command passed; exact source/build/runtime/Codex provenance is in `live/build-provenance.json`. The fixture uses a restricted native-tool profile and a synthetic authenticated local channel, not Discord transport. Both disposable homes were removed. This is not a fresh live baseline/fix A/B comparison or a full package/declaration/PR-CI run.

The ZIP includes the headerless `fix.patch`, verified `BRANCH.json`, regression receipts, original baseline helper/source/license, sanitized historical observation, live observations, and exact executed harness source. `SHA256SUMS.json` covers the payload. The separate Markdown was byte-identical to the original submission text inside the ZIP; subsequent readiness updates above are not part of that original archive. The original branch was based directly on the stated upstream commit, not on another fix branch; native proof-baseline refresh is identified above.

## Exact limits

- A separate shared-renderer API migration renames `buildInboundUserContextPrefix` to `buildInboundUserContext` returning `{ text, hasHistory }`. If that migration lands first, migrate this branch's added SQLite rendering-test call to the new API and select `.text` where the old string result was consumed. A mechanically clean merge does not establish type compatibility; rerun the focused tests and typecheck after rebasing.
- This is a standalone branch, not a pre-integrated series. A mechanical combination with the separately prepared completed-run attribution change conflicts in the shared projector, SQLite tests and Discord documentation. If that change lands first, rebase and reconcile those owners before landing this branch; combined behavior has not been tested here.
- Recorded historical observations and the prior synthetic-channel proof are separate. Neither implies this branch was installed on the production Gateway.
- No regression-from-known-good release, population-wide incidence, or end-to-end performance rate has been established. The historical observation and deterministic fixtures do not prove such claims.
- The original submission changed only the requested fix branch. Subsequent authorized work published the native proof candidate and updated this existing PR body; no merge, issue comment, release or production service change was performed.

prs.title: fix(ui): agent-excluded skills inflate Needs setup
prs.body:
Closes #198026

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Skills page counts skills excluded by the selected agent's allowlist as **Needs setup**, even when they have no missing prerequisites.

## User Impact

Users can distinguish **Excluded** skills from skills that actually need setup, using consistent counts, filtering, row badges, and details. A skill with missing prerequisites still needs setup even if the agent also excludes it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The inventory now shares one status classifier and adds a neutral Excluded filter. Disabled remains distinct, and existing ClawHub warnings, agent access rules, and the global enable toggle retain their behavior.

## Evidence

Validated merge commit `e60d606f99b1501c079dcfb7ef456d060bf75565`, with upstream `6f2bd815fecb4427081663be328946ba184e6514`. The conflict resolution carries the classification into upstream's standalone Skills detail page and preserves its route and focus behavior. The diff remains limited to six Skills UI files (+109/-50).

The previous `checks-ui (3/3)` failure was the chat startup test's immediate user-row assertion. This branch includes [upstream #202220](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/202220), which waits for the Solid render while retaining the count and Retry/Discard assertions. Chat sources are identical to the pinned main.

- **96 tests passed in 10 files**, including that exact chat recovery case and Skills inventory, page, mutation and agent-policy coverage, on the CI-pinned Node 24.22.1.
- UI type checking, typed lint, formatting, i18n verification, controller/window-open guards and applicable line budgets passed. Independent review found no actionable code issue.
- Complete `pnpm build` passed on the clean commit above in **492.870 seconds**, using Node 26.12.1 and pnpm 12.15.0 on WSL2 Ubuntu 26.04. Build metadata matches the commit. Main and candidate both report the same six UI size-budget warning categories; this is not a budget-pass claim.

### Actual UI and CLI comparison

The screenshots use synthetic skills, Chromium and a real isolated Gateway without RPC stubs. Before UI assets were independently built from `6f2bd815` with `pnpm ui:build`, then served through `gateway.controlUi.root`. After assets come from the complete `e60d606f` build. Both runs use the candidate's production Gateway and CLI: all non-UI sources are identical to pinned main. Served HTML/assets were verified against the respective builds.

| Agent | Needs setup before | Needs setup after | Excluded after | CLI missing prerequisites, both runs |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| main allowlist | 58 | 36 | 22 | 36 |
| empty allowlist | 55 | 36 | 19 | 36 |

The `proof-` name filter narrows visible rows; the selector counts the full agent inventory. The eligible `proof-excluded` fixture moves out of Needs setup, while `proof-missing` stays there. The standalone detail page changes Needs setup to neutral Excluded, retaining the exclusion reason and the globally Enabled switch.

Before inventory:

![Before: main incorrectly counts 58 skills as Needs setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Malpin07/openclaw/568c791c4e8db0ce50b8f5150a4b8649c72e4a98/before-inventory.png)

After inventory:

![After: only 36 skills with missing prerequisites need setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Malpin07/openclaw/568c791c4e8db0ce50b8f5150a4b8649c72e4a98/after-inventory.png)

Before detail:

![Before: agent exclusion is mislabeled Needs setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Malpin07/openclaw/568c791c4e8db0ce50b8f5150a4b8649c72e4a98/before-detail.png)

After detail:

![After: Excluded is separate from the global enable toggle](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Malpin07/openclaw/568c791c4e8db0ce50b8f5150a4b8649c72e4a98/after-detail.png)

[Capture provenance and image hashes](https://github.com/Malpin07/openclaw/blob/568c791c4e8db0ce50b8f5150a4b8649c72e4a98/README.md).

Real agent switching, filters, detail-page navigation and retained filters passed. At 400/820/1280 px there was no horizontal overflow; the 1280 px run recorded two small layout shifts (0.009807 and 0.002017). Gateway/CLI process groups exited, ports closed and temporary runtime state was removed.

The full repository test suite, every core typecheck shard, full `check:changed`, native Windows/macOS product runs and external model execution were not rerun for this merged revision. Earlier validation applies to its recorded older commits, not this head. Hosted CI and maintainer review are tracked separately.

prs.title: feat(agents): compact from the warm prompt cache on every route
prs.body:
## Problem

Automatic compaction builds its own summary request: the client summarizer sends `SUMMARIZATION_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, no tools and one `<conversation>` sample; OpenAI/xAI API keys use `/responses/compact`. Neither shares a prefix with the session's prompt cache, so every compaction pays full uncached input. Only native ChatGPT sign-in (V2 `compaction_trigger`) reused the warm prefix.

## Solution

One request-boundary compaction for every built-in route, chosen by capability:

- `chatgpt-v2-compaction.ts` → `request-boundary-compaction.ts`. It keeps the shared trigger (smaller of reserve budget and 90% of the window), the `compact_only` fallback and the `failed` latch, and selects a variant: `native-checkpoint` (ChatGPT V2, unchanged) or `text` (every other route).
- The `text` variant runs the session's threshold compaction (`agentSessionRunWarmCompaction`). Its first history summary is the session's next normal request — same system, tools, `tool_choice`, `max_tokens`, thinking, cache key, every earlier message — plus one appended user item with the existing summary instructions (`prepareCompactionSummaryRequest`, plain prompt, no `<previous-summary>`: the request already holds it).
  - Default mode: the core path uses it through `compactFromSource` with no turn-prefix request (split turn: one request, empty `latestContext`).
  - Safeguard mode (the default for new configs): it is attempt 0 of the safeguard; the quality audit still runs and corrective retries use the existing bounded summarizer.
  - A tool call, a non-`stop` stop reason (`length`, `error`) or empty text rejects the warm summary: nothing is written (safeguard returns a plain cancel, no attempt row), the boundary raises `compact_only`, and the client compactor runs once.
  - After commit the attempt stops at the settled boundary with a maintenance precheck; the run retries from the compacted transcript (existing "compaction already happened in this attempt" recovery branch), so the loop never keeps the stale uncompacted context.
- The appended item carries `cacheCheckpoint: false` (new optional `UserMessage` field); Anthropic Messages and Chat Completions place no cache marker on it, so history markers stay where the previous request put them.
- Reply-level token maintenance that still fits the window defers to the boundary (`defersTokenCompactionToRequestBoundary`, generalized from the ChatGPT-only check). Required compaction (prompt does not fit), byte-triggered compaction, configured context engines, `compaction.model`, `compaction.provider`, CLI/Codex runtimes and memory-flush turns keep their existing owners.

Out of scope (later PRs): manual `/compact`, overflow recovery, removing `/responses/compact` / `params.responsesCompactEndpoint` (shipped config key; needs xAI and quality evidence).

Decisions recorded (defaults taken without asking):
- `compaction.model` excludes the warm path whenever set (existing predicate), not only when it differs from the session model.
- Context-engine ownership is not known before the attempt; reply-level maintenance keeps running for sessions with a non-legacy `plugins.slots.contextEngine`.
- Trigger is the shared V2 soft trigger, so text compaction fires later than the old 75% client threshold; the hard window guard is unchanged.
- Quality: sold as cost parity plus full-history input, not better summaries (probe: 52.1% vs 53.1% on 48 questions).

## Impact

Users on Anthropic, OpenAI API key, cliproxy and other routes: automatic compaction reads the warm prompt cache instead of a cold summarizer request. No new config, prompt or wait.

## Evidence

Tests (red on base: the module and behavior do not exist there):
- `request-boundary-compaction.test.ts`: anthropic-messages attempt above the trigger sends a request equal to the uncompacted request (system, tools, params, all messages and markers) plus one unmarked user item; commit keeps summary + tail from `firstKeptEntryId` with the pending request once; split turn sends one summary request; `tool` and `length` replies write nothing, raise `compact_only`.
- `compaction-safeguard.degraded-fallback.test.ts`: warm summary is attempt 0 (no `<previous-summary>`, no `<conversation>`), corrective retry stays bounded; warm failure cancels without a recorded failure.
- V2 boundary suite, runreplyagent ownership cases, agent-runner-memory suite, prefix-stability: green.

Real-route E2E (isolated scratch Gateway; forced 24k `contextTokens`, safeguard mode):

First automatic compaction request per route. R/W/U/O = provider cacheRead / cacheWrite / uncached input / output. "Prior prompt" is the previous normal request's input tokens on that side.

| Route / window | Base R/W/U/O | Head R/W/U/O | Head read ÷ prior prompt | Fact before cut answered (base/head) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Anthropic direct API key, Sonnet 4.6 / 24k | 0 / 8,442 / 3 / 380 (client safeguard) | **12,213** / 7,760 / 477 / 427 | 12,213 / 12,216 = 99.98% | ✓ / ✓ |
| OpenAI API key, GPT-5-mini / 24k | 0 / 0 / 22,042 / 1,583 (`/responses/compact`) | **10,112** / 0 / 6,920 / 3,343 | 10,112 / 10,164 = 99.5% | ✓ / ✓ |
| cliproxy Claude, Sonnet 4.6 / 40k | 0 / 16,232 / 3 / 471 (client safeguard) | **20,420** / 8,234 / 3 / 572 | 20,420 / 20,423 = 99.99% | ✓ / ✓ |
| ChatGPT sign-in (regression) | not run: no usable native credential | not run | — | — |

Head cacheWrite is the turn appended since the previous request (the history marker writes it, as a normal request would); the appended instruction itself carries no marker. On cliproxy at a 24k cap the resumed head session had already passed the window, so the hard guard used the existing deterministic fallback with no summary request; the matched 40k run (base and head with identical settings) is the proof row. Head warm requests kept all tools and the normal system prompt. Total paid E2E spend ≤ $3.80.

Local review fixes:
- Warm compaction consults the shared context-pressure owner first, so a run that declined maintenance sends its request instead of compacting again.
- The warm boundary runs the internal `session:compact:before/after` hooks and post-compaction memory sync (`postIndexSync`) that reply-level compaction ran, and marks its session events hook-handled so plugin hooks run once.

`pnpm check:changed`: green except `dead export scan` (`scripts/lib/docker-e2e-watchdog.mjs: parseTimeoutMs`, a file this PR does not touch) and one lint error in a new test, fixed.

Accepted change, recorded: fitting token maintenance after a delivered reply (idle session maintenance) also defers to the next attempt's boundary, as ChatGPT V2 sessions already did, so those sessions now compact warm inside the next turn once it reaches the boundary trigger instead of with a cold request at the old client threshold.

prs.title: fix(telegram): name a DM topic's session after its auto label right away
prs.body:
Closes #203958

## What Problem This Solves

When `autoTopicLabel` renames a Telegram private (DM) topic, the topic gets the generated name but its session keeps the placeholder title (for example `Garden irrigati...`) until the user sends another message there, so session lists and the Control UI sidebar show the wrong name in the meantime.

## User Impact

A DM topic's session takes the generated label as its name as soon as the bot renames the topic. Manual session labels still win, and sessions that don't exist yet are not created.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram sends no `forum_topic_edited` service message for the bot's own `editForumTopic`, so the title-update path from #166011 never runs for an auto label, and `scheduleDmTopicLabel` refreshes only the topic-name cache. After a successful rename it now records the label through `recordInboundSession` with `createIfMissing: false`, the same call the `forum_topic_edited` path in `bot-message.ts` makes. The new call sits inside the existing try/catch, so a failed write is logged like any other auto-label failure and does not affect the reply.

## Evidence

**Live, before and after:** real Telegram and a real model. A throwaway bot with Threaded Mode on, on a throwaway Gateway (DM allowlist, `autoTopicLabel` on, model `claude-cli/claude-haiku-5-5`). One build at a time polls the bot. For each build, a person opens a new DM topic from the Telegram app and sends one message, then nothing more. A watcher reads `sessions.list` from the Gateway every 2 s, starting before the message and ending 150 s after the new session appears. The topic name is what the Telegram app shows afterwards.

| Build | First (only) message | Topic renamed to (Telegram app) | Session `displayName`, 150 s after the label turn |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026.11.10-beta.1 | `Planning the garden irrigation schedule for the tomato beds this spring. Reply with just OK.` | `Garden Irrigation Plan` | `Planning the gar...` (placeholder, never changed) |
| this PR (`d9c5d59ae7`) | `New topic first message` | `New topic message` | **`New topic message`** |

`label` stays unset in both rows, so no manual label is involved. On the fix build the session row read the generated label the first time the watcher saw it after the rename; on beta it kept the placeholder for the whole window, matching the issue (it catches up only at the next user message, per #166011).

Screenshots from the Telegram app of the two runs above: Telegram renamed the topic on both builds; only the session name in the table differs.

| 2026.11.10-beta.1 | this PR (`d9c5d59ae7`) |
| --- | --- |
| ![Telegram DM topic auto-named Garden Irrigation Plan on beta](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/warm-cloth/openclaw/50947c1c42e72ff3a543818a33b937d1a28ca34a/before-beta.jpg) | ![Telegram DM topic auto-named New topic message on the fix build](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/warm-cloth/openclaw/50947c1c42e72ff3a543818a33b937d1a28ca34a/after-fix.png) |

**Session name in the Control UI, second live run.** Same setup with fresh Gateways and new topics. On each Gateway, the Control UI Sessions page was screenshotted about 150 s after the last new session appeared. On beta, two new topics each got one message, starting `Planning the garden irrigation…` and `Sorting out the bookshelf…`. Telegram renamed them to `Garden Irrigation Planning` and `Spare bedroom bookshelf` (topic bar from the Telegram app below). On the fix build, one new topic got `Booking a dentist appointment for the kids…`, and its session took the generated label about 40 s later.

| 2026.11.10-beta.1: Sessions page | this PR (`d9c5d59ae7`): Sessions page |
| --- | --- |
| ![Control UI Sessions page on beta: the two sessions are still named after the first message, Planning the gar... and Sorting out the](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/warm-cloth/openclaw/50947c1c42e72ff3a543818a33b937d1a28ca34a/r4-beta.png) | ![Control UI Sessions page on the fix build: the session is named after the generated label, Booking kids' dentist before holidays](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/warm-cloth/openclaw/50947c1c42e72ff3a543818a33b937d1a28ca34a/r4-fix.png) |

![Telegram app topic bar during this run: the beta topics already renamed to Garden Irrigation Planning and Spare bedroom bookshelf; the fix-build topic still shows its first-message placeholder Booking a dentis because the app had not yet shown the rename](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/warm-cloth/openclaw/50947c1c42e72ff3a543818a33b937d1a28ca34a/r4-beta-topics.png)

**Stubbed, for the call sequence.** The same scenario with Telegram's Bot API and the model stubbed locally (the model always answers `Status labels`) also records which Bot API calls each build makes, and the step after a second user message:

| Build | Bot API calls | Session `displayName` after the rename | After the next user message |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026.11.6 | `sendMessage`, no `editForumTopic` | `Garden irrigati...` | `Garden irrigati...` |
| 2026.11.10-beta.1 (includes #166011) | `sendMessage`, `editForumTopic: Status labels` | `Garden irrigati...` | `Status labels` |
| this PR | `sendMessage`, `editForumTopic: Status labels` | **`Status labels`** | `Status labels` |

Tested on `d9c5d59ae7` (based on `b419318b217`; current main `656c84413d0` has not touched either file since).

- Tests: `titles a private topic session with its auto label, which Telegram never echoes` in `bot-message-context.dm-session.test.ts` fails on main and passes here; the Telegram shard, lint and typecheck pass.
- Review: autoreview (claude) on `b419318b217..d9c5d59ae7`, highest priority none, clean.
- Known gap: the write re-records the turn's own context. If a second message in the same topic lands while the label is being generated, the fields it re-applies (origin, client capabilities) come from the same DM topic, so they carry the same values.

<details>
<summary>Claude Opus 5.5</summary>

Why reuse `recordInboundSession` instead of a dedicated title setter: it already maps `ThreadLabel` to the private-topic name that `displayName` reads (`session-utils-display.ts`), keeps manual labels in front, emits the session lifecycle event the sidebar listens for, and with `createIfMissing: false` can't create a stray session. No `updateLastRoute` is passed, so routing state is untouched.

On 2026.11.6 the topic is never renamed at all in this setup (no `editForumTopic` call); beta and main do rename it, so that row is shown only for context. #183368 (open, refines generated labels once) renames through the same path and would get the same session update from this change.

</details>

prs.title: fix(codex): keep workspace persona stable across incremental requests
prs.body:
Related: #142501 (parent-only workspace profile delivery)

## What Problem This Solves

Managed Codex sessions send workspace persona and per-turn guidance together in the top-level instructions. When the guidance changes, an incremental request cannot reuse the unchanged persona as part of its input prefix.

## User Impact

Eligible managed Codex sessions keep unchanged persona text in a stable input prefix. Turn-specific guidance remains request-local. Removing a persona file or switching profiles rebuilds the prefix without carrying forward the previous selection.

## Why This Change Was Made

The relay projects persona only when the native request shows incremental tool declarations in a Responses Lite window. Append-only edits add the new text; replacements, removals and compaction rebuild from the current selection. The relay does not persist persona in native history or project it into native child, warmup or compaction requests. WebSocket continuations require the preceding response on the same socket and admission. Legacy and unrecognized requests retain the existing instruction carrier.

## Evidence

- The pinned Codex app-server completed two turns over both HTTP and WebSocket through the relay to a synthetic upstream. The second request preserved the first input prefix while the top-level instructions changed. The same regression checks failed before the fix.
- On the published head, 50 focused tests passed, including the two native transports and fork coverage. Extension type checking, scoped lint and formatting checks passed.
- The credentialed provider test was not run. This verifies the wire layout, not live provider behavior, cache hits or billing.

prs.title: docs: run update repair with the Gateway stopped after a manual install
prs.body:
Refs #202925

## What Problem This Solves

When an older installed updater is stuck, the recovery guidance tells people to install a newer OpenClaw by hand and run `openclaw update repair`. The manual procedure ends by restarting the Gateway. If the stuck update left an interrupted handoff, repair then refuses with `Handoff descendants remain alive or unverified: PID …` and names the Gateway that was just started. Nothing in the docs says to stop the Gateway first.

## User Impact

People recovering a blocked update are told to run repair while the Gateway is still stopped: right after `openclaw doctor --fix`, or after `openclaw gateway stop` if it is already running. They then start the Gateway themselves. The same note appears in the manual procedure, in the `update repair` reference, and next to the pinned-lease-store repair that #202925 needs.

## Why This Change Was Made

While repair recovers an interrupted update handoff, it counts OpenClaw processes, such as the Gateway and its workers, as possible handoff work. A process is exempt only if its whole process ancestry started after the handoff's last activity plus the recovery grace. A Gateway started inside that window keeps repair refusing. This follows the existing advice for the launcher-ownership case, which already says to run repair after Doctor and before refreshing and starting the service. Main and 2026.11.6 share this census logic, so no code changes.

## Evidence

- **Live reproduction** (Crabbox Linux, npm global install, systemd user Gateway):
  - A 2026.11.3 → 2026.11.5 Gateway update was interrupted at `publication-complete`, with a stale `triage`/`uncertain` handoff lease in the journal-pinned store. 2026.11.5 repair refused with `Another update executor owns this installation.`
  - After the documented manual hop to 2026.11.6 (which ends with `openclaw gateway start`), 2026.11.6 repair refused with `Handoff descendants remain alive or unverified: PID 40242, 40398, 40449`. Those are the just-started Gateway and its two spawn-broker workers.
  - `openclaw gateway stop`, then `openclaw update repair`, exited 0, reconciled the stuck run, recorded it as succeeded, and left the Gateway stopped with start guidance.
  - `openclaw gateway start` came back healthy, and a later update to a current main build succeeded.
- **Source check:** `outsideHandoffFamily` in `src/infra/openclaw-process-census.ts`, with `familyDeadline` set to last activity plus grace in `src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-cleanup.ts`. The logic is identical in v2026.11.6 and main.
- **Docs checks:** `pnpm check:docs` passed and `git diff --check` is clean. `pnpm docs:check-links:anchors` reports only pre-existing failures in untouched files (release notes, code-mode troubleshooting) and a pre-existing duplicate ID in the `update cleanup` section. Both new links resolve.
- **Review:** autoreview (Codex) at P0–P2 came back scoped-clean.

prs.title: fix: keep queued WebChat turns on their Codex subscription route
prs.body:
Related: #202519. This PR verifies the WebChat queue trigger, not the Goal or exec-completion triggers in that issue.

## What Problem This Solves

A WebChat follow-up can be accepted into the queue and then fail before inference when it drains on a Codex session configured for subscription sign-in only. The error asks the user to sign in again even though the turn was admitted with a compatible subscription route.

## User Impact

A queued WebChat turn can use the same configured Codex subscription as a direct turn. It still runs in the original session and replies once. No configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native model capability rows do not carry all transport facts. Resolve the route from the published picker catalog captured on the turn's prepared runtime snapshot, not from an ambient borrowed snapshot that the queue does not necessarily have. The same catalog fallback remains for snapshots without a capture. Runtime selection, authentication policy, account selection, permissions, and queue delivery are unchanged.

## Evidence

On upstream `3ff1109b0a666e1163fea47abc5d24afb80cda1e`, the synthetic queued case fails before inference: `openai-responses` requires an API key, but the configured profile supports subscription auth. With this change the queued turn reaches the synthetic Codex harness once with `openai-chatgpt-responses` and its configured OAuth profile, retains its session/thread, and delivers one reply.

117 tests passed across 8 files; typed lint and formatting passed. Focused suites cover native/host route ownership, authentication planning, catalog capture, queued custody and settlement, WebChat admission, and queued cancellation/revocation. The regression uses real queue drain and route planning with an invented catalog and a synthetic harness; it does not use a real account or launch the native Codex app server.

The fork branch is based on its existing main; its clean merge with the upstream SHA above produces the exact tree tested locally.

prs.title: feat(msteams): show pie and bar charts in Teams messages
prs.body:
Closes #204138

## What Problem This Solves

When an OpenClaw agent sends chart data to Microsoft Teams, the Teams adapter turns the chart into a list of values before sending the card. Teams users lose the visualization even when the chart can be represented in an Adaptive Card.

## User Impact

Teams messages can show native pie charts and vertical bars, including grouped bars for multiple series. Line and area charts continue to show readable text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Teams renderer maps portable chart blocks to Microsoft's chart elements. Cards that contain native charts declare Adaptive Card schema 1.5. The adapter reuses OpenClaw's chart text formatter and preserves authored fallback replies when no chart or control can render natively. [Microsoft Teams chart reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/task-modules-and-cards/cards/charts-in-adaptive-cards)

## Evidence

- An isolated OpenClaw Gateway sent two cards through the production `msteams` adapter to a loopback Bot Framework Connector. Both requests returned HTTP 200. The mixed card contained `Chart.Pie`, `Chart.VerticalBar`, and `Chart.VerticalBar.Grouped` on schema 1.5. The capture matched the input values, category order, axis titles, and grouped series names.
- The mixed card retained readable area-chart text alongside the native charts. The area-only card delivered the same text on schema 1.4.
- The outbound regression reproduced the text-only result on the base revision. All 97 focused Teams tests passed on the PR head. The full local build, extension typecheck, targeted lint, formatting, and docs lint passed.
- The Designer preview shows the single-series bar’s explicit y-axis title and omits a separate series legend. Live Teams web rendering is pending. Independent local autoreview of `e6b42e3..f47ca50` at P2 was unavailable because the CLI account rejected the review models.

### Before and after in Microsoft’s Adaptive Card Designer

Both previews use the same synthetic chart data and Standard preview width. The baseline card came from the renderer at `e6b42e3`. The after card was the exact payload captured from the Gateway at `f47ca50`.

| Before · text fallback | After · three native charts and area fallback |
| --- | --- |
| ![Base renderer shows all chart data as text](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/12794ac0-8d4e-453d-8b83-c4085c1e708c) | ![Captured card shows pie, vertical bar, grouped bar, and area chart fallback](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b4514fec-851b-44cc-a213-fbe3e147317b) |

prs.title: feat(mcp-events): accept a callback base URL with a path prefix
prs.body:
Closes #184684

## What Problem This Solves

MCP Events can't receive callbacks through a reverse proxy or webhook relay that gives the Gateway a path instead of its own hostname, because `callbackOrigin` rejects any URL with a path.

## User Impact

User impact: operators set `callbackBaseUrl` to an HTTPS URL that can include a path prefix, such as `https://proxy.example.com/openclaw`, and callbacks go to `<callbackBaseUrl>/plugins/mcp-events/callback/<binding>`.

`callbackBaseUrl` replaces `callbackOrigin`. A config that still has `callbackOrigin` fails validation with the next step, `openclaw doctor --fix`, which also runs during `openclaw update` and, when the state databases are older than the build, in the state upgrade at Gateway start. Doctor moves the value as it is, so the callback URL doesn't change and existing subscriptions are kept.

## Why This Change Was Made

The proxy removes the prefix and forwards `/plugins/mcp-events/callback/<binding>`, which the existing route already serves, so only the URL OpenClaw gives the MCP server changes. Voice Call's `publicUrl` already works this way: a full public URL with a path that a reverse proxy maps to a local route.

I also considered carrying callbacks over MCP Relay, so a local Gateway would need no proxy at all. I left it out: the relay's ingress currently refuses webhooks, and MCP Events would then depend on a second plugin.

`callbackOrigin` shipped in stable releases from 2026.10.10 through the current latest, 2026.11.7, so the rename ships a Doctor migration, following the existing plugin config renames. Doctor only moves values the old setting accepted. A `callbackOrigin` with a path fails at startup today; moved as a base URL it would start and send callbacks to the wrong path. Doctor removes such a value instead, without echoing it (it can hold credentials; the config backup keeps it), and asks for `callbackBaseUrl`. A disabled entry is then valid, and Doctor's existing quarantine for invalid plugin configs disables an enabled one, so `openclaw update` still proceeds.

The tests add 141 lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/mcp-events-callback-base-url.txt`. The config surface doesn't grow.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: `pnpm test:extension mcp-events` (17 passed) and the new config and Doctor tests (17 passed in 0.8 s). The Doctor contract closure guard passes. Cases are listed below.
- Red/green: with the resolver from `main`, all 13 new config tests fail; with this change they pass.
- Docs: `pnpm docs:check-config-examples`, `docs:check-mdx` and `docs:check-links` pass (0 broken links), and `git diff --check` is clean.
- `pnpm check:changed`: everything this change touches passes, including type checks, lint, format, the config baseline, the Doctor contract guards and the test-line ratchet. Three checks fail locally for reasons outside this change; details below.
- Live run on macOS with an isolated Gateway (own home, state and profile, loopback port 18871):
  - `callbackBaseUrl` set to a hosted webhook relay URL that addresses receivers by path and forwards to localhost. The Gateway subscribed to a real MCP Events server, a signed test event reached its callback, and the automation started.
  - A config with only `callbackOrigin` stopped the Gateway with the Doctor hint. `openclaw doctor --fix` moved it to `callbackBaseUrl` with a backup, and `openclaw config validate` then passed.
  - An invalid `callbackOrigin` containing credentials, with the entry disabled and then enabled: `openclaw doctor --fix` removed it without printing it, quarantined the enabled entry, and `openclaw config validate` passed both times.
- Upgrade from 2026.11.7, the latest stable, installed from npm, with a live subscription, on macOS with an isolated Gateway and a real model (`anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`). 2026.11.7 accepts only a bare origin and Hookdeck relay URLs carry a path, so these runs used a public HTTPS tunnel as `callbackOrigin`. On 2026.11.7 the Gateway subscribed, the MCP server's verification challenge and a signed test event reached the callback, and the automation ran. Each upgrade path below starts from its own 2026.11.7 state, on this branch's build at 4faa40fa358:
  - Doctor first, as `openclaw update` runs it: `openclaw config validate` failed on `callbackOrigin` with the Doctor hint. `openclaw doctor --fix` moved `callbackOrigin` to `callbackBaseUrl` and migrated the state databases, with backups. The Gateway then loaded the subscription 2026.11.7 had saved in plugin state, with the same binding, callback URL, signing secret and remote subscription, sent nothing to the MCP server, and a new signed event reached the callback and the automation ran.
  - Gateway start with no Doctor run: since #198389, a Gateway whose state databases are older than its build runs the build's Doctor chain on a copy of the state before it starts. That chain moved `callbackOrigin` to `callbackBaseUrl` and migrated the databases, kept the previous config and databases as `*.pre-2026.11.7-<commit>-<stamp>`, and the Gateway started; `openclaw config validate` then passed. So on current `main` the Gateway no longer refuses to start on a 2026.11.7 config; the refusal with the Doctor hint shows only if that chain fails. The Gateway loaded the same binding, and the refresh run below continues from here.
- Data-model compatibility: the subscription record 2026.11.7 wrote (plugin state `mcp-events/subscriptions-v1`) loads unchanged on this build. Field by field against the record 2026.11.7 wrote, the Doctor-first run changed only the event cursor (`cursor`, `cursorRevision`) and `updatedAt`; binding id, callback URL, signing secret, remote subscription id, status and refresh deadline stayed the same. The refresh run also changed only what a refresh writes: refresh deadlines, a rotated signing secret with the old one kept as `previousSecret` for a short grace period. Both paths moved the state databases to this build's schema versions (`state/openclaw.sqlite` 36 to 41, the agent database 38 to 43; the others unchanged), and `openclaw config validate` passed afterwards.
- Verification challenge through a path prefix, on this branch's build (12 Nov run, on an earlier head of this PR): `callbackBaseUrl` set to a public HTTPS tunnel URL with an `/openclaw` prefix, in front of a reverse proxy that removes the prefix. The MCP server received the prefixed callback URL, sent its verification challenge to it, and the Gateway answered (200). A signed test event then reached the callback (200) and started the automation, and removing the automation unsubscribed with the same URL.
- Refresh after the upgrade: the Gateway-start upgrade from 2026.11.7 above, with the MCP server granting 7-minute subscriptions so a refresh fell due about 5.6 minutes after 2026.11.7 subscribed. This branch's Gateway refreshed the subscription with the same callback URL and the saved cursor, and the MCP server kept the same subscription, rotated its signing secret and moved its expiry forward. A signed test event after the refresh reached the callback (200 in the Event Gateway's delivery record, the same destination as the 2026.11.7 delivery) and the automation ran.
- TTL expiry after a restart (12 Nov run, on an earlier head of this PR, after the 2026.11.3 refresh run): with the same short grant, removing the automation after a Gateway restart left the subscription on the MCP server (`cleanup_failed`). When the grant ran out, the MCP server expired it and removed its delivery resources, with no manual cleanup. SEP-3415 makes unsubscribe optional for this reason: subscriptions expire when the client stops refreshing.
- Gaps:
  - The 2026.11.7 upgrade and refresh runs used a real model, and each automation run finished `ok` with the event's comment id as its reply. The earlier relay, path-prefix and TTL runs had no model, so their automation runs were admitted and then failed at the model step.
  - Removing the automation after a Gateway restart doesn't send `events/unsubscribe` (`cleanup_failed`), so the subscription stays on the MCP server until its grant expires, as the TTL run shows. 2026.11.3 alone does the same, so this change doesn't cause it.
  - Local review: the `autoreview` helper isn't installed here, so I ran independent agent reviews and the repo's `pr-simplify` pass instead. They led to the Doctor handling of invalid origins described above and the test-line allocation.

How I tested it, and why: I work at Hookdeck, and I hit this connecting OpenClaw to the [MCP Events bridge](https://github.com/hookdeck/mcp-events-bridge), an open-source MCP server I work on that turns webhooks into MCP events. For a Gateway on a laptop, the bridge gives the client a public relay URL on Hookdeck's Event Gateway (`https://hkdk.events/<id>`) that forwards to a local port. The live run used that setup: the bridge as the MCP server, the relay URL as `callbackBaseUrl`, and the relay forwarding to the Gateway on localhost.

prs.body:
## November 19 CI correction

- CI run 44354939034, attempt 2, failed PostgreSQL conformance (2/4), job 135604219541: `server-database-engine-cron.postgres.test.ts` polled `/readyz` after SIGINT and received `ECONNREFUSED`. This was a real failed run, not a green result.
- Integrated landed baseline `4aa45837b5dc9139769cfcbadf8fc206a2ba0747`, which repairs that exact test synchronization: observe completed HTTP shutdown using the existing trace, then retain the blocked-writer, original-process liveness, durable receipt, clean exit, restart, and no-replay assertions. No runtime shutdown policy, timeout, retry, or skip was changed.
- Published signed candidate `3e4055586de638536ef72bef1225bc2d60729898` through native proof publication. An independent review verified the original three-file attribution patch is byte-for-byte unchanged relative to the incorporated baseline; `git diff --check` passed.
- Exact-candidate CI [44569022550](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44569022550), attempt 2, completed **SUCCESS** at `3e4055586de638536ef72bef1225bc2d60729898`. All five PostgreSQL lanes passed. [Job 135720243773](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44569022550/job/135720243773) explicitly passed “drains accepted cron finalization before graceful stop and preserves it on restart” (46,442 ms), plus in-process restart and killed-Gateway recovery. Current CI, dependency-review, and security-sensitive-review gates are successful; the earlier cancelled context check was superseded by successful run 44569099368. R1 is resolved with this PR’s own new-head proof, not sibling results. No merge is authorized or claimed.


## Historical review-readiness qualification (November 16, 2026)

The following readiness and CI statements describe the prior heads named below, not the current November 19 candidate.

- Published conflict repair head: `a1d535cdcecd825cbee05d1480ffabb7e435f5ed`, preserving original contributor head `98a2597e6d2aba5fe7c77f780f97d52f0216f134` as the first parent and integrating main `7bccde609cbb0eaa054ac07a6d5ccd91ec712a92`. This is a merge into the existing fix branch, not a merge of this PR into main.
- Independent source review found no actionable P0–P3 findings. The adaptation preserves main's delivery-only projection envelope/filter and both the existing and added SQLite regression blocks. `git diff --check` passed.
- Existing live/regression evidence below remains prior-head evidence. This conflict-only adaptation has not been executed locally: the supported secretless AWS proof environment could not acquire credentials (no EC2 instance role). Exact-head CI run [43600215086](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43600215086) completed. Production types, core test-type stripes, lint, and test-line accounting passed; whole CI is not green. Its failures match three existing main defects: identity worker build budget (240 evaluated modules versus 220), TS18048 at scripts/perf/state-read-worker-bench.ts:373, and mock export preservation at src/infra/worker-idle-gc.test.ts:13. I independently compared the exact failure text with contemporary [main run 43599691199](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43599691199), specifically [build job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43599691199/job/132461948967), [type job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43599691199/job/132461949721), and [ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43599691199/job/132461948989). No unrelated repair or retry was added to this PR. All selected changed Node test jobs passed. The [owning SQLite regression job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43600215086/job/132463736345) passed all 16 tests, including completed-run steering attribution, identity mismatch, textless-user barriers, and main’s delivery-only restart case. The separate changed-channels job passed 73 tests across 8 files, including runtime context. The original live model proof is still prior-head evidence.
- Attribution and bounded lookup remain separate reviewable fixes under the existing transcript projection/reconciliation owners. Combining them later requires reconciling the shared projector, SQLite append tests, and documentation; neither is represented as testing their combination.

### Readiness boundary

Native review and preparation are now complete for this exact head. The independent P0–P3 conflict review was recovered and its saved attribution patch verified byte-for-byte against the current base-to-head diff. Its conclusions and the retained proof were recorded in the exact-head native review, which validated with `READY FOR /prepare-pr`, while preserving `tests.result: fail` and the attributed CI run 43600215086, attempt 2. The trusted native `prepare-run` then completed with `GATES_MODE=github_pending`, explicitly recording no successful gate proof. It verified that the remote was already at the same head and skipped pushing; no source, ancestry, or test result changed.

This is technical/native preparation readiness, not merge readiness or a waiver of enforced CI/security/review. Current head remains open, non-draft and mergeable but blocked. The existing ClawSweeper comment reviews original candidate `98a2597…`, not current head. GitHub has no submitted reviews or outstanding review requests; the inspected branch rule requires zero generic approvals with code-owner review enabled. No `required402` refusal was encountered during native review validation or preparation; no claim is made that an unobserved gate was cleared. The two required `openclaw/ci-gate` statuses remain failed. No merge was requested.

### Exact-head CI qualification

The four failed jobs in CI run [43600215086](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43600215086) reduce to three inherited defects, not four independent patch failures:

| Failed job | Observed failure and attribution |
| --- | --- |
| build-artifacts | `agents/identity-file.worker.js: 240 evaluated modules exceeds budget 220`; identical assertion in contemporary main job 132461948967. |
| PostgreSQL conformance (3/3) | The same 240/220 build assertion stops runtime preparation before any Vitest shard executes. Schema/trigger parity completed; this is not a failed PostgreSQL behavioral assertion or a conformance pass. |
| check-test-types | `scripts/perf/state-read-worker-bench.ts(373,52): TS18048: entry.tasksCompleted is possibly undefined`; same diagnostic in contemporary main job 132461949721. |
| checks-fast-baseline-ratchets | `src/infra/worker-idle-gc.test.ts:13: ../logging/subsystem.js` violates mock-export preservation; same failure in contemporary main job 132461948989. |

The automated failure table labels these jobs new because it compares against older scheduled main run 43594951095, whose matching jobs passed. The attribution above instead uses observed identical failures from main run 43599691199 at `559f68a57d14f997a7e7face4e2d07d574e9747c`. The failing benchmark, mock, worker entry, and budget-check files are unchanged between that main commit and this PR head. No CI result is relabeled green. Both red `openclaw/ci-gate` statuses report the underlying failed CI, rather than another product failure. The canceled PR-context run is superseded by the successful same-head [job 132470881354](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43602768456/job/132470881354).

Closes #197994

## What problem this solves

Recent-history reconciliation previously credited a completed assistant answer only to the nearest preceding user row. With full transcript coverage of `original user -> accepted steering user -> completed final`, the steering row received credit but the original could be re-quoted in a later model input, even when the completed run had answered both requests.

This can duplicate an already-answered request in context. Token cost and answer-quality effects have not been measured. The demonstrated case is an attribution problem, not a missing delivered final or insufficient lookup coverage.

## Implemented behavior and owners

The fix reuses producer-owned canonical metadata and the existing reconciliation owner:

- `src/config/sessions/transcript-recent-text.ts` adds `runId` and user `steerTargetRunId` only to the private turn-evidence projection. The public SDK text projection does not gain those fields.
- `src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.runtime.ts`, `omitAnsweredRecentHistory`, walks the returned chronological rows backward. A completed assistant records its known run ID. A user is attributed to `steerTargetRunId` when present, otherwise its own `runId`, and can be covered by a later completed answer of that run.
- Known conflicting run identities do not qualify through the nearest-user fallback. When either side lacks usable run identity, the legacy immediately preceding-user behavior remains; the code tracks unidentified completed replies separately from known completed runs.
- Every projected user resets the adjacency-only completion state. Private evidence now retains textless/image-only users as `text: ""` barriers, so an unrelated final is not paired across an invisible user row. Public recent text still excludes empty user text.
- Final omission still requires the same transport ID and unchanged trimmed body. Attachments, edits, unseen discussion, incomplete replies, earlier unrelated runs, and missing completion evidence remain eligible in the tested cases. Session/agent scope and the existing completion classifier are unchanged.

This does not remove the conservative reset, mark all consecutive users answered, create a second completion owner, add schemas/configuration, or change steering admission. The earlier explanatory documentation was subsequently trimmed; the current PR changes only the three source/test files listed above.

### What completion and acceptance mean here

This is host-side completed-run bookkeeping, not semantic answer grading. Accepted steering metadata alone is insufficient: the reader must also observe a completed assistant answer with the relevant run identity. Conversely, a host completion flag is not a generic guarantee that an answer's content satisfies every request. No semantic-answer detector was added.

The historical collector separately inspected the combined final's content. The regression fixtures supply canonical metadata and a final classification to exercise reconciliation; they do not themselves prove real steering admission or semantic coverage.

## Evidence: historical observation versus new verification

The evidence package is attached here: [openclaw-197994-evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34783568/openclaw-197994-evidence.zip)

`historical/observation.json` is a sanitized read-only reinspection of retained production canonical records and the native rollout. Its event date is November 11, 2026, and collection date is November 13. It reports:

- Original input and accepted steering belong to the same completed run.
- The final stopped normally and carries terminal-run metadata.
- The collector inspected two corresponding final-answer sections; the full final body is omitted from the public excerpt.
- The original request was subsequently quoted in a native recent-history input.

Run membership was copied separately from canonical metadata; the baseline projector did not expose these identity fields. The collector used the real retained events as an injected read-only page, not a fresh storage/channel/Gateway experiment. Its installed/source commit labels are provenance fields, not a new attestation that this fix ran on the historical date.

**The original candidate-only live proof passed on `98a2597e6d2aba5fe7c77f780f97d52f0216f134` before the conflict repair**, completing at `2026-11-13T03:55:07.004Z`. This is prior-head evidence, not a live execution of current head `a1d535cdcecd825cbee05d1480ffabb7e435f5ed`. A synthetic authenticated local channel exercised the real Gateway/core dispatch, canonical storage, native Codex and configured provider. A declared read-only tool held a checkpoint while a second actual inbound request was admitted through native steering; the gate was released only after a correlated steering acceptance. Original `runId`, steering `steerTargetRunId` and completed-final `runId` agree in the persisted transcript. A subsequent request supplied both inputs plus an unrelated ambient candidate: core removed the two answered inputs and retained only the unrelated candidate.

The executed harness required exact submitted-body matches for all three primary native requests and all three newest provider-user inputs. One native conversation and one separate auxiliary recap were observed. The newly appended input does not repeat the answered requests; their earlier retained native history is not deleted. The build completed with exit zero in 354 seconds and exact build/runtime/Codex provenance verified. Fixture and runner cleanup succeeded. `LIVE-EVIDENCE.md` indexes the raw synthetic records, exact executed harness and verification scope. This is a candidate-only synthetic-transport live test, not Discord transport, a fresh live base/fix A/B, or a production deployment.

## Original candidate red-on-baseline and green-on-fix validation

The original integrator ran the then-current 15-test persisted SQLite suite against the two original production owner files from the base, then restored the fixed source. `attribution-persisted-red.log` records **5 failed, 10 passed**:

- Completed original plus accepted steering remained eligible incorrectly.
- Two explicit run-mismatch/steering-target-precedence cases incorrectly omitted a pending input.
- Empty-user and image-only-user barriers incorrectly allowed omission of an earlier unanswered input.

These are owner assertion failures, not the earlier compiler setup failure. `attribution-source-restored.json` records the restored production hashes; both match original tested candidate `98a2597e6d2aba5fe7c77f780f97d52f0216f134`, not the later conflict-repair head.

`attribution-final-green.log` records **38 passed** across three files on original tested candidate `98a2597e6d2aba5fe7c77f780f97d52f0216f134` (prior-head evidence):

- SQLite reconciliation: **15/15**. Covers successful shared-run completion; error, abort, truncation, commentary, and unsettled native output; explicit mismatch; steering-target precedence; missing-identity fallback; edited text; attachments; textless/image-only barriers; and unchanged public text projection.
- Provider prefix stability: **14/14**.
- Channel context runtime: **9/9**.

The final wrapper took 274.83 seconds, including 124.87 seconds of cold worker compilation. The SQLite file took 155.47 seconds including preparation/transform; its test bodies totaled about 6.6 seconds. These timings describe the original candidate handoff, before PR CI; current-head CI results are recorded above.

Original candidate `98a2597e6d2aba5fe7c77f780f97d52f0216f134` has the same four source/doc hashes as the reviewed tested candidate; the commit's formatting hook did not change them. `candidate-review.json` records those hashes and review scope. Core production and plugin-sdk test-leaf typechecks, dedicated-core lint, four-file formatting and diff checks passed; the bounded static receipts are included under `attribution-static/`.

### Re-run the fix tests

From the prepared branch with repository dependencies installed according to `CONTRIBUTING.md`:

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/steering-attribution-cache \
  pnpm test src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.sqlite.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts \
  src/channels/inbound-event/session-transcript-context.runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

For the persisted baseline comparison, use a separate checkout at the base commit and apply only the regression-test file from the prepared commit, leaving production files at the base. Then run the SQLite test file alone. Do not overwrite a running checkout's source or reuse another run's active dependency installation.

## Portable reproduction of the original mechanism

The unchanged bundled baseline helper requires Node 26.12.1+ and no checkout, install, credentials, network, model, or Gateway:

```sh

# Optional baseline checkout comparison:
node reproduce.mjs /path/to/openclaw > checkout-observed.json
```

It resolves `source/` relative to itself and was verified after copying the package outside the checkout and running from `/`. `SOURCE-MANIFEST.json` pins the bundled owner to `489774034984cd3ef78706125f20f4b25723288b` (package `2026.11.3`) with its exact hash and MIT license. `current-base-reproduction-output.json` confirms the same baseline owner/behavior on the newer base.

The seven executed baseline cases include full coverage (limit four, all three rows returned, original retained), an ordinary single-input completion, a larger candidate budget that does not repair attribution, incomplete output, an unrelated earlier unanswered request, and independent edit/attachment controls.

These are exact production-function probes with a synthetic bounded reader. They do not exercise persistence, admission, the real projector, prompt rendering, or a provider. The helper's assertions deliberately describe the old bug. It is not a green-on-fix acceptance script: its synthetic rows do not carry the newly required run identities. Use the persisted branch tests for the implemented contract.

## Limits and submission state

- The existing `candidate count * 2` read budget remains in this branch. Run attribution only uses returned evidence; older or unavailable evidence can still cause conservative re-quotation. This handoff does not claim unconditional all-history suppression or alter lookup policy.
- The persisted regressions verify storage, projection and `InboundHistory` reconciliation; the separate fresh live records establish real native steering acceptance and next-input behavior. Neither is semantic answer grading.

A mechanical combination with the separately prepared candidate-coverage change conflicts in the shared projector, SQLite tests and Discord documentation. If that change lands first, rebase and reconcile those owners before landing this branch; combined behavior has not been tested here.

- No known-good multi-input release, population-wide rate, production latency, or token-cost improvement was established. Do not label this a bisected regression.
