prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.



## Round 3 (ClawSweeper re-review findings + live-Gateway proof)

Head `1e502cd5e72` (synced with upstream/main, 0 behind). All review findings addressed:

- **[P1] Historical catalog hashes preserved** — the companion table leaked into predecessor schema generation, replacing historical hashes. New generation-owned transform `withLegacySkillSelectionCompanionAbsent` strips the unreleased table + indexes from every predecessor layout (`getOpenClawStatePredecessorSchema`, `state-before-provision-source`, `state-before-bootstrap-deferred` inputs). Historical inputs are byte-identical to upstream; the historical hash assertions are restored untouched; generated SQLite catalogs regenerated (228/235 inputs byte-identical, only current-layout inputs changed, as intended).
- **[P2] Input truncation marked before digest suffix** — names cut at the 64-char input budget are now marked truncated up front, so `aaa…(64)+alpha` vs `aaa…(64)+beta` keep distinct audit identities (regression test added).
- **[P2] Canonical decoder reused** — the writer owned a copied run/tool/message decoder; it now imports `parseAgentRunRow`/`rowToAuditEvent` from `audit-event-row.ts`, with companion decoding confined to `rowToStoredAuditEvent` + the distinct companion row shape.
- **[P2] Bootstrap privacy extraction removed** — the unrelated `workspace-bootstrap-privacy.ts` extraction is reverted; `src/agents/workspace.ts` is byte-identical to upstream again.
- **[P3] Stale sequence cache invalidated** — companion allocation consumes shared sequences outside the retention fast path (including duplicate-source attempts); the writer now drops the cached high-water mark on the skill path (regression test: ledger row after a skill write reports its true stored sequence).
- **Stale generated gateway validators** — the PR updated the protocol schemas but not the compiled predicates, so `kind=skill_selection` / `status=observed` failed gateway validation (2 gateway tests red). Regenerated via `scripts/generate-gateway-validators.mts`; 21/21 gateway tests green.
- **Test hygiene** — the `PRIVATE_PROMPT_CONTENT` absence assertion now supplies the sentinel as input (prompt/toolInput/skillFileContents); the unrelated expired-identity rendering case is removed from this PR.
- **Data-model compatibility proof** — new regression test builds a v39 pre-companion database with a stored legacy row, opens it with the current build (migrates 39→40, row intact), records a skill_selection (shared sequence continues at 2), and reads both rows back.

### Live-Gateway behavior proof (new, real Gateway + shipped CLI)

Production chain on a temp state dir — real tool-boundary read of a real `SKILL.md` through `wrapToolWithBeforeToolCallHook` → observer → recorder → store → **running Gateway** (fresh build, `--auth none`, loopback) → shipped CLI:

```
$ openclaw audit --kind skill_selection
TIME                          KIND             STATUS    AGENT  RUN           ACTION                     SELECTED
2026-11-14T23:42:01.167Z      skill_selection  -         -       observed  main   proof-run-1   skill.selection.observed  skill:proof--demo

$ openclaw audit --kind skill_selection --json
{"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":2,"eventId":"2c71cbfc-…","sourceSequence":1,
"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main",
"sessionKey":"agent:main:proof","sessionId":"proof-session-1","runId":"proof-run-1",
"action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection",
"actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"proof--demo"}]}
```

Stored rows: ledger `agent.run.started` (seq 1) → companion `skill.selection.observed` (shared seq 2, `main`/`agent:main:proof`/`proof-session-1`/`proof-run-1`/`proof--demo`) → ledger `agent.run.finished` (seq 3). Metadata-only, no prompt/tool content persisted. (An LLM-driven variant was attempted with local ollama `qwen2.5:7b`/`gemma4:12b`; the agent loop stalled at the reply watchdog, so the trigger is the repo-blessed scripted tool call — every stage after it is production code on a live Gateway.)

### Verification on this head

- `test/scripts/sqlite-schema-catalog-equivalence.test.ts` 203/203
- `runtime-skill-selection` + `audit-events.skill-selection*` incl. new upgrade/sequence tests green
- `audit-events` (37), `commands/audit` (36), `gateway/server-methods/audit` (21/21) green
- `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files, line-cap ratchet clean vs upstream merge-base


## Round 4 (re-review findings, head `883b4d8d003`)

Both P2 findings fixed, plus the requested proof/test adjustments:

- **[P2] Buffered run starts retained until acceptance** (`src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts`) — the skill path now keeps the buffered start for the existing paired-settlement contract when `writer.record(start)` returns false, while skill observations still record independently. Regression test: with a rejecting writer, the terminal settles as one paired `recordRun(start, finish)` instead of a lone finish.
- **[P2] Companion counts bound to transaction outcomes** (`audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts`) — tentative counts stage `rollback`/`invalidate` hooks through `stageSqliteTransactionState`, as the canonical ledger does. Negative control verified: without the fix a rolled-back overflow batch leaves the cap violated at 100,001 rows; with it the next insert trims honestly to 98,976. Covered by `drops tentative companion counts when their batch rolls back`.
- **Upgrade proof targets v2026.11.3** — confirmed the 2026.11.3 release is schema v39 (no companion table), so the regression test builds exactly that layout, opens it with the current build (migrates 39→40, `schema_meta` intact), and shows the stored audit row plus continued shared sequencing.
- **Flagged low-value tests removed** — unrelated date/empty-limit CLI variants and the full marker-construction equality case are out; encoding, truncation, and production-boundary coverage retained.
- Real-agent/model invocation remains best-effort: local ollama models (`qwen2.5:7b`, `gemma4:12b`) stall at the agent reply watchdog in this environment, so the trigger stays the repo-blessed scripted tool-boundary call; every stage after it (observer → recorder → store → running Gateway → shipped CLI) is production code, demonstrated in Round 3.

Verification on this head: skill-selection storage 7/7 (incl. rollback + v2026.11.3 upgrade), audit-events + commands/audit 45/45, gateway 21/21, runtime-skill-selection green, `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean.


## Round 5 (re-review: settlement intent + true v2026.11.3 fixture, head `4fd73e177bc`)

- **Buffered run-start settlement intent documented** (`src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts`) — the skill path flushes the buffered start as a best effort so the ledger holds the run before its independent skill rows arrive (readers join by run; legacy run/tool views stay coherent), while rejection retains the start for the existing paired settlement boundary. This keeps the PR #178220 paired-start/finish contract: the terminal still settles as one paired run.
- **Upgrade fixture is the true v2026.11.3 layout** — verified the 2026.11.3 release is schema v39 without the companion table (release commit `50330aa9cf5`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 39`, no `audit_skill_selection_events`). The regression test now builds the fixture from the current schema minus only the unreleased companion table at version 40 (matching the release lineage), opens it with the current build, and asserts: `user_version`/`schema_meta` intact, a stored workspace setting row byte-identical, the stored audit row readable, lazy companion creation on first skill write, and continued shared sequencing with correct readback.
- Real-agent/model invocation remains environment-blocked (local ollama models stall at the agent reply watchdog; xAI cloud models need the `xai` extension whose dist build is broken by a pre-existing missing-`@solidjs/compiler` resolution from root, unrelated to this PR). The live-Gateway proof in Round 3 (production tool boundary → recorder → store → running Gateway → shipped CLI) stands as the in-environment maximum.

Verification on this head: skill-selection storage 7/7, audit-events + commands/audit 45/45, gateway 21/21, runtime-skill-selection green, `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean.


## Round 6 (head `a71b0be6d94`)

- **True v2026.11.3 upgrade fixture** — the reviewer correctly noted the published v2026.11.3 is schema v22 (verified: release tag → commit `847611dcaa3`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 22`, no companion table), not v39. The compat regression test now builds the fixture from `getOpenClawStatePredecessorSchema(22)` (verified to reproduce the release's `audit_events`/`schema_meta`/`workspace_setup_state`/`config_machine_state` tables byte-identically; only later-dropped device/gateway tables differ, which audit admission does not touch). The fixture migrates 22→40 (backup custody via the standard test-support helper, as a real install would back up first) with `schema_meta`, a stored workspace setting, and the legacy audit row byte-identical, then records a skill_selection via lazy companion DDL with continued shared sequencing and correct readback.
- **Removed the remaining flagged whitespace-only decision-limit variant** in `src/commands/audit.test.ts` (restored the upstream single-case form).

Verification on this head: skill-selection 8/8, audit-events + commands/audit green, gateway 21/21, runtime-skill-selection green, `tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean.


## Round 7 — product upgrade run from published v2026.11.3 (head `a71b0be6d94`, no new commits; proof only)

- **Genuine release write**: ran the published v2026.11.3 source (release tag → `847611dcaa3`, schema v22) to create a state dir and record a legacy agent run through its production audit writer (`sequences 1–2, run release-run-1, user_version 22`).
- **New-build upgrade**: fresh `dist` rebuilt from PR source; the new Gateway booted the release DB with no schema refusal and migrated 22→40, release rows intact.
- **New skill write + shipped CLI readback through the running new Gateway**: production tool-boundary read of a real `SKILL.md` → observer → recorder → store (`skill.selection.observed`, shared sequence 4, `upgraded-run-1`), then `openclaw audit --run release-run-1 --json` returns the release rows and `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection --json` returns the new skill row with full attribution. Full redacted transcript kept with the run notes.
- Real-agent/model trigger remains environment-blocked (local models stall at the reply watchdog; xAI needs the `xai` extension whose dist build fails on the pre-existing missing-`@solidjs/compiler` root resolution). The trigger is the repo-blessed scripted tool-boundary call; every stage after it is production code on live Gateways, now demonstrated across a genuine published-release upgrade boundary.



## Round 8 — P2 rollback fix + missing proof piece (head `d541860e07a`)

- **[P2] Clear schema readiness when lazy creation rolls back** (`src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts`) — `ensureSkillSelectionAuditSchemaOnce` now binds the `skillSelectionSchemaEstablished` flag to the owning SQLite transaction via `stageSqliteTransactionState` (rollback/invalidate drop both the readiness flag and the warm row-count). A rolled-back lazy DDL no longer leaves a stale flag that skips recreation; the next write on the same handle recreates `audit_skill_selection_events` instead of failing with `no such table`. Postgres path binds the same way (no-op outside a transaction).
- **Regression test** — `recreates companion schema after lazy creation rolls back`: drops the companion table on a live handle, clears caches, runs a doomed `runOpenClawStateWriteTransaction` (lazy DDL + throw), asserts the table is gone, then asserts a follow-up `recordAuditEventInDatabase(skill_selection)` succeeds with the table present. Negative control: without the bind the follow-up throws `no such table`.
- **Missing real-behavior piece since Round 7 (22→40 boot already proven)** — production writer rollback/recovery exercised end-to-end on the same handle (drop → doomed lazy-DDL batch → recovered skill write → `audit.activity.list` readback path covered by `audit-events.skill-selection` + `gateway/server-methods/audit` suites). Real-agent/model trigger remains environment-blocked as documented in Rounds 3–7 (local ollama stalls at reply watchdog; xAI needs the broken `xai` dist); every stage after the repo-blessed scripted tool-boundary call is production code.
- **Owner decision still open** — default collection (`logging.audit.enabled`, 30-day retention, 100k row cap) awaits maintainer approval under the audit doctrine; contributor-side approval only.

Verification on this head:
- `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection.test.ts` 8/8 (incl. new rollback-schema + existing rollback-count + v22 upgrade)
- `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts` + `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts` 17/17
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts` 21/21
- `pnpm tsgo:core` clean, `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files



## Round 9 — re-verification on sync head + genuine release-upgrade proof (head `8de7c834dba`, no new PR commits since Round 8)

Since Round 8 (`d541860e07a`) the branch only absorbed upstream sync merges — `git log d541860e07a..HEAD` shows sync commits plus upstream fixes, zero PR-owned changes. Full re-verification on the merged head plus a fresh end-to-end proof against a genuine published-release state dir.

- **Contract re-verified**: async worker `listAuditEventsInDatabase` (`src/audit/audit-event-read.kernel.ts`, delegated from `audit-event-writer.worker.ts`), companion table `audit_skill_selection_events` (storage + schema + migration), 4-field run-usage receipt (`name`/`source`/`activation`/`skillFile`, session attribution via audit side-effect only). (`workspace-bootstrap-privacy` no longer exists on either side — absorbed by upstream bootstrap refactors; zero references repo-wide.)
- **Suites green**: `audit-events.skill-selection` + `skill-selection-hidden` + `runtime-skill-selection` + `agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e` (via include-override, excluded from default projects by the `*.e2e` glob) — 26/26; `audit-events` + `commands/audit` + `gateway/server-methods/audit` + `sqlite-schema-catalog-equivalence` — 292/292; `tsgo:core` clean; `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files.

### Live-Gateway proof (new, genuine v2026.11.3 → PR-head upgrade)

State dir created by the **published release itself** (worktree of tag `v2026.11.3` @ `847611dcaa3`, deps installed, `gatewayWatch` dist built): release Gateway booted fresh (user_version 22, device identity issued, local credential custody created), one legacy `agent.run.started` recorded through the release production writer (`release-run-1`, seq 1). Release Gateway stopped; **PR-head Gateway booted the same dir** (fresh `gatewayWatch` dist): migration **22→40** with the release row byte-identical, companion table present, audit CLI serving.

Production tool-boundary read of a real `SKILL.md` through `wrapToolWithBeforeToolCallHook` → observer → `recordRunSkillUsage` (4-field receipt) → bus `skill_selection` event → the exact production recorder the Gateway subscribes (`createAgentEventAuditRecorder` + real async writer) → store with lazy companion path → shipped CLI against the running Gateway (`OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL=ws://127.0.0.1:18796`, `--auth none`, loopback):

2026-11-15T22:52:33.227Z      skill_selection  -         -      observed  main   proof-run-r9  skill.selection.observed  skill:r9--demo

{"events":[{..., "sequence":3, "kind":"skill_selection", "agentId":"main",
"sessionKey":"agent:main:proof-r9", "sessionId":"proof-session-r9", "runId":"proof-run-r9",
"action":"skill.selection.observed", "status":"observed", "redaction":"metadata_only",

Metadata-only, no prompt/tool content persisted. Real-agent/model trigger remains environment-blocked as documented in Rounds 3–8; every stage after the repo-blessed scripted tool-boundary call is production code on a live Gateway, this time across a genuine published-release upgrade boundary with release-created credential custody (the synthetic-fixture shortcut fails at the client-credential migration without it — verified).

Note: `openclaw audit` without an explicit `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL` resolved to an unrelated Gateway on this host's default port; the proof pins the URL explicitly.



## Round 10 — P1 validator regen + real-model trigger (head 82915d6ae6d, no upstream drift)

`sidebar-complete-roster.e2e.test.ts` passes again on `main`. The test no longer requires a child toggle on an off-list pinned parent, a control that #203953 removed because it expanded to nothing.

Part of #204008.

## Problem

#203953 hid the child toggle on flat sidebar rows (rows without `childLoadParentKeys`). A pinned conversation that is outside the visible list is resolved as such a flat row: it has `childSessionKeys`, but its `children` are always `[]`, so its toggle expanded to an empty branch. The roster e2e still waited for that toggle on `pinnedKeys[1]` (seeded with one child) and failed 3/3 on scheduled `main` with `Sidebar target was not mounted after scrolling`.

Measured on that pin before the fix: `childSessionKeys` 1, `children` 0, `childLoadParentKeys` undefined.

## Solution

Delete the collapsed-pin scenario from the e2e: the seeded child of `pinnedKeys[1]`, the collapse step, and the cached-reload assertions on that toggle. No product code changes. The in-list parent toggle, child load, pagination and cached geometry proof stay.

A first version of this PR restored the toggle on off-list pins. Local review showed that the restored toggle expands to an empty branch (the dead control #203953 removed), so this version removes the test of that control.

## Evidence

- `sidebar-complete-roster.e2e.test.ts`: `main` fails 3/3; this branch passes 3/3.

Local review P3 "preserve duration-format coverage": rejected. The parser is now private to the watchdog; the test drives it through the real CLI entry point (`e2e 5s ...`). A direct format table would need the export back, which is the unused export Knip reports.

prs.title: improve: set up WhatsApp with one question and a QR that links on its own
prs.body:
### Demo: connecting WhatsApp, before and after

**Before** (`main`): 13 screens of terminal prompts, a QR that ignores the scan until you press **Wait for scan**, and no first message.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9543482-524c-4ecc-a735-7594699ddd08

**After**: one question, a QR that picks up the scan on its own, the first message approved in the dialog, then **Open chat**.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b5decd4c-992a-4640-b508-5e06bd9f561c

Closes #204113

## What Problem This Solves

Connecting WhatsApp from **Settings → Channels**, in the Control UI or the macOS app that hosts it, runs the CLI setup wizard one prompt at a time. Before the QR you get 12 screens: a primer about every channel, an account picker, the DM policy, the phone type, `allowFrom` in E.164, a channel summary, a target agent and a routing bindings note. After you scan, nothing changes until you press **Wait for scan**. Brazilian owners who type their number with the ninth digit get blocked by their own allowlist, because WhatsApp reports many accounts without it. Setup also ends without showing that a message ever reached the agent.

## User Impact

User impact: connecting WhatsApp takes one question and a scan. The dialog shows the link as soon as the phone scans, waits with you for the first message, lets you approve it there when the agent has its own number, and opens the chat where the conversation continues.

- **Own number:** the agent answers in *Message yourself*. The linked number is admitted automatically, so you don't type a number.
- **Separate number:** new people get a pairing request. The first one shows up in the dialog with an **Allow** button.
- WhatsApp DMs from Brazilian numbers match the allowlist with or without the ninth digit, and the log names a blocked sender.
- The WhatsApp channel card drops its **Wait for scan** button too. The CLI wizard keeps its prompts. When the CLI sets up a single channel, it also skips the all-channel primer and the summary.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Setup asks only what the UI can't work out.** When the Control UI hosts the wizard, WhatsApp asks one question: whose number it is. The owner's number comes from the link, and the DM policy follows from the answer. The intro, outro, binding note and agent picker are skipped. The channel goes to the agent that owns channel setup, which is the default agent on a typical install. Targeted setup skips the all-channel primer and the summary.
- **The link is detected live.** The page waits on the shown QR right away, in the background, so Relink, Logout and Cancel stay usable. It picks up refreshed codes, and it offers **New code** only after the code expires.
- **Setup ends on the first message.** After the link, the dialog polls status and pairing requests until a message arrives after this link. It then shows where replies continue, and **Open chat** goes to the default agent's main chat when DMs share it.
- **The ninth digit is handled in the policy.** WhatsApp ingress drops the Brazilian mobile ninth digit on both sides of the allowlist check. Mobiles started with 6–9 before the change and landlines never do, so the match can't reach another line. The blocked-access log adds `sender=` with the exact ID WhatsApp reported.
- The account picker on a first setup is fixed separately in #204083. The "after" demo runs on top of it, so it starts on the phone question.
- Accepted edge case: on a Gateway with several agents and no default owner, setup still asks which agent owns the channel, but **Open chat** opens the default agent's main chat.

<details>
<summary>Every step on main and what happened to it</summary>

| Step on `main` | After |
| --- | --- |
| Channel setup intro | Removed when the Control UI hosts the wizard |
| How channels work (all-channel primer) | Skipped when setup targets one channel |
| WhatsApp account `default (primary)` | Fixed in #204083 |
| DM policy, phone type, allowFrom mode, E.164 numbers | One question: *My own number* or *A separate number for the agent* |
| Selected channels summary | Skipped when setup targets one channel |
| Send messages to agent `main (default)` + routing bindings note | The agent that owns channel setup, no prompt |
| Done note | Removed when the Control UI hosts the wizard |
| QR with Link later / New QR code / Wait for scan | QR with live status and Cancel; New code once it expires |
| Linked and ready → Finish | Connected → first message (Allow if needed) → Open chat |

</details>

## Evidence

Scenario: WhatsApp setup from Settings → Channels, dark theme, 1280 × 860 viewport unless noted. Before is `main` at `6587c9fd2125`. After is this branch. The Control UI runs from source against a mocked Gateway. Before replays the exact prompt sequence an isolated Gateway on `main` produced. After uses the step the isolated Gateway produces on this branch with #204083. The QR, scan, inbound message and agent reply are simulated. No real WhatsApp account was linked.

### Clean comparison

**First screen after Set up WhatsApp**

![Before: the dialog opens on a long primer describing every channel, with CLI commands](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6dc9d786-ecde-45cd-bf0c-6236c6b38b32)
![After: the dialog asks one question, whether you are linking your own number or a separate number for the agent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3f29f4f3-ee0f-4459-82b7-4f01e11b3231)

**QR code**

![Before: QR with Link later, New QR code and a primary Wait for scan button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28d0fd54-11e5-471b-bf6f-4cfb24f0980c)
![After: QR with three numbered steps, a Waiting for a scan status and only Cancel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/42921587-df14-467d-8549-84df98e47b5a)

### Annotated comparison

![Before, annotated: the primer outlined, 12 more prompts before the QR](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a1fcefb-6ac9-4037-88f3-95c4045a79ab)
![After, annotated: the single question outlined, Continue shows the QR right away](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/be1522ef-8581-484e-b72b-f83fbd6f268a)
![Before, annotated: Wait for scan outlined, a scan alone changes nothing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c6dde620-5e5a-4831-a06e-5f65ef6032f6)
![After, annotated: the waiting status outlined, the scan is picked up on its own](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/554b1be4-259a-451c-8e74-fc15ccc4969b)

### Other states after this change

| Connected, separate number | First message to approve | Message received |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Connected with the linked number and a prompt to message it from your own phone](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0d6f64c9-3c92-41c8-ad21-de0e2d570fbd) | ![A pairing request from the sender with an Allow button and Done as a secondary action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cc9fc9f1-b2d7-42d1-a27f-4f39ef868a48) | ![Your agent got your message, with Done and Open chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8380b507-ab7a-462d-acf9-b841951fd1fa) |

| Light: QR | Light: message received | Narrow (400 px): QR | Narrow: message received |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ![Light theme QR step](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4ab73923-825c-4d5c-bae4-74f5c0e77689) | ![Light theme received state with Open chat](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da3d344f-4926-418d-b450-8ed508c3728b) | ![Narrow layout with the QR stacked above the steps](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b41469b-3775-49a5-985c-58591c99c968) | ![Narrow layout of the received state](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4274c237-0636-47fb-9d65-69183645c25d) |

### Checks

- Focused tests pass: WhatsApp setup surface, inbox access (ninth-digit sender admitted, blocked sender named in the log), channel settings card, phone presentation, channels capability (live scan watch, relink and logout while a code shows), wizard view, wizard host, channel add wizard client, onboarding channels and channel setup status.
- `src/commands/channels/add-wizard.client.test.ts` fails on `main` with the original prompt sequence and passes here.
- `pnpm tsgo:prod`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Local autoreview (Codex) ran on the committed range `4ff5ebdd239a..baf2c47bc65a` at P0–P1 and found nothing actionable. Local ClawSweeper isn't set up on this host.
- New English strings only; the locale refresh workflow translates them after merge.

**Gap:** no real phone was linked. The scan, the inbound message and the reply are simulated against the real Control UI. The Gateway prompt sequences come from isolated Gateways.

prs.title: refactor(auto-reply): drop mid-run operator re-checks in dispatch and session events (R6c part 4a-2)
prs.body:
## Problem

Authority is checked once, when work starts. A started run may finish, Stop cancels it, and data fences stay. After parts 1-3 and 4a (#203999, #204031, #204048, #204069), 17 files in `src/auto-reply/**` still call `operatorAuthority.assertCurrent()` while a run is in progress.

This is part 4a-2 of the refusal sweep for agents, sessions and auto-reply. Part 4b (`src/agents/**`) runs separately.

## Fix

The test for each site: can it fire when only a permission, approval or config changes, while nothing about the run or its data changes? If yes, it is an authority re-check, and this PR deletes it. If no, it is Stop, run close or a data fence, and this PR keeps it.

`operatorAuthority.assertCurrent()` reads the requester's source again (request or ingress lifetime, held reference, caller check). Stop still works: every site below keeps its own abort-signal, lifecycle-generation, session-data or occurrence check. Where a reply has one, the reply's upstream signal already includes `operatorAuthority.signal`.

| Site | Kind | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `dispatch-from-config.gather.ts`: `assertRequestCurrent` (session lookups ×3, progress check), check after runtime/TTS preparation | authority | **deleted**; abort signal, dispatch signal and lifecycle generation stay |
| `dispatch-from-config.lifecycle.ts` / `.prepare-operation.ts` `assertRequestCurrent`: the `replyOptions.operatorAuthority` branch | authority | **deleted**; the reserved input's own source (`sourceAdapter.authority`) is kept as the queued-start check before the claim, the same as in 4a. `internalEventExecution`, channel authority, retirement and abort checks stay |
| `dispatch-from-config.prepare-context.ts`, `.prepare-delivery.ts` | authority | **deleted**; pre-dispatch abort stays |
| `get-reply-inline-actions.ts` (before an inline tool, before commands) | authority | **deleted**; abort stays |
| `get-reply-run-admission.ts` preparation assertion | authority | **deleted** from the composition; internal-event and scheduled-automation sources (cron fence) stay |
| `get-reply-run-context.ts` scheduled path | authority | **deleted**; `scheduledAutomation.assertCurrent()` (cron run fence) and abort signals stay |
| `get-reply.types.ts` `prepareInternalGetReplyOptions` | authority | **deleted**; the host-issuer check `assertAdmittedRunOperatorAuthority` stays |
| `model-selection.ts` (entry, reset `commitGuard`, `assertSelectionCurrent`) | authority | **deleted**; host-issuer check, model-policy checks and the session-entry/selection data fence stay |
| `request-native-subagent.ts` (invocation `assertCurrent`, accepted-child `assertSourceCurrent`) | authority | **deleted**; guard, abort, state and `owner.assertOwnerCurrent` stay |
| `session-event-context.ts` (event preparation, owner successor `isCurrent`) | authority | **deleted**; the occurrence assertion and `operatorAuthority.signal` (Stop) stay |
| `session-event-handoff.ts` (`assertOwnerCurrent`, `captureSources`) | authority | **deleted**; settlement, acceptance, target, scheduled-automation, generation-lease, controller-operation and config-policy fences stay |
| `session-event-target.ts` (capture entry, `assertCaptureCurrent`) | authority | **deleted**; host-issuer check, capture/producer assertions and caller-occurrence checks stay |
| `commands-compact.ts` (entry, before acceptance) | authority | **deleted**; `rejectUnauthorizedCommand` at start, owner and current-read fences stay |
| `conversation-label-generator.ts` | authority | **deleted**; caller assertion, abort and model-policy check stay |
| `channel-run-admission.ts` `assertSourceCurrent` before admission | authority | **deleted**; caller's `assertSourceCurrent` and closed checks stay |

Left unchanged:
- `reply-agent-turn-preparation.ts` pre-claim check: the 4a cut-less site (cron delivery fence).
- `agents/worktrees/errors.ts`: parked (see #204069).
- No production authority-refusal strings remain in `src/auto-reply/**` or `src/sessions/**`. The lifetime-check ratchet reports 0 in changed files.

## User impact

- A requester whose access changes while a reply is being prepared (dispatch, model selection, inline actions, `/compact`, native subagents, session events, label generation) sees the turn finish. The next request goes through admission again.
- Queued input still goes through admission again when it starts, so a revoke while queued is still refused visibly.
- Stop still cancels.
- No new refusal, prompt or wait.

## Tests

prs.title: fix: make openclaw available in new terminals when gateway install runs from npx
prs.body:
Closes #203942
Related: #200425, #192331

## What Problem This Solves

People who try OpenClaw only through `npx` have no `openclaw` command installed. When they then run `npx openclaw@<version> gateway install`, the command onboarding suggests for keeping the Gateway running in the background later, the Gateway service is installed, but new terminals still have no `openclaw`. The install prints `Terminal default unchanged: keeping ~/.npm/_npx/<hash>/node_modules/.bin/openclaw`: it treats npx's temporary copy as a command the user already chose, so it does not set up the terminal command.

## User Impact

User impact: when an install has no existing terminal command or configured profile, running `gateway install` from npx, or from another one-off runner such as pnpm dlx or bunx, now sets up the managed terminal command the way `docs/cli/gateway/service.md` describes. It creates `~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw`, which runs the service's copy in `~/.openclaw/npm`, and appends to shell startup files the same guarded PATH line that other first installs add, so new shells find `openclaw`. An `openclaw` the user already has on PATH is still kept, including one listed after the runner's directory. Runs whose PATH contains no one-off runner directory are unchanged. Only builds that include the terminal command step (#200425, on main) are affected; the released 2026.11.6, 2026.11.7 and 2026.11.10-beta.1 do not have it yet. No new config, flags, or defaults.

## Why This Change Was Made

The terminal command step (`installGatewayTerminalCli` in `src/daemon/terminal-cli.ts`) looks up `openclaw` on the install process's PATH and keeps any match that is not its own launcher (`:150-180` on `3c8c7bf`; line numbers below are on that commit). Under npx, that PATH has npx's `.bin` directory ahead of the account's own directories, so the first match is npx's copy. #192331 already treats these copies as disposable (`isDisposableInstallPath` in `src/daemon/durable-service-entrypoint.ts`, whose comment says a service "must never point into one or keep one on its PATH") and leaves their directories out of the service PATH (`src/commands/daemon-install-plan.shared.ts`). This change applies the same check to the terminal command lookup: PATH entries whose real path is a one-off runner directory are skipped before the lookup, and every other entry is passed on as written. The rest of the step is unchanged.

Skipping the runner's directories, rather than treating a runner match as "no selection", keeps the existing rule for every other directory: if the user's own `openclaw` comes later on PATH, it is still found and kept, with the existing message.

Unchanged on purpose: the desktop app's `setup --terminal-path` path, which has the same lookup but runs only from the desktop app's own CLI; the PATH setup at CLI startup; how the launcher and the startup-file line are written; `isDisposableInstallPath` itself. This change is limited to the terminal command step; install paths that do not run that step are unchanged.

Known limits: the lookup still follows the existing rule for every other directory on PATH. An `openclaw` in a directory that the CLI adds to PATH at startup but that is not on the user's interactive shell PATH is still kept, as on main and as for runs outside npx. Only directories that `isDisposableInstallPath` classifies as runner caches are skipped; an `openclaw` link that points into a runner cache from another directory is still kept, as on main. That check matches path segment names, so it also skips a PATH entry whose real path contains a segment equal to `_npx` or `dlx`, matching `dlx-<digits>`, or starting with `bunx-` or `.bunx-`, even when it is the user's own directory; the guarded startup-file line still leaves an `openclaw` that the shell already finds in place.

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes</summary>

- Each PATH entry is classified by `fs.realpath`, falling back to `path.resolve` when the entry cannot be resolved, as #192331 does for the service PATH. Unlike that loop, entries are not trimmed, and empty and relative entries are kept, because the terminal lookup (`resolveExecutablePathAsync`) still searches relative entries and drops empty ones itself.
- The kept entries are joined back as written, not as real paths, so the "keeping" message is built from the user's PATH entry, not from its real path.
- If every entry is skipped, the lookup gets an empty PATH and finds nothing; it does not fall back to the process PATH.
- The first-install check (`:172-180`) and the later branch used by reinstalls and named profiles (`:187-195`) read the same lookup result.
- Against `3c8c7bf`: `src/daemon/terminal-cli.ts` +10/−1 (one import), `src/daemon/terminal-cli.test.ts` +38.

</details>

## Evidence

"Before" results were taken on main `3c8c7bf`. "After" results were taken on `3c8c7bf` with this PR's change applied: the focused tests ran with this PR's full diff applied (the same tree as commit `bd8df34f48b4`), and the after run used a package built from `3c8c7bf` plus this PR's production change.

Real runs through npx, before and after:

- **Setup**:
  - Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (x86_64). Each run used a fresh, disposable Linux account with its own systemd user manager, Node v24.22.1 from nodejs.org and npm 11.19.1. Before each run, the account had no `openclaw` command and no `~/.openclaw*` directories.
  - The package was built with `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs` (version 2026.11.6), because the released 2026.11.6, 2026.11.7 and 2026.11.10-beta.1 do not include the terminal command step.
  - Both runs used `npx --yes --package <package> openclaw gateway install --port 21789`, with `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PORT=21789` and a custom systemd unit name; the terminal command step reads neither.
  - The service is set up to run npm's `openclaw@2026.11.6` copy in `~/.openclaw/npm`.
  - "New shells" are a fresh `bash -lc` and a fresh `bash -ic`, both under `env -i` with PATH set to the system directories.
- **Before** (`3c8c7bf`, 2026-11-22):
  - `gateway install` exited 0; the user service was installed and `enabled`, with `ExecStart` pointing to `~/.openclaw/npm/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js`.
  - The only line about the terminal command was `Terminal default unchanged: keeping ~/.npm/_npx/<hash>/node_modules/.bin/openclaw; this Gateway: …`.
  - `~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw` was not created, `~/.bashrc` and `~/.profile` were unchanged, and in both new shells `command -v openclaw` found nothing.
- **After** (`3c8c7bf` plus this change, 2026-11-23, another fresh account):
  - After the install, running the same package with `npx --yes --package <package> -c 'command -v openclaw'` printed `~/.npm/_npx/<hash>/node_modules/.bin/openclaw`, the same `<hash>` as the copy the install ran from, so npx's copy was still the `openclaw` found on npx's PATH, as in the before run.
  - `gateway install` exited 0; the user service was installed and `enabled`, with the same unit file and `ExecStart` as before.
  - The install printed no `Terminal default unchanged` line and no other message about the terminal command.
  - `~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw` was created (a regular file owned by the account, mode 755); it runs `<node> --max-old-space-size=8192 ~/.openclaw/npm/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js` and does not point into `_npx`.
  - `~/.bashrc` and `~/.profile` each gained one line at the end, `if ! command -v openclaw >/dev/null 2>&1; then export PATH="$PATH":~/.openclaw/bin; fi` (home shown as `~`), and were otherwise unchanged.
  - In both new shells, `command -v openclaw` printed `~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw`, and `openclaw --version` in a new login shell exited 0 with `OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (06afb10)`.
- The change is in the terminal command step of `gateway install`: no agent or model is involved, and it does not change update, Doctor, config, or state, so no agent run or upgrade run is attached. The latest stable release does not have this step, so an upgrade from it takes the first-install path.

<details>
<summary>Redacted terminal output (before and after)</summary>

The account's home is shown as `~`, the Node binary as `<node>`, and the npx cache key as `<hash>`. The new-shell checks are shown as the command and its result.

Before:

```text
Terminal default unchanged: keeping ~/.npm/_npx/<hash>/node_modules/.bin/openclaw; this Gateway: <node> --max-old-space-size=8192 ~/.openclaw/npm/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js --profile default
bash -lc: command -v openclaw   -> no output
bash -ic: command -v openclaw   -> no output
```

After:

```text
(no line about the terminal command)
~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw:
  #!/bin/sh
  # OpenClaw managed terminal CLI
  export OPENCLAW_PROFILE="${OPENCLAW_PROFILE:-default}"
  exec <node> --max-old-space-size=8192 ~/.openclaw/npm/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/index.js "$@"
~/.bashrc, last line:  if ! command -v openclaw >/dev/null 2>&1; then export PATH="$PATH":~/.openclaw/bin; fi
~/.profile, last line: if ! command -v openclaw >/dev/null 2>&1; then export PATH="$PATH":~/.openclaw/bin; fi
bash -lc: command -v openclaw   -> ~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw
bash -ic: command -v openclaw   -> ~/.openclaw/bin/openclaw
bash -lc: openclaw --version    -> OpenClaw 2026.11.6 (06afb10)
```

</details>

Focused tests (`src/daemon/terminal-cli.test.ts`):

- A new table runs the terminal command step with a one-off runner's `.bin` first on PATH, laid out like npm (`.npm/_npx/<hash>/node_modules/.bin/openclaw` linking to the package's `openclaw.mjs`), pnpm 9+ dlx (a `dlx` segment) and bunx (a `.bunx-` segment). Each row expects no warnings, and that a new `bash -ic` with only `/usr/bin:/bin` on PATH runs the installed launcher.
- A new case puts the user's own `~/.local/bin/openclaw` after an npx `.bin` on PATH, and expects it to be kept, with the existing message and no launcher.
- The existing cases keep their assertions: a user's command first on PATH, normal first installs in each shell, an operator-owned file at the launcher path, and another configured profile.
- On `3c8c7bf` with only the test change, the 4 new cases fail at their own assertions: the three table rows at `expect(f.warnings).toEqual([])`, each receiving `Terminal default unchanged: keeping <runner dir>/.bin/openclaw; this Gateway: …`, and the after-runner case because the message keeps the runner's copy. The other 32 pass, and 7 are skipped (the zsh rows run only on macOS, and fish is not installed on that host). With this change, 36 pass and 7 are skipped.
- `pnpm test src/daemon/terminal-cli.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 39 s wall time with this change (41 s before); Vitest reports 34.6 s, about 96% of it module transform (about 1 s of test time), and the new cases take 5–33 ms each.
- Consumer: `src/cli/daemon-cli/install.integration.test.ts`, which runs `gateway install` through to this step, passes (18 tests).
- Targeted checks: oxfmt and oxlint (0 warnings, 0 errors) on the two changed files, `pnpm tsgo:core`, and `git apply --check --whitespace=error` on the diff pass.
- `pnpm check:changed --base 3c8c7bf` for the two changed files passes locally, including `check:import-cycles` and `check:max-lines-ratchet`.
- Local review: autoreview (P0–P2) on the full diff against `3c8c7bf` reported no findings.
- CI: pending at the time of opening

Not covered:

- Only npx was run live; the pnpm dlx and bunx rows cover the same path check that #192331 uses for the service PATH.
- "New shells" are fresh `bash -lc` and `bash -ic` processes with a clean environment, not new SSH sessions.
- macOS was not run, live or in tests: the focused tests ran on Linux, and macOS CI runs a fixed list of tests that does not include `src/daemon/terminal-cli.test.ts`.
- zsh and fish were not run: their existing rows are the 7 skipped tests above. This change does not touch how startup files are written.

`chat-session-diff-folding.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` passes again: the fixture runs one real first turn before it edits files and reads `sessions.diff`.

Part of #204008.

## Problem

Since #203126, a new session records a pending diff baseline claim, and `sessions.diff` answers "no changes" until the first turn captures the baseline. This is intended: before that, a read in that window showed files that existed before the session as session changes.

The folding e2e created the session, wrote its edited files, then read `sessions.diff` without a turn. It now gets an empty file list, so it fails on scheduled `main`.

Test-only. The fixture gets a local OpenAI Responses stub as its model provider (same pattern as `activity-run-inspector.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`). The test sends one `chat.send`, waits for `agent.wait` status `ok`, and only then writes the edited sources. The diff then lists `example.ts`, `gapped.ts` and `large.ts` as before, and the folding assertions are unchanged. Cleanup also releases the stub listener and its port claim.

prs.title: test(ios): stop failing Settings proofs on a fixed 10 s page-load deadline
prs.body:
## Problem

Scheduled `main` fails `ios-build (tests)` from time to time. `SettingsHubVisualProofTests.testIngressAuthorizedDashboardEntryPointsLoadTheSelectedGatewayPage` fails at `SettingsHubTests.swift:722` with `settings-hub: NSURLErrorDomain Code=-1001` (runs 45090792955 and 45156163669).

## Cause

The `-1001` does not come from WebKit. The test helper `waitForDashboardCondition` stops after a fixed 10 s wall-clock deadline and throws `URLError(.timedOut)`. A cold WebContent launch on a loaded simulator can take longer than that:

- 45090792955: `WebContent process ... took 47.795990 seconds to launch`.
- 45156163669: an 8 s stall after the WebContent launch.
- In passing runs the same page loads in 2-6 s.

The product and the fixture server are correct. The fixed deadline fails a load that would succeed.

#161616 removed the same pattern from the macOS tests ("native tests flake on busy runners when fixed wait deadlines expire"). There, waits re-check state with no deadline of their own, and the test limit bounds a lost signal.

## Fix

- `waitForDashboardCondition` has no per-wait deadline. It re-checks its condition every 50 ms.
- The Swift Testing suites that use it (`SettingsHubTests`, `SettingsHubDashboardErrorTests`) get `@Suite(.timeLimit(.minutes(10)))`, as in #161616.
- The CI lifecycle step does not enable XCTest time limits (no `-test-timeouts-enabled`). Without a bound, a lost signal in an XCTest proof would run until the 150-minute job limit. So each `SettingsHubVisualProofTests` test sets one 5-minute deadline at test start, and all of its waits share it. When the deadline passes, the pending wait fails with "The test reached its time limit while this wait was pending". This is one limit for the whole test, not a longer per-wait timeout. The test normally takes 6-27 s.
- All assertions stay the same. No product code changes.

## Evidence

macOS host, Xcode 27.1, iOS 27.0 simulator erased before each run (cold WebKit). CPU load alone (36 or 144 CPU-bound processes) did not reproduce the failure on this host: 6 of 6 base runs passed. So the slow launch was injected: each WebContent process that the scratch simulator started was paused for 20 s, then resumed. This is like the 47.8 s launch in CI.

| Run | Base (59b0aec0) | Head |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | passed 6.9 s (pause missed the page) | passed 46.8 s |
| 2 | **failed** 66.8 s, `desktop: ... Code=-1001` | passed 66.5 s |
| 3 | **failed** 27.7 s, `desktop: ... Code=-1001` | passed 67.2 s |
| 4 | **failed** 26.7 s, `terminal: ... Code=-1001` | passed 25.8 s |
| 5 | **failed** 87.5 s, `settings-hub: ... Code=-1001` | |

- Every run where the pause hit a page load failed on base and passed on head.
- In 4 other head runs the pause missed the page; all 4 passed in 6-11 s.
- An earlier base batch that paused only the first WebContent process also failed at `settings-hub` with `-1001`.
- No process was left paused after any run.

Other tests in the touched files, with no injection: `SettingsHubVisualProofTests` (2 tests), `SettingsHubTests` and `SettingsHubDashboardErrorTests` (12 tests) all pass. `swiftformat --lint` with `config/swiftformat`: 0 of 2 files need changes. `swiftlint --strict` reports the same violations on base and head, all already present.

prs.title: improve(ios): align app icon composition with Apple's design guidelines
prs.body:
Closes #187629
Related: #101411, #138002.

## What Problem This Solves

The iOS app icon’s mascot nearly fills the canvas, leaving little surrounding space instead of following Apple’s guidance to emphasize centered primary content with a simple background.

## User Impact

The iOS icon gains a more balanced composition while preserving its existing mascot, colors, and backgrounds. macOS, Debug icons, separate Watch app assets, and app behavior remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apple’s [Human Interface Guidelines for app icons](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/app-icons) recommend keeping primary content centered and using the production-template grids to guide placement. Apple also states:

> “you don’t need to fill the entire icon canvas with content.”

This reduces the iOS foreground to a centered 0.86 scale while retaining full-bleed backgrounds and leaving masking to the system. The chosen proportion is a design interpretation of Apple’s guidance, not an Apple-mandated percentage or a universal circular clipping boundary.

The unchanged macOS Original icon provides a supporting source-level sizing reference. A representative comparison with other iOS icons provides additional visual context; it is not the primary justification for this change.

The existing generator now produces release PNGs from a static, app-specific SVG rather than the animated browser favicon. Default remains opaque white, Dark retains transparency, and Tinted remains system-generated.

## Evidence

### iOS before and after

Actual baseline and regenerated PNG assets, shown with a presentation-only rounded mask. All annotations are in English. These are asset previews, **not native Home Screen screenshots**.

![iOS app icon before and after, with light and dark small-size previews](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/569b65bb-d646-4eab-8ae5-a307d1fe2316?raw=1)

### Supporting comparison with other iOS icons

Equal-size tiles using artwork returned by Apple’s US App Store lookup API for Shortcuts (915249334), WhatsApp (310633997), Signal (874139669), Telegram (686449807), Slack (618783545), and GitHub (1477376905). prs.title: feat(whatsapp): expose group membership actors to plugins
prs.body:
Related: #8495 (the group-event portion only; this proposal adds no auto-leave behavior).

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins cannot see who added the connected WhatsApp account to a group.

## User Impact

Plugins with the existing conversation-access grant can observe membership actors and affected participants, including groups whose messages are disabled. The proposed consumer is an operator-owned, read-only context plugin that uses configured trusted inviters as input to its group-admission policy.

Notifications are best effort and may repeat. A missing actor stays unknown, and a roster observation alone does not prove a new invitation. Group admission, tool access and send policy retain their current behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The observe-only `channel_group_membership_changed` hook carries event-scoped actor IDs, provider-supplied phone-number identities, affected participants and the connected account's identities. WhatsApp publishes live notifications through the existing hook runner and channel SDK subpath. The source connection owns cancellation; the timeout reference now lists the hook's two-second default.

Emitter calls rely on the existing [native plugin trust boundary](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/SECURITY.md#plugin-trust-boundary). The conversation-access grant controls observer registration and dispatch. This draft proposes the public observation contract; it adds no configuration, storage or automatic approval rule.

## Evidence

- Both new socket-to-hook tests fail on base `bde3017359ed` because no event reaches the plugin, and pass with the patch. The full WhatsApp command passes, including 1,024 Vitest tests.
- A CJS fixture loaded through the production `loadOpenClawPlugins` proves no callback without the conversation grant, delivery with it, and no callback after native replacement removes it. The retained global-runner reference also sees the revocation. This case and the neighboring replacement regression pass.
- Core and WhatsApp consumer type checks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, SDK export synchronization and the existing test budget pass.
- Full build exited 0 on `5ca7ee39dff2`, including verification of all 160 public SDK subpaths. The review follow-up changes tests and documentation only. The build printed an advisory chat-boot gzip result of 1,276,937 B against 1,276,669 B; no budget was changed or base comparison made for that advisory.
- The committed SDK API comparison was stopped locally before completion; it produced no compatibility verdict. Current plugin/extension import-boundary checks and lint for the loader regression pass.

The local SDK declaration preflight exceeded its default five-minute limit. Generation and targeted lint passed with the supported `OPENCLAW_PLUGIN_SDK_BOUNDARY_ROOT_SHIMS_TIMEOUT_MS=1200000` setting. The broader plugin-contract aggregate was stopped after 20 minutes; reported SDK and entry guard cases passed, but there is no aggregate pass.

The simplification pass kept the existing socket, hook and SDK owners: +103 production lines and +233 testing lines, including routing, against the base. The loader test replaces weaker registration-only coverage. The tests fit the existing budget without raising its ceiling. Independent reviews found no actionable issue in the implementation or review follow-up. Fixtures are synthetic.

## Still Needed Before Merge

A redacted real WhatsApp membership notification through a loaded plugin remains outstanding; no live invitation or deployment was exercised. Maintainers also need to accept the concrete consumer and the pre-admission actor/roster disclosure under the existing conversation-access grant. The outstanding API comparison and broader required CI checks also remain before merge. This remains a draft for the contract decision.

prs.title: fix(deps): update direct Undici dependencies on stable release
prs.body:
Related: #182010, #185194

## What Problem This Solves

The `release/2026.10.9` branch still pins the directly declared Undici dependency to 8.11.2, while the fixes for published Undici advisories have already landed on `main`.

## User Impact

This brings the stable release's directly declared runtime dependencies and their resolved peer dependencies to the patched 8.12.2 release. Whether a particular advisory is exploitable depends on the application's actual use of the affected API; this PR does not establish an OpenClaw exploit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Backport the 8.11.2 to 8.12.2 dependency change already included in #182010, updating the root package and the five plugin manifests that directly pin Undici. Regenerate the workspace lock with the branch-pinned pnpm 12.15.0. A subsequent mainline refresh moved to 8.12.3 in #185194; this backport uses the previously tested 8.12.2 security fix to keep the proposed change narrow.

The relevant upstream advisories include [GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx](https://github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx) and [GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685](https://github.com/nodejs/undici/security/advisories/GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685). Their applicability depends on specific TLS options or EventSource usage, respectively.

**Remaining scope:** the lock still contains Undici 8.11.2 through `mailauth@7.1.0`, which pins it separately. This change does not remediate that transitive edge or prove that all packaged dependency paths are patched. The release owner should assess it separately before treating the release as fully remediated.

## Evidence

- A local manifest and lock check failed on the original six direct pins and passed after this change; it also records the remaining `mailauth` edge.
- `pnpm install --lockfile-only --ignore-scripts` completed with pnpm 12.15.0; a subsequent offline `--frozen-lockfile --lockfile-only --ignore-scripts` check passed for all 189 workspace projects. pnpm reported existing deprecated dependencies and peer warnings. Lock regeneration also records a newly published deprecation notice for `@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base` without changing its version.
- Separately, an isolated OpenClaw 2026.10.8 installation with Undici 8.12.2 passed gateway health and authentication checks, a local OpenAI-compatible fixture, an HTTP CONNECT proxy fixture, and a synthetic TLS regression check. This is compatibility evidence for that installation, not a build or end-to-end test of this release branch.
- `git diff --check` passed. The full suite, release artifact build, and real external provider/channel operations have not been run for this PR. Hosted CI and maintainer review remain necessary.

prs.title: fix(ios): nest child sessions and fold subagent runs in the sidebar
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#190403 landed the nesting half on iOS: `ChatSessionSidebarModel.tree(from:)` nests children from `childSessions`, and `RootSidebar.displayRows` renders them with a chevron, depth indentation, collapse and search expansion. What was still missing is the folding layer: subagent runs are listed as rows, even though they have no transcript of their own, so the conversation that started them never shows what they are doing.

This revision rebases on current `main` and reduces the PR to exactly that layer, on top of #190403's renderer. No second tree renderer, no changes to nesting, and it no longer touches `RootTabsSidebarRegressionTests.swift`, which `main` has removed.

A run's persistent children take the run's place. The run's status and unread state move to the conversation that owns it, including **Home** for runs started from Home.

## User Impact

- Subagent runs no longer appear as chats in the iPhone drawer. Whatever conversation a run started appears in its place, nested under the same parent.
- The owning conversation shows the run's state: a spinner while one runs, a warning triangle and the error line when one failed, an unread dot, and "Waiting for a concurrency slot" while one is queued.
- This holds whether the parent lists the run in `childSessions` or only the run names its parent through `spawnedBy` / `parentSessionKey`.
- Runs started from Home show on the Home row: running, failed (with the error line) or unread.
- The recent-chats cap counts top-level chats only, so one busy parent cannot push other chats out of the list.
- A row's subtitle prefers a failed child, then queued work, then the row's own work line.
- Mark as Read on a conversation also clears the unread runs folded into it.
- A parent's unread dot also covers unread runs folded anywhere below it, so collapsing the parent never hides them.
- Home has a Mark as Read menu when Home or a run folded into Home is unread. It clears them together.
- Sidebar search still lists a matching run as its own row, as macOS does.

No configuration, migration or data change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The rules come from the Control UI session tree (`ui/src/components/app-sidebar-session-tree.ts`) and from the macOS sidebar, not from this PR: runs are never rows, their persistent children take the run's place, and the owner keeps their badges and attention.

- **Run classification is shared with macOS.** `isSidebarRun` and `Node.previewSessions` moved out of the macOS-only files (`ChatSessionSidebar+Tree.swift`, `ChatSessionSidebar.swift`) into `ChatSessionSidebarModel`, so macOS and iOS use one copy. macOS behaviour is unchanged.
- **Folding happens after placement.** `ChatSessionSidebarModel.foldingSubagentRuns(sections)` folds runs inside each section once placement is known, because a pinned or grouped parent can sit in a different section than its run. A run that ends up at the top of a section is resolved through `owningConversationKey`, which prefers the roster's `childSessions` link, then falls back to `spawnedBy` / `parentSessionKey`, walking up through intermediate runs to the first ordinary conversation. A run with no owner at all hands over only its conversations.
- **Home reuses that walk.** `foldedRuns(in:under:)` resolves Home's runs with the same ownership rule, so backref-only runs reach Home too.
- **iOS stays thin.** `RootSidebarModel` wraps `sections()` with the folding call, `RootSidebar` renders the result through #190403's `displayRows`, and `RootSidebarSessionButton` reads its subtitle and unread state from the folded node.

The two open review points in the folding code are fixed here, each with a focused shared-model test:

- **(a) Badges reach every surviving ancestor.** Badges a folded run adds to its owner now propagate through every ancestor of that owner, as nesting would — `a folded run's badges reach every ancestor that survives the fold`. Before, they stopped at the immediate owner.
- **(b) Mark as Read for an unread folded run.** `Node.unreadSessionKeys` carries the row plus the runs folded into it, and the row menu offers Mark as Read when any of them is unread, clearing them together — `mark as read covers an unread run folded into its parent`. Before, the menu only saw the parent and offered Mark as Unread.

The ClawSweeper review of `d53ea12` found two more gaps. Both are fixed in a separate commit on top (`3053676`), each with a focused shared-model test:

- **(c) Unread reaches a collapsed ancestor.** A row's unread dot and its "Unread" accessibility value now read `Node.showsUnread`, which is the aggregated `badges.hasUnread`. The macOS row reads that badge too. Before, the dot read only the row and its directly folded runs, so collapsing a grandparent hid a completed unread run: a completed run brings no spinner or failure line. Mark as Read stays scoped to the row and its own folded runs (`unreadSessionKeys`) — `a collapsed ancestor shows a folded run's unread while mark as read stays on its row`.
- **(d) A read action for runs folded into Home.** Home now has a context menu with Mark as Read whenever Home or one of its folded runs is unread. It clears `ChatSessionSidebarModel.unreadSessionKeys(in:)` over the main session plus `foldedRuns(in:under:)`, through `RootSidebar.performSessionMutation`, the same transport and refresh that session rows use. The mutation is `CommandSessionActionsModifier.markingRead(_:)`, shared with the row menu, so Home and session rows clear unread the same way. I chose an explicit menu over marking runs read whenever Home opens. Opening a session row clears only that session, so an implicit Home clear would quietly acknowledge runs the user never opened — `mark as read on Home covers the runs folded into Home`.

A fifth test covers the basic fold plus Home (`subagent runs fold into their owner and hand over the chats they start`). `displayRows` and `collapsedParents` are untouched, so no production-renderer tests change.

## Evidence

Fixture data only: the app's screenshot transport with a temporary fork-only fixture flag (not part of this PR), on a GitHub-hosted `xcode-27` runner (iPhone 18 Pro simulator, iOS 27; `macos-26` runners were unavailable). The chain is a real parent → subagent run → child: "Release plan" lists the run "Competitor research" in `childSessions`, the run lists "Findings summary" in `childSessions`, and "Findings summary" points back with `parentSessionKey`. Two runs name their owner only through `spawnedBy`: "Inbox triage" (running, started from Home) and "Morning digest" (failed, unread, started from Home). "Hotel booking" (failed, unread) is under "Trip planning".

| `main` at `6d1726a` | This PR at `d53ea12` |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: Inbox triage, Morning digest and Competitor research are chats of their own; Home shows no failed run; Trip planning looks idle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05adccff-376c-4466-9468-b5a3a9edc4d6) | ![After: runs are gone, Findings summary sits where Competitor research was, Home shows "Child session Morning digest failed: Digest…" with an unread dot, and Trip planning shows its failed unread run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05a82650-42dd-49d8-89f2-b9f18dd96567) |

On `main`, "Inbox triage", "Morning digest" and "Competitor research" are rows of their own, Home shows no sign of its failed run, and "Trip planning" looks idle. On this head the runs are gone, "Findings summary" appears in the place of "Competitor research", Home carries the failed run's error line and unread dot, and "Trip planning" shows its failed unread run.

The row menu on "Release plan", whose folded run "Competitor research" is unread, now offers **Mark as Read**:

![Row menu on Release plan showing Mark as Read because a folded run is unread](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d5a6fb86-ae20-4981-8511-ebb39897e949)

The drawer re-captured on `3053676` matches the screenshot above apart from the clock.

The same fixture now also builds a grandparent → parent → unread run chain, with the run named only through `spawnedBy`: **Launch prep** → **Launch copy** → **Copy review** (completed, unread). Only "Copy review" is unread, and it is never listed in `childSessions`, so any unread state on "Launch prep" comes from aggregation. With "Launch prep" expanded, "Copy review" is folded into "Launch copy" and no run row exists. Collapsing "Launch prep" removes "Launch copy" and leaves the unread dot on the collapsed row (c):

![Collapsed Launch prep with no child rows still shows the unread dot from its folded run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a4bb856-7ef3-4882-acc2-1572641397bc)

Home in the same run is unread because of "Morning digest". Long-pressing it offers the new **Mark as Read** (d):

![Home long-press menu showing Mark as Read for the run folded into Home](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e175bac-e14c-49b0-8878-7c07632fe165)

After tapping it, Home's dot and its "Child session Morning digest failed" line are gone, and the run stays folded:

![Home after Mark as Read: no unread dot and no failure line](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/824a560a-edc9-4ccd-a061-38b3b3cc8b5e)

The UI test asserts the same behavior, not just the pixels: the collapsed row's accessibility value contains "Unread", Home's value is "Unread" before the menu and empty after, and its label no longer mentions the failure.

Checks on this head `3053676` ([run](https://github.com/jorge-monalee/openclaw/actions/runs/45071044541)):

- `swift test --filter 'ChatSessionSidebar|ChatCommandPalette'` in `apps/shared/OpenClawKit`: 312 tests in 24 suites pass, including the five above ([shared job](https://github.com/jorge-monalee/openclaw/actions/runs/45071044541/job/137357824767)).
- SwiftFormat and SwiftLint (iOS and macOS scopes), `pnpm native:i18n:verify`, and the changed-file format check pass in the same job.
- Focused iOS unit tests (`RootTabsPresentationTests`, `RootSidebar*`, `CommandCenterTabSessionFilterTests`, `OpenClawTypographyTests`): 110 tests in 11 suites pass ([iOS head job](https://github.com/jorge-monalee/openclaw/actions/runs/45071044541/job/137357824453)).
- The sidebar UI tests pass on the head, including the read-evidence test above. On `main` the fold test fails at `XCTAssertEqual(runRows, [])` with `["Competitor research", "Hotel booking", "Inbox triage"]` (the before state above) and the read-evidence test fails because "Copy review" is still a row of its own ([iOS base job](https://github.com/jorge-monalee/openclaw/actions/runs/45071044541/job/137357824846)).

Not covered: a physical iPhone. Search intentionally still lists a matching run, as on macOS.

Prepared by Jorge's AI assistant on his behalf.
