prs.title: fix(config): repeated $include entries make config loading take minutes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: config loading takes minutes when config files include the same child file several times across a few levels of `$include`.

## User Impact

User impact: a config tree with repeated includes now fails fast with an error that names the limit and the recovery step, so the CLI, the Gateway and config reloads stop spending minutes on it. Real configs stay far below 1024 include file loads.

```
Maximum include file loads (1024) exceeded at: ./l10.json. Each repeated $include entry loads its file again, and arrays from every load are concatenated. Combine the included files into fewer files that give the same merged config, keeping array entries from every load in order, then rerun openclaw config validate.
```

Recovery for an existing installation that hits the limit is the step the error names. Include merging concatenates arrays, so a file included twice adds its array entries twice. For example a file that sets `mcp.servers.docs.args: ["mcp-server-fetch"]` and is included twice gives two arguments. Removing a repeated reference therefore keeps the merged config only when the file sets no arrays, or when the user moves the array entries that the repeat added into the remaining files. A repeat that comes after a different file (A, B, A) also applies A over B again. The upgrade run below shows the recovery on a config tree whose included files set no arrays.

## Why This Change Was Made

`$include` already has a depth limit of 10 and a cycle check, and each file is capped at 2 MB. Both checks look at one include chain. A file may still list the same child file several times (`"$include": ["./b.json", "./b.json", ...]`), and each repeat reads, parses and merges the whole subtree below it again. The work grows as fan-out to the power of depth. Nine levels that each include the next level four times load 349,524 files, built from eleven files of about 100 bytes.

The include resolver now counts file loads in one resolution and throws a `ConfigIncludeError` once it reaches 1024 loads. The check sits next to the depth check in `loadFileSync`, and the error flows through the same config validation path as the depth and cycle errors. The docs list the new limit next to the depth limit, together with the same recovery step.

## Evidence

The proof script generates nine levels where level i includes level i+1 F times, then runs `openclaw config validate` from source (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts config validate`) with `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` pointing at that tree. Wall time includes about 30 s of dev-mode CLI startup on this machine.

| Fan-out | Include file loads | main `00b62dd` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 10 | 28.0 s, Config valid | 31.0 s, Config valid |
| 2 | 1,023 | 30.0 s, Config valid | 30.8 s, Config valid |
| 3 | 29,524 | 67.3 s, Config valid | 29.7 s, include error |
| 4 | 349,525 | 389.9 s, Config valid | 30.9 s, include error |

Branch output for fan-out 4:

```
Config needs correction: .../fan4/openclaw.json
  - <root>: Maximum include file loads (1024) exceeded at: ./l10.json
```

Calling `resolveConfigIncludes` directly on main for the same trees took 0.56 s, 7.3 s and 80.3 s for fan-out 2, 3 and 4. On this branch fan-out 2 resolves in 0.39 s and fan-out 3 and 4 throw the include error.

### Upgrade from stable 2026.11.6 (recorded 2026-11-21)

This section publishes the existing 2026-11-21 upgrade run after checking its raw logs and confirming that the PR still points to `e65d63e`; these timings were not rerun on 2026-11-22.

This run installs `openclaw@2026.11.6` (npm `latest` on 2026-11-21, commit `06afb10`) into a local npm prefix. It then upgrades in place to this branch built from source (`pnpm build:runtime` at `e65d63e`, run as `node openclaw.mjs`, which prints `OpenClaw 2026.11.3 (e65d63e)` because the branch sits on an older main). Both CLIs share one state dir and one HOME inside the proof dir. The stable release runs every step first. The branch then runs `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` as the upgrade step, followed by the same steps. Node 24.22.1 on Linux. Every command runs in a bubblewrap sandbox that mounts the proof dir at `<proof>` below a sticky `/tmp`, because OpenClaw rejects temp roots below the world writable parent directory on this host.

Configs:

- `normal`: a modular config with eleven files. It uses include arrays (`logging`, `agents.defaults`), sibling overrides (`gateway.port`, `messages.responsePrefix`, `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds`), and nested includes three levels deep (`openclaw.json` to `agents/index.json5` to `agents/defaults.json5` to `shared/timezone.json5`, and the same shape under `messages`).
- `fanout4`: nine levels where each level includes the next level four times (349,525 include loads).
- `recovered`: `fanout4` after following the error's advice, so each level lists the next level once (10 include loads). No included file in `fanout4` or `recovered` sets an array, so listing each file once gives the same merged config.

| Config | Command | 2026.11.6 | this branch `e65d63e` after `doctor --fix` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| normal | `config validate` | 2.6 s, Config valid | 4.0 s, Config valid |
| recovered | `config validate` | 2.7 s, Config valid | 3.9 s, Config valid |
| fanout4 | `config validate` | 193.2 s, Config valid | 5.8 s, include load error, exit 1 |
| normal | `gateway run` until `/readyz` 200 | 33.5 s, ready | 25.1 s, ready |
| recovered | `gateway run` until `/readyz` 200 | 24.7 s, ready | 25.0 s, ready |
| fanout4 | `gateway run` until `/readyz` 200 | 825.3 s, ready | 14.3 s, exits 78 with the include load error |

`config get --json` for `gateway`, `agents.defaults`, `logging`, `messages` and `ui` on the normal config, and for `ui` and `gateway` on the recovered config, print byte identical output on both CLIs. The gateway token prints as `__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__` on both. Merged values on both:

```
agents.defaults  {"workspace":"./workspace","userTimezone":"America/Chicago","thinkingDefault":"medium","timeoutSeconds":1200, ...}
logging          {"level":"info","consoleLevel":"warn"}
messages         {"responsePrefix":"[proof]","ackReaction":"eyes","ackReactionScope":"all", ...}
gateway          {"port":18891,"mode":"local","bind":"loopback","auth":{"mode":"token","token":"__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__"}}
ui (normal)      {"seamColor":"#336699"}
ui (recovered)   {"seamColor":"#000000"}
```

`agents.defaults` shows all three include levels merged. `userTimezone` comes from the third level, `thinkingDefault: "medium"` from the later array entry and `timeoutSeconds: 1200` from the sibling override.

Authored files. The sha256 of all 33 authored config files was taken before the stable run and again after the branch run. The included files of all three configs and the root files of `fanout4` and `recovered` are byte identical. The stable Gateway added `openclaw.json.last-good` next to each root file, a byte copy of that root file. The branch `doctor --fix` upgrade step rewrote `normal/openclaw.json` and saved the authored file as `openclaw.json.bak.1` (same sha256 as before the run). The rewrite keeps every `$include` entry and every authored value. It adds `agents.entries.main`, `skills.entries`, `wizard` and `meta`. The same `doctor --fix` from 2026.11.6 on a fresh copy of the authored normal config makes the same kind of rewrite with the same `$include` entries and the same added top level keys, so this comes from doctor itself. The branch `config validate` and `config get` steps after doctor leave every file unchanged, and the branch Gateway refreshes `normal/openclaw.json.last-good` to a byte copy of the rewritten root file.

```
$ sha256sum (before stable run -> after branch run), changed lines only
  ./normal/openclaw.json            e3f172b6...  ->  9993e283...  (doctor --fix rewrite)
+ ./normal/openclaw.json.bak.1      e3f172b6...  (the authored file)
+ ./normal/openclaw.json.bak        e5c387d5...  (doctor's intermediate write)
+ ./normal/openclaw.json.last-good  9993e283...
+ ./fanout4/openclaw.json.last-good 1bcbea34...
+ ./recovered/openclaw.json.last-good 1bcbea34...
```

Branch `config validate` output for `fanout4`:

```
Config needs correction: <proof>/configs/fanout4/openclaw.json
  - <root>: Maximum include file loads (1024) exceeded at: ./l10.json. Each repeated $include entry loads its file again, and arrays from every load are concatenated. Combine the included files into fewer files that give the same merged config, keeping array entries from every load in order, then rerun openclaw config validate.

Run `openclaw doctor --fix` to repair, or fix the keys above manually.
Run openclaw config schema to inspect supported settings and values, then rerun openclaw config validate.
```

Branch `gateway run` on `fanout4`:

```
OpenClaw config is invalid
File: <proof>/configs/fanout4/openclaw.json
Problem:
  - <root>: Maximum include file loads (1024) exceeded at: ./l10.json. Each repeated $include entry loads its file again, and arrays from every load are concatenated. Combine the included files into fewer files that give the same merged config, keeping array entries from every load in order, then rerun openclaw config validate.

Inspect: openclaw config validate
Audit, status, health, logs, and doctor commands still run with invalid config.
Run "openclaw doctor --fix" to repair the config, then retry.
```

It exits with code 78. After the recovery edit, the same Gateway on `recovered` reaches ready in 25.0 s, and `config get ui` prints `{"seamColor":"#000000"}` on both CLIs.

### Tests

Commands run on this branch:

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/config/includes.test.ts src/config/includes.top-level-key.test.ts src/config/include-write-boundary.test.ts src/config/mutate.agent-delete-include.test.ts`: 42 passed on `e65d63e`, including a new test that pins the array concatenation for a file included twice. Both limit tests match the full error text, recovery step included. With the previous message they fail. On main the two new tests fail. The budget test resolves 1025 loads without an error, and the fan-out test runs for 101 s and resolves without an error. On this branch they take 660 ms and 352 ms.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the touched files, `git diff --check`: clean.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed.
- `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts`: OK at `4e62b0f`, net +34 test lines. `e65d63e` adds 7 test lines (+41), within the 400-line allowance. On `e65d63e`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean on the touched files.

prs.title: fix: offer suggested-task worktrees only from repositories
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an agent suggests a follow-up task from a folder that is not a Git repository (for example, the agent's default workspace), the suggestion card still offers **Start in a new worktree**. Choosing it only shows "Choose a repository with a commit to start this task in a new worktree", and in short chat panes the repository chooser and task instructions stay hidden below the error, so the card looks like it lost its instructions.

## User Impact

User impact: suggested tasks from a plain folder now offer a worktree only from a repository that can host one. **Start in a new worktree** lists registered projects with a repository, plus **Choose repository** for any other path; picking a project starts the task right away, with no error first.

If a folder stops being a repository between the suggestion and the click, the card shows one explanation and the chooser, with the project list and Cancel in view, instead of the same error three times.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The Gateway records `worktreeSource` on each suggestion when it is created, using the same checkout check that acceptance already runs. Acceptance still rechecks, so the flag only decides what the card offers.
- The card turns the worktree option into a submenu of projects from the shared project catalog (registered or cloned checkouts; agent workspaces are excluded). The catalog loads only when a card needs it, so chat startup is unchanged.
- The recovery chooser sits above the instructions and is the only error message in that state. The chat toast and the inline alert are no longer repeated there.
- `suggest_task` now tells agents to use the target repository checkout for code changes. Non-code tasks still need no Git.

## Evidence

Scenario: isolated Gateway on this branch with a real agent (Claude CLI), dark theme, 1100×820. The suggestion's folder is the agent workspace (not a Git repository). Two registered projects (`openclaw`, `clawhub`). Before is `main` at `59b0aec099f5`; After is this branch.

![Before: choosing Start in a new worktree on a workspace suggestion ends in an error, and the card body shows no chooser](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bb4aae32-f146-4cea-9dd5-acd383d525c1)

![After: Start in a new worktree lists registered projects with a repository and Choose repository](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/255de0b6-e73c-40d1-97d0-f24daa87307b)

Recovery when the folder stops being a repository after the suggestion (After only):

![After: the repository chooser shows one explanation, both projects and Cancel beside the start button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1bdd81b2-610a-4928-bff8-03c523dd0992)

- Live: a real agent turn called `suggest_task` without `cwd`; the Gateway returned `worktreeSource: false`. Choosing `openclaw` from the submenu sent `taskSuggestions.accept` with `mode: "worktree"` and the project path, and the Gateway created a worktree session in that project.
- Regression tests, red on `main` and green here:
  - `src/gateway/server-methods/task-suggestions-session-start.test.ts`: suggestions report `worktreeSource` for a plain folder, an unborn repository and a repository with a commit.
  - `ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.task-suggestions.e2e.test.ts`: a workspace suggestion starts in a registered project's worktree with no failed accept first; workspace and repository-less projects are not listed.
  - `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-task-suggestions.test.tsx`: the recovery chooser renders above collapsed instructions with no repeated error.
- Focused checks: those suites plus `task-suggestions.test.ts`, `task-suggestions.owner-recovery.test.ts`, `chat-task-suggestions.test.tsx` and `task-suggestion-tools.test.ts`; `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:ui`, oxlint, stylelint, format, `ui:i18n:verify`, protocol and Swift model generation. `ui:build` budgets match `main`.
- Review: local autoreview (Codex) on the uncommitted change found one P2: with no registered projects the submenu was a dead end. Fixed by adding **Choose repository**, which opens the existing chooser.

prs.title: fix(models): model picker switches chat to models the user cannot sign in to from chat
prs.body: Supersedes #180828, which Barnacle closed for inactivity on 2026-11-18 and which GitHub cannot reopen. This is the same branch, updated to current `main`. Live proof is below. ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: selecting a listed but unauthenticated model in the chat model picker (for example `meta/muse-spark-1.3` before Meta sign-in) reports success, pins the chat to a model that can only fail authentication, and then answers every message with a generic HTTP 401 that gives no direct way to authorize — forcing the user to switch back to another model and hunt for the sign-in flow. ## User Impact Tapping a model whose provider has no working sign-in now keeps the current model and immediately shows how to connect that provider: a tappable sign-in button for OAuth/device-code providers, secure API-key entry instructions for API-key-only providers (for example OpenCode Go), and a deep link to Control UI → Settings → Model Providers (carrying `?provider=&agent=`) when the gateway advertises a public origin. Auth failures at run time name the provider and carry the same buttons instead of generic boilerplate. Not blocked: ready, unconfirmed, and cooling-down models; reset-to-default and default selections; and selections on a gateway whose `cloudWorkers.requiredProfile` is a worker-inference device profile (provider credentials live on the node there, per #170132), unless the selection pins an explicit Gateway account. No secrets are requested or stored in chat, and no credential-bearing links are placed in chat. Sign-in from the gate finishes the job: - **The blocked selection applies after sign-in.** Tapping **Sign in** on the gate remembers the blocked model for that chat (30 minutes, in memory). When that chat's sign-in completes, the model is switched and the reply says ` login complete. Model changed to .` If the chat picked another model meanwhile, it says `Select again with /models.` instead. - **Only a sign-in that finishes in chat promises a switch.** The gate remembers the selection and says `Sign in below and this chat switches to it.` only when the provider's resolved login route runs in chat (`mode: "chat"`). API-key entry, app-only OAuth (for example Chutes, which declares no `channelLogin`), and providers with no single resolved route hand off to the app, where nothing applies the selection. For those the gate says `Sign in below, then select the model again.` and remembers nothing. - **A bare `/login` names the chat's model.** When the chat runs on another provider, completion says ` login complete. This chat still uses . To use here, send /models.` and Telegram adds a ` models` button that opens that provider's page in the picker. A chat already on the provider keeps `Try your request again now.` - **No terminal commands in chat.** API-key guidance reads `Add the API key in the OpenClaw app under Models → Connect provider.`, following upstream #203394. ## Why This Change Was Made The picker already computed per-model readiness for display, but selection ignored it, and failure copy dropped the provider before rendering. - The policy lives in the shared selection owner (`applySessionModelSelectionInternal`). Adapters opt in by passing the exact menu facts they rendered (`authReadinessMenu`); a rejection is a dedicated `reason: "auth"` result with a required `authBlock`. Telegram only renders the result. Typed `/model` and `sessions.patch` keep their current behavior and only gain the better failure guidance. - Menu readiness describes Gateway credentials, so it cannot judge required worker-local inference. The #170132 exception is now one exported predicate in the runtime-normalization owner (`isProviderAuthOwnedByRequiredWorker`), used both by runtime preparation and by the picker gate. Gateway inference, optional placement, and explicit account pins stay gated. - Each provider's concrete login route is resolved so recovery can tell API-key entry from OAuth sign-in. The provider is carried through failover facts, including typed auth errors buried in the cause graph. Provider ids are slug-validated before they are embedded in commands or guidance. **Needs a maintainer decision (ClawSweeper "Decision needed"):** should Telegram reject unauthenticated picker selections through the new optional `authReadinessMenu` SDK parameter and `reason: "auth"` result variant, while other selection surfaces (Discord/Mattermost pickers, typed `/model`, `sessions.patch`) keep their current behavior? The PR is built so other adapters can opt in with the same contract later. ## Evidence Head `8458b80cd17`, which merges current `main` (`8ab24647379`, version 2026.11.6). The merge overlapped upstream #203394 ("one owner for provider sign-in failures"): - Import conflicts were resolved as unions, and the stale `buildProviderAuthRecoveryHint` import was dropped. Upstream's plain recovery hint is kept. - `/login` authority is checked once at the start, so the auto-apply step no longer re-checks it (upstream removed `assertCurrent` from the Telegram login handler). - Picker selection keeps this PR's `prepareTelegramPickerSelection` helper and adopts upstream's optional default model. - Picker API-key guidance drops the `openclaw models auth login …` command, per #203394's no-terminal-commands rule. New since the last review (`3605425fd50`). Each regression fails on the previous code and passes on this head: - `8ad3ccd8ecb`, blocked selection applies after sign-in. Tests: "switches the chat to the blocked model once sign-in completes" and "keeps a model picked while signing in and names the blocked one to select". This commit also merges the two duplicate `commands-models-menu` cases ClawSweeper flagged. - `d38bf3aba1f`, chat still uses its model after a bare `/login`. Tests: "says a chat on another provider keeps its model and offers that provider's models" (Telegram) and "keeps the current session profile when connecting another provider" (chat). Before the fix, both got `Try your request again now.` - `18e49439c3f`, API-key gate wording. The loopback test now runs once per login kind. Device code: "this chat switches to it", with the selection remembered. API key: "then select the model again", with nothing remembered. Before the fix, the API-key case failed on both counts. - `8258953809e`, ClawSweeper's P2 on `8458b80cd17`: the switch promise now keys on a chat-completable route (`chatLogin`, from the resolved route's `mode === "chat"`) instead of "not an API key". The loopback test adds an app-only OAuth case (`mode: "sign-in"`): "then select the model again", nothing remembered. It fails on the previous gate. - `c56bd7bbf4b` merges current main (conflict in `ui/src/pages/model-providers/route.ts`: kept main's `pluginId` and this PR's `agent` cold-link parameter). `3e9adbcb0e5` drops a test import the earlier main merge left unused. Tests on this head (`3e9adbcb0e5`, `vitest run` over every test file this PR touches): 11 files, 223 tests, all passing. `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:ui` pass, and oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the changed files. With #180830 and #180831 combined: 6 files, 131 tests, all passing. Typecheck: `tsgo` core, extensions and the extensions test project are clean. `oxlint` and `oxfmt` are clean on touched files. `check-plugin-sdk-exports` passes in the build, within the declaration budget. ## Live proof Real Telegram private chat and Control UI on a live Gateway. The current build is `e8ec8a4`: this head merged with #180830 and #180831, because the author runs them together. Telegram IDs, device codes, the Gateway host and the Control UI session sidebar are redacted. **(1) Blocked picker selection with recovery (2026-11-20).** In `/models`, tapping a model labeled `Sign-in needed` replies `⚠️ Model not changed: … needs a working sign-in first … Your current model is unchanged.` with a **Sign in** button. `/status` confirms the model is unchanged. Two providers were checked: Meta (Muse, native) and xAI. | Meta: selection blocked | xAI: selection blocked | |---|---| | | | **(2) Sign-in from the gate switches the chat (2026-11-21).** 1. With xAI signed out, the chat on `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` taps Grok 4.7. 2. The gate says `Sign in below and this chat switches to it.` 3. After the device approval: `xAI (Grok) login complete. Model changed to xai/grok-4.7.`, with no second tap. 4. The next turn went to `xai/grok-4.7` with the new sign-in. xAI answered 402 for account billing, which is outside OpenClaw. | Gate | Device code | Login complete, model changed | Next turn on Grok 4.7 | |---|---|---|---| | | | | | **(3) A bare `/login` from a chat on another provider (2026-11-22).** `/login meta` from the deepseek chat ends with `Meta login complete. This chat still uses opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash. To use Meta here, send /models.` and a **Meta models** button. The button opens Meta's page in the picker. | Notice and button | Button opens the provider page | |---|---| | | | **(4) API-key provider handoff (Groq, enabled temporarily).** - The provider list and gate show `Add the API key in the OpenClaw app under Models → Connect provider.`, with no command. - The gate says `Sign in below, then select the model again.` - **Sign in** replies `Groq API key needs provider setup …` with an **Open OpenClaw** link to `/settings/model-providers?provider=groq&agent=main` on the Gateway's public origin. - The link opens Models for agent `main`, filtered to Groq. | Provider list | Gate (current wording) | Sign in → handoff | Link target | Lands on provider + agent | |---|---|---|---|---| | | | | | | **(5) Run-time 401 with recovery (2026-11-23).** 1. An invalid Groq key was saved. 2. A fresh session on `groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b` sent one message. Groq answered HTTP 401 (`failoverReason=auth`). 3. The reply is `⚠️ Couldn't sign in to groq. Sign in again with /login groq or under Models in the OpenClaw app. For now, switch to a working model with /model.`, stored with cause `{provider: groq, failoverReason: auth}`. 4. The Control UI renders it with **Open Models**. Clicking it lands on `/settings/model-providers?provider=groq`, where Groq shows `Credentials rejected`. The Telegram rendering of these buttons is covered by `agent-runner-failure-reply` and the Telegram delivery tests. On Telegram, this run would have needed the owner's main chat (about 500k tokens of context) on a 128k model. | 401 with recovery actions | Expanded reason | Open Models → Groq | |---|---|---| | | | | **(6) Upgrade with real data, and from v2026.11.6.** Full traces: [TRACES-20261123.md](https://github.com/ivankuznetsov/openclaw/blob/3f750da88cc5f376796b5b260bb2076c2d8e255b/shared/TRACES-20261123.md). - **The owner's real state**, written by a 2026.10.10 main build, upgraded to the Nov 21 head and then to this merged head. All 163 stored session rows are unchanged: 50 model overrides, 61 account pins, 43 thinking levels, 119 harness ids and the stored runtime pin. v2026.11.6 itself refuses this data (state schema 39 is newer than its 36), so it cannot be the starting point. - **A literal v2026.11.6 → head upgrade.** v2026.11.6 created and seeded a fresh state with model overrides, thinking levels, fast mode, a user account pin and a stored `openclaw` runtime pin. This head migrated it (state schema 36 → 41, integrity checks passed). All 5 sessions are field-identical, and the stored pin is still read as `source: session-key`. - **The live Gateway** was upgraded in place to this build. The migration chain completed and the previous files were kept. **Not covered live:** the required-worker case, because there is no worker node. It stays covered by `apply-session-model-selection` ("shared auth gate defers Gateway readiness only to required worker inference"). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: fix(meta): Muse subscription sign-in cannot be finished from chat and turns are rejected after sign-in
prs.body: ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: `/login meta` in chat can never start the Muse device-code subscription sign-in (it always hands off to Control UI guided setup), and even after a successful sign-in every turn on `meta/muse-spark-1.3` fails — first with missing-auth errors on the wrong runtime, then with `Requested agent harness "muse" does not support meta/muse-spark-1.3`. ## User Impact User impact: users can add and authorize Meta Muse models end-to-end in Telegram (device-code in the browser, no API key or secret handling in chat), and signed-in models actually run. Control UI guided setup behavior is unchanged. Security boundaries are preserved: nothing starts in chat without the plugin's explicit `channelLogin` opt-in (the same mechanism GitHub Copilot, xAI, MiniMax, and Codex device-code already use), API-key entry still hands off to secure setup, and no credentials pass through chat. ## Why This Change Was Made Four stacked gaps, each fixed at its layer: 1. The `muse-code` choice never declared `channelLogin`, so chat could not start it. 2. `projectChannelChoice` only computed a login kind for `credentialOnly` choices; harness-owned sign-ins (no credential profile saved — the credential lives in the Muse CLI) always projected to setup-only even with an explicit chat opt-in. 3. Credential-only login persistence dropped the auth result's declared `agentRuntimeId`, so the model kept resolving to the default API runtime. It now stages the same per-agent model runtime policy guided setup writes (`prepareSetupModelRuntime`), scoped to the signing-in agent and the login's own default model, ignored for the default `openclaw` runtime. The persistence owner (`runProviderAuthMethod`) reports the staging outcome (`stagedRuntimePolicy`) itself, so chat completion and model-access consent do not reconstruct it from result metadata that the credential-only path drops. Runtime-plugin repair after the write receives the login's agent and authority: before each package, marker, or install-record effect, it reruns the caller's `beforePersistentEffect` and `assertCurrent`. 4. Prepared native routes carry a blank `baseUrl`, which masked the configured official Meta endpoint in harness support facts while `endpointOverrides` was derived from that same config — the Muse harness therefore rejected every turn. Blank prepared baseUrls now fall back to the configured endpoint (live diagnostic before the fix: `rt=muse provider=meta transport=none endpoint=present baseUrl= api=openai-responses`). ## Evidence **Resolved head `6892508c688` (2026-11-23).** `af7f1a5026c` merges current `main` (`38f4f8fe018`). Its one conflict was the manifest field table in `docs/plugins/manifest/setup-and-auth.md`. It keeps main's new `choiceLabel` and `appGuidedActionLabel` wording and this PR's `credentialOnly` and `channelLogin` rows. `6892508c688` folds one test callback onto a single line, so `auth.test.ts` stays under its 1016-line cap after main's edits to that file. Checks on this head: the five test files this PR touches (`bot-native-command-login`, `commands-login`, `auth.test.ts`, `provider-login-options`, `harness/selection`) all pass, 190 tests. `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:extensions` pass, and oxlint, oxfmt and `git diff --check` are clean on the changed files. Previous head `a65800e4a42`, which merges current `main` (`8ab24647379`, version 2026.11.6). There were two conflicts: - `auth.ts`: upstream dropped an OpenAI tip and reformatted the call. Kept upstream's call and this PR's `stagedRuntimePolicy`. - `provider-auth-login-flow-runtime.ts`: upstream removed `parseModelsAuthLoginFlowResult` and now returns the typed result directly. Removed it here too; `stagedRuntimePolicy` flows through the typed `ModelsAuthLoginFlowResult`. **[P3] Profileless harness sign-in in Telegram's native adapter (`45d76dd0ef1`).** A Muse sign-in saves no credential profile, so there is no account switch that can fail. The adapter now applies the same rule as the chat `/login` handler: - A profileless result reports completion. - A result that saved nothing (no profile and no staged runtime) hands off to Control UI setup. Tests "reports a harness-owned sign-in that saves no credential profile as complete" and "hands a profileless sign-in that saved nothing usable to setup" fail on the previous head and pass on this one. Live check: (C4) below. Tests on this head: the Telegram `bot-native-command-login`, `commands-login` and `provider-auth-login-flow-runtime` suites, 46 tests, all passing. With #202564 and #180830 combined: 131 tests, all passing. `tsgo` core and extensions are clean. **[P2] Keep the provider's agent model settings when staging its runtime (`de2e57b6a04`).** `auth-runtime-staging.ts` merges the staged `agentRuntime` into the provider's own model entry instead of replacing the agent entry. Regression "keeps the provider's own agent model settings when the CLI path stages its runtime": before the fix only `agentRuntime` survived; after it, the alias and params are kept. **[medium] Chat-owner authority through final effects.** Upstream already proves both halves with real effects: the doctor repair stops before the npm install, the marker and the install record when the hook refuses, and the ids-based repair fences real index writes on revocation. This PR's test shows the login passes its hook into that repair. A single unit test from login through a real npm install would need a registry-served `@openclaw/muse` package. Live owner revocation is shown below (C3). Earlier fixes, still on this head: ClawSweeper findings fixed on this head (`src/commands/models/auth.test.ts`): - **[P2] Return the persisted runtime-staging outcome to chat.** `runProviderAuthMethod` now returns `stagedRuntimePolicy` once the staged policy is persisted (or already present). `runModelsAuthLoginFlow` passes it through instead of re-deriving it from `result.agentRuntimeId`, which credential-only results drop. Regression "reports the persisted runtime staging to chat for credential-only harness sign-ins": without the fix, `expected undefined to be true`; with the fix it passes. (Red runs used this head's tests with only the fix reverted, before the module extraction, which is behavior-preserving.) The cross-provider test now also asserts that nothing is reported staged. - **[P1]/[high] Carry login authority into runtime-plugin repair.** `repairModelSelectionRuntimePlugins` accepts `beforePersistentEffect`, and its internal repair chain already forwards that hook to its dependency-marker, payload-retirement, and install-record effects. The login passes a hook that reruns its own `beforePersistentEffect` and `assertCurrent`, plus the login's `agentId`, so the agent-scoped staged policy is the one the repair evaluates. Regression "rechecks login authority before runtime-plugin repair effects" revokes authority while repair is pending. Without the fix, the login resolves and the repair effect runs; with the fix, the login rejects with "Login authority ended." and no effect runs. **Data-model compatibility.** New test "keeps an existing stored config intact and valid when a chat harness sign-in stages its runtime". It starts from a config shaped like those earlier releases persisted: an authored `agents.entries.main` with `workspace` and per-model `alias`/`params`, an `agents.defaults.model.primary`, and an unrelated enabled plugin. The test checks that config validates, runs a chat (credential-only) harness sign-in, then asserts: - every pre-existing value is unchanged; - only `agentRuntime` is added to the signed-in model's existing entry; - the unrelated plugin entry is untouched; - the result still passes `validateConfigObject`. No schema or migration changes. Session rows and auth-profile stores are not touched by this PR. The test passes both before and after the finding fixes; it proves preservation and is not a regression for a bug. Focused suites (`node scripts/test-projects.mts --maxWorkers=1`), all passing. After the merge: 6 files, 209 tests. On this head `auth.test.ts` is 48/48. The combined proof branch ran all three PRs' focused suites: 21 files, 598 tests, 0 failed. - `src/commands/models/auth.test.ts` - `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-login.test.ts` - `src/plugins/provider-login-options.test.ts` - `src/agents/harness/selection.test.ts` - `src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth-login-flow-runtime.test.ts` - `src/commands/promos/claim.test.ts` (the other `repairModelSelectionRuntimePlugins` caller) `tsgo` core and the `commands` test project are clean. `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and the pre-commit line-cap ratchet pass. To stay within the line caps, the PR's runtime-staging computation moved unchanged from `auth.ts` into `src/commands/models/auth-runtime-staging.ts`, and its tests moved into `auth-runtime-staging.test-support.ts`, which `auth.test.ts` registers. Live verification on a real Telegram + gateway install, before/after on the same account: - Before: `/login meta` answered "Meta API key needs provider setup. Open Control UI…". After an out-of-band sign-in, turns failed with missing-auth on the API route, then with `Requested agent harness "muse" does not support meta/muse-spark-1.3`. - After (earlier head, author's install): Muse Spark and Muse Wonder Full turns succeed with the session reporting the Muse runtime. ## Live proof Real Telegram private chat with a live Gateway on 2026-11-20. The Gateway ran upstream `main` `8479dacd2e1` merged with #180828, #180830 and #180831 (combined build `28efb83`; the three PRs were merged together because the author runs them together). Telegram IDs and device codes are redacted. Screenshots are hosted at [ivankuznetsov/openclaw@224a663](https://github.com/ivankuznetsov/openclaw/tree/224a6636a4ada057f2c61f0e7445f364e765e967). **C1: owner sign-in from a private chat.** Selecting a Muse model that isn't signed in offers **Sign in** (#180828). The device code appears in chat, and after approval the chat says `Meta login complete`. `/model meta/muse-spark-1.3` then replies `Runtime set to muse`, and a turn reaches Meta through the Muse runtime. Meta answered `429 … Subscription quota exhausted`, which shows the signed-in account works. A completed reply is in C5. No consent prompt appears, because upstream #190019 now allowlists the provider's models at sign-in. | Device code in chat | Login complete | Model available, runtime `muse` | Turn reaches Meta | |---|---|---|---| | | | | | Finding outside this PR: after `Meta login complete`, the models still showed `Sign-in needed` (). The config had a credential-less `models.providers.meta` API route, and `model-catalog-view.ts` returns the host evaluation whenever a provider has an authored host binding, so Muse readiness is never consulted. With that entry removed, the models are available immediately (). Tracked in #201818.. **C3: owner revoked while a sign-in is pending.** The owner sent `/login meta`, then `commands.ownerAllowFrom` was replaced with a different owner while the code was pending, and the code was then approved. Results: - The sign-in did not complete. - The only config path changed is the `commands.ownerAllowFrom` edit made by the tester. - All 191 plugin records are identical before and after. - The Muse credential file was not rewritten. One caveat: the config reload restarted the Telegram channel, which ended the pending chat sign-in silently, before the authority recheck ran. The user got no message that the sign-in was cancelled. That is worth a follow-up, but no effect occurs either way. **C4: Muse re-login no longer says "kept its previous account" (2026-11-21).** Two `/login meta` runs on the live build ended `Meta login complete.` After #202564's follow-up, a chat on another model now reads `This chat still uses …`. **C5: Sign-in and a completed Muse reply on upgraded real data (2026-11-23).** The copy of the operator's state was written by a 2026.10.10 main build and upgraded twice, to this head (combined build `e8ec8a4`, 2026.11.6). It ran in an isolated Gateway with the live state read-only. 1. The Meta device sign-in completed and the credential was saved. 2. On the unfixed config, the first attempt reproduced #201818: `Requested agent harness "muse" does not support meta/muse-spark-1.3`. 3. After removing the key-less `models.providers.meta` host route (the #201818 fix), both Muse models were available. 4. A fresh session on `meta/muse-spark-1.3` (runtime `muse`) replied **`OK — Muse Code powered by Meta Muse Spark`**. Native-runtime consent was granted for the test copy. [Trace](https://github.com/ivankuznetsov/openclaw/blob/3f750da88cc5f376796b5b260bb2076c2d8e255b/shared/TRACES-20261123.md). **Upgrade traces** ([TRACES-20261123.md](https://github.com/ivankuznetsov/openclaw/blob/3f750da88cc5f376796b5b260bb2076c2d8e255b/shared/TRACES-20261123.md)): - **Real data, 2026.10.10 → Nov 21 head → this merged head.** All 163 stored session rows are unchanged: model overrides, account pins, thinking levels, harness ids and the runtime pin. v2026.11.6 refuses this data (state schema 39 is newer than its 36). - **Literal v2026.11.6 → this head.** v2026.11.6 created and seeded a fresh state. This head migrated it (state schema 36 → 41), and all 5 sessions are field-identical. - **The live Gateway** was upgraded in place to this build. The migration chain completed and integrity checks passed. **Not covered live:** C2, a non-owner `/login meta`, because no second Telegram account was available. It stays covered by the `commands-login` tests. **Needs a maintainer decision (ClawSweeper "Decision needed"):** should explicitly opted-in (`channelLogin`) profileless native sign-ins run from private chat and persist agent-scoped runtime routing without guided setup activation? This PR keeps runtime installation, native-permission consent, and current-authority checks in place for that path. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

releases.body:
## 2026.11.10-beta.3

### Highlights

- **Update recovery:** Keep interrupted package and source updates recoverable, including updates that cross a schema change or restart the machine. (#200273) (#200366) (#200460) (#200866) (#200994) (#201600) Thanks @fuller-stack-dev.
- **Reliable delegated work:** Keep completed subagent answers available across Gateway restarts and while sibling tasks are still running. (#200279) (#200649) (#200823) (#190999) (#201563) Related #188422 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @vincentkoc, @RomneyDa, @obviyus, @gouyu-hou, and @esqandil.
- **Responsive long-running chats:** Reduce memory and main-thread work when compacting or opening large conversation histories. (#201304) (#188397) (#202234) (#202547) Related #195361 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @jalehman and @garrytan.
- **Private credentials and attachments:** Preserve SecretRef-backed credentials when editing settings and avoid downloading Signal view-once attachments. (#200539) (#197319) (#201428) (#196841) Related #193149, #175333 Thanks @obviyus, @tommyjoseph, @mmaps, @anmol0b, @sallyom, @masatohoshino, and @drobison00.
- **Provider sign-in:** Sign in to OpenCode Console and OpenCode Go in the browser and discover the models available to the signed-in account. (#202949) (#202976) Thanks @daniel-lxs, @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, and @obviyus.

### Changes

- **Templates:** Open a durable chat before completing verified template setup, and allow a previously deleted template agent to be added again. (#196392) (#200628) Related #198475 Thanks @Patrick-Erichsen, @DonnieFi, and @vincentkoc.
- **Plugin side questions:** Let plugins fork live conversation context for hidden background turns, with session-policy-governed file access and execution. (#170146) (#190950) (#200636) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @vincentkoc, @RomneyDa, and @obviyus.
- **Managed installs:** Keep releases in separate directories on OpenClaw-owned installations. (#198835) Thanks @fuller-stack-dev.
- **Hooks:** Accept hook bodies up to 1 MiB, report rejected bodies, and handle batched Gmail pushes. (#200514) (#130002) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @garrytan and @obviyus.
- **MCP configuration:** Apply saved MCP server changes from the CLI without stopping the Gateway. (#200582) Thanks @obviyus.
- **Model discovery:** Refresh signed-in ChatGPT model availability independently of OpenClaw releases or npm, retain provider catalog details, and avoid advertising models omitted by the provider. (#201130) (#201493) (#202618) (#202490) (#167460) Related #201480 Thanks @RomneyDa, @obviyus, and @daniel-lxs.
- **MiniMax documents:** Stop offering retired MiniMax models and enable PDF reading through the current model integration. (#203998) Thanks @RomneyDa.

### Fixes

- **Access boundaries:** Preserve administrator permissions across native clients and prevent removed Discord DM senders from continuing through an old session binding. (#194443) (#196848) Thanks @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, @VACInc, @jjjhenriksen, @sallyom, and @drobison00.
- **Network and call boundaries:** Bind realtime voice streams to signed calls and prevent self-hosted web endpoints or workspace Azure redirects from silently changing the destination host. (#136506) (#196847) (#202031) Thanks @drobison00 and @mmaps.
- **Session ownership:** Keep requested sessions and automations assigned to the requester, preserve Telegram owner/account identity, and route owner-targeted failure alerts to the owner rather than the last chat. (#200952) (#201008) (#201159) (#189953) (#203409) Related #189947, #203403 Thanks @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, @VACInc, @obviyus, @Satoshi-Kusumoto, @chelsealong, and @nousclawds4.
- **Restart delivery:** Deliver final answers interrupted by a Gateway restart and resume persisted requests when transcript metadata advances. (#200553) (#201477) (#200924) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @vincentkoc, @RomneyDa, and @obviyus.
- **Subagent completion:** Retain finished results when parents turn over, access-policy lookups fail, or sibling tasks are waiting; surface delivery failures instead of silently dropping work. (#195275) (#198807) (#200967) (#200249) (#200760) (#201460) (#201544) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @vincentkoc, @RomneyDa, @jalehman, and @obviyus.
- **Subagent steering:** Send new instructions to busy subagents promptly, retain original task instructions on retries, and let resumed parents collect interrupted children. (#200574) (#201636) (#202139) Related #201605 Thanks @RomneyDa, @obviyus, and @mike1122real-hub.
- **Queued conversations:** Avoid duplicate queued follow-up answers, preserve active work when directives arrive, and answer messages sent immediately after a delayed stop reply. releases.body:
## 2026.11.10-beta.2

### Highlights

- Update recovery: keep OpenClaw runnable when package replacement is interrupted, and let the next update finish safely after a crash or reboot. (#200273, #200366, #200460, #200550, #200994) Thanks @fuller-stack-dev.
- Reliable background work: preserve finished subagent results and resume their delivery after Gateway restarts, interrupted parent turns, and sibling activity. (#200279, #200649, #200249, #201544, #201563) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, and @obviyus.
- Faster first conversations: accept the first chat while model catalogs load, keep readiness checks responsive, and compact long histories without holding them entirely in Gateway memory. (#201127, #200370, #201304) Related #195361 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @jalehman, and @garrytan.

### Changes

- Agent templates: open a durable chat before verified setup finishes, while retaining rollback authorization for newly created agents. (#196392, #200300) Related #196048 Thanks @Patrick-Erichsen and @anmol0b.
- Plugin side questions: let plugins fork a session’s live context for background work with their own tools and policy-controlled file and command access. (#170146, #190950, #200636) Thanks @obviyus.
- Webhooks: accept bodies up to 1 MiB, report rejected requests, and fan out batched Gmail notifications. (#200514, #130002) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @garrytan and @obviyus.

### Fixes

- Secret-backed skill keys: preserve SecretRef values when keys are edited through the Skills page or skills.update instead of replacing references with plaintext. (#200539, #197319) Related #193149 Thanks @obviyus, @tommyjoseph, and @mmaps.
- Permission boundaries: retain the admitted requester’s authority across restart recovery and native UI clients, and keep queued input from ending without a recorded cause. (#200394, #181363, #194443, #200433) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, @jjjhenriksen, @sallyom, @VACInc, and @obviyus.
- Chat delivery: finish replies interrupted by Gateway restarts, preserve channel message IDs on oversized history entries, and reject stale-pane sends after a conversation branch switches. (#200553, #201698, #113073) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @vincentkoc, @RomneyDa, and @obviyus.
- Subagent conversations: deliver completed results while siblings are still running or waiting, preserve each result under its requester turn, and stop sessions_send from blocking beyond its timeout. (#190999, #200967, #200873, #201373) Related #188422 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @vincentkoc, @RomneyDa, @gouyu-hou, @obviyus, and @esqandil.
- Live steering: deliver new instructions to busy subagents immediately, keep background turns running through configuration edits, and allow steering while a Code Mode command is active. (#200574, #200516, #200998) Thanks @obviyus, @RomneyDa, and @VACInc.
- Automation continuity: retain scheduled work when chats, groups, or sharing change, preserve owner/account bindings across handoffs, and keep carried-over jobs running after updates. (#200314, #200396, #201434, #201008, #200653) Related #200307, #200600 Thanks @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, @hannesrudolph, @obviyus, @daniel-lxs, and @VACInc.
- Automation outcomes: distinguish recovered tool errors, genuine tool failures, and successfully delivered reports; suppress notices for expected skips rather than reporting them as failed starts. (#201638, #107735, #139037, #120056, #152165, #186652, #194276, #200032) Related #102206, #116731, #194261, #200030 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @obviyus, @joshavant, @solavrc, @hartmark, @NarahariRaghava, @warren2008-2020-spec, @pash-openai, @wr-web, @slatem, and @daniel-lxs.
- Telegram: keep receiving messages when update IDs restart, and answer messages even when an attachment cannot be downloaded. (#201167, #200682) Thanks @RomneyDa and @obviyus.
- Discord and WhatsApp: reconnect all Discord accounts after network outages, preserve independent requests instead of replacing active tasks, and avoid flooding sessions with WhatsApp reconnect notices. (#201415, #201518, #191037) Related #162189, #190640 Thanks @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, @obviyus, @mattreyes0824, @ericcurtin, and @sercada.
- Matrix and Slack: prevent quoted bot mentions from starting new Matrix turns, render Matrix polls and votes in Element X, and retain Slack questions when an unauthorized person presses a button. (#197091, #191700, #201371) Related #197065, #191678, #201348 Thanks @Jo2234, @obviyus, @chelsealong, @geekforlife, and @shannon0430.
- Media and meetings: expose inbound Twilio MMS photos to agents, retain long Feishu streaming replies, and keep meeting audio and captions alive after a join request returns. (#200890, #161777, #191059, #178415) Related #200804, #139443, #173896, #178413 Thanks @deepujain, @obviyus, @potterdigital, @ArthurNie, @Simon2256928, @valkyriweb, @jeremynorris, and @sukhdeepjohar.
- Talk and mobile: load conversation history for fresh calls, keep iOS spoken replies beside the turn that prompted them, and avoid stale roles in approval alerts. (#201352, #197136, #200360) Related #197129 Thanks @davelutztx, @xena68, @obviyus, @Marvinthebored, @Peetiegonzalez, @vyctorbrzezowski, and @joshavant.
- Claude CLI: retain final answers after progress and large tool results, avoid redoing completed tool work on fallback, and preserve long child results in completion turns. (#200501, #166127, #200801, #200470, #200226) Related #186967, #200744, #199633 Thanks @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, @obviyus, @Trinity-AI-Coder, @RTapiador, @fede-kamel, @jzmudzinski, @chaeyn, @etzelm, @VACInc, and @mulderp82.
- Codex conversations: preserve instructions and oversized request content, recover media-only turns, avoid MCP name collisions, and retain line breaks in streamed replies. (#200690, #200735, #185186, #194831, #201102) Related #185079, #194825 Thanks @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, @obviyus, @kaguranananana, @UHDPass, @lonexreb, @NicoBoom13, and @freeqaz.
- Model discovery: discover new ChatGPT subscription models independently of npm releases, use published catalog limits, retain account reasoning limits, and keep healthy fallback models available. (#201130, #201493, #200403, #200446, #200946) Related #201480 Thanks @RomneyDa, @daniel-lxs, @vincentkoc, @obviyus, and @VACInc.
- Tool access: show required arguments for wide schemas and initial Knowledge tools, preserve full Tool Search pages, validate compact-tool arguments, and leave an empty tools.allow unrestricted. (#200064, #200339, #201487, #114461, #197590) Related #194857, #96115, #111704, #197552 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @jalehman, @vincentkoc, @lyrakat, @cbertucci33, @pallaoro, @wr-web, and @primepal2.
- Browser control: keep page reads attached to the correct page after navigation, preserve the user’s focused Chrome tab, and allow screenshots of background tabs in headless mode. (#196659, #134400, #201626) Related #196658 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, @martins-oss, @obviyus, and @scotthuang.
- Install and update: tolerate concurrent database writers, preserve completed core updates when plugin or service refreshes need retrying, and finish when unchanged plugin configuration is read-only. (#200742, #201545, #201330, #200507, #200331, #201331) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @fuller-stack-dev.
- Older installations: bridge older updater layouts, preserve valid archives, recover interrupted source-checkout updates, and retain package installs when an old wrapper cannot be removed. (#200662, #201314, #200659, #200733, #201009, #200579) Related #200594 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @RomneyDa, @SimonAIbot, and @fuller-stack-dev.
- Linux and Windows updates: avoid RAM-backed temporary-directory exhaustion when TMPDIR is unset, accept pre-existing service drop-ins, validate staged Windows plugin dependencies, and redact Windows home paths from Doctor failure reports. (#199689, #197378, #200595, #200457) Related #197377, #200573, #200451 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @kitiyeung, @holgergruenhagen, @sallyom, @desksk, and @LolPanda2004.
- Storage recovery: preserve PostgreSQL startup and backup restore paths, allow supported moves between SQLite and PostgreSQL, and speed up network database ports. (#197425, #193596, #197795, #200383, #201299, #201374) Related #196966, #197779, #200356, #201250, #201249 Authored by @steipete. Thanks @ceckert, @VACInc, @etzelm, @chelsealong, @evemorgen, and @deepujain.
- History and responsiveness: reduce stalls in transcript searches, sparse-history reads, filesystem-heavy work, plugin reload recovery, and background page cleanup. (#200355, #201566, #200793, #197510, #200320, #200374, #201445) Authored by @steipete. Thanks @VACInc and @RomneyDa.
- Desktop startup: let the macOS app answer its first chat and reopen after credential startup failures; finish VNC authentication before readiness probes close. (#200373, #201505, #193487) Related #200340, #193444 Thanks @jalehman, @jjjhenriksen, @SebTardif, @obviyus, and @lakemike.

- Replay timestamps: preserve the original user-turn timestamp across attachment preparation and worker replay. Thanks @RomneyDa and @vincentkoc.
- Setup and authentication: discover cold account models before inference and classify model-route credential mismatches correctly. Thanks @RomneyDa, @daniel-lxs, @vincentkoc, and @DanCanadian.
- Update diagnostics: retain nested handoff failure details and distinguish snapshot capacity failures from database corruption. Thanks @qodelicious, @RomneyDa, @vincentkoc, and @machine3at.

### Complete contribution record

This audited record covers the complete v2026.11.10-beta.1..906bbc529b0bfd24a9108d124c1aeefe9acc0176 history: 356 in-range PRs + 0 retained seed-only PRs = 356 unique PRs. The generation manifest also supplies direct commits as editorial input; the grouped notes above prioritize user impact.

issues.title: /status reports cumulative turn input as context when estimation is unavailable
issues.body:
## Bug description

When the prompt estimator returns zero or raises, `/status` falls back to `last_usage.input_tokens` for the context line. `LLMUsage.__add__` sums that field across every model request in the turn. As a result, a tool-heavy turn can appear to exceed the current model's input budget even when every request fits.

The fallback is present in [v0.4.2](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/0dc8679edcc6061fbcdf3de13c7e16000e9d1b65/nanobot/command/builtin.py#L188-L201) and in [main at b16ae2bc](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/b16ae2bcfca35beb9899c8238d21e8b6527db972/nanobot/command/builtin.py#L126-L141).

## Steps to reproduce

In an isolated test, populate the session's previous-turn usage with the following synthetic data. Configure a 204,800-token context window and a 4,096-token completion limit. Stub `estimate_session_prompt_tokens` to return `(0, "none")`, then dispatch `/status`. Raising an exception from the estimator reaches the same path.

```python
from nanobot.providers.base import LLMUsage

usage = LLMUsage.reported(input_tokens=82_000, output_tokens=500)
for _ in range(16):
    usage += LLMUsage.reported(input_tokens=82_000, output_tokens=500)
usage += LLMUsage.reported(input_tokens=80_000, output_tokens=500)
session.metadata["_last_usage"] = usage.to_dict()
```

On v0.4.2 this produces the following output.

```text
📊 Tokens: 1474000 in / 9000 out
📚 Context: 1474k/204k (738% of input budget)
```

The first line correctly reports the aggregate across 18 requests. The most recent request in this example used 80,000 input tokens.

## Expected behavior

Show the live prompt estimate when one is available. Otherwise report that the current estimate is unavailable. If the previous turn contains a recorded per-request context value, show it with a label identifying it as historical. The token-use line should continue to show aggregate turn usage.

## Environment

- Reproduced on v0.4.2 and main at `b16ae2bcfca35beb9899c8238d21e8b6527db972`
- Python 3.12 on Linux
- Built-in command with synthetic provider usage. No channel or provider connection required.

issues.title: feat(providers): add bf16.ai built-in uncensored LLM gateway provider
issues.body:
### Problem / Motivation

When running unattended `nanobot` personal agent routines, multi-step tool chains, security/log triage, or IM group workflows, mainstream hosted LLM APIs often emit false-positive prose refusals instead of structured `tool_calls`, halting multi-step automation even when `nanobot`'s own `tools.restrictToWorkspace` and sandbox rules already govern local execution.

Users currently have to hand-configure `providers.bf16` and `modelPresets` in `~/.nanobot/config.json` manually. Adding `bf16.ai` as a built-in OpenAI-compatible gateway provider (similar to recent gateway additions such as #6647) gives users one-click onboarding via `nanobot onboard` and the WebUI model settings.

### Proposed Solution

Add `bf16` (`bf16.ai`) to `nanobot/providers/registry.py`, `nanobot/config/schema.py`, `nanobot/cli/onboard.py`, `nanobot/webui/settings_models.py`, and WebUI provider picker:

- **API Base URL:** `https://api.bf16.ai/v1` (standard OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions + public `GET /v1/models` catalog, no key required to list models)
- **Env var / Key prefix:** `BF16_API_KEY` (`sk-bf16-v1-...`)
- **Default model:** `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-uncensored` (1M context window, native vision, reasoning, and deterministic structured `tool_calls`)
- **Other active uncensored open-weight models:** `zai-org/glm-5.3-uncensored`, `zai-org/glm-5.3-flash-uncensored`, `moonshotai/kimi-k3.1-pro-uncensored`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-uncensored-fast`, plus `bf16/auto*` smart routers.

### Alternatives Considered

Manual custom OpenAI-compatible configuration in `~/.nanobot/config.json` works today (and we maintain a setup guide at https://bf16.ai/docs/clients/nanobot), but lacks built-in onboarding discovery, provider icon/branding in WebUI, and preset defaults.

### Related Component

LLM Provider

### Additional Context

- Disclosure: I work on bf16.ai.
- Respecting `CONTRIBUTING.md` (PRs currently restricted to repository collaborators), I am opening this issue first to discuss the integration. Happy to provide a complete, tested patch or collaborate if approved!

issues.title: AI/ML API as a hosted MCP server for NanoBot
issues.body:
### Problem / Motivation

Hi! I'm from AI/ML API (aimlapi.com). We'd like to add our official hosted MCP server to the MCP presets list, so NanoBot users can connect it without typing the URL by hand.

### Proposed Solution

One new entry in `nanobot/webui/mcp_presets.json` and one row in the table in `docs/mcp-presets.md`, following the format of the existing entries (an OAuth preset, like TickTick). No code changes.

I understand pull requests are accepted only from collaborators. Could you confirm you'd accept this entry? If yes, could a collaborator add it from this issue? The exact entry is here: https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/compare/main...aimlapi:hkuds-nanobot-aimlapi:feat/aimlapi-mcp

### Alternatives Considered

_No response_

### Related Component

Other

### Additional Context

**What it is**
- Official AI/ML API MCP server: one connector with access to 10,000+ AI tools and models
- Remote MCP server (streamable HTTP), hosted by us: nothing to install or run locally
- Endpoint: https://mcp.aimlapi.com/mcp
- Auth: OAuth sign-in, or `Authorization: Bearer <API key>` (keys: https://aimlapi.com/app/keys)
- Docs: https://docs.aimlapi.com/quickstart/mcp
- Listed in the Official MCP Registry as `com.aimlapi/mcp`

**What the agent can do with it**
The agent can call tools and AI models through this one server.

Tools (examples, not the full list):
- Web search, crawling and page extraction
- Document parsing: PDF, Office files, images and code to Markdown, with OCR
- Social media data: X, Reddit, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn jobs, Meta Ad Library
- SEO data: Ahrefs and DataForSEO
- GitHub and Hacker News trending, AI model leaderboards and benchmarks (Code Arena)

Models: chat and reasoning LLMs, image, video, music and speech generation, speech-to-text, OCR and embeddings. The agent can search and compare models by price and speed, and then run them.

**Billing**
One AI/ML API account (OAuth sign-in or an API key). Third-party tools are called through the same account, so no separate accounts or subscriptions with those providers are needed. Billed per use, no subscription. Model lookups and account checks are free.

prs.title: feat(webui): redesign session management with Mission Control, Live Pulse bar, and Active Drawer
prs.body:
## Summary

Pure-frontend redesign of WebUI session management to move beyond the cramped 272px chat-history sidebar and match nanobot's multi-project, concurrent-agent runtime:

- **Workspace Top Bar & Cross-Project Live Pulse (`WorkspaceTopBar.tsx`)**: Replaces the permanently docked sidebar with a slim 48px navigation bar (releasing 100% viewport width for chat & Workbench split panes). Includes contextual `Host / Project / Session` breadcrumbs, unified system controls (`Apps`, `Automations`, `Settings`, theme), one-click **Done**, and a **Live Pulse capsule** that aggregates `waiting / running / ready` counts across all projects with an interactive live popover (real-time elapsed timers + one-click Done).
- **Wide-Screen Mission Control Overview (`MissionControlView.tsx`)**: Smart-landing workspace overview (`#/overview`) featuring:
  - Cross-project **Needs Attention** card deck (`recovery` -> `running` with live elapsed timer -> `ready to review` with inline Done).
  - **Decoupled Split Workspaces** section so Workbench multi-pane groups no longer swallow child panes out of their native projects or create double nested tree lines.
  - **Smart Cleanup Suggestions** (`session-intelligence.ts` + `useSessionAutomationCounts.ts`): purely frontend heuristics surfacing stale (`>= 7d` idle) and quick one-off (`<= 5m` span, `>= 24h` idle) sessions for review and one-click undoable archiving (both globally and per project), automatically protecting running, recovery, unread, pinned, and automation-bound sessions.
  - Dedicated **Open / Done** lifecycle separation so archived sessions no longer mix invisibly into active projects.
- **On-Demand / Pinnable Active Drawer (`ActiveSessionDrawer.tsx`)**: Floating overlay drawer by default (with desktop pin-to-dock option), keeping an **Active Now** section pinned at top and single-level collapsible project groups that retain live running/recovery/unread rollup badges even when collapsed.
- **Upgraded `⌘K` / `Ctrl+K` Search Palette (`SessionSearchDialog.tsx`)**: Adds status filters (`All / Active / Open / Done`), project filter pills, project badges, relative timestamps, muted `@handle` tokens, automation indicators, and keyboard `⌘E` / `Ctrl+E` Done/Restore.
- **Visual De-Noising (`SessionVisuals.tsx`, `ThreadShell.tsx`)**: Replaces loud colored `@handle` underlines with neutral monospace pills so saturated colors strictly signify actionable runtime states; upgrades multi-pane Workbench headers to show `project / title` + muted `@handle`.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — passed
- `npm run typecheck:browser` — passed
- `npm run lint` (`--max-warnings 0`) — passed
- `npm run build` — passed
- Vitest (`session-intelligence.test.ts`, `mission-control.test.tsx`, `session-search-dialog.test.tsx`) — 12/12 passed
- Visually inspected light/dark Mission Control, Smart Cleanup review, Split-Pane + Live Pulse popover, Collapsed-project Active Drawer, and Search Palette via Playwright screenshots.

> Draft PR for visual & UX review before aligning remaining legacy sidebar layout tests (`app-layout.test.tsx`).

prs.title: fix: deliver empty final replies as structured turn failures
prs.body:
When a model finished without a final answer, the runner wrote English fallback text as assistant history and reported success. The runner now records a failed turn instead, distinguishing a confirmed output limit from an otherwise empty reply. A same-chat reply already delivered by the message tool is not reported as a failure.

WebUI shows recovery decisions in a persistent toast **inside the owning conversation pane**. Continue, Dismiss and applicable settings remain reachable. Switching conversations or leaving the conversation hides its notices; returning shows pending recovery. App-level notices such as undoing a deleted session remain global. TUI and text channels project their own notices. Existing history, model budgets, retry and compaction behavior are unchanged.

Verification includes runner/delivery regressions, live and restored recovery, conversation switching, and browser interactions with recovery actions and global Undo. Browser fixture: `/browser/fixture.html?case=chat-failure&notice=recovery&reason=empty_final_response_length&lang=zh-CN`.

Resolves [NAN-491](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-491/通过回合失败事件交付空答复由渠道负责提示)

prs.title: fix(session): preserve timezone offsets for new inputs
prs.body:
## Why

Live activity uses the input's creation time. If a gateway writes a local timestamp without an offset and another gateway timezone later interprets it during history backfill, the timer includes the timezone difference. For example, 1m 27s becomes 481m 27s when UTC input history is read in UTC+8.

## What changed

Capture the local UTC offset when assigning a new inbound message its default timestamp. Both canonical history and queued-input recovery already serialize this field as ISO 8601, so they now retain the original instant. Legacy timestamps and the WebUI wire format are unchanged.

## Verification

Extended the existing WebUI history route test to persist a default admission timestamp and check the recovered user event's epoch milliseconds. The test failed on the missing offset before the fix; the prompt-index and follow-up commit suites pass (30 tests).

Resolves [NAN-496](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-496)

prs.title: fix(exec): allow scoped tmp cleanup commands
prs.body:
## Summary

- replace the blanket recursive `rm` substring deny rule with a target-aware guard
- allow test/build scripts to clean static, directly named `/tmp/<name>` targets, including cleanup inside compound commands
- keep broad, dynamic, traversing, nested, mixed-target, and unsafe-redirect recursive deletes blocked
- keep user-configured deny patterns authoritative and stop treating non-recursive `rm -f` as recursive deletion

## Root cause

The built-in regex matched `rm` flags anywhere in the full command string without inspecting deletion targets. As a result, an otherwise valid validation script was rejected solely because it contained controlled `/tmp` cleanup.

## Safety boundary

The automatic exception is intentionally narrow: every recursive-delete target must be a static direct child of `/tmp` with a concrete name. Commands targeting `/tmp` itself, `/tmp/*`, variables, command substitution, nested paths, traversal, non-`/tmp` paths, mixed targets, or non-benign redirects still fail the deny guard. Explicit user deny patterns are evaluated normally.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/tools -q` — 642 passed, 24 skipped
- `ruff check nanobot/`
- `git diff --check`

prs.title: fix: keep preset drafts out of history and confirm command delivery
prs.body:
## Why

A failed preset switch already preserved the unsent prompt, but retrying could create another visible session containing only internal commands. A slow outbound channel could also lose the `/restart` acknowledgement, and each detached Dream notification left a turn sequence entry behind.

## What changed

- Reuse the failed draft in the same client and workspace scope. Keep internal picker activity out of history and previews until a user message arrives; preserve manually typed `/model` commands. Do not probe the provider or migrate old sessions.
- Use the canonical preset returned on a successful switch. Keep ordinary receipts as the text sent, use explicit results for stop/reset presentation, and select help entries before rendering them.
- Give one-shot notifications a stable sequence of 1. Restart after the channel sends its acknowledgement (after the socket write for WebSocket), with a 10-second fallback if delivery never confirms. This is not a client read receipt.
- Restore hover hints in file-edit rows and reasoning-guide alignment at non-default font sizes. Protect SDK snapshot ordering and exercise narrow-pane actions rather than pinning their padding.

## Verification

- Real browser and isolated gateway: session list stayed empty after failed selection, then contained one session after retry and first send. Both attempts used the same chat ID.
- Focused Python, WebUI, and Chromium regressions passed, including restart delivery, notification sequencing, locale-independent previews, file hover, and resized layout. Ruff, TypeScript checks and `git diff --check` passed.

Contributes to [NAN-480](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-480)

prs.title: perf(ci): speed up full WebUI regression gates
prs.body:
## Why

Frontend changes currently wait roughly 14 minutes for the browser lane. Across 150 recent CI runs (117 PR runs, November 12–16), successful PR browser jobs had a 13m54s median and 17m21s p95; the combined static/unit/build lane had a 4m42s median. This PR shortens the full-suite critical path rather than selecting fewer tests.

## What changed

- Run static checks, production build, full unit coverage, and four browser shards independently. Balance every natively discovered browser file using recorded timings; new tests are included without timing entries. Check executed case identities against full discovery and require every lane to pass.
- Load only the selected browser fixture and its existing mocks/provider. Preserve all 40 scene URLs, moved component bodies, real components/styles/motion, and ordinary local commands. Retain JSON results, coverage summaries, and browser failure traces.
- Preserve every existing assertion. Add a responsive-toolbar readiness assertion before comparing activity-label positions across toggles. Fix attachment details' redundant delayed focus restoration, which otherwise steals focus from the next keyboard Tab; the existing keyboard/download regression remains unchanged.

## Scope

One integrated frontend CI improvement. The only production behavior change is the two-line attachment focus fix exposed by verification. No dependency upgrade, affected-only selection, merge-queue/protection change, automatic retry, increased timeout, disabled isolation, or reduced-motion shortcut. SHA-based workflow concurrency and per-file browser scheduling remain unchanged. Uses standard free-tier `ubuntu-latest` runners with seven-day artifact retention.

Resolves [NAN-452](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-452/在保留全量回归保障的前提下加速-webui-ci)

## Tradeoffs

Parallel browser runners repeat setup, so lower wall time is not a claim of lower total runner minutes. Timing weights are scheduling hints, not a test inventory.

Unit coverage deliberately remains one full native Vitest run with the original 85/80/80/85 thresholds. We tested native blob sharding and rejected it: Vitest 2.1.9 merges already-converted Istanbul maps, and an unhit inner branch can inherit hits from another shard's outer range (a real 0-hit branch became 949 hits). Merely retaining numeric thresholds would therefore weaken the gate. This PR does not introduce a custom coverage merger or upgrade the toolchain to work around it.

## Blast Radius

Browser-fixture initialization, CI job/failure aggregation, and the attachment detail focus handoff. Artifact/discovery checks prevent an empty or incomplete browser shard from turning green. The new resize precondition waits for the real responsive action row, not a fixed delay; all position tolerances and keyboard assertions remain intact.

## Verification

Baseline: [`e91906bc3` CI run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/43882721408), 212 unit files / 3,875 unit tests and 64 browser files / 590 browser cases. Local runs used Node 22.18, Bun 1.3.13, Chromium 156, and an eight-logical-CPU Linux host.

- Full baseline: 3,875 unit tests and 590 browser cases passed. Coverage: statements/lines 94.31%, branches 89.51%, functions 91.88%.
- Browser discovery assigns all 64 files exactly once. Initial four-shard execution ran all 590 cases; three shards passed, and one exposed the responsive-toolbar measurement race. The unchanged attachment keyboard test also reproduced a focus race on the baseline (1/5 paired trials), not just the candidate. After the two narrow fixes, both existing cases passed five fresh repetitions each (10/10), with no retries or relaxed assertions.
- Final local full suite: all 212 unit files / 3,875 tests and 64 browser files / 590 cases pass. Original native coverage: statements/lines 94.31%, branches 89.51%, functions 91.88%, matching local baseline percentages. Seven CI helper tests and 97 Python scope/workflow/failure-gate tests pass. Import boundary checks/checker tests, ESLint, application/browser/production TypeScript, production build, frozen Bun install, npm lock verification, and whitespace checks pass.
- Both hosted frontend runs passed every lane. Independently compared all four native browser artifacts with the baseline: the same 590 case identities, all 64 files exactly once, no skipped/flaky/failed cases and zero retries. Full native unit artifacts contain all 212 files / 3,875 passing tests. Hosted coverage is statements/lines 94.31%, branches 89.52%, functions 91.88%; original thresholds remain enforced.

### Actual hosted critical path

| Run | Longest browser job, including setup | Change selection finished → WebUI gate finished |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| [Baseline `e91906bc3`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/43882721408) | 17m35s | 17m44s |
| [Initial PR code `691108c90`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/43913643900) | 4m00s | 4m09s |
| [Final timing weights `e55eccdfe`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/43915386888) | 4m34s | 7m45s |

The final observation reduces the longest browser job by 74% and frontend gate latency by 56% versus the baseline run. One final browser runner started 3m06s after change selection, explaining much of the wider gate latency; the initial observation was faster. These are two candidate observations with the same full workload, not a newly established median or p95. Timing-weight balance is predictive, not a guarantee of equal runtime across hosted runners. The table measures the frontend gate, not whole-workflow completion: unchanged Python/native-package checks can still dominate the complete CI.

The initial PR's entire workflow passed. The final timing-only commit's first attempt passed all frontend checks but hit a 30-second Python gateway process-exit timeout in `test_real_gateway_goal_single_run_and_stop[True]`. That check passed in the initial full workflow. A single manual rerun of failed jobs passed unchanged, and the final workflow is green on `e55eccdfec5b1c950bc6c03afe4c93ccf0dbf749` (attempt 2). The timeout's root cause is unconfirmed; its initial failure is retained rather than hidden. No backend code, timeout or automatic retry policy was changed.

### Fixture measurement

Five alternating paired trials per scene, fresh isolated browser contexts with HTTP caching disabled, warm Vite/OS caches, identical semantic readiness checks, and real motion. All 70 measured and 14 warmup navigations passed without page/console/request/HTTP errors. Measurements were serialized with the other heavy runs. This measures local scene readiness, not hosted CI p95.

| Scene | Baseline → candidate median readiness | Script requests at readiness |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Default dialog | 420.5 → 239.8ms | 498 → 61 |
| Reopened history | 475.7 → 329.9ms | 536 → 200 |
| Heavy Markdown | 668.9 → 497.2ms | 564 → 252 |
| Settings/API preview | 500.1 → 417.0ms | 498 → 317 |
| Skeleton | 394.7 → 253.3ms | 498 → 273 |
| Initial history loading | 505.3 → 440.1ms | 498 → 393 |
| Chinese history paging | 440.8 → 293.4ms | 556 → 267 |

Retained readiness improvements are 12.9%–43.0%; selected fixture-source script requests fall from 37 to 2–3. Existing targeted layout, highlighting, settings, skeleton, history-loading and anchor cases also passed (25/25). The hosted comparison above uses actual CI job boundaries rather than extrapolating from these samples.
