issues.body:
## Problem

Changing a profile's sandbox settings (`terminal.docker_volumes`, `docker_env`, `docker_extra_args` and the rest of the `terminal:` section) does nothing until the whole gateway is restarted. Nothing tells you this: `hermes -p <profile> config set terminal.…` prints "✓ Set …", the next session starts, and it quietly builds the sandbox from the old settings.

Setting up one sandboxed coding profile took three gateway restarts. Each restart also cuts every live chat, WhatsApp included. This is a poor design choice, not an edge case. Sandbox setup is trial and error by nature (a mount here, a tool path there), and every attempt costs a full restart that drops every session.

## Where it happens

`gateway/run.py`, `_bridge_terminal_config_to_env()`: the terminal settings are copied into `os.environ` (`TERMINAL_DOCKER_VOLUMES`, `TERMINAL_DOCKER_ENV`, …) when the profile is loaded, and are never compared with config.yaml again. The rest of the config is read live (mtime-cached in `hermes_cli/config.py`), so the terminal section is the odd one out.

## What we expected

- A new session, or at least a fresh sandbox container, picks up the current `terminal:` settings, the same way model, tools, skills and SOUL.md changes already apply without a restart.
- If a live container no longer matches the config, Hermes rebuilds it at the next session boundary (or says that it is still using the old settings).
- At the very least, `config set terminal.*` warns that a gateway restart is needed while one is running.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Gateway running; a profile using `terminal.backend: docker`.
2. `hermes -p coder config set terminal.docker_volumes '[... add a mount ...]'`
3. `docker rm -f` the profile's sandbox container and start a new chat with that profile.
4. The new container is built without the new mount (check with `docker inspect`). Only `hermes gateway restart` makes it appear.

Hermes Agent v0.23.3 (2026.9.24), macOS, local gateway, Docker Desktop.

Related, but not the same: #159224 (1Password secrets need a gateway restart, and nothing says so).

issues.title: pm strips UV_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS, so a slow link cannot lower download concurrency — parallel large wheels all hit the HTTP timeout

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: area/install-update
labels.description: Installer, updater, packaging, wheels, doctor

issues.body:
### Bug Description

On a slow link, `hermes update` fails its dependency stage because uv requests several large wheels in parallel and each one times out. The natural mitigation — lowering `UV_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS` — is impossible, because PM's environment isolation strips it.

Output from the failing run (v0.22.6, stable channel; paths shortened):

```
→ Installing Python dependencies…
  ✗ Installing Python dependencies failed; last 26 lines of output:
    Downloading botocore (15.4MiB)
    Downloading google-api-python-client (16.0MiB)
    Downloading cryptography (3.7MiB)
    Downloading pydantic-core (1.9MiB)
    Downloading openai (1.6MiB)
    error: Failed to download `pydantic==2.14.1`
      cause: Request failed after 5 retries in 127.8s
      cause: Failed to fetch: https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/35/ea/…/pydantic-2.14.1-py3-none-any.whl
      cause: operation timed out
```

Six large wheels are requested concurrently. The link is slow enough that none of them finishes inside the 30s per-request default, and uv's own 5 retries just re-enter the same contention.

Raising `UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT` does work — it is forwarded (see below) — but that only buys waiting time. It does not remove the contention: the same wheels, fetched with fewer parallel downloads, complete instead of timing out.

### Root cause (code)

`pm/index_config.py` already forwards transport knobs, but the set is incomplete:

```python
FORWARDED_UV_SETTINGS = frozenset({
    "UV_INDEX_URL", "UV_EXTRA_INDEX_URL", "UV_DEFAULT_INDEX", "UV_INDEX", "UV_NO_INDEX",
    "UV_FIND_LINKS", "UV_INDEX_STRATEGY", "UV_KEYRING_PROVIDER",
    "UV_NATIVE_TLS", "UV_INSECURE_HOST", "UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT",
})
```

`pm/environment.py::_base_environment()` keeps only keys in that set and drops every other `UV_*`:

```python
base = {k: v for k, v in source.items()
        if not k.startswith("PYTHON") and k != "VIRTUAL_ENV"
        and (not k.startswith("UV_") or is_forwarded(k))}
```

So `UV_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS` and `UV_HTTP_RETRIES` never reach uv. Verified against the installed tree:

```python
os.environ["UV_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS"] = "2"
os.environ["UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT"] = "900"
pm.environment._base_environment().get("UV_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS")  # -> None
pm.environment._base_environment().get("UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT")          # -> "900"
```

### Why this belongs with the transport knobs

`UV_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS` is not an index redirect: it cannot re-resolve the lockfile against a different index, so it carries none of the #124418 / #125071 risk that `INDEX_REDIRECT_SETTINGS` exists to prevent. It sits in the same uv networking bucket as `UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT`, which the whitelist already trusts. On a congested or high-latency link, concurrency is the first lever to reach for — ahead of raising the timeout, because raising it only lengthens the window in which the parallel downloads keep starving each other.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a link slow enough that a ~2 MB wheel takes more than 30s to transfer (or shape the interface to that rate).
2. Run `UV_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS=2 hermes pm repair`.
3. Observe that uv still opens its default number of parallel downloads (the variable is stripped), and the tail of `~/.hermes/logs/update.log` shows the multi-download / `operation timed out` pattern above.

### Expected Behavior

`UV_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS` — and ideally `UV_HTTP_RETRIES` — accepted through PM's isolation, alongside `UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT`.

If widening the set is undesirable, an alternative is to default `UV_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS` to a low value for the runtime-environment build, where on a slow link parallelism only adds contention.

### Actual Behavior

Every non-whitelisted `UV_*` is dropped. The only available workaround is inflating `UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT`, which wastes wall time on fast links and still fails when contention is severe.

### Affected Component

Setup / Installation

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A - CLI (`hermes update`), observed via the desktop updater hand-off.

### Hermes Version

v0.22.6 (stable, f0d9488)

### Operating System

macOS (Apple Silicon)

### Additional Context

This is the same downstream consequence as #145470 (dependency follow-up fails → gateway left stopped → exit 0), but a different trigger: that report is the musl libc mis-detection path, this one is plain HTTP contention on a slow link. Filed separately because the fix here sits upstream of the failure — a missing transport knob in `FORWARDED_UV_SETTINGS` — whereas #145470 is about the exit status and gateway lifecycle.

issues.body:
# Feature: Provider scopes — multiple named credentials for the same provider, selectable per scope

## Summary

Allow a **single provider endpoint** (e.g. OpenCode Zen) to be configured **more than once under
distinct names**, each with its own credential, so a user can keep separate subscriptions
(personal / work) and switch which one a session uses — without editing config by hand and
without the two entries collapsing into one.

This is the Hermes-side analogue of OpenCode v2's personal/work key scoping.

## Motivation

A real, common setup:

- Two paid subscriptions to the **same** gateway (OpenCode Zen), same `base_url`
  (`https://opencode.ai/zen/v1`), two different API keys, two different billing pools.
- The user wants a *personal* Hermes and a *work* Hermes, **or** a single Hermes where they can
  switch scope on demand ("today I'm doing work → bill the work key, don't burn personal credits").

Today this is painful for three independent reasons:

1. **Secrets manager only injects one variable.** With Bitwarden Secrets Manager (BWS) the
   allowlist is a hardcoded `frozenset` (`_EXTRA_ENV_KEYS`), so only the canonical
   `OPENCODE_ZEN_API_KEY` is injected. A second scoped variable
   (e.g. `OPENCODE_ZEN_WORK_API_KEY`) is skipped with a warning at startup and the provider ends
   up with no key. → tracked by #97596, open PR #98772.
2. **The setup wizard collapses same-endpoint entries.** `_save_custom_provider()` in
   `hermes_cli/main.py` dedups `custom_providers:` by `base_url` and, on a match, updates
   model/context_length but **not** `api_key` — so the second key is silently dropped.
   → tracked by #40977 and #81789.
3. **Built-in providers don't honour `key_env`.** A built-in like `opencode-zen` reads its
   canonical variable only; there is no supported way to point an instance at a differently-named
   variable. → tracked by #75367.

The net effect: the *only* supported workaround is hand-writing `providers:` entries, and even
then the secret injection path (1) still drops the custom variable.

## Proposed Solution

Introduce a first-class notion of **provider scope** (alias / instance name):

- Allow N `providers:` entries that share a `base_url` but differ by name, each carrying its own
  `key_env` / `api_key`. ✅ *already supported in-tree for the `providers:` dict* — the resolution
  code in `_get_named_custom_provider()` and the credential pool already handle multi-key setups;
  the gap is the save path (2) and the injection allowlist (1).
- Honour `key_env` on **built-in** providers so a named instance of `opencode-zen` can read
  `OPENCODE_ZEN_WORK_API_KEY` / `OPENCODE_ZEN_PERSONAL_API_KEY` (3).
- Document a scoping convention for env var names so secrets managers can inject them:
  `<PROVIDER_BASE>_<SCOPE>_API_KEY`.
- Surface scope in the model picker / `hermes model` so a user can see and pick
  "OpenCode Zen (work)" vs "OpenCode Zen (personal)".
- Provide a way to switch the active scope for a session without editing config.

## Non-goals

- Rotating multiple keys of the *same* account (that is the credential pool, #54011 / #54524).
- Per-key tool policy on the API server (#44615) — different surface.

## Prior art / related

| Ref | What it covers | State |
|-----|----------------|-------|
| #97596 / PR #98772 | BWS/secret-injection allowlist excludes custom provider `key_env` | open |
| #40977, #81789 | `custom_providers` dedup by `base_url` blocks a second key | open |
| #75367 | `key_env` for built-in providers | open |
| #91077, #102725 | same provider+model+base_url with a different credential/api_mode skipped/healed | open |
| #39020 | Desktop Providers settings section with per-provider API keys | closed (implemented) |

I searched open **and** merged issues/PRs before filing; no entry covers the *scope* framing as a
whole. This issue is intended as the umbrella that ties the three gaps together, not a duplicate
of any single one — happy to narrow it to a specific fix if maintainers prefer.

## Alternatives considered

- **Just use two config files / two Hermes profiles.** Works, but doesn't let a single install
  switch scope, and duplicates the whole config.
- **Rely on `providers:` + `key_env` only.** Blocked by the injection allowlist today (1).
- **Convention in `.env` with a manual alias.** Not discoverable, and still hits (1).

## Environment

- Hermes Agent on Windows 11, `opencode-zen` + `opencode-go` providers, Bitwarden Secrets Manager
  (`bws`) as the secret source.

issues.body:
### Bug Description

In `tools/todo_tool.py`, `TodoStore._sanitize_parents()` inspects item hierarchies to break circular parent references:

```python
for item in items:
    seen, node = {item["id"]}, item
    while node.get("parent"):
        if node["parent"] in seen:
            item.pop("parent", None)
            break
        seen.add(node["parent"])
        node = by_id[node["parent"]]
```

When walking up the ancestor chain starting from `item`, if an ancestor cycle is detected higher up in the tree, the algorithm pops the parent attribute from `item` rather than from the ancestor node (`node`) where the cycle was closed.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. In Python, run:
   from tools.todo_tool import TodoStore
   store = TodoStore()
   items = [
       {"id": "1", "content": "subtask", "parent": "2"},
       {"id": "2", "content": "parent", "parent": "3"},
       {"id": "3", "content": "grandparent", "parent": "2"},
   ]
   print(store.write(items))
2. Inspect the result for task "1".

### Expected Behavior

The cycle between "2" and "3" should be broken, while task "1" retains its parent link to "2":
[
  {'id': '1', 'content': 'subtask', 'status': 'pending', 'parent': '2'},
  {'id': '2', 'content': 'parent', 'status': 'pending'},
  {'id': '3', 'content': 'grandparent', 'status': 'pending', 'parent': '2'}
]

### Actual Behavior

Task "1" has its parent reference stripped even though it is not part of the cycle:
[
  {'id': '1', 'content': 'subtask', 'status': 'pending'},
  {'id': '2', 'content': 'parent', 'status': 'pending'},

labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

issues.body:
### Title:
[Bug]: Gateway SIGTERM shutdown hangs on orphaned tool children; lack of bounded subprocess sweep before adapter teardown

### Bug Description
A SIGTERM-initiated gateway shutdown can complete every visible phase and then hang indefinitely without running its final exit path, eventually requiring an unclean supervisor kill (e.g. s6-supervise or systemd SIGKILL). On a production node this resulted in a 4 minute 34 second messaging outage (Telegram and API server down).

The graceful shutdown reaches its last logged phase (`api_server disconnected`), stops logging for 3+ minutes with the process still alive, and never writes an `asyncio.run.returned` or `gateway.exit_nonzero` exit record.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Run Hermes Gateway containerized under a supervisor (`s6` or `systemd`).
2. Have a long-running tool invocation whose subprocess is wrapped in `timeout` (or a child waiting on disk/NFS/FUSE I/O in uninterruptible `D` state).
3. Send `SIGTERM` to the gateway process.
4. The shutdown drain reports `timed_out=False` (0 active sessions).
5. The process halts logging and hangs indefinitely until killed by the supervisor.

### Root Cause Analysis
In `gateway/run_shutdown.py`:
`_stop_interrupt_remaining_work` (which invokes `_stop_kill_tool_subprocesses_off_loop`) is guarded strictly by:
```python
if ctx.timed_out:
    return
```
When `ctx.timed_out` is `False`, orphaned child processes that outlived session cleanup are NOT swept prior to adapter teardown. A `ps` snapshot taken during the hang showed the dying gateway PID still had three `timeout`-wrapped bash subprocesses attached to it (one grandchild in `D` state).

### Expected Behavior
- Child tool subprocesses should be reaped with a bounded timeout regardless of whether `ctx.timed_out` was true or false.
- A hard deadline should be enforced on post-drain teardown, logging any remaining children and escalating to `SIGKILL`.

### Environment
- Hermes Version: v0.22.2 (commit `d923a5eb`)
- Python Version: 3.14.7
- OS: Debian 13 (Docker container under Linux kernel 7.0)
- Supervisor: s6

issues.body:
## Feature Request: Inline Annotations + Main Reply as Structured Dual Input

### The core idea
Allow the user to attach small inline annotations to specific words/phrases/sentences in the assistant's response (like Word comments or GitHub PR inline reviews), while also composing a separate main reply in the input box. Both are sent together in one turn, and the agent receives them as structured context.

### Interaction flow

Step 1. User selects text in the assistant's response -> an "Annotate" button appears (not just "Reply with selection")

Step 2. Clicking it opens a small inline popover attached to that text like Word's comment bubble

Step 3. User types a short annotation (e.g. "this term is misleading" or "expand on this point")

Step 4. The annotation gets pinned to the selected text as a visual badge/chip

Step 5. User then types their main reply in the regular composer input

Step 6. On send the agent receives a structured payload: main_reply plus annotations array with each annotation containing selected_text and annotation text

### Why this is better than basic quote-and-reply

- Solves ambiguity when discussing specific parts of a long response. With a simple quote, the agent has to guess which part the user is reacting to. With annotations, the connection is explicit.

- Enables point feedback plus summary feedback in a single turn. The user can say "this number is wrong" on one sentence while writing "overall analysis looks good" as the main reply.

- Reduces back-and-forth clarification rounds. One structured message replaces several clarifying exchanges.

- Feels natural to anyone who has used Word comments or GitHub PR reviews.

### Relationship to existing PR #41300

PR #41300 (per-message Reply button + Send Selection to Composer) handles the basic case of quoting text into the composer. This feature request is an enhancement on top of that — adding structured inline annotation capabilities that preserve the connection between feedback and the original text.

The current workaround (copy-paste and manual quotation marks) breaks flow and loses the visual connection. An inline annotation system preserves that connection and enables richer structured communication with the agent.

issues.body:
### Bug Description

I use Hermes Desktop on Windows with 11 profiles hosted in WSL. The Claude Subscription DirectSDK (Experimental) plugin is installed across these profiles. Profile-scoped CLI calls to Sonnet succeeded, with the DirectSDK provider confirmed in the session records.

After restart, Claude remained selectable in the default profile, but I observed the provider missing from both the Desktop chat model picker and Bot Chat in at least three profiles: local-ai-comfyui, prompting, and jmoon-digital-identity. In local-ai-comfyui it had briefly become visible in both pickers before disappearing again after a PC restart.

I also compared default and local-ai-comfyui in the browser Dashboard connected to the same WSL backend. In that comparison, default listed 13 Claude models. The affected profile showed the provider name but offered no models.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a WSL backend serving multiple Hermes profiles and connect Hermes Desktop on Windows to it.
2. Install Claude Subscription DirectSDK in the default and named profiles. Configure the named profiles to use the existing Claude Code login. Verify that a named profile can complete a Sonnet CLI call through DirectSDK.
3. Restart the system and reopen Hermes Desktop. Before using Refresh Models, compare the model picker in default with the pickers in named profiles. Check both a new chat and Bot Chat.
4. In the browser Dashboard connected to the same backend, open Models for default, then for an affected profile. Select Claude Subscription DirectSDK in each and compare the lists.

The set of affected profiles varied between starts. These steps describe the observed setup and symptom. A controlled reproduction of one possible trigger is described under Root Cause Analysis.

### Expected Behavior

After restart, each profile with a working DirectSDK installation and Claude Code login should list its available Claude models in Desktop, Bot Chat, and the browser Dashboard. I should be able to choose Sonnet or Opus for a conversation while keeping that profile's existing default model.

### Actual Behavior

Desktop and Bot Chat: the DirectSDK provider was absent in local-ai-comfyui, prompting, and jmoon-digital-identity. It remained selectable in default.

Browser Dashboard: default listed 13 Claude models. In local-ai-comfyui, selecting the provider displayed:
  run `hermes model` to configure (api_key)
  no models listed for this provider

The live Dashboard request resolved to the correct local-ai-comfyui profile directory. Its response already contained an empty provider row. The same server-side measurement was not taken for the other two profiles.

### Affected Component

Other

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Selected output from `hermes -p local-ai-comfyui debug share --local`:

version:     0.23.3 [caafe538] (2026-11-19)
os:          Linux 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64
python:      3.14.9
openai_sdk:  2.54.0
profile:     local-ai-comfyui
model:       gpt-6.1-sol
provider:    openai-codex

The model and provider above are the profile defaults. The issue occurs when opening the picker to select Claude Subscription DirectSDK. Live Dashboard observations for the default and affected profiles are included in “Additional Logs / Traceback”.
```

### Operating System

Windows desktop client with Ubuntu on WSL hosting the Dashboard and gateway

### Python Version

3.14.9

### Hermes Version

v0.23.3 (caafe5389ae); Claude Subscription DirectSDK plugin v0.3.5

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
Live Dashboard REST diagnostics, summarized from two correlated requests:

default:
  profile directory resolved correctly
  DirectSDK present in profile layer
  provider decision: ok
  result: 13 models

local-ai-comfyui:
  profile directory resolved correctly
  raw registry entry: external_process
  DirectSDK absent from profile layer
  cp_config=False
  provider decision: not_in_auth_registry
  result: placeholder row, 0 models, auth_type=api_key

Temporary diagnostic instrumentation was removed after capture. No fix was applied to the live installation.
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

The live capture narrowed the failure to the provider registration visible to the affected profile. We reproduced the full symptom in isolation by forcing the profile's first plugin scan to run while `_COLLECT` was active. The Claude registration went into the collector, leaving the profile's staging layer empty. `import_into_layer` in `providers/plugin_reload.py` recorded the plugin fingerprint anyway. A later scan saw the same fingerprint and skipped loading the plugin again.

The actual model-options builder then returned 0 models and the `api_key` hint for the affected profile, while default still returned 13. A normal `bundled_profiles()` call did not trigger this sequence in isolation. Whether `_COLLECT` was active during the first scan in the live process remains unknown.

### Proposed Fix (optional)

Consider preventing `import_into_layer` from recording a successful load when a model-provider registration was diverted away from its staging layer.

Across six related test files, the baseline and candidate each had 16 passes and the same three failures in the isolated environment. The candidate has not been validated in a live installation.

### Problem or Use Case

When a site sends a sign-in code by email, Hermes pauses at the verification step until the user copies the code into the masked prompt. This interrupts browser tasks that could otherwise complete unattended, including on sites that offer email as their only verification method. The [credential vault documentation](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/credential-vault#two-factor-codes) describes the current behavior.

Add an opt-in option in Desktop Settings → Passwords & Logins to autofill emailed sign-in codes for a saved login. Keep the existing masked prompt available when automatic autofill is disabled or Hermes cannot confidently match a fresh code to the current sign-in.

### Alternatives Considered

The masked prompt works when someone is available. Saved authenticator keys already support automatic TOTP autofill on sites that offer that method.

issues.title: Desktop: MEDIA path followed by CJK full-width parenthesis (（1...) is captured into path — preview fails

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: comp/desktop
labels.description: Electron desktop app (apps/desktop/*)

labels.name: desktop/chat
labels.description: The chat view of the desktop app: composer, sending messages, message rendering, markdown, streaming

issues.body:
## Bug Description

On Hermes Desktop, when an assistant emits a `MEDIA:` tag whose path is immediately followed by a **CJK full-width parenthesis containing a digit** on the same line, the Desktop renderer captures the parenthesis and the digit as part of the path. The generated file card then points to a non-existent path and preview fails.

This is the Desktop-renderer counterpart of the already-fixed gateway issue #88038 / PR #88044. The gateway side now accepts CJK full-width punctuation as MEDIA path terminators, but the Desktop-side parser still does not.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In Hermes Desktop, have the assistant emit a single line containing:
   `原始 INSERT：MEDIA:C:/Users/Administrator/Desktop/tmp/op-history-retry-raw.sql（1 条 ieai_sysm_button + 1 条 ieai_sysm_menu_button_rel）`
2. The file card is rendered and the user clicks Preview.
3. Observe the error dialog.

`desktop.log` shows:

```
[hermes] [renderer error:main] 预览不可用: Error: C:/Users/Administrator/Desktop/tmp/op-history-retry-raw.sql（1 — That path does not exist on this computer
```

The captured path is `...sql（1` — the `（1` suffix was swallowed into the MEDIA path.

## Root Cause

In `apps/desktop/src/lib/chat-messages/parts.ts` at commit `caafe5389ae585` (v0.23.3):

```ts
const _MEDIA_PATH_BARE = '[^\\s`"]+'            // stops only at whitespace
const _MEDIA_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION = '.,;:!?'    // ASCII only — no CJK full-width punctuation
```

`MEDIA_TAG_RE` / `MEDIA_LINE_RE` capture `...sql（1` (the `（1` has no whitespace before `条`). `splitTrailingPunctuation()` then trims only ASCII `.,;:!?; the trailing character here is the digit `1`, which is not punctuation, so nothing is trimmed. `isPlausibleMediaPath()` accepts the result because it contains `/`, so a dead link is rendered.

Meanwhile `gateway/platforms/base.py` at the same commit already has:

```py
_MEDIA_CJK_TERMINATORS = "（）『』《》：，。；！？、“”‘’【】"
```

in the trailing lookaheads of `MEDIA_TAG_CLEANUP_RE` and `MEDIA_EXTENSIONLESS_TAG_RE` (added by #88044). The Desktop and gateway parsers are separate implementations and the CJK fix was never mirrored to `parts.ts`.

## Expected Behavior

Desktop should treat CJK full-width punctuation (`（`, `：`, `。`, `，` etc.) as a MEDIA path terminator even when followed by a digit, matching the gateway behavior: the card should link to `...op-history-retry-raw.sql` and the `（1 条...）` text should remain plain prose.

## Actual Behavior

The card links to `...op-history-retry-raw.sql（1`, which does not exist; Preview fails with "That path does not exist on this computer".

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Hermes Desktop v0.23.3, commit `caafe5389ae585` (2026-11-19), stable release channel, local build
- Install path: `C:\Users\Administrator\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent`

## Related Issues

- #84361 — Desktop MEDIA tag regex absorbs trailing markdown punctuation (fixed in PR #127248, but only ASCII punctuation is trimmed)
- #88038 / PR #88044 — gateway-side fix for CJK full-width punctuation; the same defect, different code path
- #141584 — MEDIA-only streamed reply leaves partial path in preview (different cause)

## Workaround

Put `MEDIA:<path>` on its own line with no trailing text.

## Suggested Fix

Mirror the gateway `_MEDIA_CJK_TERMINATORS` set into `apps/desktop/src/lib/chat-messages/parts.ts` and make the bare-path capture / trailing-split logic treat those characters as boundaries regardless of what follows them (including digits). Add a regression test covering `MEDIA:/tmp/a.sql（1 条...）`.

issues.title: MCP connect backoff raises OverflowError at 1025 consecutive failures, aborting the discovery pass

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/tools
labels.description: Tool registry, model_tools, toolsets

labels.name: tool/mcp
labels.description: MCP client and OAuth

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
## What happens

`tools/mcp_tool_discovery._record_connect_failure` computes the retry cooldown as

    min(_CONNECT_RETRY_BASE_BACKOFF_SEC * (2 ** (n - 1)), _CONNECT_RETRY_MAX_BACKOFF_SEC)

Python evaluates the product before `min()`. Once one server has failed 1025 times in a row, `2 ** 1024` can no longer be converted to a float:

    OverflowError: int too large to convert to float

`_discover_all` calls `_note_connect_failure` (which records the failure) in a plain loop over the `asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True)` results, with no `try` around it; `_run_discovery_pass` catches only `TimeoutError` / `InterruptedError`, and `discover_mcp_tools` wraps the pass in `try/finally` without `except`. The exception therefore leaves the discovery pass, and the cooldown for that server is never recorded.

## Reproduction

With the pinned constants (30.0 / 600.0):

    >>> min(30.0 * (2 ** (1025 - 1)), 600.0)
    OverflowError: int too large to convert to float

`n = 1024` still returns `600.0`; `n = 1025` raises.

The counter is per connection key and is only dropped by `_clear_connect_failure` (called on a successful connect); while the process keeps running, a server that keeps failing (wrong URL or token) increments it on every attempt, so a long-running process can in principle reach `n = 1025`.

## Expected

Any failure streak keeps the capped cooldown; failure bookkeeping must never raise.

## Environment

main @ 4f676af2, Python 3.14.7, pytest 9.2.0

labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.description: Local model inference/runtimes: llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, MLX/vLLM, GGUF, VRAM and offload

labels.name: provider/other
labels.description: Calling models through a small provider without its own label (for example Kilo Code, Hugging Face I

issues.body:
## Background

`/fast` (and `agent.fast_mode` windows) works well, but `resolve_fast_mode_overrides()` gates the params to first-party hosts via `_fast_mode_route_supported()` (`hermes_cli/models.py`): only `api.anthropic.com`, `api.openai.com`, `chatgpt.com`, `api.x.ai`. The comment is explicit — "Only the first-party endpoint that bills for fast mode may receive its params" / "so proxies never see the params".

That gate is right for *billing-driven* fast modes, but local inference servers are now growing their own priority mechanisms. Concretely: a feature request is going to Strata (local Qwen3.8-Flash-Next server, OpenAI-compatible API) for a **Fast Mode** — preempt in-flight generations for a priority request, hold the normal queue ~1–2 min after the last fast request, then resume (https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/6990). The intended architecture:

```
voice/assistant client → Hermes (fast turn) → local server processes it within seconds
                                              → background agent/worker generations paused & requeued
```

With the current gate, Hermes marks the turn fast and then silently drops the override before it ever reaches the custom base_url — the local server never learns which requests are interactive.

## Proposal

Keep the billing gate as the default, but add an explicit user opt-in so the override is forwarded on custom routes:

```yaml
providers:
  my-local-llm:
    base_url: http://127.0.0.1:47831/v1
    fast_mode: priority        # forwards {service_tier: "priority"} (or speed: fast) on fast turns
```

- Default off (unchanged behavior; proxies still never see the params).
- When explicitly enabled for a provider, `resolve_fast_mode_overrides()` skips the host allowlist check for that provider.
- The existing 429-based `_fast_mode_unavailable_models` learning stays as the safety net: a server that rejects the field (unknown-parameter 4xx) disables it per session, same as today.
- Optional: `fast_mode: passthrough` to forward whatever tier words apply, for servers that mirror the OpenAI/Anthropic field names.

This is a small change at a single gate function and makes `/fast` useful for the local-server tiering that's emerging (Strata Fast Mode, llama.cpp proposals), which is exactly where interactive latency hurts most.

issues.title: [Bug]: Skills installed from a well-known index outside /.well-known/skills/ can never be checked or updated

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/tools
labels.description: Tool registry, model_tools, toolsets

labels.name: tool/skills
labels.description: Skills system (list, view, manage)

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
### Bug Description

`hermes skills install` accepts a well-known index at any path in the form `well-known:<index URL>#<skill>`. But it records the installed skill as `well-known:<base>/<skill>`. `WellKnownSkillSource._parse_identifier` can read that recorded form back only when the URL contains `/.well-known/skills/`. For an index anywhere else, the update check's `fetch` gets `None`, so `hermes skills check` reports the skill as `unavailable` from then on and `hermes skills update` can't refresh it.

This affects indexes published at `/.well-known/agent-skills/`, such as ones declaring the discovery 0.2.0 schema (`https://schemas.agentskills.io/discovery/0.2.0/schema.json`).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `hermes skills install "well-known:https://taskaid.ai/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json#getting-started" --yes`. It installs, with scan verdict SAFE.
2. `hermes skills check`

For comparison, `hermes skills install https://taskaid.ai/.well-known/agent-skills/taskaid/SKILL.md` (URL source) reports `up_to_date` in the same check.

### Expected Behavior

`skills check` resolves the skill through the index it was installed from and reports `up_to_date` or an available update, and `skills update` can refresh it.

### Actual Behavior

```
┃ Name            ┃ Source     ┃ Status      ┃
│ taskaid         │ url        │ up_to_date  │
│ getting-started │ well-known │ unavailable │
```

The cause shows up directly:

```python
from tools.skills_hub_sources import WellKnownSkillSource
w = WellKnownSkillSource()
w._parse_identifier("well-known:https://taskaid.ai/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json#getting-started")  # parses
w._parse_identifier("well-known:https://taskaid.ai/.well-known/agent-skills/getting-started")             # None: the identifier recorded at install
```

### Affected Component

Skills (skill loading, skill hub, skill guard)

### Debug Report

From `hermes debug share --local`, with the home path redacted and the log section left out:

```
version:          0.23.3 [caafe538] (2026-11-19)
os:               Darwin 27.2.0 arm64
python:           3.14.9
profile:          default
hermes_home:      <redacted>
model:            (not set)
provider:         (auto)
features:
  toolsets:           hermes-cli
  mcp_servers:        0
  skills:             2
```

### Operating System

macOS (Darwin 27.2.0, arm64)

### Python Version

3.14.9

### Hermes Version

0.23.3 (caafe538). The same code is on `main` at 8fc0374.

### Root Cause Analysis

- `_meta` and `fetch` record `_wrap_identifier(parsed["base_url"], skill_name)`, which is `well-known:{base_url}/{skill_name}` ([L30](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/8fc0374447313e276f6b9a2764bfc750190c966a/tools/skills_hub_sources.py#L30), [L93](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/8fc0374447313e276f6b9a2764bfc750190c966a/tools/skills_hub_sources.py#L93), [L150-L151](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/8fc0374447313e276f6b9a2764bfc750190c966a/tools/skills_hub_sources.py#L150-L151)).
- `_parse_identifier` splits that short form only when `BASE_PATH` (`/.well-known/skills`) is in the URL, and otherwise returns `None` ([L121](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/8fc0374447313e276f6b9a2764bfc750190c966a/tools/skills_hub_sources.py#L121)).
- `check_for_skill_updates` calls `src.fetch(identifier)` with the recorded identifier and reports `unavailable` when it gets nothing back ([skills_hub_install.py L353-L359](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/8fc0374447313e276f6b9a2764bfc750190c966a/tools/skills_hub_install.py#L353-L359)).

### Proposed Fix

When the base URL isn't under `BASE_PATH`, have `_wrap_identifier` record the index form, `well-known:{base_url}/index.json#{skill_name}`, so the identifier round-trips. Keep the short form for `/.well-known/skills/` so existing lock entries still parse. Add a test that installs from an index at another path and then checks it.

There's a separate, larger gap: a 0.2.0 index lists each skill with a `url` and a `digest` rather than `files`. Reading those would let the adapter follow `url`, and let `check` compare digests without downloading. I can file that as its own feature request if it's useful. I'm also happy to send a PR for the bug above if this approach looks right.

issues.title: Kanban dashboard /dispatch endpoint bypasses max_in_progress and max_in_progress_per_profile caps

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/cron
labels.description: Cron scheduler and job management

labels.name: comp/plugins
labels.description: Plugin system and bundled plugins

labels.description: File tools (read, write, patch, search)

issues.body:
## Summary

The kanban dashboard's `POST /dispatch` nudge (`plugins/kanban/dashboard/plugin_api.py`) calls `kbd.dispatch_once(...)` without passing `max_in_progress` or `max_in_progress_per_profile`. Both default to `None`, which skips cap enforcement entirely, so a single click can spawn up to `max` (default 8) workers of one profile — even when the gateway tick and CLI honour the configured caps.

This is the same class of defect as #29034 (unbounded worker swarms) and #28805 (caps only reachable via CLI), but on the dashboard path that #34337 did not cover.

## Reproduction

1. Configure:
   ```yaml
   kanban:
     max_in_progress: 3
     max_in_progress_per_profile: 1
   ```
2. Restart the gateway (caps take effect; verified in gateway.log).
3. Open the Kanban dashboard and click **Dispatch** (or POST `/dispatch`).
4. Observe N workers spawn for a single profile, ignoring the per-profile cap of 1.

## Evidence

- Gateway log after restart: `kanban dispatcher: max_in_progress=3`, `max_in_progress_per_profile=1`.
- Dashboard-spawned tasks show `claim_lock = <dashboard-pid>` (e.g. `theseus-cachy:284396`), distinct from the gateway's own pid, proving the claim came from the dashboard route, not the 60s tick.
- Result: lane saturation (HTTP 429) and stranded ready cards.

## Root cause

`plugins/kanban/dashboard/plugin_api.py`:

```python
result = kbd.dispatch_once(conn, dry_run=dry_run, max_spawn=max_n, board=board)
```

`dispatch_once` accepts `max_in_progress` and `max_in_progress_per_profile` (both default `None` → no cap). The CLI path (`hermes_cli/kanban_ops.py::_cmd_dispatch`) and the gateway tick resolve these from config and pass them; the dashboard route does not.

## Suggested fix

Resolve the caps from config in the route, mirroring `_cmd_dispatch`:

```python
try:
    from hermes_cli.config import load_config
    _cfg = load_config()
    _kanban_cfg = _cfg.get("kanban", {}) if isinstance(_cfg, dict) else {}
    _max_per_profile = kbd._positive_int(_kanban_cfg.get("max_in_progress_per_profile"), None)
    _max_in_progress = kbd.resolve_max_in_progress(kbd._positive_int(_kanban_cfg.get("max_in_progress"), None))
except Exception:
    _max_per_profile = None
    _max_in_progress = None

result = kbd.dispatch_once(
    conn, dry_run=dry_run, max_spawn=max_n, board=board,
    max_in_progress=_max_in_progress,
    max_in_progress_per_profile=_max_per_profile,
)
```

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.22.4 (local 4d04303818b6)
- Dashboard service: `hermes-dashboard.service`
- OS: Linux (Arch/CachyOS)

## Related

- #29034 (unbounded worker swarms)
- #28805 (caps only reachable via CLI)
- #34337 (added `max_in_progress` to CLI + gateway)

prs.title: Console 'cron run' no longer silently resumes a paused job (salvage #158501)
prs.body:
Running a paused or disabled cron job from `hermes console` used to quietly switch it back on and erase the note saying why it was paused. Now the console refuses with the same message the other run commands give, and the job's saved record is left untouched.

Salvage of #158501 by @harshaygadekar
Salvage of #158630 by @andreygaag

Fixes #156575

## Before / after (real console engine, scratch `HERMES_HOME`)

| Stored job before `cron run` | main @ 5725d1d3 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| paused, `paused_reason="paused by owner"` | `ok` · `Triggered job: paused-job [scheduled]` · `enabled=True`, `paused_reason=None` | `error` · `Job is paused/disabled; resume it before running.` · `enabled=False`, `state=paused`, `paused_reason="paused by owner"` |
| disabled only (`enabled=False`) | `ok` · `Triggered job` · `enabled=True` | `error` · same refusal · `enabled=False` |
| `cronjob(action='run')`, paused job with relay-fronted delivery | `success: true, forwarded_to_gateway: true` (POST `/api/jobs/<id>/run`, which resumes the job and clears `paused_reason`) | not forwarded; `execution_skipped: Job is paused/disabled; resume it before running.` |

**Root cause:** console `cron run` called `trigger_job` directly. `trigger_job` deliberately force-resumes (the dashboard's Trigger-now contract), but the console was skipping the `is_job_runnable` gate that the tool / `hermes cron run` / gateway `/cron run` claim path applies first.

## Changes
- Console `cron run` checks `is_job_runnable` under the jobs lock before `trigger_job`, so a pause that lands mid-check isn't lost. Terminal-job and not-runnable `ValueError`s come back as console errors instead of exceptions (#158501 + #158630).
- One refusal string, `cron.constants.NOT_RUNNABLE_ERROR`, now shared by the tool's claim refusal and the console. It was two literal copies.
- The tool's relay-forward path also skips paused jobs. It POSTed to the gateway run route, which ends in `trigger_job`, so on a relay-fronted delivery `cronjob(action='run')` on a paused job resumed it silently. It now falls through to the normal claim refusal.
- `trigger_job` is left as it is. #158501 also gated it, which fails the existing contract test `tests/cron/test_paused_job_run_override_remains_allowed` and the dashboard's force-trigger (`test_trigger_cron_job_forces_paused_job_atomically`). That part was dropped, and so was the rewrite of that test.

## Tests
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_console_engine.py::test_cron_run_refuses_paused_or_disabled_job[paused|disabled-only]` and `::test_cron_run_surfaces_terminal_refusal_without_mutating_job` check that `jobs.json` is byte-identical after the refusal.
- `tests/cron/test_cron_relay_run_forward.py::TestForwardRelayFrontedRun::test_paused_job_is_not_forwarded`
- Red on base: these 4 fail with the console + tool sources swapped to origin/main. Green on head. Full `tests/cron` passes: 1792 passed. The touched console/cron/tool/api-server test files pass: 174 passed.

**Live repro:** a scratch `HERMES_HOME` with one paused job and one disabled job, driven through `HermesConsoleEngine().execute("cron run <id>", confirmed=True)`, then reading back `jobs.json`. On main both jobs are re-enabled and `paused_reason` is cleared. On head both are refused and the records are unchanged.

## Infographic
PENDING

![phone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/feat/desktop-redesign/apps/desktop/docs/images/redesign-phone.png) | ## The toggle One persisted choice, one presentation read, one CSS gate. Nothing else decides which shell renders. ```mermaid flowchart LR Choice["$shellChoice
localStorage, null = default on"] --> Preferred["$portalPreferred
behaviour every window agrees on"] Choice --> Portal["$portalShell
this window renders the redesign"] Portal --> Hook["usePortalShell()"] Portal --> Attr["html[data-shell='portal']"] Attr --> CSS[":root[data-shell='portal'] rules"] Preferred --> Policy["shell-policy.ts
named behaviour gates"] ``` ```ts // src/store/shell-variant.ts export const $shellChoice = persistentAtom('hermes.desktop.agentShell.v1', null, …) export const $portalPreferred = computed($shellChoice, choice => choice !== false) // The chromeless HUD and the popped-out Browser keep the classic look in every mode. export const rendersPortalShell = (choice: boolean | null): boolean => choice !== false && !isHudWindow() && !isBrowserWindow() export const $portalShell = computed($shellChoice, rendersPortalShell) ``` ```css /* Dialogs, menus and popovers are body-portalled, so the gate is on , never an ancestor. */ :root[data-shell='portal'] [data-contrib-shell] { background: … var(--portal-window-background); } ``` - `installShellAttribute()` runs before the first render, so no surface paints a mixed shell. - Pane layout is persisted per shell; flipping the toggle never rearranges the other shell. - Wording follows the toggle too. Classic renders the base catalog exactly as `main` words it; the redesign merges a typed per-locale overlay (`src/i18n/redesign/`) over it in `resolveTranslations`: | Classic | Redesigned | | --- | --- | | Sessions | Chats | | Artifacts | Library | | Profiles | Agents | | Cron jobs | Routines | | Gateways | Machines | Hardcoded messages outside the catalog (main-process sign-in and connection errors, browser-bridge refusals) follow the same choice through `electron/shell-wording.ts` and `src/lib/shell-copy.ts`. ## Sidebar - The open rail destination's button folds and shows its sidebar or panel ("Hide chats" / "Show chats"); ⌘B still toggles. - Folded: Simple mode shows one floating reveal button at the stage corner, Advanced keeps the band button. - Dragging the sash 72px past the minimum width folds the sidebar; reopening restores the previous width. - New chat starts a chat with the agent of the chat on screen, else the most recently used one. Picking an agent in its dropdown opens a chat with that agent at once and does not re-target the button. - Each agent carries a Routines chip (count, and a dot while one is failing). ## Routines | All routines | One routine | | --- | --- | | ![routines](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/feat/desktop-redesign/apps/desktop/docs/images/redesign-routines.png) | ![routine](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/feat/desktop-redesign/apps/desktop/docs/images/redesign-routine.png) | - `/cron` renders `src/app/routines/` in the redesign: every agent's routines grouped Needs attention / Scheduled / Paused, a failure banner with Retry, and a searchable table. Classic's cron page, sidebar section and status-bar item are unchanged. - The rail page offers quick actions only (Run now, Pause/Resume, Rename, Delete). Editing lives in the agent's settings, reached by "Edit in "; Agent › Settings › Routines is the same list for one agent. - No backend changes. Mock elements with no data source (suggestions, "Uses", push delivery) are left out. - A schedule's clock is the machine's wall time, so it is marked with the machine's zone ("Every day at 7:00 AM (UTC−6)") when that differs from the viewer's. ## Plugins - Plugin contributions keep working in the redesign: session-row and profile-group slots render in the new sidebar, plugin panes and rail buttons stay on screen, `sidebarNav.prefs` order and hide rail destinations, and title-bar items stay mounted on Agents, Routines and Settings. - `host.state.viewport.narrow` means below 640px in both shells. - The Capabilities switch enables both halves of a plugin; per-agent settings override it. - Plugin i18n gets the same per-shell layer: `ctx.i18n.register(bundles, { redesign })`. - `src/contrib/__fixtures__/contract-probe/` registers into every area; `contract-probe.integration.test.tsx` asserts it in both shells. The matching e2e spec has not been run. - Not done: status-bar contributions have no home in the redesign's Simple mode, and plugin themes are not restyled. Both are `todo` cases in the probe suite. ## Design language Figma values live in one folder, `src/app/redesign/tokens/`, and nowhere else. ```mermaid flowchart LR Raw["raw.css
ink ladder, navy, brand"] --> Role["color · type · space · shape · motion · layers
one value per role"] Role --> Bridge["bridge.css
maps roles onto the app's --ui-* names"] Role --> Sidebar["sidebar.css
the chat sidebar's own variant"] Bridge --> Sheets["portal-*.css, page and feature styles"] Guard["scripts/check_desktop_design_tokens.py
+ eslint no-portal-arbitrary"] -. "fails on a raw value
outside tokens/" .-> Sheets ``` - `DESIGN.md` § Portal design language documents every role with generated tables. - Shared primitives carry the geometry: `PageHeader` / `PageTabs` (title, description, actions and tab bar at one position on every page; equal-width tabs that reserve room for counts), `PageSidebarPanel` (the panel column), `SettingsCard`, `EmptyState`. - Icons are Pixelarticons (MIT), mapped once in `src/lib/pixel-icons.ts`; classic keeps its icons. - Fonts are the bundled OFL faces: Oswald (display), Mona Sans (body), JetBrains Mono. ## Responsive ```ts // src/app/redesign/breakpoints.ts export const BREAKPOINT_MEDIUM_PX = 640 // below: compact — no rail column, band menu opens a sheet export const BREAKPOINT_WIDE_PX = 1024 // below: sidebar and page panels become sheets export const SHORT_QUERY = '(max-height: 30rem)' // landscape phone or raised keyboard: one-row composer ``` - Coarse pointers in the browser get 44px targets and 16px fields at any width. - Menus and dialogs are capped to the viewport; compact dialogs are full-screen with the footer pinned. - A page whose chunk is still loading waits in its own frame (band, panel title, header skeleton), not an empty window. ## Navigation Code-split pages render synchronously once their chunk is loaded and are warmed at idle (`src/lib/lazy-view.tsx`, `src/app/page-views.tsx`). The Capabilities catalog groups its ~100k rows in one pass behind `useDeferredValue`. Both changes are shared code, so the classic shell gets them too. Production builds, Chromium 1280×880, ms from pointerdown to the painted frame, median of 6 cold / 12 warm interleaved runs. prs.title: chore(catalog): update Model Router to v0.15.0
prs.body:
## Scope
Updates only `plugin-catalog/model-router.yaml` from the merged v0.13.2 entry (`366e32a1eece5c3be70f27b3392eca3b17b4cbb7`, PR #155752) to **v0.15.0**, source commit `d91afc213a8ec38ea437989454e77f80bcfe6de6` on `metamindedu/hermes-model-router` main. It keeps `tier: community`, `category: models`, the Windows-only platform claim and the `>=0.23.1` floor. `version`, `requires_hermes` and every `capabilities` list were compared with `plugin.yaml` at the pin; only `version` changed since v0.13.2, and the capability lists are identical. The screenshot file is byte-identical to the previous pin and is re-pinned to the new SHA.

## What changed for users since v0.13.2 (from `docs/releases/` at the pin)
- **v0.14.0**: the router reads the conversation, ordinary delegation, compression and title models from each profile's current Hermes settings at read time (no background sync, no write). An edit made in Hermes settings or by CLI is followed instead of reported as drift; slots that follow a native model use its verified current route. A Desktop model save writes only the edited roles. A role Hermes cannot resolve (unverified destination, endpoint/credential override, managed value) is read-only and only dependent slots refuse it.
- **v0.15.0**: every settings-section save sends only the values that changed, and each selected profile keeps every value that was not changed. Edited task slots, edited per-slot spare models, an edited delegation method, changed time-limit fields and allow-list additions/removals/descriptions are merged into each target's own settings, with the same compare-and-set and readback. Picking targets no longer copies the loaded profile's whole settings; the earlier copy is an explicit per-section **현재 설정 전체 복사** checkbox (unticked by default). Partial requests carry a `partial_save_schema: 1` marker and are sent only when the backend advertises it; marker-less requests keep their earlier meaning. Consent rules are unchanged: cost consent for each submitted custom spare-model slot, profile-access consent only for new authority computed on the merged result.

The description and known issues were updated for these; no other entry text changed.

## Validation of the exact source
- `hermes plugins validate <clean clone at d91afc2> --install-deps` returns **`ok: true`**, with the same two warning classes as before:
  1. `security scan caution: exec_string (plugin.js:3489)`: the page's own staged-save `exec('stage', …)` wrapper that sends save pieces to the plugin's CLI command through Hermes `cli.exec` (line moved from 3023). No `eval`, `new Function` or dynamic code.
  2. **Private core imports: 65 sites** (62 at v0.13.2; the v0.14.0 native-settings projection added `hermes_cli.config_backend` / `utils.fast_safe_load` reads). Same inherited public-surface debt as the earlier entries.
- `scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/model-router.yaml --json` returns ok with no errors or warnings.
- Exact-commit tests: Node **477 pass / 0 fail / 19 skip**. The full Python suite fails the identical set of **137 environment-dependent real-core integration tests** as the v0.14.0 base (failure IDs compared, none new), 1655 passed. Three rounds of independent review; the final delta review returned GO on the exact reviewed tree, which the commit reproduces. GitHub Actions `Desktop plugin tests` run 45161514433 on `d91afc2` passed.

## Private-core-import warnings
The validator passes and the no-core-override check is clean, but the inherited private-core-import warnings (catalog rule 9) remain. This request does not treat earlier listings or a passing validator as a waiver: if any import must move to public `ctx.*`/documented APIs before listing, please say which and it will be addressed in a follow-up release. No core changes are proposed here.

## Disclosures (rule 13)
- Explicit, previewed settings saves write the selected profiles' `config.yaml` through Hermes's config CLI (backups under `plugin-data/model-router/backups`); v0.15.0 narrows each write to the changed values. Keys: main/compression/title models, `fallback_providers`, the two `auxiliary.*.fallback_chain` keys, `delegation.backend`/`delegation.backends.*`, and `skills.disabled` for re-enabling routing. Slot models live in `plugin-data/model-router/settings.json`.
- Reading models from Hermes (v0.14.0) never writes and never grants cost consent.
- Routing guidance defaults ON for installed profiles without a saved choice; saved OFF stays OFF. Installation selects no backend, changes no models and grants no profile, cost or full-profile-job access.
- Spare models and Fast inheritance can raise cost; allowlisting a profile grants use of its model, credentials and tools; profile-job journals keep prompts and results locally. The AI role proposal sends the profile description, whole SOUL.md and skill names to the owner's saved main model only after Generate.
- No telemetry, self-updater, credential store or approval bypass.

## Boundaries and rollback
Previous pin: `366e32a1eece5c3be70f27b3392eca3b17b4cbb7`. Store and config formats are unchanged since v0.13.2, so rolling back keeps saved values; an older page simply sends whole-section requests again. Automatic preparation of missing profiles remains unavailable; install with the native CLI at the exact SHA with dependency consent.

This is the owner's SHA-bump PR under rule 4. A maintainer merge is what lists the version; submitting this PR does not.

prs.title: ComfyUI no longer queues the same workflow twice when a submission times out (salvage #146328)
prs.body:
When ComfyUI was slow to answer a "run this workflow" request, the helper gave up waiting and sent the same request again, up to three times, so the server could queue the same job two or three times. Now a request whose fate is unknown is sent once and the error is reported. Requests the server clearly never accepted (connection refused, "busy, try later" answers) are still retried, and ordinary reads keep their retries.

Salvage of #146328 by @akhilraija

Fixes #146034

Live: a local server that reads `POST /prompt` and then stalls past the 1 s client timeout, a server answering 503, and a refused port, all driven through the real `_common.http_post`:

| | main | head |
|---|---|---|
| POST /prompt, stalls (job may be queued) | `TimeoutError`, server saw **3** POSTs | `TimeoutError`, server saw **1** POST |
| POST, definite 503 | HTTP 503 after 3 POSTs | HTTP 503 after 3 POSTs (unchanged) |
| POST to refused port | `ConnectionError` (retried) | `RequestNotSent` (retried: nothing was sent) |

**Root cause:** `http_request` retried every timeout, connection error and retryable status the same way for any method, though a POST that timed out after sending may already have queued a job.

## Changes
- From #146328: requests with a body or a non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS method are no longer replayed after an unknown outcome; bodyless GET/HEAD/OPTIONS keep the full retry policy.
- On top (the original capped *every* POST at one attempt, which also dropped recovery from rate limits and refused connections):
  - New `RequestNotSent` (a `ConnectionError` subclass) is raised when the failure provably happened before any request bytes left: requests `NewConnectionError`/`ConnectTimeout`, stdlib `ConnectionRefusedError`/DNS failure. Submissions retry on it.
  - Submissions retry only on `NOT_PROCESSED_STATUS_CODES` = 408/429/503/522. 500/502/504/524 can follow a request the server already queued, so they are returned, not replayed.
  - Multipart uploads stay single-shot: their file stream is used up by the first attempt.
- Callers checked: `submit` (POST /prompt), upload image/mask (multipart), `/queue` delete and `/interrupt` (already `retries=1`). Every GET caller is unchanged.

## Tests
- `tests/skills/test_comfyui_http_retries.py`: `submit()` against each failure kind (timeout, connection drop, OSError, 500/502/504/524 sent once; `RequestNotSent`, 408/429/503/522 retried once), plus the original method × body matrix. RED on base (22 failed), GREEN on head (32 passed).
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/skills/test_comfyui_*.py optional-skills/creative/comfyui/tests`: 153 passed.

**Live repro:** scratch stdlib HTTP server on 127.0.0.1 that stalls `POST /prompt` for 5 s; main `_common.py` vs head through `http_post(..., timeout=1)`. See the table.

prs.title: fix(cron): refuse console run for paused and disabled jobs (#156575)
prs.body:
### Fixes #156575

## Summary

In Hermes Agent, cron jobs can be paused or disabled with an optional audit explanation (`paused_reason`). While the CLI (`hermes cron run`), gateway chat (`/cron run`), and agent tool (`cronjob(action="run")`) properly refuse to run paused or disabled jobs, typing `cron run <job>` inside `hermes console` silently reactivated the job and deleted its audit history.

This change ensures `cron run` in the console behaves consistently with all other interfaces: paused and disabled jobs are refused, and their audit fields remain untouched.


### Before vs After Fix

| Stored Job Before `cron run` | Before Fix (Upstream Main) | After Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Paused with reason (`paused by owner`) | Silently reactivated (`enabled=True`, `state="scheduled"`), and `paused_reason` erased to `None`. | Refused with `"Job is paused/disabled; resume it before running."` Record and audit fields are untouched. |
| Disabled-only (`enabled=False`, `state="scheduled"`) | Silently re-enabled (`enabled=True`). | Refused with the same message. Record stays disabled. |
| Terminal completed one-shot (`state="completed"`) | Uncaught `ValueError` crashed out of the command handler. | Handled cleanly with an informative error message. |

---

## Changes

- **`cron/jobs.py` (`trigger_job`)**:
  - Added an `is_job_runnable(job)` check before scheduling. If the job is paused or disabled, it raises `ValueError("Job is paused/disabled; resume it before running.")`.
  - Removed `"paused_at": None` and `"paused_reason": None` from the update dictionary so manual run triggers cannot clear audit details.
- **`hermes_cli/console_engine.py` (`_cron_job_action`)**:
  - Caught `ValueError` alongside `AmbiguousJobReference` and converted it into `ConsoleCommandError`. This presents clean refusal messages in the console for paused, disabled, and terminal jobs instead of raising unhandled exceptions.
- **`tests/hermes_cli/test_console_engine.py`**:
  - Added parameterized regression test `test_cron_run_refuses_paused_or_disabled_job` covering both paused-with-reason and disabled-only records, asserting that the stored record remains identical before and after.
- **`tests/cron/test_terminal_job_rearm.py`**:
  - Updated legacy test to verify that calling `trigger_job` on a paused job is refused directly at the API boundary and preserves the stored record.



## Testing

- **Reproduction & Red-Green Verification**:
  - Confirmed the defect on upstream `main`: calling `cron run` in the console returned status `ok` and overwrote the stored record.
  - Verified red-green cycle on the new regression tests: base unpatched code failed (`assert 'ok' == 'error'`); patched code passed cleanly.
- **Practical Verification Across Scenarios**:
  - Verified 10 real-world operational scenarios in an isolated test environment:
    1. Paused job with reason (`paused by owner`): execution refused, audit fields preserved.
    2. Paused job without reason: execution refused, record unchanged.
    3. Disabled-only job: execution refused, remains disabled.
    4. Terminal completed one-shot job: returns clean terminal error message without crashing.
    5. Terminal failed one-shot job: returns clean error message without crashing.
    6. Non-existent job reference: returns clean "Job not found" message.
    7. Ambiguous job identifier: displays list of matching candidates.
    8. Normal active job: schedules successfully for the next tick.
    9. Complete lifecycle: Pause -> Refusal on Run -> Explicit Resume -> Successful Run.
    10. Cross-interface parity: confirmed identical refusal message and record preservation across CLI, chat, agent tool, and console.
- **Automated Test Suites**:
  - `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_console_engine.py`: 14 passed.
  - `pytest tests/cron/test_terminal_job_rearm.py`: 14 passed.
  - `pytest tests/cron/test_jobs.py`: 113 passed.
  - `pytest tests/cron/test_manual_run_extra_fire.py`: 9 passed.
  - `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_cron.py`: 30 passed.


## Risks / Notes

- **Low Risk**: The fix relies on the existing `is_job_runnable` helper already used across the scheduler and tool execution paths.
- **Expected Behavioral Change**: Users who previously used `cron run` in the console to restart a paused job must now explicitly run `cron resume <id>` first, matching the requirement of every other interface.

prs.title: uv on slow links honours UV_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS and UV_HTTP_RETRIES again (salvage #148267)
prs.body:
On a slow connection, `hermes update` could fail because several large downloads ran at once and all timed out, and the usual fix (telling the installer to download fewer files at a time) was silently ignored. Now that setting, and the retry count, reach the installer, and the timeout hint tells you to use it.

Salvage of #148267 by @akhilraija
Folds #148298 by @marlonferreira1800-hue (same fix; credited via Co-authored-by)

Fixes #148262

| | `UV_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS=1 UV_HTTP_RETRIES=2 UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT=300` in the uv child env |
|---|---|
| main | `{'UV_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS': None, 'UV_HTTP_RETRIES': None, 'UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT': '300'}` |
| head | `{'UV_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS': '1', 'UV_HTTP_RETRIES': '2', 'UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT': '300'}` |

**Root cause:** PM's uv allowlist (`FORWARDED_UV_SETTINGS`) forwarded the timeout but not the concurrency or retry knobs, so isolation stripped them.

## Changes
- `pm/index_config.py`: forward `UV_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS` and `UV_HTTP_RETRIES` as transport knobs (not index redirects, so they also survive `no_config` isolation). Only those two exact keys; project/interpreter/cache selectors stay stripped.
- Timeout hint now suggests lowering `UV_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS` before raising `UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT`.
- `website/docs/reference/package-management.md`: lists which `UV_*` network settings survive PM isolation.

## Tests
- `tests/pm/test_download_transport_environment.py` (from #148267): runs a real child through `PythonEnvironment._run` with and without `no_config`; the knobs arrive, `UV_PYTHON`/`UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT`/`UV_CACHE_DIR` stay PM's, `UV_NO_SYNC` is stripped, index URL is dropped only under `no_config`. RED on base (2 failed), GREEN on head.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/pm/`: 1244 passed; the one failure, `test_cold_runtime_e2e.py`, fails identically on origin/main on this host (it picks up `~/.local/bin/python3.11`), so it isn't caused by this change.

**Live repro:** a real `PythonEnvironment(..., env=_base_environment(), no_config=True)._run(probe)` with the env above prints the table rows: stripped on main, forwarded on head.

prs.title: Todo cycles no longer detach valid subtasks, and restored lists get the same cleanup (salvage #157758)
prs.body:
When a task list accidentally had two subtasks pointing at each other as parents, the cleanup step cut the wrong link: a perfectly valid subtask sitting under the loop lost its parent, and the loop itself survived. Now the loop is broken at the link that closes it, every valid parent link stays, and task lists restored from history get the same cleanup so they no longer vanish after context compression.

Salvage of #157758 by @akhilraija
Salvage of #104096 by @aniruddhaadak80

Fixes #156671

| Input | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `write` `1→2, 2→3, 3→2` | `[('1', None), ('2', None), ('3', '2')]` — valid `1→2` lost, two edges dropped | `[('1', '2'), ('2', None), ('3', '2')]` — only `2→3` dropped |
| `write` two disjoint cycles with tails (`x→a↔b`, `y→c→d→e→c`) | tails `x`, `y` detached, 4 edges dropped | tails kept, 1 edge dropped per cycle |
| all 5,168 orderings of 4 cycle fixtures | 2,570 orderings drop a non-cycle edge | 0 |
| `restore` `1→2, 2→3, 3→2` | cycle survives; `format_for_injection()` → `None` (plan lost after compression) | acyclic; plan injected as a tree under `2` |
| `restore` `a→ghost` | `format_for_injection()` → `None` | `- [ ] a. task a (pending)` |

**Root cause:** `_sanitize_parents` popped `parent` from the walk's starting item instead of the node whose parent closes the loop, and `restore()` never ran `_sanitize_parents` at all.

## Changes
- `TodoStore._sanitize_parents`: on detecting a revisit, drop the parent of the node that closes the cycle (@akhilraija).
- `TodoStore.restore`: run `_sanitize_parents` after truncation, same as `write()` (@aniruddhaadak80). Both callers (`run_agent._hydrate_todo_store`, gateway snapshot mirroring in `hermes_cli/gateway_agent.py`) go through it.

## Tests

prs.title: fix(comfyui): avoid replaying unknown-outcome submissions
prs.body:
## Summary
Fixes #146034 (currently labeled P2).

The shared ComfyUI HTTP transport retries POST after a lost response or retryable HTTP status. A workflow can already have been accepted, so repeating the request can submit it again; `client_id` is an event-routing identifier, not an idempotency key. Upload streams may also have been consumed.

Limit automatic retries to bodyless GET/HEAD/OPTIONS. Other requests receive at most one attempt, preserving the original exception or HTTP response for the caller. This deliberately includes POST connection failures and 429/503 responses: this generic transport cannot establish safe replay. No claim of an observed duplicate charge is made.

## Verification
Tested on Linux/WSL with Python 3.14.2.

- RED on base `0b95c4716371`: 19 failed, 6 passed in the new regression suite. Failures demonstrate replay and swallowed first-attempt errors.
- GREEN: `HERMES_PYTHON=/home/tony/hermes-agent/.venv/bin/python HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0 scripts/run_tests.sh tests/skills/test_comfyui_http_retries.py tests/skills/test_comfyui_skill.py -q` — 27 passed, 0 failed.
- `python scripts/check --base upstream/main` — 13 checks, ok; health: 0 blocking/advisory.
- Manual loopback HTTP probe using the real `ComfyRunner.submit` and each transport: server read the POST body then disconnected without a response. Both requests and urllib received exactly one POST and propagated the connection error. No remote service, credentials, GPU generation or billing used.

Tests cover the submit caller, timeout/connection/OS exceptions, retryable HTTP responses, safe bodyless retries, and body-bearing requests including empty bodies. The whole repository suite was not run.

## Scope and duplicate checks
No matching PR found by issue-number and ComfyUI retry/submission searches; issue comments were empty immediately before publication. This is the transport retry loop, not the operator-facing wait-timeout hint tracked in #145545. No unrelated workflow repair or timeout UI changes.
