prs.title: fix(plugins): run a marked profile's plugin code under the name it was opened by
prs.body:
## Infographic

![Linked profiles stay refused. Before: Plugin load: asks wrong folder; Providers: own launcher runs; Host child: .env reaches host. After: Plugin load: asks by name; Providers: launcher refused; Host child: .env stays empty. Change: home_path → owner_home.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/575ad7dd-e163-4962-b03f-aa95cb840152)

## What does this PR do?

This PR fixes the gap my last review on #156725 raised (finding 11), now that it has merged. #156725 asks the run-elsewhere marker by the name a profile was opened by. `b912bfb00e7` passed that name (`owner_home`) only to the plugin host's launcher check. The plugin manager still bound `home_path`, the resolved directory, around discovery, loading, unload and a plugin's calls, and `PluginHost` built the host's scope and child environment from it too.

When `profiles/<name>` is a link to a directory outside the Hermes root, code under those bindings asks the marker about a directory with no marker folder above it, and is told the profile runs here. On `main`, for a marked profile linked that way:
- `hermes -p ops tools list`, `profile list` and `memory status` each start the launcher the profile's own `config.yaml` names. This is the model-provider extraction, and it happens when no extraction is cached yet.
- A `PYTHONPATH` in that directory's `.env` reaches the plugin host's child process and runs a module from it.

With this PR, the manager and its host run code under `owner_home`. `home_path` stays the registries' key. For a home that isn't a link, both name the same directory.

A process keeps one manager per directory, so a linked profile renamed while it runs keeps the manager it was opened by. `owner_home` follows the rename, so a plugin host restarted after it runs under the new name and finds a marker set under that name.

Points to review:
- All ten `_plugin_home_scope` call sites move together, so one manager never binds two homes. The new tests catch the host binding and the per-plugin load scope. On the first head I reverted four of the other scope sites one at a time, and none of the new tests failed.
- `owner_home` is the name the profile was opened by, made absolute (`Path.absolute()`, links left unresolved). Left relative, a symbolic profile id resolved against the working directory of each later bind, which failed five gateway test files on this PR's first head (fixed in `4393d411b7`).
- `owner_home` is a property. When that name no longer leads to the manager's directory (the link was renamed or removed while the process kept the manager), it takes the other profile under the same `profiles/` dir that does: a live profile id, read lowercased as the marker lookup reads it, not `default`. A name also needs the process's remembered key for it (`hermes_home_key`, cached per path text) to agree, so a link repointed from another directory isn't bound to the old directory's key (`1c4e1984e0`). With none, it is the directory itself, which is what `main` binds (`ec62cbb8cb`, `60cfaa1f03`, `248ff26dea`, `2aba283105`).
- The plugin host reads `owner_home` once per start and takes its context, environment, working directory and launcher from that one value. The launcher is chosen in a fresh context bound to that home, so a crash restart and a caller bound elsewhere get the same one, and no caller's secrets are lent to it. Whether the home is the launch profile's is decided once per start (`_is_launch_home`, by the key the process remembered for its own path), and that answer drives the launcher's env layer and `.env` templates and the host child's env: the credential scrub, the launch-residue strip, the overlay's templates and the bootstrap tokens. So after the launch link is renamed the restarted host keeps the launch profile's service-only values, and after it is repointed at a secondary's directory that secondary's host gets none of them (main leaked them there). Every other profile expands its `${VAR}`s, `.env` templates included, through its own files, multiplexing or not; on `main` a restart read the launch profile's env for any profile. The launch profile reads the process env outside multiplexing, as before. Inside a launch-profile request (the TUI gateway, or the dashboard's stamped scope, both even single-profile) or under multiplexing, it reads the launch scope rebuilt from that home, under the request's task-local multiplexing; under multiplexing its `.env` templates resolve against the frozen launch env, peeled by the dotenv record frozen with it under the loader's lock, a name a secret source holds there never peeled. A managed-overlay launcher always expands against the process env, as `apply_managed_overlay` documents, whichever profile's scope the start binds; a run-elsewhere profile takes only that one, as #156725 specifies (`01b93a32c5`, `ab028cc238`, `7bb619bb8a`, `4450d0a128`, `d91acd10e8`, `18510dfbf2`, `00a06d8511`, `31e3d49d39`, `98afe23b63`, `95f4cf4417`, `faa2ff9277`, `f905ed0d51`, `ad700ae4d8`, `6509e6c1ce`, `caca72f6bb`, `14f5b04ad1`, `109d8ff1d5`, `535f068a4e`, `8a8a2dfa14`, `f1fc75a67f`, `626734b4e7`, `a6c62f3088`, `3a2bf61780`).
- Shared helpers gained opt-in parameters that only the plugin host passes: `build_profile_secret_scope(process_home=, template_env=)`, `launch_secret_scope(frozen_templates=, process_home=)`, `served_profile_child_env(own_profile=)` and `strip_launch_profile_env(routed=)`. The launch-env capture keeps the dotenv publication record (`env_loader.dotenv_publication_record`, `dotenv_lookup_from`), and its first capture holds the loader's publication lock (`dotenv_publication_lock`) before its own; `env_loader` documents that order. `host_launcher` reads a launcher the managed overlay sets first, in a context with no scope bound; the host start and the provider-extraction child both call it. Every other caller keeps its behaviour. Not part of this PR: whether every launch-profile body under multiplexing should resolve its `.env` templates against the frozen env, and which names a hosted provider's ambient-credential declaration may pull from the launch profile's service env under multiplexing (it reads the profile's files there, as on `main`).
- Discovery still records user plugins under `home_path`, so a plugin's path survives a rename. `_install_record` compares canonical paths, so installer records still match for a linked home (`b65a110095`, `3b0eb311d8`).
- A hosted model-provider proxy addresses its plugin by the profile home resolved plus the plugin's installed path below it. That survives a rename of the profile's link, and a plugin removed by deleting its own install link stays removed (`2c8046d88d`, `1aa867cbcb`). The one-shot provider extraction child gets the home as named, so code there finds the marker too (`4a55d8e18f`). The extraction reads the plugin through that same address, taken first, so a link repointed while it runs can't pair one installation's profiles with another directory's path (`53b7106218`).
- #156606 adds another `_plugin_home_scope(self._manager.home_path)` call site, in `plugins_capability_ctx.py`. Git merges it cleanly with this branch, but whichever of the two lands second should switch that call to `owner_home`.

## Related Issue

Refs #156725

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## How to Test

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_host.py tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_host_route_auth.py tests/agent/test_proactive_prune_checkpoint_gate.py tests/hermes_cli/test_secret_source_refresh_launch_scope.py
```

`test_plugin_host.py` has 34 new tests (54 cases with parameters). 35 cases fail on `main` (`fe9a4b58ec`) and pass here; the reload-race test among them fails on `main` only because the dotenv record it races doesn't exist there. The other 19 pass on `main` and cover regressions on this PR's earlier commits: a manager opened by a relative home (failed on `7a7d95ffa8`), a recall matched by the recorded repo (failed on `9e61d03cfc`), a hosted provider whose install link was removed (failed before `1aa867cbcb`), a hosted provider's address and extraction naming one installation (failed on `f1fc75a67f`), a profile link repointed at another directory (failed before `1c4e1984e0`), the launch row of the crash-restart test (failed on `ab028cc238`), a marked profile's managed launcher and a single-profile launcher (failed on `7bb619bb8a`), a secondary's managed launcher with no caller (failed on `535f068a4e`) and one that expands to nothing (failed on `626734b4e7`), a sibling profile served under task-local multiplexing (failed on `0d64a03a7b`), a host started inside the launch profile's bound scope (TUI row on `6d69a64015`, dashboard row on `7d05d35d4f`), a launch body under task-local multiplexing (missing name on `5dd81681db`, `.env` template on `f905ed0d51`), a launch `.env` template naming a key set later in the file (reloaded since the freeze on `bfb015ea06`; the single-load row guards the peel), and a secondary bound to itself after the launch link was repointed at its directory (on `7d05d35d4f` and `98afe23b63`). `test_secret_source_refresh_launch_scope.py` has two new tests: a launch `.env` template follows the frozen env through a source's rotation and removal (failed on `6509e6c1ce`), and keeps a source's value equal to what the `.env` once published (failed on `109d8ff1d5`). The four files pass on `3a2bf61780`.

Manual check:
1. Make `profiles/ops` a link to a directory outside the root, then mark `ops` (`mark_profile_run_elsewhere("ops", "<plugin>")`).
2. In that directory's `config.yaml`, set `plugins.isolation: host`, `plugins.host.launcher: [<stand-in>]`, and a model-provider plugin as `model.provider`.
3. Empty its `cache/`, then run `hermes -p ops tools list`.

On `main` the stand-in runs once; here it runs 0 times. Unmarked, it runs twice on both.

I tested on Linux arm64. The manual check ran with real `hermes -p ops` processes on `main` and on `7a7d95ffa8`, and later heads were checked by the tests. The first commit's diff on #156725's last head passed 230 related test files there (4097 passed, 0 failed). On `3a2bf61780`, 215 related test files ran: 4219 passed, 36 skipped, and 1 failed (`test_update_secret_import_lock.py::test_complete_update_dispatch_does_not_import_cryptography`, which fails the same way on `main` in this environment). `scripts/check --only ruff,health` against `fe9a4b58ec` is clean. Windows and macOS were not run locally.

prs.title: fix(a2a): retain bounded terminal task history after restart
prs.body:
Withdrawn in favor of the existing discussion in #92494. That proposal already retains bounded terminal task history after restart. The current main branch still uses an in-memory task store. This alternative SQLite implementation has not been merged.

## What does this PR do?

A completed inbound A2A task currently disappears from `GetTask` when the adapter/Gateway restarts, although its conversation log may survive. Persist the existing bounded terminal-task history in a profile-owned SQLite database so callers can retrieve the original task/context IDs and result text after restart.

This is terminal-result durability only. It does not resume inference, persist an in-flight local Task, replay a `SendMessage`, or change forwarded-profile owner coordination. Existing access checks and the 500 terminal-record bound are preserved. No new dependencies, configuration keys or core/plugin imports.

## Related work and draft scope

This draft overlaps the terminal-result persistence portion of https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/92494 (current inspected head `9ffd2553263ecda4e57430778f42c028177cefeb`). That proposal also changes routing, fan-out and in-flight/delivery recovery. This is offered as a small standalone alternative for maintainer selection, using a single SQLite terminal history and no routing/lifecycle expansion; the two competing persistence implementations should not be landed together.

https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/134286 concerns forwarded-task identity/owner coordination. This change is scoped to the local terminal-result store and does not replace that lifecycle work. The broader #92494 proposal does include terminal durability; this draft does not claim that gap is absent from all open work.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Changes Made

- Capture the adapter's owning profile once; HTTP worker threads never resolve an ambient default home for task history.
- Commit terminal facts before changing observable terminal state or waking Task observers. SQLite errors are surfaced, without silent RAM fallback.
- Retain up to 500 records in `a2a/terminal_tasks.sqlite3`; preserve agent/tenant/peer metadata, exclude push callback settings and Futures.
- Document the private-backup/retention boundary and the unsupported in-flight restart window.

## How to Test

Run `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/plugins/test_a2a_task_restart.py tests/plugins/test_a2a_plugin.py` using the checkout's test interpreter.

1. The first regression loads the actual plugin through `PluginManager`/platform registration, sends a task over real local HTTP and obtains its terminal reply. A newly constructed adapter then reads the same Task over HTTP while the ambient profile differs. On the baseline the lookup returns task-not-found; with this change it retains ID, context, state and result, with one dispatch.
2. The second regression makes the SQLite destination unavailable. Completion must raise while the Task and observer remain nonterminal; after restoring storage, off-thread completion writes only the owning profile. Scope filtering, callback exclusion and bounded retention are also checked.

Validation on macOS arm64, rebased onto `9ffa7dff23726d8daa8b3e167b20a5fabc2e04ef`: **114 A2A tests passed**, and **all 15 `scripts/check` checks passed**, with zero code-health findings. The local test interpreter wrapper only sets `NO_PROXY=*` so macOS's system proxy does not intercept loopback fixture hosts; the normal hermetic test runner and network fence remain in use. HTTP tests use a deterministic handler, not a model: full Gateway/model and cross-platform qualification are not claimed.

## Checklist

- [x] Read the contributing guide and applicable instructions
- [x] Conventional commit; related change only
- [x] Searched existing open/merged A2A persistence and owner-recovery work
- [x] Added regressions and reproduced the original missing-task failure
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes on the rebased head
- [x] Targeted tests pass on macOS arm64
- [ ] Full repository test suite (targeted A2A suite only locally; broad CI remains separate)
- [x] Relevant documentation updated; no new config/tool schema
- [x] Considered cross-platform impact: stdlib SQLite/path APIs; Linux/Windows execution remains CI qualification

prs.title: feat: add K8s-style audit logging system
prs.body:
## Summary

Add comprehensive audit logging system with hash-chain tamper protection for hermes-agent.

- Four audit levels: `None`, `Metadata`, `Request`, `RequestResponse`
- First-match-wins policy rules (match by verb, resource, opType, channel)
- Async batched JSONL file backend with 500MB rotation and 180-day retention
- SHA256 hash chain for tamper detection
- Stage-based lifecycle: `RequestReceived` → `ResponseComplete`
- Opt-in: only activates when configured in `config.yaml`

## Motivation

Hermes-agent currently has no audit trail. Operations performed by the agent (especially mutating tools like docker, kubectl, etc.) are not logged in a structured, tamper-evident way. This is a compliance and security requirement for enterprise deployments.

## Design

The audit system is inspired by K8s audit logging patterns but adapted for hermes:

- **audit/events.py**: `AuditEvent` and `OperationContext` dataclasses
- **audit/levels.py**: Four audit levels
- **audit/policy.py**: `AuditPolicy` + `PolicyRule` with first-match evaluation
- **audit/engine.py**: `AuditEngine` central dispatch
- **audit/chain.py**: `AuditHashChain` SHA256 tamper protection
- **audit/backends/log_backend.py**: Async batched JSONL writer
- **audit/integration.py**: Helper functions for tool call and message auditing

## Example Audit Event

```json
{
  "ts": "2026-05-15T10:30:00.000+08:00",
  "stage": "RequestReceived",
  "stage_ts": "2026-05-15T10:30:00.000+08:00",
  "user": "wecom:zhangsan",
  "platform": "wecom",
  "channel": "ops-group",
  "sessionId": "a1b2c3d4",
  "verb": "execute",
  "resource": "docker",
  "opType": "Mutate",
  "source": "agent",
  "eventId": "uuid",
  "requestBody": "{\"command\":\"docker ps\"}",
  "prev_hash": "",
  "hash": "sha256(...)"
}
```

## Configuration

```yaml
audit:
  enabled: true
  policy:
    - level: RequestResponse
      verbs: [create, update, delete, exec, patch]
      operationTypes: [Mutate]
    - level: Metadata
      verbs: [get, list, watch]
  log:
    path: ~/.hermes/logs/audit/
    rotation:
      max_size_mb: 500
      backup_count: 10
  tamper_protection:
    enabled: true
```

## Test Plan

- [x] All audit modules import without errors
- [x] Python syntax check passes on all modified files
- [ ] Manual integration test with actual tool execution
- [ ] Verify hash chain integrity with `AuditHashChain.verify()`

## Notes

- No new dependencies (stdlib only: `hashlib`, `json`, `queue`, `threading`)
- Disabled by default — zero impact on existing deployments
- Integration hooks added to `model_tools.py` and `hermes_logging.py`

prs.title: fix(desktop): route browser actions through the focused conversation
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

**Draft pending exact-head upstream CI and interactive packaged-app acceptance.** Local scoped verification and independent review passed; this is not presented as a released or installed repair.

Fixes ordinary stacked Desktop chats being refused by `drive_preview` while preserving foreground-only, requester-owned browser control. A tab-strip `+` and the occupied-workspace new-session path create a hosted session tile; that tile can be focused while the route-driven primary session stays bound. The existing action guard compared only against that primary, so open/read worked but inventory/scroll/click were refused until sidebar reselection.

The browser action claim now follows the actual focused conversation with **tile precedence**, not `primary OR focused tile`. A renderer hosting an unfocused conversation declines its scoped `preview.act` request using the existing unanimous-decline protocol, instead of settling the first-response race with a refusal. Existing preview-tab/profile ownership remains derived from the **requesting** session, not the currently focused page.

## Related issue and prior work

Fixes #133421.

This overlaps #133448 by andrexibiza and draft #133437 by liuhao1024, and follows the earlier focused-chat work in closed #125582 by SmelterLabs. Credit belongs to those contributors for their investigations and alternative patches; these alternatives must be reconciled, not applied cumulatively.

Why another candidate: the published #133437 head retains primary OR tile permission and bypasses eligibility on replay. The published #133448 head `db2cae4d7b78d59b92ed6b6db857bf2c5400384d` corrects focus precedence/replay but still lets a hosted unfocused renderer answer a terminal refusal. Its body describes a later follow-up that is not at the published PR head. This candidate is implemented against current official main, narrowly addresses browser actions/read identity, and preserves current pane-based focus retention. It deliberately does **not** change tour/theme/terminal foreground policy.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Regression coverage

## Changes made

Only three renderer files change under `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event/`:

- `server-requests.ts`: focused-tile precedence, fail-closed unbound/dangling tiles, existing runtime/stored/same-row-lineage matching for browser tile identities, decline-based action claims, method-preserving replay revalidation, and focus recheck before deferred local execution.
- `server-requests-preview-focus.test.ts`: two behavior-invariant tests exercise the production dispatcher/layout/focus/ownership/navigation/reader modules. They cover browser-chrome focus retention, manually and agent-opened requester tabs, hidden-primary/background-tile declines, background reads, stored-tip rotation, sibling branches, unbound/dangling tiles, foreign-profile pins, replay, async focus revocation, and requester-owner popout payloads.
- `server-requests.test.ts`: synchronize the fixture's primary ref with its passed primary identity; retain the owned-page assertion after explicitly refocusing the primary. Existing tour policy assertion remains unchanged.

No backend, source/provenance mutation, settings, dependencies, tool/schema, account/auth, or installed-app changes.

## Root cause and safety boundaries

`use-message-stream/index.ts` passes the route-driven primary `activeSessionIdRef` to the dispatcher. Window hosting includes tiles, while the old `previewAct` foreground predicate only matched that primary. Browser opening follows focused routing, producing an open/read/act disagreement. Ordinary visually single chat tabs use the tile path; this is not limited to Bot Mode or split panes.

The repair preserves the primary ref for primary draft/resume freshness, but gives a genuinely focused bound tile exclusive action eligibility. Missing tile bindings do not inherit primary permission. Existing conversation matching avoids merging sibling branches merely because they share a root. Background reads keep their existing ability to read requester-owned tabs. A background host cannot beat the owner with a terminal action refusal. Focus is rechecked after lazy import or unanswered popout forwarding before local input.

## Reproduction

1. Keep an existing chat A loaded.
2. Open a new ordinary chat B via tab-strip `+` (or sidebar workspace new-session with A occupied), send a harmless prompt, and keep B focused.
3. Open a harmless public page in B's embedded browser; read it, then request element inventory/scroll.
4. Before the fix: the page reads but actions return `The in-app browser only takes actions in the session the user is looking at.` Closing/reselecting B from the sidebar can restore control.
5. Candidate contract: B can drive only B-owned tabs without reselection; A/background tiles decline. Browser chrome retains B as the content conversation. Reconnect and async dispatch reevaluate current authority.

## Verification

Published candidate: `6924a8159ba6faaee4d4d72cdc3e98bb63ea94f3`, rebased onto official main `e06df9c2eae6901f4c88f464e0ae6e753c0428b8`. Relevant production/focus-store code was unchanged between the original reproduction baseline and this rebase; the final 243-test run, full Desktop typecheck, scoped lint/format and root commit checks were rerun after rebase.

Verification executed locally:

| Check | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| New invariants with unmodified official baseline dispatcher | **2 failed**, expected focused-tile and deferred-local-entry assertions, exit 1 |
| Corrective regressions against the first candidate, then corrected candidate | **2 failed → 2 passed**, catching missing-cache sibling matching and non-browser replay scope |
| Final gateway-event, action engine, popout, ownership/focus/runtime-map, preview and new-session suite | **243 passed, 26 files**, exit 0 |
| Full Desktop `npm run typecheck` | Passed |
| Scoped ESLint, zero warnings | Passed |
| Scoped Prettier and `git diff --cached --check` | Passed |
| `python scripts/check --staged` | **12 checks, ok; 0 blocking/advisory health findings** |
| Added-line secret/eval/shell/pickle scan | No matches |
| Backend decline aggregation | **6 passed**: action/read × bystander-first, owner-first, unanimous-decline; isolated real aggregator with fixture requests/clients, not live transport |
| Full Desktop UI suite on published head | **10,874 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 1,240 test files**, exit 0; parsed JSON assertion results and verified unchanged published head |
| Independent exact-diff review | Accepted after correcting missing-cache sibling matching and preserving non-browser replay scope; reviewer independently reran 36 request tests |

| Installed Mac/Windows packaged-app acceptance | Not performed on the candidate |

These tests are renderer/jsdom integration tests with the popout transport boundary substituted. They are not an installed Electron/browser or authentication-flow claim. Local execution uses preinstalled workspace dependencies; exact upstream pinned CI remains separate. The Python 3.11 test interpreter available locally could not import the current Python 3.14-targeted full server fixture, and the Python 3.14 interpreter lacked pytest; no canonical backend-test pass is claimed from that attempted run. The six-case aggregation probe instead imports the stdlib-only settlement module in a fresh process.

## Limitations / non-goals

- No claim to fix the separate pointer-delivery witness error after successful navigation.
- No `full` flag forwarding or unrelated ref/typing fixes bundled here.
- Ongoing physical typing focus-cancellation and remote popout cancellation remain baseline limitations; the new check revokes permission **before deferred local execution**.
- Tour/theme/terminal eligibility remains unchanged.
- No automatic merge, maintainer review assignment, public deployment or replacement of the reporter's app.
- AI-assisted implementation and review; human-reported reproduction/workaround, tool-backed verification, and explicit evidence limits are separated.

| openrouter | newest OpenAI = `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` | `openai/gpt-6.2-astra`, `-astra-pro`, `-sol`, `-sol-pro` listed first in the OpenAI block |

The OpenRouter leg is **NOT_COVERED**: the local OpenRouter key is expired (HTTP 401), so it isn't proven. OpenRouter does list the slugs with tool support.

prs.title: fix(pm): forward UV_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS and UV_HTTP_RETRIES (#148262)
prs.body:
### What happens
On slow or high-latency links, running dependency updates can fail due to multiple large wheels being downloaded concurrently and hitting the HTTP timeout. Setting `UV_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS` (or `UV_HTTP_RETRIES`) had no effect because PM's environment isolation stripped all non-whitelisted `UV_*` variables.

### Root cause
In `pm/index_config.py`, `FORWARDED_UV_SETTINGS` whitelist only contained `UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT`, `UV_NATIVE_TLS`, `UV_INSECURE_HOST` alongside index URLs, omitting `UV_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS` and `UV_HTTP_RETRIES`. Because they were omitted, `_base_environment()` in `pm/environment.py` dropped them.

### Fix
Add `UV_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS` and `UV_HTTP_RETRIES` to `FORWARDED_UV_SETTINGS` so they are forwarded to `uv`. These are transport tuning knobs rather than index redirection knobs, so they carry no index redirect risks and survive `no_config` isolation.

Closes #148262

## What does this PR do?

Preserve explicit uv download concurrency and retry settings through PM's environment isolation. On slow links, `UV_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS` was silently stripped, preventing operators from reducing parallel wheel downloads. `UV_HTTP_RETRIES` was also dropped despite the existing transport-setting exception.

prs.title: feat(catalog): add new models to every provider's picker from the remote manifest
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Lets a model added on `main` show up in the model picker of an already installed release, for every built-in provider and not only OpenRouter and Nous Portal.

**The problem in plain terms.** Each provider's list of models is written into the code. When a provider ships a new model, someone adds it to the list on `main`, and people on the stable release still don't see it until the next release. GPT-6.2 is the recent example: it landed on `main`, and people on stable have to wait for the next release to pick it.

Hermes already has the fix for two providers. Every 20 minutes it downloads a small JSON file (`model-catalog.json`, published from `main` by the docs deploy) and reads the OpenRouter and Nous Portal lists from it. This PR puts the other providers' lists in that same file and teaches the picker to read them.

**How it behaves.**

- The manifest now carries one block per built-in provider row in `_PROVIDER_MODELS` (33 of them: `anthropic`, `openai-api`, `bedrock`, `gemini`, `opencode-zen`, ...).
- On the client the block only adds to the row the install ships: the ids the install doesn't have come first, in manifest order, then the shipped row exactly as it is. It doesn't reorder or respell a shipped id.
- It only adds. Nothing an install lists is removed, and a provider with no built-in row gets nothing from the manifest, so third-party provider plugins stay on their own lists, including a plugin whose name happens to match a published block.
- It only feeds places that *list* models: `/model` on every surface, `hermes model`, and the check for whether a typed id is known. An added id is accepted where that provider's merge rule, applied to the listing the validation just fetched, offers it, and not on a provider whose live listing stands alone.
- It does not feed anything that *chooses* a model. The default for a provider with no model set and the short aliases (`sonnet`, `opus`) read the built-in table. The `default` label is honoured on the OpenRouter and Nous blocks only. The Desktop onboarding recommendation chooses, in the requested profile, from the list the picker would have had without the manifest's rows. Provider detection for a bare name (`/model some-model`) treats an added row as something to offer, not as proof the current provider serves it. Detection leaves out the rows only the manifest supplied, and onboarding leaves out every row the manifest supplied, both from that cache record, so a discovery outage doesn't change where a name goes or what onboarding picks. `providers.<slug>.models` pins keep their place. A manifest edit cannot change what an unconfigured install runs, what it costs, or which provider a typed name lands on.
- These rows are read from the disk cache only. They never fetch on their own; the existing fetch points (`/model`, the gateway refresh, `hermes update`) keep the cache warm.

**Two things I was careful about.**

1. The manifest stays at `version: 1`. `_validate_manifest` rejects a higher version, so a bump would cut every existing install off from its OpenRouter and Nous updates. Old clients only look up the `openrouter` and `nous` blocks and ignore the rest.
2. An entry can carry `requires`. A build that doesn't satisfy it skips the entry. Once pickers follow `main`, a stable build could otherwise be shown a model whose request handling it doesn't have yet. Nothing sets the field in this PR; #157319 does. It has to be in the first release that reads these rows, because a release without the check can't be gated later.

I also made the in-process copy of the manifest a single `(path, mtime, manifest)` tuple that is replaced whole. It was three globals written one after another, and with these rows read from more places, two profiles served by one process could pair one profile's manifest with the other's path.

Not published on purpose: `openai-codex` (only the account's live Codex catalog may advertise a model, which is what 444a6b8644 and 864fd57c59 enforce), `xai` / `xai-oauth` (their rows come from the models.dev cache, so they differ per machine) and `moa` (a preset name). The reader ignores a block for any of these as well. On `openai` and `openai-api` it never takes `gpt-6-astra` from the manifest, because only the account's own listing may advertise it.

This is 1 of 4. The later PRs (#157318, #157319, #157320) use the same manifest and the same "only fills what the install doesn't have" rule for context windows and metadata, the id sets that gate request handling, and pricing. Each one works without the ones after it.

## Related Issue

Part of #157322 (1 of 4). The stack, in merge order:

1. #157316: picker lists for every provider (this PR)
2. #157318: context windows and metadata
3. #157319: the id sets that gate request handling
4. #157320: pricing

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/model_catalog.py`: adds `cached_manifest()` (in-process copy, else disk cache, never a fetch; `None` when `model_catalog.enabled` is false), `manifest_provider_models()`, `manifest_additions()` and `merge_remote_models()`. The in-process cache becomes one tuple. A cache file that can't be decoded is a cache miss.
- `hermes_cli/models.py`: the six places that build a provider's curated list (`curated_models_for_provider`, `_stepfun_catalog`, `_anthropic_catalog`, `_openai_catalog`, `merge_profile_catalog`, `_static_catalog`) merge the manifest rows in. `static_catalog()` itself is unchanged, which is what keeps defaults and aliases on the built-in table. `fetch_ai_gateway_models` adds the manifest's rows after the shipped pairs and caches only the gateway's live index. Each provider-model cache row records which ids the manifest supplied; a row the manifest stops listing, or a disabled catalog, is dropped on read (falling back to the shipped row if nothing is left), and a warm account listing survives a manifest change. The file is over the size cap and ends 4 lines shorter.
- `hermes_cli/model_switch_providers.py`: `_build_curated_lists` merges per row, and reads the Nous list first because that call is the one that refreshes the manifest.
- `hermes_cli/model_setup_flows.py`, `model_setup_flows_bedrock.py`: the `hermes model` flows list the merged rows. The "long enough to skip the live probe" cutoff counts the shipped row only.
- `hermes_cli/models_detect.py`: a match on an added row is confirmed against the provider's own list before it keeps a bare name on the current provider.
- `hermes_cli/models_validate.py`: an added id is accepted where that provider's picker lists it.
- `hermes_cli/web_routers/models.py`: the onboarding recommendation skips added rows.
- `hermes_cli/codex_models.py`: `model_requires_account_discovery()`, one predicate for ids only an account listing may advertise. The manifest reader and the picker cache both use it.
- `scripts/build_model_catalog.py`: publishes every built-in row, minus the exclusions it now shares with the reader.
- `website/static/api/model-catalog.json`: regenerated (35 KB, was 12 KB).
- `website/docs/reference/model-catalog.md`: documents the per-provider blocks, the merge rule and `requires`.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_model_catalog_provider_rows.py`: 31 tests (44 cases), one or two per behaviour. `tests/hermes_cli/test_provider_catalog_hooks.py`: one more, for a plugin's static row. `tests/hermes_cli/test_model_cache_swr.py`: two existing tests patched the globals the single cache slot replaced; they patch the slot now.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_model_catalog_provider_rows.py`: 44 pass. They seed a manifest into a temp `HERMES_HOME` cache and go through the real entry points (`provider_model_ids`, `cached_provider_model_ids`, `detect_provider_for_model`, `validate_requested_model`, the onboarding endpoint, the setup flow). Each covers a behaviour this PR adds or a regression found in review, and fails without the change; I dropped the ones that only pinned behaviour that already held.
2. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_model_catalog.py`: 30 pass, including the existing check that the committed manifest matches the builder's output.
3. Related suites: on earlier heads of this review I ran the test files that reference the changed code; every failing id also failed on `main` on Windows. I haven't rerun them for the latest head, only the files above.
4. `python scripts/check`: 21 of 22 pass. `shims` fails on `main` on Windows as well (`.gitattributes` line endings).
5. By hand: add an id to a row in `~/.hermes/cache/model_catalog.json` and open `/model`; the id leads that provider's list.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [ ] I've run `just test` on the tests for the code I changed, and they pass. I ran the 308 related files with `scripts/run_tests.sh` rather than the whole suite; see How to Test.
- [ ] `just check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs). All but `shims`, which fails on `main` on Windows too.
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11, Python 3.14

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A (no new keys)
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

Limits worth knowing:

- `hermes model` reads the cache but doesn't refresh it. A CLI-only install with a cold cache sees the built-in rows until `/model`, the gateway or `hermes update` has fetched the manifest once.
- Six providers (`zai`, `nvidia`, `moonshot`, `deepseek`, `opencode-zen`, `huggingface`) show their plugin's `fallback_models` while their live `/models` probe is unavailable. The manifest rows join when the probe answers. I left that path alone because the list is plugin-owned.
- The manifest never removes a row, so a retired id still leaves the picker with a release, as it does today.
- Each provider-model cache entry records, from the build that wrote it, which ids the manifest supplied (`manifest_rows`) and which of those the provider's own listing didn't report (`manifest_only`). Both come from the one build: no extra provider call, and nothing to disagree with. An entry written before the upgrade never held a manifest row and reads as having none.
- `deepseek`, `zai` and the other providers that serve their plugin's `fallback_models` offline get no added rows on the cold picker read either, so the first read and the offline lookup agree.
- Vercel AI Gateway lists an added id after its shipped rows, and only once the gateway's live catalog serves it (offline it falls back to shipped plus added).

Not tested: macOS and Linux, and a live Desktop or gateway session against the published manifest (it only exists once this merges).

prs.title: fix(doctor): accept sealed bundle CLI links and warn when ~/.local/bin is off PATH
prs.body:
## Infographic

![Doctor knows sealed bundles. Before: Check: flags wrong target; Repair: writes PM wrapper; PATH: silent when missing. After: Check: accepts bundle bin; Repair: symlinks bundle bin; PATH: warns with rc hint. Change: is_bundled_payload(), always check PATH.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94873305-0ad2-408b-b626-fc829aaad67e)

## What does this PR do?

On macOS `.app` and Linux AppImage desktop bundles, `hermes doctor` expected `~/.local/bin/hermes` to target `<payload>/hermes-agent/hermes` instead of the bundle's own `<payload>/bin/<cli>` trampoline that `cli-provision.ts` links, so every run warned `points to wrong target` and exited non-zero. In addition, `hermes doctor --fix` staged a source-style PM wrapper instead of symlinking the bundle trampoline, and `doctor` only warned about `~/.local/bin` missing from `PATH` when `--fix` created a missing link.

Now `hermes doctor` recognizes sealed bundles, validates and repairs their `<payload>/bin/<cli>` symlinks (including channel-qualified names like `hermes-canary` and Linux AppImage stable payload copies), and checks whether a new terminal would have `~/.local/bin` on `PATH` even when the link is already valid. Desktop-side macOS PATH provisioning UI is intentionally deferred to a separate follow-up PR so `#149774` can land cleanly on its own.

Points to review:
- Sealed-bundle branching uses `hermes_cli.steward.is_bundled_payload(PROJECT_ROOT)` (never a filesystem probe), resolving the expected launcher from `manifest.json` (`pm.environments.payload_command_dir`/`cli_command_name`), then `install-stamp.json` `runtime.commands.hermes` (contained under the payload root), then `<payload>/bin/hermes`.
- `--fix` creates a missing link with a plain `symlink_to` and leaves alone anything another installer publishes meanwhile. It replaces only dangling `agent-payload/bin/<cli>` or superseded sibling AppImage links, with a staged swap, matching `apps/desktop/electron/cli-provision.ts` and leaving live foreign symlinks and non-symlink files untouched.
- The `PATH` check judges the PATH doctor inherited, not the one startup leads with the bundle's own bin dirs and the tool store. The first step that writes PATH (`pm.environments.activate_dependencies()`, `pm.install.activate()`, or a `PATH` line in the Hermes `.env`, which a new terminal never reads) keeps the PATH it found in process memory, and `inherited_path()` returns it (no env var, one reader). The check accepts trailing slashes or another `PATH` entry resolving to the same launcher (looked up through `hermes_platform`'s `locate_command`), and prints a non-failing info note when a shell rc file the new terminal reads already puts `~/.local/bin` on `PATH`: it reads each PATH setter's own value with the shell's quoting, counts the setter only as a command of its own (not `PATH=x cmd`, `env PATH=…` or `echo export PATH=…`), and compares whole entries with the directory, and takes a `~` already in `PATH` literally, as `sh` does (preserving Linux PM E2E runs before shell reload). It honors `ZDOTDIR` (compatible with `#154769`) and fish's `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. For bash it trusts only the first readable login file bash reads plus `~/.bashrc`, and names both in its advice.
- Merge order: open PR `#127118` touches the old PATH hint line in `hermes_cli/doctor_platform.py`, and `#154294` rewrites the same `if prefix:` block in `activate_dependencies`. Whichever lands second keeps `remember_inherited_path()` ahead of the PATH write.

The commit messages carry the detail, including the review fixes.

## Related Issue

Fixes #149774

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How to Test

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_doctor_command_install.py tests/hermes_cli/test_doctor_exit_status.py --file-retries 0
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/test_managed_runtime_resolution.py tests/pm/test_startup_activation.py --file-retries 0
```

Manual check on a desktop bundle: run `~/.local/bin/hermes doctor` from a terminal with `~/.local/bin` on `PATH` (passes with no wrong-target warning) and from a terminal without `~/.local/bin` on `PATH` and without a `~/.zprofile` entry (accepts the symlink and warns with the `~/.zprofile` export hint).

Tested on Linux arm64 at `3ddd1ee002`: `test_doctor_command_install.py` 94 passed, `test_doctor_exit_status.py` 7 passed, `test_managed_runtime_resolution.py` 8 passed, `tests/pm/test_startup_activation.py` 7 passed. The 156 test files that reference `doctor_platform`, `activate_dependencies`, `inherited_path`, `env_loader` or `load_hermes_dotenv`: 2,641 passed, 1 failed, 76 skipped. The one failure, `tests/pm/test_cold_runtime_e2e.py::…[python3.11]`, fails the same way on `e728e6f9ce` without the `pm` change: this host has a uv `python3.11` in `~/.local/bin`. On this host `tests/hermes_cli/test_doctor_pm_store_probe.py` errors in its fixture (8, home-I/O guard) the same way before and after these changes; CI runs it green. `test_path_check_judges_the_path_doctor_inherited` runs real `activate_dependencies()`, the tool-store reorder and doctor in one child process. 83 rc lines run in bash, with a child `sh` looking up a command in `~/.local/bin`, agree with doctor's verdict. `scripts/check --only ruff,health` passes, and the head merges cleanly into `origin/main` (`c1e19ca2ed`). Not run: a physical macOS host or a real bundle (the bundle layout is a test fixture), and Python 3.11/3.12 (the symlink-loop case is emulated in its test).

prs.title: plugin-catalog: bump traceverse_hermes_otel to 2.2.1
prs.body:
## What this changes

Re-pins the owner-submitted community entry `traceverse_hermes_otel` ([Mandark-droid/hermes-otel-plugin](https://github.com/Mandark-droid/hermes-otel-plugin)) from `084c773` (v2.1.0) to `735fd3d` ([v2.2.1](https://github.com/Mandark-droid/hermes-otel-plugin/releases/tag/v2.2.1)), bumps `version` to `2.2.1`, re-pins the two screenshot URLs to the new commit, and adds the two new resource attributes to the description's disclosure. Hooks, tools and middleware are unchanged.

## Commit range to review (`084c773..735fd3d`)

- `cb62d10` feat: stamp `hermes.gateway.platform` and `hermes.bot.profile` on the OpenTelemetry resource of every span and log record of a run (v2.2.0). `hermes.gateway.platform` is the messaging platform the gateway is serving the turn on (`slack`, `telegram`, ...), and `hermes.bot.profile` is the Hermes profile name. Both are names, never message content, so they are sent whether or not content capture is on.
- `9911c75` fix: only a human chat channel sets `hermes.gateway.platform`. A turn on one of Hermes' non-messaging surfaces (`local`, `api_server`, `webhook`, `desktop`, `tui`, `cli`, ...) carries no platform.
- `735fd3d` fix: `pyproject.toml` no longer declares `[build-system]` (v2.2.1). Hermes builds one uv workspace for every profile's plugins and keeps a buildable member's declared name, so the plugin enabled in two profiles failed `uv lock` ("Two workspace members are both named `hermes-otel-plugin`") and was disabled in every profile. A member without a build system is renamed per profile. `pip install git+…` and `python -m build` still work through setuptools' PEP 517 fallback, and the wheel keeps the `hermes_agent.plugins` entry point.

## Rule 9 warning (read-only imports)

`hermes plugins validate` passes, with one warning: two read-only imports of undocumented core names, used to read the platform and profile of the current run.

- `gateway.session_context.NON_MESSAGING_SESSION_SURFACES` (`identity.py:44`), to leave non-chat surfaces unmarked. If it moves, the plugin falls back to a copy of the v0.23 set.
- `hermes_cli.profiles.get_active_profile_name` (`identity.py:84`), used when `HERMES_SESSION_PROFILE` is not bound. If it moves, the attribute is omitted.

Neither is overridden, wrapped or written, and each call is wrapped so a missing name changes nothing else. If there is a documented way for a plugin to read the active profile name and whether the current turn came from a messaging platform, I will switch to it, or open an issue for that seam if you prefer.

## Surfaces and disclosures

Otherwise unchanged from the existing entry: hooks only (no tools, middleware or core overrides), no credentials or required environment variables, no self-updater. Telemetry goes only to the user-configured OTLP endpoint, and prompt, response and tool content is sent only when `HERMES_OTEL_CAPTURE_CONTENT=true`. Python dependencies are unchanged.

## Validation

- At `735fd3d`: the entry parses cleanly with `scripts/ci/catalog_entry_fields.py`, and `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` passes on a fresh clone at the pinned commit (manifest, declared hooks match registrations, security scan and no-core-override all pass; the rule 9 warning above).
- Hermes v0.23.2: `hermes --profile <name> plugins install Mandark-droid/hermes-otel-plugin --ref 735fd3d… --enable` installs and enables the plugin in two named profiles while it is also enabled in the default profile. The same command at 2.2.0 failed `uv lock` with the duplicate-member error.
- Plugin test suite: 70 tests pass.

prs.title: fix(version): bound the startup git probes against orphaned descendants (#144964)
prs.body:
## What

`hermes_cli/version_info.py` had two git probes that treated `subprocess.run(..., timeout=3)` as a bound:

- `_run_git` (`rev-parse`, `branch`, `log`, `tag`, `rev-list`, `describe`, `show`)
- the `dirty` probe (`git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain -uno`) inside `_git_version_info`

On Windows that timeout bounds only the reader-thread `join`. CPython's own branch says so (`Lib/subprocess.py`, `except TimeoutExpired`):

```python
process.kill()
if _mswindows:
    # Windows accumulates the output in a single blocking read() call run on child
    # threads, with the timeout being done in a join() on those threads. communicate()
    # _after_ kill() is required to collect that and add it to the exception.
    exc.stdout, exc.stderr = process.communicate()
```

So the post-kill `communicate()` is unbounded. When the killed child is a launcher whose descendant inherited duplicates of the captured pipe handles (the bundled two-level `git.exe`, or a lazily-fetching `git status` child), EOF never arrives and the probe never returns — the stack in #144964 (`_stamp_version_info → _run_git → subprocess.run → communicate → join`, with orphaned `git.exe rev-parse HEAD` left behind) is exactly this.

Both probes now go through `hermes_cli._subprocess_compat.bounded_probe_run`, the helper this repo already built for this class (`kill_process_tree` names it; `bounded_git_probe`/`bounded_probe_run` are used by the shell-hook, LSP, checkpoint, gateway and coding-context probes — #68609, #66037, #73403, #87134). No new helper, no change to `_subprocess_compat.py`, and the fail-open-to-`None` / `dirty = False` contracts are preserved.

## Reproduction (real function, not a re-implementation)

`_run_git` imported from the pinned worktree, driven against a native launcher shim whose descendant sleeps while holding the captured pipes (`git.exe` = a copy of the git install's own `usr/bin/bash.exe`, which execs the cwd script named by `argv[1]`; the in-suite shim now uses `cmd.exe` instead — see [Follow-up](#follow-up-regression-coverage--community-contributions) — and the numbers below are left as the original run):

| arm | descendant | `timeout=` | measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| before (`subprocess.run`) | 40 s | 3 s | **40.14 s**, survivor `sleep.exe` alive at t+4.5 s |
| after (`bounded_probe_run`) | 40 s | 3 s | **3.36 s**, zero survivors |
| control: real git, before | — | 3 s | 0.03 s, correct sha |
| control: shim that exits immediately | — | 3 s | 0.10 s (proves the shim is the git that runs) |

The status probe measured the same way: **25.1 s → 3.4 s**.

Pytest-level, same test file, only `version_info.py` differing:

```
RED   _run_git took 12.1s with timeout=3: the descendant that outlived the kill held the
      captured pipes, so run()'s post-timeout communicate() blocked
      2 failed, 2 passed
GREEN 4 passed, 1 skipped
```

Rejected alternative, for the record: plain `Popen` + `kill_and_drain`/`taskkill /T` on timeout returned bounded (4.24 s) but **leaked** the descendant — `taskkill /T` walks live parent pids and an `exec`ed MSYS child has a dead parent (#73403). The job-object containment is what makes "no orphan" true, so reuse was preferred over a new seam.

## Behaviour parity

Pristine vs patched, same fixture directories, 5 cases (`tagged_clean`, `tagless_clean`, `tagless_dirty` incl. untracked, `not_a_repo`, `missing_dir`): **zero differences** in `base_version`, `display_version`, `distance`, `commit`, `branch`, `source`, `dirty`, `commit_date`, and in `_run_git`'s values/`None`s. `hermes_user_agent()` unchanged (`hermes-cli/0.22.5`). A status probe that times out still reads as not-dirty.

## Cost

Fresh interpreter per sample, `get_version_info()` = 6 git probes, both trees clean:

| run | before | after | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| cold FS cache | 0.4945 s | 0.6213 s | +126.8 ms |
| warm ×3 | 0.3757–0.3782 s | 0.5097–0.5169 s | +134.0 / +138.7 / +138.7 ms |

Across six probes, those end-to-end deltas correspond to approximately **+21–23 ms per probe** (including the surrounding call overhead). A later isolated `_run_git` benchmark measured **+12.8 ms per probe** under different conditions, reported below. The additional job-object and `CREATE_SUSPENDED`/resume overhead is incurred on live-Git version lookups. If that is not acceptable, a lighter seam is possible — spawn as today and assign the already-running child to the job object so only the timeout path pays — but it needs new code in `_subprocess_compat.py`, deliberately out of scope here.

## Tests

`tests/hermes_cli/test_version_info_bounded_git.py` (5 tests): the PATH-shim control, the `_run_git` bound + no-surviving-descendant assertion, the status-probe routing/contract pin (exact argv + `timeout=3`, timeout ⇒ not dirty, healthy dirty ⇒ dirty), a `platforms("linux", "macos")` twin for the status bound via an `sh` shim, and a normal-path identity contract test. On Windows the launcher shim is a copy of `cmd.exe` plus a `rev-parse.cmd` batch; it was originally a copy of the git install's MSYS `usr/bin/bash.exe`, which cannot be read when the git on `PATH` is the Hermes-bundled one (see the follow-up section).

Original local run (Windows 11, Python 3.13.13, git 2.53.0.windows.3, bash-equivalent shim): new file **4 passed / 1 skipped**; `test_version_info.py` + `test_bounded_probe_run.py` + new file **27 passed / 3 skipped**; related suite (`test_version_info`, `test_bounded_probe_run`, `test_banner`, `test_version_command`, `test_update_version_report`, `test_dump_git_commit`, `test_managed_runtime_resolution`, `agent/test_codex_cloudflare_headers`, `agent/test_provider_attribution_headers`) **63 passed / 2 skipped**; `ruff check --config ./ruff.pre-commit.toml` clean.

`tests/hermes_cli/test_version_info_stdin_isolation.py` (1 test) is @kvnloo's stdin-isolation regression, integrated with original authorship; current cross-platform results below.

## POSIX

`bounded_probe_run` takes `process_group=0` on POSIX (Python ≥ 3.11; repo pins `>=3.11,<3.15`) and kills the group only when `pgid == pid`, then drains bounded. At the time of the original patch the `sh` shim used by the POSIX-only test was validated through MSYS bash here (delegates for `rev-parse`, blocks for the status argv), but the POSIX tree-kill path itself was **not executed** on a Linux/macOS host, and that was flagged as a verification gap rather than claimed green. Incidentally, `subprocess.run(timeout=5)` against that launcher/`sleep` tree in the same harness only returned after **12.1 s**, i.e. the same pathology exists on POSIX when a descendant holds the pipes.

**Update:** the POSIX tree-kill path has since been executed on native Linux (Debian containers, git 2.47.3, Python 3.11.18 and 3.13.18). The `platforms("linux", "macos")` status-bound twin ran and passed in both, with 31 passed / 0 skipped per run. macOS remains unexecuted.

### Independent Windows evidence: request-path version resolution (#154336)

- [@Galden62](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/145055#issuecomment-7115109205) reported eight matching watchdog dumps across v0.23.0 and v0.23.1. The first Nous request was still being built: `build_extra_body` → Portal tags → `get_version_info()` → the Git-source stamp's `rev-parse HEAD` → Windows' post-kill `communicate()` / reader-thread join. OpenCode Zen/Go reaches the same probe via `LazyHeaders` → `hermes_user_agent()` on the first header read, which can occur during client construction before a turn watchdog starts. In that comparison, profiles resolving version metadata were the affected lanes; switching static vs OAuth keys did not change the result. The earlier pre-watchdog signature is consistent with lazy header resolution, not independently proven by a matching stack.
- [@IuriiKotov48](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/145055#issuecomment-7097198188) confirmed that OpenCode Go took the live `rev-parse` path. In a separate Windows A/B, the real `_run_git` with a `cmd.exe` launcher and a pipe-holding descendant returned `None` in **40.34 s on main `249dc60308a1` vs 3.81 s with the two PR hunks applied**, with no surviving shim descendant on the patched arm. A profiler captured the same post-kill join on the unpatched arm. Shallow fetches failed, so the patched arm was **not** a checkout of the exact PR head. With real Git and the tested managed-worker spawn flags, both arms completed the version-resolution path in **0.13–0.40 s**: no natural stall reproduced and no end-to-end worker run was completed. No orphaned `git.exe` was observed in that A/B.
- [@Tvolex](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/145055#issuecomment-6965404786) separately reported the same Nous request-build stack in 16/16 watchdog dumps on Windows 11 / Python 3.14.9 with bundled Git 2.56.1, and reported that the wedge no longer reproduced after testing this branch on that host.

The fix covers both request paths at `_run_git`; there are no provider changes or worker-startup changes. This evidence supports bounding the pipe wait, not an explanation of what originally makes real Git stall. Moving version resolution out of request construction would be separate work.

### Follow-up: Regression Coverage & Community Contributions

The PR is rebased onto `fe9a4b58ec`. Both production hunks and the original authors and author dates were preserved.

| commit | author | scope |
|---|---|---|
| `27c0fca5c5` | @ranggaoscar | the bounded Git-probe fix (production) |
| `d5b34caedc` | @kvnloo | stdin-isolation regression test (test-only) |
| `310624ddc6` | @ranggaoscar | Windows test-launcher improvement (test-only) |
| `b5e1648cf2` | @ranggaoscar | Windows request-path regressions (test-only) |

**Kevin Rajan (@kvnloo)**

- Contributed the stdin isolation regression test.
- Original commit: https://github.com/kvnloo/hermes-agent/commit/f6e3083c3a6c28b4417aecfd1dab25aeafac2c63
- Integrated as `e595eb820f`, now `d5b34caedc` after rebasing, with original authorship preserved (`Author: Kevin Rajan <7121943+kvnloo@users.noreply.github.com>`).
- The test fails on pre-fix code and passes on the patched implementation: on the old tree all eight intercepted Git probe calls use `stdin=None` (`rev-parse --git-dir`, `rev-parse HEAD`, `branch --show-current`, `log -1 --format=%ct`, `--no-optional-locks status --porcelain -uno`, `tag`, `describe`, `rev-parse --short=7`), and on this branch they are all `DEVNULL`.
- Verifies that the Git identity probes and the dirty-status probe do not inherit managed-worker stdin — an invariant none of the original tests pinned, so a future change back to inherited stdin would otherwise leave the bound/no-orphan tests green.

**ranggaoscar**

- Implemented the original bounded Git-probe fix.
- Updated the Windows test launcher to use `cmd.exe`, avoiding dependence on bundled MSYS binaries: a Hermes-managed git lives under the real `HERMES_HOME` (`tools/git-*`), where `tests/home_io_guard.py` refuses every Python read by design, so probing for or copying that `bash.exe` either failed the fixture as a `TEST BUG` or skipped. The new shim copies `cmd.exe` (from `COMSPEC`) and ships a `rev-parse.cmd` batch in the shim directory already on `PATH`; `cmd.exe` runs the shim batch via `/c`, and the batch's blocking child (`ping`) inherits the captured stdout/stderr handles.
- Preserved the existing `home_io_guard` protection without weakening or bypassing it: no `allow_real_home_io` marker or additional fixture-level skip.
- The new local Windows-only regression covers a cold Git-source install stamp through both real provider consumers: the Nous request body and OpenCode Go's first lazy `User-Agent` read. It redirects only the `rev-parse HEAD` spawn into a real launcher with a 12-second pipe-holding descendant, and checks bounded return, no surviving descendant, the stamped tag/UA and cached identity. The test ceiling is 9 seconds on Windows to allow for tree cleanup and runner load; the production per-probe timeout remains 3 seconds. The existing POSIX test ceiling is unchanged. No API call, authentication path, or live worker is involved.

### Local validation of the rebased candidate

On native Windows 11, Python 3.14.9, Git for Windows 2.56.1, `scripts/run_tests.sh` ran 11 related test files: **87 passed, 3 platform skips, 0 failures**. Both new request-path cases passed, including the no-survivor checks. The same two cases on unpatched `fe9a4b58ec` **both failed as expected**, waiting about **12.2 s** for the synthetic descendant instead of returning within the 9-second test ceiling. Ruff and `scripts.code_health` passed (0 blocking / 0 advisory). The focused suite on Debian Linux (Python 3.13.18, Git 2.47.3) returned **31 passed, 2 Windows-only skips, 0 failures**; the POSIX status-probe case ran. These are local results, not hosted CI. macOS was not run.

### Historical cross-platform validation (before the rebase)

These are **local** runs on my machine and in Linux containers, not GitHub Actions results for the rebased candidate. The previous head `5122c5a303` had three GitHub Actions workflows marked `action_required`; that is not a CI pass or failure.

| Environment | Results |
|---|---|
| Windows 11, Python 3.13 | 28 passed, 3 skipped |
| Windows 11, Python 3.11 | 21 passed, 2 skipped |
| Linux, Python 3.13 | 31 passed, 0 skipped |
| Linux, Python 3.11 | 31 passed, 0 skipped |
| macOS | Not run |
| Ruff | Passed |
| Code-health | Passed |

- **Windows**: native Windows 11 host, Python 3.13.13 and 3.11.18, run twice — once with the Hermes-bundled git `2.53.0.windows.3` on `PATH` and once with Git for Windows `2.55.0.windows.3`. The 3 skips are platform-gated tests (`platforms("linux", "macos")` in the new file, the POSIX-only FIFO case in `test_version_info.py`, and `platforms(posix)` in `test_bounded_probe_run.py`).
- **Linux**: Debian containers, git `2.47.3`, Python 3.13.18 and 3.11.18. The POSIX process-group tests were **executed, not merely collected or skipped**: the `platforms("linux", "macos")` status-bound twin ran and passed in both runs.
- **macOS**: not run. Not claimed.
- **Lint / ratchet**: `ruff check` clean with both `./ruff.pre-commit.toml` and the repo config; `python -m scripts.code_health` reports 0 blocking and 0 advisory against `9b904dcc`.

Later measurement on this branch, with a conditions set distinct from the original harness above (Windows 11, Python 3.13.13, Git for Windows 2.55, shim = `cmd.exe` + `rev-parse.cmd`, descendant `ping -n 13`, so the block lasts 12 s): `_run_git` **12.14 s before → 3.47 s after**, and `_git_version_info` **24.32 s → 6.79 s**. Parity and probe cost were re-measured on the same fixtures: identical identity fields across all five cases, and `+12.8 ms` per probe (median 22.44 → 35.25 ms), measured using a narrower probe-level benchmark than the end-to-end `get_version_info()` runs above.

### Acknowledgments

- @kvnloo — contributed the stdin isolation regression test.
- @nareshh74 — independently reproduced and validated the timeout issue.
- @lkaiiu — supplied Windows diagnostics and the stdin/console inheritance analysis.
- @roelvde — supplied the related managed-worker Windows report (#152551).

The production implementation was contributed by @ranggaoscar. Independent reports, diagnostics, and the additional regression test are credited to their respective contributors; `e595eb820f` preserves @kvnloo's authorship.

## Notes

- Sibling seam: #141846 applies the same remedy to `tools/checkpoint_manager.py::_run_git`. Different module; this PR does not touch it. Happy to fold both onto one shared runner if you prefer.
- The `encoding=` / `errors=` behavior from #122265 is already on `main`; the bounded runner preserves UTF-8 decoding with replacement.
- This makes the probe bounded and non-leaking. It does **not** explain why git blocks inside the managed worker in the report — that part of #144964 remains open, and I am not claiming it as diagnosed.

prs.title: fix(skills): keep well-known identifiers resolvable outside /.well-known/skills
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`WellKnownSkillSource` records a skill as `well-known:<base>/<skill>`, and `_parse_identifier` reads that short form back only when the URL contains `/.well-known/skills/`. Search and install both accept an index at any path (`…/index.json`), so for an index anywhere else:

- search results carry identifiers that `install` can't parse, and
- a skill installed with the `…/index.json#<skill>` form is recorded in the short form, so `hermes skills check` reports it `unavailable` and `hermes skills update` can't refresh it.

`_wrap_identifier` now keeps the short form only where it parses back (under `BASE_PATH`), and records `well-known:<base>/index.json#<skill>` for any other index. That form already parses. Identifiers under `/.well-known/skills/` are unchanged, so existing lock entries there keep working.

Skills already installed from another path keep their old unparseable identifier until they're reinstalled. Repairing those would mean widening what `_parse_identifier` accepts, so I left it out of this fix.

## Related Issue

Fixes #159541

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `tools/skills_hub_sources.py`: `_wrap_identifier` becomes a classmethod and returns the index form outside `BASE_PATH`.
- `tests/tools/skills_hub_sources/test_well_known.py` (new): searches an index at `/.well-known/agent-skills/`, installs the result, then fetches again by the recorded identifier, as the update check does. It's in a new folder because `tests/tools/test_skills_hub.py` is over its file-size cap.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/tools/skills_hub_sources`: fails on `main`, passes with this change.
2. `pytest tests/tools/test_skills_hub*.py tests/tools/skills_hub_sources tests/hermes_cli/test_skills*.py`: 232 passed, 1 skipped.
3. `python scripts/check --staged`: 22 checks, ok.
4. Live, with no mocks: searching `https://taskaid.ai/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json` lists `well-known:…/index.json#taskaid` and `#getting-started`. Both install, and both fetch again by their recorded identifiers.

Tested on macOS (Darwin 27.2.0, arm64), Python 3.14.9.

prs.title: fix(bedrock): warn when a configured guardrail cannot be applied on the resolved route
prs.body:
## Problem

`bedrock.guardrail` reaches Bedrock two different ways:

| route | how the guardrail travels |
|---|---|
| `bedrock_converse` | `guardrailConfig` in the Converse body (`_build_bedrock_kwargs`) |
| `anthropic_messages` (Claude on Bedrock) | `X-Amzn-Bedrock-Guardrail*` InvokeModel headers — added in #107815 |
| `codex_responses` (Mantle, `openai.gpt-5.x`) | **nothing** |

`_resolve_bedrock_runtime` routes every `openai.gpt-5.x` model to the Mantle Responses
endpoint. Nothing on that path attaches a guardrail, so a user who sets `bedrock.guardrail`
in `config.yaml` and then selects a Mantle model runs **unguarded with no runtime signal at
all**. The only mitigation on `main` today is one sentence in
`website/docs/guides/aws-bedrock.md` (line 91), which a user who already configured the
guardrail has no reason to re-read.

Measured on `682a95258c` with `bedrock.guardrail` set, `us-east-2`:

```
openai.gpt-5.6-sol                         -> codex_responses      no guardrail attached
us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5               -> anthropic_messages   InvokeModel headers
us.meta.llama4-maverick-17b-instruct-v1:0  -> bedrock_converse     guardrailConfig
```

## Fix

`_resolve_bedrock_runtime` is the one place that knows both the configured guardrail and the
route it has just chosen, so the warning goes there, inside the Mantle branch. 12 lines.

- Converse and Claude routes: silent — they do enforce the guardrail.
- No guardrail configured: silent — nothing to warn about.

`logging.WARNING` so it lands in `~/.hermes/logs/errors.log` per AGENTS.md. If you would
rather surface it in the init banner next to the existing `" + Guardrails"` label in
`_init_bedrock_client`, that is a one-line change — say so and I will move it.

## Testing

`tests/hermes_cli/test_bedrock_guardrail_unenforced_route.py`, 4 tests:

```
4 passed in 0.44s
```

Negative control — revert only `hermes_cli/runtime_provider_backends.py` and keep the test:

```
1 failed, 3 passed in 0.49s
FAILED ...::test_mantle_route_with_guardrail_warns - AssertionError: []
```

The failure is the warning test; the three route assertions still hold on `main`, so the test
file is not just asserting its own new code.

Surrounding suites on this branch:

```
tests/agent/test_bedrock_integration.py
tests/agent/test_bedrock_guardrail_claude_route.py
tests/agent/test_bedrock_adapter.py          116 passed in 3.32s
```

`tests/hermes_cli/ -k 'runtime_provider or provider'` gives **24 failed, 1217 passed** both
with and without this change — I ran the same selection on clean `682a95258c` and diffed the
`FAILED` lines; the two sets are identical, so those failures are pre-existing on `main` and
unrelated.

## One observation, not changed here

`_resolve_bedrock_runtime` sets `runtime["guardrail_config"]` (line 217), but
`_runtime_agent_kwargs` in `gateway/run.py` is a fixed whitelist of ten keys that does not
include it, so the value is never read — gateway-created agents get their guardrail from
`bedrock_guardrail_config()` reading `config.yaml` directly instead. Harmless today, but the
key is dead. Left alone to keep this diff to one concern; happy to remove or wire it in a
separate PR if you want it.

## Context

Follow-up to #52179 / #107815. I searched open PRs and issues for `mantle guardrail`,
`guardrail warning bedrock`, `guardrail not applied`, `bedrock guardrail route`,
`guardrail_config runtime` and `_runtime_agent_kwargs` before writing this — no PR owns it.

prs.title: fix(mcp): clamp connect backoff exponent to avoid int-to-float overflow
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Clamps the exponent of the MCP connect-failure backoff before the float multiply, so a server that never connects cannot make the failure bookkeeping raise `OverflowError` and escape the discovery pass.

`min(30.0 * (2 ** (n - 1)), 600.0)` evaluates the product first; at `n >= 1025` the int to float conversion overflows. The patch computes `exponent = min(n - 1, 32)` first and keeps the same 600s ceiling. The ceiling is already reached at `n = 6`, so no real backoff changes: the clamp only removes the overflow.

## Related Issue

Fixes #159557

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `tools/mcp_tool_discovery.py`: `_record_connect_failure` clamps the exponent before the float multiply.
- `tests/tools/test_mcp_connect_backoff_overflow.py`: a 2000-failure streak stays capped at 600s, and the n=1..6 curve stays 30/60/120/240/480/600.

## How to Test

1. `pytest -q tests/tools/test_mcp_connect_backoff_overflow.py` -> 2 passed.
2. Pre-fix reproduction without the patch: `python -c "min(30.0 * (2 ** 1024), 600.0)"` raises `OverflowError: int too large to convert to float`; `n = 1024` still gives `600.0`. With the patch, a 2000-failure streak stays at 600s (covered by the new test).
3. Sibling suite unaffected: `pytest -q tests/tools/test_mcp_reconnect_retry_reset.py` passes. `tests/tools/test_mcp_startup_summary_names_failures.py::test_register_summary_names_failed_server_with_reason` fails on a clean checkout too (spawned-binary case), so it is not caused by this change.

## Checklist

- [x] Commit message follows Conventional Commits (`fix(mcp): ...`)
- [x] Tests added for the fixed behavior
- [x] No configuration or user-facing docs change required

Note: a full `pytest tests/` run is not claimed green here; the pre-existing failure above is unrelated.
