prs.title: fix(models): resolve a provider's implicit default from the account's live catalog, not a curated snapshot
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`get_default_model_for_provider()` — the resolver that answers "which model does a non-interactive run send when a provider is configured but no model was ever chosen?" — now resolves that default against the account's **known live catalog** before falling back to the hand-written curated seed row. A curated id that the account provably does not have can no longer become the default.

Behaviour change is deliberately narrow: cold cache ⇒ byte-identical to today. The only ids removed from consideration are ones the disk cache proves the account cannot call.

## Related Issue

No tracking issue — the full context is in this description. Happy to open one and re-link if you prefer the issue-first flow.

## The problem

`get_default_model_for_provider()` (`hermes_cli/models.py`) returns `static_catalog(provider)[0]` — the first entry of a **hand-written curated row**.

Curated rows rot, and this resolver is not a display path: it is what a non-interactive invocation actually sends. A seed that names a retired model turns "the provider is configured" into a guaranteed `HTTP 400 model_not_supported` that reads like an auth or quota failure, not a default-resolution bug.

### The case that surfaced it (GitHub Copilot, 2026-11-23)

The Copilot provider plugin (`hermes-labs-plugins`, provider `copilot`) carries:

```python
STATIC_MODELS = (
    "gpt-5.4", "gpt-5.4-mini", "gpt-5-mini", "gpt-5.3-codex", "gpt-5.2-codex", "gpt-4.1", "gpt-4o", "gpt-4o-mini",
    "claude-sonnet-4.6", "claude-sonnet-5", "claude-sonnet-4", "claude-sonnet-4.5", "claude-haiku-4.5",
    "gemini-3.1-pro-preview", "gemini-3-pro-preview", "gemini-3-flash-preview", "gemini-2.5-pro",
)
```

Verified against the live enterprise catalog (authenticated `GET https://api.githubcopilot.com/models`) the same day:

| | count |
|---|---|
| live chat models returned | 22 |
| curated ids still in the live catalog | **1** (`gpt-5.3-codex`) |
| curated ids retired upstream | **16** |
| `STATIC_MODELS[0]` (the non-interactive default) | `gpt-5.4` — **retired** |

So a home with `model.provider: copilot` and no `model.default` — the exact configuration the plugin's own setup flow leaves behind when the user picks a provider but not a model — resolved to `gpt-5.4` on every non-interactive run, months after GitHub removed it.

## How we came upon it

The investigation started from the opposite direction: we were updating the plugin's model list to include `gemini-4-neon`, assuming the curated tuple was the authoritative picker list. Two findings reframed it:

1. **The tuple is not the catalog.** Core already prefers live → disk-cached live → curated (`cached_provider_model_ids`, `_disk_serve_tier`: 1h fresh TTL, ≤7-day stale-while-revalidate, and `_live_result_entry` refusing to let a curated placeholder replace a real row). The picker shows whatever the API returns; `gemini-4-neon` was live the whole time. The tuple is a *cold-start seed*: first run before a token exists, plus this default resolver.
2. **Regenerating the tuple only fixes the symptom.** We patched the plugin's seed to the current 22 ids — and that is exactly the kind of fix that returns: a hand-maintained snapshot with no refresh path had already drifted a full generation and would drift again.

Tracing who consumes `static_catalog()` is what exposed the real defect. The precedence used by `cached_provider_model_ids` is already correct and carefully reasoned ("a curated fallback never replaces the account's real catalog for the same credentials"). `get_default_model_for_provider` bypasses that entire chain and reads the seed directly — including when the account's true catalog is sitting on disk one function away.

## The challenge

"Just use the cached catalog" is wrong in three ways, which is why this is not a one-line change:

1. **Order carries intent.** The curated rows are cost-ordered on purpose — the Copilot seed leads with a cheap model; `_SILENT_DEFAULT_PROVIDERS` + `get_preferred_silent_default_model` exist so curated snapshots can carry a preferred default. Taking the live catalog's own ordering would silently promote flagships: GitHub returns `claude-fable-5.1` first ($16 / $80 per 1M), and `test_openai_cost_safe_defaults.py` exists because an implicit default escalating the price budget is a real regression class in this codebase.
2. **The disk cache is not unconditionally this account's catalog.** A row can be (a) a curated placeholder written during an outage — flagged `fallback: true`, 60s TTL, deliberately short so it cannot masquerade as a catalog — or (b) a row for a previous credential. Rows are keyed by `fp`, the credential fingerprint, precisely because a rotated key must invalidate them.
3. **This resolver must stay side-effect free.** It is reached from non-interactive paths (bare `hermes -m`, gateway/preflight model checks). It must not perform egress, must not block on a fetch, and must not trip the no-egress invariants that `_RELAY_AWARE_CATALOG_FETCHERS` and the configured-relay degrade path protect.

## Solution

- New private helper `_cached_live_model_ids(provider)`: reads the same disk row `cached_provider_model_ids` serves, never fetches, rejects `fallback: true` rows and `fp` mismatches, and returns `[]` on any error (a missing/corrupt cache must not be able to change a default).
- `get_default_model_for_provider` now intersects the curated row with those live ids — **preserving curated order, so the cost-safety intent survives** — and falls back to the account's own ordering only when no curated id survives:
  - curated ∩ live non-empty → first surviving curated id (unchanged intent, dead ids skipped)
  - curated ∩ live empty → first live id (the seed had nothing usable)
  - no cache row → seed[0], exactly as today (cold start / `hermes auth add`, before any token exists)
- `_SILENT_DEFAULT_PROVIDERS` precedence is untouched: the preferred default is still honoured first, now against the filtered list.

## Why not simply delete the seed, or fetch live here

- `hermes auth add copilot` prints a model list **before a token is exchanged** — there is nothing to fetch, and an empty list would make the provider unselectable.
- A non-interactive run needs a concrete model *name*; `""` means the provider cannot be a default at all.
- Fetching from this function would put network I/O on paths that are deliberately offline (`hermes status` warms catalogs for every authed provider; relay-routed providers must never egress to the vendor host).

## Alternatives considered

| Alternative | Why not |
|---|---|
| Regenerate the plugin's curated tuple only | Fixes today's instance, not the class. The seed has no refresh path and already rotted a full model generation. Done in the plugin repo as a stopgap, tracked as a follow-up here. |
| Use the live catalog's ordering as the default | Silent cost escalation (see challenge 1). |
| Resolve inside the plugin | The defect is provider-agnostic: every provider with a curated row is affected, and a plugin cannot see another provider's row. |
| Generate the seed in CI from the live catalog | Complementary, not a substitute: it keeps the seed fresh but still leaves the default trusting a snapshot over the account's actual catalog. Follow-up in `hermes-labs-plugins`. |

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/models.py`
  - add `_cached_live_model_ids(provider)` (read-only disk-cache reader; filters placeholder rows and stale credential fingerprints)
  - `get_default_model_for_provider(provider)`: intersect the curated row with the live ids, preserving curated (cost) order, then fall back to the live ordering; cold-cache path unchanged
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_default_model_live_catalog.py` (new)
  - retired curated id is skipped in favour of the cheapest surviving curated id
  - curated order (cost intent) beats live order when both contain the id
  - cold cache ⇒ seed[0] (unchanged legacy behaviour)
  - `fallback: true` placeholder row is ignored
  - credential-fingerprint mismatch is ignored
  - no curated id survives ⇒ first live id
  - unreadable cache ⇒ seed[0] (never raises)

## How to Test

1. `just test tests/hermes_cli/test_default_model_live_catalog.py` (or `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_default_model_live_catalog.py`) — 8 new tests, all green locally.
2. `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_models.py tests/hermes_cli/test_model_catalog.py tests/hermes_cli/test_provider_catalog.py tests/hermes_cli/test_configured_builtin_models.py tests/hermes_cli/test_profile_model_seed.py tests/hermes_cli/test_models_catalog_late_plugin_provider.py tests/hermes_cli/test_model_cache_fallback_rows.py tests/hermes_cli/test_models_detect_live_catalog.py` — 141 passed on this branch.
3. `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_openai_cost_safe_defaults.py tests/hermes_cli/test_static_models_home_scope.py tests/hermes_cli/test_provider_catalog_hooks.py tests/hermes_cli/test_cached_fetch_api_models.py` — the neighbouring default/catalog suites, unchanged by design (cold cache in each fixture).
4. Real-world repro (Copilot, before/after): with a `provider_models_cache.json` row holding the live 22 ids and a seed whose `[0]` is dead, `get_default_model_for_provider("copilot")` returned the dead id before this change and returns the cheapest *live* id after it. `hermes -m <resolved> --provider copilot -z "ping"` succeeds.

## Screenshots / Logs

<details><summary>Live Copilot catalog vs the curated seed (2026-11-23)</summary>

```
live models: 22
  claude-fable-5.1 … gemini-4-neon … gpt-6.2-sol … grok-4.7 … mai-code-2
hardcoded STATIC_MODELS: 17
MISSING from static: [21 ids incl. gemini-4-neon, gpt-6-luna, claude-sonnet-5.5]
STALE in static (not live): [claude-haiku-4.5, claude-sonnet-4, claude-sonnet-4.5,
  claude-sonnet-4.6, claude-sonnet-5, gemini-2.5-pro, gemini-3-flash-preview,
  gemini-3-pro-preview, gemini-3.1-pro-preview, gpt-4.1, gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini,
  gpt-5-mini, gpt-5.2-codex, gpt-5.4, gpt-5.4-mini]
```

</details>

## Risk

**Low.** Read-only, exception-swallowing, no new I/O, no new dependency; cold-cache behaviour is identical to today. The only behavioural delta is that an id the account provably lacks is no longer eligible to be the default. Pure Python, no path or OS assumptions — it reuses the existing cache helpers, so Windows/macOS/Linux behave identically.

## Follow-ups (separate repos)

- `hermes-labs-plugins`: regenerate the `copilot` `STATIC_MODELS` seed from the live catalog in CI (diff-checked), and shrink it to a ~4-id seed rather than mirroring the catalog, so rot costs nothing.
- Optional: surface "default resolved from a stale seed" in `hermes status` when no live row exists.

---

prs.title: fix(scratch): the idle rule must hold for a process that never restarts
prs.body:
Fixes #148451.

Related to #134896 and #134907. #148451 reports the long-lived gateway case (§2); this PR also
covers recurring sweeps for every served profile (§3). #134896 includes a separate CLI bootstrap
path where the global once-per-process gate is spent on the first root. #134907 addresses that
bootstrap path; this PR does not replace it.

## Problem

Two independent defects in how idle-scratch retention is scheduled. They share a deployment — the
gateway, the process that never restarts.

**1. The gate is stamped before the hour is checked.** `_prune_scratch_dir_once` set
`_scratch_pruned_once = True` and only then asked whether the cross-process hour had elapsed. A
process whose first call landed *inside* that hour therefore spent its single per-process chance on
a pass that pruned nothing, and returned on every later call for the rest of its life.

**2. A per-process gate cannot serve a process that never restarts.** `get_scratch_dir(prune=True)`
is the only trigger, and it fires at most once per process. A fan-out of short-lived children
re-arms it constantly; a gateway that stays up for weeks does not.

## Fix

- **§1 — the order.** `_scratch_prune_due()` (one `stat`, fail-open on an unreadable stamp) and
  `_run_scratch_prune()` (stamp, then hand off) are extracted; the flag is set only once a pass is
  actually handed off.
- **§2 — a caller that outlives many hours.** `prune_scratch_dir_if_due()` is a public entry that
  re-asks the *stamp*, not the process age. The housekeeping chore calls it every tick; the check is
  one `stat` and the scan still goes to a detached child.
- **§3 — every served profile.** The chore is registered through `profile_scoped_chore`.
  `prune_scratch_dir_if_due()` resolves its root through `get_hermes_home()`, and the housekeeping
  thread carries no turn, so nothing binds a profile for it: registered bare, every tick sweeps the
  **launch** profile's scratch and no named profile ever gets a pass. This is the recurring
  gateway-side counterpart to #134896's named-profile problem; #134907 separately addresses
  the bootstrap-time per-root gate.
- **Facade growth.** `gateway/run.py` sits at its FILE_LINES cap, so the growth is offset in the same
  PR by moving an existing chore out: `_housekeeping_paste_sweep` becomes
  `housekeeping_paste_sweep` in `gateway/run_housekeeping_disk.py`, behaviour unchanged.

## Relation to existing PRs

**#134907** — per-root shape for the same guard. Complementary and touching the same function: it
gives each root its own ticket at bootstrap, this PR gives a long-lived process a recurring one.
It keeps `_scratch_pruned_roots.add(root)` ahead of the stamp check, so a root's ticket can still be
spent inside the hour — §1 is the same defect one level up. @foma-agent tested the two together on
this branch: the combined 11-file scratch/housekeeping slice is **68/68** with
`add(root)` moved after the due check, and the direct `profile, default, profile` probe passes.
Whichever lands second needs a rebase; the per-root shape should win where they overlap.

**#138954 (closed without merge on 2026-10-30)** — proposed re-sweeping scratch on the housekeeping
tick through `(60, "Scratch prune", ...)` calling `prune_scratch_dir()` directly. This PR instead
gates on the cross-process stamp (`_SCRATCH_PRUNE_INTERVAL_SECONDS`), runs per served profile,
and fixes the gate-order defect (§1). #138954 is no longer a competing open PR.

**#133280** — the checkpoint prune tick per served profile. **This PR does not touch the checkpoint
chore**; it stays exactly where it is so that line is not contended.

**#134896** — reports the named-profile axis. §3 is the recurring half of it; #134907 is the
bootstrap half.

## What this does not change

- `SCRATCH_MAX_IDLE_HOURS = 24` — the idle rule itself.
- `_SCRATCH_PRUNE_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 3600` — the cross-process floor.
- The detached child that performs the scan and the `rmtree`.
- `reap_processes_rooted_in` and the process-ownership check, including the registered-process
  ledger and the pre-delete revalidation.
- The checkpoint chore, the media-cache chores and every other housekeeping cadence.

## Observed

On a gateway that had been up 5.2 days: `.last_prune` was stamped 14 minutes before that process
started, so its first call fell inside the hour, the gate closed on a tick that pruned nothing, and
nothing swept again for the rest of the run — 108 entries, 18.4 MB. The size is incidental; the
mechanism is the point.

Independent evidence in #148451 (2026-11-03) shows the same once-per-process failure on four
macOS gateway hosts. Two accumulated 389 idle entries (~64 GB) and 296 (~18 GB), respectively,
with no later prune-log entries after startup. A follow-up from a multiplexed gateway serving
about 18 profiles shows that only the first served root is pruned after restart, reinforcing
why both the recurring trigger (§2) and profile-scoped traversal (§3) are needed.

## Effect on the reap (what #132401 settled and what it left open)

@teknium1's triage there states the 24h idle rule and the reap are the deliberate contract from
#118575, and that the real collision is the docs (#126419) — not the retention policy. This PR does
not change either. What it does change is *when* the reap can run: previously the gateway effectively
never reached it, so it now runs on the hourly cadence §2 establishes. Three properties keep that
safe, and all three are unchanged by this PR:

- `reap_processes_rooted_in` only considers processes whose **cwd** is under scratch.
- A process in the spawn ledger, or one owned by Hermes, is protected — and its entry is pulled from
  the deletion list.
- The pruner's own lineage is never killed.

The remaining `needs-decision` item in #132401 — telling a live worker from an orphan — is unaffected
here: this PR changes cadence, not the discrimination.

## Tests

`scripts/run_tests.sh` (per-file isolation), clean `HERMES_HOME`:

```
tests/test_scratch_dir.py                 34 passed, 2 failed
tests/test_scratch_prune_undeletable.py
tests/test_scratch_registered_clock_step.py
tests/test_scratch_scan_failures.py
tests/gateway/test_scratch_prune_housekeeping.py
tests/gateway/test_housekeeping_profile_scope.py
tests/gateway/test_checkpoint_prune_housekeeping.py
tests/gateway/test_cron_delivery_housekeeping.py
tests/gateway/test_memory_trim_housekeeping.py
tests/gateway/test_plugin_check_housekeeping.py
                                          31 passed, 0 failed  (9 files)
```

The two failures are pre-existing and environmental: `TestScratchDirPermissionPolicy` asserts `0o700`
and this host (uid 10000, container) produces `0o750`. They fail identically on unmodified
`19b7c7c24d`.

New coverage:

- `test_the_process_gate_keeps_its_chance_when_the_hour_is_not_up` — inside the hour nothing is spent
  and the later call still walks through. Fails on a build with the production change reverted, at
  the spawn assertion.
- `test_the_process_gate_still_holds_after_a_real_pass` — the gate still closes after a real pass, so
  a fan-out does not become a per-call scan.
- `test_a_long_lived_caller_re_asks_the_hour_not_the_process` — `prune_scratch_dir_if_due` prunes on
  the stamped hour even with the process gate long closed.
- `test_multiplexed_scratch_chore_reaches_every_served_profile` — two homes, one tick: the chore
  visits both, each resolving its own home. Red before §3.

`python scripts/check --base 0431192d69d4afd2443a7da15bb9e129a424414c`: **health ok, 5 files, 0
blocking, 0 advisory**. `ruff` in the same run reports one pre-existing FURB192 in
`tests/gateway/test_native_http_auth.py:230`, a file this PR does not touch — it comes from the local
ruff being newer than the pinned 0.15.22, not from this branch.

## Known limitations

- If handing the pass to the detached child raises, the attempt is suppressed and the stamp is
  already touched, so that hour is skipped. Pre-existing behaviour, unchanged here; a retry policy is
  a separate change.
- Behind a multiplexed gateway each profile's sweep is independently stamped, so one profile's
  unreadable store does not stop the next (`_for_each_served_profile` provides the per-profile
  boundary).

prs.title: feat(matrix): passive rooms ingest non-mention traffic as context
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `MATRIX_PASSIVE_ROOMS` (env) / `matrix.passive_rooms` (config.yaml) — parsed exactly like the sibling `MATRIX_FREE_RESPONSE_ROOMS`. In listed rooms, messages the mention gate would drop are persisted as **ambient context**: `observed: True` rows in the room's shared session transcript. No agent turn, no reply, no read receipt. A later @mention sees the room transcript — including cached media paths — as context-only observed context.

This is the Matrix port of the in-tree Telegram observe pattern (`TELEGRAM_OBSERVE_UNMENTIONED_GROUP_MESSAGES`). The core runner (`gateway/run.py`) already withholds observed rows from replayable history and prepends them API-only to the addressed message; this PR generalizes that marker to the platform-neutral `"observed group context"`.

Matrix rooms currently have two extremes and no middle: default mention-gating drops everything in between (a later mention has zero visibility into what was said or which files were posted), while free-response rooms trigger a full LLM turn on every message. Passive rooms are the middle mode: the transcript is ingested silently (media is downloaded/decrypted/cached at arrival under the existing `MATRIX_MAX_MEDIA_BYTES` cap) and the agent only acts when mentioned.

| Case | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Non-mention text in passive room | ambient row `[Name\|@user]\nbody` — no turn, no reply, no read receipt |
| Non-mention media | downloaded/cached (size-capped) → row with the cached path; oversize / non-MXC / failure → note row, never silent, never a turn |
| Unmentioned `m.notice` | ambient even with `MATRIX_PROCESS_NOTICES=false`; a *mentioned* notice still never gets a turn |
| @mention in passive room | full turn on the room-scoped shared source + observe prompt; admitted at the runner **only** via `MATRIX_GROUP_ALLOWED_CHATS` (new variable, mirrors `TELEGRAM_GROUP_ALLOWED_CHATS`) |
| Unauthorized sender (allowlist/pairing denies) | no ambient row, no media download, no session lookup — the guard fires before any I/O |
| Room in both passive + free lists | free-response wins byte-identically — no ambient rows ever (incl. notices and rejected media) |
| `MATRIX_REQUIRE_MENTION=false`, bot threads, commands, DMs, parked voice | unchanged — the source swap applies to passive-room **mention** turns only |

Security: passive rooms add a *context* channel, not an access channel. All upstream filters (room/user allowlists, pairing, bot/system/`m.notice`) still apply; ambient ingestion is gated by the gateway's user-level authorization **before** session lookup or media download; and passive-room mention turns (user-less shared source) are admitted at the runner only via the `MATRIX_GROUP_ALLOWED_CHATS` group-scoped grant — the same mechanism Telegram's observe-unmentioned mode uses. Deliberately out of scope: the startup access check and dashboard posture display still hardcode `TELEGRAM_GROUP_ALLOWED_CHATS` (pre-existing plugin-group-var pattern; generalizing it is a separate change).

Configuration — a room must be listed in **both** variables:

```yaml
# config.yaml
matrix:
  passive_rooms: "!room1:example.org, !room2:example.org"
  group_allowed_chats: "!room1:example.org, !room2:example.org"
# or the MATRIX_PASSIVE_ROOMS / MATRIX_GROUP_ALLOWED_CHATS env vars
```

Interactions with open PRs (none duplicates this one):
- **#63044** (Discord bounded room observation, open) — introduces a core platform-neutral `MessageDisposition.OBSERVE`; if it merges first, this PR rebases cleanly on it.
- **#101366** (Matrix mention-time backfill, open) — complementary alternative (fetch timeline at mention, no persistence, no media); both enabled = double context, no code coupling.
- **#148139** (`MATRIX_MENTION_STRICT`, open) — same adapter/mention path, rebase-friendly (strict mode narrows "mention", which only widens ambient ingestion).
- Context: #43445 (LINE), #145997 (Mattermost) — same per-platform port pattern; #147143 (merged, per-room `allow_silence`) — recent per-room-policy precedent.

## Related Issue

N/A — feature request (no tracking issue). Nearest related work: PR #101366 (alternative backfill design) and #63044 (core observe disposition), linked above.

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/matrix/adapter.py` — `_passive_rooms` parsing (via `_extra_csv_set`, identical to free rooms); ambient call sites at the mention-gate drop + the three media-rejection sites (all behind `_is_ambient_passive_room` for free-room precedence); `_resolve_message_context` 8-tuple (adds `is_mentioned`, `in_bot_thread`); `_YAML_BRIDGE` rows for `passive_rooms` + `group_allowed_chats`.
- `plugins/platforms/matrix/passive_rooms.py` (new) — `PassiveRoomObservationMixin`: `_observe_passive_room_message` (authorization check first), media-row builder, room-scoped shared source, observe prompt, mention-only attribution swap.
- `plugins/platforms/matrix/clock_skew.py` (new) — `ClockSkewMixin` (late-arrival grace pair extracted; adapter line-cap offset).
- `plugins/platforms/matrix/gateway_env.py` — AUTHZ `group_allowed_chats_env: MATRIX_GROUP_ALLOWED_CHATS`.
- `gateway/run.py`, `gateway/run_turn_runner.py` — observed-context marker generalized to `"observed group context"`, de-Telegram-ified header.
- `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py` — observe prompt wording → `"observed group context (Telegram)"` (keeps the marker substring).
- `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py`, `hermes_cli/config.py`, `hermes_cli/setup_hidden_env.py` — `passive_rooms` default, profile-isolable env var, hidden-setup-form suffix (exactly like `MATRIX_FREE_RESPONSE_ROOMS`).
- `plugins/platforms/matrix/plugin.yaml` — `optional_env` entry.
- Docs: `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/matrix.md` (Passive Rooms section) + `website/docs/reference/environment-variables.md` (rows for both new vars), EN + zh-Hans in sync.
- Tests: `tests/gateway/test_matrix_passive_rooms.py` (new, 26), `tests/plugins/platforms/matrix/test_passive_rooms_config.py` (new, 11), `tests/hermes_cli/test_setup_hidden_env.py` (suffix tests); updated 8-tuple/marker consumers in `tests/gateway/test_matrix.py`, `test_matrix_project_context_isolation.py`, `test_telegram_group_gating.py`, `test_telegram_mention_context.py`, `test_message_timestamps.py`.

## How to Test

Automated (green on this branch):

```bash
HERMES_PYTHON=$PWD/.venv/bin/python scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_matrix_passive_rooms.py \
  tests/plugins/platforms/matrix/ tests/gateway/test_matrix_mention.py tests/gateway/test_matrix.py \
  tests/gateway/test_matrix_project_context_isolation.py tests/gateway/test_telegram_group_gating.py \
  tests/gateway/test_telegram_mention_context.py tests/gateway/test_message_timestamps.py \
  tests/hermes_cli/test_setup_hidden_env.py
python scripts/check
```

Manual (live Matrix homeserver):

1. Set `MATRIX_PASSIVE_ROOMS=!room:example` **and** `MATRIX_GROUP_ALLOWED_CHATS=!room:example` (both required — mention turns ride the user-less shared source and are admitted only via the group grant).
2. Post a plain unmentioned message → the bot stays silent (no reply, no read receipt).
3. Post an image/file → still silent; the file is cached under the `MATRIX_MAX_MEDIA_BYTES` cap.
4. `@bot what was said in this room just now?` → it quotes the ambient messages; `@bot look at the file that was posted` → it reads the cached path from its context.
5. Negative: remove the room from `MATRIX_GROUP_ALLOWED_CHATS` → ambient rows still recorded, but mentions get no turn (by design).
6. Negative: list a room in both passive and free → free-response turns on every message, zero ambient rows.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.) — single `feat(matrix):` commit
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate — #63044/#101366/#148139 are related but distinct (see above)
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — via the repo runner `scripts/run_tests.sh` (per AGENTS.md, never bare pytest): focused selection **264 passed / 0 failed**; full `tests/gateway/` lane **13,341 passed** — the 3 remaining anomalies (1 flaky E2E, 2 heavy-E2E timeouts) reproduce identically on the pre-branch base commit and are environment artifacts, not branch-induced
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs) — 14 checks ok, health 0 blocking / 0 advisory

- [x] I've tested on my platform: Docker image built from this branch (Debian 13 trixie, x86_64) — in-image import + entrypoint smoke tests; live-room verification on the k3s deployment in progress

prs.title: Skills from a well-known index outside /.well-known/skills/ can be checked and updated again (#159541)
prs.body:
Installing a skill from a well-known index that isn't at `/.well-known/skills/` (for example the newer `/.well-known/agent-skills/` layout) worked, but afterwards `hermes skills check` always said the skill was `unavailable`, so `hermes skills update` could never refresh it. Now those skills check and update like any other, and skills you already installed work again without a reinstall.

## What changes

| Lock-file identifier | `skills check` on main | `skills check` on this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `well-known:https://taskaid.ai/.well-known/agent-skills/getting-started` (recorded by installing `…/agent-skills/index.json#getting-started`) | `unavailable` | `up_to_date` |
| `well-known:https://example.com/.well-known/skills/demo` | resolves | resolves (unchanged) |
| bare `https://example.com/foo/SKILL.md` | URL adapter | URL adapter (well-known still refuses it) |

- `tools/skills_hub_sources.py::WellKnownSkillSource._parse_identifier`: the `/.well-known/skills/` path requirement now applies only to bare URLs. An identifier carrying the `well-known:` prefix already names its adapter, and the prefixed short form is exactly what `_wrap_identifier` writes at install time.
- I fixed the read side rather than changing what install records (the issue's proposal), because the read-side fix also repairs every lock entry already on disk.
- `TestWellKnownSkillSource` moves to `tests/tools/test_skills_hub_well_known.py` so `test_skills_hub.py` stays under its line-count cap. It gains one invariant test: a fetch through an index at another path returns an identifier that fetches again. That test fails on main.

**Root cause:** install writes `well-known:<base>/<skill>`, and the parser rejected that form whenever `<base>` was not under `/.well-known/skills/`.

**Live repro:** I used a scratch `HERMES_HOME` against the real `https://taskaid.ai/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json`. I ran `hermes skills install "well-known:…/index.json#getting-started" --yes` and then `hermes skills check`. On main the check said `unavailable`. On this branch the same lock entry gives `up_to_date`, and `hermes skills update` says `No updates available.`

**Not covered:** the 0.2.0 index's per-skill `url` and `digest` fields are still ignored (files still resolve as `<base>/<name>/SKILL.md`). The reporter is filing that separately as a feature request.

Fixes #159541

prs.title: Add hermes-habitica
prs.body:
## Add `hermes-habitica`

**What it does:** Full-suite Habitica integration for Hermes Agent as eight agent tools:

1. **Character state** — `habitica_status` (level, class, HP, MP, XP, gold, gems, longest daily streaks) and `habitica_tasks` (list one task type with streaks, values, checklists; one type per request, matching the API).
2. **Task CRUD** — `habitica_task_create` (habits, dailies with frequency/everyX/repeat_days, todos, rewards with gold values, checklists, tag ids), `habitica_task_update` (partial), `habitica_task_delete`, plus `habitica_tags` for id lookup.
3. **Scoring** — `habitica_tick` (score up/down; returns streak, new stat totals, delta and drop notifications).
4. **Party** — `habitica_party` with actions: summary (party + quest state), chat_list, chat_post and chat_delete (own messages only).

**Hermes surfaces used:** `ctx.register_tool` (via `tools.py::register_tools` + `provides_tools` in the manifest), `config_schema`, `requires_env`. `kind: tools`; no hooks, no middleware, no platform adapter. `register()` and `tools.py::register_tools(ctx)` register the identical tool set and `ctx.register_tool` replaces by name, so both entry paths are idempotent and declared-tools match passes cleanly.

**Rule 13 disclosure** (also in the entry description and the README):
- Network: HTTPS calls to `https://habitica.com/api/v3` only, carrying the stored user ID and API token. No other endpoints, no telemetry. HTTP 429/503 retried up to three times with capped backoff (server `Retry-After` wins).
- Writes are real, irreversible state changes: scoring affects streaks, stats and gold with no undo; deleted tasks and chat messages cannot be restored; party chat posts are visible to party members. The `habitica_tick` tool description instructs the model to tick only when the user names the task or explicitly asks; `habitica_task_delete` and `chat_delete` state irreversibility in their descriptions.
- File reads/writes: none. No background processes, no state of its own.
- Credentials: read only through Hermes's scoped secret route (`agent.secret_scope.get_secret`). The plugin never reads `.env`, `os.environ` or any other credential store; a dedicated unit test proves environment values are ignored even when set.
- Inbound/approval surface: none. Tools act only when invoked by the agent in a session.
- Independent implementation of the public Habitica API v3; not affiliated with or endorsed by Habitica. No listed entry integrates Habitica at all (catalog checked 2026-11-19/20); the nearest entries are generic habit trackers with no Habitica API surface.

**Validation:** `hermes plugins validate --install-deps` at the pinned commit passes (manifest, loadable, capability probe, declared tools match, security scan safe, no core override). Unit tests (stdlib unittest, mocked transport, no live network) also pass: header construction, one-type-per-request with the plural type forms, credential route (env ignored), 429 backoff, chat body encoding, schema sanity.

**Repository:** https://github.com/Jessy-Boo/hermes-habitica pinned at `be3ff7797b11a53903519cdf4b707a18c2d8f27e`. README covers install, credentials (both from Habitica's Settings, Site, and Mobile Data page), config knobs, and the machine-impact section; `assets/hero.png` follows the catalog hero format.

prs.title: fix(providers): publish overlapping profile discoveries independently
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Two profiles can scan their provider plugins at the same time. Each scan saves and restores the same discovery flag. The order in which they finish can leave the flag set and skip the model picker and auth registry refresh, even though the plugin loaded in its own profile.

Use the existing context-local registration target to tell whether the caller is scanning a profile. The process-wide flag still covers bundled discovery. A home scan can finish and publish its own providers while another home is still loading.

## Related Issue

Fixes #159442. #156224 and #157976 cover empty staging publication when two scans target the same home. #118779 covers re-entry during a scan.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

Run `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/providers tests/hermes_cli/test_provider_catalog.py tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_registry_home_scope.py tests/hermes_cli/test_list_picker_providers.py -q`.

The regression controls two real plugin imports with thread events in a fresh interpreter. Both profiles load their providers on the original code, but the second provider is missing from the picker catalog. With the fix both providers appear. All 138 tests in the selected files and all 22 code checks passed on macOS.

prs.title: feat(gateway): add launchd_network_identity switch for direct macOS job identity
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a `gateway.launchd_network_identity` config switch (`osascript` | `direct`, default `osascript` — behavior unchanged) that lets a host choose the launchd job-root identity for the macOS gateway LaunchAgent.

Today `launchd_program_arguments()` always wraps `gateway run` in a JXA `/usr/bin/osascript` script, because macOS Local Network Privacy only exempts a platform-binary job root (#71206 — a bare venv Python dies with `EHOSTUNREACH` on LAN connects). But TCC responsibility-based attribution follows the same job root, so while osascript owns it:

- Calendar/EventKit probes return `notDetermined` from the gateway/cron domain (NorethSea's A/B/C in the issue: re-pointing `ProgramArguments[0]` at the real interpreter restores `fullAccess` on the same build),
- OneDrive File Provider access fails for the gateway context (mkravitz72 runs a locally patched direct-Python LaunchAgent to keep it working),
- Privacy & Security shows an unauditable generic `osascript` "Background App Activity" entry.

These two properties (Local Network exemption vs. TCC attribution) are mutually exclusive on the job-root identity, so the fix is a documented per-host switch, not a new default. `direct` makes the existing stderr-timestamp launcher chain the `ProgramArguments` itself:

- launchd signals the wrapper directly; its signal forwarders (SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP/SIGUSR1/SIGUSR2) already pass lifecycle signals to the gateway child,
- stdout/stderr keep landing in the same files (plist `StandardOutPath` + the wrapper's `--error-log` timestamped sink), so operator log tooling is unchanged,
- KeepAlive `SuccessfulExit` semantics are unchanged (the wrapper already exits with the child's code).

Because all plist regenerators (`gateway install`, `start` self-heal, `refresh_launchd_plist_if_needed`, and therefore `hermes update`) go through `generate_launchd_plist()` and read the config, a chosen `direct` identity now survives upgrades and service refreshes — replacing the hand-patched plists and watchdogs issue reporters currently maintain.

Two guard rails:

- `configured_launchd_identity()` fails safe: a missing key, unloadable config, or any value other than the exact string `direct` keeps the osascript identity, so a broken `config.yaml` cannot silently cost a host its Local Network grant.
- `gateway.status._gateway_command_subcommand()` now skips the direct wrapper's ps line (`hermes --run-module hermes_cli.stderr_timestamp … -- … gateway run`) the same way it skips the osascript wrapper: the job root is the supervisor-owned wrapper, and the gateway child is matched on its own command line. Without this, a stale-PID-file stop/status scan could match the wrapper as a second "gateway".

prs.title: File tools show log tails, list folders, say when a search found everything, and give execute_code cells ready-to-use results
prs.body:
Models kept sending file work to the shell because a few ordinary jobs had no file-tool equivalent: showing the end of a log, listing a folder with sizes, trusting that a search had found everything, and using read or search results inside a Python cell without reparsing them. The file tools now do those jobs themselves, so in a live 8-task test on the final heads the model took the right route 19 times out of 24 instead of 9, and it still used the shell for git and for running tests.

Outcome: on the final head (e54d5a9e) the stock tool list grows by **12 tokens** (7,913 → 7,925 on main 3371c03d, cl100k), and the consolidated final-head run (Final-head results) took Opus from 38% to 79% correct routing on t1..t8 with every answer correct. The earlier tables were measured on the commits named in each column.

## Results: main vs this PR (live, Opus 5.5 on Nous Portal)

Correct = the job went through a file tool, a parallel batch or `execute_code` with **no** terminal file op; for the two controls, correct = the job's own command (`git blame`/`log`, the test runner) went through terminal. Each column names the PR commit its runs used; every HEAD column is composed with #157517 + #157524, as in the eval harness. Source: each run's own `state.db`, scored by `score_route.py`.

| task | main | first head 5672c54 | 1101bef5 (extra reps) | 465fb78 (V6 as shipped) | 8b1e8db3 (final smoke) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| t1 compare 5 model files | 1/2 | 2/2 | – | 2/2 | – |
| t2 per-file count of a symbol | 0/2 | 0/2 | 1/2 | 1/2 | – |
| t3 last 40 lines of a log | 0/2 | 2/2 | – | 2/2 | – |
| t4 case-insensitive search | 0/2 | 0/2 | 0/2 | 2/2 | **2/2** |
| t5 3-before / 1-after context | 0/2 | 2/2 | 1/3 | 3/5 | – |
| t6 rename across 8 files | 0/2 | 0/2 | 0/2 | 0/2 | – |
| t7 top-5 orders from JSON | 1/2 | 2/2 | – | 2/2 | – |
| t8 list data/ with sizes | 0/2 | 0/2 | 0/2 | 2/4 | 1/4 |
| **non-control, reps 1–2** | **2/16 (13%)** | **8/16 (50%)** | – | **10/16 (63%)** | – |
| terminal file ops (non-control, reps 1–2) | 17 | 11 | – | 9 | – |
| CONTROL t9 git blame | 2/2 | 2/2 | 2/2 | 1/1 | – |
| CONTROL t10 run tests | 2/2 | 2/2 | 2/2 | 1/1 | – |
| answer correct | 20/20 | 20/20 | 15/15 | 23/23 | 6/6 |
| spend (estimated_cost_usd) | $1.04 | $0.88 | $1.00 | $1.41 | $0.33 |

- **main** = `origin/main` when the matrix ran; its stock `tools[]` is byte-identical to this PR's merge base b1db37d.
- **5672c54**: the first matrix ran at 12:02, before bb6909c and 1101bef existed; its tool code is identical to 5672c54 (the same commit before the rebase).
- **1101bef5**: extra HEAD reps on 1101bef5 + #157517 + #157524 (merge 2057a27), run as the HEAD leg of the V6 A/B.
- **465fb78**: the V6 tree, byte-identical to 465fb78 for the four changed tool files. (465fb78 + the rejected `patch` hint, 8 runs on t2/t4/t6/t8, is reported separately below.)
- **8b1e8db3**: final-head smoke, 8b1e8db3 + #157524's `(?i)` fix.
- gpt-6-astra, first head only, 1 run per task: 6/8 non-control, controls 2/2, 9/10 answers correct, $1.91.
- Total live spend across every run: **$8.13** (115 runs).

### Final-head results

One consolidated run on the code that would merge. MAIN = `origin/main` 3371c03d. FINAL = origin/main 3371c03d + #157534 9c0bc71a + #157517 512856b5 + #157524 b7ffacb8 + #157545 e54d5a9e, merged in that order. Opus 5.5 on Nous Portal: t1..t8 ×3 per leg, controls ×2 (FINAL t9 rep 1 is the harness smoke run, scored like the rest). gpt-6-astra: FINAL ×1 per task as a reference. Fresh `HERMES_HOME` per run, scored from each run's own `state.db`. Correct = no terminal file op AND right answer (controls: the git/test command went through terminal). Cells: correct (terminal file-op calls). Re-checks = grep/rg in terminal after a correct file-tool answer.

| task | MAIN Opus | FINAL Opus | re-checks MAIN → FINAL | FINAL gpt-6-astra |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| t5 3-before / 1-after context | 0/3 (6) | **2/3** (2) | 0 → 0 | yes (0) |
| t6 rename across 8 files | 0/3 (5) | **0/3** (4) | 6 → 7 | yes (0) |
| t7 top-5 orders from JSON | 3/3 (0) | **3/3** (0) | 0 → 0 | yes (0) |
| t8 list data/ with sizes | 0/3 (3) | **2/3** (1) | 0 → 0 | yes (0) |
| t9 CONTROL git blame | 2/2 (0) | **2/2** (0) | 0 → 0 | yes (0) |
| t10 CONTROL run tests | 2/2 (7) | **2/2** (8) | 0 → 0 | yes (0) |
| **t1..t8 correct route** | **9/24 (38%)** | **19/24 (79%)** | | 7/8 |
| terminal file ops per run (t1..t8) | 0.83 | 0.29 | | 0 |
| $ per run (t1..t8) | 0.067 | 0.041 | | 0.201 |
| answer correct (t1..t10) | 28/28 | 28/28 | | 9/10 |

- The two controls stayed on terminal on both legs (t9 2/2 → 2/2, t10 2/2 → 2/2).
- t2 is 3/3 on MAIN in this run (2/2 → 0/2 in the first matrix): main's own variance on that task is large; FINAL holds 3/3.
- Remaining terminal file ops on FINAL: t6 rename (4: a `sed -i` edit in every run plus one `grep` confirmation), t5 one run that used `grep -B3 -A1` (2), t8 one `ls -la data/` after a `read_file` (1).
- gpt-6-astra's one miss is t2: it counted with `search_files` + `execute_code` (correct route) but reported exact-name occurrences (`calc_total` in 10 files, 21 total), which the scorer's answer check rejects.
- FINAL includes #157517's terminal sentence and #157524's `(?i)` fix, so it measures the set.
- Tokens (stock `tools[]`, same method as below): main 3371c03d **7,913**; main + this PR alone **7,925 (+12)**; composed FINAL 7,928 (+15).
- Spend for this run: $8.18 (78 runs, all legs and models).

## What changed

| Gap (from real commands) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `tail -n 40 app.log` (4.3% of Opus terminal file commands, 2,353 in 7 days) | `read_file` rejected `offset < 1`. A tail took two calls (read once for `total_lines`, then read again) or `tail` in the terminal | `read_file(path, offset=-40)` returns the last 40 lines with their real line numbers (`2961|…`…`3000|…`). `limit` still bounds the page. If the log rotates or grows between the count and the read, the tool re-reads once; if it changes again during that retry, it returns "File changed during tail read; retry with the same negative offset." instead of a stale page. Works on extracted documents (pdf/docx/ipynb) too |
| `ls -la dir/` (`ls` is in 13% of those commands, `ls -l`/`stat`/`du` in 1.2%) | `read_file(dir)` returned an error: "not a regular file (directory…)" | `read_file(dir)` returns a listing: a header line, then `size  mtime  name` rows, folders first. Every entry carries its lstat size, folders included, as `ls -la` shows it. Inside a cell it also returns `entries: [{name, type, size, mtime}]`. Capped at 500 entries, with a pointer to `search_files(target='files')` |
| grep re-checks after a correct `search_files` | nothing told the model a search was whole, so Opus re-ran it with grep "to check hidden/gitignored files" | a first-page, untruncated model-side content search gets a `complete` line naming the requested scope and whether hidden/gitignored files hold more matches (see V6 below) |
| Cells parsing `read_file()['content']` (~100 cells in 14 days ran `l.split('\|',1)[1]` to drop the gutter) | content is always `N|line` | inside `execute_code` every successful read (empty files and extracted documents included) also has `text`, the same page without the `N|` prefixes |
| Cells reading `search_files()['matches']` / `['files']` | 5+ matches came back as a `matches_text` string, so `['matches']` raised `KeyError` (seen in production); a filename search with no hits had no `files` key | inside a cell, a content search always has `matches`, the list of `{path, line, content}` dicts (`[]` when nothing matched), and a filename search always has `files` (`[]` on a miss). The model's own calls keep the compact text block |
| Cells reading a big file | the 100K-char budget meant a `next_offset` loop even though nothing reaches the model unless the cell prints it | a cell's read skips the char budget. The line limit (`tool_output.max_lines`) still applies |

How it works: the cell-only behaviour keys on the existing `programmatic_file_read()` context, which `execute_code` already sets for both the kernel and the RPC dispatch. For the model's own calls, only the tail, the directory listing and the search `complete` line are new. The read helpers live in `tools/file_operations_common.py`, the existing leaf module for read/search helpers; the completeness probe is `hidden_match_counts` in `tools/file_operations_search.py`. `read_file_tool` stays under its complexity ratchet (`scripts/check --only health` ok on the final head).

Schema text, the only words changed:
- `read_file` description: "…with line numbers and pagination**, or list a directory**. Use this instead of cat/head/tail**/ls** in terminal." It also drops "Suggests similar filenames if not found. Use offset and limit for large files.", which said nothing the parameters don't already say.
- `read_file.offset`: drops `minimum: 1` and adds "; negative reads the last N lines".
- `execute_code` helper lines: `read_file` returns `{"content", "text" (no line numbers), "total_lines"}`, and `search_files`: `target="content"` returns `{"matches": [{"path", "line", "content"}]}`, `target="files"` returns `{"files": [path]}`.

- `read_file.path` (V6b, 465fb78): "File to read, or a directory to list with each entry's type and size (absolute, relative, or ~/path)".

**Token delta (final head e54d5a9e):** stock `tools[]` (all default toolsets, 18 tools), cl100k via tiktoken over `json.dumps(get_tool_definitions(quiet_mode=True), ensure_ascii=False)`, rendered from a `git archive` of each tree with a throwaway `HERMES_HOME`, no model calls: main 3371c03d **7,913** → main + e54d5a9e **7,925** (**+12**; +14 in compact JSON). On the merge base b1db37d the same method gave 7,890 → 7,902. The same method gave +2 on the first head and +10 more for V6b. V6a and every later fix are result-only (0 schema tokens). The CI prompt-surface report (chars/4 estimate) shows +10 to +11 tool tokens per surface on 8b1e8db (e.g. cli.claude 9,464 → 9,475) and 0 system-prompt tokens.

## Gap inventory (STEP 1)

I sampled 417 of the 55,086 terminal commands that `anthropic/claude-opus-5.5` sent in the last 7 days and that the audit classifier (`terminal_file_tool_share.py`) marks view/search/mixed/edit/list. The sample is stratified by the splitter's buckets. Each command is labelled by what in our toolset does the same job:

- **A**: one file-tool call
- **B**: several file-tool calls in one parallel batch
- **C**: one `execute_code` cell (file tools plus Python: counts, sorts, json, regex)
- **D**: legitimately terminal (git, gh, test runners, `/proc`, processes)
- **E**: nothing today, but a small change to a file tool would make it A, B or C

| bucket (classifier / splitter) | n | A | B | C | D | E | examples |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| search / chained | 136 | 0 | 79 | 47 | 2 | 8 | B: `grep -rln "_cmd_config_check" tests/ \| head; cat tests/…py \| head`; E: `sed -n 128,140p …tsx; grep … \| tail -5` |
| mixed-search / chained | 43 | 0 | 9 | 5 | 28 | 1 | D: `grep -n "^logger" …; scripts/run_tests.sh …` |
| search / count/transform | 38 | 0 | 6 | 28 | 3 | 1 | C: `grep -rno X . \| cut -d: -f1 \| sort \| uniq -c \| sort -rn`; E: `grep -h "11:53:" gateway.log \| cut -c1-300; ls -la` |
| edit | 31 | 4 | 7 | 0 | 20 | 0 | A: `cat >> F37.md <<'EOF' …`; D: heredoc + `git commit` in one command |
| mixed-search / count/transform | 29 | 0 | 0 | 6 | 22 | 1 | D: `for p in $(pgrep -f …); do grep … /proc/$p/environ` |
| mixed-view / chained | 24 | 0 | 2 | 0 | 22 | 0 | D: `sed -n 170,176p hooks.py; …; git fetch …` |
| search / piped filter | 20 | 0 | 12 | 7 | 1 | 0 | C: `grep -rln -i X \| grep -v test` |
| mixed-view / count/transform | 18 | 0 | 0 | 4 | 11 | 3 | D: `git worktree add …; wc -l …` |
| view / chained | 17 | 0 | 13 | 0 | 0 | 4 | B: `sed -n 1200,1300p a.py; sed -n 140,310p b.py`; E: `tail -3 xdist_crash.log; ls logs/` |
| mixed-search / piped filter | 12 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 9 | 0 | D: `grep -n … -A30 …; gh pr view …` |
| view / single | 12 | 8 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 4 | A: `cat BRIEF.md`; E: `tail -20 t1.log` |
| mixed-view / single | 7 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 6 | 0 | D: `git diff --no-index …` |
| view / count/transform | 6 | 0 | 4 | 1 | 0 | 1 | E: `wc -l $L; tail -c 3500 $L; ls -la …` |
| **total** | **417** | **19 (5%)** | **146 (35%)** | **99 (24%)** | **128 (31%)** | **25 (6%)** | |

Every E falls into one of three gaps: `tail` of a file (15 of 25), `ls -la`/`stat` of a directory (13), and byte-ranged `head -c`/`tail -c` (5); some commands hit more than one. Across all 55,086 commands, `tail <file>` appears in 4.3% and `ls` in 13.2%. Byte ranges come to under 0.1%, so they are not worth a parameter. Then I ran the C recipes for the top buckets in a real `execute_code` cell, which turned up the three frictions in the table above: the `N|` gutter, `matches_text` instead of `matches`, and the 100K-char budget inside cells. Patch and write_file in a cell already return their `lint` verdict and the stale-guard refusal as dict fields, so nothing to fix there.

## Routing eval method (STEP 3, live, no mocks)

Each run is a real `hermes chat -q` on Nous Portal in a disposable 20-file repo (`shopkit`: models, pricing, tests, a 3,040-line log, an orders JSON, git history). Each run gets a fresh `HERMES_HOME` and its own auto-started gateway, reaped after the run, and is scored from its own `state.db`. Prompts are plain user asks that never name a tool. Opus: 2 runs per task per leg in the first matrix. The results table above has every number.

What the first-head misses were:
- **t2, t4, t6:** Opus calls the right file tool first, gets the right answer, then runs the same search again with `grep` "to check". This is a trust habit, not a missing capability; V6a answers it for t4.
- **t8:** Opus did not discover the directory listing from the one-phrase schema mention and used `find -printf` on both legs. V6b fixed discovery in part.

## V6: make search results self-evidently complete, make the listing findable (14d7ddb, 465fb78)

The first eval left four tasks at 0/2: t2, t4 and t6 got the right answer from `search_files` and then re-ran the search with grep. Opus's reasoning gave the reason: *"I should also check hidden/gitignored files that grep might be skipping."* On t8 Opus never tried `read_file` on a folder.

- **V6a (result-only, 0 schema tokens):** a first-page, untruncated content search from the model gets a `complete` line. On the final head it reads, verbatim from the t4 smoke run: `Complete: 4 result rows in 4 files in the requested search scope under . (hidden and gitignored files checked too, except dependency/build trees such as .git, node_modules, .venv, build, dist, vendor): none match among the additional files checked.` The hidden/gitignored part comes from one bounded count-only `rg --hidden --no-ignore` probe, run on the same expanded root as the search with pipefail kept. When that probe finds files, the line names them. If the probe fails, passes its bound or rg is missing, the line ends "Hidden and gitignored files were not verified." and the primary rows still come back. Count mode lists files highest first and ignores `grep -c` zero rows. A result with a warning or omitted secret files claims nothing. Cells get no line.
- **Truncation fix this needed:** `files_only` and `count` pages were never flagged truncated, because the pipeline fetched exactly `offset+limit` rows, so a page that had dropped rows looked whole. The pipeline now fetches one extra row and both modes flag truncation (with the `offset=` hint) the way content mode does. Count pages return only their own rows. `files_only` rows are marked on stdout before stderr joins them, so a readable filename with a space survives, including on a partial (exit-2) scan.
- **V6b (+10 tokens):** the `read_file.path` description names directory listings. Directories now carry their lstat size the way `ls -la` shows it: the `-` sent Opus back to `stat` when asked for "every entry's size".
- **Tried and dropped:** a one-clause rename hint in `patch` ("replace_all=true with one call per file in parallel", +15 tokens). t6 stayed at 0/2: one run used `sed -i`, one used execute_code, and both still ran `grep` to "confirm nothing still refers to get_price".

V6 A/B legs (Opus 5.5, same harness), "re-check" = after a correct file-tool answer the run searched again with grep in terminal:
- **HEAD**: first head 5672c54 (reps 1–2) + 1101bef5 (reps 3–4), each + #157517 + #157524
- **V6-early**: an uncommitted first cut of V6a whose line said hidden files were skipped, with no hidden-file probe and `-` for folder sizes
- **V6**: 465fb78, plus 465fb78 with the rejected `patch` hint (8 runs on t2/t4/t6/t8, which only touched patch's description)

| task | HEAD correct (re-check) | V6-early correct (re-check) | V6 correct (re-check) |
|---|---|---|---|
| t2 per-file count | 1/4 (3) | 2/2 (0) | 2/4 (2) |
| t4 case-insensitive search | 0/4 (4) | 0/2 (2): "I should also check hidden/gitignored files" | **4/4 (0)** |
| t6 rename across files | 0/4 (3, +1 `sed -i`) | 0/2 (1, +1 `sed -i`) | 0/4 (3, +1 `sed -i`) |
| t8 list data/ with sizes | 0/4 (`find -printf`) | 0/2 (1 read_file then `stat` for the folder's size) | **4/6** (read_file dir) |
| CONTROL t9 git blame | 4/4 terminal | 2/2 terminal | 1/1 terminal |
| CONTROL t10 run tests | 4/4 terminal | 2/2 terminal | 1/1 terminal |

V6 on the full 8-task set (465fb78, 2 reps each): **10/16** vs HEAD 8/16. t5 came out 0/2 in that pair; 3 more reps per leg gave HEAD 1/3 and V6 3/3, so t5 is 3/5 on both legs. Every answer was correct. V6 spend: **$3.85** for 58 runs, all legs.

Final-head smoke (8b1e8db3, after the completeness wording was scoped to the search that ran): t4 **2/2**, one `search_files` call each and no grep re-check; t8 1/4 (3 runs used `find -printf` in terminal). The read_file schema text on 8b1e8db3 is identical to 465fb78, so t8 is 5/10 across both samples. Spend $0.33.

## Composes with #157517 and #157524

#157517 changes the terminal description so it points batched reads and counts at parallel calls or `execute_code`. #157524 makes the grep fallback honour `(?i)`. This PR supplies the behaviour those words point at: tails, listings, completeness and cell-ready results. Every HEAD leg above runs all three together. This PR changes no other tool's text.

## Prompt surface

`tests/fixtures/prompt_surface/` is regenerated (`read_file.json`, `execute_code.json`, `surfaces.json`). Schema text changed, so this needs a **hermes-agent-core approval**.

## Tests

- `tests/tools/test_file_tools_read_views.py`: four behaviour contracts through real `handle_function_call` and the real `execute_code` dispatch: negative offset with limit, a log rotating mid-tail (and changing again during the retry), the directory listing plus its cap in both views, and cell result shapes (empty file, zero hits, 11 hits, filename miss → `files: []`). All fail on `origin/main`, and all 4 fail on the first head (bb6909c), before the review fixes.
- `tests/tools/test_search_completeness.py`: real rg and grep, no fakes. 19 tests (10 functions, parametrized): a page holding every row is complete and one row short is truncated, in all 3 modes on both engines; count ranking and paging; context rows; the hidden/gitignored check and its failure path; `~` roots; unreadable paths claim nothing; spaced filenames on full and partial scans and a name ending in a space, in all three search lanes. Each review round's new cases failed on the previous head (on aa6762e: 2 of 16).
- `tests/tools/test_file_read_guards.py`: the old "directory → error" test now asserts the listing; the FIFO, device and missing-file guards are unchanged.
- Final local run (`scripts/run_tests.sh`, 152 file-tool/search/code-execution/model-tools files + `tests/ci`): 2,727 passed, 39 skipped, 0 failed; `scripts/check --only health` ok.
- First-head broad run `tests/tools tests/ci`: 15,581 passed, 163 skipped; the 6 failures and 1 import error (`test_bot_desktop_idle_self_stop` timing, `test_sudo_askpass_delivery` live local backend, `test_fal_sdk` missing `fal_client`) also show on `origin/main` in the same fake HOME. `python scripts/check`: 22 checks ok.
- On e54d5a9: `scripts/run_tests.sh` over the PR's test files plus every `tests/tools/test_file_*`/`test_search*` file and `tests/ci` (98 files): 1,670 passed, 17 skipped, 0 failed; `scripts/check --only health` ok.
- CI on e54d5a9e: 15 checks passed, 22 skipped, 0 failed.

## Review fixes (1101bef)

I fixed every Greptile and BearHuddleston finding on bb6909c and replied inline on each one. The fixes: the tail keeps `limit`, survives rotation and works on documents; `text` and `matches` are always present in cells; the listing `entries` respect the cap; the helpers moved into `file_operations_common.py`; the `execute_code` line names both search shapes.

## Review fixes (16b6276, aa6762e, 8b1e8db, e54d5a9)

- 16b6276: a tail whose log changes again during the one retry now returns a retry error instead of a stale page, and a filename search inside a cell that finds nothing now returns `files: []`.
- aa6762e: 5 BearHuddleston and 2 Greptile findings on V6a: count paging, the context-row label ("result rows"), the probe's exit status and `~` root, a probe failure no longer costing the primary result, naming the pruned trees, no claim on final pages, and filenames with spaces.
- 8b1e8db (co-authored with BearHuddleston): the `complete` line describes the search that ran ("in the requested search scope under <path>", "none match among the additional files checked") instead of claiming every file was searched and that grep would find the same lines; `files_only` rows are tagged on stdout so a spaced filename survives a partial scan; the test HOME helper handles a home path with a space.
- e54d5a9 (co-authored with BearHuddleston): a `files_only` name that ends in a space (`"report.txt "`) comes back byte-exact instead of trimmed to a neighbouring file's name. `test_a_filename_ending_in_a_space_reads_back_the_file_that_matched[rg-native|rg-shell|grep]` reads the returned path back; all three lanes fail on 8b1e8db3 and pass here.

Every fix has a test that fails on the previous head, and each thread has an inline reply. The 8b1e8db3 smoke above re-measured t4 after the wording change: still 2/2 with no grep re-check.

## Caveats

- 2 Opus runs per cell is a small sample; per-task numbers are directional. The tail (0/2 → 2/2), asym-context and json-sort gains held across legs; t5 is 3/5 on both HEAD and V6 once more reps are added.
- t6 (rename) is still 0/4: the task asks the model to confirm nothing still refers to the old name, and every run does that with grep.
- The directory listing and the tail read the host filesystem only (`_file_ops_uses_host_paths`). On remote backends a directory still returns the old error, and a tail does one extra `read_file(…, 1, 1)` probe for `total_lines`.
- I did not add the `paths` list, exclude or regex-replace parameters to `patch`: the inventory shows multi-file reads and edits as B/C (a parallel batch or a cell already covers them), and bulk `sed -i` is 0.4% of commands.
- The listing caps at 500 entries. Folder sizes are the directory inode's own size, as in `ls -la`, not the size of the contents.
- The `complete` line costs one extra bounded `rg` run per complete model-side content search (count-only, prunes `node_modules`/`.venv`/…, 30 s cap, gives up past 1,000 files). Without rg (grep fallback) the line says hidden and gitignored files were not verified.

prs.title: feat(catalog): price models the install ships no rates for from the manifest
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Prices a model released after an install, from the same remote manifest the picker already reads.

**The problem in plain terms.** Hermes ships a table of per-token rates so it can show what a session costs. A new model isn't in an installed release's table, so its cost reads "unknown" until the next release carries the row.

**What changes.** `model-catalog.json` now publishes the rate tables as they are on `main`, under `pricing`:

- `official_docs`: the standard-tier snapshot (`_OFFICIAL_DOCS_PRICING`), keyed by billing provider and model id. 103 rows today across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Bedrock, DeepSeek, Fireworks and MiniMax.
- `anthropic_fast_mode` and `openai_ultrafast`: the two fast-tier snapshots, keyed by model id.

Field names are the ones `PricingEntry` uses and rates are decimal strings, so the builder is a straight dump of the dataclass and there's no second schema to keep in step.

Each lookup consults the manifest only after the bundled table has no row for the model, under the same name normalizing (dotted Anthropic versions, Bedrock region prefixes).

**Three rules.**

1. **A bundled rate is never replaced.** If the install has a row, that row is used even when the manifest disagrees. So for any model a release already prices, nothing changes, and a price correction still ships with a release. Same reasoning as the rest of the stack: a row on `main` is paired with the code on `main`.
2. **A malformed rate is unknown, never a price.** Every rate must be a finite, non-negative decimal and an entry needs both token rates. An entry that fails is dropped whole. That follows the existing sentinel handling for OpenRouter's `-1` rates: a wrong number is worse than no number.

3. **An endpoint's own rate comes first.** With `model.base_url` set, a price that endpoint's `/models` listing advertises for the model is used before the manifest's. A relay's own tariff says more about what it charges than the vendor's list price.

GPT-6.2's fast-tier rates aren't in the tables. They're computed in code from the standard rates and carry a launch discount that ends on a date (`_openai_served_tier_entry`), which doesn't fit a flat table. A later model the manifest adds to that contract goes through the same calculation, but only on a vendor snapshot rate (bundled or published). When the standard rate came from anywhere else (an endpoint's own price, models.dev), its Priority, Fast and Ultrafast costs are unknown, never the standard rate or a multiplied relay tariff.

This is 4 of 4 and builds on #157316, #157318 and #157319. **The diff here includes those PRs' commits; the change to review is the last commit.** It needs #157319's `on_gpt62_contract()` for the tier pricing, so the order matters. Please merge the earlier ones first; I'll rebase this onto `main` as they land.

## Related Issue

Part of #157322 (4 of 4). The stack, in merge order:

1. #157316: picker lists for every provider
2. #157318: context windows and metadata
3. #157319: the id sets that gate request handling
4. #157320: pricing (this PR)

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `agent/usage_pricing.py`: adds `_manifest_pricing_entry()`, which parses and validates one manifest row into a `PricingEntry`. `get_pricing_entry` consults the published standard rate after the bundled table and after the endpoint's own listing. `_anthropic_fast_mode_entry` and the non-contract branch of `_openai_served_tier_entry` fall back to their published tables. The GPT-6.2 branch and the `fast` → `priority` mapping use `on_gpt62_contract()`, and derive the tier rate from the bundled or published standard rate.
- `scripts/build_model_catalog.py`, `website/static/api/model-catalog.json`: publish the three tables (87 KB, was 46 KB).
- `website/docs/reference/model-catalog.md`: documents the section and both rules.
- `tests/agent/test_model_catalog_pricing.py`: 7 tests (21 cases).

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_model_catalog_pricing.py`: 21 pass. They cover a model priced from the manifest (including the dotted Anthropic spelling), malformed rates, the fast-mode and Ultrafast tables, GPT-6.2-contract tiers from a published rate, an endpoint's own rate beating the manifest, and a contract tier never repricing another tariff. Each fails without the change.
2. Related suites: on earlier heads of this review I ran the test files that reference the changed code; every failing id also failed on `main` on Windows. I haven't rerun them for the latest head, only the files above.
3. `python scripts/check`: 21 of 22 pass. `shims` fails on `main` on Windows as well.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits). It carries the three earlier PRs' commits until they merge.
- [ ] I've run `just test` on the tests for the code I changed, and they pass. I ran the 18 related files with `scripts/run_tests.sh`; see How to Test.
- [ ] `just check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs). All but `shims`, which fails on `main` on Windows too.
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11, Python 3.14

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A (no new keys)
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

Limits worth knowing:

- This is the PR that makes the manifest noticeably bigger (46 KB to 87 KB). Clients refetch it every 20 minutes, and #54792 is still open about the fetch reading the body without a cap. If size is a concern, the fast-tier tables are the cheapest thing to drop.
- A manifest-sourced rate is reported with `source: official_docs_snapshot` and the manifest's `pricing_version`, the same as a bundled one, because it is the same snapshot. Say so if you'd rather it had its own source label.
- The manifest is plain HTTPS from the docs site with a raw GitHub fallback, unsigned, as it is today. With pricing in it, a wrong manifest could show a wrong cost for a model the install doesn't price. It can't change a cost the install already knows, and it doesn't affect what is actually billed.
- On a relay that advertises no rate of its own, a manifest row prices the model at the vendor's list price. A bundled row does the same today for any base URL, and a manifest row is that row arriving early, so I kept the two consistent rather than add a host allowlist that only remote rows obey. Say so if you'd rather remote rows be stricter.

Not tested: macOS and Linux, and a live session against the published manifest (it only exists once this merges).

prs.title: feat(catalog): let the manifest add a model to the id sets that gate request handling
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Lets a new model that behaves like an existing one be driven correctly by an installed release, without waiting for the next one.

**The problem in plain terms.** Some request handling is keyed on an exact list of model ids in the code: which models take the `low`..`max` effort ladder, which accept a fast tier, which go through a different API. When GPT-6.2 came out, none of its behaviour was new. Its two ids only had to be added to lists the code already read. That still took a code change in several files and a release, and it is the part that actually blocks a stable user: a picker row alone isn't enough if the request then goes out with the wrong effort level and gets a 400.

**What changes.** `model-catalog.json` now publishes five of those lists under `model_sets`, and each membership check also accepts an id the cached manifest adds:

| Set | Built-in constant | What an id in it gets |
|---|---|---|
| `openai_gpt62_contract` | `GPT62_MODEL_IDS` | The `low`..`max` effort ladder, the strict request sanitizer on official OpenAI, Codex and US/EU residency routes, account discovery before the Codex picker lists it, no Ultrafast on the EU host |
| `bedrock_openai_responses` | `BEDROCK_OPENAI_RESPONSES_MODEL_IDS` | Treated as a Bedrock-hosted OpenAI model |
| `anthropic_fast_mode` | `_ANTHROPIC_FAST_MODE_MODELS` | Accepts `speed: "fast"` |
| `openai_ultrafast` | `_OPENAI_ULTRAFAST_MODELS` | Accepts `service_tier: "ultrafast"` |
| `openai_fast_eu` | `_FAST_REGION_MODELS` (EU host) | Accepts a fast tier on `eu.api.openai.com` |

So the next model on the GPT-6.2 contract is one line in a JSON file on `main`, and installed releases pick it up within 20 minutes.

**What the manifest can and can't do.**

- It can add an id to a set. It can't add a set: a set only exists because code reads it, so an unknown name is ignored and a model that needs new behaviour still needs a release.
- It can't remove an id an install ships.
- It can't choose a host. A set decides which *model* may use a tier. Which *endpoint* may receive it stays in the built-in route checks (`_fast_mode_route_supported`, `_FAST_REGION_MODELS`). There is a test that no set can make `au.api.openai.com` accept Ultrafast.
- A fast tier is still opt-in. A set only makes `/fast` available for the model, and only for a model and route the built-in family and route checks already allow.
- A set name means one behaviour for good. `requires` checks the name, not a revision of the code behind it, so if a set's request handling ever changes, that release gives it a new name. Older builds then skip the row instead of driving the model the old way.

**The picker gate from #157316 gets its writer here.** The builder now adds `requires` to a picker entry whose model is in a set it can't be driven without (`openai_gpt62_contract`, `bedrock_openai_responses`). A build that doesn't read that set skips the entry. In practice: a release with only #157316 won't list a future GPT-6.2-style model it can't drive, and a release with this PR will list it and drive it.

Pricing keeps its own built-in id set in this PR. `_openai_served_tier_entry` indexes the bundled price table directly for GPT-6.2 ids, so I left `agent/usage_pricing.py` alone. A model added through a set shows an unknown fast-tier cost until #157320 or a release carries its rates.

This is 3 of 4 and builds on #157316 and #157318. **The diff here includes those PRs' commits; the change to review is the last commit.** Please merge those first; I'll rebase this onto `main` as soon as they land.

## Related Issue

Part of #157322 (3 of 4). The stack, in merge order:

1. #157316: picker lists for every provider
2. #157318: context windows and metadata
3. #157319: the id sets that gate request handling (this PR)
4. #157320: pricing

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/model_catalog.py`: adds the `MODEL_SETS` registry (name → whether a model needs it to be driven) and `in_model_set()`. `manifest_provider_models()` now skips an entry only when `requires` names a set missing from the registry. `cached_manifest()` reads `model_catalog.enabled` off the uncopied config, since these checks run on request paths.
- `agent/reasoning_effort.py`: adds `on_gpt62_contract()`, the one place that answers "is this id on the GPT-6.2 contract"; `codex_supported_efforts` uses it.
- `agent/transports/codex.py`: `_is_official_openai_responses_route` uses it.
- `hermes_cli/codex_models.py`: `codex_model_requires_account_discovery` uses it, and compares the normalized id in lowercase.
- `hermes_cli/models_fast_regions.py`: the EU Ultrafast exclusion uses it, replacing a second copy of the two ids; EU Fast reads `openai_fast_eu`.
- `hermes_cli/models.py`: `model_supports_ultrafast` reads `openai_ultrafast`. Net zero lines.
- `agent/model_metadata.py`: `is_anthropic_fast_mode_model` reads `anthropic_fast_mode`. Net zero lines.
- `agent/bedrock_adapter.py`: `parse_bedrock_openai_model_id` reads `bedrock_openai_responses`.
- `scripts/build_model_catalog.py`, `website/static/api/model-catalog.json`: publish the sets and the `requires` fields. The builder fails if its table of constants and `MODEL_SETS` name different sets.
- `website/docs/reference/model-catalog.md`: documents the sets and their rules.
- `hermes_cli/models.py`: `openai_ultrafast` only widens OpenAI routes: the Anthropic and xAI route checks don't accept the Ultrafast tier, and the model has to be an OpenAI fast-eligible id.
- `agent/bedrock_adapter.py`: `merge_bedrock_openai_model_ids` also appends published Mantle ids, so a new Mantle-only model shows up after successful discovery.
- `tests/agent/test_model_catalog_model_sets.py`: 15 tests (24 cases).

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_model_catalog_model_sets.py`: 24 pass. A made-up `gpt-9-test` and `claude-test-9` go through the real code: the effort ladder, the Responses sanitizer on official routes, Codex account gating (including a mixed-case id), fast tiers on code-owned hosts only, Anthropic `speed`, Bedrock OpenAI recognition and the Mantle picker and wizard, the publisher's `requires` tags, and entries with requirements this build can't meet. Each fails without the change.
2. Related suites: on earlier heads of this review I ran the test files that reference the changed code; every failing id also failed on `main` on Windows. I haven't rerun them for the latest head, only the files above.
3. `python scripts/check`: 21 of 22 pass. `shims` fails on `main` on Windows as well.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits). It carries the two earlier PRs' commits until they merge.
- [ ] I've run `just test` on the tests for the code I changed, and they pass. I ran the 24 related files with `scripts/run_tests.sh`; see How to Test.
- [ ] `just check` passes (the blocking lint and code-health checks CI runs). All but `shims`, which fails on `main` on Windows too.
- [x] I've added tests for my changes (required for bug fixes, strongly encouraged for features)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Windows 11, Python 3.14

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example` if I added/changed config keys — or N/A (no new keys)
- [x] I've updated `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `AGENTS.md` if I changed architecture or workflows — or N/A
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact (Windows, macOS) per the [compatibility guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#cross-platform-compatibility) — or N/A
- [x] I've updated tool descriptions/schemas if I changed tool behavior — or N/A

Limits worth knowing:

- Five sets, not all of them. I picked the exact-id lists behind the GPT-6.2 change plus one each for Anthropic and Bedrock. Lists matched by prefix or regex (`GPT6_TIER_PREFIXES`, the Grok and Kimi ladders) already cover new variants on their own. Adding another exact-id list later is one registry line, one builder line and one call.
- `MODEL_SETS` in `hermes_cli/model_catalog.py` and the constants table in the build script are one registry in two files. The build fails if they drift, and the manifest sync test runs the build.
- A manifest row can make a billable tier *available* for a model. That is the point of the set, but it is the one place where this stack lets remote data widen what a request may ask for, so it deserves a careful look. The hosts and the opt-in are not remote.
- The system prompt and `tools[]` are untouched; this only changes request parameters.

Not tested: macOS and Linux, and a live request for a model added through the manifest (there is no such model yet).
