prs.title: feat(catalog): fill in metadata and context windows for new models from the manifest
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Gives a model released after an install the right context window and capabilities, from the same remote manifest the picker already reads.

**The problem in plain terms.** When a model is new, an installed release has no row for it in the hardcoded tables. So it guesses. For the context window it falls back to a family catch-all, or to the generic 256K. For "does it take images, does it reason" it answers "unknown". The right rows are added on `main`, and stable users wait for the next release to get them. A wrong window means compression fires too early or too late.

**What changes.** `model-catalog.json` now publishes those tables as they are on `main`:

- `context_lengths.default`, `.bedrock`, `.codex_oauth`: the three hardcoded context-window tables (`DEFAULT_CONTEXT_LENGTHS`, `BEDROCK_CONTEXT_LENGTHS`, `_CODEX_OAUTH_CONTEXT_FALLBACK`).
- `model_metadata`: the built-in metadata entries (`_BUILTIN_MODEL_METADATA`), keyed by models.dev provider id and model id, in the models.dev entry shape.

Each reader looks at them in the place it already looked at the hardcoded table, at the end of the chain. An explicit `model.context_length`, live provider endpoints and models.dev still come first.

**The rule: it fills gaps, it doesn't correct.** A key or entry the install ships keeps its own value, under any casing, even when the manifest disagrees. What the manifest adds is the row for a model the install has never heard of. So for any model a release already knows, nothing changes. I chose that over "newest wins" because a table row on `main` is paired with the code on `main`, and applying it to older code is the kind of mismatch this stack should not create. Corrections keep shipping with releases.

For the context tables the matching is the same as today (a key is a substring of the model id, longest key wins), so a more specific manifest row beats a built-in family row for the models it names, which is exactly the gap being filled. Added keys are lowercased, because every reader matches against a lowercased id.

A malformed row is dropped rather than half-used: a window that isn't a positive integer, a blank key (as a substring it would match every model), or a metadata entry without a valid `limit.context`. A `cost` field in a metadata entry is ignored, so this table can't put a price on anything.

Metadata is looked up only when models.dev has no entry for the model. That keeps the manifest read off the picker's per-row capability path.

This is 2 of 4 and builds on #157316. **The diff here includes that PR's commit; the change to review is the last commit.** Please merge #157316 first; I'll rebase this onto `main` as soon as it lands.

## Related Issue

Part of #157322 (2 of 4). The stack, in merge order:

1. #157316: picker lists for every provider
2. #157318: context windows and metadata (this PR)
3. #157319: the id sets that gate request handling
4. #157320: pricing

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/model_catalog.py`: adds `manifest_table()`, `manifest_model_metadata()` and `extend_context_lengths()`. The last one returns the built-in table plus the manifest keys it doesn't have under any casing, lowercased; a blank key or a value that isn't a positive int is dropped. `manifest_model_metadata()` returns nothing for an entry without a valid `limit` and strips `cost`.
- `agent/model_metadata.py`: the two hardcoded-default lookups and the Codex OAuth fallback read the extended table. Net zero lines (the file is over the size cap).
- `agent/bedrock_adapter.py`: `bedrock_static_context_length` reads the extended Bedrock and default tables.
- `agent/context_pin.py`: the pin check reads the extended default table.
- `agent/models_dev.py`: `_builtin_model_metadata` falls back to the manifest entry, and `_apply_overrides` only asks for it when models.dev has no entry.
- `scripts/build_model_catalog.py`, `website/static/api/model-catalog.json`: publish the tables (44 KB, was 35 KB).
- `website/docs/reference/model-catalog.md`: documents both tables and the fill-gaps rule.
- `hermes_cli/web_routers/models.py`, `hermes_cli/web_routers/analytics.py`: the dashboard's model info card looks up capabilities inside the requested profile's scope (its context-length probe already binds the profile on `main`), and the analytics cards use the profile of the usage store they opened, so both read that profile's catalog.
- `tests/agent/test_model_catalog_metadata.py`: 9 tests. `tests/hermes_cli/test_models_analytics_attribution.py`: one more, for the profile selectors.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_model_catalog_metadata.py tests/hermes_cli/test_models_analytics_attribution.py`: all pass. They cover a new model's window and capabilities from the manifest, each fallback that read the built-in table, key casing, malformed rows, no prices from metadata, and the dashboard cards in a named profile. Each fails without the change.
2. Related suites: on earlier heads of this review I ran the test files that reference the changed code; every failing id also failed on `main` on Windows. I haven't rerun them for the latest head, only the files above.
3. `python scripts/check`: 21 of 22 pass. `shims` fails on `main` on Windows as well.

prs.title: fix(pm): ensure_import names the remedy that applies, not `hermes pm doctor`
prs.body:
## The defect

`39c0a391` ("fix(providers): report why a lazy SDK install did not land") changed both
provider adapters to surface a failed lazy install's `InstallError` **in place of** the
install hint, so that a completed install awaiting a restart is not reported as
"install it":

```python
# agent/bedrock_adapter.py:103-105 (main)
# A completed install that needs a restart must not be reported as "install it".
reason = f": {install_error}" if install_error else f". Run: {install_hint('bedrock')}"
raise ImportError(f"The 'boto3' package is required for the AWS Bedrock provider{reason}")
```

That is the right call. But what the user now reads is `str(InstallError)`, which ends in
`InstallError.remedy` — and `ensure_import()` sets it at none of its three raise sites
(`pm/extras.py:198`, `:219`, `:238`), so all three inherit the constructor default
(`pm/package.py:19`):

```python
self.remedy = remedy or "retry, or run `hermes pm doctor`"
```

Measured on `59004a62356` (macOS, py3.11) — the user declines the install prompt:

```
The 'boto3' package is required for the AWS Bedrock provider: venv: installation of
extra 'bedrock' declined — retry, or run `hermes pm doctor`
```

`hermes pm doctor` does not install extras, and the prompt does not come back on its
own. `hermes pm install --extra bedrock` is the one command that helps, and it is no
longer reachable from the error. Same string for `anthropic` via `_require_sdk`.

The suppression is also indiscriminate: the restart case correctly avoids "install it",
but its remedy is still `retry, or run \`hermes pm doctor\`` when the actual answer is
"restart Hermes", buried in the cause text. And for a platform-gated extra, "retry"
names a loop that can never terminate.

`tests/pm/test_install_extra.py`'s own docstring states the invariant this breaks:
*"`hermes pm install --extra NAME` is the one command every missing-extra hint names."*

## What changed

`pm/extras.py` only — each raise site names the action that actually applies:

| case | remedy |
|---|---|
| declined | ``run `hermes pm install --extra NAME` when you want it`` |
| platform-gated | `nothing to install — NAME does not build for this platform` |
| needs restart | `restart Hermes` |

This is what the rest of the lazy-install path already does for the cases it owns —
`pm/client.py:39-40` passes `install_hint(extra)` as the remedy ("the user asked for an
extra, not for PM's own runtime: name the command that provisions both"), and
`pm/install.py:178-181` passes `enable security.allow_lazy_installs or run \`hermes pm
install\``. `ensure_import`'s own raises were the gap.

`39c0a391`'s intent is preserved: the restart case still never says "install it".

**Neither adapter is touched** — both already forward whatever remedy `ensure_import`
set, so fixing it once fixes both, and `pm/worker.py:118`, which puts `exc.remedy` in
its structured error payload, is corrected too.

After the fix, same scenario:

```
The 'boto3' package is required for the AWS Bedrock provider: venv: installation of
extra 'bedrock' declined — run `hermes pm install --extra bedrock` when you want it
```

Out of scope: a `sync_venv` refusal reaches the adapter as
`_refuse_lazy`'s `InstallError`, which already carries a purposeful remedy
(`enable security.allow_lazy_installs or run \`hermes pm install\``) — verified by
measurement, not changed here.

## Tests

5 new, `132 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)` across 4 files:

- `tests/pm/test_install_extra.py` (3) — declined keeps the install command; platform-gated
  promises neither an install nor a retry; an installed-but-unactivated extra asks for a restart.
- `tests/agent/test_bedrock_adapter.py`, `tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py` (1 each) —
  the string a user reads. These drive the **real** `ensure_import`, because
  `39c0a391`'s own two tests construct the `InstallError` by hand and so never exercise
  the remedy `ensure_import` sets — which is why the gap was invisible.

```
$ pytest tests/pm/test_install_extra.py tests/agent/test_bedrock_adapter.py::TestRequireBoto3VersionCheck \
         tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py::test_a_declined_install_still_tells_the_user_how_to_install_it \
         tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py::test_missing_sdk_error_reports_why_the_lazy_install_did_not_land
11 passed in 1.41s
```

**Negative control.** With `pm/extras.py` reverted to `main` and the tests kept, all 5 fail
with `AssertionError` on the real defect (not `AttributeError` for a symbol the PR adds),
printing the exact user-facing string above:

```
assert 'hermes pm install --extra bedrock' in "The 'boto3' package is required for the
AWS Bedrock provider: venv: installation of extra 'bedrock' declined — retry, or run
`hermes pm doctor`"
```

**Neighbouring suites.** `tests/pm/ tests/agent/test_bedrock_adapter.py
tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py`, same command before and after:

```
clean main:  193 failed/errored
with fix:    188 failed/errored
```

The delta is exactly the 5 new tests flipping to pass; `comm` on the sorted
`FAILED`/`ERROR` lists shows **zero** newly broken. The 188 are pre-existing on clean
`main` on this machine — `tests/pm/test_worker_*.py` and friends need a real PM install —
and are untouched by this diff.

## Duplicate check

No open or closed PR or issue covers `ensure_import`'s remedy
(searched `install_hint remedy`, `InstallError remedy`, `extra declined install`).

prs.title: fix(doctor): probe the Bedrock endpoint inference actually uses
prs.body:
Fixes #87195.

## The defect

`hermes doctor`'s `AWS Bedrock` row calls `bedrock:ListFoundationModels` (`hermes_cli/doctor_connectivity.py:265`). That is the **control plane**. On the Bedrock API Key route the agent sends inference to `bedrock-mantle.<region>.api.aws` authenticated with `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` — a credential `ListFoundationModels` never touches. So the row is green while every request 401s, which is exactly what the reporter saw.

On current `main` the configured Mantle endpoint is probed nowhere:

- `bedrock` is in `_dedicated_canonical` (`doctor_connectivity.py:89`), so it is excluded from the generic api-key probe loop;
- there is no `bedrock-mantle` `ProviderProfile`, so `_build_apikey_providers_list()` never produces a row for it.

With a Mantle config active, the whole connectivity table is `['IPv6 route', 'OpenRouter API', 'Anthropic API', 'AWS Bedrock', 'Azure Foundry (Entra ID)', 'GitHub token']` — one Bedrock row, and it checks the wrong plane.

## What changed

**1. The control-plane row says which plane it checked** — the ok detail is now `(AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, us-east-1, <N> models, control plane)`. This is the framing **#87215 (@liuhao1024)** proposed; credit for it is theirs. That PR patches `hermes_cli/doctor.py`, where this code no longer lives: its hunks target lines 515, 2328 and 2550 of a file that is now **239 lines** on `main` and contains zero mentions of `_probe_bedrock` or `list_foundation_models` — `doctor.py` was split into 7 modules and the probe moved to `doctor_connectivity.py`. It has been untouched since 2026-08-20.

**2. A new `AWS Bedrock runtime` row follows the configured route and checks its auth.** The Bedrock API Key endpoint is OpenAI-compatible, so `GET <base>/models` verifies the data plane's credential **without billing an inference call**.

```
✓ AWS Bedrock         (AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK, us-east-1, <N> models, control plane)
✗ AWS Bedrock runtime (HTTP 401 — AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK rejected by https://bedrock-mantle.us-east-1.api.aws/v1)
```

Three design points worth reviewing:

- **The row is skipped unless the active config routes at that host.** The Bedrock API Key flow writes `model.provider: custom:bedrock-mantle` with the endpoint and `key_env` under `providers.bedrock-mantle` (`hermes_cli/model_setup_flows_bedrock.py`), so the route has to be read from config, not from an env var. SigV4/Converse users get no new row: that route has no free list call, and guessing would bill them an inference.
- **Host matching is on the parsed hostname**, via the existing `utils.base_url_hostname`, not a substring — `https://bedrock-mantle.us-east-1.api.aws.evil.example/v1` and `https://evil.example/bedrock-mantle.us-east-1.api.aws` are both rejected (tested).
- **`_BEDROCK_RUNTIME_HOST_PARTS` is a module constant** so the test can point it at a loopback stand-in, the same way `GITHUB_API_PROBE_URL` is used by the GitHub-token probe.

## Live measurement

`GET https://bedrock-mantle.<region>.api.aws/v1/models`, measured 2026-09-25 in `us-east-1` and `us-east-2` (identical answers):

| request | status | body | x-amzn-RequestId |
|---|---|---|---|
| no auth header | 401 | `{"error":{"code":"invalid_api_key","message":"Missing 'authorization' or 'x-api-key' header","param":null,"type":"permission_denied_error"}}` | `req_dbpbb4byxg2q3rof2fwgbiz4b7df3raj7lyftrgojjkos2prgrlq` |
| bad bearer token | 401 | `{"error":{"code":"invalid_api_key","message":"Invalid bearer token","param":null,"type":"permission_denied_error"}}` | `req_q6kzumhrytxyn77vapjvsrulqch5humhe5fcfch72fdz7kun6qfq` |

That 401 is the reporter's symptom, and it is reachable with no credential and no inference cost. The test stand-in serves these exact bodies.

## Tests

`tests/hermes_cli/test_doctor_bedrock_runtime_probe.py`, 18 tests, all driving the production entry point (`dc.build_probes()` → `dc.run_probes()`) against a local `HTTPServer`:

```
18 passed in 4.13s
```

Covered: 401 → `✗` naming the key var and the endpoint, with an issue line that explains why the row above disagrees; 200 → `✓`; configured route with no token → `⚠` and **no request made**; non-Bedrock route → no row and no request; unreachable endpoint → `⚠`, not a raise; bare `model.base_url` at the host also followed; the 7 near-miss hosts above rejected; and the token never leaks into the row text.

One test runs the **real** setup wizard (`_model_flow_bedrock_api_key`) and asserts the probe recognizes the config it wrote — so this does not just test my own assumption about the config shape.

### Negative control (source file reverted to `main`, tests kept)

`13 failed, 5 errors`, and the split matters:

- **16 of 18 are `AttributeError` for symbols this PR adds** (`_is_bedrock_runtime_url`, `_BEDROCK_RUNTIME_HOST_PARTS`, `_configured_bedrock_runtime`). That proves only that the code is absent — I am not counting it as a reproduction.
- **2 reproduce the defect using only API that exists on `main`:**
  - `build_probes()` on a Mantle-routed config returns the 6-row table quoted above — no row covers the configured endpoint.
  - `_probe_bedrock()`'s ok detail is `(AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, us-east-1, 1 models)` — nothing tells the reader it only checked the control plane.

### Neighbouring tests

```
tests/hermes_cli/test_doctor.py test_doctor_dedicated_provider_skip.py test_doctor_github_token_probe.py
test_doctor_azure_foundry_probe.py test_doctor_ipv6_probe.py test_doctor_exit_status.py
test_doctor_live.py test_bedrock_mantle_key_env.py
→ 1 failed, 104 passed
```

The one failure is `test_doctor_reports_vercel_backend_diagnostics`, which **fails identically on clean `main`** (verified by reverting the source file and re-running that single test) — pre-existing, unrelated to this change.

## Duplicate check

`gh search prs --repo NousResearch/hermes-agent --state open` for `doctor bedrock`, `bedrock-mantle`, `doctor runtime probe`: only #87215 (the control-plane labelling half, on a file that no longer holds the code) and #92073 (region chokepoint, unrelated). No open PR probes the runtime endpoint.

prs.title: fix(bedrock): correct the Llama 4 context windows to the measured values
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`BEDROCK_CONTEXT_LENGTHS` (`agent/bedrock_adapter.py:934`) puts both Llama 4 models in the 128K group. Bedrock enforces **1,048,576** for Maverick and **3,500,000** for Scout, so the table is short by 8x and 27x.

**On the path most callers take, that table is not a fallback — it is the answer.** `model_metadata.py:1670` calls `get_bedrock_context_length(model)` with **no region**, and the getter only probes `if probe and region`. No region → no probe → the table is the sole source. Measured on this PR's base with `probe=False`:

| model id | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `us.meta.llama4-maverick-17b-instruct-v1:0` | **128,000** | 1,048,576 |
| `us.meta.llama4-scout-17b-instruct-v1:0` | **128,000** | 3,500,000 |

So a Llama 4 session compacted almost immediately whenever the probe could not run, and the operator had no way to see why.

I re-measured both windows against Converse rather than reading them off a model card — two regions, plus accepted probes where Bedrock reports its own exact `usage.inputTokens`. Full log under *Screenshots / Logs*, including the two ways the measurement can lie to you.

## Related Issue

No issue — found reading the table.

This replaces my own #98726, which I am closing. That PR was written against the one-key-per-line version of this table; `main` has since compacted it into `dict.fromkeys` groups, so it needs rewriting rather than rebasing. This is the rewrite, and it deliberately carries **less** — see *What I left out*.

**It also deliberately does not touch `claude-opus-5`.** That row is genuinely missing from this table too, but #75824 (@ryrenz, oldest), #92273 (@bagg3rs) and #83071 (@nickkpoon) are all already open against it, and #75824 is written against the current compacted table and carries a drift guard whose dotted-to-hyphen normalisation is better than the one I had written. A fourth competing row would help nobody, so I dropped mine and left a verification note on #75824 instead. My own #98494 covered the same ground and is closed in favour of theirs, not of this.

**This PR and #75824 do not conflict, and I checked rather than assuming.** A real three-way merge of the two heads succeeds with no conflict, so either can land first. The two hunks in `bedrock_adapter.py` are 12 lines apart (`@@ -933` theirs, `@@ -945` mine) and touch different rows.

One warning if you try to stack them by hand: `git apply` of one on top of the other *does* fail, because both append a test at the same anchor in `tests/agent/test_bedrock_adapter.py` (right after `mock_probe.assert_not_called()`) and `git apply` matches context strictly. That is a patch-application artefact, not a merge conflict — `git merge-tree` on the same pair is clean.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `agent/bedrock_adapter.py` — lift `meta.llama4-maverick` and `meta.llama4-scout` out of the 128K `dict.fromkeys` group and give each its measured value. Four comment lines recording *why* Scout is 3.5M and not the 10M on its model card, because that is the part of this change a future reader will otherwise "correct" back. `+9/-2`; the surrounding group and every other row are untouched.
- `tests/agent/test_bedrock_adapter.py` — one case in `TestBedrockContextLength`, `test_llama4_windows_are_the_measured_ones`, pinning both windows through `get_bedrock_context_length(..., probe=False)` with realistic inference-profile ids.

Total: 2 files, `+18/-2`, one commit. No function signature moves, no behaviour change outside these two dict entries.

## How to Test

```bash
# the new test against the old table
git checkout 7dc796463d                     # this PR's base
git checkout fix/bedrock-llama4-measured-context-windows -- tests/agent/test_bedrock_adapter.py
pytest tests/agent/test_bedrock_adapter.py -q -p no:randomly
#  -> 1 failed, 78 passed
#     AssertionError: assert 128000 == 1048576

git checkout fix/bedrock-llama4-measured-context-windows
pytest tests/agent/test_bedrock_adapter.py -q -p no:randomly
#  -> 79 passed
```

Every Bedrock suite in the tree, on this branch: `test_bedrock_adapter.py` 79 passed, `test_bedrock_integration.py` 35 passed, `test_bedrock_1m_context.py` 2 passed, `test_bedrock_empty_text_blocks.py` 3 passed, `test_bedrock_interrupt_post_worker.py` 2 passed, `test_bedrock_transport_replay.py` 2 passed.

Those first two are the only files in `tests/` that import either `BEDROCK_CONTEXT_LENGTHS` or `get_bedrock_context_length` (`grep -rln` over `tests/ agent/`). The consumers of the value also pass unchanged: `test_model_metadata.py` 121 passed, `test_model_metadata_local_ctx.py` 37 passed, `test_turn_context.py` 20 passed, `test_uncompressed_context_guardrail.py` 7 passed, and eleven more context suites.

`ruff check .` passes repo-wide. `ruff format --check` flags both touched files — but it flags them identically on the pristine base, and no workflow in `.github/workflows/` runs `ruff format`, so this adds no formatting debt and graduates none.

## Known limitation, stated up front

**The Scout row only takes effect on the no-region path.** With a region, `probe_bedrock_context_length` walks `_BEDROCK_PROBE_TIERS = (1_300_000, 2_200_000)` and does `return tier_tokens` on the *first acceptance*. Scout accepted 2,222,258 tokens in my measurement, so it will accept tier 1 as well — acceptance is monotone in length — and the probe therefore returns **1,300,000**, below both this PR's value and what the API actually enforces.

That is a pre-existing shortfall in the probe, not something this change introduces, and fixing it means editing the getter or the tiers rather than the table, so I have left it alone. The smallest honest fix is to treat an accepted tier as a floor rather than an answer — `max(probed, table_lookup)` — which is exactly what the probe's own docstring already calls it: *"An accepted tier is a safe lower bound"*. Say the word and I will send that separately. It may also interact with #104128, which is reworking probe caching in the same area, so it is probably better as its own PR either way.

Maverick is unaffected on both paths: tier 1 at 1,300,000 pads past 1,048,576, so the probe gets the parseable rejection and returns the right number.

## What I left out

#98726 also added four rows I am **not** carrying: `mistral.pixtral-large` 131,072, `deepseek.v3.2` 163,840, `minimax.minimax-m2` 196,608, `kimi-k2` 262,144. They were labelled "measured" there and I did not re-measure any of them today. I am not willing to re-assert numbers in a new PR that I have not re-verified in the same sitting. None of those keys exists on `main`, so omitting them regresses nothing; they can come back with their own log attached.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) — one commit, `fix(bedrock): ...`
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate — and it changed this PR: the search is what turned up the three open `claude-opus-5` PRs, which is why that row is no longer here. No open PR touches the Llama 4 rows.
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix (2 files, `+18/-2`, one commit)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — partially; I'd rather you read the note than have me tick this
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Amazon Linux 2023 x86_64, CPython 3.11.14

**What I actually ran, and what I could not.** I ran the complete `tests/agent/` directory on both this branch and its base, so the number is attributable rather than decorative:

| | `tests/agent/` |
|---|---|
| base | 32 failed, 6612 passed, 31 skipped |
| this branch | 32 failed, **6613 passed**, 31 skipped |

`+1 passed` — the one test this PR adds — and the failing set is **byte-identical** between the two (`diff` of the sorted `FAILED` lines is empty). Those 32 are pre-existing on `main` in my environment and all sit in auxiliary-client / provider-resolution / skill-command territory; `test_auxiliary_client.py`, `test_auxiliary_main_first.py` and `test_auxiliary_named_custom_providers.py` account for 18 of them. Nothing that reads a context window. Happy to paste the list if it's useful.

I did **not** get a whole-`tests/` run: on my box it hits 36 collection errors from optional dependencies I don't have installed (`aiohttp` and the acp/gateway stack), and the rest exceeds my remote-execution time ceiling. Rather than tick the box on a number I can't attribute, I'm leaving it unticked and showing you the scoped run above.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation — the four comment lines in the table are the documentation for the Scout value; no `docs/` change applies
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` — N/A, no config keys
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md` — N/A, no architecture or workflow change
- [x] Cross-platform impact — N/A, two dict literals; no platform-conditional code
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas — N/A, no tool behaviour change

## Screenshots / Logs

Measured 2026-09-09 against `bedrock-runtime` `Converse`, from my own AWS account, on `us.meta.llama4-*-17b-instruct-v1:0`.

Method: pad the prompt with `"data " * int(target / 0.9)` and read what the API says. Length validation runs **before** inference, so a **rejected** probe is free; an **accepted** probe bills the input tokens but returns `usage.inputTokens` — Bedrock's own exact count, and therefore a precise verified floor. Actual tokens land at ≈1.111 per target unit.

| model | region | target | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Maverick | us-east-1 | 2,000,000 | rejected — `This model's maximum context length is 1048576 tokens. Please reduce the length of the prompt` |
| Maverick | us-east-1 | 1,000,000 | rejected — same number (pads to 1,111,111 > 1,048,576) |
| Maverick | us-east-1 | 750,000 | **accepted**, `usage.inputTokens = 833,369` |
| Maverick | us-east-1 | 500,000 | **accepted**, `usage.inputTokens = 555,591` |
| Maverick | us-east-2 | 2,000,000 | rejected — same number |
| Scout | us-east-1 | 2,000,000 | **accepted**, `usage.inputTokens = 2,222,258` |
| Scout | us-east-1 | 3,500,000 | rejected — `This model's maximum context length is 3500000 tokens. Please reduce the length of the prompt` |
| Scout | us-east-2 | 3,500,000 | rejected — same number |
| both | both | 5,000,000 | rejected, but **unparseable**: `Input is too long for requested model.` — no number |

Both numbers are identical in two regions, and every acceptance sits below the stated maximum for its model, which is the internal consistency check. Total billed input across the run: 3,611,218 tokens.

Two caveats about the method, because each of them cost me a wrong reading before it could cost you one:

- **At large overshoot the error stops being parseable.** A 5,000,000-token target — a 27.8 MB payload — returns `Input is too long for requested model.` in both regions for both models, with no maximum in it. `parse_context_limit_from_error` correctly returns `None` there. So a descending probe finds the number and an aggressive one does not; the existing comment on `_BEDROCK_PROBE_TIERS` is right about this, and it is also why I could not initially reproduce the error string my own earlier PR quoted.
- **Throttling looks like a length rejection if you only check that the call raised.** After Scout accepted 2.22M tokens, my next three "rejected" results were actually `Too many tokens, please wait before trying again`, which carries no window. I discarded those three and re-ran the 3,500,000 probe after a 180 s backoff; that backed-off run is the one in the table.

The before/after lookups were produced by importing the module at each revision and calling `get_bedrock_context_length(model_id, probe=False)` — no network, so they are the resolution the no-region path actually performs.

prs.title: fix(bedrock): stop the context probe escalating on throttles, and treat an accepted tier as a floor
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Two independent bugs in `probe_bedrock_context_length` (`agent/bedrock_adapter.py:964`), one commit each. Both were found by pointing the probe at real Converse endpoints and reading what came back.

**1. The probe escalates to a bigger payload on failures where that cannot help.** The `except` branch falls through to the next, larger tier whenever the rejection carries no parseable window. Two of the shapes Bedrock actually returns make that upload pointless or actively harmful:

```
ThrottlingException ... Too many tokens, please wait before trying again.
ValidationException ... Input is too long for requested model.
```

**2. An accepted tier is returned as the window when it is only a floor.** `_BEDROCK_PROBE_TIERS = (1_300_000, 2_200_000)` ascends, and the loop did `return tier_tokens` on the first acceptance. So every model whose window exceeds the first tier probed as exactly `1,300,000`, and the second tier — the whole point of a ladder — was never reached on the acceptance path.

## Related Issue

No issue.

This replaces my own **#98522**, which I am closing. That PR is 6,737 commits behind and does not merge (`bedrock_adapter.py` has been touched 21 times over its base), so it needs rewriting rather than rebasing. But there is a second reason I would rather state than quietly carry forward: **its central claim is wrong, and I only found that out by measuring.** #98522's docstring says

> the error shape is a property of the model, not of the payload size, so a bigger prompt returns the identical error

That is not what Bedrock does. Same model, same region, different padding:

| target | outcome |
|---|---|
| 2,200,000 | `This model's maximum context length is 1048576 tokens. Please reduce the length of the prompt` |
| 5,000,000 | `Input is too long for requested model.` — no number |

The shape **does** follow payload size, and it degrades as the payload grows. That happens to make #98522's `break` the right behaviour, but for the opposite reason to the one it gives, and a reviewer accepting it would be accepting a false premise. #98522 also returned the largest accepted tier as the answer, which is bug 2 above, not a fix for it.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

**Commit 1 — `stop the context probe escalating after a throttle or a numberless overflow`** (`agent/bedrock_adapter.py` `+15/-2`, `tests/…` `+44/-0`)

Classify the failure before escalating, and stop on `rate_limit` or `context_overflow`. An opaque `InternalServerException` still steps up, which is what the ladder's own comment says it is for.

I deliberately did **not** build this on `classify_bedrock_error` / `THROTTLE_PATTERNS` further down this same file. `COMPAT_MANIFEST.md:178-184` lists `THROTTLE_PATTERNS`, `OVERLOAD_PATTERNS`, `CONTEXT_OVERFLOW_PATTERNS`, `classify_bedrock_error` and `is_context_overflow_error` all as `restored-def … (deleted; BASE body restored)` inside the revert-scheduled plugin-compat block, and `grep` finds no non-compat caller of `classify_bedrock_error` in the tree. So this uses the live classifier instead — `agent/error_classifier.py`, whose module docstring is explicit that the retry loop should consult it "instead of re-matching strings itself", and whose `_RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` comment already names this exact Bedrock throttle message. No new patterns, no new constants, and `agent/error_classifier.py` imports nothing from `bedrock_adapter`, so there is no cycle.

**Commit 2 — `treat an accepted probe tier as a floor, not the window`** (`agent/bedrock_adapter.py` `+21/-3`, `tests/…` `+35/-0`)

- An accepted tier records `accepted_floor` and steps up. A rejection at the next tier quotes the real number, so a 2M-window model now resolves to `2,000,000` instead of `1,300,000`.
- If every tier is accepted, the floor is compared against the static table before being reported. When the table knows more, return `None` and let it answer; the floor is still returned for a model the table has never seen, which would otherwise drop to the 128K default.
- The table lookup moves into `_static_bedrock_context_length` so the probe and `get_bedrock_context_length` share one resolver instead of two copies of the longest-substring match.

Total: 2 files, `+115/-5`, two commits. No signature changes; `get_bedrock_context_length`'s behaviour is identical for every input that does not reach the probe.

## Why the two belong in one PR

Commit 2 is what makes the throttle reachable. Today a wide model accepts tier 1 and returns immediately, so tier 2 is never sent. Once acceptance escalates, the second call is a 12.2 MB upload — and that is precisely the call that came back throttled in my measurement, after 256 s, with boto3 having already spent its four internal retries. Landing commit 2 without commit 1 would mean a wide model can get throttled and then answer by uploading more. They also touch adjacent lines of the same function, so as separate PRs the second would go stale against the first.

They are still two commits, independently coherent, if you would rather take only one.

## Known cost, stated up front

**Commit 2 makes a second probe call for models wider than the first tier, and an accepted probe is billed.** A rejected probe is free — length validation runs before inference — but an acceptance bills the padded input. Per probe, worst case goes from ~1.44M input tokens (tier 1 only) to ~3.9M (both tiers). It buys the exact window instead of a floor, and it only happens for models whose window exceeds ~1.44M actual tokens. #104128 (@rodrigogs) is adding a negative memo so a repeatedly-failing probe stops re-sending these payloads at all, which bounds the repetition; the two changes compose and do not conflict (see below).

## How to Test

```bash
# the six new tests against the old implementation
git checkout 9e6c4100cb                        # this PR's base
git checkout fix/bedrock-probe-escalation-and-floor -- tests/agent/test_bedrock_adapter.py
pytest tests/agent/test_bedrock_adapter.py -q -p no:randomly \
       -k "throttle or numberless or opaque_server or accepted"
#  -> 5 failed, 1 passed
#     e.g. AssertionError: assert 1300000 == 2200000

git checkout fix/bedrock-probe-escalation-and-floor
pytest tests/agent/test_bedrock_adapter.py -q -p no:randomly
#  -> 84 passed   (78 on base + 6)
```

Five of the six fail on base. The sixth, `test_opaque_server_error_still_escalates`, **passes on base by design** — it is a regression guard for the escalation that must survive, not evidence of a bug. I would rather say that than present 6/6.

Every Bedrock and consumer suite on this branch: `test_bedrock_adapter.py` 84, `test_bedrock_integration.py` 35, `test_bedrock_1m_context.py` 2, `test_bedrock_empty_text_blocks.py` 3, `test_bedrock_interrupt_post_worker.py` 2, `test_bedrock_transport_replay.py` 2, `test_model_metadata.py` 121, `test_model_metadata_local_ctx.py` 37, and `test_error_classifier.py` 140 — all passed.

`ruff check .` passes repo-wide.

## Relationship to the other two open PRs in this area

Both verified with a real three-way merge against this branch's head, not assumed:

| | files | `git merge-tree` vs this branch |
|---|---|---|
| #106492 (mine, Llama 4 table rows) | `bedrock_adapter.py`, `test_bedrock_adapter.py` | **clean** |
| #104128 (@rodrigogs, probe caching) | `model_metadata.py`, `test_model_metadata.py` | **clean**, no file overlap |

**#106492 is the PR that asked for this.** Its *Known limitation* section says the Scout row only takes effect on the no-region path, because the probe returns `1,300,000` for a 3.5M model, and offers to send the probe fix separately. This is that PR. Either can land first: with only this one, Scout's table value is still 128K so the floor `1,300,000` wins and nothing changes; with only #106492, the region path still answers `1,300,000`; with both, it answers `3,500,000`.

**#104128 matters for the design, not the diff.** It reworks `_resolve_bedrock_context_length` to call `probe_bedrock_context_length` directly and `save_context_length` the result. That is why commit 2 puts the floor-vs-table comparison **inside the probe** rather than in `get_bedrock_context_length` — under #104128 a fix in the getter would be bypassed on that path, and the truncated `1,300,000` would be persisted. Returning `None` when the table knows more also respects #104128's stated invariant that only a probed value may be cached.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) — two commits, both `fix(bedrock): ...`
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate — `probe_bedrock_context_length` and `BEDROCK_PROBE_TIERS` return only #104128 (different file, different problem), my own #98522 (being closed) and my own #106492
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix (2 files, two commits)
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — partially; the note below is why
- [x] I've added tests for my changes — 6, five of which fail on base
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Amazon Linux 2023 x86_64, CPython 3.11.14

**What I ran, and what I could not.** The complete `tests/agent/` directory on both sides, so the number is attributable:

| | `tests/agent/` |
|---|---|
| base `9e6c4100cb` | 32 failed, 6621 passed, 31 skipped |
| this branch | 32 failed, **6627 passed**, 31 skipped |

`+6 passed` — exactly the tests this PR adds — and the failing set is **identical**: `diff` of the sorted `FAILED` lines is empty. Those 32 are pre-existing on `main` in my environment; 18 of them are the three `test_auxiliary_*` files, the rest are skill-command / provider-resolution cases. Nothing that reads a context window.

I did **not** get a whole-`tests/` run: my box hits 36 collection errors from optional dependencies I don't have (`aiohttp` and the acp/gateway stack), and the remainder exceeds my remote-execution time ceiling. Rather than tick the box on a number I can't attribute, it stays unticked with the scoped run shown above.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation — the docstring and the two comment blocks in the probe are the documentation for this behaviour; no `docs/` change applies
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` — N/A, no config keys
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md` — N/A, no architecture or workflow change
- [x] Cross-platform impact — N/A, no platform-conditional code
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas — N/A, no tool behaviour change

## Screenshots / Logs

Measured 2026-09-09 against `bedrock-runtime` `Converse` from my own AWS account, padding with the production expression `"data " * int(target / _WORDS_PER_TOKEN)` — so these are the exact payloads the tiers send. Actual tokens land at ≈1.111 per target unit.

**The two tiers against models of known width:**

| model | table window | target (= tier) | payload | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `us.meta.llama3-3-70b-instruct-v1:0` | 131,072 | 1,300,000 | 7.2 MB | rejected, **parseable** — `maximum context length is 131072 tokens` |
| `us.meta.llama3-3-70b-instruct-v1:0` | 131,072 | 2,200,000 | 12.2 MB | rejected, **parseable** — same number |
| `us.meta.llama4-maverick-17b-instruct-v1:0` | 1,048,576 | 2,200,000 | 12.2 MB | rejected, **parseable** — `maximum context length is 1048576 tokens` |
| `us.meta.llama4-scout-17b-instruct-v1:0` | 3,500,000 | 2,200,000 | 12.2 MB | **`ThrottlingException` … `Too many tokens, please wait before trying again.` after 256.0 s, `reached max retries: 4`** |

That last row is the one commit 1 exists for, and it is not a contrived case: Scout accepts tier 1, so under commit 2 it always proceeds to this call.

Two things worth recording, since both cost me a wrong reading first:

- **Inside the current tiers, length rejections are parseable.** I expected to find the numberless shape here and did not. It needs a far larger overshoot: a 5,000,000-token target (27.8 MB) returns `Input is too long for requested model.` for both Llama 4 models in both `us-east-1` and `us-east-2`. So the numberless shape is what escalation *produces*, which is the argument against escalating into it — and it is why I could not reproduce the error string my own #98522 quoted.
- **A throttle raises exactly like a length rejection.** Earlier in this measurement, three results I first recorded as rejections were `Too many tokens, please wait before trying again`, which carries no window at all. Only `classify_api_error` separating `rate_limit` from `context_overflow` distinguishes them.

**The live classifier's verdicts on the measured strings**, since the whole fix rests on them (`agent/error_classifier.py`, no network):

| measured string | `classify_api_error(...).reason` |
|---|---|
| `ThrottlingException … Too many tokens, please wait before trying again.` | `rate_limit` → stop |
| `ValidationException … Input is too long for requested model.` | `context_overflow` → stop |
| `ValidationException … maximum context length is 131072 tokens …` | `context_overflow` (never reached — parsed and returned first) |
| `InternalServerException … Internal server error` | `unknown` → escalate, as before |

**Commit 2 is provably behaviour-preserving on today's table.** Computed by importing the module at this PR's base: `BEDROCK_CONTEXT_LENGTHS` has 28 entries taking five distinct values — 128,000 / 200,000 / 272,000 / 300,000 / 1,000,000 — so its maximum is `1,000,000`, below the `1,300,000` first tier. The new floor-vs-table comparison therefore cannot change any lookup that resolves against `main` as it stands. It starts mattering with the `3,500,000` Scout row in #106492.

The probe path this affects is `_resolve_bedrock_context_length` (`agent/model_metadata.py:1687`), which calls `get_bedrock_context_length(model, region=region, probe=bool(region))` at `:1705`. The no-region caller at `:1670` never reaches the probe and is untouched.

This updates the holographic entry from 0.30.0 (merged in #157174) to the released 0.31.2, pinned to e4b7552a19f524d57db4ed54a38cbf9009f22f03. It replaces 0.30.2, 0.31.0 and 0.31.1, which this PR proposed first and which 0.31.2 contains.

**0.30.2:** `auto_extract` takes the compaction helpers it uses (`_MERGED_PRIOR_CONTEXT_HEADER`, `_MERGED_SUMMARY_DELIMITER`, `is_compaction_summary_message`) from `session_rules.turns`, where v0.23.3 moved them, falling back to `agent.context_compressor` on older cores.

**0.31.0** (`auto_extract` stays off by default):
- Turns the gateway injects as `role="user"` are no longer stored as facts about the person: delegation notices, skill prompts, system notes, preserved task lists and planning carryovers, `[System:` / `[CONTEXT` rows, cron wrappers, `<memory-context>` blocks (the prefixes follow the core's `_SYNTHETIC_USER_ROW_PREFIXES`).
- The person's words behind the gateway's notes (the cron hint and run time, an interrupted-turn system note, a quoted reply) and inside a `/steer` are kept; of a slash skill only the typed instruction is kept (the core's `extract_user_instruction_from_skill_message`).
- Spanish preferences and decisions.
- A reply to a cron delivery no longer counts the quoted report as the person's words, in recall before a turn too.

**0.31.1:** a `fact_store` write takes only the four categories the tool declares (`user_pref`, `project`, `tool`, `general`); another value is refused with the four named, and search and list still filter by any category a store already holds (reported by HouMinXi).

**0.31.2:** two screen patterns run in linear time and decide every text as before: a credential value that almost names a model no longer backtracks exponentially ("tokens gpt" + 28 letters + "/" took 11 s), and a long word without a Latin letter is no longer rescanned from each letter (12 000 CJK characters took 1.8 s).

Contributions by abcapr and Tormen28. No change to defaults, schema or network behaviour. Checked against v0.23.3: the plugin's CI, release lane (v0.23.3) included, 6/6 on 0.31.2.

# Update privacy-shield → 1.9.5 and injection-shield → 0.9.1 (MOTHR/hermes-security-suite)

Owner pin-bump per the catalog schema (sha + version bumped together, Rule 5 continuation of PR #150309). Both entries move from `ec34c44` to the suite `main` commit `6ef24dfc575f8c44df514e486ed869f11b754f49`.

## What's in the range (ec34c44 → 6ef24dfc)

**privacy-shield 1.9.3 → 1.9.5** (three community-fixed releases):
- **1.9.4** — Issue #7: reasoning-redaction read-only property path (`qwen/llama.cpp`) is now primary with dict-synthesis as fallback; loud `reasoning_redaction_failed` event + unredacted-block blocking on double failure (commit `7a819e2`).
- **1.9.5** — Issue #5: BIC detector hardened per ISO 9362 (strict 8/11 length, registered ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 at positions 5–6, curated common-word blocklist — the reporter's verification table cases all pass: 0 FP / 0 misses); delegated-subagent transit restore made lossless (commit `ec49aa2`); Issue #6: `transform_is_inline` signal restores exactly once on mid-string token restore (commit `02c1b5d`); lint-noqa fix (commit `22fe3b2`).

**injection-shield 0.8.2 → 0.9.1:**
- **0.9.0** — FrontierBreach P0: `destructive_ops` category + severity-gated `pre_tool_call` blocking (review waves 1–3: orakel/agent-smith/seraph; commit `494d00b` ff.).
- **0.9.1** — Store install-scanner compliance: defense-in-depth firewall text assembles its example phrases at runtime, demo defaults reworded (dashboard smoke test still demonstrates a real hit: 1 violation, high/injection), stale `build/` artifacts removed (commit `6ef24df`).

## Validation at the new pin (`6ef24dfc…`, fresh-clone workflow per schema)

- `hermes plugins validate privacy-shield --install-deps` — **Validation passed**
- `hermes plugins validate injection-shield --install-deps` — **Validation passed**
- `hermes plugins doctor --ci` both packages — **OK** (0 tools, 5/6 hooks registered)
- Install-scanner (`tools.plugin_guard.scan_plugin`) on both packages — **safe** (before: `dangerous` on private detector-name collisions; now verdict-safe)
- Suite test suite — **515/515 passed** (injection-shield), CI on suite `main` green at the pin
- Peer review: orakel t_908b8d61 (round 1: CHANGES-REQUIRED → both blockers D1/D2 fixed) + round-2 re-verify t_67110f11 = **APPROVE**, evidence-based on commit bytes (git-archive replay)

## Note for maintainers: stale `build/` artifacts can flip the scanner

The install-scanner's directory exclusions cover `.git`, `__pycache__`, `node_modules`, venvs and cache dirs — but **not** `build/`. A plugin checkout with a historical `build/lib/...` copy gets scanned with *both* the current and stale sources, which can produce phantom high/critical findings with unchanged code (this is how our `0.8.2`-era pin would now fail validation, while the code is unchanged). Suggestion on our side is included in 0.9.1 (removed the artifacts); upstream-side, adding `build`/`dist` to `_EXCLUDED_DIRS` would make validation robust for the same class of checkout.

prs.title: feat(mattermost): optional per-thread sessions for DMs
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds an opt-in `dm_thread_sessions` to the Mattermost adapter.

With `reply_mode: thread`, a top-level channel post already counts as a thread root and gets its own session; the same check excludes DMs. In a DM that means your message carries no `thread_id`, the answer nests under it, and your follow-up inside that thread carries a `root_id` and keys a different session — so the thread starts without the message that started it. Same split as #138303, seen from the other side.

With `dm_thread_sessions: true` the top-level DM post becomes the root itself, so the message and everything under it share one session from the first turn. It is the DM half of #37144 / #54229, behind a config key because the current behaviour (one long DM session) is what some setups want and flipping it for everyone is what #138318 is about.

Default `false`. Channel behaviour is unchanged either way.

## Related Issue

None — opt-in behaviour, no issue to fix.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/mattermost/adapter.py`: `dm_thread_sessions` read from the platform `extra`; `_handle_ws_event` includes DMs in the top-level-post-as-thread-root assignment when it is on.
- `tests/gateway/test_mattermost.py`: `_make_adapter(**extra)` accepts overrides; two tests — the default keeps the DM session (`thread_id is None`), the flag makes the post its own root.
- `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/mattermost.md`: the key documented in the session-model section.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/gateway/test_mattermost.py -q` → 31 passed, the 2 new ones included.
2. `scripts/hermes-python scripts/check` → 22 checks, ok; code health 0 blocking.
3. Live, on a Mattermost platform with `reply_mode: thread` and `dm_thread_sessions: true`: send a DM that is not a reply, then answer in the thread it opened. Both turns log one session; the next fresh DM starts a new one.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate — #54229, #138318 and #94067 touch the same DM session code; this change stays behind a key, so none of them are overrun
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix/feature (no unrelated commits)
- [x] I've run the tests for the code I changed and they pass: `pytest tests/gateway/test_mattermost.py -q` → 31 passed
- [x] `just check` passes — ran as `scripts/hermes-python scripts/check` on this branch: 22 checks, ok

prs.title: bedrock: don't turn unparseable streamed tool input into {}
prs.body:
On the ConverseStream path, `normalize_converse_stream_events` builds each tool call from the accumulated `toolUse` input via `_parse_tool_args`, which returns `{}` on a JSON error (`agent/bedrock_adapter.py`, `contentBlockStop` branch). If the input is incomplete, because the stream was cut or Bedrock ends the message with `stopReason: malformed_tool_use`, the call reaches the loop with arguments `"{}"`. That is valid JSON, so `turn_tool_validation` accepts it and the tool is dispatched with no arguments. A tool with required params returns an error that the model reads as its own mistake. A tool whose params are all optional runs its default action. `malformed_tool_use` is also not in the stop-reason map, so it falls back to `stop` and gets upgraded to `tool_calls`.

With this change, input that doesn't parse is passed through raw as the call's `arguments`. The loop's existing invalid-JSON handling then applies: truncated args are refused, other bad JSON is retried. Empty input still becomes `{}` (no-argument tools), and the `bedrock_content_blocks` sidecar still stores the decoded object, because Converse requires a JSON document when the turn is replayed.

The new test in `tests/agent/test_bedrock_adapter.py` streams a cut-off `write_file` input with `malformed_tool_use` and asserts that the arguments do not decode. It fails on main (`DID NOT RAISE`) and passes here. All 11 `tests/agent/*bedrock*` files pass (178 passed, 8 skipped).

# Hermes Agent v0.23.4

**Release Date:** November 23, 2026

> Patch release. This tag rolls up the ~229 PRs merged since v0.23.3 into a stable release for the GitHub release (CLI and installers), the Microsoft Store app, Docker and Hermes Cloud. Full curated notes for this window ship with v0.24.0.

<!-- HERMES_BUILDS_TABLE -->

## About this release

Measured at commit `8fc03744473`, the window since v0.23.3 contains **1,122 non-merge commits** across **1,316 changed files** (+96,873 / −6,703), **229 merged PRs** and **281 closed issues**.

Also in the window, undocumented here on purpose: Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Neon and Carbon on Nous Portal, OpenRouter and Vertex, `hermes gateway migrate --backends` to move an old serve/dashboard backend onto the gateway (with a System page card in the dashboard), `hermes plugins config` to edit a plugin's settings from the terminal, approval cards in Desktop for a sandbox's folder and site requests, gateway clients announcing who they are so plugins can see which client sent a turn, a long run of Desktop streaming and transcript performance work, a retryable indicator for slow profile switches, `hermes dashboard password` without a TTY prompt, configurable skill index description length (`skills.index_desc_limit`), managed-scope config honored by security and URL-safety reads, and a large batch of new plugin-catalog entries.

**Full curated release notes for this window ship with v0.24.0**, which will document everything from v0.23.0 onward — highlights, feature areas, and complete contributor credits. Nothing in this window is skipped.

## Updating

- Microsoft Store app: updates through the Store.
- Desktop app installed from the installer (.exe / .dmg): no change in this release; it updates with the next bundled release.
- CLI: `hermes update`, or re-run the installer one-liner.
- Docker / Hermes Cloud: `nousresearch/hermes-agent:stable` (or `:latest`).

**Full Changelog**: [v0.23.3...v0.23.4](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/compare/v0.23.3...v0.23.4)

prs.title: Sync with upstream/main (1095 commits) + forward-port magicform customizations
prs.body:
## Summary

- Merges ~1095 commits from `sipeed/picoclaw` `upstream/main` (last sync was at `7ea7bb0`).
- Forward-ports our 6 customization commits onto upstream's restructured layout: agent loop split into `agent_*.go`, tools reorganized into `pkg/tools/{fs,integration}/`, channel config moved to a map+Settings model.
- Drops the launcher subsystem (deps deleted upstream, MagicForm doesn't use it).
- Phase 1 of the multi-tenancy port: tenant hints from `bus.InboundContext.Raw` plumb onto `processOptions`. Phase 2 (effSessions/effProvider/effContextBuilder threading) is deferred to a follow-up PR.
- New `MAGICFORM_CUSTOMIZATIONS.md` indexes the fork's customizations by subsystem so future syncs are predictable.

## Commit shape (deliberately one-customization-per-commit for sync friendliness)

```
763e5690 docs: add MAGICFORM_CUSTOMIZATIONS.md sync index
9a0b2817 forward-port: multi-tenancy hint plumbing on agent processOptions (phase 1)
cd1720f4 forward-port: write size cap + crypto/rand temp suffixes in fs sandbox
94d28c1b forward-port: bound search response size with LimitReader
0c8ebde2 forward-port: register magicform channel in gateway init
93fb7b87 Merge upstream/main into sync/upstream-2026-05-07
```

## Notable upstream changes incorporated

- Agent loop split (#2585) — `pkg/agent/loop.go` → 30+ `agent_*.go` files. Multi-tenancy customization moved into a new isolated `agent_tenant.go` to minimise future conflict surface.
- Tool packages reorganized (`4c133dc2`) — `pkg/tools/{filesystem,web}.go` → `pkg/tools/{fs,integration}/`. Hardening re-applied at the new locations.
- Launcher migrated to `web/backend/` (#1275) — old launcher dropped (see below).
- Channel config switched to map+Settings model — `MagicFormConfig` rewritten as `MagicFormSettings` with `SecureString` token, registered alongside other channels in `config_channel.go`.
- `AgentDefaults.Model` deprecated field removed; `SessionConfig.DMScope` replaced by `Dimensions`; `Config.Bindings` replaced by upstream's legacy bindings migration.

## Things that changed in our fork

- **Launcher dropped.** Half its dependencies were deleted upstream (`auth_config.go`, `process.go`, `server_test.go`, etc.), and MagicForm doesn't use the launcher's HTTP API. Upstream's `web/backend/` is the replacement when an admin UI is needed.
- **Multi-tenancy split into phases.** Phase 1 (this PR) validates and plumbs tenant hints onto `processOptions`. Phase 2 (next PR) wires `effSessions`/`effContextBuilder`/`effProvider`/`effModel` through the turn execution path. Phase 1 is a no-op functionally for current MagicForm traffic (which doesn't yet send webhooks) but locks in the protocol so phase 2 is a clean diff against the agent loop only.
- **Workspace overlays using the deprecated `model` JSON key are now silently ignored.** Migrate them to `model_name`.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./pkg/... ./cmd/...` (excluding matrix, which has a Windows+CGO=0 libolm constraint that's environment-only and pre-existing)
- [x] `go test ./pkg/agent/` — tenant-extraction tests pass (4 happy-path/escape/no-boundary/CSV cases)
- [x] `go test ./pkg/pathutil/` — workspace-boundary resolver tests pass
- [x] `go test ./pkg/tools/integration/` — web tool tests pass
- [x] `go test ./cmd/picoclaw/internal/agent/` — workspace path validation tests pass
- [ ] CI build on Linux (matrix/libolm needs gcc + CGO; should be set up in CI)
- [ ] Manual smoke test of agent CLI: `picoclaw agent "hello" --workspace tenant-a` against a workspace_root config
- [ ] Manual smoke test of magicform webhook (deferred until MagicForm starts sending)

Two pre-existing test failures are environment-specific Windows issues unrelated to this PR (`TestSecurityPath` hardcodes Unix path separators; `TestHostRW_Read_PermissionDenied` uses Unix file modes).

## Out of scope (follow-up PR candidates)

- Phase 2 multi-tenancy: actual session/provider isolation per turn
- Forward-port launcher security hardening to `web/backend/` if/when MagicForm starts using it
- Documentation refresh (`docs/cli.md`, `docs/magicform-integration.md`) for new upstream features

prs.title: WIP: feat: base multi-agent collaboration framework & shared context
prs.body:
## 📝 Description

**WIP** — Base multi-agent collaboration framework with shared context pool, agent handoff, and discovery tools.

Builds on top of the merged PRs #213 (provider protocol refactor) and #131 (model fallback chain + multi-agent routing) to add:

- **Blackboard** — Thread-safe shared key-value context pool (`pkg/multiagent/blackboard.go`) for inter-agent data sharing with scoped entries (author, scope, timestamp)
- **BlackboardTool** — LLM-callable tool for read/write/list/delete on the shared context
- **Agent Handoff** — Synchronous delegation between agents via `ExecuteHandoff()` with automatic context propagation through the blackboard
- **HandoffTool** — LLM-callable tool that resolves target agent, writes context, builds system prompt, and delegates via `RunToolLoop`
- **ListAgentsTool** — Discovery tool listing all registered agents with ID/Name/Role
- **AgentResolver interface** — Decouples `pkg/multiagent` from `pkg/agent` to avoid circular imports
- **AgentLoop integration** — Blackboard snapshot injection into system messages, per-session blackboards via `sync.Map`, tools auto-registered when >1 agent configured
- **Config extensions** — `Role` and `SystemPrompt` fields on `AgentConfig` and `AgentInstance`

### Architecture decisions
- Zero overhead for single-agent setups (multi-agent tools only registered when `len(registry.ListAgentIDs()) > 1`)
- `registryResolver` adapter bridges `AgentRegistry` → `multiagent.AgentResolver` at the integration boundary
- Blackboard entries carry authorship metadata for audit/debugging

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## 🔗 Related Issue

Closes #294

## 📚 Technical Context (Skip for Docs)
- **Reference URL:** https://github.com/sipeed/picoclaw/issues/294
- **Reasoning:** Foundation layer for multi-agent collaboration. Blackboard pattern enables shared state without tight coupling. Handoff mechanism provides synchronous delegation with context propagation. Built on merged PR #213 (protocol refactor) and PR #131 (routing + fallback chain).

- **Hardware:** Linux x86_64
- **OS:** Ubuntu (kernel 6.11.0-29-generic)
- **Model/Provider:** Claude CLI (claude-code), Codex CLI (codex-code) — both integration tested

**Integration tests**: Claude CLI (3/3 PASS), Codex CLI (3/3 PASS)

issues.title: ncl groups config add-mount silently mounts read-only — CLI never stores readonly:false

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

issues.body:
## Repro

```bash
ncl groups config add-mount --id <group> --host /path/to/data --container data
ncl groups restart --id <group>
```

The mount appears in the container at `/workspace/extra/data`, but read-only: `docker inspect` shows `RW=false`, and any agent write fails.

## Cause

Two defaults disagree:

- The CLI's `add-mount` only has a `--ro` flag. Without it, the stored `additional_mounts` entry contains **no `readonly` key at all** (`{"hostPath": ..., "containerPath": ...}`).
- `validateMount` (`src/modules/mount-security/index.ts`) computes `requestedReadWrite = mount.readonly === false` — an **absent** key is treated as a read-only request, so even a root with `allowReadWrite: true` in the mount allowlist ends up mounted ro.

So the CLI's implied default (rw unless `--ro`) never survives to spawn time: every `add-mount` without `--ro` lands read-only, silently — no warning, no error, the config just doesn't do what the command suggested.

## Suggested fix (either works)

1. `add-mount` stores `"readonly": false` explicitly when `--ro` is not passed (keeps the security-side conservative default for hand-edited configs), or
2. `add-mount` gains a required explicit choice / prints the effective mode back, so the operator sees `readonly: true` at add time instead of discovering it from failed agent writes.

Workaround meanwhile: update the stored JSON to include `"readonly": false` and restart the group.

issues.title: [bug] ncl ignores flags written as --name=value

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

labels.name: triage/unresolved
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer triage. Applied by issue forms

issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

53099d28

### Host platform

macOS

### What happened?

`ncl` does not understand the `--name=value` form. `src/cli/parse-argv.ts:24-33` takes everything after `--` as the key, so `--rebuild=true` becomes a flag named `rebuild=true` with the value `true`. No command reads that key, so the flag is dropped without an error.

For a required flag this fails loudly (`ncl groups config add-mount --id=ag1 ...` gives "--id is required"). For an optional flag it fails silently:

- `ncl groups restart --id ag1 --rebuild=true` restarts without a rebuild.
- Once #3742 lands, `ncl groups config add-mount ... --ro=true --rw` will store a read-write request, because `--ro=true` is never seen.

### What did you expect?

Either `--name=value` works the same as `--name value`, or `ncl` rejects it with a clear error. A silently ignored flag is the worst of the three.

### How can we reproduce it?

From a checkout at 53099d28:

```
pnpm exec tsx -e "import {parseArgv} from './src/cli/parse-argv.ts'; console.log(JSON.stringify(parseArgv(['groups','restart','--id','ag1','--rebuild=true'])))"
```

Output:

```
{"command":"groups-restart","args":{"id":"ag1","rebuild=true":true},"json":false,"stdinJson":false}
```

### Suggested fix

Split on the first `=` in `parseArgv`, so `--name=value` sets `name` to `value`. It is a few lines, and it covers every command at once. Rejecting the form instead also works, but users of other CLIs expect it to work.

Found while reviewing #3742.

Assisted by Claude; reviewed and verified by a human before submission.

issues.title: channels package.json can drift from the versions skills pin, and no check catches it

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something is not working as expected

labels.name: triage/unresolved
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer triage. Applied by issue forms

issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

channels bb4127cfe, main (skill pins as of 2026-11-23)

### Host platform

Other

### What happened?

The `channels` branch has its own `package.json` and lockfile for the channel adapters. The skills on `main` pin their own versions. Nothing checks that the two match, so they drift:

- **Baileys:** `add-whatsapp` pinned `7.0.0-rc14` (#4024), but `channels` still resolved `7.0.0-rc.9` until #4516 fixed it by hand.
- **Resend, today:** `add-resend` pins `@resend/chat-sdk-adapter@0.3.0` (since #4042, 2026-10-17). `channels` still has `^0.1.1`, and its lockfile resolves `0.1.1`.

So the tests on `channels` run against a different adapter version than the one users get when they install the skill.

### What did you expect?

A CI check fails when a package in the `channels` `package.json` has a different version than the one a skill pins for it, and names the fix.

### How can we reproduce it?

1. `git show origin/main:.claude/skills/add-resend/SKILL.md | grep resend/chat-sdk-adapter@` gives `0.3.0`.
2. `git show origin/channels:package.json | grep resend/chat-sdk-adapter` gives `^0.1.1`.
3. CI on both branches is green.

### Install or update path

Development checkout

### Notes

Related: #3155 (registry branches drift from `main` in code). This issue is about dependency versions only.

`skill-pins:check` compares the skills with `.github/skill-pins/package.json` on `main` only. `dependencyProblems()` in `scripts/test-registry-skills.ts` checks the `package.json` after a skill is applied, not the one on `channels` (as #4516 says). Of the 20 packages both files list, Resend is the only mismatch today.

prs.title: feat(skills): add /add-antigravity with its own payload
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/add-antigravity`, a provider skill that runs agent groups on Google's Antigravity CLI (`agy`) and Gemini models, switchable per group with `ncl groups config update --provider antigravity`.
- **Problem**: there is no way to run a NanoClaw agent on Gemini through Google's own agent harness; OpenCode reaches Gemini models but not Antigravity's tools, planning and conversation store.
- **Fix**: a provider skill shaped like `/add-cursor`. All code and tests live in the skill's `payload/`; apply wires the five provider barrels and adds a pinned, sha512-checked `agy` 1.5.8 to the agent image. Auth is a Gemini API key held only by the credential gateway; the container sees a placeholder.
- **Out of scope**: Google-account (OAuth) sign-in, which Google's terms do not allow from a third-party harness; a generic manifest for native binaries (see "Core changes" below).

<details>
<summary>Core changes outside the skill, and why</summary>

agy is a native Go binary that is not published on npm, so `container/cli-tools.json` (npm only) cannot install it. The block has to run as root, before the setuid sweep and `USER node`, and is best placed above the often-bumped layers so a lockfile or Claude Code bump does not re-download 265 MB. No existing hook does that, so this PR adds one:

- `container/Dockerfile`: an empty `# >>> nanoclaw:provider-binaries` / `# <<< nanoclaw:provider-binaries` marker region just above `# ---- agent-runner deps`. With nothing installed it changes no layer.
- `docs/skill-directives.md`, `scripts/skill-directives.ts` (comment), `docs/skill-guidelines.md`, `docs/skills-model.md`: one line each naming the region as the native-binary path.
- `scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts`: the scratch root gets a stub Dockerfile carrying the region, the same way it already stubs `cli-tools.json`.

Alternatives considered: a prose-only Dockerfile edit like `/add-mnemon` breaks setup's deterministic provider install (`setup/providers/install.ts` fails on any step it cannot apply); appending at end of file with `USER root`/`USER node` breaks on remove, which deletes by line and would also delete core's own `USER node`. A `json-merge` manifest for native binaries (url + sha512 per arch) would be cleaner long term but is a bigger core feature. I'm happy to split the marker into its own PR first, or to rework it into a manifest, if you prefer.

Other edits: the `registry-skills.yml` matrix entry, the provider list in `skill-descriptor.test.ts`, `.github/skill-pins/not-covered.json` (regenerated; `AGY_VERSION=1.5.8` now appears as a hand-checked binary pin), and README (Antigravity listed next to Codex, Cursor and OpenCode).
</details>

## Related work

No issue. It is a self-contained provider skill in the `/add-cursor` shape (#4107), so it can be reviewed directly; nothing changes for installs that don't apply it.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation
- `pnpm run format:check`, `pnpm run skill-pins:check`, `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint` -> pass (lint: 0 errors)
- `pnpm test` -> pass: 345 files, 5082 tests
- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/test-registry-skills.ts add-antigravity` -> pass: apply, host and container typecheck, payload tests (vitest 102, bun 87), provider-contract verifier (9/9), image build (agy 1.5.8 amd64, `cli.tar.gz: OK`), byte-exact remove, re-apply
- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/test-registry-skills.ts --combined-providers` -> pass with codex, cursor and opencode (vitest 288 passed, bun 462 passed)
- **Live end-to-end on Linux x64** (Docker, Iron Proxy gateway, CLI channel, real Gemini key): two turns in one session; resume after `ncl groups restart` (new container, `--conversation` reused, earlier codeword recalled); the `conversations/` archive written with both exchanges; inside the container `ps` shows agy and no claude; the gateway saw only Google hosts (0 Anthropic requests); `REMOVE.md` restored the tree byte-exact and re-apply reproduced it. The real key was found nowhere in container env or filesystem, the image, logs, process args or the checkout. An earlier run of the same setup also covered file and shell tools, MCP `send_message`, `ask_user_question`, and a 12-case scripted eval against the live API.
- **arm64**:
  - (a) Native GitHub `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runner ([run](https://github.com/kennethleungty/nanoclaw/actions/runs/44118483750)): apply/remove, image build, all tests (bun 759 pass), and agy reaching the Gemini API from the arm64 image.
  - (b) QEMU-emulated arm64 on x64: full NanoClaw chat behind the gateway (reply, resume, tools, MCP, `ask_user_question`).
  - (c) Both ran before the installer switched from `TARGETARCH` to `uname -m`, so the final 5-line block was rebuilt for arm64 under QEMU on the pinned base image: arm64 tarball selected, sha512 OK, `agy --version` 1.5.8 on aarch64 as `node`. A mismatched `AGY_VERSION` stops the build before any download.
- **Live on a real chat app, behind OneCLI**: a long-running downstream install (2026.10.0 core, OneCLI 1.42 gateway, Telegram channel, GCP e2-small x86_64). That core predates the Dockerfile region and the exchange archive (#4105), so both were backported first, plus the provider list in `skill-descriptor.test.ts`. The skill's own pre-flight check then passed and its directives applied cleanly (host build, runtime typecheck, payload tests, verifier 9/9, image build with agy 1.5.8). The key went in through `setup/index.ts --step provider-auth antigravity` at the masked prompt and landed in OneCLI as a project-scoped secret for `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` with `x-goog-api-key` injection. Then the group was switched with `ncl groups config update --provider antigravity`:
  - Messages sent from the Telegram mobile app were answered by agy. In the session container `agy … --model gemini-4-hydrogen-medium --conversation <id>` was running, and there were 0 `claude` processes.
  - The container env held only `GEMINI_API_KEY=nc-antigravity-placeholder`, and OneCLI logged only Google hosts (`generativelanguage`, `play`), with 0 Anthropic requests.
  - The conversation resumed across a model change and `ncl groups restart`, and one `conversations/` archive covered both turns.
  - `agy models` from inside the container, through the gateway, listed the slugs the key can use.
  - Replies arrived about 11 s after the Telegram message on `gemini-4-hydrogen-medium`, including a cold container start.
  - On current `main`, OneCLI also records the connection for the group's provider from `provider: 'antigravity'`, the same target shape as `/add-cursor`, asserted in `setup/providers/antigravity.test.ts`.
- **Apple Silicon** (`macOS arm64`, Darwin 27.2.0, Node v24.15.0, commit `009028b`):
  - Static and CI checks: `pnpm run format:check`, `pnpm run skill-pins:check`, host and container `tsc --noEmit`, `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run lint` (0 errors), and `registry-skills.yml` matrix discovery (`23/23`) -> pass.
  - Skill lifecycle and composition (host-side, no local Docker daemon): `scripts/test-registry-skills.ts add-antigravity` (pre-flight, 21 payload files, 5 barrels, `Dockerfile` `nanoclaw:provider-binaries` block, host/setup 101 pass, container 87 pass, `provider-contract-verifier` 9/9, byte-exact `REMOVE.md` restore and re-apply) and `--combined-providers` with codex, cursor and opencode (`update-skills` refresh, verifier 9/9, 287 host + 462 container pass) -> pass; both pinned `1.5.8` (`4602374149505024`) `amd64` and `arm64` tarballs verified `OK` with macOS `/sbin/sha512sum -c`. (Docker Desktop on Apple Silicon runs the same `linux/arm64` image validated on the native arm64 runner and QEMU runs above.)
  - Live agy 1.5.8 native integration on Darwin `arm64`: `antigravity.native.test.ts` (7/7 pass) against the signed macOS `arm64` agy 1.5.8 binary — two-turn stream-JSON session with `nanoclaw.md` memory rules and `x-goog-api-key: nc-antigravity-placeholder`, `--conversation` resume, unknown-conversation fallback notice, stdio MCP tool call across macOS `/var/folders -> /private/var/folders` symlink, turn abort, HTTP 400 auth classification, and queued follow-up respawn; plus `HTTPS_PROXY` + `SSL_CERT_FILE` TLS gateway check confirming `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` and `play.googleapis.com` carry only `nc-antigravity-placeholder` with zero secret leakage.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
New /add-antigravity skill: run agent groups on Google's Antigravity CLI (Gemini models) with a Gemini API key held by the credential gateway.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- **Credentials:** the Gemini key goes only to the credential gateway, through `getCredentialStore().connection()` with a `GatewayCredentialTarget` that sets `provider: 'antigravity'`. Containers get `GEMINI_API_KEY=nc-antigravity-placeholder`, which agy sends as `x-goog-api-key`; the gateway swaps it for the real key on the wire. The key is never in `.env`, container env, argv, mounts or logs. The live runs scanned for it and found it nowhere.
- **Supply chain:** one exact build (1.5.8, execution id 4602374149505024) downloaded from `storage.googleapis.com`, a sha512 pinned per architecture and checked with `sha512sum -c` before extraction, a `--version` check that fails the build, and auto-update forced off. The tarballs are byte-identical to the assets on Google's GitHub release.
- **Egress:** model domains are `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` and `play.googleapis.com` (agy telemetry, which 1.5.8 cannot turn off in API-key mode). Requests from antigravity groups pass without an approval card; with Iron Proxy, model domains are allowed install-wide (as for other providers).
- **Permissions:** agy runs with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and its terminal sandbox off (it needs user namespaces, which Docker's seccomp profile blocks), so the container is the boundary, as with the other providers. The image still ends as `node`, with no setuid binaries.
- **Prompt injection:** per-session instructions go in-band as a `<nanoclaw_system_context>` block in agy's first turn. Core's formatter escapes `<` in inbound text, so a chat message cannot forge that block.

## Skill delivery

- **Apply:** the pre-flight check refuses a core without the provider contracts, the credential-connection seam, the exchange archive or the Dockerfile region, and leaves no partial change. Apply then copies 21 payload files (host, container and setup provider code, their tests, and `container/install-antigravity.sh`). It appends one import to each of the five barrels (`src/providers`, `src/provider-contracts`, `container/agent-runner/src/providers`, `container/agent-runner/src/provider-contracts`, `setup/providers`) and adds the 5-line Dockerfile block inside the region. It then rebuilds the image and host and runs the copied tests.
- **Remove:** `REMOVE.md` reverses each step; every appended line is unique to this skill. After removal the checkout is byte-identical to before (checked by `test-registry-skills.ts`).
- **Fresh clone:** `test-registry-skills.ts` applies the skill to a fresh clone, builds, tests, removes and re-applies it, alone and combined with codex, cursor and opencode.

## Summary

The registry sign-in asks "Email me security and project updates?" with Yes preselected, so pressing Enter opts people in. It now preselects No.
