prs.title: fix(cli): add-mount --rw, so a read-write mount is expressible (--ro is currently a no-op)
prs.body:
Fixes #3690.

## The bug, plus one part #3690 doesn't mention

`ncl groups config add-mount` cannot create a read-write mount — and **`--ro` is currently a no-op**.

The handler stores `readonly: true` when `--ro` is passed and **omits the key otherwise** (`src/cli/resources/groups.ts`). `validateMount` computes `requestedReadWrite = mount.readonly === false` and starts from `effectiveReadonly = true` (`src/modules/mount-security/index.ts`), so an *absent* key is a read-only request. The two shapes the CLI can produce are therefore identical at spawn time: passing `--ro` and omitting it do the same thing, and no CLI-created mount can ever be read-write — even when the matched allowlist root has `allowReadWrite: true`.

The help text points the other way: `[--ro]` reads as "read-write by default, opt out", the inverse of what the validator does.

**There is no sanctioned path to a read-write mount today.** `/manage-mounts` manages only the allowlist and never attaches a mount to a group; templates cannot declare mounts; the setup wizard doesn't write them. What remains is hand-editing `container.json` before a `container_configs` row exists, or raw SQL into that table — which `docs/skill-guidelines.md` calls "a smell, not a workaround". So an operator can grant `allowReadWrite: true` on a root and still have no supported way to use it.

## The change

Keep the conservative default exactly as it is and add an explicit opt-in.

```ts
const readWrite = args.rw === true || args.readonly === false;
const readOnly = args.ro === true || args.readonly === true;
if (readWrite && readOnly) throw new Error('--ro and --rw are mutually exclusive');
...(readWrite ? { readonly: false } : args.ro || args.readonly ? { readonly: true } : {}),
```

- **No default changes.** With neither flag, no `readonly` key is stored — byte-for-byte today's behaviour.
- `mount-security` is untouched. The two-gate design stays: the allowlist root is the operator's standing policy, the per-mount flag is the caller's request, and requiring both still stops a caller inheriting write access from a permissive root by accident. The bug was only that the CLI couldn't express one of the two gates.
- Help text now documents `[--ro | --rw]` and states that `--rw` is granted only when the matched root also has `allowReadWrite: true`.

### Deliberately different from the issue's first suggestion

#3690 proposes storing `readonly: false` by default when `--ro` is absent. That fixes the same breakage but flips the default to read-write, which changes behaviour for every existing caller and for hand-edited configs. An explicit `--rw` fixes it with no default change. Happy to switch if maintainers prefer the other shape.

### On the issue's second suggestion (echo the effective mode)

Not done, deliberately. Knowing the effective mode at add time means calling `validateMount()`, which loads the allowlist and `realpathSync`es the host path. That would make a pure DB-write handler fail (or report "read-only") for a path that doesn't exist yet but will by restart time, and would read a possibly-stale module-cached allowlist. Both are snapshots that can be wrong by spawn — a confidently wrong answer. Instead the `--rw` path returns a `note` naming the remaining gate, alongside `added`, which already shows what was stored.

## Why this is safe

`add-mount` is `hostOnly`, and `src/cli/guard.ts` denies `hostOnly` commands **before** scope and **before** approval, at any `cli_scope`. There is also no mount surface in the agent-side tool set — `container/agent-runner/src/mcp-tools/` has `install_packages` and `add_mcp_server` only — and `config update` handles scalars, so there's no back door to `additional_mounts`. Worst case is an operator writing a mount to a directory they have already marked `allowReadWrite: true` in a file that lives outside the project root precisely so containers can't reach it.

## Tests

Four new cases in `src/cli/resources/groups.test.ts`: `--rw` ⇒ `readonly: false`; neither flag ⇒ **no `readonly` key at all** (asserted with `'readonly' in mount === false`, which is what actually pins the default — the existing test only ever passed `ro: true`); `--ro` ⇒ `readonly: true`; `--ro` + `--rw` ⇒ rejected with nothing written.

`vitest run src/cli/resources/groups.test.ts src/modules/mount-security` → 2 files, 20 passed. `tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint clean on both changed files.

Note: `docs/SECURITY.md` does not pass `prettier --check`, but that is pre-existing on unmodified `main` — I left the formatting alone rather than balloon the diff. Also left alone as out of scope: `--ro false` parses as the truthy string `"false"` and still sets read-only. `--rw` is unaffected, being checked with `=== true`.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Moves the `add-anydoc` pin to 0.2.5, since 0.1.6 ships a `zip` crate with a critical CVE.

- **Problem**: AnyDoc opens docx, xlsx, pptx and the other ZIP-based formats through the `zip` crate. 0.1.6 uses zip 8.6.0, and every 8.x release is affected by CVE-2026-115905 (critical), CVE-2026-115907, CVE-2026-115908, CVE-2026-115909 (high) and CVE-2026-115906 (moderate). Agents feed it chat attachments, so the input is untrusted.
- **Fix**: AnyDoc 0.2.5 moves to zip 9.5.1. The pin changes in the preflight script, the JSON block, `anydoc-manifest.test.ts` and `.github/skill-pins/package.json`.
- **Upgrade path**: preflight step 3 stopped on any version other than the pin. An entry at 0.1.6 is now moved to 0.2.5 on reapply, and anything else still stops.
- **Out of scope**: the container skill. Scanned PDF pages now fail with `pages N of M need OCR` instead of being dropped (0.2.4), and it already treats scanned PDFs as unsupported. Hosted OCR is opt-in, and the skill already forbids uploading without the user's authorization.

## Related work

No issue. It's a pin bump with its upgrade path, so it's safe to review directly. The Dependabot skill-pins job hasn't opened a PR for it.

prs.title: feat(setup): new installs follow the branch they were cloned from
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

A new install follows the update channel of the branch it was cloned from. Setup no longer asks, and never moves the checkout.

- **Problem**: a fresh clone installs the tip of `main` on the default `stable` channel, so once `main` is past the latest release the first `/update-nanoclaw` stops with ahead-of-release.
- **Release branches**: the repository publishes `stable` and `beta` branches next to `main`. After each release, a separate `channel-branches` job in `release.yml` moves them, fast-forward only, and each only to its channel's newest tag, the one the updater picks (`release.mjs branches`). A patch to an older line moves neither.
- **Quick Start**: the README and its Japanese, Korean and Chinese translations clone `--branch stable`, and so does the v1 migration. `beta` is one line below it.
- **Recorded, not chosen**: `nanoclaw.sh` hands setup the channel of the cloned branch (`stable` or `beta`), and setup saves it to `.env`. A clone of `main` records `stable`, the updater's default, and is told its first update waits for the next release; `--update-channel edge` follows `main`. The note prints after the splash and goes to `logs/setup.log`, with one line on how to change the channel later.
- **Explicit choice**: `--update-channel`, `NANOCLAW_UPDATE_CHANNEL`, a channel already in `.env` and the Advanced field work as before and are never overridden. Choosing stable or beta on `main` past its releases prints a hint that the first update waits. A bad env value stops setup unless a flag overrides it; uninstall ignores it.
- **Left alone**: existing installs, forks, other branches, local commits, and a local branch that only shares the name `stable` or `beta`.

**Before this merges**: the `stable` branch must exist upstream, or the new Quick Start fails. Its rulesets are already in place (`channel-branches-no-rewrite`, `channel-branches-locked`). `release.yml` creates `beta` only from a release that has `setup/lib/update-channel.sh`: a clone of older code saves no channel, so its first update would stop. Until that release, the README's `--branch beta` line fails. It also needs the `channel-branches` environment and the GitHub App that `RELEASING.md` describes: `verify` fails until the environment exists.

## Related work

Follow-up to #3986. No issue: scoped with the maintainers. See [Upgrading](https://docs.nanoclaw.dev/operate/upgrading).

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- CI at `ee80ca62` (main merged in): all checks pass.
- `setup/lib/update-channel.test.ts` (46 tests) runs the helper and the real `nanoclaw.sh` in stub official clones of `stable`, `beta` and `main`, including a shallow clone, a fork, an existing install and a local namesake branch. It checks the shell reads `.env` as the updater does, with 16 `.env` cases that the shell and the updater must read as the same channel, and that the updater resolves `stable` and `beta` from a clone of each branch.
- `scripts/release.test.ts`: 18 new tests. 12 of them run the real plan and move scripts with a fake `gh`: an existing branch only moves forward, a missing one is created, a refused move or a failed lookup still moves the other branch and fails the job, a missing App token fails the job after printing both pushes, a wrong or lightweight tag or an unpublished release moves nothing, a retry skips a branch that is already moved, and `beta` is never created from a release without the channel helper. One more checks the job wiring in the parsed workflow.
- Not run: an e2e install at this head, and the new `channel-branches` job, which only runs in a real release. It runs on a fresh runner with no checkout, so no repo code runs next to the token. It mints a 1-hour token from a GitHub App, which an organisation owner must create and add to the bypass list of the branches' ruleset. The App's key goes in the `channel-branches` environment (main only, no reviewers, so a release still needs one approval). Without the App, the job prints the `git push` for an admin to run and fails. It runs after the release is published, so a red job alerts without blocking.
- Shell changes also pass under `ubuntu:26.04` (uutils 0.10.0).

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
**New installs follow the branch they were cloned from.** `git clone --branch stable` installs the latest release and follows releases; `--branch beta` adds release candidates. A clone of `main` also follows releases; pass `--update-channel edge` to follow `main`. Switching branches later doesn't change the channel: `pnpm exec tsx scripts/update-nanoclaw.ts set-channel --channel <stable|beta|edge>` does.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- Setup no longer checks anything out or writes `.env` from the shell. It reads the current branch and the remotes' URLs, and passes a channel name to setup.
- New installs run the code `stable` and `beta` point to. Two rulesets protect them: no force-push or deletion for anyone, and creation or updates only by organisation admins. `release.yml` can move them only once a GitHub App is on that bypass list; the default Actions token cannot. The App's key lives only in the `channel-branches` environment, and the job that uses it checks out no code and moves a branch only to an annotated tag with a published, immutable release.

- [x] Not a skill
- [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

prs.title: fix(add-codex): keep the turn open on an error Codex will retry
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

A short model outage that Codex retries on its own no longer fails the reply.

- **Problem**: before each automatic retry, Codex sends `error` with `willRetry: true` ([`bespoke_event_handling.rs:1083-1100`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.169.0/codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs#L1083-L1100)). `runOneTurn` ended the turn on every `error`. So a 502 or network blip failed the reply with "Reconnecting... 2/5" while Codex went on, and the message was acked with no retry.
- **Fix**: a `willRetry: true` error yields a `progress` event and leaves the turn open. Text the broken stream left half-written is dropped. A completed message stays only if it is an answer: a final answer or an unphased message, the same rule as Codex's turn summary ([`thread_state.rs:243-251`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.169.0/codex-rs/app-server/src/thread_state.rs#L243-L251)). So commentary like "Checking the sample." is not kept as the reply (found by @poisdahl). Any other error still ends the turn.
- **From #4014** (by @poisdahl, carried over as their commit): `turn/completed` counts as a reply only with `status: 'completed'`. This is a guard: Codex 0.169.0 sets `failed` only with an error, which main already handles, and `interrupted` only after NanoClaw aborts.
- **10-minute limit (unchanged)**: Codex retries a lost connection without limit ([`responses_retry.rs:96-118`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.169.0/codex-rs/core/src/responses_retry.rs#L96-L118)). In a long outage the turn now ends at the existing 10-minute limit, not at the first retry. #4254 replaces that limit with an inactivity budget.
- **Not fixed**: Codex sends no notice for the first WebSocket retry ([`responses_retry.rs:146-160`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.169.0/codex-rs/core/src/responses_retry.rs#L146-L160)); that is #3338.
- **Not changed**: when commentary is the last thing the agent says before the turn ends, it is still the reply, as on main. Only a retry after it drops it.

## Related work

Closes #4530. Carries #4014.

Stacked on #4165, which changes the same handler. When #4165 merges, GitHub retargets this PR to main.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- add-codex container suites with the payload applied: 222 pass, `tsc -p container/agent-runner` clean; the 2 failures are the `cli-tools.json` tests the quick harness can't merge (main fails the same 2). `test-registry-skills.ts add-codex`: PASS.
- Tests in `codex.turns.test.ts`: a retry keeps the turn open and takes steered input; a completed answer survives a retry, even with commentary after it; half-written text, commentary, a partial answer and blank text do not; non-retried errors end the turn; a sub-agent's retry leaves the main turn alone; non-`completed` statuses fail; the turn deadline still applies during retries.
- Live on exe.dev (Codex 0.169.0, OpenAI API key, public wizard install of main `080bd7809`), OpenAI cut off for 14 s mid-turn: on main the first retry notice ended the turn and the user got "Sorry, something went wrong". With this PR, 4 retries showed as progress and the real reply arrived once the connection was back. A turn that spawns a sub-agent still ends with the main agent's answer.
- CI on this stacked PR runs only `label`, `template-compliance` and `verify`; the full suites run once it targets main.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below

```release-note
Codex agents no longer fail a reply when the model connection drops briefly and Codex reconnects on its own. If it stays down, the reply fails at the 10-minute turn limit instead of right away. Thanks @poisdahl (#4014).
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None. The change only affects provider event handling.

prs.title: feat: add /add-early-compact-nudge feature skill
prs.body:
## Type of Change

- [x] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)

## What

A feature skill that pushes a one-shot `<system-reminder>` into the active SDK query when effective context crosses a configurable fraction of the auto-compact ceiling. The reminder asks the agent to consider running `/compact` (with an `instructions` argument) at a natural pause point.

## Why — dynamic compaction, not a static prompt

The SDK already has a static compact prompt baked in. The problem with anything static — whether the built-in or a custom per-project override — is that it cannot know what the conversation is actually about *right now*. It produces a generic summary and drops the specific identifiers, exact phrasing, open question, and pending next step that the work depends on.

This skill is dynamic in a different sense: it doesn't replace the compact prompt at all. Instead, it nudges the agent to invoke `/compact <instructions>` itself, with an instructions payload it just wrote — informed by the conversation context it's still holding. Because the agent generates that payload from live context, the preservation rules are tailored to whatever the session is doing in that moment.

A natural follow-up is whether the nudge needs to vary between projects, workspaces, or sessions. It doesn't. The nudge text is constant; the *instructions the agent ends up passing to `/compact`* are what change, and those are produced from the agent's view of the live conversation. There's no per-project prompt to maintain.

A secondary benefit of pushing the reminder as a user message (rather than a silent context prefix) is that the agent has to acknowledge it and verbalize the decision — say whether this is a natural pause or it's mid-task — instead of being free to ignore it.

## How it works

- The Claude provider yields a new `usage` event after every assistant turn (`input_tokens + cache_read + cache_creation`).
- A pure state machine (`compact-nudge.ts`) tracks effective context. When it crosses `ceiling * ratio` for the first time in the current compact cycle, `onUsage()` returns the reminder text.
- The poll loop pushes that text into the active query via `query.push(...)`.
- The Claude provider also yields a new `compact_boundary` event; the tracker resets so the latch can re-arm if usage climbs again post-compact.

## Prior art — #2327

PR #2327 tried the same delivery mechanism — push a reminder into the active query — and was closed. This PR reuses the mechanism deliberately, with the safety rails the earlier attempt lacked:

- **One-shot per compact cycle.** A latch ensures exactly one push between compact boundaries. The earlier approach would have fired repeatedly as usage hovered near the threshold.
- **Auto-reset on `compact_boundary`.** The SDK's compaction event resets the latch so the nudge can arm again next cycle.
- **Configurable threshold + disable switch.** `COMPACT_NUDGE_RATIO` (default `0.75`) and `=0` to opt out entirely.
- **Dynamic instructions payload.** The reminder explicitly tells the agent to pass `instructions` to `/compact`, so the preserved details are written from live context rather than left to the static built-in summary.
- **Test coverage.** 19 unit + 2 integration tests around arming, one-shot semantics, post-compact re-arm, and the push wiring.

The fact that the agent treats the push as a user turn and replies to it is a feature here, not a bug — the reply surfaces the agent's compaction decision in the conversation.

## Configuration

Two env vars, both optional:

| Variable | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` | `165000` | The SDK's auto-compact ceiling (already read by the SDK). |
| `COMPACT_NUDGE_RATIO` | `0.75` | Fraction of the ceiling that arms the nudge. `0` or `>= 1` disables it. |

## How it was tested

- `bun test` — 110 agent-runner tests pass (19 unit + 16 integration + the prior 75).
- `bun run typecheck` clean.
- Unit tests cover config parsing, threshold arming, one-shot semantics, and post-compact re-arming.
- Integration tests script `usage` and `compact_boundary` events through the poll loop and assert the nudge is pushed into the active query exactly once per compact cycle.

## Usage

```
/add-early-compact-nudge
```

Merges the `skill/early-compact-nudge` branch, rebuilds the container, restarts the service. Disable later without uninstalling by setting `COMPACT_NUDGE_RATIO=0`.

prs.title: fix(agent-runner): sweep processing_ack rows whose message no longer exists
prs.body:
`sqliteGetPendingMessages` filters pending messages against every row in `processing_ack`, with no time bound:

```js
const acked = new Set(
  (outbound.prepare('SELECT message_id FROM processing_ack').all() as Array<{ message_id: string }>).map(
    ({ message_id }) => message_id,
  ),
);
const unclaimed = pending.filter(({ id }) => !acked.has(id));
```

An ack's only job is to stop one message being processed twice. Once its `messages_in` row is gone the ack can never be consumed again — but it stays in the table forever, as a filter against an id that may come back.

## The failure

`processing_ack` is keyed on the platform message id, which is assumed unique for the life of a session. When that assumption breaks, a **new** message arrives carrying an id an old ack already holds and is dropped before the agent ever sees it. The host reads the same stale row and marks the message completed, so nothing errors and nothing reaches the dropped-message log. Asked about it, the agent truthfully reports that nothing arrived.

Ids repeat more easily than the design assumes. Recreating a Telegram bot restarts its per-DM counter at 1; so does re-adding an integration, and so does any channel that numbers per conversation rather than globally.

On the install where this surfaced, a bot recreated on 2026-08-28 reset its counter, and a later message reusing id 32 matched an ack written sixteen days earlier and was never delivered. It went unnoticed for eight days — because the workaround (send it again) works, which makes the loss look like a flaky network. That is the part that seems worth fixing rather than documenting: the failure trains users not to report it.

## The fix

`sqliteClearStaleProcessingAcks` already runs at container startup to clear `processing` entries left by a crashed turn. It now also deletes acks with no corresponding `messages_in` row — no new call site, and nothing on the hot path.

That is enough for the case above: the stale rows would have been swept on the first container start after the messages they referred to were pruned, and the later message would have been delivered normally.

It also bounds a table that otherwise grows for the life of a session. The host prunes `messages_in` (expired and overflow `pending` rows) and nothing swept the acks left behind — 899 rows on one long-running session in that install.

## Tests

Three, in `sqlite.test.ts`:

- orphaned acks are removed while acks whose message still exists are kept
- a message reusing a pruned id is hidden by the stale ack, and delivered after the sweep
- `processing` entries from a crashed turn are still cleared (the existing behavior)

`bun test` in the agent-runner tree: 450 pass, 3 skip, 0 fail. `tsc --noEmit` clean.

prs.title: fix(signal): inline inbound attachments so the agent container can read them
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Lets the agent open images and files sent over Signal.

- **Problem**: signal-cli saves attachments under the host's `<SIGNAL_DATA_DIR>/attachments/`. The adapter handed the agent that host path as `[Image: /home/...]`. The container doesn't mount that directory, so the agent can't read it. Non-image files (PDFs etc.) were dropped entirely.
- **Fix**: read each saved file and attach it as base64 `data`, the same shape the chat-sdk bridge uses. `session-manager` then stages it into `/workspace/inbox/<msg>/` like Slack/Telegram/Discord attachments, and the formatter renders `[image: <name> — saved to /workspace/inbox/...]`.
- **Scope**: every attachment except a voice note that gets transcribed. Files over 25 MB, or missing on disk, become `[<type>: <name> - file not available]` instead of a dead path.
- **Out of scope**: mounting the signal-cli data dir into containers (it also holds account keys).

## Related work

Closes #2528

Overlaps open PRs #2695 (images only, same base64 approach), #2529 and #3837 (larger, bundled changes). This one is the small version that also covers PDFs and other files, with tests. Happy to close in favor of whichever a maintainer prefers.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels src/session-manager` → 92 files, 1012 passed, 20 skipped.
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p .` → clean.
- `eslint src/channels/signal*.ts` → no new errors (the two existing ones, `signal.test.ts` unused `args` and the empty `catch` in `signal.ts`, are already on `channels`).
- New `signal-attachments.test.ts`: inlines bytes, adds an extension from MIME when the id has none, marks missing/oversized files, refuses `../` ids.
- `signal.test.ts`: replaced the test that asserted the old `[Image: <host path>]` text with one that drives an image + PDF through the adapter and checks the `data` payload and that no host path appears in the text, plus a missing-file case.
- Manual: running this patch on a live v2026.11.0-rc.3 install. Before it, the agent replied that the attachments "never made it" to it. signal-cli had saved the JPEGs on the host the whole time.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Signal: images, PDFs and other files sent to the agent now land in its inbox and can be opened, instead of arriving as an unreadable host path.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Attachment ids come from signal-cli (sender-influenced). They are `basename()`d before joining onto the attachments dir, so an id can't read outside it. The written filename still goes through `session-manager`'s `isSafeAttachmentName` + `AnchoredDir` exclusive-create path. Bytes are capped at 25 MB per file before being inlined. No new mounts.

prs.title: feat(telegram): render markdown tables as monospace pre blocks
prs.body:
markdownToTelegramHtml previously passed markdown tables through as raw pipes, which Telegram renders as a jumbled single line. Now a line containing '|' followed by a delimiter row (colons + 3+ dashes) is detected at line start, header/data rows are split into trimmed cells, and the table is re-rendered inside <pre> with per-column alignment padded by UTF-8 codepoint count so Cyrillic cells align. Embedded pipes deterministically split into extra cells; a lone '|' line without a delimiter row stays untouched (graceful degradation). All temp allocations are freed (leak-checked by the test allocator).

Risk: low — additive block handler, only triggers on table-shaped input; all existing conversion tests must pass unmodified. Ragged rows are clamped to the header column count (GFM behavior: excess cells dropped, missing cells padded); an all-whitespace header falls back to the data-row column count; CRLF line endings are tolerated.

prs.title: fix(mcp): refcount shared McpServer across tool wrappers
prs.body:
applyToolCustomizations deinits the wrappers of tools disabled via tool_customizations. Under the old ownership model only the first wrapper of an MCP server owned the server (owns_server = idx == 0), so removing a disabled tool freed the whole shared McpServer while the remaining wrappers still pointed at it. The next tools/call then worked on freed memory and crashed with SIGSEGV (exit 139).

Give McpServer a live-wrapper count. Every HTTP-transport wrapper takes one reference when it is wrapped as a Tool (McpToolWrapper.tool) and releases it on deinit; the server is freed by the last wrapper, so all wrappers of one server own it collectively instead of the first one.

The regression test only uses the pre-fix API surface: it compiles on unpatched main, where it aborts with a use-after-free in the second wrapper's deinit, and passes with the fix.

Validation: zig build test --summary all passes with zero failures and zero leaks (7501 passed, 9 skipped); zig fmt --check clean.

prs.title: fix(dsh): skip absent optional logs on export and keep presets in DSH sessions
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes two DSH migration regressions affecting desktop log export and existing session model selection:

1. **Log export missing-file warning (`dsh.log` / optional logs)**:
   - DSH host stdout/stderr is forwarded by `DshBootstrap` into `main-YYYY-MM-DD.log` (`[DSH:stdout]` / `[DSH:stderr]`) rather than creating `userData/dsh-profile/dsh.log`.
   - `getLogExportEntries()` previously included `dsh.log` (and Windows `install-timing.log` / `cowork.log`) unconditionally, causing `exportLogsZip()` to report missing entries and write 0-byte placeholders on every export.
   - Added `buildLogExportEntries()` so optional log files (`cowork.log`, `dsh.log`, and Windows `install-timing.log`) are only included when present as regular files on disk.

2. **Missing Fast / Ultimate model presets in existing DSH sessions**:
   - `CoworkStore.getSession()` now resolves `imPlatform` from `im_session_mappings` (matching `listSessions()`), exposed on `CoworkSession`.
   - Updated `isChatPresetSession()` to exclude IM-backed sessions via `imPlatform` while recognizing native DSH desktop session keys (`dsh:*` / `session-*`) regardless of whether the session currently has a saved `modelPresetId`.
   - Existing DSH desktop sessions—both preset-started and concrete-model-started—now retain the Fast (`快速`) and Ultimate (`旗舰`) options and context-window controls in the task detail model selector, while IM sessions remain excluded.

## Electron / IPC / Storage Changes

- **Storage (`CoworkStore.getSession`)**: Joins `im_session_mappings` (when the table exists) to populate `imPlatform` on returned `CoworkSession` objects; no schema migration required.
- **IPC (`log:exportZip`, `model-presets:select-session`, `model-context-window:*`)**: Log export omits absent optional log files instead of returning them in `missingEntries`; preset selection and context-window IPCs accept native DSH desktop sessions and reject IM sessions.

## Verification

- **Unit tests**: 141 passed across 6 Vitest suites (`logExportEntries.test.ts`, `constants.test.ts`, `modelPresets.test.ts`, `modelContextWindows.test.ts`, `CoworkPromptInput.modelSelection.test.ts`, `coworkStore.test.ts`).
- **Lint & Typecheck**: `npx eslint --max-warnings 0` clean on all touched TypeScript files; `npm run compile:electron` and `npm run build` succeeded.
- **Live Electron acceptance (Windows + Playwright/CDP against staging)**:
  - **Before fix**: Exporting logs from Settings → About showed `日志导出成功（缺失日志已按空文件补齐）: dsh.log, install-timing.log` with 0-byte entries in the zip; reopening a DSH session hid `快速` and `旗舰` from the model picker.
  - **After fix**: Exporting logs showed `日志导出成功` with only existing logs (`main-2026-11-24.log`, `cowork.log`) in the zip; reopening both a `快速`-created DSH session and a `DeepSeek-Flash`-created DSH session displayed `快速` and `旗舰` in the picker, and switching `快速 → 旗舰` and `DeepSeek-Flash → 快速` succeeded with real follow-up replies.

prs.title: fix(startup): prevent DSH migration hang and cold-boot timeout
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes severe first-launch startup hangs (observed up to 38 minutes in QA Windows upgrade logs) and intermittent 35s DSH cold-boot timeouts when upgrading from OpenClaw to DeepSeek Harness (DSH).

### Root Causes Addressed
1. **Pre-boot synchronous legacy archival (~14.7 min in QA logs)**: `legacyOpenClawMigrationV2` synchronously read, concatenated, and gzip-compressed the entire `openclaw/state` directory (and `third-party-extensions`) on the main thread before window creation, and deleted `openclaw/state` (risking broken historical session/IM media paths under `openclaw/state/media`).
2. **Unbounded pre-window proxy resolution (~23.3 min in QA logs)**: `initApp()` awaited `applyProxyPreference()`, which ran `session.defaultSession.setProxy` and 4 sequential `resolveProxy` calls without timeouts before `createWindow()`. After a long main-thread freeze, Chromium's NetworkService could wedge indefinitely while the single-instance lock was already held with no window visible.
3. **Aggressive DSH cold-boot timeout on Windows**: Windows cold launches could exceed the hardcoded `35s` timeout without Node compile cache reuse.

### Changes
- **Legacy migration & storage (`legacyOpenClawMigrator.ts`, `dshBootstrap.ts`)**:
  - Keep legacy `openclaw/state` (including `openclaw/state/media`) and `third-party-extensions/` in place on disk instead of tarring/deleting them (`legacyStateArchivePath: null`), recording only a lightweight top-level directory manifest in `sqlite/legacy_extensions_manifest.json`.
  - Add `getLegacyOpenClawDisposableCacheDirs()` and async `cleanupLegacyOpenClawDisposableCaches()`, deferred via `deferDisposableCacheCleanup: true` so pure disposable caches (`openclaw/logs`, `.compile-cache`, `repair-backups`, `state/cache`, `state/tmp`, `state/worktrees`, `dsh-runtime`) are removed asynchronously after window creation.
- **Windowing & proxy init (`systemProxy.ts`, `main.ts`)**:
  - Wrap `setProxy` and `resolveProxy` in a `2,000 ms` timeout (`setSessionProxyModeWithTimeout` / `runWithProxyTimeout`) and probe all 4 targets concurrently (`Promise.all`) while preserving target priority.
  - Run `refreshFakeIpNetworkState()` and `setSessionProxyModeWithTimeout()` concurrently inside `applyProxyPreference()`.
  - Stop awaiting `applyProxyPreference()` before `createWindow()`; chain `bootstrapOpenClawEngine({ reason: 'startup' })` onto `proxyPreferenceReady` so DSH still inherits resolved proxy env vars without delaying window creation.
  - Exit cleanly (`app.exit(1)`) in `initApp().catch()` if startup fails before any window exists, preventing headless processes from stranding the single-instance lock.
- **DSH runtime startup (`dshHostManager.ts`)**:
  - Increase default DSH boot timeout to `90,000 ms` on Windows (`45,000 ms` on macOS/Linux).
  - Inject version-isolated `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` (`<dshHomeDir>/cache/node-compile-cache/<sanitizedRuntimeVersion>`) into DSH child processes and log ready duration.

## Electron-Specific Behavior Changes
- **Storage / Migration**: `openclaw/state` and `third-party-extensions` remain on disk after V2 migration; no `legacy-openclaw-state.tar.gz` is created. Disposable caches are cleaned asynchronously after `createWindow()`.
- **Windowing / Lifecycle**: Main window creation no longer blocks on system proxy resolution; fatal pre-window `initApp()` failures now terminate the process instead of holding the single-instance lock invisibly.
- **Runtime (DSH)**: Default boot timeout raised (`90s` win32 / `45s` non-win32) and versioned `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` enabled for child Node processes.

## Verification
- **Unit tests**:
  - `src/main/libs/systemProxy.test.ts`: 3/3 passed
  - `src/main/libs/dsh/dshBootstrap.test.ts`: 8/8 passed
  - `src/main/migration/legacyOpenClawMigrator.test.ts`: 32/32 passed
  - `src/main/libs/dsh/dshHostManager.test.ts`: newly added timeout & `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` tests passed (2 pre-existing Windows path-separator assertions unrelated to this PR remain untouched)
- **Lint & Build**:
  - `npx eslint --ext ts,tsx --report-unused-disable-directives --max-warnings 0` on all 8 touched files: 0 errors, 0 warnings
  - `npm run compile:electron` and `npm run build`: passed
- **Real-machine Windows stress test** (isolated profile with `68 MB` sqlite + `432 MB / 18,193` files in `openclaw/` + `150 MB` media artifact + `useSystemProxy = true`):
  - `legacyOpenClawMigrationV2`: `528 ms` (previously `63s` locally / `14m 44s` in QA)
  - Window ready (cold upgrade): `3,879 ms` (`applyProxyPreference` non-blocking)
  - DSH cold boot ready: `16,464 ms`; warm second launch ready: `5,982 ms` (main window `875 ms`, migration `skipped` in `24 ms`)
  - Verified `openclaw/state/media` and `third-party-extensions` preserved and 6 disposable cache directories removed asynchronously after window creation.

prs.title: feat: add Atlas Cloud as a provider
prs.body:
## What

Adds **Atlas Cloud** as a provider in the Global section, next to OpenRouter. 5 files, +38/-4.

```ts
{
  id: ProviderName.AtlasCloud,
  label: 'Atlas Cloud',
  website: 'https://www.atlascloud.ai',
  apiKeyUrl: 'https://console.atlascloud.ai/api-keys',
  openClawProviderId: OpenClawProviderId.Lobster,
  defaultBaseUrl: 'https://api.atlascloud.ai/v1',
  defaultApiFormat: ApiFormat.OpenAI,
  codingPlanSupported: false,
  region: 'global',
  enPriority: 0,
  defaultModels: [
    { id: 'deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-pro', name: 'DeepSeek V4 Pro', supportsImage: false, supportsThinking: true, contextWindow: 1_048_576, maxTokens: 393_216 },
    { id: 'deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash', name: 'DeepSeek V4 Flash', supportsImage: false, supportsThinking: true, contextWindow: 1_048_576, maxTokens: 393_216 },
    { id: 'zai-org/glm-5.3', name: 'GLM 5.3', supportsImage: false, supportsThinking: true, contextWindow: 1_048_576, maxTokens: 131_072 },
    { id: 'moonshotai/kimi-k3', name: 'Kimi K3', supportsImage: true, supportsThinking: true, contextWindow: 1_048_576, maxTokens: 1_048_576 },
  ],
},
```

Atlas Cloud (`https://api.atlascloud.ai/v1`) is an OpenAI-compatible gateway serving open-weight models from DeepSeek, Z.ai, Moonshot, Qwen and MiniMax under one key.

## `openClawProviderId: OpenClawProviderId.Lobster` — why, not a guess

Atlas Cloud has no OpenClaw-native extension, and `Lobster` is the id this codebase already documents as the fallback for that case — both `ProviderRegistry`'s own id-resolution method and `openclawConfigSync.ts`'s `DEFAULT_DESCRIPTOR` use it the same way. Consequently `openclawConfigSync.ts` itself needs **no new entry**: its `resolveDescriptor()` already falls through to `{...DEFAULT_DESCRIPTOR, providerId: providerName}` for anything not in its map, which is exactly the right behavior for a provider with no special OpenClaw routing. I checked this rather than assumed it, by reading `resolveDescriptor` end to end before deciding where the line belonged.

## Model data

Context windows and output caps came from the gateway's own catalog (`GET /v1/models`, public, no key needed), and every one of the four ids was called against the live API before being added:

```
deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-pro   -> LOBSTER OK
deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash -> LOBSTER OK
zai-org/glm-5.3               -> LOBSTER OK
moonshotai/kimi-k3            -> LOBSTER OK
```

## Icon

`AtlasCloudIcon.tsx` reuses the Atlas Cloud brand path data, re-wrapped in this repo's own icon-component shape to match `OpenRouterIcon.tsx`'s structure exactly.

## Checks

- `eslint` on the five touched files — clean
- `tsc --noEmit` — 0 errors
- `vitest run src/shared/providers/constants.test.ts` → 34 passed (two count assertions updated: 18→19 total providers, 6→7 in the `global` region — these are accurate counts, not arbitrary numbers, so they had to change)
- `vitest run` (full suite) → 5531 passed / 33 failed / 163 skipped, **identical to `main`** with this branch stashed — the 33 failures are pre-existing and unrelated.

## Disclosure

I work at Atlas Cloud. Happy to adjust the model list, label, or `enPriority` to whatever you prefer.

prs.title: feat(experts): contribute Lynxce desktop and WorkBuddy experts with avatars
prs.body:
## Summary

Contribute the current **Lynxce (灵策智算)** expert sources, existing avatars, and brand attribution for maintainer review: **43 desktop presets, 53 expert teams (328 member/lead roles), and 783 WorkBuddy experts**, totaling **879 catalog entries**.

The content lives entirely under `contributions/lynxce-experts/`. Start with its README and `index.json`. WorkBuddy packages include their complete latest local agent/skill/reference/script deliveries, deduplicated by slug; source revision selection and 27 same-version prompt conflicts are recorded.

**Disclosure:** I work on Lynxce. The original WorkBuddy metadata includes commercial distribution flags and some external Lynxce services. The contribution preserves those facts; it does not claim free access to services or WorkBuddy approval.

## Changes Made

- Add complete desktop preset/team definitions, existing local SVG avatar mappings, 783 WorkBuddy source packages and their existing portraits.
- Reference the separate Lynxce brand mark and `灵策智算 LynxceAI` attribution on every contributed entry. Portraits are retained without painting new marks onto them.
- Inventory another **215 third-party imported experts** with origin and hashes only. Their prompts, packages and original portraits are excluded because whole-package redistribution permission is unconfirmed.
- Preserve source package notices, author metadata, dependency declarations and distribution flags; include SHA-256/size integrity records and a standard-library, read-only verifier.

## Integration and review boundaries

This PR proposes **content**, not automatic runtime registration or live-store publication. LobsterAI currently publishes its expert catalog remotely. Maintainers can select entries, host approved assets on the existing CDN, map to `ExpertCatalog`, validate, and publish through that existing process. No Electron, IPC, agent storage, CDN allowlist or production configuration changes are included. It is independent of #2874/#2875.

- The 43 desktop presets declare 17 skill IDs; their desktop skill bodies are not included and require mapping to upstream equivalents.
- WorkBuddy bundled skill bodies are included. Its plugin conventions require conversion before installation in LobsterAI.
- 397 WorkBuddy entries declare MCP dependencies, 98 appear in the local CPS inventory, and 309 retain `needEncrypt` source metadata. External services, purchases, credentials and platform review states were not exercised or asserted.
- Team portrait hint IDs are preserved, with real local SVG fallback assets supplied; they are not represented as bundled remote photos.
- The snapshot contains 5,457 files, mostly resource/package content. All WorkBuddy delivery files are retained byte for byte apart from excluding four Python cache files. Historical blank lines at EOF in original package text are preserved.

## Testing

- `python3 contributions/lynxce-experts/verify.py`: **passed**; 879 entries, all 5,457 files, image formats/paths, package references, branding, source hashes and file integrity checked.
- Independent full-file comparison of **all 783 selected WorkBuddy packages**, including **311 ZIP sources**: matched the selected local source deliveries; no missing package references or relative Markdown links.
- Additional private-key, token, credential-assignment and personal absolute-path scans: no actual credentials or machine paths found.
- `git -c core.whitespace=-blank-at-eof diff --cached --check`: passed; only historical EOF blank lines in verbatim source imports are exempted.
- Runtime build/tests were not run because application code is unchanged. Individual expert workflows and external integrations have not all been executed.

## Type of Change

- [x] Other: expert content and asset contribution for catalog review
- [x] Documentation update

## Electron-Specific Changes

- [x] None

The source attribution and third-party boundary are documented in the contribution README. Validation establishes content completeness and consistency, not upstream acceptance or live marketplace availability.
