issues.title: [Bug][Console] Transcript jumps back several screens when the content height shrinks (send, compaction, or a reasoning block collapsing)
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version
2.3.1-beta.1 (QwenPaw Desktop, Windows 11 26H2 build 26300.10075, x64, WebView2 157.0.4341.60 / Chromium 157.0.8103.80)
> Note: `navigator.userAgent` and the `ProductName` registry value still say "Windows 10" (Microsoft keeps that string on Windows 11). Identified as Windows 11 from `DisplayVersion=26H2`, `CurrentBuild=26300`, and UA-CH `platformVersion=19.0.0`.

## Component(s) Affected
- [ ] Core / Backend
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels / Skills / CLI / Docs / Tests / CI

## Description
In a conversation where context compaction has already run, typing a new message and pressing send makes the transcript viewport jump **upward, several screens back to much earlier turns**; the user has to drag the scrollbar all the way back down. Reproduced repeatedly.

Session length turned out **not** to be the deciding factor. The same jump reproduces in a short, already-compacted session whenever the transcript content shrinks while the reader is scrolled away from the bottom — see Runtime trace (c) and (d).

- No navigation popover / previous-next button was used.
- The jump happens right after the new user bubble is appended (reply not finished).
- The session is long enough that context compaction has already run (this workspace's `history.db` holds 18 `context compressed` markers, counted 2026-11-24).

## Expected
Appending a new user message must not change the viewport offset. If the backend swaps the whole context mirror (compaction), the list should either keep the reader's anchor or explicitly scroll to the newest message — never leave the viewport parked somewhere in the middle of history.

## Code path (bundled assets, names differ per build)
The transcript is the reverse-order list
`[class*="chat-anywhere-message-list-bubble-scroll"][class*="bubble-list-order-desc"]`,
whose `scrollTop` lives in `[-maxScroll, 0]` — `0` is the newest turn, negative values go back in history.

**(1) Wheel path — already fixed, and it works.** `messageScroll-*.js`:

```js
function u(e, l, r, o, n) {            // scrollTop, scrollHeight, clientHeight, deltaY, deltaMode
  const s = Math.max(l - r, 0);
  const t = i(o, n, r);
  return Math.min(0, Math.max(-s, e + t));
}
function E(e, l, r, o) {               // E(target, listEl, deltaY, deltaMode)
  const n = l.closest(c);
  if (!n || !e.contains(n) || a(l, n, r)) return false;
  const s = u(n.scrollTop, n.scrollHeight, n.clientHeight, r, o);
  return s === n.scrollTop ? false : (n.scrollTop = s, true);
}
```
wired as `const H = V => { ng(P, V.target, V.deltaY, V.deltaMode) && V.preventDefault(); }`
(`index-*.js`, capture-phase `wheel` listener). Every `scrollTop` write we captured from this path steps by exactly ±100 px and clamps correctly.

**(2) Auto-scroll gate — the actual suspect.** `index-*.js`, effect on `[messages, sessionId]`:

```js
useEffect(function () {
  var w = m.current;                                  // {messages, sessionId}
  if (fx(w.messages, n, w.sessionId, c)) {            // gate
    p.current && p.current.scrollToBottom();          // only scrolls when the gate says so
  }
  m.current = { messages: n, sessionId: c };
}, [n, c]);

function fx(e, t, n, r) {          // prev, next, prevSession, nextSession
  return t.length
    ? n !== r || !e.length ? true
    : t.length <= e.length ? false
    : !e.some(s => s.id === t[0].id)
    : false;
}
```
`fx` only compares **message count** and **the first message id**. If compaction swaps the whole mirror so the count stays equal (or drops) the gate returns `false`, so nothing re-anchors the list after the DOM swap.

**(3) Dead "stick to bottom" state.** `HostBubbles-*.js` (`bubble-list`):
```js
S = useCallback(function () {                 // isAtBottom
  var Z = $.current; if (!Z) return true;
  return p ? Z.scrollTop <= 2 : Z.scrollHeight - Z.clientHeight - Z.scrollTop <= 2;
}, [p]);
```
For the reverse list (`p === true`) `scrollTop` is always `<= 0`, so `scrollTop <= 2` is **always true** — presumably meant `>= -2`. `Q.current = S()` is written but never read anywhere in the bundle, so the component has no working "follow the newest message" state; everything depends on the `fx` gate above.

## Runtime trace (CDP, `--remote-debugging-port=9222`, 2.3.1-beta.1)
Two distinct failure modes show up, both on the same reverse list:

**(a) `scrollTop` changes with no writer — Chromium scroll anchoring.** Every time content height changes (tool card expand/collapse, cards collapsing on re-render) the offset is *pushed* without any `scrollTop` setter call:

| t (s) | trigger | scrollTop | scrollHeight | shift |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| +150.26 | open tool card | -359 → -868 | 3631 → 4139 | -509 |
| +151.48 | expand reasoning card | -1108 → -1416 | 4379 → 4687 | -308 |
| +152.71 | content collapse | -1116 → -276 | 4887 → 4047 | +840 |
| +166.70 | content collapse | -1356 → -128 | 6171 → 4943 | +1228 |
| +180.70 | content collapse | -2116 → -728 | 8593 → 7205 | +1388 |
| +398.20 | content collapse | -2056 → -456 | 12527 → 10927 | +1600 |

On a reverse list a growing/shrinking transcript moves the offset the *opposite* way, so any un-anchored height change reads to the user as "the transcript jumped".

**(b) whole-list swap right after send.** `MutationObserver` on the list container:

```
+33.82  scrollTop := 0            (scrollToBottom from the bubble list)
+35.04  +12 / -12 children, kids=13  scrollHeight 10860 -> 2358
+74.83  scrollTop := 0
+79.77  +14 / -14 children, kids=15  scrollHeight 12370 -> 2726
+95.01  +14 / -14 children           scrollTop -1513, scrollHeight 2726 -> 13522
```
i.e. sending makes React re-create **every** message node, `scrollHeight` drops by ~10 000 px for a frame or two, and the offset the browser computes during that window is what the user sees. In this capture Chromium's anchoring happened to pull it back to the bottom; when the anchor node is one of the replaced nodes it does not, which matches the intermittent "jumps and stays there" report.

**(c) short transcript, live re-capture 2026-11-24 — length is not the variable.** A short transcript (`scrollHeight` 2035–4842, `clientHeight` 1212, i.e. 0.7–3 screens of headroom, 4–6 bubbles, context already compacted) reproduced the same class of jump within two minutes of ordinary use:

| # | `scrollHeight` delta | `scrollTop` move | shift | what the user sees |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | -1639 | -929 -> -518 | +411 (0.77 screen) | pulled toward the newest turn |
| 2 | **+1668** | -200 -> -1868 | **-1668 (1.54 screen)** | **pushed up into history — the reported symptom** |
| 3 | -600 | -1955 -> -1355 | +600 (1.12 screen) | pulled toward the newest turn |
| 4 | -1568 | -1871 -> **0** | 0 | slammed back to the newest turn |

All four carry a non-zero `scrollHeight` delta and **no `scrollTop` writer on the stack** (Chromium scroll anchoring). In the same capture, **151** `scrollTop` writes *did* come from the app (`at E (messageScroll-*.js) <= at H (index-*.js)`) and each stepped by exactly +/-100 px, correctly clamped. The app never "decides" to jump: the browser shifts the offset every time the content height changes and nothing re-anchors afterwards, because the `fx` gate only fires on a count change or a first-id change.

Magnitudes matter here: on a 1212 px viewport a single collapsed/expanded card already moves the offset 1–1.5 screens, and the list itself swung `scrollHeight` 4186 -> 4842 -> 2035 within the same session while the message array was being rebuilt.

**(d) the reported symptom, isolated: a collapsing reasoning block clamps the offset to a boundary.** Re-probing while the assistant streamed (10 un-stacked offset changes in a 190 s window) splits them into two classes:

- **4 / 10 have `dSt === -dSh`** — Chromium scroll anchoring working as intended: content shrinks or grows and the browser compensates exactly, so the reader's content does not move. Harmless.
- **6 / 10 have `dSt !== -dSh`** — no compensation was applied, the *old* offset is now outside the new range, and the browser clamps it to a boundary. Every one of these is a visible jump.

| scrollHeight before -> after | dh | scrollTop before -> after | new maxScroll | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3781 -> 2142 | -1639 | -1340 -> -929 | 930 | **clamped to TOP (oldest turns)** |
| 5635 -> 1993 | **-3642** | -1436 -> -780 | 781 | **clamped to TOP (oldest turns)** |
| 3567 -> 2039 | -1528 | -1440 -> -826 | 827 | **clamped to TOP (oldest turns)** |
| 5838 -> 4270 | -1568 | -1480 -> 0 | 3058 | clamped to BOTTOM |
| 3246 -> 2578 | -668 | -479 -> 1 | 1366 | clamped to BOTTOM |
| 3266 -> 1212 | -2054 | -760 -> 0 | 0 | whole list collapses to one screen |

The three TOP clamps are exactly the user report: *scroll up half a screen, one reasoning step finishes and collapses, and the transcript lands on the oldest turn* — three times in a row during one reply. The trigger is **content shrinking**, not sending: a step/reasoning block going from expanded to collapsed is enough. The larger the collapse relative to what remains, the further the clamp overshoots — a 3642 px collapse against a remaining 781 px of scroll range parks the reader at the very top of history.

Same root cause as the `fx` gate plus a missing guard: nothing records "which message is at the top of the viewport and at what offset" before a layout change, and `overflow-anchor` is left at the default `auto`, whose anchor selection is discarded as soon as the node being resized is itself replaced.

## Downstream impact: the composer stops accepting input while the run is still going

The same list rebuild leaves the composer in a state where **every** action path returns early — sending, queueing (insert), and interrupting all do nothing, silently, and the only way back is to wait for the current run to finish on its own.

**Reported behaviour** (same session, same rebuild as the jump above):

1. The transcript jumps back, as described above, while a reply is still streaming.
2. The round send/stop action button falls back to the grey send state instead of the stop state.
3. Typing a message and pressing enter does nothing. Adding it to the queue does nothing. No error, no toast, no state change.
4. Nothing recovers until the current run completes; then typing works again.

**Code path — one readiness ref gates everything.** `index-*.js` (Composer), minified identifiers as shipped in 2.3.1-beta.1:

```js
// submit / interrupt-and-send / retry / skip all open with the same guard
const S = () => !h.aborted && $e.current && Be.current && On.current === v && P.isReady(...);
if (!S()) return false;   // silent: no error, no toast
```

`Be.current` is pessimistic: it is cleared unconditionally at the top of its effect and restored only by an async callback.

```js
Be.current = Et;                                     // Et is state, starts false
useEffect(() => {
  os(!1), ar(!1);                                    // always clear first
  const s = new AbortController;
  ...
  pc(v, s.signal)
    .then(() => { if (!s.signal.aborted) return mc(v, () => { os(!0), ar(!0) }, s.signal); })
    .catch(z => { ...; console.error("Unable to recover chat queue", z); });
}, [C, v, P, I]);
```

Consequences:

- Any effect re-run drops `Be.current` to `false`; the full list rebuild on the transcript side is one of the things that perturbs these dependencies.
- If `pc()` rejects, or the effect re-runs and aborts the in-flight recovery before `mc()` settles, the `.catch` only logs. Nothing retries and the gate stays closed.
- The only reliable way to flip it back is the effect running again, which the next run-status change supplies — hence "you can only wait for the current run to finish".

**Why this is worse than the scroll jump**

| | scroll jump | dead composer |
|---|---|---|
| visible feedback | obvious | none — the button simply stops working |
| can still interrupt a run | yes | **no** |
| recovery | drag the scrollbar | wait for the run to end |

Interruption is the user-facing safety control over a running agent; losing it silently for the duration of a run is a functional failure, not a cosmetic one.

**Suggested hardening** (independent of the scroll fixes)

1. Fail open: treat the composer as ready by default and flip to not-ready only when recovery *explicitly* fails, instead of clearing it on every effect run.
2. Never swallow a blocked submit: if the guard rejects, surface why (disabled with a reason) instead of `return false`.
3. Split the gates: "stop the current run" must not share a readiness condition with "send a new message".

A DOM-level sampler is attached to the affected window (`aria-label`, `disabled` and `opacity` of the round action button, plus `scrollTop` / `scrollHeight` / input length at 250 ms) to capture the exact transition timeline; happy to attach the trace once it fires.

## Steps to reproduce

Two independent paths, both on 2.3.1-beta.1:

**A. Send path**

1. Open a conversation long enough that context compaction has already run.
2. Scroll up a few screens into earlier turns, so the viewport sits more than half a screen away from the newest message.
3. Send a new message.
4. The transcript jumps up to much earlier turns and stays there until dragged back.

**B. Content-shrink path (no send involved; this is the one captured live)**

1. Open any session whose transcript is taller than the viewport. A short, already-compacted one is enough — the capture below had `clientHeight` 1212 and `scrollHeight` between 2035 and 4842.
2. Scroll away from the bottom, i.e. leave `scrollTop` at any non-zero value in `[-maxScroll, 0]`.
3. Let a reasoning / step block finish and collapse, or trigger context compaction.
4. In one mutation the list's `scrollHeight` drops by 1.5k-3.6k px. The stored offset is now beyond the new `maxScroll`, Chromium clamps it to a boundary, and the viewport top-aligns with an older turn — up to a full screen or more of history appears to be "jumped" over.

## Workaround
Start a new session (shorter transcript), or drag the scrollbar back / use the floating "back to bottom" button.

## Notes
- Relation to existing reports: #8284 (wheel-only snap-back, fixed by #8339) and #8852 (`content-visibility` height re-estimation on the same list) are the same class of symptom. #8339 fixed the wheel path; the send/compaction path above is still unhandled on 2.3.1-beta.1.
- Captured with `WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS=--remote-debugging-port=9222`, hooking `HTMLDivElement.prototype.scrollTop` (setter + stack), `MutationObserver`, `ResizeObserver` and `scroll` on the list container. Happy to attach the raw probe script / recording if maintainers want it.

issues.title: [Bug] Media data blocks in tool results cause 400 BadRequestError on non-multimodal models, resulting in "Internal error" on all subsequent messages
issues.body:
## Description

When a tool returns a media data block (e.g. `view_video` returning `video/mp4`, or `send_file_to_user` returning `application/x-zip-compressed`), the media reference gets embedded in the session's conversation context. On every subsequent message, this data block is sent to the model API. If the model doesn't accept that media type, the API returns `400 Invalid request parameters`, and the user sees **"Internal error"** — permanently, for every message in that session.

## To Reproduce

1. Use a non-multimodal model (e.g. `mimo-v2.6-pro` via an OpenAI-compatible provider)
2. In a chat session, trigger `view_video` with an `.mp4` file, or `send_file_to_user` with a `.zip` file
3. The tool result contains a `data` block like:
   ```json
   {
     "type": "data",
     "source": {"type": "url", "url": "file:///...", "media_type": "video/mp4"}
   }
   ```
4. Send any subsequent message in that session → **every message returns "Internal error"**

## Root Cause

The `retry_chat_model` / `openai_chat_model_compat` layer sends all context content to the model API without filtering out media data blocks that the target model cannot accept. The API rejects the request:

```
openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'code': '400', 'message': 'Invalid request parameters'}}
```

The session is permanently poisoned — the data block persists in the session JSON and is resent on every call.

## Expected Behavior

Media data blocks that the target model cannot accept should be filtered out before sending to the API. Or at minimum, the system should catch the 400 error, strip media blocks, and retry — instead of surfacing "Internal error" and poisoning the session permanently.

## Actual Behavior

Every subsequent message in the session returns "Internal error". The session remains broken until the media data blocks are manually removed from the session JSON file.

## Workaround (manual)

Remove the `data` blocks from the session file:

```python
import json

path = r'~/.qwenpaw/workspaces/default/sessions/dingtalk/<session>.json'
d = json.load(open(path, encoding='utf-8'))

for turn in d['agent']['state']['context']:
    for c in turn.get('content', []):
        if isinstance(c, dict) and c.get('type') == 'tool_result':
            out = c.get('output', [])
            if isinstance(out, list):
                c['output'] = [
                    x for x in out
                    if not (
                        isinstance(x, dict)
                        and x.get('type') == 'data'
                        and any(
                            x.get('source', {}).get('media_type', '').startswith(p)
                            for p in ['video/', 'audio/', 'image/', 'application/']
                        )
                    )
                ]

json.dump(d, open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8'), ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
```

## Suggested Fix

Before sending context to the model API, filter out `type: "data"` blocks whose `media_type` is not supported by the target model. Or at minimum, catch the 400 error and strip media blocks + retry instead of surfacing "Internal error" and poisoning the session permanently.

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version**: (check `qwenpaw --version`)
- **OS**: Windows Server 2022 (AMD64)
- **Model**: `mimo-v2.6-pro` (provider: `mimo-tokenplan`)
- **Channel**: DingTalk
- **Python**: 3.12

## Logs

```
openai.BadRequestError: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'code': '400', 'message': 'Invalid request parameters', 'param': '', 'type': 'BadRequestError'}}
  File ".../qwenpaw/providers/retry_chat_model.py", line 895, in __call__
  File ".../qwenpaw/token_usage/model_wrapper.py", line 263, in __call__
  File ".../qwenpaw/providers/openai_chat_model_compat.py", line 771, in __call__
  File ".../agentscope/model/_openai_chat/_model.py", line 280, in _call_api
  File ".../openai/resources/chat/completions/completions.py", line 2714, in create
```

issues.title: [Bug]: [creator] Creation Assistant input lags on every keystroke — full AgentDock re-render re-parses all conversation markdown (no memoization)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

QwenPaw 2.3.0 (pip venv install), PawApp plugin `qwenpaw-creator` 2.0.5.

## Description

In a project workspace, typing into the left-side "Creation Assistant" (创作助手) input box lags noticeably: characters appear with a per-key delay that grows with conversation length. Chinese IME composition makes it worse, since every composition update travels the same path.

I recovered the plugin's own `ui/src` from the shipped sourcemaps (`ui/dist/app/assets/*.js.map`) and traced this to a render-path defect in `AgentDock.tsx`: **every keystroke re-renders the entire dock, which re-parses the markdown of every message in the conversation through ReactMarkdown**.

**Related PR(s):** none

**Security considerations:** none (pure front-end render performance).

## Component(s) Affected

Not covered by the checklist — PawApp plugin frontend: `qwenpaw-creator` (`ui/` React bundle), specifically `ui/src/components/agent/AgentDock.tsx` and `ui/src/components/agent/MentionInput.tsx`.

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0, plugin qwenpaw-creator 2.0.5
- **OS:** Windows Server 2022 (x64)
- **Install method:** pip (managed venv)
- **Python version:** 3.12
- **Browser:** Chromium-based; the console serves the plugin UI inside an iframe

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Creator app and enter a project whose Creation Assistant conversation already has a substantial history (dozens of messages, including long assistant markdown replies with tables/code blocks).
2. Click the assistant input box (the contentEditable `MentionInput`) and type a sentence at normal speed, optionally via an IME.
3. Observe typed characters appearing with a per-key delay; the longer the conversation history, the worse it gets.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** the main thread blocks on every keystroke (per-key delay scales with conversation size and markdown complexity); typed text lags behind the keystrokes.
- **Expected:** keystrokes appear immediately regardless of conversation length.

## Root cause analysis

Line numbers refer to the sourcemap-recovered `ui/src` of plugin 2.0.5.

1. `MentionInput.tsx` (~L443): the contentEditable's `onInput` → `sync()` → serializes the DOM → calls `onChange(text)` **on every keystroke** (and on every IME composition update).

2. `AgentDock.tsx` `handleInputChange` (~L1909) performs three re-render-triggering writes per keystroke:

   ```ts
   const handleInputChange = (text: string) => {
     const content = inputRef.current?.getContent();             // 2nd DOM serialization
     setCanSend(Boolean(content?.text.trim()));                  // local state
     setInlineRefs(content?.refs.map((item) => item.ref) ?? []); // new array identity every time
     setDraft(text);                                             // zustand agentDockUiStore
   };
   ```

   - `setInlineRefs(... ?? [])` creates a **new array identity on every keystroke**, so this state always counts as changed even when the ref list is identical.
   - `setDraft` writes `agentDockUiStore.draft`, and **AgentDock subscribes to that same slice itself** (~L1156: `const draft = useAgentDockUiStore((state) => state.draft)`), so the dock re-renders from its own write.
   - A `useEffect` keyed on `[draft, open]` (~L1748) runs after each keystroke and calls `getContent()` again (3rd DOM serialization per key).

3. `AgentDock.tsx` is ~2,900 lines and contains **zero `memo()` / `React.memo` in the entire file** (verified: no occurrence of `memo`). Every re-render redraws the whole conversation (~L2407–2455): each `ConversationMessage` → `MessageParts` → `MarkdownContent` (~L304) → `ReactMarkdown` with `remarkPlugins={[remarkGfm]}` (an inline array, new identity per render). ReactMarkdown re-parses **every historical message** through the unified/remark pipeline on **every keystroke**; `ToolCallCard` (~L760), `AgentProgressOverview`, and `DecisionTray` re-render in full as well.

Net effect: per-key main-thread cost grows with conversation size × markdown complexity. A fresh conversation feels fine; a long one becomes painful — matching the reported symptom.

## Verified local hotfix (workaround)

Wrapped five typing-stable-prop components with `React.memo` in the shipped bundle: `MarkdownContent`, `ConversationMessage`, `ToolCallCard`, `AgentProgressOverview`, `DecisionTray` (a one-line append to the built chunk, `X = react.memo(X)` per component; minified names are build-specific). Their zustand subscriptions live inside the components, so streaming updates and tool-progress re-renders are unchanged; memo only skips the keystroke-driven redraws. After applying it (and clearing site data, since `ui/dist/app/assets/*` is served `immutable`), typing is immediately responsive even in long conversations — confirmed by the reporter on the same projects that previously lagged.

## Suggested proper fix (in impact order)

1. `memo()` the per-message components (`ConversationMessage`, `ToolCallCard`, `MarkdownContent`) and hoist the `remarkPlugins` array to a module constant.
2. Isolate composer state (`canSend`, `inlineRefs`, draft writes) into a small composer child component so keystrokes never re-render the dock and the conversation list.
3. Let AgentDock not subscribe to the same `draft` slice it writes on every keystroke — read it via `getState()` inside the restore effect, or debounce draft persistence.
4. Skip the `setInlineRefs` update when the ref list is unchanged (compare with the previous value).
5. Reuse the single serialization result from `MentionInput`'s `onChange` instead of serializing the contentEditable DOM three times per keystroke.

## Differentiation from existing perf issues (searched; not duplicates)

- #8288 — main-console chat full re-render on conversation **switching**; different surface and trigger (this one is per-keystroke, inside the creator plugin).
- #8668, #8135, #3915, #7176 — main-console perf (compositor/CSS, streaming render cost, virtual scrolling); this issue lives in the creator PawApp bundle and is driven by React re-render + markdown re-parse on each keystroke.
- #6889 — console IME event-target correctness; IME here only amplifies the same re-render chain.

## Logs / Screenshots

No server logs — this is purely front-end render performance, and no profiler trace is attached. The fix direction is validated by the memo hotfix above: with the same long conversations, the typing lag disappears.

issues.title: [Bug]: Creator review round becomes permanently undecidedable - REJECT always returns 422 "visual artifact reference references missing id" (+ expired provider source_url 502, frame_stats ignores CREATOR_FFMPEG_PATH)
issues.body:
> **This report bundles three independently reproducible backend defects** found in one session on the same Creator project. Defect 1 is a hard blocker (a review round that can never be decided); defects 2 and 3 were found while tracing it. **Happy to split this into three issues** if that is easier to triage.

## QwenPaw Version

| | |
|---|---|
| QwenPaw core | **2.2.2.post1** |
| qwenpaw-creator | **2.0.4** |
| Python | 3.12.13 |
| OS | Windows Server 2022 Datacenter (10.0.20348), x86_64 |
| Install method | pip (venv) |
| Image provider | DashScope-compatible gateway, model `wan2.7-image-pro` |

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend — `plugins/qwenpaw-creator/backend`: `services/project_files/review.py`, `services/project_files/models.py`, `services/media_files/image_execution.py`, `models/image/dashscope_provider.py`, `vendor/media_toolkit/frame_stats.py`, `services/run_review/media_review.py`

## Description

### Defect 1 (blocker) — a pending review round becomes permanently undecidedable: every REJECT returns 422

`POST /api/qwenpaw-creator/projects/{projectId}/runtime/reviews/{reviewId}/decisions` returns **422 `VALIDATION_ERROR`** with **`details={}`**, forever, as soon as one specific (and easily reachable) state exists:

> a **later** commit made some *other* visual variant style-reference an artifact version that the **still-pending** review round would delete on rejection.

Consequences:

* the review stays `PENDING` with every operation `PENDING`;
* retrying is deterministic — 8 identical attempts in 15 s all produced the same 422;
* there is **no way out through the API**: `runtime/reviews` exposes only `GET /active` and `POST /{review_id}/decisions` (`api/project_file_routes.py:1051`, `:1083`) — no cancel/expire/invalidate endpoint;
* the UI can only show a generic failure, because `details` is empty.

#### Reproduction

1. In a Creator project, generate an image for entity `char:aaa` / variant `v1`. This creates `artifact-version-A` (+ its `IndexedFile`) and opens a review round `R` containing 6 operations (create version, create file, slot `version_ids`, slot `selected_version_id`, variant `generated_artifact_version_ids`, variant `selected_artifact_version_id`). `R` is `PENDING`.
2. **Before deciding `R`**, let the runtime (or any later commit) set another variant's style reference to that image, i.e. `char:aaa / v2 . reference_artifact_version_ids = ["artifact-version-A"]`. This lands in a *different* round/commit, so it is **not** one of `R`'s operations.
3. Open `R` in the UI, mark **all operations REJECT**, add feedback, submit.

#### Actual

```
WARNING | qwenpaw.creator.api.errors | dependencies.py:185 | Creator request failed
  error_id=error-<redacted> status=422 code=VALIDATION_ERROR method=POST
  path=/api/qwenpaw-creator/projects/<projectId>/runtime/reviews/<reviewId>/decisions details={}
```

The real reason is only in `observability/traces/*.jsonl` (`creator.error.reported`):

```
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for Project
  Value error, visual artifact reference references missing id artifact-version-<40-hex>
  [type=value_error, input_value={'schema_version': 9, ...}, input_type=dict]

  File "<plugin>/backend/api/project_file_routes.py", line 1190, in decide_project_review
  File "<plugin>/backend/services/project_files/facade.py", line 373, in decide_review
  File "<plugin>/backend/services/project_files/review.py", line 989, in decide
  File "<plugin>/backend/services/project_files/review.py", line 1097, in _decide_locked
    Project.model_validate(
```

#### Expected

Either the rejection succeeds (cleaning up references that pointed at the deleted artifact version), or the round is reported as **stale/conflicted** with an actionable message and a way to clear it. Not an endless 422 with empty `details`.

#### Root cause (verified offline against the live project file)

`review.py:1093-1101` deliberately dry-runs the rollback before publishing:

```python
compensation_required = bool(rejection_changes)
if compensation_required:
    # Reject invalid partial rollbacks before publishing a durable
    # decision. A failed schema check must not lock this Review.
    Project.model_validate(
        apply_changes(current.project.model_dump(mode="json"), rejection_changes),
        context={"reject_retired_authoring_fields": True},
    )
```

`_rejection_changes` (`review.py:1588`) inverts **only the round's own operations**. Deleting `artifact-version-A` therefore leaves `v2.reference_artifact_version_ids = ["artifact-version-A"]` dangling, and the model validator rejects it:

```python
# models.py:1542-1549
for ref in variant.reference_artifact_version_ids:
    anchor = visual_style_anchor(self.visual.entities, ref)
    if anchor is None:
        _require_key(artifact_versions, ref, "visual artifact reference")   # -> models.py:1986
```

`visual_style_anchor` (`models.py:499`) only resolves refs shaped `visual:<entityId>:<variantId>`; a raw `artifact-version-…` ref must exist in `assets.artifact_versions_by_id`, so the rolled-back document is invalid.

Note the irony in the code comment: the guard exists so that *"a failed schema check must not lock this Review"* — but because the invalid input is the **rollback itself**, the guard is precisely what locks the review permanently.

I reproduced this offline with the plugin's own code, read-only:

| step | result |
|---|---|
| `Project.model_validate(current project.json)` | **OK** |
| apply the inverse of the round's 6 operations, then `Project.model_validate(...)` | **fails with the byte-identical message above** |
| remove the single stale entry from `v2.reference_artifact_version_ids`, then validate both the live and the rolled-back document | **both OK** |

#### Suggested fixes

1. **Cascade the rollback**: when a rejection deletes an artifact version, also drop it from every `reference_artifact_version_ids` / `generated_artifact_version_ids` / `selected_artifact_version_id` / slot `version_ids`+`selected_version_id` that points at it (a single `_prune_artifact_references(project, version_id)` pass before validation).
2. **Or detect the conflict at write time**: the round already tracks `baseline_generation` / `candidate_generation`; if a later commit adds a dependency on an artifact covered by a pending round, rebase or invalidate that round instead of leaving an impossible decision.
3. **Make the failure survivable either way**: put the `ValidationError` message into the 422 `details` (today it is `{}`), and add `DELETE`/`POST …/cancel` for a review round so a stuck round can be cleared without hand-editing `project.json`.

#### Verified workaround

Submitting **all-ACCEPT** for the same round succeeds (no rejection changes ⇒ `compensation_required` is false ⇒ the dry run is skipped). Confirmed: the round moved to `RESOLVED` immediately after. This is an escape hatch, not a fix — the user loses the ability to reject.

Not the same defect as #8163 (long runtime paths breaking the decision journal) or #7720; different code path, different symptom (that one could not *write* the journal, this one refuses to *compute* the rollback).

---

### Defect 2 — an expired provider `source_url` is reused as a reference image: 502 `MODEL_ERROR`, flagged `retryable: true`, with a misleading hint

`image_execution.py:809 _resolve_version_references` prefers the provider URL stored in artifact metadata and **never checks its expiry**:

```python
# image_execution.py:835-842
source_url = provider_meta.get("source_url", "")
if source_url:
    ...
    urls.append(source_url)      # used as-is
    continue
...
# image_execution.py:880 — only reached when there is no source_url
urls.append(_indexed_path(project_root, indexed).resolve().as_uri())
```

`dashscope_provider.py:223 _public_reference_url` passes any `http(s)://`/`oss://` straight through (`:245`); only **local** references get read and uploaded to model-bound temp storage (`:247`, `:252`). So a dead URL also **short-circuits the healthy local-file path**.

These URLs are short-lived pre-signed object-store links (~24 h TTL here). Observed, same project:

| event | UTC |
|---|---|
| `artifact-version-B` created; metadata stores `provider.source_url = https://<provider-oss-host>/<…>.png?Expires=1793857725&OSSAccessKeyId=<redacted>&Signature=<redacted>` | 2026-11-04T05:48:47Z |
| that URL expires (`Expires=1793857725`) | 2026-11-05T05:48:45Z |
| first regeneration dispatch referencing it → **HTTP 403** at the provider | 2026-11-05T05:52:02Z (**3 min 17 s after expiry**) |
| second attempt → same failure | 2026-11-05T09:07:08Z |

Surfaced to the caller:

```
status=502 code=MODEL_ERROR  retryable=true
POST /api/qwenpaw-creator/projects/<projectId>/work-graph/nodes/visual:char:aaa:variant:v1/dispatch
Image generation failed with status 400: Failed to download image from
[https://<provider-oss-host>/<…>.png?Expires=1793857725&OSSAccessKeyId=<redacted>&Signature=<redacted>]:
HTTP 403. Check creator_image_model configuration.
```

Three problems in one message:

* **`retryable: true`** — a permanently expired signature can never succeed on retry, so the runtime/user keeps retrying;
* **`Check creator_image_model configuration`** — the model configuration is fine, this sends the user to the wrong place;
* the **full pre-signed URL, including `OSSAccessKeyId` and `Signature`, is echoed** into the API error payload, the trace file and `creator.log`, while the same logger redacts `api_key=[redacted]` one line earlier.

Meanwhile the local artifact was perfectly intact (`IndexedFile` present, 2,400,646 bytes on disk) — nothing was lost but the URL. In this project 3 of 4 artifact versions had already expired, i.e. **any regeneration that references yesterday's image fails**, every day.

#### Suggested fixes

1. Parse `Expires` (provider-specific, but this one is a plain UNIX timestamp) and treat an expired/near-expiry `source_url` as absent, falling through to the local-file branch at `image_execution.py:880` — the provider already knows how to upload local bytes to temp storage.
2. On a provider response matching "failed to download image … 403", retry **once** via the local-file path before failing.
3. Mark this failure `retryable: false` and replace the hint with something actionable ("reference image URL expired; re-select the reference or re-upload the asset").
4. **Redact signed URLs** (`OSSAccessKeyId`, `Signature`, `x-oss-*`, `X-Amz-*`, …) in logs, trace payloads and error messages.

---

### Defect 3 — `vendor/media_toolkit/frame_stats.py` ignores `CREATOR_FFMPEG_PATH`, so media review never runs and silently burns its budget

`plugin.json` declares the contract:

```json
"ffmpeg": {
  "required_for": "media probing, rendering, and composition",
  "path_env": "CREATOR_FFMPEG_PATH",
  "bundled_fallback": "imageio-ffmpeg"
}
```

and the environment honours it — `CREATOR_FFMPEG_PATH` points at the bundled binary shipped by the declared dependency, and the file exists:

```
CREATOR_FFMPEG_PATH = <venv>/Lib/site-packages/imageio_ffmpeg/binaries/ffmpeg-win-x86_64-v7.1.exe   (87,638,016 bytes, exists)
```

But `frame_stats.py:122 _run_signalstats` shells out to a bare `"ffmpeg"` (`:129`):

```
FileNotFoundError: [WinError 2] The system cannot find the file specified
  -> frame_stats.py:149  FrameStatsError("signalstats sampling failed")
  -> media_review.py:493 / :511 / :826 / :1043
ERROR | creator.run_review.media | media_review.py:1107 | media review loop failed for artifact-version-<40-hex>
```

Grepping the whole backend, `CREATOR_FFMPEG_PATH` appears **only inside three error-message strings** in `models/asr_model.py` (`:149`, `:776`, `:979`); there is no resolver at all (`imageio_ffmpeg`, `ffmpeg_exe`, `shutil.which("ffmpeg")` → 0 hits in `backend/`). So on any host without `ffmpeg` on `PATH` — i.e. exactly the hosts that rely on the documented `path_env` / `bundled_fallback` — objective media QC never runs.

Second-order damage: the failures consume the per-slot review budget, ending in

```
WARNING | creator.run_review.media | media_review.py:1014 | media review budget exhausted for
  slot asset:char:aaa:variant:v2:image: new versions of this artifact will no longer be auto-reviewed
```

so the slot is permanently left without auto-review, and nothing in the UI says "your ffmpeg is missing" — the only visible symptom is that reviews silently stop happening.

#### Suggested fixes

1. One resolver used everywhere: `CREATOR_FFMPEG_PATH` → `shutil.which("ffmpeg")` → `imageio_ffmpeg.get_ffmpeg_exe()` (and the same for `CREATOR_FFPROBE_PATH`, which `plugin.json` also declares), instead of the literal `"ffmpeg"` in `frame_stats.py:129`.
2. Do **not** consume review budget when the probe binary is unavailable; fail with an actionable configuration error that reaches the UI.

## Steps to Reproduce (condensed)

1. Windows Server 2022, QwenPaw 2.2.2.post1 + qwenpaw-creator 2.0.4, DashScope-compatible image model, `ffmpeg` **not** on `PATH` but `CREATOR_FFMPEG_PATH` set to the bundled `imageio_ffmpeg` binary.
2. Generate an image for `char:aaa/v1` → review round `R` opens (`PENDING`).
3. Have a later commit set `char:aaa/v2.reference_artifact_version_ids = ["artifact-version-A"]`.
4. REJECT all operations of `R` → **422 `VALIDATION_ERROR`, `details={}`**, repeatable forever (defect 1). ACCEPT all → succeeds.
5. Wait ~24 h, then dispatch a regeneration that references the artifact generated yesterday → **502 `MODEL_ERROR`, `retryable=true`, "Check creator_image_model configuration"** (defect 2).
6. Inspect `creator.log`: every generated artifact shows `media review loop failed … signalstats sampling failed` (defect 3).

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** a review round can enter a state where rejection is impossible and uncancellable (422 with empty `details`); regenerations die on expired provider URLs and are reported as retryable model-configuration errors; media auto-review never runs and silently exhausts its budget.
- **Expected:** rejection cascades reference cleanup (or reports a stale round and offers a cancel); reference resolution validates URL expiry and falls back to the intact local file; ffmpeg resolution follows the documented `CREATOR_FFMPEG_PATH` / `imageio-ffmpeg` contract.

## Logs / Screenshots

Key lines quoted inline above. Full local evidence kept: `creator.log`, `observability/traces/creator-trace-*.jsonl` (`creator.http.request.finished` with `errorType=ValidationError` + full stack, `creator.error.reported` with `causeChain`), `runtime/reviews/<reviewId>/review.json`, `runtime/change-rounds/<roundId>/changeset.json`, `runtime/tasks/<taskId>/task.json`. Identifiers, hostnames, account names and signed-URL credentials are redacted here.

## Additional Notes

* **Security consideration:** defect 2 writes provider pre-signed URLs (access-key id + signature) into logs, trace files and API error payloads.
* Defect 1's guard (`review.py:1093-1101`) is a good idea; it just needs the rollback to be reference-complete, plus a surfaced message and an escape hatch.
* All three were reproduced on 2.0.4 / 2.2.2.post1; I could not find any existing issue or PR covering them (`"visual artifact reference"`, `"references missing id"`, `"Review candidate changed"`, `signalstats`, `frame_stats`, `CREATOR_FFMPEG_PATH`, `source_url expired`, `VALIDATION_ERROR decisions` → 0 hits in this repo).

issues.title: [Bug]: 窄屏下整条消息的文字被剪裁，超宽内容（表格 / 代码块）同样被裁切且无法横向滚动

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body: ## 环境 - QwenPaw: `v2.3.0.post1`（升级前为 `v2.3.0`，升级后出现窄屏剪裁问题） - 界面: Console（Web UI） - 桌面端: Chrome / Windows 11，视口宽度约 `1903 px` - 移动端: 手机 Chrome，视口宽度 `375 px`（竖屏） - 设置: 设置中心 → 消息展示 → 消息宽度 = **标准** ## 复现步骤 1. 打开 Console，进入任意会话 2. 设置中心 → 消息展示 → 消息宽度选择「标准」 3. 让 Agent 输出以下任一内容： - 列数较多的 Markdown 表格（本次测试 20 列、30 列） - 超长单行的代码块（`text` 或 `css`，约 490~505 字符） 4. 观察消息气泡右侧 5. 用手机浏览器打开同一个会话，观察同样的消息 ## 实际表现 内容宽度超过气泡宽度时，**右侧被直接裁掉，不出现横向滚动条，也没有任何方式查看被裁掉的部分**。 各内容块表现一致。 ### 1. Markdown 表格 20 列表格只渲染到第 13 列（C13 仅显示一半），C14 至 C20 完全不可见。 - 实测表格渲染宽度：`1421 px` - 外层消息区宽度：`990 px` 30 列表格被裁得更早，实测宽度 `1651 px`。 | 截图 1 · 表格 | |---| | | ### 2. text 代码块 单行 505 字符的 `text` 代码块，只能看到前约 100 字符，其后内容全部不可见。块内每 20 字符放置一个 `` 标尺，用于定位裁切位置。 | 截图 2 · text 代码块 | |---| | | ### 3. css 代码块 单行 489 字符的 `css` 代码块（带语法高亮），表现与 `text` 块完全一致，同样从右侧被裁。 | 截图 3 · css 代码块 | |---| | | ### 4. 手机端（窄屏）：不只是表格和代码块，整条消息的文字都会被裁 375px 视口下打开同一个会话，消息区可视宽度只有 `303 px`，而承载内容的容器实测被撑到 `988 px`： - 一个两列的 Markdown 表格渲染宽度 `987 px`，右侧完全看不到，也无法滑动 - **同一条消息里，表格之后的普通段落文字也会一起被裁掉**，因为整块响应内容都被撑到 988px，超出部分被外层 `overflow: hidden` 静默裁掉 - 表现上就是「这条回复右边的字少了半截」，而且没有任何滚动条提示 ![Screenshot_2026-11-18-23-04-21-633_ai.qwenpaw.shell-edit.jpg](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d1a92d9-d241-4ee3-a51a-95835a78e263) ## 补充观察 1. **不是「标准模式特有」**。把「消息宽度」切到「加宽」后，只是可用宽度变大、部分内容刚好能放下；一旦内容宽度超过容器，仍然会被裁且同样没有横向滚动条。标准模式因为容器更窄，所以更容易触发。 2. **同一条消息内的多个内容块全部受影响**。上例中三个块连续排列，每一个都在相同的位置被切断。 3. 通过 Browser 实测，承载消息内容的 `.x-markdown` 元素的实际渲染宽度会被内容撑开（`1651 px`），而外层消息区仍为 `990 px`，超出部分既不可见、也无法滚动到。

issues.title: [Design] Reference-counted archival for long-term memory: stale entries as status changes, not deletions
issues.body:
### Context

The README promises "Never forgets", and #7571 (8 comments) reports the user-facing symptom: the agent "keeps forgetting" what matters while stale entries pile up. Both symptoms share a root: distilled long-term memory entries have no TTL, no reference tracking, and no decay. The only cleanup paths are session-file expiry by mtime (`as_agent_wrapper.py:237`) and proactive topic expiry (`steps/evolve/proactive/utils.py:242-254`) — neither touches distilled long-term memory.

### Consequence

Memory only grows: stale facts and conflicting entries accumulate, and retrieval quality degrades over time — "forgets what matters, remembers everything else".

### Proposal (direction, not spec)

1. **Reference tracking**: refresh a last-referenced timestamp when an entry is retrieved and actually used in a response.
2. **Archival, not deletion**: entries unreferenced for N days (e.g., 90) transition to an `archived` status — a status change, not a delete; a later session can re-promote an archived entry with a fresh reference.
3. **Placement TBD**: reme is an external dependency (reme-ai 0.4.2.0), so the fix may belong in the QwenPaw wrapper layer or upstream in the reme repo — happy to follow the maintainers' view on where this fits best.

This mirrors a pattern discussed in the DeepSeek Harness community (cross-session memory with reference-counted archival) and would complement the existing proactive expiry rather than replace it.

issues.title: [Design] Enforce tenant scoping at the memory retrieval layer instead of relying on directory conventions
issues.body:
### Context

Memory isolation currently relies on directory conventions: per-agent workspaces (`workspaces/<agent_id>`, see `app/workspace/workspace.py:108-117` and `app/migration.py:128`). At the retrieval layer, the filter is optional — reme's `vector_search(query, limit, search_filter)` returns an unfiltered matcher when no filter is passed (`local_file_store.py:1060-1076`: `if not search_filter: return lambda chunk: True`).

### Why this matters

For single-user, single-machine setups the directory convention is fine. But with the Hub multi-tenant edition (2.2.0, #7318), a shared reme workspace or a misconfigured `workspace_dir` means the retrieval layer has no enforced tenant boundary to fall back on. There's precedent for the concern in this repo: #4845 reported WeWork channel users leaking other users' chat history — channel-level isolation gaps are already a known pain point.

### Proposal (direction, not spec)

1. **Enforce tenant scoping at the retrieval entry points**: `vector_search` (and similar) require an `agent_id`/`tenant_id` filter; a missing filter is rejected (fail-closed) rather than silently matching everything.
2. **Storage-layer backstop**: entries carry a tenant identifier at write time; retrieval re-validates at the storage layer. Directory conventions become an optimization, not the security boundary.
3. **Scope**: retrieval paths only; no upstream reme data-format changes (backward compatible).

Happy to elaborate or contribute a reference implementation if the maintainers see this as worth exploring.

issues.title: [Security] Default skill-scan mode "warn" proceeds on CRITICAL findings; scan timeout also fails open
issues.body:
### Summary

The skill scanner's default mode is `warn` (`src/qwenpaw/security/skill_scanner/__init__.py:97-107`, overridable via `QWENPAW_SKILL_SCAN_MODE`). In `warn` mode, CRITICAL findings are logged but the skill installs anyway (`:475-483`):

```python
if not result.is_safe:
    should_block = block if block is not None else (mode == "block")
    if should_block: ... raise SkillScanError(result)
    _record_blocked_skill(result, resolved, action="warned")
    logger.warning("... but blocking is disabled – proceeding anyway.")
```

Additionally, a scan timeout returns `None`, which allows installation (`:466-469`) — a fail-open on timeout.

### Risk

Under the default configuration, a skill with a CRITICAL malicious finding installs and runs with only a log line. External research on skill-marketplace hygiene (e.g., NVIDIA's SkillSpector study: ~26% of skills contain vulnerabilities, ~5% likely malicious) suggests the exposure is real, not theoretical.

### Suggested direction

- Source-tiered defaults: built-in skills stay `warn`; community/remote-sourced skills default to `block`.
- Timeout semantics: fail closed — a timed-out scan holds the skill in a pending state instead of allowing it.

I recognize `warn` is a deliberate default (and the env override is appreciated); this suggestion is only about tiering the default by source and tightening the timeout path.

issues.title: [Tracking] max_processes / max_memory_mb are accepted but not enforced by any sandbox backend
issues.body:
### Summary

`src/qwenpaw/sandbox/config.py:173-177` documents (honestly — thank you) that `max_processes` and `max_memory_mb` are accepted but not enforced by any backend:

```
max_processes: Max subprocess count. NOT ENFORCED by any backend
    today; the value is accepted and ignored.
    TODO: needs Linux cgroups / Windows Job objects.
```

### Why track it now

With the Hub multi-tenant edition released in 2.2.0 (#7318), resource limits shift from a single-machine UX concern to an isolation boundary concern: one runaway agent can exhaust host resources for all tenants on the same host.

### Suggested direction

- Linux: cgroups v2 (`pids` controller for process count, `memory` controller for memory).
- Windows: Job Objects.
- Interface stays the same; backends gain enforcement.

Would the maintainers consider a tracking label for this so it doesn't get lost between releases? Happy to help test on Linux if useful.

issues.title: [Design] Minimal egress policy for coding mode: deny-by-default for metadata endpoints, policy-file allowlist on top of existing Landlock ABI v4 port rules
issues.body:
### Context

First off — thank you for the sandbox work. The filesystem isolation is real (Landlock + userns on Linux, plus `runtime_boundary.py` verifying kernel state rather than trusting env vars), and the honesty of `config.py` about what is and isn't enforced is appreciated.

### The gap

In coding mode, the sandbox is configured with no isolation and unrestricted network (`src/qwenpaw/modes/coding/_process.py:51-56`):

```python
config = SandboxConfig(
    mode=SandboxMode.NONE,
    workspace_dir=str(path),
    network_allow=[f"*"],
)
```

`governance/resource_governor.py:405-421` documents why (`pip/git/npm need network`, `Landlock ABI v4 not mainstream`, `macOS has no domain-level filtering`) — so this is a deliberate trade-off, not an oversight. The consequence is still real: a sandboxed process can freely reach intranet segments and cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254 etc.). The "kernel-level sandbox" boundary currently covers files but not network.

### Proposal (minimal, non-breaking)

1. **Deny-by-default for link-local/metadata ranges** (169.254.0.0/16): one default rule, doesn't break pip/git/npm workflows.
2. **Policy-file allowlist**: users/enterprises can re-allow ranges via a policy file, compatible with the existing `network_allow` semantics.
3. **Reuse what's already there**: `linux_sandbox.py` already implements Landlock ABI v4 port-level rules (`_landlock_add_net_port_rule`). This proposal is mostly productization of defaults + policy file, not new kernel capability.

### Rollout

A config switch, e.g. `egress_policy: off | minimal | strict`, defaulting to `off` or `minimal` (maintainer's call). `off` keeps today's behavior exactly.

Happy to elaborate on the policy-file format if useful.

issues.title: [Bug]: Context meter under-reports usage for Anthropic Messages providers (cache read/write tokens are not counted)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2b4 

## Description

When a provider uses the Anthropic Messages protocol with prompt caching, the context meter next to the chat input shows a much smaller value than the real context size.

In Anthropic's usage, `input_tokens` counts only the uncached part of the prompt. Cache reads (`cache_read_input_tokens`) and cache writes (`cache_creation_input_tokens`) are reported separately, and both are part of the prompt the model processed. The context size of one request is therefore:

```text
input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens
```

`TokenRecordingModelWrapper._record_usage()` in `src/qwenpaw/token_usage/model_wrapper.py` sets `last_prompt_tokens` to `input_tokens` alone. The console channel (`src/qwenpaw/app/channels/console/channel.py`, around line 440) sends this value as `context_usage.estimated_tokens` in the live `turn_usage` event, and the meter divides it by the context window. Once most of a conversation is cached, the meter shows only the few thousand new tokens of each request.

The same file already handles this correctly for the cache hit rate: for Anthropic models, `_cache_usage_metrics()` uses `prompt_tokens + cache_read_tokens + cache_write_tokens` as the input denominator. The context value does not get the same adjustment.

OpenAI Chat Completions and Responses are not affected, because their `prompt_tokens` / `input_tokens` already include cached tokens.

**Related PR(s):** #7899 (added `last_prompt_tokens` and the live per-call context value)

**Security considerations:** None.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2b4
- **OS:** Windows
- **Install method:** pip
- **Python version (if applicable):** 3.12.10

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Add a custom provider that uses the Anthropic Messages protocol (`AnthropicChatModel`) with a Claude model that supports prompt caching.
2. Hold a multi-turn conversation (tool calls help) until most of each request is served from cache.
3. Watch the context meter while a reply is streaming, and compare it with the usage returned by the provider.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** For a request with `input_tokens=3000`, `cache_read_input_tokens=120000`, and `cache_creation_input_tokens=5000` on a 200k window, the meter shows about 3k / 200k (1.5%).
- **Expected:** The meter shows 128k / 200k (64%).

## Logs / Screenshots

Minimal offline reproduction with the installed package (no network request):

```python
from types import SimpleNamespace
from agentscope.model import AnthropicChatModel
import qwenpaw.token_usage.model_wrapper as mw
from qwenpaw.token_usage.model_wrapper import TokenRecordingModelWrapper

mw.get_token_usage_manager = lambda: SimpleNamespace(enqueue=lambda event: None)
captured = {}
inner = object.__new__(AnthropicChatModel)
inner.context_size = 200_000
wrapper = object.__new__(TokenRecordingModelWrapper)
for key, value in {
    "_model": inner,
    "_provider_id": "demo",
    "_compact_threshold": None,
    "model": "demo",
}.items():
    object.__setattr__(wrapper, key, value)
wrapper._store_usage = captured.update
wrapper._record_usage(SimpleNamespace(
    input_tokens=3_000,
    output_tokens=500,
    cache_input_tokens=120_000,
    cache_creation_input_tokens=5_000,
    metadata={},
))
print(captured["last_prompt_tokens"], captured["cache_eligible_input_tokens"])
```

Output:

```
3000 128000
```

`last_prompt_tokens` (used by the context meter) is 3000, while the wrapper's own cache denominator for the same request is 128000.

## Additional Notes

A possible fix in `_record_usage()` is to reuse the value `_cache_usage_metrics()` already computes:

```python
"last_prompt_tokens": cache_eligible if cache_observed else pt,
```

For Anthropic models this gives `input + cache read + cache write`. For OpenAI Chat and Responses, `cache_eligible` equals `pt`, so their behavior stays the same.

From reading the code: at the end of each turn, `_commit_turn_usage()` sends another `turn_usage` event whose `context_usage` comes from the character-based estimate in `snapshot_context_usage_for_state()`. The meter may therefore switch between the provider value during streaming and the local estimate after the turn.

We hit the same problem in a local usage-statistics plugin and fixed it by adding cache read and cache write tokens for Anthropic models.

issues.title: [Bug]: Status-less model overload in an OpenAI-compatible stream bypasses retries
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

Observed twice on 2.3.0.post1. Reproduced against `main` at `228e303` using a mock HTTP transport.

## Description

An OpenAI-compatible gateway can return HTTP 200 for a streamed request and then send an SSE error with the message `Our servers are currently overloaded. Please try again later.` and no status code. The OpenAI SDK raises a base `APIError`. QwenPaw classifies this as `unknown`, so it skips its existing retry policy even if the model call has not yielded meaningful content.

**Related issue:** #8864 concerns disconnects **after** partial output. This report is limited to overload classification and does not propose replaying emitted output or tool calls.

**Security considerations:** No changes to authentication. This report uses a synthetic stream; it does not include the original request, response dump, or configuration.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (providers)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0.post1
- **OS:** Linux container on Docker Desktop for macOS
- **Install method:** Docker (`agentscope/qwenpaw:latest`)
- **Python version:** 3.11
- **OpenAI SDK version:** 2.33.0

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable model retries and use an OpenAI-compatible chat model with streaming enabled.
2. For the first request, have a mock gateway respond with HTTP 200 and `Content-Type: text/event-stream`. Before sending any content, emit this SSE event:

   ```text
   data: {"error":{"message":"Our servers are currently overloaded. Please try again later."}}
   ```

3. Configure the mock to return a normal completion on the next request. Observe the request count and result.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** One model request; `openai.APIError` escapes and the turn fails with `MODEL_EXECUTION_ERROR`.
- **Expected:** Treat this specific status-less overload as transient. Apply the configured retry limit and backoff if meaningful output has not been emitted. Keep the existing no-replay behavior once meaningful output has been emitted.

## Logs / Screenshots

```text
openai.APIError: Our servers are currently overloaded. Please try again later.
ModelErrorDecision(kind='unknown', status_code=None, retryable=False, fallback_eligible=False)
```

## Additional Notes

I reproduced this with the real OpenAI SDK and a mock transport and have a scoped fix and regression tests in progress.

issues.title: [Bug]: Discord chunk_text duplicates a code fence that starts on a chunk boundary
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

main @ 2b4e13e (from source)

## Description

In the Discord channel, `chunk_text` (`plugins/channel/discord/qwenpaw_channel_discord/formatting.py`) updates the code-fence state before it decides whether to flush. When the opening fence line of a code block is the line that overflows the chunk, the previous chunk gets a stray closing fence and the next chunk starts with the opener twice, so the code block renders wrong in both messages. With `max_len=2000`, a chunk can also go over Discord's 2000-character limit in this case.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)

- **OS:** macOS 26
- **Install method:** from source

## Steps to Reproduce

```python
from qwenpaw_channel_discord.formatting import chunk_text  # plugins/channel/discord on sys.path
text = "intro line one is here\nintro line two is here too\n```python\nx = 1\n```\nafter"
print(chunk_text(text, max_len=60))
```

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** `['intro line one is here\nintro line two is here too\n```', '```python\n```python\nx = 1\n```\nafter']`
- **Expected:** `['intro line one is here\nintro line two is here too', '```python\nx = 1\n```\nafter']`


issues.title: [Bug]: MCP streamable_http client masks server 4xx as "not connected" and tears down the session

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## 环境

- QwenPaw 2.3.0.post1（`pip show qwenpaw` 与 `qwenpaw --version` 双向确认），Linux 容器，Python 3.11
- 驱动：自定义 MCP driver，transport: streamable_http
- 服务端：一个远端 MCP 服务（URL 已脱敏为 `<relay-endpoint>`），只实现 legacy 握手（server/discover 回 unknown method，客户端会 fallback 到 legacy）

## 影响

误导性错误信息 + 无谓的 session 抖动。调用方只能看到 "MCP client 'x' is not connected. Call connect() first."，会把"我的请求被服务端判为 400"误判成"连接器坏了"，实际排查因此走错方向数小时。

## 复现

1. 配置一个 streamable_http MCP driver，指向对某些 tools/call 返回 HTTP 400 的服务端。
2. 调用该工具，例如 register_agent，其中某个字段形状不合服务端 schema（本案：egress.ip 填了 "1.2.3.4, 5.6.7.8" 这种逗号拼接的多 IP，服务端要求单个 IP）。
3. 观察返回：

   ```
   RuntimeError: MCP client 'agent-relay' is not connected. Call connect() first.
   ```

4. 同一时刻其它工具（get_agent_card / list_groups / list_tasks）全部正常返回 → 极易被误判为"只有某个工具坏"。

## 实际发生的事（traceback 证据）

qwenpaw.log 中该 WARNING 下方的 ExceptionGroup 才含真因：

```
httpx.HTTPStatusError: Client error '400 Bad Request' for url '<relay-endpoint>'
  at mcp/client/streamable_http.py:381, in _handle_post_request -> response.raise_for_status()
```

链路：raise_for_status() 未被捕获 → anyio ExceptionGroup 冒泡出 TaskGroup → _handle_transport_error() 调 _begin_session_teardown() 并把 session 置空 → 在飞行的 call_tool 走到 _rpc_gone_error()，返回 "not connected" 文案 → 生命周期任务 0.9s 后重连成功，一切恢复正常。

## 期望行为

1. 非 2xx 响应应把状态码 + 响应体回传给调用方（包装成 ToolCallError 之类），而不是让 raise_for_status() 把异常抛穿 TaskGroup。
2. 即便是传输层错误，返回文案也不应断言 "not connected"；至少区分 "server returned HTTP 400" 与 "session gone"。
3. 可选：服务端 4xx 属于请求问题，不应触发整条 session 的拆除与重连（其它并发 RPC 会被一起打断）。

## 建议修法（最小改动）

- streamable_http 的 _handle_post_request 捕获 httpx.HTTPStatusError，读取 response.aread()，转成非致命的结构化错误（不冒泡出 TaskGroup）。
- _rpc_gone_error() 在存在已知 transport 根因时，附带原始异常摘要。
- 日志层面：把底层 httpx.HTTPStatusError 的 url / status / body 摘要提到 WARNING 主行，而不是只留在 ExceptionGroup 里。

## 备注

同样的表象在 15:56 / 15:59 / 23:19 / 23:22 出现 4 次，每次 payload 都是同一个坏字段，说明这是稳定可复现的，不是偶发网络问题。改对字段后连续 3 次调用全部 ok，证明通道本身健康。

issues.title: [Bug]: Streaming reply aborts mid-output with RemoteProtocolError and is not retried once partial content is emitted
issues.body:
### Environment

- QwenPaw 2.3.0
- Windows 10 (AMD64), `console` channel
- Provider: `deepseek` / model: `deepseek-v4-flash`
- `thinking_level: max`
- Context usage at failure: `last_prompt_tokens: 82682`, `context_size: 900000` (~9%). This is **not** a context-overflow issue.

### Symptom

In one session, three consecutive replies aborted mid-stream. The UI shows `UNKNOWN_AGENT_ERROR` with:

```
peer closed connection without sending complete message body (incomplete chunked read)
```

Two aborted replies were long, but one aborted after a single sentence, so output length is not the trigger.

### Evidence

From `qwenpaw.log`:

```
2026-11-23 14:11:03 | builder: built agent ... model=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash
2026-11-23 14:12:01 | runtime: unhandled error session=...: peer closed connection ...
2026-11-23 14:15:31 | builder: built agent ... model=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash
2026-11-23 14:16:01 | runtime: unhandled error session=...: peer closed connection ...
```

The second failure landed exactly 30.0s after the request started.

The dump's `exception_type` is `httpx.RemoteProtocolError`, **not** `StreamIdleTimeoutError`. There is no `LLM stream ... produced no content for 30s` warning at these timestamps. (That warning does appear on 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-20, so the first-content watchdog itself works.)

The traceback ends in `openai/_streaming.py` -> `httpx._models.aiter_raw`, i.e. the upstream closed the SSE connection while more chunks were expected.

### Root cause

`qwenpaw/providers/retry_chat_model.py`, `_wrap_stream`:

```python
except Exception as retry_exc:
    pending_stream = None
    if emitted:
        raise
```

`httpx.RemoteProtocolError` is classified as transient/retryable in `model_error_policy.py`, but once any meaningful chunk has been emitted the retry is skipped unconditionally. A transient upstream disconnect therefore destroys the whole turn and surfaces a hard error, even though the failure is recoverable.

### Expected behavior

A transient mid-stream disconnect (`RemoteProtocolError` / `APIConnectionError` / read timeout) should not discard the turn. Either:

1. retry the request once and replace/resume the partial assistant message; or
2. persist the partial content and return a soft "response interrupted, retry?" state instead of `UNKNOWN_AGENT_ERROR`.

### Suggested fix

- In `_wrap_stream`, only skip retry when `emitted` **and** the error is non-transient. For transient errors, allow at least one retry (optionally with a flag telling the UI to replace the partial block).
- If a full retry is undesirable because it duplicates tokens, resume by sending the partial assistant content back as context and asking the model to continue.
- At minimum, include the partial content in the error dump so the user can recover it manually.

### Workaround

Setting `QWENPAW_LLM_STREAM_FIRST_CONTENT_TIMEOUT=180` and `QWENPAW_LLM_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT=120` reduces false-positive idle timeouts, but does **not** prevent an upstream mid-stream close and does not change the `if emitted: raise` behavior.
