issues.title: [Bug]: Memory backend silently falls back to ReMeLight on a startup race (plugin installed but not yet registered) and never self-heals
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0.post1 (plugin `memory-openviking` 1.0.0)

## Description

An agent configured with `running.memory_manager_backend = "openviking"` sometimes runs on the
built-in **ReMeLight** backend for the entire process lifetime, even though the OpenViking plugin
is installed, enabled, and registers successfully a few seconds later.

On cold start, workspace service creation can win the race against plugin backend registration.
`_effective_memory_backend_id()` catches `MemoryBackendUnavailableError` and falls back to
`remelight`, logging:

```
WARNING ... workspace.py:80 | Configured memory backend 'openviking' is unavailable for agent
'default'; using 'remelight' until the configured backend is available
```

The message promises a temporary fallback, but **nothing re-resolves the backend once the plugin
finishes registering**. There is no invalidate/rebuild hook on memory-backend registration, so the
"temporary" fallback becomes permanent until the agent config is manually changed or the agent is
reloaded.

Impact: long-term memory is silently diverted into the local ReMe store instead of the configured
remote backend. Auto-recall serves local `memory/*.md` files, `memory_search` returns local-index
results, and the remote (possibly shared, multi-agent) memory space stops receiving updates. The
only signal is a WARNING log line — nothing is surfaced in the Console.

This contradicts the explicit contract in `get_memory_manager_backend()`:

> Unknown backends fail explicitly; memory data must never be redirected into another backend as
> an implicit fallback.

**Related PR(s):** #7663 (introduced the fallback), #3386 (two-phase background startup + parallel
agent initialization), #7616 (ADBPG/PowerContext moved to plugins). Closest analogous, already-fixed
bug: #8538 (channel plugin activation racing a fixed startup window).

**Security considerations:** memory content is silently written to a different store than the one
the operator selected. Where the configured backend is a remote/shared space and the fallback is
local (or vice versa), this changes the data residency of conversation-derived memories without any
user-visible indication.

### How the two PRs combine

* #7663 added the fallback for a legitimate case: a user upgrades, the backend moved to a plugin
  (#7616), and the plugin is **not installed yet**. Its stated recovery path is manual:
  "After the plugin becomes available, **reloading the Agent** restores the configured backend."
* #3386 made startup two-phase, with agents/plugins/services initializing **in parallel in the
  background** (`Server ready in 0.280s (agents loading in background)`).

Together, "plugin installed but registration not finished yet" became a common transient boot state,
and it is handled identically to "plugin permanently absent" — with no automatic recovery.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0.post1
- **OS:** Linux 6.18 x86_64 (NAS, fnOS-based)
- **Install method:** pip (venv), managed by QwenPaw Hub runtime
- **Python version:** 3.12.4
- **Memory plugin:** memory-openviking 1.0.0, backend id `openviking`
- **Backend config:** `commit_policy=auto`, `auto_memory_search_config={enabled:true,max_results:3}`,
  `retrieval_token_budget=2048`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install the `memory-openviking` plugin and select `openviking` as the agent's long-term memory
   backend in the Console. Confirm it works (recall returns `viking://...` results).
2. Restart the QwenPaw process.
3. After startup, inspect the effective backend — e.g. call `memory_search`, or grep the log for
   `workspace.py:80`.
4. Repeat across several restarts. The outcome depends on whether workspace service creation
   completes before plugin backend registration.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** On some cold starts the agent silently runs on ReMeLight indefinitely. Memory writes
  and recall both go to the local store; the configured remote backend receives nothing. Recovery
  requires manually editing the agent's memory config (or reloading the agent).
- **Expected:** An installed-and-enabled plugin backend should be used. A transient
  "not registered yet" state during boot should either be awaited, or self-heal as soon as
  registration completes — and any diversion of memory data should be visible to the operator.

## Logs / Screenshots

### Observed frequency: 2 of 7 cold starts

Plugin backend registration consistently lands ~5-6s after "Server ready"; workspace memory-manager
creation time varies. When creation is faster than registration, the fallback fires.

| Cold start (`_app.py:490`) | `openviking` registered (`plugins/api.py:672`) | ReMeLight constructed (`reme_light_memory_manager.py:291`) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-12 00:17:42 | 00:17:47 (+5s) | — | openviking |
| 2026-11-12 01:29:33 | 01:29:39 (+6s) | — | openviking |
| 2026-11-12 02:01:03 | 02:01:08 (+5s) | — | openviking |
| 2026-11-12 14:29:07 | 14:29:12 (+5s) | — | openviking |
| 2026-11-13 21:18:00 | 21:18:05 (+5s) | — | openviking |
| **2026-11-18 17:48:37** | 17:48:43 (+6s) | **17:48:42 (+5s)** | **fell back** |
| **2026-11-23 18:48:30** | 18:48:36 (+6s) | **18:48:33 (+3s)** | **fell back** |

Note the counter-intuitive direction: a *faster* workspace startup makes the fallback *more* likely.

### Failure timeline (2026-11-23)

```
18:48:30 INFO  _app.py:490              | Server ready in 0.280s (agents loading in background)
18:48:30 INFO  plugins/loader.py:650    | Scanning plugin directory: <runtime>/working/plugins
18:48:30 INFO  plugins/loader.py:669    | Discovered plugin: memory-openviking
18:48:33 INFO  workspace.py:416         | workspace default: bootstrap_plugins complete (hooks=7 commands=36 ...)
18:48:33 INFO  workspace.py:765         | Starting workspace: default
18:48:33 WARN  workspace.py:80          | Configured memory backend 'openviking' is unavailable for agent 'default'; using 'remelight' until the configured backend is available
18:48:33 INFO  reme_light_memory_manager.py:291 | ReMeLightMemoryManager init: agent_id=default
18:48:34 INFO  reme_light_memory_manager.py:348 | ReMe memory manager started for agent 'default'
18:48:34 INFO  workspace.py:804         | Workspace started successfully: default
18:48:36 INFO  plugins/api.py:672       | Plugin 'memory-openviking' registered memory backend 'openviking'
18:48:38 INFO  _app.py:617              | Core agents ready in 8.184s
```

`bootstrap_plugins complete` is logged **before** the memory backend is registered, so the name is
misleading if read as "all plugin registration finished".

The 2026-11-18 failure has the identical structure (fallback at +5s, registration at +6s).

### Symptom confirmation while in the fallen-back state

`memory_search` returns local ReMe index results rather than OpenViking results:

```
========== memory/2026-11-23/<note>.md:12-89 [score=3.8963] ==========
```

Expected OpenViking shape is a leading untrusted-history notice followed by
`[1] viking://user/<user>/memories/..., score=0.9xx`.

Remote-side confirmation: no new session was created on the OpenViking server for any conversation
after the fallen-back startup, while sessions created earlier the same day (after a config-triggered
rebuild) are present.

## Additional Notes

### Relevant code

* `src/qwenpaw/app/workspace/workspace.py:59` — `_MEMORY_BACKEND_FALLBACK = "remelight"`
* `src/qwenpaw/app/workspace/workspace.py:67-88` — `_effective_memory_backend_id()`: catches
  `MemoryBackendUnavailableError`, logs the "until ... available" warning, returns the fallback.
* `src/qwenpaw/app/workspace/workspace.py:521-534` — `_create_memory_manager()`: same fallback branch.
* `src/qwenpaw/agents/memory/base_memory_manager.py:1162` — `get_memory_manager_backend()` docstring
  forbids implicit redirection of memory data.
* `src/qwenpaw/plugins/_memory.py` — no invalidate/rebuild hook when a memory backend is registered.

### Possible fixes (any one would resolve it)

1. **Barrier:** await memory-backend registration before constructing an agent's memory manager.
2. **Self-heal:** when a plugin registers a memory backend, invalidate/rebuild the memory_manager
   service of agents whose *configured* backend matches — this actually delivers the promised
   "until the configured backend is available" semantics.
3. **Make it visible:** surface the fallback in the Console (not only a WARNING log) and offer a
   "retry backend resolution" action.
4. **Honor the contract:** fail explicitly instead of redirecting memory data. Safest for data
   residency, but reduces availability in the genuine "plugin not installed" upgrade case that
   #7663 was written for — so options 1-3 are probably preferable.

A refinement worth considering: distinguish "plugin present on disk but not yet registered" from
"plugin not installed at all". Only the latter is the scenario #7663 targeted.

### Workaround

After startup, change any value in the agent's memory backend config (and change it back if
desired). This triggers `Service 'memory_manager' is not compatible with the reloaded configuration
... creating a new instance`, and by then the plugin is registered, so the configured backend is
resolved correctly. Verified twice in our deployment: a config-triggered rebuild restored OpenViking
both times, and remote sessions resumed immediately afterwards.

issues.title: [Bug]: Console freezes on iOS WebKit in long conversations due to UserMessageAnchors layout thrashing and content-visibility:auto in column-reverse list
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

`2.3.0.post1` (commit `ee58cb1a64f2b21e825c525f73dc44bc7941edea`, Console using `@agentscope-ai/chat` `^1.2.0-beta.1792133067831`)

## Description

On iOS Safari / WebKit, opening or continuing a long chat session with substantial context causes the Console UI to freeze / become unresponsive, even though initial DOM load itself is fast (~742ms).

Investigating both `console/src/pages/Chat/` and `@agentscope-ai/chat` points to **4 interacting root causes** that combine into severe layout thrashing / main-thread hang on iOS WebKit:

### 1. `UserMessageAnchors` still observes every bubble and forces synchronous layout in `navigator` mode
- `console/src/pages/Chat/longChatPerformance.ts` enables `LONG_CHAT_USER_MESSAGE_ANCHORS = { enabled: true, variant: "navigator" }`, with the comment assuming `navigator` mode does not observe or measure every bubble.
- However, in `@agentscope-ai/chat/lib/AgentScopeRuntimeWebUI/core/Chat/MessageList/UserMessageAnchors/`:
  - `index.js:531-538`: Whenever there are ≥ 3 user messages (`visible === true`), even with `variant === 'navigator'`, it:
    1. Calls `observeMessageLayout(scrollEl, ...)` (`targetLayout.js:105-116`), which attaches a `ResizeObserver` to **every `[data-role][id]` bubble** in the scroll container.
    2. Attaches a `MutationObserver` with `{ childList: true, characterData: true, subtree: true }` to the entire message scroll container.
    3. Listens to `scroll` events on the scroll container.
  - `index.js:454-463`: On every scroll frame, resize, or streaming character mutation, `measureAnchors()` queries all `[data-role][id]` bubbles and calls `target.getBoundingClientRect()` on **every single bubble** **before** the `if (variant === 'navigator') return;` early-return on line 463.
- On iOS WebKit, this triggers forced synchronous layout across the entire message list during streaming and momentum scrolling.

### 2. `content-visibility: auto` + `contain-intrinsic-size: auto 160px` inside `flex-direction: column-reverse` on iOS WebKit
- `@agentscope-ai/chat/lib/Bubble/Bubble.js:83-85` applies inline styles `contentVisibility: 'auto'` and `containIntrinsicSize: 'auto 160px'` to every bubble.
- `@agentscope-ai/chat/lib/Bubble/style/list.js` renders the message list with `flex-direction: column-reverse` (`order="desc"`).
- On iOS 18+ WebKit, `content-visibility: auto` inside a `column-reverse` scroll container—especially when real bubble heights (long Markdown, Prism code blocks, tool cards) greatly exceed `160px` and `UserMessageAnchors` repeatedly calls `getBoundingClientRect()` and observes every bubble via `ResizeObserver`—causes severe layout thrashing, scroll anchor jumps, and WebContent hangs.

### 3. `setSessionMessages` in `Chat/index.tsx` omits `history: true` (bypassing SDK pagination), and SDK pagination never unmounts offscreen bubbles
- `@agentscope-ai/chat/lib/AgentScopeRuntimeWebUI/core/Chat/MessageList/index.js:82-98` only paginates (`PAGE_SIZE = 10`) messages with `m.history === true`, and `loadMore` uses `flushSync` (line 102) without virtualizing/unmounting scrolled-away bubbles (related to #3923).
- While `ChatAnywhereSessionsContext.js:244-248` adds `history: true` on initial session load, `console/src/pages/Chat/index.tsx` calls `chatRef.current?.messages.setSessionMessages(...)` with refreshed history messages (`recovered.messages` / `session.messages`, e.g. queue recovery and handoff refresh) without marking `history: true`, causing the entire session history to mount synchronously at once.

### 4. `ComposerAccessibilityLabels` observes the entire chat layout subtree
- `console/src/pages/Chat/components/ComposerAccessibilityLabels.tsx:112-115` attaches `MutationObserver({ childList: true, subtree: true })` to `-chat-anywhere-layout` (which wraps the entire `MessageList` as well as the composer), running `querySelectorAll("button")` over newly added message nodes during streaming/history loads.

**Related Issue(s):** #3923

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** `2.3.0.post1` (`ee58cb1a64f2b21e825c525f73dc44bc7941edea`)
- **OS:** iOS (Safari / WKWebView)
- **Install method:** pip (`qwenpaw==2.3.0.post1`)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a chat session in QwenPaw Console on iOS Safari / WebKit with a long conversation history (many turns, long Markdown/code blocks/tool calls).
2. Scroll through the conversation or continue streaming new replies.
3. Observe UI responsiveness.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** Initial DOM load completes quickly (~742ms), then the page freezes / becomes unresponsive on iOS once the long conversation renders, scrolls, or streams.
- **Expected:** Long conversations remain responsive and scrollable on iOS WebKit without main-thread hangs.

## Suggested Fixes

### Console-side mitigations
1. Disable `userMessageAnchors` on iOS / iPadOS WebKit (or until `@agentscope-ai/chat` stops observing/measuring all bubbles in `navigator` mode).
2. Override bubble `content-visibility: visible; contain-intrinsic-size: none;` under `@supports (-webkit-touch-callout: none)` to avoid WebKit `column-reverse` + `content-visibility: auto` layout hangs.
3. Mark hydrated messages with `history: true` when calling `setSessionMessages` with refreshed session history in `console/src/pages/Chat/index.tsx`.
4. Scope `ComposerAccessibilityLabels`'s `MutationObserver` to the sender container (`-chat-anywhere-chat-sender` / `-sender`) instead of `-chat-anywhere-layout`.

### Upstream `@agentscope-ai/chat` SDK root fixes
1. In `UserMessageAnchors`: in `navigator` mode, do not attach `ResizeObserver` to every bubble or `MutationObserver({ subtree: true, characterData: true })` to the whole message list, and avoid measuring all bubbles with `getBoundingClientRect()` on every scroll/mutation frame.
2. Revisit `content-visibility: auto` on `Bubble` inside `column-reverse` lists on WebKit, and consider windowed/virtualized rendering for long histories instead of append-only `flushSync` pagination.

issues.title: [Bug]: Opening the Voice Transcription settings page imports whisper into the server process (~690 MB RSS, never released)
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

`2.3.0b1`, installed from source at commit `b12b06ed`.

## Description

`GET /api/workspace/local-whisper-status` calls `check_local_whisper_available()`, which performs a real `import whisper` just to tell the UI whether the optional dependency is installed:

```python
# src/qwenpaw/agents/utils/audio_transcription.py
whisper_ok = False
try:
    import whisper as _whisper  # noqa: F401
    whisper_ok = True
except ImportError:
    pass
```

Importing `whisper` pulls in `torch` and the whole CUDA runtime (`libtorch_cuda`, `libcublasLt`, `libnvrtc`, `libnvJitLink`), plus `librosa` → `numba`/`llvmlite` and `tiktoken`. Measured on this machine: **163 MB → 853 MB RSS (+690 MB)** for a single call. Python imports are permanent, so the memory stays in the server process until it is restarted.

The Console calls this endpoint unconditionally when the **Voice Transcription settings page** mounts (`api.getLocalWhisperStatus()` inside the `Promise.all` in `loadSettings`), regardless of the configured provider:

```ts
// console/src/pages/Settings/VoiceTranscription/useVoiceTranscription.ts
const [modeRes, provTypeRes, provRes, lwStatus] = await Promise.all([
  api.getAudioMode(),
  api.getTranscriptionProviderType(),
  api.getTranscriptionProviders(),
  api.getLocalWhisperStatus(),   // even when provider_type is "whisper_api"
]);
```

Consequence: a user who only uses the remote Whisper API (or has transcription disabled) permanently pays ~690 MB of RSS for visiting a settings page once. In the observed instance an otherwise idle `qwenpaw app` process sat at ~1.9 GB PSS / 1.6 GB anonymous memory, with 14 torch/CUDA/numba `.so` files mapped, while the remote transcription provider was the one actually configured.

**Related PR(s):** #8431 (converts local Whisper into an SDK plugin — may relocate this code, but the probe still runs in the main server process today)

**Security considerations:** none.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0b1 (source, `b12b06ed`)
- **OS:** Ubuntu (Linux 7.3.0)
- **Install method:** pip editable install from source, `openai-whisper` installed in the same environment
- **Python version:** 3.12

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install QwenPaw in an environment that also has `openai-whisper` installed (so `import whisper` succeeds).
2. Start `qwenpaw app` and record the server process PSS (`/proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup`).
3. Open **Settings → Voice Transcription** in the Console.
4. Record PSS again, and check `/proc/<pid>/maps` for `libtorch*` / `libcublas*`.

Standalone reproduction of the underlying call (no HTTP needed):

```bash
python -c "
import sys
def rss():
    return [int(l.split()[1])/1024 for l in open('/proc/self/status') if l.startswith('VmRSS:')][0]
from qwenpaw.agents.utils.audio_transcription import check_local_whisper_available
before = rss(); check_local_whisper_available()
print(f'{before:.0f}MB -> {rss():.0f}MB, torch={ \"torch\" in sys.modules }')
"
```

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** `check_local_whisper_available()` costs ~690 MB RSS and loads torch/CUDA permanently; the process never returns to its pre-visit footprint.
- **Expected:** a read-only availability probe should be effectively free. `importlib.util.find_spec("whisper")` answers the same question with 0 MB and ~4 ms, because it only performs a file-system lookup.

## Logs / Screenshots

Memory-map evidence from the affected process:

```
Pss / Pss_Anon / Pss_File = 1886 MB / 1646 MB / 240 MB
14 unique mappings matching libtorch*, libcublas*, libnvrtc*, libnumba, libllvmlite
GPU memory in use: 15 MiB (CUDA context created, nothing running)
```

Probe cost, same interpreter:

| Probe | RSS delta | wall | torch loaded |
|---|---|---|---|
| `importlib.util.find_spec("whisper")` | +0 MB | 3.8 ms | no |
| `check_local_whisper_available()` (current) | **+690 MB** | 1.35 s | **yes** |

## Additional Notes

Suggested fix (opened as a PR): resolve the module instead of importing it —

```python
try:
    whisper_ok = importlib.util.find_spec("whisper") is not None
except (ImportError, ValueError):
    whisper_ok = False
```

A broken install would now be reported as "installed" by the probe and fail later, but `_transcribe_local_whisper()` already logs that failure as a warning, so no functionality is lost while the 690 MB is avoided.

Optional follow-up on the Console side: only request `/local-whisper-status` when the selected provider is `local_whisper` (the value is currently only consumed by `AudioModeCard`), so the endpoint is not called at all for remote/disabled setups.

Related memory reports: #7222 (unbounded growth of a long-running backend), #7818 (UI freeze / high memory) — different root causes, but they explain why a permanent ~690 MB baseline is noticeable.

prs.title: refactor(runtime): unify session configuration for ACP and native execution
prs.body:
ACP and native execution now use the same session configuration snapshot. Two sessions of one agent can select different settings without changing saved defaults or other processes.

- Define session settings once in `SessionConfig`, inherited by `AgentProfileConfig`. Core `RuntimeParameters` merges global defaults, agent settings, startup defaults, and session overrides, preserving omitted fields and explicit `false`, `null`, and empty lists. ACP inherits the constructor and translates protocol inputs; new session fields require no ACP mapping.
- Support workspace/project directories, models, permissions, coding mode, goal, mission, and loop gates. Keep existing ACP flags, metadata, model/permission setters, and load/resume behavior. Resetting `qwenpaw.config` clears that layer without confusing it with retained legacy metadata.
- Let registered modes declare configuration or entry commands. Resolve saved mode state and Mission's pinned directories before constructing the execution snapshot. Remove duplicated Builder precedence, ACP-specific runtime hooks, the global stop-handler bridge, and obsolete state-loading entry points.
- Keep gate state and resource ownership session-local. Workspace replacements are prepared before publication; failed service or MCP preparation preserves the previous owner. Switching modes replaces derived defaults rather than accumulating them.
- Use one effective iteration limit throughout QwenPaw. Positive limits may exceed 500; disabling the iteration gate removes the fallback limit while cancellation and other enabled stopping conditions remain effective.

Validation: concurrent session and separate-process isolation, legacy restore semantics, no override persistence, failed resource replacement, restored mode switching, Mission directory consistency, ACP stdio lifecycle, and real execution beyond 100 iterations with cancellation. Existing regressions were extended and obsolete helper/forwarding tests removed. English and Chinese documentation matches the final behavior.

Results: 4,031 regression tests passed and 14 were skipped. The three frozen-worker tests needed the ignored official-channel bundle generated by the existing build hook, then passed on rerun. After the final parameter API cleanup, all 32 affected configuration/ACP tests passed again. Pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed.

prs.title: fix(plugins): keep llama-server from outliving a crashed backend
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`llama-server.exe` survives QwenPaw dying (#8830). The plugin launches it with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` and nothing else — no new process group, no job — so when the backend crashes or is force-killed, nothing tells the server to stop. The reporter's table shows four successive starts each leaving a healthy server behind on its own random port; the fifth start then finds no RAM commit left, the child dies inside `load_model`, and all the user sees is `llama.cpp server exited before becoming ready`.

`stop_server` covers the orderly path (SIGTERM, then kill, bounded). It never runs on a crash, and the reporter notes the `atexit` path does not run either. The same hole exists on POSIX: `start_new_session` puts the server in its own group, but the group signal is also sent by `stop_server`, which a `SIGKILL` of the provider skips.

**Fix: bind the server's lifetime to the provider, at the kernel level, on both platforms.**

- **Windows** — a job with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`. When the provider's last job handle goes away, on any exit path including `TerminateProcess`, the kernel terminates every member.
- **Linux** — `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` set in a `preexec_fn` that runs between fork and exec. `SIGKILL` of the parent makes the kernel deliver `SIGKILL` to the child.

No exit handler has to run in either case, which is the point: crash-path coverage by construction, not by cleanup code a crash skips.

macOS has no equivalent knob, so it keeps the existing behaviour (`start_new_session` + group signal on an orderly stop).

## Evidence

**Windows** — same `process_options()` arguments the plugin uses, then `taskkill /F /PID <parent>` without `/T`, exactly as a crash leaves it:

```
parent pid=10460 child pid=1448
child alive after parent was killed: True      <- orphan reproduced
```

with a kill-on-close job:

```
parent pid=10308 child pid=12188
child alive after parent was killed: False     <- fix verified
```

**Linux** — real kernel, Ubuntu 24.04 / kernel 6.8.0-138 / Python 3.12.3, run against the patched `io_helpers.py` (not a stand-in):

```
process_options keys: ['preexec_fn', 'start_new_session']
--- control (no hook) ---           child_alive_after_parent_sigkill=True
--- patched process_options() ---   child_alive_after_parent_sigkill=False
VERDICT: FIX HOLDS
```

**On the documented `preexec_fn` risk.** The Python docs warn that it is not safe with threads, because the child can deadlock before exec. That is a probability, not a certainty, so it was measured rather than assumed:

| shape | worst case | stalls |
|---|---|---|
| 8 / 32 / 96 hog threads, 400–800 forks each | 0.016s / 0.061s / 0.126s | 0 |
| 16 / 48 / 96 threads forking simultaneously, 30–40 rounds | ≤ 0.029s | 0 frozen |
| bare `os.fork()` without exec, 32 / 128 / 256 threads | ≤ 0.014s | 0 stuck |
| 64 threads, 180s soak | 0.015s over 38,244 forks | 0 |

About 150,000 fork/exec cycles in total: **the deadlock never reproduced**. It is not eliminated on principle — the window the docs describe is "another thread held a C-level lock at fork time", and only libraries that fail to register an `atfork` handler keep that window open. This hook calls `libc.so.6` and nothing else, which is why it held up.

The measurement also changed the implementation: with the lookup `LIBC.prctl(...)` inside the child, the 96-thread worst case was **0.126s** — 15× the control — against **0.016s** once the function pointer is taken in the parent. The code resolves `_PRCTL` at import and the child does exactly one call.

## Scope

Type: B (process lifecycle / failure handling)

- **This stops new orphans; it does not reclaim existing ones.** Servers left over from earlier crashes keep running — they need a restart or a manual kill. Reclaiming them means deciding which `llama-server.exe` on the machine is ours; separate change.
- **Adopting an already-running server** instead of spawning a fresh one is the other half of what the report describes. It needs a persisted port/pid contract and a handshake; out of scope.
- macOS: no `PDEATHSIG`, so nothing changes there.

## Self-review

1. **Job creation fails / prctl unavailable** — logged, server still starts, only the protection is missing. No start path throws.
2. **Repeated launches** — one job per backend, later servers join it; `assign` on the same process is idempotent.
3. **Two launches at once** — `assign` runs synchronously after the `to_thread(Popen)` await, on the event-loop thread, so two coroutines cannot both see an empty handle; `_server_transitioning` already serialises server switches.
4. **Test doubles without `_handle`** — skipped with a debug log instead of raising, so the existing fake-`Popen` tests keep working.
5. **Parent already dead before `prctl` runs** — the child checks `getppid() == 1` and leaves immediately, since `PDEATHSIG` would never fire.

## Test scope

prs.title: fix(scroll): recognize url-referenced media in tool-result folding
prs.body:
## Description

When a chat session accumulates enough turns to trigger context compression, historical completed tool results are inspected by `ScrollContextManager._tool_result_fold_candidates()` to collapse long or media-carrying results into compact pointer stubs (`[scroll folded] ...`).

Previously, `_tool_result_has_inline_media()` only checked for `source.get("type") == "base64"` or `source.type == "base64"`. URL-referenced media blocks (`source.type == "url"`), such as video, audio, or image outputs generated by `send_file_to_user` and similar tools, were not recognized as inline media. Consequently, these media tool results failed the `has_media` check and, having short text captions (<= 200 chars), were skipped by `_tool_result_fold_candidates()`.

As a result, uncollapsed media blocks were carried over across turns and re-spliced verbatim into rebuilt request payloads after compression. Subsequent model API requests failed repeatedly with errors such as `400: Video count 2 exceeds limit 1 per request`, permanently hanging the session for that channel.

This change extends `_tool_result_has_inline_media()` to recognize `source.type == "url"` with non-empty URL values for both dictionary-based and object-based sources.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8474

**Security Considerations:** None.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Why the issue happens

In `src/qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/manager.py`:

```python
    @staticmethod
    def _tool_result_has_inline_media(block: Any) -> bool:
        ...
        for item in output:
            if ScrollContextManager._block_type(item) != "data":
                continue
            source = (
                item.get("source")
                if isinstance(item, dict)
                else getattr(item, "source", None)
            )
            if isinstance(source, dict):
                if source.get("type") == "base64" and source.get("data"):
                    return True
            elif getattr(source, "type", None) == "base64" and getattr(
                source,
                "data",
                None,
            ):
                return True
        return False
```

When a tool output provides a data block with a URL source (`source={"type": "url", "url": "https://..."}`), `_tool_result_has_inline_media` returned `False`.

In `_tool_result_fold_candidates`:

```python
    has_media = self._tool_result_has_inline_media(block)
    if (
        not has_media
        and self._tool_result_text_chars(block) <= _PRE_TRIM_MIN_CHARS
    ):
        continue
```

Because `has_media` was `False` and media tool results generally have little or no text characters (`<= 200`), the block was skipped and never folded. During context compression and payload rebuild, the raw media block remained in the active payload.

## The change

1. In `src/qwenpaw/agents/context/scroll/manager.py`, `_tool_result_has_inline_media` now also checks:
   - For dict sources: `source.get("type") == "url" and source.get("url")`
   - For object sources: `getattr(source, "type", None) == "url" and getattr(source, "url", None)`
2. In `tests/unit/agents/context/test_scroll_manager.py`:
   - Added `test_tool_result_has_inline_media_recognizes_url_sources` to test both base64 and URL sources across dict and object representations as well as negative cases.
   - Added `test_pressure_fold_recognizes_url_media_independently_of_text_length` to verify that tool results carrying URL media bypass the text length restriction and fold into pointer stubs under context pressure.

prs.title: fix(task_tracker): bound the run completion callback and always clean up
prs.body:
## Description

Fixes the **run-cleanup half** of #8173: a chat run whose completion callback hangs or is cancelled never releases its entry in `TaskTracker._runs`, so the run stays `running` forever.

### Root cause

`TaskTracker._producer` clears its `_runs` entry and pushes the end-of-stream sentinel at the end of a `finally` block, *after* awaiting the `on_finished` completion callback. Two paths meant that cleanup never completed:

1. **The callback hangs.** `on_finished` is `ChatManager.mark_chat_finished`, which persists a completion marker under a lock shared with ~24 other manager methods. Lock contention or a stalled repo suspends the producer task *inside its own `finally`*. The task is then not done **and** the entry is still registered, so every status reader reports `running` — workspace reload is blocked and inbound messages are dropped with HTTP 409.
2. **The producer is cancelled mid-callback.** `CancelledError` is a `BaseException`, so it escapes the `except Exception` guard and skips cleanup entirely, leaving subscriber streams without their sentinel.

### The fix

- Run the callback through `asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(...))` bounded by `ON_FINISHED_TIMEOUT`, so a hung callback is logged and given up on rather than holding the run open.
- Move the cleanup into a nested `finally` so it always runs.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8173

Deliberately *not* `Fixes` — see the scope note below.

### Scope — what this does **not** fix

This addresses the cleanup leak only. The other items from #8173 are **not** implemented here: the post-spawn connection health probe, the idle watchdog, `force` semantics on the reload/disable-enable paths, and in-channel hints for `/new` and `/stop` on backends that do not support them. Those are larger design questions and I would rather land the narrow fix first.

Note that the wedge is now **bounded** by `ON_FINISHED_TIMEOUT` rather than eliminated: the run stays `running` while the callback runs, because `test_attach_or_start_reports_completion_before_becoming_idle` pins that ordering deliberately (it asserts `get_status == "running"` from inside the callback). Reordering the pop ahead of the callback would break that contract.

### What the new tests cover

New `tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py` (6 tests) covers a hung callback, a callback that raises, a callback that raises `TimeoutError`, a producer cancelled mid-callback, and `request_stop` against a slow callback. Waits are event-based rather than fixed sleeps.

Against unmodified source these fail on behavioural assertions (`run entry survived a hung completion callback`, etc.), not on import or attribute errors.

### Security Considerations

Not applicable — no change to channel auth, credentials, or config handling.

## Evidence

Verification is a real failure on unmodified source followed by the **same command** against the patched tree. Base is `5c56644a` (`main`), patch is `e2b7b8be`.

**1. Unmodified baseline — the new tests genuinely fail.**

```

=========================== short test summary info ============================
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_hung_completion_callback_does_not_block_new_messages
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_completion_callback_timeout_is_logged_not_raised
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_cancellation_during_callback_still_clears_the_run
FAILED tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py::test_request_stop_with_a_slow_callback_does_not_wedge_the_run
4 failed, 1 passed in 8.32s
```

**2. Same command with the patch — all green.**

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app/test_task_tracker_cleanup.py
.......................                                                  [100%]

```

**3. Full `tests/unit/app` with the patch — no regression.**

```
$ python -m pytest tests/unit/app
3118 passed, 1 skipped, 12 warnings in 58.77s
```

One caveat worth stating plainly: the baseline run pins the module source with `PYTHONPATH` pointing at a pristine checkout. The venv's editable install points at the patched worktree, so simply `cd`-ing to the unmodified tree would still have imported the patched code and produced a false green — that happened on the first attempt and the baseline above is from the corrected invocation.

prs.title: feat(plugins): support CLI commands and extension points
prs.body:
## Description

Adds plugin CLI commands to the existing Click command tree and connects them to the plugin registry, dependency checks, and resource lifecycle.

### 1) Key CLI features

- Register root commands, nested commands, or complete Click groups through `ctx.register_cli(CliSpec(...))`. Native commands retain priority.
- Installed, enabled plugins expose their commands. Disable/uninstall removes them. Core commands remain available without plugins.
- Plugin commands run without starting the App. Root help uses static declarations; selecting a command checks dependencies and loads its implementation.
- Invocation cleanup completes before resources and source leases are released, including after Ctrl-C. No dedicated session thread or process is added.
- Core `models`, `channels`, and `doctor` commands discover plugin contributions. Unavailable implementations retain their saved configuration without becoming executable.

### 2) Supporting plugin-core changes — review requested

The design separates application declarations, capability registration, driver execution, and resource ownership, following OS concepts.

#### 2.1 Shared registration, independent receiver execution

Previously, `entry.descriptor` and `entry.backend` were mutually exclusive. They can now coexist under one plugin instance and rollback ledger.

Simplified flow:

    App loading:
        register static channel metadata
        register lightweight public contributions

    Plugin CLI:
        load the public entry and selected command

    Enabled workspace receiver:
        start the existing channel worker

This lets a channel plugin also provide CLI or client Tools without requiring its receiver to run. Global plugin disablement still blocks execution. Public registration failure rolls back the combined registration; per-capability failure isolation is not implemented.

#### 2.2 Capability dependencies and invocation side effects

Package-wide dependencies remain supported. Named `optional_dependencies` and per-contribution `requires` distinguish lightweight operations from SDK-dependent operations:

    status.requires = []
    send.requires = ["transport"]

    install/update/repair:
        prepare packages referenced by declared capabilities

    selected command:
        check requires -> build implementation -> execute -> clean up

This prevents an unrelated SDK prerequisite from gating a lightweight command. Authors must keep the public entry lightweight and defer SDK imports themselves.

CLI execution also skips installation callbacks and backend provision commits. It reuses registration and runtime cleanup without rewriting existing Tool/Skill configuration.

#### 2.3 Update: reduce plugin CLI startup and cleanup overhead

Cleanup previously imported memory/model implementations just to inspect resource ownership. The existing memory registry now lives in a lightweight module, preserving public imports and the shared registry instance.

    Before: cleanup -> public memory API -> memory/model imports
    After:  cleanup -> lightweight ownership registry

Dependency observation now retains only file paths matching imported modules while still validating every RECORD row. Existing dependency checks, cache invalidation, and ownership protection remain in place.

For the same local Hello command, median peak RSS fell **214.77 → 193.69 MiB (-21.08 MiB)** and runtime fell **2.656 → 2.385 s (-10.2%)**.

The fixed plugin still uses **17.86 MiB / 0.591 s more** than the native reference. This includes shared-environment inspection and loader/SDK setup. Runtime environment inspection remains a current design tradeoff; reducing it further requires the environment-management work described below.

### 3) Reviewer decisions and TODOs

- [ ] Approve version choices: proposed SDK `1.1.0`, new API `since` values, and channel versioning/schema changes.
  - Channel descriptor schema v3 adds named `requires`; schema v2 remains supported.
  - Review compatibility and migration policy. The worker IPC protocol version is unchanged.
- [ ] Review test necessity and cost: 32 added runtime scenarios took approximately 70.4 seconds locally, primarily real installation and worker rollback.
- [ ] Complete installed-SDK author type validation and cross-platform CI.

Follow-up TODO comments cover installation/runtime lifecycle separation, Tool/Skill dependency declarations, live cross-plugin services, broader extension consumers, per-capability failure/reclamation scopes, and shared runtime/source ownership infrastructure.

Current boundaries: SDK modules may remain cached in the App process; synchronous checks cannot be forcibly interrupted; source locks provide cooperative replacement protection rather than sandboxing.

Additional TODO comments in `loader.py` and `python_backend.py` describe a future environment-management change:

    install dependency updates into a new directory
    new processes use the new packages
    running processes keep their existing packages
    delete the old directory after its last process exits

The package/file lookup could then be prepared during installation and reused at runtime. This belongs in a separate PR covering installation, process startup, recovery, and cleanup. It must define when an existing App restarts to activate new dependencies and preserve desktop/user-managed Python environments.

Until those guarantees exist, retain runtime observation of the mutable shared environment. Its cost depends on installed packages and loaded modules; the measured residual memory difference is not a fixed per-plugin charge.

The performance follow-up also adds two focused regression tests and adapts one existing memory test fixture. These should be included in the test-cost review.

prs.title: fix(context): reap interrupted recall subprocesses
prs.body:
## Description

The opt-in local `recall_history_python` runner owns a subprocess, but cancelling its coroutine currently only cancels `communicate()`: the child process keeps running after the recall tool exits. The timeout path calls `proc.kill()` without draining its pipes or awaiting exit, leaving the child unreaped.

This change handles both `asyncio.TimeoutError` and `asyncio.CancelledError` at the `_run_subprocess` boundary: it kills the child (ignoring `ProcessLookupError` if it already exited), drains its pipes and awaits exit via `run_async_to_completion(proc.communicate())` so repeated cancellation cannot orphan cleanup, and then re-raises `CancelledError` or returns the existing timeout message.

**Security Considerations:** Only changes subprocess cleanup in the explicitly opted-in unsandboxed recall path. Sandbox refusal, authorization checks, and sandboxed execution are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(console): keep wide tables and code blocks scrollable in bubbles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Wide Markdown tables and long code blocks are silently clipped at the right edge of the message bubble with no horizontal scrollbar, on both desktop and mobile (#8811). On narrow screens the whole reply is clipped because the same mechanism stretches the entire markdown block past the viewport — users see half a row of text with no way to reach the rest (issue screenshots: 20-column table cut at C13, 505-char `text` block cut after ~100 chars, mobile message clipped at ~1/3 width).

Root cause: `v2.3.0.post1` introduced the `quoteResponse` wrapper (`HostBubbles.tsx`) between the SDK bubble content and the markdown root:

```
bubble-content → .quoteResponse (new, unconstrained) → .x-markdown → pre / table
```

The SDK bubble content sizes itself intrinsically, and a flex child defaults to `min-width: auto`. The markdown root is already capped (`min-width: 0; max-width: 100%`, the #5480 fix), but the new wrapper was not, so the `max-content` width of wide tables (`width: max-content` in the vendor `x-markdown` stylesheet) and long code lines widened the wrapper instead of scrolling inside the block — the bubble then clipped the overflow silently.

## Evidence

- Regression pinpointed with `git diff v2.3.0 v2.3.0.post1 -- console/src/pages/Chat`: the `quoteResponse` wrapper addition is the **only** chat-style change in that release, matching every symptom timeline in #8811 (worked on v2.3.0, broke on post1; desktop table/code clipping, mobile whole-message clipping, both width modes).
- Independent confirmations in the issue: @elain0205 verified the mechanism against the shipped `2.3.0b1/b2` console assets, and @ginohero confirmed the same on Docker `v2.3.0.post1`, including that the `quoteResponse` wrapper "has no `min-width: 0`".
- After the fix, the wrapper is capped like the markdown root, so tables and `pre` keep their own horizontal scroll (`max-width: 100%; overflow-x: auto`, the #6852 rules) exactly as in v2.3.0.

## Fix

Give the wrapper the same shrinkability the markdown root already has:

```css
.quoteResponse {
  min-width: 0;
  max-width: 100%;
}
```

One rule covers all viewports; `env()`-free, no effect on normal-width content.

## Verification

- New regression test in `HostBubbles.test.ts`, following the existing source-assertion pattern used for the #5480 / #6852 / #6583 style fixes.
- `vitest run` on `HostBubbles.test.ts`, `index.module.test.ts`, `uiFontSizeCoverage.test.ts`: 53/53 passed.
- `tsc -b` clean; prettier and eslint clean on the changed files.

Fixes #8811

prs.title: fix(agents): fall back to the global default when a run-config provider is disabled
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Disabling a provider on the Models page does not update agent run-configs that still pin a model on it (`agent.json` `active_model`). Every subsequent channel message (Feishu / DingTalk / WeChat / ...) for such an agent fails at model-build time with `ProviderError: Provider is disabled`, and the channel surfaces an unactionable "Internal error" to the end user. Worse, the run-config model selector only lists enabled providers, so the stale selection is invisible in the UI — the user cannot see or fix it without knowing to edit the run-config by hand.

## Evidence

- #8579 documents the full timeline: `kexin_token` disabled → 8 consecutive `Provider is disabled` failures from `create_model_and_formatter` over 7 minutes → run-config manually changed to `minmax` at 19:27:08 → zero errors afterwards.
- Code path: `create_model_and_formatter` only consulted the global default when the agent had **no** run-config model at all (`model_slot or manager.get_active_model()`); a configured-but-disabled slot raised immediately with no fallback and a message that named neither the provider nor the agent.
- New tests reproduce all three behaviors against stubbed providers (fallback, explicit-override error, no-usable-default error); the existing `tests/unit/agents` + `tests/unit/runtime` suites still pass (4869 passed, 8 skipped).

## Fix

In `create_model_and_formatter`, treat a persisted run-config model whose provider is disabled like an unset run-config model:

- Fall back to the global default chat model and log a warning naming the agent, the disabled slot, and the fallback slot.
- Explicit per-request model overrides (`model_slot_override`) still raise — the caller asked for exactly that model — now with an actionable message: `Provider 'X' is disabled; choose another model for agent 'Y'`.
- If no enabled global default exists either, raise an actionable error asking to reselect a model for the agent.

The async wrapper delegates to the sync factory, so both entry points are covered.

Scope note: directions 1 / 4 / 5 from the issue (cascading run-config updates when a provider is disabled, surfacing disabled selections in the UI selector, unifying validity checks) are intentionally left out — they are UI/product decisions; this PR fixes the runtime death path they all build on.

## Verification

- 5 new test cases in `tests/unit/agents/test_create_model_and_formatter_override.py` (fallback asserts the warning text; explicit override asserts the actionable message; no-usable-default is parametrized over missing/empty global slots).
- `pytest tests/unit/agents tests/unit/runtime`: 4869 passed, 8 skipped.

Fixes #8579

prs.title: fix(token-usage): count Anthropic cache tokens in the live context meter
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #8057.

For Anthropic Messages providers, `usage.input_tokens` counts only the
uncached part of the prompt; cache reads (`cache_read_input_tokens`) and
cache writes (`cache_creation_input_tokens`) are reported separately. On a
long cached turn An example from the issue: `input_tokens=3000`,
`cache_read=120000`, `cache_write=5000` on a 200k window showed as 3k/200k
(1.5%) in the console context meter instead of 128k/200k (64%).

`TokenRecordingModelWrapper._record_usage()` set `last_prompt_tokens` to the
raw `input_tokens`, even though the same method already computes the correct
input denominator in `cache_eligible_input_tokens` (the value used for the
cache hit rate).

## Change

`last_prompt_tokens` — the per-request value the console channel sends as
`context_usage.estimated_tokens` in the live `turn_usage` event
(`app/channels/console/channel.py:440`) — now uses the cache-aware
denominator:

- Anthropic: `input_tokens + cache_read + cache_write` (cache reads/writes
  really are part of the prompt the model processed).
- OpenAI Chat / Responses: unchanged, their `prompt_tokens` / `input_tokens`
  already include cached tokens, and `_cache_usage_metrics()` returns
  `cache_eligible == prompt_tokens` for them.
- Providers without verifiable cache semantics: unchanged
  (`cache_observed` is False, so the raw input tokens are kept and the cache
  counters are zeroed by the existing guard).

Session totals (`prompt_tokens`, the usage event) deliberately still carry
the uncached input tokens, so billing/statistics input accounting is not
affected — only the live per-request context meter.

## Evidence

- `tests/unit/token_usage/test_token_usage.py`:
  - `test_last_prompt_tokens_counts_anthropic_cache_tokens` — the issue's
    numbers (3000 / 120000 / 5000) now produce `last_prompt_tokens == 128000`
    while `prompt_tokens` stays 3000. Fails on `main` (asserted 128000 == 3000).
  - `test_last_prompt_tokens_keeps_openai_input_tokens` — an OpenAI adapter
    with `cache_input_tokens=3000` inside a 4000-token prompt keeps
    `last_prompt_tokens == 4000` (no double counting).
  - `test_last_prompt_tokens_ignores_unverifiable_cache_tokens` — an unknown
    adapter keeps raw input tokens and drops the cache counters.
- Full runs: `pytest tests/unit/token_usage/ tests/unit/channels/test_console.py`
  → 142 passed.
- Lint: `add-trailing-comma` + `black --line-length=79` clean,
  `flake8` clean on the changed lines (the one B017 hit is pre-existing at
  `tests/unit/token_usage/test_token_usage.py:439`), `pylint` 9.48/10 with the
  pre-existing import-outside-toplevel note only.

prs.title: test: stop leaking unawaited coroutines from scheduling mocks
prs.body:
## Summary

Six unit tests leak a coroutine: a scheduling mock replaces the scheduler
without consuming what production handed it, or a test runs a production
path in the wrong execution context. The tests pass, but the
`RuntimeWarning: coroutine ... was never awaited` noise hides real async
lifecycle defects (the issue cites #7857) and makes a clean test run
impossible to certify.

This fixes all six and tightens each test so it asserts the behaviour it
claims to cover.

Refs #7858

## What Problem This Solves

Running the affected files with `-X tracemalloc=5` emits **7**
unawaited-coroutine warnings. Six come from tests that pass for the wrong
reason, so a genuine async defect introduced nearby would be invisible in
the noise — the warnings are attributed to whichever test happens to
trigger the delayed GC, not the one that leaked.

Concretely, `test_download_attachment_exception` patched
`qq_channel._loop.run_coroutine_threadsafe` while production calls the
module-level `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe`, so the mock never fired
and the "returns None on failure" assertion was never exercising the
intended exception path. Similarly, `test_run_stream_forever` called the
sync thread entry point from inside a test coroutine, where `asyncio.run`
raises and the entry point's `except Exception` swallowed it — the test
asserted nothing about the stream loop at all.

## Changes

| Test | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `test_proactive_trigger_logic.py::TestEnableDisable::test_enable_stores_config_and_workspace` | `create_task` mock returned a stub task and left `_run_trigger_loop` unawaited | close the coroutine in the stub scheduler |
| `test_hub.py::TestClientLifecycle::test_aclose_hub_client_drain_timeout_warns` | fake `wait_for` raised `TimeoutError` without consuming the `Event.wait` coroutine | close it, and assert the warning the timeout path is supposed to log (was: `# must not raise`) |
| `test_dingtalk.py::TestDingTalkStreamMode::test_run_stream_forever` | async test called the sync thread entry point; `asyncio.run` failed inside the running loop and was swallowed | run it in a real thread and assert the stream loop actually executed |
| `test_qq.py::TestDownloadAttachmentSync::test_download_attachment_exception` | patched the loop's method; production uses the module-level function | patch `qwenpaw.app.channels.qq.channel.asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe`, assert it was scheduled on the channel's loop |
| `test_telegram.py::TestTelegramTypingIndicators::test_start_typing_creates_task` | `create_task` mock left `_typing_loop` unawaited | close the coroutine in the stub scheduler |
| `test_telegram.py::TestTelegramTypingIndicators::test_start_typing_replaces_existing` | same | same |

No production code is touched — every defect here is in the tests.

## Evidence

The issue's reproduction command, before and after:

```
$ python -X tracemalloc=5 -m pytest -q \
    tests/unit/agents/acp/test_acp_service.py \
    tests/unit/agents/memory/test_proactive_trigger_logic.py \
    tests/unit/agents/skill_system/test_hub.py \
    tests/unit/channels/test_dingtalk.py \
    tests/unit/channels/test_qq.py \
    tests/unit/channels/test_telegram.py

# before: 755 passed, 38 warnings   → 7 unawaited-coroutine warnings
# after:  755 passed, 33 warnings   → 1 unawaited-coroutine warning
```

The one remaining warning is `ACPService.close_all_sessions`, which is the
separate production defect tracked in #7857 — the issue's acceptance
criteria explicitly asks for this PR to land before that one.

Wider runs (no new failures; the single failure is a pre-existing
network-dependent one):

```
$ pytest tests/unit/channels tests/unit/agents -q
1 failed, 5864 passed, 4 skipped
# tests/unit/agents/utils/test_file_handling.py::TestDownloadFileFromUrl::test_remote_download
# fails on clean main too (needs network)

$ black --line-length=79 / flake8 / pylint (10.00)   # clean
```

prs.title: feat(telegram): isolate agent sessions by forum topic
prs.body:
## Description

Telegram forum topics were invisible to session routing: every topic in a forum resolved to `telegram:<chat_id>`, so all topics shared one agent session, one memory and one Console conversation. Topic identity existed only as a reply-routing field, which meant outbound replies could land in the right topic while the conversation history was mixed. Issue [8827](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8827)

This PR makes the session id carry the topic, and teaches outbound target parsing the resulting format.

```diff
 _message_meta(update)
+  is_topic_message = message.is_topic_message
+  thread_id = message.message_thread_id
+  if supergroup and thread_id == 1 and (is_topic_message or chat.is_forum)
+    thread_id = None            # General topic is chat scope
+
+_session_id(meta)
-  return telegram:<chat_id>
+  if supergroup and is_topic_message and thread and thread > 1
+    return telegram:<chat_id>:<thread>
+  return telegram:<chat_id>
```

Session mapping:

| Chat | `message_thread_id` | `is_topic_message` | Session |
|---|---|---|---|
| private | — / 77 | — | `telegram:42` |
| non-forum supergroup | — | — | `telegram:-100` |
| non-forum group, reply thread | 77 | false | `telegram:-100` |
| forum, General topic | 1 | true | `telegram:-100` |
| forum topic | 77 | true | `telegram:-100:77` |

Outbound target parsing (`TelegramDriver._target`) was a prefix branch plus a `split(":", 1)[1]`; it now does `session.removeprefix("telegram:").partition(":")` — one path for both `telegram:<chat>` and `telegram:<chat>:<thread>`. Parsed thread ids are normalized before use: leading zeros stripped, `1` collapsed to "no thread" (General), and anything non-ASCII/non-decimal raises `OUTBOUND_TARGET_UNKNOWN` (the existing empty-topic rejection also stays). `meta["message_thread_id"]` still wins when present; the parsed value is the fallback for replies opened from a session id alone. Non-`telegram:` session ids keep the old behavior of addressing the captured user id as the chat.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #(issue_number) or Relates to #(issue_number)

**Security Considerations:** Routing-only change, no auth or secret handling touched. The new parsing path is stricter than before: a malformed or empty thread segment in an outbound session id raises `OUTBOUND_TARGET_UNKNOWN` instead of being passed through, and thread ids are restricted to ASCII decimal digits before they become `send_message(message_thread_id=...)` kwargs.

prs.title: fix(crons): persist cron and heartbeat token usage to turn records
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cron and heartbeat runs drive `workspace.stream_query` directly instead of going through `Channel.consume_one`, so their token usage was never committed to the session's turn records. The console usage panel undercounts all scheduled task consumption: cron jobs (daily digests, reminders) and heartbeat runs make model calls whose usage never lands in the persisted turn records, even though the session data model already distinguishes cron sessions from chat turns.

Failed runs had a second, subtler problem: staged usage was never dropped, so a failed run's tokens could leak into the next run on the same reused session.

Fixes #8705

## Description

- Extract `commit_turn_usage` / `discard_turn_usage` into `qwenpaw.token_usage.turn_usage`:
  - `commit_turn_usage` resolves and persists one finished turn's usage, never raises
  - `discard_turn_usage` drops staged usage when a run does not finish normally
- `Channel._commit_turn_usage` and `_clear_session_turn_usage` now reuse the shared helpers (no behavior change)
- Cron executor: commit usage after a successful run; discard on timeout / cancel / error
- Heartbeat: same treatment for all three `stream_query` sites
- New e2e regression: `e2e/tests/test_cron_usage.py` (auto-skips without a model API key via `requires_llm`)

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

prs.title: fix(crons): accept named weekday lists in heartbeat cron
prs.body:
## Description

A heartbeat `every` such as `0 9 * * mon,wed,fri` or `0 9 * * sat,sun` was not recognised as cron. The day-of-week pattern in `is_cron_expression` allowed only one named day or one named range, never a comma list. The value fell through to `parse_heartbeat_every`, which logged `invalid, using 30m`, so the heartbeat ran every 30 minutes instead of three times a week. The Cron Jobs page writes weekly schedules in this `mon,wed,fri` form, and APScheduler accepts it.

The fix allows a comma list of the existing tokens (numeric, named day, named range, optional step). Every value accepted before is still accepted.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8865

## Type of Change

New test `test_is_cron_expression_accepts_named_dow_list` fails on main and passes with the fix. I also compared the old and new pattern on about 9.4k generated day-of-week strings: nothing the old pattern accepted is rejected now.

prs.title: feat(desktop): add Linux deb and AppImage packaging to the Tauri build
prs.body:
## Description

Linux currently has no desktop artifact. `desktop-build.yml` builds only Windows and macOS, `tauri.conf.json` declares `"targets": ["app", "nsis"]` with `.icns`/`.ico` icons only, and `RELEASING.md` documents the desktop apps as "Windows + macOS" — so Linux users must run the Docker image or build from source.

Related issues: **#8442** — the Linux parity umbrella; this PR lands its packaging half (deb + AppImage), while Computer Use and Chrome Native Messaging follow in separate PRs. **#5668** — the x86_64 AppImage request; the AppImage build is added here, and release publishing plus the updater follow in the next PR.

The packaging chain was already platform-neutral, which is why this is a packaging shell rather than a port:

| Piece | Already handled |
|---|---|
| Resource lookup | `backend/command.rs` resolves `python/bin/python3`, `node-runtime/bin/node`, `qwenpaw-backend` (no `.exe`) for every non-Windows target |
| Python runtime | `stage_python_runtime.py` maps Linux to `{arch}-unknown-linux-gnu` |
| Node runtime | `stage_node_runtime.py` maps Linux to `linux-{arch}` |
| Backend build | `build_pyinstaller.sh` is a generic unix script; macOS signing lives in its own wrapper |
| PyInstaller spec | platform branches exist only for darwin codesign and win32 executable names |
| Icons | generated from `scripts/pack/assets/icon.svg` |

### What this PR does

**Bundle configuration** (`console/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`)

- add `deb` and `appimage` to `bundle.targets`, keeping `app` and `nsis` untouched
- list the existing 512×512 `icons/icon.png` so Linux bundlers have a PNG
- add `bundle.publisher` and `bundle.copyright` (the deb `Maintainer` field is mandatory)
- declare `bundle.linux.deb.depends` explicitly: `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0`, `libgtk-3-0t64 | libgtk-3-0`, `libayatana-appindicator3-1`

**Build entry point** (`scripts/pack-tauri/build_linux_pyinstaller.sh`)

Mirrors the macOS orchestration without signing: `npm ci` → version sync → console build → `build_pyinstaller.sh` (PyInstaller backend plus bundled Python/Node runtimes) → `tauri build --bundles deb,appimage` → collect both artifacts into `dist/`. `QWENPAW_SKIP_BACKEND_BUILD=1` retries packaging without rebuilding the backend.

**Five build-host defects this exposed, each fixed in place**

1. **Python series came from the bootstrap interpreter.** On a 3.14 host the staged runtime left the `requires-python` range and dependency installation failed. `stage_python_runtime.py` now uses the host series only when it is supported (3.11–3.13) and otherwise falls back to 3.13 with a printed notice.
2. **The bundle carried the CUDA stack.** `whisper` pulls torch, and the default Linux wheel declares the CUDA runtime through `DT_NEEDED` on `libtorch_cpu.so` itself (`libcudart.so.13`), so `nvidia-*` plus `triton` added ~4 GB and could not be stripped after the fact. Linux builds now install torch from the CPU index first, so the requirement is already satisfied and the CUDA payload never enters the bundle.
3. **The product name broke `linuxdeploy`.** A space in `productName` puts a space in the AppDir and resource paths (`usr/lib/<productName>/`), which splits the `ldd` invocation linuxdeploy performs for every ELF; `ldd` exits 1 and bundling aborts with the unhelpful `failed to run linuxdeploy`. Linux now uses the space-free `QwenPawDesktop` (the window title still comes from `app.windows[0].title`; data remains under `~/.qwenpaw`).
4. **A failed run poisoned the next one.** Tauri merges into an existing AppDir, so leftovers under the previous product name survived; the bundle directories are now removed before bundling.
5. **linuxdeploy cannot infer dependencies for a bundled runtime.** It walks every ELF in the AppDir — thousands of files inside the Python runtime — and aborts on the first unresolved name, which is pure overhead for a tree that ships its own dependencies. When bundling fails, the script now deduplicates the resource tree that Tauri emits under two names (one real copy plus a symlink), points `.DirIcon` at the icon named by the desktop entry, and packs the AppDir with `appimagetool`.

**Packaging hygiene** — a single build left ~20 GB of intermediates behind (`target/release/binaries` 9.7 GB, `target/release/bundle/appimage_deb` 9.7 GB). They are now removed after the artifacts are collected (`QWENPAW_DESKTOP_KEEP_STAGING=1` keeps them).

**CI** (`desktop-build.yml`, new `build-tauri-linux` job on `ubuntu-24.04`)

Installs the Linux packaging dependencies, builds both formats, verifies the launched app with Playwright through a new `.github/actions/verify-tauri-linux` action (plus `scripts/verify/launch_tauri_linux.sh`, which runs the AppImage under Xvfb, waits for `~/.qwenpaw/desktop_port`, and exports `BASE_URL`), records checksums, and uploads the deb, the AppImage and the verify logs. `desktop_verify.py` gains the `tauri-linux` UI mode (Playwright WebKit).

**Docs** — a Linux section in `website/public/docs/desktop.{en,zh}.md` (requirements, deb vs AppImage install, first-run data paths, updates, uninstall) and the release support matrix.

### Evidence

Environment: Ubuntu 26.04 (GNOME 50, Wayland-only), rustc 1.99.1, webkit2gtk-4.1 2.52.6, node v24.21.0, host Python 3.14.

```text
$ bash scripts/pack-tauri/build_linux_pyinstaller.sh
== Checking prerequisites ==
  [INFO] python3 3.14 is outside 3.11-3.13; the bundled runtime will be staged as 3.13
== Step 2: PyInstaller backend + bundled runtimes ==
== Installing CPU-only torch ==
...
== Step 3b: tauri bundling failed; packing the AppDir with appimagetool ==
    deduplicating usr/lib/QwenPaw Desktop -> symlink to QwenPawDesktop
-rwxr-xr-x 976M  dist/QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b1-linux-x86_64.AppImage
-rw-r--r--  1.3G dist/QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b1-linux-x86_64.deb
```

```text
$ dpkg-deb -I dist/QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b1-linux-x86_64.deb
 Package: qwen-paw-desktop
 Version: 2.3.0-beta.1
 Architecture: amd64
 Installed-Size: 3489035
 Maintainer: QwenPaw Contributors
 Depends: libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0, libgtk-3-0t64 | libgtk-3-0, libayatana-appindicator3-1, ...
```

```text
$ dpkg-deb -c dist/...deb | grep -oE "usr/lib/[^/]+" | sort -u
usr/lib/QwenPawDesktop            # single resource tree

$ apt-get install --dry-run ./dist/...deb | tail -3
The following NEW packages will be installed:
  qwen-paw-desktop
0 upgraded, 1 newly installed
```

Installed and launched on the target machine:

```text
$ sudo apt install ./dist/QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b1-linux-x86_64.deb && qwenpaw-desktop
[backend] packaged command: /usr/lib/QwenPaw Desktop/binaries/qwenpaw-backend/qwenpaw-backend
[backend] bundled python runtime: .../python-runtime/python/bin/python3
[backend] bundled node runtime: .../node-runtime
[backend] shared runtime 2.3.0-beta.1 connected after 9534ms (launched=true)
```

The window renders, the sidecar connects, and `~/.qwenpaw` is created on first launch.

### Open items (separate changes)

- Release plumbing (`desktop-publish.yml` / `desktop-promote.yml`, OSS paths, `linux-x86_64` in the updater manifest) and the AppImage updater client branch — PR2.
- Arm64 (`ubuntu-24.04-arm`) — follow-up once x86_64 is green.
- The AppImage has been built, structurally verified (valid AppImage, correct desktop entry, deduplicated payload) and **launched successfully on the target machine**; CI covers the launch on every build.

### 描述

Linux 目前没有桌面产物：`desktop-build.yml` 只构建 Windows 与 macOS，`tauri.conf.json` 的 `targets` 只有 `["app","nsis"]`，图标只有 `.icns`/`.ico`，`RELEASING.md` 也写着「Windows + macOS」——Linux 用户只能跑 Docker 或从源码构建。

相关 issue：**#8442** —— Linux 对齐的总 issue，本 PR 落地其中的打包部分（deb + AppImage），Computer Use 与 Chrome Native Messaging 由后续 PR 完成；**#5668** —— x86_64 AppImage 提案，本 PR 补上 AppImage 构建，发布与自动更新由下一个 PR 完成。

打包链本来就是平台中立的，所以这是补一个打包壳，而不是移植：

| 部分 | 已就绪 |
|---|---|
| 资源查找 | `backend/command.rs` 对所有非 Windows 目标已按 `python/bin/python3`、`node-runtime/bin/node`、无 `.exe` 的 `qwenpaw-backend` 查找 |
| Python runtime | `stage_python_runtime.py` 已映射 Linux 到 `{arch}-unknown-linux-gnu` |
| Node runtime | `stage_node_runtime.py` 已映射 Linux 到 `linux-{arch}` |
| 后端构建 | `build_pyinstaller.sh` 是通用 unix 脚本，macOS 签名单独封装 |
| PyInstaller spec | 平台分支只有 darwin 签名与 win32 可执行名 |
| 图标 | 由 `scripts/pack/assets/icon.svg` 生成 |

### 本 PR 做了什么

**打包配置**（`console/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`）

- `bundle.targets` 追加 `deb` 与 `appimage`，保留原有 `app`、`nsis`
- 列入已有的 512×512 `icons/icon.png`，供 Linux 打包器使用
- 补 `bundle.publisher` 与 `bundle.copyright`（deb 的 `Maintainer` 是必填项）
- 显式声明 `bundle.linux.deb.depends`：`libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0`、`libgtk-3-0t64 | libgtk-3-0`、`libayatana-appindicator3-1`

**构建入口**（`scripts/pack-tauri/build_linux_pyinstaller.sh`）

照抄 macOS 编排、去掉签名：`npm ci` → 版本同步 → console 构建 → `build_pyinstaller.sh`（PyInstaller 后端 + 内嵌 Python/Node runtime）→ `tauri build --bundles deb,appimage` → 两个产物归集到 `dist/`。`QWENPAW_SKIP_BACKEND_BUILD=1` 可在不重建后端的情况下重试打包。

**这次暴露并修复的五个构建机缺陷**

1. **Python 版本跟随引导解释器**：3.14 宿主会让内嵌运行时越出 `requires-python` 范围、装依赖失败。现在宿主 3.11–3.13 直接用宿主版本，否则回退 3.13 并打印提示。
2. **包里带上 CUDA 栈**：`whisper` 引入 torch，而 Linux 默认 wheel 通过 `libtorch_cpu.so` 的 `DT_NEEDED`（`libcudart.so.13`）硬依赖 CUDA runtime，`nvidia-*` 与 `triton` 合计约 4GB 且**事后删不掉**。改为 Linux 先装 CPU 版 torch，依赖需求即被满足，CUDA 载荷根本不进包。
3. **产品名里的空格打断 `linuxdeploy`**：AppDir 与资源路径（`usr/lib/<productName>/`）都带空格，linuxdeploy 对每个 ELF 调用的 `ldd` 会被拆参，`ldd` 退出码 1，整体报 `failed to run linuxdeploy` 且无细节。Linux 改用无空格的 `QwenPawDesktop`（窗口标题仍来自 `app.windows[0].title`，数据仍在 `~/.qwenpaw`）。
4. **一次失败会污染下一次**：Tauri 合并而非重建 AppDir，旧产品名的残留会留下；现在打包前先清空 bundle 目录。
5. **linuxdeploy 对内嵌 runtime 做依赖推导没有意义**：它会遍历 AppDir 里每个 ELF（内嵌 Python runtime 有数千个），任一解析失败即整体中止；而我们的树自带全部依赖。现在失败时自动去重 Tauri 的双份资源（一份真身 + 一个软链）、修正 `.DirIcon`、改用 `appimagetool` 直接压 AppDir。

**打包卫生**：一次构建会残留约 20GB 中间产物（`target/release/binaries` 9.7GB、`target/release/bundle/appimage_deb` 9.7GB），现在归集产物后自动清理（`QWENPAW_DESKTOP_KEEP_STAGING=1` 可保留）。

**CI**（`desktop-build.yml` 新增 `build-tauri-linux`，`ubuntu-24.04`）

安装 Linux 打包依赖、构建两种格式、用新增的 `.github/actions/verify-tauri-linux` 通过 Playwright 验证启动后的应用（配套 `scripts/verify/launch_tauri_linux.sh` 在 Xvfb 下运行 AppImage、等 `~/.qwenpaw/desktop_port`、导出 `BASE_URL`），记录校验和并上传 deb/AppImage/验证日志。`desktop_verify.py` 增加 `tauri-linux` 模式（Playwright WebKit）。

**文档**：`website/public/docs/desktop.{en,zh}.md` 增加 Linux 章节（系统要求、deb/AppImage 安装、首启数据目录、更新与卸载），并更新发布支持矩阵。

### 证据

环境：Ubuntu 26.04（GNOME 50，仅 Wayland），rustc 1.99.1，webkit2gtk-4.1 2.52.6，node v24.21.0，宿主 Python 3.14。

```text
$ bash scripts/pack-tauri/build_linux_pyinstaller.sh
  [INFO] python3 3.14 is outside 3.11-3.13; the bundled runtime will be staged as 3.13
== Installing CPU-only torch ==
== Step 3b: tauri bundling failed; packing the AppDir with appimagetool ==
    deduplicating usr/lib/QwenPaw Desktop -> symlink to QwenPawDesktop
976M  dist/QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b1-linux-x86_64.AppImage
1.3G  dist/QwenPaw-Tauri-2.3.0b1-linux-x86_64.deb
```

```text
$ dpkg-deb -I dist/...deb
 Package: qwen-paw-desktop | Version: 2.3.0-beta.1 | Architecture: amd64
 Installed-Size: 3489035 | Maintainer: QwenPaw Contributors
 Depends: libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0, libgtk-3-0t64 | libgtk-3-0, libayatana-appindicator3-1, ...

$ dpkg-deb -c dist/...deb | grep -oE "usr/lib/[^/]+" | sort -u
usr/lib/QwenPawDesktop            # 只有一份资源树

$ apt-get install --dry-run ./dist/...deb | tail -3
The following NEW packages will be installed: qwen-paw-desktop
```

真机安装并启动：

```text
$ sudo apt install ./dist/...deb && qwenpaw-desktop
[backend] packaged command: /usr/lib/QwenPaw Desktop/binaries/qwenpaw-backend/qwenpaw-backend
[backend] bundled python runtime: .../python-runtime/python/bin/python3
[backend] bundled node runtime: .../node-runtime
[backend] shared runtime 2.3.0-beta.1 connected after 9534ms (launched=true)
```

窗口正常渲染、sidecar 连接成功、首启生成 `~/.qwenpaw`。

### 未完成项（独立 PR）

- 发布链（`desktop-publish.yml` / `desktop-promote.yml`、OSS 路径、updater manifest 增加 `linux-x86_64`）与 AppImage 自更新的客户端分支 —— PR2。
- arm64（`ubuntu-24.04-arm`）——x86_64 绿了之后跟进。
- AppImage 已构建、通过结构核验（有效 AppImage、desktop 条目正确、载荷已去重），并已在真机**成功启动**；CI 每次构建都会覆盖启动验证。

## Release Notes

- New: the desktop app now builds and ships for Linux (x86_64) as a `.deb` and an AppImage, alongside the existing Windows and macOS artifacts.
- New: on Linux, `apt install ./QwenPaw-*.deb` resolves the runtime dependencies (WebKitGTK 4.1, GTK 3, AppIndicator); the AppImage is a single portable file.

## Release Notes

- 新增：桌面版开始为 Linux（x86_64）构建并发布 `.deb` 与 AppImage，与现有 Windows/macOS 产物并列。
- 新增：Linux 上 `apt install ./QwenPaw-*.deb` 会自动补齐运行时依赖（WebKitGTK 4.1、GTK 3、AppIndicator）；AppImage 为单文件便携版。

prs.title: feat(providers): let custom gateways declare OpenAI prompt cache params
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #8058.

Since #7899, request parameters pass through `cache_request()` in
`providers/adapters/cache_policy.py`, which rejects
`prompt_cache_key` / `prompt_cache_retention` unless the provider's cache
capabilities include `openai` / `openai_explicit`.
`OpenAIProvider.cache_capabilities()` only returns those modes for
`api.openai.com`, so a custom provider pointing at an OpenAI-compatible
Responses gateway fails **before sending anything** with
`ValueError: Unsupported cache control: prompt_cache_key` — including when the
key is only in `extra_body`, which `cache_request()` lifts out and re-validates.

Users had no way to declare the capability: `cache_modes` is a class
attribute, so `"cache_modes": ["openai"]` in the provider JSON is ignored and
dropped on the next save. Losing `prompt_cache_key` measurably lowers cache
hit rates on long agent sessions that share a prefix.

## Change

New persisted provider field (backend-only, default off):

```json
"supports_openai_prompt_cache": true
```

`OpenAIProvider.cache_capabilities()` now opens **only** the explicit prompt
cache parameters for a non-`api.openai.com` base URL when this flag is set —
i.e. it adds the `openai` mode, which is exactly what gates
`prompt_cache_key` / `prompt_cache_retention` in `cache_policy.py`.

Deliberately still gated (`openai_explicit` is not granted): `prompt_cache_options`,
`enable_prompt_cache_breakpoint` and `cache_control` keep raising, so the opt-in
cannot be used to unlock TTL/breakpoint controls that a host model may not have.

Why a config flag instead of forwarding unconditionally for custom providers
(the issue's option 2): the wire-level gate is intentionally fail-closed for
unverified services, and this keeps it that way while giving operators a
declared, reviewable escape hatch. Because it is a real pydantic field, it is
no longer discarded on save (the `cache_modes` class attribute was), and
`update_config()` only touches keys present in the request, so console-driven
provider updates do not clobber it.

## Evidence

- `tests/unit/providers/test_openai_provider.py`:
  - `test_custom_gateway_rejects_prompt_cache_key_by_default` — the issue's
    minimal repro (both `prompt_cache_key` in kwargs and in `extra_body`)
    still raises before this flag is set.
  - `test_declared_capability_forwards_prompt_cache_parameters` — with the
    flag, both forms forward a single `prompt_cache_key`, and
    `prompt_cache_retention` too.
  - `test_declaration_does_not_unlock_explicit_cache_controls` —
    `prompt_cache_options` and `enable_prompt_cache_breakpoint` still raise.
  - `test_official_host_capabilities_are_unaffected` — `api.openai.com`
