prs.title: feat(providers): honor runtime-profile thinking for OpenAI
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Carry the existing opted-in runtime-profile thinking level with each request, independently of native token budgets, so two profiles sharing an OpenAI alias can select different reasoning efforts.
  - Resolve the neutral level against the actual selected OpenAI model, API, tool mode and public/subscription capability set, including fallback attempts and lazy streams.
  - Preserve the selected level across existing runtime adapters and disable response-cache reuse for explicit native-thinking overrides; document precedence, capability fallbacks and Rust source migration.
- **Scope boundary:** OpenAI Responses, native Chat Completions and the existing Codex subscription path. No new configuration key, global `runtime.reasoning_effort` values, authentication path, compatibility retry, provider family or runtime subsystem. Other providers keep their existing native budgets and wire behavior. Approval and dispatch authority, receipt/observer-event formats, history handling and cancellation semantics are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** Public Rust request construction, runtime CLI/channel/Agent/RPC/delegate request propagation, routing and recovery, streaming/tool rounds, and response-cache eligibility. This requires cross-owner review and the separate runtime exception before merge.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12054. Depends on #12057. Related #10705 concerns accepting literal global `max`, which this PR does not implement.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12054
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12057
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10705

### What this does, simply

A profile could change thinking prompts or temperature while OpenAI's native reasoning effort still came from global provider options. The native Chat Completions path also lacked profile-derived effort. With `native_thinking = true`, a turn now carries the selected level to the actual OpenAI model making that request. Inline override takes precedence over session override, then the profile default; direct Agent/RPC sessions use their profile default.

`off` becomes `none` when supported, otherwise the lowest supported effort. `minimal`, `low`, `medium` and `high` use the matching effort, or the next higher supported effort capped at the maximum. `max` selects the model's highest supported effort. Public API and subscription capabilities stay separate. Unknown models and API/tool combinations absent from the capability table retain existing global/default behavior and emit an explanatory diagnostic. For GPT-5.4, GPT-5.5, and GPT-5.6 models that support Chat Completions with tools, the tool-enabled Chat subset is `none`. Use Responses when the turn needs both tools and reasoning.

The level survives tool rounds, max-iteration summaries, request rebuilding, recovery, fallback model changes and deferred streams. Independent delegates and live SOP steps that switch agents use the executing agent's profile. Bounded delegates and same-agent SOP steps keep the caller's level. Legacy auxiliary one-shot requests keep their existing behavior. Existing raw-body overrides in Azure, custom and other compatible adapters retain their precedence.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The CLI runtime library test calls `agent::loop_::run` in process and captures the outgoing Responses body. The channel and Agent tests use in-process providers that capture the neutral level and budget before serialization.

The merge preserves upstream model-specific prompt placement and the opted-in effort on the same request. The repair also scopes live cross-agent SOP calls to the executing agent's default while keeping the same-agent override and the pre-existing token budget.

Core Team approval of the runtime placement is recorded on the separate, unmerged exception PR #12057. Implementation review and the exception's merge remain separate decisions. https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12057#issuecomment-6502718792

prs.title: feat(channels): add SimpleX messaging, voice notes, and encrypted calls
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Add an opt-in SimpleX channel for direct text, native voice notes, and incoming encrypted audio calls so a phone can converse with an agent without a phone number or telephony service. Live text updates and streamed speech reduce the wait before a reply becomes visible or audible.
- Keep channel admission, agent ownership, peer grants, outbound filtering, and model execution in the existing native channel path. The official SimpleX CLI owns identities, messaging, and signaling; a separate Node/Chromium helper runs the official WebRTC assets and media transport.
- Connect calls to the owning agent's existing STT/TTS providers. Optional Parakeet-compatible streaming transcription supplies speech-onset interruption and final utterances; bounded batch transcription remains available. Playback observations tell the next turn which generated audio was interrupted without rewriting assistant history.
- Finalize the existing upstream feature branch with the current master sync (`9d56e8a9b`) and the reusable topic follow-ups below. Serpentine text now uses SimpleX-compatible headings, arrows, and separators; incoming link-preview text is forwarded without its preview metadata; queued previews are not falsely audited; voice ingress and provider preparation timings are traced; SimpleX joins the typed-channel migration and generated feature selections; and plaintext WebSocket transports are restricted to exact loopback hosts.
- **Scope boundary:** Direct contacts and incoming audio calls only. No groups, video, outgoing calls, generic attachments, global shared session, new history backend, summary deck, compaction changes, or transcript migration.
- **Blast radius:** Optional channel factory/configuration, attribution, channel control metadata, draft-to-speech forwarding, delivery outcome handling, migration/feature registration, and shared audio assembly. Existing channel implementations inherit a no-op live-speech callback. The feature is absent from default builds and included in `channels-full`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12276. The SimpleX-specific changes begin after merge commit `4987e0113`; the current feature-level changes are the six commits after integration base `9d56e8a9b4125f0a7b36e518cbda17dc74f134d3`.

### What this does, simply

A user pairs their Android SimpleX app with a locally stored agent profile and explicitly grants that numeric contact access. They can then send text or voice notes, receive text plus speech, or start an encrypted audio call. The same contact's text and calls use the existing channel conversation. Different contacts and channel aliases remain separate.

Replies remain at `Processing…` while waiting for provider output, including prompt prefill. They switch to `Thinking…` only after nonempty reasoning progress is observed; providers without reasoning output move directly from processing to response text. Approved response text replaces the label. Completed narration alongside tools is delivered separately from the final answer. During a call, sentence/paragraph speech can play before generation finishes; speaking again stops playback and cancels the current call turn. A passive observation describes completed and partially played speech before the next utterance. This is estimated sender playout, not a word-accurate hearing receipt. Tool effects already completed are not undone.

The adapter is disabled by default, calls require a second explicit switch, and wildcard grants do not admit contacts. The official SimpleX CLI API remains an unauthenticated loopback service: ZeroClaw accepts only `ws` URLs on exact loopback hosts and rejects remote, wildcard, credential-bearing, or `wss` CLI endpoints. Live transcription likewise accepts only exact loopback `ws` or `wss` endpoints and rejects remote or wildcard hosts before opening a connection. Setup and operational limits are documented in `docs/book/src/channels/simplex.md`.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes: verify the adapter delivers replies and playable audio through an agent's SimpleX profile, streams call audio, and handles interruption and finalization correctly.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli` for daemon startup; `channel=simplex` for messaging and calls.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Build with `--features channel-simplex`; install the helper's locked Node dependencies, ffmpeg/ffprobe, sandboxed Chromium, and the pinned external SimpleX artifacts. Follow the channel documentation to start a private loopback CLI, pair an Android contact, grant its numeric ID, assign the channel to an agent, and select working speech providers.
- **Steps to run:** Send text, then a voice note. Select `output_modality = "voice"` and confirm both text and a playable note. Start an audio call, verify the encryption indicator, speak, interrupt a reply, and ask about its unfinished point. Follow up in text. Confirm interrupted audio stops, stale queued audio does not resume, and the next prompt reflects the playback cutoff. Send a heading, arrow expression, and horizontal rule and confirm readable SimpleX formatting. Send a link-preview message and confirm its user-authored text reaches the agent without preview metadata. Try a non-loopback `websocket_url` and confirm configuration refuses it. Also remove the peer grant during use and confirm access is revoked.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Live text finalizes in its original bubble; private reasoning and hidden tool details stay private. Voice input reaches the agent, voice output plays, calls stream speech and stop on interruption, and a follow-up retains the same contact's context. Link-preview text is retained, formatting is compatible, and every non-loopback transport is refused before connection. Removed grants prevent further admission or audio handoff.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** There is no `channel-simplex` feature, adapter, helper, typed-channel migration entry, or generated SimpleX feature selection; these SimpleX interactions cannot reach the native agent.

### How I tested

Exact tested revision: `bf405ff9a8383f4a35b8f88927187d5e8e6103d9`.

Rust checks used the project's Rust 1.98.0 toolchain, the shared debug-free target, `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0`, `CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0`, and `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`.

```text

# passed

cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib simplex -- --include-ignored
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored

cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-simplex --lib simplex
test result: ok. 17 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored

cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-simplex --lib note_synthesis_starts_early_and_force_finalization_keeps_prepared_audio_and_text -- --include-ignored
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored

cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-simplex --lib pcm_stream_authenticates
test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored

test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored

cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets --features zeroclaw-channels/channel-simplex -- -D warnings
Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized] target(s) in 10m 35s
```

Node helper checks used the locked dependencies with `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund`.

```text
npm test
tests 36
pass 28
fail 0
cancelled 0
skipped 8

node --test format.test.mjs live.test.mjs bridge.test.mjs
tests 20
pass 20
fail 0
```

The eight skips are explicit external-artifact or public-relay scenarios. The parent integration run also passed the V3 typed-channel migration regression and the full installer drift check after registering SimpleX. Fresh GitHub CI on exact head `bf405ff9a` has green `Lint` and `Test` jobs with no failures at handoff time; image-build and one CLI-only test were still running.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Fresh exact-head `Lint` covers strict Rust warnings. Fresh exact-head `Test` covers the workspace test suite. Focused Rust tests exercise config admission, SimpleX live text, calls, voice notes, PCM streaming, transport rejection, and ffmpeg output. The Node suite exercises the stdio bridge, formatter, live-message state machine, voice-note handling, and endpoint rejection.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Public-relay and real browser/WebRTC scenarios are opt-in and remained skipped locally. Android receiving-app layout, screen locking, Bluetooth routing, and background execution remain client-owned and are not part of this adapter's scope. Final image-build and CLI-only jobs were still running when this body was prepared.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Included above.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source and boundary review confirmed that remote, wildcard, credential-bearing, and non-loopback transports are rejected before a socket is opened; link-preview metadata is discarded while user text is retained; and queued previews are not represented as confirmed delivery. No live contacts or paid model providers were exercised in this finalization pass.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Exact final protocol output for compatible Markdown and live-text transitions.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `bf405ff9a8383f4a35b8f88927187d5e8e6103d9`; `channel=simplex` protocol behavior through `contrib/simplex/format.test.mjs`, `live.test.mjs`, and `bridge.test.mjs`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Formatter and live tests require bold headings, Unicode arrow conversion, text separators, unchanged code/link destinations, and one physical live item updated through preview and finalization. This PR does not change the Android UI.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** A remote or wildcard WebSocket is refused with `ok: false` before connection; loopback PCM preserves the bearer header; live text uses one physical item; incoming link previews admit only their text; and calls finalize or cancel without replaying an uncertain final edit.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** A duplicate final migration run and another full local release build were intentionally skipped after the parent reported both migration and installer gates green and fresh GitHub CI began on the exact pushed head.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** An explicitly enabled channel launches its configured bridge executable without a shell; the helper uses private temporary audio files and a sandboxed browser. Both channel admission and calls default closed, and every contact needs an explicit numeric peer grant.
- New external network calls? **Yes.** SimpleX messaging/file relays and WebRTC TURN carry encrypted traffic; the selected STT/TTS/model services receive their ordinary decrypted inputs. Plaintext WebSocket APIs are restricted to exact loopback hosts and are never exposed remotely by this adapter.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** Live transcription reuses the selected local provider's optional bearer token on a validated loopback WebSocket; call keys remain in the helper/browser signaling path. No new credential store or committed key material is introduced or logged intentionally. The official CLI owns its identity database, which operators must protect and back up.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Fixtures use temporary profiles, synthetic peers, and local mock services.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Authorized messages, link-preview text, and transcripts are untrusted conversational input and pass through the existing agent/tool policy. Trusted speech-onset control is explicit adapter metadata, never parsed from message text. Outbound text/speech follows existing sanitization, leak detection, and hook decisions.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Transport endpoints use exact host allowlists, reject credentials in URLs, default disabled, require explicit numeric peer grants, and keep the unauthenticated SimpleX API on loopback. Outbound hooks defer speculative content; approved speech already audible cannot be recalled.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Existing serialized configuration and channel behavior: Yes. Rust source compatibility: No for exhaustive literals of the extended public structs or exhaustive matches on `ProgressEvent`.**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes:** optional `channels.simplex.<alias>` configuration, `channel-simplex` feature, and optional `local_whisper.stream_uri`. Helper paths use the documented `CHROMIUM_PATH`, `SIMPLEX_CALL_ASSETS`, and setup directory. None are required by existing installations.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.** The separately installed helper requires Node.js 20+, ffmpeg/ffprobe, and sandboxed Chromium; the supplied CLI download targets Linux x86-64, with other platforms requiring a compatible official CLI.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: Existing users need no config migration. Opting in requires the documented feature build and helper setup, a private CLI identity, explicit peer grants, and an owning agent. Update the native adapter and helper together. Rust consumers constructing exhaustive `ChannelMessage`, `ChannelsConfig`, or `LocalWhisperTranscriptionProviderConfig` literals must add the new default fields (`control: None`, an empty `simplex` map, or `stream_uri: None`) or use `..Default::default()`. Exhaustive `ProgressEvent` matches must handle the new content-free `Reasoning` variant. The new live-speech trait callback has a no-op default.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Disable the SimpleX channel and reload/restart the daemon. Revert the squash-merge commit to remove the whole feature, or revert `bf405ff9a`, `a89f84ec6`, `65130af2d`, `1103b0ab4`, `b0db93b51`, and `d0d832bb8` in reverse order to remove only this finalization series while retaining the dependency branch. Preserve CLI identity databases and existing ZeroClaw transcripts.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Omit `channel-simplex`, set the channel's `enabled = false`, or set `calls_enabled = false` to stop admitting calls while retaining messaging. Disabling the channel plus reload/restart terminates its helper.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Daemon logs `SimpleX event processing failed`, `Live call speech update failed`, `simplex_live_recognition_failed`, or `Final answer delivery uncertain; not resending`; missing finalized live text, a failed-note notice, a refused loopback endpoint, or a dropped call. Uncertain delivery requires inspection, not automatic answer replay.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- **Superseded PRs + authors (`#<pr> by @<author>`, one per line):** N/A.
- **Scope materially carried forward:** N/A; this finalizes the existing dependency stack rather than superseding it.
- **`Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors?** No.
- **If `No`, why (implementation commits retain their original authors and commit history rather than being re-attributed):** The branch history remains intact and the follow-up commits retain their originating commit provenance through cherry-pick footers where applicable.

prs.title: fix(ssh): keep the Python task helper agent-only
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** keep the standalone Python helper agent-only, localize existing diagnostics, and preserve the predecessor's process-group cleanup.
- **Scope boundary:** no catalog reads, key loading, cryptography dependency or HTTP client-pool change.
- **Blast radius:** the opt-in helper and its documentation/tests.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #11869 and its placement record #12266. Related #12438.

### What this does, simply

The helper reuses the operator's configured SSH agent and OpenSSH aliases. It does not read a credential catalog or resolve a vault. This branch includes the predecessor's helper-death proxy cleanup; the unrelated HTTP repair has been reverted and remains in #12323.

## Testing

### How you can test

Run `python3 scripts/ssh/test_ssh_task.py` on Linux with `/usr/bin/ssh` and `/usr/bin/setpriv`. Confirm the proxy-death test runs rather than skips. Configure a disposable host alias, run two commands under one task and close its input; verify the master and proxy descendants exit. The local source suite passed 21 tests, including ProxyLifecycleTests, without skips.

### How I tested

Current source validation results and exact commit IDs are recorded in the follow-up comment below. Historical evidence is explicitly labeled and is not acceptance of a later revision. Hosted CI on the published head remains authoritative for the full workspace.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.**
- New external network calls? **No.**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.**

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes.**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No.**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback:** restore the prior protected helper executable and PATH wrapper, or revert this PR's diagnostic/documentation changes after respecting the predecessor's merge order.
- **Feature flags/config toggles:** unset `ZEROCLAW_SSH_TASK_HELPER` to disable the opt-in transport.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** unexpected `zeroclaw-ssh:` refusals, failed connections, stalled shutdown, or leftover `ssh -M`/ProxyCommand processes.

## Shared security prerequisite

#12552 has merged into master as 3773cae2d7288f9e6af1ad8414e6d2cd33e90451. This branch incorporates that master revision; no separate SMTP change is carried in this feature diff. CI is rerun on the published head.

prs.title: feat(tools): add scoped WebDAV operations for remote files
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** add an operator-defined WebDAV resource catalog and independent encrypted Remote Files grants; register an opt-in `remote_files` tool for directory listing and file metadata; implement bounded WebDAV transport and transfer primitives without shell fallback.
- **Scope boundary:** the agent-facing tool exposes only `list_directory` and `get_file_info`. Transfer/mutation primitives and the Linux mount adapter are draft implementation scaffolding, not supported agent operations. External vault subprocess resolution and production acceptance are not established.
- **Blast radius:** config/grant admission, the dedicated credential API and WebUI, tool inventory/registration, call-scoped credential approval and HTTPS egress.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12596. Related #12690 and RFC #12422. This remains draft pending review and the cross-platform acceptance matrix.

### What this does, simply

An operator registers an HTTPS WebDAV root under an alias, binds a credential alias and grants Remote Files access separately from HTTP or Browser access. The agent supplies the resource alias and a relative path. Stored grants, current resource binding, credential revision, HTTPS egress policy and any required human approval are checked before credentials are used. A missing approval response denies access.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes; use disposable HTTPS WebDAV endpoints and synthetic local credentials.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** tool execution and WebUI credential permissions.
- **Setup / preconditions:** encrypted catalog, operator-registered resource, dedicated Remote Files grant and an allowed public HTTPS endpoint.
- **Steps to run:** list a directory and inspect a file; revoke the grant and repeat; require human approval and test approval, denial and absent approval; change the bound origin or credential revision while approval is pending.
- **Expected on this branch:** only the two read operations are exposed to agents; missing/revoked grants, stale approval and retargeted resources fail closed.
- **Prior behavior on master:** there is no Remote Files resource catalog, grant or tool.

### How I tested

Earlier focused Linux WebDAV, grant, transfer and dispatcher results are recorded in the existing follow-up comments and apply to their named revisions. They do not prove a later head or a live production server.

The current repair configures a synthetic WebDAV resource in the maximal-registry fixture and adds `remote_files` to the optional tool documentation table. These address the inventory-registration and documentation drift failures reported by Linux, Windows and macOS CI. Updated test results and exact revisions are recorded in the follow-up comments. The separate fixture repair is draft #12700. Local maximal-registry compilation did not complete because build artifacts exhausted local disk; those artifacts were removed. Hosted CI on 9de670625 remains authoritative. Platform-suite failures outside this feature are tracked separately; they are not claimed resolved by the inventory repair.

Cross-platform contract execution against disposable endpoints, actual-interface evidence for the permissions editor, live server validation and independently approved runtime placement remain acceptance requirements. The code and the passing WebDAV CI legs do not alone establish that complete matrix.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** Independent resource/operation grants default closed; mutation primitives are not exposed by the agent tool.
- New external network calls? **Yes.** HTTPS WebDAV calls use validated resource roots, bounded responses, disabled redirects and egress restrictions; no shell fallback.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** Dedicated Remote Files grants reference the existing encrypted catalog; binding, revision and authorization are rechecked. Missing approval denies access.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Fixtures use synthetic aliases and data.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Remote names and metadata are untrusted tool output and convey no authorization.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes.** Empty resource configuration registers no tool.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** Adds `remote_files.webdav` and dedicated credential grant metadata; operators must explicitly configure both the resource and its grant.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** remove Remote Files resources/grants to disable registration, then revert the feature commits or restore the previous binary. Preserve encrypted configuration backups.
- **Feature flags/config toggles:** empty `remote_files.webdav` disables registration; revoking a grant prevents credential use.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** missing tool registration, refused/stale grants, unexpected approval behavior, remote path/egress refusals or WebDAV transport failures.

## Cross-platform acceptance and dependencies

Linux, Windows and macOS must expose the same supported operation contract, approval semantics, credential scope and failure categories. A missing host prerequisite disables its backend. A platform-specific adapter does not establish a supported platform-only product feature. Runtime placement and the #12596 / RFC #12422 dependencies require independent review; this feature grants itself no exception.

prs.title: feat(ssh): scope password and TOTP authentication to vault grants
prs.body:
## Scope

One operator form under Secrets → Usage permissions → Add authorization. SSH shows the destination list, authentication mode and, when required, a TOTP alias. Other consumers keep their existing form.

| Primary alias | Modes |
| --- | --- |
| SSH key | Key; key followed by TOTP |
| Username and password | Username and password; password then TOTP; TOTP then password; password and TOTP in one field |

The password credential supplies the SSH username and password, with port 22 by default. A key uses the destination account. The authorization binds the selected TOTP alias to its exact SSH destinations. Edits and revocation use the catalog revision. The OpenAPI documents the write contract.

The optional portable-ssh feature adds a scoped SSH authorization parameter to the existing shell tool. The task pool verifies operator host pins before resolving credentials, follows protocol authentication events independently of prompt text, rejects an incomplete factor sequence and revalidates the encrypted grant before each new channel. The existing shell policy and sandbox denial still apply. See the development documentation for the daemon environment and a structured tool example.

## Verification

* Linux and Windows native loopback SSH protocol tests exercised all six modes for the transport.
* The disposable QEMU OpenSSH fixture authenticated with password and TOTP from an encrypted test catalog. Two commands reused the connection. Revoking the TOTP prevented the next command.
* The production-equivalent WebUI build passed. The isolated Chrome fixture exercised both credential types, multiple destinations, both default and explicit ports, and revision-checked revocation.

The PR stays in draft while completing the integrated rollout and platform validation. Earlier evidence using the Linux prompt-label form applies to the previous implementation. The scoped catalog and broker dependencies remain #12596 and #12438.

A compatible published Matrix storage dependency is required before landing. Tracked at https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-rust-sdk/issues/7456. The bridge was removed from independent ZeroClaw PRs; the Security success here is not release readiness.

The security gate currently fails because the bundled SQLite is vulnerable. Updating just SQLite is blocked by Matrix's dependency pin. prs.title: feat(web): manage scoped HTTP credentials
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** add write-only, locally encrypted HTTP Basic and API-key aliases, bound to one HTTPS origin and a separate explicit HTTP Request grant. Reject catalog changes through generic gateway/RPC config writers.
- **Scope boundary:** local Basic, Bearer and X-API-Key only. SSH, TOTP, directory destinations and external resolvers remain in draft #12517 behind RFC #12422; Token is the separate #12490 increment. Plugin TLS management is inherited from #12402.
- **Blast radius:** config admission, dedicated credential API, audit/OpenAPI, Secrets editors and HTTP authentication/redaction.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12402 and #12563. Related RFC #12422 and #12490.

### What this does, simply

An operator registers an alias in Settings → Secrets. Creation starts denied and use requires a separate explicit grant. Every caller already allowed to use HTTP Request at the stored origin can use that alias; there is no separate per-agent selector. Scope binds scheme, host and port, without path or method restrictions.

Same-origin rotation preserves the grant; changing origin clears it. Listings and audits never contain values. Host overrides are refused, redirects disabled, auth headers sensitive, reflected values scrubbed, and truncated authenticated bodies omitted.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, with disposable credentials and an allowed HTTPS endpoint.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** WebUI Secrets, dedicated gateway credential API and HTTP Request execution.
- **Setup / preconditions:** encryption enabled with an existing key, operator access and an origin allowed by network policy.
- **Steps to run:** create a denied alias; grant and use it; rotate at an equivalent origin and then a different origin; revoke/delete; attempt generic property, section and map-key mutations with a broad HTTP editor.
- **Expected on this branch:** explicit grant required, same-origin grant retained, cross-origin grant cleared, no secret listing, and generic mutations refused without changing persisted config.
- **Prior behavior on master:** no managed scoped HTTP catalog or dedicated editor.

### How I tested

The current follow-up is e3a5aa5267. Focused rustfmt checks and git diff checks passed. Existing route, rotation, generic gateway/RPC write and redaction regressions are retained. Fresh CI on the published revision is authoritative; pending checks are not a passing result.

Both optional review suggestions are addressed: the shared enum is `CredentialOperation`, and the origin regression includes `https://evil-example.com` and `https://example.com.evil.test`.

[Desktop/narrow HTTP captures](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/tree/0fbb8fcbae826d7f62d9042efdcdfe66713b7671/pr-12408) and [inherited TLS captures](https://github.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/tree/e96bc6ba9c12544962e6a9a50afd0567d1507869/pr-12408/tls) render the actual components at 391cce0 with synthetic data and a mocked catalog API. Those component files are unchanged here. The captures cover desktop/narrow empty, encryption-disabled, denied, grant/revoke, replace and delete states where applicable. They remain component-harness evidence, not a new full-gateway deployed exact-head validation. Earlier broader deployment evidence is historical.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** Operator-only mutations and default-denied HTTP grants, shared by callers already authorized for HTTP Request at that origin.
- New external network calls? **Yes.** Opt-in authenticated HTTPS requests use the existing HTTP transport and network policy. No external vault resolver or new process execution is added.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** Locally encrypted values, write-only API, value-free audit and authenticated-response redaction; generic catalog mutation is rejected.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** Synthetic fixtures and evidence.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** HTTP responses remain untrusted data and convey no new execution authority.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes.** Empty catalogs preserve the existing HTTP workflow.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** Adds scoped credential config, the dedicated API and an optional tool credential-alias argument. Enrollment and grants are explicit.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revoke grants, remove feature aliases through the dedicated API, preserve an encrypted backup, then revert the feature or restore the previous binary.
- **Feature flags/config toggles:** empty catalog or revoked per-alias grants disables use; existing network policy remains authoritative.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** unexpected credential refusal, grant loss during same-origin rotation, generic-write acceptance, catalog validation errors or reflected secret material.

## Landing prerequisites

Merge #12402 and the independently approved placement record #12563 before this feature, then #12490. This feature grants itself no runtime exception. Both prerequisite merges and outstanding human implementation reviews remain required. Shared SMTP, URL/Ruma and cookie remediation comes from master; no advisory waiver is introduced by this feature.

## Summary

The initial HTTP credential PR #12408 is limited to locally encrypted API keys and Basic credentials bound to one HTTPS origin. The native broker PR #12438 is limited to existing SSH-agent authentication. This draft preserves the additional catalog implementation removed from those review slices.

Depends on #12408 and #12438. Related #12422 and #12373. Approval and merge are conditional on acceptance of RFC #12422 and any requested changes to its credential ownership, consumer grants and record model.

The preserved features include TOTP, SSH key records and destination grants, non-HTTP service descriptors, external secret references, the permissions WebUI, OpenBao-backed native SSH authentication and the existing provider-reference adapters. OpenBao provisioning and the other provider writers remain in #12481 and #12482.

These features are used on our company's Jarvis production server for live testing with actual operational workloads. OpenBao-backed credentials and the associated skills are in active use. That deployment supplies operator feedback and does not imply upstream acceptance. We will adjust this draft as RFC #12422 evolves.

The operator-managed service credential stays hidden from the model. Consumers resolve the configured alias under explicit grants. Unsandboxed same-UID shell processes retain the service user's OS authority, including access to catalog state and signer sockets. Destination constraints provide defense in depth.

## Testing

The HTTP redaction production function passed four focused regressions for quote-bearing secrets, decoded JSON strings/keys, numeric secrets and large integer preservation. Native broker lifecycle tests are being refreshed for process-group cleanup and pre-bound socket refusal. Prior operator acceptance covers OpenBao credential creation and real HTTP and managed SSH use. Full CI on this draft must be reviewed independently.

Reviewer testing requested when the RFC scope is accepted. On an isolated deployment, register a synthetic credential, grant its consumer and exact destination, verify use succeeds, revoke it and verify denial, then rotate the secret and verify the new value reaches the protected endpoint.

## Security

Secret values are encrypted locally or referenced from the configured external store. New HTTP grants remain denied by default. Host and consumer authorization continue at use time. The draft documents the same-UID security boundary and remains subject to the RFC.

## Compatibility

This draft preserves the implemented record shapes used by the integrated Jarvis build. The RFC may require schema migration before upstream release. Apply the integrated feature set when testing existing external-source catalogs.

## Rollback

Use a protected state backup and the corresponding integrated binary. A binary supporting only the reduced local HTTP slice cannot consume the extended catalog. Downgrades require an explicit state migration.

## Documentation

The credential and SSH guides describe the retained implementation. RFC #12422 is the decision owner. The separate drafts #12481 and #12482 retain their provider-specific setup and validation.
## Updated validation and dependencies

Depends on #12490 for the Authorization Token header, retained here so the extended catalog can represent existing Token credentials. The live Jarvis build combines both slices.

prs.body:
## Summary

- Base branch: `master`. Depends on #12481. Related #12422 and #12373.
- Provide operator-only create and rotate for 1Password Connect, Azure Key Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, and Google Secret Manager.
- Reuse the external reference form and provider-scoped editable defaults. Retain explicit linking, blank preservation on replacement, and catalog-only deletion.
- Use verified HTTPS, per-operation write authorization, and configured vault or name scope. Store only encrypted references. Existing read adapters still use their own identity.

### What this does, simply

An operator can provision a value from the same Secrets form regardless of which configured vault holds it. Azure and 1Password check for a name collision before creating. Their APIs provide no atomic conditional create by name, so configure a dedicated single-writer namespace. Google may create a resource before its first version fails. The UI directs the operator to check, link, and replace in that case.

## Testing

### How you can test

Enable one provider with a disposable prefix according to the WebUI guide. Use a scoped test identity. Add a synthetic value, verify the reference, replace it and confirm it advances, then delete the catalog alias. A blank replacement preserves the external value. Repeat with an existing name to see the conflict.

### How I tested

Added mock HTTP tests for all four providers. Tests cover expected request bodies, routes, AWS signing headers, scope validation, collision handling, 1Password IDs, and Google's partial-create recovery. `cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib cloud_vault_write::tests` passed all five tests. The integrated WebUI passed TypeScript build and Vite production bundling. Real accounts are not available in this environment.

## Security and privacy

- New capability and external calls: yes, opt-in operator-only writes to a configured scope via verified HTTPS. Redirects and proxy environment routing are disabled.
- Secrets: transient write authority and value. Neither is included in catalog responses, audit output or persistent configuration.
- Personal data and untrusted model inputs: none added. Provider responses are never forwarded to the model.

## Compatibility and rollback

Remove the writer prefix to disable writes while preserving existing references. Reverting the code restores link-only behavior for these four providers. No migration is required. To remove an external resource, manage it in the vault.


### Integrated smoke test

The Linux release built with XMPP enabled. A disposable OpenBao KV v2 instance over verified TLS and an isolated gateway passed create, path denial, collision, versioned replacement, blank preservation, deletion of the alias and catalog-response redaction through the shared mutation route. After deployment to the Jarvis lab, the gateway, WebUI, OIDC and XMPP were healthy and the SSH helper remained Rust. The four cloud writers remain opt-in and unconfigured in that environment.

### Review and dependencies update

The branch inherits the catalog and manifest-validation corrections from #12408 and #12402 through the OpenBao work in #12481. The four cloud adapters are covered by mocked provider HTTP tests. The real OpenBao smoke test covers the shared mutation route. Live provider validation remains open for contributors with access.

### OpenBao managed authentication and live validation

The OpenBao form uses the server's configured identity and never asks the operator for a vault write token. It preserves the editable reference suggested from the mount, prefix, alias and field. Add writes the value through the gateway. Link existing saves only the reference and performs no vault write. The server can use the existing OpenBao Agent token sink from BAO_TOKEN_PATH or a dedicated ZEROCLAW_OPENBAO_WRITE_TOKEN_FILE.

Validated on the integrated Jarvis build 0504477e9. The operator confirmed a real WebUI save without a token field after the OpenBao policy was scoped to the configured credential prefix. A synthetic OpenBao API test with the Jarvis identity verified create, read and rotation; the fixture was removed. Validation here covers OpenBao. The other cloud providers retain their own authorization flows.


## RFC scope and deployment status

Depends on #12517. Approval and merge are conditional on acceptance of RFC #12422. This remains a draft. The OpenBao implementation is in actual operational use on our company's Jarvis production server for live testing, with existing secrets and skills. Provider-specific claims retain their documented test coverage. We will adapt these features as the RFC evolves.

prs.title: feat(web): provision scoped catalog credentials in OpenBao
prs.body:
## Summary

Base branch `master`. Depends on #12408. Related #12422 and #12373.

The external credential editor separates **Add**, **Link existing secret**, **Replace**, and **Delete**. OpenBao KV v2 writes support existing catalog credential types, including TOTP. An operator-configured mount and prefix supply an editable default identifier. The other external providers keep the same reference editor while their write adapters are pending.

### How to test

1. Configure an HTTPS OpenBao origin, a disposable KV v2 prefix and a server-side OpenBao identity scoped to that prefix. Sign in to the dashboard as an operator.
2. Add a synthetic TOTP entry. Check the prefilled identifier, save, and verify the remote KV entry and local metadata.
3. Try to add to the same destination. Confirm the CAS rejection.
4. Replace at the same path and verify its new version. Leave the value blank on a second replacement and verify the version stays the same.
5. Delete the catalog entry and verify the vault still owns its data.

### Validation

- `git diff --check` passed. Includes a regression test for prefix enforcement.
- The gateway typecheck, focused Rust prefix test, integrated Linux release build and WebUI build passed. An isolated gateway and OpenBao KV v2 server using TLS verified operator authentication, path confinement, creation, CAS collision, versioned rotation, blank replacement, catalog deletion and absence of secret values or write token from the local config. The integration test caught a duplicate Content-Type header during rotation, which is corrected and verified in 584d7f717. The integrated build was deployed on the Jarvis lab host with the OpenBao write prefix scoped to its own tree and the existing private CA verified. The gateway uses the configured OpenBao authentication when writing. Downstream use still requires the runtime read identity to have access to that path.

## Security and privacy

The gateway authorizes the operator and config mutation before contacting OpenBao. It uses verified HTTPS with redirects disabled, a constrained prefix, CAS zero for create, and a versioned patch for rotation. For OpenBao, the gateway uses the server-configured token file. The gateway persists only the encrypted reference. No credentials or personal data are included in fixtures. Remote failures are reported without printing response bodies. Agent-side vault access continues through the existing resolver.

## Compatibility and rollback

Additive opt-in gateway configuration. Existing link-only requests remain supported. Unset `ZEROCLAW_OPENBAO_WRITE_PREFIX` to disable writes or revert the change to roll back. Manage existing remote secret versions in the vault.

### Review and dependencies update

The branch inherits the catalog and manifest-validation corrections from #12408 and #12402. The earlier live evidence covers OpenBao KV v2 over TLS. Please review the new CI on this head separately. The draft still depends on #12408.

### Visual evidence

Historical captures from before the managed-writer change, using a synthetic alias and vault path. Playwright verified that the editable reference defaults to the entered alias. Add displays the value and vault write-token fields. Link existing hides both fields. The captures submit no writes. The isolated HTTPS OpenBao tests above cover the actual write lifecycle.

![Add a TOTP credential in OpenBao](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/1b8b6d49e1e65c0048623874dd0af58533c17a02/evidence/12481-openbao-add.png)

![Link a TOTP credential already in OpenBao](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/1b8b6d49e1e65c0048623874dd0af58533c17a02/evidence/12481-openbao-link.png)

### OpenBao managed authentication and live validation

The OpenBao form uses the server's configured identity and never asks the operator for a vault write token. It preserves the editable reference suggested from the mount, prefix, alias and field. Add writes the value through the gateway. Link existing saves only the reference and performs no vault write. The server can use the existing OpenBao Agent token sink from BAO_TOKEN_PATH or a dedicated ZEROCLAW_OPENBAO_WRITE_TOKEN_FILE.

Validated on the integrated Jarvis build 0504477e9. The operator confirmed a real WebUI save without a token field after the OpenBao policy was scoped to the configured credential prefix. A synthetic OpenBao API test with the Jarvis identity verified create, read and rotation; the fixture was removed. Validation here covers OpenBao. The other cloud providers retain their own authorization flows.


## RFC scope and deployment status

Depends on #12517. Approval and merge are conditional on acceptance of RFC #12422. This remains a draft. The OpenBao implementation is in actual operational use on our company's Jarvis production server for live testing, with existing secrets and skills. Provider-specific claims retain their documented test coverage. We will adapt these features as the RFC evolves.


## Shared security prerequisite

#12552 has merged into master as 3773cae2d7288f9e6af1ad8414e6d2cd33e90451. This branch incorporates that revision. Hosted CI is rerun on the refreshed head; no separate SMTP policy change is carried in this feature diff.

## Managed credential RPC placement

Depends on #12563, the separately reviewed bounded Core Team exception record for the generic-RPC credential write guard. The guard stays enabled; this feature does not approve its own placement. The record must land before this feature merges.

<!-- pr-maintenance-20261122:start -->
## Maintenance validation (2026-11-22)

Tested/check-tracked head: `9c7f882ccba3b28de500eeb06d1b6108591fd685`. The branch includes master `e02b7fb6f61b2872e45e876b9f2de0faeb825f20`; no base refresh was needed at this checkpoint.

The lockfile carries the same dependency remediation as #12656: `url` 2.5.9 and `ruma` 0.17.2 / `ruma-identifiers-validation` 0.14.1 for RUSTSEC-2026-0592, RUSTSEC-2026-0588 and RUSTSEC-2026-0589. `matrix-sdk` remains 0.19.1. This maintenance update changes no advisory exception or manifest requirement. Local `cargo metadata --locked --no-deps --format-version 1` and `git diff --check` passed for the dependency update.

prs.body:
## Summary

An OIDC session needs `features.config` to open Browser Voice and Audio. Enabling voice and using the microphone and speaker in chat requires both `features.config` and `features.chat`, including in a fresh browser without device pairing. A Chat-only session cannot access voice settings or enable the OIDC controls. Preferences are stored per verified account in the browser, using a SHA-256 account digest. Capture and playback state reset when the account changes. The paired-device flow, dashboard permissions and global silence setting continue to use their existing paths.

## Merge order and scope

#12269 merged first in fa48765b3e3c80681d01d637b3629af37cb0398f. That merge is an ancestor of this PR head. The nine parent screenshots are outside this PR's diff. The URL/Ruma security remediation is inherited from master; Cargo.lock is no longer part of this PR’s diff.

## How I tested

Historical frontend evidence: `8ad61210cc6924f3849e3fecef79b285a05e566d`. Follow-up commit `50945fa04` changed only the permission documentation. Current rebase validation is recorded below; the linked earlier CI is not claimed as a run of the new head.

- Local Node 24: production frontend build and `npm run test:voice` passed, 42/42.
- [Hosted Web Permission Tests](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45079738616/job/137385031992) explicitly ran `npm run test:voice` and passed **OIDC voice settings enable chat controls without pairing and isolate accounts**. The [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45079738616/job/137396536637) passed.
- Real Chrome and Keycloak OIDC on Jarvis, from fresh browser profiles with no paired token. The browser served the compiled frontend of this PR head only in the test window. Jarvis provided the real authentication and gateway endpoints. Entry asset `index-DFCfYcNp.js`. The build reused the generated dashboard API type inputs from the Jarvis integration. The voice source files were from the stated PR head.
- Both viewports showed the enabled settings and the chat microphone and speaker. The screenshot check did not record audio or test audible playback.

## OIDC evidence

### Desktop settings
![Browser Voice and Audio configuration on desktop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/400f75c3f896632d9936d4aede9f23d01b2f9dba/jarvis-production/voice-oidc-settings-desktop-8ad61210.png)

### Desktop chat
![Microphone and speaker in the OIDC desktop chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/400f75c3f896632d9936d4aede9f23d01b2f9dba/jarvis-production/voice-oidc-chat-desktop-8ad61210.png)

![Microphone and speaker in the OIDC mobile chat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/400f75c3f896632d9936d4aede9f23d01b2f9dba/jarvis-production/voice-oidc-chat-mobile-8ad61210.png)




## Rebase validation (2026-11-23)

Rebased onto master `74c8af5cf` as `bb72687f8`. The branch is one commit ahead and zero behind that base. The old history carried copies of the already-merged #12269 parent; the refreshed branch contains only this PR’s seven-file delta. The complete diff is byte-identical to the pre-rebase delta at `95e01f1be5c3e768949d838fe11a68f1ca9c359c`. Administrator paired-device selection, account isolation, permission checks and narration fixes are preserved. No new interface change was introduced by the rebase.

Local Node 24.19.0, using the Windows Jiti equivalent of `npm run test:voice`:

```text
✔ OIDC voice settings enable chat controls without pairing and isolate accounts
ℹ tests 43
ℹ pass 43
ℹ fail 0
```

`git diff --check` passed. The voice runtime files, voice test file and npm lockfile are unchanged from the previous head. The local suite emits the existing react-test-renderer deprecation warning; no warning suppression or dependency change was introduced. The earlier screenshots remain historical evidence at their stated source revisions. New hosted CI is running for the rebased commit; earlier passing checks are not reported as current-head results.

prs.title: feat(ssh): add a native Rust task broker
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** implement the task-owned OpenSSH transport as a native Rust executable using the operator's existing SSH agent and effective host configuration.
- **Scope boundary:** no catalog-backed credential loading, broker-managed vault signing, credential editor or cloud resolver.
- **Blast radius:** opt-in Linux task broker and inherited task-lifetime wiring.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #11869, #12418 and the bounded placement record #12266. Related #11867 and #12518.

### What this does, simply

Commands to the same alias and effective configuration reuse a master for one task. EOF, cancellation and idle retirement close masters and proxy process groups. Select the executable with `ZEROCLAW_SSH_TASK_HELPER`; it does not introduce credentials or change target authorization.

## Testing

### How you can test

On Linux with OpenSSH 8.7+ and util-linux setpriv, configure a disposable SSH alias and the native helper. Verify reuse, effective-configuration separation, EOF shutdown, idle expiry, and a TERM-ignoring proxy surviving its leader. Exact reduced-source CI run 44313896064 passed seven broker tests in both Test and Test (opt-in tools); that is historical evidence for its named head, not proof of the refreshed head. New-head CI will validate this revision.

### How I tested

- Linux: `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib task_ssh_broker::tests::` passed 11/11 at 7be9c01ad. The new regression uses a controlled connector and the real lease pool. It verifies that two concurrent requests for the same pool key attempt setup once, return a setup error to the first caller and the cached failure to the second, and leave zero active leases. The test uses no network.


Current source validation results and exact commit IDs are recorded in the follow-up comment below. Historical evidence is explicitly labeled and is not acceptance of a later revision. Hosted CI on the published head remains authoritative for the full workspace.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.**
- New external network calls? **No.**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.**

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes:** the opt-in task protocol and idle-timeout contract are retained.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes:** the Rust executable is an additive helper choice selected through the existing helper path.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.** Native operation requires Linux, OpenSSH 8.7 or later and util-linux setpriv.
- Upgrade: build `zeroclaw-ssh-task`, retain a protected copy of the previous helper executable and PATH link, then point both managed helper paths to the native executable.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback:** restore the previous helper executable and PATH link from a protected backup and restart the service.
- **Feature flags/config toggles:** unset `ZEROCLAW_SSH_TASK_HELPER` to disable managed transport.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `tool-native-ssh-connection`, `tool-native-ssh-denied`, `Task SSH cleanup timed out`, or leftover `ssh -M` processes.

## Shared security prerequisite

#12552 has merged into master as 3773cae2d7288f9e6af1ad8414e6d2cd33e90451. This branch incorporates that master revision; no separate SMTP change is carried in this feature diff. CI is rerun on the published head.

## Summary

Add an opt-in stdio MCP bridge for scoped configuration changes. A directly authorized agent can discover settings and request a write through the existing gateway. The gateway authenticates an OIDC principal and enforces that principal's grants and writable paths. The bridge does not write the configuration file or expose an operator reload tool.

### What this does, simply

An operator can allow a particular agent to change a particular setting, such as one runtime profile's context limit. If runtime work is active, the bridge returns a job ID and waits for an idle observation. Idle is not an admission lock or operator approval. RPC execution now holds an active-turn lease during the actual turn; an idle open session does not count as work.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

Follow the scoped OIDC example in the MCP guide, grant one writable leaf and enable delegate-inheritance denial for the server. Verify an allowed change, rejection outside that path, and that a delegated agent cannot access the withheld server. Exercise a queued write during an active RPC turn.

### How I tested

All 25 Python bridge tests passed on the changed implementation. The branch includes Rust coverage for OIDC activity access and delegated MCP isolation. Consult the checks on the current head for hosted Rust validation.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

The bridge requires an explicit loopback gateway and OIDC provider selection. It reads the service token from an owner-only file and disables HTTP redirects and proxy inheritance. Native pairing tokens are no longer the setup path. The gateway remains responsible for authorization: configure a non-admin principal with only the necessary grants and exact writable paths. A broad profile would still grant broad authority. Use the documented delegate-inheritance denial for this server. Queued mutations are not blindly replayed on uncertain delivery. No live credentials or production data are required for tests.

## Compatibility (required)

This is opt-in. The bridge requires a daemon supporting the authenticated configuration activity probe, an OIDC service credential, and an explicit server and bundle grant. Earlier draft configurations using operator pairing must be replaced. Existing MCP servers retain their prior inheritance policy unless the new option is enabled.

## Rollback

Remove the bundle grant and revoke the service credential. Stop outstanding bridge workers before removing their private job records. Revert any already-applied configuration changes through the normal configuration interface.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A.

prs.title: chore(lint): fix clippy lints introduced by Rust 1.99
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - CI pins Rust 1.98.0, where the workspace is clippy-clean. On Rust 1.99.0, `scripts/ci/run_clippy.sh --scope workspace` fails on existing code, so the next toolchain bump would be blocked by unrelated lint fallout. This clears it ahead of time.
  - `fetch_update` on atomics is deprecated in 1.99 in favour of `try_update`, which has the same signature and semantics. 4 call sites, plus one comment that names the method.
  - `needless_borrows_for_generic_args`: 4 capture-free (`Copy`) closures passed as `&f` are now passed by value.
  - `assert_is_empty` (pedantic; only the root crate opts into `clippy::pedantic`): 40 flagged `assert!(x.is_empty())` test assertions now print the value on failure, which is the lint's point (CI failures show *what* was there). Call results are bound to a `let` first so the message does not re-evaluate the call.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not bump the CI toolchain or MSRV, does not add any `#[allow]`, and touches no production logic beyond the two behaviour-preserving mechanical edits above. Only the exact lines clippy flagged were changed: unflagged `is_empty()` assertions on non-slice types were left alone.
- **Blast radius:** None at runtime. Test failure messages for the rewritten assertions now include the offending value.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12642 (spotted while validating that PR on a local 1.99 toolchain)

### What this does, simply

The Rust toolchain on newer machines (1.99) added and changed some lint rules. CI still uses 1.98, so nothing is failing today, but anyone on 1.99 sees `cargo clippy` fail on code nobody touched, and the next CI toolchain bump would hit the same wall. This PR fixes those lint findings. Two are pure renames or simplifications with identical behaviour. The rest are test assertions that, when they fail, will now print the unexpected value instead of just "assertion failed".

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: lint-only change; the evidence is clippy on three toolchains plus the crates' own test suites, listed below.

### How I tested

Ran CI's exact clippy invocation (`scripts/ci/run_clippy.sh --scope workspace` → `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings`) on the new toolchain, the CI-pinned toolchain, and the MSRV.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Clippy` (1.98.0) and `msrv` cover compatibility of every edit; the crate test jobs cover the rewritten assertions.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI does not run 1.99, which is the point of the PR; the 1.99 run below is local.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
# Before (upstream master 665904f6d6, Rust 1.99.0), with --keep-going, iterated as
# each failing crate unblocked its dependents:
error: use of deprecated method `...Atomic::<usize>::fetch_update`: renamed to `try_update` for consistency
error: the borrowed expression implements the required traits     (x4 across providers, runtime, channels)
error: used `assert!` to check that a value is empty               (x39, root crate)
error: used `assert!` to check that a value is not empty           (x2, root crate)

# After, Rust 1.99.0 (CI command + --keep-going)
exit=0
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 25.89s

# After, Rust 1.98.0 (CI-pinned toolchain), same command
1.98 clippy exit=0
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 4m 00s

# MSRV: Rust 1.96.1 (same feature set as rust-version 1.96.0)
$ cargo +1.96.1 check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all
1.96.1 check exit=0

$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(clean)

$ cargo test --locked --no-fail-fast -p zeroclaw --lib --bins --features ci-all
test result: ok. 335 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
test result: ok. 813 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
test result: ok. 19 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored

$ cargo test --locked --no-fail-fast -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib
test result: ok. 1399 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored
test result: ok. 6263 passed; 0 failed; 10 ignored

$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib
test result: ok. 2061 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored

$ cargo test --locked -p zerocode --test oidc_login
test result: ok. 10 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored

$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib reasoning_effort   # covers the edited fn
test result: ok. 21 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - `try_update` exists and compiles on 1.96.1 (probe crate), so the MSRV is unaffected.
  - Probed `clippy::assert_is_empty` on 1.99 with a non-`PartialEq` element type: the message form passes and compiles. Clippy's own `--fix` suggestion (`assert_eq!(x, [] as [T; 0])`) does not compile for such types, which is why `cargo clippy --fix` rolled back.
  - Checked every new `let` binding for shadowing of an existing local that is used later; none.
  - Confirmed each edited root-crate module has tests compiled and run under `ci-all` (`--list`).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `d8a264228b`; local clippy on 1.99.0 / 1.98.0, check on 1.96.1
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The full `zeroclaw-providers` lib suite is flaky on this host **with and without this change**: 1 to 6 failures per run in `openai::tests::responses_provider_honors_runtime_proxy_config` and `openai::tool_round_policy_tests::native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults` (mock-HTTP/proxy tests). Reproduced the same failures on a tree with no providers changes. The flaky test passes 5/5 in isolation. Not addressed here (separate concern).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No (verified on 1.96.1 and 1.98.0)
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk: `git revert d8a264228b`.

prs.title: docs(runtime): propose ADR-016 exception for daemon-held OIDC refresh grants
prs.body:
> **Refreshed (`e57e860fbf`):** #12608 has merged, so `master` was merged in. This PR now adds only the refresh-grant row, unchanged from `5f6c8ee82f`, after #12608's two Okta/Entra rows.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds the `zeroclaw-runtime` exception row for the refresh-grant implementation that the ADR-017 amendment (#12496, approved) records. The existing #12317 OIDC row explicitly excludes "refresh-token storage", and #12496 now states that each implementing PR touching the auth-provider owner in the holding crate needs its own row first. Proposed ahead of the implementation, as ADR-016 requires and as the plugin-admission row did.
  - Scope names exact paths and limits: retaining the refresh token the existing device-grant and browser responses already return (`EnrolledToken::refresh_token`), a refresh request that omits `scope`, RFC 7009 revocation, never-sent vs unknown-outcome classification (`enrollment.rs`); a new `refresh_grant.rs` module *inside the existing auth-provider subsystem* for the pending grant (keyed by a hash of its paired access token) and the durable, `SecretStore`-sealed grant with version, single-flight, in-flight marker and uncertain state, registered in `auth_provider/mod.rs` limited to declaring the module and re-exporting its public types; a grant table in the existing ledger database so the claim commits in the same transaction as `record_issued`, plus deletion on revocation or unrenewed lapse (`cert_ledger.rs`); and a pre-auth refresh method admitted like `cert/renew`, sign-out, and grant deletion on provider removal/repoint (`rpc/{auth,dispatch,types}.rs`).
  - Explicit exclusions: no dashboard refresh or client-held refresh token, no OAuth flow beyond refresh and revocation, no change to introspection or `initialize`, no new subsystem. Encryption reuses `zeroclaw_config::secrets::SecretStore` (ADR-013) rather than adding crypto to runtime. Gateway hand-off, the Zerocode trigger, and `zeroclaw-rpc-proto` method names stay in their own crates.
- **Scope boundary:** Governance record only; no code. Does not cover #12497/#12498 (that's #12608).
- **Blast radius:** None at runtime. Gates the refresh implementation PRs.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12608. Related #12496, Related #8289

### What this does, simply

The ADR now says how ZeroClaw will keep a laptop's sign-in alive across sleep: the daemon holds the identity provider's refresh token, and the device certificate lets Zerocode ask for a fresh access token. Most of that code has to touch sign-in code in a temporary "holding" crate, which needs a written, approved exception before anything lands there. This is that exception, drawn tightly around what the refresh work needs and nothing more, so the implementation can be reviewed against a fixed boundary.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Governance-table edit with no behavior.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Docs style covers the edited Markdown table.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
$ DOCS_FILES=crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
Summary: 0 error(s)
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Column count matches neighbouring rows. Every named path exists on `master` except the new `refresh_grant.rs`, which the row names as new; `EnrolledToken::refresh_token` already exists in `enrollment.rs`; the `cert/renew` pre-auth admission it mirrors is `MethodAuthz::Handshake` in `rpc/dispatch.rs`; `SecretStore` lives in `zeroclaw-config`. Each limit traced to a decision in #12496 at `9c84e4f8a5`. The "Approved by" cell is a placeholder until a Core Team member approves; I'll replace it with the approval link. I can't approve my own PR.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `e57e860fbf` (docs quality gate: 0 errors; all 62 table rows keep 6 columns)
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Cargo checks skipped: no code changed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No (this records permission; the capability arrives with the implementation)
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No (record only). The scope it permits introduces daemon-held refresh tokens; the threat analysis and containment are in ADR-017 (#12496): sealed at rest, one owner per token, versioned deletion that wins races, never a bearer, deleted on every refusal path.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: revert this PR's squash commit, which adds one table row.
