prs.title: feat(oidc): accept untyped access tokens and declared claim names for JWKS
prs.body:
> **Stacked:** Depends on #12497 and on the ADR-016 exception in #12608. Until #12497 merges this PR also shows its commit (`140e9e594f`); review `fd2bb3da4c` onward.
>
> **Update (`26b2d63d68`):** after review on #12496 and #12498, a token accepted through the `require_at_jwt = false` waiver must carry exactly the configured audience. An ID token's `aud` may list audiences beyond its client (OIDC Core §2), so a nonce-free ID token with `aud: [client, api]` previously passed. Typed tokens are unchanged.
>
> **Update (`b82232c518`..`b3c911620b`):** after @JordanTheJet's review, a declared client claim no longer decides on its own whether a token is a person or a service. The fix is @IftekharUddin's ([tidux/zeroclaw#5](https://github.com/tidux/zeroclaw/pull/5)), cherry-picked with his authorship. On the untyped or declared-client-claim path, a token is a person only with a nonblank human marker at `actor_claim` (Entra `scp`, Okta `uid`), and a service only through the new exact map `actor_claim_values` (Entra `idtyp`: `app`/`user`). A declared client can't override missing or contradicting evidence. Also: an untyped token with an `events` claim (a back-channel logout token) is refused, a blank `azp` contradicts a declared client claim instead of counting as absent, and a test comment that failed the comment-hygiene gate is fixed.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Okta and Entra ID are required for v1.0 (#12496), and the JWKS verifier refused both. Okta access tokens have no header `typ` and name the client in `cid`. Entra ID tokens have `typ: JWT`, use `uti` instead of `jti`, and name the client only in `azp`, including for service principals. Entra has no introspection endpoint to fall back to.
  - **Untyped tokens, without weakening token purpose.** `require_at_jwt = false` (previously rejected for `jwks`) now admits a header with no `typ` or `typ: JWT` only when `audience` is an API identifier that no client signs in as: not `client_id`, not in `interactive_clients`/`service_clients`/`allowed_authorized_parties`/`service_profile_map`, and not a client of another `[oidc.*]` entry for the same issuer. An ID token's `aud` must include its client and may include other audiences. Untyped tokens must therefore carry only the configured API audience, as enforced by `audience_is_exactly`. Config validation enforces client/API separation; the verifier re-checks the entry's own clients through the same `OidcConfig::audience_shared_with_a_client` while cross-entry separation remains enforced by config validation. Other header types (`logout+jwt`, `dpop+jwt`, ...), `nonce`, an `events` claim on an untyped token, and non-access purpose markers are still refused.
  - **Declared claim names instead of vendor detection.** `client_id_claim` (default `client_id`) and `token_id_claim` (default `jti`). Chosen over built-in fallbacks (`cid`/`uti`) because `azp` means different things on Keycloak (stamped on user tokens of service clients) and Entra (the client of every token): only an operator declaration can safely let `azp` prove a *service* client, and fallbacks would grow into a per-IdP mapping table. A declared client claim has no `azp` fallback and must agree with any present `client_id` or `azp` (a blank one disagrees). Both are JWKS-only and refused for introspection (RFC 7662 answers use `client_id`).
  - **Actor from signed per-token evidence, not from the client.** One Entra registration can sign in people *and* run `client_credentials`, and both tokens carry the same `azp`, so a client declaration can't tell them apart. On the untyped or declared-client-claim path, the actor kind comes only from the token: a nonblank human marker at `actor_claim` with `actor_claim_marks = "human"` (Entra `scp`, Okta `uid`), or an exact match in the new JWKS-only `actor_claim_values` map, the only way such a token identifies a service (Entra `idtyp`: `app` → service, `user` → human). Evidence must agree with any client declaration. `actor_claim` may not be the client claim, which is checked at config load and again when the provider is built.
  - Removes the now-unread `Claims.jti` field; the token id is read from the declared claim.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to introspection, typed (`at+jwt`) tokens with default claim names, the resolver, or refresh. Okta and Entra are NOT added to "Tested providers": they still need real-tenant verification (an acceptance gate in #12496).
- **Blast radius:** JWKS bearer verification for every surface (RPC/WSS, gateway, dashboard). With defaults the accepted set is unchanged; the new behavior is reachable only by setting `require_at_jwt = false` or the new claim keys.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12497, Depends on #12608. Related #8289, Related #12496

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw checks that a sign-in token is really an *access* token meant for it, and not an *ID token* (which only proves someone logged in to some app). It did this by requiring a "this is an access token" label that Okta and Microsoft Entra ID don't put on their tokens, so neither could sign in. This adds a second, equally strict way to tell them apart, based on who the token is addressed to: it accepts only tokens addressed to ZeroClaw's API identifier alone, and that identifier must not be used by any app for sign-in. It also lets the operator say which field a provider uses for the app's name and the token's ID, rather than ZeroClaw guessing per vendor. Because a person and a background job can share one Entra app, ZeroClaw decides which one it's talking to from a signed field in the token itself, never from the app's name. Existing setups behave exactly as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Verification is covered with signed tokens against a mock JWKS issuer; real Okta/Entra tenants are a tracked gate in #12496.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Rust lint/test jobs cover `zeroclaw-config` and `zeroclaw-runtime` (verifier) and `zeroclaw-gateway` (consumer). Docs style covers `identity-providers.md`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No real Okta or Entra tenant in CI.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (CI-pinned toolchain `1.98.0`, on `b3c911620b`)

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(no output, exit 0)

$ cargo +1.98.0 clippy -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 19s

$ cargo +1.98.0 check --workspace --all-targets
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 1m 17s

$ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-config
test result: ok. 2000 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
(integration targets: 106, 9, 8, 5, 1, 1 passed)

$ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib security::
test result: ok. 413 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; 0 measured; 5816 filtered out
(security::auth_provider alone: 147 passed)

$ cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib oidc
test result: ok. 49 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 867 filtered out

$ DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/security/identity-providers.md scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
Summary: 0 error(s)
$ DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/security/authentication.md scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
Summary: 0 error(s)
$ scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
🚫 Errors...........0
$ scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Tests were written first. Config tests failed to compile (missing fields); of the 9 new verifier tests, the 4 asserting newly accepted shapes failed on behavior before the implementation, while the 5 refusal tests already passed, confirming nothing previously refused was relied on. New verifier coverage: untyped refused while typing is required; `typ: JWT` and no-`typ` accepted once waived with a separate audience; other header types, an untyped ID token (`aud` = client), and `nonce` still refused when waived; the verifier refuses untyped tokens without separation even if config validation was skipped; Okta `cid` names the client and is refused when undeclared; declared claim contradicted by `client_id` refused; declared claim has no `azp` fallback; Entra service token (`typ: JWT`, `azp`, `uti`) resolves to a service principal only when `azp` is declared, and is refused with defaults; token id read from the declared claim only. New config coverage: defaults, separation against `client_id` (empty and equal), each client list, a same-issuer sibling entry (and not a different-issuer one), TOML round-trip with an Okta shape, claim-name format, JWKS-only. Review follow-up: the two new refusal tests (`events` on an untyped token; a blank or disagreeing `azp` under a declared client claim) failed at their refusal assertions before the fix while their positive controls passed. @IftekharUddin's commits add a person and an app-only token from the same Entra app carrying the same mapped role, resolved through the permission resolver: each gets only its own profile's grants. Missing, unknown, wrong-case, `null`, array and boolean `idtyp` values, and a service declaration contradicted by evidence, are refused. Not verified: real Okta/Entra tokens.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `b3c911620b`
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full `cargo test --workspace` skipped: changes are confined to `OidcConfig` and the OIDC provider; affected crates were tested and the workspace type-checked.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No (synthetic ids, `example.com`/`example.okta.com`)
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: This changes which bearer tokens authenticate. Risk: an ID token accepted as an access token. Mitigation: opt-in only (`require_at_jwt = false`); accepted only when `aud` is exactly an audience that is provably not any configured client of that issuer (the entry's own clients re-checked in the verifier from one shared definition; sibling entries for the same issuer checked at config load only); non-access header types, `nonce`, and payload purpose markers remain refused; tests mint an untyped ID token and assert refusal. Residual (documented, and recorded in #12496): the IdP must never sign anyone in *as* the API registration itself, which ZeroClaw cannot observe. On the vendor paths a client claim never proves the actor kind: a service needs an exact signed value in `actor_claim_values`. The Keycloak default (`azp` never proves a service) is unchanged.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes (defaults unchanged; `require_at_jwt = false` was previously a validation error for `jwks`)
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: `[oidc.<alias>] client_id_claim`, `token_id_claim`, `actor_claim_values`; `require_at_jwt = false` newly permitted for `jwks` under the audience-separation rule.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: None required. prs.title: fix(web): announce completed full-page sign-ins to other tabs
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch** `master`
- **What changed and why** A dashboard tab starting full-page sign-in records a random notice ID in its own session storage. The gateway appends that ID to the validated return location after a successful callback. The returning tab consumes its matching notice, cleans up the URL, and announces `signed-in` after it adopts the cookie session.
  - Retain a matching callback notice if the first session check fails transiently. Consume it only after successful adoption or when a subsequent session change supersedes it.
- **Scope boundary** This covers full-page sign-in and the full-page option after a blocked re-auth popup. A dashboard with unavailable tab storage falls back to its existing sign-in navigation.
- **Blast radius** Dashboard OIDC sign-in initiation, successful callback redirects that request a notice, and the recipient tabs' existing session check.
- **Linked issue(s)** Closes #12108. Related #11965 and #12106. [PR #12533](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12533) separately guards adoption when sign-out supersedes a probe.

### What this does, simply

If two tabs show the sign-in screen and you sign in through one, the other can enter the dashboard too. It checks its own session cookie before showing account data. An ordinary reload or a bookmark from an earlier sign-in stays quiet.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. A configured dashboard identity provider and two tabs exercise the real browser and provider together.
- **Interface(s) exercised** Web dashboard.
- **Setup / preconditions** Open the same dashboard in two tabs on its sign-in screen.
- **Steps to run** Complete a full-page sign-in in the first tab. Watch the second tab. Then reload the first tab and watch requests to `/api/auth/session` in the second tab.
- **Expected on this branch (after)** The second tab reads its session and enters the dashboard. Reloading the first tab produces no additional session read in the second tab. A tab still showing another account reloads before adopting the new account.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before)** The second tab stays on its sign-in screen until reloaded.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on** The Linux gateway suite can run the mock-IdP test `full_page_sign_in_returns_the_notice_to_the_dashboard`. It exercises a real auth start and callback, checks for the session cookie and checks the returned path, query, anchor and notice together.
- **Known CI coverage gap** External identity-provider deployments and browser privacy settings remain untested. The local WireMock fixture could not bind its loopback port. The actual `full_page_sign_in_returns_the_notice_to_the_dashboard` callback test passed on the signed PR head in the hosted Linux Test job. [Linux Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44250861455/job/134620918599)
- **Commands run and tail output**
  - `npm run test:auth` in `web/` on Node 24 passed 223 tests across 17 test files at the original head. After a review follow-up, 226 passed on `c84240dfe1`.
  - `npm run typecheck`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` passed.
  - `cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib dashboard_sign_in_appends_only_the_requested_uuid_to_the_safe_landing` reported `1 passed; 0 failed`.
  - The docs quality gate reported zero issues. The links gate passed six collector tests and found no added links.
- **Beyond CI** Disabling the sender's `post` made the full-page regression fail with an empty event list. Restoring it returned the suite to green. The hook tests cover an abandoned attempt, a lookalike fragment, an ordinary reload, an old bookmark, and preserving an existing query and anchor.
- **Visual interface evidence** The hook tests mount the dashboard sign-in screen, use its auth provider and observe the actual browser-compatible broadcast channel. The two-browser check above remains available for final interactive verification.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path** The initial callback test ran on signed feature head `88350adf86`. Updated head `c84240dfe1` passed all 226 web auth tests and TypeScript; it retains the same gateway change. See `web/src/hooks/useAuth.test.ts` and `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src/dashboard_session.rs`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence** The newly emitted message was exactly `{ type: "signed-in" }` once. The cleaned return URL was `/agent/main?sort=new#turn`. After reload, the event list still contained one message.
- **Action or changed state and observed result** The returning tab became authenticated and emitted the notice. The existing receiving-hook checks cover adopting the same account and reloading for another account.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why** The local verification focused on dashboard auth, gateway landing behavior, type checking and documentation. CI covers the wider workspace.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No. Other dashboard tabs use their existing same-origin session probe.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. The notice is a random correlation value. Possessing it grants no access. Broadcasts contain the event type alone, and each recipient verifies its own cookie.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. Existing login URLs and direct clients can omit the optional `notice` parameter. The callback still uses an HTTP 303. The validated return-path size and same-dashboard checks apply before the gateway attaches a parsed UUID.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps for existing users? None.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path** Revert the merged commit on a review branch. Dashboard tabs will pick up full-page sign-ins when they refresh.
- **Feature flags or config toggles** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms** A signed-out tab remains on its sign-in screen after another tab signs in, or a routine reload wakes other tabs.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A. This implements the follow-up to #11965.

prs.title: feat(providers): support Qwen MP4 video-file input
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Send explicitly supplied Qwen MP4 video files as `video_url` parts containing `data:video/mp4;base64,...`, across streaming, non-streaming, history, and native-tool Chat Completions requests.
  - Scope local file reads to the current Agent turn's filesystem policy, with no-follow directory/file opens, regular-file checks, and a request-wide raw-video budget below 7,000,000 bytes.
  - Preserve mixed image/video requests and separate system text. Unavailable, unsupported and over-budget user videos retain their literal markers; history cannot stop later chat. Successful loads consume the shared budget newest message first. Tool-result bodies and system/assistant video examples remain literal.
  - Add factory-to-HTTP, Agent-turn, filesystem-boundary, and opt-in live Qwen tests.
- **Scope boundary:** Chat Completions MP4 files and inline MP4 Data URLs. MCP attachment promotion is tracked in the dependent draft #12579. Responses, remote video fetching, frame extraction, audio-track interpretation, and codec validation are outside this change.
- **Blast radius:** Qwen/Qwen Code compatible-provider request shaping, the shared compatible message-part enum, current-turn filesystem-policy propagation, and provider documentation. Other providers retain their request behavior.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12671 for the separately reviewed, Core Team-approved runtime exception record required before this feature merges. Related #11383 for the earlier video-input discussion and tool-body marker trust-boundary concerns. This is Qwen-specific and carries no code from that MiniMax PR.

### What this does, simply

A Qwen user can supply `[VIDEO:/absolute/path/clip.mp4]` or an inline MP4 Data URL and have the actual file reach the model. Previously the video reference reached Qwen as text. Files are read only when the current Agent policy permits them; low-level provider callers without a policy scope can use inline bytes but cannot open local paths. The service samples the video using its default settings.

The supported model families and dated snapshots are enumerated in `qwen_video::supports_model`. Only Qwen3.8-Flash was exercised against a real service; the other documented IDs have transport validation coverage.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; deterministic factory/HTTP and Agent-turn tests cover the changed boundary. The ignored provider live test documents optional paid reproduction; no paid run was made for this revision.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Quality Gate on `28a00b928`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/45314198597) completed successfully, including CI Required Gate, Security, Lint, Test, parallel runtime tests, platform checks and the declared MSRV. It covers the current code and docs; the local HTTP/policy and negative-control tests below supply focused behavior evidence. The branch merges upstream `74c8af5cf`, including #12694. Passing CI does not replace Core Team review or the #12671 merge dependency.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Local platform is macOS/aarch64 with rustc 1.97.1. The linked CI supplies its cross-platform and MSRV checks. Live inference is explicit opt-in and was not rerun for this revision.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers -- --test-threads=1
lib: 2030 passed; 0 failed; 4 ignored
integration: 1 passed; 60 passed; 3 ignored

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib qwen
16 passed; 0 failed

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib agent_turn_applies_its_filesystem_policy_to_qwen_video --config 'profile.test.package.zeroclaw-runtime.opt-level=2'
1 passed; 0 failed; macOS ld compact-unwind size warning remains

cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
Finished dev profile; no warnings

cargo fmt --all -- --check
git diff --check
BASE_SHA=github/master DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/providers/catalog.md scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
BASE_SHA=github/master DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/providers/catalog.md scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
0 Markdown errors; 8 link-check tests passed
```

The initial parallel provider run had two OpenAI failures: a runtime proxy-config test received an extra request, and a streaming fixture decoded that proxy's JSON instead of a Chat response. The complete serial run above passes without filtering. The Agent policy test passed at opt-level=1 and opt-level=2, but both emitted macOS ld's compact-unwind table size warning. It is recorded as a platform limitation, not a zero-warning run; Clippy remains warning-free. Diagnostics are not disabled. An initial docs-lint attempt lacked npm network/cache access; the successful rerun uses the existing temporary npm cache. Optional HTTP link checking is unavailable because lychee is not installed.

The directory-replacement negative control changes only `open_dir_nofollow(name)` to `open_dir(name)`: `video_open_rejects_intermediate_directory_replacement` must fail with the relative `private` symlink. The original source is restored in `finally`; the same test and all Qwen tests then pass. The normal and private targets contain different bytes.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Factory-to-actual-HTTP regression exercises all eight Chat entry points with MP4, oversized MP4, WebM, missing files, unsupported `qwen-plus`/`qwen3-coder-plus`, Discord CDN URL, invalid Base64, absent read scope, policy denial and mixed valid/invalid references. Every unavailable-video case sends a subsequent ordinary chat retaining the history. Deleted history falls back; two 4 MB clips in different turns send the newer clip and retain the older marker as text. Valid inline MP4 makes tool-body non-promotion tests sensitive to a removed carrier guard.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no presentation or rendered interface changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `28a00b928`. Automated assertions live in `compatible_qwen_video_tests.rs`, `qwen_video.rs::tests`, and `agent/qwen_video_tests.rs`. No runtime/config/channel public types change in this follow-up.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** HTTP assertions check the dispatched request, decoded video bytes, mixed image/video, preserved literal markers, unchanged assistant role coalescing, and streamed/non-streamed parity.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Valid video is delivered; failed promotion preserves original user text and continues dispatch. Preparation explicitly carries text and loaded video parts to serialization, so fallback text is not rescanned. Existing task-local policy, resolved-path validation, per-component no-follow, nonblocking regular-file checks and bounded reads are retained.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Paid Qwen validation remains opt-in. Historical smoke on `016e14f67` used Qwen3.8-Flash and a public OpenCV sample (3559 input/151 output tokens, 4.21s); it is not evidence for the new fallback behavior. No full workspace or local Linux/Windows/MSRV claim.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes:** an additive video-input capability can read and transmit user-selected MP4 files. It uses the current turn's existing read policy and does not enlarge allowed roots.
- New external network calls? **Yes:** the existing authenticated Qwen Chat request can now carry video bytes. No separate fetch/upload endpoint is added.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No:** runtime authentication is unchanged. The ignored live test reads explicitly supplied test-only environment variables.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No:** committed fixtures are synthetic; live media is external and uncommitted.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes:** explicit genuine-user video references become model-visible media; tool bodies, system, and assistant text are excluded from promotion.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: File disclosure is constrained by lexical and resolved read-policy checks, per-component no-follow opens, nonblocking regular-file checks, and bounded reads. Only successfully validated video bytes become media; failed references remain literal text and do not abort dispatch. Container-header checks do not guarantee valid codecs; the service owns decoding.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes:** additive Qwen video-file support; existing image and text requests retain their behavior.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes:** additive handling of the existing VIDEO marker syntax for supported Qwen models and `ZEROCLAW_TEST_QWEN_*` opt-in test variables. No runtime configuration field or CLI flag is added.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: Existing deployments need no migration. To opt in, use a supported Qwen model and an allowed MP4 reference. Direct provider consumers reading paths must use `with_video_read_policy`; the Agent turn supplies this automatically. The live test documents its explicit credential, endpoint, model, and fixture variables.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this PR's eventual merge commit. The follow-up fix is `28a00b928`; the branch also includes the original feature commit and an upstream merge. Revert the dependent MCP PR first if both have landed.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added; image/text requests remain available.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Service rejection of video content, missing expected video parts, or a response indicating that the file is unavailable. The factory HTTP regression exposes missing/malformed video parts.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

N/A. Related #11383 is contextual reference; this PR does not supersede it or incorporate its code.

The full provider run preceded one additional missing-sibling assertion; the focused three-test rerun covers that final edit. An initial tools filter `embedded_video_tests` matched zero tests; the corrected module filter above ran all three. Docs lint uses the existing temporary npm cache after a network-limited initial attempt; lychee is unavailable for optional HTTP link checks.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The integration uses real local MCP HTTP, the production wrapper and `Agent::turn`, then captures actual Qwen-shaped HTTP for native and XML modes. The first continuation contains byte-identical MP4; a new user turn contains no replayed tool video. Provider tests mix a valid MP4, a missing MP4 and an image; only the bad attachment degrades. Tool body examples remain literal and external provenance survives.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no rendered interface changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `63f79e8c5`, including parent fix `28a00b928`. Evidence: `compatible_mcp_video_tests.rs`, `embedded_video_tests.rs`, `tests/mcp_video.rs`, and retained `tests/live/`/`tests/support/` layout.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** The native/XML HTTP assertions require one video only in the tool continuation, string-only native tool messages, preserved XML `[Tool results]` attribution and no tool-video replay in the next user turn. Ordinary `--test live` reports the paid smoke ignored.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** User and declared tool video share the parent's newest-first raw-video budget; preparation failures are per attachment. Native serialization consumes prepared content instead of reconstructing raw video declarations. Resource URIs are provenance and are never fetched.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No paid Qwen call was made for this revision. Historical live smoke on `f1b5ac448` succeeded with Qwen3.8-Flash (7.58s), but is not evidence for this head. No full workspace/platform/MSRV claim; optional HTTP link checking needs lychee. After #12578 merges, merge latest master, confirm the diff is MCP-only and repeat focused checks before leaving Draft.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes:** declared MP4 resources gain model-video delivery. Workspace writes use the existing materializer; provider reads use the parent's current-turn policy and bounded no-follow loader. Allowed filesystem roots are unchanged.

- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: An untrusted MCP server can supply video evidence, but cannot promote a VIDEO example in its body or trigger a fetch of its resource URI. Existing 10 MiB per-file/aggregate and 64-item limits remain in force, plus the parent's smaller Qwen dispatch budget. Only current-turn declared videos are delivered; stale/invalid/unsupported attachments degrade without replacing sibling text.

## Compatibility (required)

The MCP Agent capture test exposes missing bytes, lost provenance, and stale-video replay. Saved files remain under the existing workspace upload lifecycle.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; merge only after the dependencies below.
- **What changed and why:** Add the registry editor with compare-and-swap draft/save state; use exact model keys in pickers, entity links, Quickstart and Doctor; update Web tests and retain explicitly labeled reference evidence.
- **Scope boundary:** Primarily consumes the parent V5 registry and RPC contracts for the Web UI. The increment also carries the small migration, Ollama normalization and cost-attribution safeguards already reviewed; no new backend changes are added by this evidence update.
- **Blast radius:** Web configuration editing, navigation, onboarding, model selection and responsive editor states.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related to #9809. Stack part 11; reference implementation `d0dd630146`. Depends on #12452.

### What this does, simply

The dashboard consumes the parent registry editor and updates onboarding, model pickers, entity links, Doctor/health routes and cost-rate navigation to use exact model keys. The layer also removes the retired per-alias model combobox and keeps the model-catalog fields driven by the canonical registry.

## Testing (required)


### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes` — the interactive workflow below supplements automated CI.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `web`; the actual current-head application and matching daemon were exercised in Chromium at desktop and mobile widths for every workflow linked below.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Check out this head with its parent commits; use the repository toolchain and existing test fixtures.
- **Steps to run:** Run the Web unit suite and `cargo web check` in CI. Start the dashboard, create a connection/model, edit and save the registry, select a dotted model key and complete Quickstart at desktop and mobile widths.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Registry edits preserve masked baselines and drafts, stale edits are rejected, and model selection/linking preserves the exact configured key.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The Web UI edits provider-family tables and derives model selections from legacy profile layout.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** At final head `cf6a0473f3`, [Quality Gate 44944829693](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44944829693) passed the full workspace, runtime, platform and Web matrix. Web Permission Tests passed with the Quickstart exact-key, clear/reselect and required-field tests included in the CI-run `test:permissions` script.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Live provider inference was not exercised. The real Web/daemon interaction gap is now covered by the current-head desktop/mobile evidence below; workspace, platform and automated Web behavior remain covered by the passing current-head Quality Gate.
- **Commands run and tail output:** `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 RUSTC_WRAPPER= cargo build --offline --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw` (exit 0); locked `npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund` (exit 0); actual Chromium workflow driver completed at both widths with no page exceptions. Existing master warnings are documented in the evidence record. Full tests/lint use the current-head passing GitHub Quality Gate.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Using matching current-head Web/daemon and an isolated, normally paired synthetic configuration: opened the exact dotted model link, confirmed credential masking, held and released a real save PUT, verified persisted values, caused a real second-client conflict while retaining the first draft, completed Quickstart with an existing dotted model, and switched both created agents to another dotted model key. Checked stored agent references and encrypted credentials independently.
- **Visual interface evidence:** 18 direct Chromium screenshots of the actual current-head application, English, desktop 1440×1000 and mobile 390×844. No reconstructed interface or mocked server response.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `cf6a0473f368268f1661fbe30576ee73a4b9293e`, matching Web source and daemon. [Immutable desktop/mobile evidence and reproduction record](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/df640ebba7e4865d029b425ec96d3c2137305723/pr12453/README.md); includes binary hash, screenshot hashes, capture script and actual API observations.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Workflow-by-workflow screenshot table](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/df640ebba7e4865d029b425ec96d3c2137305723/pr12453/README.md#evidence-by-requested-workflow): editor, masked connection, pending save, persisted result, concurrent conflict, Quickstart selection/completion and agent picker/switch at both widths.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Both real saves returned 200 and persisted the selected model values. Both stale saves returned the existing `400 / validation_failed` conflict without replacing the saved value or losing the draft. Both Quickstart calls returned `kind: applied`; both agents then switched to `chat.backup.prod` through the real config write and socket reconnect. No inference request was sent.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local full test/clippy reruns use the already passing current-head GitHub CI. Local compilation and browser execution were performed specifically for the requested actual-interface evidence.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No additional permissions.
- New external network calls? No additional provider endpoints; existing backend RPC remains the transport.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes; the editor handles masked secret baselines and submitted replacements.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No additional model-visible input path.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Registry edits use backend validation and compare-and-swap baselines. Masked fields and stale drafts must not overwrite live credentials. Screenshot fixtures use synthetic data; interactive verification remains pending.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Requires the parent V5 backend and its registry-edit RPC contract.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes; dashboard onboarding, registry editing and model navigation use the new shape.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: Merge dependencies first, migrate existing configuration to V5, and deploy the dashboard with the matching backend. Old profile editing is not retained in the new UI.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert the dashboard layer before backend downgrades. For a complete V4 downgrade, restore its matching configuration backup.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added for staging the stack.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** CI compile errors, configuration load failures, or changed provider behavior in the layer-specific regression tests.

Stack integration: this repository grants this author read-only access. These fork PRs therefore target `master` and have cumulative diffs. Review the incremental layer against its declared parent; merge parents first and refresh each child before merging. Original #9809 is closed; this stacked PR remains the Web layer.

Incremental review: [declared parent to this layer](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/compare/694f90f412e81549822aac1ec5904e64dc436d81...cf6a0473f3).





### Latest head validation (2026-11-20)

- Current head: `cf6a0473f3`; declared parent: `694f90f412`. The final head includes the latest fork master (`9cd75ac349`) through the validated parent stack.
- Rebuilt from the corrected Zerocode parent. The increment contains Web registry editing, exact model selection, Quickstart coverage and related UI tests, together with the small migration, Ollama and cost-attribution safeguards already present in the reviewed head.
- Changed-file formatting was checked. Locked Web dependencies are now installed for the actual-interface capture; the passing current-head GitHub Web CI remains the automated test source.
- Current-head desktop/mobile screenshots and real workflow outcomes are public above. Formal reviewer approval and parent-first integration remain maintainer decisions.
- Baseline dependency-security findings remain outside this PR scope.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; merge the declared dependencies first.
- **What changed and why:** Zerocode edits the canonical connection/model registry and consumes exact model references in configuration, Quickstart and chat. Masked editor baselines preserve credentials; text navigation, save help and the independent Fluent catalogs match the JSON workflow. Chat switch feedback and the title use the same resolved registry model ID.
- **Scope boundary:** The parent supplies the V5 registry and backend protocol. This layer covers the TUI and follow-up integration fixes, including the Web cost-rate navigation correction; the broader Web registry UI is a separate child.
- **Blast radius:** TUI onboarding, configuration save/reload, model selection, validation feedback and cost-rate navigation.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related to #9809. Depends on #12450. Current head: `694f90f412e81549822aac1ec5904e64dc436d81`.

### What this does, simply

The terminal setup screens now edit the same reusable connections and named models that the backend resolves. A name such as `chat.demo.gateway` stays one complete model reference. Users can save the registry, pick that model in Quickstart and switch to it in chat. The editor shows its revision and distinguishes Enter (new line) from Ctrl+S (save). The current-head screenshots below exercise all three workflows with the matching daemon.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes; the interactive workflow supplements automated CI.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui`, English locale, actual xterm at 160 columns × 50 rows, matching local daemon.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Build this head and its dependencies. Use an isolated V5 configuration with connection `openai.demo.gateway`, model `chat.demo.gateway`, a synthetic credential and an enabled agent referencing that exact model and a supervised risk profile. The local evidence fixture is under `target/quickstart-evidence/5685d0c6/config`.
- **Steps to run:** Build with `RUSTC_WRAPPER= CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target cargo build --offline --locked -p zeroclaw -p zerocode --bins`. Launch the matching daemon and `target/debug/zerocode --config-dir <isolated-config-dir>`. Open Config → Provider registry → providers.registry; change the model ID, Ctrl+S, and Enter to reopen. Then open Quickstart → Model and select the configured model. In Chat, enter `/model-provider` and select the same key.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The registry preserves complete dotted keys and masked credentials, the reopened editor shows the saved model ID, revision and correct footer, and both selectors use the exact model key. Chat feedback and the title show the resolved upstream model ID.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The terminal UI edits provider-family/profile tables and derives selections from profile references; it does not expose this V5 registry edit and exact-model selection workflow.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Current-head Quality Gate [44939059604](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44939059604) passed at `694f90f412`, including Security, lint, workspace tests, CLI-only tests, parallel runtime tests and platform checks. This includes the chat feedback regression. The risk report and Greptile passed, with no unresolved review threads. Independent Docker source-image builds are still running; no failure is observed in those tasks at this update.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI does not replace interaction evidence. The manual run covers the actual rendered editor, save/reopen transition and both model selectors. No local full test matrix was repeated.
- **Commands run and tail output:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: exit 0. `git diff --check`: exit 0. Both docs gates passed for the two updated English pages (0 Markdown errors; six link-script tests and the local target check). Matching `zeroclaw` and `zerocode` binaries built successfully in the worktree `target`; final incremental build: `Finished dev profile ... in 34.07s`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Changed `models["chat.demo.gateway"].model` from `gpt-synthetic-before` to `gpt-synthetic-after` through the TUI, saved with Ctrl+S and reopened. Parsed the saved TOML independently: the complete model key holds the new ID and the stored credential is not the mask. The reopened editor still masks it. Quickstart selects the same literal key. Chat `/model-provider` selects it and both title and success feedback show `gpt-synthetic-after`. No provider inference request was made.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Direct screenshots of actual xterm on an isolated Xvfb display, captured with ImageMagick; the interface was not reconstructed. Text captures come from the same 160×50 tmux pane, with its status line disabled.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `694f90f412e81549822aac1ec5904e64dc436d81`, `tui`, English, 160×50, November 21, 2026. [Immutable evidence and reproduction record](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/16c35a21d9a795e5ce587f1c63258794ecd0ae17/README.md). The visual evidence was captured on the pre-restack equivalent UI revision `5685d0c670`; the final head changes only the declared parent integration and the JSON conflict fix. The evidence is on a standalone fork branch and is excluded from the implementation diff.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Registry save/reopen](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/16c35a21d9a795e5ce587f1c63258794ecd0ae17/registry-reopened.png), [Quickstart picker](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/16c35a21d9a795e5ce587f1c63258794ecd0ae17/quickstart-picker.png), [Quickstart selected](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/16c35a21d9a795e5ce587f1c63258794ecd0ae17/quickstart-selected.png), [Chat picker](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/16c35a21d9a795e5ce587f1c63258794ecd0ae17/chat-picker.png), [Chat selected](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/16c35a21d9a795e5ce587f1c63258794ecd0ae17/chat-selected.png). Raw terminal captures and binary hashes are linked in the evidence record.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Save → reopen shows the changed model ID, full dotted keys, masked credential, `revision`, and `Enter=new line  Ctrl+s=save  Esc=cancel  No pending edits`. Quickstart marks the model selected. Chat reports `model_provider switched to chat.demo.gateway (model: gpt-synthetic-after).`
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local full test/clippy runs are delegated to GitHub CI. Local compilation was performed specifically to satisfy the requested actual-interface evidence. Routine English documentation corrections omit generated translation-cache churn per the localization policy.

![Current-head registry after save and reopen](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/16c35a21d9a795e5ce587f1c63258794ecd0ae17/registry-reopened.png)

![Current-head Quickstart model picker](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/16c35a21d9a795e5ce587f1c63258794ecd0ae17/quickstart-picker.png)

![Current-head chat model switch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/16c35a21d9a795e5ce587f1c63258794ecd0ae17/chat-selected.png)

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No additional provider endpoints; existing backend RPC remains the transport.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes; registry editors preserve unchanged masked fields through the backend baseline contract.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No additional model-visible input path.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: A mask must not replace a stored credential. Saves carry the expected baseline through validated backend persistence and normal encryption. Evidence uses synthetic data; configuration, encryption keys, tokens and daemon state are excluded from the evidence branch.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No; this client requires the parent V5 registry-edit RPC contract.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes; onboarding and editors use reusable connections and exact model keys.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: Merge dependencies first, migrate configuration from the frozen V4 format to V5, and rebuild Zerocode with the matching daemon. Old profile editing is replaced by registry editing.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert this client layer together with dependent UI layers; retain the matching V5 server/configuration, or restore the V4 backup for a full downgrade.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added for staging this client layer.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Registry save errors, missing model picker entries, incorrect selected model identity or configuration load failures.

Stack integration: these fork PRs target `master` and have cumulative diffs. Review the incremental layer against its declared parent, merge parents first, and refresh each child before merging. Original #9809 is closed.

Incremental review: [declared parent to this layer](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/compare/800a86be67269d46c7a8a46da3f2b033ad61132b...694f90f412).

### Latest integration review (2026-11-21)

- Current head includes the fully validated #12450 parent at `800a86be67`, including upstream fixes #12610 (Wasmtime advisory) and #12600 (removed-file risk report). No independent security upgrade was added here.
- Post-merge fixtures use the stack's existing memory constructor, typed temperature and text-tool parsing APIs.
- Greptile's stale agent-guide and gateway-error examples now describe exact model keys and the migration boundary. Its earlier busy-session refresh, regional endpoint and cost-rate navigation findings remain addressed.
- Manual self-review found and fixed empty model IDs in canonical chat switch feedback. A regression test drives the actual configure/registry RPC boundary and checks both title identity and feedback against one resolved model.
- The current-head 160×50 evidence above replaces the earlier 80×24 transcript for the requested terminal evidence.

- Current-head CI Required Gate is green. During the final check master gained one further commit, `10b8af3b04` (#10960, Anthropic cache TTL `off`); this branch is now one commit behind that newer master and remains mergeable. That new provider option has not been merged into this captured/tested head.

prs.title: feat(providers): adopt the canonical V5 registry and runtime model bindings
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; merge only after the dependencies below.
- **What changed and why:** Activate canonical registry admission and backend consumers, promote V4 configuration to V5, materialize complete models for routing/fallback/switching, and wire secret-safe registry editing. Registry types, native protocols, chat transport and reflection are prepared in #12454, #12455, #12456 and #12457.
- **Scope boundary:** V5 admission, persistence/editor wiring, canonical model construction and backend consumer/lifecycle cutover. Activation and affected consumers remain together so no intermediate revision clears profiles that active consumers still read. This layer also includes the minimum Zerocode cost navigation and Web registry/cost-editor integration needed at activation; the broader client follow-ups remain separate.
- **Blast radius:** Config persistence and secret handling; provider construction; agent/session lifecycle; memory, speech and decision consumers; channel/gateway/RPC dispatch.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related to #9809. Stack part 9; reference implementation `320aa43a62`. Depends on #12457.

### What this does, simply

The preceding layers prepare independent registry types, native capability protocols, chat transport and generic reflection. This layer activates those components: V4 input is promoted at the V5 admission boundary, backend consumers resolve exact model references, and routing, fallback and switching build complete target bindings. Configuration activation and dependent consumers stay together to avoid a partially switched runtime. This remaining cutover is still large; the preparatory layers make their own architectural boundaries independently reviewable.

## Testing (required)


### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes` — the migration or interactive workflow below supplements passing current-head CI.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli`; current-head Quickstart was exercised interactively in the actual terminal for both fresh creation and existing-model reuse. The linked captures show both completed flows.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Check out this head with its parent commits; use the repository toolchain and existing test fixtures.
- **Steps to run:** Run workspace Quality Gate, migration and registry edit tests, provider protocol tests, runtime route/switch/fallback/refresh tests and feature-matrix checks; exercise `zeroclaw config migrate` with a V4 backup.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** V4 configuration becomes V5 connections/models; internal consumers resolve exact model keys; switching/fallback materializes all target configuration and a failed update preserves the previous binding.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Master stores provider-owned profiles and consumer-specific capability settings, and has no canonical decoupled registry.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Earlier green runs are historical only. Current-head workspace Quality Gate [44936965439](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44936965439) passed after the latest master merge and API-fixture fixes; the PR-risk reporter also passed on this head.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Current-head CLI interaction evidence is now public below. No live provider inference was exercised; the current-head GitHub Quality Gate supplies workspace/platform test coverage.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Current-head evidence build: `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 RUSTC_WRAPPER= cargo build --offline --locked -p zeroclaw --bin zeroclaw` (exit 0), followed by two completed PTY Quickstart flows and independent TOML assertions. At the current head, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check` pass locally; Quality Gate 44936965439 passed the full workspace matrix. Expanded config unit suite passed 2,085 tests, including the final fallback and timeout regressions. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `git diff --check` and the changed-line docs quality gate passed. Existing Rust-toolchain deprecation/unused-dependency warnings were not changed.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Completed current-head fresh and existing-model Quickstart flows as documented in the public evidence below, including encrypted persistence and model/connection reuse. Addressed previous-head split dependency errors (retained embedding factory, complete timeout helpers, deferred dispatch-dependent sampling, and secret-test trait import). The registry and provider libraries compile on the cleaned head. Compared the integrated provider and UI trees byte-for-byte with the saved pre-split snapshot. Preserved the frozen V4 fixture. Corrected previous-head CI failures caused by unnecessary TOML rewriting; the existing comment-preservation and atomic-save assertions remain intact. Inspected ownership, imports and the incremental diff against the declared parent. Runtime/network behavior remains delegated to CI.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Actual xterm screenshots and direct 160×50 PTY output for both fresh connection/model creation and existing-model reuse. Both flows completed and created agents.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `800a86be67269d46c7a8a46da3f2b033ad61132b`; CLI, English, 160×50. [Immutable public evidence and reproduction record](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/30e3173ad20362b925773c6863ecc66a9b56eb2b/pr12450/README.md). The original reviewed `6fe2985212` record is separately labeled and linked there.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** [Screenshots, terminal captures, binary hash and TOML assertions](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/blob/30e3173ad20362b925773c6863ecc66a9b56eb2b/pr12450/README.md). No local-only path is required to inspect the evidence.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Fresh Quickstart created `evidence_fresh` with canonical connection/model `openai.default`; the second run selected that literal key and created `evidence_existing`. Parsing saved TOML confirmed both references, one shared connection/model, and encrypted credential persistence. No inference request was made.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Local full test/clippy reruns remain delegated to the passing current-head GitHub CI. Local compilation was performed specifically for the requested actual-interface evidence.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes; existing capability selection is represented in the new registry. Existing admission boundaries remain in force.
- New external network calls? Yes; native capability adapters use the selected connection and protocol. No additional allowlist bypass is introduced.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes; connection credentials and sensitive headers use the existing encrypted persistence and masked edit contracts.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes; shared extraction policy is selected per materialized model.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Migration, registry editing and provider selection cross configuration trust boundaries. Preserve ciphertext, use masked compare-and-swap edits, validate references before installation, and keep the previous binding when construction fails. Provider output remains subject to runtime tool admission.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Older files are converted at the migration boundary; the new internal API and persisted V5 shape replace profile-owned construction.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes; connections, models, presets, fallback references and configuration editing use the V5 shape.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: Back up the existing configuration and run `zeroclaw config migrate`. Inspect the resulting connections/models and exact model references. V1-V3 first migrate through the frozen V4 step, then V4-to-V5. Install the dependent clients before the complete interactive rollout; restore the V4 backup for a V4 downgrade.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert merged children before this layer. Restore the pre-upgrade V4 backup when returning to a V4 binary; retain memory identity checks and never downgrade by editing only the version number.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None added for staging the stack.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** CI compile errors, configuration load failures, or changed provider behavior in the layer-specific regression tests.

Stack integration: this fork PR targets `master` and is reviewed as the activation layer after #12457. The lower layers have been rebuilt to keep one concern per PR; merge parents first and refresh children. Original #9809 is closed and replaced by this stack.

Incremental review: [#12457 head to this layer](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/compare/5009081e53ae1876f4e05a017a56a49db1f20ca5...800a86be67269d46c7a8a46da3f2b033ad61132b).



### Review fixes (2026-11-17)

- Preserve V4 primary selection and non-strict text tools; strict policy follows named models, routes and fallback targets, with conflicting agent policies refused. Materialize fallback connections even when a canonical model shadows legacy input.
- Preserve non-streaming versus streaming timeout semantics with `api.stream_request_timeout_secs`; keep Grok subprocess deadlines bounded.
- Reject registry saves when disk edits diverge, compare stored references without resolving external secrets, and avoid blocking chat sessions for speech-only edits.
- Compare legacy embedding identity against the actual endpoint digest, and normalize image recovery using the served fallback model policy.
- Follow-up native Azure/Bedrock/Gemini timeout wiring is in #12455 and propagated to descendants. Follow-up `96a2d022fd` regenerates only the V5 fixture and fixes the recovery test setup and Clippy condition; `3e7455f7f0` fixes strict Clippy fixture initialization. The existing registry RPC adapter placement was accepted in the subsequent review; current-head Quickstart evidence is public above. Formal approval remains with the reviewers.





### Latest head validation (2026-11-20)

- Current head: `800a86be67269d46c7a8a46da3f2b033ad61132b`; declared parent: `5009081e53ae1876f4e05a017a56a49db1f20ca5`.
- The branch is restacked on the clean reflection parent; lower layers contain only their declared protocol/reflection slices, while this layer contains the V5 activation and dependent consumers.
- Registry model defaults preserve unset reasoning extraction (`None`) outside the documented MiniMax/Groq defaults, so think-only responses are normalized and explicit `false` remains an opt-out.
- Registry edits reject deleting the configured vision model, in addition to the existing embedding reference guard.
- `cargo check --offline -p zeroclaw-config --lib` and `cargo check --offline -p zeroclaw-providers --lib` passed with `RUSTC_WRAPPER=`.
- GitHub CI is the source of truth for the full workspace and feature matrix; baseline dependency-security findings remain outside this PR's scope. The runtime RPC is the control-plane transport entry; registry mutation authority remains the shared zeroclaw-config editor consumed by runtime and gateway.


This backend cutover layer supersedes #9809; the original PR remains the historical reference only.

prs.title: refactor(providers): separate chat connection and timeout construction
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (stacked layer; merge after its declared parent).
- **What changed and why:** Separate chat connection construction from request and stream timeout policy across compatible, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic and OpenRouter providers, while keeping the legacy stream lifetime contract explicit.
- **What changed and why:** Reuse native chat clients through the live proxy authority, with request/read timeouts, headers and redirect policy included in the cache identity. Propagate Responses streaming client construction failures instead of silently dropping proxy policy.
- **What changed and why:** Restore Anthropic streaming header/error-body phase deadlines without bounding successful SSE bodies, and make compatible client setup fallible through the same live-proxy cache (including custom headers and CA bytes).
- **What changed and why:** Restore provider-layer think-only handling that must remain in place until the later runtime extraction policy is activated; preserve Ollama/Hailo answer fallback and Azure semantic-empty checks.
- **Scope boundary:** Provider chat factories, connection/timeout construction, and provider response normalization only. V5 registry admission and runtime model selection remain in later layers.
- **Blast radius:** Existing provider factory callers and chat streaming behavior; no new CLI, web, or root configuration surface.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12455. Related to #12450. This stacked series Supersedes #9809 (closed).

### What this does, simply

The old provider timeout setting has two established meanings: it limits ordinary HTTP requests and raises the read-idle floor for streams. It must not terminate a stream that is actively receiving bytes. This layer keeps that behavior in the legacy factory path and leaves a separate hook for the later canonical `stream_request_timeout_secs` cutover to supply a total stream deadline. It also keeps the adapter behavior needed before runtime extraction is enabled: Ollama can recover an answer from its `thinking` field, Hailo removes reasoning envelopes, and Azure rejects a think-only terminal completion.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; provider unit and loopback tests exercise the changed boundaries.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Fresh exact-head GitHub checks are requested for `76e4cace8e`; they cover the provider workspace, feature matrix, platform builds, stream regressions and lint. No pending check is claimed as passed.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No paid/live-provider request is claimed. The report-only risk workflow has an existing captured-head evidence-binding failure and does not mutate repository state.
- **Commands run and tail output:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — exit 0; `git diff --check` — exit 0. Full provider execution is delegated to GitHub CI.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Restacked onto final #12455 head `37099bbde7`; the incremental diff is provider chat construction and response policy only. A real HTTP regression checks TCP connection reuse, separate timeout pools, and invalidation on proxy-policy publication. Explicit legacy timeouts no longer create total stream deadlines; timeout tests continue past an active delay. Ollama uses the `thinking` fallback for think-only content, Hailo strips reasoning envelopes, and Azure treats think-only strings as semantic-empty. Configuration error hints remain on the legacy `[providers.models.<family>.<alias>]` grammar until #12450 activates the V5 registry consumer.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no interactive interface changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `76e4cace8e`; exact-head checks at [#12456 checks](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12456/checks).
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Static and formatter checks passed; the exact-head CI will provide the provider loopback and feature-matrix results.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full local provider compilation is delegated to GitHub CI to avoid duplicating the repository matrix.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No new endpoint family; existing provider requests now use the shared construction policy.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No new secret source. Existing credentials continue through the selected provider client; redirect policy and client setup errors remain explicit.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Legacy factory and active-stream lifetime semantics are preserved. Client setup failures now propagate instead of silently creating a direct client without the configured proxy/timeouts. Malformed optional compatible PEM retains its existing system-roots behavior.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No active root-format change. The later V5 consumer layer owns new canonical model API fields.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert dependent consumer layers first, then revert this provider chat-construction layer.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Active streams terminate at a legacy request deadline, think-only replies become semantic-empty incorrectly, or provider factory diagnostics point at the wrong configuration grammar.

Stack integration: final #12455 parent `37099bbde7991fda278d3580e446fef9464ed6c1` is an ancestor of this head. Review the [incremental diff](https://github.com/NiuBlibing/zeroclaw/compare/37099bbde7991fda278d3580e446fef9464ed6c1...a3dbb1f289). Original #9809 is closed.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- Superseded PRs + authors: #9809 by @NiuBlibing (replaced collectively by this stacked series).
- Scope materially carried forward: This PR carries the chat connection and timeout construction slice; other slices remain in the declared stack.
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? No.
- If `No`, why: The original PR and this stack have the same author; no additional contributor requires a co-author trailer.

prs.title: feat(config): prepare nested registry reflection and input normalization
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`; stacked after #12456.
- **What changed and why:** Add the reusable configuration reflection machinery needed by the registry editor: nested map CRUD through flattened `Configurable` prefixes, generated secret lifecycle hooks, and input normalization generated from the same field definition.
- **Scope boundary:** This PR contains only the reflection/configuration layer. V5 registry admission, migration, provider activation, RPC/UI cutover and downstream consumers remain in #12450 and later layers.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-config`, `zeroclaw-macros`, and the small generated map-path consumers that must carry owned paths.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related to #9809 and #12450. Split layer 5d. Depends on #12456.

### What this does, simply

A flattened nested configuration can now list and edit map sections using the same fully qualified paths. Secret fields declared by extensions participate in encrypt/decrypt/mask/restore together with regular fields. The input DTO is generated from the same schema fields as the runtime type, so normalization cannot silently drift from the owning configuration definition. The reflection layer does not activate the V5 root configuration.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes; review this incremental layer after #12456.

- **Steps to run:** Run the Configurable and configuration reflection tests, including listing a returned map section and passing its path back to create/edit operations.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Flattened paths are rebased consistently for listing and editing; dotted keys remain unambiguous; generated hooks use the existing secret store and return errors.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Nested flattened map routing and shared input/secret hooks are unavailable.

### How I tested

- **Commands run and tail output:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check`: exit 0. Heavy local Cargo builds/tests were delegated to GitHub CI.

- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; this is configuration machinery only.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `5009081e53`; [exact-head GitHub checks](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12457/checks).
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** No interactive action performed.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full local compilation/test/clippy was skipped to use GitHub CI as requested.

### Restack note

This PR was force-restacked onto the completed #12456 head `a3dbb1f289`. It contains only the six reflection-layer commits `e9a87b87e1`, `8d61807d12`, `90b0991b01`, `eb79797658`, `9200268637`, and `cdf1929c97`, replayed as `65608cfa00` through `5009081e53`. The previous polluted cumulative history was removed.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Secret lifecycle hooks are generated for extension fields and use the existing store/error contracts; no new secret source is introduced.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, fixtures, or tests? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Existing secret masking, encryption, decryption and restoration contracts remain authoritative; root activation is owned by #12450.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for existing configuration types and consumer entry points; this layer adds reusable reflection behavior without activating the new root layout.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No active root-format change.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.

prs.title: refactor(providers): share native capability protocols and HTTP transport
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (stacked layer; depends on #12454).
- **What changed and why:** Add shared OpenAI-compatible embedding, transcription, speech, and native Decisions protocol adapters, plus one transport builder that applies resolved headers, credentials, TLS, timeout, and live proxy policy.
- **Scope boundary:** This layer owns provider-side wire protocols and transport reuse. Registry activation, migration, active consumer switching, agent/session selection, CLI, Web, and ZeroCode remain in later stacked layers.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-api` embedding contract and `zeroclaw-providers` capability adapters/transport. Existing legacy embedding construction remains available and lenient; registry construction can opt into strict declared dimensions when a later consumer supplies them.
- **Linked issue(s):** Depends on #12454. Supersedes #9809 as part of the stacked replacement series.

### What this does, simply

Provider vendors can share the same wire protocol. This layer keeps those wire implementations in one provider-owned protocol namespace and gives all capability adapters one transport construction path. Error responses are bounded and sanitized, redirects are disabled for capability calls, empty bearer keys are omitted, and cached clients are invalidated when the live proxy policy changes.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A; mock HTTP boundary tests cover protocol parsing, bounded errors, legacy embedding construction, resolved dimension validation, and transport-cache reuse.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** GitHub CI runs the workspace tests, lint, feature/platform matrix, security, and source-image checks for the exact head; the current Quality Gate is [44921289445](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/44921289445). Full provider execution remains delegated to CI per the stacked workflow.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No paid/live-provider request is claimed; no registry consumer or user-facing surface is activated here. The report-only risk workflow and source-image checks are evaluated by the same current-head CI run; no non-required baseline failure is carried into this head.
- **Commands run and tail output:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — exit 0; `git diff --check` — exit 0.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Rebuilt the layer on top of #12454's current head `8ae63adb4e` and retained only the native protocol/transport commits. The legacy `OpenAiEmbedding::new` path remains dimension-lenient; the resolved `EmbeddingProviderConfig` path validates an explicitly supplied width. Shared error and transport-cache tests remain in the provider/config boundaries.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no CLI, web, TUI, or channel surface changes.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `59df8164e3`; exact-head validation is provided by the GitHub checks on this PR.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Native capability calls now share protocol serialization/parsing and transport policy without activating registry consumers.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace tests/builds are delegated to GitHub CI because this layer's matrix is expensive locally.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No new caller is activated; existing capability calls use the shared transport.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Shared transport supplies selected credentials and headers, omits empty bearer keys, disables redirects, and propagates client construction errors. Upstream error bodies are capped before sanitization.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Redirects are disabled so credentials cannot follow an unexpected endpoint; proxy/client cache entries are invalidated by the existing live proxy authority.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? No for the three deliberate transport behaviors listed below. Existing constructors and legacy embedding width behavior remain available in this preparatory layer.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No root-format or CLI change in this layer.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: Capability requests use a 60-second embedding deadline, reject redirects, and omit empty bearer headers. Existing legacy embedding construction continues accepting server-reported widths; only resolved construction validates a declared width. Later registry activation owns migration behavior.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Revert dependent consumer layers first, then revert this protocol/transport layer.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Protocol parsing, timeout, redirect, client construction, or vector-width checks fail at the provider boundary.

Stack integration: this PR is based on #12454 and contains only native protocol/transport changes. Refresh later layers after this PR's head is accepted. Original #9809 is closed and replaced by this stack.

## Supersede Attribution (required only when `Supersedes #` is used)

- Superseded PRs + authors: #9809 by @NiuBlibing (replaced collectively by this stacked series).
- Scope materially carried forward: This PR carries the native protocol and transport slice; registry activation and UI slices remain in later PRs.
- `Co-authored-by` trailers added in commit messages for incorporated contributors? No.
- If `No`, why: The original PR and this stack have the same author; there is no additional contributor to attribute with a co-author trailer.
